## ESSAYS (one `### path` section per file)

### deploy/docker/Dockerfile + Dockerfile — the images (fleet pods + the single container)
`deploy/docker/Dockerfile` builds the FLEET image (one pod per user, the pets model): the runtime base (dtach, rclone/fuse3, the in-container desktop — TigerVNC + XFCE + Debian chromium — xpra pinned to 6.* from xpra.org, xvfb, xdotool/wmctrl, at-spi), the agent CLIs, and the app as a SEED at /opt/vibespace-dist cloned from the PUBLIC repo at `VIBESPACE_REF` (the entrypoint copies it into the PVC on first boot; a pod's checkout git-pulls ahead of its image from then on). Only the Dockerfile and `deploy/docker/{boot-root.sh,entrypoint.sh,xfce/}` come from the BUILD CONTEXT — a lane's unpushed app code is never in the image. Build: `docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile --build-arg VIBESPACE_REF=master -t <registry>/vibespace:<tag> <checkout>`. The root `Dockerfile` is the single-container deployment (`COPY . .`, `node server.js`, no desktop, no browser). Pinned downloads fail the build by name (mc by tag + sha256, agent-browser by its own `--version`).

**3.6.0 (lane fleet-image-2, 2026-10-01) — pid 1 is `tini` in BOTH images.** Before, pid 1 was `runuser` (boot-root.sh `exec runuser`) in the fleet image and `node` in the root one; neither reaps an orphan, so every detached process the product starts whose parent died (dtach masters, agent-browser daemons and their Chrome, xpra + its Xvfb, the xpra install runner) stayed a ZOMBIE until the pod restarted — thousands per pod, measured on two fleet pods. A zombie reads ALIVE to `kill -0` and to `tail --pid`, so the install launcher's follower of an orphaned runner never ended (test-desktop-serve hung on a pod). Measured on the built image: 100 orphans (`setsid sh -c "sleep 0.2 & exit 0"`) ⇒ 0 zombies under tini, 100 (ppid 1) on the previous image. Shutdown is unchanged: tini forwards SIGTERM to the boot wrapper, runuser passes it to the supervised entrypoint and SIGKILLs it 2 s later (`docker stop` ≈ 2.1 s on both images — runuser's own grace, older than this change). `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "/usr/local/bin/vibespace-boot"]`; the chart sets no `command`, so the image's entrypoint is what runs.
**agent-browser 0.38.1 is baked** (`npm install -g agent-browser@0.38.1`, the TABLE_VERSION src/browser-verbs.js measured — `AGENT_BROWSER_CLI.table`, the ONE version row {table, floor, recordingFloor}; test-browser-cli-pin ⑦ pins this Dockerfile and package.json to it; npm's EBADENGINE warning for node 22 is harmless — the postinstall points /usr/local/bin/agent-browser at the native binary). Nothing is downloaded at runtime: with no `~/.agent-browser/browsers` it launches the Debian chromium (154, in the CDP census) — headless (`HeadlessChrome/154`), or headed on its OWN Xvfb (`Chrome/154`, the hidden-window rung) — measured in the image with no network. A copy a user installs with `npm i -g` lands in /usr/local (the image layer, owned by the user) and is replaced by the image's at the next roll. **Tools added:** x11vnc (the Xvfb + x11vnc spelling of the vnc-display rung), xclip (the server's clipboard image paste, the xpra clipboard gate), ffmpeg (a shared window's pixels, `captureVerdict`), python3-setproctitle (xpra rewrites its own title and environ with it — the shape the rung was measured on; without it the environ stays as spawned, test-desktop-display pins both).
**The suites the fleet image is measured by** (the fleet e2e's table, re-run on the rebuilt image): a suite that met a fleet fact it was not written for now runs it or names it — test-desktop-serve (a zombie runner is a named skip, never a hang), test-desktop-vnc-fit (xfwm4's frames), test-desktop-display (xpra's environ by python3-setproctitle, both shapes), test-desktop-xpra (the clipboard token without xclip), test-browser-display-chrome (the Debian chromium is the system browser agent-browser launches), test-browser-live ⑤ (no `~/.agent-browser/browsers` ⇒ the system browser, never a skip), test-browser-propose-chrome ④b (the press goes to the element it checked).

### data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs

**Lane S3 (2026-09-26, naive-user study 2): the Stop text is the SERVER's, reworded.** The hook forwards `/api/agent/stop-check`'s `reason` verbatim (as it always did — codex's wrapper wraps the same reason in `<vibespace-reminder>`), and that reason is now ONE function, `stopNudgeReason(T, extra)` in src/agent-routes.js. The old closing "Then stop again." left the nudge turn's MESSAGE to the model: it restated its whole answer ("Task complete — …") and narrated the bookkeeping ("Status is set to done — no task group is linked…"), and the testers read both as the conversation. The new closing: "Make these calls first, then stop: do not restate your answer; end with at most one short line (the user already has your answer above, and this bookkeeping is not news to them)." — tools first, then at most one line (a turn's substance goes at its END: CLAUDE.md "claude CLI 中途文本丢失"); the head names itself "this note is from VibeSpace, not from the user"; step (2) says "the For you tray only notifies". The marker phrase `VibeSpace bookkeeping before you stop` still opens the text after the user's `agents.stopNudgeExtra` — the chat's note classifier (src/lib/chat-run-summary.js `NOTE_MARKER`) reads it on the pre-S3 and the S3 wording alike. Budget: the largest extra the setting allows (500 × a 4-byte glyph) keeps the reason ≤ 9600 B (test-chat-hygiene §2). The hook file itself is unchanged.

**Browser takeover C2 (2.369.168):** unchanged — the Browsing line it delivers is the server's text (`browserIntroLine`), so the one-tool teaching reaches every harness through it without a hook edit.

**Lane artifacts-prompt-hint (2.369.223):** unchanged — the Artifacts sentence it delivers is composed server-side (src/agent-routes.js `fileToolsOf` + src/harnesses/artifacts-of.js `artifactsIntroLine`), once per session in the tools intro / task context, never in the per-turn reminder.

**Lane prompt-budget (B-2aad, 2.369.227):** unchanged — the intro it delivers (no-task SessionStart, codex first prompt) is `sessionToolsIntro`'s, now ~3.4 KB (was 7.6 KB); every seen-gate and fit-or-wait decision is the server's as before.


data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs — Dual-harness hook (SessionStart→task context OR a baseline tools intro for no-task sessions, UserPromptSubmit→first-prompt context + status-override notices + per-turn micro-reminder, Stop→bookkeeping nudge (2.79.0, CLAUDE-ONLY registration): calls GET /api/agent/stop-check and emits {decision:'block', reason} when the server says the board state is stale — the agent gets ONE follow-up mini-turn to set status/mirror asks/log progress, gated by stop_hook_active (never loops), server-side staleness+cooldown thresholds (agents.stopNudgeStaleMinutes/CooldownMinutes, defaults 10/30min, clamped 1-240/2-720 — 2.89.0; an EXPLICIT 0 = every-stop mode: 0 stale = always stale, 0 cooldown = none — 2.210.0 user request; stop_hook_active/nudgeTurnActive still cap it at ONE mini-turn per user turn); codex's equivalent rides codex-chat-wrapper's turn/completed (maybeStopNudge → synthetic <vibespace-reminder> turn, nudgeTurnActive guard) since the app-server has no blockable Stop in JSON-RPC mode; generated at startup; env-gated no-op only when VIBESPACE_API/TOKEN are absent — a MISSING VIBESPACE_TASK_ID no longer no-ops (2.38.0), so any VibeSpace session still learns `vibespace-status`; emits ONLY nested hookSpecificOutput). Registered idempotently for BOTH events in ~/.claude/settings.json + ~/.codex/hooks.json by ensureAgentHooks — only the vibespace entry is ever touched. **THE HOOK NAMES ITS EVENT (channel-jump verify r7, 2026-09-27): both context calls carry `X-VibeSpace-Hook-Event: <event>` — the codex app-server runs these hooks and DROPS their answers (measured 0.142.5), so the routes answer a hook-originated call empty on a chat session whose harness delivers through its wrapper (`inject.kind: 'wrapper'`) and drain nothing for it; task-context is empty for any harness with `sessionStartHonoured: false` regardless of the header. The script is the template in src/server/agent-tool-generators.js (`createHookHelper`, regenerated at every boot); the tracked file must equal it byte for byte (test-stash-strip ②h pins the equality).** **TEMP-SERVER GUARD (2.225.1, real incident): a server running from under os.tmpdir() skips ALL global hook writes (register AND strip; hookRegistrationSafe) — a /tmp worktree smoke server once rewrote the global hook command to its throwaway path, and after cleanup every hook errored MODULE_NOT_FOUND for two days (the CLI snapshots hook config per session, so healing the file doesn't reach running sessions). Any test harness that boots server.js should also set VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1 (all four worktree smokes do); VIBESPACE_FORCE_AGENT_HOOKS=1 overrides.** **INTEGRATION MASTER SWITCH (2.190.0, settings category "Integration"): `agents.vibespaceIntegration` default ON; OFF = the model gets a pristine CLI. SCOPE = AGENT-VISIBLE integration ONLY (2.190.1, user decision): model-invisible plumbing is EXEMPT — the usage statusline, billing/account env, Ctrl+G editor, keeper transport all keep working either way. PER-FEATURE toggles under it (2.211.0, user request '注入context但不给ask/progress'): `agents.contextInjection` (group payloads/diffs; per-group injectContext stays the finer grain) + `agents.toolStatus`/`toolAsk`/`toolTask` — a disabled tool is neither TAUGHT (sessionToolsIntro()/renderContext's _toolsSectionParts/per-turn reminder/stop-nudge steps all compose from enabledTools(); teaching a refusing command trains dead ends) nor SERVED (its write endpoints 403 with skip-and-continue-do-not-retry guidance); toolStatus off also silences the stop-check arbiter (it is keyed on status staleness); contextInjection off falls back to the baseline tools intro; reads (GET /api/agent/task = `vibespace-task show`) stay governed by the master, not toolTask. Route smoke: scripts/test-tool-toggles.mjs (21 asserts).** Hook entries stripped live on toggle (persistence writeSettings' `onSettingsWrite` callback → stripAgentHookEntries; boot re-checks the setting so a flip-while-down converges; the boot ensureAgentHooks call is DEFERRED until after setupPersistence so the setting is readable), new spawns get NO VIBESPACE_API/tools-PATH/remote-prelude (keeper still ships; VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN stays for Ctrl+G editor auth, inert alone since every consumer guards on api+token), and agent-routes gates every model-visible CONTENT response for pre-toggle sessions too: the three deliveries return empty (prompt-context also consumes-and-DROPS pending status-override notices — deferring them injected stale reminders on re-enable) and GET /api/agent/task 403s (it returns the same steering substance; `vibespace-task show` must not bypass the pristine state) while WRITE endpoints stay live. Both Install routes (local /api/agent-hooks/install AND host /api/hosts/:id/agent-tools/install) refuse while OFF; the Manage-Agents host row shows the residue + keeps Remove as cleanup. Dial spawns drop the `$HOME/.vibespace/bin` PATH segment too (leftover tools from earlier ON spawns must not be name-resolvable). Distinct from the data/.agent-hooks-optout marker (manual Manage-Agents Remove) — the setting never writes the marker, and re-enable does NOT override it. E2E: scripts/test-integration-toggle.mjs. vibespace-hook-register.mjs = self-locating installer distributed to remote hosts (P3); its `--uninstall` mode (2.129.0) strips ONLY our entry from the remote configs (foreign hooks untouched) — the Manage-Agents remote Remove path. **SSH→DIAL GRADUATION (2.248.0, B-6640; **AUTOMATIC since 2.311.0** — `hosts.onSshConnected` fires after every successful ssh device connect and the server graduates in the background. Gates, each of them a way to do something the operator did not ask for: setting `agentd.autoGraduate` (default on) + an operator-declared `agentd.publicUrl` (it must NEVER self-publish this instance to the relay — that side effect is the operator's choice) + per-machine `autoGraduate:false` + one attempt/machine/6h; failures serverNotice and leave the machine on ssh. The install half is `graduateHostToDial()`, shared by the button and the auto path. Test: scripts/test-auto-graduate.mjs): an ssh machine can install the daemon as a persistent service and DIAL BACK over ws — `POST /api/hosts/:id/graduate-dial` (`{serverUrl|viaRelay}`, `{remove:true}` rolls back). The record keeps `transport:'ssh'` and gains `deviceId`+`dialTokenHash`+`dialRoot`; `_deviceConnect` prefers the live dial link and falls through to ssh on ANY failure (never worse than before), `findByDeviceId` falls back to non-dial records so dial-in auth resolves, `onDialIn` evicts a cached ssh dm, `list()` exposes `graduated`/`dialLive`. INVARIANTS: ssh stays the bootstrap+rescue channel (never removed); the base URL is explicit>publicUrl>relay and the MACHINE is asked whether it can reach it BEFORE anything installs (unreachable ⇒ abort, stay pure-ssh — a daemon that can never dial in is worse than no daemon); `dialRoot` must mirror the installer's own derivation byte-for-byte (hostname-only + `tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9.-'`) or removal tears down the wrong directory; removal always clears the local record even if the host is dead. E2E: scripts/test-graduate-dial.mjs (10 asserts against a real host; needs an ssh reverse tunnel so the host can reach the throwaway server). REMOTE-TEST GOTCHAS the harness encodes: server.js honours NO data-dir env (a worktree's own data/ IS the isolation), an inherited VIBESPACE_PASSWORD turns auth on and 401s everything, a worktree is at HEAD so uncommitted changes must be copied in, and `pkill -f vibespace-agentd` over ssh matches its OWN command line and kills the session (use `pgrep -f "[v]ibespace-agentd" | xargs -r kill`).** **BOUNDED DEVICE CONNECT (2.246.2/2.247.0, B-fa6f — userN's flapping H200s): `hosts.deviceBounded(id, connectMs=6000)` races device() against a deadline for every READ-ONLY/interactive data-plane consumer (~26 sites: discovery/RemoteFs/dirComplete/slab sync/usage harvest/mount heal/ports/exit) — the connect ladder runs up to ~2.7min and on a lossy path where TCP opens but the ssh banner hangs (ConnectTimeout only bounds the TCP connect, verified live) every surface sat on it BEFORE its own ssh fallback. THREE INVARIANTS (adversarial-review-hardened, do not regress): ① session-ESTABLISHING consumers keep the FULL ladder or ≥15s — findKeeperFor (adopt-vs-respawn: a deadline reads as 'no live keeper' → writer sweep SIGTERMs the healthy claude), _hostShell (accountsStatus rides it inside CREATE's linked/host-held rescue), homeDir (feeds the create cwd default, B-0d70 shape); ② the race OBSERVES the loser promise (p.catch(()=>{})) — an abandoned ladder's late rejection is an unhandledRejection = process crash on Node≥15; ③ device() DEDUPES in-flight connects per id (_deviceInflight → _deviceConnect) — without it every timed-out probe stacked another 13×ssh ladder under a 5s-polling sidebar. Any hosts-like TEST MOCK must also implement deviceBounded (two suites broke on the missing method). **B-218d FIXED in 2.247.1-2.247.3** (2.247.2: EXPLICIT-host ssh resumes probe findKeeperFor too — before, only host-inference and dial did, so a sidebar resume with the host selected always swept; 2.247.3: findKeeperFor rewritten — the ssh leg scanned only legacy run/ and NEVER saw agentd sessions, and grep-in-state-json only matches RESUMED spawns (--resume embeds the cid) — now ONE scan over both stores + a childPid→~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json lock leg for fresh spawns, returning {sid, kind} so the consumer routes to the right attach binary): findKeeperFor's agentd pipe sids are tagged `keeperKind:'agentd'` and the ssh branch adopts them via the attach-cli with a NO-spawn-spec cfg (the dial branch's contract) — before this, they were fed to the legacy keeper binary (which only reads ~/.vibespace/run) so the 2.218.0 keeper-attach optimization silently never worked over ssh and every such resume degraded to sweep+respawn. Legacy keeper sids (client discovery K lines) keep the old runTail; provisioning failure degrades to it too.** **NODE RESOLUTION (2.244.2-2.244.4, userN's Novita chicken-and-egg): hook entries register with the ABSOLUTE process.execPath (hooks run via /bin/sh with claude's PATH — nvm-managed node never resolves there, and claude is a native binary), and ALL FOUR register invocation sites (ssh prelude / dial install / manual Install / Remove) run a POSIX node finder (PATH → newest nvm → common paths) then EXPORT the found node dir onto the session PATH — a bare `node` invocation of the register silently no-op'd on dash hosts, so the fix could never apply itself AND every #!/usr/bin/env node agent tool was dead there. Any new remote code path invoking node must use the finder, never bare `node`.**

### data/bin/vibespace-task

data/bin/vibespace-task — Agent task-reporting CLI (STATIC tracked file, not generated — inline template-in-template escaping was unmaintainable): show [--full]/progress "summary" [--detail]/backlog/backlog-add/backlog-done/backlog-drop → /api/agent/task* (scoped to the session's own context task). **progress SUCCESS OUTPUT reminds the agent (2.210.0, the vibespace-ask 2.111.21 pattern): the activity log is agent-facing — deliverables (URLs/paths/results) must ALSO go in the chat reply (real pattern: agent logged a URL via progress and ended the turn without saying it).** **CHECKLIST REMOVED (2.121.0, user decision):** `plan-check/plan-uncheck/plan-add` are gone — a group-level list of agent WORK ITEMS never made sense (those live at the SESSION level = the agent's own todo list, surfaced as the card's Steps). The subcommands now print a redirect; `/api/agent/task-plan` answers old CLI copies (remote hosts) with 410 + guidance; stored `plan` arrays stay DORMANT in data/task-groups.json (never rendered/written; update() ignores plan patches; config-bundle import passes them through). **BACKLOG ADDED (2.122.0; CLAIM MODEL 2.123.0 — a DIFFERENT concept on the same shelf):** the group's PARKING LOT for NON-immediate items (deferred user decisions, "later" work; item = {**id: stable `B-xxxx`**, text, detail?, status open|done|dropped, **claimedBy: [session keys]**, addedBy/At, resolvedBy/At}); agents park via `backlog-add` when the user defers something (parking AUTO-CLAIMS for the caller) and are taught to NEVER start parked items unasked. Refs everywhere = id / 1-based OPEN-list index / unique substring; **the id travels** — the user copies it from the viewer and hands it to ANY member agent ("看一下 backlog B-ab12"), which runs `backlog <id>` (full item view, works on resolved items) and `backlog-claim <id>`. **INJECTION IS SUMMARY-ONLY + TARGETED (user directives): the hook never dumps the backlog** — renderContext gets `sessionKey` and emits a compact reminder block ONLY for open items THAT session CLAIMED (+ a one-line "N open — `vibespace-task backlog`" pointer otherwise); change events (PARKED/RESOLVED/DROPPED/CLAIMED/UNCLAIMED/reworded/REMOVED) ride the diff updates but reach ONLY sessions that created or claimed the item — diff matching is by the stable id (text edit ⇒ "reworded", not REMOVED+NEW). TASK.md/`show` carry the full open list with ids+claimants. One-time seed: dormant plan's unchecked items → open backlog items; id + creator-auto-claim backfill for pre-2.123.0 items (constructor, idempotent). **SUMMARY+DETAIL split (2.69.0):** progress entries carry a one-line `note` (what everyone sees inline — board rows, injected context marked `†`) + optional `detail` (≤6000 chars; TASK.md renders it as an indented blockquote, `show --full` prints it, the board's Activity rows expand on click) — this keeps the byte-budgeted injection dense without losing information. session-status records gained the same: `reason` = one-liner on chips, `detail` (≤2000) shown in Session Properties + `vibespace-status show` **PRIORITY (2.369.154):** `backlog-add "item" [--detail] [--priority high|normal|low]` and `backlog-edit <id> [--text] [--detail] [--priority]` (the server refuses a value outside the set by name, exit 1); `backlog` prints the list IN THE SERVER'S ORDER (sortBacklog — this static file ships to checkout-less hosts and never re-sorts, so its numbers stay the route's) with `!` high / `↓` low before the id and a `(you)` / `(you + N others)` / `(claimed by N)` / `(unclaimed)` tail (GET task's `you`); `backlog <id>` prints the priority. **A `#` is the number in the list the session was LAST SHOWN (2.369.154 r2):** the route remembers the ids it served to each session's GET task and resolves a number against them (a later add by anyone never moves what `backlog-done 3` means; a since-resolved item is refused, nothing changed); `backlog-done/-drop` print `resolved [B-xxxx] <text>` from the server's echo; the usage steers mutating verbs to ids. Gate: test-backlog-priority. **THE CLEANUP NUDGE (2.369.154):** `backlog-add` / `backlog-edit` / `backlog-claim` print the server's `nudge.text` on its own stdout line prefixed `note:` (the `note: ALSO claimed by` convention; exit code stays 0) when the answer carries one — never on done / drop / unclaim. Gate: test-backlog-nudge §4 (the real CLI over loopback + source pins with a cut-copy control).

**"Clear content…" (2026-09-28).** `progress-redact <P-id|at>` → `POST /api/agent/task/progress-redact` clears an Activity-log entry THIS session wrote (its words become "[cleared at the user's request]"; time, place and author stay). `progress` now echoes the new entry's id (`progress recorded as [P-…]`, from the route's `entry`) and `show` prints the id of the caller's OWN entries only (`session === you`) — the handle the verb takes. A 404 with no `code` = an older server ("ask the user to update, or to clear it from the Task Group log window"). Kept outside the backlog-add…backlog-claim slice test-backlog-no-truncation reads.

### data/bin/vibespace-ask

data/bin/vibespace-ask — Agent CLI for the GLOBAL USER-TODO inbox (2.65.0, STATIC tracked): files items the USER must act on (decision/input/review) → POST /api/agent/user-todo (vsst_ scoped to own session). `"text" [--detail] [--urgency]` / list / resolve <id|text>; `help|-h|--help` and any flag-looking first arg print usage instead of filing (2.76.0 — a real agent filed the literal item "--help"); idempotent re-file by same text; the SUCCESS OUTPUT reminds the agent (2.111.21) that the inbox is only a notification mirror — the full content must ALSO go in the chat reply (real pattern: agents filed and ended the turn silently). **Semantics (2.76.1, user directive): MIRROR every chat question** — whenever an agent asks the user anything in chat / ends a turn waiting on them / sets needs-input|blocked|review, it must ALSO file the item (the user is often not watching that window), and the moment the user answers ANYWHERE (chat counts) the agent resolves it itself — taught in all three surfaces (SESSION_TOOLS_INTRO, renderContext tools section, the CLI's own usage text); taught in SESSION_TOOLS_INTRO + renderContext; distributed to remote hosts like the other tools

**2.369.169 (design-user-inbox-reply D1.3/D3a).** `--options "A|B|C"` = up to 6 one-click answers (split on `|`, trimmed and sent AS TYPED — inbox r1: an empty label (`"A||B"`, a trailing `|`) is no longer dropped client-side, the store refuses it by name like every other bad shape; §5b of test-inbox-reply runs the CLI against the store's own rule) — the filed-item echo prints them and `list` prints `options: A | B`; `show <id>` prints one item of this session in full, any status, with the user's inbox reply (the reply quote's cut line points here). The usage text says a reply arrives as a user message opening with `[For you reply #<id>]`; the full shape is in docs/agent/ask-manual.md `## Replies from the inbox`.

**"Clear content…" (2026-09-28).** `vibespace-ask clear <id>` → `{clear: id}` on the same route: an item this session FILED ITSELF keeps its place, status and time in the tray; its words (text, detail, i18n, chips, reply) go. A helper's permission ask filed under the session's key by the SERVER is not its own (403 `not_yours`). An older server answers the unknown body with its named 400.

### data/bin/vibespace-usage

data/bin/vibespace-usage — PASSIVE usage capture (STATIC tracked file, not generated; 2.60.0). A `statusLine` hook injected via `--settings` into LOCAL CLAUDE TERMINAL sessions only (2.62.0: the ws-handler injection is gated `backend==='claude'` — only the claude CLI understands `--settings`; un-gated it rode on `zsh -l` and codex spawns too, making every shell terminal (incl. the Manage-Agents Update/Login helpers) and local codex terminal exit instantly as "terminated"; NOT gated by the Integration master switch — 2.190.1 user decision: the switch scopes to AGENT-VISIBLE integration only, and the statusline is model-invisible plumbing) — the CLI feeds it the payload's `rate_limits` (5h/7d used_percentage+reset, "only after first API response" — and NOTHING else: model-scoped buckets like the Fable weekly cap are NOT in the statusline payload, verified vs the 2.1.206 payload builder) which it writes to data/usage-cache/<accountKey>.json (throttle 8s; **PRESERVES `scopedWeekly`/`scopedFetchedAt` from the existing file** — 2.70.0, clobbering them to [] every write is what made Fable vanish from the quota popup) + passes through the user's own statusline. Also harvests `model.id` → data/usage-cache/__models__.json (passive model discovery). ZERO Anthropic calls — this is why VibeSpace makes no background /api/oauth/usage poll by default (that off-CLI fixed-cadence sub-token call is the #1 ban trigger — see §ban-safety on accounts.js). Chat/stream-json has no statusline → those accounts show last-known. **THE ACCOUNT KEY IS THE LINK, RESOLVED PER WRITE, ONE REQUEST BEHIND IT (2026-09-07 + r3).** `VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_KEY` is fixed at SPAWN, so a hot-switched pooled session filed every later reading under the member it STARTED on; ws-create also ships `VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK` (the credential SYMLINK the CLI reads) and `accountKey()` readlinks it. But the payload's `rate_limits` is the CLI's LAST API response — made with the credentials the link pointed at BEFORE a re-point — so resolving the link alone honoured a switch one request EARLY and the old member's numbers landed on the new one, stamped `fetchedAt: now`, where the anchor sweep turns any usage-cache write into ground truth (the B-b3cd odometer-flap class on the write path). The server's twin pins the slot for the TURN; a statusline has no turn, so it pins on the NUMBERS: a `.slot-<session_id>` sidecar beside the cache (deliberately no `.json` — every usage-cache scanner filters on that extension) holds `{key, fp}` for the last payload OBSERVED (updated even when the 8s throttle skips the write — a payload seen under the old target is still evidence about which credentials produced it), and while the link has MOVED but the fingerprint has NOT, the reading is left where it is. The first differing payload is the first one the new credentials produced. A session with no link writes no state file at all (it cannot switch under itself). **2026-09-08 — it asks the SHARED rule, and it had two defects of its own (round 3, reproduced).** The sidecar now records `{key, fp, win, at}` and calls the mirrored `decideLagShadow`, so it can also answer the case the fingerprint clause could not: a payload whose WINDOW is the previous slot's even though the numbers moved. **(a) It must hand that rule a RE-POINT age, and it was handing it an OBSERVATION age.** `st.at` dates the last render under the old slot, which necessarily PRECEDES the re-point that ended it, so it systematically overstates — and one ordinary render of an IDLE pooled terminal (30 min since its redraw, link re-pointed a second earlier) answered `shadow-expired` and filed the previous member's 96 % onto the low-usage one, second false pool switch and all, in a shape master's unconditional r3 rule had protected. The pool's re-point MINTS the symlink (`repointPoolSymlink` = symlink-to-temp + rename), so `fs.lstatSync(VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK).mtimeMs` IS the re-point instant (measured: 7200 s on an untouched link, 0.001 s straight after); unreadable or future-dated ⇒ `null` ⇒ UNKNOWN, which does not expire. `st.at` stays as forensics. **(b) It was the one value producer with NO window guard** — the engine guards every write and this file, at up to 8 renders a minute per account, guarded none: every path that reaches the write without a shadow (no link, unreadable link, re-point past the horizon, a payload the windows cannot place) wrote whatever `accountKey()` resolved. It now runs the mirrored `decideReadingTarget` against its own `establishedWindows()` (keyed off the CACHE FILES, like the engine's), re-filing onto the one matching account and otherwise REFUSING — writing nothing anywhere and recording the reason in `.window-refused.ndjson` beside the cache (no `.json`, per-day shard on overflow). A single shipped file has no identity-group table, so an org-merged login reads as TWO matches and is refused rather than re-filed: the conservative direction, and the server's guard still sees every later reading. **2026-09-09 r2 — IT STOPPED ENUMERATING WHAT TO KEEP.** The `out` literal listed the fields worth preserving, and that list is the most expensive line in this store's history: it has now silently deleted `scopedWeekly` (2.70.0), the org identity, `spend` (B-87fe), `corroborated`, the established window (which is why THAT lives in a sidecar) — and `limits`, the typed canonical half, measured against the REAL tool over a migrated copy of a real cache file: three limits in, ZERO out, the `overage` object gone with them, and the next reader re-deriving them under THIS producer's name and clock. Six losses, one mechanism, so the default is inverted: `out` now SPREADS the stored object and states only the fields this render measured (`fiveHour`/`sevenDay`/`overallStatus`/`fetchedAt`/`source`, plus `scopedWeekly` defaulted so a reader can still tell a claude snapshot from a codex one). It touches `limits` exactly once, and by REMOVING: it DROPS the `plan` limit — the only one it can measure, whose reading it has just written into the legacy buckets — so `liftCacheObject` reconstructs it with this object's own `source`/`fetchedAt`, and every other limit survives byte-identical with the provenance of the producer that DID measure it. A producer that cannot express a window state or another limit's age can never forge one, and this file never has to carry a second spelling of the model's window rules. It never AUTHORS the array on a not-yet-migrated file (a one-element list claiming to be all of them would delete that file's scoped cap the moment anything lifted it), and `corroborated` is the one field it deliberately does NOT inherit — that is a verdict about a different reading, and this producer has no observation to re-earn it. §⑮ of scripts/test-quota-model.mjs drives the REAL file; its negative control is a patched copy with the spread reverted to the enumerated literal. **MODEL-SCOPED WINDOWS (claude 2.1.274, measured in the binary's statusline schema — inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** `rate_limits.model_scoped[]` = {display_name, utilization = the server row's PERCENT (the binary's `Yde` projection puts `s.percent` there; ÷100 unconditionally, never by magnitude — 2.369.99), resets_at ISO} beside the older `seven_day_<model>` fields; `scopedFromRateLimits` writes each as the scoped bucket of that NAME (the lane is decided by what names it — never into `seven_day`), an empty list states nothing (the previous entries survive: the 2.70.0 rule), and the limits this render measured (the plan + the named model caps, matched by NAME never by re-spelling the id) are dropped so the reader reconstructs them with this producer's provenance. The statusline never carries `seven_day_overage_included` (census ⑩); the reading-lag mirror block is byte-identical still. test-quota-model ⑲ TOOL drives the real file (percent, ISO reset, an un-named Opus keeps its age, an empty list retires nothing, a top-level `seven_day_opus` names its lane the same way).

Fallback ladder: op → script-ship over the device link → ssh. E2E: scripts/test-usage-scan-op.mjs (13 asserts, real daemon).** **R4 step 2 (2.287.0): ①PUSH-triggered harvest — the daemon's discovery watch (now also `.codex/sessions`) pushes debounced `discovery-dirty`; hosts._armDirtyPush (armed at every _deviceConnect; client re-arms on reconnect like reverse forwards) fans it to discovery cache invalidation + server-side per-host debounced harvest kick (60s floor unchanged) — remote ledger/billing-popup freshness ≈1min for ANY activity incl. mid-turn/codex/external; the dirty signal previously had NO consumer. ②CODEX ROLLOUTS in all three walkers (synthetic rid = cumulative total, turn_context model/cwd persisted in cursor, input−cached split, heartbeats skipped, CODEX_HOME honored); ingestRemoteEvents honors `be` — remote codex usage lands in the ledger. Codex parity leg in test-usage-walk-parity (21).** Harvest chain: hosts.harvestUsage (15min/host idle throttle; **EVENT-DRIVEN since 2.284.3: a remote session's `result` kicks a prompt harvest with a 60s/host floor** — the ledger/billing-popup lag is ~1min, not 15; the pool control loop never depended on this cadence, it eats relayed stdout live via noteLive) → usageHistory.ingestRemoteEvents (**PER-ACCOUNT since 2.294.0**: resolves the real account by the SAME by-time attribution walk local events use — VibeSpace records the spawn account for remote sessions too, the ingest just discarded it; pool tag included. Only sessions VibeSpace never spawned (external terminals, pre-attribution) keep acct=<hostId>/atype='host'/billing 'remote-host', which now honestly means 'that machine's own login'. No back-billing past the grace window; `host` field always kept so the device dimension still works; rid namespaced `h:<id>:`; host-bucket events stay EXEMPT from _loadEvents re-attribution — the local log would re-bucket them to global) → POST /api/usage-stats/harvest-hosts (kicked on Usage-window open, reload on added>0). Quota side: /api/usage/refresh {host} = on-demand ⟳ with hosts.readRemoteOAuth (READ-ONLY remote token peek, never refresh, §ban-safety) → usage-cache/host-<id>.json → GET /api/usage `hosts` field (every configured host listed) → popup "Remote hosts" section (bars + per-host ⟳, class usage-host-refresh). **Walker v3 (codex per-message meta, 2026-09-06; mirrored line-for-line from src/usage-walker.js): codex events ADD `mid` = the `response_id` of the 0.153 `token_usage_record` that PRECEDES the token_count (parked in the CURSOR as `pendMid`/`pendTotal` so a harvest landing between the pair still pairs on the next run; adopted only when its `usage.total_tokens` equals `last_token_usage.total_tokens`; pre-0.153 rollouts get no mid — never invented) and `effort` (turn_context.effort, persisted like model). `rid` is UNCHANGED — it is the dedup key already baked into every permanent ledger; changing it would double-count every scanned rollout. Parity leg 21→32 incl. the scan-boundary case.**

### src/browser-job-principal.js + scripts/test-jobs-browser.mjs — A BACKGROUND WORK JOB BROWSES AS ITS OWNER CONVERSATION (lane jobs-browser, B-dbc1, 2026-10-02)

**Why.** A user's daily reconciliation job could not leave the old desktop Chromium: every `/api/agent/browser/*` route admitted only a `vsst_` session token and the job's process carries `VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN` (`jbt_`), so a scheduled job had no way into the logged-in profile its conversation uses. Every other agent route (vibespace-msg's `msgCaller`, channels `withdraw`, docs) already admits a job AS THE CONVERSATION THAT OWNS IT; the browser now does too, under the same rules.

**PURE (imports only browser-profiles' key shapes).** `jobPrincipalOf({job, ownerKey})` → `{ok, principal:{kind:'job', jobId, ownerConversationId, ownerKey}}` or a refusal by name: `unauthorized` (no job), `job_not_running` (state not in `RUNNING_STATES` = starting | up — a token outlives its run), `job_no_owner` (no owner conversation), `no_browser_key` (the owner never had a browser key, or the "key" is a child handle). **Admission = the owner's**: the job's lease key is a CHILD HANDLE of the owner's key (`bk-<owner>.<n>`, recorded `job: <jobId>`), and `mayAttach` / `whoMayUse` judge a child key as its parent — a conversation refused `not_owner` ⇒ its job refused the same; the owner's Task Groups are the job's. **Routes**: `JOB_ROUTES_ALLOWED` (profiles status providers resolve audit tab dialog direct passkey) / `JOB_ROUTES_REFUSED` (use pin new new-child detach backend blocked site-hint site-reset resume — everything that would change the conversation's browsers); `jobRouteVerdict` fails CLOSED (an unknown route is refused `job_token`); the gate censuses every route in src/routes/browser.js into exactly one list. **The profile** (`jobResolveVerdict` over the owner's `resolveHandle`): the owner's pin or attachment; the owner's temporary browser and a helper's handle never (`job_no_profile`). **Lifetime**: `carriedJobHandles(children, isRunning)` = the handles a running job carries (the keeper adds them to its live set, so a job whose owner conversation is gone keeps browsing until it ends); `jobChildrenToRelease` = the evidence rule (a job not running — finished, archived, unknown, an engine that throws — releases). **Names**: never persisted with the browsing (lane-redact verify r9) — `jobLabelOf` is read live.

**THE ORCH HALF (step 2).** *src/routes/browser.js*: `agentFacts` admits `jbt_` through ONE door (`jobAgentFacts`): the route judged first (`jobRouteVerdict` — a refused route never mints), then `jobFactsOf(token, {mint})` = the engine's `jobByToken`, the owner conversation's LIVE session if any (msgCaller's rule — it lends its Task Groups; else `tasksForConversation(cid)`), the owner's key (the live session's `_browserKey`, else the recorded binding `bindingsLookup(cid)`), `jobPrincipalOf`, the remote fence (`remote_session`), and the job's handle (`keeper.jobHandleFor`); a job whose owner is not running gets a STUB session (a name only — never spawn pairs). `askerOf` (the belt) resolves a job WITHOUT minting (`keeper.findJobHandle`). `resolveForJob`: the OWNER's set read through `resolveHandle` (never changed: no pin attach, no `told`, no stamp) → `jobResolveVerdict` → `k.attach({profileId, browserKey: <job handle>})` (its own lease ⇒ its own window, lane browser-windows) → `k.resolveFor(<job handle>)` (a takeover of the job's window pauses the job alone) → the attachment answer + `job: true`. Codes `job_token` 403, `job_not_running` / `job_no_owner` / `job_no_profile` 409. `/api/browser/session/:id` adds `jobNames` (handle → the job's name, READ LIVE off the engine; a cleared or gone job shows its id) and browser-stream's `browserListFor` marks the child row `helper.job` — the strip says "Job: <name>" (zh 后台任务, ja ジョブ). *src/server/browser-keeper.js*: dep `jobRunning(jobId)`; `liveKeys()` = the sessions' keys + `carriedJobHandles` (a running job carries its handle, so its lease outlives the owner); `jobHandleFor` / `findJobHandle` / `jobOf` / `releaseJob` (detach every lease of the handle — its window closes, a takeover of it ends — then drop it); `reconcile` releases every job handle whose job is not running BEFORE the carrier rule (boot + every tick: a run that ended without its finalize hook too); `statusFor` children carry `job` + the job's lease profile. *src/jobs.js* `_finalizeRun` calls `onRunEnded(job, run)` first (jobs-wiring forwards it; server.js → `browserKeeper.releaseJob`). *src/browser-trace.js* `entryFor({job})` stores the job by ID (`jb-<hex>` only; a user's own act never); the recorder asks `keeper.jobOf`. *data/bin/vibespace-browser*: `TOKEN = VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN || VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN` (a job's env carries only the latter). **VERIFY r1 (2026-10-02, MED — reproduced on the real routes + keeper, r1-repro/t1-real.mjs):** `jobFactsOf` found the owner's live session by `claudeSessionId === cid`, so a PENDING FORK still carrying its parent's id (first in the live set) was taken as the owner — the job's handle was minted under the FORK's browser key and judged by the fork's pin and reach (`job_no_profile` for a pinless fork; a pinned fork would have lent its logins). The channel-withdraw r4/r5 class: the lookup is `addressableId(t) === cid` now (the ladder's own predicate — a borrowed id is nobody's address); a job of a conversation with no addressable live session falls to its recorded binding as before. Measured and held in the same round: the owner gone ⇒ the job's handle AND lease survive the tick's 2-min grace and the boot's grace 0 alike (`keyCarried` reads the running job's handle in the live set); a human takeover of the job's window ⇒ the job's next verb is `browser_paused` (409, typed) — the job's process is told on every try, the drive's end is announced to the OWNER's live session only (a gone owner's job hears nothing — r2); the job handle STRING is recycled by the next run after `releaseJob` (`nextChildN` reuses `.1`; leases + leftTabs cleared by `dropChild`, a `rung2Refusals` memo keyed by it may carry — LOW); no mint for a not-running job's token (refused before any side effect), a mint before `job_no_profile` leaves a leaseless handle until the job ends (LOW, held); the owner's attachment (not only its pin) is the job's profile by design.

**Gate: scripts/test-jobs-browser.mjs (fast, 111, ~30 s — ⑥ runs a real jobs engine).** ④ THE REAL-ENGINE LEG: the real routes + keeper over test-browser-windows ④'s fake agent-browser 0.38.1 + window model — a `jbt_` resolve is admitted (it was 401), gets its own handle + lease in the owner's pinned profile, a window apart from the owner's, reuses its handle, is refused pin/use/new-child/detach/resume `job_token`, `not_owner` when the owner is (its tab closed with the refusal), `job_not_running`, `job_no_profile`; the owner gone ⇒ the running job's lease kept and it still resolves; `releaseJob` at finalize and the reconcile sweep release it; the journal names the job by id. ⑤ wiring pins + the trace's job id + the strip model. ① the principal table (12 rows), the route census + table (fail closed), the profile table, the handle + release rules; ② admission through the REAL `mayAttach`/`decideAttach` (owner and job admitted / refused together; the job's handle gets its own lease beside the owner's); ③ three mutant-copy controls (route rule fails open, no running check, the owner's temporary browser handed to a job).
**accept-fixes-jobs (2.369.204):** a job's `status` answers `job` (routes `jobBindingOf`: the profile `resolveForJob`'s verdict picks, the owner's pin, the job's own lease — read only); the jobs engine exports `VIBESPACE_JOB_CWD` (the job's absolute `cmd.cwd` only) and vibespace-browser's write fence takes it as the root inside a job (`writePathVerdict({job})` words); `attachmentsFor` keeps a child's `job` tag (the strip's "Job: <name>" row); `releaseJobHandle` closes the job's own tabs over CDP (`jobWindowCloser`, holders read before the detach) and keeps no left-tab for it. ⑥ = a real JobManager running the real CLI (F6 + every run end calls `onRunEnded`).

### src/browser-backends/ — ONE FILE PER BROWSER BACKEND + ONE REGISTRATION LINE (lane dc-browser-backends, decoupling wave 2b, 2.369.215)
**2.369.242 — the health sweep asks TWO questions (lane mount-liveness).** `_healthSweep` / `_afterMounted` only gather witnesses (`_probeLiveness`: `ls -d` = the daemon's liveness, served from rclone's VFS root without a backend call; `ls` = readiness; a fresh `rclone lsf` only when the listing hung; the daemon's CPU Δ from /proc) and apply src/mount-liveness.js's verdict (`_livenessApply`): a slow listing blocks the path 65 s and says so — never a teardown; `dead` needs `probe.strikes` (≥ 2) silent root checks; `wedged` needs the backend to answer while the listing hangs twice; `unreachable` tears down only at the 30-min ceiling. Never a copy; dirty / unread ⇒ the daemon restarts on the old dir and the row's `cache` cell says why (sidebar-mounts.js one line, network only). `remove()` uses the same child (`_dropCacheDir`, only a dir named after the record). `mediation` is passed); `validateProfileInput(input, {mediation})` threads it
and the value's `sharing` is the verdict's; `newProfileRecord` takes
`sharing`; `isMediatedProfile(p)` = `instance` on a record the migration did
not create — the legacy "Shared (legacy)" record keeps `sharing:'instance'`
for ADMISSION but is never mediated (cooperative, labelled legacy, promises no
isolation). Gate: test-browser-mediation ①.

**P4 second half (2026-09-17; §7.4 / §7.5):** the `cloud:*` FAMILY is `wired`
(`starts:true`, `binary:'agent-browser'` — our own daemon started with
upstream's `-p <name>` and the vendor's key in THAT child's env; `ownsDir`
stays false because the browser is the vendor's) except `agentcore`, unwired
BY NAME through `CLOUD_UNWIRED` (its field set is unverified against upstream,
so the refusal says so instead of a spawn that fails at the vendor); `cloak`'s
row names the `cloakbrowser` binary (the in-place switch opens the SAME
directory with the other binary + `--fingerprint=<seed>`). `validateProfileInput`
takes an INJECTABLE `control` (the keeper hands its own, which a gate may
override — one gate ignoring the override is an inconsistent seam) and a
`defaultBackend` (§7.4's per-profile default: a row id, validated like any
provider; whether it can be used HERE is the switch's question);
`newProfileRecord` carries `defaultBackend` + `lastSwitchAt`; the registry
carries `seats` (integrationId → the seat reading from the first real launch),
`majors` (provider → the Chromium major last seen writing) and `blocked` (the
agent's claims, a bounded list where every entry is `by:'agent'`). Gate:
test-browser-providers ① + test-browser-backend ③.

**P4 (2026-09-16; §7.1–§7.3, §7.2.1, D34):** the provider ROWS are the
backend-caps discipline — `PROVIDERS` (+ the `cloud:<name>` FAMILY,
`providerRow`/`providerIds`) carry every capability cell a control reads (tier
/ wired / keyScope / canSwitchTo / ownsDir / leaseKind / remote / starts /
headed / binary; deliberately NO `swept` cell — P5 sweeps exactly `ownsDir`;
lane dc-browser-providers: + THE LAUNCH SHAPE and the build cells — `buildChoice` /
`automationFlag` / `launchArgs` / `seeded` / `launchFlags` / `executable` (+ `exeSetting`) /
`egressProxy` / `integrationId`, defaulted by `NO_LAUNCH`; `DEFAULT_PROVIDER` names the
provider an absent one means. browser-switch `launchEnvFor` / `providerNeedsSeed` /
`integrationIdFor`, the keeper's launch + heal + build sites, the build verdict and the
client build line / panel menu / New profile… read these cells, never the id —
test-architecture §78's browser family counts what is left (the lane's §79, folded in at integration), test-browser-switch's fakebrowser row is the proof);
`providerControl(provider, {host})` = THE ONE typed refusal a disabled control
shows, structural refusals first (`provider_needs_local_key` for a
`keyScope:'local-only'` row on `host != null` — D34's (a), `provider_local_only`
for a row with no remote transport) then `provider_unavailable` naming WHY
(`cloak`: the §7.2.1 record's refusal by name); `capabilityRefusal(provider,
cell)` per control; `providerRows({host})` = the rows + the local verdict + the
per-host verdict + the proof beside the row it explains. `CLOAK_EGRESS_PROOF`
is the §7.2.1 precondition in local-oracles' SHAPE (tool + date + version +
per-run INET counts, `status:'refused'`, `refusal:'binary_absent'`,
`blocks:'cloak.wired'`) and `proofVerdict` enforces the discipline: a `blocks`
claim's cell must really be false (a row re-enabled without re-measuring FAILS
the suite), a measured record must carry all four runs each with a count, a
refused one carries no runs. `validateProfileInput` admits `host` (a machine
id; whether it is PAIRED is the keeper's question) and `cdpPort` (cdp only,
required there); `newProfileRecord` keeps `dir:null` for a row that owns no
directory or a profile on a paired machine. `attachedEnvFor({cdpUrl})` emits
`AGENT_BROWSER_CDP=<hub-side loopback url>` INSTEAD of a profile directory for
a reached browser (a non-loopback url is never handed to a session — only
through the forward); `isCdpPair` names the ONE pair `use --print` withholds;
`forwardedCdpUrl`/`cdpPortOf` re-point a loopback url at the hub's forward
(scheme + path kept). `parseEgressAllowlist`/`egressVerdict` (exact hosts or
`.suffix`; loopback/link-local NEVER; empty = deny). (The cloakserve CONTAINER
plan — `cloakservePlan` / `CLOAKSERVE_IMAGE` behind `browser.cloak.enabled` — was
deleted by lane dc-browser-providers: its docker argv was never run.) Gate:
test-browser-providers ①.

**lane-cloak (2026-09-28) — THE RECORD IS A MEASUREMENT (supersedes the
`binary_absent` refusal above).** `CLOAK_EGRESS_PROOF` = the measured record:
wrapper `0.5.10`, `chromium: '146.0.7680.177.5'`, `platform: 'linux-x64'`, the
pins (`CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION`, `CLOAKBROWSER_AUTO_UPDATE=false`), the download
(url, 216 890 134 bytes, sha256, the local Ed25519 check), the binary (path in
the cache, sha256, 729 MB unpacked, `Last Version`), the `install` entries
(npm: registry.npmjs.org; the vendor's offline `info --quick`: 0), the four
runs with every target NAMED (a DNS answer names each address; loopback /
resolver by what they are) and PHASE-tagged (`EGRESS_PHASES` npm / download /
launch), `freeTier` (no key, no sign-in — measured; a key's route read in the
vendor's code, NOT measured) and `notReached` (api.github.com, the wrapper's
own registry check, the licence hosts). The record is declared ABOVE `PROVIDERS`
because the cloak row's `wired` cell is DERIVED from it (`CLOAK_WIRED` =
measured ∧ the discipline accepts it): a row cannot be re-enabled without a
record, and a refused record's `blocks` claim still guards the reverse.
`proofVerdict` (measured, cloak) additionally requires the Chromium build +
platform and refuses an UNNAMED non-local address or a host with no phase.
`egressHostsOf(record)` DERIVES the allowlists from the tags — `install` (the
download: cloakbrowser.dev, github.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com),
`run` (none), `npm` (named, not proxied) — and `cloakInstallAllowlist` /
`cloakRunAllowlist(record, sites)` (+ the named sites; empty stays empty =
deny) are the proxies' inputs, so no second list exists. The record's strings never name the hidden CLI
(`by: 'browser driver'`; test-architecture §52b censuses them, and they reach
agents through `/api/agent/browser/providers`). Gates: test-browser-providers ①
(the record + a control per rule) and ⑦ (the allowlists through a real proxy).

**P1 second half (2026-09-16; §3.7 / §3.8):** `aliasFor`/`isAlias` (a handle =
the label's slug, unique within a session's set), `childHandleFor`/`nextChildN`,
`looksLikePath` (a `--profile` value that is a PATH is refused by name —
`agent-browser`'s own flag takes a path, ours never does), `attachmentsFor` =
the SET view (leases of one key with their aliases; the DEFAULT = the pin when
among them, else the only member, else none; a `fingerprint` that moves on
add/remove/default-move and on nothing else; children beside it),
`resolveHandle` (none / one / ≥2 ⇒ `profile_required` listing every handle
with the default marked — the sub-agent clause is an ASIDE, never the reason /
alias·id·label / `ambiguous` / `not_attached` / `profile_path_refused` carrying
the `new --adopt` remedy), `toldView`/`blindnessVerdict` (the one-time
`profile_changed` = the fingerprint moved since the session was last told;
never told ⇒ told now, not refused), `profileChangeNotice`/
`renderProfileChangeNotice` (the typed layer-② notice), `auditLine`/`auditVerbOf`
(`{at, sessionId, browserKey, profileId, verb, ok}` — never a fill's content),
`childEnvFor` (a child's OWN session + daemon; rung C `unset`s the inherited
profile symlink — two daemons on one dir die on SingletonLock), and the
registry keeps `children` + `told`. Gate: test-browser-handles ①.

**PURE (imports nothing) — the agent browser's IDENTITY and its SPAWN
ENVIRONMENT** (docs/design-agent-browser-v2.zh.md §3.2, phase P0). Every
decision lives here; the half that touches the filesystem is
`src/server/browser-env.js`, and the machine fact is `src/browser-facts.js`.

* `sessionNameFor` / `mintBrowserKey` / `isBrowserKey` — `bk-<8 hex>`, and the
  ONE spelling of `vs-<browserKey>` both variables carry (§3.2.4's two names ask
  two questions — browser context, daemon socket — about ONE browser).
* `browserKeyFor({prior, resume, fork, mint})` — **the continuity ladder**, shaped
  like `resume-continuity.js`: an answer plus the ORIGIN that produced it. A
  RESUME reuses the conversation's key; a FORK mints a new one (D15 — a fork is a
  new conversation and must not inherit another one's cookies or pinned tab); a
  resume that finds nothing answers **`resume-unknown`, never `'new'` wearing a
  hat**, because that is the leak the ladder exists to prevent and it has to be
  visible when it happens rather than inferred later from orphaned directories.
* `VARIANTS` / `REJECTED_VARIANTS` / `variantLadder` / `configNamesProfile` — the
  (D) → (C) → (N) → `none` user-data-dir ladder, D12. **The design's (A) AND (B)
  are NAMED REJECTS, both measured (r3)**: §3.2.2's table says (A) "SESSION
  only" cannot collide because one daemon owns the directory, and on 0.32.0 it
  collides exactly like (B) — every `--session` launches its own chromium, so
  two sessions on any config that names a `profile` die on `SingletonLock: File
  exists` whatever the namespace count. Round 2 shipped that shape as its floor
  and called it "(A)". The floor is now (N) = the three names alone, reachable
  ONLY when the EFFECTIVE config names no profile (each daemon then gets the
  CLI's own ephemeral dir, measured), else `none` = nothing emitted, today's
  shared browser, with the profile that decided it in the journal — a stolen tab
  is the smaller harm than a browser that cannot start. `H` = REMOTE, decided on
  the host (below). The descent is ONE RUNG AT A TIME (leaving D is always
  "D → C", even when C then fails too — collapsing it hides that C was tried).
  **A FENCED config never lands on C (r4)**: rung C IS `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE`,
  which the CLI refuses beside `--allowed-domains` at the argument check, so
  round 3's `D → C` under a fenced effective config was a browser that answered
  every command `✗ --allowed-domains is not supported with --profile` where the
  bare CLI works (measured, one injected variable — the config writer throwing).
  `fenced` is an INPUT of the ladder (`variantLadder({…, fenced})`); a fenced
  descent skips C by rule and is journalled as "C → N" with the fence as the
  reason (`fencedRungReason`, ONE exported spelling) — "C was refused, and here
  is why" is a different sentence from "C was tried and failed". A fenced config
  cannot name a profile (the CLI refuses that combination whole), so the descent
  lands on N by construction and the fence stays intact.
* `USER_CONFIG_REL` / `PROJECT_CONFIG_NAME` / `layerProjectConfig` — the CLI's
  own two-file precedence (r3): `~/.agent-browser/config.json` and then
  `./agent-browser.json` in the invocation directory at HIGHER priority, both
  replaced by `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG`. Round 2 carried only the first, so a
  project-level fence was deleted from every local session with `dropped: []`.
  The merge rule is MEASURED, one variable per arm: a key in both takes the
  project value (its `args` reached the chromium cmdline, the user file's did
  not), a key in one file survives (`userAgent`), and `extensions` is the one key
  CONCATENATED user-first (`--load-extension=<user>,<project>`; the `--help`
  says so). The CLI does not walk up, so the project file is EXACTLY the
  session's directory's — which is the stated boundary of the generated config
  (it applies that file for the whole session; a different one in a directory
  the agent cd's into does not).
* `REMOTE_SCRATCH_DIR_SH` / `REMOTE_SCRATCH_STALE_DAYS` / `TOP_LEVEL_PROFILE_AWK`
  / `remoteBrowserPrelude` — the REMOTE rung (r3). A POSIX shell fragment for
  `buildRemoteExec`'s `browser` slot that runs AFTER the `cd` on the host: it
  asks whether the host's effective config names a profile and, only then,
  `export AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE=$HOME/.vibespace/browser-profiles/vs-<key>`
  (rung C there — a dir the CLI creates lazily, measured); otherwise nothing
  (rung N there, ephemeral per daemon). Unconditional would break a FENCED host
  (`--allowed-domains is not supported with --profile`, measured), and none at
  all was the collision. **The question is answered in ONE spelling per side,
  over ONE table (r4)**: round 3's `grep -qs '"profile"[[:space:]]*:'` was a
  LOOSER spelling than `configNamesProfile` — it counted `"profile": null` and
  `""` (a host config `{…, allowedDomains, profile: null}` works bare and was
  handed a profile the CLI refuses beside the fence, measured), a key nested in
  another value, and could not see a project `null` overriding a user string.
  `TOP_LEVEL_PROFILE_AWK` is a one-line, quote-free POSIX awk that walks the JSON
  with a depth counter (strings and escapes honoured) and prints `yes` / `no` /
  `absent` for the TOP-LEVEL key; the project file is asked first and a `yes` or
  `no` there is final (the CLI's per-key precedence, `layerProjectConfig` on this
  side). The gate drives the awk and the predicate over twelve rows under every
  shell AND every awk on the box (mawk, busybox via a PATH shim), with the grep
  spliced back as the control. **The socket-root rule rides here too (r4)**:
  from the host's own `$HOME` (or `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, the CLI's second rung),
  bytes counted with `printf | wc -c` like the kernel, the tail the PURE half
  computes from the names, a pre-set `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` left alone, and
  `<base>/vs-ab-$(id -u)` exported only when it exists, is not a symlink and
  `-O` says this user owns it. The same fragment sweeps stale per-key dirs
  (`find -mtime +7`) that hold no live browser, and liveness is `[ -L
  SingletonLock ]` because chromium's lock is a DANGLING symlink while it runs
  (`-e` says absent for a LIVE profile and would sweep it out from under the
  browser). Single-quoted throughout, no glob, ends in `; `, last statement an
  `if` so `$?` stays 0 — driven under sh/bash/zsh/dash/busybox by the gate.
* `SOCKET_PATH_MAX` / `SOCKET_DIR_BASE` / `utf8Bytes` / `socketTailBytes` /
  `socketRootFor` / `socketDirBaseOf` / `socketDirDecision` — THE FIFTH VARIABLE
  (r4). A unix socket path is 103 bytes at most and the CLI checks it before
  anything launches; the root is `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` > `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/
  agent-browser` > `$HOME/.agent-browser` (measured on `session info --json`), the
  tail for our names is 50 bytes, so a 38-character home fits (103) and a
  39-character one does not (104 — `tab list` refused before launching, while
  the bare CLI's `default` name still fits): round 3's regression, recorded then
  and closed now. `socketDirDecision({browserKey, home, xdgRuntimeDir, socketDir,
  uid, base})` answers `needed` from the root the SESSION's environment would
  give the CLI, names `<base>/vs-ab-<uid>` and says whether that itself `fits`;
  `SOCKET_DIR_BASE` is the LITERAL `/tmp` (a short root is the point, and
  `TMPDIR` may be the long path being escaped); `socketDirBaseOf` refuses a base
  a shell could read as syntax. Bytes, never characters — the kernel counts
  `sun_path` in bytes. The design's name shape is untouched.
* `PIN_APPLIES_FROM` — WHEN A PIN TAKES EFFECT, MEASURED (r4). Rounds 1–3
  inherited the pool's sentence ("never a browser already running; on the NEXT
  launch") and on 0.32.0 it is false in the direction that costs the page: the
  pin leaves the running chromium alone until the NEXT COMMAND, which RELAUNCHES
  chromium onto the new directory (`get url` ⇒ `about:blank`, new pid on the
  pinned dir; the no-pin control keeps page and pid). One exported sentence for
  both rungs; P1's route owes a `close` first or a refusal while a browser is
  live.
* `browserEnvFor` — the ONE composition, returning `KEY=VALUE` strings because
  that is what BOTH spawn shapes consume (the local `r6Argv` `env` prefix and the
  remote `buildRemoteExec` `parts`). `hostId` never appears: it is a parameter of
  the caller's transport choice. **Integration OFF ⇒ ZERO pairs** — the suite
  asserts the empty array, never "a smaller set".
* `pinResolution` / `generatedConfig` / `EPHEMERAL_DENY` / `deniedKeys` —
  §3.2.5's indirection, and **the generated config is a DENY whose set is the
  CLI's own classification** (r2). A custom `--config` REPLACES the user's files,
  so anything of theirs that must survive has to be carried explicitly; round 1
  carried an ENUMERATED seven keys, which silently deleted the user's browsing
  FENCE and the whole confirmation/action-policy family from every local session.
  MEASURED end to end on 0.32.0 with two daemons and one variable: through the
  user's own config `agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:<p>/` answers
  `✗ Domain '127.0.0.1' is not in the allowed domains list`; through the config
  the product generated FROM THAT SAME FILE it answers `✓`. The design names that
  anti-pattern in its own words (§6.3: the registry must REFUSE a fence
  "而不是接受一个之后会被悄悄丢掉的标志") and §3.2.2 sells variant D on
  "能否带 `--allowed-domains`: 是" — a promise the ALLOW list cancelled. It also
  dropped `restore`, `state`, `sessionName`, `autoConnect`, `cdp`, `initScripts`,
  `downloadPath`, `maxOutput`, `hideScrollbars`, `colorScheme`, `plugins`,
  `screenshotDir` and everything else, all of them REAL typed keys of the CLI's
  schema (probed: a wrong type answers `invalid type: … expected a string`, while
  an unknown key is ignored — so the schema is known-key-typed and the list was a
  loss, not a filter).

  **The deny set is DERIVED, not enumerated.** `--allowed-domains` is refused
  beside exactly the flags that mean "this is not a fresh, isolated, controllable
  context" — which is the property P0 sells — so the deny set is "the keys that
  make the binary refuse to install a fence". MEASURED, one arm per candidate
  (config = `args` + `headed` + `allowedDomains` + the candidate; the refusal is
  an argument check, so nothing launches and `autoConnect` never reaches a real
  browser): **`profile` / `restore` / `sessionName` / `state` / `autoConnect` /
  `cdp` are refused**, while `extensions` / `userAgent` / `downloadPath` /
  `engine` / `initScripts` / `actionPolicy` are fine and `confirmActions` demonstrably
  WORKS (`Confirmation required:`). `sessionName` is why this is measured rather
  than reasoned: "a key, not a switch" is the obvious reading and the binary
  answers it with the `--restore` refusal. `session` and `namespace` are
  deliberately NOT denied — the documented precedence is config < env < flags and
  we always set both variables, so a config-file copy cannot win; a smaller deny
  set is a better deny set. `deniedKeys` names what a given config actually
  carries so the ORCH half can journal it, and `generatedConfig` uses that same
  function, so the drop and the line about it cannot drift. A user config the CLI
  already refuses stays refused: carrying a badly-typed value through reproduces
  their own situation rather than silently repairing it, and it is not a new
  failure class — the seven keys the ALLOW list carried had the same property.
  `profile`'s ABSENCE is still the ephemerality.
* `configFence` / `pinFenceConflict` — §1.5's mutual exclusion, made enforceable
  by the fix above. Once the generated config CARRIES `allowedDomains`, a PIN
  adds `profile` back and the CLI refuses **every** command (measured: `open` and
  `get title` alike). "一个按任务的域名白名单和一个持久的已登录 profile，在浏览器
  这一层是互斥的。任何同时承诺这两样的设计都在撒谎" — so the pin is REFUSED with
  the reason and the way out, which is §6.3's ruling transposed. An EMPTY
  `allowedDomains` is measured NOT to be a fence (`[]` + a profile opens the
  page) and may not block a pin.
* `PIN_ORIGINS` / `P0_PIN_ORIGINS` / `pinPick` — the pin's origin ladder written
  whole so P1 adds rows rather than a second vocabulary. `'task-group'` is listed
  and deliberately **never emitted by P0**: it is a fifth value in a vocabulary
  `resume-continuity.js` froze at four, whose client mirror
  (`agent-meta.spawnValueOrigin`) whitelists those four and **silently mislabels**
  anything else — adding it is a two-place change in P1's own commit.
* `FLOOR_VERSION` / `cmpVersion` / `floorVerdict` / `floorNotice` — D1. Four
  outcomes because "we could not tell" is neither "too old" nor "not installed":
  `ok` · `too-old` (ONE notice, capability off) · `absent` (SILENT — never nag
  about a tool nobody uses) · `unknown` (fails CLOSED on the capability and says
  so in its own words rather than claiming a version).

MEASURED on the installed 0.32.0 (2026-09-13, this box), because every rung rests
on one of these: SESSION+NAMESPACE alone still resolves the shared
`~/.agent-browser/default-profile` (that is variant B, and it is why the gate
asserts the RESOLVED directory instead of the env strings); `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG`
at a config with no `profile` key gives an ephemeral `/tmp/agent-browser-chrome-<uuid>`;
`AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE=<dir>` resolves to exactly that dir and the CLI creates it;
a missing or invalid config file makes the CLI print `⚠ …` and **exit 1** — a hard
dependency pointing the UNSAFE way, which is the whole reason the ladder exists
and the whole reason the variable is only set after a successful READ-BACK.
Gate: scripts/test-browser-profiles.mjs (fast).

  **P10 (design §7.6 tier 3 / §7.1, D27 (b) / D31, 2026-09-21):** the `local-window` row is WIRED — `tier: 3`, the three "no"s, `leaseKind:'window-target'`, and three new cells on EVERY row: `cdp` / `allowedDomains` / `pinTab` (true on every tab-lease row, false on local-window) plus `consent` (the setting that must read true — `'window.realDesktopTargets'` on local-window, null elsewhere). `providerControl(id, {host, desktopConsent})` adds the rung `provider_needs_consent` (after the structural refusals and `wired`: on a host the row is still `provider_local_only` first); `providerRows({host, desktopConsent})` passes it through; the keeper's `control` wrapper injects the setting's value on every read. `capabilityRefusal` gains `cdp` ("no url to print — vibespace-window"), `allowed-domains` (a CDP-side rule; the site is whatever the user opened), `pin-tab` (leased by handle, no target id) and `live-view`, and the local-window `switch` refusal names the act (the switch, then a WINDOW TARGET — §7.6 rule 3: no re-pointing). `validateProfileInput` refuses a `leaseKind:'window-target'` provider `tier3_is_a_window_target`: tier 3 is NOT a profile — no record is created, none re-pointed (a record would have no dir, no seed, nothing the ladder or the sweep could act on). A profile RECORD carries no `tier` field (derived from `provider`, §3.3) — test-browser-tier3 pins it.

**Lane H verify r2 (2026-09-25) — liveness vs signalling, and the lock verdict.** `pidLiveness({alive, sameStart, startKnown})` → `ours` / `gone` / `recycled` (alive with ANOTHER starttime, both readable) / `unknown` (no starttime to compare) — the keeper's "is it running" (a `recycled` pid is as gone as a dead one; `unknown` is never guessed gone), beside `pidVerdict`, which still alone decides what may be SIGNALLED. `userDataDirsOf(cmdline)` reads a Chrome's `--user-data-dir` off a NUL-separated OR title-rewritten (space-joined) cmdline, both spellings; `sameDir` ignores a trailing slash. `profileLockVerdict({lock, holder, hostname, dir, ns, recorded})` decides who holds `<dir>/SingletonLock` before every launch: `free` (no lock / a stale one / a recycled pid that does not name the dir — Chrome clears those), `own-orphan` (alive, names the dir, AND it is the browser recorded at launch — pid + starttime — or its environ names this keeper's namespace, AND no live browser daemon is its parent), else `foreign` (another host's lock, an unreadable process, a human's Chrome, a live daemon holding it). `profileLockedRefusal` = `{code:'profile_locked', error (the pid + dir, never the raw exit code), holderPid}`. Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (the 15-row table).

**Lane H verify r3 (2026-09-25) — the witness that holds on the real binary, the exact argv, the unrecorded pid.** `profileLockVerdict({lock, holder, hostname, dir, minted, recorded})` — the `ns` / "its environment names this keeper's namespace" rung is GONE: the real 0.38.1 scrubs every `AGENT_BROWSER_*` from its Chrome, so it never fired on a real one (a relaunched Chrome was `foreign` forever). `own-orphan` = alive, names the dir, no live daemon parent, AND (the recorded/re-captured browser — pid + starttime — OR `minted`: the caller's fact that `dir` is a directory the keeper created). `foreign` carries `user: true` ONLY for a holder on a directory VibeSpace never minted that nothing recorded names — and `profileLockedRefusal` says "it may be the user's" ONLY then (another machine / unreadable / a live daemon holding it read "VibeSpace does not end it; once it has exited … run the command again"). `userDataDirsOf(cmdline, known = [])`: a cmdline WITH NULs is parsed EXACTLY (the whole argv element — a space in the value kept; a flag merely mentioned inside another argument is not one); only a NUL-free (title-rewritten) one is scanned as words, where each `known` dir is also matched WHOLE (flag, dir, optional `/`, then whitespace or end) and its space-truncated twin dropped. `pidLiveness({…, startReadable})` gains `unrecorded` (alive, its starttime readable, the record has none) — gone for liveness; `unknown` only when no starttime is readable at all (no /proc). Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ PURE (16 rows + the refusal wording + 3 userDataDirsOf rows).

### src/browser-mediation.js

**Lane S2 (2026-09-26) — THE USER'S OWN INPUT PASSES THE PAUSED FENCE ON A CREDIT.** `INPUT_CREDIT_MS` 1200, `isInputMethod`, `creditExpectation(record)` / `creditMatches(expect, msg)` / `takeCredit(credits, now, {msg})` (the credit is BOUND to the CDP call its record becomes; only a matching `Input.*` spends it; expired ones leave wherever they sit and their waiter is told), `creditReceipt(reply)` (the browser's own reply ⇒ `{ok}` / `browser_refused` / `no_reply`). Why: a mediated lease's live view streams from the session's daemon over its scoped url, so the stream server's `Input.*` for the user's takeover arrive on the connection `judge` fences with `paused` — every key was refused `browser_paused` (measured on 0.38.1: one record = one `Input.*`, the stream server says nothing back). Only an `Input.*` spends a credit; an uncredited one is still refused while the user drives. **VERIFY S2 (2026-09-26, CRITICAL, fixed in the verify round): the credit was a per-grant COUNT — the agent's own commands ride the same daemon connection (and a second socket of the lease) as the stream server's dispatches, so a concurrent `agent-browser click` / `Input.insertText` spent the user's credit and LANDED during the takeover while the user's own key was refused `browser_paused` and its receipt said "delivered" (with the pointer moving: 30 credits/s × 1.2 s = the fence open). Now `creditExpectation(record)` names the call (measured verbatim on 0.38.1: `params.type` = `eventType`, a mouse record's x/y/button/clickCount/modifiers[/deltaX/deltaY], a key's key/code/text/windowsVirtualKeyCode/modifiers, a touch's touchPoints; 1:1 and in order under a 61-record burst) and `takeCredit` spends only a credit the arriving `Input.*` MATCHES — anything else is judged as if no credit existed and burns nothing; the agent can pass the fence only by issuing the exact event the user just made.** Gate: test-browser-fact ③ ⑤ (the theft legs + the head-credit mediator copy as the control). **VERIFY r2 (2026-09-26, MAJOR, fixed): the r1 binding named the call's method + params but not its TAB.** Measured on 0.38.1: every dispatch rides a page `sessionId`, the daemon uses ONE connection for the stream server and the CLI, and the stream's `tabs` record names each tab's CDP `targetId`. So an agent's OWN CDP socket on the lease's url, attached to ITS tab B, flooding the exact Enter the user was about to press on tab A, spent the credit first: a TRUSTED Enter landed on B, the user's Enter was refused `browser_paused`, the receipt said delivered (real binary, 3/3). Now `creditExpectation(record, {targetId})` carries the tab the user is looking at (the bridge's `relay.activeTarget` off the `tabs` record) and `creditSessionOk(expect, sid, target)` admits only an `Input.*` on a PAGE session the lease was HANDED (`scope.sessions` sid → targetId) whose target IS that tab; `takeCredit(credits, now, {msg, sessionTarget})` FAILS CLOSED (no resolver / no session / an unhanded session / the browser session / another tab ⇒ no credit, nothing burnt). A credit naming no tab (a `tabs` record without `targetId`) takes any handed page session. Residual, documented: an agent session on the user's OWN tab mirroring the user's key lands ONE such key on that tab either way (the user's tab, the user's act). Gate: test-browser-fact ③ (the session table, fail-closed) + ⑤ (the cross-tab / unhanded / bare mirrors refused while the user's Enter waits, then lands; CONTROL = a mediator copy where any handed session answers the credit's tab — the theft lands). **Verify r3 (2026-09-26, the third round; measured on 0.38.1 + Chrome, the agent's own socket):** `Input.setIgnoreInputEvents` is ALWAYS_REFUSED with its own words (`ALWAYS_REFUSED_WHY`): armed BEFORE a takeover (allowed then — the lease's own tab) Chrome answered ok to every credited dispatch of the user's while the page received NONE — a lost keystroke with a "delivered" receipt; no lease has a use for a deaf page (the binary never calls it). `DOM.focus` is PAUSED (measured: the user's `a` in #i, the agent's DOM.focus(#j), the user's `b` in #j — a non-script door on the input side). `Page.bringToFront` is deliberately NOT paused: refusing it, even with a screencast restart on another tab, does not stop the daemon's `tab <n>` (`Target.setAutoAttach` carries the switch) and leaves the switched-to tab HIDDEN (no frames, mouse dispatches never answered, the stream dead after the handback) — the switch is refused where it is SEEN, the bridge's takeover ANCHOR (src/server/browser-stream.js). `takeCredit` also returns `otherTab` = the live credits this call MATCHED but could not spend because its session is on another tab: the mediator MARKS them (never burns — a hostile mirror on its own tab must not cost the user their key), so an unspent marked credit expires `other_tab`; `creditExpiryReceipt(c)` = `no_reply` (spent — the browser never answered; a hidden tab's mouse input) / `other_tab` / `not_dispatched`. Script evaluation stays unfenced (D6 (a)) and this is the documented limit, measured: while the user drives, the agent's `Runtime.evaluate` on the driven tab can `execCommand('insertText')`, replace the field's value and swallow the user's keys through a capture listener (their receipts say delivered — the dispatch DID reach the page); it is the access the agent has to a shared profile's page a second later, and the smallest fence, if the owner wants one, is the script methods on the anchor's tab only while paused. `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled` / `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog` pass while paused (no effect on a screencast the user cannot pick a file through). **PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the proxy, the keeper, the routes, the CLI AND
the bundle share ONE rule set) — THE CDP MEDIATION RULES** (agent browser P6,
2026-09-21; design §6.2 / §6.5 / D6). A profile's CDP endpoint is
unauthenticated and confers authority over EVERY target in the browser
(§3.4), so a lease is handed its OWN url and every message through it is
judged here. Invariants, one each: `judge(msg, scope, {paused})` answers
forward / refuse / drop — `Target.attachToTarget` / `activateTarget` /
`closeTarget` / `getTargetInfo` / `Browser.getWindowForTarget` need
`params.targetId` IN SCOPE (`target_out_of_scope`), a message on a CDP
`sessionId` the proxy never handed out is `session_out_of_scope`, the
whole-browser acts (`Browser.close` / `crash*`, `Target.exposeDevToolsProtocol`
/ `setRemoteLocations` / `sendMessageToTarget`) are `method_refused` always,
a BROWSER-level `Target.setAutoAttach {waitForDebuggerOnStart:true}` (no
`sessionId`) is `auto_attach_pause_refused` (identity verify r4, 2026-09-28 —
measured on Chrome 153: one client's arm pauses ANOTHER client's new tab at
its first `Page.navigate` until the arming client resumes it, and the proxy
drops that `attachedToTarget` for a foreign target, so a lease could freeze
every other conversation's and the user's new tab and never resume them; the
page-level form the 0.38.1 daemon sends passes; `autoAttachRelated` with the
pause needs its target in scope),
and while the USER holds the input side every `Input.*`, the navigation
family (`Page.navigate` / `reload` / `navigateToHistoryEntry` / `close` /
`stopLoading` / `setDocumentContent` / `handleJavaScriptDialog`),
`DOM.setFileInputFiles` and the target acts that change what the user sees
(`Target.createTarget` / `closeTarget` / `activateTarget`) are
`browser_paused` — `Runtime.evaluate` and `Page.captureScreenshot` are NOT
(a read during a takeover is the honest use; the CLI's typed refusal (P3)
already stops the cooperative path — stated, never sold as a DOM fence); a
refusal is a CDP error `{id, error:{code:-32000, message:'<code>: …'}}` on
the same session (`refusalCodeOf` reads it back); `admitReply(reply,
pending, scope)` → `{reply, emit}` GROWS the scope from what the browser
handed back (createTarget → the tab; attachToTarget → the session;
createBrowserContext → the context) and FILTERS `getTargets` /
`getBrowserContexts` to the scope; `filterEvent` forwards only what concerns
the scope and admits the admissible — a tab OPENED BY a scoped page
(`openerId`), a target born in an owned context, a child auto-attached under

**Measured ordering (0.32.0 + Chrome 153): Chrome announces
`Target.targetCreated` BEFORE it answers `Target.createTarget`**, so the tab a
lease is creating is out of scope for one message — `scope.recent` (bounded
`RECENT_MAX`) remembers withheld announcements and the createTarget reply
REPLAYS the one it names before itself (without it agent-browser's target
registry never learns its own tab and `open` hangs forever).
`parseMediatedPath` = the five paths under `/m/<32-char token>/…` (anything
else null ⇒ 404); `mediatedBrowserUrl` = the `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/m/<token>/
