PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the mediator, the keeper, the CLI and the bundle share ONE table). THE CDP CENSUS (verify S2 r4, 2026-09-27; design-agent-browser-v2 §6.2.1): `ROWS[domain][method]` = ONE row per method of the installed Chrome's own `GET /json/protocol` — 58 domains, 664 methods on `CENSUS_CHROME` 153.0.8010.47 (the fixture scripts/fixtures/cdp-protocol-153.0.8010.47/protocol.json, names only, written by scripts/cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs). `CLASSES` (closed): `input` 15 (keys / pointer / touch / drag / text / files / focus / autofill INTO the page), `view` 106 (which tab, the page, viewport / scale / screen / emulated media, a frozen page — Debugger pause + breakpoints, virtual time, script execution off, lifecycle —, overlays, casting), `page-mutation` 195 (script evaluation, DOM / CSS / animation edits, cookies / storage / cache / permissions / service workers / WebAuthn / request interception / headers / UA / geolocation / sensors), `read` 176, `session` 11 (Target attach / detach / discover / contexts — the scoping rules, never the fence), `harmless` 147 (enable / disable / acks / releases), `refused` 14 (Browser.close / crash*, exposeDevToolsProtocol, setRemoteLocations, sendMessageToTarget, executeBrowserCommand, Tethering, an unpacked extension, desktop mirroring, Page.crash, the deaf-page arm). `PAUSED_RULE` per class: refuse (input, view) / switch (page-mutation — only under `browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven`, default OFF) / allow (read, session, harmless) / always (refused). A row is `'cls'` (since = SINCE), `['cls', 'since']` (the P6 list of 2026-09-21, the r3 doors) or `{cls, since, fence, why}`; `fence: 'anchor'` names the ONE method the mediator does not refuse although its class says so — Page.bringToFront, refused by the live view's takeover anchor instead (measured r2 + r3: refusing it at the mediator leaves the switched-to tab hidden and the stream dead). TAB SCOPING IS LEASE-WIDE for every class (decided r4, in the file's header so it is not re-litigated one method at a time): the mediator cannot tell a tab from an out-of-process iframe under the driven tab, the CLI rung already refuses every page verb while the user drives, the daemon's own `tab <n>` moves the active tab. API: `rowOf(m)` / `classOf(m)` / `rows()` / `methodsOf(cls)` / `census()` (the counts) / `compare(protocol)` → `{unclassified, stale, sameSet, listed, rows}` (a method the protocol lists with no row is UNCLASSIFIED — the legs print it and fail; a row naming a method the protocol lacks is STALE — dead data or an older Chrome) / `validate()`. A NEW CHROME: run scripts/cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs (a scratch headless Chrome's own protocol → the fixture dir named by its version), bump `CENSUS_CHROME`, write a row per printed method; until then the mediator refuses each by name while the user drives (`[cdp-mediator] … has no row in the CDP census`, once per method per grant; `grantView().unclassified`). **SHARED (node builtins + the PURE model) — what `agent-browser` IS on this
machine.** P0 needs one fact, the installed VERSION for D1's floor, and this
answers it for a machine handle rather than for "here" (P1's keeper adds "which
browsers are running" beside it, which is why it is its own module now).

**A PROBE THAT COSTS A FORK MAY NOT RUN PER ACTION**: `spawn` blocks the calling
thread in proportion to the PARENT's RSS (1.8 ms at 45 MB, 72.5 ms at 1.5 GB on
this box, and both production servers sit at 1.5–2 GB), so the version is probed
at most once per 10-minute TTL and **the negative answer is cached like a
positive one** — `null` means "we asked and there is no binary", which is a FACT.
It never throws: a probe that threw on a machine without the tool would turn "this
user does not browse" into a spawn failure. `''` (it ran and would not say) is
deliberately a DIFFERENT value from `null`, because only one of them deserves a
sentence.

the answer more true. It is the same rule `agentEnv()` in `src/ws-handler.js`
already applies on the SPAWN path, naming this exact operator shape in its own
comment — the probe was the one layer away that did not.

  never be spelled the same way as "there are none". The C rung's `<key>.cwd`
  record (r4) is swept with its link. The reported `ageMs` is
  clamped at zero: `Date.now()` truncates where `mtimeMs` does not, so a file
  written microseconds ago measures −1 ms old, and a negative AGE in a log line is
  a bug report against whoever reads it.
* `writeJson` is INJECTED so the read-back guard has a control: the failure it
  exists for is "our writer produced a file the CLI will refuse", which cannot be
  staged by breaking the filesystem (that also breaks the write). Production never
  passes it.

### src/server/browser-key.js
**ORCH (B-f7ab, 2026-09-27) — a live session's browser key, decided at SPAWN or on FIRST USE.** `mintKey()` = THE mint and `applyKey(session, {key, env, pin})` = THE writer of the key's session fields (`_browserKey/_browserVariant/_browserProfileId/_browserPinOrigin/_browserEnv`) — ws-create's spawn calls both (test-browser-share-model ③e pins that ws-create spells neither itself). `create({browserEnv, keeper, activeSessions, integrationEnabled, readMeta, persistMeta, onLiveFactsChanged, log})` → `{ensureBrowserKey(session, {sessionId}), keylessFactOf(session)}`, built in mounts-plugins-wiring over the routes' browser-env memo (server.js hands `readSessionMetaOf` + THE `integrationEnabled`).
* **Why**: a session spawned before the feature / while `browser.isolateSessions` was off had no key and every route 409'd; nothing needed a respawn — the CLI builds its child env from `/resolve`'s answer (the recorded pairs, the NAMED config, the keeper's socket root).
* **The rules = the bindings' (D15/r5–r7) as PURE `B.lateKeyVerdict`** (order: session_gone › remote › integration_off › isolation_off › unavailable › conversation_unknown › fork_pending › held_elsewhere; words `B.lateKeyRefusal` — the restart-remedied ones read "restart this session (Terminate → Resume) to get a browser key: <reason>", never a command line). Fork = `restoredForkPending` over the record with the live ids (catches a pre-forkSourceId terminal fork's bare `forkRequested`) OR `bindableIdOf({…, browserKeyFor: sid}) !== sid`. A conversation already bound (`priorKeyFor`: bindings, then the meta join) gets THAT key back via `B.browserKeyFor({prior, resume:true})` unless another live session carries it (`held_elsewhere`, named) — never a second key per conversation.
* **Same path as the spawn**: `be.envFor({…, remote:false, cwd: session.cwd, pinnedDir:null})` (config + scratch/pin link + socket dir), `keeper.pinForCreate` (conversation pin > Task Group > instance default) + `setPin` when not the conversation's, `stampGroupCap`/`capOf`. **THE PIN IS A PREFERENCE (2.369.196, the "Who can use it" list):** a pin names the profile a bare command opens; whether that profile admits the conversation is `whoMayUse` at EVERY command. Verify r1's dated default pin (`setPin(…, {at: B.latePinAt(…)})` — a pin was then an authorization, `userPinAuthorizes`, so a pin stamped at the mint outranked a narrowing made after the session started) is GONE with the rule it served: `latePinAt`, `userPinAuthorizes` and `setPin`'s `at` are deleted, no admission reads a pin or its date, and a default pin (`task-group` / `instance`) never adds the conversation to the list. The binding is written by THE choke point: `persistSessionMeta(session, {browserKey, browserVariant, browserKeyFor: <its own conversation id>, browserEnv, …})` → writeSessionMeta → `bindableIdOf` → `record`; only over a REAL record (`webuiSessionId`), never a partial one — none ⇒ this process keeps the key, journalled. A binding the store refused is journalled, never thrown.
* **Verify r2 (2026-09-27, reproduced on the real keeper + routes and a real server): A DEFAULT REACHES A CONVERSATION ONLY AT ITS START.** The ladder was read at the mint, so a default the user set AFTER a keyless session started reached it; the spawn-keyed twin had landed on the default in force at ITS start. Now the late pin is PURE `B.lateDefaultPin({witness, ladder})`: `witness` = the record's `browserPinAtStart` (ws-create writes it for every keyless spawn: `{profileId, origin, at, by, cap}` — the ladder's pick dated at the start, a fork's parent row verbatim, an EMPTY one when the ladder picked nothing) ⇒ restored as that pick (`keeper.restorePin`: its own date, informational; it NEVER edits any profile's `owner.who` — a witness widens nothing, even a `chosen` one); no witness ⇒ the current default as a LANDING (`setPin(…, {origin, by:'user'})` — a default's origin, so nothing is added to the list: the bare command names it and the list answers, `not_owner` by the button on a profile kept from it); the conversation's own row untouched. The cap: `stampGroupCap(bk, facts, {value: B.witnessCap(witness)})` — the group is never read live (none witnessed ⇒ none stamped). `res.locals.minted` rides refused answers too (LOW). The witness WRITE was attacked and refuted on a real server (synchronous with the spawn; field-for-field the keyed twin's row + cap; restart-stable; first route at boot+27 ms). (Verify r3's two LOW rows — a landing dated 0, a start-less witness — pinned the dated-pin rule and went with it at .196.)
* **Single-flight by construction**: synchronous end to end; the second caller finds `_browserKey` (`minted:false`); a refusal touches nothing and is journalled once per (session, why).
* `keylessFactOf` = in-memory only (called per active-sessions broadcast): local, both switches on, a conversation id, no pending fork ⇒ `BF.keylessFact()` ("no browser yet"), else null.
* Gates: test-browser-share-model ③ (real engine + routes + keeper + browser-env over the fake 0.38.1; CONTROLS: a copy that mints twice, a copy without the fork rule; ③f r2: the default-after-start scenes beside their spawn-keyed twins, the 8-row spawn ↔ late parity table (the list, never the clock), the pre-r2 engine as a control that ignores the witness, a live-cap control; ③f .196: a `chosen` witness and a landing on a profile kept to another conversation leave every owner byte-identical and are refused by the list, CONTROL a restorePin that adds the conversation), test-browser-fact ⑦, test-browser-share ⑦ (heavy, real binary + Chrome), test-browser-continuity ⑤ (heavy, a real server: the real wiring + the real writeSessionMeta choke point; the late key survives Terminate → Resume; r2: a keyless spawn's record carries its witness).

### src/server/browser-bindings.js

**ORCH (r5) — the conversation → browser-key binding, in a store whose lifetime
is the CONVERSATION's, not the webui session's.** `create({dataDir, log})` →
`{record(conversationId, key, {at}), lookup(conversationId), keys(), refusals(),
conversationIdOf(meta), bindableIdOf(meta), file, dir}` over `data/browser-env/bindings.json` =
`{v: 1, byConversation: {<sid>: {key, at}}}`, in the directory browser-env
already owns (its sweep skips it: `bindings` is not a browser key).

**"Who can use it" (2026-09-27): the REVERSE read.** `conversationOf(key)` (one file read, '' when unbound) and `conversationsByKey()` (the whole map, read once per request) — the Agent browser panel's chip for a STOPPED conversation on a profile's list is named by the client from its own session rows through this id (`GET /api/browser/profiles/:id/use`'s `conversationId`, the housekeeping row's `use`). Bound: the store prunes to the newest 4096 conversations — a chip whose key fell off names nothing ("A conversation that is not running now").

* **Why it exists**: §3.2.1 promises a resumed conversation keeps its browser
  key, and rounds 1–4 recovered it from `data/session-meta` — the file the
  product's own Terminate → Resume flow UNLINKS (ws-handler's kill case,
  session-stdout's pty-exit path). So the `conversation` rung fired only while
  the previous session's meta still existed, i.e. never in the flow it was
  written for; every resume of a stopped conversation minted a new key,
  warned `resume-unknown`, and orphaned the previous namespace's daemon +
  chromium (~1.4 GB RSS, 16 processes) until the 15-min idle timeout —
  unbounded once P1's leases set that timeout to 0. Measured on a real
  worktree server with a real claude session before the fix.
* **Written at the ONE meta choke point**: `session-stdout.writeSessionMeta`
  calls `record(bindableIdOf(meta), meta.browserKey)` after the meta write
  (lazily constructed against the same data dir). Every producer of a meta
  record passes through that function, including the ones that learn the
  conversation id LATE — the init frame, the lock file — so the binding lands
  the moment a record carries both facts. `deleteSessionMeta` never touches it.
* **The id rule is `claudeSessionId || backendSessionId`**, the same rule
  `reading-repair._sessionKeyMap` files a conversation under, spelled once as
  `conversationIdOf` so the two rungs of `priorKeyFor` can never disagree.
* **A RECORD MAY NOT BIND THE CONVERSATION IT WAS FORKED FROM (r6, the
  round-5 verifier's HIGH, reproduced end to end on the pristine r5 store
  before a line was changed).** r5 wrote here "a fork binds under ITS OWN new
  id and never rewrites its parent's" — true of the ADOPTION write and false
  of every write before it. A claude fork is created with `claudeSessionId` =
  the PARENT's id (`--fork-session` resumes the parent; the fork's own id is
  announced by the init frame later and adopted then), a codex fork with the
  parent's thread id (the wrapper's `thread/fork` reports the new one in a
  later `wrapper_meta`), and both mint a NEW browser key (D15). So the fork's
  FIRST meta write carries {<parent id>, <fork key>}, and r5's hook — "does
  the record carry a conversation id and a key" — bound the PARENT to the
  FORK's browser. Measured on a real worktree server: resume X → `bk-2afad4b8`,
  kill, fork X → `bk-02d028a3`, and within 800 ms `bindings[X].key` =
  `bk-02d028a3`; kill the fork, resume X → the parent's process carries the
  FORK's `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` (two conversations on one browser — `close
  --all` from either closes the other's tabs, the incident P0 exists to stop,
  D15 reversed), the parent's own daemon + chromium orphaned under its old
  namespace, and NOT ONE journal line (rung 1 answered confidently). TWO
  LAYERS, each with its own control:
  * ① **the RULE, at the choke point** — the record SAYS which conversation
    it was forked from: `forkSourceId` (`data.forkedFromId || data.resumeId`
    under `data.fork`) is written by ws-create's origin meta write and carried
    by every later write's spread (a printed census in test-browser-profiles
    pins that exactly ONE producer rebuilds the record from scratch — that
    origin write — and every other spreads the previous record), and
    `bindableIdOf(meta)` answers '' while the record's conversation id IS that
    source. The id a record may BIND is not the id it NAMES — `conversationIdOf`
    is unchanged and still names the parent for every other reader. After the
    harness adopts the fork's own id the record names a different id and binds
    it; an opencode fork is minted BEFORE the spawn, so its first record already
    differs from the source and binds at once, exactly as before.
    `forkRequested` was deliberately NOT the fact asked: it stayed `true` in
    the file after a claude adoption (that write spread the old record and
    never re-listed it — re-listed `false` since the fork-group round 2, older
    records keep it) and stays `true` for ever on a codex or opencode fork
    (nothing clears it) — asking it would have left every fork unbound and every resume of a
    fork a `resume-unknown`.
  * ② **the BELT, in the store** — a binding is written ONCE per conversation.
    A different key for a conversation that already has one is REFUSED,
    journalled once per (conversation, offered key) with both keys named, and
    counted (`refusals()`, telemetry `browser-binding-move-refused`). A
    refusal is never a lost binding — the conversation keeps the key it had,
    which is the direction the incident wants. **r7 adds the other half: a
    key is ONE conversation's** — a NEW conversation offered a key another one
    already holds is refused the same way (`browser-binding-share-refused`,
    once per pair, the same census).
* **A KEY IS BOUND TO THE CONVERSATION IT WAS DECIDED FOR (r7, the round-6
  verifier's MEDIUM — the IMPLICIT fork, reproduced on a real worktree server
  through the real stream consumer).** r6 claimed "no producer we ship
  re-binds"; one does, with no fork flag: a `claude --resume X` whose
  conversation is LOCKED by another live claude silently forks to a NEW id Y
  (claude's own double-writer protection; a codex/ACP resume can re-mint
  too), the consumers ADOPT it (2.219.0, `forkedFrom: [X]`), and the record
  then names Y beside the key K decided for X — which r6's rule ("were you
  forked FROM this id?") bound: Y → K, two conversations on one browser for
  ever, no journal line. Three pieces, one fact:
  * ws-create's origin write states **`browserKeyFor`** = the conversation the
    key was DECIDED for — a resume's `resumeId` (the ladder looked THAT id up
    or minted for it); a fork NEVER (its key belongs to the id the harness will
    announce, `forkSourceId` guards the parent); a new session NONE (its first
    announced id is the one). Spread forward by every later write like
    `forkSourceId`.
  * `bindableIdOf` refuses any id that is not the decided one, and
    `priorKeyFor`'s meta rung asks the same rule (a live record that may not
    bind a conversation may not answer for it either).
  * The choke point SAYS it once per (session, id) through `noteUnbound`
    (`browser-binding-implicit-fork`, `implicitForks()`): the running process
    keeps the browser it spawned with — a spawn env is immutable — and the
    announced conversation mints its own key on its next resume, with the
    honest `resume-unknown` line. The fork-source case is not announced (it is
    expected and transient).
  * Honest boundary: two conversations an OLDER build already bound to one key
    stay bound (the store is not migrated); the belt only refuses new shares.
  * Honest boundary: a terminal-mode claude fork never announces its own id to
    us (no stream), so its record keeps naming the parent for its whole life
    and binds NOTHING — its browser is reclaimed by the idle timeout like any
    conversation that was never bound; the parent is untouched, which is the
    half the incident was about.
* **B-f7ab (2026-09-27): a LATE key binds through the same door.** `src/server/browser-key.js ensureBrowserKey` mints a key for a live session that has none (pre-feature / isolation was off) and persists it into the session's OWN record with `browserKeyFor` = its own conversation id, so this module's rule binds exactly that conversation; it refuses (`fork_pending`) before a fork still carrying its source's id could bind the parent, and reuses the conversation's bound key instead of offering a second one (the belts never need to fire).
* **Bounded** at `MAX_BINDINGS` (4096) newest by `at`, **atomic** (tmp + rename), **0600**
  in a 0700 dir, **change-detected** (the recorder caches what it wrote; the
  dozens of meta writes a session makes per turn cost no disk write once the
  binding is on disk), and the reader re-reads the file per lookup (one resume
  = one read; the writer is another module instance). A write that fails is
  journalled (`could not record the browser key … a later resume will mint`)
  and never thrown — the meta write it rides is not held up.
* Gate: test-browser-profiles §⑳(b) (the store's rules, `priorKeyFor` over an
  unlinked meta with a patched-copy pre-fix control, the sweep leaving the file
  alone, source pins on the choke point and on the two deleters) + §⑳(b′) (r6:
  the rule table over the three harness shapes, the belt's refusal/journal/
  count, the choke point mirrored over the real module and over three patched
  copies — rule off (the belt alone holds), belt off (the rule alone holds),
  both off = r5's bytes and the parent MOVES — the `forkSourceId` wiring pin,
  and the meta-writer census; r7: the `browserKeyFor` rule table, the share
  refusal, the once-per-pair journal + counters) + test-browser-continuity §②
  (a real server: create as resume → ws kill → meta gone → resume again ⇒ the
  SAME `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` in the spawned process's `environ`, one
  `resume-unknown` line in total; then FORK ⇒ the fork's process carries a
  DIFFERENT key, `bindings[X]` is unchanged and no refusal line was needed ⇒
  kill ⇒ resume the parent ⇒ its own key, ONE namespace ever spawned for it)
  + §③ (r7: a CHAT resume of X whose fake claude announces a DIFFERENT
  `session_id` Y after 1 s ⇒ the real consumer adopts Y (`forkedFrom:[X]`, no
  `forkSourceId`), the record carries K + `browserKeyFor: X`, `bindings[X]` =
  K and `bindings[Y]` is EMPTY with exactly one implicit-fork journal line and
  no refusal line ⇒ kill ⇒ resume Y ⇒ its OWN key + one `resume-unknown` ⇒
  kill ⇒ resume X again ⇒ X's key again, both bindings unchanged, a second
  journal line, the belt never reached).

The file: `machineConfigFile(kind)` = `data/browser-env/machine.json` (a profile browser: `VERBS.sanctionedConfig({user})` — the user file minus `cdp`/`autoConnect` and the raw-debugging switches — + the `browser.headed` setting) or `machine-ephemeral.json` (an ephemeral browser whose pairs carry no config: `B.generatedConfig` over the user file, EPHEMERAL_DENY dropped); written 0600 atomically only when the content changes, read back; a user file that does not parse (the binary would refuse it too) or an unwritable dir ⇒ null + ONE journal line, the call unchanged. `configFileFor({ephemeral, pairs})` = the pairs' own AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG else that file — what `/resolve` names. `cdpUrl` in browser-facts gained `extraEnv` for it. Gate: test-browser-ephemeral r3 (launch + answer + command carry the same file; the pre-r3 keeper in a patched copy launches with none).

**r4 (2.369.168, browser r4).** `machineConfigFile` names its file from the memo only while `lstat` says it is a regular file (never a symlink) of this uid whose content is exactly what it wrote (`JSON.stringify(cfg, null, 2)`); anything else is re-written through `writeJsonAtomic` (the rename replaces a planted link itself) — symmetry with the CLI's lstat-checked composed file.


**r1 (2.369.168):** a failed named-profile start says `the browser did not start: <text>` (it reaches the agent through `/use` and `/resolve`; it no longer names the hidden CLI), a confirmation answer's fallback error `the browser CLI failed` — test-architecture §52b r1 counts the name in this file's string literals.


**Browser takeover C3 (2.369.168; design-browser-takeover §5 T3, D1/D2).** `ensureEphemeral({browserKey, sessionId, envPairs, sessionName, variant})` = a conversation's MANAGED ephemeral browser: reuse the record whose `owner.id === browserKey` (resume ⇒ the same record; a fork's new key ⇒ a new one; a child key ⇒ its own) else mint one; ONE lease `{profileId, browserKey, alias:'ephemeral'}` (never an attachment); remember the pairs (`ephPairs`, and `envPairs` on the browser record so a restart can ask); then `start()`. `nsOf(id)` answers `vs-<browserKey>` for it — P0's SESSION/NAMESPACE ARE its identity, so the live view (`streamPortFor` kind `ephemeral`), the takeover key `<bk>|ephemeral` and the trace scope `ephemeral` are untouched (parity pinned). `startEphemeral`: the ceiling (`ceilingNow({ephemeral:true})` ⇒ `browser_cap` with holders + remedy) → the runaway park → ADOPT a daemon an escaped command already started (`rt.info(null, {extraEnv: pairs})`) else `rt.launch(null, {extraEnv: pairs, idleMs: <the idle the PAIRS name (B.pairsIdleMs), the setting browser.idleTimeoutMs only when they name none — lane P verify r2 F2>})` — NEVER a re-run of the browser-env ladder. A local record whose pid is gone is `markEphemeralGone` (state `stopped`, `stoppedBy:'idle'`, no error; judged in `start()` too so the next verb restarts it). `stop()` closes it under its pairs (`closeAll(null, {extraEnv})`). `reconcile` retires every ephemeral record left with no lease (after the same grace as any lease; at once at boot): `retireEphemeral` = stop(`conversation gone`) then `removeProfile` BY ITSELF (a named profile never; a lease that came back meanwhile keeps it; single flight); `r.retired` is awaited by `tick`/`boot`. `adoptAll` asks it under its recorded pairs. It emits NO lease events (the recorder never arms a profile tap on it). Named-only surfaces: `list().profiles`/`leases`/`chips`, `profileByRef`, label uniqueness, pins, `attach` (⇒ `not_attachable`), `updateProfile` (⇒ `not_editable`), `switchBackend`; `list().ephemerals` + `ephemerals()`/`ephemeralFor(key)` carry its rows; `statusFor(key).ephemeral`. `cap.used` and every start's ceiling count the desktop apps through `otherHolders`/`setOtherHolders(fn)` (server.js wires `desktopKeeper.liveRecords()`, D2). Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ②③, test-browser-mediation ⑤.


**P6 (2026-09-21; §6.2 / §6.5 / D6):** `mediator` (src/server/cdp-mediator.js) is injected by the wiring and its presence is the `mediation` fact `createProfile` / `updateProfile` hand the §6.2 verdict (`sharing` is editable through `updateProfile` — refused `leased` while any session holds a lease, `bad-request` on the legacy record). `isMediated(p)` = `B.isMediatedProfile`. A mediated `attach` REFUSES by name with no proxy in this process (`mediation_unavailable`, never a silent fall-back to the cooperative env) or a browser that answered no CDP url (`mediation_no_cdp`), else asks ONE grant per (profile, browserKey) (`grantFor` with the lease's targetId and a `paused` reader over `inputStateFor(...).input === 'user'` — read per message) and answers `mediated:true`, `M.mediatedEnvFor` (the scoped url, a per-session namespace, no directory), `cdpUrl` = the scoped url, and the `note`. `start` re-points every grant on the profile (local + external arms), `stop` nulls them, `detach` and a reconcile drop `revoke` (1008 + the lease's tabs closed upstream), `switchBackend` admits each re-opened tab into its lease's scope, `streamPortFor` asks the SESSION's own daemon (`M.mediatedNamespace`, `AGENT_BROWSER_CDP` in `extraEnv`) for a mediated lease, `answerConfirmation` likewise; `list()` carries `mediation:{available, port, grants}` and `pview`/`leaseView` carry `mediated`; `shutdown()` ends the proxy (it is the keeper's). **A mediated profile is attached, never pinned**: a pin hands the next launch the DIRECTORY (P0's spawn env) and a shared browser has one owner, so `setPin` refuses `pin_refused` by name, `pinForCreate` skips a Task-Group / instance default (or a stale pin) naming one with the reason on `refused` (ws-create journals it and starts ephemeral), and `updateProfile` to `instance` refuses `pinned` while any conversation pins it. Gate: test-browser-mediation ④.
**P4b install action (2026-09-17, §7.4 failure form (1)):** `cloakExecutable()` gains a THIRD rung — the package this keeper installed under `data/browser-tools`, its executable read from that package's OWN `package.json` `bin` (`installedCloakBin`, never a guessed name); `installVerdict({host})` = the PURE verdict over the §7.2.1 proof record (`providers.proof` injectable, else `B.CLOAK_EGRESS_PROOF`), the executable rung and the single flight; `installCloak()` acts ONLY on an ok verdict (a refusal is thrown by its code and spawns nothing): ONE `npm install --prefix <data>/browser-tools … cloakbrowser@<measured version>` (npm from the session PATH, `install_unavailable` when absent), output to `install.log`, a 15-min bound, exit recorded in `installState` and announced through the profiles broadcast; the switcher view carries `install`. Invariant: the install pins the version the measurement describes — an unpinned download would invalidate the record it is gated on.

**P4 second half (2026-09-17; §7.4 / §7.5 / D33 / D34):** `start` runs the
capability control for the profile's machine (`backend_unavailable` naming

source}`; nothing recognisable ⇒ the reading stays unknown, never a fabricated
number) and the Chromium MAJOR (`probeCdp` → `/json/version` → `reg.majors`

returns `{mode:'proposal', text, detail, affected}` for the route to file and

(Chromium's process singleton: no live handover) → `provider`/`seed`/
`defaultBackend`/`lastSwitchAt` written → `start` on the SAME directory with
the carried seed → for every lease `open <lastUrl>` under ITS OWN session name
(`--pin-tab` at/above the floor) → `targetId` rewritten on the SAME lease
object (the lease is looked up by (profileId, browserKey) and never destroyed)
→ `lastChromiumMajor` raised to the ladder's `recordMajor`; mid-way `attach`,
`switchBackend` and `resolveFor` answer the NAMED `browser_restarting`, never a
timeout. `noteLeaseUrl` stamps a lease's `lastUrl` from BOTH producers (the
live view's `url` mirror through `noteUserUrl`, the CLI's navigation through
the audit route); `switcherView` (rows with reasons, the masked source chip,
seats, versions `{recorded, dir, majors}`, blocked claims, hints, leases);
`chipFor` (`chromium 146` / `cloak 146 (free)`); `seatStates` (`used` = this
instance's own count, `runningOf(provider)`); `blocked` (one claim per
(conversation, host), bounded 50; a dead conversation's claims go at

directory's own `Last Version`, read-only); `cloakExecutable` (the setting's
path, else PATH — nothing is ever downloaded). `list()` carries `chips`,
`seats`, `majors`, `blocked`, `siteHints`, `switching`. Gate:
test-browser-backend ③.

**lane-cloak (2026-09-28) — cloak on the real binaries.** (a) THE LAUNCH IS AN
ENV PAIR: `SW.launchEnvFor('cloak', {seed, executablePath, proxy})` (the row's `launchArgs` + seed + proxy) =
`AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` + `AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS=--no-sandbox,
--fingerprint=<seed>,--proxy-server=<the run proxy>,--proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>`,
merged into `rec.launchEnv` so EVERY call of the keeper's session carries the
same launch view — measured: as argv on `open` alone, the keeper's own `get
cdp-url` right after it relaunched the browser without its arguments (and
without `--no-sandbox` it died on Ubuntu's userns restriction);
`rec.launchFlags` stays true (a heal never relaunches cloak). (b) THE RUN PROXY
(`cloakEgressUrl` / `cloakEgress()`, see egress-proxy.js) is awaited before the
launch; a proxy that cannot listen refuses the start `egress_proxy_missing`.
(c) KEY OPTIONAL: `keyRequired(id)` asks the key consumer (browser-backend
`keyRequired` = the PURE `keyRequiredFor`: cloak false — measured, every cloud
row true) — `start`, the gate and the view read the ONE answer; with no key the
cloak child gets no vendor env. (d) THE SWITCH'S RE-OPEN is `--pin-tab tab new
<lastUrl>`: 0.38.1's pin is sticky per session and the bound tab died with the
old browser, so `open` answered `tab_gone` for every lease (found by the first
switch on the real binaries, test-browser-share ⑧). (e) THE EXECUTABLE RUNG:
the setting (a chrome file), else the MEASURED build this keeper installed
(`installedCloakBin()` = `SW.cloakBinaryPath` under `cloakCacheDir`, counted
only while `installedStamp()` names the record's Chromium + SHA-256); PATH is
never asked — the `cloakbrowser` command is the vendor's management CLI.
(f) THE INSTALL is three named steps (`installState.step`): package (npm, skipped
when the pinned version is present) → binary (the package's own `cloakbrowser
install` under `SW.cloakInstallEnv` — the pins, the cache, every other
CLOAKBROWSER_* dropped, the install proxy — refused if a browser appeared with
nothing admitted) → verify (SHA-256 = the record's, then `cloak-installed.json`);
a platform the record does not describe is `install_unmeasured_platform`
(409). `egressResolve` (create option, identity in production) lets the gates
point an admitted name at a loopback target.
**Verify r1 V3 of lane browser-propose (2026-09-30): "Approve again" means
again.** The vendor's CLI returns a pinned build whose `chrome` exists and is
executable AS IS (0.5.10 `ensureBinary` — nothing downloaded, nothing verified)
and unpacks IN PLACE (`extractArchive`, not atomic). So a build THIS install
unpacked and then rejected (a SHA-256 that is not the measured one) failed every
later try with the same words, and an unpack cut after its `chrome` was written
(a full disk, exit 1) was stamped installed on the next try with its other files
missing (both reproduced over a vendor-shaped fake). Now the install removes its
OWN unpack when the binary or verify step fails (`dropOwnUnpack`, only when the
build was not in the cache before this run — `had`), and marks an unpack in
flight (`cloak-unpacking.json`) so one a dead process left (a restart
mid-install) is removed at the next run; a build that WAS in the cache before
(seeded by the measure script, linked by a suite, shipped in an image) is never
touched — its refusal names the directory to remove. Gate: test-browser-backend
⑤ V3 rows + a patched-copy control.

**P4 (2026-09-16; §7.3 / D5 (b)):** `hostId` is a parameter the ACCESS layer
dispatches on, never a branch here — `access`/`hostKnown` are injected (the
wiring hands `browser-access`). `createProfile` refuses an unpaired `host` BY
NAME (`unsupported-host`, never a silent local fallback) and makes a directory
only for a row that owns one on THIS machine (a paired machine composes its own
through `browser-serve`; `cdp` has none). `start` has three arms: a LOCAL
chromium (unchanged), a chromium on a PAIRED machine (the `start` op there →
its own loopback cdp url → `forwardCdp` → the record carries `hostId`, the
device's pid/starttime/dir, `remoteCdpUrl` and `forward:{remotePort,
localPort}`; a start reporting no CDP url is `launch_failed`, because an env
with no CDP pair would launch a LOCAL browser instead), and an EXTERNAL
browser over `cdp` (`external:true`, no pid: the port is forwarded when
`host` is set and PROBED at `/json/version` — a dead port is `cdp_unreachable`
with the Chrome ≥ 136 non-default-user-data-dir remedy and NO launch).
`isLocalRec` gates every pid act: a remote/external record is never
pid-judged, never sampled by the runaway guard and never signalled here —
`stop` asks the device's own `stop` op (an unreachable machine is SAID, never a
silent success) and closes only the forward for an external browser (left
running: it is somebody else's); `adoptRemote` at boot re-forwards and re-ASKS
(status + cdp-url / a fresh probe), recording `stopped` WITH the reason when the
far side is gone. `attach` hands the env the hub-side CDP url for a reached
browser (`attachedEnvFor({cdpUrl})`); `browserView` strips `cdpUrl` AND
`remoteCdpUrl`; `list()` carries `providers` (the rows with their local
verdicts); `streamPortFor` refuses a reached/remote browser's live view by
name (`stream_unavailable`, not bridged in this release). Gate:
test-browser-providers ④.

**ORCH — the profile registry, its leases and the keeper of its browsers**
(P1, 2026-09-16; design §3.3–§3.5). Owns `data/browser-profiles.json`
(writeJsonAtomic, 0600 because a profile may carry a credentialed proxy;
`browser-profiles-updated` broadcast on every commit), the leases (one per
(profile, browserKey)), the browser records (one daemon per profile,
reuse-or-spawn through `browser-facts.createBrowserRuntime` = the CLI's own
`open` / `session info --json` / `get cdp-url` / `close --all` under ONE
namespace with a sanitised env), the conversation's pin, the ceiling and the
runaway guard (`src/keeper-limits.js`). Invariants: lazy — no timer until a
profile is attached; the daemon is launched with `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=0`
and THIS tick owns the idle clock (a lease that drops and returns never costs
a cold browser); `boot()` = `reconcile({graceMs:0})` → `adoptAll()` → maybe
`startTimer()`, in that order and no other; an unproven pid (starttime differs
or is unreadable) is recorded ended and never signalled; `stop()` = the CLI's
own `close --all` first, a SIGTERM/SIGKILL only when pid+starttime prove the
process ours; a runaway is stopped, parked for `RUNAWAY_COOLDOWN_MS`, telemetered
and announced; `removeProfile` refuses a leased or running profile and never
deletes the directory. `keeper()` is the module singleton ws-create asks for the
`conversation` rung lazily (the ws ctx contract is untouched); server.js calls
`bootBrowserKeeper()` (mounts-plugins-wiring) right after `restoreSessions()`.
Gate: test-browser-pin (fast) — the real keeper over a fake `agent-browser`
whose daemon is a real `sleep`.

**P1 second half (2026-09-16; design §3.7 / §3.8 / §3.2.5):** the registry
gained `children` (child handles `bk-<parent>.<n>` a conversation minted for its
sub-agents — reaped by prefix with the parent, at boot at once, at runtime
after the lease grace) and `told` (what each conversation was LAST TOLD about
its attachment set — the memory layer ①'s one-time refusal fires on;
persisted only when the fingerprint moved, dropped with the conversation).
`attach({alias})` stores the HANDLE on the lease once (an explicit alias must be
well-formed and free, else `bad_alias`/`alias_taken`; otherwise the label's slug
— a later rename never renames a handle an agent is using). `setFor(key)` is
the attachment-set view (`browser-profiles.attachmentsFor`), `tell(key)` records
the told view, `resolveFor({browserKey, handle, subagent})` = the blindness
check FIRST (a moved fingerprint ⇒ `profile_changed` once, and the session is
told) THEN `resolveHandle`; every agent-route mutation ends in `tell`, a USER's
UI act deliberately does not. `newChild`/`dropChild`, `audit()` appends ONE
`{at, sessionId, browserKey, profileId, verb, ok}` line to
`data/browser-audit.jsonl` (0600, the verb only — never a fill's content),
`adoptScratch({label, scratchDir, owner})` MOVES a rung-C scratch directory
under `~/.agent-browser/vs-bp-<id>` (the login kept; EXDEV refused by name),
and `taskGroupDefaultFor(facts)` asks the wiring's `taskGroupDefault` dep (the
Task-Group rung's fact) — a throwing dep answers `''`, never a throw out of a
create. Gate: test-browser-handles + test-profile-blindness (fast).

**P2 (2026-09-16; design §4.2):** `streamPortFor(target)` = the ONE way the
live view learns a port — an attachment target starts the profile's daemon if
it is not live and asks `stream status --json` (then `stream enable` only when
disabled) under the lease's own session name; an ephemeral target is asked with
the session's spawn pairs and starts nothing of ours; every failure is
`{ok:false, code, error}`, never a throw into the bridge.

**P3 (2026-09-16; design §4.3 / §4.3.1):** the INPUT SIDE of every
(conversation, browser) pair lives here IN MEMORY (`inputs`, keyed
`browser-takeover.inputKeyFor(browserKey, profileId|null)` — never persisted: a
restart is a handback by construction, the lease's `input` field is only a
mirrored VIEW). `takeover`/`handback` (PURE decisions, `onInput` listeners: the
bridge mirrors, the announcer decides what to deliver, server.js re-publishes
live facts), `noteUserInput`/`noteUserUrl` (the idle clock and the handback
URL), `pausedVerdictFor` + `resolveFor` refusing `browser_paused` while the user
drives (a child handle never), `inputSummaryFor`/`inputsFor` (the card and the
status route), the tick's `sweepIdleTakeovers` (setting `browser.takeoverIdleMs`,
default 10 min, 0 = never, floor 30 s) and `sweepPending`, detach/reconcile
dropping the state with a `detach` handback, and the `--confirm-actions`
registry (`notePending`/`resolvePending`/`pendingFor`/`pendingAllFor`,
`answerConfirmation` = the CLI's OWN `confirm|deny <id>` under the lease's
session in the profile's namespace — or the ephemeral browser's spawn pairs —
`onConfirmation`). Gate: test-browser-takeover (fast).

**Lane H verify r2 (2026-09-25) — A KEEPER THAT STARTS A BROWSER IS THE ONE THAT ENDS IT.** (M1: a SIGKILLed daemon's Chrome kept the profile's SingletonLock ⇒ the relaunch died "exit code: 21"; an ephemeral's orphan leaked.) Every launch and adoption records `rec.browser = {pid, starttime, dir}` (`captureBrowser` over `F.browserOfDaemon`; the binary's temp dir on rung N). A daemon seen gone — the tick (`markDaemonGone` for a named record, `markEphemeralGone`), a view's port, a start (a NAMED ready record is judged by its process now too), stop() after its own SIGKILL (a 1.5 s grace for the browser to exit first), a boot — runs `reapOrphan`: while the recorded browser is STILL that process naming that dir, SIGTERM then SIGKILL (`endProcess`, real time, never the injectable clock), said in the journal; single flight per profile in `reaping`, which every launch and the tick await. BEFORE EVERY LAUNCH on a directory (named, and a rung-C/D ephemeral) `clearProfileLock` judges the lock holder by PURE `profileLockVerdict`: its own orphan is ended, anything else refuses the start `profile_locked` naming the pid (the record says why; never signalled). **L4:** `livenessOf` / `daemonGone` = dead OR `recycled` (alive with another starttime) for the tick, `judgeEphemeral`, `streamPortFor`'s rec0 leg and start(); `stop()` keeps `pidVerdictOf` (an unproven pid is never signalled). **L8:** `detach({…, by})` — `by` defaults to `'agent'`; while the user drives that browser (`pausedVerdictFor(browserKey, inPid)`, `inPid` = null for a managed ephemeral, whose input key is `<key>|ephemeral`) an agent's detach throws `browser_paused` ("your detach did NOT run …", `takenAt`), before anything moves; the UI route passes `by: 'user'` and still ends the takeover with a `detach` handback. Gates: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ + ④ L8, test-browser-takeover ② / ⑥, test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (heavy, real 0.38.1).

**Lane H verify r3 (2026-09-25) — A RECORD OF A BROWSER IS RE-CAPTURED EVERY TIME IT IS JUDGED.** (MAJOR: the 0.38.1 daemon relaunches its Chrome in place — the launch-time `rec.browser` named a dead pid, the tick found it 'gone' after a daemon SIGKILL and never ended the relaunched Chrome, and a named profile answered `profile_locked … it may be the user's own browser` forever; an ephemeral's relaunched Chrome leaked unseen.) (a) `recaptureBrowser(rec, seenBy)` — the record kept while it is still the recorded process naming its dir; else, ONLY while the daemon is provably ours (`livenessOf === 'ours'`), re-captured: the dir's LOCK first (its holder a child of THIS daemon naming it), else the daemon's child naming it (rung N: dir unknown); a daemon with no Chrome records none; `rec.browser` now also carries `devtoolsPort`. Called by the tick (every ready local record, after the gone checks), `start()`'s live return, `streamPortFor` (ephemeral and named), `stop()` at entry AND right before its SIGTERM, and boot adoption. `followRelaunch` = the same + a NAMED ready record's cached `cdpUrl` dropped and re-asked through `leaseCdpUrl` (the keeper's own session + launch view; the mediator repointed) when a NEW browser was captured — a lease never dials the dead endpoint. (b) `mintedDirOf(p, dir, recorded)` — a named profile's `<homeDir>/.agent-browser/vs-<id>`, an ephemeral's own `p.dir`, or the temp dir recorded for an ephemeral's browser; an ADOPTED dir never. `clearProfileLock` passes it as `minted`; `reapOrphan` ends the recorded browser first, else judges the LOCK of each minted dir of the record (`own-orphan` only — `foreign` is never signalled; a survivor is recorded for stop's message); `stop()`'s post-SIGKILL reap now runs whenever the recorded browser OR a minted dir's lock holder is alive (1.5 s grace first). LOW 3: `daemonGone` = `gone | recycled | unrecorded`; a launch whose daemon starttime is unreadable twice (50 ms apart, `launchStart`) on a machine that reads starttimes is `failed` (`launch_failed`, "was gone right after its launch"), never `ready`. Gates: test-browser-ephemeral ⑥ (+ four keeper-copy controls and two runtime neuters), test-browser-mediation-chrome ④ (heavy, the real binary's in-place relaunch).

**Lane profile-lock-roll (2026-10-01, userW's pod roll) — THE LAUNCH-HOST WITNESS, THE TAKEOVER, AND THE REBIND.** (L1) `stampLaunchHost(rec, prev)` right before every `rt.launch` (a named profile's start, a rung-C/D ephemeral's) = `B.withLaunchHost` over `launchHostsFor(prev)` (`B.launchHostsOf(prev, fileHost)`; a new record is born carrying the previous one's lineage like its mark); `save()` stamps `reg.host = os.hostname()` and `load()` captures `fileHost` BEFORE the first save re-stamps it — the legacy witness. `clearProfileLock` / the heal pass `launchHosts`; `stale-previous-host` ⇒ `takeOverStaleLock(p, dir, v)` = `F.removeSingletonFiles` + `p.renamedFrom = {host, at}` + the journal line "the lock named this machine's previous name <old> — taken over (… removed from <dir>; this machine is <new>)"; `reapOrphan` passes it over. `list().machine.host` = this machine's name (the panel compares). Belt: at 'open' the grant is re-checked — `closed`, `grants.get(g.token) !== g`, `!g.upstream`, or the dialed url no longer the target's CURRENT one (`g.upstream` / `upstreamPageUrl`) ⇒ `up.close()` + 503 by the same words. Before: a lease revoked 100 ms into a 300 ms handshake upgraded its client anyway (101), answered by the upstream, in NO grant's `conns` — revoke's 1008, closeTargetsOf and shutdown never reached it (the upstream still open after shutdown: 1 opened / 0 closed); a repoint wired it to the OLD browser; a shutdown threw on the nulled `wss` (L7). Gate: test-browser-mediation ③c (revoke ⇒ "503 Lease Gone", 0/0 upstreams; repoint ⇒ 503 then the same url reaches the NEW browser, old 0 messages; shutdown ⇒ "503 Server Shutting Down", no uncaught; each layer ALONE refuses; CONTROL = the pre-fix copy with both removed via scripts/mutant-copy.mjs ⇒ 101 + the upstream open / old 1 new 0 / the TypeError). kb-bugfix-invariants "A LEASE REVOKED WHILE ITS CLIENT WAITED…".

**Verify r2 (2026-09-25, found beside desktop lane C's F1) — THE CLIENT SOCKET PARKED ON THE UPSTREAM OPEN LISTENS FOR ERRORS.** onUpgrade parks the client's socket while the upstream CDP websocket opens (up to `UPSTREAM_OPEN_MS`); node's http server removed its 'error' listener at 'upgrade' and ws adds one only in `handleUpgrade`, so a client that RESET meanwhile was an uncaught `ECONNRESET` — in the hub, the process's exit. Now `parkedError` (destroys the socket) and `parkedGone` (a client gone before the upstream opened ⇒ `up.terminate()`) are attached BEFORE the park; at the open a half-closed client closes the upstream (ws would drop it without its callback and the upstream stayed open, read by nobody — measured 1 opened / 0 closed), else the error listener is handed to ws's own right before `wss.handleUpgrade`. Gate: test-browser-mediation ③b (a reset and a half-close during a 300 ms upstream handshake; CONTROL = the pre-fix copy through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs ⇒ ECONNRESET + the upstream left open). kb-bugfix-invariants "A VIEWER'S RESET DURING THE PAIRED-MACHINE FORWARD…".

**ORCH — THE CDP-MEDIATING PROXY** (agent browser P6, 2026-09-21; design
§6.2 / §6.5 / D6). One loopback http server started LAZILY (a fresh instance
listens on nothing until the first grant), serving each (profile,
conversation) lease its OWN url: `GET /m/<token>/json/version` and
`/json[/list]` (the upstream asked and re-pointed / filtered), `WS
/m/<token>/devtools/browser` (the browser endpoint, every message judged by
the PURE rules) and `WS /m/<token>/devtools/page/<id>` (in scope only, 403
by name). Invariants: the upstream socket is opened HERE (the raw endpoint
never leaves the server; nothing is logged with a token or a raw url in it)
and the client is upgraded only AFTER the upstream is open (no message is
ever queued into a socket that may not come; an unreachable upstream is 502
on the upgrade); `grantFor({profileId, browserKey, upstream, targetIds,
paused})` mints a token ONCE per lease for the process's life and re-uses it
after (the scope KEPT, `targetIds` ADDED, the `paused` reader replaced — it is
read PER MESSAGE, never cached; a reader that throws is logged and read as
not paused, so a broken reader never wedges the browser); `repoint(profileId,
upstream|null)` follows the profile's browser (a restart closes live
connections 1012 `browser_restarting` and the SAME url reconnects; a stop
nulls it and every path answers 503 `browser_stopped`); `revoke({profileId,
browserKey, closeTargets=true})` closes the lease's connections 1008
`lease_gone` AND closes the lease's own tabs IN THE BROWSER over one bounded
upstream connection (`closing` is the promise) — because `Browser.close` is
refused through a session url, a mediated `close --all` closes the session's
daemon side only and its tabs would outlive the lease (measured on 0.32.0 +
Chrome 153); an unknown token is 404 on every path (never 403 — nothing is
confirmed); `list()` = grant views (counts only); `shutdown()` closes every
connection 1001 and forgets every grant (tokens are not persisted — a lease
that survives a server restart is re-granted lazily on its next `resolve`,
exactly as a forwarded port is). Gate: test-browser-mediation ③ (fast, the
real proxy over a fake CDP upstream) + test-browser-mediation-chrome (heavy,
the real chrome — the §6.2 exit).

**THE TAKEOVER INTERRUPTS (the owner's ruling, 2026-09-27).** `interrupt({profileId, browserKey})` — the keeper calls it at the takeover instant, before anything is announced, synchronously: per connection of the grant, PURE `M.interruptPlan` over `conn.pending` ⇒ every aborted call is answered `browser_interrupted` (its words = a new call's) and MARKED `aborted` (the browser's late reply is swallowed in `up.on('message')`, but `admitReply` still runs — a tab a cut createTarget made stays in the scope and the revoke closes it; a credit on it is settled `browser_interrupted`), and each session running an aborted script call gets ONE `Runtime.terminateExecution` under the proxy's OWN id (`INTERNAL_ID_BASE` 2000000000 counting down, never a pending client id; its answer lands in `g.lastInterrupt.terminateAnswers`, never at the client). → `{aborted:[{method, sessionId}], terminated, at}`; one journal line by count and method. MEASURED (test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑦, 0.38.1 + Chrome 153): the CLI's JSON carries `browser_interrupted` 2 ms after the takeover; a RUNNING 5 s loop stops (the page answers a probe at once, its last statement never runs); a script awaiting a timer is not recalled; a `fill`'s one `insertText` already at Chrome completes, a `type` stops mid-word. **BLAST (verify r5, measured): `terminateExecution` is page-context — if the aborted script call was only AWAITING (nothing of the agent's running) and the USER's own page script is executing at that instant, that one synchronous run is aborted (6/6 forced-busy trials; the interval keeps firing, an in-flight navigation still lands, the page stays `complete`); inherent to CDP, bounded, documented in design §6.2.2.** The r4 `fenceScripts` grant option is gone (a stale caller's is ignored). Gates: test-browser-mediation ⑦ (≤ 50 ms, a read left alone, terminate on the script's session, late answers swallowed, the cut tab kept; CONTROL: the old pause) + -chrome ⑦.

### src/browser-takeover.js
**Lane dialog-keys (the owner's "ok", 2026-09-30, on takeover-keyboard r4's proposal): A DIALOG YOUR OWN ACT OPENED TAKES THE KEYS; ONE THAT OPENS BY ITSELF NEVER DOES.** Before (verify r3 F4): every app modal was taken back while the user drove the agent's browser — Delete → the confirm → Enter put a line break into the PAGE and the file was kept (said once, "click the dialog's buttons"). `dialogOpener({press: {at, trusted, picture}, openAt, windowMs = USER_PRESS_MS})` → `{byUserPress, why}`: `'no press'` | `'synthetic press'` (isTrusted false — the browser's own flag) | `'pressed the page'` (the press landed on the live view's picture: it went to the page and opens nothing in the app) | `'stale press'` (outside 250 ms, before, unreadable) | `'pressed'`; the lines are distinct from `userPressFocus`'s (the controls anchor by text). `DIALOG_OPENERS` = `['app', 'page']`. `dialogVerdict({owns, yielded, held, byUserPress, opener})`: not `'app'` ⇒ `'allow'` (the agent's PAGE dialog on the view's own bar is never an app modal); `byUserPress` ⇒ `'take'` (whatever the view's state: a held dialog stacks, a yield returns to its box, an off-screen view keeps the dialog's hold); else `owns && !yielded && !held` ⇒ `'reclaim'` (the password guard), else `'allow'`. `dialogReturn({left, back: {valid}, base: {to: 'sink'|'yield', valid}})` → `'back'` (the older dialog's element) | `'older'` (verify r1: an older dialog still holds but the element the keys would return to is gone — its OWN field, never `<body>`) | `'sink'` | `'yield'` | `'stay'`. `dialogReclaimCue({verdict, at, lastCueAt})` = a `'reclaim'` said once per `RECLAIM_CUE_MS` (the Q1 limiter). `keyboardOwnership({…, dialog})` → `{owns: false, why: 'dialog'}` after `hidden`, before `yielded`; `keyboardTransition` compares `dialog` too (a take is a `release`: the keys held in the page let go). Gate: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (DV / DO / DR / DC tables + 10 patched-copy controls + the KT rows `kt-no-dialog`).

**Lane takeover-keyboard (userW inc-mum339id-1zsb, 2026-09-28): THE USER'S OWN PRESS YIELDS.** `focusVerdict({owns, editable, insideView, byUserPress})`: owning + an editable outside the view + `byUserPress` ⇒ `'yield'` (the keys go to the box the user pressed; the takeover continues); without it ⇒ `'reclaim'` as before (lane J r2's password guard — no fact given = no press, fail closed). `USER_PRESS_MS` 250. `userPressFocus({press: {at, trusted}, sameInput, focusAt, windowMs})` → `{byUserPress, why}`: `'no press'` (a script's .focus()), `'synthetic press'` (`trusted !== true`), `'pressed elsewhere'` (the picture, the sidebar, a taskbar button whose handler then focuses the composer), `'stale press'` (outside [press, press + windowMs], or unreadable), else `'pressed'`. `keyboardOwnership({…, yielded})` → `{owns: false, why: 'yielded'}` after the older refusals. `YIELD_EVENTS` + `yieldAfter(yielded, event)`: `'yield'` sets, `'press-view'` / `'claim'` / `'release'` clear, anything else keeps. **verify r1 (K4):** `heldReleases(pressed)` → the keyups a yield sends TO THE PAGE for every key still held there (the last pressed first, each carrying the modifiers still held after it; `MODIFIER_KEY_BITS` = CDP's Alt 1 / Control 2 / Meta 4 / Shift 8) — without them the keyups reach the text box the user pressed and the page holds the keys down for good (measured in chrome: Shift held across the press, the page logged its keydown and never its keyup). Gate: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (the tables + five patched-copy controls, each failing exactly its rows: the pre-fix verdict, the guard gone, no window, no trust, no same-input; the held-releases table + two controls: nothing released, no modifiers carried). **verify r2 (H1, the reverse direction):** `focusVerdict` takes `mine` — the takeover is the view's while it does not drive (minimized, another desktop, its stream reconnecting): not owning + `mine` + `byUserPress` ⇒ `'yield'` (the caret's home wins until a press on the view); not owning otherwise ⇒ `'allow'`. `keyboardTransition({was, now, caretOutside})` → `{changed, moveCaret}` = ONE ownership transition (`{owns, yielded}` before / after; `was` null = never judged): `changed` ⇒ redraw at once, `moveCaret` ⇒ the keys just moved to the page while a text box (or a frame) outside the view holds the caret — the caret moves to the sink, never only the keys routed past it (measured on cd867c05: restored with the caret in the composer, nothing said, "c2" to the page). Gate ⑦: four `mine` rows + control `h1-prefix`; nine transition rows + controls `kt-no-move` / `kt-owns-only`. **verify r2 (H3):** `keyboardTransition` also answers `release` = the keys just LEFT the page (owning → not) — the view lets go (`heldReleases`) of every key still held there while it can still send (measured: Shift held across a minimize or a press on Hand back reached the page as a keydown, never a keyup). Gate ⑦: two rows + control `kt-no-release`. **verify r2 (Q1):** `reclaimCue({why, press, focusAt, lastCueAt})` + `RECLAIM_CUE_MS` 6000 — a reclaim the user's OWN fresh press on something else caused (a button of his that focuses a box: the composer's expand button, a Reply that opens its box) stays a reclaim (binding it would reopen verify r1's K2 — a message arriving within ANY press's window would take the keys) but is SAID, at most every 6 s; a script's focus (no press), a synthetic or stale press never. Gate ⑦: eight rows + controls `rc-no-limit` / `rc-any-reclaim`. **verify r2 (H1b'):** `yieldHomeVerdict({yielded, drivesNow, drovePrev, homeVisible})` → 'end' | 'keep' + the `YIELD_EVENTS` row `'homeless'`: a yield made while the view was off screen whose HOME is gone when the view comes back to driving (the box pressed on another desktop is hidden; the caret fell to <body>, or a browser left it focused but hidden) ends — never while the view drove all along (a click on the message list keeps the yield: the risky direction would be chat text into the page). Gate ⑦: six rows + control `yh-always-keep`.

**Lane live-input (2026-09-27, the owner on a Mac driving the agent's Linux Chromium) — THE ⌘ CHORD TABLE, THE COPY CHORDS, THE JOURNAL'S URL.** MEASURED on Chromium 151: a `keyDown` carrying Meta TYPES its letter on Linux (⌘A / ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘Z put "a" "c" "x" "z" into the page). `macChord(k, {viewerMac, remoteMac})` translates a key already routed to the PAGE (keyRoute runs first — Ctrl+Backslash, Ctrl+Alt+←/→ and the ⌘V paste route keep theirs) when the viewer is a Mac and the browser is not: ⌘ itself → Control (held on its keydown, released on its keyup), ⌘ + any other key → Ctrl + that key with `dropText` (a chord never types), ⌘←/→ → Home/End, ⌘↑/↓ → Ctrl+Home/End (Shift kept), ⌥←/→/↑/↓ → Ctrl+arrows (Alt+← is the browser's Back on Linux), ⌥⌫ / ⌥⌦ / ⌘⌫ → Ctrl+Backspace / Ctrl+Delete, an ⌥-produced character → that character without Alt; identity otherwise (`rule` null). `MAC_CHORD_ROWS` = the table as data (from / to / why). `isMacPlatform(s)` reads navigator.platform / userAgentData / a UA / node's `darwin` — a plain-http page has NO userAgentData (a secure-context API), so the view falls back to navigator.platform. `copyChordOf(k)` = copy (Ctrl/⌘+C, Ctrl+Insert) | cut (Ctrl/⌘+X, Shift+Delete) | null — the chord still goes to the page (its own copy runs; a web terminal's Ctrl+C still interrupts). `urlForLog(url)` = origin + path, a query marked `?…`, never the fragment; about:/file: spelled by protocol, data:/blob:/javascript: as `<proto>…` — what the keeper's handback line prints. **verify-r6 B1 (2026-09-28) — A `--confirm-actions` CONFIRM RUNS WHAT ITS CARD SHOWED.** The pending confirmation's id and action were parsed from mirrored upstream records INCLUDING an error string, so a `click` whose error text echoed "requires confirmation c_<the pending upload's id>" became `{id: <upload's id>, action: 'click'}`; `notePending` silently overwrote the upload's entry (no re-broadcast; the For-you item read "click"), and Confirm made upstream confirm the UPLOAD; `answerConfirmation` / POST /api/browser/confirm never checked the id was pending for that browser; the card showed only the verb (verify-r6 agentA, probe2). **Verify r7 (S2, 2026-09-27) — THE SIBLING SPEND RULE.** `announceVerdict({cause, announceIdle, sibling, rerun})`: an explicit handback MIRRORED to a sibling conversation (`sibling: true` — taken WITH the primary, the user never on its view) delivers only when `rerun` is non-empty (its cycle interrupted or refused something — its agent was told to wait for the handback that names it); otherwise `{deliver: false}` and the zero-spend notice rides its next turn. The primary's explicit handback delivers as before; idle / viewer-left stay zero-spend whatever `rerun` says. **Lane S3 (2026-09-26):** `handbackFacts(text)` READS BACK what `handbackText` wrote → `{cause, target, dur, url, title:{key, params}}` | null — the chat card of a delivered handback is titled from it ("VibeSpace · you handed control back after 17 s — the page is now …"), and on a transcript rebuild the card has only the text. ### src/record-shape.js — lane S1 verify r4: the control_request's REQUEST is declared

`claude:stream:control_request` carries a nested spec for `request`: the 2.1.281 binary's five outbound subtypes as the `subtype` enum (can_use_tool · request_user_dialog · elicitation · hook_callback · mcp_message) and the union of their fields (can_use_tool's `pn` zod: tool_name, mcp_server, input, permission_suggestions, blocked_path, decision_reason(_type/_code), classifier_approvable, suppress_always_allow_rule, default_to_no, matched_ask_rule, title, display_name, tool_use_id, agent_id, description, requires_user_interaction, server_prompt, computer_folder, tool_kind; request_user_dialog: dialog_kind, payload; elicitation: mcp_server_name, message, mode, url, elicitation_id, requested_schema; hook_callback: callback_id, input, issued_at, deadline_ms; mcp_message: server_name, message) — a new subtype is an enum-drift card, a new field inside the request is named; before, the ask's own vocabulary was invisible (the studies' silence for a FUTURE shape). The binary oracle (test-record-shape §4) judges top-level fields only; the nested set was read by hand from the 2.1.281 binary. Gate: test-helper-ask ⑱ (the measured asks stay clean).

**Verify r5 (2026-09-27) — §4d THE PERMISSION-OUTCOME SENTENCE CENSUS.** The binary oracle now also reads the CLI's OWN lists of the tool_result texts it writes for a permission outcome — the anchor is the constant holding "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]"; from it the list `function X(){return[…,N,…]}` (2.1.281's `Gd()`) and the LARGEST `Y=new Set([…,N,…])` (its exact is_error set `IS`, with `a+b` suffix forms — a two-member `If` and a five-member `Fbe` also name the marker and are not the census); every member resolves to its string on a strings-dump line that declares another member (a reused minified name elsewhere — `ok="tengu_worker_owner_rows_killswitch"` — is not that). Every resolved sentence must be a row of src/permission-outcome.js and every list-backed row must be in the lists (literal rows spelled in the bundle): a newer build's extra sentence PRINTS and FAILS until classified — the same discipline as the field census, lenient on the mirror. Controls: a planted sentence and the table without the subagent's denial row are each named; the extractor on a synthetic bundle (a reused name, a template literal ending at its line, the suffix), without an anchor, without a list.

### src/server/browser-handback.js
**Lane browser-windows verify r5 ② (2026-10-02).** `announceDriveEnded(ev)` on the keeper's `drive-ended` event (never human-marked — the `if (ev && ev.human) return;` pin is untouched): the keeper says the user's drive of a browser ENDED (no window of it driven any more — a handback, his Browse-yourself window letting go, his row ending) and names the holders whose `tab new` was refused `window_busy` (`user_driving`) meanwhile; each live one gets ONE zero-spend `browser-window-free` notice (`WIN.driveEndedNotice`, `queueNotice` — never a delivery, never a card: nobody typed it; a holder with no live session is skipped). ### src/browser-stream.js
**Lane live-input (2026-09-27, "我似乎无法从外面复制文本进入那个浏览器" + "中文输入法也不 work") — THE KEY-TEXT CAP.** MEASURED on the agent's own Chromium 151 (and Chrome 153): CDP `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` refuses a `char` / `keyDown` text of 4+ UTF-16 units (-32602 Invalid 'text' parameter — Blink's key-event text cap, 4 incl. the terminator) and the stream server swallows the refusal: every paste ≥ 4 units and every IME commit ≥ 4 units landed nothing while a direct lease's receipt said "sent" (lane J r2's "a multi-character char inserts all of it" was measured with 'abc'). `CHAR_TEXT_MAX_UNITS = 3`. `textChunks(text)` = code points into ≤ 3-unit chunks (never a split surrogate) with the control-character rules measured on the same build: a `char` that STARTS with "\t" inserts the tab and drops the rest ⇒ a tab ends its chunk; a `char` that is only "\n" inserts nothing ⇒ a line break STARTS its chunk ("\nz" in a one-line field gives " z", like a paste) and line breaks in a row stay together; a lone final one joins / borrows from the previous chunk, else is DROPPED and counted (`dropped` — "x\t\n", "\n😀\n", a text that is only "\n" ⇒ `empty`); CRLF/CR → LF, NUL stripped; refused whole past `TEXT_MAX` (TEXT_CHUNK is gone). `textRecords` = the bridge's half (the `char` records), `inputTextRecord` = the viewer's half (ONE `input_text` record). WHY THE STREAM AND NOT `Input.insertText`: a direct insertText beside the stream was MEASURED to land between the first and the second of 20 keys queued before it on a busy page (the daemon dispatches serially) — text in the wrong place is worse than a slow paste (20 000 characters = 3.6 s on a quiet page). `viewerMessageVerdict`: `input_text` is holder-only (`text: true`), empty / too long refused by name; an `input_keyboard` whose text passes the cap is refused `text_too_long`. `receiptBook`: `noteInputSent(book, now, {ms})` gives a record its own wait (`textReceiptMs(chunks)` = 1.5 s + 10 ms a chunk, ≤ 2 min), `noteInputReceipt` keeps `landed` / `dropped` (`book.last`). `mouseRecord({…, held})`: a move while a button is held carries that button + `buttons` (a drag selects — `button:'none'` moves selected nothing), a press/release its `clickCount`; `clickCountNext` = the view's own multi-click count (≤ 500 ms, ≤ 4 px, same button, capped at 3). `hello({platform})`. `pickViewportTarget(…, {targetId})` prefers the stream's active tab by its CDP id. Gates: test-live-input §1/§2/§6 (fast) + test-browser-live-input ① (heavy — the cap and the chunker on the real Chromium).

And A TAKEOVER IS ANCHORED TO THE TAB IT BEGAN ON — `takeoverAnchor(activeTarget, now)` / `takeoverAnchorStep(anchor, {activeTarget, now})`: a `tabs` record naming another active tab within `TAKEOVER_ANCHOR_GRACE_MS` (62 since verify r4 — measured, below) of the takeover re-anchors silently (the in-flight switch that raced the takeover — measured on 0.38.1: the daemon's tabs record lands 11–45 ms after its switch, ahead of its first dispatch; 15 bursts of 40 keys at 50 ms, 0 lost, every receipt honest); after the grace it marks the takeover `switched {from, to, at}` — the user's inputs are answered `tabSwitchedReceipt()` (`tab_switched`, the way out in the words) and NEVER forwarded, until a handback + a fresh takeover (consent to drive what is now on show); the anchor's own tab coming back clears the mark; a record naming no tab judges nothing. **Verify r4 (2026-09-27): THE GRACE IS A MEASURED CONSTANT** — r3's 1 s was 50× the latency it covers (F6: a whole second in which an agent's switch was FOLLOWED); scripts/measure-anchor-grace.mjs (real binary + real Chrome + real mediator + real bridge, a recording proxy stamping every daemon CDP call, 2 × 100 switches) measured the CLI-to-`tabs`-record span at p99 15.37 / 20.37 ms (max 20.37; from `Page.bringToFront` p99 11.0 / 8.3): `TABS_RECORD_LATENCY_P99_MS` = 20.37, `TAKEOVER_ANCHOR_GRACE_MS` = ⌈3 × p99⌉ = 62 — a switch the record cannot explain by latency is a switch; a loaded box that stretches the record past it mis-judges a takeover as switched, which the user undoes with a re-takeover (fail closed, recoverable). No alias can spell it (ALIAS_RE starts with [a-z0-9]). Gate: test-browser-profiles ㉒.
**Lane J r2 (2026-09-25):** `LIVE_ALIGN = 'top'` — the live view draws its picture TOP-aligned (CSS `object-position: 50% 0`) and `drawnRect(elRect, picW, picH, align)` / `pointerToDevice({…, align})` / `deviceToViewport({…, align})` take the same word (default `'center'` for every other caller), so the spare room sits below the page and the pointer, the ripple and both cursors share one placement. `textRecords(text, {chunk = TEXT_CHUNK 200, max = TEXT_MAX 20000})` → `{ok, records}` of `input_keyboard` `char` records (measured on 0.38.1: the stream hands `eventType` to CDP `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` verbatim; a multi-character `char` inserts all of it) — split on code points, CRLF → LF, refused as a whole past the max (`too_long`, never trimmed). `keyRecord` takes the DOM's `keyCode` for `windowsVirtualKeyCode` (F-keys were 0; 229 ignored) and keeps the text on a chord (Ctrl+A still selects — measured; AltGr characters arrive as Ctrl+Alt on Windows).

**Lane J (2026-09-25, inc-muhgv0fb-9i4u — owner: "接管浏览器的时候鼠标操作位置不对").** TWO sizes, never one: the PICTURE (the JPEG as decoded — what `object-fit: contain` letterboxes) and the PAGE (the CSS viewport every `input_*` record is in). `frameGeometry({picW, picH, page, meta})` → `{picW, picH, cssW, cssH, source}`: the page's own layout reading (`page` = `{clientWidth, clientHeight}`, the bridge's `viewport` record) when it fits the picture (`pageViewportFor`: exact when its aspect is the picture's; a scrollbar shrinks ONE side — the untouched side × the picture's aspect, accepted within `SCROLLBAR_MAX_PX` 32, else stale ⇒ refused), else the metadata/status claim ONLY when its aspect IS the picture's (`sameAspect`, 1.5 picture px of rounding), else the picture 1:1 (an undownscaled screencast at DPR 1 — the headless default). Measured on 0.32.0 AND 0.38.1: `metadata.deviceWidth/Height` + the status' `viewportWidth/Height` are the CONFIGURED 1280×720 (0.32.0 even stamps `timestamp: 0`); Chrome's own screencast metadata says the page (1280×577 headless; a headed 2560×1440-screen window 1265×1277, downscaled into a 713×720 JPEG). The checked-in fixture's frame was ALWAYS a 1280×577 JPEG — nobody sized it. `pointerToDevice`/`deviceToViewport` take `picW/picH` (the letterbox) beside `frameW/frameH` (= cssW/cssH, the scale; picW defaults to frameW so an old two-size-equal call is unchanged); `toLocal` puts a viewport point into a positioned host's layout px (the overlay's ONE basis); `jpegSize(b64)` reads the SOF off the head (no Buffer — the bundle carries it; 2 KiB fast path); `pickViewportTarget` = the ACTIVE tab's url, else the first ordinary page; `privateUpstream` = the daemon's `cdp_url` command/result pair (never relayed). Gate: the lane J table in test-browser-takeover (fast) + test-browser-live ⑤ (heavy, the real rung).

**PURE — the live view's decisions** (agent browser P2, 2026-09-16; design
§4.2 / §4.4 / §3.7). CJS with no imports so the server bridge and the browser
bundle carry ONE set of rules. Invariants, one each: `streamTargetFor` picks the
pane a live view shows — a handle, else the set's default, else its only
member, else the FIRST attachment (a view is not a command; refusing to open a
window would be a silent failure of a user act), else the session's own
ephemeral browser under its P0 `AGENT_BROWSER_*` pairs, else a typed
`no-browser`/`no-key`; `classifyUpstream` makes `frame` latest-wins and every
other record ordered, and an unknown type is relayed rather than silenced (a
newer upstream must not be muted by an old bridge); `parseStreamStatus` /
`streamPlan` read the MEASURED 0.32.0 answers (`stream status --json` →
`{data:{enabled, connected, port, screencasting}}`; `stream enable` on an
enabled session exits 1 with "already enabled" and is NOT a failure; a launch
failure surfaces inside `stream status` and IS one); `viewerMessageVerdict`
aggregates `config` per viewer, consumes `ack`, and forwards `input_*` only from
the viewer holding the lease's input side (Watch mode refuses every input with
the typed `watch-mode` code; P3's `takeover`/`handback`/`confirm` are CONTROL
verbs the keeper decides, never forwarded); P3 adds the CDP-shaped input
builders `mouseRecord`/`wheelRecord`/`keyRecord`/`touchRecord`/`modifiersOf`
(the stream server's own shapes; modifiers alt 1 · ctrl 2 · meta 4 · shift 8)
and `deviceToViewport`, the inverse of `pointerToDevice`, for the agent cursor; `frameGate` drops a frame for a
viewer that still has more than the LOW-water mark queued (latest-wins per
viewer, one slow tab never stalls the others) while `backpressureVerdict` keeps
the VNC bridge's 8 MiB pause / 1 MiB resume verbatim; `drawnRect` +
`pointerToDevice` are the ONE DPI conversion (viewport px in, device px out,
letterbox-aware, `null` outside the picture — never a clamped edge). The real
shapes live in `scripts/fixtures/browser-stream/session-0.32.0.json` (one real
headless session captured on 2026-09-16: status/tabs/frame/command/result, no
`seq` on 0.32.0, a foreign Origin 403, loopback/absent accepted). Gate:

lane-mirror-197, 2026-09-29):** the three `CONTROL (naive study 2)` legs went red
once on the Actions mirror of 2.369.197 (green on the gate's retry) with the

Chrome's /json showed no page target within a fixed 30 s. Two orders, neither
