### src/ws-keepalive.js + src/server/browser-stream.js — THE ONE WS KEEPALIVE (lane stream-ping, browser-windows BL-r5-2, 2026-10-02)
`src/ws-keepalive.js` (imports nothing) is THE rule every long-lived ws bridge arms: `keepaliveStep(state, 'tick'|'pong', now)` → `{state, send: 'ping'|null, drop: false|{code: 1006, reason: 'no pong for <2 × pingMs> ms'}}` (PURE: a peer that answered no pong since the previous tick is dropped, else pinged), `armKeepalive(ws, {pingMs, now, onDrop})` = the timer (unref'd) + the socket's pong driving it; a drop calls `onDrop` (the bridge names the close) and TERMINATES (a half-open peer would never read a close frame). PING_MS = 20 s (2.369.118's number). desktop-stream's two hand-written pingers are now `KA.armKeepalive` (its lines byte-identical: `closed (no pong for 40000 ms) after …`); browser-stream's viewers had NO keepalive — a half-open live view (no close frame, 17 MB buffered in 10 s, no send error, measured by browser-windows r5) stayed counted until the kernel's TCP timeout, the window "watched". Now `watchViewer` arms every viewer (agent and Browse-yourself paths), and `dropViewer` — the ONE leave path for a clean close, an error and a keepalive drop — stops the timer and logs ONE named line `[browser-stream] <relay>: viewer N closed (<who>) after Ns, code C, F frame(s) sent`; the count falls, the watched state follows, the upstream and the other viewers are untouched. The client's reconnect ladder reads every close alike (pinned). `create({keepaliveMs})` exists for the suites. Census: test-architecture §68 + test-ws-keepalive ③ (every src/server/*-stream.js arms it, none pings by hand). Gates: test-ws-keepalive (fast — the real bridge drops a never-pong viewer in 2 × 200 ms), test-desktop-stream-keepalive (unchanged, green), test-browser-live ④ (heavy — the REAL 0.38.1 stream: a half-open viewer dropped by the production 20 s rule in ≤ 40 s, the other viewer's picture continues).
**Verify r1 (2026-10-02): OUR OWN STALL IS NO VERDICT (the 2.369.16 rule).** The pong is read on our event loop: a sync burst right after a tick's ping (the 2.369.16 storm — bursts back to back, one loop turn between them) left every pong unread and the next tick dropped every live viewer at once (measured: 3 viewers answering in 30 ms, two 3 s bursts at keepaliveMs 200 ⇒ all 3 gone — a reconnect storm into a stalled server). `keepaliveStep(state, 'tick', now, {loopGapMs})` now judges only a CLEAN round: a tick late by > `stallGraceMs` (= min(5 s, pingMs / 2)) or a loop gap > it ⇒ `stalled`: nobody dropped, the silent peer re-pinged and judged next round (reason then `no pong for 40000 ms after N stalled round(s)`); bound MAX_STALLED_MISSES = 6 (ws-heartbeat's), then `no pong for <ms> ms (7 stalled rounds in a row)`. The gap comes from `createLoopGauge` — ONE unref'd 1 s pulse per process (`LOOP_GAUGE`, retained while any keepalive is armed, its own monotonic clock); a tick `read(since)`s it, sampling first, so a block ending in the tick's own loop turn is seen. The classic path is byte-identical (both desktop pingers: same frames, rounds and lines as b924041f). The ping is FIFO behind queued frames (ws never interleaves a control frame): a live viewer whose link needs > pingMs to drain the bytes ahead of a ping is dropped (measured at 1 s: a 16 MiB frame on a 4 MiB/s link) — the frame gate bounds those bytes to ~1 MiB + one frame on this bridge. Census scope (§68): every `new WebSocketServer(` in server.js + src/** is a *-stream.js bridge or named outside the rule with its reason (the /ws main socket = ws-heartbeat; the agentd dial-in = the device mux's pings; cdp-mediator = loopback only). Gates: test-ws-keepalive ⑤ (stall table, gauge, wiring + controls) ⑥ (the real bridge through a storm; control: the pre-fix rule drops all 3).

### src/server/browser-stream.js
**Lane browser-stuck (2026-09-28): A PAGE DIALOG IS SHOWN WHERE THE USER LOOKS.** Additive: `create({dialogs})`; `armDialogs(relay)` on the upstream's open (the watch is on the browser before the user looks); the watch's events ⇒ `{type:'dialog', state:'open', dialog}` / `{state:'closed', id|ids, answered:{how, by, at}}` to the relays of that browser whose `activeTarget` is the dialog's tab (any before the first `tabs` record); a late viewer is replayed the open one (`dialogRecordFor`); a viewer's `{type:'dialog-answer', id, accept, text}` is intercepted BEFORE `viewerMessageVerdict` and answered as the USER through the watch (any viewer — the user's own chrome, not a forwarded page input) ⇒ `{type:'dialog-ack', ok, code, error}` (a gone dialog `no_dialog`). `activeTargetsFor({browserKey, sessionId, profileId})` = the watch's scope — ONE conversation's relays (by its browser key, else its session; neither ⇒ none — verify r2 #3: it answered every relay, and conversation A's chip carried B's dialog); `tapDialogAct({sessionId, profileId, action, dialog})` hands the TAPS (the recorder) the stream mirror's own dialog command/result pair — never a viewer. Gate: test-browser-stuck ④.

**Lane live-input (2026-09-27) — ONE ORDERED INPUT PIPELINE, COPY OUT, THE CLAIM.** Every forwarded input of the holder goes through `relay.inq` → `pumpInput` → `forwardInput` (credit, then the write): `input_text` becomes ONE queued act (`enqueueText` → `S.textRecords`) whose ≤ 3-unit chunks keep their place among the keys and clicks around it; ONE receipt answers the act when its last chunk settles (`landed`, `dropped`); a refused chunk stops the act (its tail is not typed around the hole) and the receipt says how much landed. A DIRECT lease forwards at once (the daemon keeps the order); a MEDIATED lease keeps ≤ `INPUT_WINDOW` (16) records waiting on their credits (the mediator holds 256 for 1.2 s — a chunked paste sent at once evicted its own first credits). The receipt carries `landed` / `dropped`. COPY OUT: a takeover arms ONE copy watch (`keeper.watchCopiesFor(target, {targetId: relay.activeTarget})`, browser-viewport.js `watchCopies`) that follows the tab on show and ends at the handback / relay end; the page's copy/cut reaches the HOLDER as `{type:'clipboard', kind, gesture, text, length, truncated}` — **ONLY on the holder's own gesture the bridge forwarded (verify 2026-09-27: `relay.copyArm` stamped in `forwardInput` by T.armCopyGesture on every forwarded record, judged in `deliverCopy` by T.copyDeliverVerdict — a chord / a press arms ONE delivery for COPY_GESTURE_MS; a copy the page fires on its own is dropped here, `stats.copiesDropped`, nothing leaves the server; the arm is cleared with the watch)** (a duplicate within `COPY_DEDUP_MS` 150 is one copy; the text is never a journal line); a watch that cannot arm is said once in the journal. THE CLAIM: a `fit {claim:true}` makes `relay.fitClaim` = that viewer (cleared when it hides or leaves); `fitVerdict` / `fitTarget` get it; every `fitted` broadcast carries the ruling viewer's `place`. `hello` carries `platform` (create's `platform`, default process.platform). `stats()[].input = {queued, inflight, claim, copyWatch}`. Gate: test-live-input §6 (fast; the pre-fix record, a window-less bridge, a watch-less bridge and a door-less bridge as patched-copy controls) + test-browser-live-input ② + the door leg (heavy).

**Builder r2 (2026-09-27, the reality verifier's A + B — reproduced on the real stack first).** (A) A SHARED (mediated) browser refused the bridge's own `set viewport` while the user drove (the mediator's paused fence answers every viewport call on the lease's url `browser_interrupted`, the product's own included): the view printed the agent's refusal text, `fs.failed` kept the page "could not resize" for FIT_RETRY_MS after the handback, and a failed set's command mirror that landed AFTER the CLI returned (a busy stream — the failure path had dropped `fs.pending`) was read as THE AGENT'S choice ("Agent's size 1398×835" = our own refused set). Now: the keeper answers `held_while_driving` (below); the bridge never records it as `fs.failed` (the handback re-fits at once), says it ONCE per takeover in the journal (`fitHeldSaid`, never a warning) and broadcasts `unavailable` with that `code`; EVERY failed set is `setAsideOwn` (its late mirror is `prevOwn` = ours), the put-back's failure too. (B) The page is never resized under the driver's HELD button: `noteButtons` feeds PURE `FIT.buttonStep` from the records the bridge FORWARDS (a watcher's never reach it); a set that comes due while `btnDown` is non-empty waits (`fitHeld` + a timer at `FIT_HOLD_MAX_MS` 15 s — a release that never arrived) and runs at the last release (`releaseButtons`, also at every handback); and a MODE change fits AT ONCE (`scheduleFit(relay, 'mode', {delay: 0})`) — the 250 ms debounce put the takeover's resize under the first press (a second tab's close restarted it: the verifier's drag moves jumped y=232 → y=361). **Lane S4 (naive study 2, 2026-09-26) — THE PAGE IS THE PANE'S SIZE, THE TRAILING FRAME, THE FRESH FRAME.** A viewer's `fit` report lands in `relay.fits`; `scheduleFit` (250 ms, single flight + one trailing re-run) asks PURE `fitVerdict` over the reports, the holder/mode and the per-KEY `fitStates` entry (`{target, applied, baseline, agent, floorW, pending, restoreTimer}` — it OUTLIVES the relay: the page keeps the size we set, the agent's choice stays the agent's; `closeForSession` forgets it) and sets the page through `keeper.setViewportFor` (a keeper without it = no fitting, the old view). The baseline is the page's own size before the first fit (`pageSizeOf`: the lane J reading restored by the picture's aspect, else the picture after 1.5 s). `{type:'fit', state: fitted|agent|restored|unavailable, width, height, viewerId, rule, drawScale, floor, device, error}` goes to every viewer and is REPLAYED to a late one (`relay.lastFit`). `noteViewportCommand` runs before the taps and the fan-out: OUR mirror (PURE `ownViewportRecord`, `fs.pending`) is DROPPED (never a viewer's "Running a command", never a tap's); an agent's `viewport`/`device` command sets `fs.agent` (applied cleared, restore cancelled, the journal says so) and every later ruling letterboxes until a viewer's `fit {force}`. `checkFit` reads the first pictures after a set: 'scaled' ⇒ `floorW` = 500 and a re-fit. `armRestore(key)`: nobody visible (or the relay ended) ⇒ after RESTORE_AFTER_MS the baseline is set back — re-checked at fire (somebody back / the agent took it ⇒ nothing). **THE TRAILING FRAME** (`fanOutFrame` + `armTrail`, one timer per viewer): a frame the gate refused is followed by the relay's LATEST frame as soon as `S.frameGateWait` says the gate is open (a buffer-held viewer is polled at 50 ms); a `config` raising a viewer's fps catches it up. `relay.frameSeq` / `viewer.sentSeq` say whether a viewer has the latest. **THE FRESH FRAME** (`noteNavigation` on a changed `url` record or active tab → `armFresh`): no upstream frame within FRESH_FRAME_MS ⇒ `captureFresh` = `keeper.freshFrameFor` → a `frame` record `{metadata:{…, fresh:'navigation'|'refresh'}}` through the same path as an upstream frame (lastFrame, the taps, the gate + trail) unless the stream's own frame came meanwhile; a viewer's `refresh` first catches it up, then asks (≤ 1 per REFRESH_EVERY_MS). A size the keeper could not set is SAID (`unavailable`, the reason) and not asked again for `FIT_RETRY_MS` 30 s (each ask is a CLI spawn — the fork tax); a new pane size is. A NEW relay's FIRST picture re-checks the size we set (`fitHonored` ≠ exact ⇒ `applied` cleared): a browser started again at its own size (an idle release, a crash) is set again, never "kept". `stats()` adds `fit` + `frameSeq`, counters `trailed` / `fresh` / `own`. Gate: test-browser-fit ② (+ four bridge controls) + test-browser-live-fit (heavy).

**Lane H verify r1 (2026-09-25) — H2: an ephemeral stream closing is reported to the keeper.** In `connectUpstream`'s `up.on('close')`, before `upstream-closed` is broadcast, a relay whose `target.kind === 'ephemeral'` calls `keeper.noteStreamClosed(relay.target)` (guarded, one line: the suite's mutant copy deletes exactly it). The daemon's death is usually first seen here. The keeper judges the process and takes the holder row out at once, so the viewer's 1 s reconnect is refused `browser_stopped` and never becomes a CLI `stream status` that would START a daemon. Measured: the row left in 25 ms (pre-fix: still `ready` after 1014 ms, until the tick). Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ④ H2 (the REAL bridge over the real keeper, a real ws upstream; a bridge copy without the call leaves the row standing = the control). **Naive study 2 (finding 4):** `tap(sessionId, '~child:<key>')` resolves a sub-agent's browser under ITS pairs (`keeper.ephemeralPairsFor`). `relayKeyOf` = `<session>|<profileId | child:<key> | ephemeral>`, and the relay's `browserKey` / `envPairs` are the target's (the child's), never the parent's. A viewer's request carries no child pairs and is refused `no-browser`. `broadcastTo` skips child relays. `tap()` answers `target.child/browserKey`.
**Lane J (2026-09-25):** the relay notes the PICTURE size off every frame's JPEG head (`S.jpegSize`) and the ACTIVE tab off every `tabs` record, and `scheduleViewport(relay, why)` asks `keeper.viewportFor(target, {activeUrl})` — single-flight, one trailing re-run — on the first frame, a picture-size change, an active-tab change and a TAKEOVER (a window resized in the same proportions keeps its picture size); every viewer gets `{type:'viewport', ok, clientWidth, clientHeight, picture, why}` and a late viewer is replayed the last GOOD one; a failed read reaches the viewers typed and the journal ONCE (the view then maps by the picture). `S.privateUpstream` records (the `cdp_url` pair the ephemeral read causes) are dropped BEFORE the taps and the fan-out. `stats()` carries `picture` + `viewport`. Gate: test-browser-takeover ④b.
**2.369.180 (lanes H + J integrated) — a late viewer is told the upstream is OPEN.** `attachViewer` sends `{type:'status', state:'upstream-open'}` to a viewer that joins a relay whose upstream is already open (after the hello + replays). The broadcast went out before it came, and lane H's recorder taps a holder's relay before anybody watches — so every live view of an ephemeral browser is such a joiner; without the record the view never read itself `connected`, and lane J's `keyboardOwnership` (connected is one of its facts) never let a takeover own the keyboard (test-browser-live ⑥ red 2/2 in the heavy tier; the bridge leg now asserts the late viewer's record, and a copy without the line reproduces both). Invariant: a state a relay BROADCASTS on a transition is also said to whoever joins after the transition.

**ORCH — the live view's ws bridge** (P2). `GET
/api/browser/stream?session=<webuiId>[&profile=<handle|id>]` upgrades a
COOKIE-authed WebSocket (401 before the upgrade — never a socket that opens
then dies) and bridges it to that session's loopback stream server in
`bridgeVncSocket()`'s shape: ONE upstream connection per (session, target)
fanned out to N viewers (a late viewer is replayed the last status/tabs/url and
the last frame at once); the `maxFps` sent upstream is the MAX across viewers
and each viewer is served at its own rate; a viewer over the low-water mark has
frames dropped, the upstream is `pause()`d past 8 MiB on ANY viewer and resumed
by a 50 ms poll once EVERY viewer is under 1 MiB; every refusal (`not-found`,
`unsupported-host` for a remote session, `no-key`, `no-browser`,
`not_attached`, the keeper's own launch codes) reaches the viewer as a typed
`status` message before the close; the upstream dying, the last viewer leaving
and the session ending each tear the relay down with a reason. The port comes
from `keeper.streamPortFor(target)`: an attachment's profile daemon (started
when stopped — a view is a start, like an attach), asked under the lease's own
session name `vs-<browserKey>`, or the ephemeral browser asked with the very
pairs the session was spawned with (`session._browserEnv`, kept in meta so a
restart still finds it). **P3 (§4.3):** `takeover`/`handback` ask the KEEPER
(the one owner of the input side) and `relay.mode`/`relay.holder` mirror its
answer; every relay on that browser learns a flip through `keeper.onInput` and
sends ONE `mode` record per viewer (`mine` for the holder); the holder's socket
closing and the relay ending hand back as `viewer-left`; the holder's inputs
restart the keeper's idle clock (≤ 1/s); the `url`/`tabs` mirrors feed the
handback URL; a `confirmation_required` result becomes a typed `confirmation`
record (+ the keeper's registry, replayed to late viewers) and a viewer's
`confirm` is answered through `keeper.answerConfirmation`; a keeper without the
P3 surface degrades to relay-local mode bookkeeping. Built in

**Lane live-input (2026-09-27): `watchCopies(cdpUrl, {targetId, activeUrl, onCopy, onEnd, nonce})`** — one PERSISTENT page socket on the stream's active tab (by targetId): `Runtime.enable`, `Page.enable`, `Runtime.addBinding({name:'__vsCopy_<nonce>', executionContextName:'vs-copy-<nonce>'})`, `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument({worldName, runImmediately})` + `Page.createIsolatedWorld` + evaluate for every frame already there (`copyWatchSource`: capture copy / cut listeners reading the focused field's selection — never a password field, which fires no copy anyway — else the document selection, through same-origin frames; ≤ `COPY_TEXT_MAX` 200 000). ### src/lib/keyboard-owner.js

**THE ONE KEYBOARD OWNER OF THIS CLIENT** (lane J r2, 2026-09-25). `claimKeyboard({id, owns})` (a re-claim moves it to the end), `releaseKeyboard(id)`, `keyboardOwner()` = the LAST claim whose `owns()` is true right now (PURE `ownerOf`; `owns` re-asked every time — a dropped socket / a hidden view / a handback release without bookkeeping), `keyboardOwned()` = THE guard every "caret into my text box" path asks: `ChatInput.focus` (the attach/reconnect path via `ChatView.focus`) and `TerminalSession.focus` stand down while it is true; the owning live view's `focusin` reclaim is the backstop for every other `.focus()` site (a per-site guard would be the patch this module exists to avoid). Imports only browser-takeover.js. Gate: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (ESM import of the real module).

**Lane takeover-keyboard (userW inc-mum339id-1zsb, 2026-09-28): THE YIELD IS PART OF THE ANSWER.** A claim is `{id, owns(), yielded?()}`: when the user's OWN press put the focus in a text box outside the view (src/lib/keyboard-yield.js), the view's `owns()` answers false (PURE `keyboardOwnership({…, yielded})`, why `'yielded'`) while the claim STAYS — the takeover continues, the agent stays refused — so `keyboardOwned()` is false and ChatInput / TerminalSession behave as always; a press back inside the view makes `owns()` true again. `keyboardYielded()` = nobody owns AND some claim's `yielded()` is true (the composer's line reads it). `onKeyboardChange(fn)` → unsubscribe, `keyboardChanged()` = the ONE signal a view sends when the answer may have changed (claim, release, yield, a press back in the view, a closed window); a throwing subscriber never stops the rest. Gate: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (the registry legs) + test-takeover-keyboard (the DOM-mini).

Its caller is session-lifecycle's `lateFocus(view)` (a window's focus on the server's answer); a throw answers `'take'`. Gate: test-session-title-ui's PURE table.

**Lane dialog-keys (the owner's "ok", 2026-09-30): the dialog half.** `createKeyboardYield({…, picture})` (the element the page's pointer is forwarded from). ### src/lib/live-bar-layout.js

**PURE (imports nothing, no DOM) — THE CHROME-BAR FOLD RULE** (lane I, 2026-09-25). `barLayout({widthPx, items:[{key, px, priority}], gapPx, overflowPx})` → `{shown, overflow, need, fits}`: `widthPx` = the bar's CONTENT width, `px` = an item's natural width (the ONE flexible item: its MINIMUM), an item with `px ≤ 0` is ABSENT (neither shown nor folded); nothing folds while everything fits (the exact boundary included); otherwise items fold by PRIORITY, never by position — 0 never folds, a higher number folds earlier, equal priorities right-to-left — until the rest fits; the ⋯ button's width + one gap is charged only while something is folded; never-fold items alone too wide ⇒ every foldable folded and `fits:false` (shown = exactly the never-fold items, the ⋯ charged after them — a bar that narrow CLIPS its right end, so a view must never be handed one); `shown` / `overflow` in DOM order; `floor` (verify r1) = the never-fold items + the ⋯ (charged when anything CAN fold) + gaps = `need` with everything foldable folded, INDEPENDENT of `widthPx` (a view raises its container to it without a feedback loop — the live view's split floor). Properties (test-live-bar-layout §2, 3000 seeded bars): fits unless the never-fold items alone overflow, MINIMAL (un-folding the last fold would not fit), MONOTONE (a wider bar never folds more), a bar at least as wide as its `floor` ALWAYS fits. `shortModeBadge({mode, mine})` = the bar's never-fold badge words (English keys through t(); both the live view and the desktop strip). Consumers: bar-fold.js (the DOM half) and the heavy census (node-imported).

**Lane toolbar-fold (2026-09-30) — GROUPS + THE ICON STEP.** `barLayout` takes optional `groups: [{key, gapPx}]` and `item.group`: the bar's children are the declared groups (flex boxes, each with its OWN gap between its items, the bar's gap between the groups — an EMPTY group still pays its two bar gaps) and the ⋯ is a direct child AFTER them (`more + gapPx` while anything folds); an item naming no declared group is charged as a direct child (its px + one bar gap). Without `groups` the arithmetic is exactly lane I's (`moreCost` = `more + (shown.length ? gap : 0)`). `barLadder({…, items:[{…, compactPx?}], groups?})` = barLayout with THE ICON STEP first: nothing is compact while the whole bar fits; otherwise the items with a shorter form (`compactPx` < `px`) give up their words ONE AT A TIME in the fold's own order (priority desc, ties right-to-left, never-fold items last) until nothing folds; only when every one is compact does barLayout fold — over the compact widths. Returns barLayout's verdict + `compact` (shown keys, DOM order) + `floor` over the all-compact widths. Properties (test-toolbar-fold §3, 3000 seeded grouped bars placed by an independent geometry walk): no overlap, inside the bar when `fits`, ONE ⋯ iff folded, DOM order, minimal + monotone compaction, nothing folds while a compactable item keeps its words, ≡ barLayout without compactPx.

### src/lib/bar-fold.js

**THE DOM HALF of the fold** (lane I). `createBarFold(bar, {items, more, moreAlways, signal, onLayout})` → `{schedule, layoutNow, measure, folded, last, dispose}`. `items()` = `[{key, el, priority, flexMin?}]` in DOM order; an item whose `style.display` is 'none' (its view says it is absent — a Hand back while the agent drives) or whose clone measures 0 (a media rule) takes no part. THE RULER: an offscreen, `visibility:hidden`, `aria-hidden` host (`.bar-ruler-host`) appended to the bar's PARENT (never a direct child of it, so no `parent > .x-bar` rule — e.g. the seamless strip's — reaches it) holding a div with the bar's own classes, so every `.x-bar > y` rule and the inherited font apply to a CLONE of the item; `offsetWidth + 1` (conservative rounding), cached per (class minus the fold class, text, children, inline style minus display) — a resize is arithmetic; the cache empties when `document.fonts.ready` resolves and at 400 entries. A ResizeObserver on the bar and a MutationObserver on its subtree (text, `style`, `class` — a class record that differs ONLY by `bar-folded` is our own toggle and is skipped, so a fold never re-triggers itself) schedule ONE layout per animation frame; a hidden bar (clientWidth 0 — another desktop, minimized) decides nothing. The fold is the CLASS `bar-folded` (`.browser-live-bar > .bar-folded, .desktop-bar > .bar-folded { display: none !important }`) — an independent layer over the views' own `style.display`. A ⋯ shown ANYWAY (`moreAlways()` — the xpra strip's Show window frame ▸ / Scale ▸) is charged as an always-present item at its DOM place (else barLayout charges it only while something folds — the first heavy run caught a ja strip whose Paste sat outside the bar). SELF-CHECK: an applied verdict that still overflows (`scrollWidth > clientWidth + 1`) drops the cache and re-runs ONCE. The AbortSignal (the window's `_listenerCtl`) disconnects both observers, cancels the frame and removes the ruler.

**Lane toolbar-fold (2026-09-30).** `createBarFold(bar, {…, groups, rulerIn, suspended})`: the verdict is `barLadder` (identical to barLayout when no item has a compact form). An item may carry `compactClass` (measured twice — full and with the class — and worn by the verdict's `compact` keys; the class joins FOLDED in the instance's `ownClasses`, stripped from cache keys and skipped by the MutationObserver like FOLDED), `live: true` (measured from its own rendered box `offsetWidth + 1`, never folded, never compact — the toolbar's usage / For-you / desktop-preview widgets whose `#toolbar #id` rules a clone without its id cannot carry) and `group` (passed with `groups()` to the rule). `rulerIn` hosts the ruler INSIDE another element (the toolbar passes the bar itself so `#toolbar …` rules and the toolbar's own zoom reach the clones); mutations inside the ruler host are never news (`!host.contains(r.target)`). `suspended()` true ⇒ every item unfolded and full, the ⋯ hidden, `onLayout({suspended:true, …})`. The cache key adds the descendant count (a custom grid added inside the layout presets changes no text). `compact()` beside `folded()`.

Every child of `.browser-live-bar` and `.desktop-bar` is `flex: 0 0 auto; white-space: nowrap` (the ONE flexible item: `.browser-live-bar > .browser-live-url` `flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 120px` with ellipsis; `.desktop-bar > .desktop-status` `flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 40px`; the one-time copy hint keeps its own shrink); the bars' text buttons are `.browser-live-bar > .file-tool-btn` / `.desktop-bar > .file-tool-btn` = `width: auto; height: 22px; padding: 0 8px; font-size: 10px` at (0,2,0), icon buttons `.bar-icon-btn`; the live bar clips (`overflow: hidden`, defense in depth — the census still sees an item painted outside). Never reorder the stylesheets (every other file-tool-btn would move). test-live-bar-layout §4 = the DERIVED census (every class co-occurring with file-tool-btn in src/lib × every single-class rule setting a property the icon rule sets) with a planted pre-fix rule as its control.

### src/lib/toolbar-fold-model.js

### src/lib/toolbar-fold.js

**THE TOP TOOLBAR'S FOLD — the DOM half** (lane toolbar-fold). `installToolbarFold(app)` (called at the end of app `_setupToolbar`, AFTER the arrangement is applied; `app._toolbarFold` = the fold handle) creates the ⋯ (`#toolbar-more.icon-btn.toolbar-more`, `UI_ICONS.more`, t('More'), `aria-haspopup=menu`) as a DIRECT CHILD of `#toolbar` after the zones — never a zone child, so Customize's `applyArrangement` never moves it — and drives `createBarFold(#toolbar, {more, rulerIn: bar, groups: the three zones (.toolbar-left / [data-zone=toolbar-center] / [data-zone=toolbar-right]) with their computed column gaps, items: every zone child in the ARRANGED order at every layout (an id-less element counted as `<zone>#n`, rigid), suspended: app._customize.active})`. `onLayout`: every `.toolbar-action` names itself (`nameCompact`: compact ⇒ `aria-label` = its words, `title` = compactTitle(words, its own title stored once in `data-tb-title`); full ⇒ both restored); the title's `data-squeezed` (visibility hidden) when narrower than TITLE_MIN_PX — a DATA attribute, never a class, so the fold's observer is not woken; elements of the table Customize moved OUT of the toolbar shed `bar-folded` / `tb-compact`; while suspended the Customize alignment chip is re-placed (the unfolded bar may have wrapped). ### src/lib/chain-layout.js

**PURE (imports only the shared colour sequence; CJS so the fast suite
requires it and the bundle carries it) — THE TAB CHAIN'S LAYOUT** (agent
browser P7, 2026-09-21; design §4.6 / §3.7, D19 / D24). A chain
`{ tabs, active }` gains `layout: 'tabs' | 'split'` (a MISSING field reads
as 'tabs' — old records need no migration) and `split: { pair, ratio, dir }`
while `tabs` and `active` keep their meanings to the byte. Invariants, one
each: `normalizeChain` mutates IN PLACE (the chain is shared by reference
across its windows) and is the ONE validation of `split` against `tabs` — a
pair member not in `tabs`, a duplicated id, or a split without a record
collapses the layout to tabs and DROPS split (never a dangling id, never a
substitute); `clampRatio` = [0.15, 0.85], junk → 0.5; `chainSyncKey` = tabs +
layout + pair ORDER, the ratio deliberately NOT in it (a divider drag is applied
in place through `ratioDiffers`; a rebuild would re-parent two live views);
`displayedPanes(chain, {narrow})` = the pair on a wide layout, the focused pane
alone on a NARROW one — the phone renders tabs and the model is untouched;
`splitAnchor` = the chain host when it is in the pair, else the left member,
and `splitReplaceable` = the other one (D19 (a): a third tab replaces the
non-anchor pane); `pairFor` orders the pair by the side the CALLER's verb
names (never a pointer position); `splitColumns(ratio, mins?)` is the ONE spelling of the
host's grid columns — lane I verify r1 (2026-09-25): `mins` = the panes' OWN floors
[left, right] (layout px) become the tracks' minimums (`minmax(<floor>px, …fr)`; no floor =
`minmax(0, …)`, the old spelling byte for byte), `paneMinPx` rounds up and caps at
`SPLIT_PANE_MIN_MAX` (320 − the divider: a host at the window floor still holds a pane at
its floor), junk / ≤ 0 = none; the RATIO is untouched (the user's intent); **split UX (2026-09-23, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md):
`dropSide` is GONE** (the title-bar half decided the side — the owner dragged
left and landed right) and three PURE helpers replace it: `visualTabOrder`
= the strip as SHOWN, [left pane, right pane, …the rest in chain order] (a
tabs chain / an invalid split keeps the chain order; a rendering, `tabs`
never changes); `swappedPair` = the valid pair reversed (Swap left and right

**SPLIT TABS v2 (2026-09-25, inc-muhfb5al-jzk6, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md §8 — the owner: the tabs all sat on the
left, no drag reorder, only the right side switchable).** `tabs` keeps its meaning (membership; `tabs[0]` = the host —
a reorder NEVER re-hosts) and the chain gains `order` (the strip order; missing ⇒ `tabs` order). In a split EVERY tab
belongs to a SIDE: `split.left` / `split.right` ordered, union = `tabs`, each id once, `pair[0] ∈ left`,
`pair[1] ∈ right`, `order = left ++ right` (unsplit keeps "left then right" by construction). `normalizeChain` stays
the ONE validation — a pair member on the wrong side or an EMPTY side collapses to tabs (the validator never guesses; the
VERBS pick the substitute first) — and repairs a pre-v2 record by ONE rule (`sidesFor`: the non-anchor pane alone on its
side, every other tab with the anchor; a member in neither list joins the anchor's side). PURE verbs, each in place and
ending in normalize: `showTab` (shown on ITS OWN side — `splitReplaceable` / D19 (a) RETIRED), `enterSplit` (the guest
alone on `side`, the rest with the anchor; on a chain ALREADY split the anchor keeps its side and the guest goes to the
OTHER one — "beside the source" never covers it), `insertTab` (`afterId` = on that tab's side; a split defaults to the
RIGHT), `moveTab` (a reorder; across the boundary a DISPLAYED tab carries its display and the side it left shows its

window), `swapSides`; readers `sidesOf` / `sideOf` / `visualTabOrder` (= the normalized clone's order) / `cloneChain`.
`chainSyncKey` = members | order | layout | the side cut + pair, over a normalized CLONE (an old record keys like its
repair; `active` / `recent` / the ratio never). `splitPartner` falls back along the STRIP order. Gate:

**window.js — `revealWindow(id, {replay, raise})` = THE ONE DOOR FOR "THE USER NAMED THIS WINDOW" (inc-muiq348r-jwb5, 2026-09-26):** **It goes to the window's DESKTOP first (inc-muv3qfo7-96tm, 2026-10-05):** PURE `revealDesktop` (view-visibility.js) over the frame's desktop + this client's DesktopManager / Stage ⇒ `dm.switchTo` (or `stage.enter()`), then the door runs again; a switch that did not land toasts where the window is; `raise:false` never switches (test-window-reveal-desktop, §62c). `focusWindow` raises a FRAME — for a tab group's HOST it never switched the group's tab (only a guest's focus did), so every door that named a host whose group showed a guest changed nothing on screen while the title and the highlight said it did (on the phone the tabs group has no title bar, so no strip either: no path to the host at all). `revealWindow`: PURE `revealTab` → `switchTab(ch, i)` (the tab click's own path: `active` persists through captureState and broadcasts in the layout save, `chainSyncKey` excludes it so another live client keeps its own tab, the §6b guards untouched; `_followPartner` is null ≤768 px, so the phone never drags a partner pane) → a minimized group restored (by the HOST's flag) → `focusWindow` (on an active stage a member is focused as its HOST — the stage materializes frames). `replay: true` = a machine path (a layout replay, boot restore, remote apply, a `syncId` open that found the window) — only `focusWindow`, as before (the record's `active` decides; a replay no longer restores a minimized singleton — only a user's own restore changes shared state); `raise: false` = choose the tab only (find on another desktop). `focusWindow` itself is unchanged (its two `activeWindowId = id; syncHiddenViews(); _notify()` lines stay pinned). The doors: mobile-nav's rows, taskbar `activateWindow` / the grouped chooser / the window list, the overlap switcher, app `goToWinId` / `flashWindow` / `moveSessionWindow` / `_focusOpenInChain`, session-lifecycle `_focusExistingSession` (+ `attachSession({machine})` from layout.js's four restore sites) and the tmux view, fifteen singleton re-opens + the workflow agent-log dedupe, chat-view's two sub-agent viewer dedupes, browser-live-window's fold-back. **`_focusFromPointer` asks PURE `pressTab`** for ANY chain host (was: a split only): a press keeps the tab on show and names it (in a tabs group the shown guest, whose content lives in this element; a split's pane under the pointer; the title bar's own area the focused pane). Census: test-architecture §62 — every `.focusWindow(` / `wm.restore(` in src/lib is a listed RAISE-ONLY site with its reason (pointer, machine, the door's internals), every door counted; a new bare focus anywhere is red.

**window.js — `requestClose(id)` (round 3 A2, 2.369.166):** THE ONE veto point for a USER'S close — the title-bar ✕ (since B-a67c through tab-group.js `requestCloseGroup`, which is `requestClose` for a lone window and asks before a group's members each pass here), a tab ✕ (tab-group.js asks `tabWin.onCloseRequest` before `removeFromTabChain`), the taskbar menu's `window.close`, Ctrl+\\ x (`activeWindow.close`), the phone nav's ✕ and its switcher rows. `winInfo.onCloseRequest()` returning false keeps the window (a desktop-app window asks its APP to close first); a throw closes (logged). Programmatic closes — layout sync, desktops, the stage, a window closing itself — call `closeWindow` and are never vetoed. Pinned by test-desktop-apps §12.

**tab-group.js — `requestCloseGroup(id)` + `confirmCloseGroup({names})` — A WHOLE TAB GROUP CLOSES ONLY AFTER A QUESTION (B-a67c, 2026-10-02; the owner: "当窗口是tabbed或者side by side的时候，注意点击整体的关闭要有个警告提示确认要关闭x个标签页吗，避免想关闭tab但点错").** Found by the census: before it NO door closed a whole group — the frame's ✕ (`requestClose(hostId)` → `closeWindow` → `removeFromTabChain`) and the taskbar group's "Close group" (`window.close` on the host) both ended only tabs[0], the HOST, usually not the tab on show (the heavy control reproduces it: C on show, ✕ ⇒ A gone, B + C stay). Now the THREE group doors — window.js `.win-close` (the frame's ✕), the frame's own title-bar menu (window.js passes `group: true` + "Close group" when the window heads a chain of ≥ 2; a tab's own menu never does) and the taskbar group button's menu (`group: true`) — reach `requestCloseGroup`; the window menu's `window.close` routes `ctx.group` there (`showWindowContextMenu` carries `group` into the ctx). It asks PURE chain-layout `closeAsks({scope, members, user})` (asks iff a person ends a group of ≥ 2) and names the members through `groupCloseList(chain, titleOf, exists)` (strip order — a split's left half then its right — and the tab labels); a lone window (no chain / a chain of one) is `requestClose`, synchronously, never asked. The question = `showConfirmDialog({title: 'Close {n} tabs?', items: names, confirmText: 'Close {n} tabs', danger})` — utils.js gained `items` (text `<li>` rows in `.dialog-list`, 40vh scroll; Enter = confirm, Esc / Cancel / the backdrop = keep). The confirm closes exactly the NAMED tabs still in the chain, each through `requestClose` (a member's veto stands — a desktop app asks its app), guests first and the host last; one question per chain (a module WeakMap — a second door while it is open shares the promise); a question that throws or rejects is a Cancel. Every other user close ends ONE window and never asks: a tab ✕ / a tab's menu / a chooser row / a window-list row / a single taskbar button / Ctrl+\\ x / the phone nav ✕ and its rows / Esc in properties. Programmatic closes (layout replay, desktop records, the Stage, sessions ended elsewhere) call `closeWindow` and never ask. No setting, no "don't ask again". Gates: scripts/test-tab-close-confirm.mjs (fast: the 112-row closeAsks table + groupCloseList; the REAL requestCloseGroup body over a fake WM, 12 rows; THE DOOR CENSUS over comment-stripped src/lib — a close verb inside a loop over a chain's members exists only in the gate, after the question; every requestClose / requestCloseGroup / showWindowContextMenu call is one of 17 classified rows with its scope; patched-copy controls: a verdict that asks a lone window / a programmatic close, a helper that closes on Cancel / closes the live chain / asks twice, a planted close-all loop, the frame ✕ back on requestClose) and heavy scripts/test-tab-close-confirm-ui.mjs (real clicks on a scratch copy: tabs, a tab ✕, side by side, both menus, a lone ✕, a programmatic close; CONTROL = the pre-fix ✕ rebuilt into the scratch bundle).


**tab-group.js — `_notifyChainChange(ids)` (round 3 lane B, 2.369.177):** every `_renderTabBar(chain)` and both places a window LEAVES a chain (`_tabChain = null` in the removal and in `_ungroupLast`) call `winInfo.onChainChanged` (a microtask later, a throw logged) — a seamless desktop-app window pauses in a chain because the tab bar lives in the title bar it would fold (docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.3). Gate: test-desktop-seamless §5 (pin) + test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (7).

**tab-group.js — the inbox chip's number (2.369.179, lane G, 2026-09-25):** `_inboxBadgeEl` writes the count through PURE `inboxCountText` (title-chips.js — never wider than "99+"; the aria-label/title keep the real count) and the chip is `flex: none` with a tighter padding on a tab (style.css) — the number stays, at its minimal width, so the title keeps the room. The billing chip beside it is re-applied after every `_renderTabBar` (the microtask `setAuthBadge` loop) and re-decided per tab by window.js `_fitChipsOf` (THE TITLE WINS — see window.js below). Gate: test-title-chips §4 + test-user-todos-layout (the count is TEXT).
**tab-group.js — `setPaneMinWidth(id, px)` + `_paneMins(split)` (lane I verify r1, 2026-09-25):** a window's OWN floor as a split PANE (`winInfo.paneMinWidth`, declared in window.js createWindow; layout px, null clears; LOCAL to the client — never persisted, every client's view measures its own). Every write of the host's grid columns (`_applyChainLayout`, `setSplitRatio`, `setPaneMinWidth` — the binding-model suite counts them) passes the pair's floors to `splitColumns`, so the track never renders the pane narrower; the divider drag keeps computing its ratio from `clientX` (the cursor may overshoot, the divider stops — the window resize drag's rule) and the partner pane takes the rest. `setPaneMinWidth` re-spells the grid only while the window IS a pane of a split (a tab / a free window just keeps the value for the next split) and resizes the panes a frame later. The phone layout ignores the grid (`display: flex !important`). The one caller today: the live view (its bar's floor). Gates: test-window-binding-model ①③, test-browser-live-ui ⑥.
**tab-group.js — `restoreTabChain` notifies (lane K verify r1 low ①, 2026-09-25):** it ends with `this._notify()` like every other chain mutation, so the taskbar re-derives at once — a reload used to show a restored group as separate single buttons until the first window event (layout.js's chain restore never calls `updateTaskbar`), and the first click after a reload landed on a single button, not the group. Silent inside a restore batch (`wm._restoring`); the autosave it schedules is gated by the layout manager's own restore / anti-echo guards. Gate: test-taskbar-group §7 (pin) + test-taskbar-group-ui (n) with CONTROL 2 (the call reverted ⇒ SSS).

**tab-group.js.** A split is another RENDERING of the same chain: the host's
element becomes a grid (title bar across, pane / divider / pane below) and the
pair's `content` elements both lose `.tab-hidden` — no re-parenting, no
second container, the window's EXTERNAL geometry is untouched (gridBounds /
snap / minimise / desktop moves keep working because they act on the host).
`_normalizeChain` runs at EVERY chain mutation (create / add / detach /
restore / switch / bind / unbind) and `_applyChainLayout` re-derives every
pane's display + the host columns + the divider after it (idempotent; it also
calls syncHiddenViews because a pane's display changed). Three exit paths, one
decision: closing the browser pane, closing the CHAT (host promotion) and
dragging either pane out all reach `_detachFromChain` → `_normalizeChain` ⇒
the layout collapses to tabs and nothing else moves. `_clearSplitDom` strips
the marks off whoever leaves and off an old host. The divider drag follows the
three laws: a PER-DRAG AbortController, rAF-coalesced moves, ONE kind of pixel
(the host's bounding rect and `clientX` are both viewport px — `clientWidth`
and `uiScale` never enter, so the ratio lands where the pointer is under any
body zoom); double-click = 0.5; pointer capture so a pane's iframe cannot eat
the moves. `bindSplit(anchor, guest, {side})` puts both in ONE chain (the
anchor's wins), `unbindSplit` returns to tabs with nothing leaving.
`switchTab` on a third tab replaces the non-anchor pane in place (D19 (a)).
**EXPLICIT ENTRY, NO DRAG ZONE (split UX chunk 1, 2026-09-23 —
docs/design-split-ux.zh.md, the owner: "I wanted to drag the window to the
left and it went side by side"):** the P7 `_detectSplitDropTarget` (the
left / right half of another window's title bar = 80 % of it, no dwell, no
modifier, evaluated every drag frame and checked BEFORE snap on drop, so it
shadowed an edge snap and picked the side by the TARGET bar's half) is
DELETED with `_markSplitDrop`, `.tab-split-drop-*` and both drop branches;
no body zone replaces it. A window / tab drag = move / snap / grid, and the
tab MERGE is the one drag exception. The three USER merge drops (icon drag
onUp, tab-drag merge branch, title-bar-drag merge branch) each call
`_afterUserMerge(chain)` exactly once — the bridge to the second step: the
strip's button pulses once (`chain._pulseUntil` survives a re-render; the
keyframe is off under prefers-reduced-motion) and `showToast('Grouped as
tabs', {action: 'Show side by side'})` kept as `chain._mergeToast` — every
`bindSplit` on that chain withdraws it (`_withdrawMergeToast`: the offer is
taken, whichever entry took it), and if its action still runs after the
group changed it SAYS so ('Already shown side by side' / 'The tab group
changed — nothing to show side by side'), never a silent no-op (split r1);
restore / remote sync /
`createWindow({intoChain})` never call it (nothing the user did), and the
phone (≤768px) is skipped. The ONE `.tab-split-btn` (UI_ICONS.columns,
inserted after `.tab-bar-tabs`, before the controls; mousedown / dblclick
stop so it is never a drag handle nor a maximize; window.js's title-bar
mousedown excludes it) has two states: tabs ⇒ `splitActive(chain,
{announce:true})` = the ACTIVE tab left, PURE `splitPartner` right, focus
kept — its title/aria-label come from `_labelSplitBtn(chain, btn)`, which
`switchTab` re-runs after it moves `chain.recent` (split r1: a label computed
once at render named the partner BEFORE the switch, on a ≥3-tab chain not
the one the click used); split ⇒ `.on` + `aria-pressed` and a menu Unsplit / Swap left and
right (`unbindSplit` / `swapSplit`; the divider's right-click opens the same
`_showSplitMenu`). A ResizeObserver hides it on a title bar < 260 px
(`.split-btn-hidden`); ≤768px the stylesheet hides it and the glyph.
`bindSplit(anchor, guest, {side, announce, focus})`: `focus:'anchor'` keeps
the focus on the window the user ACTED ON and every user verb passes it (the
button's `splitActive`, the window menu's "Beside {name}", command mode's
`chain.splitBeside`; split r1 — the menu used to land the focus on the NAMED
partner); the default 'guest' is the programmatic `intoChain` bind's and the
live view's Snap beside (its guest is the acted-on window). `announce` snapshots
BEFORE the mutation `{guestWasFree, guestRect, hostRect (style l/t/w/h/z +
gridBounds of the element that SHOWS each), chainBefore{layout, split,
activeId}}` and toasts 'Side by side: {left} | {right}' with Undo (5 s);
`undoSplit` acts only while the chain is the same object, still split, the
same pair, both windows alive and in it — a free guest is detached and both
rects put back, a tab guest gets the chain's previous layout back (nothing
moves); otherwise it SAYS 'Nothing to undo any more — the group changed'.
`_renderTabBar` draws PURE `visualTabOrder` — [left pane, `.tab-split-glyph`
(aria-hidden paint), right pane, …] — each pane tab `.tab-pane` (+ the old
`.split-member`) with `--pane-color` from `_paneColorOf` (badge dot ⇒ the
session's `ownerColor` ⇒ `ownerColor(win.id)`) as a 2 px underline, the
active pane `.tab-split-focus`; because the strip is no longer in chain
order, `switchTab` marks tabs by `dataset.winId` and window.js's tab-bar
merge maps the strip neighbour back to its CHAIN index by id. `switchTab`
also maintains `chain.recent`. Right-click on a tab opens THAT tab's own
window menu (it used to open the host's). A window's `_ownerBadge` renders on
its tab (the guest's own title bar is hidden). **window.js.** `createWindow({… intoChain: {hostId,
split, side}})` = BORN IN THE CHAIN: `display:none` from the first byte so the
window is never painted standalone (no jump, no created-then-merged autosave
churn), then bound/added before the trailing focus. `syncHiddenViews` derives
the narrow-split hider from PURE `displayedPanes(chain, {narrow:true})` —
every hider suspends (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq). `setOwnerBadge(id, {dots})` draws
the ownership badge after the title span (setTitle wipes the span's children)
and re-renders the tab bar when grouped. **2.369.169 (design-user-inbox-reply
§3) its twin `setInboxBadge(id, {count, urgency})`**: `win._inboxBadge` (null
at 0), keyed `count:urgency`; `_placeInboxBadge(win)` puts the standalone
`.win-inbox-badge` after the title span — none while grouped, none at 0,
rebuilt only on a key change; grouped ⇒ `_renderTabBar` purges every chain
member's standalone badge and draws `_inboxBadgeEl` on each window's tab
(tab-group.js, beside the owner badge), and `_detachFromChain` /
`_ungroupLast` call `_placeInboxBadge` so a window that leaves the chain gets
its own badge back at once. The element is a `<button>`: `UI_ICONS.inbox`
(aria-hidden, icons.js) + the count as textContent, `data-urgency` colours it,
`aria-label` = title = "{n} items from this agent" (never the session name);
its mousedown/dblclick stop there (the title-bar drag, focus and maximize and
the For-you panel's outside closer never see them), the click calls
`app.openMiniInbox(el, winId)` (user-todos-panel.js). **layout.js.** captureState persists
`layout` + `split` through the ONE writeLayouts choke point; both restore
sites hand them to `restoreTabChain`; the remote-vs-local chain key is
`chainSyncKey` (the pre-fix `tabs.join(',')` did not carry the layout — a
remote tabs→split flip of the same tabs read as "unchanged", a silent fork) and
a remote ratio on a structural match is applied in place with no notify. The
four §6b anti-ping-pong guards are untouched and pinned. **Mobile.** ≤768px
the stylesheet shows only the focused pane (`.tab-split-focus`) and hides the
divider; the model keeps the split, so a phone's save carries it verbatim and
never flattens the desktop's layout (§6b guard 5's class). Gates:
test-window-binding-model (fast, 96 — the drop-zone pins FLIPPED to negative
ones: zero hits of the zone in tab-group/window/style, no drag body calls
bindSplit, exactly one `_afterUserMerge` per user merge drop and none on the
restore / sync paths) + test-window-binding (heavy chrome, 63;
its teardown kills the fake sessions it created — a dtach'd fake claude
outlives the server otherwise) + test-hidden-view-suspend (the switchTab
re-derive pin).


**THE ONE RETIREMENT + THE HELD CLOSE (inc-mukeyzpt-lpou, 2026-09-27).** window.js `_retireWindow(id, {held})` = every register that can bring a window back forgets it in the same tick as its removal: `stage.onWindowClosed`, `desktopManager.purgeClosedWindow` (every cached desktop record — switchTo's merge-preserve cannot tell closed from not-yet-materialized), `layoutManager.noteClosed`. Both terminal deletions run it: `closeWindow`'s free branch (a record-only id: `held: false`) and tab-group.js `removeFromTabChain` (before `_detachFromChain`). The tab ✕ is `this.requestClose(tabWinId)` — the ONE user-close door (the pre-fix handler duplicated the veto and called removeFromTabChain directly, skipping the purge: the owner's closed viewer was replayed with its old id on the next desktop round trip). layout.js: `noteClosed(id, desk)` holds a LOCAL close made while the user is active (not under `_restoring`; an idle client's programmatic close is not held — it would never be sent), `_closeHeld(id)` (≤ `CLOSE_HOLD_MS` 60 s, void once a window with that id exists again), `_releaseHeldCloses(desk)` at every save that leaves (the `_doAutoSave` line beside `_releaseHeldRatios`, desktop-manager `_broadcastDesktopState`), `_resendHeldClose()` (the `_resendHeldRatio` shape: dirty re-set with the close's real time); `_applyRemoteState` computes `heldIds` once, never `_createRemoteWindow`s one, reads chain records through `withoutMembers(rw.tabChain, heldIds)` and re-sends once after the 1 s gate. Gates: test-window-binding-model ⑥ (the comment-aware census of window-ending deletes + control, the wiring pins), test-desktop-apps (the tab ✕ user-close pin), heavy test-split-close-resurrect.

**A REMOTE TEAR-OFF LANDS WHERE THE RECORD SAYS (stage-blank verify r4, 2026-09-30; layout.js).** `_applyRemoteState` applies the record's boxes in its windows loop and only then breaks a local chain the record no longer holds — and tab-group's `_detachFromChain` copies the HOST's box onto each leaving guest (a tear-off drops the tab beside its frame), so a tab torn off and dropped at X on another device stood on its old host here and this page's next save wrote it back there for every client. Now the broken chain's members go back to the RECORD's boxes after the break (`recorded` = the record's row per window id; a member on the Stage excepted). Gates: heavy test-stage-dragout-ui § 7 (the real function on a real page), test-window-binding-model's layout.js pin.

**THE HELD CHAIN ACT (stage-blank verify r5, 2026-09-30; layout.js + tab-group.js — found on the merged tree with lane desktop-move, pre-existing on master).** The held close and the held ratio witness a close and a divider drag; desktop-move's `_boundsAt` witnesses a window's box; nothing witnessed a CHAIN act. A tab torn off with a real drag while another page's record (still naming the group) was deferred under the pointer, or landed in the 500 ms before the tear's save left, was put back into the group by `_applyRemoteState`'s "create remote chains not present locally" (`restoreTabChain` → the guest's box = the host's) — the drop point lost, this page's next save carrying the re-formed group to every client (measured on two pages: `_detachFromChain` at 173 ms, the tear's own save at 675 ms with the button still down, the deferred record applied at 1742 ms ⇒ the group back). Now tab-group's `_noteChainAct(ids)` — the tear-off right after the detach, the ONE merge-drop body `_mergeDrop`, `moveTabInChain` / `bindSplit` / `unbindSplit` / `swapSplit` / `undoSplit`; never `restoreTabChain` / `applyChainRecord` / `_detachFromChain` / `createTabChain` / `addToTabChain` / `removeFromTabChain` / `_ungroupLast` — tells layout.js `noteChainAct(ids, desktopId)`, refused under an apply / the boot (`this._applying ?? this._restoring` — desktop-move's `_applying` once merged — and `_booting`) and for an idle user (`_lastUserInputAt` past CLOSE_HOLD_MS), keyed per window (`_heldChainActs`). `_applyRemoteState` asks `_heldChainIds(state)` first: a held window's entry is skipped whole (its box in the record is its OLD frame's) and the three chain sites (the in-place apply, the break, the create) skip a chain naming a held window; `heldClosed` then re-sends the act once through `_resendHeldClose` (a held chain act rides it at its real time). RELEASED BY AGREEMENT, never by the save: a record whose `chainSyncKey` for the window (`_recordChainOf`: the host row's tabChain) equals this page's (alone = '') releases it — a hold released at the save would have let the deferred record through, and membership alone let a stale strip order through (the key judges members, order, layout and sides, as the in-place path does); expired after CLOSE_HOLD_MS, void once the window is gone. The no-op guard ends any echo between two pages each holding its own act. Gates: test-window-binding-model ⑦ (in process over the real classes, the door census, two RED controls), heavy test-stage-dragout-ui § 8. **A SAVE WAITS FOR THE DROP (verify r5 ⑤):** `_doAutoSave` under `_pointerDown` re-arms itself every 300 ms and, once the pointer is up — or within 400 ms of a drop the tab drag's handler stamped (`noteDrop` → `_dropAt`: a release just before the debounce fired) — waits 400 ms more (`_saveWaitsForDrop`) before capturing — a tab torn off and held past the 500 ms debounce used to go out standing on its old host's box (the detach copies the host's box; the drop's capture runs 250 ms after the release), and another page's save from that moment handed the box back. The dirty bit and `_lastUserInputAt` are untouched (§6b guard 2 keeps its meaning). Gates: test-window-binding-model ⑧ (+ control), test-stage-dragout-ui § 8 (a).

### scripts/cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs

THE CDP PROTOCOL FIXTURE WRITER (verify S2 r4, 2026-09-27; NOT a test-*.mjs, no tier — the browser-flag-census.mjs shape): launches ONE scratch headless Chrome (a scratch.mjs root, the process group ended, the root removed), reads its `GET /json/protocol` + `/json/version`, writes the NAMES-ONLY listing (domains → commands, deprecated / experimental flags; parameter schemas dropped — the census classes METHODS, a 690 KB fixture would carry nothing the leg reads) to scripts/fixtures/cdp-protocol-<chrome version>/protocol.json and prints `{chrome, protocol, domains, methods, file}`. Exports `namesOnly` / `fetchLiveProtocol` / `chromeVersionOf`. Re-run after a Chrome upgrade, bump `CENSUS_CHROME` in src/cdp-census.js, then class every method test-browser-mediation ⑥ prints.

**2026-09-28 (lane-cdp-154).** The listing also carries each command's parameter NAMES (`params: ['url', 'referrer?']` — an optional one ends in `?`; never a type, schema or description) and each domain's `events` (name, flags, `params`): the 153 fixture had neither, so the 153 → 154 parameter / event changes could not be read off it (measured instead against Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12). PURE `diffListings(older, newer)` → `{domains, methods: {added, removed, reflagged}, params: {changed}|null, events: {added, removed, changed}|null, unrecorded}` — a side that never recorded parameters / events makes that part `null` and says so in `unrecorded` (never "nothing changed"); a live /json/protocol is read the same way. CLI: `--diff <old> <new>` (two fixtures), `--scratch-name <name>` (the scratch root's name, default `cdp-protocol`). `fetchLiveProtocol` now truly never throws: a binary that cannot be spawned (ENOENT) was an unheard 'error' EVENT — the process crashed and left its scratch root; now `{ok:false, error:'could not start …'}` and the root removed. A new Chrome now appends to CENSUS_CHROMES (src/cdp-census.js) — never replaces.

THE TAKEOVER ANCHOR'S GRACE, MEASURED (verify S2 r4; NOT a test-*.mjs): the real agent-browser + a real headless Chrome + the real mediator + the real live-view bridge, a RECORDING proxy between the mediator and Chrome stamping every CDP call of the daemon, N alternating `tab t2` / `tab t1` switches — per switch the latency from the CLI's invocation / the daemon's first call / `Page.bringToFront` / `Target.setAutoAttach` / `Page.startScreencast` to the `tabs` record at the bridge, p50 / p90 / p99 / max; then a takeover with the user's key + mouse and the agent's paused verbs, and the daemon's CDP method INVENTORY per phase with each method's census class (the evidence that nothing the stream server issues for the user's own view is a paused class — the user's `Input.*` rides the credit). `WT=<checkout> node scripts/measure-anchor-grace.mjs [N=100] [out.json]`; zero vendor calls, scratch only. 2026-09-27, 2 × 100 on 0.38.1 + Chrome 153.0.8010.47: CLI→record p99 15.37 / 20.37 ms ⇒ `TAKEOVER_ANCHOR_GRACE_MS` = ⌈3 × 20.37⌉ = 62 (src/browser-stream.js).

### scripts/browser-flag-census.mjs

THE BROWSER CLI'S GLOBAL FLAGS, MEASURED (browser takeover r3; NOT a test-*.mjs, so no tier). `flagCandidates(buf)` = every flag-shaped string in the binary's bytes (split at `--` boundaries — the Rust string pool concatenates them — plus each `-`-prefix, plus `-<letter>`); `measureGlobalFlags(bin, {dir, env})` runs each launch-free as `<flag> zzq9 session list` under a scratch HOME / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR / TMPDIR with every inherited `AGENT_BROWSER_*` stripped (a session shell's AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG would make each probe read that config): the list answers ⇒ value, `Unknown command: zzq9` ⇒ boolean, `Unknown command: <flag>` ⇒ not global, else `other` (--config checks its file first; --help / --version print). ~0.5 s for 792 strings. `node scripts/browser-flag-census.mjs [<bin>] --write <fixture>` records it; test-browser-verbs holds `VALUE_FLAGS`/`BOOL_FLAGS` EQUAL to the checked-in 0.32.0 fixture and test-browser-mediation-chrome re-measures the installed binary.

**r4 (2.369.168):** `censusArgs(argv, {PATH, exists, isShim, shimDirs})` = the command line: the positional binary in either order around `--write <f>` (r3 dropped index 0 without `--write`), a bare name resolved on PATH by `resolveRealBinary` past the shim (r3 realpath'd it against the cwd ⇒ ENOENT); no binary ⇒ exit 2 with a sentence. test-browser-verbs runs the CLI mode against a fake binary in both orders and through PATH.

### data/bin/agent-browser

**THE SHIM (STATIC tracked, in AGENT_TOOLS; design-browser-takeover §4 T2, owner 2026-09-24 "从系统 path 隐藏 agent-browser … 不要兼容").** `#!/usr/bin/env node`; its first comment line carries `VIBESPACE-AGENT-BROWSER-SHIM` (resolvers skip it by content). Prints ONE stderr line `agent-browser is driven by VibeSpace here — run: vibespace-browser <argv shell-quoted>` (no args ⇒ `… vibespace-browser help`) and exits 2 — never forwards, reads no env, opens no network, spawns nothing. It must say the name it hides (the one exception to §52b). Local: `AGENT_BIN_DIR` is first on an integrated session's PATH (ws-create), so it shadows the nvm/npm-global binary; Integration OFF ⇒ no data/bin on PATH ⇒ no shim (VibeSpace manages nothing there). Remote: shipped to `~/.vibespace/bin` (every ship path chmods it by name — it does not match the `vibespace-*` glob) and kept first by the prelude order `REMOTE_PRELUDE → nodeFinder → tools`. Honest: an absolute path bypasses it (single uid; the four `AGENT_BROWSER_*` pairs, D1, make such an escape land in the same watched browser). A pre-update session sees it on its next call (data/bin is the same directory). Gates: test-browser-verbs ②, test-remote-shell's real-`sh` leg, test-architecture §52a.

the row; `use --print` WITHHOLDS the `AGENT_BROWSER_CDP` pair of a reached
browser and says so (§5.1: `use` never prints a CDP url — the subshell and the
`--` form carry it without printing it). Gate: test-browser-providers ⑤.

STATIC tracked, in `AGENT_TOOLS`; auth `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN`. `use` execs
a subshell with the attached env (`--print` prints the exports) and NEVER a
CDP url; `-- <args>` runs `agent-browser` against the attached profile with
this session's flags, adds `--pin-tab` when the server says the floor is met,
refuses `close --all` while another session is attached, and drops the lease
after a `close`; every answer names the profile it acted on (§3.8 layer ①).
**P1 second half (§3.7):** `--profile <handle>` (anywhere, taken OFF the argv
the wrapped CLI sees) or `VIBESPACE_BROWSER=<handle>` names ONE attachment;
with two or more a bare `--` command is refused `profile_required` listing
every handle and the default, a filesystem path is refused
`profile_path_refused` with the `new <label> --adopt <dir>` remedy, a set the
USER changed refuses the next command ONCE with `profile_changed` (was → now)
— all printed with their codes; `use <ref> --alias <h>`, `new-child` (prints
the child's env), `status` (the set with handles, `*` the default, children),
`pin <handle|label|id>`; after every wrapped command ONE audit line is posted
(verb only). Gate: test-browser-handles.

**Lane H verify r2 (2026-09-25) — L6: `close --all` on an ATTACHMENT closes only its session.** The binary's `close --all` closes every session of the namespace — for a profile, the keeper's daemon and the one Chrome every lease shares (measured on 0.38.1: `{closed:2, sessions:[both]}`, the profile's daemon dead with ONE holder). In the attachment branch `close --all` sets `closeAllScoped`: the child argv drops `--all` (the session's own `close`), the post-exit detach drops the lease as for any `close`, and a note says so (`[close_all_scoped]`, naming how many others stay). The old `close_all_refused` (others > 0) is gone — subsumed. An ephemeral / child / shared session's `close --all` is unchanged. **L8:** `detach` while the user drives prints the server's `[browser_paused]` and exits 1. Gates: test-browser-pin ⑤ (+ a CLI copy passing `--all` through), test-browser-takeover ⑥, test-browser-ephemeral ④ L8.

**Lane H verify r3 (2026-09-25) — the post-`close` lease drop is said when it is refused.** After a `close` on an attachment the CLI drops the lease with its own request (`{soft: true}` now): a takeover that began while the binary ran answers `browser_paused`, and the CLI prints `note: your \`close\` ran, but your lease on "<label>" was NOT dropped — <server's words> [<code>]; run \`vibespace-browser detach\` after they hand it back` and exits non-zero (the command's own code when it failed, else 1). r2 had it in a bare `try { … } catch {}` — the non-soft `call`'s `process.exit(1)` still printed the server's refusal, but as a `detach` the agent never typed, never saying the close ran. Gate: test-browser-pin (the fake's `FAKE_CLOSE_HOLD` holds the close while the suite begins a takeover; control: a CLI copy with the r2 line).

**THE AGENT IS TOLD (the owner's ruling, 2026-09-27).** Every page verb's audit carries `since` = the SERVER's instant its `/resolve` answered (`r.at`, on the keeper's clock — a remote host's clock never compared) and, for a helper, its `handle`; an audit answering `interrupted` (a takeover began at or after it) ⇒ the tool prints `<THE sentence> [browser_interrupted]`, when, whether the user still drives or control is back, and cut (a mediated lease's calls were aborted) vs ran-to-its-end (no proxy, binary exit 0) — and exits 1 whatever the binary said; said AFTER a `close`'s own lease bookkeeping. `watch` and USAGE say a takeover INTERRUPTS and the handback names what to re-run. Gates: test-browser-verbs (the words), test-browser-takeover ⑥/⑧ (end to end), test-browser-pin (the close case).

**The owner's ruling (userW's fleet pod, a FRESH Google sign-in refused "This browser or app may not be secure"): the agent PROPOSES the switch, the user APPROVES with one click; D31 stands — nothing switches by itself.** A tier-2 `vibespace-browser blocked` claim files ONE proposal ON the keeper's claim record (`reg.blocked[i].proposal`, keeper `blocked`); the words = the card's claim + plan lines as i18n STRUCTURE; answered when the user decides, re-opened when a run fails) — and **runs** the user's Approve (`approve(id, {shown})`: the PURE step — actor `user`, state open|failed, `shown` === the digest — then ONE run per proposal): (a) the install when CloakBrowser does not answer (`install` dependency = the keeper's own runner: `installCloak` + `installProgress` — the log tail's last percent — + `cloakExecutable`; (c) the plan — `switch`: `keeper.switchBackend` by the user with `confirmDowngrade` = the plan's `confirm` (its gate still runs and refuses by name; a `mode:'proposal'` answer — somebody drives the browser — fails by name); `new-profile`: `createProfile({label, provider:'cloak'}, {owner: instance, createdBy: key})` → the conversation's PIN (routes/browser `pinAnswer(…, {by:'user', quiet:true})` — the approved message is its telling, `k.tell` updates the told fingerprint) → `attach` (CloakBrowser launches) → `keeper.openInLease` (the claim's page in THIS conversation's tab); (d) the agent TOLD — `browser-handback.tellProposal` (the ladder's ONE site with `noWake`: a running codex turn steered for free, else the ladder's stash for the next turn, else the zero-spend `browser-proposal` notice) — `approvedText` ("Approved: your browser is now CloakBrowser …; Re-run the sign-in at <url>"). A failure is the `fail` transition with its step + error (on the card, in the `browser-proposal-updated` broadcast the pressing client toasts); Approve again runs the same frozen fields. `reject(id)`; `rejectionFor({browserKey, host})` = the audit's once-only rejection line (`told`). The client card (`browser-proposal-card.js`: `renderProposalCard` / `patchProposalCard` — keyed children, textContent only, ONE primary Approve + a quiet Reject shown only while they work, "Approve again" after a failure, the state line = `proposalStateText`; `approveProposal` sends `shown`; `listenProposalUpdates` toasts a failure of a run THIS client started) is wired in chat-renderers `renderSystemMsg` (`noticeKind 'browser-proposal'`) and chat-view `_onEditMessage` (a `content`-only edit of a proposal card PATCHES, never swaps). The For-you row (user-todos-row `proposalAskHtml`: the plan lines ABOVE Approve / Reject, never folded — the exit-ask lesson), the panel (`.ut-action-proposal`, Approve armed like the exit ask's Allow — press-arm V1), the For-you window (`proposal-approve` / `proposal-reject` actions, the detail verbatim) and `user-todos-actions.runAction` answer through the same two routes. **What the card DRAWS is what runs:** the URL on the card, in the item and in the approved message is `SW.proposalUrlOf` — the agent's URL PARSED (ASCII by construction: a character that is not drawn or reorders a line is percent-encoded; a URL that does not parse reopens the site's root) and exactly the page `openInLease` opens; the keeper's `blocked` strips THE one hidden set (src/hidden-chars.js `HIDDEN_RE`) from the agent's `why` and `evidence` and from the conversation name that becomes the new profile's label. test-approval-census row `browser-proposal` claims the four doors (the item's action, the card's and the For-you model's two routes, the server's approve / reject) and pins (a) the digest the item and the card send, (b) `proposal_changed` + `shown_required`, (c) ACTION_IDENTITY `id`, the actor refusal, the bearer refusal and the popup's press-arm, (d) the parsed URL + the stripped words. **Verify r1 V2 (2026-09-30): THE CARD IS ITS CONVERSATION'S.** An Approve after the proposing conversation ended ran anyway: the switch plan switched the profile under the conversation now using it ("told: failed"), the new-profile plan fetched the 217 MB and added the site before failing. The runner now asks for the proposing conversation (`sessionFor`: its webui id, else its browser key — a resumed conversation keeps its key) BEFORE anything runs and again after the install (it takes minutes): gone ⇒ `session-gone` by name, nothing ran; resumed ⇒ Approve again runs the same frozen card. PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the keeper, the routes, the ORCH key consumer
AND the bundle share ONE spelling of every refusal) — **agent browser P4
second half (2026-09-17; design §7.4 / §7.5 / §7.6, D17 / D32–D34, round
8)**: the live backend switch and the key-consumer half as DECISIONS; nothing
here touches a file, a process or the network. One sentence per invariant:
the version ladder (`versionLadder`) answers BEFORE a byte moves, reading the
registry's `lastChromiumMajor` beside the directory's own `Last Version` and
taking the HIGHER when they disagree (refusing one legitimate downgrade is
cheaper than allowing one that destroys a profile), a lower target is
`downgrade_refused` naming both majors with two ways out (upgrade / clone
through export-import, saying what that drops — sessionStorage and
non-extractable CryptoKeys), and nothing recorded, or a target whose major is
not yet known, is `downgrade_unknown` — refused until ONE explicit human
confirmation; the fingerprint seed is minted ONCE (`seedForSwitch`, from crypto
bytes the keeper hands it, a positive 31-bit integer) and carried through
every later switch, never re-minted per launch, and `fingerprintChange` /
`fingerprintNote` word the dialog from the FACT (chromium→cloak GAINS a
fingerprint, the reverse LOSES one; cookies cross untouched either way);
seats are THREE STATES (`seatState`: known-fresh within `SEAT_TIER_STALE_MS`
= 7 d carrying the reading's age / known-stale saying what the LAST tier was
and constraining nothing / unknown = this key never launched), the total
comes from the FIRST REAL LAUNCH (`tierFromLaunch`; nothing recognisable ⇒
null, never a fabricated number) and never from Test or a poll, and an
UNKNOWN or STALE total never satisfies the ceiling test (`seatVerdict` refuses
only while known-and-fresh — `unknown` is neither 0 nor ∞); the ceiling
wording forks on key SOURCE (the user's own key: every seat is on this
instance, so the holders are NAMED and stopping one is offered; the cluster
default: this instance cannot see other users' browsers, so NO profile is
listed, the sentence says the seats are shared and `action.openIntegration`
is the way out — a refusal may only state what its own reason knows);
`classifyLaunchFailure` turns a licence/concurrency launch failure into
`backend_seat_taken` (the criterion is the family of words `SEAT_TAKEN_RE`
until §12.40 is measured — said in the comment, waiting to be narrowed), and
under a cluster default it says the seats are shared fleet-wide ("stop one of
yours" is the wrong advice); `KEY_ROWS` carries the six rows' VENDOR env names
(`vendorEnvFor` emits only the fields that carry a value; `VENDOR_ENV_NAMES`
all pass through `agentEnv` by rule — exactly why the cluster may inject ONLY
under the store's `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATION_*` prefix) and the per-row EGRESS rule
(`testHostFor`: a constant for browserbase/browseruse, the host INSIDE the
field the user typed for browserless/kernel, the region for agentcore, none
for cloak; a host it cannot derive is `host_underivable`, never "let us try
the default"; `testRequestFor` puts the key in a HEADER, never the URL, which
every error path logs); `launchArgsFor` = `--executable-path <p> --args
--fingerprint=<seed>` for cloak (the two shapes upstream supports) and `-p
<name>` for cloud — the key never rides argv; `siteHintVerdict` keys per-site
memory by EXACT host (never a registrable domain — that needs a public-suffix
list, a second source of truth that expires) with `by`/`at`/`why`, and `tier`
is legal ONLY while `backend === null` (`hint_tier_with_backend` — once a
backend is named the tier is derived, never stored twice, §7.6 rule 2);
`blockedClaim` is made by the agent of a conversation (a claim `by:'server'`
is refused; the record has no field for a detection) and `blockedText` says
WHO, never "detected"; `navHint(403|429)` is a typed HINT naming its source;
`switchVerdict` is THE GATE in this order and no other — the row exists →
not a no-op → the capability control for THIS machine (`backend_unavailable`
naming what is missing / `provider_needs_local_key` BEFORE `resolveKey` is
ever called, leg viii) → `canSwitchTo` of the target AND the current backend
(`switch_refused` for cdp / local-window, `switch_export_only` naming the

`action.openIntegration`) → the ladder → seats → direct vs PROPOSAL (a browser

agent's switch while another session holds a lease, or on a profile it does
not own, is a proposal naming the affected sessions); `switcherRows` = every

state and the chip; `backendChip` = `chromium 146` / `cloak 146 (free)` /
`cdp`; `restartingRefusal` = the NAMED gap. Gate: test-browser-backend ①
(the ladder matrix, the seed, the three seat states with the unknown-as-0 and

in-process for device #0, inside the agentd for a paired device. The hub names
