### src/server/browser-access.js

ORCH — **ONE way to reach a profile browser on ANY machine (P4)**, the
opencode-access shape on purpose: `call(hostId, action, params)` picks the
transport (falsy/`local` = the shared runner in-process; a paired device = the
`browser-serve` agentd op; a handle that cannot run the op = REFUSED
`host_needs_daemon` — a silent local fallback would start the browser on the
wrong machine. ON THE REAL HostManager (measured, lane C1, test-desktop-serve
§5): an ssh host is given the bundled daemon over ssh stdio (`device()` →
ensureAgentdOnHost), so it is SERVED, not refused; a bootstrap that fails is
`host_unavailable` naming the reason, at the latest after `connectMs`; the real
DeviceManager always has `browserServe`, so `host_needs_daemon` there comes
only from the client's capability gate — an agent that predates the op) and turns a machine-side `{ok:false}` into a coded throw so
callers see one shape. `forwardCdp(hostId, remotePort, {remoteUrl})` = the
hub-side loopback listener (`net.createServer` on 127.0.0.1:0, each connection
piped into `device.tcpForward(remotePort)` — PortForwardManager's shape, the
device resolved PER CONNECTION so a re-dial never leaves a stale handle),
REFERENCE-COUNTED per (hostId, remotePort): two records may name one port (a
profile browser's own port and a `cdp` profile pointed at it), so a release
drops ONE reference and the listener closes at zero, never under the other
record's feet; concurrent first callers join ONE listen. For the LOCAL machine
no forward is made. `shutdown()` is the only unconditional teardown. An
unwired process refuses LOUDLY (`host_unavailable`). Gate:
test-browser-providers ④ (bytes round-trip over a fake tcpForward).

### src/server/egress-proxy.js

ORCH — **the allowlisting egress proxy (P4, §7.2.1 "make the boundary
enforcing rather than observed")**: a tiny HTTP forward proxy on the hub's
loopback — `CONNECT host:port` (TLS passes through untouched) and absolute-form
`GET http://…` — admitting a host ONLY when the PURE `egressVerdict(host,
allowlist)` says so and answering `403` with the verdict's own sentence
otherwise (a blocked fetch is a NAMED refusal in the browser's network log,
never a hang); the allowlist is re-read per request (liveApply), loopback and
link-local targets are refused by the verdict itself (never a way back into the
hub's services), origin-form requests are 400 (it is a proxy, not a server). No
auth (loopback only, like the stream port), no caching, bounded header read.
Started by the keeper per cloak launch (its run proxy) and per pinned install
(its download proxy) — a fresh instance listens on nothing. Gate:
test-browser-providers ⑥ (real loopback sockets).

**lane-cloak (2026-09-28): the two proxies the keeper owns.** (1) THE RUN
proxy — one per keeper, started at the first cloak start
(`cloakEgressUrl()`), allowlist = `B.cloakRunAllowlist(record, the
browser.cloak.egressAllowlist setting)` = the §7.2.1 record's run hosts
(measured: NONE — the browser itself needs no site) + the sites the deployment
names; the browser is launched with `--proxy-server=<it>` AND
`--proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>` (Chromium otherwise bypasses the proxy for
loopback, and the proxy — never admitting loopback — is what keeps the hub's
own services out of reach); closed at keeper shutdown. (2) THE INSTALL proxy —
per install, allowlist = `B.cloakInstallAllowlist(record)` = the record's
download hosts (cloakbrowser.dev, github.com,
release-assets.githubusercontent.com); the wrapper's `cloakbrowser install`
runs with HTTPS_PROXY + `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (Node's fetch honours the proxy
only then — measured on Node 24.12), and a browser that appeared while the
proxy admitted NOTHING is refused (a Node ignoring the variable would have
downloaded around the allowlist). `recent()` = the last 20 refusals (host +
sentence + time, no bodies) — `keeper.cloakEgress()` and the install state
read them, so a blank page / a failed step names what was refused. Over http a
refused site renders as the proxy's one line (`egress refused: <host> is not in
the egress allowlist (…)`); over https Chrome's CONNECT fails. What the proxy
cannot see is a non-HTTP(S) connection — the measured build made none. The
`resolve` hook (identity in production) lets the gates admit a name into a
loopback target so nothing leaves. Gates: test-browser-providers ⑦ (the
record's two allowlists through a real proxy), test-browser-backend ③c (real
CONNECTs to the keeper's own proxy refused by name), test-browser-share ⑧ (the
real binaries).

### scripts/measure-cloak-egress.mjs

**The §7.2.1 measurement, as a script — RUN 2026-09-28 (lane-cloak, the
owner's 「下载吧」).** Modelled on src/local-oracles.js: `env -i
HOME=<empty dir> PATH=… strace -f -qq`, every `connect(AF_INET|AF_INET6)`
counted (a DNS `:53` connect counts as INET), over the four runs the design
names. What the REAL package (npm `cloakbrowser` 0.5.10) taught it — the first
version assumed a shape the package does not have:
1. the package's `bin` (dist/cli.js) is a MANAGEMENT CLI (`install | info |
   update | login | logout | clear-cache`), not a browser; the download is
   `cloakbrowser install` (prints the executable) and the browser is
   `<cache>/chromium-<v>/chrome`;
2. ONE VibeSpace-owned `CLOAKBROWSER_CACHE_DIR` across the runs (a fresh HOME
   per run re-downloaded 200 MB each time) — never `~/.cloakbrowser`;
3. the wrapper's launch path schedules an hourly update check (the GitHub
   releases API + the npm registry) that silently downloads a newer build —
   the runs pin `CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION` + `CLOAKBROWSER_AUTO_UPDATE=false`,
   exactly as the product's install does;
4. the package is ESM without `./package.json` in its exports — read from an
   explicit `--prefix`;
5. launched the way the product launches it: the browser driver (0.38.1) with
   `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` / `AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS` on EVERY call (a call
   without them relaunched the browser without its arguments — measured), and
   the trace adds `execve`/`clone` so each connect is attributed (wrapper /
   driver / chrome);
6. `--no-sandbox` (the vendor's own default; a Chromium unpacked under a data
   dir has no AppArmor profile — "No usable sandbox!" on Ubuntu 23.10+);
7. DNS goes through the 127.0.0.53 stub, so names come from the DNS
   queries/answers in the send/recv buffers (`-s 1024 -xx`); getaddrinfo's
   port-0 source-address probes stay in `inetConnects` (the literal method)
   and are listed apart (`addrProbes`); every target is tagged with its PHASE
   (`download` / `launch`).
Run 1 downloads — `--first-launch` must be passed (a run nobody authorized
never fetches 200 MB); a first launch that never started the browser is
re-taken, a start is judged by EVIDENCE (an execve of the binary without
`--type=`), never a recorded flag, and `--first-start <trace>` names an
interrupted run's trace when that is where the binary first started. The
result (run 1: 21 INET — cloakbrowser.dev ×2, github.com ×1,
release-assets.githubusercontent.com ×1, 4 DNS, 1 loopback CDP, 12 probes;
runs 2–4: 1 INET each, the loopback CDP port) is
`src/browser-profiles.CLOAK_EGRESS_PROOF`. Never in ci.mjs (a measurement,
not a test — like measure-input-receipts.mjs).

### src/browser-trace.js
**Lane trace-fits (2026-10-01, the owner: every resize / move of the live view was an action — 37 of 194 entries in the busiest production scope were `viewer-fit` rows with 36 KB of frames each).** `FIT_COALESCE_MS` (10 s, beside AFTER_SETTLE_MS), `FIT_ACTION` = 'viewer-fit', `isFitEntry` / `fitCount` (a coalesced run counts every fit folded in: `n`). F1 `fitCoalesceVerdict(prev, next, {now, between, coalesceMs})` = the same browser key + scope within 10 s of the run's LAST fit (`lastAt`) with no traced action `between` ⇒ `{coalesce: true}`; every refusal named (no previous fit / the previous action is X / another action between / another browser / another scope / N s since the last fit / out of order). `coalesceFits(prev, next)` = the run keeps its FIRST id / at / before frame / session, takes the LAST geometry / text / result / after frame (the run's own when the new fit brought none), `n` summed, `lastAt`. `entryFor` stamps a fit `n: 1, lastAt: at`. F2 `foldFits(entries, {expand})` = the rows every list draws — an agent action its own `{kind:'entry', id, entry, fit}` row, CONSECUTIVE fits ONE `{kind:'fits', id: the first's, entries, n, at, lastAt, last, failed}` row (a click between keeps two runs apart; `expand` = the toggle: every fit its own row marked `fit`); `visibleEntries(rows)` = what a dialog steps through (the agent actions + the LAST fit of each run). `traceSummary` → `{n, failed, first, last, fits}` with `n` / `failed` over AGENT actions and the fits beside; `scopeDigest` → `+ fits, fitBytes`. F3 `traceSizePlan`: a scope over its limit loses the FRAMES of its fit entries FIRST (the plan's entries carry `fit`; oldest fit first across sessions; `why` "page-size frames go first; its action list is kept"), then the old session rule; `kept[].fitFrameBytes`. The agent's own `viewport` verb stays untraced (never a fit). Gate: test-browser-trace ① ② ④ (+ controls (a) (b) (c)).
**Lane live-input (2026-09-27):** `cleanRecordError(raw)` = a failed `record start`'s own sentence without its echoed command line ("Command failed: agent-browser record start /abs/…webm") and without absolute paths (≤ 240 chars) — what the digest's `recordingRefused.error` keeps. `recordingChipWords({recording, refused, hasProfile, since}, {t})` = the live bar's recording chip: `on` "Recording video" (since when, never a file path), `off` "Video off" (the click opens Agent browser; the action list is kept either way — video stays a per-profile opt-in, no default changed), `none` (a temporary browser has no profile to record under), `refused` "Video did not start" + a remedy by code (floor / not ours / not local / no CDP / folder / record_failed "turn video off and on again"), the detail after "Details:". Gate: test-live-input §5.

**RETENTION BY SIZE ONLY (2026-09-27, the owner: "记录不要按照 7 天上限，而是按照容量，每个浏览器 profile 最多保留 1GB 记录").** `TRACE_RETENTION_MS` and `traceRetentionPlan` are gone; there is no age rule anywhere in this file or in src/server/browser-trace.js (test-browser-sessions ② censuses both and requires `traceSizePlan`'s body to read no clock). `TRACE_BYTES_PER_PROFILE` = 1 GiB, `TRACE_BYTES_FLOOR` = 64 MB, `TRACE_BYTES_SETTING` = `browser.traceBytesPerProfile` (MB); `traceBytesLimit(settingMb)` = the limit (unset / garbage ⇒ 1 GiB, never below the floor). `traceSizePlan({scopes:[{key, sessions:[{id, startAt, open, entries:[{id, at, frameBytes, listBytes}]}]}], bytesPerScope})` = per scope (a named profile; the ephemeral scope counts as one): over the limit, the FRAMES of the oldest CLOSED sessions go first, a whole session at a time; only when every closed session is bare, an OPEN session's oldest actions one at a time (the newest stay); an action LIST is never planned away (`removeFrames` is the only output list; `kept[]` says `used / frameBytes / listBytes / limit / overBy` and why). `entryFrameBytes` counts each distinct FILE once (an `afterSame` after IS the before file); `entryListBytes` = the index line. `entryFor` gains `browserSession` (`bs-…`, null only for a pre-session record). The video recordings keep their own bound in src/browser-recording-retention.js. Control: a patched copy that also sweeps by age fails the plan legs.

Before, the before/after dialog's dot was scaled by the claimed 1280×720 (27 px too high on a 288 px thumbnail of a 1280×577 page).

**PURE** (imports only the sibling PURE registry model for the provider rows;
CJS so the recorder, the routes, the CLI AND the bundle share ONE spelling of
every rule). Agent browser P5 (2026-09-18, design §4.5 / §6.4 / §7.1 / §8
step 3, D7 / D8 / D35). THE ACTION TRACE: `TRACED_ACTIONS` is the closed
action table (click / fill / press / mouse* / scroll / navigate … → the KIND of
position an entry records); anything not in it — `get`, `snapshot`, `launch`,
`boundingbox`, `screenshot`, `wait` — is an OBSERVATION and is never traced
(`isTracedCommand`). `redactParams` keeps a fill's value and a type's text as
`«N chars»` and an upload's file NAMES only (the §3.7 audit rule applies to the
trace); `commandText` rebuilds the human-readable command from the REDACTED
params. `positionOf` = point (CSS px) / box (the target's `{x,y,width,height}`
from ONE `get box <selector>` probe) / target-without-box saying why / keys /
scroll / navigation. A result is judged by its ERROR, never by `success`
(measured on 0.32.0: `false` on every result, clicked or not). `afterFramePick`
= the first frame ≥ 400 ms after the result, else the latest by 1.5 s (`same`
when nothing repainted). `entryFor` = the record `{id, at, sessionId,
browserKey, profileId, scope, action, kind, text, params, ok, error,
durationMs, position, before, after, afterSame, url}` (+ `browserSession` since 2026-09-27). RETENTION:
BY SIZE since 2026-09-27 (`traceSizePlan`, above) — every removal names its
rule, every kept scope what it holds. `recordingVerdict`
refuses BY NAME (off / not ours / not local / below the 0.37.0 floor).
HOUSEKEEPING: `sweepScope` = exactly the provider rows with `ownsDir` on this
machine; `queueVerdict` refuses `cloud:*` / `local-window` / `cdp` / a remote
record as `not_ours`; `housekeepingVerdict` answers a state from the closed
`HOUSEKEEPING_STATES` (`not-ours` / `in-use` / `live` / `recent` — in-flight
grace with its age / `stale` / `kept`) with its `why` and NEVER answers
"delete"; `forgetVerdict` refuses while leased or running; `orphanCandidates` =
a Chromium-marker directory no record names; `orphanPathVerdict` = a top-level
dir under the base only. THE CLIENT'S DOM-FREE HALF (P5 client, 2026-09-21):
`commandDrivesBrowser` + `toolCommandText` (claude's string / codex's argv
array) gate the tool card; `traceWindowFor` = a card's window (its ts − 2 s →
the next message's ts + 2 s, or now); `unionWindow` = ONE fetch for many cards;
`assignEntriesToWindows` gives each entry to EXACTLY ONE card — the one with
the latest ts that was RUNNING when the action happened (500 ms skew; an entry
only later cards can hold goes to the earliest of them); `overlayGeometry` =

### src/server/browser-trace.js
**Lane trace-fits (2026-10-01) — F1 AT THE SOURCE.** Every tap keeps `lastCmd` (the last TRACED command; a pending record carries `prevCmd`), `lastFit` (the fit row written last) and `lastFitCmdId`. In `finalize` a `viewer-fit` asks PURE `fitCoalesceVerdict(run, next, {now: p.at, between})` — `between` = the previous traced command unless it is the run's own last fit — and on `coalesce` REPLACES the run: its id / at / before frame / session kept, this fit's geometry + result taken, this fit's latest frame written as a NEW file `<id>-after-<n>.jpg` (a client may hold the old one cached under the same URL — the clients add `?v=<n>`), the superseded after frame UNLINKED at once (never left for the sweep; the run's before file never), `<id>.json` rewritten, `replaceIndex` (in memory the run's slot; on disk the line APPENDED under the same id — the index stays append-only; `loadIndex` folds: a later line under an id already loaded SUPERSEDES it, the sweep's rewrite compacts; no tombstone, the id is the key). The stream `trace` record and `browser-trace-appended` carry `replaced: true` (+ `n`, `lastAt`) so the clients patch the row in place. A session counts the agent's actions only (`bs.count`, the end marker, `ensureOpenLoaded`); a fit moves its `lastAt`. `scopeForPlan` flags `fit`; `usageOf` → `{used: the agent actions' bytes, fitBytes, total, frameBytes, listBytes, limit}` (the panel's `{used} of {size}` + "page-size frames: N"). Gate: test-browser-trace ③ (the flood: 157 + 37 ⇒ 167 entries / 10 fit rows / 334 frame files, the index 194 lines / 167 ids folded at reload) + ④ + control (d).
**Lane browser-resume, chunk A (2026-09-30):** `housekeeping()` also carries `kept` (the kept store's rows), `keptSweep` and `limits.keptOn/keptPerConversation/keptTotal`; the route (`keptRowsFor`) gives an agent's token the counts only. The panel's Sweep route also kicks the kept store's sweep (it answers by its own broadcast).

**Lane live-input (2026-09-27, the owner's journal: "recording bp-… → …132332.webm" then, 106 ms later, "record start failed … 132438.webm"): ONE `record start` AT A TIME.** `maybeStartRecording` is single-flight per recording (`profileId|browserKey` — each conversation on a profile records its own tab under its own session): the `attach` every agent command emits and the panel's record-on fan-out raced through its awaits; a second ask while one is starting answers with THAT start (`already: true`), and `recordings.has(key)` answers a running one. `startRecording` writes a refusal only when it is REAL (this recording is not running — a start another ask won can never fail it), broadcasts the digest on a failure too, keeps the CLI's error through `cleanRecordError`, and stops a recording that was switched off while it started. Gate: test-live-input §8 (the pre-fix start as control) + test-browser-live-input (the journal: one start while video is switched on during agent commands).


**BROWSER SESSIONS + THE SIZE SWEEP (2026-09-27, the owner: "最关键是能在聊天界面和浏览器查看界面两个地方都能看到 session 的开始和结束，以及每个浏览器 session 的回放").** The same lease seam opens and closes a SESSION per (browser key, trace scope): `sessionsOnEvent` runs AFTER the taps' own handling (so the in-flight actions a detach finalizes still carry the session they happened in) — `attach` / a profile's `browser-ready` (per lease) / an ephemeral `browser-ready` or `verb` OPEN (`startSession`, a no-op when one is open); `detach` (released), `lease-dropped` (dropped), a `browser-stopped` whose why is not idle (`stopped`; `switch` ⇒ switched) CLOSE (`endSession`) — `idle` and `turn-idle` never do (PURE `stopEndsSession`: a lease that lives is a session that lives). A marker is `{kind:'session', phase, id:'bs-…', browserKey, profileId, ephemeral, webuiSessionId, label, at, url?, count?, durationMs?, reason?}` appended to `data/browser-trace/<scope>/sessions.ndjson` (0600) and held in memory per scope (`loadMarkers`); every entry `finalize` writes is tagged `browserSession` (`sessionForTap` — an action with no open session OPENS one, reason `action`: it is its own session) and counted. The open set is read from disk ONCE (`ensureOpenLoaded`: a start with no end; two open for one key ⇒ the older ends `restart`) before any event decides anything; `boot()` then RE-OPENS a session whose lease is back in the registry and ENDS the rest with reason `restart` at `max(start, last action)` (never the downtime) — `{reopened, endedAtBoot}`. `browser.actionTrace` OFF ⇒ `startSession` opens nothing (an open one still ends). Every marker goes to `onSession(marker)` (the wiring: the live chat card) and to every client as `browser-sessions-updated {browserKey, profileId, marker}`. Readers: `sessions({browserKey, profileId, sessionId})` (PURE pairing per scope, a conversation's helpers included, newest first; ties by the marker file's order), `sessionEntries(id)`, `chatCardsFor(browserKey)` (with the limit). THE SWEEP is size-only (`traceSizePlan` over `scopeForPlan(sc)` — each entry filed under its session, implicit ones included): the chosen entries' frame FILES are unlinked, the entry keeps everything else and is stamped `framesRemoved:{at, why:'size', limit}` (index line + `<id>.json` rewritten) — EVERY index line stays; `lastSweep` = `{removed, framesRemoved, bytesRemoved, limit, recordingsRemoved…}`. Recordings: `RR.recordingRetentionPlan` (their own 7 d / 200 MB). `usageOf(scope)` = `{used, frameBytes, listBytes, limit}` — each housekeeping row's `trace` and the ephemeral digest carry it; `limits` = `{bytesPerProfile, bytesDefault, bytesFloor, recordingRetentionMs, recordingBytesPerProfile, …}` (no `retentionMs`). Gate: test-browser-sessions ③ (+ the list-dropping patched copy), test-browser-housekeeping ②.

**Lane H (2026-09-25) — the ephemeral browser is traced with nobody watching.** The C3 note below ("armed by the live view's tap") described the bug: no view, no trace (the owner's data/browser-trace/ was empty after an `open`). `onLeaseEvent` now RETURNS the arming promise (the keeper holds the verb on it, bounded) and handles the ephemeral seam: `browser-ready` / `verb` with `ephemeral` ⇒ `armEphemeral` ⇒ `watch({sessionId, profileId: null, browserKey})`. `browser-stopped` / `lease-dropped` / `detach` ⇒ `unwatch`. A `child` is skipped, because its pairs are not its session's. `watch` taps with `S.EPHEMERAL_REF` for `profileId` null (it used to pass `''`, the session's DEFAULT pane — an attachment's actions filed under `ephemeral`). An ephemeral tap needs its HOLDER ROW (`keeper.holdersFor(bk)` has a non-child ephemeral row for that key; the same rows the digest is, so ONE mutation kills window + trace + chip, which is the controls' design). Concurrent callers share `tp.arming`. A tap disarmed while connecting lets its relay go, and neither it nor `tap-end` deletes a newer tap under the same key. `boot()` taps a READY ephemeral lease too (an adopted one after a restart), never a sub-agent's, never a screencast. Gates: test-browser-ephemeral ④ (the REAL recorder over the real keeper, a fake bridge) + test-browser-live ③b / ④ (heavy; ④ over the real 0.38.1 stream server: a real `open` recorded as `navigate`).

**Lane H verify r1 (2026-09-25) — L1: the arm wait belongs to the verb that started the browser.** `browser-ready` arms (`armEphemeral`) and may be waited on; a `verb` goes through `armOnVerb`, which answers `null` (the keeper waits on nothing) whenever ANY tap already holds the key, armed or still arming (it used to return `had.arming`, so a tap stuck arming held EVERY verb for the whole wait: 3150 / 3098 / 3108 ms measured on 0.38.1), and within `ARM_RETRY_MS` (30 s, exported) of a FAILED arming of the same key (`armFailedAt`, stamped on every failure path of `arm()` — a throw, a refusal, a stream that ended at once — cleared on success and by `unwatch`; a failed tap used to be deleted and re-armed + waited on by every next verb). Gate: test-browser-ephemeral ④ L1 + a mutant copy whose `verb` joins the pending arming (the control).

The box probe and the per-profile screencast run through `keeper.leaseCliOpts` (CDP, never the directory; finding 1). **ORCH** (P5). THE RECORDER hangs on two seams and decides nothing: the
bridge's TAPS (`browserStream.tap(sessionId, profileId, cb)` — every
`command` / `result` / `frame` / `url` record of a live relay; a tap holds a

A traced `command` snapshots the LAST frame held as the before-picture; the
matching `result` starts the after-clock and, for a target action, ONE bounded

is itself never traced). The entry lands as 0600 files (`<id>.json`,
`<id>-before.jpg`, `<id>-after.jpg`) + a line in `index.ndjson` under
`data/browser-trace/<profileId | ephemeral>/`, is pushed to the live view's
viewers as a `trace` stream record and to every client as
`browser-trace-appended` (never the bytes). `browser.actionTrace` (default ON,
D35) gates the whole thing. THE SCREENCAST (D7 opt-in per profile): `record
start <file>` / `record stop` under the lease's session, `record: true`
profiles only, refused below the floor with the refusal kept for the panel;
files under `data/browser-recordings/<profileId>/<sid>-<ts>.webm`. THE SWEEP
(hourly + boot) applies the PURE size plan to the traces (frames only, since
2026-09-27) and the recordings' own bound to the recordings, and logs what it
removed and why. HOUSEKEEPING: sizes by `du -sb` in a CHILD (never a sync walk —
98 GB lived under `~/.agent-browser` on the design's machine), cached 10 min;
`orphans()` under `~/.agent-browser`; `forgetProfile` RENAMES the directory
beside itself (`<dir>.forgotten-<ts>`) — verify r8: its lineage key asked BEFORE
the rename (`keeper.lineageKeyOf(dir, {retireOf})`); verify r9: the entry re-keyed
AND WRITTEN before the rename (`moveLineageFirst` → `keeper.moveDirLineage`; a
refused write = `forget_failed`, nothing moved; a failed rename rolls the key
back), `forgetOrphan` the same — and files a ledger row in
`data/browser-forgotten.json` BEFORE the record goes; `deleteForgotten` is THE
one permanent deletion (a `.forgotten-` directory under the base, a human's
click); `adoptOrphan` labels a directory in place (§8 step 3). `list({sessionId,
browserKey, anyOf})` matches by the webui id OR the key (a resume re-carries the
key while the id churns). Every housekeeping change broadcasts

### src/routes/browser-trace.js
**Lane trace-fits (2026-10-01):** `GET /api/browser/actions` answers `summary` = `T.traceSummary(entries)` (`n` / `failed` over the agent's actions, `fits` beside).
**2026-09-27 — `GET /api/browser/sessions`.** Cookie only (not under `/api/agent/` — the only prefix the bearer tokens pass; the agent routes got nothing new). The key is resolved exactly like `/actions` (the live session's, the bindings store's for `conversation`, a `browserKey` given); `profile` ALONE lists every conversation's sessions on that scope (the Agent browser panel's Replay…); a conversation this server cannot name answers an EMPTY list, never every session. `session=bs-…` adds that session's `entries` (oldest first, ≤ 1000) and `session`. Answers `{traceOn, limit, browserKey, keyFrom, sessions}`. Bad `session` / `browserKey` / `profile` ⇒ 400; a host ⇒ `unsupported-host`.

**Owner ruling A (2026-09-26):** GET housekeeping decorates each row with `scope`, `scopeConversation`, `createdBy`, `usedBy` ([{browserKey, sessionId, name, leased, pinned}]) and answers `conversations` (every live conversation with a browser key — the panel is the user's, names allowed); PATCH accepts `scope`/`conversation` and queues a layer-② notice for each conversation a narrowing detached; POST forget `{release, unpin}` = Delete… (ctx `releaseProfile`, then ctx `unpinProfile` — lane S2's seam — then the set-aside); without the flags the old `leased` / `running` refusals stand.

**"Who can use it" is a LIST (2026-09-27; `scopeConversation` and the scope PATCH retired).** `useViewOf(p, live, cache)` names each row where the server can (a live session's name / webui id / backend; a stopped key's `conversationId` from `bindings.conversationsByKey()`, read once per request; a Task Group's title, `deleted` / `archived` / `unreadable` from `keeper.taskInfo`); housekeeping rows carry it as `use`. **`GET /api/browser/profiles/:id/use`** = the dialog's FRESH read (+ `base`, `usedBy` with each holder's `taskIds` and `live` — a stopped holder's groups are not readable now; the dialog's count mirrors the keeper's undecided rule —, `createdBy`). **`PATCH`** (async now): shape → base (409 `list-changed` `{added, removed}`) → every `{session:<webui id>}` row through `ctx.keyForPickedSession` (one refusal ⇒ its code + `name`, NOTHING written); a `{key}` row carried by a live session on ANOTHER machine (`remoteHolderOf`) is refused `no_browser_key` `why:'remote'` like a picked one (2026-09-28 — the picker never offers it, so a request naming its key is answered the same way; control (h)) → `k.updateProfile(id, patch, {knownKeys})` (which re-asks the base after these awaits) → the layer-② notice for each detached conversation. `fail()` carries `added`/`removed`. Wiring: `setupTraceRoutes({…, keyForPickedSession})`.


**takeover r2 (2.369.168):** test-architecture §52b counts the hidden browser CLI's name in this file's string literals (its refusals reach the agent) — clean; a planted name in a patched copy of routes/window-targets.js is the census's control.

Thin over the two above; `host` refused by name (local-only in this release).
`GET /api/browser/actions?sessionId=&conversation=&browserKey=&profile=&from=&to=&limit=`
— ONE conversation's actions by the live session's key, else the bindings
store's key for the CLI's own `conversation` id (a STOPPED conversation's
cards still find their actions — the point of a review; the wiring hands the
routes a `browser-bindings` reader that reads the file per ask), else a
`browserKey` given outright (validated); at least one of the three; **nothing to
match by ⇒ an honest EMPTY answer, never every entry** (the client-half suite
caught the route answering everything for an unbound conversation). Answers
`{sessionId, conversation, browserKey, keyFrom: session|conversation|given|null,
traceOn, entries}`. `GET …/trace/:id` (never the bytes) · `GET
…/trace/:id/frame/before|after` (image/jpeg + nosniff + private cache) · `GET
/api/browser/housekeeping` (the panel's whole view — nothing here is a
deletion) · `POST …/housekeeping/sweep` · `PATCH /api/browser/profiles/:id`
`{record?, label?, notes?}` (anything else refused by name) · `POST
…/profiles/:id/forget` (409 leased / running, 400 not_ours) · `POST
/api/browser/orphans/adopt {dir, label}` · `POST /api/browser/orphans/forget
{dir}` · `POST /api/browser/forgotten/:fid/delete` (THE one permanent deletion)
· `GET /api/browser/recordings/:profileId[/:file]` (video/webm|mp4, no-store).
Statuses by the closed `STATUS` table. Gate: test-browser-housekeeping ④.

### src/lib/browser-trace-view.js
**Design 015 — lane browser-panel-tidy (2026-10-03, the owner: 「这个界面UI也优化一下吧 目前有点乱」, then 「…每个信息横向都不对齐。应该思考下哪些信息可以展示的时候truncate，哪些可能很长需要单独一行」).** The Agent browser panel is ONE table: `.bprof-table` holds the only `grid-template-columns` (`minmax(140px,1.5fr) minmax(100px,1fr) minmax(170px,1.3fr) 120px max-content`, gap 10) and the column titles (`.bprof-head`: 配置 · 状态 · 谁能使用 · 占用 · 记录) and every profile row are `grid-template-columns: subgrid` of it, so a cell's left edge is the table's track; the acts track is `max-content` — the widest row's buttons, shared by every row (per-row grids with an `auto` acts column were the first mockup's misalignment — the heavy census's second control). Every cell is two lines (`.bprof-l1` 24 px, `.bprof-l2` 16 px, always present): profile = chevron + name (ellipsis, whole in its title and the fold) / chips (browser first and whole, then machine · legacy · separate tabs · renamed-from, folded by WIDTH into "+n"); state = dot + word / ONE sentence by priority (stuck > closed > accepts leave-page dialogs > the row's why); who = `whoCell` (chips folded by WIDTH into "+n" through the bar-fold rule `barLayout` — `fitLine`; CHIPS_WIDE is only the upper bound; the one value "All agents" shrinks with an ellipsis before Change… is cut; Change… never folds) / the amber nobody line; size (never cut) / actions · recordings · recording (red). The fold (`.bprof-fold`, per row, its open state in `openFolds`, outside the signature) holds name, directory, every state sentence, memory, the Chrome build (`.bprof-build`), records used of limit + page-size frames + last, recordings, display fact, your browsing. Acts: ONE primary (Browse yourself / Open your browsing window — absent, never greyed) and ONE ⋯ (`showContextMenu`; each row's label carries its act's class: `bprof-record` / `bprof-record-mine` check rows, `bprof-replay`, `bprof-build-btn`, `bprof-rename`, `bprof-stop`, `bprof-restart`, `bprof-restart-hold`, then a separator and `bprof-forget` (Delete…) in red); `RUN` runs them by the model's id. What the words and which acts exist is the PURE `src/lib/browser-panel-model.js` (`rowLine`, `rowFold`, `rowMenu`, `rowActs`, `nameChips`, `stateLines`, `GRID` / `gridNeed`, `orphanOrder`; it imports nothing — the view passes its word functions). `layout()` (after each render + a ResizeObserver on the body) sets `.bprof-stacked` when the list is narrower than `gridNeed(widest acts)` (the phone / a narrow window: five lines per row by grid areas, titles hidden) and fits every line that folds by width. The header is one line (summary · ⓘ popover with the retention sentence · New profile… · ⟳); the Browser CLI row, the last sweep + Sweep now and the retention text sit in the last section, 维护 / Maintenance; "Browsers without a profile" left the profile list (its counts are the Ephemeral section's head); Unregistered directories fold by default (count · size; open = largest first). The ≤ 768 px two-column fallback no longer touches profile rows. Gates: test-browser-panel-model (fast: the tables, THE ACT CENSUS + a patched-copy control, the grid pin), test-browser-profiles-ui ⑧ (heavy: the rect census at 860 / 1280 in zh / ja / en + two controls, the walk, 390 px).

**Lane browser-unresponsive (src/lib/browser-panel-model.js):** a live row of this computer whose `r.unresponsive` stands (src/browser-trace.js carries the keeper's fact) reads "Not answering since 16:34" as its state word and offers ONE primary — Restart (`id: 'restart'`, the view runs `RUN.restart`, the user's cookie route); Browse yourself is not offered then and the ⋯ menu never lists Restart twice.

### docs/agent/browser-manual.md
**verify r3 (lane browser-windows, 2026-10-02):** the refusal table gains `window_busy` (the window lives, no tab right now — ONE retry after a moment, never a loop); the WINDOW bullet says `tab new --json` names the rung (`opened.rung`: opener / activate / new-window) and the one-time `tabs_in_other_windows` note of a conversation from before this version.

**Lane browser-recipes (2026-10-02, userR's pod): §0 "What the user asked for → what you do" comes FIRST, before every verb.** The incident: asked to work "in the Chrome logged in as <her>", the agent ran `vibespace-browser status`, read only what it could NOT do (no profile, ephemeral), launched the system chromium itself and died on "Missing X server or $DISPLAY" — the recipe (a NAMED profile, the user logging in ONCE through the live view, the login kept) was only implied across §3 and a refusal row. A naive agent reads the first screen only, so §0 (≤ 40 lines, before the old intro paragraph) is four recipes in plain imperative words, each ending in the ONE sentence to say to the user: (a) the user's login = `new "<site> — <user>'s login"` → `use` → `open <url>` → "Open the Agent browser window and take over to log in; I will continue once you hand it back" (never a password; the login stays in the profile); (b) look something up = bare verbs; (c) the same login for other agents = a profile is usable by all conversations unless narrowed, `--sharing instance` = own tabs, `not_owner` = the user widens "Who can use it"; (d) no display = only `vibespace-browser` (a hidden window / headless), never chromium / google-chrome / playwright by hand. Gate: scripts/test-browser-recipes.mjs (§0 first, the four recipes, the exact user sentence, the naive-reader leg: in the first 60 lines `new "` precedes every page verb; mutant control = the manual without §0).

**P4 (2026-09-16)**: the verb table gained `providers [--host]` and `new`'s
`--provider/--host/--cdp-port`, and one bullet ("Other providers and other
machines") says what a paired-machine profile and a `cdp` profile are, that a
reached browser's CDP pair is withheld by `use --print` too, and that their
live view is not available yet.

**P1 (2026-09-16)**: the manual gained the `vibespace-browser` section (named
profiles, the lease, what `use` does and does not print, the `close --all`
rule, the pin) and its "not available yet" sentences about shared profiles
were replaced; the tools intro's isolated sentence now points at
`vibespace-browser new/use` instead of telling the agent to wait.

The manual `vibespace-docs browser` serves (registered in `AGENT_DOC_TOPICS`,
`src/agent-routes.js`), beside the one budgeted line in the tools intro —
**a line that is now chosen by the session's OWN recorded rung (r5)**:
`browser-profiles.isolatedVariant` (D/C/N/H) gets the "this session has its own
browser, `close --all` closes only yours" sentence, and every other session
(rung `none`, the feature off, a resolver that threw, a session predating it)
gets the manual's own words for the shared browser, because telling a shared
session that `close --all` is safe is the incident P0 exists to stop. It
describes what SHIPS: the four variables and what they mean for the agent, the
TWO config files the generated config is built from and the one boundary of
that (the session directory's `agent-browser.json`, once, for the whole
session — r3), the three things to stop doing (`--profile` / `--session` /
`--namespace`), and the honest limits — a remote host decides the user-data-dir
itself (its own per-key dir when its config names a profile, the CLI's
throwaway dir otherwise), one local corner gets nothing at all (a profile-naming
config with neither D nor C deliverable — the names alone would make the browser
fail to start), nothing watches the browser, a login does not survive, there is
no live view and no handover yet, shared named profiles are a later phase, and
the CLI's own 103-byte socket-path limit (`$HOME` + 65 bytes for our name shape
⇒ a home longer than 38 characters would break every command) — which r4 now
closes by setting `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` at an owned 0700 directory only
when the CLI's own root is over the limit, so the manual names it as the FIFTH
variable the session may carry and tells the agent what the refusal means if it
ever still appears (the directory could not be used and the journal says why).

### transcript-service.js

  transcript-service.js — **2.369.167 (perf lane A): `page()`'s DEFAULT branch answers `mm.tailWindow()` — the attach slab counted in TEXT cards (src/text-window.js), not tail(50).** The offset/limit and untilUuid branches are unchanged. This is the HTTP `withStatus` read AND the daemon's `transcript-op page` (agentd.js bundles this service — no new op, no capability): test-transcript-parity's tool-heavy fixture (its last 50 records hold 3 text cards) answers 360 records / 24 text cards byte-identically on both legs, and goes red on the unfixed code (50 on both) and on a ONE-SIDED edit (a server that learned the rule while the daemon bundle did not). An OLD daemon still answers tail(50) and the client renders any N.
  transcript-service.js — ONE interface over the transcript parse stack (R3 of docs/design-three-tier.md; 2.283.0 step 1 = server-hosted, HTTP read family rerouted through it). **SWITCHED LIVE in 2.292.0** — remote page/turnmap/searchIndexed/status/taskState run as `transcript-op` on the owning machine (parsed KBs on the wire, no whole-file pull). LADDER not replacement: device op → transcript-cache pull + local parse → honest error; capability-gated (an old daemon is never asked — unknown ops hang), failures log throttled and degrade. TWO CARVE-OUTS, both load-bearing: ① a LIVE session never reads from the device (the server owns the stdout buffer overlay + live normalizer — the device would drop the un-flushed tail); ② the huge-file SEEK family switched ATOMICALLY in 2.293.0 once the daemon gained a `searchFull` op — `gapInfo` returns an OPAQUE HANDLE (`\0device:<host>` or the local path) that every follow-up (slab/search/turnmap) honours, so line numbers never come from two sources (the route already treated fp as opaque, so nothing above the service changed); device streaming search degrades honestly to one batch. Ladder test: scripts/test-transcript-switchover.mjs (7). **2.285.0 step 2: the DEVICE DAEMON hosts the SAME service** — agentd's `transcript-op` op (lazy-constructed, no buffer overlay device-side — the stdout overlay stays a server concern) runs page/turnmap/searchIndexed/status/taskState/gapInfo/gapSlab/fullTurnmap next to the bytes and streams JSON over a count-gated byte channel (read-range contract); client = DeviceManager.transcriptOp. DARK: no production consumer until the parity substrate soaks (retirement-order law). scripts/test-transcript-parity.mjs (19 asserts) pins BYTE-IDENTICAL results across in-process vs real-daemon — incl. >½MB multi-window payloads, a ~36MB fixture's real seek family, codex, and honest unknown-method/missing-file shapes. Its first run caught the tool-card ts bug (below). SafeFs/transcript-worker degrade INLINE inside the bundle (worker file absent next to the bundle → spawn fails → sync fallback, by design). **B-21e4 item 5:** `view()` warms through `harnessOf(backend).store.warmTranscript(id, cwd, {remote})` (claude parse-cache warm as before; codex thread/read fallback for a missing rollout, local only) — no backend ternary.

### session-store.js

  **NO claude model reader lives here (B-6b6d round 2)** — and the long comment where one used to be is the reason. Round 1 shipped `lastClaudeTurnModel` (tail scan for the last MAIN-THREAD assistant record's `message.model`) as the claude descriptor's `store.lastTurnModel`; it is REMOVED, because that field answers *which model served a turn* and the ladder asks *what should this resume command*. Two measurements decided it: (a) across the whole local corpus (2650 transcripts / 3.5 GB) **zero** `message.model` values carry a `[…]` context-variant suffix while the CLI's own `model_refusal_fallback` records prove conversations running `claude-fable-5[1m]`, so commanding the served id silently turns a 1M conversation into a 200k one on every resume; (b) a classifier reroute is an ASSISTANT record already ON the fallback model carrying a `{type:'fallback',from,to}` block, with the `system/model_refusal_fallback` record written 2–10 lines AFTER it — round 1's ≤20-line backward look-back matched 1 of 139 reroutes, and 16.8% of main-thread assistant records sit inside a reroute run. So a claude resume commands NEITHER model nor effort and the CLI's own session record (variant-exact) decides. Re-adding a reader is one hook in `src/harnesses/claude.js` if a future CLI ever records the commanded value.

  session-store.js     — SessionMessages + JSONL parsing + session discovery helpers. **THE LOCAL SWEEP'S PID-REUSE RUNG IS A RECORDED TWIN OF THE SWEEP'S IDENTITY RULE (B-3185 r3, RADIUS CORRECTED IN r4):** `isLockClaude` prefers B-2104's `procStart` match (no fork) and falls back to `isProcessClaudeAsync` = `ps -o comm=` + `.includes('claude')`. **r3 recorded this twin as "the local sweep's PID-reuse fallback" and that described only HALF of it: the SYNC `isProcessClaude` had one caller — `/api/kill-pid`'s local branch — so the substring rule GATED A SIGTERM. r4 deleted the sync half (that route now asks `isCliProcess` for both CLI names, like its own remote branch) and what survives is DISCOVERY-ONLY: one caller, `isLockClaude`'s no-`procStart` fallback (macOS locks write `procStartFt`; Linux answers with the file read first), deciding whether a card reads RUNNING and nothing else.** It is not an executable test the way it looks, either: `comm` is 15 bytes the process may set for itself (node renames its main thread to `MainThread`, so an npm-installed `node …/claude-code/cli.js` answers NO) matched as a SUBSTRING (`claude-keeper` answers YES) — the "4277 processes, same 16, zero divergence" measurement was of THIS box's native install, not of the rule. It stays un-ported because the rung that reaches it is macOS, where `isCliProcess` is SYNCHRONOUS and a per-lock blocking fork is the 2.242.0 event-loop stall this async family exists to avoid; adding a `comm` rung to the shared predicate instead would widen a KILL path. **It must never move back onto one** (test-writer-sweep §14 asserts the single caller and the sync twin's absence). It has a live parity gate too — scripts/test-local-discovery-device.mjs asserts device-facts sweep === local sweep, which compares the two rungs on every run (its fixture must therefore be a REAL binary named `claude`, never a `#!/bin/sh` script: the kernel gives that argv[0] `/bin/sh` while `comm` stays `claude`). **Merge is POSITION-PRESERVING (2.74.0):** surviving buffer records interleave at their true chronological spot (anchor = jsonl index of the last buffer record that deduped; a rotated buffer's unmatched head anchors just before the first match) instead of all appending at the end — end-append made an EARLIER turn's stream-json-only `result` replay AFTER a still-running tool_use, flushing the live pending tool card to ✗ Interrupted on every server restart (real report), and scrambled turn boundaries in the replay. **`chatStatus()` IS THE ATTACH/HTTP TWIN OF THE LIVE COMMAND-LIST OP (§2.6), AND ITS RULE IS AN ORDERING (round 3):** the tail scan records the POSITION of the newest `commands_changed` and of the newest `init`, and the push replaces the frame's `slashCommands` only when it is genuinely newer (plus the degradation branch: an init that declares no list cannot erase the push before it — live, `_emitSlashCommands` returns early on such a record, so the last thing that SPOKE stands). Applying the push unconditionally was actively harmful, not merely absent: a buffer holds one init per SPAWN (33 in one real conversation here), so `[…, commands_changed, …, init]` is the ordinary shape of a resume or wrapper respawn, and `applyStatus()` runs AFTER `loadHistory`'s render loop — the pre-restart list OVERWROTE the correct one the slab's own init-card side effect had just set, and was then mixed with the newest frame's `terminalSlashCommands`. The invariant the twin exists for is that **a window that opens after the push agrees with one that watched it happen**, so the gate drives the SAME records through both paths (scripts/test-init-frame.mjs `chatStatus twin`, with the pre-fix rule kept as the negative control). **THE INCREMENTAL TAIL CACHE (perf lane chunk C, 2.369.167 — "an attach of a loaded session re-parses nothing it already holds"):** every re-attach of a loaded chat session reads `sm.activePendingPermissions()` + `sm.chatStatus()` ⇒ `_ensureParsed` ⇒ `parseSessionJsonl` SYNC on the loop, and the cache was keyed by (mtime, size) — a live transcript grows between any two attaches, so each re-attach re-read and re-parsed the whole 32 MiB tail (measured on the §1c 48 MB fixture: 45–62 ms and 32 MiB per re-attach after a 130 KB append) to learn about the few KB the CLI had appended. The entry is now the BYTE SPAN it was parsed from — `{mtimeMs, size, ino, dev, spanStart, spanEnd, messages, starts, partial, headProbe, tailProbe, incr}`, built by ONE reader, `readJsonlTail(fp, prev, {dropSubagent, stat, appendOnly})` in src/adapters/codex.js beside readJsonlBounded (whose tailOnly rule it restates in bytes: a file ≤ HEAD+TAIL is kept whole, a bigger one keeps every line whose first byte is strictly after `size − TAIL` — `jsonlTailLower`). A call: same (mtime, size, inode) ⇒ the cached array, one stat and no read (the zstd magic read comes AFTER the hit test); the SAME inode strictly grown, the cut still below `spanEnd`, and the ≤ 4 KiB probes at both ends of the cached span re-read byte-equal (the append-only check) ⇒ read `[spanEnd, size)` only, parse its whole lines, drop head records whose line start is ≤ the new bound (`starts[]` gives the exact slide), re-anchor the head probe; anything else (a shrink, a new inode = rotation/replace, a rewritten probe byte, a single line longer than the tail) ⇒ today's full read. The unterminated trailing line is PARSED when it parses (the string path always did — a valid record whose '\n' has not landed yet is in today's output) but never CONSUMED: `spanEnd` stops at the last '\n', `partial` marks the extra record, and its bytes are re-read with the next append — so it is counted exactly once either way. OUTPUT IDENTITY is the invariant (scripts/test-jsonl-incremental.mjs holds a VERBATIM copy of the 2.369.160 reader as its oracle, not the module's own). `messages` is ALWAYS a new array (slice+concat, never grown in place): a SessionMessages whose `_all` is the old array — or a convertHistoryAsync iterating it across yields — keeps what it read. The ASYNC warm (the attach/HTTP entry point) folds an append ≤ 4 MiB (`WARM_INLINE_APPEND_MAX`) inline (`appendOnly:true`: never a full read on the loop) and hands everything else to the worker's new `jsonlTail` op, whose FULL read returns the same span entry — so a worker-filled entry's next change is an append too. **THE MERGE MEMO:** the position-preserving buffer merge (2.74.0) is a pure function of (the jsonl array, the buffer string); a WeakMap keyed by the cache's array remembers the last merge and its buffer, so a burst of SessionMessages over one unchanged session merges once — `_all` is shared exactly as the no-insert case always shared the cache's array, `_pendingPerms` is copied per instance; chatStatus/taskState/activePendingPermissions read the same `_all` untouched. Metrics: `srv-jsonl-parse-bytes` (bytes read AND parsed; the probes are not counted) + `srv-jsonl-parse-ms` on EVERY non-hit read, sync and warm alike (the ms metric used to fire only past 200 ms). JSONL_CACHE_MAX=30 LRU unchanged; read-only (never a write — the B-4058 two-writer class untouched). The daemon bundles this module for `transcript-op` ⇒ test-transcript-parity's append-between-calls + truncate legs are the drift guard (an old daemon keeps whole-file parses — structurally the same output). **THE CODEX TWIN IS DELIBERATELY LEFT (the standing sweep):** `parseCodexSessionJsonl` (adapters/codex.js, same 32 MiB `JSONL_TAIL_BYTES`) has NO parse cache at all — every read is a full tail parse — and its records are then tagged in place (`tagRecordThread`) and merged across fork ancestry by `mergeCodexRecords`, whose no-shared-mutation discipline was written for per-read arrays; giving it a cache means auditing that discipline for records shared across reads, a change with its own gate. `readJsonlTail` is generic (`dropSubagent` off) and ready for it.

  **ZERO SPAWNS PER SESSION IN THE LOCAL SWEEP (2026-09-09).** `discoverClaudeSessions` now starts AT MOST ONE child process — `tmux list-panes`, and only where a tmux binary is on PATH — however many locks and live sessions the machine has. Three decisions carry it: (a) the parent of a lock's pid comes from `/proc` via `cli-identity.readPpid`, so `findTmuxTargetAsync` costs no fork, and an EMPTY pane map short-circuits before it even reads (that is the shape on every machine without tmux); (b) the children of a live session's `_childPid` come from `cli-identity.readChildPids`, so the per-session `pgrep -P` is gone AND with it the 15 s `_childPidCache` that existed only to blunt it — the cache was also a correctness cost, because a wrapper that forked a new claude inside the window stayed unmapped; (c) `getTmuxPaneMapAsync` asks `tmuxOnPath()` (fs.statSync over the PATH entries, memoised 60 s — never a `which`, which would be one more fork) and caches its map for `TMUX_MAP_TTL_MS` = 4 s so a create/kill burst shares one. `isLockClaude` keeps B-2104's `procStart` file read first and, where there is no usable stamp, now asks THE identity (`isCliProcess`) on any procfs machine — the DAEMON snapshot's own rule (`pidLooksClaude`), one implementation — leaving the `ps -o comm=` twin reachable only where there is no /proc at all. The SYNC tmux twins (`getTmuxPaneMap`/`findTmuxTarget`) are DELETED: they had no callers (the old kb line "sync variants remain for boot paths" described boot-restore's own `execFileSync` calls) and they spelled the retired per-pid fork. Measured, same fixture, same box: 50 locks + 50 live sessions went **101 spawns / 360.8 ms → 1 spawn / 6.6 ms**; at 1.5 GB RSS **7,140.6 ms → 74.2 ms** (cold) and **3,540.9 ms → 1.0 ms** (warm); at userW's shape (61 locks, no tmux, 1.5 GB) **8,441.8 ms / 123 spawns → 3.0 ms / 0 spawns**. Gate: scripts/test-discovery-spawn.mjs (the census over the real sweep with master's own module as the negative control) + test-architecture §45 (the grep-derived spawn census, in the build). **r2: the sweep was only ONE of the two readers of "what did this wrapper fork"** — the other, `refreshWebuiPids()` in server.js, is on the KILL path and was still spawning a synchronous `pgrep -P` per live session; see the server.js entry. The lesson for this file is the census's, not the sweep's: §45's file set is now DERIVED, so the next reader of a fact this module owns cannot be invisible to it.

### codex-chat-wrapper.js (P2 verbs, 2.369.20)

  data/bin/codex-chat-wrapper.js — **lane-codex-0159 (2026-09-30): `codex-reset-credit` sends `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume {idempotencyKey}` — the key the verb carries (the engine mints ONE per press), else its own `crypto.randomUUID()` (a server older than the key); ONE retry, only on a consume TIMEOUT and with the SAME key (`VIBESPACE_CODEX_RESET_TIMEOUT_MS` shortens the per-try budget for a suite); `reset_credit_result` echoes `idempotencyKey` + `attempts` (the echo IS the per-process truth the engine reads — no caps advert needed). Every `request()` it makes is judged by scripts/test-codex-protocol-drift.mjs against the measured codex tables: a new call needs a re-measure (`node scripts/measure-codex-protocol.mjs`).** **2.369.157 r4: a failed or empty post-reset `account/rateLimits/read` emits `rate_limits_updated {error, onDemand:true, afterReset:true}` (was `catch { }` — the server could not tell failed from late).** **2.369.157 r3: `codex-reset-credit` emits the post-reset `rate_limits_updated` BEFORE `reset_credit_result` (the server decides the pool on the account's cache; answering first let an eval in the ≤ 20 s re-read gap move the pool off the account the credit had just re-opened) — the answer is emitted whatever the re-read did; pinned by test-codex-pool R15.** **USER-RECORD PRODUCER RULES (round 3-4, 2026-09-07): our copy is spelled `userInputToContent(encodeUserInput(text, attachments))` — the exact inverse of what we SEND, so it matches codex's rollout copy block for block (a hand-rolled attachments-first array doubled every image message on reload); EVERY submission that will not be committed AS WRITTEN is withdrawn with `retractUserRecord(id, reason)` → `event_msg webui_user_retracted` — `turn/start`/`thread/queue/add` threw, the queued item was removed by the user or by Stop before it ran, the wrapper ANSWERS it itself (a slash command: ONE gate `isWrapperSlashCommand`, retracted BEFORE `applySlashCommand` runs because `/compact` takes minutes), or **the `edit` verb REWROTE its text while it waited** (the sixth path, merge review 2026-09-07: the submission really does RUN, just with different words — codex commits the NEW text and can therefore never retire the claim our PRE-EDIT bubble made; gated on `queuedFullText(item.input) !== text` because a no-op save still commits as-written, on the SUCCESS branch only because a failed update leaves the queued text untouched, and by the row's own `cid` so an INHERITED row — which has no record of ours yet — is a no-op). **There is no write-time marker (round 4 deleted `webui_no_commit`): a typed message also has the SERVER's preview copy (`CodexAdapter._buildUserPreview` → `session.buffer`, ws-handler) under the same `webui_msg_id`, it lands FIRST and is the copy that CLAIMS, so anything the wrapper writes on its own record is unreachable — the retraction names the ID, which both copies carry.** The retraction makes the merge withdraw that record's twin CLAIM (an unconsumable claim deletes an unrelated message later), never removes the bubble, and an item the app-server had already drained (`{deleted:false}` = it RAN) is never retracted. The queued peer copy carries its cid as `webui_queue_id`.** chat-input: slash commands are served by the WRAPPER (`applySlashCommand`: /compact → `thread/compact/start` (real compaction; `context_compacted` from the contextCompaction item or the RPC), /review → review/start uncommittedChanges, /model + /effort → the set-* verbs, `command_applied` notice), then **queue-while-busy**: `meta.activeTurnId` set ⇒ `thread/queue/add` + `queued_input` event, never `turn/start` (codex steers a regular turn / rejects review+compact turns). Both `wrapper_meta` records advert `slashCommands`; CodexMessageManager stores them in `_status.slashCommands`, fills the init card and patches it in place (edit op) when they arrive after the card. Live item visibility: mcpToolCall/dynamicToolCall/webSearch/imageView/contextCompaction are recorded as function_call/function_call_output twins (names chosen for collapseKindOf: `mcp__<server>__<tool>` → mcp fold; web_search → search fold, view_image → image fold since 2.369.33/34). The imageView stub records `{path}` only while codex's own rollout copy of the same call carries `{path, detail}` and an `[{input_image, image_url:data:…}]` output twin — the normalizer's call_id dedupe + input_image lifting (2.369.43) is what keeps that ONE card; the stub contract itself is pinned by test-codex-p2-wrapper and test-image-cards.. **Race guard**: `turn/completed` can be processed before the `turn/start` reply's promise resolves (same stdout chunk) — `completedTurns` makes startTurn skip re-marking a finished turn active. Pins: scripts/test-codex-p2-wrapper.mjs (30); test-chat-frame-guard's stub completes turns at once. **Fork echo (B-21e4):** the wrapper's session_meta record dedupes `forked_from` (`[...new Set(chain)]`, own id dropped) and echoes `forked_from_id` from the thread/start|resume|fork response (`Thread.forkedFromId`, 0.153.4 bindings); the fork BOUNDARY ordinal is not on the wire — only the rollout's own session_meta carries it, and extractCodexThreadMeta reads it from the file. **webSearch completion = codex's OWN rollout shape (2.369.43, owner: every card read `{"query":"","action":null}` / "(empty)"):** the v2 WebSearchItem is an EMPTY stub at item/started (query '', action null — the function_call recorded there is the pending card and stays so) and complete only at item/completed, which the wrapper records as `event_msg web_search_end {call_id, query, action, results?, error?}` (key order mirrors codex-rs; `results` omitted when the item has none, `error` only when present) — NOT a function_call_output of raw JSON. The normalizer renders it (src/search-card.js), so the live record and the rollout's own web_search_end are one renderer and one card (the two copies fingerprint-dedupe on re-attach or edit the same call_id in place). Pin: test-codex-p2-wrapper (stub emits the real started-stub + completed pair; asserts the event shape, key order, no output twin, ONE complete card with the rendered result list). **imageView parity (2026-09-06):** a real `ImageView` item carries a `file://` URL (48/48 in the 0.153.4 corpus) and the normalizer strips it when it routes the rollout's own `item_completed` copy — the wrapper's live `view_image` twin strips it too, or the ONE card (both copies use the item id) rewrote its own text on re-attach. Pin: the same suite asserts the stripped path in the live `function_call` arguments + output AND that feeding the rollout copy afterwards leaves one card with unchanged text. **The 0.153.4 rollout writes NO `web_search_end`** (it persists the search as `item_completed` `Extension web.search`) — the wrapper's `web_search_end` is a LIVE-only relay of the same v2 item under the same `exec-…` id; see the cli_version table in the codex-message-manager.js essay before changing either side. **THE INPUT QUEUE — QUEUED vs STEERED (2026-09-06, owner ask; §queue-steer):** the wrapper OWNS the queue but does not KEEP it — `thread/queue/list` is the truth, re-read on every `thread/queue/changed` (the notification carries only `{threadId}`) and published as ONE typed event `queue_changed {items:[{id, msgId, preview≤120, ts, kind, from}], turn_id}` (fingerprint-deduped; also at boot and at each `turn/started`, so a client attaching mid-turn can rebuild the strip from the buffer). `queueMeta` (clientUserMessageId → {kind, msgId, ts, from}) is registered BEFORE the `thread/queue/add` RPC — the change notification's refresh can beat the add's own reply, and an item whose msgId we learn late renders with no bubble chip. The `queue-op` stdin verb serves `steer` / `remove` / `steer-all`. **MEASURED ON A LIVE 0.153.4 app-server, all four load-bearing (the design assumed a `thread/queue/remove` that does not exist):** ① the removal verb is `thread/queue/delete {threadId, queuedSubmissionId}` → `{deleted:true}`; the ClientRequest enum (printed verbatim by the server's own unknown-method error) is add/list/update/delete/reorder/start — **no `remove`** ② `turn/steer {threadId, input, expectedTurnId, clientUserMessageId}` → `{turnId}`, and it does **NOT** dequeue the item even when it carries that item's own clientUserMessageId ⇒ the wrapper deletes it or the message runs twice ③ several `turn/steer` calls inside ONE turn are accepted ⇒ `steer-all` is sequential steers in queue order, each keeping its own input (images + per-message ids survive), never one concatenated blob ④ a `thread/queue/add` on an IDLE thread starts a turn by itself — the app-server drains its own queue, we never call `turn/start` for a drained item. **ORDER IS STEER-FIRST, DELETE-ON-SUCCESS:** a steer failing is a DESIGNED path (`cannot steer a review turn` / `cannot steer a compact turn` = CodexErrorInfo::ActiveTurnNotSteerable, and `expected active turn id \`X\` but found \`Y\`` when the turn ended between the click and the RPC), and on that path the item must stay queued IN PLACE — which delete-first could not restore (re-adding appends). The wire carries only `{code:-32600, message}` (the typed CodexErrorInfo variants never reach the client), so `classifySteerFailure` discriminates on the message TEXT — deliberately, with the strings quoted from the binary's own table. Every outcome rides `queue_op_result {op, id, msg_id, ok, reason, detail}`; a steer that succeeded but whose delete failed reports `ok:true, reason:'steered-not-dequeued'` so the user is warned about a possible double run instead of it happening silently. An OWN-thread `agentMessage` whose text starts with the inter-agent envelope (`Message Type: … / Task name: … / Sender: /root/x`) is ALSO an `agent_message` (author = the Sender line) — it was written FOR another agent, never a reply to the user. **The ENVELOPE is the only signal; `delivery === 'async'` is NOT (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06, MAJOR):** on an own-thread `agentMessage` that flag marks a question/async reply the USER is meant to read, and treating it as inter-agent DROPPED the text from the transcript entirely (an asked question simply vanished). Pinned with the stub: an own-thread `delivery:'async'` message with no envelope must appear as an assistant message. **`meta.agentPath`** (this thread's own path, the reference point that makes a message inbound or outbound) is ASSIGNED from the thread/start|resume reply when it carries one and echoed in the wrapper's `session_meta` record — it used to be READ in three places and never written; 0.153.4's `Thread` struct carries agentNickname/agentRole/parentThreadId but NO agentPath (checked against the installed binary's serde field list), so the '/root' default is what a VibeSpace-spawned thread actually is, and a RESUMED sub-agent conversation gets its real path from codex's own `session_meta` at line 0 of its rollout. `subAgentActivity` items fill the map and emit the live `event_msg sub_agent_activity` (the 0.153.4 rollout carries the same fact as `item_completed/SubAgentActivity`; the normalizer routes both to ONE path). Every item record now rides `recordItem()`, which stamps the notification's `thread_id`/`turn_id` — **both are stripped from `recordFingerprint` (codex-session-store) and `CodexMessageManager.recordKey`, or every buffer record becomes a stranger to its rollout twin (double cards on each attach)**. `caps.threadScoped: true` adverts it. `AGENT_ENVELOPE_RE`/`parseAgentEnvelope` are MIRRORED in src/codex-message-manager.js (a shipped single file cannot require it) — change one, change both. Pins: test-codex-p2-wrapper ④ (stub pushes a child agentMessage / an own-thread envelope one / a subAgentActivity / a plain root reply ⇒ exactly ONE assistant record). RESIDUE: records a PRE-B-7473 wrapper already wrote keep their root-assistant shape (the normalizer cannot tell them from a real reply) — they age out with the buffer; only NEW traffic is gated, and a restart of that session is the immediate cure.

### plugin-loader.js / plugin-manifest.js / plugin-client.js (Plugin Ph2 minimal, 2.369.24)

  The plugin system's first runtime slice (docs/design-harness-plugins.md §3.2–3.3). **Trust model as shipped**: iframe tier = untrusted UI (opaque origin, the published-pages CSP posture — NEVER add allow-same-origin; the bridge exposes only namespaced localStorage, toasts, close); server tier = a separate PROCESS with an IPC-only API (`route`/`tool`/`shutdown`) — plugin code is never require()d into the orchestrator; agent tools = generated shims that carry the calling session's vsst_ token to `/api/agent/plugin-tool/<id>/<name>` (cookie-exempt prefix ⇒ the route validates the bearer itself; unknown token = 401). Invariants: an invalid manifest is LISTED with its errors (never silently skipped) and cannot be enabled; enable/disable is atomic + broadcast; a crashing plugin restarts with backoff and is parked after 5 crashes/10min (never a crash loop against the box); shims are regenerated on every change and removed on disable; `hostVersion` is read from `<rootDir>/package.json` (never a relative require — the 2.341.1 lost-binding class). Trusted client modules, contributed settings/themes/keybindings, install UI, capability enforcement and remote shim shipping are the next slices (B-bb56/B-93f9). **SECURITY POSTURE after the 2.369.43 review (kb-bugfix-invariants “PLUGIN SECURITY BATCH”): a manifest is untrusted input — its free text may reach generated code only as a JSON literal (jsLiteral) and is sanitized once in the validator (cleanText); a declared fs path is collapsed — and its `*` wildcard MODELLED as the string prefix node actually matches (2.369.44) — before the forbidden-root test; contributed agent tools NEED consent (a shim is a program on every session PATH, outside the sandbox — the shipped hello-plugin example is consent-gated now); consent is recorded per PACKAGE (contentHash + source) and the reset is keyed on the REGISTRY RECORD, not on a folder having been replaced (2.369.44 — consent outlives a hand-deleted plugin dir), so replacing the code behind a trusted id disables it and re-prompts; proxied /x/* replies are data (nosniff + sandbox CSP, no document content-type from an untrusted plugin).** Pins: scripts/test-plugin-security.mjs (62) + scripts/test-plugin-loader.mjs (43: validator matrix + the shipped docs/examples/hello-plugin driven end to end — assets/CSP/traversal, IPC routes, tool + shim + 401, lifecycle).

  contributions.js — the second client contribution-point registry (docs/design-harness-plugins.md §3.2 `commands[]` + `menus[] {where, when, group}` + `keybindings[]`), built to window-types.js's rules: DOM-free at import (only telemetry-client), node-imported directly by its gate. `registerCommand({ id, title (string | ctx→string), run(ctx), when?(ctx), icon?, signal? })`, `registerMenuItem({ menu, command | label+run, id?, group?, order?, when?, label?, labelHtml?, disabled?, style?, tooltip?, children?, expand?, separator?, kind?, icon?, danger?, keepOpen?, decorate?, signal? })`, `menuItems(menu, ctx)` → showContextMenu-shaped items, `registerKeybinding({ key, command, when?, inTerminal?, signal? })` + `installKeybindings(document, { signal, getCtx })` (ONE bubble-phase dispatcher, app-lifetime AbortController in app.js), `runCommand(id, ctx)`. **Semantics (do not regress):** items sort by group ('navigation' first, then lexicographic), then `order`, then registration; `when` gates SURFACES (menus/keys) — `runCommand` never consults it (VS Code executeCommand); **SEPARATORS ARE EXPLICIT contributions** (VS Code's automatic between-group rule cannot reproduce the hand-built window menu, which joins Minimize and Close with NO rule when the session block is absent) and leading/trailing/doubled ones collapse; an EMPTY `children` result drops the item (the legacy `if (groups.length)` guards); `mod` = ctrl OR meta (the app's `(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey)` convention), unlisted modifiers must be up; keys inside `.xterm` never match unless `inTerminal`; later bindings win. **Loud:** duplicate/malformed registrations THROW at module load; `runCommand` of an unknown id THROWS + telemetry `command-unknown`; an unknown command named by a menu item / keybinding warns once + telemetry (`menu-unknown-command` / `keybinding-unknown-command`) and is skipped; a throwing `when()` hides the item and warns once; a throwing keybound command is logged + `command-failed`. Every register* returns dispose() and honours `signal` — the plugin host API (plugin-client.js `api.registerCommand/registerMenuItem/registerKeybinding/runCommand`, ids namespaced `plugin:<id>:<slug>`) binds all three to the plugin's AbortController so contributions leave with the plugin; `api.registerMenuItem` REFUSES a `submenu:true` head without an explicit id SLUG (verifier r2 nit: the host's generated `item-N` id used to smuggle an id-less head past the registry's explicit-id rule — a head no member could name in `parent`). **Core dogfoods it, byte-identical:** the sidebar card menu = `session.*` commands + `registerSessionCardMenu()` in session-card.js (ctx `{ app, state, settings, s, card, event, displayName, customName, originalName, onRename, agentOpts }`); the window title-bar/taskbar/window-list menu = `window.*` commands + `registerWindowMenu()` in taskbar.js (ctx `{ app, id, win, s, switchSubmenu, closeLabel }`; `showWindowContextMenu`'s wrapAct fires `onAction(kind)` after items AND submenu children — Task Groups / Move to Desktop — never the Switch-window submenu; the session block REUSES `session.restart` (Restart / Resume labels via the item label override), `session.locate`, `session.properties`); the ⚙ menu = gear-menu.js `registerGearMenu()` (since 2.369.124 a TREE — see the gear-menu.js essay below; `buildGearMenu(app, pop)` renders with escHtml'd labels; mobile-nav's gear shares it via `_showGlobalSettings`). **THE TREE (2.369.124, docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md §2c):** `submenu:true` marks a HEAD (needs an explicit `id` + `label`; forbids command/run/expand/children/separator — its members come through `parent`) and `parent:'<head id>'` files ANY item (a row, a separator, an `expand`, or another head) under it. Validation is LOUD wherever the chain is already known at registration (non-string parent, self-parent, a registered NON-head parent, a parent from another menu, a head chain deeper than two levels — checked from above AND from below, a cycle — the closing edge points at the record being registered, which findRec cannot see, so it is checked explicitly); a parent registered LATER is legal (module load order is not a contract). Resolution is LAZY at `menuItems()` over the VISIBLE heads: an unknown / `when`-hidden / non-head parent warns once (`parent:<menu>:<id>`) + telemetry `menu-unknown-parent` and the row **falls to top level — never dropped** (a lost row is the silent-failure class; the same rule surfaces a disposed head's members). A head's members become its `children` (same sort — NOTE group sorts BEFORE order inside a head too, so members carry no `group` — same separator collapse, `expand` splices INTO the head), an EMPTY head drops itself (the existing empty-submenu rule) unless it carries a `panel` (its content); the produced head item has `submenu:true`, `children`, no `action`, and the renderer hints `panel(ctx)` / `caption` / `keepOpen` / `checked` (a boolean on choice rows) pass through validated; a FUNCTION caption is ALSO handed through unresolved as `captionOf` (verifier r2, 2026-09-21: the Appearance head kept its build-time `14px` beside a stepper that said 15) so the renderer can re-evaluate it LIVE — a string caption carries no captionOf. showContextMenu consumers still read `children` (they know nothing of heads); the gear renderer is the only tree renderer today. Command mode registers every single-key action as `activeWindow.*`/`layout.*`/`desktop.*`/`session.new`/`sidebar.toggle`/`browser.open`/`explorer.open`/`commandMode.toggle`; the palette registers `session.palette`. **SIDE BY SIDE AS VERBS (split UX chunk 2, 2026-09-23, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md R1 ②③ / R2 — no drag ever splits, so the menu and the keys ARE the entries beside the tab strip's button):** the 'window' menu gains, inside `1_window` after Task Groups, ONE `window/side-by-side` submenu **Show side by side ▸** whose children are "**Beside {name} (on the right)**" per OTHER tab of the window's chain (name = the title's part before ` — `), each calling `wm.bindSplit(thisWin, thatWin, {side:'right', announce:true, focus:'anchor'})` — the verb NAMES the side (this window left, the named one right), never a pointer, and the focus stays on the window right-clicked (split r1: it used to land on the named partner); gated on `c.win._tabChain` with ≥ 2 tabs, `layout !== 'split'`, and NOT `app.isMobile` (the phone shows one pane, R6). A chain-less or ONE-tab window gets none of them, so the pre-registry matrix stays byte-identical (the gate's matrix runs every state with no chain AND with a one-tab chain). A tab's right-click opens THAT tab's own window menu (chunk 1), so the submenu excludes the window it was opened on. Every refusal is `{type:'error', code:'queue-op-unsupported', scope:'action', sessionId, error, message}` — and the CLIENT rule is an EXPLICIT SET, not "anything coded": **a per-session `error` is a scoped refusal (renders in chat, window untouched) when it carries `scope:'action'` or one of `SCOPED_REFUSAL_CODES` (input-rejected, not-codex-chat, queue-op-unsupported); everything else is the attach failure it used to be read as** (inc-mt2arppw was `input-rejected`; `not-codex-chat` had been read-only'ing live windows the same way ever since — but `ended-during-attach`, raised right here after the history rebuild, is CODED AND FATAL and must keep taking the view-only rescue; round-1 review caught the over-generalization). The attach payload gained `queue` (`session._normalizer.queueState()`) + `queueSupported`, and `created` carries `queue: []` + `queueSupported: false` (a just-spawned wrapper has reported nothing yet; its own baseline `queue_changed` turns the controls on) — the 2.368.4 enumerate-every-window-birth rule. **THE VERB TABLE (2026-09-07):** the gate is now `capsOf(backend).inputModes.queueVerbs` — no verbs ⇒ "<Harness> owns its own input queue", an undeclared verb ⇒ its OWN sentence from `queueVerbRefusal(op, label)`, each of which says what happens to the message anyway (a refusal that only says "no" leaves the user wondering whether it is lost). The frame grew `afterId` (carried ONLY when the client sent one, because `null` MEANS the front) and `text`; every refusal also carries a machine `reason` beside the sentence. The wrapper gate became a VERB gate too: `wrapperCaps().queueVerbs` (sidecar) or the normalizer's in-band `queueVerbsPublished()` (remote), with a wrapper that adverts `inputQueue` and no list mapped to `LEGACY_QUEUE_VERBS = remove/steer/steer-all` — an old build must neither be asked for a verb it would drop nor lose the verbs it does serve; a verb it does not serve is refused by NAME, listing what it does serve. The attach payload gained `queueVerbs` next to `queueSupported`, so the client renders exactly the controls this process will honour — **`null`, never `[]`, when the server knows nothing** (`created` always, `attached` when neither sidecar nor in-band list is readable): an empty ARRAY is a real answer the client INTERSECTS with, and sending it for "unknown" hid the entire strip from a session the server was serving the legacy three for (round-2 review). **ROUND-2 SERVER HARDENING (2026-09-07):** ① every refusal ECHOES `op` and `id` — this reply never becomes a `queue_op_result`, so the id is the only way the strip can find the row it marked pending (those rows spun forever); ② `edit` is the one verb carrying USER TEXT into a RAW PTY STDIN write, so it is bounded twice, both loudly: `QUEUE_EDIT_MAX_CHARS` (20000 — the wrapper's OWN cap, the one above which it publishes no `text` and therefore offers no edit control; parity-pinned) and, after the frame is built, `QUEUE_OP_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB, the same threshold the `input` case treats as the shredding line — JSON escaping can multiply a control-char string sixfold, so the char cap does not imply the byte one). Both constants live in src/server/wrapper-files.js beside `LEGACY_QUEUE_VERBS`, which itself moved to the PURE `src/backend-caps.js` because the CLIENT applies the same mapping.

Canonical cards: `image_gen` with input `{prompt, path}` and output `status: <status>` + `saved <path>` (base64 `result` NEVER enters a card — the 2.369.35 law), `sleep` with input `{durationMs}` and output `slept 30s` (`formatSleptMs` is the ONE server-side duration formatter; the renderer's countdown formats a DIFFERENT thing, time remaining). Both are `collapseKind: null` — VISIBLE work, because a 20-minute wait folded into "N tool calls" is precisely how a deliberate pause reads as a hang. `_processServerRequest` also renders `mcpServer/elicitation/request` through the existing AskUserQuestion family (`kind:'user_input'`, rows from the wrapper's `payload.questions`; `mode:'url'` falls back to the plain approve card), and `isAllowedServerDecision` spans all five reply vocabularies. **TWO EFFORT FACTS, NEVER ONE (2.369.62):** `_status.effort` = what the CURRENT (or last) turn is running at — the value `_attachUsageMeta` bakes onto every message of that turn — and `_status.effortNext` = the pick that applies from the next turn. Conflating them is how a turn codex ran at 'ultra' reported 'xhigh' on every message: the live buffer held exactly ONE `turn_context` (the wrapper's synthesized copy, quoting a stale spawn env) for a session whose whole life was one app-server-started turn. `_noteEffort(live, next, emit)` is the ONE writer, so every carrier lands the same way — `turn_context` (a record that names an effort also SETTLES the pending question: `effort_next` present = a re-pick is waiting, absent = nothing is), the wrapper's `wrapper_meta` pair (the FALLBACK that makes a mid-turn attach honest when no turn_context is in range), and codex's own `thread_settings_applied` (the THREAD's effort = the NEXT turn's; it must NOT relabel the turn in flight, and only answers "now" before any turn has named one). It also EMITS `{op:'meta', subtype:'effort', data:{effort, effortNext}}` — chat-view routes it to `ChatStatusBar.setEffort`, so a `/effort` typed into the chat or another client's pick moves the chip live instead of waiting for a re-attach. Gate: scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs. **`webui_queue_id` — the SECOND-CLASS user identity (2026-09-07):** the wrapper stamps it on the bubble it writes for a submission it never typed (an INHERITED queue item entering the turn). `_processResponseMessage` reads it into the same `webuiMsgId` field the chip joins on (`_stampUserIdentity`, the ONE writer of the bubble-id ⇄ userMessageIds pair), but it is deliberately second class: it does NOT suppress peer detection (most of the owner's 25 inherited items were agent-to-agent messages and must keep their labelled card, which a `webui_msg_id` would have turned into an anonymous "You" bubble), and `recordKey` STRIPS it (with `webui_queue_via` / `webui_after_commit`) exactly like `webui_peer` so the buffer copy and codex's rollout copy of that message mint the SAME message id — either may be the one that survives the merge. **Round 2:** such a bubble is also marked `midTurn` on the MESSAGE, and `_finalizeStreaming`'s backward scan treats it like a peer card (`m.role === 'user' && originKind !== 'peer-message' && !m.midTurn` is the boundary).
