**A RESUME ANSWERS THE ITEM (lane exit-item-heal, owner 2026-10-03).** After the 15:45 freeze three "… restarting it did not work — resume it if you need it" items sat in For you for hours although all three conversations were resumed minutes after the reboot (two by the coordinator, one by the owner). `healResumed()` runs at the top of server.js `activeSessionsPayload()` — the builder of every active-sessions broadcast AND of a fresh client's first list, so every create, resume and restore passes it — ONE pass per live session and conversation key (a WeakMap on the session object; a fork adopting its own id or a captured id ⇒ a new pass; a pending fork still carrying its parent's id answers nothing — `addressableId`). Each OPEN item of ours under that key (`sessionKeyFor`, the key it was filed under) whose stored `i18n.text.key` is one of TEXTS `failed` / `no-window` / `again` / `respawned` (`HEALS`; never the words) and that was filed BEFORE the session's `createdAt` is resolved through the store's `resolveAnswered(ids, 'resumed', {resumedAt})` — `resolvedBy: 'resumed'` (the system, not the user), `resolvedFact.resumedAt` = the new session's start; one save + one broadcast, the status listeners hear it. The client words it "running again (resumed HH:MM)" on the device's clock (src/lib/user-todos-row.js `resolvedByText(by, t, item)` — the row, the popup, the phone; the For-you window's pane passes the item through `ctx.resolvedBy(by, item)`). Read off the STORE, never `pending`, so it holds across a restart. `no-conversation` stays (nothing to resume). Gate: test-exit-forensics §6d (the real orchestrator files into the real store; resumed by a client ⇒ done with the words; resumed before the filing ⇒ untouched; another conversation ⇒ untouched; a fresh install over the kept store ⇒ resolved, on disk; a second publish writes nothing; PIN + census: the one entry point; CONTROLS: a copy without the pass, a copy without the filed-before rule, a words-matching copy caught by the census).
### src/mount-providers/ — ONE FILE PER STORAGE PROVIDER + ONE REGISTRATION LINE (lane dc-mount-providers, decoupling wave 2c, rv-server M6)
**dirCache (lane mount-argv-dir-cache):** every row that runs rclone declares `dirCache {ttl, poll?}` (src/mount-argv.js builds `--dir-cache-time` / `--poll-interval` from it); only a row of ONE ChangeNotify backend (onedrive, drive) may declare `poll`, and poll < ttl — test-mount-providers ⑥ + test-mount-argv ②.
**The owner's standard (2026-10-04): a member of a family is its own file + one registration line; the core gates on a declared capability row, never on an id.** `src/mount-providers/index.js` (PURE) = `rows` (one `require('./<id>.js')` line per provider, in the order rows are asked — a raw rclone record is adopted by the FIRST row whose `adopts` claims its backend), `byId` (no prototype), `rowOf(type)` (no type → the `default: true` row = s3; an unknown type → `{}`, every cell absent) and `defaultRow`. Each provider file is PURE (requires nothing but a sibling — vibespace.js spreads webdav.js; test-architecture reads the folder into its PURE set): **s3, drive, gmail, onedrive, cloud, webdav, vibespace, sftp, rclone, cephfs**. CELLS (facts): `oauth` (the vendor of the client a record may lend a channel account — google / microsoft / null; `MountManager.OAUTH_CLIENT_VENDOR` is DERIVED from it), `rcloneType`, `presetClient` (`{idAlone, reauthSwitch}` — the D2 client-identity rule: Drive's custom id alone is its identity and Re-authorize may switch it; Gmail's needs the secret), `driveModeDefault`, `sharedDrives`, `s3Share`, `rawRclone` (the generic row), `filesystem: false` + `rclone: false` (Gmail — a sync worker), `daemon: false` + `fstype` + `probeMs` + `hungStrikes` + `cephShare` + `replacesMyStorage` (CephFS — a kernel mount), `revocable` + `everyFileErrors` + `davUrl` (the VibeSpace bridge), `labels` + `syncStateFile` (Gmail). HOOKS (the provider's arms of the old per-type switches, moved verbatim with `this.` → `x.`): `label(m, MM)`, `config(m, out, dec, x)`, `create(m, cfg, x)`, `child(m, cfg, p, x)` (absent = "don't support mount points yet"), `updateChild` / `update(m, patch, setIf, x)` (Gmail answers `'reseed'` on a scope change → the core drops its `syncStateFile`), `rclone(m, env, P, R, x)` → the remote (absent → the default row's), `fromRclone(cfg)` / `adoptRecord(m, x)` + `adopts(rcloneType, MM)` (ONE Google Drive / OneDrive / the cloud list out of a raw rclone record or add), `oauthBacked(m, MM)`, `rootMayBeDenied(m, MM)`, `s3Backend(m)`, `preMount(m, id, x)` (OneDrive's Graph drive resolve, the bridge's self-mount refusal — `undefined` = go on), `mount(id, x)` / `unmount(m, id, mp, finish, x)` / `isMounted(m, x)` / `listFields(m, x)` (Gmail's worker, CephFS's `x._mountCephfs` / `x._kernelUnmount`), `reauthClient(m, x)` (the client Re-authorize signs in with), `writeToken(holder, tok, x)` + `afterToken(holder, x)`. Fact predicates get the class `MM`, lifecycle hooks the manager `x` (suites call the predicates on a bare `this`). **A new provider touches 2 files (its row + one index line); before: src/mounts.js's ~40 branch sites (10 switches / ladders) + the client.** Proof: scripts/test-mount-providers.mjs (a fake `acme` row through ONE added index line drives add / list / config / edit / child / rclone env / OAuth facts / the lent-client offer of the REAL manager; a base-vs-tree DIFFERENTIAL over 20 provider scenarios; two patched-copy controls). NOT moved (named): the client — src/lib/sidebar-mounts.js (43 `mount` + 8 `channel` id branches) and mounts-dialog.js's PROVIDER_LABELS still ladder on types; the census family `mount` (scripts/id-branch-census.mjs) holds them at their baseline.

  **CLIENT CELLS (lane dc-mount-client).** Each row's `client` cell is pure data (i18nKey words): the Source type entry (`pick`, `pickLabel`), the Connect form (`form`, `connect` fields with `when` key tests, `submit` renames), the submount dialog (`child`, `offersChild`), the Edit dialog (`edit`, `editChild`), the sidebar row's words (`tag`/`tagFromSource`, `sync`, `unmountLabel`), the re-authorize names (`names`, `signins`, `driveReauth`), `presets`, the D2 rule (`clientSwitch`) and the dialog widgets (`widgets`). `clientRows()` flattens them (+ id, default, oauth) and GET /api/mounts publishes them once as `providers`; the client renders from them and names no provider (§78 `mount` 0). A new provider = its row (server hooks + client cells) + one index line.

### mounts.js

  **THE ARGV IS ONE PURE BUILDER (lane mount-argv-dir-cache, 2.369.242 — the owner's OneDrive disconnect forensics).** `src/mount-argv.js` `rcloneMountArgs({row, remote, mountpoint, cacheDir, cacheGB, s3, readOnly, hasFlag, rcSocket, dataDir})` writes every mount flag; `_mountArgv(m, …)` hands it the record's EFFECTIVE row (`rowFor(this, m)`, lane mount-liveness's ONE resolver, int241 — `rowOf(child)` is the s3 default row, and /mnt/gdrive_39ai_shared's argv carried `--s3-use-accept-encoding-gzip=false` its drive parent did not) and the backend's s3 fact. THE DIRECTORY CACHE IS A ROW CELL: `dirCache {ttl, poll?}` — onedrive + drive `{5m, 1m}` (rclone's own defaults for a ChangeNotify backend), every other rclone row `{30s}` with no poll flag. We ran OneDrive at 30 s under rclone's default 1 m poll (poll < ttl broken), so every root listing older than 30 s was a Graph round trip (109 entries, 1.4–2.1 s; warm 5 ms) and the 60 s sweep's `ls` was cold by construction. THE LOG: `_openMountLog(id)` opens data/mount-logs/<id>.log APPEND (it was 'w' at every spawn — the dead daemon's last words destroyed), rotates to `.1` past 1 MB before the spawn, writes one `LOG_MARK` line per spawn; `tailMountLog(id, n, {current})` is a bounded (64 KB) read — `current` = the newest daemon's lines (the start verdict's tail-2), else the previous daemon's last words too. The fd is opened right before `spawn` (the early refusals no longer leak it). THE RC SOCKET: `_rcSocketReady` (hasFlag('rc-addr')) = `rcSocketPath` (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/vibespace-mounts/<id>.sock`, else `/tmp/vs-mounts-<uid>/`; never under dataDir, never on a network fs by statfs magic — bindfs/NFS/SMB/FUSE/Ceph) + sock-path's `ensureSocketDir` 0700 verdict + an unlink of the dead daemon's socket (measured on v1.69.3: a socket left by a SIGKILLed daemon makes the next mount die "Failed to start remote control … address already in use"). `_rcStats(m)` = ONE `rclone rc --unix-socket <sock> core/stats` + ONE `vfs/queue` child, 2 s bound each, async → `{stats, queue}` | `{error}` — a seam the health sweep may read; nothing calls it yet. Gates: test-mount-argv (fast: the production OneDrive argv as fixture, the dirCache census, s3/child legs, the rc rule, the twin census = no mount flag literal outside mount-argv.js, log legs, `_rcStats` over a fake rclone, 3 patched-copy controls), test-mount-starting ⑧ (a killed daemon's last line survives the remount).

  **PROVIDER ROWS (lane dc-mount-providers).** Every per-type switch / ladder (`_sourceLabel`, `config`, `add` + its raw-rclone normalization, `addChild`, `update`, `_rcloneFor`, `_normalize*Record` → `_adoptRawRclone`, the mount / unmount / health / liveness branches, `_oauthBacked`, `_revocable`, the client-identity rule, `startDriveAuthForMount`, `applyDriveToken`'s token write, `canShareFromMount` / `canCephShare`, `listSharedDrives`, the CephFS My-storage import) asks the record's row through the module function `rowOf(m)` (src/mount-providers/, above); the GENERIC lifecycle (start / adopt / starting-state / cache scan / health / stranded / shares) stays here. `_kernelUnmount(m, mp, finish)` = CephFS's sudo umount, reached by its row's `unmount` hook.

  **STARTING — A DAEMON STILL REBUILDING ITS CACHE (lane mount-cache-scan, 2.369.213).** `_mountInner` → spawn → `_watchStart(m, mp, pid)`: the `_starting` map (`{pid, since, files, capped}` → the row's `starting`), `blockPath(mp, ceiling + 60 s)`, `_countCacheFiles` (a child `find -printf .`, cap 200 000), `_waitMounted(m, pid)` → 'mounted' | 'died' | 'hung' (no ≥ 30-tick CPU progress for 60 s) | 'ceiling' (15 min) → `_startSettled` (mounted → `_afterMounted`: IO probe, unblock, access check; "is not empty" → `_mountInner(id, {retried: true})` once; otherwise the error + unblock, hung/ceiling also kill + backoff). A caller gets the real verdict within `quickMs` (5 s), else `'starting'` (the route answers `{success: true, starting: true}`). `mount()` hands a second caller the in-flight promise; `_mountInner` answers `'starting'` while `_starting` holds the id and ADOPTS a daemon already on the mount point (`_daemonPids`). `_healthSweep` skips starting records; its hung branch spares a daemon whose CPU advanced during the probe. Timing: `MountManager.STARTING` (tests set `_startingT`). A connect-time stranded move → `_noteStranded` → the row's `stranded`.

  **COMPANY PRESETS FROM THE PRESETS DIRECTORY (lane cluster-presets, 2.369.200, B-53fe).** `drivePresets()` asks `src/server/cluster-presets.js`'s process-wide instance (`sharedPresets().entries('gdrive')`) FIRST — the directory's `gdrive-clients.json` (the cluster Secret) with `override/gdrive-clients.json` (the release) merged per key — and only when the directory says nothing about Google clients (`null`: neither file) falls back to the env rung `_envDrivePresets()` (VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS through PURE `parseDriveClients`, then the legacy single pair as `default`; an unparseable / non-array env logs `describeJsonError` and answers `[]`). ONE rung, never a mix: while the directory speaks, an env-only key is not served. Every Google consumer (`_driveClient`, gmail-sync `_client`, the drive-defaults route, the Gmail channel row through the integration store's injected `drivePresets`) asks this one function, so a `..data` swap reaches all of them in the same instant; a running rclone mount takes a rotated secret at its next (re)mount; a withdrawn key is `null` for the mount that named it (never another preset). Gate: test-mounts-oauth (17, control = the env-only reader).

  **A MOUNT'S OWN OAUTH CLIENT, LENT TO A CHANNEL ACCOUNT (2.369.195, design-integrations-per-account §2.7).** Two halves split by who may see what. `oauthClientsFor(vendor)` = the READ-ONLY offer: `{mountId, name, type, email, clientIdPrefix}` (first 12 chars) per TOP-LEVEL record whose type lends a client (`OAUTH_CLIENT_VENDOR`: drive/gmail → `google`, onedrive → `microsoft`) and that holds its OWN client — `clientId` AND `clientSecretEnc` (`_lendsOAuthClient`; a preset record, an id-only record, a child and `my-storage` lend nothing). `oauthClientOf(mountId, {vendor})` = SERVER-ONLY, no route: with `vendor` named, another vendor's mount is refused `mount-client-vendor` BEFORE `_dec` (verify r1 — nothing is decrypted for a refused body, and the refusal names the vendor, never the key state; a mounts copy with the order swapped is ⑬'s control), then the client DECRYPTED with `.mounts-key` for the channels engine, which re-seals it under `.channels-key` in the same call; refusals are TYPED (`mount-gone` / `mount-no-client` / `mount-client-vendor` / `mount-secret-undecryptable`) and never carry a value. **Verify r2: `oauthClientIdOf(mountId, {vendor})` is the KEY-LESS HALF** — gone / no client / another vendor / the client ID, nothing decrypted — and `oauthClientOf` is it plus `_dec`; a caller that can refuse on the id alone (the registry's id rule, a sign-in's client compared by id) asks the head first. `lentName(m)` bounds a name for every list row and message (control chars out, 60 — a newline in a name forged a journal line). Wired by src/server/channels-wiring.js (`getMounts` → the engine's `mountClients {list, head, of}`). Gate: test-channels-engine ⑮.

  **AT-REST ENCRYPTION MOVED OUT (P0b, design §14.7):** the inline `_key()`/`_enc()`/`_dec()` are gone; `_enc`/`_dec` delegate to `src/secret-box.js` on the SAME `data/.mounts-key` (decision 24 — the key file does not move), the ciphertext format is byte-identical (parity-pinned both directions by scripts/test-secret-box.mjs, so no stored mount secret is re-encrypted), and the ONE behaviour change is the fix mounts inherits: a key file that exists but cannot be read is now a TYPED error instead of a silently minted replacement key that orphaned every stored ciphertext (the bare `catch` at the former :360-367).

  **`applyDriveToken(id, token, client?)` — A CLIENT SWITCH LANDS WITH ITS TOKEN (2.369.165, integrations 4a, D2 of docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md §6).** The optional `client` (`{clientPreset}` or `{clientId, clientSecret}`, the body's `client` on `POST /api/mounts/:id/drive-token`) is written TOGETHER with the token: a record never holds a new client beside the old token (the Edit dialog's silent save, `invalid_client` at the next refresh). The two forms EXCLUDE each other — a custom id wins at resolve (`_driveClient`), so a preset stored beside a leftover custom id would mint under the preset and refresh under the custom client; a preset CLEARS `clientId` + `clientSecretEnc`, a custom client clears the preset; a custom id without its secret is refused by name before anything is written. Google Drive records only (refused by name otherwise) — a Gmail switch lands through `update()`'s PATCH `{clientPreset, token}`, which already writes both in one save and restarts the sync. The children bounce exactly as for a plain re-authorize. Gate: test-mount-oauth-probe §4 (a real MountManager in a scratch dir, mount/unmount stubbed).

Never remove the shim 'because modprobe exists in the current image'**); flat-connections model — no special my-storage slot, env auto-migrates to a normal mount. **SUBMOUNT model (2.108.0→2.108.2, user-refined twice): ANY top-level storage record can hold submounts — children reference the parent via `parentId` + their own path fields (`remote:path`) and resolve connection through `_connOf()` at use time (addChild allows any non-child parent; no nesting). `kind:'credential'` now means CREDENTIAL-ONLY (root unmountable — bucket-scoped token): UI shows a key ICON in place of the status dot (no text badge, user directive) and NO Connect action; mount() auto-heals kind on a later successful root probe — refreshing the credential's token/keys heals every child (update() bounces mounted children). AUTO-RECONNECT supervision: desired now ONLY reflects user intent — internal teardowns (hang defense) keep desired=mounted and _healthSweep's dead-mount branch remounts with backoff 1→2→5→10min (_maybeAutoRemount; _noteReconnectBackoff), auth-class errors (denied/revoked/expired/AccessDenied…) excluded from retry so the actionable message survives; unmount(id,{internal:true}) is the internal teardown that doesn't rewrite intent; mount() is wrapped by a _connecting guard (one connect in flight per record). rcloneBin() NFS trap: executing the 57MB binary from a network FS demand-pages it per exec (~22s measured) — _fastBin copies it once to ~/.cache/vibespace keyed by size+mtime (22s→0.03s), detection via /proc/mounts longest-prefix fstype**) **OAuth-death detection (2.368.6, real OneDrive incident): a dead refresh token hides behind a HEALTHY-looking mount — fuse dir cache keeps listings working while every download fails 'unauthenticated: Unauthenticated' (EIO on every file open, zero UI signal). _oauthBacked mounts (drive/onedrive/cloud/rclone-OAuth) now get the fresh-process backend probe on a slow clock (10min; every sweep while an auth error shows or the mountpoint fails), the denied-regex knows the OAuth phrasings (unauthenticated/invalid_grant/InvalidAuthenticationToken), the health message names the fix (re-authorize), and the client button regex matches it. Gated by scripts/test-mount-oauth-probe.mjs (15). Do not narrow _revocable back to 'my own Drive can(not) expire' — it can. SECOND HALF (2.368.7): an EIO-wedged daemon SURVIVES fusermount -uz, so the re-auth bounce stacked a fresh daemon on the dead-token one and changed nothing (4 leaked daemons found); unmount() now polls _daemonAlive and kills survivors BEFORE resolving (bounce callers mount() right after — a later kill would murder the fresh daemon), and mount() kills any stale daemon before spawning. Never resolve an unmount while the daemon lives. TRUE ROOT CAUSE (2.368.8, corrects 2.368.6's dead-token diagnosis): the token was ALIVE — refresh/list/upload all worked, only the /content DOWNLOAD endpoint 401d (Microsoft's migrated consumer OneDrive vs rclone 1.65.2; A/B with identical config: 1.69.3/1.75.0 download fine). Pin bumped to v1.69.3 (stays in the Cloudflare-STS-safe 1.63–1.69 range) + restore() self-heals data/bin/rclone to the pin at boot (nothing else ever re-runs the installer — a pin bump alone reaches no existing install). The sweep also runs _probeBackendRead (1-byte cat of the first root file) because this failure mode PASSES lsf — auth-class failures must be located per-ENDPOINT (refresh/list/upload/download), never collapsed into 'token dead'.** **STRANDED WRITES (2.369.15, real OneDrive "is not empty, use --allow-non-empty" incident): a mount point that is NOT mounted is a bare local directory, and anything written there (the task store's generated TASK.md recreated a whole tree while OneDrive was down) both disappears once the storage reconnects and blocks that reconnect. Never `--allow-non-empty` (it hides the files). `_ensureMountpointDir(mp, {quarantine:true})` on BOTH connect paths (rclone + cephfs; never on the mount-point edit path) moves leftovers aside to a sibling `<mp>.stranded-<ts>/` — never delete, never merge — recreates the mount point empty and broadcasts a level-2 server-notice naming the path and items. `shadowedBy(p)` = the registered storage whose mount point contains p but is not mounted (gmail/credential records excluded; `isMounted(m, live)` accepts a pre-read /proc/mounts): files.js refuses every op under it with 503, task-groups skips its TASK.md and retries on every `mounts-updated` (the wiring tees the broadcast into `onMountsUpdated` + one boot resync after mounts exist — the constructor's boot regen runs before them). ### harnesses/ (the harness registry — S1/S4/S6, 2.369.18–22)

  **`store.lastTurnModel` / `store.lastTurnEffort` (B-6b6d)** — "what did this CONVERSATION last run at", for the resume ladder (src/resume-continuity.js). The hook's PRESENCE is the declaration that this harness can answer, so there is no second boolean to drift: **codex** declares both (its rollout writes a `turn_context` per turn), **opencode** declares the model (`serve.facts().sessionModel`, round 2), **claude** declares NEITHER (round 2 — its transcript cannot express the model's context variant and records no effort at all; see src/session-store.js), **shell** and the generic ACP harness neither. ws-create asks the descriptor and never branches on a backend id — this is where the B-21e4 codex-only env post-fill went. A hook returning `''` means "this conversation has nothing recorded" ⇒ the instance default, LOGGED; a missing hook means "this harness cannot answer" ⇒ send nothing.

  src/plugin-manifest.js — PURE manifest validator + the consent vocabulary (Ph2 2.369.24, Ph4 2.369.30): validateManifest(raw, {hostVersion, folderName, homeDir, forbiddenRoots}) normalizes tiers (none|iframe|module; "trusted" = alias), clientEntry, contributes windows/agentTools/routes/settings(boolean|string|number|select)/themes, capabilities.server {fs.read/write (abs or ~, no .., never covering a forbidden root), childProcess (spawn⇒childProcess warned), net (declared only)}; needsConsent(m) = module tier, any declared server capability, OR any contributed agentTool (2.369.43 — a generated shim is a program on every session PATH, outside the plugin sandbox); capabilitySummary(m) = [{id,text,params}] the SAME items server (409 payload) and client (dialog via t(text, params)) render; capabilitiesHash(m) = key-order-independent fingerprint of the consent surface (tier/server/capabilities/agent tools/routes) — array order is significant by design. **2.369.43 hardening: cleanText() strips control chars + U+2028/U+2029 from EVERY free-text field (description/label/window title/tool description/setting+theme labels) — free text ends up in generated code, so it is sanitized ONCE here; normalizeFsPath COLLAPSES the path (own segment walk — the file has ZERO requires by design) before the forbidden-root prefix test, because node's permission model collapses `//`, `/./` and `/.` (`--allow-fs-read=/.` = the whole filesystem); the fs-write summary says "write AND read" (permissionArgs adds a read grant per write path).** **2.369.44: normalizeFsPath also MODELS node's `*`** — node reads a declared path only up to the FIRST `*` and grants every path whose STRING starts with what came before it (probed against node v24: `--allow-fs-read=/t/a/*` and `/t/a/*/ignored` both read `/t/a/b/c/f.txt`; `/t/a/z*` reads `/t/a/zz.txt` but not `/t/a/b/…`; `/*` reads /etc/hostname). Treating a pattern as a plain path let `["/*"]` and `["<parent-of-a-forbidden-root>/*"]` pass validation and grant the install/data dir. Now: at most ONE `*`, only as the LAST character (a mid-pattern `*` is refused LOUDLY — it grants everything before it and silently ignores the rest); the containment test runs on the literal prefix (`r.startsWith(prefix)` — a wildcard over a parent of a forbidden root is forbidden, and `…/dat*` catching `…/data` too); `/` and `/*` are refused with or without roots; `/dir/*` is never collapsed into `/dir*` (different grants — the latter also covers `/dirty`), and the accepted pattern is stored VERBATIM so the string the owner consented to is the string node gets. **B-7638: the collapse rule and the wildcard rule MEET at `~/.*`** — node only collapses a LONE `.` segment, so `<home>/.*` is the prefix `<home>/.` (dotfiles), but collapsing the dot HERE emitted `<home>*`: a string prefix covering the whole home directory AND every sibling path that starts with those characters (`/home/u*` reaches `/home/u2/…`). A home-dir glob may not widen to every user, and the widening was invisible — the manifest said one thing and node was handed another — so a `.` segment immediately before `*` is REFUSED with the prefix it would have produced (write the directory `…/` or a literal name prefix). `~/.config/*`, `~/./*` (a lone `.` node itself collapses) and `~/.ssh` are unaffected. Invariant: no other module mutates or reinterprets a manifest — and any rewrite this file performs on a declared path must be one node performs too, or it must refuse.

A repeat fingerprint on a turn_context is a REFRESH of one turn, never a second turn: `mergeCodexRecords` keeps the FIRST copy's position and folds the better copy's VALUES onto it — codex's own always wins (`isWrapperTurnContext` = `payload.wrapper === true` or the legacy `modelPinned !== undefined` marker), a later wrapper copy overrides only an earlier wrapper copy (that is the wrapper's own late correction), and codex's copy deletes `effort_next` (nothing is pending in a rebuilt history). The fold never mutates a shared parsed payload — `kept` is sortRecords' own shallow copy and gets a NEW payload object. `chatStatus()` gained `effortNext` alongside `effort`, filled from the wrapper sidecar, `turn_context`, `wrapper_meta` and `thread_settings_applied` in that ranking. **SETTINGS TWINS fold the same way (r2 review):** our `thread_settings_applied` and codex's differ in key set, so the fingerprint can never see them as twins — `settingsSignature()` keys on the VALUES both spellings carry (model / approval_policy / reasoning_effort / personality) and the fold is scoped to ADJACENCY among settings records within one turn, because `high → ultra → high` is a real sequence and folding the third into the first would leave a rebuilt status reporting `ultra`; codex's unmarked copy replaces our `wrapper: true` one in place, and `lastSettings` only ever points at a record that really made it into `merged`. Gate: scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs ⑤⑥⑥b. **THE ID-KEYED USER TWIN (2026-09-07, mergeCodexRecords):** one user message reaches a rebuild TWICE — the wrapper's buffer copy (written as the text passed through it, carrying `webui_msg_id`) and codex's rollout copy (written when the app-server COMMITS it into a turn, carrying its own `msg_…` id and nothing of ours). `recordFingerprint` keys the first by ID and the second by CONTENT, so they never dedupped: measured on the owner's real session, all three typed messages rendered TWICE after a reload, and the queued path can even put the two copies in DIFFERENT turns (ours at send time, codex's in the turn that drained it), where a turn-scoped content key would not have collided either. Keying user records on content is wrong on BOTH sides (round 2, 2026-09-07 — two different sends of the same text are two messages): the round-1 content key for an inherited bubble deleted the second of two same-text steers on reload, and the pre-existing content key for CODEX's own records deleted **27 of the 95** user messages in the owner's own rollout and **133 across the local corpus** of 89 rollouts (every collision a different `id` AND a different `create_time` — distinct submissions, zero genuine duplicates). So EVERY user record is keyed by the id its producer minted: ours by `userRecordIdentity` (webui_msg_id / client_msg_id / **webui_queue_id** — the cid a previous wrapper minted, one namespace because it names the same submission), codex's by `codexRecordIdentity` (its `msg_…`, own namespace). Pre-0.15x records carry no id (144/572 in the corpus, all in files ≤2026-05, none mixed) and fall back to a CONTENT key — but ours and codex's stay in SEPARATE namespaces there too (`user#ours:` / `user#codex:`), so `seen` can only ever collapse one producer's own record; that is what makes "a record dropped as a duplicate has already had its twin effect applied" true. The ours↔codex pair is retired by the **CLAIM** (`userTwinKeys`, turn-independent): every copy of OURS claims its content key and the next codex-side copy consumes it and is dropped — n copies in, n bubbles out, in order, with OUR copy surviving so the queue chip's `webuiMsgId` join and the live message id are preserved. **FORWARD ONLY, never a pre-pass:** letting a late claim swallow an EARLIER codex record would DELETE an old message from history the moment its text was typed again after the buffer had rotated away (a duplicate is a nuisance, a deletion is data loss). The producers of ours that write AFTER the commit — the app-server's drained `item/completed` twin and the IDLE peer path — cannot be retired by a forward claim, so they say so with `webui_after_commit` (`twin.late`) and YIELD to an unconsumed codex copy of the same content **in the same turn** (dropping themselves, never deleting anything); an early copy never yields, so a same-text neighbour cannot swallow it. One more asymmetry, deliberate: a record short-circuited by `seen` retires the claim it stands for ONLY when its identity was inferred from content (a pre-0.15x record) — there a "duplicate" is a guess, and an unretired claim would later delete an unrelated message. `userRecordIdentity` / `codexRecordIdentity` / `userContentKey` are the ONE spelling of each question, shared by the fingerprint and the twin rule. **ROUND 3 — ONE SPELLING, AND A CLAIM ONLY WHEN THERE WILL BE A TWIN.** (a) `userContentKey` now normalises each content block before hashing: an `input_image` is compared on `{type, image_url}` alone, because codex stamps its own `detail` on the block it persists (34 of the 40 image blocks in the local corpus, `input_text` always exactly `{type,text}`) — the record-level `TWIN_VOLATILE_FIELDS` rule applied inside the array. The other half of that pair is upstream: THREE producers write our copy (the server preview `CodexAdapter._buildUserPreview`, the wrapper's chat-input record, the inherited-queue bubble) and two of them hand-rolled `[...attachments, text]`, reversing codex's own order (0 of 5489 corpus user records begin with an image) — they all spell it `userInputToContent(encodeUserInput(…))` now, and the PREVIEW is the one that matters most because it carries the same `webui_msg_id` and is written first, so it wins the fingerprint and its key is the one that claims. (b) `userTwinKeys` returns `claims`, TRUE for every copy of ours (round 4 removed the write-time exemption): a submission answered by the wrapper itself (its slash commands) never becomes a user message, so a claim under it can never be consumed and would later DELETE an unrelated codex-only record of the same text (round-2 finding ④'s second back door) — but a MARKER could not say so, because the copy that claims is the server's PREVIEW (written first, and only the wrapper knows its own command list; the r3 marker was inert in production and its test scaffold simply had no preview). `webui_no_commit` survives on WEBUI_USER_MARKERS as a compat strip only, so an r3-era wrapper's buffer still keys like the same message (dtach outlives an update). Every case now speaks out of line: `mergeCodexRecords` keeps `oursByIdentity` (submission id → the content key that claimed under it) and a `webui_user_retracted` event (`retractionIdOf`) withdraws exactly one claim by IDENTITY — never by content, because the text can be a megabyte data URL and a second copy of this file's key algorithm inside the wrapper would drift. Clamped at zero, idempotent under `seen`, a no-op for an unknown id; the RECORD is never dropped, only its claim. (c) The queued PEER copy now carries its app-server cid as `webui_queue_id`, so it has an identity to be retracted by — and two peer messages with the same text in one turn stop colliding on the content key. Gates: scripts/test-queue-steer.mjs ⑨ (rollout-shape fixture scripts/fixtures/codex-steer-all-rollout.jsonl + (j) = the round-2 and round-3 scenarios, each with a negative control loaded from a PATCHED COPY of this file), scripts/test-codex-p2-wrapper.mjs ⑥⑦ (the real wrapper's own bytes, rebuilt against synthesized codex copies; ⑦ also compares the server preview and the wrapper record BYTE FOR BYTE and drives every retraction path), scripts/test-peer-msg-card.mjs (both peer orders). **SUB-AGENT CLASSIFICATION (2026-09-24, owner: "截图里这么多subagent啥情况，为啥没自动filter掉").** A codex 0.153 multi-agent v2 child's OWN session_meta (keys measured on this box, 35 of 48 rollouts under 2026/09): `{session_id, id, [forked_from_id], parent_thread_id, timestamp, cwd, originator, cli_version, source: {subagent: {thread_spawn: {parent_thread_id, depth, agent_path, agent_nickname, agent_role}}}, thread_source: "subagent", agent_nickname, agent_path, model_provider, base_instructions: {text, provenance}, history_mode: "paginated", [subagent_history_start_ordinal], multi_agent_version: "v2", context_window: {window_id}}` — `agent_role` null on every child measured; 32/35 also carry `forked_from_id` + a COPY of the parent's meta on line 2. The classification is ONE rule, `classifyCodexThread` in src/discovery-facts.js, read from the thread's OWN first session_meta (whole payload, not just `source`): the nested `thread_spawn` and the top-level `thread_source: "subagent"` are two spellings of one fact, either one ⇒ agentKind `subagent` with `parentThreadId`/`agentNickname`/`agentPath`; `source.subagent: "review"` ⇒ review; any other `source.subagent` shape ⇒ subagent; a USER fork (`forked_from_id`, no thread_source subagent) stays PRIMARY. No role is synthesized from `agent_path` (a path leaf is a task slug, not a role — a made-up badge would be a claim codex never made); the name stays the nickname (deriveCodexAgentName, moved to discovery-facts with the classifier). The local listing already classified correctly before this (the owner's flood was the sidebar's persisted ALL — see sidebar.js); what was missing was the REMOTE twin (SC lines) and a gate. RECORD SHAPE (one JSON line per event, stdout + buffer file): {ts,type:'acp',kind} with kinds session/config/user/prompt_start/prompt_end/update(raw SessionUpdate, replay:true during load)/permission_request/permission_resolved/client_request/notification/notice/peer_result — documented in the file head; the buffer IS the history (no transcript API in ACP). Sidecar meta = caps {frameFile:true, peerMessage:false}, streaming, sessionId, model/agentMode/configOptions/modes/availableCommands/todos/usage/pendingRequests/acp{agentInfo,capabilities}. TURN INVARIANTS (review batch after 2.369.31, kb-bugfix-invariants "ACP WRAPPER: STOP DIDN'T STOP…"): the turn is claimed synchronously but `fetchContextPrefix()` is a real HTTP round trip, so `runPrompt` re-checks its OWN handle's `cancelled` after the await and a cancelled prompt ends as prompt_end 'cancelled' WITHOUT dispatching (a lone prompt_end is legal — prompt_start is a no-op in the normalizer and the consumer only toggles streaming); the boot-failure notice fires on ANY exit before the session is ready, exit code 0 included (finalizeExit exits synchronously, so boot()'s own catch never runs from the child-exit path — the gate on code!==0 left a blank window). Gate: scripts/test-acp-harness.mjs (107) — cancel-during-await, queued+interrupt, Stop-drops-the-queued-nudge, Stop-inside-the-stop-check-round-trip, deny-with-no-reject-option, exit-0-before-initialize, each with a positive control. **THE BOOKKEEPING NUDGE IS OURS, NOT THE USER'S (B-7638, three residuals):** ① a Stop landing INSIDE the `/api/agent/stop-check` round trip must not be followed by a nudge turn — the answer lands after the interrupt (activePrompt is already null), so the old code walked into runPrompt and BILLED a turn the user had just stopped, with a reminder appearing out of nowhere as the only trace; the interrupt bumps `stopEpoch` and aborts the in-flight request, and an answer whose epoch is gone is discarded with a logged reason (the latch is never set, so the NEXT completed turn nudges normally). ② when it queues behind a running turn it queues with `silentQueue` — a `queued_input` for an internal reminder painted a "Queued" chip on a bubble that does not exist (peer messages already ride silentQueue); it still appears in `queue_changed` as kind 'system', so the strip stays honest about what is waiting. ③ the 'queue-cleared' notice counts USER entries only — a dropped PEER message is not the user's to re-send either (it goes back to the delivery ladder and arrives on its own), so nudges AND peers are subtracted; the log line keeps the true total (`dropped=N (nudges=M, peers=P)`). **THE INPUT QUEUE (2026-09-06):** ACP v1 has no queue verb, so `promptQueue` IS the queue — and therefore the wrapper is its PUBLISHER: `queue_changed {items:[{id,msgId,preview,ts,kind,from}], turn_id}` on every push/drain/drop/remove (plus an empty baseline right after the session is up), `queued_input {msg_id, turn_id}` where the old "Queued — runs after the current turn" NOTICE used to be (the state is now a chip on the bubble; codex parity, one client path), and the `queue-op` stdin verb for `remove` only. A steer that somehow reaches this wrapper answers `queue_op_result {ok:false, reason:'not-steerable'}` — `backend-caps.inputModes.steer=false` stops it at the ws layer and `AcpAdapter.formatQueueOp` refuses it with a reason, so this arm exists purely so nothing is ever dropped in silence. `remove` obeys the same two rules Stop already obeyed: a removed PEER entry goes back to the delivery ladder (`peer_result ok:false`, the consumer re-stashes), and a removed NUDGE entry clears `nudgeTurnActive` (per-turn state dies with the turn it belongs to). Removing an id that already drained answers `reason:'gone'` — never a fake success. **Stop reports its drop as removals**: each dropped entry gets its own `queue_op_result {op:'remove', ok:true, msg_id, reason:'stopped'}` BEFORE the emptied republish — the normalizer clears the chip of anything that leaves the queue with no result (= "it ran"), so a bare empty `queue_changed` told the user their message had RUN when Stop had thrown it away (round-1 review). Order is the fix; the result stamps `Removed` first and the republish then leaves those bubbles alone. **REORDER + EDIT (2026-09-07):** `promptQueue` is a local array, so the verb table adds `reorder` and `edit` as splices — driven by the SAME relative frame the codex wrapper translates (`afterId:null` = the front; an anchor that has left puts the entry BACK where it was and answers `reason:'anchor-gone'`), with the same exclusion rule for edit (the first text block takes the new words, every other content block stays in place) and the same two refusals: a PEER entry is not yours to rewrite and a NUDGE entry is VibeSpace's own bookkeeping (`reason:'not-editable'`), an empty edit is `reason:'empty-text'`. `run-now`/`run-all` are declared FALSE for a structural reason, not an unfinished one: this queue only HAS entries while a prompt is running (an idle wrapper dispatches immediately), so "run it now" could only ever answer busy — a frame that arrives anyway says exactly that (`reason:'not-startable'`). Entries carry their full `text` (user entries only) so the client's edit control opens the message rather than the preview, and `ACP_QUEUE_VERBS` is advertised in the sidecar AND on every `queue_changed`. Pins: test-acp-harness (reorder/edit/anchor-gone/empty-edit/not-startable + the advert parity with the caps row; negative control: an anchor-ignoring reorder fails the leg).

  src/opencode-serve.js — OpenCode serve-mode STORE FACTS (S9 of design-harness-plugins §2.4, B-03f2; SHARED — facts about a machine). WHY: the ACP harness has no transcript files (OpenCode keeps sessions in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db), so stopped OpenCode conversations never reached the sidebar. `opencode serve` (verified 1.18.29, OpenAPI at /doc) exposes that store on 127.0.0.1. THREE PIECES: (1) OpencodeServeClient — fetch over a base URL, 1.5s default timeout, every failure an OpencodeServeError {status, code: timeout|network|http|NotFoundError…}; listAllSessions = /project × `/session?scope=project&directory=<worktree>` deduped (VERIFIED 1.18.29 on the real store: a bare `directory=` is an EXACT-directory filter — `directory=/` lists NOTHING, which the first live run caught as "0 sessions"; `scope=project` lists the whole project; a serve's bare /session is scoped to ITS cwd's project, so the iteration is the safe shape); v1 `/session/:id/message?limit=` returns the NEWEST N, so the first user message comes from v2 `/api/session/:id/message?limit=3&order=asc`; fork = POST /session/:id/fork?directory= (body {messageID?}) → the new Session (title "<parent> (fork #n)", no parentID — parentID means a SUB-AGENT child). Basic auth only when OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is in the spawn env. (2) createServeLocator — ONE instance per VibeSpace: reuse data/opencode-serve.json {port,pid,startedAt,command,cwd} when /global/health answers AND its own project is safe (a previous server's child that outlived a SIGKILL restart; never killed by stop() — only our own child is), else spawn `<cmd> serve --port <free> --hostname 127.0.0.1 --log-level WARN` detached + stdio ignored under agentEnv() **from its own empty data/opencode-serve/cwd** (2.369.50 — see WHERE IT RUNS below), wait ≤20s for health (1.2s locally), write the record atomically, probe /doc ONCE → onCaps({fork}) (the CLI version comes from /global/health — /doc's info.version is the API doc's own "1.0.0") — the ONLY writer of capsOf('opencode').fork (setVerifiedCap in backend-caps, PURE in-place row mutation) which cli-env then BROADCASTS as 'harness-caps-updated' (open clients learned fork:false from /api/home BEFORE the lazy start — the notify law). Keeper: exit → respawn after 1s·2^n (≤30s), crash counter resets after 60s of uptime, PARKED after 5 crashes (loud in user actions, silent in the poll), stop() on process exit (stopOnExit) — a SIGKILLed server leaves the serve running for the next boot to reuse. Started LAZILY by the first discovery, never at boot, only when cli-env resolved the CLI AND autostart is on: `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` disables it explicitly, and the test-harness belt `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` disables it implicitly (every worktree smoke sets it and SIGKILLs its server — a spawned serve outlives that kill and would pile up per `npm run ci`; `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=1` wins over the belt); with autostart off a RECORDED live instance is still reused, otherwise discover is [] and user actions name the switch. **WHERE IT RUNS AND WHAT IT MAY TOUCH (2.369.50, the 2.369.42 runaway — full incident in kb-bugfix-invariants):** OpenCode boots an INSTANCE per DIRECTORY and each instance recursively indexes + inotify-watches that tree (`fff-*` fast-file-finder + `notify-rs` threads). Measured with /proc against a real 1.18.29 serve: the v1 routes (`/session`, `/session/:id`, `/session/:id/message`, `/project`) boot NOTHING; **every** `/api/session/{id}/…` v2 route boots an instance for that session's `location.directory` (+19 indexer threads, +180 MB, a full-tree watch). So: (a) the serve runs from `data/opencode-serve/cwd`, an empty directory made into a throwaway git repo by `ensureServeCwd` — OpenCode's project resolution walks UP for a git worktree, so a plain directory inside the checkout resolves the WHOLE VibeSpace checkout and a FAKE `.git` does not stop the walk, while with no repo above it the project is the `'/'` catch-all (a README next to it says why; `git init` failing only degrades the isolation, loudly). Accepted side effect: while our serve runs it pins the store's mutable `'global'` project row worktree to that empty dir — the field is last-writer-wins and every `opencode` invocation rewrites it, sessions carry their own `directory`, and our listing is worktree-independent. (b) NAMING uses v1 only, byte-capped. (c) `listAllSessions` takes the DIRECTORY-LESS listing first and only issues `scope=project&directory=` for worktrees passing `bootstrappableWorktree` (never `'/'`, `$HOME`, `os.tmpdir()`, nor the vcs-less `'global'` row — a real project row carries `vcs`, the API's own signal, so no fs call is needed); skipped worktrees surface in `facts.state().skippedWorktrees`. (d) `forkSession` — the one call handing a directory to a mutating endpoint — calls `POST /instance/dispose?directory=` afterwards (best effort; the forked session stays readable). **RUNAWAY GUARD:** the child's own `/proc` (`readProcUsage`) is sampled every 60s; >150% CPU sustained ≥5 min, or RSS >2 GB on a single sample, STOPS it, parks the locator `parkedKind:'runaway'` with the numbers in `lastError`, `console.error`s what to turn off, fires telemetry `opencode-serve-runaway`, pushes `harness-store-updated` and refuses to respawn for an hour (then exactly one retry). An unreadable /proc never parks anything; the locator never signals `process.pid`. **BOOT SELF-HEAL:** a recorded serve whose `GET /project/current` worktree is `'/'` or `$HOME` (a 2.369.42 leftover — its record also has no `cwd`) is SIGTERMed and replaced from the isolated cwd; a record written by this code (matching `cwd`) skips the probe, and a FAILED probe never churns a healthy instance. **AUTOSTART** is `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` (default ON, live-read through a function): `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins, `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` forces off, else the setting.  (3) createFacts — the store members: discover({activeSessions}) = 10s list cache → 10s negative cache (returns the LAST GOOD list, [] before any) → refresh bounded by the 1.5s budget (client({budgetMs}) returns null while the serve boots; a HUNG serve costs ≤1.5s, pinned <2s) — NEVER throws, NEVER stalls the 5s /api/sessions poll; entries {backend:'opencode', backendSessionId, sessionId, sessionKey, cwd=directory, startedAt=time.updated, status live|stopped (live = an activeSessions opencode session holds the id; 'external' is undetectable — another process driving the same sqlite leaves no signal), name, agentKind primary|subagent (parentID), parentThreadId, webuiId/Name/Mode, opencode:{slug,agent,model,projectID}}; names = discovery-facts nameFromText over the FIRST user message read from the **v1** `/session/:id/message` list (the WHOLE conversation oldest-first — v1 `limit` is the NEWEST N so it cannot page from the front), capped at NAME_MAX_BYTES=1MiB by the client's streaming `maxBytes` (over the cap → code `too-large` → the title fallback; six unbounded whole-conversation fetches into this process is an OOM). THE v2 asc endpoint IS SMALLER AND MUST NEVER BE USED HERE — it boots an instance (2.369.42). ≤6 lookups per tick (progressive, no burst), cached per id, retried every 60s while a session has no user message, fallback = OpenCode's title unless it is the "New session - <date>" placeholder; readConversation(id) (8s, LOUD: not installed / parked / unreachable / 404 all name the cause) and forkSession(id,{cwd}) (refused with code unsupported when the OpenAPI lacked the fork path); **sessionModel(id) (B-6b6d round 2)** = the model this conversation is on, as `provider/model`, for the resume-continuity ladder — the opencode descriptor's `store.lastTurnModel`, so an OpenCode resume keeps its own model instead of taking `opencode.defaultModel` (a NEW-session default). It shares `discover`'s cache through the one `listNow(budgetMs)` helper, so it is v1-only, bounded and adds NO route the sidebar poll does not already use; `''` = we could not read it (the service is opt-in and default OFF, or parked/unreachable/gone) and the ladder then takes the instance default and LOGS which rung it used. The installed singleton (install() by cli-env; facts() = NULL_FACTS when unwired: discover [] silently, user actions say "not configured"). NOT wired (seen in the 1.18.29 OpenAPI): POST /session/{sessionID}/revert, GET /question + POST /question/{requestID}/reply, /pty*, SSE /event + /global/event (could replace the 10s list poll), /session/{sessionID}/todo. Accepted side effect: while our serve runs it pins the store's mutable `'global'` project row worktree to that empty dir — the field is last-writer-wins and every `opencode` invocation rewrites it, sessions carry their own `directory`, and our listing is worktree-independent. (b) NAMING uses v1 only, byte-capped. (c) `listAllSessions` takes the DIRECTORY-LESS listing first and only issues `scope=project&directory=` for worktrees passing `bootstrappableWorktree` (never `'/'`, `$HOME`, `os.tmpdir()`, nor the vcs-less `'global'` row — a real project row carries `vcs`, the API's own signal, so no fs call is needed); skipped worktrees surface in `facts.state().skippedWorktrees`. (d) `forkSession` — the one call handing a directory to a mutating endpoint — calls `POST /instance/dispose?directory=` afterwards (best effort; the forked session stays readable). **RUNAWAY GUARD:** the child's own `/proc` (`readProcUsage`) is sampled every 60s; >150% CPU sustained ≥5 min, or RSS >2 GB on a single sample, STOPS it, parks the locator `parkedKind:'runaway'` with the numbers in `lastError`, `console.error`s what to turn off, fires telemetry `opencode-serve-runaway`, pushes `harness-store-updated` and refuses to respawn for an hour (then exactly one retry). An unreadable /proc never parks anything; the locator never signals `process.pid`. **BOOT SELF-HEAL:** a recorded serve whose `GET /project/current` worktree is `'/'` or `$HOME` (a 2.369.42 leftover — its record also has no `cwd`) is SIGTERMed and replaced from the isolated cwd; a record written by this code (matching `cwd`) skips the probe, and a FAILED probe never churns a healthy instance. **AUTOSTART (2026-09-07 — the setting `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` and the `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS` smoke belt are BOTH GONE):** the decision is ONE pure function here, `decideAutostart({env, pluginWantsUp})` — the ops override `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins (`serveEnvOverride`, the single parse of that var, also read by the plugin panel so it can show "forced by the environment"), else the `opencode-serve` plugin record (`enabled && desiredUp`); DEFAULT OFF. cli-env passes it as a FUNCTION over `plugins.wantsServiceUp(SERVICE_PLUGIN_ID)` so enabling takes effect without a restart, and the descriptor names its control plugin as `store.servicePlugin` so `/api/home` can carry `plugins.serviceState()` on the harness row (the client's first-use prompt and the sidebar's hidden-history row gate on THAT, never on a backend id). With default OFF a fresh smoke instance starts nothing, which is why the belt could be deleted. **A DELIBERATELY-OFF SERVICE IS NOT A BROKEN STORE (2026-09-07 follow-up):** `/api/home harnesses[].storeReason` is now the SAME predicate as the live `harness-store-updated` push — `storeFailureReason()` in src/server/cli-env.js, exported for the gate — and it fires ONLY on a PARK (crash loop / runaway). The old half also fired on "not ready and the keeper's autostart flag is off", which was the ops kill switch alone while autostart defaulted ON; with the plugin default OFF it became the normal shipped state, and app.js turns every reason into a RED ERROR TOAST ⇒ one per page load, on a fresh instance, after "Not now", and on instances that never had OpenCode. Off-ness travels on `row.service` instead and is shown passively (sidebar row + ⚙ card); the sidebar row also renders for the ops-forced case now, with no Enable button, since nothing the user clicks there could work.  (3) createFacts — the store members: discover({activeSessions}) = 10s list cache → 10s negative cache (returns the LAST GOOD list, [] before any) → refresh bounded by the 1.5s budget (client({budgetMs}) returns null while the serve boots; a HUNG serve costs ≤1.5s, pinned <2s) — NEVER throws, NEVER stalls the 5s /api/sessions poll; entries {backend:'opencode', backendSessionId, sessionId, sessionKey, cwd=directory, startedAt=time.updated, status live|external|stopped (see THE S9 REMAINDER below — 'external' became DETECTABLE, with positive evidence only), name, agentKind primary|subagent (parentID), parentThreadId, webuiId/Name/Mode, opencode:{slug,agent,model,projectID}}; names = discovery-facts nameFromText over the FIRST user message read from the **v1** `/session/:id/message` list (the WHOLE conversation oldest-first — v1 `limit` is the NEWEST N so it cannot page from the front), capped at NAME_MAX_BYTES=1MiB by the client's streaming `maxBytes` (over the cap → code `too-large` → the title fallback; six unbounded whole-conversation fetches into this process is an OOM). THE v2 asc endpoint IS SMALLER AND MUST NEVER BE USED HERE — it boots an instance (2.369.42). ≤6 lookups per tick (progressive, no burst), cached per id, retried every 60s while a session has no user message, fallback = OpenCode's title unless it is the "New session - <date>" placeholder; readConversation(id) (8s, LOUD: not installed / parked / unreachable / 404 all name the cause) and forkSession(id,{cwd}) (refused with code unsupported when the OpenAPI lacked the fork path). Not going to spawn (no CLI / service off) ⇒ `'keep'`: nothing overwrites it, so nothing may act on it — it still NAMES the process `stop({killRecorded})` would signal. Otherwise **`classifyRecordedPid` (PURE, the procfs reads injected)** decides what that live pid IS: `'ours'` (running `serve` with the RECORDED `--port`, under our own uid — the port is the discriminator, not argv[0], because the launcher may re-exec its runtime), `'other'` (a different uid, THIS server process, or a different command line ⇒ the recorded serve is GONE and the record is stale bookkeeping we may delete — but that pid must NEVER be signalled: a recycled pid is somebody else's program), `'unknown'` (procfs said nothing — no /proc on this platform, hidepid, a zombie's empty cmdline). `'ours'` gets ONE longer confirm probe first (`RECORD_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS` 4s — a cold 1.18.29 answers in ~1.2s, and SLOW must not read as WEDGED; if it answers we ADOPT it and nothing is stopped), then a warn naming pid/port/budget, a SIGTERM (never `process.pid`: the classifier answers `'other'` for our own pid, so a self-kill is unreachable), a BOUNDED wait for the exit, and only then the clear. Anything left — an unverifiable live pid, or one that ignored the SIGTERM — is `'blocked'`: no kill, no spawn, and a PARK (`parkedKind:'blocked'`) whose `lastError` names the pid, the port, the record file and both ways out. The park is the loud channel on purpose (`storeFailureReason` speaks only for a park), it re-tries on its own `BLOCKED_RETRY_MS` cooldown through the generalized `state.retryAfter` gate (the state can heal without the user: the serve may answer again, or the process may exit) — and a park's DEADLINE belongs to the park that set it, so `start()` clears it and a crash park declares none, or the terminal-until-restart crash park would inherit a blocked park's elapsed cooldown and quietly restart itself (its own 3-replacement control), and the ⚙ Plugins card carries its own row so a blocked record is never described as a crash loop.
