Before this it SIGTERMed `state.pid || rec.pid` behind a self-pid guard: exactly the pid the blocked park had just refused to touch, from the ONE control the ⚙ card leaves enabled in that state. Legs: a pure four-verdict table; the `ps` rung driven DIRECTLY over three real fixtures and asserted to reach the SAME verdicts procfs does (including a spaced argv word, where the two spellings genuinely differ and the verdict must not); both readers stubbed absent ⇒ no park, one spawn, zero signals, one host-level warn (negative control: with `'blind'` removed the same machine parks BLOCKED forever); the discrimination leg (blinding ONLY the recorded pid still BLOCKS); and Disable-in-a-blocked-park ⇒ zero signals + record cleared + an honest `lastError` (negative control: with the verdict route removed it SIGTERMs that pid), with positive controls that Disable still stops an adopted serve and never complains about a recycled one. **S9 RESIDUALS (2026-09-07).** (a) **A deliberately-OFF service is not a broken store.** `storeFailureReason` reads `parked` and nothing else, so the `blocked` park this very module raises — a live recorded serve we can neither identify nor stop — SURVIVED the Disable that answered it: /api/home stayed red and the toast fired on every page load for a service the user had just switched off. `stop({killRecorded})` now retires a `blocked` or `runaway` park after clearing the record (the park is a retry schedule for a record that is now gone). A `crash` park is deliberately NOT retired — it is terminal until an explicit `start()`, which already clears every park, and retiring it here would make Disable→Enable quietly forget a crash loop. `lastError` stays as history for the ⚙ card; what goes is the CLAIM that the store is broken right now. (b) **`hostCanIdentify()` memoises the YES only.** "This platform has a readable process table" never changes back, so caching `true` is free — but `false` is one reading of one probe, and the probe misses for reasons that are about the MOMENT (EMFILE/ENOMEM, a `ps` fork lost to a load spike, /proc still being mounted in a container at boot). Caching that turned a transient miss into a PERMANENT capability downgrade, and the downgraded answer is verdict `'blind'` — the one verdict that clears a live recorded pid's record and spawns over it without ever identifying it. A NO is re-probed (at most once per settlement/stop, which is where the callers already are); `data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op` carries the same rule and the parity table drives both. (c) the identity ladder is no longer this module's: see src/cli-identity.js.
  • **ROLL BACK / RESTORE.** Client methods `revert(id,{messageID,partID})` / `unrevert(id)` + facts `revertTo` / `unrevert`. **v1 ONLY, and that is a measurement, not a preference:** with /proc against a fresh serve, `POST /session/:id/revert` restored the working tree (hello.txt really disappeared) while the process stayed at 16 threads / 0 `fff` indexer threads, whereas ONE `POST /api/session/:id/revert/clear` took it to 37 threads / 19 indexer threads / +165 MB — the v2 stage/clear/commit trio is the instance-booting family, so it is deliberately not wired and `unrevert` IS the v1 "clear". There is NO v1 "commit"; the next prompt commits, which is what the UI says. The staged state rides the Session's own `revert` field: `messagesToAcpRecords` emits a `notice` (noticeKind `'revert'`, text from `revertNoticeText`) immediately BEFORE the message it rolled back to, so a rolled-back conversation SAYS so wherever it renders, and the discover entry carries `opencode.revert` so the chat's message-metadata popup can offer "Restore" only while one is actually staged.
  • **THE ASK CARD.** `GET /question` + `POST /question/:id/{reply,reject}` (both boot no instance). A `question` tool part becomes the harness-neutral `permission_request` with `kind:'user_input'` — the SAME card claude's AskUserQuestion uses — carrying `via:'opencode-serve'` so the ws layer answers it on the serve's route instead of a session's stdin (a stopped conversation opened read-only has no process here at all). Verified shapes on a real turn: the pending request is `{id:'que_…', sessionID, questions:[{question, header, options:[{label,description}], multiple?, custom?}], tool:{messageID, callID}}`, an answered part carries `state.metadata.answers = [["Blue"]]` (one array of labels per question, in order), and `POST /question/:id/reply {answers:[["Blue"]]}` completed the turn. `askAnswersToPositional` converts the card's question-text map back to that positional form and splits a comma-joined multi-select ONLY when every piece is a known option label (a free-text answer containing ", " survives intact). RELOAD SURVIVAL: the transcript only knows the tool CALL id, the live route wants the `que_…` id, so `readConversation` joins them (re-reading `GET /question` once when the live map is cold — a just-restarted server); an ask with no live request behind it is marked `stale` and the card renders it WITHOUT a Submit that could only fail. **REACHABILITY, measured:** `opencode acp` (the mode our live sessions run in) does not expose the `question` tool at all — the model itself listed its tools and there was none — and question events are per-PROCESS, so this lane fires for turns the SERVE drives, not for our own ACP sessions. That is recorded here rather than hidden behind a card nobody can reach. **`answerQuestion` re-reads `GET /question` when the warm map does not know the request**: the card's answers are keyed by question TEXT, so converting them to OpenCode's positional form needs the question list, and a server that restarted between rendering the card and the user pressing Submit had an empty map — it refused its own user's answer with "no answers". Positional answers need no lookup and skip it.
  • **THE SERVE TERMINAL** — see src/server/opencode-pty-bridge.js below.
  • **THE LIVE LANE** — see src/opencode-events.js below. The 10s list-cache timer is GONE while the lane is healthy: `discover` refreshes only when an event marked the cache dirty (with a 1s serial-burst floor, because five browser tabs each poll /api/sessions), and falls back to the timer STRUCTURALLY when the lane is down — a broken lane must not freeze the sidebar forever. **The dirty signal NOTIFIES** (`onChange`, wired in src/server/cli-env.js): the sidebar caches this list too, so a change nobody asked about — a TUI writing the same sqlite — is pushed as `opencode-updated {kind:'store'}` instead of waiting for that browser's own 5s poll. Coalesced at 2s and with streamed message parts excluded, because each push costs EVERY open client one /api/sessions discovery sweep and our own opencode turns write that sqlite too. **A (re)connect also PRIMES the busy map** from `/session/status`: `session.status` frames are its only other source, so a serve that was already running a turn when the stream came up read `stopped` for the length of that turn — rung 1 of honest liveness blind exactly when it matters.
  • **'external' LIVENESS, with positive evidence only** (`deriveStatus`): `live` = one of OUR sessions holds the id; `external` = either this serve's own `/session/status` says busy/retry (in-process truth, no directory needed, boots nothing) OR the row's `time.updated` MOVED while we were not the ones moving it, within `EXTERNAL_WINDOW_MS` (90s) — the cross-process signal, since another opencode's events never reach our bus but the sqlite row it writes does reach our list, and the store-watch lane makes us re-read within ~0.4s. Anything else is `stopped`; the label DECAYS on its own, and `state().liveLaneHealthy` says when we cannot see at all, so the honest answer is a fact in the panel rather than a lie on every row. Verified against two real serves on one store: an external write flipped the row to external, our own write stayed live, and stale evidence decayed back to stopped. **"WE" INCLUDES THE USER'S OWN CLICK (round 3, a reproduced defect): "we were not the ones moving it" originally meant only *a live session of ours holds this id*, so every mutation through our OWN serve routes on a STOPPED conversation — roll back, restore, answer/reject an ask — moved `time.updated` and was then attributed to a stranger for 90s** (reproduced 3/3 through the real product routes: the card dimmed to opacity .7, its title read "Running in unsupported terminal (PID ?)", the Fork… row vanished from its menu, and a sidebar filtered to exclude 'external' lost the conversation entirely — all from the user's own click). `noteOwnWrite(id, session)` writes the mutation down and `ownWriteVerdict` consumes it: **by VALUE where we have one** — MEASURED on 1.18.29, `revert`/`unrevert` return the row's FINAL `time.updated` and nothing bumps it afterwards (0ms delta at +250ms…+8s), so the listing that reports exactly what we wrote is ours no matter how late it arrives, a listing carrying an OLDER value (one that was already in flight while we wrote) keeps the entry, and the first value PAST ours is somebody else's and says so immediately — and by a short `OWN_WRITE_WINDOW_MS` (10s) clock only for the actions that return no Session (an answered ask; the reply/reject paths therefore re-read `/question` even for positional answers, because the question is the only thing that names the conversation they are about to move). Fork writes nothing down and that is measured too: forking does not move the SOURCE row, and the fork's own row is a first sighting. The gate carries both directions — our own roll-back stays stopped on a REAL store, while a SECOND real `opencode serve` writing that same store still reads external.
NOT wired, with the reason: the v2 `/api/session/:id/revert/{stage,clear,commit}` trio (measured instance boot, above) and `POST /sync/history` — the DURABLE cross-process event log, which DOES carry another process's writes (proven: a session created by a second serve appeared in the first serve's history), but whose first read has no "from now on" cursor and would download the whole log; the list re-read the store-watch triggers is bounded and answers the same question. Gates: scripts/test-opencode-serve.mjs (135) + scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs (the remainder: roll-back/restore incl. "the v2 family is never requested", the ask card end to end incl. the stale case and the free-text-with-comma control, the pty bridge over a real websocket, the live lane replacing the poll with a negative control for the timer fallback, liveness with three negative controls, wiring pins, and a REAL-BINARY section that SKIPS WITH EVIDENCE when `opencode` is absent) + scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs (the three rungs cannot drift). test-opencode-serve details: (mock serve in scripts/dev/mock-opencode-serve.mjs, which MODELS the instance boot: any v2 per-session route adds `state.instances`, so 'a whole discovery tick bootstraps ZERO instances' is a real assert, plus a spawn-cwd spy, the '/'-worktree boot self-heal, the runaway guard driven by a fake /proc reader + fake clock, dispose-after-fork and the byte cap — mock serve in scripts/dev/mock-opencode-serve.mjs, which MODELS the instance boot: any v2 per-session route adds `state.instances`, so 'a whole discovery tick bootstraps ZERO instances' is a real assert, plus a spawn-cwd spy, the '/'-worktree boot self-heal, the runaway guard driven by a fake /proc reader + fake clock, dispose-after-fork and the byte cap); manual: `node scripts/dev/opencode-serve-live.mjs --measure [seconds]` runs the REAL loop against the REAL store and prints CPU/RSS/threads/indexer-threads/inotify-watches (healthy = single-digit CPU%, flat RSS, 0 indexer threads, 0 watches).
  src/opencode-events.js — THE LIVE LANE that replaced OpenCode's 10s list poll (S9 remainder piece (d), B-eac2; SHARED — node builtins only, the daemon bundles it). TWO SOURCES, because one of them is provably blind and saying so is the point. ① `GET /global/event`: measured with /proc, it boots NO OpenCode instance and needs no `directory`, so it is the ONE subscription per serve; frames are `{directory, project, payload:{id,type,properties}}` and a `server.heartbeat` lands about every 10s (undocumented, observed on the wire) — which is why an open socket with NO frame for 45s is treated as DEAD and aborted, not as idle. `createEventStream` reconnects with 1s·2^n backoff (≤30s) and re-asks the LOCATOR each time, so a serve that respawned on a new port is followed. ② `fs.watch` over the store dirs (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode`, `~/.local/share/opencode`, and the serve's own `GET /path` home when it differs — resolved lazily, because before the serve exists we do not know whose HOME it runs under): **THE MEASURED BLIND SPOT** — a SECOND opencode process on the SAME sqlite (a TUI, another serve) produces NO frame on `/global/event` at all (reproduced: serve A subscribed, serve B created a session, A's stream carried only `server.connected` + heartbeats for 30s while A's `GET /session` listed it immediately). The store is shared, the event bus is per process, so SSE alone cannot replace the poll; the watch never READS the db, only its mtime events, is debounced 400ms, and an unwatchable dir degrades to "no external signal" LOUDLY once and is retried on the next reconnect. `classifyEvent` is PURE: one testable table from event type → {kind, sessionId, dirty:{sessions|conversation|questions}, status, question, …}; an UNKNOWN type is `kind:'other'` with NO dirty flags, so an OpenCode upgrade can never make us drop a lane. `createLiveLane` is the pair behind one `state()` — `{sse:{connected,…}, watch:{watching,failed,active,…}}` — and "healthy" means BOTH, which is exactly the condition under which the timer refresh is allowed to be gone. **The lane FOLLOWS the serve, on an EDGE**: while nothing is reachable the stream is in backoff (up to 30s), so `install()` wraps the locator's own `onState` and calls `lane.kick()` when a port becomes READY or CHANGES — enabling the plugin, or a keeper respawn on a new port, goes live at once. It must be the edge and not every `notify()`: the runaway guard samples /proc once a minute, and kicking on each of those would re-open the SSE socket for nothing (both directions are pinned in scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs). **AND THE SLEEP IS PART OF THE SOCKET (round 3, a reproduced defect): `kick()` originally reset `attempts` and aborted the fetch controller — but during a backoff there IS no fetch to abort, and nothing cleared the `setTimeout` the loop was sitting in, so the kick only shortened the NEXT wait.** Since the service ships OFF, "nothing to connect to" is the normal state before first use, so this was the first-use path, not a corner: measured 25.1s from "the serve is ready" to "the lane is healthy" end to end (and 11.0s to the next connect attempt in the unit shape), during which `laneHealthy()` is false and the 10s timer this feature replaced is still the only source of freshness. The loop's sleep now keeps its resolver (`wake`), and `kick()`/`stop()` both wake it before aborting — 51ms after the fix, with the regression driving the REAL stream to a ≥3s pending backoff so a sub-second reconnect cannot be an accident of a short timer. **ROUND 4 — the lane could LIE about itself, two ways, both closed.** `active` is what `laneHealthy()` switches the list-refresh fallback OFF on, and it was true for ANY directory that merely existed; meanwhile `armWatch()` ran at `start()` — before any serve — and latched (`watchTried` was only reset when the watch attached NOWHERE), so the documented "resolved LAZILY once the serve answers GET /path" never ran on any machine where `$HOME/.local/share/opencode` already exists, which is every machine that has ever run opencode. Reproduced with the real wiring: `state().liveLane.watch` = the SERVER process's store with `liveLaneHealthy` true, and a session created by a SECOND opencode process on the serve's REAL store never appeared (8s of 100ms-spaced `discover()`, ZERO `GET /session` issued because the lane claimed health); the same probe with the serve's actual store saw it in 493ms. In the default deployment the two resolve to the same dir (agentEnv keeps HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME), so this was a latent gap plus a FALSE HEALTH SIGNAL — and a false `active` is worse than none, because it is the flag that turns the fallback off. Fixes: `createStoreWatch` refuses a directory with no `opencode.db` (recorded in `failed`, `active` stays false ⇒ the timer fallback stays on and the next reconnect re-arms — the serve creates the db at boot); and `armWatch(why)` RE-RESOLVES on every `connected` against the serve's own `GET /path` home, re-arming only when the dir set actually DIFFERS (`watchedDirs` + a `rearms` counter in `state()`), so a reconnect storm cannot churn the watchers. **ROUND 5 — the lane is only STARTED while the service is on.** Nothing changed in this module: `start()` still arms the watch and the stream, and that is exactly why `install()` (src/opencode-serve.js) may not call it while the OpenCode background service is OFF — a lane that merely has nothing to connect to still holds an fs.watch on the user's store. The owner of "may this run at all" is the locator's autostart decision; this module owns only "how well is it running". **ROUND 6 — and `stop()` is TERMINAL for an arm already IN FLIGHT.** Round 5 gated whether the lane may START; both of its starts are async before they own anything, so a disable landing in the gap still leaked. `armWatch()` awaits `resolveDirs()` (the serve's `GET /path` on a 2s budget — spent in full exactly when the serve is parked or absent, the state a user turning the service off is in), and the continuation used to assign `watch = createStoreWatch(...)` onto a lane nobody holds: an fs.watch on the user's real store unreachable by any later `stop()` or `uninstall()`, and a LIVE one — a write to `opencode.db-wal` still fired `onExternal` ⇒ `markDirty` ⇒ an `opencode-updated` broadcast ⇒ every client re-running /api/sessions for a feature that was OFF (measured: 1 inotify wd at a 0 ms disable and at a 1200 ms disable, and with the keeper PARKED). `connectOnce()` had the same shape around `locator.client({budgetMs:8000})`: a stop there aborted a controller that did not exist yet and the continuation opened an SSE subscription the serve then held open forever (heartbeats keep it under the 45s idle abort), with `state().sse` reporting `stopped:true` AND `connected:true` at once. So: `laneStopped` is set FIRST in `stop()`; `armWatch()` re-checks it on entry AND hands the built watch to the single attach point `attachWatch()`, which closes it rather than store it; `resolveDirs()` skips its second round trip when the lane died during the first; `connectOnce()` re-checks `state.stopped` after the locator and after the fetch settles. The lane is SINGLE-USE by construction (`stopLive()` drops it, `armLive()` builds a fresh one per enable), which is what makes a one-way door safe — `kick()` is a no-op once stopped. Gated by scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs's ROUND 6 legs, each run twice: once against this file and once against a copy with exactly these guards removed (the negative control MUST leak, and its replacements are asserted to match once each so a stale control fails loudly).
  src/opencode-remote.js — THE OP TABLE (S9 remainder piece (e), B-eac2; PURE — imports nothing). `OPENCODE_OPS` maps an op name to {member, required[], build(params), result(v)} and `runOpencodeOp(facts, op, params)` executes it against a facts object. That is the WHOLE machine-side implementation, and all three rungs use it: the local rung (hostId falsy, in-process), the `opencode-serve` agentd op (the daemon bundles src/opencode-serve.js and calls this same function against ITS facts), and — mirrored, because a checkout-less ssh host cannot require it — data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op. `checkOpParams` refuses an unknown op WITH the known list and a missing param WITH the op and key names, so no rung can fail as an unexplained 500. Gate: scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs parses the shipped script's own OPS object and fails on any op the table has and the script lacks (or vice versa), compares result KEYS rung by rung against a mock serve, and pins the three-touch rule on the device side. **The daemon holds its facts in a MODULE-LEVEL `ocFacts`, never on `this`**: inside a Mux control handler `this` is the MUX — the CONNECTION — so a per-`this` cache is rebuilt on every reconnect and each `install()` arms another live lane (an SSE subscription + fs.watch handles) while the old one keeps running; a dial-out device reconnects on every link blip, which makes that leak silent and unbounded. The suites assert the declaration sits ABOVE `serveConnection` and that `this._ocFacts` appears nowhere. **Rung choice** (src/hosts.js `opencodeOp`): a DIAL device has no ssh fallback and rethrows the device error (2.271.0 T3-6 — the ssh path would misdiagnose it); an SSH host falls through on ANY device failure, like the usage-scan and transcript rungs, because the daemon may be old, down or mid-upgrade and the shipped script answers the same question. That fallback is FREE: the daemon's locator and the script use the SAME record `~/.vibespace/opencode-serve.json`, so the ssh rung REUSES the daemon's serve instead of starting a second one (pinned).
  data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op — REMOTE-side op runner for checkout-less ssh hosts (STATIC tracked, shipped to ~/.vibespace/bin; the documented single-file exception, same class as vibespace-usage-scan). Reads `{op,params}` on stdin, prints ONE `{ok,result}|{ok:false,error}` line. It carries the full 2.369.50 resource discipline onto someone else's machine: the serve is started from its OWN empty `~/.vibespace/opencode-serve-cwd` git repo (never $HOME — OpenCode's upward worktree walk would adopt it), ONLY v1 routes are used, the listing is directory-less and never bootstraps a project row that is not ours, every response read into memory is byte-capped, the record is written atomically, and a healthy recorded serve is reused instead of spawned per call. **AND THE RECORD IS SETTLED BEFORE ANYTHING OVERWRITES IT (round 11 — this file was the UNFIXED TWIN of the round-10 local bug):** `locate()` used to probe the recorded port and, on ANY non-answer, spawn a second serve and rewrite the record, orphaning a live `opencode serve` on a machine with no keeper, no runaway guard, no park and no ⚙ card — nothing there can ever reach it again. Now: dead pid ⇒ delete the record + spawn · a pid the identity ladder (`/proc` then `ps -p <pid> -o uid=,args=`, a VALUE read; `kill -0` stays the liveness probe) proves is NOT that `serve --port <recorded>` ⇒ stale bookkeeping, deleted, never signalled · a host that can identify no process at all ⇒ same (a live pid means nothing there) · verified ours and still silent after a LONGER confirm probe ⇒ SIGTERM + bounded wait, then clear · unidentifiable, or still running after the wait ⇒ `fail()` naming the pid, the port, the record path and both ways out, instead of spawning over it (there is no park out here — the honest failure IS the channel, and the hub surfaces the machine-side message). PARITY-PINNED as a DECISION, not just as a data walk: scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs lifts this file's `classifyRecordedPid` out of its source and drives it and the module's over ONE 16-row table (a row per decision boundary — `serve` vs `server`, port-present vs absent, exact vs prefix port match, the four verdicts), pins the three budgets to the module's exported constants, and then runs the REAL script through each verdict against a real silent socket and real processes, with a PRE-FIX copy as the negative control (it starts the second serve and orphans the first). `read` ships the RAW v1 messages — the 'acp-events' synthesis stays in ONE place (the hub's `messagesToAcpRecords`, applied by the access layer), proven record-for-record identical to the local rung. The pty ops REFUSE with the reason (the serve's pty websocket is loopback-only on that host). Its rows are always `status:'stopped'` and that is deliberate, not a lag: liveness rung 2 is a LEDGER across listings (and, since round 3, across our own writes), and a one-shot ssh invocation has no memory between calls — so this rung claims nothing rather than guessing. The paired-device rung keeps the ledger because the daemon's facts live per PROCESS.
  src/server/opencode-access.js — the ONE way to reach the OpenCode serve on ANY machine (ORCH; wired once from mounts-plugins-wiring so server.js stays inside its size ratchet, and published as a module singleton `access()` that ws-handler / ws-create reach without a server.js cross). `call(hostId, op, params)` picks the transport and nothing downstream ever asks "is this remote?" again. Two normalisations live here because they must be identical on every rung: `readConversation` synthesises records from the ssh rung's raw messages with the SHARED function, and `publicView` strips the serve ws url + auth header from anything a ROUTE returns (they are how the SERVER connects; only ws-create's bridge sees them, through `openPtyBridge`). `LOCAL_ONLY_OPS` refuses the pty family for a remote machine BEFORE the transport is used, naming why.
  src/server/opencode-pty-bridge.js — THE SERVE TERMINAL (S9 remainder piece (c), ORCH). `opencode serve` owns real ptys and streams them over a websocket; this connects to it SERVER-SIDE and presents `{pid,onData,onExit,write,resize,kill}` — the same duck the daemon pipe-session shim uses — so ws-create can hand it to `setupSessionPty` and the xterm window, input, resize, the buffer file and every window action work with ZERO terminal-side changes. THE SERVE PORT NEVER REACHES THE BROWSER. Verified on the wire against 1.18.29: `GET /pty/{id}/connect` upgrades with NO ticket on an unsecured loopback serve (and `POST /pty/{id}/connect-token` answers PtyForbiddenError there, so the bridge mints one when it can and connects without one when it cannot); TEXT frames are terminal output; BINARY frames are `\0`-prefixed control json (`\0{"cursor":73}`) and rendering them would paint json into the user's shell; frames written in reach the pty. Resize is NOT on the socket — `PUT /pty/{id} {size:{rows,cols}}`. The pty belongs to the SERVE, so a dropped socket RECONNECTS (5 tries, backoff) instead of ending the session, and input typed meanwhile is queued (bounded at 200 — a dead socket must not grow memory). **But "the serve does not have this pty" is a VERDICT, not a hiccup (round 3, measured on the wire): after the shell exits, `GET /pty/<id>` answers PtyNotFoundError and the upgrade is a plain HTTP 404 — which the bounded reconnect burned all five rungs against (800+1600+2400+3200+4000 ≈ 12s of a dead-but-open terminal, plus five bogus `socket error: Unexpected server response: 404` warnings) before the window admitted the shell was gone.** `ptyGone(message)` is PURE (404/410 terminal; 502/503, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, "socket hang up" transient — a truth table in the gate) and the `error` handler sets a `gone` flag that short-circuits `close` into ONE honest log line + `onExit`; the mock serve now answers 404 to an upgrade for a pty it no longer has, exactly like the real one, so the end-to-end leg can assert ONE upgrade attempt and an exit under a second. Known limits, deliberately: it is LOCAL-only (a remote serve's ws is not reachable from the hub — a device would need the port-forward data plane), and a server restart leaves the pty alive on the serve without re-adopting it. **ROUND 4:** the bridge's `pty-close`/`pty-resize` calls still carry `cwd` on the wire (the op table's shape) but the CLIENT no longer turns it into a `directory` query — see src/opencode-serve.js: opening a terminal used to boot and permanently watch the user's whole worktree. The "a server restart leaves the pty alive on the serve without re-adopting it" limit above is now BOUNDED rather than open: it is still not re-adopted (no re-bridge), but `facts.reapPtys()` removes it on the next serve ready edge, so a stranded shell no longer runs forever. **B-ae4b (2.369.164): the duck holds a listener SET** (`ptyListeners({hold: 500})` from src/pty-duck.js). Its one slot met setupSessionPty's two registrations (the liveness stamp first, the terminal consumer second) since 2.369.82: the held banner was flushed into the FIRST registrant — the stamp — and the consumer that replaced it got nothing, so the serve terminal opened blank again (the exact bug the hold was written for), and the stamp was dropped for every later byte. Now the held bytes are replayed in a microtask to EVERY listener registered in the first tick, live bytes keep their place behind the replay, and every `onExit` listener fires (test-pty-duck §2 over the mock serve).
  src/routes/opencode.js — the OpenCode action routes (roll back / restore / asks / status / todos). Every route takes `host` and passes it straight to the access layer; every MUTATING route broadcasts `opencode-updated` (persistent state → other browsers see it without a refresh); every failure answers `{error}` with the machine-side reason (fetchJson never throws, so a 200-with-nothing would be a silent failure of a user action). ### gmail-sync.js

  gmail-sync.js        — GmailSync (2.134.0, backlog B-64db): Gmail-as-a-folder — a 'gmail' mount = local dir of .eml files synced READ-ONLY from the Gmail API (GYB-style; NOT FUSE). Own loopback OAuth for gmail.readonly (rclone authorize is drive-only; same guided UX incl. remote paste-back); seed = STREAMING + CHECKPOINTED (2.136.1-4): each page downloaded then a CROSS-RESTART cursor persisted — a DATE (`state.seedOldestMs` → `before:<sec>`), NOT the messages.list pageToken (pageToken is only stable within one run; new mail between runs shifts/expires it and silently skips OLD mail the incremental never back-fills — real user catch). historyId anchored at seed START (covers mail arriving during a long seed). Total for the N/total bar comes cheaply from users.getProfile `messagesTotal` (whole mailbox) or labels.get `messagesTotal` (label filter), persisted as `state.seedTotal` (free-text query → indeterminate). Progress broadcasts throttle (indeterminate 2.5s — a fast cadence rebuilt the card and restarted the bar animation, stuttering it 'in the first third'; the bar is a symmetric pulse so a mid-anim rebuild is invisible). Incremental via history.list (404 = expired → reseed; dir tree IS the dedup index — msg id in filename tail, _seenIds recurses one date/label dir level), messages.get?format=raw → base64url → .eml (atomic tmp+rename, RFC2047-decoded subject slug in name). Client id/secret from VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS presets (they carry gmail scope) or custom — NO built-in fallback. mounts.js integration: isMounted=worker alive, health sweep skips fuse probing (dead worker → auto-restart), unmount stops worker but keeps files (it's the archive), mode forced ro. Viewer: src/lib/eml.js (dependency-free browser-safe MIME parser, 41-case test) + file-viewer _renderEml (header card, text/html toggle, html in sandbox="" iframe, attachment blob downloads). **2.151.0 incremental-freeze fix (real 3h hang):** history.list lists ADDED ids that can be deleted by fetch time (spam auto-purge; guaranteed with includeSpamTrash) — the per-message 404 failed the whole pass and the cursor only advances after a COMPLETE pass ⇒ every 120s retry re-listed + re-404'd the same dead id forever. _writeGone404 skips gone messages (both paths); all API/token fetches bounded (AbortSignal.timeout 60s/30s) so a wedged socket errors into the backoff. Tests: scripts/test-gmail-sync.mjs (mock API e2e incl the dead-id regression), scripts/test-eml.mjs

  transcript-worker.js — heavy JSONL transcript work OFF the main thread (2.235.0, the userL degradation follow-up): a persistent SafeFs-hosted worker pool (SafeFs gained opts.workerPath/inlineRun generalization + in-flight ref()) running the EXISTING sync implementations by requiring the same modules — worker-side mtime+size caches, zero duplication. Async variants jsonlGapInfoAsync/readJsonlLineRangeAsync/scanJsonlUserTurnsAsync/readJsonlBoundedParsedAsync serve the gap/turnmap/slab endpoints; session-store.warmSessionJsonlAsync pre-warms the parse cache before the ws attach rebuild + /api/session-messages (sync machinery then cache-hits). Worker down ⇒ sync inline fallback. RULE: new heavy transcript scans go through this worker, never inline on the loop (measured: 1ms max main-thread block vs 78ms inline on a 39MB fixture, 0.6-1s on real files). Test: scripts/test-transcript-worker.mjs. Related: sysinfo.js samples event-loop lag (500ms cadence, 3-min median; ≥300ms amber / ≥800ms red → sysinfo-alert kind:'evloop' toast "sessions are NOT dead" + history field `e`) **perf chunk C (2.369.167): op `jsonlTail`** = `readJsonlTail`'s FULL read with no previous entry (the cache lives on the main thread) — the warm's cold path; it returns the span entry so the next change to that file is folded in as an APPEND on the main thread (≤ 4 MiB) instead of another whole-tail worker parse + structured-clone. `boundedParsed` stays (its only caller is now test-transcript-worker).

### agentd/

**2026-09-28 (lane-pairing ③④⑤, B-7007) — THE DIAL SAYS WHY, THE SOCKET FITS, THE INSTALLER CHECKS FIRST.** ws-min surfaces every failure (`UPGRADE_REFUSED {status, refusal, ≤ 1 KiB body}`, `probe-ok`, `BAD_ACCEPT`, a 15 s `ETIMEDOUT`); the dial loop classifies every close (PURE `dialFailureOf`), writes `state/dial-status.json` (atomic 0600, never the token) + ONE log line naming the class, and sends its streak as request headers; the `dial-status` op (three-touch: reply by id, the capability in the hello-ack, `dialStatus()` refuses an old daemon `host_needs_daemon` before asking); `cmd-result` gains `timedOut` + `signal`; `SOCK` = the rung ladder of SHARED src/sock-path.js (too long ⇒ exit 7 naming every rung's bytes, a hijacked short dir ⇒ exit 8) + the witness `state/socket-path` the `--stdio` bridge and client.js read; `--dial-check <url> --dial-token <t>` = one probe dial, no lock / socket / state, exit 0 · 10 dns · 11 tls · 12 unreachable · 13 not VibeSpace · 14 refused · 15 other. Full essay: src/dial-facts.js / src/sock-path.js in the LANE-PAIRING block at the end of this file.

**2026-09-25 (desktop lane C verify r3 M2 + L6) — THE ORPHANED CHILD NEVER DEPENDS ON ITS LOG.** `orphanRunStream`'s sink paused the child when the log's `write()` answered false and resumed it ONLY on 'drain' — a Writable that ERRORS (ENOSPC on a full disk, EISDIR, EACCES) emits 'error' + 'close' and never 'drain' (node v24.12), so a child paused at the cut stayed paused for good (measured on the built bundle, hub consumer stalled 400 ms then the link cut, `<pid>.log` a symlink to /dev/full: frozen at line 117 of 4000, wchan `sock_alloc_send_pskb`). Now a pause arms ONE resume on 'drain' OR 'error' OR 'close' (`resumeOnce`, the other two listeners removed when one fires — no accumulation), and the log's own 'error' handler nulls `out` AND resumes the child: an errored log is a pure drain (output dropped, the child runs to its end — marker in ~100 ms). **L6:** the 8 MiB cap was per orphan EVENT: a pid wrap appends to the same `<pid>.log`, +8 MiB each time (measured 15,106,486 bytes on an 8 MiB plant). `written` is seeded from the existing file's size (`statSync`, regular files only — once, at the link's death), the header says how many bytes are left (or that the file is at its cap and the output is dropped). Gate: test-desktop-remote §8 (real daemon; CONTROLS = pre-fix bundles written through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs `selfPath`: frozen at 6 s / +7.4 MB appended).

**2026-09-25 (desktop lane C verify r2 F2) — A RUN-STREAM CHILD WHOSE HUB LINK DIED IS NEVER LEFT PAUSED.** `startStreamChild` pauses a child's stdout when `mux.data()` answers false (window pressure) and resumes it on the peer's credit (`onWritable`). When the HUB's side of the link died mid-stream no credit ever came: `mux.data()` on the dead mux keeps answering false, the child was paused with no resumer and wedged in its next write (measured on the built bundle: a 4 MB producer frozen at line ~270 of 1000, still frozen after the hub re-dialed; a wedged dpkg dies mid-transaction when the daemon later re-execs). `streamChans` now holds `{child, sink}`; `onDead(reason)` hands every orphaned child to module-level `orphanRunStream(rec, reason)`: its stdout RESUMES into `~/.vibespace/run-stream/<pid>.log` (0600, a header naming the lost link, capped at `RUN_STREAM_LOG_CAP` 8 MB with a marker and DRAINED past it, the exit line appended by `sendExit`; logs older than 7 days swept there) — the child runs to its end, never signalled. No re-attach op (the install rung's own detachment covers what needs following). Gate: test-desktop-remote §8 (real daemon, hub-side `mux.destroy()` with a 4 MB producer in flight ⇒ its marker within 10 s, the log whole; CONTROL = the bundle without the orphan line ⇒ paused for good).

THREE flags, DEFAULT ON since 2.158.0 (CS graduation — local=device#0; automatic legacy fallback preserved). **ONE MACHINE MODEL since 2.160.0 (B-f3e8, resolves the user's 2026-07-15 insight that row inconsistencies = two underlying concepts): a machine is a host record, transport ∈ {ssh(absent), dial}** — the pairing credential lives ON the dial record (`dialTokenHash`, redacted from list(), migrated ONCE from dial-tokens.json via hosts.migrateDialTokenFile → `.migrated`; LOSSLESS is load-bearing: in-field daemons hold the raw tokens); roster/test/unpair = /api/hosts + POST /api/hosts/:id/test (hosts.test dial branch = mux runCmd probe) + DELETE /api/hosts/:id (server unpairDialDevice: mounts+token-file+live-stream teardown); /api/agentd/devices is GONE; `hosts-updated` broadcasts on pair/unpair/dial-in/out; hosts.dirComplete rides the device link (dial machines get real remote autocomplete); sidebar has ONE _buildHostRow for all transports + a 'This machine' local row (local=device#0 made visible). The flags: `agentd.sessions` (M1: local sessions run in the daemon — dtach attach inside agentd, survives server restarts), `agentd.remoteSessions` (M2: remote chat = persistent pipe session in the remote daemon via the vibespace-agentd-attach bridge, keeper-run-identical contract so chat-wrapper is untouched; auto install/refresh at spawn), `agentd.dataPlane` (M3 switchovers: RemoteFs fs ops / discovery raw-facts synthesized into the ssh-script line format→UNCHANGED parser / transcript INCREMENTAL slab sync (append-only delta via read-range — no more whole-file remote-jsonl pulls) / usage harvest via run-stream; per-path ssh fallback; hosts.device(id) = per-host DeviceManager registry). mux.js = length-prefixed binary mux (chan0 JSON control + credit-flow-controlled byte channels; data() SPLITS at the window — all-or-nothing starved big writes; zero deps, shared by daemon+server = invariant #3). **CONTROL-OVERTAKE INVARIANT (2.187.0, real incident): chan0 control is credit-EXEMPT, so a completion marker (fs-done/stream-exit) OVERTAKES data still queued behind the 256KB window — any "resolve on the done marker" consumer truncates big transfers to exactly INITIAL_WINDOW bytes.** fsReadRange/runStream are COUNT-GATED (resolve when the counted bytes landed; daemon reports `sent`, run-stream exits on 'close' not 'exit', both pace under window pressure via onWritable); the incident: a 45MB remote transcript cached as a 256KB prefix stamped complete → permanently ancient chat history (fetchSessionJsonl now also refuses to stamp meta for bytes not received + caps on FETCHED delta not total size; **2.188.1: cache-valid additionally requires the cached FILE to hold meta.size bytes — a pre-fix stump over a STOPPED transcript passed size/mtime forever since the self-heal only fired on remote-file change**). Any NEW byte-channel consumer must gate on a byte count, never on a control-channel done. Test: scripts/test-agentd-bigread.mjs. agentd.js = daemon (flock singleton, setsid, 0700 unix socket, multi-server, vsht_ hello auth, self-upgrade→versioned dir→re-exec (2.185.2: the re-exec PRESERVES the original argv via reExecArgv — dropping `--dial/--dial-token` re-exec'd a dial device into LISTEN mode and wedged the link behind the singleton, the userW-class 'device goes offline after updates' root cause); pipe-sessions = keeper semantics in-daemon (setsid child + buffer/fifo + offset reattach + sentinel + drain-only-never-respawn); **pipe-child identity is exec-PROOF startTime, never cmdline (2.184.1, real userL outage: chat children spawn as `sh -lc '… exec env … claude'` so cmdline loses argv0 — every daemon upgrade re-exec then misjudged the live claude as a recycled pid, synthesized a crash sentinel (session died, claude orphaned) AND made kill-pipe-session a no-op; adopted children additionally get a liveness watcher because a non-child can't be wait()ed — no watcher meant no exit sentinel ever; test-agentd-adopt.mjs guards both)**; fs-op incl read-range byte-chan slab; discovery snapshot w/ tailIds/headCwd/userLines enrichment + fs.watch dirty push; run-cmd (argv-only bounded); run-stream (unbounded stdout on byte chan); tcp-connect (loopback only = VNC bridge shape); **serve-folder (2.150.0; WEBDAV since 2.151.0, device-folder-mount): a minimal in-daemon read-only WebDAV subset (OPTIONS/PROPFIND Depth 0-1/HEAD/GET+Range; zero deps, mirrors src/webdav.js) bound to 127.0.0.1 that rclone `webdav`-mounts via tcp-connect (src/device-mount.js) — the plain-`http` backend was the 2.150.0 stall: it requests a fixed 128MB range per read then waits ~6s on the keep-alive connection after the clamped 206; webdav requests sane ranges and reads in ~7ms (verified). GOTCHAS: clamp ranged end to size-1 (rclone asks 128M ranges → clamp or truncated EIO); the SERVER-side bridge net.createServer MUST be `{allowHalfOpen:true}` + attach the data listener BEFORE `await tcpForward` (curl/rclone half-close a GET's write side + write-then-read, both lose bytes otherwise); NEVER do sync fs/exec on a device mountpoint from the process hosting the bridge — the blocked event loop can't pump the tunnel, the FUSE read never completes, SELF-DEADLOCK (the acceptance test hung itself this way for a whole debug cycle; a dir `ls` still 'works' off rclone's dir-cache, which hides it; test IO now runs in async children w/ watchdog — production safe by construction: bridge in the server, reads from other processes/safe-fs workers). Still not a MountManager UI type (next step). **SSH-BRIDGE STDIN EPIPE (2.241.1, userN's exit-code-1 crash): the client.js ssh-transport wrapper writes to child.stdin — pipe errors arrive ASYNC as 'error' events on the stdin socket itself (the wrapper's on('error') only covered the child process; the write try/catch only stops sync throws), so a dying ssh child during the heartbeat PING was an UNCAUGHT write EPIPE that killed the whole server 28s after an update restart. stdin/stdout error events are swallowed; 'close' drives mux teardown+reconnect. Any new pipe-wrapped transport must attach error listeners on the PIPE STREAMS, not just the process.** dial-in device consumption = DeviceManager `stream` transport + server deviceForDial(id) wrapping a dialed-in ws stream — **deviceForDial NEVER reuses a stop()ed DeviceManager (2.169.0, real userW outage: hours of phantom-offline against a healthy dialed-in Mac): stop() is terminal (_connectLoop throws 'stopped' forever), so a stopped dm is evicted like a stale stream and a failed connect() never stays cached; any new dm.stop() caller must not leave the object in agentdDialDevices**. **THE UPGRADE LEDGER (verify-r1 C1, 2026-09-28): the 2.330.0 loop breaker's count (3 tries, then keep the link) lives PER DEVICE in dial-pairing.js (`upgradeLedgerFor(deviceId)` → the DeviceManager's `upgradeLedger` seam), keyed by the bundle version, decaying after `UPGRADE_RETRY_AFTER_MS` (10 min) — because every fresh stream REBUILDS the instance and the handshake now runs on every dial-in: measured 180 upgrades in 45 s on a never-converging device before the ledger. Two more facts of that round: `_upgrade` names `_expectedVersion()` (the bundle's) in the upgrade op — the re-exec'd daemon reports it through VIBESPACE_AGENTD_VERSION, so a server whose package.json ≠ its bundle converges in ONE upgrade instead of one per natural restart; and `_expectedVersion()` reads the WHOLE bundle for the marker (it sat at byte 1 076 247 of 1.6 MB, past the 400 000 the reader looked at, so the 2.330.0 defense #1 had silently fallen back to the package version). Gates: test-agentd-upgrade-loop (fast, the fake never-converging daemon over the real Mux + a ledger-less control + wiring pins) and test-agentd-dial's C1 leg (a real pinned daemon: ≤ 3 upgrades in 12 s, the link kept).** **A REFUSED HOST KEY KEEPS THE LINK (verify-r1 C2): client.js's `_tryOnce` no longer destroys a `stream` transport on `auth-fail` (the mux stays alive only to answer the daemon's heartbeat), dial-pairing.js remembers the refused stream (`authFailedStreams`, re-asked after `AUTH_FAIL_REHELLO_MS` = 60 s or on a fresh stream) so every op is refused at once with the way out, and the daemon's hello handler ends only a local peer (`typeof sock.end === 'function'`; a ws-min dial link has none — kept on purpose). Before: close → re-dial → accept every second, hosts.json rewritten + `hosts-updated` per second, the row `silent` 99 % of the time. Gate: test-dial-link-kept (fast, with a no-keep control copy) + test-agentd-dial attack 18 (steady auth-fail on the same link).** **A SELF-UPGRADE IS NOT A FAILED DIAL (verify-r1 C3): agentd.js raises `upgradeLanded` the moment the new bundle is repointed, and the dial loop's `close` handler returns on it ("dial-out ended — self-upgrade re-exec": no dial-status write, no retry) — the old process's socket closed inside the 200 ms exit grace with upMs < 2 s, so `dialFailureOf` said `closed-before-hello`, streak 1 landed in dial-status.json and the re-exec'd daemon's first dial-in carried attempt=1 ⇒ the row read "before that 1 attempt failed (other)" after every healthy upgrade. Gate: test-agentd-dial's C1 leg (`neverConverging` run twice: the real bundle pins attempt 0 / a clean history / the ended line; the mutant bundle without the flag set brings the old shape back).** Dial chat TERMINATE kills the device-side claude via the daemon's `kill-pipe-session` (client killPipeSession) + rm's the session token over the device link — the ssh-only teardown threw for dial and silently orphaned claude (double-JSONL-writer class). Pairing commands render `/api/device-dial`; `/api/agentd-dial` is a PERMANENT alias (in-field daemons hold it in dial.json); env `VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT` preferred, `VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT` honored forever. **RE-PAIR / IDENTITY ROTATION (2.170.0, the userW-incident class): the daemon re-reads dial.json on EVERY dial attempt and the host-token file on EVERY hello — a re-pair heals a RUNNING daemon within one retry; never cache either at startup (the cached identity dialed a dead pairing forever while the singleton blocked its replacement + launchd respawn-spammed). The installer replaces a running same-root daemon (cmdline-verified kill); macOS singleton verifies the lock pid via `ps` (no /proc — recycled pids read as "already running" forever). Multi-instance = one root/daemon per instance (`~/.vibespace/device@<dialhost>`), re-pair replaces within a root.** **REVERSE forward tcp-listen/tcp-accept/tcp-unlisten (2.148.0, the NAT-traversal tunnel)** — daemon binds 127.0.0.1:<port> ON THE DEVICE, accepts push back over the mux as new byte channels (chan ids from 0x40000000 — never collides with server-allocated 2..N; the tcp-accept control MUST precede channel data), server pipes them into its own loopback port; on link death the listener is DISOWNED not closed (port stays bound → reconnecting server re-owns same-port via connect-loop re-registration → remote mounts heal in place); both tcp paths backpressured (credit-after-drain + mux.onWritable resume); --stdio ssh bridge mode; --dial ws dial-out (Transport B; ws-min.js = hand-rolled RFC6455 client — the `head` bytes-with-the-101 upgrade trap is handled, dropping them ate first frames on fast reconnects)). client.js = DeviceManager (transports local/ssh, openSession/openPipeSession/fs*/runCmd/runStream/tcpForward/reverseForward/discovery). Server: /api/agentd-dial upgrade branch (dial-token gated, verifies hosts.dialTokenHash since 2.160.0) + dial-pair mint (writes the hash onto the dial host record; /api/agentd/devices + /api/device-mounts RETIRED in 2.160.0 — roster/test/unpair = /api/hosts, mounts = /api/machine-mounts, see machine-mounts.js). Pairing dialog has per-OS commands (mac/linux bash; WINDOWS EXPERIMENTAL via /agentd-install.ps1, PS 5.1-compatible + win32 named-pipe SOCK in the daemon; the ps1 now also persists state\dial.json + registers a logon SCHEDULED TASK, so a Windows device survives a reboot). **EVERY URL in those commands must come from `httpBase` (= `r.relayUrl || location.origin`), NEVER location.origin directly (2.246.0 bug): a relay-paired device correctly dialed the relay but was handed origin-based installer/bundle URLs its network cannot reach — it failed before the daemon ever started.** MULTI-INSTANCE pairing: dial-out installs root at ~/.vibespace/agentd@<dialhost> (per-instance daemon/tokens/bundle; installer exports VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT — forget that and the daemon reads the default root's token). INSTALLER GOTCHA (2.152.1, real Mac report): macOS has NO setsid(1) — the installer's unconditional `setsid node …` started NOTHING and printed ✓ anyway (stderr redirected into agentd.out); now setsid-or-nohup + kill-0 verification before claiming success. **NODE-FREE PAIRING (2.246.0): the installers (bash AND ps1) no longer REQUIRE node — resolution order is `--node` override → OUR private `$ROOT/node/bin/node` → PATH → newest nvm → common absolute paths → PROVISION (pinned official tarball from nodejs.org/dist, verified against that release's SHASUMS256.txt, smoke-run, then atomically `mv`d into `$ROOT/node`; `--node-only` = resolve/print/exit, the support probe). Private-BEFORE-PATH is deliberate (a launchd plist pointing at an nvm path dies at the user's next nvm upgrade); nvm-before-common-paths is the `curl|bash`-is-non-login lesson (nvm.sh never sourced ⇒ the #1 false 'no node'). Everything lands INSIDE the root, so `rm -rf $ROOT` uninstalls the runtime too — and because agentd's `spawnEnv()` prepends `path.dirname(process.execPath)`, the `#!/usr/bin/env node` agent tools resolve on a machine that never had node (2.244.4 chicken-and-egg, solved structurally). **AND THE DAEMON IS BORN SANITIZED (2026-09-14, src/agent-env.js): `_spawnLocal`, the `--stdio` bridge's spawn and the upgrade re-exec all hand a new daemon `daemonEnv(process.env)`, and `spawnEnv()` merges every child over that same sanitized base — never raw `process.env` — because the daemon is a SECOND HOLDER of the server env that outlives its restarts, and a real pipe-session claude was measured carrying a cluster integration secret a previous server life had handed the daemon (test-agentd-session's holder leg + test-integration-registry §6(h)).** CONSEQUENCE: a provisioned device is PINNED to that node forever (no OS security updates) until the pin is bumped — documented in docs/device-agent.md § Node runtime. RULE: every later node/npm invocation in the installers uses the resolved absolute `$NODE_BIN`/`$NODE_DIR/npm`, NEVER bare `node` (launchd/systemd get no PATH of ours). set -e footguns in that block: `[ -e x ] && mv` and bare `x=$(cmd|pipe)` under pipefail both exit the script — keep new predicates inside `if`/`|| true`. musl + 32-bit Windows refuse honestly with fix instructions (official builds are glibc/64-bit only). Instance-side fallback mirror `GET /vibespace-node/:version/:file` (server.js, auth-exempt, fixed upstream + strict filename allowlist + disk cache in data/node-cache/) for devices that reach this instance but not nodejs.org. Tests: scripts/test-node-bootstrap.mjs (19 asserts, local HTTP fixture + a bwrap node-free sandbox; covers tamper/unlisted-checksum refusal, re-use, nvm discovery, override).** E2E: scripts/dbg-pair-smoke.mjs (17 asserts, REAL daemon dial + mount chain + UI rows). **2026-09-25 (lane C2 verify fix) — THE CLIENT FAILS EVERY IN-FLIGHT REQUEST THE INSTANT ITS LINK DIES.** `mux.onDead` used to tear down `sessions` but leave `conn.pending` alone, so a control op already written to the dead mux (a desktop app's relaunch / stop / keep-alive / windows through `desktopServe`) waited out its OWN `timeoutMs` — 60 s for desktop-serve, 90 s browser-serve, 20 s opencode-serve — while the device re-dialed in ~110 ms (measured on a real daemon SIGKILLed 103 ms into a relaunch: 503 after 60 004 ms). A reply can never arrive on a NEW connection (it has its own pending map), so onDead now resolves every pending entry with `{error:'device link lost', linkLost:true}` and `_request` throws it with `code:'link_lost'`; every caller already handled a rejection — it just comes now instead of at the timeout. `runStream(cmd, args, {…, timeoutMs})` / `_streamOp(req, {onData, timeoutMs = 120000})`: the deadline belt is PER OP (the 120 s constant is only the default every pre-C2 caller keeps) and settles `{error:'run-stream timed out', timedOut:true}` — the belt only stops WAITING, the device's child is never killed by it. Gate: test-desktop-remote §8 (a real daemon SIGSTOPped with the op pending, then SIGKILLed ⇒ host_unavailable in ms; CONTROL = a client copy without the reject answers at the request's own timeout; run-stream's per-op belt over the real daemon).

### machine-mounts.js

  **The pull mount's argv (lane mount-argv-dir-cache):** src/device-mount.js `pullMountArgs(mountpoint, cacheDir)` = `rcloneMountArgs({row: PULL_ROW})` — the hub's builder; `PULL_ROW.dirCache = {ttl: HELD_TICK_MS}` (5 s, webdav has no ChangeNotify), the argv token for token what it was. The REMOTE host mount (machine-mounts.js `rcloneCmd`, a shell string run on the host) is not built by it yet.

  machine-mounts.js    — MachineMounts (B-f3e8 2.160.0 — HostMounts 2.147.0 + DeviceMounts 2.153.0 collapsed into ONE manager; records carry dir:'push'|'pull', keyed by hostId, store data/machine-mounts.json, both legacy stores constructor-migrated → .migrated; routes /api/machine-mounts* (POST :hostId {dir,…}), broadcast machine-mounts-updated). PUSH = mount THIS instance's folder ON the machine, OS-aware (Linux rclone/FUSE; macOS rclone/macFUSE else native mount_webdav — macFUSE probed ON the Mac since 2.160.0, the old check read the SERVER's /dev/fuse; Windows rclone/WinFsp else net use; rclone auto-installed remote-side w/ unzip→busybox→python3 fallbacks). Transport: _davBase prefers the agentd REVERSE-FORWARD TUNNEL (remote mounts http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dav over the device link — NAT-proof; dial machines tunnel-ONLY, ssh falls back to agentd.publicUrl); tunnelPort per record. PULL = the machine's folder mounted INTO this workspace over hosts.device(hostId) (serve-folder→tcp-forward→rclone webdav ro — works for ssh AND dial identically); live chain in-memory, restore()/onMachineLinked heal recorded pulls + re-own push tunnel ports (a re-dial means the daemon RE-EXECED → stale handles torn down first, real Mac report 2.158.1) + 90s child-process-ls health sweep (never node fs on a fuse mountpoint). unmount = best-effort remote teardown but ALWAYS token-revoke + record-drop (dead machine can't hold a credential); host removal → onMachineUnpaired drops all its mounts. GOTCHAS (real e2e catches): mint() returns {raw, rec} not {token,id}; NEVER execFileSync in anything sharing the process with /dav (event-loop block = FUSE IO hang); detached remote rclone needs FULL fd redirect (</dev/null >/dev/null 2>>log) or the ssh ControlMaster never frees; setsid is LINUX-ONLY — conditionally prefixed (macOS died at command-not-found with the error swallowed into the remote log, now tail'd back into the dialog); **TRAILING SLASH on a pull's shared path 403'd EVERY file (2.168.0, real userW Mac→VibeSpace report): the daemon serve-folder confines with `root + path.sep`, so a root ending in `/` (e.g. `/Users/me/Downloads/`) double-slashes the prefix (`…Downloads//`) — the root listing passes but every subpath 403s → rclone "couldn't list files: 403 Forbidden", mount never comes up. PUSH was immune (mountPush runs path.resolve). Fix strips the trailing slash in THREE places: mountPull (intake), _up (heals an existing record without a device-daemon update), serveFolder (daemon defense) — dbg-pair-smoke now pulls a trailing-slash path so its file-read assertion guards it.** Tests: test-machine-migrate.mjs (migration guard) + test-host-mounts(-tunnel).mjs (push e2e) + dbg-pair-smoke.mjs (pull e2e over a real dialed daemon)

Separate defaults per backend (defaultAccountId / defaultCodexAccountId). 2.59.1: NO rm -rf (concurrent same-account sessions), tar --keep-newer-files newest-wins (host-side refresh rotates the live token — don't clobber it) + poison-heal probe (remote creds file missing its validity marker is rm'd pre-extract). list() returns tail-8 for keys, email/plan/loggedIn for subs (read-only). importFromCli() captures a Console primaryApiKey. **remove() POOL HYGIENE (2.335.0, owner report: deleting the account a pool sat on broke the whole pool): deleting a claude subscription strips it from every pool's explicit member list, re-points the default symlink to a live member (or unlinks it — absent = honestly signed-out, a dangling link is a phantom login), and re-points/drops per-session links that billed to it (`_healPoolsAfterRemoval`); gated by test-pool-signed-out (17).** **Re-login identity guard (2.333.0, owner directive): `reloginResolve(id)` finalizes an on-this-machine re-login by COMPARING the fresh login's identity to the record — same ⇒ in-place; matches ANOTHER record ⇒ creds move there ('moved'); unknown ⇒ auto-SPLIT to a new entry named by the email while the original stays signed-out with history intact (a friend logging the wrong account can never rebrand/pollute a record); route POST /api/accounts/:id/relogin-finalize, watcher in manage-agents toasts all outcomes; matrix scripts/test-account-relogin.mjs (13).** Lets the user's OWN subscription logins coexist per backend, switchable per session — the CLI's own /login only keeps one active at a time, so VibeSpace remembers each separately (like signing in/out without losing the others). **§ban-safety (2.59.1, after a real Max ban+refund — see [[reference_multi_subscription]]):** NO background /api/oauth/usage polling with sub tokens (that off-CLI fixed-cadence automated call on idle accounts is the #1 bot-flag: ToS §3.7 + 2026-02-20 OAuth-clarification) — usage is now captured PASSIVELY by data/bin/vibespace-usage (STATIC file), a statusLine hook injected via --settings into LOCAL TERMINAL sessions only that harvests the CLI's OWN rate_limits into data/usage-cache/<key>.json (zero API calls; chat/stream-json has no statusline → last-known; server ingestPassiveUsage reads the dir, no network). Subscription creds shipping to REMOTE is OFF by default (setting accounts.shipSubscriptionToRemote; ws-handler remoteAccountEnv gate throws with guidance) — a sub token from a datacenter IP is an impossible-travel/abuse signal; default = "log in on the host"; API keys always ship (sanctioned programmatic path)) **list() POOLED-FIRST (2.369.18, P1 codex pool UI): the pooled branch is evaluated BEFORE the per-backend branches for every backend — the codex branch used to win, so a codex pool listed as a bare ChatGPT login with no `pooled/current/currentName/memberOptions/auto/hot` (no client surface could operate it AND the engine's `type==='pooled' && a.auto` tick enumeration never saw it). The pool row reads identity THROUGH the symlink with the member's own auth reader (readCodexSubAuth / readSubCreds) and carries `hotSupported` = capsOf(backend).hotSwitch==='verified' (src/backend-caps.js) so the UI hides the hot toggle where the engine ignores it (codex). Pinned in test-codex-pool.**

  **LOGIN-SESSION EXPIRY (2026-09-07, src/login-expiry.js):** `loginStateOf(id, now)` answers "when does this account's LOGIN end" through the harness descriptor's OPTIONAL `creds.loginState` — claude declares it, every other harness simply does not and gets 'unknown' (an absent reader is honest; a fabricated 'ok' is not). Every subscription row in `list()` carries `loginState`; a POOL's row carries `poolLoginState` = its members' WORST plus `worstId`/`worstName` (a pool has no login of its own). `_poolLoginCandidates` asks TWO questions, not one (round-2 verifier, reproduced against this instance's own store): an EXPLICIT `members: [...]` list is what the user NAMED, so a signed-out member of it IS the pool's finding and stays in the summary; an IMPLICIT pool (`members: null` — the default, and the shape of the only pool here) has its membership DEFINED as `poolMembers()`, so an account that is signed out was never a member of it. Round 1 used the over-broad set for both, and on a pool whose three routing members were all logged in it read `logged-out` forever, drew a permanent red chip offering to re-login an account dead 700 h that the pool never routes to, and — because worst-of ranks 'logged-out' above 'expiring' — MASKED the CURRENT target's login dying in 16 h. The current link target is always in the set even if its own login has since died: the pool is pointed AT it, so it is the pool's problem however it got there. `resolveForSpawn`'s pool self-heal now ORDERS the alive list by `loginRank` (an 'expired' member still parses as loggedIn, because the tokens are only blanked at the CLI's next failed refresh, so without this the heal happily re-points onto a login that fails the first turn) — an ordering, never a filter: every member being expired must still start the session and then say so. **SAME-SPELLING TRAP:** the `/relogin` + `/subscription/:id/finalize` routes also return `loginState`, a STRING ('error') about how the login TERMINAL run went. Different objects, different types; never join them (a comment at that route says so too).

### account-pool-auto.js

**THE CONVERSATION'S PIN (2026-09-28, lane-pool-pin): `decidePinnedPlacement(opts)`** — `pin` null ⇒ null (the caller's `decidePoolSwitch` is master's: a seeded sweep); the pin CAN SERVE unless named (`pin-member-unknown` ∉ candidates/membership · `pin-member-excluded` · `pin-login-dead` · `pin-exhausted` = a family-view bucket under its HARD bar); on it ⇒ `{to:null, reason:'pin'}` (the soft band included — no EDF, no warm hold); elsewhere + `explicit` ⇒ `{to: pin, reason:'pin'}` now; elsewhere by the engine ⇒ a return needs SETTLE (hot bar + MIN_GAIN on every bucket, a login not about to die) ⇒ `pin-return`, mid-turn `pin-hold` (why `pin-mid-turn`), not settled ⇒ treated as `pin-exhausted`; cannot serve ⇒ `{…decidePoolSwitch(opts on autoReadCache), reason:'pin-exhausted', autoReason, pinWhy}` — priority and membership included, so pin > priority > automatic falls out of one call. Controls: stay / settle / mid-turn hold patched copies.

**MANUAL PRIORITY + THE REMOVED-MEMBER WALL (2026-09-28, lane-pool-pin; owner: "手动切换整个池其实比较confusing…做成'手动优先级'" + the 17:22 decision, and "如果用到一半把账号从池里排除，不会第一时间触发切走").** `decidePoolSwitch` takes two new OPTIONAL inputs; omitting both is byte-identical (seeded sweeps against a `git show b970f16d:` copy loaded through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs — 900 + 1200 verdicts). ① `membership` (the CONFIGURED member ids, `accounts.poolMembership`, login-blind): a `currentId` outside it answers `reason:'not-a-member'`, the HARD band — moves now, warm or mid-turn, past the no-data hold and the anti-flap gain floor; nobody left ⇒ the blocked outcome carries `notMember:{id}` and `poolBlockedNotice` says "X is no longer a member of the pool and no member can take over". A separate input from `members` (the logged-in DECISION list) so a signed-out member keeps `login-expired`. ② `priority` (an ORDERED list of member ids; empty/null = automatic): `priorityRankOf`/`priorityOrder` sort every candidate list (ranked / near / credits) by (rank, then EDF) — listed before unlisted, unlisted by today's rule; an exhausted move keeps its cause (`exhausted`) and names the rule (`placedBy:'priority'`, `priorityRank` 1-based or null); a HIGHER-ranked member that can SETTLE (every bucket over its hot bar + MIN_GAIN — the return's hysteresis) takes the conversation back with `reason:'priority-return'` whatever `proactive` says — at the next STOP: `warm.inTurn` ⇒ `none('priority-hold', {wouldTo, wouldToName, priorityRank})`, NEVER the warm-cache hold (automatic keeps EDF + the warm hold); the proactive EDF tier runs only between members of EQUAL rank (a listed member is never left for a sooner deadline); the no-data and `healthy` early returns are skipped under a priority (a return is not a judgement about the current member). Every safety bar is the same in both modes (exclude, login near-expiry, credits last, reserve floor, overage). `rankPoolMembers({priority})` orders the sealed-orders snapshot the same way. Gates: test-pool-auto (the removed-member and priority tables, both master sweeps, seven patched-copy controls, the real engine + the real routes).

**THE PROJECTION (B-f69c ③, 2.369.163, owner ruling ut-1c6c15a2db ③ "1%/min 燃烧 40 分钟读一次不够").** The pool decides on the estimate of NOW; at a fast burn a bucket a few points above its line is across it before any scheduled reading lands. Three PURE pieces: `projectCacheAhead(cache, burn, nowSec, leadSec)` advances every bucket by its own burn (`burn` = the estimator's `burnRates`, utilization per minute, keys `fiveHour`/`sevenDay`/`scoped:<name>`; an absent key is no claim) — never a window that resets inside the lead (it refills; advancing a spent number past its own reset would invent a wall) and never an EMPTY window (B-8b12), returning the SAME object when nothing moved; `projectionCrossing(cache, burn, nowSec, {hot})` = the soonest bucket to reach its switch line (the hot bar on a hot pool, else the hard bar), strictly in the FUTURE — a bucket already under its line is the estimate's business — and never past its own reset; `PROJECTION_LEAD_SEC = 300` = the fast rung's own floor (the longest a reading the projection asked for can be withheld by pacing, so an early move covers exactly the stretch no fresh reading can). **The auto-cli rule:** `decideCliRefresh` is now one eligibility rule `cliRefreshWhy(a, now, opts)` → `'projection' | 'drift' | 'stale-active' | 'stale-idle' | null` + `nextScheduledReadMs` (the age rung, or the drift rung at the current burn `estBurnPtPerMin`); a `projCrossInMs` that lands BEFORE the next scheduled read asks the SAME rung now, ranked first (soonest crossing), under the SAME 5-min floor, failure backoff and one-per-tick serialization — event-driven by a projection, never a cadence, never a new vendor path. **ONE READING PER CROSSING (quota r1, the verifier's slow-approach simulation):** the floor paces a spawn but never limited the drift rung (it needs 4 pt of movement between reads), and the projection had no such self-limiter — after each reading the crossing was still ahead and still before the next scheduled read, so `projection` was answered again every time the floor cleared (0.05 %/min from 7 %: reads at min 5, 10, …, 35 = 7 where the pre-B-f69c rule took none before the line). The loop now carries `projReadCrossAt` = the crossing INSTANT its last SUCCESSFUL projection read was spent on (server.js `projBought`, stamped after `refreshViaCliPanel` answered ok — a failed read bought nothing, the failure backoff paces its retry); `cliRefreshWhy` answers `projection` for the same instant within `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` (5 min, the estimate's own wobble) never again, a crossing that MOVED further (the burn changed) is a new question, and the drift/age/idle rungs ignore the memory. The same approach now reads once at min 5, then on the age rung. Not adopted from the verifier's sketch: a second arm "re-ask when the reading is older than the crossing is far" — on the same world it re-arms a halving sequence (min 22.5, 31, 36), i.e. the cadence again; the cold-conversation 300 s projected view covers the last stretch before the line. **THE WARM RULES STAND:** the engine hands a projected view only to a decision about a COLD conversation — a projection alone never moves a warm one (the .149 warm-cache hold and the .153 first-stop rule judge only real readings). Gates: test-pool-auto (the pure legs + a REAL-engine world with one cold and one warm conversation on a burning member, and two scratch-dir patched copies — the warm gate removed ⇒ the warm one moves too; the lead zeroed (master) ⇒ the cold one meets the line), test-auto-cli-refresh §8 (the owner's arithmetic, the drift-first case, floor, ranking, one pick, wiring pins), test-usage-estimator (burn). **THE MEMORY IS THE BUCKET, THE PASSIVE READING IS THE READING, AND THE PACING STATE OUTLIVES A RESTART (quota r2, the r2 verifier's three reproduced findings).** ① The r1 memory keyed on the crossing INSTANT, and the instant is the burn window's own noise: `burnRates` is a 10-min trailing window, so under Poisson arrivals at the SAME mean burn the projected crossing moved by more than `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` on 47-65 % of ticks (median 13.6 min, p90 52 min at 1 request/min) and every wobble was bought again at the floor — 3-4 projection reads before one line where a constant burn took 1; a 10-member fleet 42 projection reads in its first hour instead of 9. The loop now remembers WHICH BUCKET of WHICH WINDOW bought a reading: `projReads = {label: {at, resetsAt, boughtAt}}` per account (PURE `projectionReadsAfter` stamps it after a SUCCESSFUL projection read, pruning expired records), `projectionCrossing` returns the crossing bucket's `resetsAt` (0 = unknown) and the engine's `projectionRereadFor` passes it through, and `cliRefreshWhy` answers `projection` never for a bucket `projectionBucketBought` says already bought — until its window resets (an unknown reset: `PROJECTION_MEMORY_MS`, 5 h, after the purchase). A second bucket is its own question (two families ⇒ two reads; alternation between them re-buys nothing); the r1 instant band stays as the secondary guard across buckets (`projReadCrossAt` = the last bought instant). Not adopted: a proportional band (max(5 min, 0.5×distance)) — the verifier measured it halving the re-buys (42 → 29), not ending them. ② The projection arm now also needs `age >= floorMs`: a passive (statusline) reading 30 s old IS the number the projection would buy — the verifier's passive-every-minute world spent 2 projection reads with a 30-s-old reading at each (worse than no passive readings: each rebase zeroes drift and pushes the drift rung's horizon out, so the projection is 'before the next scheduled read' more often). Because `fetchedAt` lives on disk this is also the rung's restart-proof floor. The drift/age/idle rungs are untouched. ③ `attempts`, `fails` and `projReads` were closure state in server.js, the first tick 60 s after boot: every restart re-bought the same bucket with no floor (a restart every 3 min: 11 spawns in 40 min; every 2 min: 15). The loop moved to **src/server/auto-cli-loop.js** (`createAutoCliLoop(deps)` → `{tick, start, state}`, clock/RNG injectable) and persists its pacing state in `data/auto-cli-state.json` (tmp + rename after every spawn — at most one write per tick, so nothing is left to flush on SIGTERM; an unreadable file starts empty, the `age >= floorMs` guard is the floor without it). Gates: test-auto-cli-refresh §9 drives the REAL loop with the REAL rule, projectionCrossing and burnRates over a synthetic ledger (constant and Poisson arrivals, three seeds → exactly ONE projection read each; two families → one per bucket; a passive reading every minute → zero spawns; crash loops every 3 and 2 min → the no-restart control's count; a 10-member fleet → at most one projection read per member, 17/15/17 spawns per hour in every arrival model), each fix with a scratch-dir patched copy as its negative control (the r1 instant band alone re-buys under Poisson; no age guard spends a read on a 30-s-old reading; an in-memory-only loop re-buys after a restart). **THE READ IS SPENT NEXT TO THE LINE; A RECORD THAT CANNOT BE A WINDOW IS NO MEMORY (quota r3, the r3 verifier's placement and state-file worlds).** ① One read per bucket was spent at the FIRST eligible tick — the moment the reading turned floor-old — i.e. as far from the line as the floor allowed: a 10 % / 0.05 %/min approach read at min 43 for a line at min 80, so the estimate the pool met the line with was 37 min old and `PROJECTION_LEAD_SEC`'s promise no longer held. The projection arm now also needs `cross <= projWindowMs` (`PROJECTION_WINDOW_MS` = the floor + the lead = 10 min): the read lands in the last window before the line (measured 71 min for that world, 8-10 min before the line on every slow world; the fleet's spawns per hour unchanged). ② A read of ANY rung that lands while the bucket's crossing is inside that window is the purchase too (the loop marks it): the two-family world used to buy Fable twice — the idle rung at min 42, a projection at min 47. ③ `projectionBucketBought` ignores a record whose `resetsAt` lies more than `PROJECTION_RECORD_MAX_MS` (8 d — no vendor window is longer than 7 d) past its purchase (a ms-shaped resetsAt silenced its bucket until year 58 700; `projectionReadsAfter` prunes it), and answers "not bought" when the crossing names a DIFFERENT known window than the record by more than `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` (a panel-estimated reset corrected by an exact event, the next window) — a minute of disagreement or an unknown crossing window stays the same window. Gates: test-auto-cli-refresh §① (placement ≤ 10 min before the line on three worlds + a no-window patched copy reading 37 min early; each bucket bought once with a projection-only-buys patched copy re-buying) and §⑤ (the window/record pure legs, a ms-poisoned state file healing in the real loop).
