**LOGIN LIFETIME IS A SECOND WAY TO BE UNUSABLE (2026-09-07, src/login-expiry.js).** Quota was the only thing that could make a member unusable, so a member whose OAuth LOGIN had expired kept being picked (its cache still read healthy) and every turn on it died. `decidePoolSwitch`/`rankPoolMembers` take an OPTIONAL `readLogin(id)`: **omit it and every rule is inert — the decision is byte-identical to the pre-login one** (a harness that cannot read a login deadline must not have its members quietly demoted; the suite pins that with an all-unknown control). Three rules: ① a member whose login is 'expired'/'logged-out' is never a candidate, and when that empties the list the reason is its own named outcome `all-logins-expired` with `loginBlocked: [{id,name,state,msLeft}]` — NOT `no-members`, because the fix is a 30-second re-login, not waiting a week for a window. **ROUND 2: that claim may only be made when the login gate is the ONLY thing that emptied the list.** The login gate runs BEFORE the quota gate, so round 1 let one login-blocked member outrank any number of quota-dead ones: with two members out of 5h quota and one 20 min from its login deadline, the engine announced "every other member's login session has expired or is about to", suppressed `alt`/`what`/`rest`, and sent the user to re-login accounts whose logins were fine. Now `quotaBlockedN` counts the quota drops, `why` is `'all-logins-expired'` only when it is zero, `loginBlocked` is carried on the quota reasons too, and the notice appends "Also needing a re-login: …" — and each member states its OWN fact through the pure `loginBlockedText` (expired / signed out / expires in 20 min), because "has expired" is a lie about a member that is merely `expiring`. **ROUND 3: the CURRENT member's own dead login is a THIRD wall, and it was being smuggled through `deadBuckets`.** `loginBlocked` skips the current member BY CONSTRUCTION, and `all-logins-expired` is derived from that list, so the round-2 login sentence could only ever describe the OTHERS. Round 2 prepended `loginBucketLabel(current)` into `deadBuckets` instead — which the engine renders as `spent: <list>` followed by the quota remedy — so a pool whose current member was signed out printed `Pool "P": no member can serve it — spent: login signed out. Conversations on it will hit a limit until a window resets, you add a member, or you move them off the pool.` once per hour, forever: a quota remedy for the one wall that never heals on a timer, and the single account the user had to act on was the only one the notice could not name. Now `bucketDetail` emits `fromLogin` (the pure `loginWallPhrase`, a CLAUSE — "login session expired" / "login is signed out" — not the list-item label) as its own field and `deadBuckets`/`liveBuckets` stay a pure QUOTA sentence; the current member's quota facts ride as a side note (`(its quota is also spent: 5h 0%)`) and are dropped entirely when its quota is fine, because "out of quota" about a 90% member is simply false ② a member inside NEAR_MS (30 min) is never a **VOLUNTARY** switch target (a conversation moved onto a login about to die just buys a second outage) — it still serves its OWN conversation, and `rankPoolMembers` drops it too because sealed orders are executed by the DEVICE hours later. **ROUND 2: it is NOT a filter on the ESCAPE path.** Round 1 made it one, so a hard-dead current member whose only quota-healthy candidate had 20 min of login left refused to move at all — strictly worse than the shipped behaviour (measured both ways: shipped moved to a 100%-quota member, round 1 returned `all-logins-expired`). NEAR candidates now collect in their own `nearRanked` list (they still pass the quota gate) and a hard-dead current member falls back to it when `ranked` is empty; the decision keeps the `reason` that says why we LEFT ('login-expired'/'exhausted' — a new reason string would have lost the 180s dwell-belt exemption) and adds `toLoginNear` for what we landed ON, so the notice can say the reprieve is short. Soft-exhausted and proactive tiers never see the scraps ③ `edfCompare` gains `loginPenalty` as its LAST tiebreak, so an 'expiring' member ranks below an EQUAL 'ok' one and nothing the quota rules separate is ever reordered. The CURRENT member's dead login is treated as hard exhaustion (escape now, take scraps, `reason: 'login-expired'`) and OVERRIDES the no-data hold — a file saying "cannot authenticate" is a fact, not ignorance; the MIN_GAIN anti-flap floor is skipped there because it compares remaining QUOTA, which is meaningless (and `cur.remaining` is null, so `null + 3` would have blocked every escape). Engine side: ONE memoized `poolReadLogin()` per tick feeds every decidePoolSwitch/rankPoolMembers call; `quotaVerdictFor` cannot answer `usable` through a dead login and contributes NO blockedUntil for it (unlike a quota wall it does not heal on a timer — only the user does); the auth-failure notice says "login session expired (refresh token expired at T) — re-login needed" when the file says so, keeping today's wording otherwise. **The hourly pool-blocked NOTICE is the PURE `poolBlockedNotice(d, {poolName, currentName})`, not an inline composition in the engine** (round 3): it was inline, so every test ever written asserted the decision object and none the sentence — which is exactly where the login-as-a-spent-bucket defect lived. Three walls, each claiming only what it knows: `fromLogin` (the current member — leads, and its `fix` is "Re-login <name> in Manage Agents"), `all-logins-expired` (the others — `why` lists them), and the quota arrays (the shipped sentence, byte-identical when no login is dead); a sibling that also needs a re-login is still named under the `Also needing a re-login:` clause when the CURRENT login is the headline, and the "best other member is at N%" clause is suppressed under any login wall because waiting is not the fix there. Gate: scripts/test-login-expiry.mjs §3 + §3d (the notice STRING, with the pure-quota and all-logins-expired sentences as byte-exact negative controls).

**AUTH-FAILURE EVICTION (2.335.0, owner report: 封号/欠费/过期 never triggered a switch — quota was the engine's only signal and a dead-auth account often still SHOWS rich quota):** pure `classifyAuthFailure({status,message,attempt})` (403 immediate; 401 needs attempt≥2 — a lone first 401 is the mid-refresh-race shape; ban/credit/oauth-expired messages immediate; 5xx/529 never). Engine side (usage-pool-engine): `notePoolAuthFailure(session, sid, info)` fed from session-stdout's api_retry + error-result records — marks the member (10min TTL, cleared early when the creds file is REWRITTEN i.e. re-login), re-points the session's link + the pool default off it via the same rankPoolMembers EDF, notices the user, cold pools get the restart ask; quota eval + chooser exclude marked members (`healthyPoolMembers`, falling back to the full list when EVERY member is marked). Runs regardless of `auto` — routing around a dead account is the 2.330.2 heal's live-session sibling, not quota optimization. **2.335.1 review hardening: evict throttle per (member,session) not per member (else sibling conversations stay pinned 60s each); default-move collects ALL default-billing sessions into the cold-pool restart ask; auth-mark clears on TOKEN-MATERIAL change never mtime (repointPoolSymlink utimes-bumps creds on every re-point); message-only classification needs API-layer context (`API_CTX_RE`) so agent tool output can't evict; removing a pool's LAST explicit member keeps the stale list (null = ALL subs — silent widening re-pointed billing to excluded accounts). ALSO: the restore smoke now overlays the WORKING TREE (pre-commit runs used to test HEAD — how 2.335.0's lost engine binding passed a green smoke).**

**A LAPSED SUBSCRIPTION IS A DURABLE MEMBER STATE (lane pool-subscription-lapsed, 2.369.241; owner 2026-10-08: "UCI Max 订阅到期没续费，系统会自动排除它吗？续费后不想重新添加").** Production (journal): the pool moved four conversations + its default ONTO the canceled UCI Max (its cached readings looked best — a lapse leaves no reading); the first turn failed with "Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code"; the AUTH-FAILURE mark above (10 min, IN MEMORY, cleared by `credsTokenSig` — a routine token REFRESH counts as a re-login) let it attract placements again within minutes, a failed turn + a notice each repeat. NOW: the harness descriptor's OPTIONAL `quota.classifyServeFailure(info)` → `{kind: 'lapsed'|'auth', why}` reads a CLOSED census (claude-quota.js `SERVE_CENSUS`, measured with `strings` over CLI 2.1.288: that sentence = the CLI's `oauth_org_not_allowed` rendering of the API's "OAuth authentication is currently not allowed for this organization"; "account is on hold" / revoked / "organization has been disabled" stay `auth`; codex 0.159.3 has none — its plan wall `usage_not_included` stays an exhaustion enum). A lapse writes `serve: {state: 'lapsed', since, why, lastFail, todoId?}` ON THE ACCOUNT RECORD (accounts.setServeState — the atomic `_save`, no sidecar; membership, note, links, readings kept). The engine (`memberServeLapsed` / `noteMemberServeFailure`, usage-pool-engine.js beside `memberAuthFailed`) folds it into `poolReadLogin` as `li.serve` — every gate asks it, PURE `memberLapsed(li)`: never a candidate (named in `lapsedBlocked`, reason `all-lapsed` when lapses alone emptied the list), never ranked, a conversation ON it escapes with `subscription-lapsed` (band hard, past the no-data hold, the gain floor and the 180 s belt), a pin to it ⇒ `pin-lapsed`; `healthyPoolMembers` drops it with no fallback. It is said ONCE per episode (one journal line + one For-you item, origin pool; a repeat only moves `lastFail`) — never the per-attempt toast. RE-ADMISSION = POSITIVE EVIDENCE ONLY (`lapseCleared`, verify r1 ②⑦): a reading of the member's OWN window PRODUCED after `lastFail` — a verified panel answer, a `rate-limit-event`, or numbers (`readingFingerprint`) that moved from those recorded at the failure; a statusline re-stamp of the pre-lapse numbers is a write time, never evidence. A renewal's first panel, refused on the pre-lapse window witness, re-anchors it (`reanchorLapsedMember`, phase-only + nobody else's window). `quotaVerdictFor` refuses a lapsed member (no billed continue); `soonestUsableMember` / the store's default fallback / `poolChooserForModel` never pick it, and `resolveForSpawn` refuses an all-lapsed placement by name (`all_lapsed`); an account no pool lists gets no pool words (`inPools`); under refresh 'off' the words name the setting; never a clock, never a token change. The auto-cli idle rung keeps probing it at the wandering 30–60 min cadence (no failure backoff to hours); the panel's failed answer reaches the census; the roster's "subscription inactive since … · Re-check" posts the existing ⟳ (a lapsed member skips the token ladder — only the panel's answer counts); `onMemberReadingFresh` re-judges at once. Gated by test-pool-serve-lapsed (§1–§6, a token-refresh mutant red) + test-pool-auto "LAPSED:" legs.

**WALL = GROUND TRUTH + OBSERVED-ORG AWARE EVALUATION (B-2c9b, owner-approved plan A+B 2026-09-05; usage-pool-engine).** Three same-day production occurrences: a walled turn's `onWalledTurn` read the POOL scope and logged "usable via <linked member>" off the linked member's healthy cache, while `usage-limit-banner-marked` had landed on a DIFFERENT account — the org the CLI was actually running on (193 `usage-reading-reattributed` events had moved the session's readings there); the pool only moved 1.5-3 min later when an edf/exhaustion reading arrived, and in-flight subagents died with "session limit" in the gap. **Invariant: a wall is ground truth for the account it lands on; readings only confirm.** ① **Plan A — demotion on BLOCKED entry.** Every wall signal carries the org-verified cache key its mark landed on (`noteWallSignal(session, {resetsAtMs, bucket, scopedName, key})` — claude rejected event, banner boolean (bucket = the name parseLimitBanner gave the cache mark; still NO time from text), all three codex sites) and a per-account ring of walled-turn timestamps (`_wallRing`, one entry per turn per key — a turn's banner + rejected event are ONE wall; 120s window, `wallCount` sums the identity group). `demoteWalledAccount(session, sigs)` resolves the wall's member (the last signal's key, else `orgVerifiedKey(session, usageCacheKeyFor(session), 'wall')`; pool members or the linked member only — non-pooled sessions return `not-pooled`, their own cache mark already is the truth) and marks the affected bucket exhausted NOW through `captureRateLimitEvent(…, source:'wall')` — the SAME write path readings use (utilization 1, status limited, resetsAt = the signal's future reset else the cached future reset else the bounded 5h/24h guess; fetchedAt now, so anchors / the estimator (re-anchors on the newer rawCache) / verdicts see it in this tick). **Misattribution guard (the 2.368.34 class — the link is never the org a running CLI is on):** demote only when the account saw ≥2 walled turns inside 120s (any sessions) OR it IS the session's OTel-observed org (≤10min); a single wall on an account the session is not verifiably on HOLDS (journal `[wall] <id>: single wall on <name> (session not observed there) — holding the demotion`, event `wall-demote-held`) — the near-fire/pre-fire probe or the next wall inside 120s settles it. Journal `[wall] demoted <name> <bucket> until <iso> (n walls / observed-org)`, event `wall-demote`. **②bis RE-BASED 2026-09-07 (owner decision ut-1c6c15a2db ①/④, after the fire loop): plan B's rule is REFUTED for BLOCKING decisions and kept for VALUES.** The premise was "a hot-switched CLI keeps its old token, so the observation names what it is burning". The owner's post-mortem corrected it: `organization.id` on an `api_request` is the identity the CLI cached in its config dir at SPAWN — the credential file itself IS re-read (that is exactly what the re-point's mtime bump exists for). Under plan B every rejection was therefore filed against the spawn-time org while the LINKED member — whose credentials the process actually reads — stayed "healthy" in the cache forever; the verdict answered "usable via <link>" on every cycle, the per-session pass "switched" to the member the link was already on (740 `(re-point, same target)` lines in the incident journal), and `fireNow()` continued a session that was rejected again half a second later. Now: **a REJECTION is a fact about the credential SLOT** — `wallSlotFor(session)` = the per-session link (or the pool default link for a session without one), validated as a real member of THIS pool (`validateBillingSlot`, reasons `no-slot`/`slot-not-a-member`/`slot-unreadable`; ~~`poolMembers()` already filters by loggedIn, so a separate credentials leg would be an unsatisfiable guard — deleted functionality wearing a check's clothes~~ — **REFUTED 2026-09-07**: `parseAuth` reports `loggedIn:true` for a login whose access AND refresh tokens have BOTH expired, so that leg is satisfiable and it is exactly the gap that let dead-account readings look authorised; `validateBillingSlot` now carries it as `slot-wiped`/`slot-expired`/… and the suite proves the state leg fires. The suite still pins that every named reason is reachable), and its `slotOk` verdict rides ON THE SIGNAL because it is only true AT THE MOMENT THE REJECTION ARRIVES (by turn end the pool has usually re-pointed the link off the account that just refused us — measured in the repro harness). The function split is the fix: `sessionBillingMember` (link, slot-validated) answers every BLOCKING question — the demotion target, the verdict order + `viaId`, the per-session switch's `currentId`, both probe targets, `_wallScope`, and the loop breaker's fire identity; ~~`sessionReadingMember` (observed over link, the old body verbatim) answers only `resolveUsageKey`~~ — **REFUTED AND DELETED 2026-09-07 (readings-by-slot, the entry further down this file)**: a utilization NUMBER does describe whatever token produced it, but the observation never NAMED that token — it names the identity the CLI cached at SPAWN, so this half filed every hot-switched session's values under the account it started on. The one resolver is now `readingSlotFor` (the validated credential slot, turn-pinned, `wallSlotFor`'s twin) and `resolveUsageKey` calls `sessionBillingMember` like every blocking question; the observation survives only as `corroborateReading` (a label). The observation is corroboration: it still logs the divergence once per session per 10min, still appears in the walled-turn line as `[billing <link>, OTel observed <org>]`, and still authorises a demotion on the observed member (that rung stands). **The verification ladder gains a top rung**: a wall on the session's OWN validated slot is ground truth by itself (we know what the symlink points at — strictly better evidence than a telemetry attribute); anything else still needs ≥2 walls in 120s or the observed-org match, and the journal names which rung authorised it (`(1 walls / credential slot)` / `(1 walls / observed-org)` / `(2 walls / 2-walls)`). **Plus a per-SESSION memory**: `noteSessionWall(sid, member)` records "this member rejected THIS conversation" (10min, `SESSION_WALL_MS`, written even when the demotion is HELD — "it rejected me" is true either way), unioned with the breaker's own `recentFireFailures`; `quotaVerdictFor` cannot answer `usable` through such a member and `decidePoolSwitch({exclude})` cannot pick one (a NAMED pure input, reported as `all-rejected` — never a silently empty candidate list; `pessimism` was the wrong tool: "it just said no to this conversation" is not a percentage, and docking it would let a big enough gap re-select it next tick). Known bound: a member whose demotion was HELD and whose cache reads healthy is quarantined for 10min, so the arm may sit on the rejection's own `resetsAt` rather than the shorter quarantine — the wall probe ladder (0→30m→1h→2h) re-verdicts and takes over. **③ ROUND 3 — the slot is resolved ONCE PER REJECTION, not once per RECORD.** ONE rejection arrives as several records (`rate_limit_event` :323, the assistant banner :328, a banner inside a `task_notification` :563 — three producers in claude-stream-json.js, and `noteWallSignal` already counts a banner + its rejected event as ONE wall), and EVERY producer calls `maybePoolAutoSwitch` the moment it marks the cache — so the first record re-points the link and asking `wallSlotFor` again for the second one keyed it to the member the pool had just moved TO, demoting that HEALTHY member with `credential slot` authority and `noteSessionWall`-ing it (reproduced both orders + the two-events shape; harm = `usable:false, blockedUntil:+2h` against a fresh reading showing it 95% healthy, where the fix near-arms and continues in ~60s). Rejection records now read **`rejectionSlotFor(session)`** = `wallSlotFor` PINNED to the first keyed signal of `_turnWallSigs` (key AND `slotOk`); `wallSlotFor` remains the fresh reading for `wallKeyFor`/`fireIdentityFor` ("where would a CONTINUE land right now" is a different question) and for the pin's no-signal fallback. The pin is the TURN because that is what defines it — a re-point does not reach a RUNNING CLI (2.361.0) — and `noteTurnEnd` clears the signals, so it is exactly one turn wide. **The near-arm's `nearArmVeto` is an ASSERTION, not the protection** (it re-reads `sessionWalledMembers` and `console.warn`s `INVARIANT VIOLATED`; the protection is noteSessionWall + the verdict's walled override, which the suite executes functionally). Gate: test-auto-resume §11 (rewritten: the refuted rule is recorded, not deleted) + scripts/test-auto-resume-loop.mjs (158; §4d two-records-one-rejection + §4e near-arm, both mutation-tested).

② **Plan B — observed-org aware evaluation** (BLOCKING half superseded by ②bis above; the VALUES half stands)**.** `observedMemberFor(session, poolId)` = the OTel truth stream's latest org for the session (`OBSERVED_ORG_RECENT_MS` = 10min) resolved to a pool member; `sessionCurrentMember` = observed else link ({id, linkedId, observedId, divergent}), logging the divergence once per session per 10min (`[pool] session <id> observed on <X> while linked to <Y>`, event `pool-observed-divergence`). It drives: `resolveUsageKey` for pooled sessions (the live odometer feeds, probe-session matching and every derived cache key now attribute to the observed member — pooled sessions with a fresh observation therefore resolve straight to it and `usage-reading-reattributed` counts drop for them, by design); `quotaVerdictFor(scope, {model, session})` (the current member is judged FIRST so `via` names the account the session is on; the verdict carries `on/linked/divergent` + a reason note); the per-session auto-switch pass (decides FROM the observed member — a session walled on it moves even when its link reads healthy; when the chosen target is the link itself the re-point is journal-only `(re-point, same target)` + the creds-mtime bump the CLI re-reads on, no user notice); both probe targets (wall ladder + pre-fire gate). The hot-switch symlink still targets the CHOSEN member — this changes what the engine BELIEVES the session is burning, never the material. ③ **Order on BLOCKED entry** (`noteTurnEnd` → `onWalledTurn`): demote → session-aware verdict → arm → pool evaluation in `finally` (AFTER the arm, so a hot switch's `fireNow()` finds the session armed and continues it in the same tick; the normal-turn branch keeps its own `maybePoolAutoSwitch`). Gate: test-auto-resume §11 (functional — a REAL AccountManager pool with real per-session links + the real engine + the real auto-resume module + a fake OTel source, fixtures shaped from the journal: one wall holds, two walls inside 120s demote with the signal's reset and switch+continue in ONE noteTurnEnd, observed-org divergence names the observed member and moves the link, stale observations fall back, named non-demotions, the ring counts turns not records, order-of-operations pins) + test-rate-limit-capture ⑧ (the `source` option).

**A HEALTHY CURRENT MEMBER IS NEVER "NO MEMBER CAN SERVE IT" (2026-09-13, the Fable-cap pool storm).** On a HOT pool the candidate ranking runs PROACTIVELY — before anything asks whether the current member is exhausted — so an empty candidate list says NOTHING about whether the pool can serve a turn. The `!pool.length` branch nevertheless returned `no-members` / `all-rejected` / `all-logins-expired`, which the engine renders as the hourly "this pool is stuck" notice AND feeds to auto-resume's `noteNoPoolTarget` ("no usable member left"). Production printed `Pool "全部": no member can serve it — out of quota (still available: 5h 100%, 7d 69%, Fable 45%)` three times about a pool whose CURRENT member was healthy on every bucket — those numbers are ITS OWN — and the owner read it exactly as written ("有账号有 Fable 额度但总是提示没有了"). Those three refusals may now be claimed ONLY when `exhausted` (soft or hard) is already true; otherwise the branch returns the new named reason **`no-better`** (`noBetter: true`, plus the same `fromRemaining`/bucket detail for the log), which no surface renders and which `noteNoPoolTarget` is not fed. `'all-rejected'` is gated by the same clause on purpose: members that rejected THIS conversation only matter once the one it is sitting on cannot serve it either. Nothing about WHAT the three refusals say changed — only WHEN they may be claimed. **And `poolBlockedNotice` no longer contradicts itself about one member**: the `(still available: …)` clause prints only BESIDE a spent bucket, because that contrast IS the nested model's point ("spent: Fable 0% (still available: 5h 100%, 7d 66%)") while "out of quota (still available: …)" is a sentence about one member arguing with itself. Gate: test-pool-auto (the pure legs — no-better, the three refusals unchanged once exhausted, both sentence shapes) + test-fable-cap-pool-storm §3 (the same state through the REAL engine, with a patched-copy control that reproduces the owner's sentence).

**…AND A BLOCKED POOL STILL NAMES THE BUCKET THAT BLOCKED IT — THREE BANDS, NOT TWO (2026-09-13 r2, the round-1 verifier, reproduced first).** A HOT pool's `exhausted` is the SOFT (hot-raised) bar while `deadBuckets`/`liveBuckets` were split on the HARD one, so round 1's `rest = dead && live` dropped the clause for exactly the shape a hot pool exists for: current member at 4 % of its weekly window (≥ `THRESH.weekly.hard` 3, < `.hot` 5), every other member quota-dead ⇒ `Pool "P": no member can serve it — out of quota.` with **no number in the sentence at all**, breaking the standing law that every blocked outcome must SPEAK with named buckets. `bucketDetail` now emits three bands — `deadBuckets` (< hard, unchanged), **`lowBuckets`** (≥ hard but under the hot bar: usable, and the reason we want to move) and `liveBuckets` (≥ the soft bar, i.e. real headroom) — and `poolBlockedNotice` names every band that is holding the decision back (`spent: …`, `nearly spent: …`, or both) while `(still available: …)` prints beside either. **A pool that is not HOT has `soft === hard`, so `lowBuckets` is always empty and `liveBuckets` is byte-for-byte what it has always been** — cold decisions are unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION, and the suite measures that over a shape matrix rather than reading it off the diff. Gate: test-fable-cap-pool-storm §6 (the real `decidePoolSwitch` + the real `poolBlockedNotice`, a ROUND-1 patched copy that reproduces the number-less sentence, a MASTER copy that reproduces the §3 contradiction on the same shape, the byte-identity matrix, and a COLD control — which only reaches `bucketDetail` when the current member is HARD-dead, because 4 % left is simply 'healthy' at hard = 3).

**THE BYTE-IDENTITY SWEEPS AND THE SHALLOW MIRROR (scripts/test-pool-auto.mjs, lane-mirror-197, 2026-09-29).** The member / priority / pin sections each compare 300 seeded worlds against the PRE-FIX `src/account-pool-auto.js` (`b970f16d`, the tree before lane-pool-pin) to prove the new input, when inert, changes no verdict. That copy comes from `git show`, and the Actions mirror is a depth-1 checkout — the ref is absent there BY CONSTRUCTION (six reds on 2.369.197: three `fatal: invalid object name`, three copies-census legs counting a copy never made; reproduced in a local `git clone --depth 1`). `preFixCopy(M, ref, rel)` (top of the suite, git under `gitEnvFrom` with the checkout as cwd) answers `{mod}` when the ref is here, `{mod: null, why: 'shallow'}` on a shallow clone — the caller prints `⊘ SKIP …` with the reason and `copiesCensus`'s `minCopies` drops by one (the census keys on whether the control RAN, the 2.369.164 r2 rule) — and `why` naming the ref on a FULL clone, which the caller fails by name. The ref-free half of every sweep runs everywhere: the three membership shapes decide alike, null / [] / omitted priority decide alike (and the snapshot with an empty priority is the snapshot without one), the pin path answers null for every no-pin world. A control asks the helper for a sha that exists nowhere and expects `shallow` on a shallow clone and "NOT shallow" on a full one. Full clone 460 pass, depth-1 457 pass (the six reds were 450 + 6 on the runner).

### harnesses/ (the harness registry — S4 QuotaSignalSource)

  harnesses/index.js — THE harness registry (docs/design-harness-plugins.md §2.2 "src/harnesses/index.js 是唯一注册表"; S4 landed it with the QUOTA contract first, later slices add theirs beside it). `get(id)` is LOUD on an unknown or empty id — core never falls through to claude (the gemini-as-claude class); `has/list/ids`; `register(descriptor, {replace})` for contributed harnesses (built-ins can never be replaced/unregistered; a duplicate contributed id needs the explicit flag — silent shadowing is how twins are born); `assertQuotaContract` validates every registration (normalize/signalFromStream/classifyAuthFailure functions + `probe ∈ QUOTA_PROBE_RUNGS` = 'cli-usage'|'rpc-rate-limits'|null); `NULL_QUOTA` (null-quota.js, frozen) is the shell descriptor's source AND the engine's degrade target for an unknown id. Descriptors: claude.js / codex.js / shell.js = `{id, label, quota}`. SHARED tier (test-architecture): pure hooks over SHARED parsers, never reaching up into ORCH — the daemon may bundle them; the S5 stream CONSUMERS themselves stayed ORCH (src/server/stdout/, below) because they need the engine/hosts/ledger, so a descriptor only names the protocol.
  harnesses/claude-quota.js — the claude QuotaSignalSource. `normalize(raw, nowMs)` dispatches by SHAPE over the three claude reading channels: a string = the `claude -p /usage` panel text (parseCliUsageText, MOVED here verbatim from usage-routes — the MONTHS/zonedEpoch/_parseCliResetTime helpers with it), an object with `rate_limits` = the get_usage control payload (ClaudeCodeAdapter.parseGetUsageResponse, unchanged), an object with five_hour/seven_day/limits[] = the GET /api/oauth/usage REST JSON (parseOAuthUsage, MOVED verbatim = usage-routes' former `_parseUsage`; the route + the device-op consumer bind the same function). `signalFromStream(record)`: `rate_limit_event` → `{source:'rate_limit_event', kind: rejected⇒'exhausted' | utilization⇒'reading' | else 'meta', bucket, scopedName, resetsAtMs, ev}` (the parse is rate-limit-capture's parseRateLimitEvent — reached through the registry, no twin); an assistant text matching the LIMIT BANNER regex → `{source:'limit-banner', kind:'exhausted', bucket, scopedName, resetsAtMs:0}` (a BOOLEAN wall signal — design-wall-machine §1: text is never a data source; parseLimitBanner only names the bucket for the passive cache mark). `probe = capsOf('claude').quotaProbe = 'cli-usage'`. `classifyAuthFailure` = account-pool-auto's Anthropic-wording classifier, the SAME function object (pinned).
  harnesses/codex-quota.js — the codex QuotaSignalSource, PURE. `normalize` = the former usage-routes normalizeCodexRateLimit MOVED verbatim (2.368.18 P0 semantics: windows classify by LENGTH ≤480min⇒fiveHour else sevenDay, never by primary/secondary position; every exhaustion marker survives: rateLimitReachedType/spendControlReached/credits; the tripped window reads dead) — usage-routes re-exports it under the old name and the engine reads it through the registry. Owns the typed exhaustion vocabulary `EXHAUSTION_RE` (usage_limit_reached|quota_exceeded|usage_not_included|workspace_owner_usage_limit_reached|workspace_member_usage_limit_reached|workspace_member_credits_depleted) and `trippedWindow(snap)` (primary→burst window when present else weekly; secondary→weekly else burst — the engine's 2.368.20 rule). `signalFromStream(record)` accepts the server frame `{type:'event_msg', payload}` OR the bare payload: `rate_limits_updated` → kind 'exhausted' (with `tripped` + resetsAtMs) | 'reading' | 'probe-failed' (the on-demand `{error}` reply — never silent), snapshot carries the on-demand resetCredits count; `task_failed` → 'exhausted' (errorInfo, resetsAtSec/Ms, snapshot when one rode along) | 'auth-failure' (the typed `unauthorized` enum only — a plain error text is not a quota signal) | null; `reset_credit_result` → 'recovered' | 'reset-credit-failed'. `probe = 'rpc-rate-limits'`. `classifyAuthFailure` in OpenAI/codex wording (typed unauthorized; "401 Unauthorized"/invalid_grant/token expired|revoked/not logged in/org|account deactivated|suspended; 403 immediate; 401 needs attempt≥2 — the same refresh-race rule as claude; 5xx/429 never). Codex auth-failure EVICTION is still v1 surfaced-only (`codex-auth-failure` event): the engine's member mark keys on the claude creds path (credsTokenSig) — the S2 accounts strategy object owns that arm. · **readLive / settleLive** (lane dc-pool-quota, 2.369.214): the rpc-rate-limits live read (wrapper verb codex-read-limits) + its waiters MOVED here from usage-pool-engine; the engine calls them for ANY harness that declares them (liveReadSource / pickLiveProbeSession / liveQuotaKeyFor) and names none.
  **THE CAPS-ROUTED QUOTA PROBE (S4, usage-pool-engine `probeQuotaForKey(target, {session, timeoutMs=20000})`)** — ONE dispatcher for every "refresh this identity's quota now" need: the wall machine's BLOCKED-entry verification probe, the wall probe ladder (0→30m→1h→2h), and the auto-resume pre-fire gate (`beforeAutoResumeFire`). `quotaBackendFor(key, session)` names the identity's harness (a named account's `backend` — legacy records = claude, same rule as accounts._acctBackend/capsOf; `__global_codex__` = codex; identity-less keys `__global__`/`host-*` take the asking session's own backend; else claude) and `quotaSourceFor(backend).probe` names the rung: **'cli-usage'** = `getQuotaProbe()` = usage-routes refreshViaCliPanel (`claude -p /usage`, the owner-approved auto-cli channel — server.js wiring unchanged, still the ONE spawn site); **'rpc-rate-limits'** = pick a LIVE local codex chat session on the identity (the asking session first — it sits idle-walled on exactly that identity with its app-server up; else any session whose `codexQuotaKeyFor` = account→pool current member→`__global_codex__` lands in the target's identity group), write the wrapper verb `{type:'codex-read-limits'}` (account/rateLimits/read on the session's own app-server — the official client makes the fetch, §ban-safety class unchanged) and await the next `rate_limits_updated` through `session._codexLimitsWaiters` (registered in session-schema; `recordCodexQuotaSignal` settles the waiters AFTER the cache write so the verdict taken next already reads the fresh file; a failed on-demand read settles `ok:false` with the wrapper's error; a bounded timeout drops the waiter); **null** (shell / unknown harness → NULL source) = nothing runs, the verdict stands. Before S4 every probe spawned `claude -p /usage` whatever the backend — a codex identity burned a pointless claude process and never got a fresh reading (design-harness-plugins.md §1 P2). Result `{ok, rung, backend, reason}` — every miss is named. Unknown harness id ⇒ one console.warn + `quota-harness-unknown` event + the NULL source, never a claude parse. Gate: scripts/test-quota-source.mjs (functional: real engine.create() with fake sessions — codex identity rides the live session + never spawns claude; claude identity keeps cli-usage; shell/unknown run nothing; timeout + failed read honest; beforeAutoResumeFire routed; + registry contract, every harness's normalize/signalFromStream/classifyAuthFailure on real shapes, wiring pins, and a vendor-whitelist sub-run).

### quota-model.js / usage-cache-write.js (THE TYPED LIMIT SET + THE ONE WRITE PATH, 2026-09-09)

  quota-model.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the browser bundle AND the shipped statusline tool can carry it): **2.369.157 r2: `toLegacyView` projects `extra.resetCredits` (the stored reset-credit count only an on-demand read states) as `resetCredits` when the set holds one — never a fabricated zero — so the roster's projected map (usage-routes `{...newest, ...toLegacyView(merged)}`) keeps the chip and its Use… button across the passive pushes that do not state it (test-codex-pool §R11 + a patched-copy control).** **an account key holds a LIMIT SET, not a snapshot.** The hand-shaped object it replaces — `{fiveHour, sevenDay, scopedWeekly[], overage, spend, …}` — was written by nine producers with nine merge policies and read by loose field access all over the tree, and it cannot express what the vendors actually send. Three incidents, one root: **(a) B-9213 — MORE THAN ONE LIMIT PER ACCOUNT.** The codex app-server pushes a separate `rate_limits_updated` per limit, interleaved on one session; measured on this instance's own buffers (one conversation, 208 pushes): `codex` (the plan) 32×, `codex_bengalfox` / "GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark" 149×, `premium` 27×, all collapsed into ONE cache file, last-writer-wins — the file on disk held Spark at 0 %/0 % while the plan limit at 5 % was simply GONE. A panel flips 5 %→0 % between renders and a pool reading it sees headroom that does not exist. **(b) B-8b12 — AN EMPTY WINDOW REPORTS A SLIDING RESET**: a window that has not started answers `resetsAt = now + duration` at EVERY read (measured +3 s apart between two reads; 328 empty readings land in [−489 s, −8 s] of a full window and 144 of 149 consecutive reads carry a DIFFERENT resetsAt), so the panel printed a precise reset the owner read as a banked reset being consumed, EDF ranked it as the soonest deadline forever, and auto-resume would arm on it. **(c)** claude's model-scoped cap exists for ONE family and lives in a `scopedWeekly[]` beside the plan buckets while codex has no such shape, so every reader special-cased both and every reader had its own idea of "remaining" and "deadline". THE MODEL: `{identity, fetchedAt, source, limits:[{limitId, name, scope:'plan'|'model'|'credits'|'overage', model, family, windows:[{kind, minutes, usedPct, resetsAt, state:'running'|'empty'|'unknown', measuredAt}], flags, source, fetchedAt}], extra}` with a VALIDATOR that runs at the write path (our own producer being wrong is a bug we refuse to write; a corrupt file already on disk is a fact we heal past), `windowState()` (usedPct 0 AND the reset a full window out ⇒ `'empty'` — `EMPTY_WINDOW_JITTER_SEC` 600 sits inside a measured 662 s dead band, deliberately on the empty side: calling a running-but-0 % window empty costs only its deadline, calling an empty one running re-creates the incident), `limitFor(set,{model,family})` = the ONE accessor every reader uses, `remaining()`/`deadline()` which IGNORE empty windows, and `mergeLimitSets` which merges PER limitId with provenance per limit. `'unknown'` is "no claim" everywhere — never zero, never full. **THE MODEL-CAP LANE (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21):** `MODEL_CAP_PLACEHOLDER` = {limitId 'model:cap', name 'Model cap'} — scope model, family null: it counts for the account-level min (the conservative direction), governs no named family, and is NEVER the plan; `scopedLimitId(name)` is the ONE id spelling (fromLegacy, the harness builder and the naming rule ask it; 'Model cap' round-trips to model:cap); `nameModelCapLane({limits, scoped, resetsAt, hint, jitterSec})` is the PURE ladder — the sidecar family with this reset → an existing model limit with this reset (±WINDOW_JITTER_SEC) → the hint family among several → else the placeholder; a window with NO reset is named only by a hint matching a cap the account has SHOWN; `foldPlaceholderCap`, run by every `mergeLimitSets`, is the ONE permitted collapse: the placeholder folds into the single NAMED model limit sharing its weekly reset (the newer window wins), stays put on a different or absent reset or an ambiguous pair, and two NAMED limits still never collapse (test-quota-model ⑲).   **AND THE WALL IS A READING TOO** (`windowRefutes` / `wallAttribution`, inc-mttbrtc0-6049 — see kb-bugfix-invariants). A RUNNING window cannot change its reset before it ends, so a stated reset contradicting a member's own still-future window REFUTES that member — it identifies nobody (2.369.73 r2 measured a 5h reset names a TIME, not an account, and that stands). Refutation may therefore REFUSE but may never choose a new home: identification comes from the slot LEDGER (`slotAt` at the instant the rejection arrived) and the window only corroborates it. Both witnesses must agree before a byte moves; either silent ⇒ the turn pin stands; they disagree ⇒ write NOTHING and say why. Only a vendor-STATED reset counts — `parseLimitBanner` returns `{kind}` and no time, so the banner path is untouched, which is the load-bearing half of `guardReadingTarget`'s own reason for exempting walls ("often a bounded GUESS"). `WINDOW_JITTER_SEC` is reading-lag's 120 s and the suite pins them equal: a wall judged at a different tolerance than a reading is two answers to one question.

  **r2 — WHERE THE RULE IS ASKED, AND HOW MUCH A WINDOW'S REFUTATION IS WORTH.** ① A rejection is written TWICE — per RECORD the instant it arrives (`recordRateLimitEvent`, the write that makes the pool act in the same tick) and again when the turn ends — and round 1 guarded only the second, so the incident's own foreign 5h window still landed and nothing repaired it (the round-1 fixture could not see this because its two rejections shared a BUCKET, so the pin's own turn-end write masked it; on two different buckets the victim keeps a stranger's reset, `accountRemaining` 0, ~3 h excluded). `wallAttributionFor` is now the rule over KEYS and BOTH writers ask it (`wallRecordTarget` / `wallTargetFor`); a refused record is archived under its own moment (`rejection:<bucket>` vs the aggregate's `wall:<bucket>`) and the session-scoped half still runs, because we refused to write a NUMBER, not to notice a wall. A proven re-file is stashed on the session for the rest of the turn (`_turnWallRefile`, cleared by `noteTurnEnd` with the other two pins) and the two BANNER paths follow it: they state no time of their own, so without it one rejection would mark two members — the record's true owner and the pin it just refuted. ② `refutationStrength(kind)` — measured over all 7798 claude anchor rows here with the predicate the rule actually uses (each reading against its account's own last `on-demand` stamp, which is what `establishedWindows()` serves and can be hours old — round 1 cited 4.31 %, taken on CONSECUTIVE readings seconds apart, a different quantity): a WEEKLY window (7d + every model-scoped bucket) contradicted its own account **0 times in 9998 judged readings** ⇒ `decisive`, may refuse a write alone; a FIVE-HOUR window refuted 137 of 1055 session-producer readings but **101 of those (73.72 %) state another account's own window at that instant** (true positives), and its own-producer bound is 13/1706 — all one account alternating A-B-A-B between two resets 90 min apart at constant 0.89 utilization, i.e. B-9213 inside the plan bucket ⇒ `corroborating`, may only confirm an identification the LEDGER made independently; anything unmeasured ⇒ `none`, and a new backend's bucket must earn `decisive` with its own measurement. The asymmetry is money in both directions: a wall that never lands leaves the pool sending turns to a member the CLI just refused (reproduced — with every kind decisive an ordinary 5h wall is REFUSED and the journal says so). The incident is a five-hour wall and stays fixed, because there the ledger identifies and the window only corroborates.

  **lane-hot-switch (2026-09-30) — A REFUTATION IS PROOF TOO.** The re-file proof had a twin nobody carried: when `wallAttribution` ARCHIVES a rejection record (its stated reset contradicts the pin's own window and the ledger names that same member), the window-less banner of the same wall and the turn-end fold both fell back to the pin — and the incident's Fable banner marked a member with quota, the turn end excluded it from the conversation ("nowhere to go — 2 member(s) already rejected") and the pool moved ten conversations onto a spent member. Now `wallRecordTarget`'s archive stashes `_turnWallRefuted {from, reason, at}` for the turn (cleared with `_turnWallRefile`); `wallAttributionFor`'s no-window branch answers `archive` for the refuted pin; `markLimitBannerNow` archives the banner mark with the record's reason (moment `banner`) and still raises the SIGNAL (the session IS refused); `demoteWalledAccount` asks every signal's attribution BEFORE `noteSessionWall` — a member none of whose signals lands on it (all archived ⇒ `reason:'refuted'`, journal "did not refuse this turn") is neither demoted nor excluded; `noteWallSignal` keeps a refuted key out of the ≥2-walls ring. A wall the pin's own window does NOT contradict is untouched. Gate: test-hot-switch-incident §B (+ two patched-copy controls; §A2's both-reverted control reproduces the incident whole).

  **r3 — THREE WAYS A COUNTING BUCKET STOPPED COUNTING** (all reproduced end to end before being fixed; all three cost money the same way — a bucket that makes a real claim is dropped from `accountRemaining`/`weeklyDeadline`/`bucketRems`/the anchor stream, so the pool keeps spending against a member that is actually walled). ① **A STATED SPEND IS DECISIVE ON ITS OWN, AND `windowState` NOW TESTS IT FIRST.** The deadline is what tells an UNTOUCHED window from a running one; it has nothing to say about a window the vendor just called 90 % gone. Asking for it first collapsed "we know the utilization but not the reset" into `'unknown'`, which `bucketCounts` drops. REACHABLE, NOT THEORETICAL: the `· resets` clause of a claude panel line is OPTIONAL (`parseCliUsageText`, and scripts/test-cli-usage-parse.mjs pins the reset-less shape), `refreshViaCliPanel` deliberately refuses to project the 5-hour one ("its window starts with the first request; a stale one would be a lie"), `parseOAuthUsage` maps a missing reset to 0 — and **four of the nine live claude cache files on this instance** hold exactly that shape. Measured end to end on the real write path: a member 95 % through its burst window read **80 % free** and `decidePoolSwitch` answered `healthy`. ② **A STORED VERDICT MAY NOT OUTLIVE THE READING IT DESCRIBES.** `state` is computed by the projection from a (usedPct, resetsAt, measuredAt) triple, but it lives on the bucket object every producer SPREADS forward (`{...(cache[kind] || {})}` in rate-limit-capture, `bump()` in markLimitBanner), so a producer that re-measured carried the OLD verdict onto the NEW numbers. Measured: a 5h bucket stamped `unknown` while it had no reset kept that stamp through a fully dated 95 % reading (pool read 80 % free instead of 5 %); a 7d + scoped pair correctly stamped `empty` at the weekly roll kept it while three real events climbed them to 90 % and 100 % (pool read 90 % free instead of 0, `weeklyDeadline` **null**, `bucketRems` listing only the 5h row) — **inc-msof8i22 / 2.305.0 re-opened**. TWO HALVES, because each catches what the other cannot: the PRODUCERS drop the verdict whenever they re-state a number (that half also covers a re-measurement DOWN to 0 % — a window stamped `empty` whose reset has since PINNED, where `usedPct > 0` says nothing and keeping the stamp costs the member its real weekly deadline), and `fromLegacy` keeps the CLOCK-FREE belt `!(usedPct > 0)` for a stamp that arrives from a FILE an older build wrote (it heals on the next write) or from a producer nobody enumerated. A `status`-only event re-states no number, so the reading is unchanged and the verdict SURVIVES — that is the whole reason the stamp is trusted at all, and dropping it there would hand `fromLegacy` the file's clock and flip a genuinely empty window to `'running'`, which is B-8b12 in the other direction. ③ **THE DERIVED VIEW MAY NEVER BE MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE SET IT PROJECTS.** `scopedWeekly` gives a model limit's BUDGET window a home and the plan limit's own windows have theirs, but a model limit's FIVE-HOUR window had none — `isBudgetKind` excludes `'5h'` from the scoped projection and `fiveHour` was read off the plan limit alone — and `account-pool-auto` reads the VIEW, not the accessor. Measured on the two real codex push shapes from this instance's buffers (plan 7d 33 %, `codex_bengalfox`/"GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark" 5h 90 % + 7d 10 %): the accessor answered **10 %** and the pool answered **67 %** — a 57-point drift at the exact seam B-9213 is about, and a REGRESSION, because the base commit's last-writer-wins collapse happened to keep the Spark 5h and answered 10 %. `fiveHour` therefore means what every reader has always used it for — THE BINDING BURST CONSTRAINT on this account, i.e. the min over every counting 5-hour window in the set. One rule, no backend branch: claude's model caps are weekly-only so it can only ever pick the plan window there. The guard against the NEXT hole is not a list of kinds but the invariant itself, driven as a PROPERTY over a matrix of shapes (`accountRemaining(toLegacyView(set)) <= remaining(set)`), with the plan-only projection as its negative control. **AND THE FIX FOR ③ CONTAINED ③ (r3 second pass, found by driving the property with a PASSED reset)**: "binding" was first spelled as the highest `usedPct`, but a window whose reset has passed rolled over and is FULL (`windowRemaining`'s rule, which `bucketRemaining` applies to whatever we emit), so a 90 %-spent-but-rolled-over model window displaced a plan window with a real 50 % left — accessor 50 %, pool 90 %, the same defect inside its own fix. The ranking is `windowRemaining` on the SAME clock the accessor uses (`toLegacyView(set, {nowSec})`, default now), and the plan window is SEEDED first so it wins every tie — every window of a set read long after it was measured ties at 100, and without the seed iteration order handed the slot back to the Spark bucket, undoing §⑭. The matrix now carries a rolled-over window and §⑯d asserts the property goes red on that mutant; it could not before. **r3 invariants**: the deadline answers "has this window started", never "is it spent" — ask the decisive question first; **a stored verdict is only as good as the reading it describes, and the producer that replaced the numbers is the one that must drop it** (the belt in the reader is for the files and producers you did not enumerate — two mechanisms, two negative controls, each pointed at a case only it can catch); **a lossy projection must lose CONSERVATIVELY, and that is a property to drive rather than a list of fields to remember** — every reader that consumes the view instead of the accessor is only as right as the projection, which is why `account-pool-auto`'s census row is `view-only` and not `migrated`.

  **r4 — A FREE MEMBER IS NOT AN UNKNOWN ONE** (the round-3 verifier's finding, reproduced end to end against the base commit before being fixed). r3 fenced the not-yet-started window off from BOTH answers a window gives, and only one of them is B-8b12's.

  · **"WHEN DOES THIS BUDGET END?"** — an empty window has no answer. Its reset is `now + duration` on every read, so ranking on it makes it the earliest deadline forever and arms auto-resume on a number that has moved by the time it fires. `bucketCounts` / `countingWindows` exist for THIS question and are UNCHANGED: `deadline()`, `weeklyDeadline`, the anchor stream, the window fingerprint and auto-resume's arm all ask it and are all right to drop an empty window.
  · **"HOW MUCH IS LEFT?"** — an empty window has a precise answer: ALL of it. The vendor stated a spend of 0 %. Dropping that turns a definite claim into ignorance, and ignorance is not neutral: it is `known:false`, which the pool ranks at `UNKNOWN_REMAINING_PCT` (50) and `quotaVerdict` reports as "no usage data" (`usable:null`).

  MEASURED HARM. A brand-new claude account whose panel says `0% used` on both plan buckets — the ORDINARY shape, because the `· resets` clause of a panel line is optional, `refreshViaCliPanel` deliberately refuses to project the 5-hour one, and a fresh account has no prior reset for `projectReset` to carry forward — read back as "no usage data": `accountRemaining` `{100,known}` → `{null,unknown}`, `quotaVerdict` `usable:true` → `usable:null` (so the engine's own pool gate `verdicts.find((x) => x.v.usable === true)` finds nobody and reports the WHOLE POOL blocked), `rankPoolMembers` eff 100 → 50, and `decidePoolSwitch` off an EXHAUSTED member (4 % left) went from `{to:'new', reason:'exhausted'}` to `{to:null, reason:'no-settleable'}` — the pool keeps spending on a spent member while a fully free one sits beside it. That is a REGRESSION against the base commit, and this branch's OWN backfill demonstrates it on real data: run over a copy of this instance's `data/usage-cache` (12 scanned / 12 stamped / 31 limits / idempotent on run 2) it flips exactly ONE of the twelve files — `usage-cache/__global_codex__.json`, the only one whose every window is fresh, i.e. the measured B-8b12 shape — from `{usable:true,known:true}` to `{usable:null,known:false}`. The other eleven are unaffected because their 7d is running, which is why every gate suite stayed green.

  THE FIX = TWO QUESTIONS, TWO PREDICATES, stated side by side in the PURE module so one rule in two spellings cannot drift: `windowStatesSpend(w)` (`num(w.usedPct) != null`) and its legacy twin `bucketStatesSpend(b)` (`num(b.utilization) != null`) join `bucketCounts`/`countingWindows`; `remaining()` mins over `spendingWindows(l)` and `src/account-pool-auto.js`'s `bucketRemaining` gates on `bucketStatesSpend`. `num()` and not `Number()` because `Number(null)` is 0, and "the vendor said nothing" must never read as "the vendor said zero" (P6) — which makes the legacy predicate STRICTLY MORE CONSERVATIVE than the pre-model `bucketRemaining` (it used `Number.isFinite(Number(b.utilization))` and therefore called `utilization: null` a stated 0 %); measured on this instance, 35 cache buckets and 14,286 anchor buckets, ZERO of them missing or null, so the shape that behaves differently does not occur and refusing it is the direction that cannot invent headroom.

  WHY INCLUDING THEM IS SAFE, and it is not a judgement call: `remaining` is a MIN over every applicable window, so a window at 100 % free can never lift another limit's 5 %. It can only flip `known:false` → `known:true`. B-9213's harm was a Spark push OVERWRITING the plan limit, and the per-limit MERGE is what fixes that, not this filter — §⑫'s own negative control has said so since r1: *"an empty bucket is 100 % free, so it never HID an exhaustion — the harm was always the deadline."* HONEST BOUNDARY: a file holding ONLY an empty limit (exactly what B-9213 left on `__global_codex__.json`) therefore reads USABLE — the pre-model behaviour restored, not a new claim, and `known:false` was never protection anyway (an unknown member is still offered, ranked at 50, while the POOL reports blocked). What repairs that file is the per-limit merge plus the backfill.

  TWO SECOND-ORDER FIXES RIDE ALONG, both found by this round's own controls. ① `toLegacyView`'s `toBucket` fabricated `utilization: 0` for a window with no stated spend, so a producer that stated only a reset came back off disk as `{utilization: 0}` and the pool read 100 % free and KNOWN while the typed accessor beside it correctly answered "no claim" — the view MORE optimistic than the set, which is exactly what §⑯c exists to prevent and could not see, because its property compared two KNOWN answers. The bucket is still EMITTED (a limit the vendor reported must stay visible) but carries no `utilization`, and the property grew the clause `(v.known && !a.known)`: claiming to know is itself an optimism. ② A `bucketRems` row publishes its `resetsAt` only when `bucketCounts(b)` — the row exists because the bucket states a REMAINING, its reset may only be published when the bucket may name a DEADLINE. Today a 100 %-free bucket can never be in the `dead` list `quotaVerdict` turns into `blockedUntil`, so this is safe by CONSTRUCTION rather than by that argument — which is the point, since the argument would otherwise have to be re-made by every future reader of the field.

  TWO BELTS, TWO CONTROLS. r3's `state` machinery and this split now cover the SAME money harm independently, so §⑯a/§⑯b's negative controls were re-pointed at what only THEY protect — the ANCHOR stream (the estimator's whole input and the corpus the window fingerprint identifies accounts from, driven through the real `UsageAnchors`) and the weekly DEADLINE — while new §⑯a-x/§⑯b-x remove BOTH belts and reproduce r3's own published numbers (80 % free on the 7d window alone; the spent Fable cap invisible at 90 % free with a null deadline). §⑯e drives the r4 defect itself end to end through the one write path with the engine's pool gate applied verbatim (WIRING PIN on `verdicts.find((x) => x.v.usable === true)`), the real backfill on the real-shape file, four positive controls (the deadline is STILL null, neither bucket ANCHORS, the row publishes no reset, a bucket with no number at all is STILL unknown, and a genuinely spent member is STILL refused) and its own single-mechanism mutant. Mutation-tested against the product source: reverting `bucketRemaining` → 14 red, `remaining()` → 5 red, `toBucket` → 2 red, the `bucketRems` reset gate → 1 red, restored → 0.

  A PROPERTY THAT BOUNDS A AGAINST B GUARDS THE SEAM, NEVER THE SHARED RULE UNDERNEATH IT. §⑯c compares two PROJECTIONS of one set, so an error both of them make is structurally invisible there — and that is precisely this defect, where the view and the accessor agreed that a free member had no reading. The rule itself needs a leg that names an answer.

  usage-cache-write.js — **2.369.157 r2: `resetCredits` survives a write that does not state it — the producer's own count wins, else the merged view's, else the previous FILE's (a lifted file with `limits` carries no `extra`); never on a REPLACE. One passive codex push per turn used to erase the count the roster and the rung read (test-codex-pool §R11 + a patched-copy control).** **THE ONE WRITE PATH** for `data/usage-cache/*.json` (design-account-hardening §4.2). Every producer (statusline ingest, on-demand panel, bare-token ⟳, rate_limit_event capture, the wall/demotion mark, the codex live push, the codex rollout-tail summariser, the remote host-* harvest, the repair) hands it a typed set + provenance. It guarantees: per-limit merge never last-writer-wins; the legacy `fiveHour`/`sevenDay`/`scopedWeekly`/`overage` fields are a DERIVED VIEW projected from the merged limits after every write (so an unmigrated reader still sees a consistent object — and sees the PLAN limit deterministically instead of whichever limit spoke last); a malformed set never lands; provenance per LIMIT, because three limits on one account are three separate readings and "Updated 3min ago" in the panel header describes only the newest. It does NOT decide WHICH key a reading belongs to — that is the slot/window question and it already has an owner (`readingSlotFor` + `guardReadingTarget`): composing, never forking. `writeSidecar` lives here too (`.window-<key>`, `.slot-<id>` — never `.json`, every cache scanner filters on that suffix). **A grep-derived STANDING SWEEP (scripts/test-quota-model.mjs ⑩) fails any other module that writes a usage-cache file**, each allowlisted exception stating WHY, dead entries failing too; ⑪ is the reader census (six classes incl. `spent-only`, whose property §⑬ DRIVES rather than asserts in prose) and it PRINTS the not-yet-migrated set every run as a metric to re-measure. **The lift rung restores a MODEL cap too (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** a claude object whose `limits` array lacks the limit a legacy `scopedWeekly` entry names is that entry's reading — the statusline drops the `model:<name>` limit it measured exactly as it drops the plan one (2.1.274 ships `rate_limits.model_scoped[]`) — restored with the object's own provenance; every write-path write projects the array INTO `scopedWeekly`, so an entry only outlives its limit through the producer that cannot construct one (test-quota-model ⑲ LIFT).

  **r2 — A CLAUDE ARRAY WITH NO `plan` LIMIT TAKES ITS PLAN LIMIT FROM THE LEGACY VIEW.** `liftCacheObject` gained one rung, and it exists for the shipped statusline. That tool is the highest-frequency writer on the instance (up to once per 8 s per account) and an allowlisted exception to this path, because it is a single file on hosts with no checkout; it rebuilt the cache object from a hand-written list of fields to PRESERVE and that list did not name `limits`, so ONE ordinary render deleted the canonical half of every claude snapshot (measured against the REAL tool over a migrated copy of a real cache file: three limits in, ZERO out, the `overage` object gone, and the next reader re-deriving them under THIS producer's name and clock — contradicting the same file's own `scopedFetchedAt`). Every other limit survives byte-identical with the provenance of the producer that DID measure it; a producer that cannot express a window state or another limit's age can never forge one; the tool never AUTHORS the array on a not-yet-migrated file (a one-element list claiming to be all of them would delete that file's scoped cap the moment anything lifted it); and `corroborated` is deliberately not inherited (a verdict about a different reading).   **r5 — TWO HALVES OF ONE GAP IN THE LIFT (2026-09-09, the round-4 verifier; both reproduced on a copy of this instance's own post-migration cache file).** Six of the nine producers hand this module a LEGACY object, and a legacy object is ONE reading spread over a carry-forward of everything else. ① The lift could not tell the halves apart: `fromLegacy` stamped `source`/`fetchedAt` on EVERY limit it rebuilt and `mergeLimit` prefers the newer-or-equal copy, so ONE `rate_limit_event` about the five-hour bucket re-stamped the model-scoped Fable cap and the overage limit as "via own session, just now" and moved the Fable window's `measuredAt` onto a `utilization: 1` nobody re-measured — the `limitRows` → "via X · Updated Y" rows this work added to END that class were rendering it, and 659 green asserts said nothing because the panel-provenance leg builds its `limits` array by hand and never reaches the write path. `carryUnmeasuredLimits` (lift-only) asks the FILE instead of asking the producer for a preserve list — that list is the tool which has failed on this store six times — by comparing the CLAIM (`quotaModel.limitClaimKey`: the numbers, deliberately excluding `measuredAt` and `state`, which are the provenance halves) and handing back the previous object when it is unchanged. **Granularity is the WINDOW**: the claude plan limit holds two windows and one event names one bucket, so resolving per LIMIT still re-clocked a week-old 7-day number (found by mutation-testing this round's own first leg; §⑰a carries a single-mechanism control for it). It errs deliberately toward the OLDER age (a re-measurement that lands on the same number keeps its previous date): a number that looks staler than it is costs a re-read, a stale number wearing a fresh timestamp is the incident. The retirement is LOUD, because removing a limit removes a claim and this one gates the pool.

  **r6 — THE RIGHT TO RETIRE BELONGS TO A PARSE THAT SAW THE WHOLE SET (2026-09-09, the round-5 verifier; both halves reproduced against the base commit before anything was changed).** r5's `authoritativeScopes` was gated on `u.scopedWeekly?.length` — a fact about the ARRAY, which says a model cap was seen and never that ALL of them were. Those seven call sites are fed by THREE parsers, and on one vendor state (plan 20/20, a Fable cap at 10 %, and a `seven_day_opus` at 100 % stated with NO `resets_at`) they do not agree: `parseCliUsageText` answers `plan, model:fable, model:opus` while `parseOAuthUsage` (the bare-token ⟳ and the four host legs) and `parseGetUsageResponse` (the engine's control-channel probe) both answer `plan, model:fable`, because each drops a named cap that states no reset. So SIX of the seven sites could RETIRE a real, spent cap on the strength of a parse that could never have seen it — measured end to end through the real modules and the real write path: `accountRemaining` went `{remaining:0}` → `{remaining:80}`, i.e. inc-msof8i22 re-opened by the mechanism built to end its mirror image. **Reachability is structural, not incidental**: the control-channel probe is the FIRST rung of the ⟳ route (ahead of `refreshViaCliPanel`), so on any account with a live local claude chat session the authoritative list always came from a dropping parser; and neither preserve-merge protects it (the panel replaces `scopedWeekly` wholesale when non-empty, `writeUsageCacheForKey` falls back to `prev` only when the list is EMPTY, and the bare-token leg passes the parse verbatim with no merge at all).
  **THE FIX IS A PROPERTY THE PARSE STATES.** Each producer counts what it DROPPED — a `weekly_scoped` entry it could not NAME, a bucket-shaped field it could not read a number from, a `Current week (…)` line its own regex did not match — and only a parse that dropped nothing marks itself (`quotaModel.markScopedEnumeration`); `authoritativeScopesOf(parse)` is the ONE rule every call site asks, and it keeps r5's second condition deliberately (an enumerated but EMPTY list still states nothing, because it is indistinguishable from "my scoped parsing broke" and retiring a spent cap is the money-losing direction). **The mark is a NON-ENUMERABLE, SYMBOL-KEYED own property**, which is this store's oldest law applied one more time — a fact only ONE producer may state does not belong in the object all the others rewrite: `JSON.stringify` drops it, a spread drops it, a preserve-merge of a stored file drops it (every one of those losses means "no authority", the safe direction), and no JSON a vendor, a device or a file could hand us can FORGE it. **That is why the panel site asks `cliPanel` and not the `{...cliPanel}` it writes** — and why that call site needed a FUNCTIONAL leg rather than another pin: swapping the argument type-checks, satisfies the wiring pin's shape, and silently kills the retirement at the one producer that most deserves it (mutation-tested: it reddens nothing else in the suite), so §⑱f drives the REAL `refreshViaCliPanel` through the REAL `setupUsage` with a fake `claude` on `CLAUDE_CMD` and reads the consequence.

It is the ROUTINE shape, not an edge: on this instance's own anchor streams 704 of 5631 scoped readings and 615 of 7978 seven-day readings carry no reset at all (692 of the scoped ones from the ⟳ panel). **Honest boundary: every reset-less bucket ever recorded HERE sits at u=0, so the exact spent-and-reset-less combination is latent on this instance, not live** — but it is the shape 2.305.0 found in a real payload, and the pinned assertions that said "a scoped field with no reset is still skipped" were pinning the pre-r3 belief that a reset-less bucket is useless. Two existing suites' expectations were therefore INVERTED on purpose, each with its essay and each with a replacement negative control (a window-shaped field stating no number is still not a bucket — and now it also costs the parse the right to retire).

### rate-limit-capture.js

  rate-limit-capture.js — PASSIVE quota capture from the CLI's own `rate_limit_event` stream-json records (B-e5c9, 2.289.0; discovered by 2.1.226 binary forensics — a first-class stdout record "emitted when rate limit info changes" VibeSpace dropped as unknown forever). Rides real API responses ⇒ ZERO extra calls (§ban-safety: purely passive; the banned auto-get_usage and a billable `-p` probe are both worse AND `-p` must carry a prompt + returns no 5h/7d data). Closes the chat/stream-json gap (no statusline ⇒ last-known quota only). `parseRateLimitEvent(msg)` (both key casings, 2.227.6; utilization integer-%→0..1; all 16 rate_limit_info fields) + `captureRateLimitEvent({cacheDir,key,identityIds,ev})` — ONE impl for local AND remote (remote chat stdout relays through the same server parse at server.js:1616; `usageCacheKeyFor` routes a host-login remote session to `host-<id>` not `__global__`, also fixing remote banner attribution). `status:'rejected'`⇒bucket dead+pool re-eval (banner parity); `utilization`⇒usage-cache write that becomes a dead-reckoning ANCHOR next sweep (estimator self-calibrates from live chat). Carries the 2.267.0 identity-group anti-poison discipline + ONE addition: **`fetchedAt` bumps ONLY for a real READING** (utilization or rejected) — a resetsAt/overage-only event updates fields in place WITHOUT promoting a stale file to 'freshest' (false-anchor poison). Server: recordRateLimitEvent in the claude stdout dispatch. Test: scripts/test-rate-limit-capture.mjs (20). **B-2c9b: `captureRateLimitEvent({…, source})` labels the reading write (default 'rate-limit-event'; the wall machine's ground-truth demotion passes 'wall') — ONE write path for readings AND walls, never a twin writer (suite ⑧).** **2026-09-07: `{…, corroborated}` rides the same write** — whether the OTel observation agreed with the credential SLOT this reading was filed on. A LABEL for the panel and for forensics; the KEY comes from `readingSlotFor` and nothing else (see the readings-by-slot section). **THE LANE IS DECIDED BY WHAT NAMES IT (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21; the 2.1.274 binary's own words: `unifiedWindows` = "Per-window usage for the session (5-hour), weekly (7-day), and overage-included weekly (per-model bucket; present only for accounts whose responses carry that window)").** `parseRateLimitEvent` returns the REPRESENTATIVE claim (status + top-level utilization, on the lane `rateLimitType` names; a five_hour record with no top-level number takes its own window's) AND `windows` {fiveHour, sevenDay, modelCap, scoped{<model>}} from `unifiedWindows` (null when absent — an old record claims nothing about other lanes); `seven_day_overage_included` is kind `scoped` + `modelCap:true` with NO name — never `sevenDay` (2.361.2's mapping put the bucket's 0.87 into the plan week whose verified panel said 0.43; measured on 12 live buffers the bucket reads about twice the plan on every account that has one, and the 7d donut flipped red/green between every event and every panel refresh); `resolveModelCapLane({cacheDir,key,ev,hint})` names it through quota-model's `nameModelCapLane` against the KEY's `.window-` sidecar scoped map + typed limits (sidecar reset match → existing model limit with the reset → the session's request family breaks a tie → else the `model:cap` placeholder); `lanesOf(ev)` = every lane the record states (representative first; a non-representative window's status is its own number's; a rejection kills the representative lane only); `lanesSnapshot(ev,{named})` = those lanes in the shared legacy shape (the window guard takes `named:true`, auto-resume the whole); `captureRateLimitEvent` names the lane on the key it writes, applies every lane through the one write path (sibling fan-out + fetchedAt discipline unchanged) and answers `{…, lanes, modelCapLane}`; the engine names the lane BEFORE any signal reads the kind (pre-attribution key, re-asked on the key the guard lands on), hands the guard every named lane, feeds the witness ring the plan 7d window, and no longer defers the type (it marks the CAP on arrival; a same-turn banner marks the same lane or the lane the placeholder folds into). test-rate-limit-capture ⑨ = the owner's record verbatim (5h 0.09 / plan 0.43 / bucket 0.87 → plan 7d 0.43, Fable 0.87, 5h 0.09 on a key whose sidecar names fable) + a no-unifiedWindows control (the 2.361.2 rejection → the placeholder dead, plan untouched; with a Fable cap on the same reset → Fable) + a seven_day_opus control + the measured five_hour shape; ⑩ = a tree census: every file that spells the type is allowlisted with a reason and no executable comparison exists outside the parse and the schema. **r2 (2026-09-21, verifier findings): ① the placeholder's lane is spelled ONE way — `resolveModelCapLane` sets a model-cap representative's `scopedName` to the placeholder key when nothing names it and `lanesOf` treats that key as the cap lane, so the wall signal and the fresh-window edge agree and an un-named cap wall opens on a later placeholder reading; ② the scoped dead mark has the SAME reset ladder as the plan lanes (stated future reset > stored future reset > the record's plan weekly reset > a bounded 24 h guess) — a no-reset rejection no longer parks a member with no deadline; ③ `scopedFetchedAt` is stamped with the reading's clock whenever a scoped lane carried a reading (the anchors and the estimator read it as the scoped `asOf`); ④ a non-representative window whose number did not move keeps the stored status (`limited` always lands).**

**A MODEL-CAP REJECTION HAS NO TYPE OF ITS OWN (2026-09-13, the Fable-cap pool storm).** Measured on the installed claude 2.1.267 and on this instance's own session buffers, the whole `rateLimitType` vocabulary is `{five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_overage_included, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_opus, seven_day_oauth_apps}` — **there is no `seven_day_fable`**. So when the vendor refuses a turn because a MODEL cap is spent, the `rate_limit_event` arrives on the UNSCOPED `seven_day` lane and the only thing that names the model is the banner text a few records later (`ClaudeCodeAdapter.parseLimitBanner` → `{kind:'scoped', name:'Fable'}`). The wall machine took both at face value and wrote both: the event marked the PLAN week `utilization: 1, status: 'limited'` and the banner marked the Fable cap, i.e. **one rejection, two demotions**, with the plan mark false for 12-60 h and every OPUS conversation on that member evicted by it. `parseRateLimitEvent` is unchanged and still maps by TYPE (a future `seven_day_fable` would be `kind:'scoped'` through the existing `seven_day_(?!overage)(\w+)` regex and needs no special case, and `seven_day_overage_included` stays the weekly lane's own accounting — the 2.361.2 monthly-cap incident). What changed lives in the engine: `laneIsProvisional` / `deferTurnLane` / `laneFromBanner` / `laneByEvidence` / `settleTurnLane` hold the WRITE for the rest of the turn while the SIGNAL fires immediately, so the lane is decided by the banner, or by evidence at turn end, before any bucket is marked. See the incident essay in kb-bugfix-invariants.

**THE PROJECTION FAMILY IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE STATED MODEL (2026-09-13 r2, the round-1 verifier, reproduced end to end).** `projectCacheForFamily(cache, fam)` DROPS every model-scoped cap of another known family, so the family handed to it decides which walls the pool and the verdict are allowed to SEE. Round 1 fixed `sessionModelFor` to state the REQUEST model and then handed THAT to the projection — which trades the incident's blind spot for its mirror: while a classifier reroute is STANDING, the cap of the model that is actually ANSWERING (and being billed — this instance's own anchor for the incident reads `costSince.byFamily {opus: 21.3957, fable: 0}` over 24 requests) is thrown away, so the pool proactively moves the conversation ONTO a member whose cap for that model is 100 % spent and `quotaVerdictFor` calls that member `usable`, which is what AUTHORISES a billed continue. Measured through the real engine + real pool: `fam=fable, from 80%`, notice "its fable quota was at 80%", verdict `usable:true` — where master moves nothing and answers `Opus 0% < 5%`. `projectionFamilyFor(session, model)` is now the ONE rule both projection sites ask: **a standing reroute to another (or an unnameable) family ⇒ `null`, i.e. NO projection, so every bucket counts** — round 1's own doctrine, applied where it was not; a reroute WITHIN the same family (fable-5-1 → fable-4) is one cap and keeps its projection; with no session it is exactly `familyOfModel(model)`, so every session-less caller is byte-identical. A stale stamp therefore costs CONSERVATISM, never money. `sessionModelFor` deliberately still answers the REQUEST model everywhere else — the notice text, `_wallScope`, `fireIdentityFor`, the model lock and `laneByEvidence`, which asks which cap a REJECTION was about and the CLI rejects the REQUEST (the incident's own banner named Fable while opus was answering). Gate: test-fable-cap-pool-storm §5/§5b — the incident shape with an Opus cap present, the verdict site driven on a pool where that cap is the only thing in the way, the rule's truth table off a REAL engine, a grep-derived census that every `projectCacheForFamily` site asks the rule (the SPAWN chooser is the one allowed exception: it is handed a model and has no session), and a control proving §1's revert ALONE does not reproduce it — the two are different defects, which is why §1's own control must be MASTER.

**AND THE MODEL LOCK IS THE REQUEST MODEL, THE REROUTE STAMP OUTLIVES A RESTART, AND THE TEARDOWN OWES THE LANE (2026-09-13 r3 — the owner's correction plus two round-2 verifier findings, each reproduced against the r2 commit first).**

  **(1) THE LADDER IS `LOCKED > picked > spawn > served-IF-NOT-A-FALLBACK`.** The incident's conversation was LOCKED — its frozen meta (`data/incidents/inc-mtzcj5sl-lzmw/frozen/session-meta/cw-6-1788859480777.json`) reads `modelLocked: true, lockedModel: "fable[1m]", pickedModel: "fable[1m]", spawnModel: "fable[1m]"` — and `maybeRepinLockedModel` re-sends `/model` at every turn end where the served model drifted, so the server KNEW the request model the whole time and was actively re-asserting it. "Newest wins" let a fallback-served `claude-opus-4-8` record outrank both the lock and the pick: MEASURED with those exact fields, ONE main-thread opus record after a restart gave `sessionModelFor` 'claude-opus-4-8', `projectionFamilyFor` 'opus', the move personal -> fish (Fable 100 % spent), the notice "its opus quota was at 66%", and `quotaVerdictFor` — the site that authorises an unattended continue — `usable: true` about that member. The lock sits ABOVE the pick because the two cannot disagree on the path that exists: picking a model while locked RE-TARGETS the lock on BOTH sides (`src/lib/chat-status-bar.js` sends `lockModel` with the pick, `src/ws-handler.js`'s `set-model` rewrites `_lockedModel`), and both halves are pinned as source facts rather than assumed. And because the lock is ALREADY persisted and restored, a LOCKED conversation is right immediately after a restart, before any stamp / pick / served model has been re-learned — the incident's own shape. `projectionFamilyFor` gains the mirror rung: a lock whose SERVED model is in another family is the same ambiguity a standing reroute is (both caps can refuse the next turn), so it answers `null` — the belt for a stamp we never saw. It is deliberately NOT extended to a plain pick: a `set-model` writes `/model` on the same tick, so a served model older than a pick is stale BY CONSTRUCTION and treating that as ambiguity would suppress the projection for one turn after every ordinary model switch. The CLI-side `/model` control is untouched — unlocked + served changed with no fallback on record still defines the session.

  **(2) `_servedViaFallback` IS PERSISTED (`persisted: 'meta'`).** Round 1's argument — *boot-restore's ladder falls back to picked/spawn = the REQUEST model* — is true of the **LADDER** and false of every other reader. A restored UNLOCKED conversation whose reroute was announced BEFORE the restart gets ONE main-thread opus record; nothing on the session refutes it, `servedDefinesModel` says yes, and the identical cascade runs. The reroute is announced ONCE and `scope:"session"`, so it can never be re-learned from the stream — only the file can carry it. It is written by the two GRANULAR CONSUMERS (`noteModelFallback`, and `noteServedModel`'s retirement branch) and never at their call sites, which is the twin the 1b census bans; the store arrives as a LAZY `getSessionMetaStore` dep because session-stdout is constructed after the engine in boot order, and the write follows the ws-handler `set-model` idiom (spread what is on disk, re-list only what changed). **ONE write per reroute, not one per record** — the incident announced the same reroute twice and a meta write re-runs the ledger's account-by-time attribution — so restating a standing reroute also leaves `at` alone (it dates when THIS reroute began; a retired stamp starts fresh because `prev` is null). `src/server/boot-restore.js` restores it at all THREE ladder-hydration sites through ONE `restoredFallback(meta)` expression, enforced by a DERIVED census so a fourth restore path goes red instead of silently dropping the fact. A stale restored stamp cannot SPEND money (`projectionFamilyFor` null, the REQUEST model wins) though it is not free either — see the r3-r2 block below — and the retirement clears it ON DISK.
