  **ROUND 4 (adversarial verifier — one defect, HIGH, reproduced on a COPY of this instance's stores before it was believed).**

  **THE REPAIR WAS MANUFACTURING THE MISATTRIBUTION IT EXISTS TO CLEAN UP.** `establishedWindows()` established each account's window as `{sevenDay, fiveHour:null, scoped:{}}` — it DISCARDED the model-scoped half of the evidence — so `decideReadingTarget` judged every anchor on its 7-day bucket alone. That is not a smaller check, it is a BLIND one, because **an anchor is a snapshot of a usage-cache FILE and that file has more than one writer**: the statusline rewrites `{5h, 7d}` from its own payload and PRESERVES whatever `scopedWeekly` the file already held (it has no scoped buckets of its own — the 2.70.0 Fable-vanishing rule its own comment names). So a reading that landed on the wrong key before the window guard existed leaves a record that is ITSELF A MIX: another account's 7d sitting on top of **this stream's own** Fable bucket. Measured on a copy of this instance: **444** such records, against **32** whose halves are both foreign and **4466** clean ones. Deciding on the 7d alone therefore moved **443 of the 476** re-files complete with a Fable bucket whose weekly phase the destination account contradicts — and `repairCachesByWindow` then picked one of them as `best` (it was the newest record with an agreeing 7d, `refiledFrom` naming the other member) and `_cacheFromAnchor` copied its value, its `resetsAt` AND its `scopedFetchedAt` over the target's own. `src/account-pool-auto.js` reads `cache.scopedWeekly` in `accountRemaining`, `weeklyDeadline` and `bucketRems`, so that is a misattributed reading that can flip a pool switch — the 2.305.0 scoped-bucket class, created BY THE REPAIR.

  **THE FIX: PER BUCKET, NEVER WHOLESALE.** ① `establishedWindows()` establishes each identity's **scoped** phases from its OWN on-demand rows under the same two thresholds as the 7d (`MIN_OWN_READINGS` / `OWN_DOMINANCE` per bucket name, `_tallyPhase` + `_dominant` shared with the 7d) — measurably the same phase as the 7d on every identity here (32340/32400, 532740/532800, 320340/320400/320399, 143940/144000/143999, 557999/558000, 579540/579600, 493140/493200: every cluster inside the ±120 s tolerance, and the seven distinct). ② `repairAnchorsByWindow` asks `decideReadingTarget` ONE BUCKET AT A TIME (`_bucketVerdict`, a window carrying nothing but that bucket, so a bucket can never speak for another): the **PRIMARY** half is `{5h, 7d}` — one payload, one producer, one credential, so the 5h travels with the 7d and never alone — the record follows its primary half, and it carries ONLY the buckets that agree with wherever it lands. Every other bucket is archived with its OWN reason (`_dropReason`, which answers about the DESTINATION — quoting `decideReadingTarget`'s reason here filed 443 of 444 drop lines under the sentence *"window matches the target"*, about a bucket that was dropped). A bucket that states no weekly window rides along while the record STAYS and is dropped when it MOVES — "no evidence ⇒ no refusal" is a rule about REFUSING TO WRITE, while moving a bucket onto a different account is a positive claim, and 705 scoped entries here carry no `resetsAt` while `bucketRemaining` still reads their utilization. A record with no agreeing bucket at all is archived, not moved. ③ `repairCachesByWindow` chooses `best` only among records ALL of whose judgeable weekly buckets agree (`_recordAgreesWholly`), and `_cacheFromAnchor` takes the account's window as a second, independent barrier — plus, because the per-bucket move can now leave the newest own-window record with no scoped bucket at all, it **preserve-merges** the previous snapshot's scoped bucket (filtered by the same window) instead of replacing it, exactly as all three live writers do; a rebuild that simply replaced the object would DELETE the model cap the pool decides on. ④ a cache whose 7d AGREES but whose scoped bucket does not is **stripped in place** (`scopedStripped`) — the rebuild branch cannot reach that shape, so before this round nothing on any path could clean it while the pool read it every tick.

  **THE LIVE WRITER PATH NEEDS NO CHANGE, and the reason is pinned.** All three `guardReadingTarget` call sites are handed a PRODUCER PAYLOAD, never a merged snapshot: a `rate_limit_event` names exactly ONE bucket (`kind` sevenDay|fiveHour|scoped), and a `get_usage` control answer, a `/usage` panel result and a codex snapshot are each ONE credential's single response — so the guard's whole-payload verdict already IS a per-bucket verdict there. The MIX is manufactured downstream by the per-key preserve-merge, and each of those preserves reads the TARGET's own previous list, AFTER the guard has moved `key` (source-pinned by §16b(i), including the ORDER inside the shipped statusline). One consequence is deliberate and worth stating: the seeded sidecar now carries the scoped phases too, so the live guard is armed on model-scoped buckets from the upgrade boot — which is not a new class of behaviour but the removal of an inconsistency, because the live panel producer has always stamped `windowOf(merged)` and that includes `scopedWeekly`.

  **ROUND 4 INVARIANTS.** **A record assembled by more than one writer must be judged by more than one verdict** — ask what wrote each field before deciding the record as a unit; here `{5h,7d}` and `scopedWeekly` have different producers and therefore different provenance. **Establishing "the account's window" from a subset of the evidence is not a weaker check, it is a blind one**, and a repair that cannot see half of a record will move that half onto a stranger. **A reason string answers the question the line is about**: `decideReadingTarget`'s reason answers "does this bucket belong to the stream it sits in", which is a different question from "why did it not travel", and quoting it produced 443 archive lines asserting the opposite of what happened. **"No evidence ⇒ no refusal" governs REFUSING, not MOVING** — an unjudgeable bucket may stay, never travel. **A rebuild is a WRITE and inherits the preserve rule every other writer has** (the Fable-vanishing class does not care who is writing). And **two barriers against one harm need one control each, read where each barrier speaks** — the `best` picker is only load-bearing on a store the anchor pass has not cleaned, so it is driven ALONE (§16b h2) rather than left as a guard nobody can delete and redden.

  **ROUND 5 (adversarial verifier — two defects, both reproduced on a COPY of this instance's stores before they were believed).**

  **① HIGH: AN IDENTITY CAN HOLD MORE THAN ONE CACHE FILE, AND THE REPAIR ONLY EVER TOUCHED ONE.** `repairCachesByWindow` iterated `windows` and derived the cache path from `w.accountId` — the most frequent `accountId` among that stream's rows. That answers *"who is this stream mostly about"*, which is not the question: what it needed was *"which usage-cache files hold this identity's readings"*, and an org-merged login is exactly where the two answers differ. `usageIdentityGroups` puts `__global__.json` (the machine login) and the named subscription in ONE group because they are ONE quota — measured here, `usage-cache/__global__.json` carries the same `orgUuid` as its named sibling and that identity's stream holds **47 of its 1249 rows keyed to it** (the named sub holds the other 1202, so it always won the dominance test). The machine login was therefore absent from all three of the repair's jobs, silently: it was never **REPAIRED**, so a foreign window in it survives the migration; it was never **SEEDED**, and since the live `guardReadingTarget` keys its `windows` map by **CACHE FILE NAME** (`fn.slice(0,-5)` + `.window-<that>`), that key had no entry and the guard was *structurally inert* on it — `no established window to contradict`, write as asked; and `sweepUsageAnchors` anchors the **FRESHEST** cache of an identity group, so one ordinary sweep of a stale-but-foreign `__global__.json` re-poisons the stream the migration has just cleaned. A/B on a COPY of this instance, ONE frozen snapshot with the machine login's 7d set to a sibling member's phase and only the repair changed: **r4 leaves it carrying the stranger's window and writes 7 sidecars; r5 archives + rebuilds it from the identity's own newest wholly-agreeing anchor and writes 8.**

  **THE FIX: the cache half is keyed on the FILES, resolved with the product's own rule.** `identityCacheKeys(cacheDir, windows, {accounts})` enumerates with `usageIdentityGroups`' own predicate verbatim (`.json`, never `__models__*`, never `host-*`, never `rates.json`; a file with no roster record is the zombie the product already ignores and a `pooled` record holds no quota of its own — both NAMED and skipped) and resolves each file with the product's own `identityKeyFor`, given the roster's `backend`/`type`/`email` (so the migration now receives the roster **records**, not just the ids — a ChatGPT and an Anthropic login sharing an email must never merge, and ids alone would have made this map a second, weaker spelling of the engine's). **The FORWARD answer wins whenever it names an identity.** The `acct:` rung is `identityKeyFor`'s own documented LAST RESORT — the file states no org and no email — and only there may the STREAMS be asked: exactly one established stream whose rows name that `accountId` resolves it, two leave it alone and SAY so. That rung is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the engine can key such an account by EMAIL because `accounts.list()` reads it out of the CREDENTIAL DIR, which a migration running before any `AccountManager` exists cannot, and **two live members on this instance are in exactly that state** (their cache files carry no `orgUuid` and their roster records no email, yet their streams are `anchors-email_*` and are being written today). A reassignment cannot sneak through it, because a login that moved orgs writes the new `orgUuid` into the file and the forward rung reads that first. **A PSEUDO key is never resolved from the streams**: the engine records `accountId: null` for BOTH `__global__.json` and `__global_codex__.json`, so a null row cannot tell the two apart (measured: this instance's codex stream is 1532 null-keyed rows, exactly the shape a claude machine login's would be) — and both are named by the forward rung anyway. `host-*` stays excluded for the same reason the engine excludes it from identity groups: `usage-cache/host-<id>.json` is that HOST's own claude login, no anchor stream describes it, and this migration has no established window to judge or seed it with — seeding one would be inventing it. The anchor-file slug is no longer re-spelled here either: `anchorSlug` is exported from `usage-anchors.js` (its own `_file` uses it), because the repair walks that name-mangling BACKWARDS and a second spelling of it is a twin whose drift would file readings under a key nothing else uses.

  **② LOW: A PRIMARY BUCKET THE RECORD STATES BUT THE WINDOW CANNOT DATE WAS DELETED SILENTLY.** The r4 drop lines were written off `win` — the DATED view — so a record with NO dated 7d (`prim === null`) that moved on its scoped evidence had `fiveHour` and `sevenDay` nulled on the moved row with **no drop line at all**: `bucketsArchived: 0`, counted as a WHOLE re-file, and the placeholder reason `'window'` in both the journal and the archive. The shape is ordinary — `data/bin/vibespace-usage` writes `{u: 0}` with no window for an absent bucket and `maybeRecord` keeps the utilization, and **2392 of this instance's 7106 anchors carry an undated primary bucket beside a dated scoped one**. (Zero of them are ALSO 7d-less today, which is why this is latent rather than measured harm — but a bucket moved onto an account it cannot be shown to belong to is the entire class of defect this repair is made of, and it was moving without a word.) `_primaryDrops` now decides on the RECORD's buckets: every primary bucket the record actually STATES gets its own archived line, dated or not (an undated one says it states no weekly window and so cannot be shown to be the destination's; the 5h says the seven-day half it travels with is not the destination's, or is absent), the move is counted PARTIAL, and the reason the record MOVED is the verdict of the bucket that DECIDED it — never a drop line, whose sentence is about a bucket that stayed behind.

  **ROUND 5 INVARIANTS.** **"Who is this stream mostly about" is not "which files belong to this identity"** — a dominance vote over one field answers a different question from the product's own forward map, and the difference is exactly the case (an org-merged login) where the harm lives. **A repair must enumerate with the same predicate the product enumerates with, and resolve with the same function the product resolves with** — anything else is a second, weaker spelling that drifts silently. **A guard keyed by FILE NAME needs one sidecar per FILE**: seeding "the account" arms it for one of that account's two keys and leaves the other structurally inert. **A repair is only finished if the next tick cannot undo it** — the sweep anchors the freshest cache of a group, so a cache the repair could not see is anchor material one tick later, which is why the fix had to be the cache half rather than a second anchor pass. **A fallback rung must be gated on the evidence being ABSENT, not merely inconvenient** (`identityKeyFor`'s own `acct:` last resort is that gate) **and must refuse when it is ambiguous.** **Decide a field's fate on the field the record STATES, not on the derived view of it** — the dated window is a projection, and a projection cannot see what it dropped. **A name-mangling rule with two spellings is a twin**: export it from the producer.

  **ROUND 5 MEASUREMENT (a COPY of this instance's stores; production never written).** 7 identities established and all 7 able to receive; anchors 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 42 pairs voided, rates dropped, 7106 records in and 7106 out; caches **8 keys in an identity (r4: 7), 8 seeded, 0 foreign, 0 rebuilt, 0 scoped strips**, with `__global_codex__` correctly NAMED as unresolvable (`codex:__global__` has no established window). **CENSUS: every accepted cache key that belongs to an identity ends with a sidecar (0 missing) and no bucket its identity contradicts (0), and 0 of 7106 anchor rows contradict theirs.** Idempotent on a second run (0 further moves, census unchanged), 64 ms. The two `acct:`-rung members resolve through their own streams (`via: 'stream'`) — under r4 they were reached by accident, through the dominant-accountId path.

  **HIGH: THE `__global__` KEY HAS A SECOND SNAPSHOT, AND IT IS NOT IN THE DIRECTORY THE REPAIR WALKS.** r5 fixed "one identity, more than one cache FILE" — and still assumed the usage-cache DIRECTORY was every file. The machine login's snapshot is persisted TWICE: `usage-cache/__global__.json`, and `data/usage-cache.json` (`USAGE_CACHE_FILE`, server.js), whose `.claude` payload IS that same slot. `readUsageCache()` seeds `_rateLimitCache` from it at boot, `writeUsageCache()` is its only writer, and the same-account merge (usage-routes ~:310-316, `_rateLimitCache = usage; writeUsageCache()`) writes the NAMED subscription's snapshot into it whenever the two are one quota. `repairCachesByWindow` never saw it — and because `_cacheFromAnchor` sets `out.fetchedAt = anchor.fetchedAt`, a rebuild REWINDS the directory copy to the anchor it restored from, so the untouched copy is GUARANTEED to win the merge that reads it: `if (key === '__global__') { if (!_rateLimitCache || (u.fetchedAt > (_rateLimitCache.fetchedAt || 0))) …`. Measured on a copy of this instance's stores, one frozen snapshot with the machine login's identity carrying a sibling member's phase: after the r5 migration `usage-cache/__global__.json` and its named sub both read 0.53 @ phase 1789142340 while `data/usage-cache.json` still carries 0.93 @ 1789491600 with the newest `fetchedAt`, and the REAL `/api/usage` then serves 0.93 on BOTH rows — the machine login from `_rateLimitCache`, and the named subscription because the same-account merge hands the freshest of the pair to both — and the file keeps it: the migration is one-shot and ledger-gated, so nothing runs again to notice. (Measured too: the route does not even need to rewrite it — it is already the persisted answer. The only thing that displaces it is a live producer writing a snapshot NEWER than the stale copy, which on an idle or signed-out machine login can be indefinite.)

  **THE FIX: `repairGlobalFile`, run AFTER the directory half, judged by that half's OWN answer.** This file is not an identity of its own; it is a cached copy of the `__global__` KEY, so it is judged by whatever `identityCacheKeys` said about `__global__`. Asking `identityKeyFor` again over this payload would be exactly the second, weaker spelling of the map r5 exists to make single — so when `__global__` is unresolvable (or the directory holds no `__global__.json` at all, so the map never names it) the copy is LEFT ALONE and SAID, exactly as the directory half leaves an unresolvable key alone: a copy we cannot attribute is not a copy we may delete. On ANY contradicting bucket — the 7-day one or a model-scoped one, since the pool reads `cache.scopedWeekly` and this copy feeds the same two panel rows — the whole payload is appended to `readings-window-usage-cache.ndjson` under `store: 'usage-cache.json'` with a reason, and then the file is UNLINKED rather than overwritten with the repaired directory snapshot. **Unlink, not mirror**, and the reason is structural: removing a provably-foreign CACHED COPY of a file we have just repaired is the smaller claim, and the product self-heals on its own paths — `readUsageCache()` catches and returns null, so `_rateLimitCache` starts null and `ingestPassiveUsage`'s `!_rateLimitCache` branch re-seeds it from the repaired `usage-cache/__global__.json` on the first tick, which runs synchronously inside `setupUsage` (and if that file was emptied for want of a surviving own-window reading, the same-account merge re-seeds it from the named sub of the same quota). Mirroring instead would make the migration a SECOND WRITER of a reading snapshot, owing the window filter, the identity fields and the scoped preserve-merge `_cacheFromAnchor` carries. And whatever re-seeds the file afterwards comes FROM the repaired directory, so its `fetchedAt` can never outrank it again. The report carries `globalFile: 'clean' | 'archived' | 'unresolvable' | 'absent'` beside `globalFileWhy`, both printed by the one-shot log, and an `archived` counts toward the migration's `touched` notice.

  **THE OTHER ROOTS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** A standing sweep DERIVES the persisted-snapshot roots from the source (every `path.join(… 'usage-cache…')` and `VIBESPACE_USAGE_CACHE` under server.js / src / data/bin, minus the >1 MiB downloaded rclone and the esbuild daemon bundle whose sites are copies of `src/agentd`'s) and prints the census, so a THIRD home reddens instead of surviving the next migration the way this one did. Today: the DIRECTORY (walked), `data/usage-cache.json` (this half), and a DEVICE's own `~/.vibespace/usage-cache` — named OUT of scope, because it belongs to that machine and reaches us only as `usage-cache/host-*.json`, which the repair's own predicate already refuses for the reason the engine refuses it (no anchor stream describes a host's login, so there is no established window to judge or seed it with). Confirmed independently by scanning every `data/*.json` store on this instance for a reading shape: `usage-cache.json` is the only hit.

  **ROUND 6 INVARIANTS.** **A repair's scope is the set of PLACES a fact is persisted, not the one directory it is usually read from** — r5's own lesson ("an identity holds more than one cache file") had one more level in it, and the level it missed was the one file that is not in the directory at all. **A cached copy of a store you have just repaired is judged by the store's own answer for that key, never by re-deriving one from the copy** (a second derivation is a second map, and the difference between them is where the harm lives). **A rewind makes staleness WIN**: any repair that moves a timestamp backwards must ask what else compares against that timestamp — here `fetchedAt` is the arbiter of a newest-wins merge, so rebuilding from an older anchor is precisely what guaranteed the untouched copy would be served. **Archive, then delete, is a smaller claim than overwrite** when the product's own read path treats absence as "re-seed from the store" — but that only holds if the re-seed is checked, so it is driven through the REAL route rather than asserted. **A one-shot, ledger-gated migration has exactly one chance**: anything it does not judge is not "fixed later", it is kept forever. **And "is there another one?" is a number to re-measure, not a fact to inherit** — derive the set from the source, print it, and give the "nothing else exists" arm a control that makes it fail.

  **ROUND 6 MEASUREMENT (a COPY of this instance's stores; production never written).** On the store as it stands: 7 identities, all 7 able to receive; anchors 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 42 pairs voided, rates dropped, 7117 rows in and 7117 out; caches 8 keys / 8 seeded / 0 foreign / 0 rebuilt / 0 scoped strips, `__global_codex__` NAMED unresolvable; **`globalFile: 'clean'`** — this instance's sibling agrees today (phase 1789142340 against the identity's 1789142400, inside the ±120 s tolerance), and it is a copy of the named sub's snapshot, which is how the same-account merge writes it. 86 ms, idempotent on a second run (0 further moves; `globalFile` 'clean'), CENSUS 0 contradicting buckets in any cache, any stream, or the sibling. On the same store with the incident injected (the identity's machine login and named sub carrying a sibling member's 0.93 @ 1789491600, and the sibling file carrying it with the freshest `fetchedAt`): r5 leaves the sibling and the real `/api/usage` serves 0.93 on both rows; r6 reports `globalFile: 'archived'`, and the real route serves 0.53 @ 1789142340 on both rows from a file the product re-seeded itself.

  **ROUND 6 REGRESSIONS.** §16c(h) drives the whole path: the report state and its sentence, the archive line (its own `store`, the WHOLE original payload, and only then the unlink), the REAL `setupUsage()` on a REAL express app answering a REAL HTTP `GET /api/usage` for both rows, the re-seed agreeing with the window this migration seeded for `__global__`, idempotence, a scoped-only contradiction, an agreeing copy left BYTE-IDENTICAL, `absent`, and both unresolvable shapes (a pseudo `__global__` the streams may not name, and no `usage-cache/__global__.json` at all) with the copy untouched; plus the two hardening legs — the second lookup still names the identity against the EMPTIED directory copy (the least-informative post-state this half is read in), and a copy that cannot be UNLINKED fails the migration loudly, with its archive line already written, instead of reporting a repair that did not take. The NEGATIVE CONTROL is a PATCHED COPY of the real module with this round's call reverted (replacement asserted to hit), driven through the SAME real route on the SAME fixture: it serves the stranger's 93 % on both rows and the file still holds it. Two source pins carry the product facts this half stands on (the file is the `__global__` slot's other home with one reader and one writer; it is read back newest-wins, against `out.fetchedAt = anchor.fetchedAt`). The standing sweep prints its census, proves its own scope by naming the files it must have walked, and has a control that adds one synthetic third home and requires the verdict to flip. §9b pins the new rule in the auto-loaded LAW row with the r5 row as the negative control. Mutation-checked against the product source, each mechanism alone: dropping the call reddens 13, dropping the scoped half 1, resolving the copy with a second `identityKeyFor` 2, unlinking without archiving 1, swallowing the unlink error 1; restored, green. **test-readings-attribution 390.**

  **INVARIANTS.** A reading is evidence ABOUT ITSELF: when the record names the window its numbers are counted in, that outranks every piece of bookkeeping we keep about which credentials a process holds — bookkeeping describes intent, the window describes what answered. **A window is an identity, and a rolling identity must be compared by the part that does not roll** (the weekly phase; comparing absolute `resetsAt` would read every legitimate roll as a foreign account). **A fingerprint must name the thing it claims did not change**: the r3 clause says *the numbers did not move*, and fingerprinting only the window would have shadowed nearly every reading following a re-point between two members sharing a phase (found by the suite's own shared-phase leg, in this branch's code, before it shipped). **The fact a guard reads may never be the fact a bad write produces** — `ownWindow` is stamped by the one producer whose key and credential dir are one decision, and is never inferred from `sevenDay.resetsAt`. **No evidence ⇒ no refusal**, and every refusal is archived with the reason, the target's own window and its age, so "the account's window genuinely moved" is distinguishable from "this reading was mis-filed". **A write that moves money is not silent**: the shadow and the guard each speak once per session per verdict transition. And **a repair whose only evidence is "this member's login died" can only ever see the visible half** — the silent half needs evidence carried by the data itself.

### usage-walker.js

  usage-walker.js      — THE ledger walk, ONE module (2.297.0 twin-killer): UsageHistory.scan() consumes it IN-PROCESS (cursors injected, onEvent enrichment orchestrator-side), the daemon runs it as the usage-scan op child, and data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan mirrors it for checkout-less ssh hosts (parity-pinned). **usage-events PUSH (2.299.0, R4 complete): the daemon watches transcript dirs → incremental walk → chan-0 batches → server acks after durable ingest → ONLY THEN the device commits its cursor (two-phase, roles inverted; unacked batches re-emit, rid dedup absorbs). Remote ledger = seconds-fresh; covers external sessions + workflow file-only usage the stdout relay never sees; 60s-floor dirty-kick harvest stays as the fallback rung. E2E scripts/test-usage-events-push.mjs (7) incl. the unacked-batch-does-not-advance-cursor proof.** Event fields: {rid, mid, ts, sid, be, model, cwd, i, cw5, cw1, cr, o, tier} + codex-only `effort` (v3, 2026-09-06) + **`origin` on EVERY event and `wcwd`/`wf`/`agent` on the ones that need them (2026-09-10)**. Codex block v3: `mid` = the preceding `token_usage_record.response_id` (0.153; cursor-parked `pendMid`/`pendTotal`, total-checked, consumed by the next token_count), `effort` from turn_context; the `cx:<sid>:<cumulative>` rid is the ONE key the codex normalizer must derive identically (its meta.requestId): sid = the rollout FILE's uuid (never a session_meta inside it — a sub-agent rollout also carries the PARENT's at line 1), and an identical re-emitted token_count is dropped on `rid === cur.lastRid` — the normalizer mirrors both (round 3: per-RECORD file provenance `__threadId` tagged by the merged reader, the reader's id only a default for provenance-less records, wrapper_meta re-points it; `_lastRidKeys` per thread = this cursor per file).  **THE PER-TICK BYTE BUDGET (2.369.167, perf lane ⑥): `runUsageWalk({…, budgetBytes, onBudget})` — with an `onBudget` hook (a function returning a promise; UsageHistory passes `() => new Promise(setImmediate)`) the walk YIELDS every `budgetBytes` of consumed transcript bytes and answers a PROMISE of the same `{events, cursors, cursorFile, filesTouched}`; without a hook it is the synchronous function it always was (`budgetBytes` ignored) — the daemon's `usage-scan` child (agentd.js) and the shipped scanner keep that form, a child has no loop to block. ONE WALK: the body is a generator (`walkSteps`, `scanFileWith`, `scanBufferSteps` for decompressed zst rollouts) whose `yield`s are the budget points, driven straight through (sync) or across one `await onBudget()` per yield (`driveYielding`); a yield sits only AFTER a whole line was consumed and its bytes added to `cur.offset`, so a suspended walk's cursors are always valid (one yield per whole budget: `spent %= budget`, a line is never split); a rejected hook rejects the walk and `steps.return()` closes the file it was parked in. Cursor semantics untouched (byte offsets, the incomplete trailing line unconsumed, size < offset ⇒ reset — a file truncated between two yields ends the read at EOF and resets on the next run exactly as the sync walk does —, zst plain-offset cursors, `pendMid` in the cursor, the device two-phase commit). The exported `scanBufferWith` is the sync spelling of `scanBufferSteps`. Gate: test-usage-walk-parity's budget block (a 7.4 MiB four-kind fixture incl. a zst rollout: yielding ≡ sync ≡ shipped scanner on events, cursors and filesTouched; ⌊consumed / 1 MiB⌋ yields; a hooked re-walk never yields; the rejected-hook fd check; rotation mid-walk; the UsageHistory/route leg). Measured by scripts/measure-usage-walk-yield.mjs (200 MB §1c ledger in a scratch HOME): max loop gap 359.6 → 7.9 ms, wall 358 → 352 ms.**

**ORIGIN — WHICH KIND OF TRANSCRIPT PAID FOR THIS (2026-09-10).** The walk mines three kinds of file and until now the event could not say which: a top-level transcript (`'main'`), a subagent transcript (`<sid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, `'subagent'`) and a workflow agent's (`<sid>/subagents/workflows/<wf>/agent-*.jsonl`, `'workflow'`). All three attribute to the PARENT session id — that part is 2.265.0 and unchanged — so the Usage window could not separate what a conversation spent ITSELF from what its agents spent on its behalf (measured on this instance: **58.9 % of the last 7 days' cost is workflow-agent spend**, and one conversation is 72 % agents). Three rules:

- **`origin` is stamped on EVERY event**, never "missing means main". The backfill migration has to be able to answer `'unknown'` about a row whose transcript is gone, and an absent field cannot say that. `wf` = the workflow run id (workflow only), `agent` = the agent file stem (subagent + workflow).
- **an agent event's `cwd` is the PARENT PROJECT's**, and the transcript's own directory rides along as **`wcwd` only when it DIFFERS** (an equal copy on every row is bytes carrying no information). Without this, an agent that ran in a git worktree was its own row in "By project" — 272 of this instance's 3,155 agent transcripts carry a worktree path, and 31,200 of the last 7 days' 67,877 rows now carry a `wcwd`.
- **a codex rollout is always `'main'`, by RULE not by inspection**: the codex store merges a sub-agent's rollout into the parent thread's read (src/codex-session-store.js tags each record with its own file), so there is no second kind of file to separate. Saying so in both spellings costs nothing and keeps the field total.

**THE PROJECT-cwd LADDER (`makeProjectCwdReader`, exported — the backfill migration requires it rather than keeping a third copy).** A conversation's cwd is NOT constant: measured here, 3 of 782 top-level transcripts state more than one, and one of them is the biggest spender on the instance — a directory rename left its FIRST record saying `…/claude-code-webui` while its latest records and its project directory both say `…/vibespace`. Reading "the first cwd" therefore filed **$7,828 of one conversation's agent spend under a path that no longer exists, in a second "By project" row beside that same conversation's own main spend** — the exact split this work exists to remove. The project DIRECTORY NAME is the forward ENCODING of the cwd (`cwd.replace(/[/._]/g,'-')`, deterministic that way only — the reverse is ambiguous, kb-design-lessons §5), so a candidate can be VERIFIED instead of guessed. The ladder: a candidate from the parent transcript's head window that ENCODES to the directory name → the same test over its TAIL window → **the conversation's most recent cwd** → the head's first value → a sibling top-level transcript (every transcript in a project dir shares one project by construction, so a rotated-away parent is still answerable). Every read is a bounded 128 KiB window, memoized per (file, end); the tail window is only opened when the head cannot answer, so the ordinary single-cwd conversation costs one head read per project directory.

test-usage-walk-parity + test-codex-history assert the equality on the same rollout, and test-codex-history's corpus smoke asserts minted-key-set equality against this walker over ≤30 real local rollouts (skips with a reason on CI).

Not a profile (`desktop_app_not_a_profile`); no switch into it; a page verb on its handle answers `no_cdp_on_this_backend`; the record carries `origin: 'agent-browser'` + `by: {sessionId}` (stamped in src/desktop-serve.js only from the engine's opts), the lease the same origin with `pin` / `mode` reserved null for E2b / E2c. ### src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js — WHERE THE AGENT'S DESKTOP BROWSER OPENS (lane e2a, D3)
PURE `agentBrowserPlacement({msg, chats, phone, visible})` over the `desktop-app-opened {sessionId, appId, origin}` broadcast: a client SHOWING that session's chat window (not minimized, not on another desktop, the page visible) ⇒ `beside` (app.js opens it through `linkPlacement(chatWin)` — lane F's split door), a phone ⇒ `own`, everything else ⇒ `none` (the launcher's running list and the chat's window chip still show it). Gate: scripts/test-desktop-app-rung.mjs ⑤ + CONTROL (c).

## src/server/cli-cmd.js (B-a18e — the agent-CLI command paths and their spawn-time re-resolve)

- **What it owns.** `resolveCmd(name)` (BOOT ONLY, sync: `/usr/bin/which`, then `/opt/homebrew/bin` · `/usr/local/bin` · `/usr/bin` · `/bin` · `$PATH`, else the bare name) — server.js imports it for dtach/env and hands it to cli-env; `resolveCmdAsync` = the same lookup, async (the spawn-time spelling, never blocks the loop); `createCliCmds({resolve, usable, log})` = the registry cli-env fills right after the adapter registry: `register(backend, {name, current, apply})` for claude, codex and every ACP harness (`name` = the raw command incl. the `<ID>_CMD` override, `current` = the boot answer, `apply` = write the new path into the adapter's config — `claudeCmd` / `codexCmd` + codex-thread-read / `command` + `ACP_COMMANDS`).
- **`forSpawn(backend, cmd)`** is called ONCE, in src/ws-create.js immediately before `const r6Argv = [` (the argv the local pty terminal, the chat wrapper and the daemon pipe all run), local sessions only. Present + executable ⇒ returned as-is (one `access`); gone ⇒ ONE re-resolve, adopted + applied + ONE journal line `[cli-cmd] <backend>: '<old>' is not executable at spawn time — re-resolved '<name>' to '<new>' (no restart needed)`; nothing found ⇒ returned unchanged + a "found nothing — spawning it as before" line (the existing failure path stands). A `cmd` that is not the registered current value (spec override, ssh, node, a shell, an unregistered backend) is never touched. **SINGLE-FLIGHT (batch r1):** the re-resolve + adopt + journal line is ONE shared promise per backend (`e.pending`), so creates that land in the stale window together cost one lookup, one `apply`, one line and all spawn the fresh path; it is released the moment it settles (`finally`), so a binary that stays missing is asked about again by the next create — "missing" is never cached. A caller that entered with the stale path while the shared resolve was in flight gets its answer; one that STARTS after the adoption with the old path is passed through (it is no longer the registered command).
- **Why a pre-spawn check and not an ENOENT retry:** the CLI is exec'd by `env` inside the wrapper inside dtach; its ENOENT never reaches this process. The check before the spawn is the retry.
- **Not wired (captured at construction, out of B-a18e's scope):** usage-routes' `/usage` probe, account-usage-routes (login), backend-status-route and permission-rules still read the boot value.
- **Gate:** scripts/test-cli-cmd-refresh.mjs (fast; ① incl. the single-flight legs: three concurrent stale creates ⇒ resolves=1 applies=1 lines=1, still-missing ⇒ one shared found-nothing line and the NEXT create asks again). test-architecture's sweep allowlist no longer carries server.js's `which` row (the lookup left server.js).

## src/server/wrapper-files.js (2.339.2 resolver + 2.364.1 capability reader)

Two files belong to a local chat session and they have DIFFERENT writers: `data/session-meta/<sock>.json` is the SERVER's record (webuiSessionId, claudeSessionId, account, task…; written by writeSessionMeta) and `data/session-buffers/<id>.json` is the wrapper's SIDECAR (pid, startedAt, mode, streaming, tasks, todos, goal, `caps` — written by data/bin/chat-wrapper.js itself). `resolveWrapperFiles(BUFFERS_DIR, id, sockPath)` (2.339.2) finds the sidecar even for counter-collision sessions whose wrapper argv carries a different id (reads the dtach master's argv from /proc). `wrapperCaps(BUFFERS_DIR, id, sockPath)` (2.364.1) is the ONE reader of the wrapper's advertised capabilities: `{frameFile, peerMessage, inputQueue, caps, reason:'ok'|'no-caps'|'no-sidecar', startedAt, pid}`, stateless (`inputQueue` since 2026-09-06: the wrapper publishes `queue_changed` and serves the `queue-op` verb — the ws `queue-op` case and the client's `queueSupported` both hang off it, because backend-caps only says what a KIND of agent can do). The 2.361.1 gate read caps from the session-meta file instead — which never has them — so every wrapper tested old and the frame-file bypass was dead for two releases (kb-bugfix-invariants: CAPABILITY GATE READ THE WRONG FILE). Rules: new wrapper capabilities are added to the `caps` object in chat-wrapper.js AND read through wrapperCaps only; callers cache only positive verdicts; test-chat-frame-guard §2 spawns the real wrapper and asserts wrapperCaps sees its sidecar (parity). **Both wrappers speak the same contract (design-harness-plugins §1 P1)**: data/bin/codex-chat-wrapper.js writes `caps: { peerMessage, frameFile }` into the same sidecar shape and resolves `_frame_file` pointers on its stdin path (read → unlink always → must be ONE JSON object, nested pointers refused → dispatched through `handleInput` exactly as a stdin line; every failure logs AND emits a `task_failed` event, as does an unparseable raw stdin line — the old `if (!msg) continue;` was a silent message loss; and it acks every received stdin line with `_stdin_ack` on stdout like chat-wrapper, so ws-handler's 5s broken-pty re-send never replays a pointer whose file is already consumed). The chat-input bypass in ws-handler is therefore TRANSPORT + CAPABILITY only (`>64KB && !host && socketPath` → wrapperCaps decides pointer / raw ≤1MB / evidenced refusal) — it must never regain a backend-id branch; resolveWrapperFiles' /proc fallback already matches `codex-chat-wrapper.js` (substring of the argv marker). test-chat-frame-guard §2b drives the REAL codex wrapper against a stub app-server (pointer → intact turn/start input; shredded/missing/nested files + unparseable lines → loud) and §4 pins the gate shape. **`queueVerbs` (2026-09-07):** the reader also returns WHICH queue verbs the running wrapper serves — `caps.queueVerbs` when it names them, and `LEGACY_QUEUE_VERBS` (`remove/steer/steer-all`) when it adverts `inputQueue` with no list, i.e. a 2.369.55-or-older build. Both halves are load-bearing in the same skew rule: an old process must never be ASKED for a verb it would silently drop, and must never LOSE the verbs it does serve. The ws `queue-op` case gates each op on this list (falling back, for a remote wrapper whose sidecar is on the other machine, to the normalizer's in-band `queueVerbsPublished()`), and the attach payload ships it to the client so a rendered control is always one this process will honour.

**`notificationSteer` + `notificationSteerOf` (B-d963, 2.369.164 batch 7).** `wrapperCaps()` also answers whether THIS process folds a `kind:'notification'` peer frame into a running turn: true only when its sidecar names an EXPLICIT `queueVerbs` list containing `steer` (the verb table and the notification steer shipped together in 2.369.63). The legacy three a verb-less advert maps to are this module's DEFAULT for such a process, not something it said — so `queueVerbs` still reads `[remove, steer, steer-all]` for it while `notificationSteer` is false; a missing sidecar is false too (never guessed yes). `notificationSteerOf(wc, {inBand, published})` is the attach payload's three-valued twin (true / false / null = unknown): the local sidecar first, then a REMOTE wrapper's in-band publication (a named list decides; a publication with no list = a pre-verb-table build = false), else null. Readers: the delivery ladder's rpc rung (the typed `wrapper-no-steer` miss) and ws-handler's `queueAdvert` (`queueNotifSteer`).

## src/server/auto-resume.js (2.368.0 — continue after a usage limit resets) 2.369.32: the continue prompt carries originKind 'auto-resume' (server.js sendToSession tags the user record: claude `originKind`, codex `payload.webui_origin`) → both normalizers set msg.originKind='auto-resume' → chat-renderers shows a labelled VibeSpace card, never an anonymous user bubble. The four "who said continue" lanes: auto-resume continue (server, user-role, labelled) / Stop-hook block reason (the CLI renders it as a user turn: "Stop hook feedback: …") / UserPromptSubmit additionalContext (<system-reminder>, VibeSpace's prompt-context) / "The user hasn't heard from you in a while" (Claude Code's own idle nudge — not VibeSpace).

**2.369.157 THE ARM CARD CARRIES THE RESET-CREDIT OFFER (design-reset-credits §5).** New dep `resetCreditOffer(id, session)` (server.js → the engine's `resetCreditOffer`); the delayed ARM notice calls `notify(id, s2, armNoticeFor(…), offer ? {resetCredit: offer} : undefined)` and server.js's notify spreads `extra.resetCredit` into the peer card (both normalizers sanitize it through `offerOf`). Absent dep = no offer, the sentence unchanged. Gate: test-codex-pool R7 (real auto-resume, with the no-dep control) + test-auto-resume-loop's notice-site pin.

The CLI ships this feature but only in the interactive REPL: `/rate-limit-options` is **not** in a stream-json session's `slash_commands` (verified against a real init record) and the timer is a TUI `useInterval`, so a VibeSpace chat session hits the limit and stops dead. This module is ours, with the same shape and one deliberate difference: **the wait is persisted and survives a restart** — the CLI's own says "Automatic continue cancelled · Claude Code relaunched during the wait", and a multi-hour wait that a deploy cancels silently is worse than no feature.

**Order of preference (do not invert):** exhaustion first tries `maybePoolAutoSwitch` (another account = seconds, not hours); only then does `armIfEnabled` run. The module disarms itself on any proof of recovery — a fresh non-rejected `rate_limit_event`, the user's own prompt (ws chat-input), a dead session — because firing on a recovered session is a billed turn for nothing. **Gate is tri-state**: `session._autoResume` (spawn value or the live ws toggle) wins over the `claude.autoResumeOnLimit` default, so a per-session OFF survives the default being ON; default is OFF because firing spends quota unattended. Fires at `resetsAt + 15s`, never early, never twice, never while `_isStreaming`, refuses waits >26h out or with no reset time, retries on delivery failure, and announces both arming and firing in the conversation. The continue wording is the CLI's own, verbatim. Gated by scripts/test-auto-resume.mjs (48). **2.368.27 nearest-reset arming (c1206711 incident 2026-08-26)**: the rejection may carry a FAR bucket's resetsAt (seven-day ~100h, org overage off) while a nearer reset that will actually free the account (five-hour, rolling-window recovery) sits in the usage cache — the old flow refused the far wait journal-only and left NOTHING watching. Now `pickArmReset` (PURE, exported) picks the nearest in-range future reset from event + cache buckets (fiveHour/sevenDay/opus/scoped); the engine's `armBestReset` is the ONLY way exhaustion arms (all three sites: claude dead-branch + both codex — wiring pinned, 2.355.0 lesson); a still-dead account simply re-runs the ladder on its next rejection (self-limiting at bucket cadence). A too-far refusal now NOTIFIES the session (1/h floor) — a refusal the user can't see is the incident. Suite now 71. **2.368.28 (the owner's correction — the real c1206711 story)**: the pool had hot-moved the session onto a member whose 7d then died; the 5h-exhausted sibling (7d fine) was the way back, and the pool even switched back on its own — but a hot re-point never moves an idle blocked session. ① armBestReset merges POOL SIBLING members' bucket resets (poolReadCache × poolMembers — the freeing reset lives in the sibling's cache); ② HOT switches (per-session + pool-level) `fireNow()` ARMED sessions — continue delivered the moment a healthy account lands, armed-only, cold keeps client restarts; ③ the timed fire runs `beforeFire` (maybePoolAutoSwitch) before spending. Suite 79. **2.368.32 (owner caught the premature fire — "7d重置没和5h对齐"): the wait target is the MAX over the identity's DEAD buckets** (a session unblocks only when ALL dead buckets reset; a healthy bucket's nearer reset is no candidate), min across identities (self + pool siblings) unchanged; dead = utilization≥0.999 / status limited|rejected / usedPercent≥99.5 with a future resetsAt. The limit-banner path now (re-)arms too — it used to mark the cache dead and leave nothing waiting. Suite 81. **2.368.33 false-arm suppression (owner: '没被打断任何对话'): a dead event races the hot switch that just fixed it — armBestReset skips when the CURRENT pool member has no dead bucket (shared isDeadBucket; unknown never guessed), and ANY main-thread assistant record disarms (`noteSessionProduced`, engine→session-stdout) — the readings-based disarm misses accounts that emit no events. Suite 86.** **2.368.34 — that pre-check ATE A REAL WALL (9h dark) and is REMOVED: a live CLI holds its OLD token, the org-verified banner marks the OLD member dead while the link points at a healthy one — the link is never the org a running CLI is on. Replacements that cannot eat a wall: arm unconditionally; announcement DELAYED 90s (disarm inside the window ⇒ silent); noteWorked age-gates the produced-work disarm to >30s post-arm (the banner's own trailing records land within seconds). parseBannerResetMs: the banner's "resets 12:40pm (TZ)" is timezone-parsed into the precise arm target (was a now+5h guess). Suite 91.**

**2.369.0 — THE WALL MACHINE (owner-designed, docs/design-wall-machine.md; supersedes every arm/disarm mechanism above where they conflict).** auto-resume.js is now the EXECUTOR only (persisted armed waits, tick fire, delayed announcement, veto-capable beforeFire); detection + recovery live in the engine's turn-granular machine: wall signals (rejected events / banner as a BOOLEAN — text is never a data source; parseBannerResetMs deleted) accumulate on the current turn via `noteWallSignal`, the `result` record (codex: task_complete/task_failed) classifies via `noteTurnEnd` — walled (signals with ≤1 assistant record after the last one) → BLOCKED entry: pool eval, then `quotaVerdictFor` (the account system's ONE usability answer — account-pool-auto.quotaVerdict pure: 5h<10%/weekly<5% THRESH hot tier, blockedUntil=max over dead buckets, pool=any-usable/min-over-members, model-projected + estimator-overlaid) → usable ⇒ arm now+45s (announce delay 90s keeps a quick success silent), blocked ⇒ arm blockedUntil, unknown ⇒ PROBE auto-cli /usage 0→30m→1h→2h then loud give-up. **2.369.6: blocked-with-target ALSO fires one throttled verification probe (10min/scope, _wallVerifyAt) — a confidently-lying cache armed a 2.6-day wait on an alive account (inc-mtdsoj5f); confident ≠ correct, every BLOCKED entry verifies.** A normally-completed turn unconditionally disarms (sufficient proof — kills noteWorked/30s-age; the pool-rescued mid-turn case classifies NORMAL by construction). Pre-fire: probe + re-verdict, false VETOES the spend and re-arms. Blocking identity = orgVerifiedKey (OTel-observed org over the link — the .33/.34 root cause). Session fields _turnWallSigs/_turnWorkAfterSig/_wallProbeTimer/_arFiring registered. Gate: test-auto-resume §8-10 (80). **B-2c9b (2026-09-05): BLOCKED entry is now demote → session-aware verdict → arm → pool eval (`finally`)** — the walled branch of `noteTurnEnd` no longer runs `maybePoolAutoSwitch` BEFORE `onWalledTurn`, so the wall's account is demoted (ground truth) before the verdict reads the cache and the hot switch's `fireNow()` finds the session ARMED and continues it in the same tick; `quotaVerdictFor` takes `{model, session}` and judges the member the session is OBSERVED on first. Full essay under account-pool-auto.js ("WALL = GROUND TRUTH"); gate test-auto-resume §11.

**THE LOOP BREAKER (2026-09-07, owner decision ut-1c6c15a2db ①④ — the 130-fire incident; full essay in kb-bugfix-invariants).** A fire the session answers with ANOTHER limit rejection is a FAILED fire, and until this release nothing remembered it: the walled-turn path re-armed "switched to a usable account", the hot pool switch called `fireNow()`, the CLI rejected again half a second later, and the cycle repeated 130× on one conversation (32× on a second) between 23:32 and 04:03 — ~150 junk cards in one transcript, every cycle indistinguishable from the first to every component. Now: ① ONE fire path (`attemptFire`) serves the timed tick AND `fireNow`, so the immediate path can no longer skip `beforeFire` (it used to — the incident's 130 continues all came down it, each bypassing the gate that would have re-verdicted the target; the in-flight flag `_arFiring` is raised BEFORE the gate runs, because the real gate calls `maybePoolAutoSwitch` → `fireNow` and everything before its first `await` is synchronous re-entry — measured 1992 levels deep with the flag one line late); ② a per-session breaker record `{n, windowStart, fails:[{key,at}], last, lastFireAt, notified, noticeAt, refuse}` PERSISTED under `fires` in data/auto-resume.json (a deploy must not hand the loop a fresh budget — the same reasoning as the armed wait itself); ③ rules, every refusal NAMED: `fire-pending` (never two continues in flight, 10min staleness), `same-identity` (an identity that just rejected us is quarantined 10min), `backoff` (immediate fires 0/60s/5min), `hourly-cap` (3 immediate fires per session per hour, after which only the TIMED reset path — the one anchored to a real reset — may fire); ④ the identity a fire is keyed on comes from the ENGINE (`fireIdentity` dep → `fireIdentityFor` = `wallKeyFor`), deliberately the same fact the wall machine demotes, or the breaker would quarantine an account nothing ever rejects; ⑤ `noteFireOutcome(id, ok)` — the engine's walled turn reports `false` FIRST in `onWalledTurn` (before anything re-arms or re-switches; that ordering IS the off-switch), any proof of work reports `true` through `noteRecovered`, which now clears the breaker BEFORE its armed-record early-return (after a fire there is no armed record left, so anything gated behind it would never see the proof) — **and ONLY for a caller whose evidence is WORK (round 4): `noteRecovered(id, why, {worked = true})` runs `noteFireOutcome(id,true)` only when `worked`, because round 1 handed the entire record (quarantine + hourly counter + both notice budgets + the persisted copy) to its loudest caller, the PASSIVE non-rejected `rate_limit_event` this instance sees ~20× per rejection, so neither budget was ever enforced in production; the DISARM stays unconditional for every caller. Exactly two callers claim work — a completed turn and the user's own prompt — the other four (claude reading, codex reading, codex reset credit, `disabled`) pass `{worked:false}`; the table lives in kb-bugfix-invariants and is DERIVED + enforced by test-auto-resume-loop §5, so an unclassified new caller fails the suite instead of re-opening the loop**; ⑥ the in-chat "账号池已切换到 X，已自动继续" line goes out at most ONCE per distinct target per session per hour, a repeat is journal-only, and when the breaker trips the session gets ONE honest line naming the account and either the reset time or "no member can serve — add a member / move this session" (immediate path only: a refused TIMED fire self-heals inside 10min, so saying so would be noise). `recentFireFailures(id)` is read back by the engine so a restart-surviving failure still steers the next target choice.

**Round 2 (same day, adversarial verifier — four reproduced defects; full essay in kb-bugfix-invariants).** ⑦ **What the conversation is told is now a PURE function of the refusal reason** (`refusalNoticeFor`, exported): round 1 computed the named check and then told the SAME exhaustion story for all four reasons, so a `fire-pending`/`backoff` refusal named an account that had rejected nothing, claimed the pool was empty, and said retrying had stopped while the session was still armed and continuing seconds later — and it spent the once-per-window budget, silencing the genuine line. Now `same-identity` may say "it refused us too"; the "nowhere else to go" clause requires the POOL's own verdict (`noteNoPoolTarget`, called from the `all-rejected`/`no-members`/`stuck` branch of the per-session pass — the breaker cannot know it); `hourly-cap` states its count and pause; `backoff`/`fire-pending` are JOURNAL-ONLY and spend nothing (a pacer on an intact promise). Budgets are per notice CLASS (`r.notices`), so the cap line can never eat the exhaustion line's. ⑧ **The identity is re-resolved INSIDE `deliver()`, after the gate**, and re-admitted through `canFire` (abort, never spend, if the gate moved us onto an identity we already burned): `beforeAutoResumeFire` runs `maybePoolAutoSwitch`, which re-points the link, so round 1 keyed `noteFired`/`announce`/the journal to the account we had just LEFT — quarantining the wrong one and leaving the real rejector fireable. ⑨ **The continue card names what actually unblocked us** (`continueNoticeFor`, exported): `kind === 'now'`, a near-arm reason, or the identity having MOVED during the gate ⇒ "账号池已切换到 X"; only otherwise "用量上限已重置". This matters because the near-arm is delivered by the TIMED path — the real producers re-point the link BEFORE the session is armed, so `fireNow` is not reached at all (measured: injected signal ⇒ 1 immediate continue, real `recordRateLimitEvent`/`markLimitBanner` ⇒ 0; recovery is 45 s arm + 15 s grace on a 30 s tick ≈ 60–90 s). The switch-class card keeps the once-per-target-per-window dedup on BOTH paths; the reset-class card is never deduped. `_poolAutoLast`/`_poolSwitchAt` are exported from the engine so a suite can wind the wall-clock gates back instead of sleeping. Gate: scripts/test-auto-resume-loop.mjs (122 — the matrix negative control: each pre-fix behaviour re-created through a public seam, both off ⇒ ≥10 unbounded fires, either on ⇒ it stops; plus per-fix mutation controls and the real-producer ordering legs).

**GENERIC OVER EVERY HARNESS (2026-09-08, owner ruling: "auto resume 应该是通用的, 只要支持 hook/注入的 harness 都支持, 形式可以不一样 — 有些是发消息, 有些是 start turn 之类的固有指令"; the incident essay is in kb-bugfix-invariants).** Everything above stays and stays harness-neutral; exactly TWO facts move onto the DESCRIPTOR and `capsOf(backend).autoResume` is **derived** from them (`deriveAutoResume` in the PURE src/backend-caps.js, written by `src/harnesses/index.js` at registration — never hand-set on a caps literal, which carries only the honest `NO_AUTO_RESUME` placeholder so an unregistered id still answers):

- **the LIMIT SIGNAL** = `descriptor.quota.signalFromStream`, which already existed. `signal` is true when that source is not the shared frozen `NULL_QUOTA` — asked by identity rather than by a boolean a descriptor could set, because this one gates unattended spending.
- **the RESUME VERB** = `descriptor.resume {form, deliver(session, text, deps)}`, from a CLOSED set of forms: `'message'` (claude — a user message on the CLI's chat stdin), `'turn-start'` (codex — the wrapper owns the app-server RPC connection, so an idle thread gets `turn/start`; the SAME lane the delivery ladder's `rpc-queue` rung uses, deliberately, rather than a second injector), `'prompt'` (ACP — the shared acp-wrapper's `session/prompt`), `null` (shell: there is no agent). An undeclared form THROWS at registration. The descriptors stay SHARED: they name the verb, the ORCHESTRATOR owns the socket and hands it over as `deps.sendChatInput`, so the daemon can still bundle them.

`supported = signal && resume !== null` is what a SURFACE may offer; `armIfEnabled` refuses to arm a harness with no verb (a promise nobody can keep is not made) and `deliver()` runs the descriptor's own function — one fire choke point for every harness and every path — and the P4 SPEND AUTHORIZER now sits ON it (design-account-hardening §4.4(c), integrated 2026-09-09): `deliver()` runs breaker → pre-fire gate (async, a veto HELD per wall) → `spendOk(…, {hold:true})` on the identity the gate landed on → the descriptor's verb → `noteFired` + `edgeSpent` + `noteSpend(hold)` + the one journal line, with `giveBack()` releasing the reservation on EVERY exit below the hold that does not deliver (the harness declares no verb; the verb throws or refuses) because the arm survives all of them. The pre-gate `spendOk(…, {hold:false})` PROBE is the same question asked before the gate — it must not reserve, or the charging call refuses its own request. Making the verb generic did not create a second unattended-turn path, which is why one gate still covers every harness. The client mirror is `BACKEND_META.caps.autoResume` + `autoResumeCapsFor()` in agent-meta.js, deep-compared by test-harness-contract (it left the `CLIENT_ONLY_OK` grandfather list in the same change — the law working: a client-only flag is allowed only while nothing on the server answers for it).

**THE FRESH-WINDOW EDGE** (PURE `src/auto-resume-signal.js`). A quota READING used to DISARM a waiting session. For claude that was merely useless — its readings only arrive while a turn is running, and that turn's own `result` disarms anyway — but codex's app-server pushes `rate_limits_updated` to an **idle** thread, so the same line silently broke a promise the user had switched on. A reading is now JUDGED, and `open` needs THREE facts, each of which was a real way to be wrong: the **LANE** matches (`snapshot.limitId`; a codex login reports `codex` and `codex_bengalfox` minute by minute on one account, and the spark lane read 0 % through the whole stall — "no dead bucket ⇒ fire" would have spent a turn on the very next one), the reading **STATES THE BUCKET** the wait is about and reports it not spent (a `rate_limit_event` names exactly ONE bucket, so a healthy 7d reading says nothing about a 5h wall), and **no other stated bucket of that lane is spent** (the c1206711 rule). An arm that does not know its own wall (the pool's +45 s near-arm) is never opened this way and waits out its own timer. A re-arm INHERITS the lane/bucket unless the caller states otherwise — the wall-probe ladder and the pre-fire gate re-arm from a re-verdict with no signals in hand, and before that they silently replaced a wall-aware wait with a lane-blind one that no reading could ever open again.

**A FAR RESET IS A WATCH, NOT A REFUSAL.** `armIfEnabled` still schedules no timed continue beyond `MAX_WAIT_MS` ("refuse to sit forever", intact and free), but the session is now WATCHED: `due()` skips it, the fresh-window edge can still keep the promise, and the watch retires itself once that far reset passes. This is the half the 2026-09-08 incident needed — its reset was six days out and the window reopened after 32 h. `statusFor` therefore carries `resume` / `watch` / `lane` / `bucket` so the chip prints no clock it cannot keep.

**THE EDGE IS SINGLE-SHOT PER WALL (r2, 2026-09-08 — the round-1 verifier's finding, reproduced against the real modules before it was fixed).** The fresh-window edge as shipped in round 1 put NO per-arm limit on itself: every reading whose armed bucket read healthy re-entered `fireNow`, and the only ceilings left were the loop breaker's — `FIRE_MAX_IMMEDIATE` per ROLLING hour and a TEN-MINUTE quarantine. A WATCH stands until its far reset passes, so the shape is not a burst but a standing burn: driven through this module's own seam with a clock we own (the incident's world — a watch six days out, the plan lane reading healthy every 30 s, the CLI answering every continue with another limit rejection), round 1 spends **[3,3,3,3] = 12 billed continues over four simulated hours, ~72/day, ~430 over the incident's own window**; the rule below spends **1**. The engine's own comment had already CLAIMED this bound ("a healthy `codex` reading fires once, the CLI rejects, and the loop breaker quarantines the identity") — false in both halves, and now corrected in place, because a comment that credits a mechanism nobody measured is how the loop shipped green.

The premise is reachable on this instance today and is invisible to `windowOpened`: the exhaustion record carries `rateLimits: null`, so the engine SYNTHESISES `limitId:'codex'` while the true wall may be the model lane (`codex_bengalfox`, measured interleaving on one account minute by minute) — the plan lane's very next push then reads healthy about a wall it does not describe.

- **The shot is spent AT THE DELIVERY** (`edgeSpent` on the breaker record, set in `noteFired` when the fire's `origin.via === 'reading'`), not when the CLI's rejection is reported. Stamping it on the rejection — the first draft, and the reviewer's own wording — is indistinguishable while every caller reports the outcome, and is round 1's loop again the moment one does not: measured through the public seam (arm → reading → fire → NO outcome reported → re-arm) it gives [3,3,3,3] against 1. Today's engine DOES report it (`onWalledTurn` calls `noteFireOutcome(id,false)` first, and it is the only arm site that carries a wall), so this changes no production count as wired — it is here so the bound is a property of THIS module rather than an emergent property of five call sites plus a classifier, and this feature's own incident is a classifier that matched nothing for eight months.
- **Only PROOF OF WORK re-opens it.** `noteFireOutcome(id,true)` drops the whole breaker record; a turn that produced something is the only evidence our continue mattered. The prune keeps an `edgeSpent` record alive while the wait is armed (it is not a budget that rolls over with the hour — the wait can stand for days) and drops it with the wait.
- **The key is the WALL** (`lane|bucket|scopedName`), deliberately NOT its reset instant, and both reasons were checked: (i) a reset instant is not a stable NAME for a window — on this instance's codex anchor stream (1799 readings / 30 days) the sevenDay reset carries 316 distinct values and changes between consecutive readings 414 times, and even one wall is spelled two ways (the incident's own `1789356983` ×417 beside `1789356984` ×3), the same ±wobble that made reading-lag.js compare weekly PHASE; (ii) it would not cover this finding's own premise anyway — in the mis-attributed-lane case the sibling reading carries a different reset BY CONSTRUCTION, so "the reset rolled" is satisfied and the turn is spent regardless. A DIFFERENT wall is a different question and is armed fresh; the belt there is the hourly cap, and it is driven rather than asserted.
- **A refusal by this rung is NAMED** (`already-refuted`, with `wallOpen:true` so the caller cannot mistake it for "the wall is still up") and the engine prints it through the same per-verdict throttle the negative side already had.
- **The journal says what HAPPENED.** Round 1 logged "continuing now" once per READING, BEFORE attempting — measured 492 lines against 12 actual continues (41:1) — in the exact channel this incident was diagnosed from ("ZERO [auto-resume] lines for that session"). Round 2 moved it AFTER the attempt and read `attemptFire`'s return value, which r3 shows is not an outcome; see below.
- **A monthly SPEND CONTROL opens nothing** (`spendControlReached` in the PURE rule, checked BEFORE the lane because it is a fact about the ACCOUNT, not one of its windows): the codex twin of 2.361.2, where a healthy weekly bucket sits beside an account that refuses every turn and has no window to wait for. UNVERIFIED on the wire and it says so — zero `true` in this instance's stores — which is why it may ship unmeasured: the rung can only ever REFUSE. `credits.hasCredits === false` is the rung we did NOT write, and the measurement is the reason: `usage-cache/__global_codex__.json`, the incident's own login, carries `{"hasCredits":false,"unlimited":false,"balance":"0"}` while serving turns normally off plan quota, so reading it as spent would make this edge permanently inert here — the original incident, re-introduced as a guard.

**THE PRODUCTION GATE IS ASYNC, SO ITS RETURN VALUE IS NOT AN OUTCOME (r3, 2026-09-08 — the round-2 verifier's finding, reproduced against the real module before anything changed).** `attemptFire` hands the pre-fire gate a session and, when the gate is a Promise, `return true` immediately — *"a continue was delivered OR a gate is in flight"*. In production it is ALWAYS a Promise: server.js wires `beforeFire: (id, s) => beforeAutoResumeFire(id, s)` and that function is declared `async`. Round 2's edge wrote its journal line from that value, so a gate VETO produced a line claiming a billed continue that never happened. Measured through this module's own seam with the production gate shape (`beforeFire: async () => false`, one armed watch, 100 healthy readings): **100 gate runs, 0 continues, 100 `— continued now` lines, 0 honest lines** — round 1's flood restored, in the one channel this incident was diagnosed from, and the honest else-branch at the caller was structurally unreachable for a gate veto. On the REAL engine leg the ratio was 2 claims : 1 delivery, i.e. one false line per delivery even on the happy path.

- **The line about a continue is written by the code that DELIVERS one.** Making the caller's else-branch reachable was not the fix — the caller *cannot* know, the outcome is decided one microtask later. The edge now hands its own head (`watched|armed window reopened (<why>)`) to `fireNow` as the fire's `why` and says nothing itself; `deliver()` prints it immediately after `noteFired` stamps the shot. One continue, one line, and they are the same event — 1:1 by construction, asserted on the real engine.
- **A veto must leave something behind.** `edgeSpent` is stamped only at the delivery (correctly — r2), so a veto stamped NOTHING: the single-shot guard stayed un-armed and every later push re-entered the gate, which runs a `probeQuotaForKey` (60 s floor) and an unthrottled `maybePoolAutoSwitch`. The veto branch that takes `scheduleWallProbe` changes no state, so the loop is STABLE for the days a watch can stand — **an unbounded side effect on a polled path**, the rule the new-member wake's r2 already wrote down. `noteGateRefusal` now records the veto AT THE POINT OF KNOWLEDGE (both gate branches — the sync one is unreachable in production, which is exactly why it has its own behavioural leg rather than only a source pin): one journal line per `REFUSE_LOG_MS` (the gate veto used to be the one refusal nothing said anything about — `logRefusal` covers the breaker's reasons, and this rung is not the breaker), and `edgeHeld = {wall, until: now + EDGE_HOLD_MS}`.
- **HELD, never SPENT.** The gate's answer is about NOW, and this edge exists for a window that opens EARLY; burning the wall on a veto would turn one transient disagreement into a permanent refusal for a wait with nowhere else to go. The hold is bounded (10 min), per WALL (a different window is still a different question) and dropped whole by proof of work. Cost: a recovery that has already waited 32 h may be paced by ≤10 min. Benefit, measured on the incident's own traffic (454 `rate_limits_updated` pushes in under two hours ⇒ one per ~16 s): ~225 gate runs/hour becomes 6.
- **EVERY FIELD THAT CAN REFUSE OWES `save()`'s LIVENESS PREDICATE A CLAUSE.** That predicate prunes breaker records which "can no longer refuse anything", and `save()` runs on every arm, every fire and every refusal — so a field the READER consults but the PRUNER does not know about is deleted at the next `FIRE_WINDOW_MS` boundary. Found by this branch's own cadence assert, not by reading the code: 27 gate asks per four hours instead of 24, one extra at each hour boundary. `edgeSpent` (r2) is the same rule's first instance; `edgeHeld` is bounded twice there, by its own expiry and by the armed set.
- **`gate-held` is not "the wall is still up".** It carries `wallOpen:true` like `already-refuted`, and the engine's verdict line now has its own sentence for it — the window really does read open, the gate disagreed, and we are pacing the re-ask. The generic line would print a false fact into the diagnosis channel.

**r3 invariants** = **a value that means "delivered OR still in flight" may never be journalled as "delivered"** — and the fix is to move the claim to the code that knows, not to make the ignorant caller's else-branch reachable; **a guard that is only armed on the happy path leaves the unhappy path unbounded** (the veto is the case the guard exists for); **the authority we asked said "no", so ask it again on OUR clock, not on the producer's traffic**; **a refusal nothing else reports must still be reportable** (the gate veto had no voice at all); **held is not spent** — a bounded pause and a permanent refusal answer different questions; **a pruner that deletes "records that can no longer refuse" must be told about every field that can refuse**; and **a branch production never takes needs a behavioural leg, not a source pin** (the sync gate).

**r2 invariants** = a READING IS A CLAIM AND THE CLI'S ANSWER OUTRANKS IT (a producer that pushes every few seconds must not be able to re-buy the same verdict); **a money bound belongs to the module that spends, not to a caller's classification** (stamp at the spend, not at the report about it); **a comment that credits a mechanism is an assertion — measure it or delete it** (the quarantine is 10 minutes, and the hourly cap it really rested on resets every hour, forever); **an assert that counts VERDICTS does not bound SPEND** (round 1's leg asserted `opened >= 1` and `r.n > 0`, both true whether or not a turn was billed, which is why a sustained loop shipped green — and why the constant is now pinned to a literal a human agreed to as well as read back from the module); and **the suite that owns the breaker must DRIVE every new producer of billed turns**, not grep for it.

**Gates:** test-auto-resume (221 — the incident end to end through the REAL engine + a stub of the codex channel, the pre-fix classifier as the negative control, the PURE truth table, the who-is-offered legs, and §12(d)-(d⁵⁗) the edge's own ceilings: four simulated hours at one reading per 30 s spend ONE continue AND ask the gate once per EDGE_HOLD_MS, with six patched-copy controls — round 1's un-guarded edge [3,3,3,3], round 1's optimistic log 40:1, this fix's own r2 DRAFT which is identical until the caller stops reporting outcomes, round 2's journal read from the in-flight return value, round 2's un-held veto re-entering per reading, and round 2 AS SHIPPED (both halves = one false line per reading). The edge world now takes the gate's SHAPE as a parameter and drives the PRODUCTION one: every round-2 leg passed no `beforeFire` at all, which is why only the synchronous path was ever measured. Mutation-tested against the product source: reverting the journal move, either gate branch's veto record, the hold, or the pruner clause each turns it red), test-auto-resume-loop (203 — §4g drives the new producer through the REAL `recordRateLimitEvent`, the REAL engine and the REAL pool with a clock of its own, because the breaker's backoff is a wall-clock rule and 40 readings inside one real second are bounded by it whatever the edge does), test-harness-contract (306 — the conformance run: every row re-derived from its descriptor, every declared verb driven arm→fire into a stub of its own channel, every harness without one proven never-armed, and a source census that no auto-resume site branches on a backend id), test-quota-source (112 — incl. the ENUM-SHAPE legs: `codexErrorEnum` reads the wire's externally-tagged one-key object as well as a bare string, with the REAL `{responseStreamDisconnected:{httpStatusCode:null}}` record from the incident buffer as the negative control and the pre-fix `String(enum)` reader as the mutation), test-codex-p2-wrapper (382), test-new-member-wake (119, master's wake suite — its `attemptFire` wiring pin now names the ROUTE and lets the call's trailing arguments grow, since the reading edge added the fire's ORIGIN).

## src/auto-resume-signal.js (PURE, 2026-09-08 — does this reading say the wall is gone?)

`laneOf` / `sameLane` / `statedBuckets` / `bucketSpent` / `isArmedBucket` / `windowOpened`. PURE because BOTH producers ask it (the claude `rate_limit_event` path and the codex `rate_limits_updated` push) and because the answer AUTHORISES A BILLED TURN — a decision that must be unit-testable without a server. `bucketSpent` is deliberately NOT the pool's `THRESH.*.hard` candidate gate (3–5 % left): that gate picks between accounts, this one decides whether to hold a session hostage and later spend a turn on it, so it answers only to a FULL window (utilization ≥ 1 / the harness's own `'limited'` marker) with a reset still in the future. `windowOpened`'s `why` is part of the contract — it is what the journal prints, and "we cannot tell" (`other-lane` / `other-bucket` / `unknown-bucket` / `no-reading`) must never be spelled like "yes". **Not the weekly-phase fingerprint (src/reading-lag.js)**: that is an ACCOUNT identity rule, this is a LANE question, and codex's weekly window is not phase-stable — the incident's two windows are 152 320 s apart, so the phase rule would answer 'differ' about the very reading that proves recovery.

**Output style (same release, same suite).** The CLI's Concise/Explanatory/Learning/Proactive are a SETTINGS key with no flag, and stream-json never gets `/output-style` — so it is spawn-only: `buildSessionArgs({outputStyle})` merges it into the ONE `--settings` flag (alongside `ultracode`/`switchModelsOnFlag`; never a second flag), ws-create defaults it from `claude.outputStyle`, the status-bar chip persists it as per-session config, and every surface says "applies on the next resume" instead of pretending otherwise.

## src/server/instance-url.js (2.367.0 — this instance's own public address)

**One resolver.** "The URL a machine outside this box uses to reach this VibeSpace" is needed by reverse mounts (machine-mounts), remote agent installs (mounts-plugins-wiring), the agentd auto-graduation gate and published-page share links; all four read `agentd.publicUrl` inline before this. `url()` is the single reader and resolves **explicit frp mapping → `agentd.publicUrl` → `VIBESPACE_PUBLIC_URL` → null** (null = callers fall back to the asking browser's origin, 2.366.1). The mapping is a LAYER: publishing never writes the setting, so unmapping lands exactly back on it — the owner's requirement ("不要覆盖原来的设置, incase取消了映射直接回归原来的设置").

**One publisher.** `plugins.frpPublish('vibespace-instance', PORT, …)` predates this module but ran as an invisible side effect of installing a remote agent over the relay — two callers writing one relay proxy name, with nothing recording the URL. This module owns that proxy; the install path calls `ensurePublished()`. **Explicit vs auto is load-bearing**: a user pressing Map sets `desired` and outranks the setting; an install-driven publish is `auto` — recorded and shown in the Ports panel, but never repointing share links (a side effect must not move everyone's URLs). `publish()` is REFUSED while auth is off (an open instance on the internet is RCE as the owner). `restore()` re-asserts a desired mapping at boot without clearing the persisted URL (frpc is its own process and usually outlives a restart); a failed re-assert keeps the intent and surfaces the error. UI: `_renderInstanceUrlRow` in sidebar-rail.js (Ports panel), which also states what is kept underneath. Gated by scripts/test-instance-url.mjs (39). **2.369.129: the System monitor… / Ports… rows are CHILDREN of the ⚙ System head (parent:'system'), not top-level rows — .125 had put them beside the head and the menu read "System" twice.**

## data/bin/vibespace-page (2.366.0 — publish any self-contained HTML here; its design-canvas kit retired 2026-10-02)

**What.** STATIC, in AGENT_TOOLS (ships to remote hosts): `publish <file.html> --title "…" [--public]` uploads the file body to `POST /api/agent/pages/publish` (vsst_ or jbt_; raw ≤ 25 MB; `?title&path&public` — no host param, the session's host is authoritative; `public` only when asked, so a republish keeps the user's visibility) and prints the RELATIVE `/p/<id>` path with the "write it verbatim, never prefix a host" lines; `list` shows the pages of this session or conversation. Publishing attributes the page to the session; `onPublished` → `page-published` → the chip's list updates live. agent-tool-rules: `publish` is HELD + an ASK rule, `list` pre-approved (`PAGE_VERBS = ['list']`).

**Retired (lane design-docs, 2026-10-02): the Claude CLI's /design kit.** From 2.366.0 to 2.369.201 `vibespace-page kit` handed agents a kit extracted at runtime from the installed claude — its skill text, seeding helper and editor payload, cached per CLI version under `data/design-kit/<cliVersion>/` and rewritten so the publish step was `vibespace-page publish` (`src/server/design-kit.js`; `GET /api/design-kit/status` fed the chip's kit line; `GET /api/agent/design-kit` + `/file/:name` let a remote host mirror it into `~/.vibespace/design-kit/<ver>/`). It broke on CLI changes three times in six weeks (2.366.0; the 2.1.257 zstd frames; 2.1.287 removed the skill); .200 (and the .201 hotfix) shipped a stop-gap — the kit taken from an older installed CLI version or a stored copy (lane design-kit-287) — removed with the rest in .202, executed an extracted third-party helper server-side, and taught agents a vendor template grammar. VibeSpace's own Design window replaced it (docs/design-design-window.md — `vibespace-design`, src/server/design-engine.js, the Design window); migration `2026-10-design-kit-removed` deletes `data/design-kit/` (vendor text, deleted not archived); test-design-docs' census keeps the removed surfaces from coming back. The remote mirrors are inert files nothing reads (no device migration). The three canvases published through the kit stay hosted on `/p/<id>` and listed in the chip; they do not open in the Design window (a legacy reader is P2 on demand).

## src/server/published-pages.js (2.364.0 — Published pages, "接管artifact"; 2.366.0 content publish)

Instance-hosted shareable HTML. Owner incident: the /design canvas skill publishes to claude.ai artifacts, which could not be shared outward; the canvas is a self-contained local HTML file, so the instance hosts it itself.
