**2.369.169 ORIGIN (B-328d, docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §8).** Every item carries `origin` = WHO filed it, a CLOSED set in PURE `src/inbox-origin.js` (`spend` · `login` · `pool` · `jobs` · `channels` · `browser` · `agent`). `add({…, origin})` validates through `normalizeOrigin`: **none ⇒ THROWS `origin required (one of …)` and files nothing (r2, fail closed — r1 stamped a default `agent`, so a producer the census could not see, an aliased store or a `?.add`, filed under Agents silently: the buried-notice class this field exists to end)**; a member ⇒ itself; anything else THROWS by name (`origin must be one of …`) and files nothing (a typo in a producer must fail its filing loudly, never land in a group nobody reads). Every caller declares — the agent route `agent`, each server producer its own, every suite fixture explicitly. A re-file KEEPS a declared origin (the producer of an item does not change); an item stored before the field existed takes the re-filer's declaration. `snapshot()` / the broadcast carry it as stored. NO MIGRATION: items already on disk keep no field and are classified at READ time by the client's ONE legacy rung (`originOf`, user-todos-layout.js). Every server producer declares its origin at its call — test-user-todos-layout ⑪ is the grep-derived census (12 sites when it shipped: spend-guard spend, login-expiry-watch login, usage-pool-engine pool, jobs-wiring jobs, channels-engine ×5 channels, browser-handback + mounts-plugins-wiring's browser switch proposal browser, agent-routes agent). r2 widened its match from `\w*[Tt]odos\.add(` to EVERY two-argument `.add(` / `?.add(` on any receiver (the store's `add(sessionKey, options)` shape; a DOM `classList.add(a, b)` and comment lines excluded) — the verifier's aliased-store and optional-chaining evasions, each ALL PASS under r1, are now negative controls that go red by name. **`stop()` (r2) is the manager's last act:** it clears the expiry timer AND flushes a pending debounced write (the 500 ms write timer used to outlive `stop()` and fire into a data dir its owner had already removed — ENOENT from a timer nobody could catch).

### src/inbox-reply.js — PURE the For-you reply: quote block, parser, availability verdict (2.369.169)

### src/dispatch-model.js — PURE: dispatch a brief to a WORKER conversation, compacting it first (lane worker-dispatch, 2026-10-02)
The owner (2026-10-02): worker CONVERSATIONS on the pool beat Claude Code subagents (hot switch + auto-resume survive a session wall), "不过你得及时让他们compact，不然容易积累太多历史context浪费token" — and an agent cannot run another session's `/compact`. Imports nothing; CJS. `dispatchVerdict({callerKind, senderReach, targetKind, targetState, compactFirst, compactObserved, pacer, spend})` → `{ok, steps, compact:'first'|'skipped', code?, skip?, why}`: refusals first, in order — a non-session caller `job-token` (a jbt_ job never dispatches), reach ≠ `messageable` or a gone target `unreachable` (uniform, no oracle), a TERMINAL target asked to compact `not-chat` (by name; without the compaction it is a plain wake). Then a refused PACE or SPEND ⇒ `['stash']` (no compaction, no wake — the brief rides the worker's next turn, free; the reason named). Then `['wake']` with a named `skip` (`not-asked` / `harness` — caps `compactEnd` not 'observed' / `mid-turn` / `compacting` / `unknown-state` — never compacted on a guess). Only a session caller → a messageable, IDLE chat target whose harness says when a compaction ends, pace + spend granted ⇒ `['compact','wait','wake']`. `COMPACT_WAIT_MS` = 180 s (a large conversation compacts in 1–2 min — the 2.365.0 measurement). `dispatchRecord(…)` = what the sender is told: `{target, compacted: true | false | 'skipped', why, wake: {billed, identity, delivered: 'woken'|'next-turn', reason?}}` — `true` only on the CLI's own `compact_result:"success"` (ended ≠ succeeded, §2.11 round 5); a failed (the CLI's words), outcome-less, never-started or past-the-wait compaction is `false` and SAYS the brief was delivered anyway. `targetFacts(plain fields)` → `{targetKind, targetState}` (a dispatch in flight reads `compacting`). `journalLine` = the ONE log line (ids cut to 8, never the brief's words). Gate: scripts/test-dispatch-model.mjs (fast) — §1 the table over all 3 × 3 × 3 × 4 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 1 728 combinations against an independent oracle + named rows; §5 four mutant-copy controls (compacts a busy worker / lets a job dispatch / compacts a terminal / compacts past a refused spend), each RED.

### src/usage-index-model.js + src/usage-index-worker.js + src/server/usage-index.js — THE USAGE INDEX SHADOW (design 011 lane 3, L1; 2.369.203)

  usage-index-model.js   — PURE (test-architecture's PURE set): `rowOf(event, shard)` (survey §2.2's 28 columns; an empty acct is stored NULL — falsy in memory too — and `acct_key` is computed the way aggregate buckets), `shardMarkVerdict({size, ino, headHash}, mark)` → same | append | rebuild | gone, `aggregateSql(opts)` = THE ONE GROUPED PASS (session × the raw columns every dimension derives from × UTC day × LOCAL hour / weekday through `vs_lhour` / `vs_lwday` — JS `getHours` / `getDay` registered in the worker, the calls aggregate makes; measured ~1 s per 500 k rows against ~6 s for a GROUP BY per dimension), `foldAggregate` / `finalizeAggregate` (cells per (model, account), priced by the ledger's own `_cost`), `compareAggregates(mem, idx)` (costs to 1e-9 relative, everything else exact). Its bucket rules are a deliberate SECOND SPELLING of aggregate's keyOf — a drift is exactly what a comparison reports.
  usage-index-worker.js  — the ONLY file that names node:sqlite (§73) and refuses the main thread. `~/.vibespace/db/<sha256(data/'s real path)[:16]>/usage.db` + `owner.json` (the data/ it belongs to). `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` + WAL + `synchronous=NORMAL`: no -shm, a second opener gets SQLITE_BUSY ⇒ 'locked-by-another-server', never retried. user_version ≠ 1 / NOTADB / CORRUPT ⇒ delete and rebuild. ONE FIFO of `{id, op, payload}`: `ingest` (THE PUSH — taken only when it starts at the shard's mark with the marked inode, else that shard is re-read from its mark), `recover` (every shard by its mark in name order = _loadEvents's order, so "first row of a rid wins" means the same; 16 MiB chunks each committed WITH its mark; a heartbeat and a CLOSE-flag check between chunks; an empty or torn-only shard is marked too), `aggregate`, `stats` (threadId, rows, marks, user_version, optional quick_check), `close`. SQLITE_FULL / IOERR / READONLY / ENOSPC ⇒ off by name ('write-failed'). FULL / ENOSPC / EDQUOT also close the db and remove usage.db* (owner.json stays — scripts/ci.mjs's sweep) BEFORE 'disabled' is posted: the state is a fact about the disk (mirror-green-213). The ExperimentalWarning of node:sqlite is filtered at its one load.
  server/usage-index.js  — ORCH owner: `create({getLedger, homeDir, workerFile, deadlineMs, queryDeadlineMs, closeBoundMs, pushBacklogBytes, maxPages, exitHook, onDiff, onState})`; `start()` resolves the ledger, spawns the worker (unref'd) and attaches itself as the ledger's push (`setIndex`); `REASON` names every unavailability (not-started · starting · building · no-node-sqlite · locked-by-another-server · write-failed · unresponsive · worker-exited · no-ledger · closed). A query past its deadline answers 503 'unresponsive' and the worker LIVES (unlike SafeFs: a D-state thread cannot be killed and would keep its lock); the next message clears it. A push backlog past 64 MiB stops pushing (one `recover` once the worker answers). `compare(mem, opts)` = THE COMPARER: single-flight, skips under the reason's name, a difference = `onDiff` (account-usage-routes.js records telemetry `usage-index-diff` with the query), never shown. **process.exit() JOINS worker threads** (measured: with the worker blocked in open() of a FIFO it never returns) ⇒ the `exit` hook's `closeSync` waits ≤ closeBoundMs (2 s) on a SharedArrayBuffer flag, then re-raises SIGTERM with the default action (a clean stop for systemd).
  Wiring: account-usage-routes.js creates the owner, starts it 30 s after boot (an unref'd timer — a short-lived suite that wires the routes never starts one) and calls `usageIndex.compare(answer, …)` in the SAME synchronous step as `/api/usage-stats`'s memory answer, before `res.json`. usage-history.js: both commit points push right after their append (`_pushIndex`: shard, start offset = size − bytes, inode, text); `reloadEvents` and a re-bake ask for a mark re-check. L0 rides here: `_cursors.json` is written only when its bytes change and dead keys are dropped hourly on proof (see usage-history.js). `scripts/ci.mjs` `sweepUsageIndexDirs` (after every suite) removes an index dir whose owner.json names a data/ that is gone. Gates: test-usage-index-parity, test-usage-index-owner, test-architecture §73.

The keepers exist for: LIFECYCLE (launch / adopt after a server restart / stop on request / app exit), ONE active viewer per app window, the CONCURRENCY CEILING (a refusal AT LAUNCH that names the holders — never a kill), IDLE-OUT, and — from the 2.369.42 OpenCode-serve incident (a HEADLESS service nobody watched: 209 CPU-min, 5 GB RSS, 30k inotify watches, 3.6 GB/s page-cache reads) — the runaway stop. The ruling separates the two kinds of process: a HEADLESS service the product runs for itself (the OpenCode serve) may be STOPPED + PARKED by the product; a session a PERSON or an AGENT is using (a desktop app, an agent browser) is NEVER stopped, parked or refused by a resource guard — it is REPORTED (the live row, a server notice when a crossing begins — with hysteresis, an hourly floor and delivery-latched keys (r2) —, telemetry). The thresholds are therefore the serve's stop threshold and the apps'/browsers' REPORTING threshold; the verdict is src/runaway-guard.js (the ONE comparison site, test-architecture §54).

  · Gate: test-runaway-guard (fast, 45: the verdict incl. the incident fixture through the real `cli-identity.setSample`, the multi-pid anon fixture ('anon-sum', over ΣPss, unjudged) beside the one-process 'anon', the reaped-ticks rule, the report level (hysteresis, the oscillation fixture ⇒ one fire, the floor, delivery re-sends), the words, the numbers, four scratch-copy controls — an `rssBytes` comparison calls the incident fixture OVER, a copy without the 'rss' skip judges a 90 GB sum, a copy without hysteresis/floor fires 1010101010, a copy that latches an undelivered notice never re-sends). INVARIANT: a new keeper asks THIS verdict and decides its outcome by the kind of process — headless-for-the-product may stop; used-by-a-person-or-agent only reports.

**Lane D (a) (2026-09-25, the owner's white edges after a 2× → 1.5× relaunch + Chrome's stacked bars; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.3/§3.4):** A FRACTION IS A REAL SCALE — `scaleKnobs(s, {rule})` → `{scale, gdkScale, dpi, pictureScale, rule, env, xresources}`: the default `rule: 'ceil'` draws at GDK_SCALE ⌈s⌉ at 96 dpi and the view shows the picture at `pictureScale` = s ÷ ⌈s⌉ (1.5 ⇒ 2 × 0.75, 2.5 ⇒ 3 × 0.8333, 1.25 ⇒ 2 × 0.625; integers stay 1:1); `rule: 'dpi'` = the old floor rule (GDK_SCALE ⌊s⌋ + the fraction in Xft.dpi) for an app that scales WHOLE from its font dpi — `scaleRuleOf(row|rec)` answers it for the browser rows (Chrome 153 measured: [750,131] at 1 + 144 dpi = 1.5 × [500,87]). `newRecord` stores `gdkScale` + `pictureScale` (what the app was DRAWN at); `renderOf(rec)` → `{gdk, picture, widget, perLogical}` is the ONE reader — a record without `gdkScale` (older, or from an older paired machine) is the floor rule shown 1:1 (never re-derived from `scale`); the stored 4-place picture scale is read back as the exact s ÷ gdk (a 0.8333 made the chip say "2.4999×" and a round trip drift); a browser record's `widget` (and `perLogical`) is its WHOLE scale (the dpi rule). `relaunchPaneCss({pane, mainPx, dpr, from, to})` = the pane a Scale ▸ successor needs to show the SAME app content: logical = max(pane × dpr ÷ from.picture, the main's X px when it was scaled to fit) ÷ from.perLogical (the X px the old app drew per logical px); new pane = logical × to.widget ÷ dpr (0.01 px — a 0.5 rounding drifted a round trip). `CHROMIUM_FRAME_MARKER` + `chromiumFramePrefs(prefs)` → `{ok, changed, prefs, why}`: `browser.custom_chrome_frame: true` only when ABSENT (Chrome draws its own frame ⇒ `decorations 0` ⇒ seamless), an existing choice kept, a non-object refused. Gate: test-desktop-apps §14 (the knob table, renderOf, the relaunch arithmetic + round trips, the pref table, wiring pins, a floor-knobs CONTROL copy) + §10/§13 re-pinned.
**Lane D (b) (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.4 note — the per-app default scale + the clickable chip):** `EXPLICIT_SCALES` [1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3] = the scales a PERSON picks by name (a window's Scale ▸ row, an app's default) — every value `scaleKnobs` spells EXACTLY (lane D (a)'s ceil rule: 2.5 = GDK_SCALE 3 shown at 0.8333; 3 = GDK_SCALE 3 at 1:1; the dpi rule of a browser row: 2.5 = GDK_SCALE 2 + 120 dpi) — while the Settings enum stays `APP_SCALES` [1, 1.5, 2]; `SCALE_CHOICES` = 'auto' + EXPLICIT_SCALES (the menu gained 2.5× and 3×); `appScaleFor`'s explicit branch honours the whole set. `parseScaleChoice(raw)` → 'auto' | a number of the set | null — the ONE reading of a request's scale (the relaunch's `scale`, the launch's `scaleChoice`; a boolean / empty / 1.25 / 4 is null). `scaleChoiceVerdict(body)` → `{ok, scaleChoice: number|null}` | `{ok:false, code:'bad-request', error}` — validateLaunchRequest carries `launch.scaleChoice` (both shapes; 'auto' ⇒ null = no app default) and the hub's launch route calls the SAME check before a paired machine is asked. `scalePick({setting, appDefault, choice, dpr, uiScale})`: a relaunch's `choice` > `appDefault` (an explicit scale ⇒ origin `'app'`, from null; 'auto' / junk ⇒ none) > an explicit `setting` > auto. `SCALE_ORIGINS` ['auto','setting','chosen','app'] = newRecord's closed set. `scaleMenuModel(rec, {…, appDefault})` marks the app default's row `appDefault: true` (never current by itself — the record launched AT it is current). **Verify r5 (2026-09-25, four lows) — THE INSTALL LAUNCHER'S LAST ROUND.** **L1** the exit file is `"<code> <unix nanoseconds> <lock>"` (the runner's `fin` writes `date +%s%N`) and the launcher's own instant `t0` is `date +%s%N`; a start that waited on a held lock answers the recorded exit only when it is STRICTLY newer (`-gt`) — in whole seconds (`-ge`) a start in the same second as an earlier install's exit, while a child that install left behind still held the lock, answered that stale exit instead of running (6/6). A `date` without `%N` compares as no number ⇒ the start runs (it holds the lock — the benign direction). **L2** (wording; the r4 paragraph below said otherwise) the lock's holders are the runner shell and apt-get: apt-get closes inherited descriptors for the children it forks (APT::Keep-Fds — a `file` method shim saw fds 0,1,2,10,11,12 only), so dpkg never holds fd 9; a dpkg outliving both is fenced by dpkg's own lock. **L3** the lock's directory is named by the UID, never the environment: `u=$(id -u)` (not a number ⇒ 125 "this user id cannot be read (id -u)"), `T=/run/user/$u` when it is a writable directory this user owns (`-d -w -O`), else `/tmp/vibespace-$u` (`mkdir -m 700`), and that must be a non-symlink directory this user owns and can write — else 125 "`<T>` is not a directory this user owns". From `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (r4) two spawners with different environments (the hub under systemd, a daemon from an ssh login, a runtime dir logind removed) named two locks for one state dir, and the `/tmp` file name was predictable. Honest limit now: only when `/run/user/<uid>` is unusable does the per-uid `/tmp` dir apply, and a local user who squats it before our first use denies the install BY NAME (never a second install). **L4** the launcher keeps the runner's pid (`b=$!` — `setsid` execs in place in a shell without job control, so it IS the runner) and the pidfile wait also ends when `/proc/$b` is gone: a runner started without fd 9 refuses and is reported at once with its own line naming the lock (~0.2 s, was the full 10 s); a machine without `setsid` now also answers at once. Gate: test-desktop-serve §10.

**Verify r4 (2026-09-25) — THE INSTALL LOCK IS HELD BY THE RUNNING INSTALL ITSELF AND RELEASED BY THE KERNEL.** r3's lock DIRECTORY (below — kept as the record of what was tried) had a break rule, and the break rule was a race: every claim leaves the lock ownerless for a moment (mkdir, then the owner rename), so a breaker could `rm -rf` it between another claimer's mkdir and its rename — both then spawned a runner (the verifier: 1/150 over an empty dir at natural speed, 20/20 with the rename slowed 50 ms; re-measured before the fix: 4/150, 12/20 at +30 ms, 17/20 at +50 ms with up to 4 runners). Now: `INSTALL_FILES` = `{log, pid, exit}` (no `lock`); `INSTALL_LOCK_PREFIX` = `vibespace-xpra-install-`; the launcher names the lock `<T>/vibespace-xpra-install-<first 12 hex of sha1(realpath of the state dir)>.lock`, `T` = `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when it is a writable directory, else `/tmp` — LOCAL storage (the state dir may be on NFS / FUSE, where flock is not dependable; logind may have removed a runtime dir at the last logout), opens it as fd 9 (`command exec 9>>` — a failed open is a named 125, never a dead shell) and takes `flock -n 9` BEFORE it spawns. The runner is started by `setsid sh -c … &` WITH fd 9 (fds are inherited through the fork + both execs — proven: `/proc/<runner>/fd/9` → the lock file on dash and bash; its install child holds it too; the launcher closes its own copy right after the spawn, its `tail` never has it), so the lock lives exactly as long as the install (the runner shell + apt-get — never dpkg, see r5 L2) and the kernel drops it the instant the last of them exits or is killed. Nothing is broken by hand, no owner file, no staleness rule, no 2 s wait, no pid identity for the lock. A start whose `flock -n` answers 1 (held) FOLLOWS: it polls ≤ 20 s for a live recorded runner (pidfile pid + starttime) and follows its log; if the lock frees first, the install it waited on already ended — its exit file (written BEFORE the lock frees) is this start's answer when its `at` ≥ this start's own start second, otherwise nothing ran since this start was asked and this start (now holding the lock) runs it; a lock held 20 s with no install recorded ⇒ 125 naming it (a process an earlier install started may still hold it). Any other flock failure ⇒ 125 "the install lock cannot be taken on <path> (flock exit N)" — never a fallback. After taking the lock a start re-reads the pidfile and follows a live recorded install (a belt for a lock file removed under a running install — the file itself is never removed by us; the winner `touch -c`es it so an aged /tmp never sweeps it mid-install). The RUNNER re-asserts the lock (`flock -n 9` on its inherited descriptor — the same open file description succeeds, anything else conflicts) before it records itself; not held ⇒ it appends one line to the log and exits 125 WITHOUT touching the pidfile / exit file (they are the holder's). Pidfile `"<pid> <starttime> <lock>"`, exit file `"<code> <unix s> <lock>"`. Removed: the lock dir, the owner file, the break mutex, the launcher's own starttime (and its L8 refusal — the runner's L8 refusal stays: the pidfile's identity needs /proc). L5 extended: `command -v flock` ⇒ 125 naming util-linux. Runner argv `P L X K "$@"` with K = the lock FILE. Honest limit: under the `/tmp` fallback (no usable runtime dir) the name is predictable, so ANOTHER local user can pre-create the file (our open fails ⇒ 125 naming it) or hold a lock on it (a start waits 20 s ⇒ 125 naming it) — a denial of the install, said by name, never a second install; `>>` never truncates and `protected_symlinks` keeps a planted symlink from being followed. Gate: test-desktop-serve §10 (see the suites entry).

**Verify r3 (2026-09-25, M1 + M4 + L5 + L8) — THE INSTALL SLOT IS CLAIMED ATOMICALLY AND NEVER FOLLOWED ON AN UNVERIFIED PID.** `INSTALL_FILES.lock` = `xpra-install.lock`, a DIRECTORY: the launcher claims it with `mkdir` BEFORE spawning (exactly one claimer wins — before, two `start`s inside the 5–20 ms before the runner wrote its pidfile both started a runner: 2 of 2, 5 of 5), writes its `owner` ("<pid> <starttime>", tmp + mv), and the RUNNER takes it over (its own owner line) and removes it AFTER the exit file (only if it still names the runner). A loser FOLLOWS: a live owner is waited on (≤ 20 s) until its runner's pidfile lives, then `tail --pid`; a lock whose owner is PROVEN gone (`gone`: no /proc entry, or a readable starttime that differs — an EMPTY probe proves nothing: during the fix a live claimer's lock was broken once in ~33 suite runs, the only mechanism that fits being a probe that came back empty, pinned with a pid-blind `sed`) is broken once per dead owner under `<lock>.break-<pid>-<starttime>` (a `mkdir` mutex, the owner re-read inside; a mutex held 2 s is an orphan and cleared; a break attempt that proves nothing sleeps); an OWNERLESS lock (a claim that died before naming itself) is waited on 2 s first; a state dir that cannot be written is refused by name (125), never waited on as a held slot. `follow` mode never claims. M1: the claimer resets pid/starttime, reads only the NEW pidfile, and `tail --pid` follows only that runner's pid while it is not proven gone (before: a wrapped pid in the OLD pidfile + an install that ended before the first poll ⇒ tail followed an unrelated live process — a 15-min install_timeout for a finished install). L5: `command -v setsid` before the claim ⇒ 125 naming util-linux (was 10.5 s, "no pid"), setsid's stderr appended to the log. L8: the launcher refuses before claiming and the RUNNER refuses before running when `/proc/<pid>/stat` gives no starttime after one retry (exit file 125 + the cause in the log, the slot released) — no "<pid> " pidfile nothing can verify. Runner argv is now `P L X K "$@"`. Gate: test-desktop-serve §10 (each with a mutant control).

**Lane E (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6 — the owner's D1–D7):** `browserArgv` appends the ACCESSIBILITY switch to the chromium family (`BROWSER_A11Y_FLAG` = `--force-renderer-accessibility`) and answers `env` = `BROWSER_A11Y_ENV` (`GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1`) for the firefox family (the keeper merges it into the app's env). Measured on Chrome 153 under the keeper: WITH the flag the default 600-node snapshot reaches the page (235–237 nodes, ~50 ms), WITHOUT it 4 nodes (the application + 3 frames, unreadable children) and no page in 30 s. Always on (a share after launch needs it; flipping a11y on at runtime would change org.a11y.Status for the user's whole session). Not a forbidden (automation) flag. **Chrome 154 (measured 2026-09-29, the .197 integration): the flag alone no longer puts the browser on the AT-SPI bus in the keeper's minimal env** — its application object appears only with one of `ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED` / `GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY` / `QT_ACCESSIBILITY` = 1 in its OWN env (xpra, `NO_AT_BRIDGE`, `GDK_BACKEND`, the prefs seed and the bus address ruled out one by one) ⇒ chromium also answers `env` = `CHROMIUM_A11Y_ENV` (`ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1`) — the app's env, never the session's; without it the page is unreachable and `auto` reads pixels ("no accessibility tree"). Gate: test-desktop-apps (the argv pins + the switch) + test-window-target lane E (the page reached; the negative control's reason a per-major measured row).

**Verify r2 (2026-09-25, F3 + F4) — THE INSTALL RUNS DETACHED.** `INSTALL_FILES` (`xpra-install.log` / `.pid` / `.exit`), `INSTALL_UNRECORDED_EXIT` (199), `INSTALL_RUNNER` + `INSTALL_LAUNCHER` (two constant POSIX-sh texts) and `installLauncherArgv(argv, {stateDir, mode})` → `['sh','-c',LAUNCHER,'vs-install',RUNNER,stateDir,start|follow,...argv]` — the SAME argv on both transports. The launcher starts the runner in its own session (`setsid`, stdin /dev/null, stdout+stderr APPENDED to the log), waits for its pidfile ("<pid> <starttime>" from /proc, written by the runner itself), then FOLLOWS the log (`tail --pid`); a live recorded install is followed in either mode (never a second), `follow` with none running prints the last log and exits with the recorded code; the exit is the install's RECORDED code ("<code> <unix s>", the pidfile removed after it), 199 when none was recorded. The state dir and the argv are positional parameters — only the plan's `script` runs as root. Linux + GNU `tail --pid` + util-linux `setsid` (the plan runs on apt systems only). Gate: test-desktop-serve §10.

**Lane C2 (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5):** PURE additions for apps on a PAIRED machine. `HOST_OFFLINE_STATE` = `'unknown-host-offline'` — a VIEW state only (never stored, never a transition): a remote record whose machine did not answer is kept and shown with it, so the window stays open (only `exited` / `failed` close one). `xpraInstallPlan(installFacts)` = THE install rung's plan, shown before anything runs: `no_facts` / `no_x11` (macOS / Windows — no X11 server) / `no_apt` / `no_repo` (apt's xpra < `XPRA_APT_MIN_MAJOR` 5 and not a Debian/Ubuntu codename xpra.org publishes for) refuse BY NAME; apt ≥ 5 ⇒ `source:'apt'`; else `source:'xpra.org'` = the key (`XPRA_KEY_URL`) + a deb822 `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/xpra.sources` (`URIs: https://xpra.org`, `Suites: <codename>` — the MEASURED shape of this box's own file, not the design's `https://xpra.org/<dist>/<codename>`) + `/etc/apt/preferences.d/xpra-vibespace` pinning `xpra*` to `XPRA_PIN_MAJOR` 6.x at 1001; packages = `XPRA_APT_PACKAGES` (xpra xterm xdotool xauth xvfb) + on xpra.org `XPRA_ORG_EXTRA` (xpra-x11, xpra-html5 — RECOMMENDS of xpra-server there, named so a no-recommends machine still gets the rung; `apt-cache depends`, 6.5.3); xpra ≥ 5 already installed ⇒ only the helpers. The codename is interpolated into a ROOT shell line, so it must match `CODENAME_RE` (a device reports its own facts — validated like any input). `script` (set -e, each step echoed) + `commands` (the same steps with sudo, for a person to copy) + `canRun` (root or passwordless sudo; else `code:'no_sudo'`, plan still returned). `installArgv(plan)` = `sudo -n sh -c <script>` (never a password prompt) or `sh -c` as root — the SAME argv on every transport. `machinePickRow(row)` = the launch dialog's machine verdict from what the hub knows WITHOUT asking: `ready` (this machine / a connected Linux agent with `desktop-serve`) · `connect` (an ssh machine not connected — choosing it connects) · `offline` (a dial device not dialed in) · `host_needs_daemon` (a connected agent without the capability) · `no_x11` (its hello-ack platform is not linux). Gate: test-desktop-serve §6.

**Lane C1 (2026-09-25):** `newRecord({…, hostId = 'local'})` stamps the MACHINE the app runs on — `'local'` = the machine that holds the record (the hub's own; on a paired device its own record says `'local'` too, and the hub re-labels it). Records written before are stamped by migration `2026-09-desktop-apps-host-key`.

**2026-09-25 — NO RESOURCE VERDICT, NO PARK, AND WHO MAY REMOVE A PROFILE (the owner's ruling; the Chrome desktop-app incident, docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md):** `runawayVerdict` moved to src/runaway-guard.js (`resourceVerdict`, report-only for an app) and `runawayParkVerdict` is GONE with the park — a launch is never refused by a past sample (code `runaway-parked` no longer exists; routes/desktop-apps.js + routes/window-targets.js dropped it). `TRANSITIONS` has NO `runaway` event (launching/ready → `failed` only on spawn-error / display-gone). NEW PURE `profileRetireVerdict(rec)` → `{remove, why}` + `PERSON_ENDINGS` (['user','relaunch']): a browser row's profile is removed ONLY after a PERSON's ending — Stop (`stoppedBy` 'user'), the Scale ▸ relaunch, the app's OWN exit (state `exited`, no `stoppedBy` — its user closed it) — or when no app ever ran in it (`pids.app` unset: a failed bring-up's empty scaffold); an idle-out (`stoppedBy` 'idle'), a display that died under the app, the retired guard's old `runaway` records and "keep profile" KEEP it and `why` says so ("kept: the session was ended by the keeper (idle), not by a person — remove it by hand"). **Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — the app's exit closes the window, the outer ✕ is the app's own close; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2):** three PURE decisions + one constant. `windowsLeftCount(rows)` = the windows a person could still see after the app process exited — mapped (`false` excludes, `null` = unknown counts), ≥ 16×16 (a WM's 5×5 helper, a 1×1 leader are not windows), on screen (xfwm4 parks its helper at -1000,-1000). `exitCloseVerdict(rec, {leased})` → `{close, why}` decided ONCE per window at the record's arrival in a terminal state: `failed` stays (its red sentence is the one place the error is said), an agent lease keeps it (`lease`), any stop closes (`stoppedBy` set ⇒ `stopped` — VibeSpace tore the display down on purpose, D2d), an exit closes unless the keeper's census found a window LEFT (`windowsAtExit` > 0 ⇒ `windows-left`: a forking launcher exited while its child still shows one; 0 / absent ⇒ `exited`). `outerCloseVerdict({state, stream, seat, connected, mainWid, leased, askedAt, now})` → `{act: 'close'|'ask-app'|'stop', why}`: not ready ⇒ close; a second ✕ within `OUTER_CLOSE_AGAIN_MS` (5000) of an ask ⇒ stop (even with no main window left — the app closed its window and kept running); the rfb rung (no per-window protocol), an agent lease, a blocked / Watch pane, no main window ⇒ close (today's pane-only close); otherwise ask-app. A clock that went back is not "again". Gate: test-desktop-apps §12 (the census table, 14 exit rows, 16 outer-✕ rows, wiring pins on the keeper / the window / WindowManager / every user close).


**B-bfe6 — A BROWSER AS A DESKTOP APP (2.369.166, owner 2026-09-23 "应用里面也可以加入一下浏览器"; docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.7):** a desktop-app browser is a HUMAN'S browser — a registry exec (§5, never an agent's), on the xpra per-window rung like every app, with its OWN profile the app session owns; never an agent-browser profile (those live under data/browser-* and are driven over CDP by the Browser profiles keeper, design-agent-browser-v2 §3) and never the user's real ~/.config/chromium / ~/.mozilla. `BROWSER_KINDS` = the two families `chromium` (execs chromium → chromium-browser → google-chrome) and `firefox` (firefox → firefox-esr) with the label per binary ("Google Chrome", "Firefox ESR"); `BROWSER_BINS` their union (desktop-display probes THAT list). DEFAULT_REGISTRY's `chromium` / `firefox` rows carry `browser` + `execs` (the old rows were a bare `chromium` exec and `firefox --new-instance` with NO profile — the user's real default profile, or a hand-off to their running Firefox). `validateAppRow`: `browser` a known family, `execs` bare names on a browser row only, and a browser row may NOT carry a profile or automation flag (`isForbiddenBrowserArg`: --user-data-dir / -profile / -P / --remote-debugging-* / --remote-allow-* / --enable-automation / --headless / --marionette / --start-debugger-server / --load-extension …, refused `automation-flag`). `browserRowFor(row, bins)` → the first `execs` name `bins` has becomes the served `exec`/`path`/label, else `browser-absent` naming every candidate. `validateBrowserUrl(v)` (the dialog runs the SAME function): http/https only, no whitespace/control char, ≤ 2048, parsed to its href, else `bad-url` with the why. `profileDirVerdict(dir, {home, ownedRoot, confinement, exec})`: absolute and INSIDE `ownedRoot` (the keeper's data/desktop-apps — so an agent-browser dir or a `..` escape is `profile-not-owned`), not $HOME and not inside `REAL_BROWSER_ROOTS` (deb / snap / flatpak profile roots, `profile-is-users`), and for a SNAP binary inside $HOME under a non-hidden first segment (a snap sees a private /tmp and no ~/.hidden — `snap-profile-unreachable`). `browserArgv(row, {profileDir, url})` = the row's own args, THEN chromium `--user-data-dir=<dir> --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --password-store=basic` / firefox `--new-instance -profile <dir>`, THEN the URL (one argv item; an http(s) href never starts with '-'). `firefoxUserJs()` = Firefox's first-run switch (it has no --no-first-run): user_pref lines the keeper writes into the profile. `validateLaunchRequest`: `url` / `keepProfile` (boolean) ride a BROWSER row's launch; on any other row or a typed command they are refused `not-a-browser`, never ignored; a bad URL `bad-url`. **r2 of the browser takeover (2.369.168, T6):** `browserLaunchVerdict({exec, args, exe})` → `{browser, by: 'exec'|'launcher'|'process'|null, name}` = is this launch a WEB BROWSER (the human's window — the window-targets engine refuses it to agents): the executable's basename against `BROWSER_EXEC_RE` (precise names: `google-chrome*`, `chrome`, `chromium(-browser|-freeworld)`, `microsoft-edge*`, `msedge`, `brave*`, `opera*`, `vivaldi*`, `firefox*`, `epiphany`, the Debian alternatives `x-www-browser` / `gnome-www-browser` / `sensible-browser` …) or `BROWSER_APP_ID_RE` (reverse-DNS: `org.chromium.*`, `com.google.Chrome`, `org.mozilla.firefox` …; a flatpak ref's `//branch` stripped); `launchedProgram` unwraps `flatpak run` / `snap run` / `env`; `exe` = the running app's /proc exe (a wrapper the human typed). Never a prefix: `chromium-thumbnailer`, GNU `infobrowser`, `browserslist`, flatpak Thunderbird are not browsers. **HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** `APP_SCALES` [1, 1.5, 2]; `normalizeDpr` (a finite 1..3, else 1); `appScaleFor(setting, dpr)` (`desktop.appScale`: auto/unset = 2 from a DPR of 1.5 up, else 1 (r2 — never the text-only 1.5, below), an explicit '1'|'1.5'|'2' wins, anything else 1); `scaleKnobs(scale)` → `{scale, gdkScale, dpi, env, xresources}` — the MEASURED rule: GDK_SCALE = the integer part (doubles GTK3 AND GTK4 exactly), the display's font dpi = 96 × scale / GDK_SCALE (Xft.dpi MULTIPLIES with GDK_SCALE — 192 + GDK_SCALE=2 = 4× text), GDK_DPI_SCALE never (GTK4 ignores it, GTK3 would double-count the fraction), QT_ENABLE_HIGHDPI_SCALING=1 + QT_SCALE_FACTOR=<integer part> (unmeasured — no Qt app here), and at a scale > 1 `XTerm/UXTerm*faceName: Monospace` + `faceSize: 8 × GDK_SCALE` (xterm's bitmap default no dpi reaches). `validateLaunchRequest` carries `launch.dpr` and REFUSES a dpr outside 1..3 by name; `newRecord` stores `scale` (default 1) + `dpi` (default 96). Gate: test-desktop-apps §10.

**r2 (the verifier, measured): 1.5× IS TEXT ONLY FOR GTK.** X11 GTK has no fractional GDK_SCALE, so 1.5× = GDK_SCALE 1 + fonts at 144 dpi: GNOME Calculator's minimum is 360×616 device px at 1× AND at 1.5× (720×1232 at 2×) — on a DPR-1.5 screen that is a 240×411 CSS pane, keys at 0.67× their 1×-screen size. `auto` therefore picks 2 from a DPR of 1.5 up (widgets 1.33× on a 1.5 screen, 1.14× on 1.75) and 1 below (0.8× on 1.25) — the nearer integer scale in ratio; 1.5× stays an explicit choice, labelled t('1.5× (text only in GTK apps)'). Consequence, stated: an app with a tall minimum at 2× on a small 1.5 screen (a 1080p laptop at 150 %) does not fit and is shown scaled to fit with the badge — pick 1× there. Gate: test-desktop-apps §10 (the table + the pre-fix nearest-0.5 rule as the control).

**Round 3, A3 (2.369.166 — the scale DERIVED from VibeSpace's own scale, per window; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.4):** `effectiveScale(dpr, uiScale)` = dpr × the UI scale (the body zoom — the pane is counter-zoomed to net zoom 1, so before A3 a 125 % UI drew a 1.0× app beside 1.25× chrome, M4), clamped 1..`SCALE_MAX` 3. `appScaleFor('auto', dpr, uiScale)` answers the TEXT scale by the ratio rule: below √2 as is, √2..2 ⇒ 2, 2..2√2 as is, above ⇒ 3 — so a screen of 1.5 or more never gets the text-only 1.5 (r2's invariant, kept); an explicit 1 / 1.5 / 2 is returned as given. `scaleKnobs(s)` takes ANY 1..3 and spells it by the floor rule: GDK_SCALE = floor, the rest in the font dpi (96 × s / GDK_SCALE) — 2.5 ⇒ 2 + 120 dpi, 1.25 ⇒ 1 + 120, an explicit 1.5 ⇒ 1 + 144 (text only in GTK, as ever). `scalePick({setting, choice, dpr, uiScale})` → `{scale, origin: auto|setting|chosen, from}` (a relaunch's `choice` wins; its `auto` re-derives from the RELAUNCHING client). `validateLaunchRequest` carries `uiScale` (0.6..2 = the product's own `UI_SCALE_MIN/MAX`, else refused by name); `newRecord` keeps `scale` (1..3, two decimals), `scaleOrigin`, `scaleFrom`. The per-window relaunch: `SCALE_CHOICES` (auto, 1, 1.5, 2), `validateRelaunchRequest`, `relaunchVerdict` (ready + the xpra stream + not a browser, each refusal a code), `relaunchBodyOf` (a catalog row by id, a typed command as typed), `scaleMenuModel(rec, {dpr, uiScale, leased, seat})` (the rows, which one is current — not offered again unless auto would now derive something else — and one reason CODE disabling all: the relaunch verdict, `lease`, `seat`). `exitCloseVerdict` answers `relaunched` + `replacedBy` FIRST — a replaced record never closes its window. Gate: test-desktop-apps §13 (the design's table + the √2 / 2√2 boundaries, uiScale-absent = the .158 answers on DPR 1/1.5/2 as the regression control, the refusals, the menu model, wiring pins on the keeper / the route / the launcher / the window); §10's r2 auto table moved to the new thresholds with its invariant kept.

  office-open.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS shared by desktop-apps / desktop-display / desktop-serve / the route / the daemon bundle / the browser bundle). A Word file is EDITED in LibreOffice running as a desktop app on the xpra rung; this module is every rule about it. `modules: null` — a snap — judged present). `lockFileOf(file)` = `<dir>/.~lock.<name>#`; **`staleLockVerdict(content, profileDir)`** — MEASURED: SIGTERM ends LibreOffice in ~130 ms and LEAVES the lock (the next open: "Document in use"); The profile is retired by the browser rows' rule (`retireProfile` keys on `rec.profileDir`). `relaunch()` takes the browser's STOP-FIRST path for an office record too (the running instance locks the document; the profile is carried). ### src/server/desktop-access.js — ONE WAY TO A DESKTOP APP'S MACHINE (lane C1, 2026-09-25)

**Layer 0 apps (2.369.200) — THE SLOT, GENERALISED AGAIN:** `installPackage(hostId, {what:'app:<…>', planOpts, …})` takes its plan from the PLANNER the apps engine registers (`setAppPlanner` — the machine's own `app-plan`), runs the plan's OWN argv (`plan.argv`: the root script with the machine's paths and the run's nonce as positions) through the same launcher (one install per machine, a running one FOLLOWED, `busy` / held slots as before) and answers without re-reading the xpra facts (the app's record op reads the result). `planDigest` also binds `closureKey` when a plan carries one (an app plan); an xpra / LibreOffice digest is byte-identical to r6's.

**§7.9 — THE INSTALL RUNG, GENERALISED (2026-09-27):** `installPackage(hostId, {what, onData, onReattach})` is the old `installXpra` body verbatim with the plan picked by `installPlan(hostId, what)` → `M.installPlanFor(what, facts.install)` (an unknown `what` ⇒ `bad-request` before the machine is asked); **`installXpra(h, opts)` IS `installPackage(h, {...opts, what: 'xpra'})`** (every xpra line, refusal and hold unchanged — test-desktop-serve §9/§10 green, its patched lines intact). ONE install slot per machine for every package (the launcher's pidfile + kernel-held lock keep their historical `xpra-install.*` names — a rename would orphan an install running across an upgrade; dpkg runs one install at a time anyway): an install of ANOTHER package already running is followed like any live one (`reattached`), and the route re-checks what it wanted (`still-absent`). The answer carries `what`.

**Verify r2 (2026-09-25, F3 + F4) — THE INSTALL IS DETACHED AND ITS SLOT IS THE MACHINE'S PIDFILE.** `runArgv(hostId, argv, {onData, stateDir, mode})` runs `M.installLauncherArgv(argv, {stateDir, mode})` (spelled once — the controls replace that line) as the in-process child / the `run-stream` op: what it waits on is the FOLLOWER; the install never depends on it (measured before: the starter SIGKILLed at 0.7 s ⇒ the install's shell rc 141 at its next line; after: its end marker lands). `installXpra(hostId, {onData, onReattach})`: facts first — `installing` (a live pidfile) ⇒ RE-ATTACH (`onReattach({pid, since})`, mode `follow`, the plan's refusals skipped: nothing new runs) else the plan's refusals and mode `start`; `r.code === INSTALL_UNRECORDED_EXIT` ⇒ `install_unrecorded`; the answer carries `reattached`. The in-memory `installs` map is only THIS hub's follower (`busy` 409): an `install_timeout` / `install_link_lost` hands its slot to `holdUntilGone` — `facts {installState:true}` every `pollMs` (probe-free: never `sudo -n` every poll — an older agent's `install` block read instead; default 15 s; unreachable = still held) until `installing` is null, at most `holdMs` — and the line that frees it names the EVIDENCE ("…reports the install process gone, exit N", "(the link dropped meanwhile; seen after it came back)", "was not seen to end within …", an older agent without `installing` ⇒ held to holdMs). Measured before (the verifier's stub recipe on the pre-fix file): link lost ⇒ slot null at once; timed out then link lost ⇒ freed saying "ended". `spell` says sub-second holds in ms. `finished` is gone. Gates: test-desktop-serve §10, test-desktop-remote §8.

**Lane C2 (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5):** `machines()` = the launch dialog's picker rows: this machine first, then every host record with the PURE `machinePickRow` verdict — built WITHOUT starting a connect ladder (the cached connected handle through HostManager.connectedDevice, or a live dial link bounded ≤ 3 s; an ssh machine never bootstrapped just to draw a row); `label` = the host record's name, a DISPLAY string (dialog + window title, never a spawn). `installPlan(hostId)` = `facts {install:true}` + the PURE plan. `runArgv(hostId, argv, {onData})` = ONE rung, two transports with the identical argv: an in-process child on this machine (stdout + stderr streamed), the agentd `run-stream` op on a paired one (`sh -c 'exec "$@" 2>&1'` folds stderr in — run-stream relays stdout only); a REAL exit answers `{code}`, every other ending is a coded throw (never a made-up "exit 1"): past `installMs` (15 min) ⇒ `install_timeout`, a link lost mid-run ⇒ `install_link_lost`. **The child is never killed** (C2 verify fix, 2026-09-25): it is apt/dpkg as ROOT under `sudo -n` — this user cannot signal it, and a dpkg interrupted mid-unpack leaves the database needing `dpkg --configure -a` — so `install_timeout` carries `finished` (a promise that settles when the child is really gone: the local child's close, or the device's stream-exit, which the remote run-stream keeps observing for `installMs + holdMs` — its own belt, never the 120 s default that used to report a 2-minute apt as "exited 1" while it kept running). `installXpra(hostId, {onData})` = ONE install per machine (`installs` map; ### Layer 0 apps — apps that survive a rebuilt machine (docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md §3.1 + §3.3; lane custom-app, 2.369.200)

THE WHOLE IDEA IN ONE PARAGRAPH: a machine's system files are not kept when it is rebuilt (a fleet pod is recreated on every update; only the user's home survives), so an app installed with `sudo apt install` is gone after that. An app installed THROUGH VibeSpace is kept: the ONE package slot keeps every `.deb` apt downloaded in `~/.vibespace/apps/debs` (root-owned), completed against the machine IMAGE's own package set, and after the rebuild the server puts the app back by itself — after listen, offline from that local repository (rung 1), online only when the image changed or rung 1 could not (rung 2). The door is the USER's (owner D3): the Desktop apps dialog; an agent can only PROPOSE (one For-you item, `vibespace-app install`), never install. Measured (test-app-install, Debian 12 containers): hello + xterm + a .deb + an adopted cowsay put back on a fresh root filesystem with no network in ~2 s; the next boot is the marker hit (15 ms).

**src/app-manifest.js — PURE (imports nothing, CJS; the daemon bundles it through desktop-serve → app-serve).** The index schema `{v, generation, sources, entries, resolved}` + validateManifest / withEntry / withoutEntry / withSource (the generation bumps on every write; unknown keys dropped); `validateSourceSpec` (https only, a key REQUIRED — a source without Signed-By is refused `bad_source`; the deb822 names its key under `/etc/apt/keyrings/vibespace-<id>.<asc|gpg>`, ROOT-ONLY — never a path under the user's home, which a user-level process could swap); `parseSim` / `parseUris` / `parsePlan` over apt's own words (LC_ALL=C) → `{closure, closureKey, newCount, downloadBytes (the URI lines' exact sizes), installedBytes, origins, canRun, code}` with the NAMED refusals no_facts · no_apt · bad_name · not_found · conflict (the unmet lines quoted) · removes (an install that would REMOVE a package — never) · needs_snap (the closure pulls snapd) · disk (free < installed + 2 GiB on `/`, or < download + 2 GiB on the home — WITH the numbers) · shared (a removal that would take another entry's package) · no_sudo (an ok plan that cannot run: the commands to copy). Measured shape: a Debian 12 security-mirror URI line carries NO hash (`'<url>' <file> <size> ` — a trailing space): `parseUris` takes an empty hash. `parseDesktopFile` (the [Desktop Entry] group only, the unlocalised Name, the spec's Exec quoting, %f/%U… stripped, `%%` a percent, Terminal=true ⇒ `xterm -e …`, NoDisplay / Hidden / not an Application / no Exec ⇒ skipped by name, the row through the CALLER's validateAppRow, id `app.<entry>` for the primary file and `app.<entry>.<stem>` for the others); `parseDpkgStatus` + `dpkgLines` + `dpkgListText` (= the root script's `q` lines BYTE FOR BYTE — the base identity's sha256 is computed over exactly these bytes on both sides) + `dpkgDelta`; `packagesStanza` / `packagesIndex` / `debFileName` (`<pkg>_<version WITHOUT its epoch>_<arch>.deb` — a `file:` source reads Filename as written, never a `%3a`); `cacheVerdict` (closure − base − cache, by package AND version — P15: the cache is judged against the IMAGE's base, never against what this rootfs happens to hold); `replayRungs` (refresh ⇒ 2 · no entries ⇒ nothing · rung 1 failed ⇒ 2 · the marker hit ⇒ nothing · `present` — no marker but every entry's packages installed (`missing` = 0) ⇒ nothing (verify-r1 F4) · no stored base / the base changed ⇒ 2 · else 1); `driftVerdict` (a dpkg run later than VibeSpace's own last run + DRIFT_SLACK_MS — the Post-Invoke marker OR the dpkg status file's own write time, so a plain `dpkg -i` counts (verify-r1 F7) — AND the dpkg set moved, packages the index names excluded); the dpkg set on both sides = every package whose status is INSTALLED, a held one (`hi`) too (verify-r1 F5: `q` used to keep only `ii`, so a held image package read as installed outside VibeSpace and the base sha never matched); THE ROOT SCRIPT `APP_SCRIPT` + `appArgv` + `appCommands` + `parseRunLog` (below). Gate: test-app-manifest (fast). **verify-r1 H1 (2.369.203) — THE PIN:** `sourcePin({host, packages})` = an approved source's apt preferences — `Package: *` from `Pin: origin "<host>"` at `PIN_LOW` 1 (apt_preferences' 0 < P < 100: such a version is taken only when NOTHING installed has that name — a newer build of a package the machine has, or one another source also carries, never wins) + the packages the user approved FROM it (sorted, unique) at `PIN_APPROVED` 500; `pinHost` (the URI's host, no port — measured: `Pin: origin "vs-fixture.test"` matches an `https://vs-fixture.test:8443/repo` source), `originOf(url, sources)` (an approved source when its URI is the URL's prefix up to a "/", else the host), `updatesOf(sim, pk, {debs, sources})` gives each Refresh update `origin` / `source`, `withPins` records parseRunLog's `pins` (`= pin <source> <pkg…>`) on the index's sources as `pin: {packages}` (kept by the schema; root's sys/sources/<id>.pref is what a replay re-creates).

**THE ROOT SCRIPT (`APP_SCRIPT`, one text for every run; nine modes install · deb · remove · replay · replay-online · refresh · adopt · source · source-remove).** Run ONLY through the machine's one package slot as `sudo -n sh -c APP_SCRIPT vs-app <appsDir> <mode> <id> <nonce> -- <args…>`: every name is a POSITION, never interpolated. Order: the id / nonce / mode are checked, then `= run <id> <nonce> <mode>` (every refusal below is attributable to the run), then EVERY positional argument is judged (a package by Debian's rule — an apt OPTION, a `$(…)`, a `;` are `bad-name`; a .deb / key path only under `<appsDir>/staging/`; a sha256 of 64 hex; a source https + plain suites) BEFORE root is even asked — the fast gate runs every refusal as a plain user — then `not-root`, `no-apps-dir` (the user's dir; root never creates it — the plan does, as the user), `apps-dir-not-the-users` (`SUDO_UID`'s passwd home + `/.vibespace/apps`, both `pwd -P` — a process cannot point root at another user's cache). The AUTHORITY root reads is root-owned: `debs/` (the repository) and `sys/{entries,keys,sources,base}` — `own()` refuses a directory that is a link, not root's or group/other-writable (setgid cleared — the fsGroup P3 finding), so a user-level process (an agent runs as the user) can only rearrange what root itself wrote; `sys/entries/<id>.list` (the approved top-level packages) + `.desktop` (their desktop files) are what a replay reinstalls and what the catalog rows are read from — `manifest.json` (user-writable) is the index, never the authority. A .deb / a key is COPIED into the temp dir and re-hashed before root installs it: only the approved bytes. `index()` normalizes file names, writes one stanza each (dpkg-deb -f, blank lines dropped, Filename / Size / SHA256), keeps the newest version per package, rebuilds `Packages`; `fill()` = the closure simulated against `sys/base/status` (the image's dpkg set, captured once per root filesystem — a replay on a fresh one re-takes it) minus what is cached, fetched with `apt-get download` (APT::Sandbox::User=root — P15: `_apt` cannot enter a 0700 home); `finish()` stamps `/var/lib/vibespace/{last-dpkg.list, slot-ended}` (the ephemeral rootfs markers); `apps-replayed` is written ONLY by a replay (either rung) that put EVERY entry back (verify-r1 F4: every run used to write it, so a partial replay was never retried and an install on a fresh rootfs before the boot replay suppressed it for good); `rebase` re-takes the image's base only on a rootfs VibeSpace never ran on (no slot-ended) and the hook `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99vibespace-apps` (DPkg::Post-Invoke touches `dpkg-touched` — the drift tripwire). Rung 1 = a temp sources.list with ONLY `deb [trusted=yes] file:<debs> ./` (+ its own lists dir, no pkgcache files): offline by construction. Rung 2 = the machine's own sources (third-party ones restored from `sys/sources` first) PLUS that same local repository — a `.deb` the user installed exists nowhere else, so an online rung without it could never put that entry back. Per-entry failures are `= entry <id> failed <code>` (never blocking another entry). Facts out: `= delta ± pkg:arch ver` · `= desktop <pkg> <path>` · `= service <pkg> <unit>` · `= deb <pkg> <ver> <arch> <file> <size> <sha256>` · `= base <sha>` · `= entry …` · `= refused <code> …` · `= ok` / `= partial <n>`; exit 0 / 125 (refused) / apt's code. **verify-r1 H1/H2 (2.369.203):** `pins()` runs at the end of EVERY run (`finish`) and before apt in both replay rungs (`restore` = keys + sources + pins — rung 1 too, design §3.3): per `sys/sources/<id>.sources` it writes `sys/sources/<id>.pref` + `/etc/apt/preferences.d/vibespace-<id>.pref` (the PURE sourcePin bytes — test-app-manifest §8c runs pins() itself against the table, a no-pin copy red), its allow-list = every `sys/entries/*.pin` line naming the source. `install` / `deb` / `adopt` attribute BEFORE apt runs (`--print-uris` into an empty archives dir / `download --print-uris`; `from()` = a URL under the source's URI) into `entries/<id>.pin`; `remove` drops it, `source-remove` drops the pin. `grab()` = the ONE read of a user-owned file for deb + source modes (`dd iflag=nofollow,nonblock`, ≤ GRAB_MAX_MB): no `[ -f ] && cp` gap, a FIFO returns at once and the hash refuses it.

**src/app-serve.js — SHARED (fs/path/os/crypto/child_process/https + the two PURE models; the daemon bundles it).** The machine half, `create({home, stateDir, env, binOnPath, installState, …})` — held by desktop-serve as `ds.apps` (its `stateDir` = the keeper's data dir = THE SAME slot as the xpra install). `plan({kind: search|apt|deb|source|source-remove|remove|refresh|adopt|replay, …})` simulates as the USER (bounded async children, LC_ALL=C): on the system's own apt lists when it has them, else the user's own (`~/.cache/vibespace/apt`, refreshed past 6 h, one in flight — a container image ships none); a .deb is copied into `staging/` (0700) and bound by its sha256 (dpkg-deb -I names its maintainer scripts); a source's key is fetched over https (≤ 1 MiB, ≤ 3 redirects) and its OpenPGP fingerprints computed here (`keyFingerprints`: v4 SHA-1 over 0x99‖len16‖body, v5/v6 SHA-256 — checked against gpg's own on two real public keyrings); the plan carries the argv (its own apps dir, a fresh nonce) + the commands + the slot's state (`install.installing` — a running one is FOLLOWED). The RECORD ops read the slot's own log (keyed by the nonce; `not_run` when another install held the slot, `refused` by its code) and the ROOT-OWNED `sys/entries` (a user-written list or a forged log line is never a row — `not_recorded`), then write the index through writeJsonAtomic (0600; a corrupt file set aside as `manifest.json.corrupt-<ms>`, bytes kept). THE ENTRY ID a run writes under keys ROOT's record, which the run REPLACES — so it is chosen against root's own `sys/entries` (`entryIdFor`: root's record of exactly these packages keeps its id; an index or caller id only when root holds nothing else under it), never the user-writable index alone; a package source root already holds (`sys/sources/<id>.sources`) is "already added" whatever the index says (verify-r1 F1: an agent could edit manifest.json so an approved install of sl replaced hello's root record, the digest unchanged). `status()` = the index + the catalog rows + the replay decision (the stored base sha vs the PURE reader's over /var/lib/dpkg/status; `replay.missing` = root's entries not installed here) + per entry `uncached` (its packages with no saved .deb and not in root's base — the replay can never put them back; the row says so, verify-r1 F6) + the drift verdict + updates / last refreshed + facts (memoised 30 s). `catalogRows()` / `refreshCatalog()` (signature = the entries dir's listing + mtimes) → desktop-serve's `registry()` serves them beside DEFAULT_REGISTRY (`app-missing` when the exec is not on PATH). `recordUserKind` = `vibespace-app add` (uv / npm / an AppImage — in HOME, nothing to replay). `runAppOp(apps, op, params)` = the six ops' wire (never a throw). **2.369.203:** the .deb plan reads the user's file ONCE (`readHashed`, exported: an O_NONBLOCK open, type + size judged on the fd, copied to staging while hashed — never a libuv thread parked on a FIFO); the Refresh plan runs `--print-uris` too and names each update's origin against ROOT's sources (`rootSources()` — sys/sources, never the index); every record (entry / remove / refresh / source) mirrors the run's `= pin` lines into the index.

**src/app-system.js — PURE (imports nothing, CJS) — Layer 1, the app system (docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md §3.2 + §9).** Identity (`parseIdentity` / `identityText`, refusals no-identity · bad-identity · contract), `rebaseVerdict` (ok · rebase · blocked on arch), `systemView` (GET /api/apps `appSystem`: canCreate · interrupted · rebase · canRollback · blocked), `auditVerdict`, rows + THE EXPORT TABLE (`sysRows` → `sys.<entry>` rows running their shim by absolute path, `binExports` for CLI executables, `shimName`, `resolveTarget`), the shim (`shimText` / `shimVersionOf` / `shimPlan` — only our own shims are ever written or removed), `SYS_SCRIPT` (THE root script of the app system: create · install · deb · remove · refresh · repair · rebase · rollback · drop-prev, run by the ONE package slot; `sysArgv` / `sysCommands`), `INSTALL_SCRIPT` + `SUDOERS_TEXT` + `ENV_KEEP` + `ROOT_COMMANDS` (one spelling with the helper; test-app-system pins them equal).

**src/app-system-serve.js — SHARED (fs/path + the PURE app-system / app-manifest).** The machine half held by app-serve as `sys`: the identity read as the user (root-owned, canonical), root's entries inside the userland, the catalog rows + shims in `~/.vibespace/sysroot/bin`, `view()` (the boot step after listen when `VIBESPACE_APP_SYSTEM` is set: INSTALL_SCRIPT through `sudo -n`, then `dpkg --audit` through the helper), `retarget` (an apt / .deb plan INTO the app system), `removePlan` / `refreshPlan` / `sysPlan` (Set up · Repair · Rebase · Roll back · Delete the old one).

**src/server/apps-engine.js + src/server/apps-wiring.js + src/routes/apps.js — ORCH.** The engine: `propose()` (an agent's — planned on the machine FIRST; a refused plan is never filed; the same conversation × machine × request again answers the OPEN proposal (`again`, asked before the plan and after its await — verify-r1 F2), and an app root already keeps with nothing to install is refused `nothing`; the why loses every hidden / reordering character at the door (THE one set — verify-r1 F8); ONE For-you item (keyed by the proposal id — user-todos ACTION_IDENTITY `app-install`, so another proposal of the same words never re-points this one's Install), origin `apps`, action `{type:'app-install', id, host, kind}`, words as structure; the proposal kept in data/app-proposals.json), `run()` (the user's press: `access.installPackage(host, {what:'app:<kind>:<label>', planOpts: request, expectDigest})` — the machine's own plan through the registered PLANNER, the digest binding commands + packages + source + the CLOSURE — then the record op; a proposal's item resolved by `apps`, never read as the user's Not now), `reject()` (Not now; also the item dismissed / ✓ without Install), `wait()` (≤ 100 s, answers each MOVE; a terminal answer takes the stashed copy back), `afterListen()` (the boot replay: marker hit = nothing; rung 1 then rung 2; ONE For-you notice naming what did not come back), `decorate()` (an installed app's greyed row: `restoring` while a replay runs there, `restore-failed` from the last replay), helpers (data/app-proposals.json `helpers`). The wiring = server.js's ONE line + the replay after listen; `VIBESPACE_APPS_STUB` (a module standing in for the machine + the slot) is honoured ONLY by a throwaway server (`throwawayRoot`). Gate: test-apps-engine (fast), test-app-install (heavy), test-apps-ui (heavy). **verify-r1 H3 (2.369.203):** `afterListen` WAITS a busy package slot out (`busy`, or a followed run's `not_run`: every 15 s, ≤ 10 min — `sleep` / `busyWaitMs` / `busyPollMs` injectable) and then runs the same rung; only a slot still busy past the bound fails it (ONE notice, as before).

### scripts/test-desktop-serve.mjs + scripts/test-desktop-remote.mjs — the lane C1 gates

**Lane fleet-image-2 (2026-10-01) — the suite never hangs on a machine whose pid 1 does not reap.** `launch(…, {killAfter})` spawns the launcher as its own process group and the bound kills the WHOLE group: killing the shell alone left its `tail --pid` follower holding the pipe, so the result (read at the pipe's close) never came while the followed runner was a zombie. The killedLauncher leg reads the orphaned runner's `/proc/<pid>/stat`: a runner in state Z ⇒ a named SKIP naming pid 1's command (`runuser` on the pre-3.6 fleet images) — never a hang, never an unexplained red; pA's orphaned follower is ended too. Measured: under `unshare -pf --mount-proc runuser …` (runuser as pid 1, the pod's shape) the lane's suite passes with that skip in 28 s; master's suite there HANGS (killed at 120 s); on a reaping box the leg's assertion runs as before.

**2.369.191 (the 2.369.189 mirror red — r5 L4 read 1002 ms against a literal `< 1000`):** test-desktop-serve (197, ~18 s) carries NO literal wall-clock upper bound. `waitOf` reads each launcher wait's poll and cap from `M.INSTALL_LAUNCHER` (spelled once, asserted): the pidfile wait 200 × 50 ms, the lock wait 400 × 50 ms; `AT_ONCE_MS` = ½ × the pidfile cap (5 s — the L4 control is killed AT it, so the slack is also the control's cost). `launch(…, {polls: true})` / `withPolls(env)` put a counting `sleep` first on PATH (`$VS_POLLS`, one line per call, then the real sleep) = how many polls a launcher sat out. L4: no pidfile + no exit file + `1 ≤ polls < cap` ⇒ the wait left by `[ -e /proc/$b ]` (the runner's death — the loop's only other exit) + `ms < AT_ONCE_MS`; CONTROL: the copy without `/proc/$b` killed at the bound still polling, the runner's refusal in its log, polls past the fix's. L5 / no flock / read-only / the L3 squat: `polls === 0` (refused before any wait); L8: the recorded exit 125 + polls < cap; M1: code 0 (only possible before its `M1_FIX_MS` deadline); the SIGKILLed-holder leg: first run < ½ × the lock-wait cap; §4 host_needs_daemon and §5's failing bootstrap: `beforeTurn` (settled before a setImmediate armed beside it — no timer, no I/O; the bootstrap asked once, never the deadline's words); §5's connect deadline: its own words `not responding within <round(connectMs/1000)>s`, lower bound only; install past installMs: the code is the evidence, lower bound only. Lower bounds on deadlines the leg set use one `EARLY_MS` (100: a libuv timer is armed against the cached loop time). ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants "A GATE BOUND WAS THE RUNNER'S SPEED".

**Lane D (b):** test-desktop-remote §7 gains the app-default leg — the hub keeper's launch with `scaleChoice: 1.5` to the real daemon: the `launch` op is `{body, settings}` with the field INSIDE body, the device's own record (its ~/.vibespace/desktop-apps.json) runs at 1.5× / 144 dpi with origin 'app' over the hub's explicit Settings value '1', GDK_SCALE=1 in the app's environ on the device.

**Verify r5 (2026-09-25):** test-desktop-serve (196, ~16 s) — the lock root is DERIVED like the launcher's (`LOCKROOT` = `/run/user/<uid>` when it is a writable directory this user owns, else `/tmp/vibespace-<uid>`) while the suite keeps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` a scratch dir, so every lock assertion also proves the variable is ignored; every lock this suite's launchers named (one per scratch state dir — the sha1 of its realpath, never production's) is removed at exit. §10 adds: **L1** `sameSecond(Mod)` — an install that exits 100 in the first tenth of a second leaving `sleep 1.5` on fd 9, a second start spawned the moment the first runner's pidfile is gone (same second as the exit, the lock held by that child — both recorded as evidence, ≤ 3 attempts when the box was too slow to keep them aligned) ⇒ it RUNS its own install (exit 7, one run); CONTROL = `date +%s` + `-ge` ⇒ the stale 100, no run. **L3** three starts on ONE state dir with `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` a scratch dir / unset / a gone dir ⇒ ONE lock under LOCKROOT (the exit file + installState); CONTROL = the r4 line ⇒ two locks; a fake uid (an `id` shim) ⇒ `/tmp/vibespace-<n>` created 0700; a regular file there ⇒ 125 naming it (CONTROL: without the check only the generic "cannot be opened"); a directory owned by another uid ⇒ 125 naming it — root only, SKIP with evidence otherwise; a non-numeric `id -u` ⇒ 125 named. **L4** a `setsid` shim that closes fd 9 ⇒ 125 in ~0.2 s with the runner's line naming the lock, the lock free; CONTROL = the wait without `[ -e /proc/$b ]`, still waiting at 3 s (killed — our launcher). The r3 L5 control changed with it: without the setsid check the refusal is now the shell's bare "setsid: not found" at once (the L4 bound), never the package. test-desktop-remote §8: the device's `installing.lock` is `lockPathOf(<home>/.vibespace)` under LOCKROOT, never under the daemon's scratch `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`; its lock files are removed at cleanup.

**Verify r4 (2026-09-25):** test-desktop-serve (184, ~16 s) — the whole suite sets `process.env.XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` to a scratch dir (every launcher it starts names its lock there, never in the real runtime dir; the /tmp sub-legs remove their own free lock files). §10's r3 lock-dir legs (dead owner, ownerless 2 s wait, live owner, empty-probe blind `sed`, the `mkdir -p` control) are REPLACED: **M4 at volume** — `five(M)` over an empty dir 40× (8 trials at a time, beside every other leg), ONE runner every trial, four followers, all exit 3, the lock free after each (each install runs until the four others FOLLOW it — a release file the test writes, 1.5 s at most — never a fixed sleep that a loaded box's event loop can outlast: a first draft's 1.2 s install ended before a starved check under load and the second start rightly ran a new one); **widened** 20× (a `setsid` shim +0.3 s = the lock → pidfile window, a `flock` shim +0–60 ms random = who takes it and when a loser probes); **killed install** 10× (a previous install's runner holds the lock — fd 9 → the lock file — then its SESSION is SIGKILLed ⇒ the lock free at once, five starts ⇒ one runner starting < 1.5 s after); **killed launcher** (the launcher's fd 9 read once its `tail` child exists — the close is the line after the fork, so the runner's pidfile alone does not order it; SIGKILLed ⇒ its runner lives on holding the lock and a concurrent start follows it, and only then is the install released: it answers exit 4, the second install never run); **a lock held by a non-install** (`flock K sh -c 'sleep 0.8; date > end'` — the holder stamps its end BEFORE it releases; node's own `close` event arrives after the kernel already freed the lock) ⇒ a start waits, and its install starts after that stamp; **no flock** ⇒ 125 < 1 s naming util-linux, nothing created; L8 now asserts the RUNNER's refusal through the launcher (its `cut` stub blinds only `-f20`). ### src/server/desktop-app-keeper.js — THE DESKTOP-APP LIFECYCLE (§2 row 3)

**§7.9 — THE AFTER-EDIT SIGNAL (2026-09-27):** `notify()` (every machine commit + every remote ingest) ends with **`signalFileChanges()`**: a record with `file` + `fileChanged === true` in a terminal state ⇒ ONE `broadcast({type:'file-changed', host, path, mtime, by:'desktop-app', appId, label})` — `host` null for this machine, the paired machine's id otherwise (the explorer's / the code editor's host) — stamped `fileSignalledAt` on the local record (saved by the machine's next commit via `markDirty`) or on the hub's row of a remote record, so it is never said twice (a restart, a re-broadcast). An unchanged file says nothing. A paired machine whose agent predates the office rows answers a document launch "unknown appId" — the remote `launch` names it `host_needs_daemon` ("reconnect the machine to upgrade it").

**Lane C2 (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5):** THE REGISTRY OF A PAIRED MACHINE'S APPS (D8: the device holds each record in its own ~/.vibespace/desktop-apps.json; the hub keeps what it last SAW). New deps: `access` (() => the desktop-access layer, late-bound — it needs this keeper's machine half), `hostLabel(hostId)` (the host record's name — a DISPLAY string), `remoteHosts()` (the machines dialed in now, asked at boot). The hub's copy lives in `data/desktop-apps-hosts.json` (`REMOTE_FILE`, writeJsonAtomic) — NEVER inside data/desktop-apps.json: the local machine keeper owns that file whole and would judge a remote record by THIS machine's pids and reap it. Per host: `apps` (the device's own views, `hostId:'local'` = the device's view of itself), `hub` rows (`lastInputAt` — the IDLE verdict is the hub's, a device never sees the bridge's input — and `appTitle` for a blocked pane), `online`, `lastError`, `www` (the device's xpra html5 tree). `launch(body, {host})` / `stop` / `keepAlive` (async for a remote id) / `noteDesktopSize` (⇒ the `fit` op) / `windows` / `relaunch` (the device's ONE relaunch through the op; the seat carried the moment the answer is back) go THROUGH the op with the hub's settings (`DS.SETTING_KEYS`) carried; a launch/relaunch is FOLLOWED every `REMOTE_FOLLOW_MS` (400 ms) until it settles (≤ `REMOTE_SETTLE_MS` 45 s — the window never waits a whole tick). Views: `remoteView` re-labels (`hostId` = the hub's host id, `hostLabel`), lays the hub rows over, and shows `HOST_OFFLINE_STATE` (+ `lastKnownState`, `hostError`) when the machine does not answer; `listApps()` = the machine's list + the remote views (IDENTICAL to the machine's own answer when no remote record exists — local byte-identity), `get(id)` any machine, `liveRecords()` THIS machine only (the browser keeper's ONE ceiling and the window-targets engine count this machine), `streamTarget(id)` = `{kind, port, hostId}` for a ready remote record on an answering machine (null otherwise ⇒ the bridge 404s — never a connect to that port number here). The tick: after the machine's own tick, `syncRemoteAll()` re-asks (`status`, single flight per host) every machine with a live record — one that did not answer at most every `REMOTE_OFFLINE_RETRY_MS` (30 s) — then per ready record: the idle verdict (expired ⇒ `stop` THROUGH the op, why idle), the device's latest sample judged ONCE (its instant) by the same `reportSample` (report only — the 2.369.171 law), the blocked pane's title refresh. A machine no longer on the instance (`unsupported-host`) ⇒ its records dropped. `adoptAll()` = this machine's adoption, then `adoptRemote()` IN THE BACKGROUND (a slow or dead link never holds this machine's apps): every machine the registry remembers + every dialed-in one is asked `list`, adopted by host AND id (an id another machine holds is ignored by name); one that does not answer keeps its records offline. `keeper.local` = this keeper with `get` / `listApps` answering this machine only (the window-targets engine's world — an agent acts through xdotool / AT-SPI HERE). `xpraWwwFor(id)` = the hub's own xpra html5 tree, else the paired machine's (read through its agent). Gate: test-desktop-serve §7, test-desktop-remote §7, test-desktop-xpra-window §13; test-desktop-app-keeper §6's host leg now asserts the no-access refusal (503 `host_unavailable`) instead of v1's 400.

**LANE C1 (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5) — THE KEEPER IS TWO FILES.** The machine half (bring-up, identity, teardown, stop, the belt, windows, adoption, launch, the sample cadence, the record file — rules 1–10) moved VERBATIM to the SHARED src/desktop-serve.js; THIS file keeps the hub's registry + POLICY: the x5 viewer election (unchanged), the IDLE verdict (`idleVerdict`, called by the machine's tick where the old tick asked it), the resource REPORT (`reportSample` — the §54 sampled block: verdict, report level, the live row, the notice; `guard` + `live` are cleared by the machine's teardown through `onTeardown`), the x5 title refresh (`readyTick`), `relaunch` = `machine.relaunch(id, body, {onSuccessor: carrySeat})` (ONE implementation in desktop-serve.js — the seat carried between the successor's record and the old stop; a browser's profile carried, 2.369.176; `startDeferred` re-exported), the view (`machineView` + `live` + `idle`, same key order) and the broadcast (`onCommit` ⇒ `notify`). Device #0's machine keeper runs IN-PROCESS and shares ONE store (`store.apps` reads through `machine._store()`); the returned API is the same names, delegating, plus `machine` (desktop-access's local rung runs against THAT object). Every record carries `hostId` (`'local'` for this machine: M.newRecord + migration `2026-09-desktop-apps-host-key`). Remote records in this registry, the bridge's `forwardPort`, the machine choice and the install rung are lane C2. Everything below that describes a machine act now happens in desktop-serve.js, verbatim.

**2026-09-25 — RESOURCES ARE REPORTED, NEVER A STOP (the owner's ruling: "这个keeper到底是干啥的，没必要别乱加会影响使用的feature"; the Chrome desktop-app incident, docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md). SUPERSEDES every "runaway guard ⇒ stop + park" sentence below.** The tick still samples the WHOLE session set every GUARD_SAMPLE_MS (rule 5 + the rule-10 marker census) — now AWAITED (`display.sessionSample` is async; the slot is claimed before the await, a record stopped meanwhile is left alone) — and judges it with `RG.resourceVerdict(s, …, {limits: RG.guardFor(rec, limits)})` (a browser row by the browser numbers). What it DOES: the live row `live.set(id, {cpuPct, memBytes, memMetric, rssBytes (deprecated), pids, over, since, sampledAt})` (the view's `live` — the window's chip reads `memBytes` + `memMetric`, the `over` sentence is its tooltip); `serverNotice('desktop-app-resource:<id>:<crossing>', RG.resourceNoticeText(…), {level:'warn'})` when `RG.reportTransition(g.report, v, {now, limits})` says `notify` (a new crossing, or r2's re-send of an undelivered one — the answer goes back through `RG.reportDelivery`; hysteresis + the hourly floor live in the PURE level; the `serverNotice` dep, wired in server.js, returns the clients reached); log + telemetry only on `fire`; telemetry `desktop-app-resource` (value = MB); a journal line "is over the reporting threshold … — reported, left running"; `memGuardOffLine` once when memory cannot be judged. What it NEVER does: stop, park (the `runawayParkedUntil` store map is gone — dropped on load, voided on disk by migration 2026-09-runaway-parks-void through `reshapeStore(fn)`, a MIGRATIONS-ONLY door: reshape the in-memory store + commit, because this keeper loads at construction and a file edit beside it is lost at its next save), refuse a launch, or remove a profile. `registry()` rows carry no `parkedUntil`; `stop()` has no `runaway` transition. PROFILES (F, the same ruling): `retireProfile` removes a browser row's profile only when PURE `M.profileRetireVerdict(rec)` says a PERSON ended the session (Stop / relaunch / the app's own exit / no app ever ran); an IDLE-OUT still stops the session (`desktop.idleTimeoutMin` unchanged — the owner is asked separately) but KEEPS the profile with `profileKept` + `profileKeptWhy` on the record, and the boot retirement pass asks the same verdict. Gate: test-desktop-app-keeper §5 (heavy: a CPU burner REPORTED, still running, one notice, a second launch served, nothing parked, the user's Stop ends it; a 6.2 GB PSS sampler over a real session reported + the notice text; r2: a sampler alternating 6.2 / 0.9 GB over ten samples ⇒ ONE notice, and a serverNotice answering 0 twice ⇒ the SAME key three times then silence; a stop-on-over COPY ends the session = the control) + §8(d)/r3d/r4c (a child / reaped / setsid'd burner REPORTED, their controls never over) + §18(c2) (an idle-out keeps the fake browser's profile, the next boot too).

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2): THE WINDOW CENSUS AT AN APP EXIT.** `onPartExit('app')` still flips the record to `exited` at once (`fail`), then ONE census while X is still up — `windowsLeftAtExit(rec)`: `enumerateWindows` on the record's OWN display (null on the shared singleton, with no display, or when the census fails or outlives `EXIT_CENSUS_MS` = 2000 — a warn names it) through `seamlessWindows` (xpra) or `M.appWindows` (the other rungs) into `M.windowsLeftCount` — stamped as `rec.windowsAtExit`, THEN the teardown, THEN the commit that broadcasts it. So every client decides "the app exited ⇒ close my window" from the same keeper fact (a blocked pane has no protocol windows to count). MEASURED (xpra 6.5.3): xpra keeps a managed app window inside a Corral wrapper that is MAPPED only while a client is connected — with no client the forking launcher's surviving xterm read viewable=false, so on the xpra rung the census counts the seamless rows' EXISTENCE (`mapped: null`), elsewhere X's viewability.
