LOW-4: a join whose PANE already holds the seat through an OLDER socket moves the seat to the newest one at once (a pane is one client — the older may be a silent drop the pings need two rounds to see, 29.8 s measured); the bridge then cuts the old socket. LOW-2: `refreshAppTitle(id, why)` — on the xpra rung (no keeper fit ⇒ no fitted title) the RECORD's `appTitle` is read from X through `windows(id)` + PURE `appMainWindow(rows, {seamless:true})` when a BLOCKED seat appears, at a takeover, and on the tick while one exists (≤ every `XPRA_TITLE_EVERY_MS` 10 s on the tick, ≤ 1/s off it; in-flight dedup; an unreadable name keeps the last; fire-and-forget) — a blocked pane has no protocol session to name the app. Gate: test-desktop-viewers §5. **2.369.176 BROWSER RELAUNCH CARRIES THE PROFILE** (since the C1 rebase the code below lives in src/desktop-serve.js — launch's `deferred` map, relaunch's browser branch, stop's move — and the hub keeper's relaunch passes its seat carry as `onSuccessor`): `relaunch` on a browser record mints the successor id and records it with `deferBringUp` (every refusal first, the running browser untouched), names it on the old record, sets `rec.profileCarryTo` and stops the old one (`why: relaunch` — stop's reasons stay §54b's closed list); after every part is verified gone the profile dir is MOVED onto `profileDirOf(successor)` (`profileCarriedTo` on the old record; `retireProfile` skips it; a failed move is said by name on both records and the successor starts empty), then `startDeferred(successor)`. Gate: test-desktop-app-keeper §18 (c3) on the real xpra rung + its no-carry control.

**Round 3, A3 (2.369.166 — docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.4): THE SCALE PICK AND THE RELAUNCH.** `launch(body, opts)` picks the scale ONCE through PURE `scalePick` (the setting, or `opts.scaleChoice` — a relaunch's row) over the request's `dpr` + `uiScale`, on the xpra stream only (a whole-display rung stays 1× with `scaleOrigin` null), and records `scaleOrigin` + `scaleFrom` beside `scale` / `dpi`. `relaunch(id, body)` = the per-window Scale ▸: the request validated, `relaunchVerdict` (running, xpra, not a browser — a browser's profile is its session's; also refused while stopping / already replaced), then the SUCCESSOR launched FIRST with `opts.replacing` (the one it replaces is left out of `capVerdict` — a keeper at its ceiling can still change a window's scale; a refusal leaves the running app untouched), `rec.replacedBy = next.id` COMMITTED, then `stop(id, {why:'relaunch'})` (`lastError` names the successor). So every client learns the successor no later than the stop — the window follows it instead of closing (measured on the real xpra rung, xterm: the old record's first broadcast after the relaunch already names the successor, the one carrying `exited` is the fourth; the successor ready 1366 ms after the call). Gate: heavy test-desktop-app-keeper §20 (xterm on the real xpra rung: dpr 2 × 1.25 ⇒ 2.5×/120, measured as GDK_SCALE in the app's /proc environ + Xft.dpi through `xrdb -query` on its display; relaunch at 1.5 ⇒ GDK_SCALE 1 + 144, the old one's pids gone, broadcast order; refusals; the cap; the vnc-display rung; CONTROL = a keeper copy with the pre-A3 pick ⇒ 2× / 96 for the same client). **A r1 (2.369.166) — THE RELAUNCH CARRIES THE SEAT.** `carrySeat(fromId, toId)` runs BEFORE `replacedBy` is committed: the old window's active pane (or the pane its grace holds) becomes a TIMERLESS grace on the successor's viewer set (the `desktop-app-viewers` broadcast names it active at once), so every other client that retargets from the `replacedBy` broadcast attaches BLOCKED, and the relaunching pane — same pane key, a new socket — takes the seat through `viewerJoined`'s grace branch; the returned `arm()` runs in the `finally` after `stop(old)` (a failed stop too) and starts `RELAUNCH_SEAT_MS` = 10 s (`relaunchSeatMs` option) for that pane to attach — then the ordinary re-election. Nobody active on the old window, or somebody already active on the successor ⇒ nothing carried. Before r1 the relaunching client learned its successor only from the HTTP answer (after the old session's teardown) and ALWAYS lost the first-attach election to the client that had been blocked — the user who chose the scale was blocked on their own window. Measured on the real rung: the other client attached during the teardown with pane pL already named active; the relauncher attached after the answer and was active with no Resume. Gate: test-desktop-viewers §6 (fast: the order H-then-L, the unarmed hold, the armed expiry, nothing to carry, CONTROL = a keeper without the carry elects H, the wiring pin) + heavy test-desktop-app-keeper §20 (b) + heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §11 (4).

### src/server/desktop-stream.js — THE ONE WS BRIDGE (§2 row 4)

**THE RELAYS PER STREAM KIND (rv-desktop-apps F-B4, lane dc-seams-desktop 2026-10-05):** the bridge keeps what every kind shares — auth, the 501/404/409 refusals, the x5 seats + reconcile, the stats, the named closes + lastClose, the keepalive arm it hands over (`KA`, §70 reads the relays as the bridge's text), the oversize close (1009) and the ws message cap (`WS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` = the largest declared relay cap + 8 = 16 MiB + 8), the netem knobs — and asks `STREAM_RELAYS[target.kind]` (own rows only; an unregistered kind is refused 501 by name). Moved VERBATIM:
  stream-relay-rfb.js   — RFB: the client→server classifier (RFB_INPUT_TYPES, RFB_FIXED_LEN, rfbInputSieve), RFB_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, and `bridgeRfb` inside `bridgeOf(ctx)` (ctx = the bridge's shared state, destructured by the same names, so the body is the old text).
  stream-relay-xpra.js  — xpra: the XPRA_* packet tables + held kinds, xpraPacketType / xpraStrings / xpraInputSieve, XPRA_MAX_PACKET_BYTES, `bridgeXpra`. Until xpra answers a hello only the hello goes up (e2-canvas). Declares `netem: true` (the dev-only knob is a cell, not a kind test).
  stream-relays.js      — THE REGISTRATION: one `require('./stream-relay-<kind>.js')` line per kind, keyed by each row's own STREAM_KIND. A row: { STREAM_KIND, serverName, maxMessageBytes, netem, bridgeOf }.
  src/lib/stream-views.js — the CLIENT twin: one line per view module keyed by its STREAM_KIND; `viewOf(kind)` (an unregistered kind falls to STATUS_KIND = the RFB view, as before); desktop-app-window.js makes every view through it and names no view module.
Mutant controls that patch a relay load a bridge copy whose registry carries the patched relay (test-desktop-app-keeper `relayMutant`); scripts/test-stream-relays.mjs is the fake-third-kind proof.

**THE LIVENESS RULE (lane desktop-keepalive, userW inc-muoshmqn-dect — "no pong for 40000 ms" six times in 12 h, 2026-10-02).** The keepalive was already a WebSocket PROTOCOL ping (`ws.ping()` — the browser's network stack answers it; a hidden tab's throttled timers never touch it), so the incident's first guess (an app-level pong frozen in a background tab) was wrong. MEASURED (test-desktop-stream-keepalive §6): the ping frame is queued BEHIND every byte already in the send buffer (up to WS_HIGH_WATER = 8 MiB before the RFB side pauses) — a live browser reading at 512 KiB/s behind a full queue never saw one ping and was cut as dead; on a pod reached over a slow link that is the 40–80 s cut. Now ONE `keepAlive(ws, {pingMs, onDead})` runs on both bridges and judges every round with the exported PURE `livenessVerdict`: a pong OR bytes FROM the browser (a reading RFB client asks for the next update after every one it draws; an xpra client acks frames) ⇒ alive; bytes the KERNEL accepted while a backlog waited (`bytesWritten − writableLength` — Node's `bytesWritten` alone counts what still sits in the socket's buffer, measured: a queued 2-byte ping moved it on a dead path) ⇒ draining; else silent; `SILENT_ROUNDS_TO_CUT` = 2 silent rounds ⇒ terminated and NAMED `no pong for N ms and nothing acknowledged`. Control: a patched copy with the 2.369.118 pong-only rule cuts the same live reader.

**Verify r2 (2026-09-25, F1 CRITICAL) — THE SOCKET PARKED ON THE FORWARD LISTENS FOR ERRORS.** handleUpgrade's REMOTE branch waits on the forward (4–600 ms) with the accepted socket in hand; node's http server removed its 'error' listener at 'upgrade' and ws adds one only inside `wss.handleUpgrade` (after the forward), so a viewer that RESET meanwhile was an unhandled 'error' ⇒ server.js `uncaughtException` ⇒ `process.exit(1)` — the whole hub (measured: remote path 0 listeners + uncaught ECONNRESET; local 1; a FIN none). `parkedError` (warn + destroy) is attached BEFORE the park; the socket's 'close' / the destroyed check releases the forward exactly once; right before `upgrade()` it is removed — ws attaches its own synchronously at the top of handleUpgrade — so the live socket carries exactly what a local one does. Gate: test-desktop-serve §8 `rst` (+ control). kb-bugfix-invariants "A VIEWER'S RESET DURING THE PAIRED-MACHINE FORWARD…".

**Lane C2 (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.5):** THE ONLY CHANGE lane C made here: `streamEndpointFor(target)` — a target on THIS machine ⇒ `{port}` SYNCHRONOUSLY (the pre-C2 path, byte-identical), a target with `hostId` (a paired machine's app, resolveTarget answering the keeper's `streamTarget`) ⇒ a Promise of the hub forward's loopback port (new dep `forwardPort(hostId, port)` = desktop-access.forwardPort, reference-counted: each socket holds one reference, released once when it closes); no forward wired ⇒ refused `host_unavailable` ⇒ the upgrade answers 502 "Machine unreachable"; a socket destroyed while the forward opened releases it at once. The reference rides the SOCKET's own `close` too (C2 verify fix, 2026-09-25): a viewer that HALF-closed while the forward resolved is not yet destroyed, and ws 8's completeUpgrade then drops the handshake without calling back (`!socket.readable || !socket.writable` ⇒ destroy), so `ws.once('close', release)` was never registered and the forward kept a ref for good (its listener never closed when the last real viewer left) — now `socket.once('close', release)` + a readable/writable guard before the upgrade; release stays idempotent (exactly once). The two upstream connects take the endpoint's port; x5 seats, backpressure, pings, named closes and the clipboard / input policy are untouched — the protocol is end to end (an ANONYMOUS socket is still a watch seat: the real-device leg had to name its viewer to type). Every socket takes a SEAT (`?viewer=` or a minted `anon-<n>`, `?pane=` the window's public key) and is kept in `conns`; `refresh(id)` / `refreshAll()` re-apply (the keeper's viewer listener + every lease broadcast call them). BLOCKED = NO upstream at all (no ws to xpra, no TCP to the VNC server): nothing is relayed either way, its packets are dropped (`stats.blocked`) except its HELLO (`XPRA_HELLO_HOLD_BYTES` 256 KiB) and the held kinds, which go first — hello → keymap → display size → geometry — when it becomes active (`sieve.release()`); a socket that becomes blocked while connected is CUT: its upstream closes and the socket closes 4001 `blocked: active on another client` (`stats.cut`; the pane reconnects at once as a blocked viewer — its protocol session was bound to that upstream); watch → active with the upstream open replays the held kinds at once (`strip(EMPTY, true)`); the session ending (resolveTarget null) closes a blocked socket 1001. WATCH = the P9b refused sieve, now with `configure-window` and `unmap-window` OUT of `XPRA_WATCH_TYPES` (read from xpra 6.5.3 seamless.py: `do_process_window_configure` applies ANY non-readonly client's geometry, `_process_window_unmap` unmaps for every client — the r3 open item): `XPRA_GEOMETRY_TYPES` (configure-window) is cut and HELD (≤ 16 KiB, `XPRA_HELD_KINDS` row 3) and replayed after the keymap and the display size. ACTIVE = everything (lifecycle still cut). The rfb twin: blocked ⇒ no TCP (the dormant noVNC waits for the banner), cut = TCP destroyed + 4001.

The hello's own `request: stop|exit|…` is refused by the xpra socket (desktop-display `XPRA_BIND_REFUSALS`) — the bridge never decodes a hello. Gate: test-desktop-apps §8 (the r5 strip as the control) + test-desktop-app-keeper §2 / §14 (the real rung; the r5 bridge as the control).** **r7 (2026-09-22, the two holes r6 reported and left open):** ① THE HELD-BYTES CAP — an authenticated viewer DECLARING a 2 GiB xpra packet and streaming it grew the server by ~1 GB (966 MB measured; the sieve held every incomplete packet's bytes and re-concatenated them per chunk). `XPRA_MAX_PACKET_BYTES` = 16 MiB = xpra's OWN client-packet limit (net/constants.py `MAX_PACKET_SIZE`, set on every client connection by server/core.py `accept_protocol` — a bigger one xpra refuses, so nothing legitimate is cut; it bounds what a VIEWER sends — draws flow the other way under the upstream's 64 MiB maxPayload). The declared size is judged the moment the header is readable (within the chunk that carries it); an incomplete packet + the raw chunks waiting for it may hold at most one largest packet (+ header); past either the sieve sets `oversize {declared, held, cap, what}`, RELEASES everything it held and stops for good, and the bridge closes THAT viewer 1009 `packet-too-large` (`closeOversize`: one warn line, `stats().oversize`, the close line names it; terminated 2 s later if it ignores the close frame) — its own upstream connection ends as on any close, the xpra server and the other viewers never see it. RFB has no packet framing, but ONE client message declares its own length — ClientCutText (u32; negative = the extended clipboard, judged by magnitude) — held the same way: `RFB_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` = 16 MiB (Xvnc's MaxCutText defaults to 262144, libvncserver/x11vnc closes a client over 1 MB; every other message is bounded by its type). The browser→bridge WebSocket takes at most `WS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` = 16 MiB + 8 per message (`maxPayload`; the ws default of 100 MiB is buffered before a sieve sees a header) — its `WS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE_LENGTH` is the same named close (`wsOversize`). Incomplete bytes are kept as a LIST while `need` says the next chunk cannot complete them (joined once — a 16 MiB packet in 256 messages: 11 ms). ② THE KEYMAP FENCE — measured on the real rung: a Watch viewer's `keyboard-config` reprogrammed the display's X keymap (keycode 250 XF86Prev_VMode → ydiaeresis within 2 s), because xpra 6.5.3 APPLIES a client's keymap (`set_all_keycodes`) whenever no other keyboard client is connected, and that keymap is shared state the holder / an agent's xdotool types through. `XPRA_KEYMAP_TYPES` (keyboard-config, keymap-changed) left `XPRA_WATCH_TYPES`: a refused viewer's are cut. The picture does not need them — MEASURED: hello → new-window → the first draw ~100 ms after its map-window with no keymap packet at all (xpra delays the hello's own keymap, `XPRA_DELAY_KEYBOARD_DATA` default true, so a hello programs nothing). An allowed viewer's keymap packets pass as before. (r7 kept the display-size packets as watch types; r8 fenced them, below.) LOW-3 — only a NAMED socket (`?viewer=`) joins the election; an ANONYMOUS one (the hosted upstream page, a script) is a read-only WATCH seat on a governed stream (`viewerSeats.state(id, null)` answering anything but `free`) — never elected, never blocked, never in the broadcast (it used to be seated `anon-<n>` and could take the ACTIVE seat). A CUT socket leaves the election at once (`leaveOnCut`, deferred one turn — the cut runs inside the keeper's broadcast) instead of after its close handshake (up to the ws library's 30 s on a dead peer), so neither the grace's end nor LOW-4 can re-elect it. `?prev=<pane>` (`prevOf`) is handed to `join` — a hint for the keeper's grace, never an identity. **THE INPUT POLICY (P9b, design-agent-browser-v2 §4.3 / §6.6 — the `window-live` form of this bridge, 2026-09-21).** A client names itself with `?viewer=<id>` at the upgrade (`viewerOf(url)`, `VIEWER_RE` = 1–64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, else null = anonymous as before); `create({inputPolicy, onViewerLeft})` — `inputPolicy(id, viewerId)` is asked for every client chunk and applied per MESSAGE: `rfbInputSieve().strip(chunk, allowInput)` walks the SAME parser as `feed` and returns `{inputs, dropped, relay}` where `relay` is the chunk with its input messages (KeyEvent / PointerEvent / ClientCutText / QEMU key) CUT OUT when `allowInput` is false — a FramebufferUpdateRequest riding the same frame still reaches the server, so the picture never freezes on a refused click; complete units only (a message split across chunks waits for its tail — the server could not act on half of it; a NON-input message split across chunks relays whole once complete); an `opaque` stream is all-or-nothing (a refused chunk dropped WHOLE — the direction that never injects behind a refusal; an allowed one relays raw). Every stream goes through `strip` now (allowed ⇒ byte-identical to the old raw relay). Dropped input is never reported to `onInput` (a refused click is nobody at the keyboard; the idle stop must not be fed by refused input); `onInput(id, viewerId)` carries the viewer; `stats().dropped` counts the drops; the close line names the viewer and the drop count + the last refusal code. `viewers` (id → viewerId → ws) answers `viewersOf(id)` / `viewerAlive(id, viewerId)` (the engine's holderAlive fact); `onViewerLeft(id, viewerId)` fires once per socket close so a holder whose socket died hands back. The singleton desktop (`/api/vnc`) is never gated (the wiring answers relay for it). ### src/window-targets.js — WINDOW TARGETS, SHARED (design-agent-browser-v2 §4.9 / §5.1.1 / §6.6; P9 first half, 2026-09-21)

**Mirror red on 2.369.181 (2026-09-26):** `TREE_UNREACHABLE` (closed, ⊆ `REFUSALS`: helper_missing, python3_missing, helper_timeout, helper_error, a11y_unavailable) + `treeUnreachable(r)` = the refusals that mean "this machine cannot read an accessibility tree right now" — which one a box answers is a fact about the BOX (the Actions runner has no gi binding, a box with gi and no bus gets libatspi's dbind abort = helper_error), so the engine folds the whole set under an `auto` share into ONE verdict (pixels, `mode_pixels`, the reason beside it); test-window-targets §2 derives its coverage from runHelper's own `refuse('…')` calls + the helper's import refusal. The probe memos are keyed by the ENVIRONMENT: `envKeyOf(env)` (PATH, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS, DISPLAY, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) + the interpreter/helper for `probeA11y`, + gdbus for the portal / ScreenCast rows — keyed by name alone, one process asking from two environments heard the first one's YES (§2 pins it; CONTROL = the key without the environment).

**Lane E (2026-09-25, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6 — the owner's D1–D7):** THE PIXEL ROAD. `injectKey` / `injectClick` lost `mousemove --sync` (M9, reproduced: a move to the pointer's CURRENT position waited 7 s for a motion that never came, and the second click / key in a row failed `inject_failed` — one xdotool connection orders the motion before the event anyway); `injectClick` refuses a `button` outside `CLICK_BUTTONS` [1,2,3] by name (M8: a wheel request was silently coerced to a LEFT click); NEW `injectScroll({x, y, direction, by})` = X buttons 4/5/6/7 × `by` (1..`SCROLL_MAX` 20) at a display point (Chrome: 120 px a notch, measured); `injectType({text, replace, focus})` = `xdotool [mousemove focus] [key ctrl+a] type --clearmodifiers --delay 12 -- <text>` (the text ONE argv item after `--`, never read as an option; ≤ `TYPE_MAX` 4000; the pointer rests inside the window first — keys typed with the pointer elsewhere were lost on xterm under xpra, measured); `displayGeometry` (`xdotool getdisplaygeometry`); `windowShot({xenv, out, plan})` = the helper's `windowshot` op over window-reach's `pixelPlan`; `focusNode({entry})` = the helper's act verb `focus` (Component.grab_focus). `verbVerdicts` carries a `scroll` row and the `click-at` note says x,y is a pixel of the screenshot. `refTableOf` keeps a node's `editable` / `focusable` / `focused` STATES (the engine types keys into a node editable by state without EditableText). Gate: test-window-targets §5 (the argv of every injection over a recording fake xdotool: no `--sync`, the `--` separator, ctrl+a before a replace, button 5 × N) + test-window-target §4 (the real xpra rung).

**Lane E verify r2 (2026-09-25, L5) — AN INJECTION THE LEASE CAN CANCEL, AND THE KEY IT LEAVES HELD.** Every injection (`injectKey` / `injectClick` / `injectScroll` / `injectType`) runs through `runInject(bin, args, {env, timeout, signal})`: `execFile` with the engine's AbortSignal and `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'` — node kills exactly THAT ChildProcess by its handle (never a name, never a group; test-window-targets §2b keeps a same-named decoy alive and greps for pkill / killall / a negative-pid kill) — and it resolves only after the child's 'close', so the release cannot race a keystroke still in flight. A killed run (the cancel OR the timeout) goes through `afterKill` → `releaseHeld({bins, xenv, keysyms, buttons, python})` before it answers: MEASURED on this box's Xvfb with an xev witness — SIGKILL between a key's press and its release leaves the key HELD and the server autorepeats it (37 presses in 1.5 s; a CJK character typed through xdotool's scratch keycode stays held too), so a cancel that only killed would type into the window the user just took over. `RELEASE_PY` (python3 + ctypes over libX11 / libXtst, JSON on stdin): each keysym → its keycode ON THE DISPLAY NOW, a faked release per keycode + per button; an unmapped keysym has keycode 0 and is skipped for free (a scratch-bound character IS mapped at that moment and is released — 302 keysyms in 32 ms, the autorepeat stopped); a release of a key / button that is not down is dropped by the server (measured: no event). Fallback without python3 / the libraries: `xdotool keyup` of the keysyms every keymap maps (printable ASCII in its `U<hex>` spelling + named keys) + `mouseup` — never a remap per character (300 unmapped keyups measured 3.7 s). `keysymsOfText(text, {replace})` = one `U<hex>` per distinct character + Return / Tab + the shift levels xdotool uses (Shift_L/R, ISO_Level3_Shift, Mode_switch) + ctrl + a for `--replace`; `keysymsOfChord` = both sides of each modifier + the key. A cancelled primitive answers `inject_failed {cancelled: true, partial: true, released}`, a timed-out one `inject_failed {partial, released}` ("did not finish within N ms and was killed"). `TYPE_MAX` is 1500 (was 4000: 4000 × 12.5 ms measured could never finish inside the fixed 20 s — killed after ~1,600 characters) and the timeout scales: `typeTimeoutMs(n)` = 5 s + 2 × `TYPE_DELAY_MS` (12) × n; `delay` is injectable for the suite's real-display cancel leg. Gates: test-window-targets §2b (the budget pin + a control with the old 4000 / 20 s pair; an aborted type answers at once, its child dead, the decoy alive, the fallback keyup recorded; a chord killed by its timeout releases ctrl + s; a cancelled click `mouseup 3`), §3 (the real fixture: a type cancelled mid-key leaves exactly `entry 'q'`; CONTROL = a patched copy without `releaseHeld` ⇒ `entry 'qqqq…'`).

  window-targets.js — node builtins + desktop-display only (the daemon can bundle it); every display-touching entry point takes `hostId` and refuses a non-local one by name. THE RULE IT ENCODES (D28): the agent talks to the TREE — AT-SPI2 is the native window's DOM — and to pixels only when the tree cannot answer. `snapshotTarget({pids, budget, text})` → `{snapshot, refs}`: the a11y tree of the applications whose pid ∈ pids with `@eN` minted in visit order (the agent-browser habit), the interface CENSUS every snapshot reports (§12.30: Action/EditableText/Text per node, buttons-with-Action — coverage is per toolkit and per desktop, never a constant), the `unreadable` subtrees, `truncated`, the timing. `refTableOf` keeps IDENTITY only (pid, path, role, name, bounds, actions, editable) — never the text; `resolveRef` refuses `ref_unknown` for anything not in the last snapshot. `actOnNode({entry, verb})` re-resolves the recorded path and the helper refuses `ref_stale` when the node there is no longer the one the ref named, `node_has_no_action` when a `do_action` lands on a node without `Action`, `node_not_editable` for text into a node without `EditableText`. `pickAction(actions, want)` = the preference `click > press > activate > doDefault > …`; Chromium/Electron put `showContextMenu` + `clickAncestor` on EVERY node (measured), so those and the `scroll*` family are NEVER picked unnamed (`--action` names one). `parseChord` is a CLOSED vocabulary (modifiers + one letter/digit/named key, spelled for xdotool) because the result reaches an argv — `ctrl+s; rm` is `bad_chord`, `ctrl++` is ctrl and the plus key, `ctrl+` is refused. `probeInputBackends({env, bins, ours})` = the RUNTIME ladder (§4.9 conclusion 2 — never a platform name): `xtest` (xdotool on OUR display; the only rung wired; a display that is not ours gets none — D27 (a)), `portal` (the RemoteDesktop portal on the session bus, `available:'consent'`, unwired — D29 (a)), `uinput` (a writable /dev/uinput, unwired, explicitly not recommended — D29 (b)); `injection` = the first row both available AND wired. `verbVerdicts({a11y, backends})` = §5.1.1's table PER VERB: `click`/`type`/`snapshot` ride the tree and are decided per NODE at act time; `key` and `click-at` exist only as injection and are refused WITH the probe rows when no wired backend exists; `screenshot` only from our display. `injectKey` (pointer moved into the window first — a bare Xvfb has PointerRoot focus — then `xdotool key --clearmodifiers <chord>`) and `injectClick` (`mousemove --sync x y click n`) are XTEST on our display; `screenshotDisplay` writes a PNG of a rectangle through the helper's Gdk op — the FALLBACK read.

  **THE TRAVERSAL NEVER RUNS ON THE EVENT LOOP.** `runHelper(req, {env, wallMs, python, helper})` spawns src/window-targets-helper.py with ONE JSON request on stdin, reads ONE JSON reply, keeps an `error` listener for life, SIGKILLs at `wallMs` and answers `helper_timeout` with the elapsed ms (the child is dead by then — suite §2), maps garbage to `helper_error` with the stderr tail, ENOENT to `python3_missing` naming the packages (python3-gi + gir1.2-atspi-2.0), a missing file to `helper_missing`, and any code outside `REFUSALS` to `helper_error` (+ `helperCode`) so a route never sees an unknown code. `TRAVERSAL_LIMITS` is the ONE home of the numbers: NODE_BUDGET 600 (default), SNAPSHOT_MAX_BUDGET 3000 (clamped), CALL_TIMEOUT_MS 800 (libatspi's per-method timeout inside the helper), WALL_MS 20 s (an unresponsive app costs one call timeout per node it owns, so the wall is what bounds it), ACT_WALL_MS 8 s, PROBE_MEMO_MS 60 s (a YES from the a11y / portal probes is remembered, a NO re-asked). `REFUSALS` is CLOSED and `refuse()` throws on a stranger; the routes' STATUS map must cover every member (suite §4 census).

  **P9 MEASUREMENTS (2026-09-21, this box: Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1 on Wayland, xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.1 + -gnome 50.0, at-spi2 2.60.4, python 3.14.4, node 24.12 — the four things §10's P9 row said to measure FIRST; scripts/measure-window-targets.mjs reproduces them):**
  ① **The portal from a `systemd --user` background unit** (D29 / §12.29): from a transient `systemd-run --user` service — the same manager and context as vibespace.service — `RemoteDesktop.CreateSession` answered response 0 in 3 ms, `SelectDevices(types=7, persist_mode=2)` response 0, and `Start` raised the consent dialog (journal: "Failed to associate portal window with parent window", no Response within a 3 s wait; the session was Closed). So the public "portal/D-Bus is refused in background contexts" report does NOT hold here — the D-Bus path is open; what stands between a background service and injection is the USER'S click (§6.6), which nobody clicked in this measurement, so a granted background session is unproven. D29 (a) is viable; (c) stays the shipped state.
  ② **AT-SPI coverage on Chromium/Electron** (§12.30): LM Studio 0.3.32 (Electron) launched on our Xvfb with `--force-renderer-accessibility` — 357 nodes: Component 357/357, **Action 357/357** (`showContextMenu` on every node, `clickAncestor` 290, `press` 36, `doDefault` 13, `click` 11), **buttons with Action 43/43**, EditableText 0/357 (no field on that screen), Text 328/357. Every node has an action, which is not the same as every action being meaningful — hence `pickAction`'s never-by-default set. GTK3 (the fixture): 13 nodes, Action 3, EditableText 1, buttons with Action 2/2. gnome-shell (clutter/GJS, 600-node budget): Action 49/600, **74 buttons with 0 Action**. **Qt: NOT measured — no Qt toolkit is installed on this box**; the suite prints its own census so it can be re-read on a desktop that has one. Electron exported its tree only because the flag was passed; a keeper row for an Electron app should carry it (second half).
  ③ **`do_action` → UI change**: a GTK button, 30 clicks — the call itself median 0.08 ms, the tree-visible change (the label's new name read back through libatspi) median 0.34 ms, p95 0.81 ms, max 0.82 ms. Not measured on Electron (no known-safe widget to press in somebody's app).
  ④ **The node-side binding and its per-node cost** (§12.33): no maintained node AT-SPI binding exists (npm 2026-09-21: `@girs/atspi-2.0` / `@gi-types/atspi*` = GJS typings, `@girs/node-atspi-2.0` = typings for the native node-gtk, `dbus-next` 0.10.2 last modified 2022-04-28, two zero-history packages). Per-node cost is NOT what decides it — a cold walk costs the same order both ways: libatspi through python3 GI 600 gnome-shell nodes in 111–248 ms across four runs (2,400–5,400 nodes/s), the 357-node Electron tree in 78–81 ms (4,400–4,600 nodes/s); raw D-Bus with NO cache through Gio (up to 6 calls per node: GetRoleName, Name, GetInterfaces, GetExtents, GetActions, GetChildren) 0.34–0.51 ms/node = 1,970–2,900 nodes/s. The fork tax: helper spawn → probe reply 62–70 ms from a 47 MB node (+ the parent's RSS-proportional fork cost, §1.6's 72 ms at 1.5 GB), paid ONCE per traversal. Decision: python3 + GI in the bounded subprocess — the boundary is required by the event-loop law anyway, and a raw node client would be a dependency this repo does not carry for a cost it would not save.

  **P10 (2026-09-21):** `probeScreenCastPortal({env, bins, now})` — two read-only property Gets on the session bus (`ScreenCast.version`, `AvailableSourceTypes`, bit 2 = window sources), a YES memoised PROBE_MEMO_MS; it starts no session and raises no dialog (that is the user's click). The engine's desktop-class `screenshot` hands its answer to window-desktop's `captureVerdict`.

  window-reach.js — imports nothing; CJS so the engine, the user routes, the request producer, the suites AND the bundle share one spelling. THE REACH MODEL (msg-acl / channel-acl's house pattern): two levels (hidden < exposed, hidden by default — D1); a record PER WINDOW `{windowId, mode, rows:[{principal:{kind:'session'|'group', id, name?}, grantedAt, by:'user'|'request'|'self-open'}]}`; a session principal is its DURABLE key (`sessionKeyOf` = server.js `sessionStatusKey`'s spelling — `<backend>:<conversation id>`, `webui:<id>` before one exists; test-window-reach §8 runs server.js's own function beside it), a group principal its Task Group id; ONE row per principal (`grant` keeps an existing row and its origin — widen-only; `revoke` drops only that principal's row); `reachFor(record, {sessionKeys, groupIds})` = MAX over the rows, the deciding row named (`via` session | self-open | group; a session's own row preferred); `openerGrant` = D1's exception. THE MODE (D7): `MODES` auto | tree | pixels; `usableNodes` (a non-container role with an action other than showContextMenu / clickAncestor, or editable text / state); `resolveMode({mode, probe})` (tree / pixels as shared; auto ⇒ tree when a node is usable, else pixels "no accessibility tree — pixel mode" / "its accessibility tree is closed (N nodes …)" / "the accessibility bus is unreachable"); `verbGate({mode, resolved, verb, hasRef})` — pixels refuses `snapshot` / `click @ref` / `type @ref` `mode_pixels` with `PIXELS_SENTENCE` (the owner's words), tree allows everything, auto lets a snapshot through AS the probe and follows its resolution. ### ssh-key-format.js

  ssh-key-format.js    — Private-key FORMAT classifier, PURE + shared server/browser (CJS pulled into the bundle like task-color-seq.js). **WHY a decoder and not a regex (2.246.0): an `openssh-key-v1` key's PEM armor is BYTE-IDENTICAL with or without a passphrase — the word ENCRYPTED appears NOWHERE** (only classic PEM's `Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED` and PKCS#8's `BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY` announce themselves). The old first-3-lines /ENCRYPTED/ check therefore missed effectively every key produced since OpenSSH 7.8: they imported "fine" and failed at connect with a bare `Permission denied (publickey)` that never mentions a passphrase at ANY -v level. Encryption state lives in the DECODED body (`magic | ciphername | kdfname`; none/none = plain). classifyPrivateKey → {format: empty|openssh-v1|pkcs8|pem|ppk|ssh2|unknown, encrypted, cipher?, usable, malformed?}; TOTAL (runs on every keystroke — bounded to the first 256 base64 chars, length words capped at 64, hostile input returns a verdict and NEVER throws). ssh.com armor is FOUR dashes with spaces (`---- BEGIN SSH2 …----`), not the PEM five

### ssh-key.js

  ssh-key.js           — Server-side private-key UNLOCK at import (2.246.0). prepareImportedKey(text, passphrase) → {body, wasEncrypted, format, fingerprint, type}, KeyError codes key-encrypted/key-bad-passphrase/key-ppk/key-unsupported/key-not-a-key/key-too-large/key-no-ssh-keygen/key-unlock-unavailable/key-unlock-failed (the CLIENT renders localized text off the code). **PASSPHRASE TRANSPORT IS ENV, NEVER ARGV**: ssh-keygen reads a passphrase only from a tty or SSH_ASKPASS (never stdin), so a throwaway 0700 helper (`printf %s "$VIBESPACE_KEY_PASS"`) in a 0700 mkdtemp dir is exec'd with the secret in the CHILD ENV (/proc/<pid>/environ is 0400) + SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force; argv is only `-p -N '' -f <tmpfile>` (/proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable — the 2.126.0 rule) and HOME points at the temp dir so ssh-keygen can never touch the server's ~/.ssh. Temp dir removed on EVERY path incl. throws. **NON-NEGOTIABLE ERROR ORDER: an askpass helper that can't be exec'd (noexec tmpdir) makes ssh-keygen exit 255 saying "incorrect passphrase supplied" for a CORRECT passphrase — the only discriminator is the `ssh_askpass:` marker in stderr, which MUST be checked BEFORE the passphrase branch** or a hardened container lies to users forever. Fingerprint is computed in JS from the `-y` blob (byte-identical to `ssh-keygen -l`, verified — no extra spawn). node crypto is NOT an option: it cannot parse openssh-key-v1 at all, so a crypto-based impl passes RSA tests and fails every real ed25519 key. **The STORED key is UNLOCKED — this removes the passphrase, it does not preserve it** (every ssh here is BatchMode=yes and can never prompt); disclosed in docs/device-agent.md. Tests: scripts/test-ssh-key.mjs (60) + scripts/test-ssh-key-dialog.mjs (24, real headless browser)

### ctx-sync.js

  ctx-sync.js          — **THE ctx-folder sync, ONE implementation for every machine (2.277.0).** The old split — ssh=bidirectional rsync NO caps, dial=hashed sync with a SILENT ≤400-files/≤2MB cap — meant a 3MB context file reached every ssh host and never reached a dial device, invisibly. Hashed newer-wins sync (sha-equal ⇒ untouched, echo can't ping-pong; traversal-guarded pulls) over the device link on EVERY transport; ssh degrades to its legacy rsync pair only when the link is down; caps 1000 files/16MB and **every capped skip is REPORTED** (deduped serverNotice — a bounded sync may refuse a file, never lose one silently). Local sessions read the contextDir directly (TRANSPORT-ONLY, not a divergence). Test: scripts/test-ctx-sync.mjs (13).

### cli-identity.js

**2026-09-25 — MEMORY METRICS (the Chrome desktop-app incident):** `procSample(pid, {procRoot, memory})` → `{starttime, cpuTicks, reapedTicks, rssBytes, anonBytes, pssBytes}`: `anonBytes` = status RssAnon+RssShmem (free — the same read as VmRSS), `pssBytes` = smaps_rollup `Pss` read only with `{memory: true}` (≈1.1 ms per pid — the kernel walks the page tables — so identity callers such as procStart never ask); null = that metric unreadable for the pid; a process with NO address space (zombie / kernel thread: status has no VmRSS line) is an exact 0 in every metric, so one zombie member never switches a set's memory rule off. `procSampleAsync` = the same files read through fs.promises (the keepers' ticks: never the event loop), `parseProcSample` = the ONE interpretation both use. `setMemory(samples)` → `{memBytes, memMetric, rssBytes}` = THE SET RULE: the strongest metric EVERY member provides (pss > anon > rss), summed in that metric for every member (never a mix), ΣVmRSS kept as a fact; r2: an 'anon' set with MORE than one member holding an address space is named 'anon-sum' — RssAnon counts a CoW page once per sharer and RssShmem shared memory once per mapper, so over several processes it is a per-process sum again (889 chrome pids: 22.87 GB vs ΣPss 15.15 GB) — recorded, never judged; one process (a zombie beside it holds none) keeps 'anon'; `setSample(samples, {reaped})` adds cpuTicks (own + reaped for a SET, own-only for the browser tree walk) and `pids` = how many answered. `MEM_METRICS` = the order. Users: desktop-display.sessionSample, browser-facts.treeUsage, opencode-serve's one-pid read. Gates: test-desktop-display §8 (fake /proc root), test-runaway-guard ① (the incident fixture through setSample, the reaped-ticks rule).

  cli-identity.js      — **THE agent-CLI process identity — ONE rule, two spellings (B-3185 r3).** "Is pid N the `claude`/`codex` CLI?" is asked by three consumers that used to answer it three ways: the pre-resume WRITER SWEEP (shell — decides who receives a SIGTERM), the ssh discovery **CO leg** (shell, the same text embedded verbatim — decides which codex threads read RUNNING) and **src/discovery-facts.js in JavaScript** (the local listing, the device snapshot's lock scan and its CO lines). B-3185 r1/r2 replaced the substring rule with an EXECUTABLE test in the two shell copies and RECORDED the JS one as a deliberate twin, on the grounds that it only labels a card RUNNING. r3 killed it: the blast radius genuinely differs, but a rule with two spellings has two behaviours the moment either is touched, and the loose spelling was doing real damage of its own — measured on the dev box, `cmdline.includes('claude')` answered YES for **106 of 4277 processes** against **16 real claude CLIs** (dtach masters, chat-wrappers, the generated `code` editor helper, a zsh shell-snapshot), and `isCodexCommandLine` for **30 against 4**, so any lock file whose pid had been RECYCLED by one of them produced exactly the phantom "running" session the PID-reuse guard exists to prevent. Exports `isCliProcess(pid, name)` (JS) + `cliIdentityShellFns()` (the POSIX `vs_argv`/`vs_is_cli` text, re-exported by writer-sweep.js so existing call sites are unchanged — the suite asserts it is the SAME function object, not a copy). **THE RULE, three rungs, one per shape the CLIs ship in:** ① argv[0]'s basename is the CLI name (`~/.local/bin/claude`; the codex vendor binary); ② argv[0] is an interpreter (node/nodejs/node.exe/bun/deno) and its FIRST NON-FLAG operand is the entry point (`node <prefix>/bin/claude`, `node …/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`, `node …/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`; up to 6 leading flags skipped); ③ `/proc/<pid>/exe` basename IS the CLI, or the exe is the native install's version FILE (`…/<name>/versions/<ver>`) **and** the process still PRESENTS as the CLI (argv[0] basename starts with the name, or argv[0] basename EQUALS the exe basename = nothing renamed) — the r2 narrowing that keeps a re-exec'd bundled helper (argv[0] `ugrep`, same image) out. A later ARGUMENT never identifies a process; that is exactly what the retired rule got wrong. **` (deleted)` IS STRIPPED FROM /proc/<pid>/exe (r3, defect 2).** The kernel appends it once the image is replaced on disk — which is what `claude` auto-update and `npm i -g @openai/codex` do to LIVE sessions; two of the four running agent CLIs on this box carry the suffix at any given moment. Without the strip BOTH executable rungs miss (basename `claude (deleted)`; the "nothing renamed" disjunct compares `2.1.258` against `2.1.258 (deleted)`), so the ONE process the sweep exists to stop — a mid-update CLI still appending to the transcript — survived it, and a double-writer is *most* likely right after an update lands. **argv IS A LIST OF NUL-SEPARATED WORDS AND A WORD MAY CONTAIN A NEWLINE (r4).** The JS side reads that list; the shell side could not, so `vs_argv` turned NULs into newlines and took the Nth LINE — which is the FIRST LINE of the Nth word. The two spellings therefore answered differently about the same live process whenever a word carried a newline, in BOTH directions and both harmful: argv[0] `/usr/bin/claude<LF>/usr/bin/tail` is basename `tail` to JS and `claude` to the old shell (the sweep SIGTERMs a reader — B-3185's own harm through a different door), and `<dir>/dir<LF>name/claude` is the reverse (a real writer survives the sweep, which is the double-writer the sweep exists to prevent). The shell now parks real newlines on `\001` for the line select and restores them after (`tr '\n' '\001' | tr '\0' '\n' | sed -n Np | tr '\001' '\n'`), so "the Nth line" IS "the Nth NUL-record" in either spelling; the residue is a literal `\001` inside an argv word coming back as a newline — a byte no path or flag carries, and since the swap cannot move a `/` the basename splits at the same place in both spellings, so it can only make a word look LESS like the CLI. The `ps` fallback flattens its blob first (`tr '\n' ' '`) because the JS twin's `/\s+/` split always treated a newline as a space while awk splits per line. **THAT LAST SENTENCE WAS A DESCRIPTION UNTIL r5.** The `ps` branch is the NO-/proc rung (macOS/BSD ssh hosts); on a Linux box every fixture takes the /proc rung, so the half of the r4 fix that lives there shipped with no assertion and no control — (r) again. It is now DRIVEN, with no edit to the text under test: the `/proc/$1/` root is re-rooted so BOTH reads miss (three literals, asserted — leaving the exe read live let rung 3 decide and the `ps` rung was never reached), a stand-in `ps` sits first on PATH, and the JS twin runs in a child whose two /proc reads THROW so the shipped `procArgv`/`isCliProcess` really take their own fallback. The stand-in is asserted to be necessary rather than assumed: measured, procps 4.x `ps -o args=` renders an embedded newline as a SPACE, so this box's own `ps` cannot produce the multi-line blob the flattening exists for. argv leg; .zst; non-codex holder untouched; the claude script never touches a codex holder); test §10 pins the ws-create guard functionally (real `createWsCreateHandler`) + every sweep site passing `sweepOpts`. **IDENTITY IS THE EXECUTABLE, NOT A SUBSTRING OF THE COMMAND LINE (B-3185).** The holder test used to be `case "$(ps -p $pid -o args=)" in *claude*)` — a substring over the WHOLE command line — so every process whose argv merely NAMED a path under `~/.claude` read as the CLI and was SIGTERMed: `tail -f ~/.claude/projects/<id>.jsonl`, an editor with the transcript open, and (the first casualty, patched around IN THE SUITE for a while instead of fixed) a test process running from a git worktree under `~/.claude/worktrees/` — where the worktree-only-smokes law puts every agent — which matched its own guard and killed itself: exit 143, `npm run ci` red, on code that was fine. `vs_is_cli <pid> <claude|codex>` (cliIdentityShellFns — **which lives in src/cli-identity.js since r3 and is only RE-EXPORTED here, beside its JS twin `isCliProcess`; read that entry**) now decides by the EXECUTABLE, in three rungs covering the three shapes the CLIs actually ship in: argv[0]'s basename (`~/.local/bin/claude`; the codex vendor binary `…/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/<triple>/bin/codex` that the npm `codex.js` shim spawns by path), the interpreter's FIRST NON-FLAG operand when argv[0] is node/nodejs/bun/deno (`node <prefix>/bin/claude` via the npm shebang shim, `node …/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`, `node …/bin/codex.js`), and `/proc/<pid>/exe` (a native install execs `~/.local/share/claude/versions/<ver>` behind an argv[0] of `~/.local/bin/claude`). argv is read NUL-split out of `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` where that exists (exact) and falls back to `ps -o args=` word splitting elsewhere, and a trailing ` (deleted)` is stripped from `/proc/<pid>/exe` before either exe rung matches (**r3**: the kernel appends it when the image is replaced on disk — what auto-update does to a LIVE session — and without the strip the sweep missed exactly the mid-update CLI it exists to stop). THE ARGV LEG IS DELIBERATELY EXEMPT: `codex resume <threadId>` / `CODEX_WEBUI_RESUME_ID=<threadId>` is self-evidencing (it names the thread) and the shape it catches — an orphaned VibeSpace wrapper or its dtach master — is NOT the codex binary, so `vs_codex_kill` keeps only the PROTECT check and each caller supplies its own evidence. **THE FD SCAN IS BATCHED — AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE (B-3185).** `fdScanShellFns()` emits `vs_fd_scan <ere>` (one `<pid>\t<fd target>` line per matching open fd) + `vs_fd_pids`; both backend scripts embed it VERBATIM, and `src/server/boot-restore.js` builds its "which conversations does a live claude still hold?" probe from the same export (same scan, kill removed). Measured on the dev box (32 cores, loadavg 3.4–4.8, 3678–3713 processes, 405,735 open fds): the old per-process `ls` + `grep` fork PAIR = 7356 forks, 9.9–12.2 s wall — over half the 20 s budget spent on fork/exec alone, and past it entirely on a busier or bigger machine; the batched form (one `ls -l` per 400 fd directories + one awk) = ~20 forks, 3.0–3.5 s, so the UNCHANGED 20 s budget now covers ~24k processes. boot-restore's variant was worse and silently dead: a `readlink` fork PER FD (~6.4 minutes here) against a 6 s timeout it therefore ALWAYS blew, swallowed by a bare catch — every local conversation looked "not live" and the socket dedup fell back to createdAt; it now runs the shared scan and a failure LOGS. Two shell facts are load-bearing: `/proc/self/fd` rides in every chunk so `ls -l` always has more than one operand and therefore always prints the `<dir>:` headers the pid attribution reads (with a single operand it prints none), and the scan is CHUNKED because `vs_fd_chunk` EXECS `ls`: ITS argv is one operand per process and is what ARG_MAX/MAX_ARG_STRLEN bound, and an E2BIG there fails into a discarded stderr and a silently empty answer. **The old boot probe's `/proc/[0-9]*/fd/*` glob was NOT an ARG_MAX case** (r1's comment said it was, and the r2 review caught it): a shell `for` loop expands in the shell's own memory and never reaches execve — its problem was only the 405,735 `readlink` forks. Naming the wrong mechanism in a comment is how the next person removes the right guard, so both copies and both kb twins are pinned by the suite. Next rung if a machine ever needs it: GNU `find -lname` measures 0.76 s — not adopted, because it is not portable and 3 s is inside budget. **WHICH LEG ACTUALLY REACHES A LIVE CLAUDE (measured, and it changes how you read the fix):** the installed CLI (2.1.226, native binary) does NOT keep the transcript open — it appends and closes; a machine-wide scan of this box found ZERO processes holding any `~/.claude/projects/**.jsonl` while 16 claude CLIs were running. So the claude FD leg is a rung that fires for a holder that happens to exist — an older CLI, a mid-append race, or a READER — while the leg that really catches a live claude is the CLI's own `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` lock file. That makes the old substring guard worse than it looks: the leg that almost never finds a real writer was the one matching every process that merely named a path under `~/.claude`. It also bounds boot-restore's probe honestly — it now runs correctly and fast, but it still answers "nobody" for current claude; giving `claudeAlive` the CLI registry (with the `procStart` counter-capture against pid reuse) is a separate decision, because retiring is destructive (SIGTERM + unlink the dtach socket). The CODEX fd leg is the live one: real app-servers on this box do hold their rollouts open, which is why the PROTECT list exists. Field-validated read-only against 3700 real processes: of 70 whose argv merely contains 'claude', exactly the 16 real CLIs answer yes and the dtach masters and chat-wrappers that carry the whole `…/claude --resume …` command line as ARGUMENTS answer no (the old rule said yes to all of them — and SIGTERMing a dtach master destroys the session); both real codex shapes (`node …/bin/codex app-server` through the npm shim and the `…/vendor/<triple>/bin/codex` binary) answer yes. Test §6 is now the identity matrix on real processes: WRITERS that must be swept (a native `…/bin/claude`, `node …/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`, `node <prefix>/bin/claude`) and READERS that must survive (`tail -f` on the transcript — proven non-vacuous by checking its fd first — a process running from a `.claude/worktrees/` path, a `cli.js` outside a claude package, a neutral `node -e` holder, and THE SUITE'S OWN PROCESS holding the same fd, under a SIGTERM trap so a regression is a red assertion instead of a mysterious exit 143). §1 pins the batching structurally (exactly one `/proc/[0-9]*` walk per script, no per-process `ls`, no whole-argv identity test) and asserts that every `kill -TERM` line carries a `SWEPT:` — intent, not the old count, which the dedup would have broken. §11 pins the boot-restore wiring. **R2 REVIEW ROUND (six defects, each with a negative control).** ① The §1 drift pin was UNSATISFIABLE — its regex matched neither the exact pre-fix line nor any realistic reintroduction, so the kb advertised a guard that could never go red; the pin is now asserted against the verbatim pre-B-3185 lines AND proven by splicing them back into the shipped script. ② The awk pid attribution never cleared `p` on an UNRECOGNISED directory header — and `/proc/self/fd`, appended to every chunk by design, is exactly such a header AND is the `ls` process's own fd table, which inherits the sweeping shell's fds: an inherited matching fd was attributed to whichever numeric pid came last in the chunk, and the sweep SIGTERMs on that attribution. `p` is now reset on EVERY header; §1b proves it functionally (the shell holds the target on fd 9, so `ls` inherits it in every chunk) with the sticky-`p` revert as the control — one bogus victim per chunk. ③ The ARG_MAX rationale above. ④ RUNG 3 WAS A WIDENING INSIDE A NARROWING FIX: `*/<name>/versions/*` on `/proc/<pid>/exe` classified every process running the CLI's binary IMAGE as the CLI — and the CLI RE-EXECS that image as its bundled helpers (measured live: 18–19 processes under `…/share/claude/versions/<ver>`, 2–3 of them `ugrep -G …` with argv[0] a bare `ugrep`), so a search helper that inherited its parent's transcript fd was a SIGTERM target. Rung 3 now also asks how the process PRESENTS itself and takes either honest answer — argv[0] basename starts with `<name>` (a launcher naming the CLI), or argv[0] basename EQUALS the exe basename (nothing renamed: a wrapper's `exec "$IMG"`, the shape that keeps the rung reachable at all). A re-exec'd helper fails both because it renames itself. The measured real CLI never needs rung 3 (argv[0] is `~/.local/bin/claude`, so rung 1 answers) — which is why widening it was pure downside. §6 runs ONE binary under THREE argv[0]s (same `/proc/<pid>/exe`, asserted) and reverts rung 3 to r1 against the LIVE helper pid as the control. ⑤ The "SUITE ITSELF" leg labelled its argv from `process.argv[1]`, which node ABSOLUTISES, while the guard reads the command line AS TYPED — so it announced "the real regression shape" for a run whose argv contained no `.claude` at all. A COPY of the suite (holder mode, top of file) now runs from a real `.claude/worktrees/<wt>/scripts/` checkout BOTH ways — absolute (the argv that SIGTERMed the suite) and relative (what the gate types) — with the two argvs read out of `/proc` and asserted. ⑥ THE STANDING-SWEEP TWIN: hosts.js's remote-discovery `CO` leg still carried all three retired shapes (a `tr`+`grep` fork PAIR per process over `/proc/[0-9]*`, a `readlink` fork per FD, and an argv-regex identity) — measured on this box 5.02 s / 8068 forks at 4034 processes inside a per-host discovery budget, versus 3.52 s / ~20 forks for the ported leg. `codexOpenRolloutsShell()` (hosts.js) now embeds `fdScanShellFns()` + `cliIdentityShellFns()` VERBATIM, so the sweep and discovery answer "is this the codex CLI" identically by construction; §12 pins that structurally with the pre-B-3185 leg as the control, and §9 runs it for real (a wrapper/dtach-master that merely NAMES `…/bin/codex resume <tid>` in its ARGUMENTS is no longer a RUNNING thread — the retired regex says yes to it, asserted). **THE PORT ALSO EXPOSED A LIVE HAZARD THE SUITE CAUGHT: this leg is the LAST command of the ssh discovery script and `_ssh` REJECTS a non-zero exit, and a `while read` loop exits with its LAST iteration's status — so the leg returned 1 whenever the last matching fd under `$HOME` belonged to a non-CLI holder, sending the whole host's discovery into the serve-stale-cache catch. It ends in an explicit `:`; never let a scan's FINDINGS decide a script's exit status.** ⑦ The kb's advertised assert count is now self-checked by §13. **THAT TWIN IS GONE (r3 — the standing sweep is a MEASUREMENT, and "recorded" is not "resolved"):** r2 left `src/discovery-facts.js` identifying processes by command line — `pidLooksClaude` = `cmdline.includes('claude')`, `isCodexCommandLine` = a whole-argv regex — for the DEVICE snapshot's liveness labels, on the grounds that it only decides whether a card reads RUNNING and never who receives a SIGTERM. The blast radius really is different, and it was still the wrong call: a rule with two spellings has two behaviours the moment either is touched, and the loose spelling was doing its own damage (measured: YES for 106 of 4277 processes against 16 real claude CLIs; 30 vs 4 for codex — so a RECYCLED lock pid on any dtach master, chat-wrapper or editor helper produced the exact phantom the PID-reuse guard exists to prevent). Both now call `isCliProcess` from src/cli-identity.js. §12 still pins the boundary that must never be crossed (no kill path in discovery-facts or cli-identity — they classify; only the sweep script kills), and parity is now FUNCTIONAL on both sides (test-writer-sweep §6/§12, test-discovery-interpret §8) instead of a promise.

The `.meta` therefore records `remotePath` + `compressed` next to {size,mtime}: a changed path invalidates the slot (full refetch, no cache-valid short-circuit), and a compressed remote — or an already-compressed cache file (magic-byte check, so pre-fix metas are covered too) — is NEVER delta-appended, because recompression rewrites the file rather than appending plain bytes. Without it the append-only slab path concatenated the compressed twin's bytes onto the cached plain prefix and stamped it complete; a stopped thread never changes again, so the corrupt transcript was served forever. The locate pipeline is `find … | sort | head -1` so the pick is deterministic and prefers the plain twin. **AND THE ALREADY-CORRUPTED SLOTS HEAL THEMSELVES (review follow-up, same batch):** every slot in the field carries a PRE-provenance meta, and reading “no remotePath” as “same file” is vacuously true — the hybrid a stopped thread’s slot already held kept passing the short-circuit forever. So `sameRemote` is strict (`meta.remotePath === remotePath`), a meta without provenance is NOT valid (refetch whole ONCE, rewrite it, never delta onto it), and the cache FILE is checked independently of its meta: head magic must agree with the resolved remote, and a plain cache whose last 4KB carry a NUL byte or a zstd frame header is spliced (an append lands foreign bytes at the TAIL). Single exception: a remote already past `maxBytes` cannot be refetched whole at all (the delta path is how the slot grew there), so a byte-verified cache adopts the provenance instead of failing “too large”. **THE ADOPTION IS THE ONE DECISION THAT OUTLIVES THE TAIL WINDOW (B-7638):** the pre-fix delta path kept APPENDING after it spliced, so on a long-lived slot the marker sits far above the last 4 KB and a tail-only read called the hybrid verified. A cache slot therefore scans the WHOLE file (1 MiB chunks, 3-byte carry so a magic split across a boundary is still seen) before its bytes are trusted — gated on a meta SCHEMA MARKER (`v: 2`, written by every meta writer here), NOT on “no remotePath”: the shipped tail-only adoption stamped provenance onto the very hybrids it adopted, so `sameRemote` is true for exactly that corruption (round 2). The scan is paid ONCE per slot because the verification is WRITTEN BACK (`stampVerified`: remotePath + compressed + `v` + an `adopted` marker when the bytes were verified rather than fetched) on BOTH early-return rungs; a refused slot is left unstamped, and the “too large” error says the cache could not be verified AND that the remote is past the cap (the suffix is only reachable there, so the earlier “delete it to re-sync” was advice that could not work). **The legacy ssh rung also grows now** (round 2): stamping fixes only the repeated scan, while the harm — an over-cap slot hard-failing “too large” on its next byte — was a TWIN GAP against the slab rung's 2.187.0 delta; it now runs the same append-only delta via `tail -c +N` (1-based on GNU and BSD), same legality test, short read throws, a read that OVERTAKES the stat keeps the extra append-only bytes and stamps the real size. And a transcript SHORTER than the 4-byte magic is verifiable after all: it cannot BE a zstd frame nor hide a splice, so an empty/one-record transcript short-circuits on its cache instead of being fully re-pulled on every poll forever (a cache whose head is not a record, or a sub-magic cache under a COMPRESSED remote, is still refused). Pins: test-codex-zst ⑥/⑥b/⑥c (stub device switching remote files under one slot; a pre-written hybrid + old-shape meta healing with the remote standing still, negative-controlled against the pre-fix predicate)). **ROUND 3 — the round-2 delta's own three residuals:** ① the compression-legality clause (`!isZstPath(remotePath) && !cacheIsCompressed()`) had NO negative control on either rung — deleting it left the suite green, while the case it exists for (a host RE-compressing a finished rollout: same path, magic-verified .zst cache, cached archive shorter than the remote — every other precondition satisfied) would weld a foreign frame tail onto the old frames and serve the OLD transcript with the growth silently gone; both rungs now carry a both-compressed growth leg that dies when the clause is removed from its own copy. ② The round-2 ssh delta REPLACED the whole `cat` on the LAST rung, so a failing `tail` (remote rotated between stat and read; a host whose `tail` has no `-c +N`) hard-failed a fetch the pre-delta code completed — a delta failure now falls back to the whole `cat` when `size <= maxBytes` (failure logged VERBATIM) and stays a hard error only over the cap, where a whole re-pull is impossible by construction (so the fallback is never a cap bypass). ③ Both meta writers built a FRESH object, so the next delta erased `adopted`/`slab` — the durable provenance ① depends on, on the one slot class that can never re-earn it. ONE shared `nextMeta(fields, {whole})` spreads the prior meta on both rungs; only a WHOLE refetch clears those markers (they describe bytes no longer in the slot). Pins: test-codex-zst ⑥d/⑥e. **ROUND 4 — ONE WRITER PER SLOT:** both rungs compute the append offset from a stat taken BEFORE the remote read, so two overlapping fetches of one slot (poll + a user opening the window, two clients, goal-sync + an attach) both appended the same tail and the cache grew a DUPLICATED region — self-healing until the remote passes the doubled size, after which the next delta stamps the spliced file COMPLETE and a stopped thread serves duplicated + missing records forever (duplicated JSON trips neither byte marker). `_fetchRemoteByFind` is now a single-flight wrapper over the core `_fetchRemoteByFindOnce` (in-flight promise per cache path — the second caller awaits the first's verdict; caps come from one descriptor so coalescing cannot lose a cap), and every delta goes through `_appendDeltaAt(cachePath, offset, buf)`: open `r+`, re-read the size through that fd, write POSITIONALLY at `offset`, `false` when the slot has moved ⇒ whole refetch under the cap / loud failure over it, never a splice. Over the cap all of it is a loud failure that leaves cache+meta byte-identical, and the cap error names WHICH fault (spliced bytes vs "holds N bytes where the last fetch stamped M"). No local scan can separate the two shapes — the round-5 corruption appends ordinary text — so the disputed bytes are checked against the source of truth: when a slot is over the cap AND its meta predates the `sizeExact` marker AND the file is longer than that meta claims, the gap `[stamp, file)` is read back (BOUNDED: `fsReadRange` on the slab rung, `tail -c +N | head -c LEN` on the ssh one) and compared byte-for-byte with the cache. A REFUSAL, by contrast, is memoized in memory only (`_healRefusedAt`, keyed by cache path AND the size it was made on, 10 min, carrying the verdict) — stamping a slot we would not serve freezes the corruption in. Four verdicts ⇒ four different sentences appended to the cap error (`foreign` = checked mismatch, `spliced` = local marker, `moved`, `unverified` = retryable), because claiming a check that was skipped is "an error string is not a diagnosis" with the sign flipped. Second half: round 5's data-plane degrade line is rate-limited per HOST via `_warnDegradeOnce(id, msg, nowMs)` (≤1/60s, next line carries `(+N similar suppressed in the last minute)`; the heal's own probe-failure line shares that budget) — the fault it degrades on is usually persistent and every attach/poll/goal-sync tick comes through there. Pins: test-codex-zst ⑥h (pre-fix permanent failure reproduced first; heal + delta on both rungs; durability across a dead delta; a dirty same-length cache refused and memoized; a buried marker refused with no remote read; under-cap = whole refetch; a marked meta refused without asking; a probe dying on the wire = retryable; the log rate limit with a second host and a window-expiry leg — ten mutations each red on their own). **ROUND 7 — THE HEAL'S OWN COSTS, AND A COMPARISON THAT NEVER RE-ASKED:** ① the whole-file splice scan was "paid once per slot" only INSIDE one rung — `cacheUsable` runs on the slab rung and again on the ssh rung after the degradable "too large", and the slots that owe the scan are exactly the ones that REFUSE (a refused poll leaves the meta byte-identical by design, so nothing ever retires the legacy marker) ⇒ a 64 MB slot read whole, twice, on every session poll / attach / goal-sync tick, forever. The verdict is about BYTES, so it is memoized against the bytes it judged (`_deepScanMemo`, keyed inode:size:mtime, 10 min, dropped by every writer that touches the slot); `deepDone` is gone — the heal asks the question outright instead of inferring from a flag whether someone else already answered it; and `wholeCacheOk` answers in three states (clean / marker / unreadable) so only a VERDICT is remembered (a transient EMFILE must not freeze a healthy slot for the whole TTL). ② `_warnDegradeOnce` keyed its 60 s window on the HOST alone, so the first fault held the minute and every DIFFERENT fault inside it was dropped into a "+N similar" tally that names nothing (the rate limiter becoming the silent catch it replaced); the key is now host + message CLASS (`_degradeClassKey` — the same sentence with its offsets/sizes/ids blanked), so distinct faults each speak once a minute and only genuine repeats are counted. ③ the heal's gap comparison used a `localSize` stat'd BEFORE the remote round trip and cache bytes read AFTER it: a slot that shrank in between produced a mismatch that was reported as 'foreign' ("CHECKED against the remote: they are not its own") and MEMOIZED for ten minutes, condemning a healthy over-cap slot on every later poll; `_healGapIsStillOurs` re-stats before comparing and a slot that shifted under the probe is the MOVED class — terminal for this poll, memoized by nobody. Pins: test-codex-zst (M)/(N)/(O), each with its pre-fix repro and a negative control. THE REMOTE TERMINATE ASKS THE ONE IDENTITY (B-3185 r4, `killPidShell(pid)`, exported + driven for real by test-writer-sweep §14):** `killRemotePid` used to gate its SIGTERM with `case "$(ps -p N -o args=)" in *claude*|*codex*)` — the whole-argv substring B-3185 retired, still live on a KILL path, on a machine the user cannot look at (a remote `tail -f` on a transcript, an editor, a wrapper whose ARGUMENTS name `…/bin/codex`, a dtach master carrying `claude --resume …` — killing which destroys the session — all matched, and the route answered `{success:true}`). It now embeds `cliIdentityShellFns()` VERBATIM (a host has no checkout) and asks `vs_is_cli` for BOTH CLI names; the three outcomes `VS_GONE`/`VS_OK`/`VS_NOTAGENT` and the `ps`-based existence test are unchanged (`kill -0` reports another user's process as gone), only the ACT decides the exit status, and the pid is validated to be an integer AT the builder. The local twin of the same route (`/api/kill-pid` without `host`) asks `isCliProcess` for the same two names — `hostId` is a parameter here too. **ONE CACHE SLOT, MANY REMOTE FILES (2.369.x (codex-zst review batch)):** a backend's `remoteFind` predicate may resolve DIFFERENT files across polls — codex matches `rollout-*<tid>.jsonl` OR `.jsonl.zst` and the host compresses a finished rollout — while `data/remote-jsonl/<host>/<backend>/<id>.jsonl` is keyed by conversation id alone. The `.meta` therefore records `remotePath` + `compressed` next to {size,mtime}: a changed path invalidates the slot (full refetch, no cache-valid short-circuit), and a compressed remote — or an already-compressed cache file (magic-byte check, so pre-fix metas are covered too) — is NEVER delta-appended, because recompression rewrites the file rather than appending plain bytes. Without it the append-only slab path concatenated the compressed twin's bytes onto the cached plain prefix and stamped it complete; a stopped thread never changes again, so the corrupt transcript was served forever. The locate pipeline is `find … | sort | head -1` so the pick is deterministic and prefers the plain twin. **AND THE ALREADY-CORRUPTED SLOTS HEAL THEMSELVES (review follow-up, same batch):** every slot in the field carries a PRE-provenance meta, and reading “no remotePath” as “same file” is vacuously true — the hybrid a stopped thread’s slot already held kept passing the short-circuit forever. So `sameRemote` is strict (`meta.remotePath === remotePath`), a meta without provenance is NOT valid (refetch whole ONCE, rewrite it, never delta onto it), and the cache FILE is checked independently of its meta: head magic must agree with the resolved remote, and a plain cache whose last 4KB carry a NUL byte or a zstd frame header is spliced (an append lands foreign bytes at the TAIL). Single exception: a remote already past `maxBytes` cannot be refetched whole at all (the delta path is how the slot grew there), so a byte-verified cache adopts the provenance instead of failing “too large”. Pins: test-codex-zst ⑥/⑥b (stub device switching remote files under one slot; a pre-written hybrid + old-shape meta healing with the remote standing still, negative-controlled against the pre-fix predicate). only the ACT decides the exit status, and the pid is validated to be an integer AT the builder. **AND THE EXISTENCE TEST IN FRONT OF THAT IDENTITY WAS BUSYBOX-BLIND (r5).** r4 kept `C=$(ps -p N -o args=)` with the reason "`kill -0` reports another user's process as gone" — but busybox `ps` has NO `-p` (measured, busybox 1.37.0: usage block to stderr, exit 1, stdout empty), so the capture is empty for a LIVE pid exactly as for a dead one, and on any busybox-shell host EVERY Terminate answered `VS_GONE` ⇒ `killRemotePid` returned `{success:true, gone:true}` while nothing had been signalled — the route said "already gone", the card flipped, the CLI kept writing. Existence is now a LADDER OF POSITIVE EVIDENCE (`vs_alive`): `kill -0` (POSIX, a builtin in every shell that can interpret this text — its SUCCESS is proof; its FAILURE is ambiguous between EPERM and ESRCH, which is why it is handed on rather than believed) → `[ -d /proc/N ]` (Linux incl. busybox, visible for processes we may not signal) → `ps -p N` (the no-/proc rung: BSD/macOS `ps` does have `-p`). The fact = `browserDisplayFacts(s)` beside `browserSetFacts(s)` at both delivery sites: the keeper's `machineDisplayCached()` (the last probe, sync; a stale one asks a fresh probe for the next reader, never a timer; ONE probe at boot from the wiring so the first session knows), null for a conversation on another machine. **Lane channel-withdraw verify r3 (2026-09-27):** `ownConversationIdOf(s)` = the conversation id a channel verb may record as an OWNER — none while the session has no id (`NO_CID_YET`, r2) and none while it still carries its fork SOURCE's (`FORK_PENDING`: "this session is a fork that has not announced its own conversation id yet (it still carries its parent's) — try again after its first turn"); `reply` / `compose` / `withdraw` (session callers; a jbt_ job speaks for the conversation that owns it) answer 409 `bad-member` with the sentence. A pending fork had withdrawn its parent's draft and drafted AS the parent (the receipt and an "Approve and wake now" turn landed on the parent). The rule is claude-lock-capture's `liveForkPending`, never `_forkRequested` alone. `replacesOf(b)`: `replaces` must be a STRING (400 `bad-request`) — `String()` read `["p-1"]` as the id. Gate: test-channels-engine (g2) with the guard-less copy as the control.

**Lane channel-withdraw verify r4 (2026-09-27):** the own-id rule moved INTO the caller resolver — `msgCaller` answers a SESSION caller `{cid: ownConversationIdOf(s).cid, cidWhy}` (null while the id is borrowed), so `msg send`, `groupCaller`'s verbs and `withdraw` refuse a pending fork with `who.cidWhy` (409 `bad-member`, the FORK_PENDING sentence); the jbt_ branch never lends a pending fork's session for the owner conversation (`!liveForkPending(t)`). Reproduced over the real groups engine: a pending fork's `send --wake` minted the pair under the PARENT's id and the target's reply woke the parent. `request` gained the same guard (a reach request RECORDS its principal: the parent under the fork's name, or a `webui:` placeholder nobody matches). Gates: test-msg-cli-groups (the raw-id copy as control), test-channels-engine (g2) r4, test-channel-groups (the pin).

**Lane channel-withdraw verify r5 (2026-09-27):** the rule reached the OTHER resolvers and the rosters — `jobsCaller` reads `ownConversationIdOf` (`conversationId` null while borrowed, `borrowed` = the FORK_PENDING sentence; `POST /api/agent/jobs` refuses it 409 `bad-member` — a job's owner is recorded for good and every notification is a billed turn on it; a pending fork's job was OWNED BY ITS PARENT), `pageAuth` too, the user-todo route keys a pending fork's items under its `webui:` placeholder (the item was the parent's for good and the owner's reply went to the parent), and `_msgEndpoints` reads each endpoint's id through claude-lock-capture's `addressableId` (ONE predicate with server.js's `liveSessions` roster): a pending fork listed under its parent's id with its own name let a third session mint the pair under the PARENT and authorize a billed turn on it (dead parent), and made the parent `ambiguous` (live parent). The legacy `msg send` lane relays the stash's verdict (`durable:false` + "queued in memory only — … lost if VibeSpace restarts"). Gates: test-msg-cli-groups r5 (four patched-copy controls + the server.js roster pin), test-channel-outbox v5 (the relay).

**Lane channel-withdraw verify r6 (2026-09-27):** prompt-context's NEXT-TURN GROUP REPORTS block reads the caller through `ownConversationIdOf(s).cid` (it read the raw id: a pending fork's user turn rendered the PARENT's pending group messages into its own prompt and `commitReports` moved the parent's markers — the parent's own next prompt was empty); the `FORK_PENDING` sentence names the way out as a WAIT ("wait a moment and repeat the command (a fork announces its own id within seconds of starting)" — a chat fork adopts before its first turn, a terminal fork off the lock capture; "after its first turn" was never the event) and `vibespace-msg` prints a `bad-member` remedy line. Gate: test-msg-cli-groups r6 (+ the raw-id copy as control).
