`memberLoginState` is claude-only), so a narrowed-out / wiped held member read healthy at its reset and got one automatic continue; `quotaVerdictFor` now answers `usable:false, blockedUntil:0` for it (after the walled check — the arm keeps A's own reset until then). ③ **THE MANUAL USE THROUGH A CARRIER WHOSE COLD RESTART IS IN FLIGHT IS REFUSED BY NAME** — `restartPending` carries `inFlight:true` (a request went out, `restartInFlight`) ⇒ preview/POST `code:'restart_pending'` (409); `pending:true` (the pool moved, no client asked yet) ⇒ allowed; a not-in-flight carrier is preferred. **2.369.157 r4 — the round-3 verifier's major + two mediums + four lows, each reproduced with its recipe on this real engine first (test-codex-pool §R14c/§R14d/§R15 r4/§R17b/§R19b/§R19c, each beside its pre-fix control):** ① **THE HELD MEMBER IS JUDGED DIRECTLY** — `quotaVerdictFor` builds a held session's member list from `accounts.get(heldId)`, never `poolMembers` (a held member the pool no longer lists — narrowed, or its login file wiped while the process keeps its in-memory tokens — left an EMPTY set, `usable:null` "pool has no members", and the pre-fire gate let null through: a billed continue into the process still holding walled A); an empty held set is `usable:false`; the gate refuses a held verdict that is not a positive `true`; `sessionBillingMember` validates a held member with `validateHeldSlot` (a known subscription of the pool's harness — membership and login state are not asked) so the process's own wall DEMOTES it instead of `slot-not-a-member`. ② **THE VENDOR'S `reset` IS THE FACT UNTIL A READING SAYS OTHERWISE** — `holdForResetReading` PROBES the identity at once (`probeQuotaForKey`, the leader's own app-server) and again at 30 s, holding pool decisions until a reading ENDS it (`resetReadingEndsHold`: newer than the attempt AND the leader's own or one the verdict calls usable — a sibling's stale spent push is journaled and ignored), a new wall on that identity ends it (no force), or its 10-min ceiling (`RESET_HOLD_MAX_MS`) lifts it WITHOUT a forced decision (r3 forced a re-decide on the wall's pre-reset mark at 30 s and left the re-opened account); the wrapper's failed/empty post-reset re-read now arrives as `rate_limits_updated {error, onDemand, afterReset}` and is journaled as a failure. ③ **ONE SENDER of `pool-auto-switched`** — `sendColdRestart(poolId, affected)` (default switch, per-session switch, auth-failure evict, requestHeldRestart) leaves out a conversation asked inside 10 min and stamps only what went out; `claimColdRestarts` is the manual routes' twin (their response IS the request); census: one payload builder in the engine. ④ `poolMemberOfSessionFor` no longer memoizes `unknown` (one unreadable ledger read pinned a process unknown for life) and PERSISTS a ledger answer into the session-meta (`persistHeldStamp`: `heldPoolMember` + `heldPoolOrigin:'ledger'`). Lows: `resetCreditPreview` prefers a carrier that is staying and otherwise names the leaving one (`restartPending: {id, name}` — the dialog's first sentence; a person may still choose it); `sweepResetCreditAsks` re-seeds its map once per process from the open For-you items whose `action.type === 'reset-credit'` (an item filed before a restart is swept by the new engine). **2.369.157 r3 — the round-2 verifier's four findings + three lows, each reproduced with its recipe on this real engine before the fix (test-codex-pool §R14–§R20):** ① **A HELD PROCESS IS CONTINUED ONLY BY ITS HELD MEMBER** — `quotaVerdictFor(pool, {session})` judges only `heldPoolMemberFor(session)` when the session holds one (every caller is a FIRE decision: onWalledTurn's arm, scheduleWallProbe, beforeAutoResumeFire), so a codex process still on walled A after the pool moved to B arms for A's own reset instead of a 45 s "switched to a usable account (B)" whose continue went into A's login (and re-fired every quarantine window); `requestHeldRestart(session)` (onWalledTurn's `finally`, after the pool eval) re-asks ONE client to cold-restart it onto the pool's member — at most once per 10 min per session, `_heldRestartAskedAt` stamped by EVERY `pool-auto-switched` send that actually went out (default switch, per-session switch, auth-failure evict) so a request in flight is never doubled (a double resumes the conversation twice); no client ⇒ a journal line, the conversation waits for its member's reset. ② **THE RESET'S ANSWER WAITS FOR ITS OWN READING** — `reset_credit_result: reset` with no reading of that identity newer than the attempt ⇒ `holdForResetReading(key)`: `maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool` returns while the pool's current member is held (`resetCreditPendingFor`, identity group), the identity's next `rate_limits_updated` lifts it and re-decides every auto pool holding it at once (`releaseResetHold`, force — the per-record gate would swallow it), or 30 s does; the wrapper now emits the re-read FIRST (the hold is the fallback for wrappers still running old code). ③ **ONE RULE FOR WHICH MEMBER A POOL PROCESS SPEAKS AS** — `heldPoolMemberFor` delegates to `accounts.poolMemberOfSession` through `poolMemberOfSessionFor` (a LEDGER answer is memoized onto the session as its stamp with `_heldPoolOrigin:'ledger'`; an `unknown` one is memoized too — both final); the default switch no longer re-attributes held followers (server.js's resolver reads the same rule). ④ **`held-unknown`** — `creditIdentityFor` → `{key, current, moved, unknown}`; the auto rung refuses an unknown holder by name and `resetCreditCarriers` skips it (no person's credit either). Lows: `writeResetCredit` returns the ceiling's `detail` and the wall card says `refused it (<code>) for <account> — <sentence>` (the manual `spend_refused` error carries it too); the ask-mode For-you item carries `expiresAt` = the wall's reset and `sweepResetCreditAsks` (every kickPoolEval + every preview that finds no carrier) dismisses it once no running process holds that login. **2.369.157 r2 — FIVE VERIFIED FINDINGS ON THE RESET-CREDIT RUNG, each reproduced on this real engine before its fix (test-codex-pool §R8–§R13):** ① **THE ONE-TRY FLOOR IS PER IDENTITY** — `_resetCreditTries` (credit identity → `{at, sid, origin, resetsAtSec, lane, followers, outcome}`; read through the identity GROUP by `resetCreditTryFor`/`resetCreditTriedAt`) replaces the per-session stamp as the rung's `cooldownUntilSec` AND the manual preview's cooldown; two warm conversations billing one walled account used to spend TWO credits. While an attempt is IN FLIGHT (no answer, inside the 10-min floor) a sibling walled on the same identity FOLLOWS it (the rung answers `'consumed'` — the caller returns) and the leader's `reset_credit_result` settles every follower (`settleResetCreditTry`: a reset ⇒ `noteRecovered` for each; a failure ⇒ each walks `walkLadderAfterCredit` — the ONE spelling of switch + `noteWallSignal` + `noteTurnEnd`); no answer within the floor = a failure (an unref'd timer; the auto leader walks too, once — `alreadyWalked` stops a late answer walking it twice). The AUTO rung refuses `moved` by name (`kept (pool-moved — this conversation still holds <A>'s login, the pool moved to <B>; it restarts there)`); a PERSON may still spend it on A through that wrapper (charged to A). The stored count is DATED where the engine writes it (`resetCredits.at` = the stating snapshot's `fetchedAt`) because the cache writer now carries it across pushes that do not state it: `resetCreditsLeft` trusts the session's own last read (`_resetCreditsSeen.at`) over the carried file count when it is fresher (a read whose file write lost a same-millisecond tie or was archived). ⑤ **THE COLD RUNG AFTER A SWITCH THAT MOVED NOTHING**: `resetCreditRung(…, {ladderPosition})` answers `'switch-first'` for the verdict's `cold-switch-first`; both exhaustion sites keep `rcArgs`, compare `poolDefaultOf(session)` around `maybePoolAutoSwitch`, and when nothing moved (the 10 s eval gate, nowhere after all) ask again at `'after-switch'` — the verdict's rung that had no call site (the 2.355.0 unwired class). ### usage-routes.js

  usage-routes.js      — setupUsage() (2.92.0 split): the ENTIRE usage/rate-limit cluster from server.js — passive statusline ingest, read-only OAuth token, opt-in active poll, on-demand quota refresh, codex rollout-tail summarizer (§ban-safety rules apply — see kb-design-lessons §9). **Account-identity truth (2.114.1, real mixup report):** ~/.claude.json's oauthAccount goes STALE after a /login switch (config said fish.audio, token was actually gmail — popup looked like two subs swapped quotas). The on-demand ⟳ ALSO fetches `/api/oauth/claude_cli/roles` (same human-gated click, never scheduled) and bakes orgUuid/orgName/orgEmail into the usage cache; the global↔named link prefers org-uuid equality over config-email match (proven-different org BREAKS an email match); `globalLogin.{actualEmail,identityMismatch}` drive the popup's corrected label + amber warning; data/bin/vibespace-usage preserve-merges the org fields like scopedWeekly. Smoke: scripts/test-usage-link.mjs. **2.260.0 chat-mode freshness (B-7edc/B-292b): ⟳ PREFERS the CLI's own `get_usage` control channel** — a live LOCAL claude chat session billed to the refreshed account answers `get_usage` ITSELF (first-party fetch, = typing /usage there; probeUsageForAccountKey in server.js → vsu- request_id interception in the stdout parse → usage-cache write), human-gated + 60s throttle + silent fallback to the bare read-only call. **AUTO-firing get_usage is REJECTED (user decision 2026-08-09): a machine-initiated quota check is the banned automated-access pattern regardless of who makes the HTTP call.** The chat-mode PASSIVE signal is the LIMIT BANNER instead: the CLI's own "You've reached your … limit" chat record → ClaudeCodeAdapter.parseLimitBanner (5h/weekly/scoped-by-name; unknown→fiveHour = shortest self-heal) → markLimitBanner writes the bucket dead into usage-cache (keeps a known future reset, else bounded 5h/24h guess so the marker self-expires via reset-passed⇒full) + IMMEDIATELY maybePoolAutoSwitch — zero API calls, this is what makes pool auto-switch work for chat-only accounts. LIVE-VERIFIED get_usage envelope (2026-08-09, real session, ZERO inference — the CLI answers without any turn): payload at `control_response.response.response` (DOUBLE nesting); `utilization` = 0-100 INTEGERS (parser normalizes >1); NO `model_scoped` array — named nullable fields (`seven_day_opus`/`seven_day_sonnet`) + internal CODENAME buckets. **What the parse does with them (re-verified against the code 2026-09-22 — the old words "no-resets_at codenames skipped" stopped being true at r6, 2026-09-09):** parseGetUsageResponse MERGES every named/codename bucket beside the `model_scoped` array (an array entry wins on the same name — never a fallback, 2.305.0); a bucket WITHOUT `resets_at` is KEPT (a stated spend counts, it just names no deadline — r6); a `null` field is skipped (the vendor saying there is no such limit); a window-shaped key with no readable number is counted as a DROP so the parse does not claim to have enumerated the scope. The rule is "any top-level object carrying `utilization`/`used_percentage` that is not five_hour/seven_day/extra_usage/seven_day_oauth_apps is a model cap" — which would MISFILE the credit-program keys the 2.1.280 envelope carries (`cinder_cove`, and `cedar_ember`/`juniper_tide` if they ever carry a utilization) as an exhausted model cap. **identityMismatch semantics (2.337.3, owner confusion report):** `_usageGlobalLink.email` comes from the GLOBAL ~/.claude.json oauthAccount — a field EVERY relocated dir login also stamps (CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR relocates only the secret store; the 2.244.2 consequence). ### incident.js

**dc-twins M4:** the scene is DECLARED — each harness descriptor's `store.scene { process, locks, listings: [[label, dir, max]], version }` (claude: claude / .claude/sessions / project dirs / claude; codex: codex / — / codex sessions / codex). captureLocal's process filter, its `<id>Locks` copies (claude's key stays `claudeLocks`) and REMOTE_SCRIPT's ps words, lock loops, listings and versions line are generated from `scenes()`; the generated remote script is byte-identical to before except the `grep -E` word order. test-incident: a fake harness registered with one line appears in the remote scene.

  incident.js          — FREEZE THE SCENE for a panic-button capture (2.239.0, the admin's correction: users troubleshoot their own problems — ssh/resume/kill — and destroy the evidence before anyone looks). captureLocal: process table, dtach socket stats, VERBATIM copies of session-meta + wrapper-meta (clobbered by every create/kill), claude lock files (deleted on CLI exit), and per referenced conversation the transcript IDENTITY (size+mtime+**sha256**+frozen 512KB tail — a later manual `--resume` double-write/fork becomes provable). captureRemote: one bounded probe per machine over hosts._hostShell (ssh AND dial) — remote process table, locks, keeper/agentd state, transcript stat+sha256+last timestamps, project dirs, disk, CLI versions. ALL read-only + bounded (child processes with timeouts — never node fs on a possibly-hung mount, §2.108.3; ≤6 hosts, ≤12 conversations, size-capped copies) and per-step try/caught so a dead host degrades the bundle instead of failing it. Runs ASYNC after the id is returned; `env.json.pending` marks a cut-off freeze. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (16 asserts incl. frozen-copy-survives-clobber). **B-8ebb (last row, codex rollouts in the freeze):** the transcript-identity loop no longer knows only claude's project dirs — after the claude scan it iterates the HARNESS REGISTRY (`require('./harnesses').list()`, lazy) and asks each `store.locate(cid)` where its conversation lives: codex rollouts (`rollout-*-<tid>.jsonl` / `.jsonl.zst`, the local tree or the remote-jsonl cache) get the same size+mtime+sha256 identity + frozen tail (`<cid>__<dir>.tail.jsonl[.zst]`, `harness:'codex'`, `compressed:true` for a .zst whose raw tail bytes are the evidence, not lines); claude's locate dedups against the scan. The remote probe is generated the same way — `buildRemoteTranscriptProbe(cids)` emits one `find <root> <findExpr> | probe_transcript` line per (conversation × harness) from each descriptor's `store.remoteFind(id)` (claude's expression byte-identical to before, codex's `$HOME/.codex/sessions … rollout-*<id>.jsonl(.zst)` added; `probe_transcript` is one shell function; `lastts` greps with -a for compressed bytes) and the versions line asks codex too. Never a backend id branch in incident.js — a third harness freezes by registering a store. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (+8: a codex rollout in the cache is fingerprinted + tail-frozen + tagged, the claude conversation still freezes once, remote probe lines per harness, no id branch).

**TERMINAL TAILS (2.369.118, userW's login-terminal report froze the wrapper sidecar only).** `captureLocal(dir, {dataDir, cids, terminalIds})` copies the LAST 64 KB (`TERMINAL_TAIL`, `copyTail`) of every named terminal-mode session's raw PTY buffer to `frozen/buffers/<id>.tail` and records `{bytes, truncatedFrom}` under `local.terminalTails`; ids are validated twice (the wiring's `idOk` and the freeze's own filter — a buffer id is a file name). `_incidentTargets` (incident-wiring) collects them from live terminal-mode sessions and from the reporter's terminal windows; `_incidentServerState` adds `desktop` (singleton facts, `keeper.listApps()`, `stream.stats()`) through the late-bound `getDesktop` dep. Gate: test-incident.

**SESSION-META FROZEN AS DATA (2.369.160, inc-mudv05ja-n5rv).** The 64 KiB byte cap (`copyCapped`, which keeps the TAIL bytes) froze every session-meta carrying `taskRecords` (2.369.140; the owner's own was 96 877 B) into an unparseable half — exactly the sessions with workflows, which is what a workflow incident needs. Session-meta AND wrapper-meta are now copied by `copyJsonWhole(src, dest, ceiling)` (exported with `META_COPY_MAX` = 2 MiB): WHOLE up to the ceiling; above it a VALID JSON trimmed as data — the largest top-level array keeps its NEWEST records (halving until it fits), then the next field; a non-array field too big is dropped whole; `_frozenTrimmed: {originalBytes, ceiling, dropped: [{field, from, kept} | {field, bytes, whole}]}` names every touch; a file that does not parse (or is over `META_PARSE_MAX` 16 MiB — never a sync parse that big on the server loop) freezes as `{_frozenTrimmed: {unparseable: true, …}, rawTail}`. A trimmed/failed copy is noted on `env.local.sessionMetas[f].frozen`. `copyCapped` remains only for the transcript tail (bytes ARE the evidence there). 不变量=a frozen file is truncated as DATA, never as bytes. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (+5: a 98 KB meta with 40 taskRecords freezes whole, a 3 MB one freezes ≤ 2 MiB with the marker and the newest record, the copier's three branches).

### routes/persistence.js

  routes/persistence.js — …also **LAYOUT ROLLBACK POINTS (2.296.0, after a bug flattened a user's whole desktop layout)**: `writeLayouts` is the ONE choke point every layout write passes through, so it snapshots the PREVIOUS state into `data/layout-history/` whenever the desktop→window SHAPE changes (per-desktop sorted window ids; geometry drags and z-order churn deliberately ignored or one drag would evict every useful restore point). A destructive write therefore always leaves the last good shape on disk — the thing the incident lacked, where two EMPTIED desktops made even the pre-damage mapping unrecoverable. Bounded 40; **filenames carry a sequence suffix — a bare ISO stamp has ms resolution and a mass-resume burst lands inside one millisecond, silently overwriting the older entry i.e. destroying the pre-damage state exactly when it matters (caught by the bounded-history assertion)**. Legacy top-level `autoSave` counted too (instances without virtual desktops otherwise read "0 windows"). Routes GET /api/layout-history + POST /api/layout-history/:id/restore (id regex-validated; restoring writes through the same path so it is ITSELF undoable). UI: ⚙ → Restore a previous layout… (setup-flows `_showLayoutHistory`). Test: scripts/test-layout-history.mjs (11). **2026-09-29 (userW inc-mun7qjmw-iksh): a point also records `change` = the change that FOLLOWED it (PURE `desktopChanges(prev, next)`: `[[name, before, after], …]` per desktop whose window set changed, computed at the write — the caller mutates `next` in place later; null for the forced restore snapshot), listed by GET /api/layout-history and drawn under the row as "Then: HR 3 → 1" — every row used to read the same "N windows — …" and the damage was in none of them (test-layout-history 16).** **USER-STATE CARRIES EVERY KEY (2026-09-14):** `normalizeUserState` rebuilds only the session-ref keys it migrates (`USER_STATE_DEFAULT`'s set) and carries every OTHER top-level key through verbatim — it used to return a literal of exactly the session keys, so any per-feature preference PATCHed here was dropped on the very write that carried it (measured in headless chrome: `PATCH {desktopAppAdvancedOpen:true}` ⇒ GET never carried it; the desktop-app launcher's `desktopAppRecents` never survived a reload since 2.369.96). The merge-only PATCH (B-b87b) is now real for any key; a full-document POST from a stale tab still replaces the whole document (the documented residual).

### lib/incident-recorder.js

  lib/incident-recorder.js — "Report a problem" panic button (2.238.0, the timezone-gap fix): ALWAYS-ON client ring buffers (clicks/coarse keys — typed TEXT never recorded, only a per-burst marker; ws message TYPES both directions, never payloads; console errors/warns) + on-demand full client snapshot → POST /api/incident → server adds its own scene (activeSessions digest, 30-min sysinfo history, in-memory server console ring (600 lines, wraps console.* in server.js), hosts digest, resume-breaker table + remote-discovery cache digest — the two conversation-disappeared-class facts that survive nowhere else, 2.238.1) → data/incidents/<inc-id>/bundle.json (+followup.json auto-appended 2min later; newest 30 kept). **snapshot.chatTraces (2.264.0, B-21bc user request): each open chat window's SCROLL TRACER ring tail ships automatically** — chat-view's `_trace()` is an always-on capped ring again (the 2.111.8 removal stubbed it AND the documented Ctrl+Shift+J dump, leaving viewport-jump reports blind): paging/trim/jump/runsRestore breadcrumbs + a coarse scroll sampler (>400px moves w/ pin state + wheelAgo — user-scroll vs programmatic-yank discriminator) + an unpin breadcrumb; positions/op tags only, never content. User relays the short id; admin reads the bundle. Entry: ⚙ → Report a problem…; GET /api/incidents lists. **SEMANTIC OP BREADCRUMBS (2.296.0): `window.__vsOp(name, data)` pushes into a 4th ring (`op`, cap 300) — for ops that RELOCATE OR REPLACE a window/session, the class where "what did the app just do to my layout" is the whole question. The pool-collapse incident left NO trace of its desktop reassignments (the action ring has clicks, the ws ring has message types; neither answers 'what moved these windows'), so the sequence had to be reconstructed by reading code. Wired at desktop-move / pool-cold-restart / resume-place. Names+ids only — the privacy rule is unchanged. The server bundle also carries the LAYOUT TABLE (window→desktop+sid) and the layout-history index, which is what turns a flattened layout from JSON surgery into one click.** PRIVACY: the note is the only free text — keep it that way. ### settings-view.js — what the Settings window draws (B-df40 part 2, 2.369.202; design desk settings-cleanup §2 P2)

PURE (imports nothing; `t` passed in) — the window (settings-ui.js `_renderContent`) and scripts/test-settings-view.mjs call the same functions. Two OPTIONAL row fields, pure data so a derived harness row or a plugin row survives JSON: `tier: 'advanced'` (absent = everyday) and `when: <clause> | [<clause>…]` (all must hold). A clause carries exactly ONE tag of the closed, frozen `WHEN_KINDS = ['setting','fact','harness','channel']` (re-exported by settings-schema.js — lane channel-declared-settings derives `when: { channel }` rows on it): `{setting, is}` / `{setting, isNot}` / `{setting}` (truthy), `{fact: 'vnc'|'desktopApps'}` (`WHEN_FACTS`), `{harness: <prefix>}` (that CLI resolved here), `{channel: <kind>}` (an account of that vendor exists). A clause the client cannot decide — a fact not known yet, a failed read, an unknown tag, a key without a row — HOLDS: ignorance hides nothing (test-architecture 44e makes the typo cases build-red instead). `rowRelevant(row, ctx)` / `failingClause` / `whyHidden(row, ctx, t)` (the reason in words: "turn on “Compact mode” first", "this machine has no display backend", "the Codex CLI is not installed on this machine", "no Lark account is linked"). `settingsViewModel(schema, {categories, query, showAdvanced, ctx, isModified, t})` walks the CENSUS list (a row whose category is not listed is not drawn, as §44 always said) and applies, in order: (1) a search shows every match, relevance and tier ignored, with chips; (2) a modified row always shows — an advanced one with a false `when` carries BOTH chips; (3) otherwise a false `when` hides the row, and a section with no row and no hidden-advanced line is not drawn, nor its nav item; (4) an advanced row draws only while `showAdvanced`, else it is counted in `hiddenAdvanced` (rows rules 1–2 drew never are). Chips `{kind: advanced|unused|reload, text, title}`; `hiddenAdvancedText(n, t)` = the line. The window builds the facts ONCE per open (`_buildFacts`): `vnc` from `app._vncAvailable` (undefined until probed), `desktopApps` true / false only once desktop-app-launcher's probe answered (`app._desktopAppsKnown`), `harnesses` = app.js's `_harnessesHere` from /api/home's per-harness `cli` (cli-env.js: the path cliCmds resolved — absolute — vs the bare name; `installed` keeps the New Session picker unchanged), `channels` from ONE `GET /api/channels/adapters` (routes/channels.js: id/kind/builtin/enabled from `adapterRecords()`, never the digest's conversations) fetched only when some row has a channel clause, re-rendering once on the answer. A control of a row other rows' `when` reads (`_governors`) re-draws on change, keeping the place (`_rerenderKeepingPlace`). The tier rule (the design's): timers / thresholds in s·min·ms, byte and MB budgets, per-second / per-minute paces, raw JSON state, operator and daemon switches, every `confirmOn` row, the stop-nudge numbers, CLI pass-through flags (extra args, prompt snapshot, autocompact, TUI renderer) ⇒ advanced (77 of 192); show/hide and position switches, modes, master switches, the Spending ceilings, the reserve floor, the harness defaults, the outbox guards ⇒ everyday. ### usage-eta.js (PURE)

    usage-eta.js       — THE compact reset countdown (2026-09-14; imports nothing, DOM-free, the CLOCK is an argument so no test depends on the time of day): `compactEta(resetAtMs, nowMs)` → `65m` (45 s ≤ remaining < 2 h, minutes rounded) / `15h` (2–72 h, hours rounded) / `3d` (≥ 72 h, days rounded — 72 h reads 3d, 84 h reads 4d) / null under 45 s, passed, missing or unparseable (the roster's existing 45 s guard, `ETA_MIN_MS`); rounding happens INSIDE the band (119.5 min is "120m", never "2h"). `bucketResetMs` (unix SECONDS in the cache, ms tolerated), `bucketMayNameDeadline` (state absent or 'running' may; 'empty' — a not-yet-started window whose reset slides with the clock, B-8b12 — and 'unknown' may not: quota-model's `bucketCounts` in the legacy spelling, kept here so a reader that only has the derived view asks the same question) and `bucketEta(bucket, nowMs)` composing both. Readers: manage-agents `_acctUsageHtml` (every donut column + the ≤340px pill) and the Machines-tab host pill; exported for the taskbar and any later surface. **2026-09-15 (owner: 写成 2d21h38m 的形式, 一眼扫过去就能知道哪个账号马上要可用了): `fullEta(resetAtMs, nowMs)` = the FULL form — whole minutes (45 s reads 1m, the same `ETA_MIN_MS` guard), leading zero units dropped (`21h38m`, `38m`), inner zeros KEPT (`2d0h5m`) so a column stays tabular — and `accountResetEta(entries, nowMs)` = ONE instant per account from `[{bucket, pct, label?, spentPct?}]`: a bucket at/over its `spentPct` bar (the roster passes the pool's own hard bars from account-pool-auto `THRESH`; the default 100 = reads fully used) makes the account BLOCKED and the answer is the LATEST reset among its spent buckets (that is when it is usable again), else the EARLIEST upcoming reset; only a bucket that may name a deadline counts, a spent bucket whose reset PASSED rolled over and blocks nothing, no candidate ⇒ null (never "0m"); the answer `{ms, text, blocked, label, pct}` carries the instant so the roster's 30 s tick re-spells it on its own clock. The module still mentions no raw bucket field by name (the quota-model reader census greps whole files).** Gate: scripts/test-usage-eta.mjs (the band table at every boundary, the refusals, the PURE census; §5/§6 the full form and the pick).

### resume-continuity.js (PURE, B-6b6d)

  src/resume-continuity.js — **THE RESUME LADDER**: `resumeSpawnPick({explicit, conversation, instanceDefault, resume, hasSource})` → `{value, origin}` with `origin ∈ chosen|conversation|instance|harness`, plus `continuityLogLine`. The owner's 2026-09-07 ruling in one function: **a conversation's OWN model/effort wins on resume/fork/restart; the instance default is a NEW-session default; an explicit per-session pick beats both.** TWO callers, one law — the CLIENT (session-lifecycle `createSession`, `hasSource:false` = only the server can read a conversation's records ⇒ a continuation sends NOTHING) and the SERVER (ws-create, immediately before `buildSessionArgs`, with the harness descriptor's `store.lastTurn<Knob>` reader wired in). `hasSource` is DERIVED from that hook's presence — never a parallel caps boolean. **`''` is a STATED choice, `undefined` is silence, and the difference only survives on a NEW session** (round 2): the New Session dialog's first option IS `''` ("Auto (model default)"), so collapsing it made an explicit Auto resolve to the instance default; on a non-continuation `''` wins as `{value:'', origin:'chosen'}` and the client sends the resolved value verbatim so it survives the wire. On a CONTINUATION the create message carries `model: sessionModel || undefined`, so there an explicit Auto and an absent field really are identical bytes and both mean "take the conversation's own value". A knob with NO source sends nothing on a resume rather than the default (an unconditional default there IS the defect); a source that came up EMPTY falls back to the default and the caller LOGS it. **`applyOriginHint(origin, hint)` (round 3)** — the wire's other half. On a NEW session the CLIENT resolves `<prefix>.default*` (it needs the value for its own chip, and it owns the legacy `session.defaultEffort` key + `settings.isModified`, which the server cannot see) and sends it VERBATIM, so the server saw a bare string it could only read as a pick: `_modelOrigin`/`_effortOrigin` were ALWAYS `'chosen'` for a new session, `'instance'`/`'harness'` were unreachable there, and Session Properties called `<prefix>.defaultModel` “your choice for this session” on every create path that shows no picker (openShellTerminal, the toolbar, setup-flows, manage-agents). The client now also sends the origin it computed (`spawnOriginHint`) and this reconciles: it may ONLY downgrade the server's own `'chosen'` to `'instance'`/`'harness'`, never upgrade or re-point a rung the server decided from facts the client never had, and it never touches the VALUE; a `'conversation'`/`'chosen'`/garbage hint is ignored, and an older client that sends none keeps master's answer. Gate: scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs legs ⑪ / ⑫ / ⑫ c.

**PENDING BINDS ARE A LIST PER SESSION (2.369.173).** `_pendingTaskBinds` = Map<webuiId, {taskIds[], notId}> (was webuiId → ONE taskId, and a second registration REPLACED the first). `_registerPendingTaskBind(webuiId, taskIds, {notId})` merges (PURE `mergePendingBind`); `_processPendingTaskBinds` (run on every active-sessions merge in sidebar.js) asks PURE `pendingBindVerdict(entry, liveRow)` — wait while the row is unlisted, has no id, or still carries `notId` (a fork's source id) — then binds EVERY id to `<backend>:<id>` through the ordinary `_taskBind` write-through (multi-client comes free) and drops the entry. An entry whose session was LISTED once and has left the live list (the fork died before its own id appeared) is dropped at once — the loop marks `entry.seen` on the first listing and the verdict answers `{drop:true, why:'gone'}`; before the fix round such an entry waited for the >20 cap. The cap sweep (PURE `sweepPendingBinds`) still covers entries never listed at all — a live fork waiting for its own id keeps its entry. The queue is per-tab memory: a reload before a fork's first input loses the EXTRA binds (the spawn group is safe server-side as `_initialGroupId`).

### src/claude-lock-capture.js

**Verify r3 (lane channel-withdraw, 2026-09-27):** `liveForkPending(session)` = `restoredForkPending` read off the LIVE fields (`_forkRequested`, `claudeSessionId` / `backendSessionId`, `forkedFrom`; no `forkSourceId` on the live object) — "does this session still carry its fork SOURCE's conversation id?". `_forkRequested` alone is not the fact: a claude adoption clears it, a codex adoption never does (codex-events pushes the old thread id into `forkedFrom` instead). agent-routes' channel verbs refuse an owner-recording act while it answers true.

    claude-lock-capture.js — **2026-10-07 (B-8b7b)** `forkResumedParent` / `captureForkProof` (an `onSeed` sighting in pickClaudeLock) + armLockCapture `proof`/`onResumedParent` (two consecutive sightings ⇒ verdict).
    claude-lock-capture.js — SHARED (fs/path only; `readPpid` injected from src/cli-identity.js) THE LOCAL CLAUDE LOCK CAPTURE, one implementation for ws-create's create-time chain and boot-restore's re-arm (`armRestoredCapture`, every restored dtach AND R6 pipe session). **THE WITNESS IS THE PID, NEVER THE CLOCK (round 2):** a lock (`~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`) is this session's iff its pid is ALIVE and DESCENDS from THIS session's wrapper — the wrapper writes its own pid into its sidecar (`<BUFFERS_DIR>/<id>.json` `pid`) before it spawns the CLI; `wrapperDepthOf(wrapperPid, readPpid)` walks the parent chain (≤ 8 hops; a dead pid answers 0). `pickClaudeLock({locks, createdAt, claimed, excludeId, pidDepth, isWriter})` (PURE): a witnessed lock, started at/after the session's creation (drops a file that PREDATES the session — not the reuse guard), not claimed, not the fork seed, and (round 3) WRITTEN BY ITS PID — `lockWrittenByItsPid`: a numeric `procStart` must equal the live pid's /proc stat field 22 (cli-identity `procStartTicks`), else the pid must be a claude by `isCliProcess` (a stale lock under the pid name of a `sleep` the CLI ran descends from the wrapper too); the NEAREST descendant wins (a `claude` the CLI runs from a tool is deeper), a tie or no witness ⇒ null. **Round 4: the nearest is found FIRST and judged after** — the seed, a claimed id or a pre-creation file as the nearest lock ⇒ null, never the next one down (the one-pass filter skipped a misread session's own depth-1 lock and adopted a nested `claude -p`'s depth-3 lock, persisting the foreign id). **Round 5: an unreadable lock is a witness too** — `readClaudeLocks` returns `{pid, unreadable:true}` for a torn `<pid>.json` (a vanished file is skipped), and a placeholder as the nearest ⇒ null (a CLI rewriting its own lock no longer lets the nested claude's lock become "the nearest"). No cwd rule, no pre-creation slack, no directory or start-time order. `captureLockId` = one attempt; `armLockCapture` = the chain: `captureDelay` 2 s, 1 s × 14, 5 s × 30, then 30 s — NO attempt cap, it ends only on adoption, on the session leaving the live list, or when `lockCaptureWanted` says no; one chain per session (WeakSet). `lockCaptureWanted(session)` (local + claude + (no id | a pending `_forkRequested` fork still carrying its source's id — either mode since round 3: a restored chat fork's init lost to the restart is never replayed), re-asked every attempt), `ownsItsId(meta)` (round 3: which restored metas may enter boot-restore's conversation DEDUP — a pending fork's borrowed id is not a claim; the dedup retired the live PARENT of every pending fork, and at the update boot every master-created terminal fork's parent), `claimedLockIds` (a pending fork's borrowed id claims nothing), `adoptCapturedId` (a fork pushes its seed onto `forkedFrom`, persists `forkRequested:false`), `restoredForkPending(meta)` (boot-restore's `_forkRequested`: pending only while the record still names its source or no id — an adopted chat fork whose meta kept `true` is not; round 4: with no `forkSourceId` (every pre-2.369.134 record) a non-empty `forkedFrom` without the current id = the adoption's trace ⇒ OWNS its id). **`addressableId(session)` (lane channel-withdraw verify r5, 2026-09-27) = the conversation id a LIVE session may be addressed by: its own, or null while `liveForkPending` — the ONE predicate behind server.js's `liveSessions` roster (the groups + channels engines), agent-routes' `_msgEndpoints` and `ownConversationIdOf`; listed under its parent's id a pending fork was a third session's target (the pair minted under the PARENT, a billed turn authorized on it) and made the parent `ambiguous`.** What the clock rules did (all reproduced on a scratch server with a fake CLI): two sessions created together swapped ids whenever the later one's CLI wrote first; a dead CLI's leftover lock or an external same-cwd claude started ≤ 5 s before creation was adopted (and a restored pending fork cleared its flag on that guess); a fork whose CLI took > ~17 s kept its parent's id for life. Gate: test-fork-groups ⑥/⑦.

**THE TERMINAL-MODE FORK AND THE PARENT/FORK CAPTURE RACE (2026-09-25, lane-fork-group verifier, reproduced on a scratch server with a fake CLI).** ① ws-create seeds a claude fork's row with the PARENT's id; chat adopts the fork's own from the stream, terminal mode has no parser, and the capture was gated on `!session.claudeSessionId` ⇒ a terminal fork was tracked under its parent's key for life (its real conversation in no Task Group once it ended; the pending binds waited for ever). ② The capture's claim set counted a pending fork's SEEDED id, i.e. the parent's own; a parent whose capture ran after the fork was created (the chain never re-checked whether the stream had named it first) skipped its own lock and adopted the FORK's — two rows on one conversation, the parent's conversation tracked by nobody and then taken by the next same-cwd session. STANDING SWEEP: the remote twin — a remote session never scans the local lock dir (2.156.2) and gets its id from the stream's first-capture; a remote TERMINAL claude fork therefore has no adopter (stated in the session-lifecycle paragraph); the daemon's R6 pipe sessions are chat-only. Gate: test-fork-groups ⑥/⑦ (the chain over real lock files + a real TaskGroupManager, both races in both readdir orders, and two controls: the shipped empty-id gate and the seed-as-claim set, each RED). **ROUND 2 (same day, the fix round's own verifier): the round-1 pick was still a CLOCK rule** (first unclaimed same-cwd lock started at/after creation, 5 s slack) — two sessions created together swapped ids when the later one's CLI wrote first, a dead or external same-cwd lock inside the slack was adopted (a restored pending fork cleared its flag on it, for good), and the chain gave up after ~17 s; the restored `forkRequested` of an adopted chat fork made its own id unclaimed. Now the witness is the PID (see the claude-lock-capture.js entry above), the chain has no cap, and `restoredForkPending` + the stream adoption write re-listing `forkRequested:false` close the flag. Round 1's "both readdir orders" was one order on tmpfs; the pure pick is now fed both. **ROUND 3 (the round-2 fix's verifiers):** the boot dedup retired a pending fork's parent (fixed by `ownsItsId`), a live NON-CLI descendant's stale lock was adopted (the writer witness), a restored pending chat fork never adopted (capture in chat mode + the chat consumer's preamble strip), and two pins proved nothing (a tie-green no-sidecar leg, a comment-satisfied wiring pin). Gates: test-fork-groups (127, sixteen controls) + test-fork-restore (heavy: the real SIGKILL-restart). **ROUND 4:** a pre-.134 adopted chat fork's meta (flag never cleared, no source) was misread as pending and its capture adopted a NESTED claude's lock past its own excluded one (the nearest-first pick + the `forkedFrom` trace); dtach's `[EOF - dtach terminating]` was reported as a dropped record on every natural exit (the JSON-prefix test; telemetry capped like the log). **ROUND 5:** a torn nearest lock was skipped and the nested one judged (the unreadable placeholder); round 4's `DTACH_BANNER` list was dead under the prefix test and removed — the consumer leg now feeds all five dtach banners, control (r) reverts the regex alone. test-fork-groups 148, twenty-two controls. ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants.md

    sidebar-mounts.js  — Remote tab: machines (ssh hosts) + storage (mounts) rendering (installSidebarMounts mixin, ~1000 lines; 2.152.0: "Pair a device" action + _showDevicePairDialog — dial-out device pairing, mints via POST /api/agentd/dial-pair and renders the full installer command incl BOTH --dial-token and --host-token; the host token is what the daemon verifies OUR mux hello against — omit it and the device dials in but rejects every command). **KEY IMPORT (2.246.0): `_askPrivateKey({text,error,showPass})` is the reusable, PREFILLABLE "Private key" sub-dialog** — resolves {privateKey, keyPassphrase} or null; the Add-machine POST wraps it in a RETRY LOOP (a KEY_ERR_CODES failure re-opens it with the key still pasted + the localized reason, so a wrong passphrase is never a dead end). **TWO ORDERING TRAPS, both real: (1) `createModalShell`'s close() fires onClose on EVERY path, so the submit handler must `resolve(value)` BEFORE `ctx.close()` — close-then-resolve lets the cancel-resolver win and "Use this key" behaves exactly like Cancel (the entire paste-a-key flow was dead; idempotency alone does NOT save you, the FIRST settle wins; caught only by the headless dialog test). (2) sub-dialogs REUSE the overlay id `mounts-dialog-overlay`, and createModalShell REMOVES the existing one — so from the first sub-dialog onward the Add-machine dialog is DETACHED and _mountsDialog's inline error element renders into nothing; the submit callback takes `err` and toasts when `!err.isConnected`.** Passphrase + key text are read RAW from the elements (a passphrase may legitimately have leading/trailing whitespace — verified ssh-keygen accepts `'p@ss w/ spaces '`), deliberately bypassing _mountsDialog's trimming field reader. Detection reveals affordances but NEVER blocks submit (server is authoritative; an always-available "Key has a passphrase?" toggle covers a misjudged format), and the passphrase row uses `style.display`, not a `hidden` class (no global `.hidden` rule in this project)

**Chunk 4a — D2: SWITCHING A STORAGE RECORD'S OAUTH CLIENT IS A RE-AUTHORIZATION** (the channel accounts' rule, adopted by the storage side in its own commit; docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md §6 D2). `_showEditMountDialog`'s Save asks `_mountClientSwitch(cfg, cur, presets)` whether the client the record RESOLVES to changes — the server's own resolution (`MountManager._driveClient` / gmail-sync `_client`): a custom id wins (Gmail: id + secret), else the preset key, else the resolver's fallback (the only preset, else `default`, else rclone's built-in), so `''` → the only preset is NOT a switch; the SECRET is not the identity (a rotated secret of the same client keeps its tokens and saves directly). ONE field renderer + ONE consent block + ONE cross-browser link row for every "connect a thing with a login" dialog (design-integrations-per-account §8.1 #12, D1: "two dialogs = one component"). ### src/lib/press-select.js + utils.js `installLongPressContextMenu` / `pressFacts` + chat-renderers `addMsgMoreBtn` — A LONG PRESS ON SELECTABLE TEXT IS A SELECTION (lane mobile-select, 2026-10-02)

**The report:** "手机模式下想要复制一段chatview里的内容会触发右键菜单导致选择了右键菜单的内容，无法正确选择要复制的内容" (a tester's phone: pressing and holding chat text to copy it opened the message menu, and the selection landed on the menu). **Measured** (Chrome's own touch gesture path — `Emulation.setEmitTouchEventsForMouse('mobile')`, 390×844 DPR 3, Android UA; `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` never produces the native long press in headless): +0 touchstart on the `<p>` → +501 ms OUR synthetic (untrusted) contextmenu → chat-view prevented it and opened the menu with its corner AT THE FINGER → +680 ms the native long press: `selectstart` (the word selected) → a TRUSTED contextmenu, `pointerType` touch → chat-view prevented it and built the menu a second time → `selectionchange` with the word under the menu. iOS fires no contextmenu: our timer was the only menu, racing iOS's own selection.
**PURE `press-select.js` (imports nothing):** `pressTargetClass({native, chrome, overText, userSelect})` = native (`NATIVE_PRESS_SELECTOR`, the pre-lane exclusion list) > chrome (`PRESS_CHROME_SELECTOR`: button, summary, role=button/menuitem, [data-popover], .context-menu) > text (a glyph under the finger — `pointOnText` within `TEXT_SLOP_PX` 6 of a line fragment — AND `effectiveUserSelect` ≠ none, the first non-auto value from the element up so Blink's inherited and Gecko's `auto` read alike) > chrome; `longPressVerdict({device, target})` = THE TABLE (touch × text = selection, touch × chrome = menu, touch × native = native, a mouse = menu always); `selectStartAllowed({touching, verdict, handled})` (a menu press an app handler TOOK holds the platform's selection off; nobody took it ⇒ the platform selects as before); `trustedContextMenu({touch, fired, handled, verdict})` = pass (mouse, an unfired menu press, a field) / stop (touch on text) / swallow (ours was taken); `selectionCloses({...})` (M2).
**The door (utils.js):** `pressFacts(target, x, y)` reads the DOM (caretPositionFromPoint / caretRangeFromPoint → the text node's line rects; computed user-select up the ancestors; never throws — an unreadable fact is the menu side); `touchPressVerdict` = class + verdict. touchstart arms the 500 ms timer only on a menu verdict; `fire()` records `handled` = an app handler cancelled our contextmenu (a menu opened); the platform's `selectstart` during a menu-verdict touch fires ours AT ONCE if the timer has not (Android's own timeout can be shorter) and is cancelled only when ours was handled (measured: a long press on a message's 3 px role strip opened our menu, then Chrome selected "Answer" and that selection closed it; the file viewer, with no menu, still selects); a TRUSTED contextmenu goes through `trustedContextMenu` — swallow (preventDefault + stopImmediatePropagation, one build), stop (touch on text: stopImmediatePropagation WITHOUT preventDefault — the platform's handles + Copy bar stay), else pass (a field / CodeMirror untouched, as before); a move past 10 px clears the verdict. Affected surfaces are exactly the `user-select` opt-ins (the chat list, For-you texts, the For-you window's item) — test-press-select §4 is their census.
**The chat side:** `addMsgMoreBtn(el)` (called from `addOpenInEditorBtn`, so create / swap / gap slab all get it) — touch clients only (`app.isTouch`), the same messages the hover buttons serve (user / assistant with text), a 36×28 `<button class="chat-msg-more">` (UI_ICONS.more, aria "Message actions") FLOATED as the content's first child so the first lines wrap around it — never over the words (the 21×16 hover buttons overlapped 18/18). Its tap = `onMsgMenu(el._rawMsg, …)` → `_showMsgMenu` (works for a gap-slab element with no msgId). A long press on the chrome (the role strip, a `<summary>` toggle, the `.chat-role` label — now `user-select: none`) still opens the menu. ### src/lib/drag-end.js — THE END OF A DRAG, PURE (lane-drag-release, userW's inc-muq7uk0f-e59s + inc-muq7wwfq-rruz, 2026-10-01)

**The incident (Mac, DPR 2.2, UI scale 0.9):** a PDF `viewer` window dropped onto the cell of a Desktop window did not fit — the snap highlight stayed, the window stayed put, the drag stayed ARMED; a resize released over that window kept resizing when the pointer came back; and the viewer could grow but not shrink. **THE CLASS (the lane M class, SECOND STRIKE):** the title-bar drag and the resize ended on a document-level `mouseup`; a release hit-tested on another window's iframe never reaches this document (the embedded page gets it — the Web view, the PDF viewer's own page is an iframe), and noVNC's canvas stops its mouse events — so the release was never heard and the inward-resize moves over the viewer's own frame were lost too. **THE RULE:** pointer capture at every drag's door (the title bar / the handle `setPointerCapture`s the pointer and the drag is fed from THAT element — capture delivers every pointer event there whatever the cursor crosses) + ONE end door + a drag shield.

    drag-end.js — PURE (imports nothing; bundled). `dragEndVerdict(ev, st)` = THE one place that names what ends a drag: pointerup / pointercancel / lostpointercapture of the drag's pointer, the window's blur, the page hidden (`visibilitychange` + `document.hidden`), and a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0` (a release this page never saw) ⇒ END (`release` / `cancel` / `capture-lost` / `blur` / `hidden` / `released-unseen`); another pointer's events, a held move, the page visible, an idle drag (a second end) ⇒ never (the drag ends ONCE). `DRAG_FEED` = the four pointer event names both doors listen for (the control copy names the pre-fix mouse feed here). `SHIELD_CLASS` = `wm-dragging` — `body.wm-dragging` ⇒ every window's content pointer-events:none (public/style.css), the hit test the workspace's for the whole gesture. window.js's title-bar drag + handle resize are the two consumers (the feed on the capturing element, else the document, with the same end rules); the seamless hand-over carries the press's pointerId and captures it too; the `viewer`/`editor`/`browser` window has no minimum of its own (the `.window` floor 320×180, `windowMinForPane`'s only caller is the desktop-app window), so the inward resize shrinks to the floor. Gate: scripts/test-window-drag.mjs (fast) + scripts/test-window-drag-ui.mjs (heavy, the reproduction; a pre-fix-feed overlay of today's drag-feed.js / window.js / tab-group.js as the control, the same on every machine — lane mirror-green r2). ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants.md
    drag-feed.js — the DOM half of EVERY drag door (verify r1, 2026-10-01; imports drag-end.js). `captureOn(el, e)` = the press's element captures the pointer (null = no capture: a fake DOM, a hand-over without a pointerId, a refusing browser — the feed then listens on the document, the same end rules); `attachDragFeed({ el, pointerId, onMove, onEnd, signal })` = THE feed (DRAG_FEED's four pointer events on the capturing element, the window's blur, the page's visibility; a per-drag controller joined to the owner's; `stop()` tears down + releases the capture); `setDragShield(on, key)` = `body.wm-dragging` while ANY holder remains (verify r2 #2: a SET keyed per drag — a mouse + a touch drag at once; the boolean let the first end lower it for the second); THE OWNER GONE (verify r2 #1): the owner's abort hands the door ONE `owner-gone` end — closeWindow aborts `_listenerCtl` first, the feed died with it and `body.wm-dragging` stayed up for good (every window's content dead to the mouse until another drag ended, measured in chrome) — and every door CANCELS (the title drag's cancel path, the resize op's cancel, the icon drag's no-merge, the tab drag's chrome-only cleanup; its feed joins the dragged window's controller too), nothing dropped; `startPointerDrag(el, e, {onMove, onEnd, signal, shield})` = a handle-style door in ONE call (verify r2 THE CENSUS: twelve doors still ended on the document's mouseup / a bare pointerup — the sidebar + editor Resizer, the theme editor's move + size, the minimap scrub, the top-bar scale + taskbar height handles, an explorer column, the viewer's pan + pptx sidebar, customize-mode's move, the split divider, the queue reorder (captured on the STRIP: its rows are rebuilt mid-drag) — each is this call now, the lane's compat `mousedown` kept; test-window-drag §5 is the grep-derived census over src/lib: 16 feed doors in 10 files, every document/window move-or-end listener named with its reason, three planted controls). Four doors attach the feed themselves — window.js's title bar + resize handle, tab-group.js's tab tear-off + icon drag (verify r1 found those two still on the document's mouseup: a torn-off tab released over a pane stayed armed, an icon drag left its window INVISIBLE). The tab drag captures on the strip's TITLE BAR (the element `_renderTabBar` keeps; the tab element is rebuilt by the detach and a capture on it would be lost under the finger). INVARIANT: a drag door registers no document mouse listener; test-window-drag §4 pins ONE feed and counts the doors; its pre-capture control is a closed world of three patched copies (drag-feed / tab-group / window). The xpra hand-over's hold (xpra-view.js `wmHold`) ends with the SAME verdict (release / cancel / no-button move / blur / hidden) — it used to wait for a pointerup alone and left the pane deaf + the X button down after a blur-ended drag.

### utils.js `onOutsidePress` + outside-press.js — THE ONE OUTSIDE-PRESS CLOSER (lane M, inc-muhms5kt-0ejl, 2.369.182)

**The incident (2026-09-26, client 2.369.177, Chrome as an xpra desktop app):** "vibespace中的悬浮菜单，不相应在app画面里的点击自动隐藏" — no floating menu closed on a click INTO an app's picture; a click anywhere else closed it. The bundle's action ring: `button#btn-global-settings`, two presses on `canvas<div.xpra-win…<div.xpra-pane`, `button#btn-global-settings` again (the owner closing it by hand).
**Mechanism (measured):** xpra-view.js's pane handler runs `ime.focus(); e.preventDefault(); setPointerCapture` on `pointerdown` — and a cancelled `pointerdown` suppresses the COMPATIBILITY `mousedown` in every phase. Chrome probe (a pane with exactly that handler): a press into it → document pointerdown 1 (capture + bubble), click 1, mousedown 0 (capture AND bubble); a press elsewhere → mousedown 1. On the real rung (test-desktop-xpra-window §17 (7)): every click into GNOME Calculator's picture = pointerdown ×1, click ×1, mousedown ×0. noVNC's canvas `stopEvent`s its mousedown (stopPropagation + preventDefault), so a VNC press reached only CAPTURE-phase mousedown closers. Every closer listened for a document `mousedown` ⇒ none ever saw a press into the picture (lane B hit the same class for window activation — kb-bugfix-invariants, 2.369.177).
**The helper:** `onOutsidePress(root, close, { exclude = [], ignore = null, nested = true, once = true, signal = null, selection = once })` → `dispose` (`selection`, lane mobile-select M2: on a touch device a TRANSIENT surface also closes when a text selection starts outside it — PURE `selectionCloses` in press-select.js; a persistent popup is armed for the app's life and opts out). Three document listeners — `pointerdown` / `pointerup` / `pointercancel` — CAPTURE + PASSIVE + the closer's own AbortSignal; the body never calls preventDefault / stopPropagation (the press still reaches the app; test-architecture §59c pins both). The decision is PURE, `src/lib/outside-press.js` (imports nothing): `pressCloses(facts)` = the table **root-gone > opening > inside > excluded > ignored > nested > outside** (`connected:false` ⇒ `retire` — a surface removed by Escape's [data-popover] sweep or by its own item click retires its closer at the next press WITHOUT calling close; `nested` = the chained-popover rule, a press in any [data-popover] keeps it open unless the surface opts out); `pressPhase(pointerType)` = mouse (and '' / undefined) judged at pointerdown, touch / pen only as a TAP; `tapVerdict({dx, dy, heldMs, cancelled})` = ≤ `TAP_SLOP_PX` 10, < `LONG_PRESS_MS` 500, never cancelled (installLongPressContextMenu's own numbers) — a scroll (pointercancel), a drag, a long-press never close; the tap is judged where it went DOWN (a captured pointer's pointerup targets the capturer). **It arms SYNCHRONOUSLY** and recognises the press that opened the surface by its event `timeStamp` < the arming `performance.now()` (`opening`) — the pre-lane `setTimeout(0)` deferral was STARVED on a busy page (Chrome dispatches input ahead of timer tasks: on the real rung `DOMDebugger.getEventListeners(document)` showed no closer when the click landed, and the window menu + window list stayed open). `attachPopoverClose(popover, ...excludeEls)` = `onOutsidePress(popover, () => popover.remove(), { exclude })` (returns dispose) — createPopover, showContextMenu, terminal.js's settings popover, window.js's overlap switcher and file-explorer-ops' item menu reach it. Escape stays the `[data-popover]` protocol (app.js's global handler; the For-you popup's own capture Esc) — the helper adds no second Escape path.
**THE CENSUS (every closer converted, its own rule kept):** utils.js `attachPopoverClose` (anchor excluded, nested rule) · chat-status-bar.js `showDropdown` (`ignore: t === anchor` — the exact element, as before; `nested:false`) · chat-input.js TODO popup (`exclude: [this._todoDisplay]`, `nested:false`) · chat-renderers.js code-block language picker (`ignore: t === langBtn`, `nested:false`; `closeFn` IS the dispose — a pick / Escape removes the list and retires the closer) · chat-view.js message-details popover (`nested:false`; was a capture mousedown) · customize-mode.js spring popover (`exclude: [el]`, `ignore: () => this._picking` — width-pick clicks never dismiss, `nested:false`, dispose in `_cleanup`) · mobile-nav.js window list (`ignore: t === anchor || .dialog-overlay / #dialog-overlay`, the chained rule; it closed on ANY touch pointerdown before — a scroll outside no longer dismisses it) · usage-meter.js quota popup (PERSISTENT: `once:false`, `exclude: [usageEl, mChip]`, `nested:false`) · user-todos-panel.js For-you popup (PERSISTENT, `exclude: [btn, mBtn]` — the #mobile-nav-todos tap-that-never-closes race, `ignore: .ut-mini-popover, .win-inbox-badge`, `nested:false`). The instant tooltip's hide-on-any-press is `pointerdown` capture passive (not a closer, not through the helper). **Not closers, allow-listed in test-architecture §59 with a reason:** window.js move mode (its capture mousedown PLACES the window, full-screen overlay), customize-mode's width pick (window-capture mousedown + click PREEMPT everything while picking). **Untouched:** session-card's legend (already capture pointerdown, dies on any press), the modal backdrops (createModalShell / #dialog-overlay / the session palette — a full-screen overlay, the picture cannot be pressed), blur-driven lists (autocomplete, channel-window's @-list: the xpra pane focuses its IME textarea, so they close on blur). **Known gap:** a press into an IFRAME (a Web view window, a plugin window) never reaches our document — not handled (a window-blur closer would be a separate decision).
**Gates:** test-outside-press (fast, 40: the PURE tables; the REAL helper under a fake document + a browser dispatch model — capture passive arming, the xpra-like pane and the noVNC-like canvas close, the press never cancelled or stopped, the opening press, persistent / signal / root-gone / touch taps vs scrolls / attachPopoverClose; CONTROLS: the pre-lane closer verbatim stays open over the pane, two mutant copies — the helper on `mousedown`, the helper in the bubble phase behind a stopping pane — stay open) · test-architecture §59 (the census: no document / window `mousedown` / `click` listener or on-property in src/lib outside the 3-row mode allow-list, no dead row, every document `pointerdown` capture-phase, planted controls) · test-desktop-xpra-window §17 (heavy, the real rung + a mutant-copy server).
**2.369.182 integration (× lane K):** `attachPopoverClose(popover, …excludeEls)` is `onOutsidePress` plus lane K's OWNERSHIP fields — `popover._closeExclude` = the very `exclude` array the helper reads at every press (the taskbar chooser's re-anchor pushes a rebuilt button), `popover._closeCtl = { abort: dispose }` (the hover chooser's one cleanup disposes it). test-taskbar-group §9 now reads BOTH functions out of utils.js and runs the composed closer (pointerdown, the verdicts handed in); its pre-fix / r1-minor controls unchanged. App.js's `<select>` picker tracker (lane L) is a capture `pointerdown` — a tracker, never a closer (§59 (a)).
**不变量:** an outside-press closer is a CAPTURE-phase, passive `pointerdown` through the ONE helper — never a document `mousedown` / `click`, never a closer that cancels or stops the press; a new floating surface calls `onOutsidePress` (or createPopover / showContextMenu), and a new surface that cancels `pointerdown` needs no special case.
