Row clicks inside `.ut-reply` / on a chip / on the reply button never jump. Phone: the same popup ⇒ the same box; the ≤768px block lifts `.ut-opt`, the textarea and Send to ≥ 36 px. Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑥⑦, test-inbox-reply-ui (heavy chrome), test-mobile-gaps #1.

**2.369.169 THE TITLE-BAR MINI INBOX (docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §3, chunk 3).** This module is the only client-side store of items, so it owns the per-window badges: `ingestLive` also keeps `keyByWebuiId` (payload `id` → `sessionKey`); `keysForWin(winId)` = the keys a chat/terminal window answers for — the payload key of its view's webui id (a ChatView/TerminalSession's `sessionId`, or the openSpec's `serverId` before the view exists), the openSpec's `sessionKey` (a VIEW-ONLY window of a stopped conversation has only that; `view-…`/`sub-…` view ids are never read as webui ids), and `webui:<id>` (an item filed before the CLI reported its id); a sub-agent's view has none. `syncBadges` walks `app.wm.windows` and calls `wm.setInboxBadge(winId, inboxBadgeFor(todos.open, keys))` (PURE, user-todos-layout.js: ACTION items only — a session with only notices has no badge — worst urgency) after every `apply()`, every `active-sessions` message and every window change (`app._syncInboxBadges` from app.js's `onWindowsChanged`), coalesced to one pass per microtask; setInboxBadge's key guard makes an unchanged badge a no-op. `app.openMiniInbox(anchor, winId)` = `createPopover(anchor, 'ut-mini-popover')` (so `[data-popover]`: the global Escape removes it FIRST — the panel's capture listener already defers to any `[data-popover]` — and a second Escape closes the panel) with a head (`.ut-live-dot` of the primary key patched like a group dot, "Inbox for this session", `.ut-mini-name` = `nameFor` as textContent — a session name is user/peer-controlled) and `.ut-mini-rows` reconciled by the SAME `reconcileRows` through THE row renderer with `miniCtx = {...rowCtx, mini:true}`, laid out by PURE `miniInboxEntries(layout, todos, keys)` (the store narrowed to the keys, openLayout on open / nextLayout on every broadcast — a row resolved from the popover keeps its slot until it closes). Every action is the panel's: the row click handler became `rowClick(e, item, {mini})` shared by both surfaces (reply box, option chips, ✓ ✕ ↺ ⤢, the producer's action) and `replyKeys` / `growOnInput` likewise; the ONLY difference is the row-body click — `mini` ⇒ no jump (the popover lives in that session's window). Esc inside a reply box in the popover folds the box (a bubble listener on the popover stops it before the global closer; the text is kept in `drafts`, shared with the panel by item id). The panel's outside-mousedown closer exempts `.ut-mini-popover` and `.win-inbox-badge` (a layer above it, not outside it). `patchLive` patches the popover's dot and rows too. PHONE: the ≤768px stylesheet hides window title bars, so the badge is not drawn there; the popover carries the full-width sheet rule and the ≥ 36 px targets for any path that opens it. Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑧ (the badge + popover tables + wiring pins), test-inbox-reply-ui ⑨–⑭ (heavy chrome: counts per window incl. a stopped view-only window, a notice-only session without a badge, a real click opening exactly that session's rows, reply from the popover → the stub's stdin + in-place resolve + the count down to no badge, Escape layering, the tab chain, a hostile session name as text, and a patched `miniInboxEntries` without its key filter as the isolation control).

**2.369.169 THE USAGE SET (docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §4 d/h, chunk 4).** ① A group is now `.ut-group-bar` (the head button + a `.ut-seen-all` button BESIDE it — a button never nests in a button) + its rows + a `.ut-fold` expander last; `renderPanel` reads the head through the bar and reconciles rows after the bar. ② THE FLOOD FOLD: each action group goes through PURE `foldGroup(entries, {max: FOLD_MAX, expanded, prev})`; only `fold.visible` is reconciled, and `.ut-fold` reads `t('{n} more…', {n: hidden.length})` (a click flips `expanded` and repaints; a broadcast keeps it). `folds` (group key → `{expanded, shown, hidden}` of the last paint) lives only while the popup is open — cleared on every toggle and in `renderPanel`'s hidden branch, like the layout. Notices and the mini inbox do not fold. ③ "Mark all seen" is shown while the group holds ≥ 2 open asks (`groupOpen` = the open ACTION ids of the last paint, folded rows included): ONE `POST /api/user-todos/resolve-many {ids, status:'dismissed'}` (button disabled while in flight) ⇒ ONE broadcast ⇒ every row strikes IN PLACE and the badges recount; a failure is the toast `Could not update {n} items: {why}`. ④ THE BOARD CHIP: `patchBoard(head)` draws a `.ut-board[data-state]` span between the name and the count when `app.sidebar._sessionStatuses[key]` (or its `webui:<id>` twin via `keyByWebuiId`) is `needs-input` / `blocked` / `review` / `working` — words `t('needs input')` / `t('blocked')` / `t('review')` / `t('working')` (the board's existing keys), the reason as a `title` PROPERTY; called per group in `renderPanel` and, on `session-status-updated`, by `patchBoards` in a microtask (after the sidebar-tasks mixin stored the statuses — handler order is not ours) — chips only, never a row. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑨ ⑩ + test-inbox-reply-ui ⑮ ⑯.

**2.369.169 NOTICES BY ORIGIN + THE TAB COUNTS (B-328d, docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §8).** The Notices section's skeleton = its head, a `.ut-chips` strip (`role=group`, `aria-label` t('Notices by source'); hidden while ≤ 1 origin is present) and `.ut-notice-groups` (the flat `.ut-notice-rows` is gone). `renderNotices(nBox, entries)` lays the notice entries out with PURE `noticeGroups(entries, noticeFilter, {prev: noticeOrder})` — `noticeOrder` = the origins of the last paint, reset on every open like the layout — and reconciles one `.ut-notice-group[data-origin]` per origin keyed in place: a head (`.ut-group-name` = t(label), `.ut-group-n` = its open count) then its rows through THE `reconcileRows` (the one row renderer); a filtered-out group is `display:none`, NEVER removed (a reply box in it keeps its node); `patchChips` reconciles `.ut-chip[data-origin]` buttons (label + count spans, `.on` + `aria-pressed` on the active one, a title per chip). A chip click (the popup's delegated click) sets the filter — the ACTIVE origin's chip again = all — persists it per device (`localStorage vibespace.ut-notice-filter`) and repaints; the ask groups are untouched. **THE HELD FILTER (r2, verifier):** the filter is read from the device on every OPEN, then `renderNotices` feeds it through `noticeFilterFor` on every paint once the store has loaded (`knownIds !== null`) and, when the answer differs, the answer BECOMES the filter (`setNoticeFilter`: held AND stored); the strip marks that held value. So the filter in force is always a chip that is drawn, and an arrival never changes what is shown. r1 read the stored value on every paint: a stored `login` whose group was absent at open showed All — then a broadcast carrying one login notice silently re-applied it and every other group vanished under an active All chip with no click (reproduced headless; the inc-mtw02kbq-kj96 class at group granularity). THE TABS: built ONCE per open by `ensureTabs` (`.ut-tab[data-tab]` = a `.ut-tab-label` span + keyed `.ut-tab-n[data-n=action|notice|unread]` count spans) and patched by `patchTabs` on every render, broadcast and toast (`vs-toast` ⇒ `patchTabs` on the inbox page, a repaint on the history page): Inbox = the open-ask pill (class by the worst tier, title = `actionWords(action)`, THE sentence the taskbar badge's title uses) + the grey `ut-seg-notice` pill; Notifications = `tabCounts(...).history.unread` (toasts since `vibespace.ut-history-seen`); `aria-label` carries the counts in words. `renderHistory` stamps the key (the page is being looked at); a device with no stamp is stamped at install (an upgrade never opens on the whole history as unread). A tab click switches only the PAGE (`showPage`: tabs kept, the other page removed after `stashDrafts` keeps any typed reply as its box's draft) — never `replaceChildren(tabsEl(), …)`. The phone sheet is the same popup (chips ≥ 36 px in the ≤768px block). Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑪ (wiring pins, incl. the hold) + test-inbox-reply-ui ⑰ ⑱ ⑱c ⑲ and the phone legs (⑱c over the r1 panel ⇒ 2 named failures: `login` still stored after the reopen, and the arrival flipping every group but login hidden).
**Lane M (2.369.182):** the popup's outside-press hide is `onOutsidePress(popup, hide, { exclude: [btn, mBtn], ignore: (t) => t.closest('.ut-mini-popover, .win-inbox-badge'), nested: false, once: false })` — the rules unchanged (the nav button exempt like the taskbar one; the mini inbox a layer above), the press now counted in the CAPTURE phase so a click into an app's picture hides it (test-desktop-xpra-window §17 (5)). The badge's own `mousedown` stopPropagation (tab-group.js) no longer shields anything — the `ignore` rule is what keeps the panel open.

### user-todos-row.js — THE For-you row renderer (2.369.169, design-user-inbox-reply chunk 2)

**§9 (2026-09-27):** `reconcileKeyed(container, entries, {head, isRow, keyOf, idOf, create, patch})` = THE keyed reconciler, moved out of the panel's `reconcileRows` (which is now a call to it) so the For-you window's list uses the same one — a listed key is PATCHED, a new one created, a vanished one removed, a node MOVES only when out of place. The ⤢ `.ut-view` is titled + aria-labelled "Open in the For-you window" (the viewer modal is retired).

    user-todos-row.js — ONE spelling of a row, used by the panel's reconciliation and (chunk 3) the per-window mini inbox. `renderRow(entry, ctx)` → a fresh `.ut-item[data-id]`; `patchRow(el, entry, ctx)` → the same element brought to `entry`; `applyLive(el, item, ctx)` → only the live half (reply button disabled + title = the verdict sentence through t(), chips, an open box's Send; `data-sending` disables them in flight); `replyBoxEl(t)`; `boxInUse(box)` (focus or text); plus the row words `agoText` / `expiresText` / `resolvedByText` (`'reply'` ⇒ "by your reply"). `entry = {item, resolved, notice?, tail?}` covers the four row kinds that used to be three templates in the panel (open, notice, resolved-in-place `ut-item-inplace`, the recently-resolved tail with its session name and age); `ctx = {t, nameFor, wordsOf, detailOf, replyState, mini?}`. INVARIANTS: every item string (title, detail, option labels, session name, reply) goes through escHtml — nothing else in the file builds markup (test-inbox-reply-ui ① + its innerHTML negative control ⑦); `partsOf` returns the static parts + a SIGNATURE, and patchRow rebuilds only when it changed — the live half is NOT in the signature, so a turn flip never rebuilds a row; when it does rebuild, a `.ut-reply` box is NEVER detached (the dot / body children / actions are replaced AROUND it — detaching a focused textarea blurs it) and an open detail stays open; a resolved row keeps its box only while in use (a reply to a resolved item is still accepted, D1.4), an open row always. The option chips and the reply button exist only when `replyState(item).show` (a server producer's key / a job item has no reply surface). **2.369.175: `.ut-actions` is the body's FIRST child and floats right (CSS) — the words wrap beside the buttons then use the full width; applyLive reads `:scope > .ut-body > .ut-actions > .ut-reply-btn`; patchRow's keep-branch re-inserts the fresh body children (actions included) before the kept reply box, never appends a sibling.**

### user-todos-layout.js — the popup's arithmetic (PURE)

**§9 (2026-09-27):** `sortGroups(open)` → `[[key, items]]` — the popup's group order moved VERBATIM out of renderPanel (Background Work last, the worst urgency — `low`/missing ranks as normal, the panel's `|| 1` kept — then the newest item) so the For-you window lays its list out by the SAME rule (`openLayout(sortGroups(todos.open))`); test-inbox-window-model ⑦ pins both callers and the retired inline sort.

**2026-09-27 `restoreDetails(next, fullById)` → `{todos, fullById}` (PURE, the verify round):** the client model's memory of every WHOLE detail it has seen (a snapshot carries a resolved item's as a 300-char preview + `detailTruncated`): each non-truncated detail in `next` is remembered by id (plus what `fullById` already held — a fetched one), a truncated item whose remembered whole text STARTS WITH its preview gets the whole text back and drops the flag (a preview that is not the head of what was remembered — the detail changed — is never overwritten), the memory is pruned to the ids the snapshot still lists (no unbounded growth); new objects, inputs untouched, garbage ⇒ empty lists. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑫ (the table + a patched copy that never restores).

**Lane S3 (2026-09-26):** `trayWhere(rect, vw, vh)` → 'bottom right' | 'bottom left' | 'top right' | 'top left' (i18n keys, `TRAY_CORNERS`) | null — the corner the For-you button sits in, from its measured rect; the new-item toast says it ("Added to For you (bottom right)").

    user-todos-layout.js — PURE (DOM-free; its only import is src/inbox-reply.js's PURE verdict, so the client and the reply route word a refusal identically). inc-mtw02kbq-kj96's append-only slot rule (`openLayout`/`nextLayout`/`entriesFor`), 2.369.118's notices (`isNotice`/`splitNotices`/`badgeCounts`), and **2.369.169 (design-user-inbox-reply D1.5/D1.7)**: `liveDotState(fact)` → `off` (no fact / `live:false`) · `unreachable` (a `remoteState` beats the turn) · `waiting` (turn = the harness's requires_action) · `running` · else `idle` (an older server without `turn` never paints a false "running"; a terminal session keeps its dot) with `LIVE_DOT_WHY` = one tooltip sentence each (English t() keys); `replyButtonState(item, fact)` = `replyVerdict({item, session: {live, mode, remoteState}})` projected onto `{show, enabled, why, code}` — `show:false` for `REPLY_HIDDEN_CODES` (no_session / job_item: no button), mid-turn ENABLED. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑥ (the dot table) ⑦ (the projection table, each row checked against the server's own verdict) + the wiring pins (the panel imports the row file and holds no second row template, no `popup.innerHTML =`, the active-sessions subscription calls `patchLive`, `LIVE_SESSION_FACTS.turn` is carried-only). **Chunk 3 (the title-bar mini inbox):** `inboxBadgeFor(open, keys)` → `{count, urgency}` over the open ACTION items whose sessionKey is one of the window's keys (notices never count; a missing urgency reads normal; `{0, ''}` = no badge) and `miniInboxEntries(layout, todos, keys)` → `{layout, entries}` = the store narrowed to the keys laid out by the same append-only `openLayout`/`nextLayout`/`entriesFor`, each entry marked `notice`. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑧ + test-inbox-reply-ui ⑭ (a patched copy without the `ks.has(i.sessionKey)` filter lists another session's row). **Chunk 4 (the flood fold):** `FOLD_MAX` = 5 and `foldGroup(entries, {max, expanded, prev})` → `{visible, hidden}`: more than `max` OPEN rows and not expanded ⇒ visible = every row up to and including the max-th open row in LAYOUT order (the store sorts newest first within a tier, so they are the newest; a row resolved in place among them keeps its slot), hidden = the rest; else everything. Folding only HIDES — `visible` keeps layout order. `prev` = `{shown, hidden}` id sets of the last paint while open: a row once shown is never hidden again (a ↺ above must not pull it from under the pointer), a row resolved while hidden stays hidden ("Mark all seen" on a folded group does not flood struck rows out below), an arrival (appended by `nextLayout`) joins the fold. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑨ (the table incl. the prev rows) + ⑩ wiring. **2.369.169 NOTICES BY ORIGIN (B-328d, design §8):** a second PURE import, src/inbox-origin.js (re-exported: `INBOX_ORIGINS`, `ORIGIN_LABELS`). `originOf(item)` = a declared member ⇒ itself, else THE LEGACY RUNG, exactly three rows and never extended (`sessionName 'Spending'` ⇒ spend, `'Channels'` ⇒ channels, else agent; an origin outside the set — a newer server's, a forged string, the dropped `system` — reads through it; r2 dropped a `by 'system'` row nothing had ever produced) — the read-time classification of items stored before the field, instead of a migration. `noticeGroups(notices, filter, {prev})` → `[{origin, label, entries, open, total, shown}]`: the set's order on a fresh open, while open `prev` (the last paint's origins) keeps each group's slot and a new origin APPENDS (the slot law for groups); entries keep layout order; every present group is returned, a filtered-out one `shown:false`. `noticeChips(notices, {prev})` → `all` (total OPEN) first, then one chip per PRESENT origin in the groups' order with its open count (0 while its resolved-in-place rows hold their slots). `noticeFilterFor(filter, notices)` → the filter IN FORCE: `filter` while its origin has a notice, else `all` — and since r2 the panel HOLDS the answer (it becomes the filter, held + stored), so a later arrival of that origin never re-applies a stored choice (a PURE row pins it: `all` held at open + a login arrival ⇒ every group shown; the control, the stored `login` re-applied, shows only login). `tabCounts(open, toastHistory, lastSeenTs)` → `{inbox: {action, notice, urgency}, history: {unread}}` (`action` = badgeCounts' number, `urgency` its worst tier — a notice never colours it; `unread` = toast entries with a numeric `ts` newer than the last look, null/garbage ⇒ all). Per-device keys `NOTICE_FILTER_KEY = 'vibespace.ut-notice-filter'`, `HISTORY_SEEN_KEY = 'vibespace.ut-history-seen'`. Gate: test-user-todos-layout ⑪ (these tables + the store + THE CENSUS + wiring pins).

### src/lib/user-todos-actions.js — THE For-you CLIENT MODEL (2026-09-27, design-user-inbox-reply §9)

    user-todos-actions.js — `inboxModel(app)` (memoized on `app._inboxModel`: the panel's install builds it at boot, the window asks for the same one) = the ONE client-side store of For-you items and every verb on one, shared by the popup / phone sheet / title-bar mini inbox (user-todos-panel.js) and the For-you WINDOW (inbox-window.js). Everything in it moved VERBATIM out of user-todos-panel.js with its comments (so the two surfaces cannot drift): `todos` (getter) + `loaded` + `byId`; the three ws subscriptions — `user-todos-updated` ⇒ the snapshot (`liveSeen` guards the first fetch), `active-sessions` ⇒ `ingestLive` then `emit('live')`, `session-status-updated` ⇒ `emit('status')` in a microtask (after the sidebar-tasks mixin stored them) — the reconnect resync and the first fetch; the live facts (`ingestLive` / `factFor` / `keyForWebui` / `webuiIdsFor` / `keysFor(key)` = every key ONE session's items may carry: itself, its `webui:<id>` twin(s) while live, and a `webui:` key's `<backend>:<id>` — the window's session scope); `replyState(i)` = PURE `replyButtonState(i, factFor(i.sessionKey))`; `patchDot(dot)` = PURE `liveDotState` + `LIVE_DOT_WHY` onto a `.ut-live-dot[data-key]`; `boardOf(key)` = `{rec, word}` of `app.sidebar._sessionStatuses` (the `webui:` twin too); the words (`wordsOf` / `detailOf` / `nameFor` — an `i18n` item worded by the device's t()); `jump(key, item, {close})` (job item → its interact window, `jobs` → the panel, `accounts` → Manage Agents, a helper's ask → its card, else goToWindow / attach / tmux / resume; `close` = the caller's own step-aside); `setStatus(id, status)` → resolves true on success, a failure toast otherwise; `postReply(id, text)` → true after "Reply sent" (the draft dropped), false after "Could not reply: {why}" (the route's code through t(); null = server unreachable); `runAction(rec)` = the producer's verb (today `reset-credit` → `openResetCreditDialog(app, {accountKey, sessionId, todoId})`); `drafts` (item id → unsent text, one per item across every surface); `rowCtx` (THE row renderer's context); `on(kind, fn, {signal})` → `off` (kind `todos` | `live` | `status`; a window passes its listener signal). Module exports beside it: `tierCounts(action)` / `actionWords(action)` — the badge's tiers and words (taskbar, popup Inbox tab, window Actions tab). Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑦ ⑪ (the moved pins read model + panel), test-reset-credit-ui §4, test-helper-ask ⑤, test-login-expiry, test-inbox-window-model ⑦.

**2026-09-27 THE WHOLE DETAIL (the verify round).** A snapshot carries a RESOLVED item's detail as a 300-char preview (`detailTruncated`, user-todos.js `previewOf`). `setTodos` runs every snapshot through PURE `restoreDetails(next, fullById)` (user-todos-layout.js): `fullById` remembers every whole detail this client has seen — carried whole in a snapshot, or fetched — pruned to the ids the snapshot still lists, and a previewed item whose remembered whole text starts with its preview gets it back, flag dropped; so THE READER'S TEXT NEVER SHRINKS when another client resolves the item the window shows (no fetch). `ensureDetail(id)` → `Promise<{detail, error}>`: an item carried whole answers at once; a previewed one is fetched ONCE (`GET /api/user-todos/:id`, single-flight per id through `detailLoads`), remembered, restored into `todos` and re-emitted as `todos`; a failed load resolves `{detail: null, error}` with the route's word through t() or "server unreachable" (fetchJson never throws) — the caller says it (the window's cut line / Copy's toast). Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑫ (the `restoreDetails` table + a no-restore control; the wiring pins), test-inbox-window-ui ⑭ ⑮.

### src/lib/inbox-window-layout.js — PURE the For-you window's rules (2026-09-27, design-user-inbox-reply §9)

    inbox-window-layout.js — imports nothing, DOM-free (node-importable; the suite imports it directly). `nextSelection(entries, resolvedId)` = THE MAIL-CLIENT RULE: after THIS client resolved the selected item, the next OPEN entry below it in display order, else the previous open one above, else null; the resolved id itself is skipped whatever the entry says (the call runs right after the POST, before the broadcast); an id the list does not hold ⇒ the first open entry. `holdSelection(entries, selectedId)` = the same id while the list shows it — open OR resolved in place (another client's ✓ never moves the reader) — else the first open entry, else null (a struck row is never selected by itself). `paneMode(width, {touch})` → `{mode: 'single'|'split', rowMin}` with ONE threshold `NARROW_PX` = 620 (content px) and `TOUCH_ROW_PX` = 36; an unmeasurable width (0 / NaN — minimized, display:none) ⇒ null = keep the mode. `scopeRows(entries, {sessionKey, query, tab, textOf})` = the tab (`actions` ⇒ not `notice`, `notices` ⇒ only), the session scope (a key or a session's key list; empty ⇒ all), every whitespace term case-insensitively in `textOf(item, entry)` (the caller words it — the device's t() of an i18n item, the session's display name); order kept. `rowPreview(detail, max)` = the list row's one-line cut: the first non-blank line, `**` / backticks / a `__` at a word's EDGE (emphasis) and a leading heading / quote / list / numbered mark dropped (a `__` inside an identifier — `window.__xss` — and a lone `_` in snake_case stay; the first cut dropped every `__` and printed `window.xss`, its patched copy is the control), cut with an ellipsis. `itemView(item, ctx)` = the pane as STRUCTURE with every word injected (`t`, `words`, `detail`, `name`, `origin {origin, label}`, `notice`, `resolved` — the ENTRY's view wins, `reply` = replyButtonState, `ago` / `expires` / `resolvedBy`): `meta` [{kind, text}] (status · by for a resolved item, else urgency or notice; age; expires while open; resolved-at; the producer's label), `options` [{idx, label}] (open + a reply surface only), `reply {show, enabled, why}` (a drawn-disabled box says why; NO box ⇒ where it is answered instead — card_item / job_item — except `no_session`, which would be noise on every notice), `actions` (open: reply? · done · dismiss · copy · producer?; resolved: reopen · copy), `producer` ({type:'reset-credit', accountKey, sessionId} | null — facts, never a verb), `replied` (the WHOLE reply), `copy` (title + the whole detail + the reply), and (2026-09-27, the verify round) `cut` = null while the detail is whole, else `{state: 'loading'|'failed', text}` from `ctx.detailState` + `ctx.loadError` — the sentence the pane shows under a PREVIEWED detail ("Showing the first {n} characters — loading the rest…" / "Could not load the rest of the text: {why}"), never silent; an unknown state reads as whole. Hostile strings pass verbatim (the painter escapes). `TABS` = ['actions', 'notices']. Gate: test-inbox-window-model.

### src/lib/inbox-window.js — THE For-you WINDOW (2026-09-27, design-user-inbox-reply §9)

### picture-shell.js — THE PICTURE SHELL (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22)

**THE PASTE PRESS SAYS WHAT HAPPENED, EVERY TIME (lane desktop-keepalive K2/K3, userW inc-muoshmqn-dect: two presses on a Desktop window, nothing visible, NO toast in the ring).** PROVED on the .199 shell (test-vnc-view §9, the retired file read through git): two paths left a press with no toast — the paste box opened silently (a plain-http page / a refused permission / an empty clipboard; the box sits under the bar and the eye misses it), and a `readText()` that never settles (a permission prompt nobody answers) did NOTHING. Now: PURE `pasteVerdict(state, {closed})` → `send` (connected) | `queue` (starting / connecting / disconnected / error) | `refuse` (never started / closed — "not connected"); every box opening is SAID (`pasteBoxToastKey(why)`, a toast the ring keeps, the box scrolled into view); the read has a deadline (`CLIPBOARD_READ_MS` = 3 s ⇒ `timeout`, its own box note); a press while the stream is down toasts "reconnecting — your text is pasted when it is back", calls the view's `reconnect` (a press is intent: `resetLadder` + `connect` unless one is in flight), and QUEUES the text (one, the latest) — `emit('connected')` flushes it through the view's send; after `PASTE_WAIT_MS` = 30 s it says "Not pasted — … press Reconnect". K3: `scheduleRetry` writes "Reconnecting n/N…" (+ the bridge's words) into the status chip — OPT-IN `ladderWords` (vnc-view sets it; the xpra view's chip already names its own reason and keeps it, test-xpra-client); `setCloseWords` / `closeWordsKey(code)` word the bridge's closed code set (GET /api/vnc/last-close — noVNC never exposes a close reason and a terminate() sends none). vnc-view.js: a dead RFB is never `disconnect()`ed again (`rfbLive` — noVNC logged "Tried changing state of a disconnected RFB object" ×3 in his console), a view-only (watching) pane refuses a send by name instead of "Clipboard sent", `lastClose` option (desktop-window.js reads the route). ### xpra-proto.js — THE XPRA WORDS, PURE (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22; D21 (c) (b))

**A WINDOW PER TOP-LEVEL — design 016 S2 (lane app-satellite-windows, 2026-10-03; the owner's YES to Moments as its own VibeSpace window):** `slotFor(main, secondaries)` lays the ROOT out — the main pane's display at 0,0, each secondary NORMAL window to its right (x = the main's width + Σ earlier widths + `SLOT_GAP` 32), y 0; a slot past `SLOT_ROOT_MAX` (8192) is not given (that window stays S1's guest; a later smaller one may still fit). `inSlot(g, slot)` = the belt's rule (the slot's origin); `placeInRect(g, rect)` = placeInside within a slot; `paneOf(win, slots, windows)` = which pane draws a window: a slotted window its own wid, a dialog the slot of the window it is transient for (followed up its chain, ≤ 8), a popup the slot containing its origin, else 0 (the main pane). Fast: test-xpra-client §10 (PURE rows incl. the owner's 1574×974 + 880×1120).

**THE WORK AREA FOLLOWS EVERY PANE (lane desktop-workarea, 2.369.205; the owner's 2.369.203 WeChat 「下面有条空白」):** xpra 6.5.4 sets the root's `_NET_WORKAREA` from the client's `screen_sizes` rows ALONE (server/subsystem/display.py `calculate_workarea`: the new size ∩ each row's last four numbers), and `display-configure` takes `desktop-size` / `desktop-size-unscaled` / `monitors` / `dpi` / `vrefresh` / `desktops` / `icc` — never rows (`monitors` lands in `ss.monitors`, which the work area never reads). So every resize after the hello grew the root under the HELLO's work area (measured on the owner's display: root 1660×1296, `_NET_WORKAREA` 0,0,1573,973, WeChat's main window max 1574×974 = the work area ⇒ the blank strip; reproduced on the real rung: root 2776×1566 under 0,0,1796,1110 — the hello's 898×555 CSS pane at DPR 2 — and 228 CSS px blank under a GTK main capped at the work area). New `screenSizes(w, h, dpi)` (one monitor, work area = the whole desktop; the hello uses it too). `displayPacket` sends the legacy `desktop_size` in its FULL 12-field form (w, h, the rows, 0 desktops, [], unscaled w/h, dpi x/y as whole numbers, 0 refresh, {} monitors) whenever the server's packet-types name it (6.5.4 under its default BACKWARDS_COMPATIBLE) or name neither modern spelling: xpra stores the rows, then re-dispatches the same size + dpi as a display-configure — ONE packet, so the keeper's held display packet (one per refused viewer) still replays whole. `display-configure` / `configure-display` only when that is all the server takes (XPRA_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBLE=0: the root follows, the work area cannot — the fallback would be a keeper-side `_NET_WORKAREA` write; not built). The 4-field legacy form the old fallback sent stores the rows and RETURNS on 6.5.4 (`len(packet) <= 4`) — it never resized. Gates: test-xpra-client (every size 1..7680 per axis, the owner's sizes through a modelled 6.5.4 server, a patched-copy control) and heavy test-desktop-app-fixed WORK AREA (real xpra; xprop / xwininfo on the root; fixture mode `workarea` = WeChat's capped main; DPR 2 and 1; the control tree's lever).

**Lane D (a) (2026-09-25):** `fitGeometry` — a pane SMALLER than the minimum keeps its SHAPE at the fit scale (k = min(pane ÷ minimum) per axis; the window = the pane ÷ k, the free axis snapped UP one increment), so the view's scaled-to-fit picture FILLS the pane (measured, DPR 1 at 2×: a 720×1232 minimum in an 898×913 pane was 25.8 % pane background, 116 CSS px either side; now 1212×1232). `devicePane(css, r, {cover})` — `cover` rounds UP (a resampled picture has no 1:1 grid to keep; rounded down it left a < 1 CSS px sliver). Gate: test-xpra-client §1/§6/§6b re-pinned + §7.

**Round 3, lane B (2.369.177, §3.3):** `parseMoveResize(p)` reads `initiate-moveresize` (the BACKWARDS_COMPATIBLE name 6.5.3 sends — measured) and `window-initiate-moveresize` → `{wid, xRoot, yRoot, direction, button, source}` (xpra x11/server/seamless.py `_initiate_moveresize` → server/source/window.py); anything else null. `MOVERESIZE_PACKETS` names both. The direction → operation mapping is PURE src/lib/desktop-seamless.js `moveResizeAction`. Gate: test-xpra-client §2d.

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE CROPPED KEYPAD: `METADATA_SUPPORTED` carried xpra-html5 v21's `size-hints` (the pre-4 name) and not `size-constraints` (6.x's), and the server only sends the keys a client lists — no window ever carried its minimum, the fit belt ran blind, a pane shorter than GNOME Calculator's 616 px was asked for, X clamped it and the pane cropped it (measured: the calculator's new-window carried has-alpha,title,class-instance,window-type,decorations). `size-constraints` is listed now. New: `pixelRatioOf`, `devicePane({width,height}, ratio)` (CSS × ratio, rounded DOWN since r2 — below), `minPaneCss(constraints, ratio)` (minimum-size, else base-size per ICCCM, ÷ ratio rounded UP so `devicePane(minPaneCss(h,r),r)` is never below the minimum; no hints ⇒ null). `fitGeometry` already raises to the minimum — the fit never asks below it. Gate: test-xpra-client §6 (incl. the old-list control and a 9-ratio × 4-minimum sweep).

**r2 — A FRACTIONAL RATIO IS 1:1 (the verifier, DPR 1.25/1.5/1.75: a 0.9995 stage transform, the badge on a pane that holds the app, 4.18 % of the pixels off):** `devicePane` rounds DOWN (`floor(css × r + 1e-6)` — the epsilon absorbs 700 × 1.15 = 804.99…) so the device pane's CSS box never exceeds the pane (733 × 1.5 was 1100 ⇒ 733.33 CSS). And `gridStep(r)` / `backingSize(n, r)`: Chrome paints a canvas into its box snapped to WHOLE CSS px (MEASURED — a 1:1 copy only when the box is a whole CSS px): a box of 1346 / 1.5 = 897.33… CSS (1.5 % of a calculator's pixels off) and even 1395 / 2 = 697.5 CSS (an xterm 1395 device px wide at DPR 2: 18.6 % off, every glyph edge softened; padded to 1396 ⇒ 698 CSS: 1 pixel off of 1.19 M) are resampled. `gridStep` = the smallest device step k ≤ 16 whose CSS size k / r is a WHOLE CSS px (2 ⇒ 2, 1.5 ⇒ 3, 1.25 ⇒ 5, 1.75 ⇒ 7, 1.1 ⇒ 11, 1 ⇒ 1, none ⇒ 1); `backingSize` = n rounded UP to it — the view's canvas backing. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (every pane width 200..1400 × 10 ratios; every size 1..2000 × 9 ratios; the old rounding's 733.33 / 898.4 and the unpadded 897.33 / 697.5 boxes as controls).

    xpra-proto.js        — imports nothing; bundled + imported by the node suite. `helloCaps` (the html5 v21 hello trimmed to what the window does: windows/keyboard/pointer/clipboard/cursors; rencodeplus+lz4+brotli; `share:true` for N viewers; NO rgb encodings — their in-packet lz4 lives in the worker), every packet the client sends in xpra-html5 v21's forms (read from its Client.js on this box: `key-action`, `button-action`, `pointer-position`, `map-window`, `configure-window`, `damage-sequence`, `clipboard-token/-contents/-none`, `focus`, `ping_echo`), `displayPacket` (the FULL legacy `desktop_size` — its `screen_sizes` rows carry the work area — when the server names it or names no modern spelling, else 6.5.3's `display-configure` / its alias `configure-display`), `keyboardConfigPacket` (`keyboard-config` else `keymap-changed`), the WHEEL as button 4–7 clicks accumulated per 120 units (`WheelAccumulator` — xtest has no precise wheel and `wheel-motion` trips its assert), `fitGeometry` (the pane under min/max/increment/base hints, snapped DOWN to the cell grid), `placeInside` (dialogs nudged inside), `windowKind` (popup / dialog / main), `clipboardShortcut` (Ctrl/⌘+V is the browser's — the paste event carries the text on plain http; Ctrl+C/X go to the app AND the browser); the delivery rule `clipboardDelivery` lives ONLY in picture-shell.js (every rung shares it; the unused copy that still sat here was removed in Round 3, A1 — test-xpra-client §1 asserts it is gone). **THE KEYMAP IS NATIVE (measured on 6.5.3: a client sending only `keycodes` — xpra-html5's shape — is TRANSLATED onto the server's `us` keymap, so `é`, let alone `中`, can never be typed; a client sending `x11_keycodes` + `query_struct` has the X keymap PROGRAMMED from its own map):** `X11_KEYMAP` (every keycode with its shifted level, the modifiers on their own keycodes, sent as a Map so the keycodes stay integers — a plain object would stringify them), `NAME_TO_KEYCODE` (a key-action's keycode is the one carrying its keysym: KP_Enter on 108, right-hand modifiers on the left name — one JS keyCode, Meta = Super/mod4, AltGraph = ISO_Level3_Shift/mod5), `nativeKey`, and `ImeKeymap.plan(text)` — a character outside the keymap gets a rolling keycode row (226–255, `U<hex>` / Latin-1 names) PUBLISHED by a `keyboard-config` before its press (the server reprograms the X keymap, once per new character). The file header records why the npm `xpra-html5-client` is not used (README says MPL-2.0 derived from upstream while package.json says Apache-2.0; frozen 2022-05, 4.x era; 10.7 MB / 2.37 MB ESM with node-forge+lodash-es; a whole client, not a protocol layer) and that the transport is the upstream html5 v21 Protocol.js worker served unmodified from the installed package behind our auth. Gate: test-xpra-client §1.

### xpra-client.js — THE XPRA SESSION, DOM-FREE (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22)

**A WINDOW PER TOP-LEVEL — design 016 S2 (lane app-satellite-windows, 2026-10-03):** opt-in `slots` (the view sets it only when it can open satellites; off = S1 byte for byte). A second `main`-kind window gets a slot (`slotOrder`, P.slotFor over `mainDisplay()`), is mapped at the slot's origin at its own size, and once a satellite pane is attached (`setSlotPane(wid, cssSize)`) is fitted to it in its slot; `displayFor()` = the main's display grown to every slot, and `syncDisplay()` re-lays the slots first, so ONE display packet carries the root. `on.slot(wid, rect|null)` on every slot gained / moved / lost. The belt keeps a slotted window at its slot (P.inSlot; its own size until a pane holds it, then the fit) and a satellite's dialog inside its slot; `ownerOf` (P.paneOf) / `paneWindows(owner)` scope the main pane's union minimum, front and `closeFront` to owner 0; `constraintsOf(owner)` is a satellite's (its hints, the minimum = the union of its pane). `focusPane(owner)` moves the X focus to that pane's front when another pane's window holds it (keys typed into a satellite). `pickMain` ADOPTS: the next main is unslotted and fitted at 0,0; `lostWindow` closes the slots up (configure-window each) and shrinks the root; `releaseSlot(wid)` hands a window back as S1's guest for the session (noSlot); `closeWindow(wid)` = close-window to it; `setWindowState(wid, st)` generalizes setMainState. Watch slots nothing (`newWindow` in watch), leaving Watch slots what came meanwhile. Fast: test-xpra-client §10 (CONTROL: a copy without the slot line ⇒ Moments over Weixin, no slot).

**The work area (lane desktop-workarea, 2.369.205):** `syncDisplay` still sends one `P.displayPacket` per changed display size — on 6.5.4 that is now the full legacy `desktop_size`, so after every resize `_NET_WORKAREA` = the display it asks (the pane, grown to contain the main window's fit), never the hello's pane; apps that cap themselves at the work area (WeChat; Qt / CEF / Electron commonly) fill the pane. Gate: heavy test-desktop-app-fixed WORK AREA.

**AN APP'S SECOND WINDOW — design 016 S1 (lane app-guest-window, 2026-10-03; the owner: 「对于这种app又打开一个窗口的情况你似乎没有处理好」 — WeChat's Moments drawn over its main window, cut at the bottom; MEASURED on the owner's :4: Weixin NORMAL 1574×974 min 840×816 max 1574×974, Moments NORMAL with no transient-for 880×974 at 324,0 min 880×1120, a 138×44 override-redirect tooltip):** (a) `announceConstraints` emits the main's hints with `minimum-size` raised to PURE `unionMin(windows)` — every HELD window's minimum (mapped, not a popup; `minimum-size` else `base-size`) — only when that union exceeds the main's own (a lone main's payload is byte-identical to before); it runs on every non-popup `new-window`, every `lost-window` and every size-hints change of ANY window (it was main-only). (b) A second `main`-kind window (`kind === 'main'` but not elected) is mapped by PURE `placeGuest(g, pane, main)` — centred over the main's rectangle (the pane's when there is none), then `placeInside`; the belt still only keeps it inside (no re-centring when the pane grows). (c) `on.front(win|null)` names PURE `frontOf(windows)` — the topmost held window by `z` (a dialog counts) — keyed on wid / is-main / title, fired from `focusWindow` (a new window, a press), `raise-window`, a title change and `lost-window` (so a guest elected main by `pickMain` is re-announced as the main); getter `frontWid`. (d) `closeFront()` = ONE `close-window` to the front window, same guards as `closeMain` (connected, not view-only, not Watch). MEASURED limit: the main fills the pane, so a press into it raises it over the guest and covers it; the app's own `present()` (_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW, source 1) arrives as `raise-window` and brings it back, a pager's activation (`xdotool windowactivate`, source 2) does not reach the client. S2 (a VibeSpace window per top-level, a satellite pane) is NOT built — it waits for the owner. Fast: test-xpra-client §9 (the owner's numbers as PURE rows; CONTROL = a patched copy without the union / the centring / the front). Heavy: test-desktop-xpra-window §18 (scripts/fixtures/two-windows.py).

**THE APP'S FIXED SIZE (lane app-fit-fixed, 2026-10-03 — the owner at 2×: WeChat's login in the top-left ~45 % of a blank window, Inkscape's welcome cut at the bottom; then 「对于自己定死尺寸的窗口我们应该遵循他们的尺寸并且禁止缩放」):** THE FIT RULE for a window whose app FIXES its size — size constraints minimum = maximum (PURE `xpra-proto.fixedSizeOf`; MEASURED on xpra 6.5.4 at 2×: WeChat 4.1's login 560×760, Inkscape 1.4.3's welcome 1420×1356 device px) — is FRAME = PICTURE: the client names the FIXED window (`fixedWindow()` = the main, else — the app has no main — the largest dialog with no `transient-for`: Inkscape's welcome is typed DIALOG + modal, the app's only window) through `on.fixed({wid, w, h}|null)` (device px; also the `fixed` getter), maps a LONE fixed dialog at 0,0 (`loneFixed()` — never where X centred it), keeps it there through the belt and grows the display to contain it (`displayFor`); a fixed MAIN is fitted to its own size by fitGeometry as before. xpra-view turns it into `onFixedSize({w,h}|null)` (CSS px = device ÷ the ratio, rounded up; re-read at a ratio change; never reset at a reconnect — the lock holds until the new session says otherwise) and, while `fixedFollows()` (desktop-app-window: off the phone layout), never scales the picture to fit (no badge). desktop-app-window measures the chrome like the minimum and calls `WindowManager.setFixedSize(id, windowMinForPane(fixedPane, chrome, ui))`; null ⇒ `setFixedSize(id, null)`. A fixed dialog OF a resizable main keeps the dialog rule. Resizable apps: unchanged. Gates: test-xpra-client §8, test-window-minsize §5, heavy test-desktop-app-fixed.

**THE REPAINT ASK (the .197 integration, 2026-09-29 — MEASURED on xpra 6.5.4, the box's 2026-09-28 upgrade):** a window configured to a new size while iconified and then un-iconified kept its new region UNPAINTED for good (test-desktop-app-snap's Calculator: minimize → the sidebar opens → restore = 70.9 % of the right edge and 0 % of the bottom edge drawn, identical on the .196 tree — so the upgrade, not a lane); ONE `buffer-refresh` repainted it at once (measured in the suite). The client now asks the way xpra-html5 asks after its own resize (`request_refresh`, +200 / +500 ms): `refreshSoon(win)` after a client fit that GREW the window (`refit` / the belt's configure-window — a shrink or a same-size configure exposes nothing new) and after `setMainState({iconified:false})` — debounced per window, never while the window is iconic, never from Watch / view-only / dormant (the bridge's Watch allowlist already names `buffer-refresh`); `refreshDelaysMs` is injectable, `P.bufferRefresh(wid)` = `['buffer-refresh', wid, 0, 100, {'refresh-now': true, batch: {reset: true}}, {}]`. A MAP asks nothing (it paints the whole window). Gate: test-xpra-client (the repaint-ask leg; a copy without the un-iconify ask goes red) + test-desktop-app-snap (the minrestore flow).

**Lane D (a) F3 (2026-09-25) — THE MAIN IS NAMED BEFORE IT IS FITTED:** `newWindow` registers the main with `premap: true`, emits `on.main` and the constraints FIRST, then fits, syncs the display and maps — the view folds a CSD app's bars inside `on.main` and calls `resize()` there, so the map uses the FINAL pane (measured before: every CSD connect mapped at the pane with the bars up, re-fitted ~160 ms later — a 65 CSS px band twice). `refit` / `belt` return for a `premap` window. Option `cover` (bool or function) = `devicePane`'s round-up for a resampled picture. Gate: test-xpra-client §7 (a) with the old-order CONTROL copy.

**Round 3, lane B — the app's header bar drives OUR window (2.369.177, §3.3):** `initiate-moveresize` / `window-initiate-moveresize` leave the ignore list: `on.moveresize({wid, xRoot, yRoot, direction, button, source, main})` for a KNOWN window, only from the DRIVING pane (never Watch / view-only / dormant — logged); the client applies NOTHING (no configure-window — the X main window stays at 0,0 under the belt; the VibeSpace window moves). `on.main(win|null)` fires when the main window maps / changes / is lost AND on every metadata change of it (the verdict re-reads `decorations`); `on.state(win, changed)` carries `window-metadata {maximized|iconic}` as sent. `setMainState({maximized?, iconified?})` = configure-window of the main at its own geometry with the STATE dict (xpra applies it for the ui driver — seamless.py `_set_window_state`), refused in Watch / view-only / dormant. MEASURED on 6.5.3 + GNOME Calculator: a header-bar drag = `[8 MOVE, button 1]` then, on the release, `[11 CANCEL, 0,0, button 0]` (GTK4 cancels on button release — it lands after our drop, a no-op); the ─ □ buttons = `window-metadata {iconic:true}` / `{maximized:true|false}`; `{iconified:false}` from us ⇒ `{iconic:false}` back and the app draws again. Gate: test-xpra-client §2d (all 12 directions, the not-driving panes, setMainState, a patched pre-lane copy surfacing no move) + §2e.

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166):** `closeMain()` = the OUTER ✕'s ask — ONE `close-window` naming the MAIN window (xpra's WM_DELETE_WINDOW: the app may answer with its own "save?" dialog, and nothing closes then); never a dialog's wid (the app's own ✕ on a dialog is the app's business), never from Watch / view-only, nothing before a main window exists or after it is lost — `false` = nothing sent (the window then closes its pane as before). Gate: test-xpra-client §2c. **A r1 (2.369.166, measured):** what the app DOES with WM_DELETE_WINDOW is the app's business — xterm (no client-side decorations) answers it by HANGING UP its child (SIGHUP) and exits when the child does: an interactive bash ends on the first ✕ (both windows gone 375–418 ms after it, two runs); a child that survives SIGHUP keeps xterm running — the verifier's plain `xterm` ran $SHELL = zsh in a HOME with no .zshrc, whose first-run menu (zsh-newuser-install) survives the hangup (by hand on Xvfb: the same xterm exits once that HOME has an empty .zshrc) — and then the second ✕ within 5 s (the toast names it) is the Stop. Never an automatic Stop: an app answering with its own "save?" dialog looks the same from outside. Gate: heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §10 (3b).

**2.369.165 r1 — a late worker message never acts on a torn-down worker:** `finish()` nulls `worker` before `terminate()`, and a Worker can still deliver a message it queued before that; the `onmessage` closure is bound to its own instance (`const w = worker`) and returns when `worker !== w`. test-xpra-client §late pins it with a pre-fix patched copy as the control.

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** the session speaks DEVICE px: `screen` and `resize(w,h)` take CSS px, `ratio` (a number or a function read at every resize) turns them into the device pane (`devicePane`) for the hello's desktop size, every display-configure and every fit/configure-window; windows, draws and pointer coordinates are device px. `dpi` is the DISPLAY's font dpi (the record's) — never 96 × ratio: xpra rewrites Xft.dpi to a client's dpi when it changes (measured 96 → 144), which would quadruple a GDK_SCALE=2 app's text. `on.constraints(hints|null)` announces the MAIN window's size constraints on every change (new main, a size-constraints metadata change, the main lost ⇒ null); getters `cssPane`, `ratio`, `dpi`, `mainConstraints`. Gate: test-xpra-client §6 (a patched copy with the ratio pinned to 1 as the control).

**r2 — THE DISPLAY CONTAINS THE WINDOW IT PLACES (the verifier on a 320×568 phone @2: the display was the pane, 640×982, under the calculator fitted to its 740×1232 minimum; X clamped the pointer at row 981, so '0', the lower rows and the '=' column could not be clicked — `7894564564`).** `displayFor()` = max(the pane, the main window's fit) is the ONE display rule and `syncDisplay(force)` the ONE sender (only when it differs from what this client last asked, `sentDisplay` — the hello's desktop size first): the server hello (the pane of now), `resize`, leaving Watch (forced — the watched viewer set the display), `refit` (BEFORE the configure-window, so a larger minimum grows the display first), a new main (before its map-window) and the main lost (back to the pane). Getter `display`. Measured after: display 720×1232 ⊇ the window, all ten digits land, `xdotool` reads the app's bottom-right corner. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (grown before the map; pane-sized again when the pane holds the app / the main is gone; the pane-only r1 rule as the patched-copy control) + test-desktop-xpra-window §7 (b).

**x5 (2026-09-22):** `watch` (an agent drives the window): NO geometry at all — windows are drawn where the SERVER has them (no fit at map, the map-window carries the server's geometry), the belt and `refit` return, `resize()` only remembers the pane (the verifier's LOW); leaving watch sends `display-configure` for the pane then re-fits the main + keeps dialogs inside. `dormant` (the pane is BLOCKED: the bridge holds its hello and relays nothing): the hello timeout is suspended (`armHello`) — the server's hello arrives the moment the pane becomes active; a hello answered for a pane that changed size since (`helloPane`) is followed by `display-configure` for the pane of NOW. test-xpra-client §5 (a patched copy without the Watch guards as the control; the non-dormant client timing out as the dormant one's control).


    xpra-client.js       — `createXpraClient({url, workerUrl, screen, dpi, layout, on, Worker, decode, now, log, helloTimeoutMs, pasteKeyDelayMs, beltGapMs, beltFightMs, beltMaxFights})` → `{connect, close, send, resize, keyDown, keyUp, typeText, pointerMove, pointerButton, wheel, pasteText, focusWindow, windowAt, beltState, state, closedReason, windows, mainWid, focusedWid, pane, serverCaps, packetTypes, viewOnly, lastPaste, lastReceived}`; `on.status/window/paint/title/icon/clipboard/cursor/ready`. The transport is the upstream Protocol.js WORKER (`{c:'r'}` ready → `{c:'o',u}` open → `{c:'p',p}` packets / `{c:'s',p}` sends; it frames, rencodeplus-codes and inflates off the main thread). Invariants: the FIRST top-level window is mapped at 0,0 with the pane's fitted size (the app never appears small in a corner) and `resize` re-fits it — `display-configure` first (the virtual screen follows the pane) then `configure-window`; every OTHER non-popup window (a dialog, a SECOND top-level — xpra clamps one at +2000+1500 to 20x20 px visible) keeps its size and is placed inside the pane at map, when X moves it and when the pane shrinks; THE BELT (2026-09-22): a server geometry packet (`window-move-resize` / `window-resized` — the app resized or moved ITSELF, GNOME Calculator's mode switch fell to 40 % of the pane) is checked against the fit (the main within one size increment at 0,0, a secondary inside) and answered with ONE corrective `configure-window`, at most one per window per `BELT_GAP_MS` 500 (a packet inside the gap after our own configure is re-checked when the gap ends — it may be the confirmation or X's snap), and an app that undoes the fit `BELT_MAX_FIGHTS` 3 times in a row, each within `BELT_FIGHT_MS` 2000, wins until the pane or its hints change (said once — bounded, never a ping-pong, two viewers of different panes included); a popup is drawn where X put it and never moved; draws are PAINTED IN ORDER per window (a promise chain — a later png may decode first) and EVERY draw is acked (`damage-sequence`, decode ms or -1 + the reason: an unsupported coding, an unknown window) or the server stops sending; a text `clipboard-token` on CLIPBOARD is surfaced ONCE (deduped against the last paste and the last receipt); a `clipboard-request` is answered with the last pasted text (`-none` before any); `pasteText` sends the token then the app's own Ctrl+V after 60 ms (the token must land first); a key the published keymap lacks goes publish-then-press from keyDown (its keyUp is swallowed); `typeText` (IME) publishes the rows BEFORE the presses; `viewOnly` drops every input at the source (Ctrl+V still answers `paste` so the browser keeps working); a `disconnect` names its reason, a hello that never comes closes with a deadline, a worker that cannot start (the html5 package missing on a host) closes by name; nothing is sent after the close. Gate: test-xpra-client §2 (a fake worker + an out-of-order fake decoder) + §2b (the belt and the placement as packets, with the within-one-increment CONTROL) + test-desktop-xpra-window §4 (the real rung: xterm resizing / moving ITSELF fitted back and X agreeing, a second top-level at +2000+1500 placed inside, GNOME Calculator's Ctrl+Alt+A/B mode switch keeping 100 % of the pane — the pre-fix client, run as the control, measured 78.0 % then 41.2 %).

### xpra-view.js — THE XPRA PICTURE VIEW (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22; §4.4: the window is OURS)

**A WINDOW PER TOP-LEVEL — design 016 S2 (lane app-satellite-windows, 2026-10-03):** `onSatellite({wid, title})` (asked in a microtask after the client's own step, active panes only) and `attachSatellite(host, wid, cb)` — the satellite pane: its own `.xpra-pane.xpra-satellite` with a stage, an IME textarea, a fit badge and a note; every canvas is RE-HOMED to the stage of the pane that draws it (`stageFor` — the bound satellite's while active, else the main stage), its stage translated by the window's origin (and scaled to fit only when the window is larger than the pane), its pointer mapped back to the root, its keys `focusPane`d first, the header-bar hand-over tracked per pane (`pointerOf` / `wirePointer` / `releaseWmHold(ptr)` — the main's behaviour unchanged), its title / minimum (`constraintsOf`) / fixed size / metadata / state to `cb`. `cb.onGone(why)`: 'lost' (slot null, window gone) · 'adopted' (it became the main) · 'released' · 'missing' (the window list is in — startup-complete or 3 s after the hello — without its wid) · 'main-closed' (dispose) · 'replaced'. Watch / Blocked: everything on the main stage (one picture) and the satellite's note ('Shown in the main window while an agent drives' / 'Active on another client'). The handle's `dispose()` (the person closed the satellite while the X window lives) calls `releaseSlot`. CONTROL (test-xpra-client §10): a copy whose `stageFor` never returns a satellite's stage leaves the satellite empty.

**Design 016 S1 (lane app-guest-window, 2026-10-03):** option `onFront({wid, title, kind, main}|null)` forwards the client's `on.front` (`main` false = an app's SECOND window in front — WeChat's Moments); `disconnect()` says `onFront(null)`. `closeFront()` → `client.closeFront()` (the window's ✕ while a second window is in front). `onMinSize` now carries the UNION of every held window's minimum (the client's constraints), so the window grows to hold the second window instead of the pane cutting it; the active stage still scales only for the MAIN's overflow (a guest larger than a workspace-capped pane is pinned inside, never a zoom jump).

**Lane D (a) (2026-09-25):** option `pictureScale` (() => the RECORD's, via `renderOf`): the windows are laid out at `ratio = devicePixelRatio ÷ pictureScale` (1.5× on a 2× screen = 2.667 X px per CSS px — a GDK_SCALE-2 picture shown at 0.75), the client told to `cover`, the 1:1 grid nudge skipped for a resampled picture, and the monitor-move `matchMedia` asks for the SCREEN's ratio (a `(resolution: 2.667dppx)` query never matches); getter `pictureScale`. The `main:` handler calls `client.resize(paneSize())` after `onMain` (F3). A SHRINK keeps the canvas backing `BACKING_SHRINK_MS` (1 s) before it follows (the app snapping to its own size ~650 ms after the map and the belt's same-task re-fit used to clear the rows in between — a band until the repaint). A scroll packet's moves all read ONE snapshot of the canvas taken before the packet (upstream `do_paint`; applied in turn on the same canvas a later move read rows an earlier one had overwritten — ghost rows, 593 overlaps in 66 packets on chrome://settings). A `has-alpha` window (Chrome's own frame) is `clearRect`ed under each image draw. The header-bar gesture starts at the pane's OWN press (`press.client`) when one is in flight — Chrome 153's x_root/y_root are +10,+5 off it (the window moved 110/59 for 120/64); the app's root point only for a keyboard move. Gate: test-xpra-client §7 (b)–(f) with CONTROL copies (the old scroll loop).

**Round 3, lane B (2.369.177, §3.3):** new options `onMain(meta|null)`, `onState(changed)` (main window only), `onMoveResize({direction, button, main, wid, press, held})`. A gesture the app starts in the middle of a press HANDS THE POINTER OVER: the pane releases its capture, forwards no motion (`wmHold`), and the button release reaches X exactly ONCE from a per-press document `pointerup`/`pointercancel` (an AbortController, never a per-render listener) — wherever it is let go; `press` = the gesture's X root point in VIEWPORT px (`rootToClient`: pane rect + stage offset + root ÷ ratio × stage scale; null for CANCEL's 0,0). `setAppState(st)` = the client's setMainState; `setFloatingChip` = the shell's. Gate: test-xpra-client §2e.

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166):** `closeApp()` = `client.closeMain()` (false with no client) — the desktop-app window's outer ✕ asks through it.


**Round 3, A1 (2.369.166 — the copy without a click on plain http):** THE GESTURE STAMP. The IME textarea's keydown stamps `copyGestureAt = clock()` when `client.keyDown` answers `'copy'` (Ctrl/⌘+C or +X FORWARDED to the app — a view-only / Watch pane forwards nothing, so it never stamps) AND the event is the user's own (`isTrusted === true`, not an auto-`repeat`); `onClipboard` hands the shell `gestureAge = clock() − copyGestureAt` and SPENDS the stamp on every delivery — one chord, at most one write, so a later copy nobody made on this page (an agent through P9, an app on a timer, another client) meets no stamp and keeps the chip. `clock` = the injectable `now` (else `performance.now`). A token the client DEDUPES (the same text as the last one) is no delivery and spends nothing. Measured on the real rung (test-desktop-xpra-window §9, GNOME Calculator on a hostname page): the calculator's token arrives ~30 ms after the trusted Ctrl+C and lands in the browser clipboard with no click; xclip's token 5.5 s after a chord ⇒ the chip; a copy 0.1 s after a plain digit key (the page HAS activation, no chord) ⇒ the chip. New getters `hintShown`, `copyHint`. Gate: test-xpra-client §3c (+ the WIRING PIN in §4) + test-desktop-xpra-window §9.

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** options `dpi` (number or function — the record's) and `pixelRatio` (() => devicePixelRatio, injectable). Each window's box is its device geometry ÷ the ratio and its canvas keeps the DEVICE pixels (r2: the backing is `backingSize(win, r)` and its CSS box backing ÷ r — see below) — 1:1 on a 2× screen, crisp; the pointer maps pane CSS → the stage's own coordinates (offset and scale undone) → device px; a devicePixelRatio change (a `(resolution: Ndppx)` media query, re-armed at each ratio) relayouts every box and the minimum. The stage's contain-fit is no longer Watch-only: an ACTIVE picture whose app is larger than the pane (its minimum on a phone / a narrow cell) is scaled to fit and centred — never cropped — with the `.xpra-fit-badge` t('Scaled to fit — the app needs at least {w}×{h}'); unscaled it stays at 0,0 as before (the increment leftover right/bottom). `onMinSize({w,h}|null)` hands the window the smallest pane (`minPaneCss(the main's constraints, ratio)`); getters `fitBadge`, `ratio`, `minSize`. The cursor PNG is device px: at a ratio ≠ 1 it is re-declared as `image-set(url() Nx)` with the hotspot ÷ ratio after the plain url() (kept when a browser rejects the form). Gate: test-xpra-client §6 + test-desktop-xpra-window §6 (real rung, DPR 2).

**r2 (the verifier's findings on this view):** ① ACTIVE SCALES ONLY IN THE MINIMUM CASE — the contain-fit of an ACTIVE pane reads the MAIN window only and only when the app has a minimum (`minSize`): exactly the badge's condition, so an active scale is never silent, and a dialog larger than the pane no longer zooms the whole picture mid-session (Watch still contains every non-popup window). ② `FIT_SLACK_CSS` = 1: an overflow under one CSS px is not an overflow (a fractional ratio's rounding) — a sub-1 transform resamples the 1:1 picture. ③ THE DEVICE-PIXEL GRID: `gridNudge` moves the stage right/down by < 1 device px so its origin lands on a device pixel (a pane at CSS 65 is device 97.5 at DPR 1.5), re-read at every fit, on `pointerenter` and through `resnap()` (the window's `onMoved`); ④ each canvas backing is `backingSize(win, r)` with an explicit CSS box of backing ÷ r (a WHOLE CSS px — Chrome snaps a canvas's paint box to whole CSS px, so even an odd width at DPR 2, 697.5 CSS, was resampled: an xterm 18.6 % off), the < k-px transparent margin clipped by the window's own box. Measured after (a full screenshot vs the canvas, only pixels stable across the capture): DPR 1.5 — 9 / 12 / 229 of ~1.7 M pixels off at three window sizes (before: a 0.9995 transform + the badge, 4.18 %; with the transform gone but no grid/backing, 1.3–1.9 %); 1.25 and 1.75 likewise; DPR 2 unchanged. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (the 1.5 fit identity + the canvas box 898×734 px; the oversized dialog; each with an r1 patched-copy control) + test-desktop-xpra-window §7 (a).

**x5 (2026-09-22):** the windows ride a STAGE (`.xpra-stage`, the pane now `isolation: isolate` so the blocked overlay sits above every window): identity while active, `scale(s)` in WATCH with s = min(pane / the non-popup windows' bounding box) — contain, never cropped (`stageScale`). `setMode(m)` sets the client's `viewOnly` / `watch` / `dormant` and, going active, hands the pane's size in once. A CUT (the Protocol.js close reason `4001: '<reason>'`) clears the windows and reconnects AT ONCE as a dormant viewer — never the ladder's 1 s, so the pane stays seated for re-election. **2.369.156 (the product's default, INFO b):** the Watch scale is CAPPED AT 1 and the stage CENTRED (`translate(ox, oy) scale(s)`, whole-pixel offsets; `stageOffset`) — a pane larger than the app shows it crisp at 1:1, never blown up (test-xpra-client §5 with the uncapped factor printed as the control; test-desktop-xpra-window §5 on a 1080×700 page). The vnc rung's picture is noVNC's `scaleViewport` (unchanged).


    xpra-view.js         — `createXpraView(host, {url, workerUrl, before, labels, autoReconnect, onStatus, onTitle, onIcon, Worker, decode, secure, clipboardApi, log})` → the shell's handles + `{pane, ime, chip, setViewOnly, windows(), client, chipText}`. On the shared shell (background `var(--bg-primary)`), a `.xpra-pane` (THEME colour — no root, no black; test-xpra-client §4 censuses no `#000` in the xpra files) holding ONE `.xpra-win` canvas per xpra window placed where the session says (a resize keeps the painted pixels until the server repaints), draws applied in order (image → drawImage at its rect, closed after; scroll → the canvas copied onto itself by each move), pointer from the PANE's own rect (viewport px == layout px at net zoom 1 — never mixed; capture on down; wheel prevented; contextmenu prevented), the keyboard through a hidden `.xpra-ime` textarea (focused on every pointerdown; keydown/keyup forwarded and prevented ONLY when sent — Ctrl+V is left to the browser so its `paste` event fires; `compositionend` and an `insertText` input event deliver IME text through `typeText`), a debounced (150 ms) ResizeObserver ⇒ `client.resize`, the app's title/icon (PNG bytes → `pngDataUrl`, a validated base64 data URL) handed to the caller, cursor packets as a `url()` cursor. CLIPBOARD (owner acceptance 2): the `paste` event's text ⇒ `pasteText` (works on plain http); the Paste chip is the SHELL's flow (a secure context reads the async API; plain http / a refusal / an empty clipboard opens the shell's paste box, then Send ⇒ `pasteText`, the focus back on the app — measured with REAL pastes on a hostname page); a copy inside the app ⇒ `shell.deliverCopy` (the API on a secure context with a toast; on plain http a token inside the user's own copy-chord gesture window is written with no click (Round 3, A1 above); else — and when the API refuses — the shell's "Copied in the app — click to copy" chip; a refused execCommand keeps the chip and says so). Status: "Waiting for the application window…" after the hello, "Connected" at the first window, "The application closed its window" when the last goes, "Connection lost: <the server's reason>" in red + the shell's ladder. Gate: test-xpra-client §3 (the fake DOM, both clipboard branches) + test-desktop-xpra-window (heavy, the real rung).
**Lane M (2.369.182):** the pane's `pointerdown` preventDefault suppresses the compatibility `mousedown` in EVERY phase (measured on the real rung: pointerdown 1 / click 1 / mousedown 0 per click) — anything above the pane that must see a press listens for a capture-phase `pointerdown` (utils.js `onOutsidePress` for every floating menu; desktop-app-window.js's activation). Adding a `stopPropagation` here would not break them (capture runs first) but re-run test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (6) + §14.

### src/lib/desktop-seamless.js — SEAMLESS DESKTOP-APP WINDOWS, PURE (round 3 lane B, 2.369.177; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.zh.md §3.3, D3)

**Lane D (b) (2026-09-25):** `frameKeyOf` is also THE key of an app's default scale (src/lib/desktop-app-scale.js `scaleKeyOf` = it) — one key per app for both per-app choices; the user-state LOADER that used to live in desktop-app-window.js is src/lib/desktop-app-prefs.js now (see there).

Imports nothing; bundled. THE ONE VERDICT `seamlessVerdict({csd, setting, userToggle, lease, chain, phone, connected}) → {seamless, why}` exactly as §3.3 spells it — seamless ⇔ connected ∧ ¬lease ∧ ¬chain ∧ ¬phone ∧ (userToggle = on ∨ (userToggle = auto ∧ setting = auto ∧ csd)); `why` ∈ `SEAMLESS_WHY` names the deciding fact WANTED FIRST (user / setting-off / ssd / csd) and only then the PAUSE (phone, disconnected, lease, chain — a forced 'on' is paused too; `isPaused`). `isCsd(meta)` ⇔ `meta.decorations === 0` exactly (§2.3 M3a). THE REVEAL as PURE transitions: `revealStep(state, {type: zone-enter | zone-leave | window-leave | alt {down} | tick | reset}, now) → {state, revealed, wakeAt}` — `REVEAL_HOVER_MS` 250 (a crossing reveals nothing), `REVEAL_LINGER_MS` 1500 after the pointer goes back INTO THE APP or Alt is released, leaving the window folds at once, Alt reveals at once and holds; `HOT_ZONE_PX` 6. `moveResizeAction(direction)` (X's MoveResize: 0–7 ⇒ nw n ne e se s sw w, 8 / 10 ⇒ move, 9 ⇒ resize from se, 11 ⇒ cancel, else null — an integer or a digit string only). `windowStateAction(meta, {maximized, minimized})` = 'maximize' | 'restore' | 'minimize' | null — SET semantics, only announced keys (a window born maximized never maximizes ours). THE FRAME CHOICE: the menu speaks FRAME words (Show window frame ▸ Auto / On / Off), the verdict SEAMLESS words — `userToggleOfFrame` is the one crossing (frame On ⇒ userToggle off); `frameKeyOf(rec)` = the registry app id, else `exec:<basename>` (cleaned); `frameChoiceOf` / `setFrameChoice` (auto REMOVES the key) / `frameMenuModel`. Gate: scripts/test-desktop-seamless.mjs (fast: the 192-row matrix vs the formula written out in the suite + a pause-less patched-copy control, the reveal table, the words, the WindowManager seams over a fake DOM, the pins).

### src/lib/desktop-app-scale.js — THE PER-APP DEFAULT SCALE, PURE (lane D (b), 2026-09-25; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.4 note)

Imports only desktop-seamless.js (the key) and the PURE model (`SCALE_CHOICES`, `parseScaleChoice`, `normalizeScale`); bundled; no words, no DOM. `SCALE_PREF_KEY` = 'desktopAppScale' (user state `desktopAppScale[<key>]`, synced to every client); `scaleKeyOf` = `frameKeyOf` (the registry app id, else `exec:<basename>` — a typed "xterm" and the record whose exec resolved to /usr/bin/xterm agree); `scaleChoiceOf(map, key)` → a number | 'auto' (none / junk); `setScaleChoice(map, key, choice)` → a NEW map, 'auto' and junk REMOVE the key (the frame choice's rule — the map never grows by choices that change nothing); `launchScaleChoice(map, payload)` → the launch body's `scaleChoice` for `{appId}` / `{exec}` (null = send nothing, the instance default decides); `scaleDefaultMenuModel(map, key)` = a card's rows (auto + every explicit scale, the stored one current and not offered again); `appDefaultModel(rec, map)` → `{key, def, running, make, isDefault, clear}` = the tail of a window's Scale ▸ (running = 'auto' when the scale was derived — an app default is always explicit, so a derived window offers no "Make"; a value outside the set ⇒ null). Gate: scripts/test-desktop-app-scale.mjs §4 (+ a stores-auto patched copy as the control).

### src/lib/desktop-app-prefs.js — THE PER-APP CHOICES IN USER STATE, ONE LOADER (lane D (b), 2026-09-25)

**Design 016 S2:** a third map, `desktopAppSatellite` (`SATELLITE_PREF_KEY`, in `APP_PREF_KEYS`): {appKey: {dx, dy}} — where the person last left a satellite relative to its main window. PURE `satellitePlacement(main, size, ws, remembered)` (remembered offset, else right of the main, else left, else the workspace's right edge; the top-left kept on the workspace) and `setSatelliteOffset(map, key, off)`.

Lane B's `desktopAppFrame` loader moved out of desktop-app-window.js and generalized so the launch dialog shares it: `APP_PREF_KEYS` ['desktopAppFrame', 'desktopAppScale']; `wireAppPrefs(app)` (idempotent: ONE `onGlobal` for `user-state-updated` — the broadcast carries the WHOLE user state, so it replaces both maps (a key it lacks = an empty map) — ONE `onStateChange` that RE-READS on every (re)connect, and the first GET; a GET answer never overwrites a map a broadcast replaced while it was in flight; returns the ready promise); `appPrefs(key)` ({} until loaded, so an unmade choice reads 'auto' everywhere); `appPrefsReady()`; `onAppPrefs(fn)` → unsubscribe; `saveAppPrefs(key, edit, failText)` — `edit` is `(map) => map` for ONE app's entry (`(map) => setScaleChoice(map, appKey, choice)`; a whole map is REFUSED, nothing sent): shown locally FIRST (the view = the server's map + this page's edits in flight, so a broadcast of someone else's write never hides an unsaved choice), then a fresh GET, the edit applied to the map the server holds NOW, a merge-only PATCH of that ONE key; saves from one page run one at a time (the next reads what this one wrote); a refused save leaves the view (rolled back to the server's map, subscribers told) and toasts `failText` + the reason. The whole loader is `createAppPrefs({fetchJson, toast, failDefault})` (the page's singleton = the exports; a suite builds its own over a fake socket).

**Lane D verify (2026-09-25) — THE MAP THAT TRAVELLED WHOLE:** the first build read user state once per page and PATCHed the WHOLE map from its own copy; the route merges top-level keys only, so a page whose socket had dropped for a moment (it missed the broadcast) wiped another client's choices: measured on a real server with two pages, `{"xterm":2}` → `{"gnome-calculator":1.5}`, B's card still "Auto" after its reconnect. Now the re-read on reconnect + the per-entry edit on the fresh map (after: `{"xterm":2,"gnome-calculator":1.5}`, B reads "2×"; B saving while still disconnected keeps `{"xterm":3,"gnome-calculator":2}`). Residual: two pages editing the same map inside one GET→PATCH window are last-write-wins (as any same-key user-state race). kb-bugfix-invariants has the incident. The census (test-desktop-app-scale §7): no other src/lib file builds a payload for either map; the window and the launcher save through it, and every call passes an edit. Gate: test-desktop-app-scale §8 (two pages over a fake server that merges exactly as src/routes/persistence.js and broadcasts only to connected sockets — the reopen re-reads, a save after it and a save from a stale copy keep the other page's key, a refusal rolls back (notified twice, one toast), two quick saves both land, a save that lands as shown notifies ONCE (the dialog re-focuses its control on that render — a second render would drop the keyboard), a whole map refused — for both maps; controls: no reconnect re-read, the old local-map PATCH, a kept refused edit) + heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §14 (1b) (the verifier's recipe on two real pages: B's socket closed, A stores another app's default, B's card reads it after the reconnect, B's save keeps it).

### src/lib/open-with.js + src/lib/file-changed.js — OPEN WITH LIBREOFFICE, the client door (docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.9, 2026-09-27)

open-with.js — `installOpenWith(app)` (app.js, beside the launcher) puts THE ONE door on the mediator: **`app.openWithDesktopApp({catalogId, file, host})`** — the PURE file rule first (a bad path is a toast in words), the app's own default scale (`launchScaleChoice`, the prefs loader waited ≤ 3 s), ONE `POST /api/desktop/apps {appId, file, fileHost, host?, dpr, uiScale, scaleChoice?}`; ok ⇒ `app.openDesktopApp(id)`; a refusal the user can act on (`DIALOG_CODES`: app-absent, host-unreachable, host_unavailable, host_needs_daemon, machine-mismatch, no-backend) ⇒ the launch dialog in FILE MODE, anything else a toast by `openWithRefusalText`. The explorer row calls it, and so does the Word viewer's "Open in LibreOffice" (file-viewer.js `_officeOpener`, the verdict's `catalogId`). **`app.officeOfferAt(anchor, {host, file})`** (the viewer asks it before the door): the verdict (cached, or the peek) says `app-absent` / `host_needs_daemon` ⇒ `officeMenuItems`' rows — the ONE spelling of the sentence + the install offer — as a `createPopover(anchor, 'context-menu office-offer')` under the button (the note `.context-menu-note` role note; the install a focusable `role=menuitem`, Enter / Space; sized by its words — style.css `.office-offer`), → true; anything else → false (the caller goes through the door). `app.officeVerdictFor(host, file)` → `{cached, promise}` over `GET /api/desktop/open-with?peek=1` (a paired machine not connected right now answers `unchecked` — a right-click never bootstraps an ssh machine's agent; the row's click connects; cached per machine + module for AVAIL_TTL_MS 60 s — an ok / app-absent / host_needs_daemon answer; a machine that did not answer never; cleared on an install and on a refused launch). `app.officeMenuItems(verdict, {host, file})` = the menu rows (the Open row, or the note + the install row). `installOffice(app, {host, what})` = the install dialog. The ws `file-changed` broadcast is relayed as the window event. **file-changed.js** (imports nothing): `FILE_CHANGED_EVENT` = 'vibespace:file-changed', `fileChangedDetail(m)`, `foldPath`, **`sameFile(detail, {host, path})`** (the same machine — null / '' / 'local' are one — and the same FOLDED path: the explorer names a child of / as //name), `onFileChanged(fn, {signal})` (bound to a window's listener signal), `relayFileChanged(m)`. The code editor's consumer: `onFileChanged((d) => { if (sameFile(d, {host, path})) check(); }, {signal})` — its disk-freshness check at once (a clean editor reloads, a dirty one shows the chip), on either transport. **Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — the app's exit closes this window; the outer ✕ is the app's own close; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2, the owner: "我关闭内部窗口之后外部窗口还要额外关闭一次").** `decideExit(r)` runs on every record this window applies (the broadcast, the stop's answer, a reconnect's re-read, the FIRST GET) and decides ONCE (`exitDecided` — a lease dropping later never re-decides): PURE `exitCloseVerdict(r, {leased: !!lease})`; close ⇒ `showToast(exitToastText(r, name))` — "Calculator exited" / "… stopped" / "… stopped after N min without input" / "… stopped: <why>" (textContent: the name is the app's own title) — then `app.wm.closeWindow` (programmatic, never vetoed; every client closes its own copy from its own broadcast, the layout autosave then carries the removal); keep ⇒ the ended sentence as before. `closed` makes every late answer a no-op. Module-level EXPANDED set keeps cards open across the jobs-updated panel rebuilds (sidebar-rail rebuilds the whole panel on that broadcast — renders-once guard); `focusJobsPanel(app, jobId)` is the shared entry: sets sidebar._jobsFocusId (renderRail scrolls + outlines `.jobs-focus`), rebuilds in place when the jobs tab is already active (_railGo re-click would COLLAPSE the sidebar — never call it for programmatic focus). openJobsWindow/openInteractWindow REDIRECT to focusJobsPanel and return null when the rail exists; the windows remain ONLY as the mobile / activityRail-off fallback ({forceWindow:true} escape).
