### jobs-layout.js

    jobs-layout.js       — PURE (imports nothing, DOM-free) the Background Work panel's TRIAGE arithmetic (docs/design-background-work.md §13, 2026-09-14; the user-todos-layout.js precedent — every decision the panel used to make inline, twice, lives here once): `attentionOf(job)` → awaiting | unacked-failure | acked-failure | null (a parked SERVICE can never be acknowledged — it needs a start — so it stays an unacked failure); `badgeCounts(jobs)` / `badgeText` = the ONE counter the rail badge and both panel summaries read (red = awaiting-user + UNACKNOWLEDGED failed|missed|unverified, grey = "N seen"); `familyOf(name)` = the name-family rule (a trailing ` run`, `-r<n>`, `-v<n>`, `-<n>` and version-like tails stripped until the name is stable; table-tested); `foldTasks(tasks, {expanded, sessionNames})` = owner session (sidebar display name > short id > "created by you") → family → rows, `defaultExpanded` only when the group holds a running / awaiting-user / unacknowledged row, the persisted folds applied AFTER the defaults; `familyKey(family)` = a group's fold key half (FNV-1a digest — lane-redact verify r6: the persisted map never spells a job's name) + `isFoldKey` (the load drops an older build's word-keyed entry); `pruneFolds(folds, layout)` = the user-state `jobsPanelFolds` map minus every key no live group holds (a stale fold would grow user state without bound); `heldText(digest, {t, cid})` = the held-notification sentence from the server's STRUCTURE (`{total, byConversation}`), words by the device's own t() — the server cannot say them, the digest is broadcast to every client while the language is per device. Invariants: the client READS `job.ack` and never derives acknowledgement (the server computes it over the full record; the snapshot's journal is truncated); one counter, one fold rule, both surfaces. Gated by test-job-model (137) + test-jobs-panel.

### scripts/test-jobs-triage.mjs + scripts/jobs-triage-fixture.mjs + scripts/test-jobs-panel.mjs

    the Background Work TRIAGE gates (design §13). jobs-triage-fixture.mjs = the NEUTRAL fixture shaped after the measured instance (200 done > 1 d, 36 failed with mixed acknowledgement — notified ok / stashed / polled by the owner lineage / by a stranger session / by the job's own token — a running + an awaiting-user row, cron parents + children, held notifications; names job-a…, sessions sess-1-…, groups T-1; EVERY instant derived from the injected clock, never a calendar date). test-jobs-triage.mjs (FAST, ~2 s, per-pid scratch dataDir, no fixed port/path) drives the REAL engine + REAL user routes: who archives / who stays / an unacknowledged failure never archives at any age or on any path (sweep, boot, cap), poll/show of an archived id answers archived:true, the cap keeps the newest 2000, a restart re-reads the archive, ONE broadcast per sweep, /seen stamps user-opened, ?archived=1, the CLI's --archived against a fake API, the typed held digest; §6b (2026-09-16) an OBSTRUCTED archive write (a directory at the atomic tmp path ⇒ EISDIR, the ENOSPC/EACCES class) releases NOTHING — every record stays in jobs.json in memory and on disk, the log says FAILED with the verbatim error and never "archived N", no broadcast, the next sweep moves them all once the path is writable, and a record re-archived after a failed store flush replaces rather than duplicates its copy; §2b a codex-owned failure notified on `rpc-queue` is served acknowledged. test-jobs-panel.mjs (HEAVY — chrome + a worktree server seeded with the fixture, SKIPs without chrome): at 1200×800 (rail) AND 375×667 (window) the badge counts only awaiting + unacknowledged, a group with an unacked failure is expanded by default while a done-only group is collapsed, a collapse persists across a reload through user state, a failed row shows its last line, the summary names the held notifications, the "Archived · N" row fetches ONLY when clicked.

### src/lib/taskbar.js — THE GROUPED BUTTON + src/lib/taskbar-group.js (lane K, 2026-09-25)

**The owner, on a taskbar button reading "VibeSpace 主开发 · 2 windows grouped": every click popped the two-row chooser instead of doing anything — "这个体验比较差".** A tab group's stacked taskbar button (`_buildGroupItem`) now behaves like a window button first. The DECISIONS are PURE `src/lib/taskbar-group.js` (imports nothing, DOM-free): `groupClickVerdict({inFront, pointerType, dragging, popoverOpen})` → `'activate'` (the group is behind) | `'chooser'` (it is already in front) | `'none'` (a drag's release) — the SAME rule for mouse / touch / pen / keyboard and with or without an open hover chooser; `hoverVerdict({pointerFine, touch, dragging, popoverOpen, intentMs})` → `'never'` (not a fine pointer, a touch device, a drag, ANOTHER popover) | `'wait'` | `'open'` at `GROUP_HOVER_INTENT_MS` (300 — a deliberate pause, not the gear flyout's 120: a taskbar button is crossed on the way to its neighbours); `inFrontOf({focusedId, hostId, tabIds, minimized, sameDesktop})` (host or any tab focused, not minimized, not hidden by a desktop / the stage); `groupKeyVerdict({key, inFront})` (Enter / Space = the click rule, ArrowUp = the chooser, else null). `GROUP_HOVER_LEAVE_MS` 250 = the grace after the pointer leaves button + chooser.

**taskbar.js reads the world for them.** `activateWindow(app, id)` (exported) is THE activation a taskbar button performs — `wm.revealWindow(id)` (inc-muiq348r-jwb5: its own tab — a group's HOST included —, the group restored, raised), then the session takes the keyboard; the single button's click is `focused ? minimize : activateWindow` (byte-identical behaviour to before), the group's `'activate'` is `activateWindow` on the chain's ACTIVE tab (so the tab on show stays on show). The chooser's rows and the window list's rows reveal through the same door (the chooser used to spell restore-host / focus-host / `switchTab` by hand because `focusWindow` of the host never switched tabs; the window list's host-labelled row showed the guest under the host's title). The grouped button is `role=button`, `tabIndex 0`, `aria-haspopup=menu`, `aria-expanded` (kept by the chooser), `aria-label` = active title + "N windows grouped" (t(), zh + ja); its native `title` tooltip is gone (it sat over the hover chooser and the chooser lists every title) — the single button keeps its `title` and is not focusable. Every closure resolves the chain LIVE from the host id (`liveChain()`), never the build-time object. **Hover:** the FIRST `pointermove` of a VISIT with `pointerType` `'mouse'` or `'pen'` on an `(any-pointer: fine)` device (verify r1 low ③: a pen used to get only the click rule; touch never arms) arms a timer (compat mouse events of a tap never arm — only pointer events are listened to), re-judged when it fires (a drag or a menu may have begun since); `pointerleave` / `pointerdown` / `dragstart` / `contextmenu` cancel it; a press SPENDS the visit until the pointer leaves (a click never grows a chooser under a resting pointer). **2.369.184 (lane penleg, the load construction of the .183 mirror red): the rule is PURE `hoverStep({spent}, event)`** — `move` arms once per visit, `press` spends + cancels, `leave` ends + cancels, `away` ends, a bare `enter` arms NOTHING: Chrome dispatches `pointerenter` when it RE-TARGETS a resting pointer (the taskbar rebuilt the button under it — a tab title change re-keys the structure; its hover recompute after any layout change moving the MOUSE pointer where a pen rests) and no pointermove comes with it — before, a click then a title change grew a hover chooser 300 ms later, 5 of 5. The visit is the GROUP's — module-level `_hoverSpent` (host ids, pruned in the rebuild path), never the button closure a rebuild replaces — and ONE app-lifetime capture `pointermove` on document (`_watchHoverVisits`, idle while nothing is spent) ends a spent visit when a pointer moves anywhere but that group's button (the pointer that left DURING a rebuild gets no leave on the live element). Both `pointerenter` and `pointermove` ask `hoverStep`; the ONE arming is `armFrom(e)` on its `'arm'` (so a one-row revert of the PURE table is the pre-fix hover — the gates' control). Drag = the event's held primary button OR `.window.dragging` / `.tab-ghost` / `.split-resizing` OR a window's `_resizeOp`; the CLICK's `dragging` reads only the click event's own `buttons` (a leaked drag class must never eat a click). "Another popover" = a visible `[data-popover]` that is not a HOVER chooser, `.usage-popup:not(.hidden)` (a neighbour's hover chooser yields to the next hover). Every class that guard — and app.js's autohide conceal guard in `_ensureTaskbarHotzone` — queries is one the tree PRODUCES (test-taskbar-group §7's census: a CSS rule, an index.html class, or a className / classList / createPopover spelling in src/); verify r1 low ⑤ dropped the dead `.taskbar-window-list` from both (the window list is an `overlap-switcher` [data-popover], caught by the loop).

**`showTabGroupList(app, anchor, chain, {hover, keyboard})` — THE CHOOSER** (`.overlap-switcher.taskbar-group-chooser`, createPopover's dedup class unchanged so it and the window list replace each other): `pop._chooser = {hostId, anchor, mode: 'hover'|'click', keep, leave, pin, reanchor, relist}`, `data-mode` mirrors it. Already open for the same button ⇒ never re-created (no flicker): a click / key PINS a hover chooser (`mode 'click'`, no leave timer; `keyboard` ⇒ focus the active row). Hover mode = non-modal (nothing focused), the leave timer across button + chooser (the button's `pointerenter` calls `keep()` through `_chooserOf(hostId)`, keyed on the HOST ID, so a taskbar rebuild under the pointer — a tab switch changes the structure key — does not orphan it). **A rebuild RE-ANCHORS an open chooser** (verify r1 low ②: a tab title change re-keys the structure and used to leave the chooser on a detached button — the rebuilt one said `aria-expanded="false"`, Esc dropped the focus on body, its mousedown counted as "a click elsewhere" and closed + re-created the chooser): `_buildGroupItem` calls `_chooserOf(hostId)?._chooser.reanchor(item)` — `state.anchor` = the new button, `aria-expanded="true"` on it, the button pushed onto the outside-click close's LIVE exclusion list (`pop._closeExclude`); Esc focus, the cleanup's `aria-expanded` reset and the placement read `state.anchor`, never the `anchor` captured at open. **Right-click on a ROW = THAT tab's window menu** (verify r1 low ④; the window list's row pattern): `preventDefault`, the chooser PINNED beneath (the pointer leaves it for the menu), `showWindowContextMenu(app, tid, …, {onAction})` — after the action `relist()` re-opens it from the LIVE chain on the live anchor (closed when the group is gone from this host; a Move closes it), and the cleanup leaves `aria-expanded` true when a re-list already opened the next chooser on the same button. Rows are `role=menuitem` `tabIndex -1` (`.active` + `aria-current` on the tab on show, a 2 px accent inset; `:focus-visible` = accent-dim); the popover's keydown = ArrowUp/Down wrap, Home/End, Enter/Space, Esc (focus back to the button, stopPropagation). A document CAPTURE keydown on an AbortController closes it on Esc wherever the keyboard is — also inside a terminal, where the global Esc handler stands aside — never swallowing the key. ONE cleanup whichever path removed it (a row, Esc, the outside mousedown of attachPopoverClose, the leave timer, the dedup, an activation): a MutationObserver on the popover's parent aborts the controller, ALSO aborts createPopover's outside-click close (`pop._closeCtl` — verify r1: a hover chooser opens and closes with no click, so without it every cycle left one document mousedown listener holding its detached chooser, 3 → 33 over 30 hovers), clears the timer and resets `aria-expanded`. `attachPopoverClose` (utils.js) owns that listener for every popover: an AbortController as `popover._closeCtl` (also returned as a disposer; a dispose before the 0 ms arm means it is never added), a listener that finds its popover already gone aborts itself; `popover._closeExclude` is the LIVE exclusion list (the anchors given at open; an owner that rebuilds its anchor pushes the new one). Placement: above the button (below when there is no room), measured in VIEWPORT px and written in LAYOUT px (÷ `uiScale()`; before lane K it wrote viewport px, off its button under a 125 % UI scale — `showWindowList` still does, untouched here).

**2.369.182 integration (× split tabs v2):** the chooser's rows follow the group's STRIP — `visualTabOrder(chain)` (a split's left half, then its right; a reordered strip its own order), the active row marked by window id, never the chain's internal `tabs` array.

A window the wire never listed there (moved / opened here, unsent) stays. **A HELD RECORD IS A VIEW; A WRITE MERGES (userW inc-mun7qjmw-iksh, 2026-09-29).** `_savedStates` (desktop → held record) is the server's record plus what this page has built; its ONE writer is `_setRecord`, every call handing it a wire record (boot, `cacheRemoteState` / `cacheShownState` minus held closes, `noteSent`) or a PURE `mergeDesktopRecord` result (src/lib/desktop-record.js) — census in scripts/test-desktop-record.mjs §5 (and test-record-clear-census H2b classifies the same calls for words). `recordFor(d)` = what the page WRITES for d: held ∪ `layoutManager.captureWindows(d)` − `_unbuilt` (a window in `_buildAttempts` still absent 20 s after the attempt: boot restore, `_replayMissing` = switchTo step 6 + a refused record's reconcile, the Stage's leave, a remote apply's creates; no openSpec ⇒ at once) − windows the page holds on another desktop; current global chrome; the grid only for the desktop on show; no `updatedAt`. `moveWindowToDesktop(winId, d, {speak, replaces})` → `_updateCachedDesktop(d, {from, ids, replaces})`: the target ADDS the moved chain's `captureWin` entries (and drops `replaces` — resume placement's old never-opened entry), the source drops them, a desktop not on show is marked in `_dirtyDesks` (so is one that listed a window a USER closed — `purgeClosedWindow`, not under `lm._restoring`) and `layout.js _doAutoSave` sends it from `recordFor` (`takeDirty`), first, then the desktop on show. `_departed` = the evidence ledger (`closed` / `moved` / `replaced` / `unbuilt`, 10 min, ≤ 200) every layout-sync carries (`evidence()`); `onSyncRefused` = the reconcile of the server's shrink belt (kb-design-lessons §6b item 8). ### src/lib/layout.js — PENDING CHAINS WAIT FOR THEIR LAST MEMBER (lane split-restore-hidden, 2026-10-05)
`_queueChain(key, tc, { desk })` is the ONE door every restore of a tab chain goes through: the remote apply (per record desktop — a newer record of a desktop supersedes only ITS pending chains), the boot restore and a desktop's first visit after a reload (`queueRecordChains`, called by desktop-manager `_replayMissing` — before this lane that door never rebuilt chains at all). An entry waits for its LAST member for the whole life of the page; `onWindowCreated` (WindowManager.createWindow, and restoreState's re-key) settles the queue in a microtask — there is no timer and no deadline. The verdict is chain-layout's PURE `restoreVerdict` (wait / restore whole / drop). An entry ends when rebuilt, when a member was grouped by the user since (`_chainAt` newer than the entry), or shrinks when desktop-manager `recordFor` drops an unbuilt member (`dropUnbuiltMembers`). While it waits, `captureWindows` writes the record's chain for its present members (`pendingChainOf`) — never a flat member.

### src/lib/layout.js — INBOUND RECORDS: deferred per desktop, a reconnect re-reads (lane desktop-move verify r1, 2026-09-29)

`_pendingRemote` is a Map desktopId → the latest record deferred under a gate — the pointer down (§6b guard 3) or `_restoring` (the apply's 1 s cooldown, the boot's 5 s); `_deferRemote` / `_drainDeferred` (one record per tick, lowest seq first, each only when neither gate is up; the pointerup drains via `_flushPending` 300 ms later) — a record is NEVER dropped (one slot for every desktop lost the target's record of a move; a record under `_restoring` was dropped outright — the lane's ①). `_connects` counts the socket's opens: every open but the first schedules `_resyncFromServer` 250 ms later (the sends queued during the outage leave first), which reads `/api/layouts` and feeds each desktop's record through the same inbound path as a broadcast (`resync: true` ⇒ `_applyRemoteState(state, {closeOnlyWired: true})`: the desktop on show closes only a window `desktopManager.wireListed` — a window the wire never listed is this client's own unsent change); the others are cached; the meta follows. Gates: test-desktop-record §4 i / k + controls one-slot / no-resync; test-desktop-move G / H. **THE HELD MOVE (verify r2, 2026-09-30):** every inbound record is stamped `receivedAt` when it lands (before any gate; the re-read stamps at its answer) and `moveWindowToDesktop` stamps every member `_movedAt`; the apply's update loop / close loop and `cacheRemoteState`'s gone sweep skip a window with `_movedAt >= receivedAt` (a record cannot know a move made after it arrived — r1's move-in put a window the user had just dropped on HR's preview back on Fin, and the apply's dirty clear swallowed the move's save), and `_resendHeldMove` sends the move once as the user's own act (`_movesSentAt` = moves a save already carried). Gates: test-desktop-record §4 o + control no-held-move; test-desktop-move J. **THE HELD GEOMETRY (verify r2 ⑩):** window.js stamps `win._boundsAt` at the drag's and the resize's pointerup; the apply's update loop keeps the user's box / maximize / minimize / snap over a record received before it (`heldGeom`), applies the rest, and the same re-send carries the act (test-desktop-record §4 v + control no-held-geometry; test-desktop-move M). **A record judges its own desktop's chains only (verify r2 ③):** the apply's "break local chains not in remote" loop skips a host on another desktop — it used to break every hidden desktop's tab group on every save of the shown desktop by another client (test-desktop-record §4 p + control chain-any-desktop; test-desktop-move K). **The re-read vs a record still deferred (verify r2 ⑤):** `_resyncFromServer` remembers when it asked — a deferred record received before that is dropped (or replaced), never drained over the fresh one; a broadcast received while the read was in flight stays and supersedes the read's record for that desktop (test-desktop-record §4 r + control resync-keeps-stale). **A failed re-read is retried (verify r2 ⑥):** `RESYNC_RETRIES` (3) × `RESYNC_RETRY_MS` (1.5 s, × the attempt); a non-OK status is a failure; the last failure is said (`layout-resync-failed`) — one silent try left the page on the stale base its next save wrote back (test-desktop-record §4 s + control resync-no-retry). Verify r3: `_applying` (the apply's synchronous span — what refuses a held close / a dirty desk; `_restoring` is only the cooldown gate for the apply's timers) + `_deferSave` (a user-caused save under a gate deferred 1.1 s, re-armed at the act's real time if an apply cleared the dirty bit and no save left since, `_savedAt`); the re-read's `receivedAt = min(startedAt, _movesSentAt ?? 0)` with `_movesSentAt` stamped only on an open socket; `_resyncStale` / `_resyncing` (a failed re-read holds every save, re-asks the read single-flight, one toast, released on success); window.js stamps `_boundsAt` only after the drag threshold / behind `resized`. **Verify r4 (2026-09-30):** `actHeld(t, receivedAt)` is the ONE question for every witness (`_movedAt` / `_boundsAt`): held when the record landed before the act OR while no save has carried the act (`t > _movesSentAt`), bounded by `ACT_HOLD_MS` (60 s) — asked at the apply's update loop, close loop, the held geometry and `cacheRemoteState`'s sweep (a record received in the 500 ms debounce / the cooldown after a drop or a drag used to undo it and swallow or overwrite its save; a peer saving every 400 ms undid every act); `_expiredHeldActs()` at the stale release counts the held acts past their hold before the applies prune them, one toast names the count (the page follows the server). Gates: test-desktop-record ua/ub/uc/st2 + controls unsaved-act-reverted / stale-release-untold.

**THE ACK (verify r5 ⑤).** `noteLayoutSent(desks, sentAt)` (every `layout-sync` the autosave or the switch's broadcast sends carries `sentAt`; one owed answer per desktop record) → `_onLayoutAnswer(desk, sentAt, {refused})` on `layout-sync-ack` / `layout-sync-refused` → `_settleSave` once every record is answered: `_markCarried(desk, sentAt)` stamps `_carried` (per desktop; `_carriedAt(desk)` is what `actHeld(t, receivedAt, win)`, `_resendHeldMove` and `_expiredHeldActs` read), releases that desktop's held closes up to `sentAt` and its divider ratios, and tells the desktop manager (`noteCarried` — a dirty desk stays dirty until then; `takeDirty` no longer clears). A refused desktop is carried by nothing. `_movesSentAt` (the re-read's horizon) = the time an acked save LEFT (`s.at`). A socket that dies (`onStateChange(false)`) drops the owed saves that had left and resets `_lastSentJson`; a save queued while down (`at` null) keeps its clock for the open. The old-server fallback: `_sweepUnacked` (500 ms while anything is owed) settles a save ACK_WAIT_MS (2 s) after it left on an open socket while `_serverAcks` is false — set by the first ack ever seen, never reset. The no-op guard in `_doAutoSave` skips a text identical to the last sent only when nothing is owed for that desktop.

**PURE (imports nothing; CJS) — THE STAGE'S MOVE RULE, SPOKEN (inc-muly2izg-cks3, 2026-09-28).** The rule is the owner's 2.112.4 directive and STAYS: no window moves between the Stage and a normal desktop, in either direction. What was wrong was the silence (the drag over a preview did not light up, the drop did nothing, "Move to Desktop ▸" listed desktops whose rows did nothing — the no-silent-failures law). `stageWindowKind(facts, stageId)` → 'placeholder' | 'session' (chat/terminal) | 'window' | null; `stageMoveVerdict({kind, targetId, stageId})` → `{ok:true}` | `{ok:true, same:true}` (a Stage window aimed at the Stage — no move, no words) | `{ok:false, code:'stage-window', kind}` | `{ok:false, code:'onto-stage'}`; `stageRefusalWords(v, {t})` → `{line, next}` (every string through the injected t; zh/ja in the dicts), `stageRefusalSentence` = "<line> — <next>". Readers: stage-manager (`windowKind` / `moveVerdict`), desktop-manager (`sayStageRefusal`, the menu row), window.js (the preview mark `.stage-refuse` + the pointer label `.stage-refuse-label`, kept inside the viewport — the previews sit on a bar at a screen edge; a refused drop = `_putBackAfterRefusedDrop` to where the drag began, re-maximized when it was, + the toast; no snap zone promised under a refusal). Gate: test-stage-rules (fast, 49 — PURE tables, i18n, the real StageManager + DesktopManager over a fake app, the wiring of every door, three patched-copy controls) + heavy test-stage-dragout-ui ⑤. **Verify r1 of inc-munl8jkl-gaih (2026-09-30): `carriedGeometry(facts)`** = the box a window carries into its replacement (session-lifecycle `_snapshotWinBounds`: the hero's own Resume, a billing switch, a restart) — a window borrowed by the Stage (`onStage`) carries its remembered HOME (`stageHomeBounds`, maximized per `stageHomeMax`), never the slot its element sits at (read off the element, the slot became the resumed conversation's home and every client's record of its desktop took it); no remembered home ⇒ no box (a cascade box at the next borrow); the box is a copy. ### session-palette.js

    session-palette.js — Ctrl+K session palette (fuzzy session switcher; installSessionPalette, desktop only). **SEARCH IS TOKENISED (2.249.1, userW inc-msjro90z-n6y3 — never regress to whole-query matching):** the query splits on whitespace with AND semantics; NAME hits (1000-pos) outrank path/host/id hits (300) outrank a fuzzy subsequence (100) CONFINED TO THE NAME. Matching the query as ONE literal string meant a space could never substring-hit a CamelCase/hyphenated name ("best ever" vs "BestEver-ToB-signing"), so EVERY multi-word query fell through to a subsequence over the whole haystack (name + cwd + 3 UUIDs) — a shared cwd prefix supplies almost any letter sequence, so unrelated sessions all tied at the same low score. Compounding it, the live bonus was `+1000` on that tie, sorting every live session above every stopped one, and `slice(0,12)` cut the list before the wanted STOPPED session could appear. Ranking is now `sc*1000 + (live?500:0)` — match quality dominates, live only breaks ties among equally-good matches. Fuzzy-matching against a UUID is pure noise; never re-add it. Test: scripts/test-session-palette-search.mjs (11 asserts on the real reported data).

  src/collab-row.js — the label/HTML builder for codex multi-agent collab rows. PURE tier, **zero requires** (CJS pulled into the bundle like ssh-key-format.js): the escaper, the translator and the icon set are INJECTED. That is not ceremony — it makes the XSS rule *verifiable*: scripts/test-codex-subagents ① passes a MARKER escaper and asserts that nothing outside the markers is model-controlled, then repeats with the real `escHtml` semantics. `collabRowParts` splits a row into `{pre, name, post}` so the plain-text label (which lands in the message's `tool_result` output → search previews, fold summaries, the minimap) and the HTML row can never drift; `collabRowsHtml` renders one row or the coalesced summary + one clickable chip per agent; `collabRowTitle` is the hover envelope and says *payload encrypted upstream* when the body was withheld. A row NEVER carries an encrypted blob. The default translator substitutes `{n}` so server-side text is complete without a client `t()`. **LIVE PROGRESS READOUT (2026-09-07, owner: “这种互聊如果连续发生是不是应该界面里展示下连续数量，这样我好知道对话没卡住”):** dozens of ENCRYPTED one-line rows over minutes with no assistant text between them are indistinguishable from a wedged turn, so the module gained the composers every progress surface reads — `collabTrafficStats` (count / distinct agents / first+last row `ts` / `messagesOnly`, i.e. every row is mail vs a mixed set that must say “sub-agent events”), `collabAgeText` (1s granularity under a minute, whole FLOORED minutes above — “is it moving”, not a stopwatch), `collabSpanText` (“4 min 12 s”), `collabCountParts` (REAL singular keys — never “1 messages”), `collabHeadText`, `collabRunPart` (the run-label segment) and `subAgentStreamLabel` (the spinner line). NOTHING is stored and nothing is counted into a field: every number is derived from the rows the normalizer already stamped, so a second client renders identical text off the same message state. LIVE and FROZEN differ ONLY in the last segment — a ticking `last {age} ago` while the turn runs, the absolute `over {span}` once it stops — and a row with no usable `ts` DROPS the segment rather than inventing a clock (never “over 0 s”). `collabRowsHtml` puts the head in its OWN `.chat-collab-head` element so the view's single ticker rewrites just that text (re-rendering the card would drop the fold state the user opened), and a LONE row still renders its full `agent · TYPE` label — summarising one event only loses information, and the owner's ask is about CONTINUOUS chatter, which is the coalesced shape by construction. `collabSummaryText` (the stored `tool_result` output that search previews and the minimap read) is the SAME composer in its frozen form, so the words on screen and the words in the index cannot drift. `collabRowTitle` now leads with `Time: <clock> (record timestamp|arrival time)`: the normalizer's `_stampRowTime` takes the RECORD's own timestamp when it has one (`recordTs`, which returns null instead of `toTs`'s silent `Date.now()`) and the arrival time otherwise — saying WHICH is the point, or a burst replayed from a rebuild would read as “just now”. **THREE SURFACES = THREE SCOPES (2026-09-07 r2, and they are MEANT to differ):** `collabHeadText` counts ONE coalesced card, `collabRunPart` the folded RUN, `subAgentStreamLabel` the whole TURN — a card that stopped growing at 4 events sits inside a run of 5 while the spinner counts the turn's 5, so all three are honest and only the one that floats FREE of the thing it counts has to say which scope it means (“Sub-agents working — 5 sub-agent events **this turn**, last 4s ago”); the other two are read inside their own container. Do not "fix" the divergence by making the card head turn-scoped — two cards would then both claim the turn's total. Gate: scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs ①②.

Gates: test-reattach-stagger (fast) + test-reattach-stagger-ui (heavy) ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants.md.
  chat-view.js — **perf r1: THE RESUME WATERMARK MEANS APPLIED, NOT RECEIVED.** `_onOp` advances `_lastSeq`/`_seqEpoch` only AFTER the op ran; an op that THROWS (a renderer exception — ws.js's per-handler isolation reports it and delivery goes on) sets `_seqPoisoned` and the watermark stays where the last fully-applied prefix ended (later ops still render — they are real — but never advance it). `_applyHeldResume` counts `failed` and does not stamp the replay's `opSeq` while poisoned. `_reattach` omits `sinceSeq`/`sinceEpoch` while poisoned (the server answers the full rung), and the same-epoch full-rung handler of a POISONED view rebuilds from the payload's slab (`_fullViewReset`, trace `reattach:heal`) — a catch-up from `_windowEnd` cannot reach the lost card, the live creates after it moved `_windowEnd` past it. `_fullViewReset` clears the flag only after `loadHistory` ran through (a rebuild that throws on the same card stays poisoned; no self-triggered retry loop — the next attach heals). The verifier's probe: a create throwing once for one burst id inside a 23-op held replay left the view one card short for the life of the epoch (the second held resume replayed []). **Also perf r1: every attach frame the view sends carries `slab` = `_attachSlabHint()` (view-visibility's `attachSlab` over `_suspended` and `ws.attachesInFlight()`).** Gate: test-hidden-view-suspend §7/§8 (fake ws: slab per state; the live throw ⇒ no sinceSeq; the held throw ⇒ 22/23 rendered, watermark not stamped, no sinceSeq, the full rung ⇒ `_fullViewReset` not a catch-up, the heal ⇒ resume by seq again; a clean-replay control).
  chat-view.js — **2.369.167 (perf lane D): RESUME BY SEQ.** `_onOp` records `_lastSeq = op.seq` and `_seqEpoch = this._normEpoch` for every stamped op. `_applyLiveMeta` (carries-the-key) adopts `opSeq`: `_serverOpSeq` = the server stamps; on a SLAB payload `_lastSeq = opSeq` unless the same epoch already holds a larger one (a delayed `_fullViewReset` must not rewind past live ops that landed during its 0–500 ms jitter), re-anchored on a new epoch; a HELD payload leaves the position to its replay. `_reattach` builds ONE `attachFrame` — `{sinceSeq: _lastSeq, sinceEpoch: _seqEpoch}` only when `_serverOpSeq` is known (an old server never gets asked) — and the retry ladder re-sends that same frame. In its `attached` handler, after the epoch-changed branch (unchanged: jittered `_fullViewReset`), `slab:'held'` ⇒ `_applyHeldResume(msg)`: chatStatus + `_applyLiveMeta` + the replay through `_onOp` SYNCHRONOUSLY (a frame with seq ≤ the view's last in the same epoch is skipped — a create would dedup anyway but `_noteRecordKind` would count it twice), trace `reattach:held {applied, skipped, opSeq}`, the streaming label; no loadHistory, no identical compare, no `_reattachCatchUp`. Any other same-epoch reply = today's path (`_applyLiveMeta` + `_reattachCatchUp`). `lagged` (permanent handler) ⇒ `_onLagged`: trace `lagged {lagSeq, have}` (never a `seq` key — it would overwrite the trace ring's own), client event `chat-lagged`, `_reattach(false)` unless offline/read-only/disposed. The 2.322.0 stall watchdog's `_reattach()` resumes by seq through the same frame.
  ws.js — **2.369.167 (perf lane D): `wireText(d)` adds `caps:['op-seq']` to every `attach` at the wire** (`send` AND `request`'s pending-dedup compare the same text, so a resend is never doubled); `__vsAttachFrames` entries gain `slab` (a `messages` array was present), `held`, `replay` (ops count). **perf r1: `attachesInFlight(now)` — the count of attaches this socket sent (or queued) that no `attached`/`error` for that sessionId has answered, an entry older than 15 s no longer counting; cleared on a drop (an unanswered attach on a dead socket is not in flight on the next). The 2.369.36 form (`rendered < 30`) was UNSATISFIABLE — every attach ships tail(50) and folding hides members without removing them, so the rescue was dead code; both timers clear in dispose(). Because chat-view.js is DOM-free at import, the predicate + schedule are FUNCTIONALLY tested against fake geometry in scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs. A Read is 'image' only when its RESULT carried image blocks (`content[0].images`) — EVIDENCE, never the extension (image-card review round 2: 12/12 real `Read *.svg` results in the fleet are numbered TEXT, and an extension rule both mis-counted them and let them escape the fold); codex/ACP arrive with `collapseKind` stamped. **THE IMAGE MEMBER IS EXEMPT FROM THE FOLD, NOT THE RUN (2.369.43 → image-card review round 2):** 'image' ships ON in the default kinds and the "any tool card folds, even a lone one" rule applied to it too, so every media card landed inside "1 image read" — `display:none`, invisible until clicked, and its `loading="lazy"` thumbnail never even fetched (the owner asked to SEE the image). The first cut exempted whole runs made ONLY of image views, which is the RARE shape — in real sessions the card sits BETWEEN foldable cards (Bash → Read(png) → Bash) and stayed hidden. So `flush()` computes `run.inline` = the image-kind members: they stay members of the run for every other purpose (rail, first/last, sticky mark, the floating bar's span, the summary's "N image reads") but `_setRunOpen` never gives them `.chat-run-collapsed`, so the fold closes AROUND them. A run with nothing left to fold (every member an image) gets no header at all — a fold control that hides nothing is a dead control. Pinned by test-image-cards ⑦ + the test-fold-ux browser fixture (bash|image|bash: the media card's computed display is not 'none' and its `<img>` really loads, while the Bash cards fold under the header). MEDIA THUMBNAILS: the list carries a CAPTURE-phase `error` delegate (img error does not bubble) that flags a broken `.chat-tool-img`'s `.chat-media` as `.chat-media-broken` (CSS swaps the img for the honest line) — rendered HTML never carries inline handlers; the fold's `display:none` is what keeps `loading="lazy"` thumbnails of a collapsed run from fetching. **COLLAB CLICK-THROUGH (B-7473):** a message carrying `collab` renders through chat-renderers `_renderCollabMsg` (report card / compact rows, src/collab-row.js does the escaping); the agent NAME (`.chat-collab-name`, data-agent-path + data-thread-id) is delegated in the messageList click handler to `_openCollabAgent`, which opens the child's rollout in the EXISTING sub-agent viewer when the thread id is known (0.153.4 always knows it — SubAgentActivity.agent_thread_id) and otherwise asks `GET /api/subagents?backend=codex&threadId=<root>` and TOASTS when the child is not on this machine (never a silent no-op). The run header gains `{n} sub-agent messages` (counting `collab.rows[].dir === 'in'`) and a `{n} sub-agents: …` chip list built from the run's rows — those chips get their OWN onclick with `stopPropagation()`, because the header's click toggles the fold, and they de-duplicate on `row.agentPath`, which the normalizer normalises to an ABSOLUTE path for every direction (round-5 fix: outbound rows keyed the bare `task_name` and one agent drew two chips). **The two B-7473 summary lines live in the PURE module like every other line (integration 2026-09-06 + round-5 rebase):** `'report'` — a sub-agent's written answer — is a REAL fold kind in `RUN_KINDS`/`SUMMARY_ORDER` (offered in `chat.collapseKinds` but shipping UNCHECKED, because a report is the content the window was opened to read; the one-line rows stay `'agent'`, which IS default-on), and the inbound-message count is `SUMMARY_EXTRAS = ['subAgentIn']` — a count the CALLER assigns into `byKind` (never produced by `messageKind`, never zero-filled, so an unset one renders nothing and can never go NaN) whose position in the label is decided by the same single `SUMMARY_ORDER`. chat-view NEVER keeps a second kind table. **THE QUEUE CHIP'S CAPABILITY ARRIVES AFTER THE PIXELS (2026-09-06, round-3 review):** the chip on a user bubble is built by `renderUserMsg`, which asks the view (`getQueueCaps` → `_queueCaps()` = harness `inputModes` ∧ the RUNNING wrapper's `_queueSupported`) and hands `applyQueueChip` a null handler when the answer is no — which renders it `disabled`. `_queueSupported` starts FALSE and BOTH of its sources land AFTER the bubbles: `loadHistory` renders every message and calls `_applyLiveMeta` (the attach payload's `queueSupported`) at the END, and a live wrapper's baseline `queue_changed` (`_onMeta` subtype 'queue', `supported:true`) arrives frames after the first messages. So after ANY history load the chip was permanently dead. `_setQueueSupported` is therefore the ONE writer of the flag and a change in EITHER direction schedules `_refreshQueueChips()` — rAF-coalesced, ONE pass over `_elements`, re-running `ChatRenderers.applyQueueChip` for every rendered message that carries a `queueState` (false→true makes them live, true→false makes them inert; the pending frame is cancelled in dispose()). The queue STRIP never had this bug because `_setQueue` re-renders it — the chips live inside bubbles nobody rebuilds. Gate: test-queue-steer ⑦ (render-then-deliver for both messengers + the reverse flip + a one-writer pin). **AUTO-SCROLL IS AUTOMATIC REPOSITIONING, AND IT MUST LOSE TO THE READER (B-9702, round 5 of the desktop-resume campaign):** `_forceScrollToBottom` writes `scrollTop = scrollHeight` for up to 10 frames (~166 ms) under the `_programmaticScroll` mute — the pinned view's auto-follow AND what every resume re-tail rung calls. It now carries an EPOCH: `_cancelForcedScroll(via)` bumps it and is called from `_notePositioning` and `_noteUserNav` (never from `_noteUserInput` — a click moves nothing), so every frame already queued is orphaned instead of writing scrollTop once more, while a later `_forceScrollToBottom` starts a fresh epoch so a cancel can never kill auto-follow. The mute is released ONE FRAME after the final write, guarded on `_fsbActive`: a scroll event is delivered after the callback that wrote it, so clearing the flag in the write's own frame handed our displacement to the boundary decision as if a reader had produced it. Without both, a re-tail rung armed at resume+1240 ms was still writing when the reader wheeled up at +1400 ms, its last frame landed 3 ms after their scroll, the pin re-engaged off our own write (`repin st:1760 … fsb:-1 posAgo:3` — ordinary geometry, `collapsedGeomSkip` never fired) and `_extendTop`'s pinned-tail invariant re-asserted the bottom: 5 of 20 real wheel-ups undone, 0 of 20 after. The `repin` trace (the twin of `unpin`) is what named it and stays. Gates: scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs (DOM-free chain semantics against a fake rAF queue, including the "auto-follow survives a cancel" and "the mute is never permanent" controls) + the two +1400 ms wheel legs in scripts/test-desktop-resume-paging.mjs (the second arms a chain by hand for determinism, with `_cancelForcedScroll` neutered on the instance as its control). **LIVE SUB-AGENT TRAFFIC (2026-09-07, the same owner ask):** three surfaces read the ONE composer over three SCOPES — card / run / turn (they can legitimately show different numbers at the same instant; see collab-row.js, where the free-floating one names its scope). (i) the coalesced card's head — the renderer asks the view `isCollabLive(msg)` → `_liveCollabId()`, which is the LAST message and only while `_typingSince` is set (a view-only window has no live turn, so a stopped transcript is always frozen; the moment anything else arrives the burst is over and the card freezes). (ii) the run header / footer / floating bar — `flush()` computes `collabStats` over the run's `collab.rows` and captures `mkLabel({now, live})`, a CLOSURE over that run's own counts, so the per-second repaint re-asks the ONE composer (`runSummaryLabel` gained a PRE-COMPOSED `collabPart` string — words from src/collab-row.js, POSITION from chat-run-summary.js, which still imports nothing) instead of rebuilding a second kind table; the “{n} sub-agents” text moved OUT of `chat-run-agents` into the label so the floating bar and the footer carry it too and the header never says it twice, leaving only the clickable chips there — with an explicit ` · ` in front of them (r2: dropping the old “{n} sub-agents:” colon glued the count to the names, “2 sub-agent events water_research” read as one phrase). (iii) the spinner line — `_noteRecordKind` (called from `_onOp` AFTER the message is applied, so a coalescing edit carries the grown rows) records whether the newest typed record was collab traffic, and `_applyStreamLabel` shows `subAgentStreamLabel(_liveCollabStats())` — TURN-scoped, because a report card between two coalesced cards would restart a per-card count mid-burst. THE SERVER STAYS THE LABEL AUTHORITY: `_onServerStreamLabel` is the one place that remembers the broadcast label/kind (all three call sites — the `streaming-label` frame, the attach meta, the reattach reply — go through it), and the override yields back ONLY what it took (`_collabLabelShown`); re-asserting the remembered label on every op would fight the label ChatInput sets locally on send and a stale “running Bash” from the previous turn would win. THE TICKER: ONE `setInterval(1000)` per ChatView, created lazily on the first collab record, bound to `winInfo._listenerCtl.signal` ('abort' → `_stopCollabTick`) and cleared in `dispose()` — a per-message interval over a fifty-row burst is fifty timers nobody cancels. It is a NO-OP while `_suspended` (a hidden window's ages are unread; `setSuspended(false)` runs one tick so the first frame back is right), it writes ONLY `textContent` into the head / header / footer / bar (never `_extendTop`/`_trim*`/`_pinned`/`scrollTop` — the suite greps its body), and it FREEZES every card the traffic has moved past exactly once (`_freezeStaleHeads(liveId, now)`). `_hideTyping` → `_freezeCollab()`: turn end stops the ticker and repaints every surface in its absolute-span form, because a ticking age on a finished turn reads as progress. **THE FREEZE MUST NOT DEPEND ON THE TICKER HAVING PAINTED (r2 MAJOR, reproduced 2/2):** the first cut repainted only the card the TICKER had last touched, and a burst that starts AND ends while the window is hidden (desktop switch — start an orchestration, switch desktop, come back) never ticks at all, while the RENDERER keeps painting each coalescing edit with a live age; the card then read “last 0s ago” on a turn that had ended minutes ago, contradicting the run header beside it (whose liveness IS captured in the fold pass, which runs while hidden). So the authority is a SET: `_noteCollabHeadPainted` (the renderer's `isCollabLive` hook returns its answer through it, and every `_paintCollabHead` keeps it honest — a card trimmed out of the window just leaves) and `_freezeStaleHeads(liveId|null, now)` walks it, from the tick AND from the freeze. ARMING: `_startCollabTick` is gated on `_liveCollabId()` (a claude session must not carry an interval at all) and paints ONCE immediately — `loadHistory` renders every card BEFORE `_showTyping` runs, so a window attached mid-burst would otherwise sit on the frozen span; `_onServerStreamLabel` is the event that finally makes liveness answerable, so it arms the ticker too (attaching to a STALLED turn is precisely the case the readout exists for). Gate: scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs (node composers + wiring pins, then a REAL codex rollout opened read-only and a LIVE codex chat session driven by a stub app-server through the real wrapper → real normalizer → real ws push; the stub is a reminder that a faithful fixture matters twice over — its blobs must differ inside the normalizer's 32-char fernet discriminator or the dedup silently collapses the burst, and a `commandExecution` needs its `item/started` or the wrapper records only an OUTPUT and the card falls to the unknown-tool 'mcp' kind). **THE STEER CHORD'S VIEW HALF (2026-09-07 + round-2 verifier):** `_canSteerComposer()`/`steerComposerText()` are what the contributed command `chat.steerNow` runs (see contributions.js), and `_steerAfterSend(msgId)` is its second half — a steer NAMES A QUEUED ITEM, so the chord sends on the ordinary path and this parks the msgId in a MAP until `_setQueue` drains it into the SAME `queue-op` frame the strip and the chip send. Its 8s timeout is the no-silent-failure half, and the guard that keeps it from CRYING WOLF is a TURN IDENTITY, not a flag: `_showTyping` stamps `_turnEpoch` on the same null→armed transition that sets `_typingSince`, `_steerAfterSend` captures it, and the timeout speaks only if that SAME epoch is still running. Testing `_typingSince` for truthiness (the shipped first cut) was false exactly where it mattered — the only shape that lets the timer fire is a NOT-busy wrapper running the message as its own `turn/start`, which re-arms the flag — so the window apologised for a message the agent was visibly running. `_typingSince` is a TIME and a time is not an identity (two turns can arm in the same millisecond); the epoch advances only where the flag arms, so a relabelled turn is still the same turn. Gate: test-queue-steer ⑨c drives the real `_hideTyping()`→`_showTyping()` sequence (a hand-set `_typingSince: null` fixture cannot occur on that path) with the old predicate's value asserted as the negative control. **2.369.112 the HIDDEN-REASON SET (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq): `setHidden(reason, on)` — mobile / tab / minimized / desktop compose, `_suspended` is DERIVED (`_applySuspend` holds the pin snapshot + settle + re-tail), `setSuspended(on)` = the desktop reason (desktop-manager / stage-manager untouched); a hider never writes the flag. `_applyElementMarks` ①b: a compaction summary user record (`isCompactSummaryText`) resolves the "Prompt is too long" cards before it in time (inc-mu6btbfr-uaxg). **PAGING INTENT — ONE PREDICATE (inc-mtq5bpjt-0o0n, after 2.369.42).** Every AUTOMATIC upward-paging trigger asks `_autoPagingBlocked()` and gets a REASON back (`disposed / suspended / resume-settle / pinned / settling / no-input / input-resize`) — the scroll handler's laws, in ONE place. Its callers: the gap sentinel's `IntersectionObserver` (`_observeHistoryGap` → `_loadEarlierGap(el, null, {via:'io'})`) and the scroll/wheel-driven `_maybeSeekEarlier` — the gate itself lives INSIDE `_loadEarlierGap` (chat-view-seek.js), i.e. on the path that is alive in the failure state, and traces `gapSkip {why, via}`; an explicit retry CLICK passes `{auto:false}` and bypasses it. Before this, `_loadEarlierGap`'s tail-mode branch (`!teleported && windowStart>0 ⇒ _extendTop()`) was the ONE upward-paging entry point with no gate at all, and an IntersectionObserver is PURE GEOMETRY — it needs no event, so a desktop resume's re-measure (scrollTop momentarily 0 while pinned) paged three pinned windows into history. **A new automatic paging trigger routes through this predicate; a new DIRECT `_extendTop()` call site must justify why it is user intent.**

**RESUME SETTLE + THE PINNED-TAIL INVARIANT (same incident).** `setSuspended(false)` arms `_resumeSettleUntil` (`RESUME_SETTLE_MS` 1200 ms) on top of the 2.369.1 `_lastStructuralAt` stamp: while it is open the scroll handler no-ops BEFORE it touches the pin (transitional geometry must not unpin either), `_autoPagingBlocked` says `resume-settle`, the loadHistory auto-fill DEFERS with bounded re-arms instead of deciding, and the pinned re-tail runs again when it expires (`_resumeSettleTimer`, cleared in `dispose()`). The window is armed as `RESUME_SETTLE_MS + RESUME_RETAIL_SLACK_MS` (40 ms) so it ENDS at the re-tail — the 40 ms gap between expiry and re-tail was itself a door (an input-less `scrollTop = 0` landing there unpinned the window and the re-tail, asserting on the live flag, then refused: stranded in history) — and the re-tail asserts on `_pinnedAtSuspend`, the pin SNAPSHOT taken by `setSuspended(true)` before the geometry starts lying, restoring `_pinned` itself when it acts off it. Real user input (wheel/touchmove/pointerdown/keydown) calls `_endResumeSettle()` — settle AND snapshot — so the settle suppresses input-LESS displacement only, never a reader. And the invariant the trim broke: **a PINNED view never loses its tail** — `_extendTop` skips `_trimBottom()` while `_pinned` (traced `trimSkipPinned`) and re-asserts the bottom after the prepend (`pinnedRetail`), because under transitional geometry the element anchor fails (`anchored:false`) and the delta fallback clamps scrollTop to 0. DOM growth stays bounded: the live-append path trims the TOP while pinned, and the next genuine (unpinned) page-up trims normally. Pins: scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs (source pins + a FUNCTIONAL hide→show unit: a transitional unpin still re-tails, a real reader is left alone) + the end-to-end scripts/test-desktop-resume-paging.mjs (real >34MB transcript, real desktop switch, a resume+1210 ms input-less injection, source-level negative control).

**ROUND 2 — THE TWO HOLES THE SETTLE LEFT (same incident).** ① *The re-tail was blind to readers who navigate.* Only the FOUR message-list listeners (wheel/touchmove/pointerdown/keydown) called `_endResumeSettle()`, and the surfaces a reader actually uses to go somewhere are not on the list: the minimap's pointer events live on the CONTAINER, the floating run bar on `this._container`, and `jumpToIndex` / a search reveal touch neither — so a reader who jumped 400 ms into a resume was silently dragged back to the live tail when the re-tail fired (measured: at +2600 ms pinned at the tail again). Now every off-list positioning surface calls `_noteUserNav(via)` (stamp `_lastNavAt` + end the settle): the two minimap callbacks, `jumpToIndex`, a USER `jumpToBottom({user:true})` (the re-tail passes `user:false` so it cannot cancel its own series), `_jumpToFileTime`, `_landOnHeader` (run bar + footer) and ChatSearch's reveal through the new `onNav` callback. The re-tail captures `resumeAt` and returns when `_navigatedSince(resumeAt)` — the chat-view-seek `userScrolled = _lastUserScrollAt > max(jumpAt, revealAt)` idiom generalised over every positioning stamp we own (`_lastNavAt`, `_lastUserScrollAt`, `_lastJumpAt`, `_search._lastRevealAt`). ② *The protection was a one-shot CLIFF.* The settle ended at 1240 ms and the re-tail ran there; an input-less displacement at +1400 ms unpinned the window and stranded it (3/3 sessions — +1240/+1280 survived only because `_forceScrollToBottom`'s 10-frame chain happened to still be running). Now the re-tail is a BOUNDED SERIES (`RESUME_RETAIL_AT_MS` = [1240, 2000], `_resumeRetailTimers`, `_clearResumeRetail()` on suspend/dispose/real input) **and the UNPIN ITSELF is gated on positive evidence** like the paging triggers: `_resumeDisplacement()` = inside `RESUME_DISPLACEMENT_MS` (2800 ms — past the last rung, because the displacement the rungs cannot catch is the one that arrives between them), pin SNAPSHOT still true, and nothing the reader did has landed since ⇒ keep `_pinned`, re-assert the bottom, trace `unpinSkipResume`. A real wheel/touch/key/pointer or any nav drops the snapshot, so a reader at +1400 ms unpins and pages normally. ③ The settle return in the scroll handler moved BELOW the destructure + `_updateRunBar(scrollTop)` (next to the `_programmaticScroll` return) — the bar is a READOUT, not a decision, and returning above it froze the 2.369.45 floating run bar for the whole settle; everything below that line is a decision. WHICH guard owns which part of the horizon was MEASURED, not assumed (the chrome sweep captures per-leg traces): 1240 ms is inside the settle (the scroll handler decides nothing, the rung re-tails), 1400 ms still traces `collapsedGeomSkip` — the 2.301.0 guard owns it, because its `settling` window runs 1500 ms from the resume's structural stamp — and only at 1900/2400 ms is `unpinSkipResume` the sole thing between an input-less displacement and a stranded window. Pins: the trim-guard suite's source ORDER pin restates its budgets per segment (suspend→runBar ≤400, runBar→programmatic ≤200, programmatic→settle ≤1400, settle→atBottom ≤2400) and the chrome suite adds a nav-during-settle leg, the displacement sweep (outcome for all four offsets + the gate's own trace where it is the only guard left), a real wheel-up inside the horizon (it must page and must NOT trip the gate — its final pin state belongs to the collapsed-geometry guard, not to this fix), and a PER-MECHANISM negative control for each, neutered on the instance in the same run (the source-level control rebuilds with `RESUME_SETTLE_MS = 0` and cannot host a timing-dependent repro; its cliff leg injects at the SAME 1900 ms the fixed build passes at, because at 1400 ms the 1240 rung's own `_forceScrollToBottom` chain re-pins even with the gate off — the very accident the finding named).

**ROUND 3 — A CLICK IS NOT A POSITIONING ACT (same incident, reproduced with TRUSTED CDP input).** Every message-list listener ran the same `_endResumeSettle()`, which zeroes the settle window AND drops `_pinnedAtSuspend` AND clears the bounded re-tail series — so a plain left-click/tap anywhere in the list during the 1.24 s settle disarmed the whole repair and the resume's own input-LESS displacement then reproduced the incident BEHIND the click (measured: click at +300 ms, `scrollTop = 0` at +1400 ms → unpinned, `fromBottom 1883`). THE RULE, by grade: `_noteUserInput()` — a pointerdown, or a key that is not in `NAV_KEYS` — stamps `_lastUserScrollAt` (the paging gates' `no-input` evidence, which scrollbar and keyboard readers need) and may end the settle WINDOW, and that is ALL it does; `_notePositioning(via)` — wheel, touchmove, a navigation key (PageUp/PageDown/Home/End/Arrow*/Space), or a scrollbar drag — additionally stamps `_lastPositionAt` and runs `_endResumeSettle()` (window + snapshot + series), exactly like `_noteUserNav`'s six off-list surfaces. `_navigatedSince()` reads the POSITIONING stamps only (`_lastNavAt`, `_lastPositionAt`, `_lastJumpAt`, `_search._lastRevealAt`) and never `_lastUserScrollAt`. A SCROLLBAR DRAG has no event of its own, so it is recognised by a signature: `_pointerDragScroll(scrollTop)`, stamped in the scroll handler ABOVE the settle return (the drag must be able to end the very settle it starts inside; the order pin's budgets are now suspend→runBar ≤400, runBar→programmatic ≤200, programmatic→drag ≤700, drag→settle ≤1400, settle→atBottom ≤2400). Round 3 wrote that signature in TIME — a scroll within 400 ms of a pointerdown that moved the view by more than `POINTER_DRAG_PX` (2 px) — see ROUND 4 below for why that had to become a POSITION. The chrome suite drives all three with real `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` — a click (the repair survives it), a `mouseWheel` up (unpins immediately and pages), and a native-scrollbar drag with `.chat-minimap-active` removed first (the semantic minimap sets `scrollbar-width: none`, so a native scrollbar only exists with the minimap off — with it ON the reader drags the minimap, which is already `_noteUserNav('minimap')`), each with its own instance-level control. KNOWN RESIDUAL (round-3 MINOR, backlog B-8e5e, not fixed here): a wheel-up at resume+1400 ms pages but is re-pinned ~1/3 of the time by the collapsed-geometry `atBottom` re-pin — that flag belongs to the 2.301.0 guard, and this fix does not assert it.

**ROUND 4 — THE DRAG IS WHERE THE PRESS LANDED, NOT WHEN A SCROLL FOLLOWS (same incident, two MAJORs against round 3's own signature).** ① The 400 ms window admitted the ARTIFACT: the incident's re-measure bounces run +366…+602 ms after the switch, so a plain CONTENT click with one of them landing behind it satisfied "a scroll soon after a pointerdown that moved the view" → `_notePositioning('scrollbar-drag')` → `_endResumeSettle()` (window + snapshot + series) → the incident, reproduced behind the click. Round 3's leg passed only because it put the click at +300 ms and the displacement at +1400 ms. ② …and it EXCLUDED a real reader: a drag whose first move comes later than 400 ms after the press (press, look, then drag) was never positioning, so the re-tail series yanked that reader back to the live tail — a NEW harm versus master. NOW: `_pointerOnScrollbar(e)` hit-tests the pointerdown against the list's scrollbar GUTTER — `offsetWidth - clientWidth` minus the borders, on the right in LTR and on the LEFT in RTL, plus the bottom strip for a horizontal scrollbar — with coordinates converted viewport→LAYOUT px first (the uiScale body `zoom` scales `getBoundingClientRect`/`clientX` but NOT `clientWidth`; mixing the two spaces is the 2.369.5 VNC-pointer bug). The verdict rides `_pointerDownOnScrollbar` for the LIFETIME of the press, cleared by WINDOW-scoped `pointerup`/`pointercancel` listeners bound to `winInfo._listenerCtl.signal` (a scrollbar drag routinely releases outside the list; `dispose()` also removes them, for a view torn down while its window lives on), and `_pointerDragScroll` is "the flag is set AND the view moved > `POINTER_DRAG_PX`". `POINTER_DRAG_MS` is DELETED — a content click never becomes positioning however close a displacement lands, and a press-and-hold-then-drag is positioning for the whole press. `_pointerOnScrollbar` is DOM-free (it reads injected geometry) and unit-tested in plain node; the chrome suite adds a click-at-+300 ms/displacement-at-+450 ms leg and a press-hold-900 ms-then-drag leg, each with an instance-level control that restores the pre-fix outcome (the old time-window signature strands the window; a false hit-test yanks the slow dragger back).

**Agent browser P5 (2026-09-21):** `this._browserTrace = createCardTraceLoader(this)` is ONE loader per view; `_applyElementMarks` ③ calls `observe(el)` (the one hook every element-making path shares); BOTH `_handler`s hand `browser-trace-appended` to `onAppended`; `dispose()` disposes it — see src/lib/browser-trace-view.js.
**Lane M (2.369.182):** the message-details popover (`_showMsgMeta`) closes through utils.js `onOutsidePress(pop, remove, { nested: false })` — it was a capture-phase `mousedown`, blind to a press into an app's picture.

### chat-input.js
