INVARIANTS: a run for a sha nobody can push has no verdict to wait for; a schedule's longest job goes first or it IS the wall; a suite that claims the box runs alone on it; a signal ends a run through the same exit as a supersede, never past the closing line; an affected green is green for its push only and only for the suites it ran; "could not list the change" selects everything; a fixture the suite spawned is found by walking the suite's own pids, and the one whole-box walk that remains is a measurement. Gates: test-ci-gate §4 (the hook's range on both push shapes) + §8 (laneCount, scheduleLanes, the SERIAL rows, affectedSuites over a stub tree, changedFiles over real history, fullTierDue, the affected-green block rule), test-ci-heavy-launch (the abandoned supersede beside the live-branch control, a 3-lane vs 1-lane A/B over sleeping stubs, the order-sensitive crash arm pinned to one lane), test-writer-sweep (239), test-architecture via `npm run build`.

### src/peer-text.js — PURE THE ONE BELT ON PEER TEXT TOWARD AN AGENT (lane peer-census, B-00ef, 2026-09-29)

CJS; imports only PURE src/channel-record.js (the frame rule) and src/hidden-chars.js (the hidden set). Three lanes had learned the same three rules one door at a time (channel-render: bounded before parse, linear; lark r2/r3: the frame check looks through invisibles, the line rule per line and per inline piece; browser-stuck: invisibles folded, frames inert, the words delimited; pairing r6: ONE hidden set) and every door spelled its own composition — the held LOW nobody owned was src/inbox-reply.js quoting lines with none of it. `toAgentText(raw, {max = 64 KiB, kind = 'block' | 'line'})` is the composition in the one safe order: **bound** (`cutText` — before any regex walks the text; never inside a surrogate pair; `…` counted inside `max`; `max` ≤ 0 ⇒ '', non-finite ⇒ whole) → **fold** (`foldHidden` — CRLF → LF; every hidden character of hidden-chars.js: a control / a line or paragraph separator (a lone CR too) becomes a space, a format character (ZWSP, WJ, BOM, soft hyphen, the bidi embeddings / overrides / isolates, the TAG block) is removed, ZWJ / ZWNJ stay for emoji sequences and Indic / Persian words; a LINE folds every break / tab run to one space) → **the frame rule per line** (`inertFrameLine` on each line — never a whole-text pass first: it matched `<system-reminder⏎> …` across the break and merged the next line, quote mark and all; judged per line the opener loses its `<` and every line keeps its own prefix). `toAgentLines` = the block's lines for a site that prefixes each (`> `). Idempotent; never longer than `max`; a number is text, nothing is ''. Re-exports `carriesFrame` / `FRAME_TAGS` so a site's suite asks the rule that produced the text. CALLERS (each a row of the census with a pin): src/channel-filter.js `safeLine` / `safeInline`; src/channel-groups.js `piece` (every report line, the author, the group name, the inviter + context, the lead, a byte-cut line — judged again AFTER every cut); src/inbox-reply.js `quote` / `chip`; src/job-model.js `agentPiece` (a job's announce line IS its stdout — it reached the owner conversation LIVE before this lane); src/agent-routes.js `renderMsgStash` (a PEER entry re-judged at its drain, its sender's name as a piece; a NOTIFICATION entry is VibeSpace's own frame, never re-judged) and the legacy direct `vibespace-msg` lane; src/server/channels-engine.js `agentCopy` (the agent's read / thread copy, judged on the way OUT) and `searchFor` (after the 400-character cut) and the reaction digest's title. src/browser-stuck.js ships alone to every host and keeps its byte-equal COPY of the frame rule (pinned) with its own page-text fold. Gate: scripts/test-peer-text-census.mjs.
**Verify r5 F1 (2026-09-30, the shared-store census): `src/job-model.js` `agentJobView(snapshot, {mine})`.** A job of ANOTHER lineage — one whose owner opened `access.view` (group / all) or one the caller subscribed to — is another session's words: its context payload, command, cwd, env keys / sources, marker, last line and LOG TAIL (a process another agent started) took no rule on `vibespace-job list / show / poll / logs`, and `progress` (written by the job's process or ANY viewer — the act needs view only) reached the owner raw. The door belts every such field of a `!mine` record (line pieces; the log tail as a block) and `progress` for everyone; `mine` (the owner lineage) keeps its own record raw — the `lineage` / `log` trust. Wired at the two GET routes' four answer sites in src/agent-routes.js (`jobModel.agentJobView(a.jm.snapshot…`, pinned ×4). ### src/channel-record.js (PURE)

**Lane peer-census verify r6 (2026-09-30) — `inertOpeners`: the dangling openers of a line are judged RIGHT TO LEFT.** `inertFrameLine` = `inertOpeners(inertFrames(line))`; the one-pass `replace` left the first of two openers dangling (`<system-reminder [/system-reminder`) for the next line's `>` to complete. An opener can only dangle after the line's last `>`; the walk starts at the last `<` and moves left, each opener judged with the ones after it already neutered, the first non-opener `<` blocking every one before it; `FRAME_OPEN_RE` is sticky (`iuy`, unexported — it carries `lastIndex`). Linear, idempotent; the function text is pinned byte-equal to src/browser-stuck.js's copy (test-peer-text-census §5).

**Lane lark-search-poll verify r3 (2026-09-28) — THE FOLDER: the frame check looks THROUGH what nobody sees.** r2's name door removed the invisible characters from a NAME before `peerText`, but a message BODY never goes through the name door, so a stranger's `<system-reminder>` split by a zero-width space, a bidi control, a variation selector, a tag character or a NUL / ESC / C1 control reached the agent's read and its wake LIVE to any reader that drops the character (24 splitters, all live on the lane head). `FRAME_FOLD` (every Default_Ignorable_Code_Point + the non-whitespace controls + the line / paragraph separators) is ONE class that `FRAME_TAG_RE` / `FRAME_OPEN_RE` (and so `inertFrames`, `inertFrameLine`, `carriesFrame`, `peerText` and — through it — `peerName`) allow as a run between any two characters of a tag, around its `<` / `/` and before its `>`; the neutered name is spelled clean (`[system-reminder]`). Only a MATCHED tag changes: a body keeps its own bidi, joiners and layout. Linear: after a name the run excludes whitespace (U+FEFF / U+2028 / U+2029 are both), so no two quantifiers share a character (64 KiB adversarial runs ≤ 8 ms). Gate: test-channel-record ④d′ — the frame census re-run SPLIT (every covered tag × 4 variants + a split dangling opener) judged by an independent reader that drops what it cannot see; CONTROL a copy with an EMPTY folder.

**Verify round (2026-09-27):** `safeHref`'s mailto is ONE address — `MAILTO_RE` (the e-mail rung's alphabet, a dotted host, no `?` / `#` / percent-escape / path). RFC 6068 hfields are percent-decoded by the mail client, so `mailto:you@x?bcc=evil%40y` passed the old one-@ regex as a hidden recipient. Gate: test-channel-blocks ② + control (i).

**R3 (2026-09-26):** an attachment may carry `placeholder` — the token its adapter wrote into `text` for it (Lark's `[image]` / `[video]`). It is `peerText`-neutered and bounded at 32, and present ONLY when declared: every other attachment keeps the 4-field `{id, name, bytes, mime}` shape. The window drops one occurrence per DRAWN picture; `text` itself never changes. Gate: test-channels-images ①.

THE ONE normalized message record every channel adapter produces
(docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §4). Imports nothing, so the browser
bundle, the server and a node suite all take the same rules. Three rules, each
somebody's incident:

1. **`vendorId` IS THE DEDUP KEY** (design §5 invariant 2). A replayed page —
   which Lark's anchor semantics guarantee at a boundary and a Gmail history
   replay produces too — must be a no-op. A record with NO vendor id is refused
   here rather than given one downstream; an adapter that scrapes a SCREEN
   declares a minted key (`raw.synthetic: true`), because the invariant wants
   A key, not a vendor-issued one, while an UNDECLARED minted key turns every
   re-scan into a batch of duplicates.
2. **`@_user_N` PLACEHOLDERS ARE PER-MESSAGE ORDINALS, NOT IDENTITIES.** They
   resolve against THAT message's own `mentions` array, and an ordinal with no
   mention behind it is left VERBATIM — inventing a name for it is the
   mis-attribution the rule exists to stop (it has already filed a message
   under the wrong person in an ops tool).
3. **AN EXTERNAL BODY MAY NOT CARRY OUR OWN FRAME SYNTAX** (fence 5). Every
   peer-controlled string reaches an agent prompt eventually, so
   `<system-reminder>` / `<vibespace-*>` / `<task-notification>` /
   `<persisted-output>` / `<local-command-stdout>` / `<command-name>` /
   `<command-args>` are NEUTERED (`[system-reminder]`) at NORMALIZATION —
   the record is the one shape every consumer reads, and a guard applied at one
   consumer is a guard the next consumer does not get. The sender's WORDS
   survive verbatim.

   **AND THE RULE RUNS OVER *EVERY* PEER-CONTROLLED FIELD, NOT JUST `text`
   (r2).** It ran on `text` alone, so `author.name`, `mentions[].name` and
   `attachments[].name` — all peer-controlled, all part of the same record —
   came out of `makeRecord` with LIVE frames, which made this entry's own
   claim false at SOURCE (measured with the module's own `carriesFrame`
   predicate: text inert, the other three live). The design's §7.5 agent block
   renders `from <author>`, so the author name is squarely on the path the
   rule exists for, and `makeConversation` was already doing it for `title`
   and `participants` — the omission was an oversight, not a decision.
   `peerText()` is now the ONE door every such field goes through, and
   ATTRIBUTES are matched too (`<system-reminder x>` walked straight through
   a pattern that required `<name>` exactly).

   The `vibespace-*` half is a NAMESPACE (a stripper that enumerates misses
   the fourteenth); the rest is a FIXED LIST, and a list is the tool this
   class defeats — so `test-channel-record`'s **FRAME CENSUS** derives every
   hyphenated tag name the tree writes (`git ls-files -- src data/bin
   server.js`, 266 files, 28 names) and fails on one that is neither neutered
   nor classified as prose, with a negative control that it really flags an
   unclassified name. `<channel source="…">` is deliberately NOT listed:
   `channel` is an ordinary English word with no hyphen, so neutering it would
   mangle a stranger's code paste — and unlike the names above, we never
   inject it (the CLI composes it from its own socket).

The key separator is a NUL spelled as `\\u0000`: a raw one would make the whole
module invisible to grep, `file(1)`, ripgrep and every source census in the
tree (and fail the build's repo-wide scan). Gate: scripts/test-channel-record.mjs.


**Lane channel-rich (2026-09-28).** The CLOSED sets grew by what the markup reader needs: `RUN_KINDS` + `i` (italic), `BLOCK_KINDS` + `hr` (a rule), a `card` may carry inner `blocks` (walked at depth + 1, bounded like a quote's; `lines` stays for older trees). An attachment keeps two new OPTIONAL fields when the adapter declares them: `cid` (a mail part's Content-ID, angle brackets / quotes / whitespace stripped, ≤ 256) and `role` from the closed `ATTACHMENT_ROLES = ['body']` (the message's own formatted body — the window's mail frame, never a chip, never an agent's). Gate: test-channel-record + test-channel-blocks ①.
### src/channel-focus.js (PURE)

THE FIRST SCREEN'S PREDICATE AND THE PAGE RULES (design 008, B-3cf8). CJS, imports nothing; the engine requires it, the bundle imports it, src/lib/channel-focus.js re-exports it (the client's import path).
- `statusTag` / `focusRows` / `filterRows` / `firstScreen` / `heldOf` / `heldPending` — R3's rule, moved unchanged (§23).
- `candidateOf(en, ob, now)` — could this index entry wear a tag: one clause per tag over the raw facts rowView / touchView read (the outbox count, the conversation grain's own rows, the last wake delivered / held, pending hits, the last refusal, an agent read, a single chat's unread, the owner's own message). Over-includes, never misses (test-channel-rows ① property).
- `pageOrder` (lastAt desc, then key), `pageCursor`, `afterCursor`, `selectPage(items, {before, limit, keep, at, keyOf})` (one pass, a bounded heap → `{items, next, total}`), `queryOf` (≤ `QUERY_MAX` = 100), `textMatches`; bounds `ATTENTION_MAX` 300, `HEAD_ROWS` 30, `PAGE_ROWS` 60, `PAGE_MAX` 200.

- `selfRead(r, selfId)` / `readAdvance(readAt, recs, selfId)` (lane channel-self-unread, 2.369.228 — userW inc-muxekkry-clfb, B-c91b) — THE OWNER'S OWN MESSAGE IS READ BY CONSTRUCTION: `author.isSelf` or the resolved own id (unknown ⇒ not self, never a guess); `readAdvance` → `{readAt, unread, moved}` = the line moved to the newest self instant + the batch's others past it. statusTag's `new-since-read` reads `lastAt` only when it is past `touch.selfAt`. Tests: test-channels-focus.

**VIBESPACE'S OWN TALK FOLDS (lane channels-badges, 2026-10-03 — the owner: "提供一个选项可以把vibespace内部沟通收缩起来，这样避免agent互相沟通内容太多挤占实际沟通空间").** `isInternal(row)` = an agent group (`kind:'group'` WITH its `group` — a vendor group chat's digest row is not) or a row stamped `internal`; `needsOwner(row)` = `atYou > 0` or the awaiting / unknown tag; `internalBlock(rows, {folded, now})` → `{rows, block}`: the internal rows stand as ONE block under a `{kind:'internal-head', block}` marker at the place of the newest (every other row keeps its order); folded, the head alone — the rows that need the owner first, in input order (a block whose every row needs the owner still draws its head under them). `block` = `{n, unread, atYou, pinned, folded}` over every internal row. Today no internal row needs the owner (the group model refuses an @ of the owner; statusTag tags no agent group) — the rule is pinned by PURE rows + a no-@ mutant copy in test-channels-focus.

### src/lib/channel-rows.js (CLIENT, PURE)

THE PANEL'S ROWS, KEYED (design 008). DOM-free, fetch-free; imports only src/channel-focus.js. `createRowStore`, `applyFirst` (the first read / a reconnect / a non-partial broadcast → the names of the lists left stale), `applyPage` (a page or a re-read; a row a broadcast wrote after the ask keeps the broadcast's copy), `applyBroadcast` (the never-loaded rule), `listRows`, `loadedRows`, `focusRowsOf`, `pageQueryOf`. Lists: `all`, `search` (its `q`), `account:<id>` (every account, its head + pages); the attention list is the held rows that wear a tag.

### src/channel-attachments.js (PURE)

A PICTURE THE VENDOR SENT IS SHOWN AS A PICTURE (R3, 2026-09-26, design §23.1). CJS, imports nothing; the engine requires it and the window imports it, the channel-caps pattern.
- `fetchVerdict(facts)` is THE ORDER one attachment request is judged in, and the vendor-call gate test-vendor-whitelist §7 pins: cached ⇒ `serve` · remembered (& !retry) ⇒ refuse · owner `undefined` ⇒ `lookup` · !owner ⇒ `not-found` · !fetchable ⇒ `not-supported` · !enabled ⇒ `disabled` · inflight ⇒ `join` · backoff ⇒ `backoff` · !affordable ⇒ `vendor-budget` · else `fetch`.
- `negativeTtlMs(code, {retryAfterSec})` is how long a VENDOR's refusal is remembered: 10 min for a refusal waiting cannot fix, its own wait (≤ 60 s) for a transient one. The budget and the back-off are never remembered — the gate answers them again for free.
- `thumbVerdict(answer, attempt)` is the window's next step for a thumbnail that did not draw: TRANSIENT codes retry after the server's wait (1–60 s) at most `AUTO_RETRIES` 2 times; anything else is the named chip; `{ok:true}` (the file is there, no raster) is the download chip `no-preview`; `null` is `unreachable`.
- `bodyShown(text, placeholders)` removes one occurrence per drawn picture and collapses the blank lines left.

Gates: test-channels-images ②④ (the tables + patched copies: no retry limit, no cache-first), test-vendor-whitelist §7 (no budget gate).

### src/channel-blocks.js (PURE) + src/lib/channel-blocks-view.js (CLIENT) — THE RENDER LAYER (§25, 2026-09-27)

**Security verify r2 (2026-09-28) — the inline reader's tail is tracked:** `markupRead`'s `brk()` / cell rule read a tracked `tail` character (set in `pushRun`, cleared in `flush`) instead of `/\n$/.test(last.text)` on the growing run (quadratic: 128 KB of `<li>` = 433 ms at ingest); a post element's text goes through `bounded()`. test-channel-blocks ⑱ + a re-reading copy control.

**Security verify r2 (2026-09-28) — an unclosed drop tag is a word:** `markupTokens` opens a drop (`MK_DROP`: script/style/iframe/title/select/video/svg/canvas/textarea/math/template…) only when the message CLOSES it; an unclosed one with no attributes is the typed word (walled `‹title›`), with attributes that one tag alone — the words after it stay (they were silently lost: "please set the <title> of the page" read as "please set the"). test-channel-blocks ⑰ + a drop-to-end copy control.

THE OWNER (two screenshots): "设计一个不同 connector 的 raw message to HTML 的接口 … 邮件展示的时候就需要自动折叠 quote 内容，lark 展示的时候需要自动把 markdown 格式的一些链接之类的变成链接 … 至少保证人能看清楚必要的信息." The interface is a TYPED TREE, never HTML: an adapter writes `record.blocks` at ingest, ONE renderer turns it into DOM.

- **The schema lives in channel-record.js** (imports nothing; the record's shape in one place): `BLOCK_KINDS` p/quote/sig/banner/code/img/file/card/sys, `RUN_KINDS` t/a/at/code/b, `SYS_WHATS`, `BLOCK_LIMITS` {blocks 400, text 64 KiB, depth 6, runs 4000, cardLines 60, href 2048}, `safeHref` (http(s) with a host and no userinfo, or mailto with an address — else null), `validateBlocks` = rebuild from declared fields only, `inertFrames` over EVERY string, an unsafe `a` demoted to `t`, refusals BY NAME (`not-an-array` / `unknown-kind` / `unknown-run` / `bad-field` / `too-many-blocks` / `too-many-runs` / `too-deep` / `too-much-text`). `makeRecord` keeps a valid tree as the OPTIONAL `blocks` (`OPTIONAL_FIELDS`, after `RECORD_FIELDS`); an invalid one is left off and the record keeps its text.
- **channel-blocks.js** (CJS, imports ONLY channel-record; its exports are plain identifiers so an ESM importer sees every name — `BLOCK_KINDS: R.BLOCK_KINDS` stopped node's CJS export scan there and the renderer got `validateBlocks` undefined in a node suite): `inlineRuns` (one alternation regex: markdown link, `<url>`, `<at …>`, `@_user_N`/`@_all`, bare URL with a no-word-tail lookbehind and `trimUrl`, `mailto:`, e-mail, `` `code` ``, `**b**`, and — for a stored record — `@name` from its mentions), `linkText` (a label that is a URL on ANOTHER host shows the target), `textToBlocks` (the GENERIC rung: paragraphs, strict `>` quotes — `>_<` is no quote —, `-- ` signature ≤ 15 lines, ``` fences, placeholders → `img`/`file` in place), `emailToBlocks` (+ `EMAIL_QUOTE_RULES` en-wrote / zh-wrote / ja-wrote / original / forwarded / outlook, each with its attribution; the Gmail two-line wrap; ticket banners; rules; `-- ` + mobile signatures; a `Fwd:` subject marks a bare header block forwarded), `cleanSubject`, `larkToBlocks` (the vendor item), `larkStoredBlocks` (a pre-§25 Lark record: its `[image]`/`[video]` lines matched to its attachments by mime family, `@name`s chips again), `larkPostBody` (THE ONE post-body reader — lark.js's `postBody` is this), `previewOf`, `blockStrings`. Every rung ends in `finish()` = the schema's verdict, else ONE plain paragraph — a rung never returns an invalid tree.
- **channel-blocks-view.js**: `renderBlocks(blocks, {doc, t, icon, attachment, folds, foldKey, fallbackText})` → `div.chanmsg-body.chanblk`; every node from `doc.createElement`/`createTextNode`, every string textContent; the tree validated AGAIN and `safeHref` asked at the `a.href` assignment; `a` = `_blank` + `noopener noreferrer` + its target as title; `at` = `.chanblk-at` chip; `img`/`file` = `ctx.attachment(id)` (the window's thumbnail / chip, our route); `quote`/`sig` fold by `isFolded` = the window's memory, else `lines ≥ FOLD_MIN_LINES (3)` AND other content beside it (the ONLY content is never folded); a toggle replaces its own block (`replaceWith`) and writes the memory; `sysWords` / `foldLabel` = the i18n keys; `blocksOfRecord` = the ONE body path (tree, else the generic rung over `text`); `placedAttachments`.
- **Where it runs**: Lark + Gmail declare `caps.render: 'blocks'` (and must export `blocksOf` — the registry refuses the declaration without it and the export without the declaration); their `toRecord` writes the tree (the live lanes share `toRecord`); the engine's `messages()` / `loadOlder()` fill a stored record's missing tree through `blocksOf` at READ time (`withBlocks`; the store is never rewritten), `readFor` strips `blocks` (agents read `text`), `rowView`/search clean a `titleForm: 'subject'` title (`titleOf`; the index keeps the vendor's string), `previewText(w)` takes a row's `lastText` from the newest record's tree (the STORE stays node-builtins-only — test-channel-store pins it; the first cut required channel-blocks there and went red), `adapterView` carries `sendForm` (`draft` when `idempotency: 'two-phase'`) and `sendGrant` (the module's declared `{scopes, console}` against the held scopes → `missing`).
- Gates: test-channel-blocks (fast) + test-channel-window-render (heavy).
- **Lane channel-rich (2026-09-28), D1 — LARK MARKUP IS READ, NEVER PRINTED** (the owner: "lark 有些消息里混入了 <p> 这种 raw tag"; the store held 85 `text` messages of `<p>…</p>` by one user + 2 lone `<country>` placeholders). THE ONE READER is `markupRead(text, {ictx, nameOf, md, mode})`: `markupTokens` (code spans ``` / `…` opaque; comments / declarations dropped; an UNKNOWN tag is markup only when paired, attributed or self-closed — a lone `<word>` stays text) → blocks (`mode:'blocks'`) or one run list with `\n` per block boundary (`mode:'inline'`, inside a post line). `<p>`/`<div>`/… flush a paragraph, `<br>` = `\n` in the run, `<b>`/`<strong>` = `b` runs, `<i>`/`<em>` = `i` runs (NEW run kind), `<a href>` = an `a` run through `safeHref` (else its words), `<at user_id|open_id|id|email>` / `<person>` = an `at` chip (the roster / mentions name wins over the inner text), `<pre>` = a `code` block, `h1–h6` bold, `<li>` "• " / "N. ", `<blockquote>` a quote, `<hr>` an `hr` block (NEW block kind), script / style / iframe / object / svg / math / template / … DROPPED WITH THEIR CONTENTS, everything else stripped to its text; `inertFrames` runs FIRST (a `<system-reminder>` stays the words `[system-reminder]`, never a tag to strip). Entities are decoded only in a body that carries markup. `larkMdBlocks` = Lark markdown (fences, `#` headings bold, `- `/`1. ` lists, `---` rules, `> ` quotes, `*it*` / `_it_` italic, `~~s~~` words) then each paragraph through the reader. `larkCardBlocks` = an INTERACTIVE CARD's elements → the card block's NEW optional inner `blocks` (header title via `cardTitleOf` incl. `i18n_title`; `elements` / card 2.0 `body.elements` / `i18n_elements` by locale; div text + fields, markdown / lark_md, hr, note → a banner, action / button → `[label]` words only (never the vendor url), column_set, collapsible_panel, an img's alt; the list answer's post-like lines through `larkPostBlocks`); `lines` stays empty on a new record (older trees keep theirs). **THE WALL `sealTags`**: every TEXT string of a Lark tree (runs t/b/i/a/at, attribution, banner, sys, card title / lines) has any tag-shaped `<…>` left (`TAG_LIKE_RE = /<\/?[A-Za-z][^<>]*>/`, the census's own predicate) turned into `‹…›` — code runs and code blocks are the ONE named exemption (code is code). `larkPlainText` / `blocksToPlain` / `markupPlainLine` = the same reader flattened for `rec.text` (a body without markup returned AS IT IS). `larkStoredBlocks` reads a stored record's markup-bearing text through `larkPlainText` first (the owner's 85 rows render as paragraphs at READ time, the store untouched); a stored card's text after its "[card] title" line becomes its inner blocks. **LINEAR AND SHALLOW (security verify, 2026-09-28):** `MK_TAG_RE`'s attribute run is ONE greedy `[^<>]*` (the lazy run + `\s*` was quadratic over whitespace inside a tag; the trailing `/` is peeled in `markupTokens`); `larkMdBlocks` walks fences ONCE (`noCloserFrom`, the email rung's rule); both readers bound nesting from where their output lands (`opts.depth` — a card's inner blocks start at 1; `larkPostBlocks` passes it to its `md`): a `<blockquote>` / `> ` past MAX_DEPTH is a paragraph break / its words unquoted, never a level; Lark's `textOf` is guarded (a throw ⇒ the raw words behind the wall). Gate: test-channel-record ⑦ (the tag census, new + stored, with a control) + test-channel-blocks ⑯ (bounded work + depth, child controls) + test-channels-lark-shape ⑩ (the guard).

### src/mail-frame.js (PURE) + src/lib/channel-mail-frame.js (CLIENT) — THE MAIL FRAME (lane channel-rich D2, 2026-09-28)

The owner: "gmail 这种富文本 html 内容似乎完全没有按照 html 渲染". A message whose record names a formatted BODY (`attachments[].role === 'body'`, a mail's text/html part — `bodyAttachmentOf`) is shown FORMATTED by default in a FULLY SANDBOXED iframe; the text blocks stay the Plain-text view, every preview, search, the attention list and every agent read (agents never receive HTML: `withoutBlocks` drops the body attachment, search hits too).
- **THE srcdoc, in THIS order** (the channel surface's ONE srcdoc — test-channel-record ⑧ pins it by name): ① `sanitizeMailHtml(html, {pictures, cid})` — OUR allowlist RE-SERIALIZER: the mail is tokenized and written out again from the tokens (never passed through): `ALLOWED_TAGS` kept, `DROP_TAGS` (script, iframe, object, embed, svg, math, form controls, meta, base, link, media, template, …) dropped WITH their contents, raw-text elements (`RAW_TEXT`) read to their closer, everything else unwrapped; `ALLOWED_ATTR` only (never on*, srcset, background, poster, action, target, id, name); every text escaped, every attribute value re-quoted; a URL judged AFTER its entities are decoded and tabs/newlines/controls removed (`safeOpenHref`: http(s) with a host and no userinfo, or ONE mailto address); `imageSrcVerdict`: `cid:` → the data: picture the parent fetched (else dropped + named in `cidMissing`), a data: RASTER kept (never svg), a remote picture BLOCKED (no src written, `data-vs-blocked`, counted) until Show pictures, then https only; `sanitizeCss` (style attrs + `<style>`): comments, backslashes, `<`/`>` removed, `@import`/`@font-face`/`@namespace` gone, `url()` only for a data: raster, `image-set()` / `image()` / `expression()` neutered, behavior / -moz-binding removed, URL-looking quoted strings emptied (`cssStrings`, scanned pair by pair). Bounds: `MAX_HTML_BYTES` 2 MiB ⇒ `{ok:false, code:'too-large'}` (the plain text + a sentence), `MAX_IMAGES` 200 (the rest dropped + counted), the element stack ≤ 512. ② `DOMPurify.sanitize(pure.html, DOMPURIFY_CONFIG)` — the browser's own parse, the same lists, `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP` http(s) / mailto / data: raster, `FORCE_BODY` (a leading `<style>` kept) and **`ADD_URI_SAFE_ATTR` = every allowed NON-URL attribute** (DOMPurify judges every attribute not on its URI-safe list against the URI regexp — a strict one stripped `width` / `colspan` / `bgcolor` / the blocked marker; measured in chrome). ③ `composeSrcdoc({body, nonce, token, pictures})` — `<meta charset>`, the CSP `<meta>` FIRST (`cspFor`: `default-src 'none'; img-src data: [https:]; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; script-src 'nonce-…'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; media-src 'none'; object-src 'none'`), base styles (light color-scheme, images/tables bounded), the body, then OUR resizer (`resizerScript(token)`, the only script, with the nonce).
- **THE FRAME**: `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and NOTHING else (an opaque origin — `contentDocument` is null to the parent; NEVER `allow-same-origin`), `referrerpolicy=no-referrer`, on `var(--paper)`. The resizer posts `{vsMail: token, h}` on resize/load and `{vsMail: token, open: href}` for a clicked link (clicks and submits are prevented in the frame). **The parent trusts ONE number**: `frameMessageVerdict({source, frameWindow, token, data})` — the event's `source` must be THAT frame's window AND carry THAT frame's random token (an opaque origin is `'null'` for every mail frame); a height is clamped to [HEIGHT_MIN 24, HEIGHT_MAX 20000]; an `open` is re-judged by `safeOpenHref` and opened `_blank` + `noopener,noreferrer`. A reader at the list's tail stays there while a frame grows.
- **`cid:` pictures** are the message's own parts: `cidRefs(html)` names them, the DOM half fetches each through OUR attachment route with `&inline=1` (the parent's cookie — an opaque frame has none; raster ≤ MAX_CID_BYTES, ≤ MAX_CID_FETCH) and hands them in as data:; a picture drawn inside the mail is hidden from the strip under it (`chanmail-inlined`, formatted view only).
- **Show pictures** (`picturesState` / `picturesShown` / `showPictures`): per message, remembered for the SENDER (case-insensitive) for the PAGE SESSION — a module-level state in the DOM half, never stored, never global; pressing it rebuilds every live frame of that sender with `https:` in its CSP.
- **LAZY** (`liveFrames(rows, view, {keep, cap})`): a row is a candidate while it intersects the list's viewport ± `KEEP_ZONE_PX` (1200); EVERY row on screen is live (security verify r2, continued: the cap used to blank visible mails past the sixth), the keep zone is pre-warmed nearest first while the total is under `LIVE_FRAME_CAP` (6); one IntersectionObserver per window (root = the list) + a rAF-coalesced scroll reconcile, every listener on `winInfo._listenerCtl.signal`; a dropped frame leaves a placeholder of its measured height. A background tab runs no frames, so frames go live when the tab is seen.
- **The slot** (`createMailFrames({list, base, signal, modes}).slotFor(rec, row)`): `div.chanmail` = bar (`Formatted | Plain text` segmented, `aria-pressed`; `Show pictures (N)` while a remote picture is blocked) + a note line + the box; the row carries `chanmail-formatted` (CSS hides its text body); the person's choice per message lives in the window's `mailModes` Map (like `folds`) so a full redraw keeps it. A body the route refuses / a body over the bound ⇒ the plain text + ONE sentence naming why (+ Retry) and a telemetry event — never a silent fallback.
- **Where the bytes come from**: Gmail's `walkParts` keeps the first text/html part as `htmlPart` (`part:<id>`, `part:root` for a single-part mail — `fetchAttachment` reads the root for it) FIRST among the attachments (the 64 bound never cuts it); `toRecord({onBody})` hands its bytes to the instance's bounded hold (32 MiB, 4 MiB per body); the registry passes `heldAttachment(messageId, attId)` through (sync, never throws); the engine's `persistHeldBodies` writes them into the attachment cache the moment the record is durable (both ingest paths) and `attachment()` serves a held body before any verdict (zero vendor units); a body never held is fetched on demand through the R3 verdict ladder like any attachment. The route answers text/html as `application/octet-stream` + `attachment` + nosniff + a sandbox CSP (never rendered in our origin); the DOM half reads it with `fetch().arrayBuffer()`.
- **NAIVE-USER VERIFY (2026-09-28, three MEDIUMs seen in the pixels, each fixed with a pin + a control):** ① **FIT TO WIDTH** — a 600 px newsletter at the phone's ~300 px frame was CUT on the right (the frame's overflow is hidden: unreadable AND unreachable). MEASURED in chrome: with the root's overflow hidden `documentElement.scrollWidth/scrollHeight` are the VIEWPORT's (so a frame already taller than its content never shrank either); `body.scrollWidth` is the natural width in UNZOOMED units and `body.getBoundingClientRect()` the zoomed box. **2026-09-26 — THE AGGREGATED IM (design §5 inv 6, §6.2):** `tracked` is gone from every verdict. `freshnessClaim(caps, lane, entry, now, {enabled, cadence, tiers, watched})` claims for EVERY conversation (`paused` is its own state: "refresh paused"); `cadenceFor(caps, lane, entry, now, {tiers, watched})` = override (`entry.refresh.every`) > push safety net (a live content-carrying lane ⇒ cold) > tier, clamped to [the adapter's floor, `COLD_MAX_SEC` 900]; `pollTier` = hot (watched, or a message within `hotRecentMinutes`) / warm (within `warmRecentHours`) / cold; `TIER_DEFAULTS` {hot 30, warm 300, cold 900, 60 min, 24 h}; `REFRESH_CHOICES` [30, 60, 300, 900, 'paused'] + `validRefresh`; `freshnessText(claim, {t, short})` — `short` is the row PILL's form ("19s ago" for an aged scan; since 2.369.186 also `paused` → "paused" and `never` → "no scan yet"), the full sentence stays in its tooltip; the pill never ellipsizes, so its WIDTH BUDGET is these words: every one ≤ 82 px at 9/600 in the runner's face (DejaVu Sans), which leaves a plain row's title design §4's 60 px in the 188 px panel — a new state or word is measured by test-channels-e2e ⑯ b (a census over this switch's own `case` labels, zh/ja/en, both faces); `budgetText` = the exhausted-budget sentence WITH its numbers (limit, unit, waiting, reset seconds); `pushUnavailableText` words the lane's park codes (`sdk-not-installed` = the verbatim `npm install @larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` remedy + "until then polled every 30 s – 15 min"); `pushLaneText` names the cold cadence it reconciles at. The panel's health line reads ONLY these (test-channels-aggregate ③b pins the wiring).

THE ONE place that answers "does this control exist" and "which lane is
carrying this row right now" (design §4, §6.4, §12.5). Two axes, modelled not
flattened: how messages arrive (`receive` push|poll|scan + the per-platform
`scanSources`/`scanLatency`/`historyBySource`) and what may be sent and as
whom (`sendAs`, narrowed per conversation by `convCaps`).

- **`laneState(caps, adapterRecord, entry, now)`** — the lane ACTUALLY carrying
  this conversation. Precedence **DEMOTED > LIVE > CLAIM**, and `unknown` (the
  DEFAULT — declare nothing, get the conservative behaviour) never carries
  content. Liveness is POSITIVE evidence only (the socket says live AND
  something was heard inside the heartbeat window). A demoted or dead push lane
  answers `via:'poll'`, because that is where the records come from and the
  chip must draw what is true. This exists because the same fact lived in THREE
  stores (a static declaration, a per-deployment claim, a per-conversation
  observation) with nothing saying which won — so a demoted lane kept carrying
  content while the adapter row said it had been demoted, and the freshness
  chip drew `live` off a static declaration (the `opencode-events` round-4
  lesson: a lane that lies about being active is worse than no lane, because it
  turns the fallback OFF).
- **`scanState(caps, adapterRecord, hostFacts, now)`** — the same law on the
  other lane. Precedence **FACTS FRESH > PLATFORM DECLARATION > CLIENT PRESENT >
  READ GRANT > `'ui'`**, freshness first because every level below it reads
  `hostFacts`. ONE deliberate exception keeps it from becoming what it guards
  against: **a refused read does NOT fall back to `'ui'`** — `tcc-denied` is a
  NAMED answer with `source: null`, because silently swapping a 15-second lane
  for a 5-minute one turns the latency on the row (this class's whole honesty
  contract) into a lie. It answers `via:'scan'` so the union with `laneState`
  is explicit rather than sniffed from which keys happen to exist.
- **`convCapsState`** — `convCaps` is a CACHE, not a stored fact: it is a
  vendor round trip and cannot be re-derived locally, so it pays for its
  exemption with a 6 h TTL and an honest degrade to `unknown`/`[]`/`stale`.
  `scan.hostFacts` takes the same price for the same reason.
- **`offers(caps, convCaps, what)`** — BOTH halves must allow it, `unknown` is
  "not offered + a reason" and never "allowed", and the resolution INTERSECTS
  so it can only ever narrow the declaration.
- **`identityWarning`** — `unknown` warns exactly as loudly as `marked`; the
  adapter's own sentence is shown VERBATIM (it is a statement about a vendor's
  UI, not product chrome, so it is never translated).
- **`freshnessClaim(caps, laneOrScan, entry, now)`** — takes its clock as an
  argument like every sibling resolver in this tree, because it answers "how
  long ago". `t` is injected (the `collab-row`/`permission-rules` pattern), and
  the default substitutes params exactly as i18n does for a missing
  translation — a default that dropped them would ship `within {age}` to every
  node-side caller. Gate: scripts/test-channel-caps.mjs.

**A ROW NOTHING WILL EVER FETCH SAYS SO (r3).** Every discovered
conversation is UNTRACKED by default (§5 invariant 6 — and untracked is all a
fresh instance shows until someone clicks) and a disabled adapter's rows are
refused by the tick and the pass alike, yet `freshnessClaim` fell through to
the declared poll cadence for both, so a row that would never be fetched said
"within 5m" on the ONE surface this feature calls its honesty contract. The
claim now takes `{enabled}` as its fifth argument and reads `entry.tracked`
STRICTLY (`=== true` — a fixture that forgets the flag models an untracked
row, because that is what the store mints), answering `state:'off'` with a
`why` (`adapter-disabled` outranks `untracked`, which outranks the scan
resolver's own reason); `freshnessText` renders `off` as "not scanning" on the
scan lane and "not polling" everywhere else (zh + ja entries added). The
control is a scratch-dir patched copy with the two gates removed, which claims
"within 5m" on both shapes.

**THE RESOLVERS RETURN STRUCTURE; THE CLIENT COMPOSES THE SENTENCE (r2).**
`freshnessClaim` used to build the words and the ingest engine called it with
no translator — so the freshness chip, the string this feature calls its
honesty contract, shipped ENGLISH-ONLY to a zh/ja UI (nine strings), and the
build's i18n scan could not see them because they left the server as DATA
rather than as a `t()` literal. The server structurally CANNOT fix it by
taking a translator: language is per DEVICE (localStorage) while the digest is
BROADCAST to every client at once. So `freshnessClaim` answers
`{kind, state, seconds}` and `freshnessText(claim, {t})` says the words where
the language is known; `identityWarning` answers `{level, marking, verbatim}`
(the adapter's OWN sentence is the one string allowed on the wire — it is a
statement about a vendor's UI and is never translated) and
`identityWarningText` renders the rest. `state` exists because `kind` alone
collapses distinct answers ("not scanning" vs "not scanned yet",
"reconciling" vs "polling") and a renderer that cannot tell them apart is back
to inventing the difference. The panel and the window import this PURE module
directly (the `quota-model` / `task-color-seq` pattern, with a reasoned
test-architecture exception each).

**`authState(record, now)` — 'connected' IS A RESOLUTION, NEVER AN ASSERTION
(r2).** The digest published `rec.auth?.expiresAt ? 'connected' : 'connected'`
— a ternary whose two branches are the same string — so an expired or
never-authenticated adapter was announced to the panel as connected, on the
one surface that is supposed to say whether a lane can serve. The answer comes
from the two facts the record already holds, in the order of how much they
prove: the LAST PASS'S OWN VERDICT (`code === 'auth-expired'` is the vendor
refusing us — measured, and it outranks a token whose stamped expiry has not
arrived, because a revoked or rotated credential carries a perfectly future
one, exactly like a wiped claude login), then the STAMPED EXPIRY, believed
only once it has PASSED. No credential at all is `'unknown'`, never
`'connected'`: the P0a fakes authenticate against nothing and saying so is the
point.

**THE EXCLUSIVITY MEASUREMENT + THE ROW'S SENTENCE (P1b, 2026-09-16; design
§6.4, decision 18).** `pushSamplesAdd` / `pushMissRate` / `pushDemotionVerdict`
are ARITHMETIC over batches `{at, n, p}` (n judged records, p first seen by
the poll) inside a ROLLING window — the last 24 h or the last
`PUSH_MISS_MIN_KEEP` (200) records, whichever is LARGER — demoting past
`PUSH_MISS_THRESHOLD` (2 %) over `PUSH_MISS_MIN_SAMPLES` (20); the verdict is
NEVER true for a lane already demoted (the counters clear nothing). WHEN a
sample is taken is the engine's rule (only while push carries content), not
this module's. `pushLaneText(push, lane, {t, now})` is the adapter row's
sentence — state, or the demotion's reason WITH its numbers; the silent-but-
connected case says "silent for <age>". `caps.pushOptIn` (Gmail) makes
`laneState` answer the POLL lane until the record says `push.enabled === true`
(decision 20: available, off by default). Gate: test-channel-caps ⑧/⑨.

**A GROUP'S ACCESS REACHES ITS MEMBERS; REGEX RULES; THE PREVIEW'S MATCHER.** (1) MEMBERSHIP: `validateWatchers(list, access, {inherited, members})` — `members` = the live roster `[{cid, groups}]` (server: `membersNow()` in channels-access.js over `liveSessions()`, i.e. `tasks.groupsForSession`, the crosswalk the group round-robin already wakes over; the dialog: `rosterFromApp`'s `groupIds`). A SESSION watcher not itself in the access keys is eligible when `memberVia(keys, cid, members)` finds an access-holding group it belongs to; the row is stored AS THE SESSION (`agent:<cid>` — its own cap, ledger, pending) with `via: <gid>`; a writer's own `via` is deleted (the server's finding, never the claim). `eligibleFor(keys, principal, row)` honours `via` at READ (PURE — the group's access row covers it; the group's access removed ⇒ the row is inert). WHETHER IT IS STILL A MEMBER is re-judged on EVERY WAKE: channels-access `wakeEffOf` drops a `via` item whose session is not in the group now (`memberStill`; not running = membership unknown = not woken); the row stays and is live again when it rejoins. (2) `regex` joins RULE_KINDS: `regexVerdict(src)` judges AT SAVE — compiles with `iu`, ≤ REGEX_MAX 256, refused BY NAME with the offending `piece` (REGEX_REFUSALS): backreference, lookaround, a repeated piece inside an unbounded group (or overlapping branches under one), two unbounded pieces that can eat the same text side by side (adjacency is judged through optional pieces), an unbounded piece that can re-read the match's own head when unanchored (`\d+x`, `a.*b`, `\w+@` — the search loop is itself a repeat; a fixed head the piece cannot be closes it; a head repeat that ENDS the pattern is linear and allowed), and a pattern matching the empty message. Overlap = probe samples (printable ASCII + a few non-ASCII + every character the pattern names) tested against each piece's own `^(?:piece)$`. The match runs on `regexText` = peer-text's `foldHidden(cutText(text, 8192))`; `compiledRegex` caches ≤ 256 and never runs a stored pattern the judge now refuses. Cost: the worst ACCEPTED shape (`invoice.*paid` over `invoiceinvoice…`, two-byte) is ~20 ms at the 8 KiB cap and the same at 64 KiB (pinned in test-channel-filter ⑭); before the head rule `\w+@…` cost ~140 ms at 8 KiB two-byte. `regexSpan` = the first match span on the folded text (the preview's mark).

**THE ELIGIBILITY RULE + DELIVERY.** `eligibleKeys({access, inherited})` / `eligibleFor(keys, principal)`: a watcher's principal must hold access at its grain OR ABOVE it (the account grain, a matching rule, a visible grant reaching the conversation — the caller passes those as `inherited`; `everyone:*` covers every principal but an All-agents watcher needs All-agents access). `validateWatchers(list, access, {inherited})` writes by it, `grainOf(rec, legacy, {inherited})` reads by it, `effectiveGrants(input, facts, {grantKeys, accountKeys})` reads each grain with the access above it. `DELIVERY_MODES` next-turn|wake + `deliveryModeOf(row)` (no field = wake: every pre-lane row) — the engine's dispatch, the dialog, the CLI and the proposal read it; `WATCH_ORIGINS` user|agent + `watchOriginOf`. A watcher keeps `delivery` / `origin` only spelled right (an old row gains no field ⇒ its grain stamp is unchanged). Gate: test-channel-agent-watch ①.

The filter, the assignment model and the block an agent is handed (design

editor bundles it like channel-caps, so a rule the editor draws is a rule the
route accepts. Invariants, one sentence each:

- `RULE_KINDS` is a CLOSED set of eight (`mention`, `keyword`,
  `sender-in-group`, `from-address`, `subject`, `has-attachment`,
  `not-contains`, `time-window`); `validateRule`/`validateFilter` refuse by
  name, and a null or empty filter never hits (a wake is money — fail closed).
- **A refusal is STRUCTURE beside its sentence (a3 r4):** `{ok:false, code,
  error, kind?, max?}` — `error` stays the route's English contract (the CLI
  prints it), `code` (value-required / members-required / time-format /
  tz-range / no-rules / too-many-rules / bad-match / bad-kind) is what the
  editor words through `filterProblemText(v, {t, ruleLabel})` in the
  device's language (an unknown code falls back to the sentence, never
  hidden) — "Add rule" used to print `keyword: value is required` under zh.
- **`why` is a contract, not prose**: `matchRecord` returns the rule strings
  that fired (`ruleWhy`), the wake block and the panel show the same string,
  and `whyText([])` is "matched: all messages".
- `estimate` is honest about its window: `sampled` = the reader's cap was hit
  before the window's start, `truncated` = the corpus is younger than the
  window, in which case the rate is over the span it actually saw
  (`windowDays`); an empty corpus is no evidence, not "truncated".
- `authority:'send'` is capped by TWO facts that only narrow (`authorityCap`:
  channel policy requires review — decision 9's default for every v1 adapter;
  or `offers()` says no, with caps' own reason), refused by `validateAssignment`
  with code `authority-capped`, and CLAMPED AT READ TIME by
  `effectiveAuthority` so a stored value never silently becomes a permission
  when the policy is later relaxed — the user re-chooses.
- `pickRoundRobin` stores a WRAPPED cursor and answers `null` with no live
  member — the caller holds, never "wakes them all".
- `paceVerdict` (the per-assignment daily wake cap) is PACING, layer one of
  three (§7.4); only wakes that HAPPENED (`ok !== false`) count, a cap of 0
  never wakes, and its `why` names the numbers.
- `renderWakeBlock`/`renderDigestBlock`: ≤ `BLOCK_MAX_RECORDS` (6), ≤
  `BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` (400) per record, "(N older elided)", the whole block
  under `BLOCK_MAX_BYTES` (4096 — the hook channel wraps at 10 KiB and this
  product has lost that fight once), every vendor line QUOTED (`> `) and
  passed through `inertFrames`, so an outsider cannot forge one of this
  block's own headings or a `<system-reminder>` in an agent's context; a
  coalesced burst says "N messages in S s, one wake".

WATCHERS — THE FAN-OUT (the money rule: never All × N uncapped, never N shared): `fanOutWatchers(eff, live)` replaces each stored All watcher by ONE item per RUNNING conversation (`live` = `[{cid, name}]`, deduped, id-less dropped, in the stored row's place) — principal `{kind:'everyone', id:'*', target:<cid>}`, key `everyone:*><cid>` (`fanOfKey` / `fanTargetOf`), the stored row's settings (notify, mode, filter, digest, CAP) and THAT conversation's own ledger `stats.fan[<cid>]` (`fanStatsOf`, `fanWatcher`); nobody running ⇒ nobody woken; an answer without an All watcher is returned as the same object. `ledgerRowsOf(stats)` = the card's count over every conversation's ledger; `pruneFan(stats, now)` drops a conversation with nothing in its 7-day window (the map never grows with every conversation that ever ran); `expectedWakesTotal(rows, {running})` counts an All row as one budget PER RUNNING conversation. **Lane guards-door (2026-10-09, owner "带文件是不是要直接允许也要加个开关，防止用户想要完全放权"):** `policyRowModel` gains `guardRows` (one row per guard: `{id, key, label, state: 'ask'|'allow', words, toggleTo, setZone}` — `key` = THE instance setting from `GUARD_KEYS`; `toggleTo` only when `owner: true`; off-hours without a zone offers `setZone` = the injected `localTz`), `delegationText` + `fullDelegation` (Full delegation ONLY when the grain reads direct AND no guard asks), the direct words carry the current answers (`files: ask · links: ask · off-hours: off`); `guardsText` is the summary of the same rows. `GUARD_REASONS` = the reasons a guard (not the policy) adds — the card's pointer reads it. **THE REPLY PLACEMENT (lane channel-threads placement round, 2026-09-28 — the owner: "the boolean is Lark-shaped").** A reply is `PLACEMENTS` = `chat` (a plain message) / `quote` (answers a message, shown in the main list) / `thread` (inside its thread) / `thread+chat` (inside the thread AND echoed to the conversation — Slack's reply_broadcast); `THREAD_PLACEMENTS` = the two inside a thread. The ADAPTER declares which in its `threads` cap row — `placements` + `rootReply` (its norm for a reply to a message OUTSIDE any thread: Lark quote, Slack thread, Telegram quote) — and `placementsOf(caps)` reads it CLAMPED (a read-only adapter places nothing, a thread placement needs `replyInto`, `thread+chat` needs `thread`; a row with NO `placements` reads as the pre-enum contract: chat + quote + thread where `replyInto` — suites' scripted modules only, every shipped adapter declares it: test-channel-placement's census). `placementVerdict({requested, replyTo, caps, parent:{inThread}, alias})` = PL1 an unknown word ⇒ `bad-proposal` why `placement`; PL2 a reply placement names its message (`why: replyTo`, or `inThread` when the request spoke the old boolean — the pre-enum test pin) and `chat` names none; PL3 NOTHING ASKED + a message ⇒ THE VENDOR'S NORM: a message inside a VENDOR thread (THE classifier `placeKindOf(replyTo, ix).topic` — the one the window's chip / tag read; a reply chain is a quote, not a thread — and a thread reply to a message outside any topic records no key: the vendor mints it) ⇒ `thread` (it cannot be quoted from the main list: Lark files a reply to a topic message in the topic, L6), else `rootReply`, neither ⇒ `placement-not-offered` why `no-replies`; PL4 undeclared ⇒ `placement-not-offered` why `not-declared` + `offered` ("…is not offered on this channel — offered here: chat, quote, thread", the agent's contract sentence); PL5 a quote of a threaded message ⇒ why `parent-in-thread` (the card would say "quoted" while the vendor threads it); PL6 nothing at all ⇒ chat. `validateProposal` checks only the SHAPE (PL1/PL2, a contradiction between `placement` and `inThread`) and returns `placement` (+ `placementAlias` when it came from `inThread`, + `inThread` for a thread one); the ENGINE asks the verdict with the caps before the proposal exists. `placementOf(p)` = THE READ ALIAS of a stored proposal (a valid `placement`, else `inThread` ⇒ thread, a `replyTo` ⇒ quote, else chat; null for a compose / a reaction). `receiptFor` carries `placement` (+ `inThread`/`threadKey` for a thread one) and the block says `placed in a thread (thread omt_…)` / `placed as a quoted reply, in the chat` (a pre-enum receipt with only `inThread` still says "in a thread"; the withheld receipt says none). Words: `placementWords` (the agent's English), `placementText(placement, {t, quote})` (the card line — none for chat), `placementRefusalText(r, {t})` (the toast per why / placement). Gate: scripts/test-channel-placement.mjs (the table per vendor incl. Slack/Telegram fixture rows + five patched copies).

**2026-09-27 (lane channel-withdraw — the owner: "agent 似乎没有撤回之前制作的 draft 的能力，必须要我手动 reject 是吗？"; "如果我修改后批准，agent 似乎也收不到我的修改动作 …"; "收件箱里的 approve 动作需要在账号-level 的通知配置里控制行为有点反直觉"):**

Never from `sending` (the request may be leaving), a decided state, or `unknown` (a lost outcome is the user's to check). `withdrawVerdict(p, by)` = the ONE verdict engine + route share: `not-yours` (another agent — a Task-Group sibling included — or the user's draft; identity = `draftedBy.id`, never a name) / `not-withdrawable` (the state, named). `withdrawReason` = the stored contract string (`withdrawn by the agent[: why]`); `outcomeOf` → `{kind:'withdrawn', who, userReason}` worded "Withdrawn by <agent> · <why>"; `RECEIPT_STATUSES` has `withdrawn` (+ `replacedBy`).
- **`receiptDiff(proposed, final)`** — the receipt's compact LINE diff (LCS over the changed middle; a changed run PAIRWISE, `-` then `+`; one line of context; a longer unchanged run is one `… N unchanged lines`; every line frame-inert and ≤ 600 chars; the whole ≤ 2000 with a clip line). `renderReceiptBlock(rc, {text, proposed})` prints it for an edited send ("what the user changed (- you proposed / + the user sent)"), the final text only for a caller without `proposed`; `receiptFeedback` (edited / a reasoned rejection) ⇒ the block ends `RECEIPT_GUIDANCE` "Use this as guidance for the next draft."

The outbox policy (design §9, P3). Imports only `channel-record` (PURE → PURE)
for `inertFrames`; the Outbox card bundles it. Invariants, one sentence each:

- `TRANSITIONS` is the ONE table: every allowed move names its actor
  (`agent`/`user`/`policy`/`adapter`/`ttl`/`recheck`/`reconcile`) and
  `canTransition` refuses every other move with the reason; terminal states
  leave nowhere.
- `unknown` leaves ONLY through `reconcile` — a send whose outcome was lost
  is never retried by the machine (§9.4).
- `decideOutbound`: the channel policy is the base, the guards (links /
  attachments / off-hours / authority) stack on top and can only TIGHTEN it;
  an unknown policy value or an unparseable guard config is `review` (fail
  closed); off-hours with no time zone is OFF, never guessed.
- `receiptFor` owes the agent nothing while the proposal is `unknown`; a sent
  receipt carries `sentAs` / `identityMarking` / `identityMarkingText` (null
  text only when the marking is `none`).
- `renderReceiptBlock` is a §7.5-shaped, frame-inert block.

- P4 (§9.4/§9.5): `sending → unknown` may also be caused by `boot` (a process
  that died between the audit ATTEMPT and OUTCOME lines); `honestyLine` is
  null unless the switch is ON *and* the drafter is an agent (`HONESTY_LINE_DEFAULT`
  = false), `withHonestyLine` appends it after a blank line; `canReconcile`
  refuses `idempotency:'none'` (a person's look) and a read-only adapter;
  `reconcileVerdict` maps landed ⇒ sent / not-landed ⇒ failed / anything else
  ⇒ stay; the receipt carries `reconciled` + `honestyLine`.
- **`renderReceiptBlock` neuters EVERY vendor-controlled field (2026-09-16,
  the P4 verifier): label / title / vendor id / sentAs pass through the same
  `safeInline` rule as channel-filter (inertFrames FIRST, then single-line,
  then clip 60 / 120 / 200 / 40) — the receipt path is as frame-inert as the
  wake path (fence 5); a title carrying `\n<system-reminder>` used to land a
  live frame on its own line in the drafting agent's context.

**Lane lark-threads (2026-10-01) — THE PLACE DOOR (A1).** A Lark message stored before anyone answered it in a thread carries no thread id, and the dedup kept that first copy for ever. `widenPlaces(adapterId, convId, offers, {src})` is the ONE function that widens a stored record's place — `threadKey` null → the vendor's key, `root` null → the vendor's root (the PURE rules: src/channel-thread.js `widenPlace` P1–P4), judged against the STORED place (`basePlaces`, a sparse map rebuilt WITH the dedup set) plus the patches; each widening = ONE validated side line `{k:'pl', msg, at, src, threadKey, root}` (deduped by its content), then `wrote(…, {kind:'place', patched})`. `appendRecords` / `prependRecords` offer every DUPLICATE that names a place (`widened` in their answer; a failed side write is logged, never the append's failure). Every reader serves the patched record (`readTail` non-strict, `findRecord`, `oldestRecord`, `search` — `placesOf` = the folded pl lines, cached ≤ PLACE_CACHE_MAX conversations); the strict dedup rebuild reads the bytes as written. `trimSide` KEEPS pl lines (one per message, the newest PLACE_KEEP_MAX, placed last — never forgotten like an old reaction); `trim()` FOLDS them into the message lines it keeps (temp + rename) and only then drops them from the side log. Also `aliases.json` (B3, the owner's names for authors) behind `aliases.update(fn)` — the groups.json family pattern (set aside when unreadable, blocked ⇒ refused). **Verify r3 (2026-09-27):** `OUTBOX_PRUNABLE` (exported) = every TERMINAL state of the outbox table (`sent`, `failed`, `rejected`, `expired`, `withdrawn`) — the bound drops the oldest of THESE past `OUTBOX_KEEP`. It was a hand-written four; `withdrawn` (the lane's new terminal state) never left the file, and once an agent's withdrawals / replaces were all the store held the bound dropped the owner's DECIDED records instead (540 on disk, the whole file rewritten synchronously per write). **R3 (2026-09-26):**

**Lane R2 verify (2026-09-26):** `index.blocked()` / `adapters.blocked()` answer the refusal sentence while that family's file could not be set aside (null = writable) — a synchronous caller (the migration runner's `migrateAggregated`) must FAIL rather than queue writes the door will refuse.

**2026-09-26 — the aggregated IM's store halves:** `peek(adapterId, convId)` (ONE entry, no index clone — the pass no longer deep-clones the index per conversation), `live()`/`table(name)` for the index's new tables (`accountAssignments`, `patternAssignments`, `accountGrants`), `prependRecords` (history on demand: one rewrite keeping `(at, vendorId)` order, dedup as always, never the wake funnel) + `oldestRecord`, `search(adapterId, q, {limit 100, maxBytes 64 MiB})` (async chunked read, newest first, `truncated`), and the ATTACHMENT CACHE `attachmentGet/Put/Usage` under `data/channels/attachments/<adapterId>/<convId>/` — files 0600, names hashed, an `lru.json` per account, eviction least-recently-used first to the account's byte budget; `attachmentPut` is ASYNC (the blob — up to 100 MB — and the evictions go through fs.promises, each write through its own `.tmp-<pid>-<seq>` file, so concurrent first fetches never share a temp file; test-channels-aggregate ⑧ pins it with a hand-run pid-only negative control). Gate: test-channel-store (135).

Persistence primitives for `data/channels/` (design §5): `adapters.json`,
`index.json`, `msgs/<adapterId>/<convId>.ndjson`, `audit.ndjson`, `archive/`.
fs+path only.

**§5.1 — THE SERIALIZED INDEX OWNER.** `index.update(fn)` is the ONE mutation
door: a promise chain, so overlapping Lark and Gmail passes QUEUE rather than
race, and there is deliberately NO "write the whole index back" export for
anyone else to reach for. `writeJsonAtomic` is atomic at the FILESYSTEM layer
only; the read-modify-write AROUND it is not, and two passes are overlapping BY
DESIGN (single-flight is per ADAPTER). That is verbatim the round-4
`codex-zst` delta defect — *read-then-write with a size taken before the read
is a lost update waiting for the second caller* — and it is WORSE here, because
a clobbered ANCHOR makes the next pass SKIP messages rather than re-read them.
A snapshot read is NOT a lock: compute from it, apply inside `update()`
(nothing needs more — the ACL, the filter and the policy are all PURE).

Other invariants: appending is O(1) NDJSON while the index stays atomic JSON;
dedup by `(adapterId, convId, vendorId)` in a bounded per-conversation set
rebuilt from the log tail; the cursor advances ONLY after a complete pass and
the order inside that update is fixed (log first, anchor second, coalesced
flush last — a crash anywhere costs a re-read, which the dedup absorbs);
retention is 90 days or 5,000 records whichever is SMALLER with a **7-day
floor** (the estimator is defined over the last 7 days), streamed to a temp
file and renamed; a derived value (`unread`, `hits7d`) is cached for render
speed and always re-derivable. **The audit log rolls by DATE and the day comes
from the file's OWN last record, never from mtime** (mtime is a fact about the
filesystem — a backup or an rsync rewrites it), and the shard is APPENDED to,
never overwritten: a rotation that clobbers its own shard loses the reason it
exists (the slot-transitions lesson). Gate: scripts/test-channel-store.mjs.

**THE LOG SEALS A PARTIAL LAST LINE BEFORE IT GROWS (r3 — the other half of
the r2 dedup fix).** An append is not atomic: node's `writeFileSync` loops
`write(2)` and throws AFTER earlier chunks have landed, and a SIGKILL, an OOM
kill or a power loss leaves the same bytes — so the three errnos the header
names (ENOSPC, EIO, EDQUOT) are exactly the documented short-write producers
and the log can end in HALF A LINE. The r2 fix correctly left the dedup set
untouched on that throw, so the batch was re-offered — and appended straight
onto the fragment, which made its FIRST record one unparseable line
`readTail` skips while the durable set now (correctly) remembered its id:
every later pass reported it as a duplicate. One message, silently, for ever
(measured: v1..v5 offered, `v4` unreadable on disk, a later pass
`duplicates:2`). The r2 suite could not see it because its fixture — a
DIRECTORY where the log must be — is the one failure that writes ZERO bytes.
`appendRecords` now preads the last byte (only when the file is non-empty)
and writes a `\n` first if it is not one; the fragment stays as ONE
unparseable line the readers already skip, the write LOOPS until every byte
is out (`fs.writeSync` does not retry a short write), and the return carries
`healed`.

**A FAILED APPEND DROPS THE CACHED DEDUP SET (r4 — the half of the r2 rule
that was stated backwards).** r2 said "a failed append leaves no trace at
all" and deliberately left the set untouched on a throw. But the write that
threw may have landed a PREFIX of the batch, and those bytes are durable; the
seal recovers a prefix that stopped MID-record, while a prefix that stopped
exactly on a record boundary — after a record's `}` (sealed into a valid
line) or after its `\n` (nothing to seal) — is a complete record the log now
holds and the LIVE set still calls absent. So the SAME process re-offered the
batch, appended that record again, and the append-only log served it twice
for ever: `unread` and paging carried a phantom message and no reader removes
a line. A restart was already correct (the set is rebuilt from disk and
`readTail` parses a final line without `\n`), which is what pins the mechanism
to the stale live set. Measured on the real store with `fs.writeSync` landing
the prefix then throwing ENOSPC once — the module's own named errno: cut after
`\n` and cut after `}` both served `v1,v2,v3,v4,v4,v5` with `countSince(0)
=== 6` for five records; the mid-record cut, the ONLY shape r3's suite drove,
was fine — which is exactly why r3 could not see it. Reachability is narrow
(a short write that stops on a line boundary: block-aligned ENOSPC/EIO/EDQUOT
prefixes make it roughly one in an average line length per event) and the
outcome is permanent. Now `appendRecords` DELETES the conversation's cached
set when the write throws and the retry re-derives it from the log, byte-
identical to the restart; a throw BEFORE the write (`mkdirSync` — a file where
the adapter directory must be) lands nothing and the set stays, which is r2's
own shape and the reason the two rules are two: r2 is about what the set may
CLAIM, r4 about what it must FORGET. Controls, one per layer: reverting r2's
order alone shows the r4 belt HOLDING on the zero-byte EISDIR throw and
FAILING on the pre-write shape r4 cannot see; reverting r4 alone serves six
rows on both boundary cuts and is correct after a restart over the same log;
only reverting both reproduces r1 (test-channel-store ⑤b/⑤i; the engine
suite's r1 control reverts both for that reason).

**THE REBUILD REFUSES A LOG IT CANNOT READ (r5 — the r4 class one layer
over).** `dedupSet` is the ONE reader whose answer writes bytes, and it
derived the durable set from `readTail`, whose two catches collapsed EVERY
open/read error — EMFILE, EIO, EACCES, not only the routine ENOENT — into an
empty read. The empty set was then CACHED, so the next append wrote the whole
re-offered batch as "fresh", and a replayed boundary record (the shape Lark's
anchor semantics GUARANTEE at a page boundary) landed twice, permanently: a
witness that cannot be heard was read as a witness saying "nothing". The
rebuild runs on every conversation's FIRST append after a boot and after every
trim that rewrote the log, so the post-restart pass of every tracked
conversation went through it; EIO is one of the three errnos the module's own
header designs for and this instance's `data/` lives on a FUSE mount.
Measured on the real store (a fresh store over five records, `fs.openSync`
failing ONCE on the log at the rebuild, then the replay `[v5, v6]`): EMFILE,
EIO and EACCES each answered `{appended:2, duplicates:0}` and served
`v1..v5,v5,v6` with `countSince(0) === 7` for six records. Now `readTail`
takes `{ strict }`, and the rebuild asks it strictly: ENOENT is still "no log
yet" (a brand-new conversation's first append does not throw), anything else
is THROWN out of `appendRecords` — the pass fails, the anchor stays, the retry
re-reads, and nothing is cached at the throw — because a re-read costs a page
while a guess costs a phantom message nobody can remove. Every OTHER reader
stays lenient on purpose: a render-side `readTail` that shows nothing for one
tick self-heals, and `countSince` is a DERIVED number re-computed on the next
pass that is asked inside the index owner's `update()` after the anchor has
already moved in memory, where a throw would leave a half-applied update.
Controls: ⑤j drives all three errnos through the real module with the r4
bytes (both catches swallowing) as its negative control, plus the ENOENT
positive control and a plain-reader leg; and because r5 refuses BOTH of
⑤b's fixtures (a directory where the log must be, a file where the adapter
directory must be) before the set even exists, ⑤b's two arms and the engine
suite's r1 control now run on bytes with r5 stripped as well — a control
that a newer layer silently absorbs proves nothing about the layer it names.

**`readTail` SEEKS BACKWARD, ONE 2 MiB WINDOW AT A TIME (r3).** It read the
LAST `TAIL_BYTES` once and filtered by the boundary, so once the window's
paging walked past 2 MiB every page came back empty and the window just
stopped — while `trim()` deliberately keeps 5,000 records / 90 days, so at the
retention cap the oldest were unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION for any average
record over ~419 bytes (measured: 3,000 ordinary chat lines, 2.28 MiB, `trim`
keeps all 3,000, the window reached 2,625 — the r2 paging class one layer
down). The same reader rebuilds the DEDUP SET, so it also forgot everything
older than a window and a replayed old page would have been appended twice.
Now the walk reads earlier windows until `limit` candidates are in hand or
byte 0 is reached; a window's first line may be the TAIL of a line that began
earlier, so those bytes are carried as BYTES (a UTF-8 sequence can straddle
the cut) and joined onto the earlier window before decoding. The window's own
page (no boundary, 50 records) still costs one window; a caller asking for
more than a window holds — the dedup rebuild, `countSince` — reads the whole
log, whose size retention bounds. A record filed more than a window out of
`at` order is the one shape this cannot see, and the r2 reader could not
either. A log that cannot be read is still an EMPTY read, as in r2. Control: a
patched copy with the walk pinned to one window strands 375 of 3,000 and
forgets `m00000` in its set.

**Agent groups (2.369.159, design §22.5): `groups.json` is the THIRD file
behind the single-owner rule** — `store.groups.update(fn)` is the ONE door
(a promise chain, `writeJsonAtomic` after every run), `groups.live()` the
object it mutates, `groups.snapshot()` a copy; there is no `writeGroups(obj)`.
A group's LOG is not in that file: it is an ordinary conversation log
`msgs/groups/<groupId>.ndjson` through `appendRecords('groups', id, …)`, so
it inherits the dedup / seal / backward-seek / retention invariants above, and
a busy group rewrites `groups.json` only for its `lastAt`/`lastText` summary.

`groups.json` path (a planted second writer goes red).

**g3 (2.369.159, the IM-first group list — design §22):** `appendRecords` also answers `lastText` = the text of the newest record THIS append made durable (beside `lastAt`), so the channels engine can cache a conversation's LAST LINE on its index entry (`en.lastText`, one line, ≤ 160 chars) — a derived cache like `unread`, re-derivable from the log, never a fact. Now every JSON family the store owns (`index.json`, `adapters.json`, `outbox.json`, `groups.json`, `wake-pace.json`) loads through `loadJsonFamily`: MISSING (ENOENT) = an empty store; unreadable, unparseable or the wrong shape = the file is RENAMED to `<name>.corrupt-<ISO ts>` beside itself (bytes intact, never unlinked), ONE named `[channels] …` log line, an entry in `store.quarantined` `{file, to, why, at}` (the channels engine files ONE high-urgency "For you" item per entry, words as `i18n` structure), and only then does that family start empty; if the rename itself fails the family is BLOCKED (`blocked: true` in the entry) and its door rejects every write (the index flush skips with one line) rather than overwrite the only copy. `pace` (`live()` / `set(next)` / `flush()`) is the agent groups' WAKE PACE ledger — the engine hands it PURE-computed states; written 100 ms after a change (a burst is one write) and on `close()`. The store takes `log` now. Now `index.update` rejects BEFORE running `fn` exactly like the other three doors, every blocked door rejects with `blockedError(msg)` = `{code:'store-blocked', status:503}` (routes/channels.js `fail()` answers `{error, code}`, the panel's `routeErrorText` / `groupErrorText` word it), every refused index flush is logged, and a BLOCKED `wake-pace.json` is never overwritten either (its floors live in memory, each refused flush said).
