**R4 (2026-09-27):** a new index entry is born with `access: []` and `watchers: []` (the pre-R4 `assignment: null` is read by the engine's lift until the migration removes it); `accountAssignments` / `patternAssignments` keep their names and each record holds `{…, access, watchers}`.

**lane channel-threads (2026-09-28) — THE SIDE LOG.** Reactions are append-only SIDE records beside the message log: `msgs/<adapterId>/~side/<safeSeg(convId)>.ndjson` (a subdirectory, not `<convId>.side.ndjson` — a vendor conversation called `x.side` would collide with x's side log; `~` never appears in a `safeSeg` output; `search` never opens the subdirectory). `appendSide(adapterId, convId, sides)` dedups by `sideKey` (a vendor event id when there is one, else msg:key:actor:op:at; a snapshot by msg:at) with the r2/r4/r5 discipline of the message set (a failed write drops the set; an unreadable rebuild throws, nothing cached); `readSide(…, {msgs})` reads the NEWEST `SIDE_READ_BYTES` (2 MiB) of the file — never the whole file (verify r1: it read it whole, synchronously, on every page read and every broadcast fold) — and parses only lines whose head names a wanted message (the needle before the parse); `appendSide` COMPACTS the log in place past `SIDE_COMPACT_BYTES` (1 MiB) — every message's lines fold into one snapshot + its newest thread stat (`compactSide`, the trim's own fold) so a reaction storm on one message never outgrows the window; the compaction's OUTPUT is ordered by each message's last change (most recent last) and bounded to `SIDE_KEEP_BYTES` (512 KiB — the least recently changed folds forgotten, re-read by rule 20 when shown), so an already-compact log of many messages is never re-written per event (verify r1 continued: 5 000 snapshots = 5.4 MiB re-read + re-written whole on every event, 43 ms each, and old messages' new reactions folded outside the read window) (verify r1: 20 000 events on one message = 2.8 MiB read twice per page, for ever, because compaction ran only inside a MESSAGE trim); the engine reads the side lines ONCE per page (`withView` hands them to `reactionsFor`) and an event that NAMES its conversation still needs the message to be one that conversation holds (`not-in-conversation`, dropped by name — a line about nothing is never written); `trimSide` keeps each message's newest snapshot + the deltas after it and drops the lines of messages retention dropped — it runs inside `trim`, and also for a conversation that has a side log and no message log. **verify r2 (MONEY — THE COST CENSUS, test-channel-store ⑫): every side read is a bounded WINDOW — `sideWindow` / `sideLines` (the dedup rebuild, the compaction's input) read through `sideTail(…, SIDE_READ_BYTES)` like `readSide`, never `fs.readFileSync` (a line before the window is invisible to every reader, so the dedup set and a compaction fold exactly what readers see; a file longer than the window is always rewritten); a compaction that FAILS (its temp write or rename refused) is re-attempted only `SIDE_KEEP_BYTES` of appends later (`sideCompactFailedAt`) — it used to be retried per event, each attempt reading the whole growing file (6 ms / 2 MiB per event at 1 MiB, 21 ms / 6 MiB at 4 MiB). The census: (a) grep-derived — every store function touching a side file on a closed table with its bound, no whole-file read, writes = `appendLines` + temp/rename, nothing outside the store names the side log, no engine read widens the window; (b) bytes — 100 events on a 1 / 2 / 4 MiB log read ≤ one window each (524 KiB flat with a working compaction, ≤ 2 MiB with a failing one); (c) time — 2× the log ⇒ ≤ 2.5× (×1.4–1.7); controls: the pre-r2 store reads the whole growing log per event (2 → 6 MiB), a store bound to the pre-r1 quadratic compactSide reads ×2.9–3.0 per doubling.** `locateMessage(adapterId, vendorId)` = the bounded search a Lark reaction event needs (it names no chat) — **and the engine's `convOfMessage` in front of it (verify r1, MONEY / the event loop) remembers a MISS (`msgMiss`, 20 000 × 10 min; cleared by the write hook's positive memo when the message is stored later) and spends at most `LOCATE_PER_MIN` (30) store searches per account per minute, past which an unplaceable event is dropped `message-unknown` with `why:'locate-budget'` (acked; the next list snapshot is the truth for that message's counts). It used to read and scan EVERY message log of the account per event and never remember: measured 14.3 MiB read per event on a 12-conversation account, 717 MiB for 50 events on one unknown id — and Lark delivers a reaction event for every message of every chat the bot is in, listed here or not. Gate: test-channels-engine ⑰ (the th-poll block) + the memo-less copy as control.** The `onWrite` hook (`wrote(adapterId, convId, {kind: append|prepend|trim|side, fresh, msgs})`) keeps the engine's thread index and message → conversation map current. Invariant 8 holds: `countSince` / `readTail` / `search` never see a side line. Gate: test-channel-store ⑪ (+ its control).

**B-f32b (lane channel-index-copy, 2026-10-03) — ONE-ROW READS + THE INCREMENTAL INDEX WRITE.** `snapshot()` is the whole index (0.56 s at 50,274 rows) and never on a read path: `has(key)` = is there a row (no copy), `peek(key)` = that row copied, `live()` = a read-only scan. index.json is written from cached chunks of `INDEX_CHUNK` (256) rows, byte-identical to `writeJsonAtomic`'s `JSON.stringify(ix, RUNTIME_KEYS, 1)` (`writeBuffersAtomic`, tmp + rename). Which rows changed: `entry()` marks its row; an update's fn gets a view of the root whose `conversations` — like `live()` inside an update — marks EVERY row (the next write is whole); `rows()` + `touch(key)` scan inside an update and mark only what they change. `onTouch(fn)` hands the engine each touched key (null = all) after the update's fn returns; `close()` writes the whole serialization; every interval tick `sweep()`s `SWEEP_CHUNKS` (2) cached chunks and writes + says a row changed outside the door. `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_INDEX_VERIFY=1|<file>` compares every incremental write with the whole serialization (the gates' census; a drift is said, appended to <file>, and the whole file written). `flushStats()` = {full, incremental, fallback, swept, drift, lastFull, chunks}. Gate: scripts/test-channels-index-scale.mjs.


**`adapters.json` carries the listing cursor (lane discovery-cursor-persist, 2026-10-08):** each adapter record may hold `discovery: {cursor, startedAt, at, complete, completeAt}` — the engine's discovery walk state, written only through `adapters.update` (`writeJsonAtomic`) after the index flush that holds the rows the walk listed; a missing / malformed one heals to never listed (`Drain.discoveryOf`).
### src/oauth-loopback.js (SHARED)

**NO VENDOR DEFAULT (lane dc-channels-consent, 2.369.214).** The fixed mode's callback is the caller's: `begin({registeredCallbackUrl})` = its adapter's `consent.callbackUrl` (Lark: its registry row's `setup.callbackUrl`), beaten by the machine's `fixedCallbackUrl` override and by `begin({callbackUrl})`; none ⇒ `fixedTarget` refuses by name. The file no longer imports the registry.

**Lane lark-search-poll (2026-09-28, owner decision 5).** `optionalScopes` may be ORDERED GROUPS (an array per group; a bare string = a group of one; a scope keeps its first place): `narrow()` drops the NEXT group only, accumulates `narrowed`, names `nextNarrow` (`groups` + `nextNarrow` on `status()` and the engine's `safeFlow`), and answers `already-narrowed` only once every group is gone (the single-group sentence unchanged). The dialog chains the presses (`narrowOf` → `{scopes, dropped, run}`, `run()` → `{url, next}`; "Sign in without X" / "Sign in without Y too"). Gate test-oauth-loopback ⑨b.

**OPTIONAL SCOPES + THE ONE NARROWING RETRY + THE VENDOR'S ERROR REDIRECT (lane channel-threads, owner ruling 2026-09-28).** `begin({…, optionalScopes})` names scopes the consent asks for but can do without (Lark's `im:message.reactions:read`). A vendor whose app has not enabled one refuses the WHOLE consent on its own page — Lark error 20027 ("the scope parameter contains permissions the current application has not enabled"), shown on the authorize page, NEVER redirected (the vendor's docs name only `?error=access_denied&state=` as a redirect) — so this machine never hears it. `narrow(flowId)` is the person's retry: ONCE per flow (`already-narrowed` after; `nothing-optional`, `no-flow`), the SAME state / listener / timer, `buildConsentUrl({…, without})` rebuilt without the optional scopes, and the exchange gets `narrowed` so the account can say what Lark refused — never a silent narrower consent. `status()` carries `optional` + `narrowed`. The callback handler now reads the vendor's ERROR redirect (`?error=<code>&state=<ours>`, no code): the flow ENDS by name ("Lark did not grant the sign-in (access_denied) — nothing was connected"), reported once, the port released, the tab saying the same — it used to answer "connected — you can close this tab" and leave the flow running to its timeout; the `error` value is peer-written, bounded to 64 characters of a code's alphabet before it is said; paste-back of such a URL ends the flow the same way. Gate: test-oauth-loopback ⑨ (a fake authorize page: 20027 page ⇒ narrow ⇒ 302 ⇒ exchange told `narrowed`; access_denied; a hostile error value) + two patched copies (no once-guard; no error branch) as controls; test-channels-lark-shape ⑪ end to end through the real engine.

THE ONE consent-flow machine, DUAL-MODE (design §12.4, P1; node `http` +
`crypto` + the PURE registry only). `createOAuthLoopback({now, log})` →
`begin({id, mode, callbackUrl?, buildConsentUrl, exchange, onDone, timeoutMs})`
/ `status(flowId)` / `forwardCallback(flowId, url)` / `take(flowId)` /
`cancel(flowId)` / `stopAll()`. It knows no vendor: the caller hands in the
consent-URL builder and the token exchange; this module owns the listener,
the `state`, paste-back and the port's lifetime. Invariants, one sentence
each: `ephemeral` binds `listen(0, '127.0.0.1')` and the redirect_uri is the
bare origin (gmail-sync's flow, verbatim); `fixed` takes the port AND the
URL from the `lark` row's `setup.callbackUrl` (`LARK_CALLBACK_URL` is
IMPORTED — the registry suite asserts the literal never appears here) and
refuses a request on any other path; the fixed port is bound ONLY for one
flow and released on completion, cancel and timeout alike; `EADDRINUSE` is a
NAMED `port-busy` refusal naming the port and the flow keeps RUNNING on the
paste-back path with the registered redirect_uri (a remote browser takes that
path anyway); both `state` checks are gmail-sync's lines byte for byte
(the handler's `400 state mismatch`, paste-back's `state mismatch — restart
the flow`); one exchange per flow (a replayed callback or a second paste is
ignored); one running flow per `id` (a second `begin` supersedes). Gate:
scripts/test-oauth-loopback.mjs (57; every port under test is a FREE one).

**A FLOW'S END IS THE END OF WHAT IT HELD (client-from-mount verify r3, 2026-09-27).** The `exchange` closure an adapter hands in captures the vendor client — gmail.js captures the PLAINTEXT `clientSecret` (a storage mount's borrowed one since 2.369.195) — and this map used to keep every flow for the process lifetime: `take()` has no caller in src (the engine reads results through `onDone` + its pending record), `cancel()` and the timeout left the record in place, so a cancelled / timed-out / landed flow pinned its secret for ever and 10 000 begins pinned 10 000 copies; nothing capped running flows either. Three rules now, one sentence each: `forgetExchange(st)` drops the closure at every end (cancel / timeout / superseded unless an exchange is in flight — it consults `cancelled()` and drops on return — and after the exchange returned) [r4: `forget(st)` drops `onDone` WITH it — see the r4 paragraph], and a code landing on an ended flow is said by name on the flow's status ("… before its code arrived"), never exchanged [r4: said and logged, no longer reported through `onDone`]; an ENDED flow is RETIRED from the map `FLOW_RETIRE_MS` (30 min = the engine's `PENDING_FLOW_TTL_MS`) after `endedAt`, swept at every `begin()` and `status()` (the dialog's polling still reads it meanwhile; `take()` still forgets at once); at most `MAX_RUNNING_FLOWS` (32) run at once — `begin()` #33 ends the OLDEST running flow by name [r4: its cause `over-limit`, reported once] (a human never has 32 consents open; an automated caller cannot pin more listeners or clients). Both constants are exported. Gate: test-oauth-loopback ⑦ (the closure of a cancelled / timed-out / landed flow COLLECTABLE at its end — a FinalizationRegistry with gc forced through `v8.setFlagsFromString('--expose-gc')` + `vm.runInNewContext('gc')`, the running flow's not; status() until retirement then null; a paste-back onto a cancelled flow refused with zero exchanges; the cap) with a mutant copy (scripts/mutant-copy.mjs) without the two release lines as the control (it keeps every closure); test-channels-engine ⑮ pins the bound through the engine (33 pending `fromMount` begins ⇒ the first superseded by name, 32 running).

**VERIFY r4 (2026-09-27) — THE END DROPS EVERY CLOSURE THE ADAPTER HANDED IN; THE MACHINE'S OWN ENDS ARE SAID; begin()'s OWN EXITS.** (a) r3 dropped `exchange` and KEPT `onDone` "until a late code has been reported". Both adapters create the two in ONE scope (`const {clientId, clientSecret} = cred.values; … exchange: …, onDone: …`) and closures of one scope share one V8 context, so the kept `onDone` kept the plaintext: a heap snapshot of the REAL Gmail adapter after a cancel still held the borrowed secret (until retirement, 30 min) — r3's FinalizationRegistry probe passed no `onDone` and could not see it. `forget(st)` drops BOTH (returning the `onDone` for the one report an end may still owe); while an exchange is in flight both stay until it returns. (b) Nothing can therefore report a late code on an ended flow (its landing is SAID on the flow — `status().error` "… before its code arrived" — and logged, never exchanged) — and two ends are nobody's act but this machine's: the TIMEOUT and the CAP. Each is REPORTED ONCE through `onDone` (`{ok:false, result:null, error, cancelled}`, `endByItself`; the sentence also sits on `status().error`) and then forgotten; a caller's own cancel (cancel / a newer begin of the same id / stopAll / the engine's `expired` sweep) reports nothing, as before; mid-exchange the exchange's own return is the one report. Consumers: the engine's `onAuthDone` writes `lastAuthError` + `lastAuthAt` and broadcasts (the Re-authorize dialog's watcher and the card read it — r3's cap eviction and every timeout of an account's own flow used to end SILENTLY: the watcher waited its whole 10 min, the card just stopped saying "Signing in…"); `onPendingDone` marks the pending done with the sentence (the Connect dialog's polling reads it; Connect answers `409 flow-failed` for a flow that ended without finishing). (c) The cap's cause is its own name, `CAUSE_OVER_LIMIT` = `over-limit` (r3 called it `superseded`, the word `onAuthDone` / `onPendingDone` read as "a NEWER sign-in of this account stands" and swallowed: a cap eviction mid-exchange was logged as that and said nowhere); `channel-identity.cancelledSentence` words it ("ended to make room for newer sign-ins"). (d) begin()'s own exits: a flow ended while begin() awaits its listener (a same-tick second begin of its id, the cap, stopAll — `cancel()` had no server to release yet) closes the listener it was given at once (`bound()`), in fixed mode the registered port with it (it used to be held for the process lifetime: every later Lark sign-in port-busy); a `buildConsentUrl` that throws leaves no flow / listener / closure (it used to leave a listener, a running flow and NO timer); an error exit never deletes a NEWER flow's `byId` entry. Not reachable through the HTTP routes today (the bind completes within the request's own macrotask; 34 concurrent route begins leaked nothing) — reproduced through the engine API in one tick. Gate: test-oauth-loopback ⑧ — (a) closures the adapters' way + a copy whose cancel keeps `onDone` as the control; (b) the REAL Gmail (ephemeral) and Lark (fixed) adapters: the secret they resolved is GONE from a `v8.writeHeapSnapshot` after a cancel, searched by SHAPE (`GOCSPX-R4HEAP-<24 hex>`, minted at runtime as a FLAT string — a `+` makes a cons string the snapshot names "(concatenated string)"), present while running, STILL present over the copy that keeps `onDone`; (c) the timeout and the cap report once by name, a caller's cancel / supersede / stopAll nothing, mid-exchange one report; (d) same-tick double begins (both modes) leave no listener and the next fixed begin binds, a throwing `buildConsentUrl` leaves nothing, a copy without the post-bind check is the control. test-channels-engine ⑮ (12–14): a re-authorize ended by the cap is SAID on the account (a frame, the token kept); the agent-bearer census (below); test-channels-accounts-model pins the wording.

**2026-09-26:** the contract learned `older()` (gated by `caps.olderHistory` = `page` | `none`, `OLDER_HISTORY`), `fetchAttachment` (gated by `caps.attachments === 'fetch'`) and `caps.budget {unit: request | quota-unit, default, settingKey /^channels\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/, metered}` (`BUDGET_UNITS`; the ENGINE never names an adapter — it reads the unit and the setting key off the row); `history()` may return `changed` (a hint that more is due). The fake grew attachments (a PNG every third record), `older`, `fetchAttachment`, `meter`, and a `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE_CONVS=<n>` seam that adds n synthetic rooms per lane (the scale fixture test-channels-aggregate walks).

The adapter REGISTRY and its CONTRACT. An adapter owns exactly three things —
vendor auth, vendor paging, and the vendor's message shape — and never touches
the store, the ACL, the policy or the spend guard. **GATE ON THE CAPABILITY
ROW, NEVER ON AN ADAPTER ID**, the same discipline `src/backend-caps.js`
enforces for harnesses, with a grep census asserting no call site outside
`src/channels/` branches on `kind` (the kinds are DERIVED by requiring each
adapter module and reading the exports shaped like one, so a P1 adapter joins
the census with no edit — and the unrelated `kind === 'gmail'` of the Gmail
MOUNT never collides with it).

Enforced at registration and at call time: a DECLARED capability must be
implemented and an UNDECLARED one THROWS (`not-supported`) rather than
half-working; every failure is a TYPED `{code, retryable}` from a CLOSED set
and a bare throw out of an adapter becomes one; `history()` never returns
records the caller did not ask for, reports `reachedAnchor` honestly and
ADVANCES NOTHING; `convCaps()` is never WIDER than `caps`; on `sendAs: []`
`send()` is not a failure but a typed `send-not-available` and the outbox
creates no proposal; a `receive:'scan'` adapter must declare `scanSources`,
per-source `scanLatency` and a `historyBySource` covering every named source
with no value `'none'`.

The FAKE adapter is the P0 conformance driver and talks to NOTHING — its
traffic is deterministic from a fixed seed, so the panel, a restart and a
second client all see the same conversations. Three modules exercise both axes:
`fake-poll` (sendable), `fake-push` (a real `live.start()` on a timer, and
READ-ONLY so the no-send-control rule is observable) and `fake-scan` (BOTH
sources over the same traffic — `'store'` with the client's own ids,
`'ui'` with keys minted deterministically from the message itself and marked
`raw.synthetic`, so re-scanning the same screen is a no-op by construction).
Enabled by `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE=1` — registered always, instantiated never
otherwise. Gate: scripts/test-channel-adapter-contract.mjs.

**THE DEDUP SET REMEMBERS ONLY WHAT IS DURABLE (r2, critical).** That set's
whole meaning is "the log already holds this", and `rememberVendorId` ran
inside the SELECTION loop — before `appendFileSync` — so ONE transient write
failure (ENOSPC, EIO, EDQUOT, or ENAMETOOLONG from a long percent-encoded
vendor convId) made every record in the batch a PERMANENT duplicate: the next
pass reported `appended:0, duplicates:N`, the engine read that as a complete
pass and advanced the anchor PAST messages that were never written. Silent,
permanent message loss with no crash and no error, and the exact opposite of
invariant 4's promise. Reproduced end to end on the real engine + real store
(vendor holds 9, log holds 0, anchor at `…-m8`, unread 0, and pass 3 changes
nothing). Now: SELECT against the durable set, WRITE, and only THEN remember;
duplicates WITHIN one batch are held in a local set that dies with the call;
what a FAILED write may have landed is the r4 paragraph above (the r2 wording
"a failed append leaves no trace at all" was false and is retired).

**THE PAGING ORDER IS `(at, vendorId)` — A TOTAL ORDER, NOT A TIMESTAMP (r2).**
`at` is not unique (a Lark burst shares a millisecond, Gmail's `internalDate`
is second-derived), so paging on it alone with a strict `<` made every record
of such a group at or after a page boundary PERMANENTLY UNREACHABLE — the
bytes on disk, no way to scroll back to them (measured: 12 records in groups
of three, paged exactly as the window pages, `m0,m3,m6,m9` never served).
`vendorId` is unique per conversation BY INVARIANT 2, so the pair is a genuine
strict total order; `readTail` takes `before` AND `beforeId`, SORTS by that
order before slicing (ranking on one order and slicing by another is what made
the boundary ambiguous), and a caller that cannot name a boundary record still
gets a terminating — if lossy — page.

**`adapters.json` HAS THE SAME SINGLE OWNER AS THE INDEX (r2).** It was the
read-modify-write shape invariant 3 exists to eliminate: every caller
re-parsed the file and wrote its own private array back, so a failing
adapter's persisted health was wiped by a healthy neighbour's pass landing
second — measured, five failing passes of an auth-expired adapter persist
`consecutiveFailures: 5` alone and `0` with a neighbour passing beside them,
so the amber "{n} failed passes ({code})" row, the ONE honesty signal that
compensates for a static freshness chip, is exactly what got clobbered (and in
P1 that file also holds `push.demotedAt` / `push.missRate` / `scan.hostFacts`,
where a clobbered demotion is §6.4's "a lane that lies about being active
turns the fallback OFF"). `store.adapters.live()` hands back THE object, read
once at construction; `store.adapters.update(fn)` is the only way bytes land;
and there is deliberately no `writeAdapters(obj)` for anyone to hand a private
copy to, for the same reason there is no `writeIndex`.

**`index.entry(a, c, { create: false })` IS THE LOOKUP FORM (r2).** "Create on
first touch" is right for the ingest pass — discovery is where a conversation
is born — and wrong everywhere else.

**A SCAN ADAPTER'S SOURCE IS HANDED DOWN, NEVER RE-DERIVED (r3).**
`scanState()` in src/channel-caps.js is the ONE resolver of which source is
carrying a conversation, and the shipped fake kept a `source()` closure that
fell back to `caps.scanSources[process.platform]` — a SECOND resolver, two
lines under its own comment saying there was none — which is how the engine
ingested through a lane the real resolver had just declared unavailable.
`history(convId, opts)` on a scan adapter now REQUIRES `opts.source` (one the
adapter's own `historyBySource` names) and the registry wrapper refuses a page
without it with the typed `not-supported` + `detail.needs:'source'`; a
non-scan adapter ignores the field (the rule is gated on the capability row).
The fake reads `opts.source` and nothing else, and the contract suite carries
a census: no adapter module under src/channels/ reads `scanSources[` /
`scanSources &&` (a declaration writes `scanSources: {`) or `process.platform`
outside `scanHost()`, whose job is to REPORT the platform.

**R4 (B-6acc, 2026-09-27): `caps.compose` (boolean) DECLARES a NEW conversation — `METHOD_GATES.compose` + `composeCaps` require it AND a non-empty `sendAs` (a read-only adapter composes nothing; a fixture that spreads a sendable fake's caps with `sendAs: []` stays valid). `compose({to, cc, subject, text, idemKey, as, onHandle})` is gated like `send`; `composeCaps()` (the ACCOUNT's send identity, no conversation) is NARROWED to `caps.sendAs` exactly like `convCaps`. The poll fake declares compose (the same text markers as `send`; the thread id a function of the key; `record.fakeNoSendScope` = no send permission); the push fake is read-only.**

### src/channels/lark.js + src/channels/gmail.js (ORCH)

lane channel-feed-authority: gmail declares `changeFeed {via:'history', authority:'authoritative'}`; `changes()` = the pass's ONE history.list → `{changed, conversations (unnamed changed threads from the query's head page), mustWalk}`; the reseed walk (listConversations under `mustWalk`) judges each listed thread's historyId against the lost cursor (`walkFrom`, persisted `gmailWalkFrom`) — no per-thread read.


**Lane lark-threads (2026-10-01).** **A2 `recentRoots(convId, {limit})`** — ONE `im/v1/messages` page, `container_id_type=chat`, newest first, NO anchor / page token / time window (the doc: a chat listing returns a topic's ROOT only, carrying `thread_id` once the topic exists — "不返回说明该消息不是话题形式的消息"); items of another chat dropped. **A4 `messageById(convId, {messageId})`** — ONE `GET im/v1/messages/:message_id` (user token; `data.items`, a merged forward's children beside the parent), judged by the PURE `readByIdAnswer` (closed set `BYID_KINDS` absent / foreign / deleted / reply / root / plain; ≤ BYID_ITEMS_MAX items, ids ≤ 512): a thread REPLY → a record of its chat + the root's patch. Both through `api()` (paced + metered) and gated on the threads / feed rows (`METHOD_GATES`). **B (MEASURED 2026-10-01: `contact/v3/users/:id` of another person under `contact:user.base:readonly` alone = 99991679 naming `contact:contact.base:readonly`)** — the consent asks `PEOPLE_SCOPE` + the field scopes `contact:user.employee:readonly` (job_title) / `contact:user.department:readonly` (department_ids) as three optional groups after the reactions (one dropped per refused consent); `PEOPLE_GRANT` (the card's "One Re-authorize adds: reading people's profiles"); `lookupPerson` / `peopleFor` (inside `allNamesFor`, so every page path): no lookup without a PEOPLE_READ_SCOPES scope held, ≤ PEOPLE_LOOKUPS_PER_CALL (3) a page — the UNNAMED first —, ≤ PEOPLE_PER_MIN (20) a minute per account, cached 6 h module-wide (`PEOPLE`, hits and refusals; a 99991679 stops every lookup of the account 6 h and is said once), a department's name 24 h (`DEPTS`, the brand's language); `toRecord` names an unnamed person from the cache, carries `author.alt` {enName, nickname, jobTitle, department}, `raw.tenant_key` and `author.external` (the sender's tenant ≠ the account's own — the consent's user_info `tenantKey`, else learned from the member list / the owner's own messages, never a call); `recordView` fills an older record from the cache; a dissolved chat (232009) is said ONCE and its members asked again after 24 h. The search's first-page probe line also prints `display_info`'s sub-field NAMES and how many hits carry a thread id. The members API lists no bots ("该接口不会返回群组内的机器人成员"; member_id_type open_id / user_id / union_id) — a bot is named by the application API only. Gates: test-channels-lark-shape ⑮ (A, doc-shaped) + ⑯ (B). **Verify r1 F3:** a `rate-limited` / `transport` answer on a profile or department read is the VENDOR's moment — the id is not remembered (it was, 6 h), `peopleRefusedUntil` = now + the vendor's Retry-After (else 60 s, ≤ 5 min; `peoplePauseMs`), and `peopleFor` asks a known person's department again after the pause within the same ≤ 3-per-page bound (`canReadDepts`).
**Verify r2 (lane lark-threads, the vendor-budget class).** A RATE refusal inside a read is the READ's: `namesFor` (the members page), `lookupPerson`, `departmentName`, `describe`'s chat lookup and `appNamesFor` THROW a `rate-limited` error to the pass (the account's ladder honours the vendor's hint and stops every shape) instead of catching it — a caught 429 kept the pass reading at pace into the vendor's stop, sent the page's profile reads after a members 429, remembered the members page refused 6 h and re-asked a 3600 s hint every 5 min. The local pause (`peopleRefusedUntil`, ≤ 5 min) stays as the guard AFTER the back-off; a transport blip still only pauses; the push path's `toRecord` catches as before (the record is built with the names it has). **Security verify r2 (2026-09-28) — gmail.js, one bounded walk:** `stripHtml` (the agent's text of an HTML-only mail, at ingest) was a regex chain quadratic on `<` / an unclosed `<style` (64 KB = 1.2 s, 128 KB = 4.7 s, no cap) — now ONE walk cut at `STRIP_HTML_MAX` 512 KiB (a tag's `>` and a raw-text closer each looked for once); `parseAddress` (the From header) was a lazy regex quadratic on `<` — now the LAST `<…>` pair found once, cut at `ADDRESS_MAX` 2 KiB. **Reply placements (2026-09-28):** Lark declares `threads.placements: ['chat','quote','thread']`, `rootReply: 'quote'` (threads are opt-in; a message already in a topic is answered there — PL3; no reply_broadcast, so no `thread+chat`), and `sendImpl` takes `placement` — `thread` sets `reply_in_thread`, `quote` is the plain reply endpoint, `chat` the chat endpoint (the `inThread` alias still honoured for a direct caller); Gmail declares `['chat','quote']`, `rootReply: 'quote'` (every reply lands in the mail thread = the conversation; `chat` answers its newest message); the built-in Agents adapter (src/channels/agents.js) `['chat']` only (the ladder answers no message — a `--to` there is `placement-not-offered` why `no-replies`). test-channels-lark-shape pins the three endpoints and the registry's refusal of `thread+chat` / chat-with-a-message with no request.

**Lane channels-full-search (2026-10-03, design 010, B-c9be) — THE VENDOR'S OWN SEARCH.** Two tiers: the store scan (`store.search`, newest conversation first by the index's `lastAt`, `coverage {scanned, total, capped, oldestAt}`) and, on the owner's Search press, the vendor's own search (`caps.search` row; `engine.searchVendor` ← `GET /api/channels/search/full?adapter&q[&page]`; `engine.aroundOwner` ← `GET /api/channels/:a/:c/around?msg&at`), never stored (F8: a log is contiguous from its oldest). Agents: `searchFor(ctx, q, {full})` → `searchFullFor` (one page, `agentShareRefusal`, `SR.AGENT_FLOOR_MS` per account per agent conversation, reach after the await), `readAroundFor` (`read?around=`). VS1–VS4 land on `rec.feed.counters.fullSearch` (`presses, pages, hits, olderThanStored, unknownConv, shape, cjk/other {queries, of, holding}, around {reads, withTarget, before, after}`); VS3's flip = lark.js `caps.search.match`. **Lane around-sheet-fix (2026-10-03, 2.369.205) — THE "AROUND THIS MESSAGE" SHEET DRAWS AS THE WINDOW.** The owner's screenshot (zh, a Lark full-history hit → 这条消息前后, 「这啥玩意啊！」): every row cut at the left ("李天雨" → "雨"), the avatar ON the name and the first line, a sideways scrollbar, a picture "图片 未找到 重试". Measured on 3452dce3 (test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑪b): `.chanmsg`'s `padding-left: calc(6px + var(--chan-gutter))` is INVALID outside a list that defines `--chan-gutter` ⇒ 0, under the row's `margin: 0 -6px` ⇒ the name and first line 6 px left of the box, the absolute avatar (`left: 6px`) over both, `scrollWidth` 6 px over `clientWidth`, the found row 21 px off centre; the picture asked our attachment route, which serves only a record of OURS (channel-attachments `fetchVerdict` rule 3 — the route is not a proxy) ⇒ `not-found` + Retry. THE FIX: the sheet's list is `chanwin-list chan-around-list` (the outbox's way — ONE rule for gutter, padding, scroll; the sheet only caps `max-height: 60vh`, `flex: 0 1 auto`); `renderAroundRows(records, {focus})` renders `renderRecord(…, {unsaved: true})` rows — a file is `unsavedChip` ("not saved — open the conversation to see it", no link, no Retry, nothing asked; the vendor read is not allowed for a record never stored) — with the window's day separators (a run folds within a day); the found row is centred by the list's own `scrollTop` (vertical only — `scrollIntoView` scrolls every ancestor); `dayLabel` names another year's day WITH its year (the sheet reaches years back). Fixture: the fake vendor's archive gains `<kind>-ops-old-pic` (李天雨, a Lark-shaped `[image]`; never matches a search). Gate ⑪b (zh / en / ja, desktop + 390 px, a fresh page each): every row's avatar, name, first line and chip inside the list, the avatar on none of them, `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, the found row centred with the page unscrolled, the chip's words with zero `/attachment/` asks, the picture's day named with its year.

**Lane channels-followups (2026-10-03, designs 008 S6 + 010 S6) — THE AGENT'S LIST BOUNDED; GMAIL'S OWN SEARCH.** `engine.listFor` sorts what the caller may see by `lastAt` (reach asked of every row — the count needs it) and builds only the newest `LIST_FOR_MAX` (200) — the answer's `more` / `moreRequestable` (the `--all` directory titles, the same bound) / `max`; a hidden conversation is in neither count; the CLI prints one "… N more … use search" line. Gmail declares `caps.search {via:'query', scope:null, pageSize:10, pagesPerPress:2, perMin:6, cost:205 (= unitsFor list + 10 metadata reads), snippet:true, context:'thread', match:'tokens'}`: `search({query, pageToken, storedAt, shows})` = `messages.list?q=` (no label filter — the whole mailbox but spam/trash), then per id: not shown to the caller ⇒ dropped with no read at all (vendor or local log); held locally ⇒ the hit at its stored instant with no read; else ONE `messages.get format=metadata` (internalDate, From, `snippet` through `SR.snippetOf`); `around` = ONE `threads.get format=full`, ≤ 50 centred on the hit, no memo / title cache / held body. **Lane vendor-search-memo (2026-10-07, design 010 as-built, .230; the owner: 「调用 channel provider 自己的在线搜索的时候缓存结果，避免重复点开搜索对话框结果就限速了」) — THE VENDOR'S OWN SEARCH IS ASKED ONCE.** `src/channel-search.js` (PURE) owns THE MEMO: `searchMemo(state, {op: get|put|clear})` → `{state, answer}` (a new state each step), key = (scope, `memoQuery` = trimmed / case-folded / spaces collapsed), scope = `'all'` (the owner) or `memoScope(convIds)` (an agent's visible set, FNV of the sorted ids — its hits were read for those only); an entry = the pages asked so far `{token, hits (merged, snippet-bearing), next}` + the first press's `askedAt` (TTL `SEARCH_MEMO_TTL_MS` 10 min runs from it; a later page APPENDS when it follows the last page's `next`), LRU by Map order (≤ `SEARCH_MEMO_MAX` 64 entries, ≤ `SEARCH_MEMO_BYTES` 2 MiB an account, UTF-16 estimate; one answer over the cap is not kept). `fullSearchVerdict` gains two rows after needs-scope: `memo` → `{act:'memo'}` (before back-off / floor / minute / budget — a remembered answer costs nothing) and `peek` → `{act:'unasked'}`; `memoText(ageMs)` / `statusText({state:'unasked'})` are the words. `channels-engine.js` `vendorSearch(rec, query, {scope, again, peek, …})` keeps the memo on the account's LIVE entry (`e.searchMemo` — `dropLive` on any account change drops it; a restart forgets it; NEVER persisted): `again` (a press) clears the caller's entry and skips the read; the read lists `['all', scope]` (an agent reads the owner's first); a hit re-merges against the store (a since-stored hit leaves, nothing re-asked) and answers `pages: 0, memo: {askedAt, ageMs}` with no floor stamped and no VS measurement; only a whole answer is remembered (a refusal, a failure, a partial or an outlived entry never). `searchVendor` passes `again` / `peek` (press-only, never with a token) and says `memo` / `unasked`; GET /api/channels/search/full reads `again=1` / `peek=1`. `channels-access.js` `searchFullFor` passes `scope: SR.memoScope(visible.keys())` and answers `remembered: {ageSec}` (the CLI's line: "answered these N min ago — remembered for 10 min, not asked again"). `src/lib/channels-panel.js` `showSearchDialog`: `run('open')` (pre-filled from an agent's row or the panel) asks section two with `peek=1` — the memo or "Press Search to ask {vendor}'s own search", never the vendor; a press without `peek` reads the memo server-side; a remembered answer's status line carries ` · From {vendor}'s search N min ago · ` + a **Search again** button (`.chan-search-again`, per account: that account's rows leave + their keys leave `shown`, then `again=1`). **Lane search-card-open (2026-10-07, 2.369.233; the owner: 「既然 agent 进行了搜索说明 vibespace 已经获取到了相关 data，为啥我点不开？」) — WHAT THE AGENT FOUND OPENS.** `src/channel-search.js` THE MEMO has no TTL (64 entries / 2 MiB an account, LRU) and FANS a put per conversation (`memoConv`, ≤ `SEARCH_MEMO_FAN`) + `all` when `covers`; derived entries have no page token; `memoToDisk` / `memoFromDisk` = the file; `isMemoScope` = the only scope read off a request; `memoText` (by, date) / `forgottenText`. `src/channel-store.js` `searchMemoRead / Write / Drop` = `<account>/search-memo.json`. `src/server/channels-engine.js` `memoOf` / `memoKeep` / `forgetSearchMemo` (dropLive: disconnected / removed; identity check at load); `searchVendor(…, {memo, convId})` ⇒ reads [memo, all, conv:<id>]. `src/server/channels-access.js` searchFullFor passes `covers` and returns `memoScope` (agent-routes moves it onto the search touches, off the answer). `src/channel-touch.js` a search touch's `memo` → openVerdict / tailVerdict; `src/lib/channels-panel.js` showSearchDialog(`memo`, `searchedAt`): section two shows the remembered hits; the agent count is its head.

**Lane lark-search-poll (2026-09-28) — THE CHANGE FEED.** `caps.changeFeed = {via:'search', scope:'search:message', option:'search', pageSize:30, pagesPerPass:5, perMin:10, maxWindowSec:3600, catchUp:{chatType:'p2p', pagesMax:20}, describes:true, timeUnit:'ms'}`, `pace.cost.feed = 1`. `changes({from, to, pageToken, chatType, pageSize})` = `POST /im/v1/messages/search?user_id_type=open_id&page_size=30[&page_token]` with body `{query:'', time_range:{start_time, end_time}(ISO whole seconds), chat_type?}` (U9: pagination in the query string, Lark's POST-search convention); each `meta_data` → `Feed.normalizeHit` in ms (U1: the id is `meta_data.message_id`, else the item's `message_id` / `id`); `display_info` is never read, kept or logged; the first page's field NAMES are logged once per process. `describe(convId, {peerIds})`: the chat lookup's `name` → else the PEER (not this account) via `contact/v3/users/:id` (cached `MEMBERS_TTL_MS`) → else `title:null` (the client words "Single chat"). U7: a single chat the chat lookup refuses reads `read:'yes'` once its history answered (`p2pRead`), narrowing only; its authors are named by the contact lookup when `/members` refuses. `typedFailure` reads a 403's `detail.requiredScopes` from the vendor's own words (the first 4 KiB, ≤ 8 whole scope tokens ≤ 64 chars). Consent: option `search` (on by default — off drops both scopes); `OPTIONAL_SCOPE_GROUPS` = [[reactions:read], [p2p_msg:get_as_user], [search:message]] (least valuable first — each narrowing press drops ONE group); `FEED_GRANT {scopes:[search:message, p2p_msg:get_as_user], console:true, option:'search'}` (registry-validated like `reactionsGrant`). **Lane lark-p2p (2026-09-30, the owner: "我怎么在频道里还是看不到lark私聊？") — THE MEASURED HIT SHAPE; the paragraph above is superseded where they differ.** The shape is READ from the vendor's own answer: the production probe (2.369.198) printed `display_info, id, meta_data; meta_data: chat_id, create_time, from_id, is_p2p_chat, message_id, position, type`, and the doc (im-v1/message/search, `message_search_item`) spells the same item — `{ id, display_info, meta_data: { message_id, type, create_time (ISO 8601 STRING, e.g. `2026-03-21T16:15:30+08:00`), update_time?, position, chat_id, from_id, thread_id?, thread_position?, is_p2p_chat (boolean) } }`; the request body is `{query:'', filter:{time_range:{start_time,end_time}, chat_type?}}` — the window and the chat type are fields of `filter`. The .197 lane declared `timeUnit:'ms'` (every hit `no-time` ⇒ 241 260 malformed, 0 single chats born) and sent `time_range` / `chat_type` at the TOP level, where the vendor does not read them (every page answered the whole history: 8 043 pages, the window never completed — invisible because no hit was readable). Now `caps.changeFeed.timeUnit:'iso'`, `reader: 2` (the hit reader's revision — the engine restarts a feed row an older reader wrote); THE ONE READER `readSearchHit(item, {now, unit})` (PURE, exported): an object, `meta_data` an object, the message id from `meta_data.message_id` else the item's `id`, `is_p2p_chat` boolean or its string, the instant via `Feed.readTime` in the declared form, `display_info` never read; an unreadable hit is malformed BY NAME (`fields`: `meta_data.chat_id` / `meta_data.message_id` + `id` / `meta_data.create_time` / `meta_data.thread_id` / `meta_data` / `item`) and `changes()` returns `malformedFields` (≤ 3 distinct lists). The first-page probe now also prints the `create_time` FORM (`valueFormOf`: iso8601 / digits(13) / … — never a value) and how many hits this version could not read (with the fields). `describe()` is unchanged (a single chat named by its peer through the contact lookup). Gate test-channels-lark-shape ⑬ over scripts/fixtures/lark/search.json (page1 = EXACTLY the probe's field list, pinned against `observedFields`; the probe line over it reproduces the production line verbatim) + ⑬b: a doc-faithful vendor (reads the window only in `filter`) with the .197 top-level body as the control (a month-old hit ⇒ `time-range-ignored`); the .197 invented page as the old-shape control (five hits naming `meta_data.create_time` ⇒ the shape park ⇒ the card's words); the .197 `ms` declaration over the observed page as the incident's control; births from the observed page (three single chats, two group hints); the reader bounded before parse. **Verify r2 — THE ENVELOPE IS JUDGED BEFORE THE PAGE IS TRUSTED:** `changes()` refuses a 200 that is not a search page — no `data` object, no boolean `has_more` (the doc's one required field), `has_more: true` with no `page_token`, `items` not a list — as the search's OWN retryable `vendor-error` (`detail.envelope` = the field; the feed's 30 s → 15 min ladder, the cursor held), never the 24-h contract park; `has_more: false` with no items is an empty page. It used to RETURN `more: false` for every one of them, and the engine completed the window and moved its cursor past everything it still held (measured: 470 of 500 hits on a page that said has_more with no token). Gate ⑬'s envelope table + the token-trusting copy as the control.

The module-level `APP_NAMES` cache (app id names one application whichever account reads it; ≤ 2000) keeps a hit AND a refusal for MEMBERS_TTL_MS (6 h; a transient failure 5 min) and the refusal is said ONCE (naming the scope `admin:app.info:readonly`); a mention with `id_type: app_id` seeds a name for free (never over the API's). The push lane waits ≤ NAMES_WAIT_MS for the same resolver. **`recordView(record)`** (on the module object; the registry validates it; the engine's `viewOf` runs it on EVERY read — the window's page, an agent's `read`, both searches): a stored bot called "app" / "" / a fallback gets `appNameOf(id)`, a stored text with markup is read by `larkPlainText` — the store is never rewritten. **D2 (Gmail):** see src/mail-frame.js — `walkParts` keeps the text/html part as the `role: 'body'` attachment (+ `cid` from `Content-ID` / `X-Attachment-Id` on every picture), `toRecord({onBody})` + the instance's `heldAttachment` hand its bytes to the engine at ingest. **R3 (2026-09-26, "lark图像不能预览吗？"):**
- `IMAGE_TOKEN` / `VIDEO_TOKEN` are spelled once. `textOf` writes them, and `attachmentsOf` carries them as the attachment's `placeholder`.

GMAIL: 40 quota units/s (one threads.get a second; `cost` fetch 40, discover 10 + META_PER_LIST × 40), `vendorName: 'Google'`; `unitsFor` is pinned against the vendor's table of 2026-09-10 (test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥b); `typedFailure(status, body, what, retryAfterSec)` — 429, a rate/usage reason (`rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, `quotaExceeded`, `dailyLimitExceeded`), a 403 in `usageLimits` or naming a quota metric ⇒ `rate-limited` carrying `detail.retryAfterSec` (`Retry-After` via `retryAfterSeconds(r.headers)`); any other 403 stays `forbidden`. LARK: 5 requests/s (10 % of tier 4's 50/s per app per tenant), cost 1 per action, paced on the token refresh and the resource fetch too; `x-ogw-ratelimit-reset` rides the refusal; `vendorNameOf(record)` = the record's brand (Feishu default / Lark) on the registered adapter object. `retryAfterSeconds(headers, now)` lives in src/channels/index.js (delta-seconds, HTTP-date, `x-ogw-ratelimit-reset`); `validateCaps` refuses a pace without a budget, a non-positive rate, a non-channels.* key, a cost for an action the drain does not price (`PACE_COSTS` = fetch / discover / scanHost), an empty vendor name. fake.js carries three FIXTURE seams for test-channels-e2e ⑰ only (`VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE_PACE` / `_VENDOR` at module load, `_RATE_LIMIT=<n>[:<s>]` per adapter).
