THE TWO REAL READ ADAPTERS (design §6.3, §12.1, §12.2, §13, §14.2; P1a). Each
is a `{kind, caps, create}` module behind the §4 contract plus the facts the
engine reads by name and never by kind: `label`, `integration` (the registry
row it consumes), `integrationTest` (the row's Test runner), `OPTIONS` (the
per-record options the panel edits) and `EGRESS` (every host the file may
construct a request to — the census's declaration). Invariants, one sentence
each: the application credential is asked of `deps.resolveIntegration(id)` and
NEVER of `process.env`, and `auth.state()` takes that answer as an INPUT, so a
withdrawn cluster default or cleared user key is `needs-credentials` however
fresh the token record looks; a refresh the vendor refuses (`invalid_grant`, a
dead grant) is STAMPED on the token record (`invalidGrantAt`) and answered
`needs-reauth` from then on instead of being retried every pass; the token is
the ENGINE's (`deps.tokens.read/write/clear`, encrypted at rest by the engine's
own secret-box), never written by the adapter anywhere else; Lark pages
`im/v1/messages` NEWEST-FIRST to the stored anchor across several `history()`
calls of ONE pass (a continuation is recognised by the anchor the previous
call returned; `FIRST_INGEST_MAX` bounds a fresh chat; both `page_token` and
`next_page_token` are read; an anchor the vendor no longer serves is read past
and SAID); Gmail treats a THREAD as the conversation under the include query,
runs ONE memoised `history.list` per pass (404 = reseed from the profile and
walk every tracked thread once; a dead thread is skipped and said) and keeps
the mailbox cursor in memory on purpose (mailbox-wide, only safe to advance
once every named thread was walked); every vendor body becomes plain text
through `makeRecord` (channel-record's neutering applies); every failure is a
typed `ChannelError` from the closed set; Lark's `brand` option is read at
construction (`rebuild:true`), Gmail's `query` is read LIVE off the record;
the push lane is P1's second half. P4 SENDING: both declare `sendAs:
['user']` and `convCaps` NARROWS to `[]` with `why:'send-scope-not-granted'`
until the HELD token carries the send scope(s) — Lark's dotted pair
`im:message` + `im:message.send_as_user`, Gmail's `gmail.send` — which the
consent now requests (one re-consent for an older token; the UI says what
unlocks it, never a greyed control). Lark: `idempotency:'key'` — ONE request
with `uuid` = the idempotency key (`uuidFor`: hashed past 50 chars), a reply
hits the reply endpoint, a transport failure AFTER the request left is
`detail.lost` (never a refusal), the response's `sender.sender_type` rides back
as `observed` (the §21-item-3 proof) while `identityMarking` stays `unknown`
in code until one real send is read; `reconcile()` scans the chat newest-first
back to the send instant for our own text, re-issues the SAME uuid inside the
vendor's dedup hour (exactly-once by construction), and answers `landed:false`
only on a COMPLETE scan past the hour — else `unknown` with the reason. Gmail:
`idempotency:'two-phase'` — ONE anchor read decides To (Reply-To/From, ours ⇒
its To) / `Re:` subject / In-Reply-To + References off the anchor's Message-ID
(never invented), `drafts.create` in the thread is the durable handle handed to
`onHandle` and awaited BEFORE `drafts.send`; a phase-1 transport failure is a
refusal (a stray draft is said), a phase-2 one is `detail.lost` with the handle;
`reconcile()` = the draft still exists ⇒ never sent (discarded, `landed:false`)
/ gone + our SENT message in the thread ⇒ `landed:true` / else `unknown`, with a
handle-less `drafts.list` fallback.
Fixtures: scripts/fixtures/{lark,gmail}/recorded.json (recorded vendor
shapes; no real credential on this box, so the real-session exit stands in
as the recorded fixture and says so). Gates: scripts/test-channels-lark-shape.mjs
(84) + scripts/test-channels-gmail-shape.mjs (90, the cluster-only two-preset
instance end to end through the REAL store + REAL engine + the REAL ephemeral
loopback) + scripts/test-channels-egress.mjs (19: the §3.1 census — every host
literal in a request-constructing server-side file is a claim, an adapter's
judged by its own `EGRESS` both ways, every other `(file, host)` by an allowlist
WITH a reason seeded with gmail-sync + mounts, dead entries red, IPv4/loopback
and RFC 2606 hosts exempt, a host held in a VARIABLE stated as the boundary) +
test-channel-adapter-contract.

**P1b (2026-09-16): both adapters declare `receive:'push'` and build their
`live` half in `create()` from the closures they already own** — Lark over
`createLarkLive` (the SDK long connection; member names awaited at most
`NAMES_WAIT_MS` on the push path because the record must be durable inside
the vendor's 3 s ack), Gmail over `createGmailLive` (`pushOptIn: true`, the
watch + pull loop over its own `api()`/token; `OPTIONS` gained `pushTopic` +
`pushSubscription` with `relive:true` = a change restarts the LANE, never the
adapter; `scopesFor()` adds the pubsub scope to the NEXT consent only while
the switch is on; `callJson` learned a `json` body for `users.watch`). The
lane normalizes through the SAME `toRecord()` the poll uses (one normalizer,
two arrivals — invariant 2). `live/lark.js` declares an EMPTY `EGRESS` (the
SDK owns the connection); `live/gmail.js` declares `pubsub.googleapis.com` +
the scope host, and the census judges live lanes as adapters.

**R4 (B-6acc, 2026-09-27) — Gmail COMPOSE:** `caps.compose: true`; `composeCaps()` = `gmail.send` held or `[]` + `send-scope-not-granted` (no vendor call); `compose()` = ONE `messages.send` of a fresh RFC-822 message (no threadId, From = the account, To / Cc / Subject, its OWN `Message-ID` `<idem.hash@domain>` = the handle, handed to `onHandle` BEFORE the request; `drafts.*` is NOT used because it needs `gmail.compose`, which the consent never asks for); a transport failure after the request left = `detail.lost` + the handle; `reconcile(null, {compose, handle})` = `messages.list q=in:sent rfc822msgid:<id>` — found ⇒ landed with the message + thread ids, absent ⇒ honestly unknown (search lags), no handle ⇒ unknown by name; `unitsFor('/messages/send')` = 100. Lark declares no compose ⇒ the engine's `compose-not-available`. Gate: test-channels-gmail-shape ⑧b. (Unmeasured without a vendor call: whether Gmail keeps a client-supplied Message-ID on `messages.send`; if it rewrites it, a lost compose stays `unknown` — never a false verdict.)

**Lane R5 verify r4 (2026-09-27) — THE ONE GATE, A CENSUS.** Every vendor request of both adapters goes through `api()`: `accessToken()` → `await pace(units)` → `meter(units)` → `bearerNow(at)` → `callJson`. `bearerNow` re-reads the token store SYNCHRONOUSLY after the wait: a disconnect that landed meanwhile refuses `auth-expired` "… disconnected while the request waited for its pace — the request was not sent" (`detail.tokenDropped`; the units already metered stay charged — never a leaked reservation), a re-authorize's or a sibling's refresh's newer token is the one sent, never the bearer captured before the wait (G1/G2 on the real adapter: 20 requests left with the dropped / old token). The refresh is SINGLE-FLIGHT (`refreshing`: siblings await the one POST, then `accessToken()` again reads what it wrote) — 20 concurrent thumbnails at one expiry were 20 refresh POSTs, and Lark's v2 refresh ROTATES the refresh token, so 11 of 12 were `invalid_grant`, each stamping the stale token back over the fresh one (the account logged out); a refused refresh now stamps `invalidGrantAt` only while the stored token is still the one it tried. Lark's `sendImpl` paces, meters and re-reads like every other request (it was neither paced nor metered since P4; an agent's direct-policy reply was N unpaced sends). Every OTHER outbound call site in gmail.js / lark.js / live/gmail.js carries a marker the suites read off the code: `// gated-inline: <id>` = a raw send with its own `await pace(1); meter(1)` within the 8 lines above (Lark: token-refresh, send, send-reply, resource); `// ungated: <id>` = a call outside the pace for a reason an agent or a loop cannot multiply, named in the module's frozen exported `UNGATED` (Gmail: `token-refresh` — oauth2 is not Gmail quota, single-flight; `consent-exchange` + `consent-profile` — once per human consent, keyed by the flow's one-time state; `pubsub` — live/gmail.js's pull + acknowledge, another API, one pull in flight, PULL_BACKOFF_MS. Lark: `consent-exchange` + `consent-user-info`; `integration-test` — the integrations panel's Test button, one tenant token per brand). Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c / test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c — `gateCensus(src)`: exactly one gate line (matched by its shape), the gate's order pinned between `const api = async` and the gate line, every other site a marker, `UNGATED`'s ids == the `ungated` markers, `gated-inline`'s pace + meter present and in order; controls (patched copies in scratch): a bare `callJson` added (`gmail labels` / `lark bot info`), a marker renamed to an unlisted id, an `UNGATED` row deleted under a live marker, the refresh's marker removed, the send's pace removed (Lark, red on both forms), the r3 tree by `git show` when available; runtime: 20 / 12 concurrent callers at one expiry ⇒ one refresh, the rotating vendor leaves the account connected holding the rotated token, a refused refresh of a since-replaced token stamps nothing, a send and a reply are pace 1 → meter 1 → send, a re-authorize landing during a held pace is the bearer sent, a disconnect during it is refused by name with nothing sent.

**lane channel-threads (2026-09-28).** Lark's `toRecord` fills the PLACE (`replyTo` = `parent_id`, `threadKey` = `thread_id` else the root chain, `root` = `root_id`); caps `threads {read:'vendor', replyInto:true, listing:'separate'}` (a topic's replies are not in the group listing — only the push lane and the walk see them) and `reactions {read:'list', add:true, remove:'own', vocabulary:'names', custom:'none'}`. New verbs, all through `api()` (paced, metered): `threadHistory(convId, threadKey, {anchor})` = `messages?container_id_type=thread` paged to the anchor with NO time window — **an item whose `chat_id` names another chat is DROPPED and counted (`foreign`), never stamped with `convId` (verify r1: the vendor's own word on where a message lives; gate ⑩ + the filter-less copy as control)**; `reactions(convId, {messageId})` ≤ 3 pages → a snapshot; `react` / `unreact` (231001 bad-emoji, 231003 not-reactable, 231007 reaction-not-mine, 231002/231008 forbidden); `send` with `inThread` = `reply_in_thread` (230019/230071 topic-forbidden — remembered on the conversation — /230072), its `observed.threadKey`; `reactionSet()` = the 182-row `LARK_EMOJI` table (key, glyph, label; `scripts/fixtures/lark-emoji-types.json` is its gate) + `LARK_QUICK`; `selfId()` = the token's open id; `convCaps` answers `threads {replyInto, mode: topic|thread|chat}` + `reactions {read, add}` from `capsOfScopes`. READING reactions needs `im:message.reactions:read`, which Lark refuses in a consent when the app has not enabled it (20027) — so it is asked only when the account's option `reactions: 'read'` says so (`consentScopes()`), and `reactionsGrant` names the scope + the console step. The live lane subscribes `im.message.reaction.created_v1` / `deleted_v1` and emits `{kind:'side'}` events through `eventToSide` (no chat id, no reaction id on the wire). Gmail declares no threads beyond the conversation and no reactions. Gate: test-channels-lark-shape ⑩.

### src/channels/live/lane.js + live/lark.js + live/gmail.js (ORCH)

THE PUSH LANES (design §6.4, fence 11, decisions 18 + 20; P1b, 2026-09-16).
`lane.js` is the CORE (imports nothing, knows no vendor): `startLane({connect,
onEvent, onState, now})` owns exactly four things — liveness is POSITIVE
evidence (`live` only on a landed handshake or a `heard()`); THE ACK IS THE
RETURN (a transport acks after the engine's `onEvent()` resolved, and the
engine resolves it after the record is durable); `stop()` IS TERMINAL FOR AN
ARM IN FLIGHT (every continuation is keyed on the arm's epoch — a connect
landing after stop is closed on the spot, `event()` on a stopped lane answers
`{ok:false, why:'stopped'}` WITHOUT calling the engine so the vendor gets no
ack and redelivers, nothing is emitted after `stopped`); the lane is
SINGLE-USE (a re-declaration or an option change arms a fresh one). Reconnects
back off 1 s → 60 s; a `connect()` throwing `err.permanent` parks the lane as
`unavailable` with that reason (the row says why). `live/lark.js` = the
official SDK (`@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` REQUIRED LAZILY — missing = a named
`sdk-not-installed` park, never a boot crash; the suite injects a stub) over
the APP credential from `resolveIntegration('lark')`; the registered
`im.message.receive_v1` handler maps the v2 payload to the REST item shape
(`eventToItem`) and RETURNS only after `onEvent()` — a stopped lane's handler
THROWS so the SDK answers the vendor with an error. Honest boundary: the event
is the APP's view (chats the bot is in), the poll is the USER's — in a chat
the bot is not in, push misses everything and the §6.4 measurement demotes
that deployment by itself; the SDK's server-set ping may exceed
`PUSH_HEARTBEAT_MS`, so a quiet chat reads `push-dead` between messages and
polls fast (the safe direction). `live/gmail.js` = `users.watch` (armed
first, renewed every 24 h — the watch dies silently after 7 days) + a Pub/Sub
PULL subscription of THIS instance (`options.pushTopic`/`pushSubscription`,
the user's token must carry the `pubsub` scope — each missing piece is a
NAMED refusal); a pulled note is a CURSOR KICK carrying the historyId, never
mail, acknowledged after the engine answered; every pull that answers is
`heard`. **A PERMANENT failure discovered INSIDE a connection PARKS (2026-09-16,
the P4 verifier): `handlers.fail(err)` says `unavailable` {why, code} with NO
reconnect and closes the connection (and `closed` closes the one it ends too —
a transport that reports its own end still owns timers; the renewal interval
leaked before); gmail uses it for a 401/403/404 pull (`pubsub-forbidden` /
`subscription-not-found`), for a REFUSED watch renewal at once and for
`WATCH_RENEW_MAX_FAILS` (3) transient renewal misses in a row
(`watch-renew-failed`) — reported through `closed`, a misconfigured
subscription re-ran users.watch + the pull every ≤60 s forever with the row
reading "reconnecting"; a 5xx pull still backs off and retries.** Gate:
scripts/test-channels-push.mjs (70; fast).

### src/channels/agents.js (ORCH)

The built-in Agents adapter (design §12.3, P3), a facade over Channels v1
behind the §4 contract so the outbox can send to an agent session with the
same verbs: a conversation is a live session (`deps.liveSessions`), reach is
answered by msg-acl through channel-acl's crosswalk (the engine asks, this
module never does), `send` is `deliverToConversation` — THE ladder, spend
reason `peer-message`, nothing beside it — and a refusal is a typed retryable
transport failure while a throw is the registry's `vendor-error {threw}` ⇒
`unknown`; `policyDefault:'direct'` (internal = direct, decision 9); identity
`marked` / `recipient-ui` in one verbatim sentence; `idempotency:'none'`;
`history()` is empty by construction (the chat window is the transcript). The
engine seeds its record (not removable, no consent) whenever `liveSessions`
was handed in — a bare suite engine has no row.

**r3 (agent groups, 2026-09-23): `sendStartsTurn: true` on the MODULE** — a send here is a WAKE (a billed turn through the ladder), so the channels engine's `wakeGate` asks the owner's consent echo and, auth off, the owner's pace before it (the Channels composer's `/send` and `/propose` and the outbox `/approve` were three unpaced, echo-less side doors beside the fenced group routes). The engine reads the declaration through `registry.get(kind)`, never the kind; the digest's adapter row carries it (`sendStartsTurn`) and a proposal's view `wakes` (0|1) so the composer and the approval card say the cost and echo it.

### src/channel-groups.js (PURE) + src/server/groups-engine.js (ORCH)

lane pair-group-fate (2.369.233): PURE `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log, liveness})` + `undeliverable` / `livenessOf` / `closePair` / `endedText` / `awaitVerdict` / `awaitState`; the engine's `ended` ledger, `onConversationEnded` / `sweepEnded` / `endedRefusal`, `post({await})` + `awaitWakes` (the SAME `wake()`); channels-wiring's `livenessReader` supplies FACTS only (roster, user-state archivedSessions, transcript on disk, the owner — a conversation-index claim ⇒ remote / ambiguous ⇒ unknown, else this machine's session-meta: no `host` ⇒ local — and whether the transcript dir was readable) and PURE `livenessFrom` judges: `gone` ONLY for a known-local conversation absent from a readable transcript dir; remote / unknown owner / unreadable dir ⇒ stopped, never closed (r2); the vibespace-msg CLI's `--await`, `(closed)` and read clauses.

**Lane group-pending (2026-10-01, the owner: "你这个最新回复应该还没有实际发出去，其实应该展示成pending的状态之类的防止confusion"):** a message to a next-turn member was drawn exactly like a delivered one. `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log})` (PURE) = WHERE A RECORD STANDS WITH EACH RECIPIENT: one row `{member, name, state, at}` per member but the author that was a member AT the record's instant (`joinedAt <= rec.at` — reportFor's floor is `joinedAt - 1`, pinned), the owner never a row; `DELIVERY_STATES` waiting | handed | muted | left. THE PIN: the engine's commit stamps `reportedUpTo` to EXACTLY the record's instant and reportFor reads `r.at > marker`, so a marker EQUAL to `rec.at` ⇒ handed (a `>` patched copy is red). The marker is a RECORD instant, so the hand-over CLOCK is its own field (the coordinator's follow-up): `markReported` stamps `members[].reportedAt = now()` beside the marker when it MOVES (persisted with the group record through the same door; validated null / absent / epoch ms) and a handed row's `at` is that clock — "Read by beta · 12:41"; a row stamped before the clock existed answers null and prints no time. One fact the engine still does NOT keep: a successful wake only stamps the marker (no receipt on the record or the member; a mention is no proof, a refused wake rides the report) — `woken` folds into `handed`. `left` reads the log the caller holds (the window's pages / the CLI read's page): the member's earliest leave / kick after the record with no invite of it in between; a departed member the page does not witness is no row. Every name through `cleanName` (the belt). The ENGINE: `view()` carries `members[].reportedUpTo` (the marker was a private fact before) and `markReported` ANNOUNCES `channel-groups-updated` when a marker MOVED (an unmoved marker sends nothing — the markRead lesson): the sender's window flips without a reload. Readers: the window's line under every message (channel-window.js `drawDelivery`, worded by channel-words.js `deliveryLineText`), the agent read route's `delivery` rows (agent-routes.js `msgDeliveryRows`) and `vibespace-msg read`'s trailing clause — ONE rule, two wordings, never a second rule. Gates: test-channel-groups §1f (the table, the engine pin, the announce + its no-move control, five patched-copy controls) · test-channels-groups-ui §2b + §4 · test-msg-cli-groups §1/§2 · test-channels-groups-e2e ④b (heavy).

**Lane peer-census (2026-09-29):** every report line and every inline piece — the author (`linePrefix`), the message (`lineFor`), the group name, the inviter + context line, the lead, a byte-cut line (`clipBytes` can leave an opener dangling — judged AGAIN after the cut) — takes `piece` = the belt's line kind (src/peer-text.js). Before: `inertFrames(clipLine(text))` neutered complete tags only, so a member's message ending in `<system-reminder` was completed by the NEXT report line when that member's words began with `>` (a quote) — a live frame in the receiver's next turn. The engine's wake lead is its own words today; a caller that names a sender in it is belted like every piece. Gate: test-peer-text-census `groups:report` legs + test-channel-groups (300; its import pin now reads channel-record + peer-text).

AGENT GROUPS (2.369.159; design §22, owner rulings D1/D2 + §22.5). The
model is PURE `src/channel-groups.js` (imports only channel-record for
`inertFrames`; no Buffer/clock/randomness — it may ride the bundle, instants
and ids are handed in): the record `{id:'g-<8hex>', name, createdBy,
createdAt, pair:[a,b]|null, members:[{member:<conversation id>, name,
joinedAt, invitedBy, notify, reportedUpTo}], archivedAt, lastAt, lastText}`
+ `validateGroup`, `newGroupId(hex8)`, `pairKey` (symmetric), and every
membership change as a PURE transition returning `{group, event}` (a NEW
object) or `{ok:false, code}` from the closed `ERROR_CODES`. Rules: a group
is made by an ACT (D1 — `makeGroup` wants two agents; an agent creator is a
member automatically; the owner is `OWNER='user'`, an actor never a row); a
duplicate invite is `noop:'already-member'`, never an error; a PAIR takes no
third member (`pair-group`) and is ARCHIVED when a side leaves (so is a group
with no agent left); kick = the creator or the owner, never yourself; a
member sets only its OWN notify, the owner anyone's; `archive` keeps the log.
`mentionsIn` = `@<name>|@<cid>`, longest name first with claimed spans, an
address-like `x@api.com` is nobody. **`wakeVerdict` IS D2**: own/not-member/
mute ⇒ no; the member's own invite ⇒ yes unless `--quiet`; any other system
record ⇒ no; an @mention ⇒ yes in every mode but mute; `always` ⇒ yes;
next-turn/mention unnamed ⇒ no — and it names the rule (`why`). **`reportFor`**
= the member's news after `max(reportedUpTo, joinedAt-1)` minus its own
lines, the invite context FIRST, newest kept under the byte budget (default
2 KiB; the newest always shows, clipped), the clipped ones POINTED to as
`read <group> --before <oldest shown>`, `upTo` covering them all; muted ⇒
null; every string frame-inert.

**Lane group-report-card (2026-09-28):** `reportFor` also answers `lines` = the SHOWN records, oldest first, `{rec, cut, body}` — `body` = the record's whole text when its line was whole, the line's own clipped (whitespace-folded) words when it was cut (`linePrefix(r)` is the ONE spelling of a line's head, shared with `lineFor`): what the member was SHOWN, which the engine turns into cards (`fits:false` answers `lines: []`).

The engine (`create({store, deliver, broadcast, now, roster, groupSetting})`,
built by channels-wiring over the channels engine's OWN store) does names,
reach, persistence, broadcast and delivery — nothing the model decides.
Reach = msg-acl asked per (actor, target) over the live roster (`liveSessions`
+ each session's `_msgReachability` + the Task Group `externalVisibility`),
`messageable` is the bar, judged from the INVITER, the owner reaches every live
session; a miss is ONE uniform `unreachable` sentence and refuses the whole
create/invite (transitions are computed first, the log written after). Every
mutation runs inside `store.groups.update` and appends its record there — unique
`at` per group (`max(now, lastAt+1)`), log FIRST, summary SECOND — then
broadcasts `channel-groups-updated {changed, groups, messages?}`. **A WAKE is
the member's pending report delivered NOW through `deliver.deliverToConversation`
with `spendReason:'peer-message'` — the engine's ONLY ladder site**
(test-spend-paths allowlists exactly that forward; a patched copy that posts
into the CLI inbox beside it reads UNWIRED). A delivered wake stamps
`reportedUpTo`; a refused one is journaled (`audit` kind `group-wake` with the
ladder's `refused`/`why`) and NEVER stashed — the message is in the log and
the report is its durable fallback (a stash would hand it over twice).
`reportsForTurn(cid, {budget})` = every non-muted membership with news, newest
group first, ONE heading, each ≤ 2 KiB inside the caller's budget (≤ 4 KiB), a
group that does not fit waits and is NAMED; `commitReports` stamps only what was
handed out. `sendToAgent` = `findOrCreatePair` (checked again inside the door)
+ `post`; D2's default applies to pairs too — `wake:true` is an explicit @ of
every other member. `read` (members; archived groups readable; pre-join history
on purpose) and `listFor(cid)` (with unread counts) are the read side.
Gate: test-channel-groups (fast) + the §3 reach legs in test-channel-acl +
the §2 row and patched-copy control in test-spend-paths.

**g3 — the owner's side of the panel (2.369.159).** THE OWNER'S READ MARK: `ownerRead {groupId: at}` beside `groups` in the groups file (same door); `list()` — the OWNER's list, what the panel and every `channel-groups-updated` carry — adds `unread` = the log records after the mark the owner did not write (derived, never stored; computed only when `lastAt` passed the mark). The mark moves ONLY by the owner's act: `markRead({group})` (`POST /api/channel-groups/:id/read`, the window opened or touched — never a repaint) and `ownerSaw` inside the owner's own create / invite / post door (the owner has seen what it wrote); a mark that did not move broadcasts NOTHING (the channels markRead lesson — an unchanged value is not a dirty signal). `liveRoster()` = the live sessions `{cid, name, groups}` (`GET /api/channel-groups/roster`) the New group / Invite… dialogs draw from — the SAME roster reach is judged over; the owner reaches every live session. Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §2 (the owner's unread, the no-op mark control) + test-channels-groups-e2e ⑦.

**r1 — the verifier's round (2.369.159, each finding reproduced first; the new legs were RED on the pre-fix tree).** ① **Every wake is PACED, not the flag**: `post` / `create` / `invite` / `sendToAgent` take `mayWake(member) → true | {reason}` and `wakeAll` asks it of EVERY wake the act would cause — an @mention in the text, `--wake`, an invite, an `always` member — before the ladder; a floored wake is a refusal like the authorizer's (`refused:'rate-floor'`, audited as `group-wake`, not billed, the message rides the next report). The agent route's floor is `wakeFloorFor(senderCid)`: one wake per (sender, RESOLVED member conversation id) per 30 s — before, `@beta` ×5 in a second woke beta five times and `--wake` by name then by id were two keys (`myCid|to`). The owner's own posts are not paced (the owner's act). ② **A report's budget is its WHOLE text**: `reportFor` tries three forms (full · compact: short foot, name ≤ 90 B · tight: name ≤ 36 B, short pointer) and returns the first that fits and shows a message; when not even the tight form fits it answers `{fits:false, text:'', upTo:null}` — distinct from `null` ("nothing new") so `reportsForTurn` leaves the marker and names the group as waiting (before: an 80-CJK-char name made a 320 B report 534 B). `reportsForTurn` names at most 3 waiting groups (each ≤ 40 B) then `+N more`, reserves the trailer when there is more than one candidate, and takes the last report back out (marker unmoved) until the WHOLE section ≤ budget (before: 60 long-named groups ⇒ 18 579 B in a 4096 B budget; `capInline` trimmed it after the markers moved). ③ **`resolveTarget(ref, by)`** is `send`'s ONE resolution: `g-…` = a group, a live conversation id = that session, a bare name that is BOTH one of the caller's groups and a messageable session ⇒ `ambiguous` with `{name, groupId}` + `{name, conversationId}` (before: a group named `beta` silently took `send beta`). ④ **`memberRef(group, ref)`**: kick / notify by a display name two members share ⇒ `ambiguous` with `{name, conversationId}` (before: the first match). ⑤ `mentionsIn` ends a name at a SCRIPT boundary too — the next character from an unspaced script (Han / kana / Hangul / CJK punctuation / full-width) or a name that ends in one: `@测试请看`, `@beta请看`, `@测试ok` mention; `@betax` is still nobody. Gate: test-channel-groups §1 (CJK rows) · §1c (the budget sweep 320..4096 with an 80-CJK name, a long inviter and an 8 000 B context, ± a lead; `fits:false` at 120 B) · §3d (two members named `beta`) · §4 (40 long-named pending groups through the REAL prompt-context: no `context trimmed`, every shown report whole, every unshown one still pending) · §4b pins; test-msg-cli-groups §2 (five `@eps` ⇒ 1 wake + 4 floored; name-then-id `--wake` floored; the shadowing group ⇒ `ambiguous`, ids route; a cid-less sender ⇒ 409).

**r2 — the second verifier round (2.369.159, nine findings, each leg RED on the pre-fix tree).** ① **THE PACE BINDS A SENDER, NOT ONLY A PAIR, AND ONE COMMAND SAYS ITS COST FIRST.** The pace's rules are PURE in the model (`paceVerdict` / `paceGrant` / `paceRefund` / `prunePace`: one wake per (sender, member) per `WAKE_FLOOR_MS` 30 s AND at most `SENDER_WAKES` 8 per sender per `SENDER_WINDOW_MS` 60 s — before, one `group create` of 25 or one plain post into 25 `always` members authorized 25 billed turns, 62 in 31 s from one sender, the receivers' slot's whole default hour); the engine's `pacerFor(sender)` is the ONE implementation (the agent route's `wakeFloorFor` now returns it). And `consentVerdict(n, {yes | expect})` is asked INSIDE the door with the number of wakes the act WOULD cause (`wakesPlanned` = `wakeVerdict` over the candidates; an invite counts its invitees unless `--quiet`), before anything is written: an agent's act over `WAKE_CONFIRM_ABOVE` 5 is `confirm-wakes` `{wakes:N}` until `yes:true` (`--yes`). ② **THE OWNER'S ROUTES: a consent echo, and paced when auth is off.** The panel sends `expectWakes` = what its preview said ("will wake N" / the composer's `wakePreview`); anything else (a missing echo = 0) is `wake-count-mismatch` `{wakes:N}` — a curl caller cannot wake members signed "User" without first knowing and saying the count. With auth OFF the routes are local-open, so `routes/channels.js` `ownerPacer` hands the engine `pacerFor('user')` (a missing switch counts as off); with auth on the owner is unpaced. ⑥ **THE PACE IS PERSISTED** — `store.pace` (`data/channels/wake-pace.json`, written 100 ms after a change and on close, pruned to its windows every grant): a restart used to forget every floor (the in-memory Map). ⑧ **A GRANT RESERVES, A WAKE THAT DID NOT GO OUT REFUNDS** (`mayWake.refund` from `wakeAll`'s refused branch) — five concurrent posts still see each other's reservation, and a wake the authorizer refused no longer floors the next legitimate one with words saying a billed turn happened. ⑤ **UNREAD IS MEMOISED, NOT RE-READ PER BROADCAST**: `unreadFor(g, who, since)` keyed `(since, lastAt)`, `appendIn` (the one door every log record passes) moves the memo it just advanced (+1 for a record `who` did not write), a moved marker recomputes once, a background `setImmediate` pass warms it after boot — before, every post/create/invite/rename re-read every unread group's whole log inside `announce()` (~100 ms of main loop per agent post at 200 groups × 500 messages; now ≈ 1–2 ms, and `list()` / `listFor()` read no log). ⑦ **A TURN WITH NO ROOM STILL NAMES THE WAITING GROUPS**: `reportsForTurn` measures its trailer reserve from the actual widest `waitingLine` (was a 294 B guess) and, when no report fits, answers the head + the trailer (fewer names if needed), no marker moved — before, the fullest prompts got an EMPTY section. ④ **A LINE CUT SHORT IS POINTED TO**: `reportFor` tracks every shown line cut (at `LINE_MAX` or to the newest line's room) and appends `(N message(s) above cut short — the whole text: vibespace-msg read <gid> --before <newest cut + 1> --limit <log records in the span>)`, budgeted up front at its widest (the marker used to move past a 6 KB message handed over as 400 chars + `…`). Gate: test-channel-groups §1c (cut pointer: one/two cuts, the 100-char control, every budget 320..4096) · §2b (the corrupt store, below) · §3e (the pointer's read returns the whole 6 KB) · §3f (400..700 B with three pending ⇒ named) · §3g (200 groups: one post re-reads ≤ 2 logs, list/listFor none, every count equal to a from-scratch count) · §3h (the owner routes over a real express router: no echo ⇒ 409, auth off ⇒ floored, auth on ⇒ not; create/invite echo) · §4c (mouse reports); test-msg-cli-groups §1 (`--yes`, `confirm-wakes` remedy) · §2 (25 invitees ⇒ `confirm-wakes` then 8 woken + 17 floored + 17 audit lines; 25 `always` ⇒ refused then 0 woken; refused-then-allowed wake ⇒ the second wakes; a restarted routes module + engine over the same store ⇒ still floored); test-channels-groups-e2e (the owner's post with its echo; the same post without ⇒ 409; auth off ⇒ the leg waits out the invite's floor).

**r3 — the third verifier round (2026-09-23).** ② **A RENAMED MEMBER NO LONGER KILLS THE OWNER'S SEND.** `view()` names are live-roster derived, so a session renamed (sidebar / first-message auto-name) changed them with no group verb and no broadcast: the panel counted @mentions against the names it drew, the door against live names, and every click was `wake-count-mismatch`. Now a `wake-count-mismatch` refusal from `post` / `invite` carries `group: view(g)` (the names the count was made against), and `noteRoster()` — called from server.js `broadcastActiveSessions`, the session list's ONE notify point — compares each group's member signature (`cid=name:live`, what the last `announce` told the clients, `rosterSig`) and announces exactly the groups that moved (nothing moved ⇒ nothing sent). ④ **A FUTURE STAMP IS NOT A WAKE**: PURE `PACE_SKEW_MS` 5 s — `prunePace` drops, `paceVerdict` ignores, `paceFuture` counts any stamp more than 5 s ahead (a backward clock step of D used to floor every pair for D + 30 s; a planted far-future stamp, for ever); `pacerFor` logs one `[groups] wake-pace.json held N stamp(s) in the future …` line as the prune drops them. ⑤ **A REFUSED WAKE GIVES BACK ITS PAIR, NOT ITS ATTEMPT**: `paceRefund(state, token, {keepSender:true})` from the pacer — the target is not floored by a refusal, but the attempt stays in the sender's minute, so a sender at the spend ceiling reaches the authorizer at most `SENDER_WAKES` 8 times a minute (60 attempts in 6 s used to be 60 authorizer asks and 60 audit lines). ① The owner's pacer is now ALSO the channels engine's (the Agents adapter's `/send`, `/propose`, `/approve` — see routes/channels.js). Gate: test-channel-groups §1e (the PURE table: future pair / sender stamps, the skew control, keepSender vs whole) · §3i (a 5-min backward step with the log line; 60 refused attempts ≤ 8 asks, spend audit ≤ 8, the pair refunded; a refused-then-allowed retry wakes) · §3j (the side doors) · §3k (rename ⇒ 409 carries the live view, the second click succeeds; `noteRoster` announces once, nothing moved ⇒ nothing).

**r4 (2026-09-23):** `mayWake.refund(member, {attempted})` — `attempted:false` (the channels engine's refund of an act that THREW before anything reached the authorizer or the adapter: a blocked / full store) returns the sender's minute too (`paceRefund(…, {keepSender:false})`); the default stays `attempted:true` (r3: a refused attempt stays in the minute). The group wakes' own refund is unchanged.

### src/channel-feed.js (PURE)

**Lane gmail-feed-gap (B-5134, 2026-10-07) — A GAP IS ONE WALK FROM THE CURSOR.** `gapVerdict({cursor, lastPageAt, now, coldTierSec, expired, freshBoundMs})` → `{verdict: catch-up | rewalk | fresh, gapMs, from, overCold}`; `addGap(gaps, {from, to})` (merged, ≤ GAPS_MAX 20); `coverageOf(records, {gaps, …sample's})` = `sample` with every record inside a declared gap excluded (`excluded`), never judged a miss. The engine declares the measured feed's long-stop span and judges the authoritative feed's gap before its walk; channel-caps `feedState` keeps a cursor-holding authoritative feed carrying (`catching-up` / `backoff`). Gate: test-channel-feed ⑩.

**Lane lark-threads (2026-10-01) — A3 / A4 / A5.** `foldHits` marks a hit's THREAD before it drops a STORED hit (`stored++` used to come first: a root re-surfaced by the search with its new topic never made the thread owed) — a stored hit marks the thread only, never an owed chat read; it also returns `threadHits` (the page's new hits carrying a thread id — the measurement) and `owedHits` (≤ OWED_HITS_MAX: the hits behind an owed chat read with no thread id — the engine reads one the read did not find BY ID). Gate: test-channel-feed ③ + the pre-lane order as a patched copy.

**THE CHANGE FEED'S ARITHMETIC (lane lark-search-poll, B-5aab, 2026-09-28 — design-communication-panel.zh.md §29; the owner: "从 lark pull 消息可以通过搜索空格+时间范围来搜索最近所有新消息吧，这样也顺便能解决私聊问题").** A change feed = ONE account-wide "what changed since …" read (Lark's `im/v1/messages/search`, empty query + `time_range`) naming every conversation with a new message — groups, single chats (which `im/v1/chats` never lists), thread replies. Declared per adapter as `caps.changeFeed` (validated by src/channels/index.js), beside `receive`, never instead of it. Imports nothing, reads no clock (CJS: the engine, the registry, the suites share it).

- **API.** `window(feed, now, decl, {overlapSec, tokenAt})` → `{act: continue|restart|new|none, from, to, gap, first}` (whole seconds; the overlap ≥ `OVERLAP_MIN_SEC` 30; the steady window never reaches past `maxWindowSec` — the older span of a long stop is `gap`, a SINGLE-CHAT catch-up; ### src/channel-budget.js (PURE)

**lane gmail-quota-share (2026-10-05).** THE LEARNED VENDOR BUDGET, imports nothing. `budgetStep(state, event, facts)` over the closed EVENTS {refused, quiet-minute, setting-changed, boot} → `{state, changed, halved, crept, loud, full}`; `facts` = {setting, minUnit (one read's price), now, burstStart?, day?}. refused: a burst's first strike halves the ceiling (floor = `floorOf` = max(10 % of the setting, one read), never above the setting) and remembers the refused ceiling as the WALL for `WALL_MS` (60 min); later strikes only restart the quiet clock. quiet-minute: each whole minute +10 % of the setting, capped one step under a standing wall; a capped creep spends the minutes it waited, the wall's end does not bank. setting-changed keeps the learned fraction; boot validates, clamps, rolls the day (`halvesToday`; `loud` = the day's 2nd halving). `ratioOf` = the pace's scale, `fullAtOf` = when the setting is back. The engine (budgetDecl / paceDecl / failPass / the good pass) only drives it; the state rides the account record (`rec.budgetLearned`, adapters.json). Gate: test-channel-budget.

**THE DUE QUEUE + THE FETCH LOG (lane channel-drain-scale, 2026-10-06 — a fleet mailbox of 88 915 conversations held the loop 18 s in every 20; liveness probes failed).** `itemsOf` rebuilt every due row on every `next`, `apply` copied `p.due` and `fetchedAt` on every fetch: D steps of O(D). Now a pass is O(due + steps · requests): `pass.due` is a PERSISTENT queue (`rows` frozen + `at` key→index, shared until a merge ADDS a key — the one O(due) rebuild: the timer's turn, discovery, a feed page, a kick's new hint; `head` + `gone` for what left — `dqDrop` O(1 + gone)); `pass.fetched` an append-only fetch log shared down the pass (a snapshot sees its first `n`; a write from a non-tip snapshot copies its `n` first); `itemsOf` walks the REQUESTS only (`dqHas` per slot) and `queueOf` is a view of the queue's head (`length`, `[0]`, `find`, `some`). `dueRows(pass)` lists it (the gate's oracle). Gate test-channel-drain: the walk's 154 893 decisions byte-identical to the base (sha256 a31b8de7), a purity pin (`0-pure`: a step never changes the snapshot it was handed), ⑦ linear by the work meter to D = 90 000 (97 units per row at 1 000 / 10 000 / 45 000; base ×3.79–3.96), controls: the queue rebuilt per step (×3.35), an `apply` writing its input.

**Rule 22 (lane lark-threads, 2026-10-01) — THE RECENT-ROOTS RECHECK.** 22a: `recheckDue(rows, {now, everyMs, activeMs, max})` = the conversations due (live, a separately-listed adapter, not a topic group, walked once, active within RECHECK_ACTIVE_MS 14 d, not rechecked within `channels.threadRecheckSec`), oldest first; `turn(snap, {recheckDue})` arms them ONCE per pass; `next` sends `{type:'recheck', key}` only with NOTHING else pending (the lowest priority), the timer's work, never in a back-off, the minute unspent, paced, ≤ RECHECK_PER_PASS (3), a key once a pass; `{skip}` = the pass goes on, `{error}` = rule 3. 22b: a fetch whose round holds the OWNER's request carries `recheck: true` (never 'open', never 'agent'); `recheckOnPress(lastPressAt, now)` floors it 60 s on the owner's OWN previous press. **Rule 21 (lane lark-search-poll, 2026-09-28) — THE CHANGE FEED as ONE drain action.** `turn(snap, {…, feedDue, feedPerPass})` marks `pass.feed` wanted (the timer's work only, once per pass); `next` returns `{type:'feed'}` when it is wanted, not done, no human waits, the minute is unspent, `feedPages.remaining > 0` (a NEW fact: the feed's own sliding minute, `perMin`) and `pages < perPass` — paced (cost `feed`), AFTER the cut and BEFORE discovery and every fetch. `apply(…, 'feed', result)`: `{due, more}` ⇒ `mergeFront` (the rows AHEAD of the plain due rows in the page's order; a pending key moves up; a key in flight or with a taken group untouched; a key this pass fetched only for a hit NEWER than the fetch — rule 13), `more` keeps it wanted until `perPass`; `{skip}` (a feed-LOCAL refusal) ends the feed and NEVER fails the pass; `{error}` is rule 3; `{noCall}` = no vendor call counted. **Lane R5 (2026-09-26, the owner: "gmail一直被限速 你可能要控制下gmail默认的读取速度") — RULE 18, THE PACE.** The vendor refused whole passes that stayed inside the minute's budget (Gmail: ~2 000–2 800 units in ~20 s = 100–200 units/s, from idle) — a per-minute cap is a sum, not a shape. New FACT `pace: null | {unitsPerSec, burst, tokens, lastRefillAt, cost: {fetch, discover, scanHost}}` (the engine evaluates the level on its PHYSICAL pace clock and hands it over as of the logical `now`); new ACTION `wait {ms ≤ PACE_WAIT_MAX_MS 1000, next, key}`: a discovery / host scan / fetch whose cost finds fewer than min(cost, burst) tokens is not sent, the step is a wait, the next step judges and picks AGAIN (a human filed meanwhile goes first). A wait is never a refusal (REFUSAL_CODES unchanged) and never a skip; refusals (5, 11, the cut) and settlements are answered at once; the minute's budget is judged BEFORE the pace (rule 9 = the outer cap); `apply('wait')` moves nothing (no row, no streak, no count). A call larger than the bucket waits for a full one and leaves a debt. Exact tolerance: any T-second window charges ≤ burst + unitsPerSec·T + max(0, the largest call − burst). **Lane lark-threads verify r3 (2026-10-01) — the ladder's two small halves.** `failPass` honours a TRANSPORT failure's hint too (a 5xx with Retry-After: `nextAt` = max(the failure ladder's rung, the hint, ≤ RATE_RETRY_AFTER_MAX_MS), `retryAfterSec` on the card); the owner's `reconcile` turns an adapter throw into `unknown` WITH `detail.retryAfterSec` (the adapters throw a rate refusal now instead of answering `unknown`); `budgetView` carries `burst` (the per-second bucket's width) — the meter is a fixed window and the bucket bounds a sliding minute at limit + burst − 1, which the budget sentence names.

**THE REFRESH DRAIN'S SCHEDULING DECISION (lane R2 verify r9, 2026-09-26 — the second structural closure).** Seven adversarial rounds (r2–r8) each found ONE money-class defect, every one in the refresh / drain scheduling of the channels engine: a foreign pass answered (r2), the owner's back-off exemption reachable by agents (r3), N concurrent refreshes of one key = N vendor calls (r4), an agent storm denying the owner and refusals delivered at the pass's end (r6), forced passes running thrice (r7), LIFO across boundaries + the owner behind 180 agents + re-requests not riding (r8). r5 moved the judgement into the one loop and r7 added the interleave and the timer's turn at every boundary; each rewrite of an imperative scheduler whose decisions were spread across `await`s introduced a new ORDERING bug only a fresh adversary found. The decision is now a STEP FUNCTION over a snapshot, imports nothing, reads no clock (CJS: the engine, the gate and a patched copy load it alike).

- **API.** `empty()` · `admit(snap, req)` → `{ok, snap}` | `{ok:false, refused:'refresh-queue-full', queued, cap}` · `withdraw(snap, id)` (a waiter left by itself — its bound's `pending`, a settle) · `census(snap)` (the UNTAKEN waiters the cap counts + `held`) · `queueAsk(prev, ask)` → `{queued, joined}` (rule 17) · `open(snap, {origin, force, backoff, timerDue, hostScan})` · `wantsTurn(snap, timerDue)` / `turn(snap, {due, discoveryDue})` (the timer's turn — the due list is a store read the model does not own) · `next(snap)` → ONE action · `apply(snap, act[, result])` (no result = an async action BEGINS; with it = it completes) · `close(snap)`.
- **The snapshot** (frozen in the module's doc comment): `{seq, requests: [{id, key, origin: owner|open|agent, principal, at, seq, taken}] in FILING order, pass}` + the FACTS the driver adds before every step (`now, stopped, dropped, connected, backoff {epoch, pressEpoch}, budget {remainingUnits}, agentShare {remaining}, floors, floorMs`). `taken` = a step judged it and ACCEPTED it. Actions: `refuse {key, code, rule, waiters, cut?}` · `answer {waiters, outcome}` · `discover` · `scanHost` · `fetch {key, chargeTo, waiters (THE ROUND), due, rider, pressed}` · `end {ok, why, cut?, carry?, waiting, timerWork}`; every action carries `accept` (the ids this step accepted) and `press` (the key granted the owner's press this step).
- **The 18 rules** (one numbered list in the doc comment, each an invariant of the gate's walk; 18 = the pace, above): 1 admission — CAP 200 untaken, an agent at CAP − RESERVE 20; 2 stop / drop ⇒ every waiter answered in ONE step, then end, no vendor call after; 3 a failed pass answers every taken waiter, a request filed during the failing call waits for the next pass; 4 not connected; 5 judgement AT SIGHT — an untaken group with no pending item judged by its highest origin at the first step that sees it (back-off with the owner's ONE press per window, one key per pass; the agent share; the budget; the floor) and a refusal answered at that step — plus, inside a back-off, an item whose owner left before its fetch is refused `backoff`, the press not spent (found by the walk: an agent riding the owner's press would otherwise be fetched alone); 6 the rider rule, at most ONE pending item per key; 7 FIFO humans first (owner / open before agent, each class by the filing order of its EARLIEST waiter, never re-ordered by a later arrival), plain due rows after; 8 the interleave — after a request-class fetch, while a due row waits, a due row (a ridden one first); 9 the budget per vendor call (fetch, discovery, host scan) and THE CUT (every accepted waiter refused by name, end); 10 an `ok` at its fetch — the fetch answers exactly its ROUND (every waiter of its key present when it began); 11 the share per FETCH (r9: r8 judged it at the boundary only, so N agent requests judged together could overspend it); 12 discovery at most once per pass, with the timer's work, never ahead of a waiting human (r8 low); 13 the timer's turn merges due rows (a key this pass fetched only when due AGAIN — `dueAt` after that fetch; a key with a taken group never doubled; hints the same); 14 the host scan once, before the first fetch of a scan-lane pass; 15 THE BOUND — with no due row pending a pass ends after STREAK_MAX (25) request-class fetches in a row, the taken rest carried to the next pass (r7/r8's pass never ended under a stream; a forced ingest queued behind it waited for the stream); 16 end — nothing pending ⇒ end, a fetchless back-off pass ends `backoff` (changes nothing), a cut before any vendor call ends `budget`; 17 one queued pass per account, `force` sticky.
- **Deviations from the r9 brief, each with its reason** (also in the doc comment): "each key fetched at most once per pass" is ONCE PER ROUND — the 70-cell table's timer-fetching-key owner cell pins two calls (a press filed during its key's fetch is a new round) and ⑥g(11a) pins a one-key stream heard within a round inside one pass; r5 verify #3 was exactly the once-per-pass failure (a re-request skipped unanswered). The due rows carry no `tier` (folded into `dueAt`); `budget` has no `unitsPerFetch` (affordability = remaining > 0, the vendor's "one more request" rule); discovery is a pass field (wanted / done); the host scan is its own action (a vendor call the budget must judge); `turn` takes the due list as an input.
- **How to change a rule.** Edit the model AND its line in the doc comment, add or adjust the walk's oracle invariant in scripts/test-channel-drain.mjs, add a mutant of the new line that turns its leg red — never a decision in the engine (the gate's census reddens `takeTimerTurn`, `interleave(`, `lastBy`, `queue.splice`, `.sort(` … in the engine's pass / request-set region, and pins ONE `Drain.next`, ONE `Drain.admit`, two `Drain.apply`).

Judged BEFORE rule 9's budget (a joined / remembered answer costs no unit); rule 18's pace stays the adapter's. The engine (`loadOlder`) keeps the memory on the live entry (`e.older`, dies with it) and the flights in `olderFlights`. `changed` is applied by BOTH writers of a log — the poll ingest and the push lane (r7: the push site was unwired) — and by the owner's `refresh()` (which a window's stale open also calls). **verify r2 (MONEY) — THE CUSTOM-EMOJI PICTURE FOLLOWS THE ATTACHMENT'S ONE ORDER.** `emojiImage(adapterId, key)` = the key's alphabet and the set's `custom` listing first, then PURE `Att.fetchVerdict` exactly as `attachment()` asks it: the account's LRU cache (`~emoji` inside the attachment budget, evicted with the attachments) · a REMEMBERED refusal (`emojiRefused`, `Att.negativeTtlMs` — a deleted / forbidden picture, one past 1 MB) · one flight (`emojiFlights`) · the back-off (the account's `inBackoff` and the picture rate limit `e.attBackoffUntil`, which a 429 on an emoji now sets for every picture) · the budget · ONE paced + metered call. An unknown key is `thread-not-loaded` (404) on the owner's route and the uniform not-found on the agent's (no oracle for another chat's ids), with no vendor call; the ONE internal exception is the post-send walk under `vendorNamed:true` (the thread id the vendor answered for a reply sent into this conversation). The BELT: a walk record stamped with another conversation is dropped and counted (`foreign`, also the adapter's own count through the registry's `threadHistory` shape). Every refusal is by name (`reactions-floor`, `thread-floor`, the ceiling's `vendor-budget`). **verify r2 — THE WALK'S CURSOR ACROSS A RESTART:** the anchor is the LOG's newest reply of the thread (never a stored cursor), so after a restart the next walk is one call when nothing is new — never a re-walk from scratch (gate: test-channels-engine ⑱ (a')). **verify r3 — THE CUT WALK'S STOP IS PERSISTED (r2's held LOW, fixed):** a walk appends page by page, so a walk cut mid-way (a transport error, the budget, MAX_PAGES) had moved the DERIVED anchor past a range it never read, and its continuation lived only in the adapter's memory (Lark's `walks`, 5 min) — after a restart that range was never walked (measured: 200 of 250). Now `threadCuts[key] = {stopAt, at}` (beside `threadWalks`, bounded the same, `writeThreadCut` FLUSHES the index at once) is written BEFORE the first page that is not the walk's last is appended (log-before-anchor), handed to the adapter as `stopAt` while it stands, and cleared only by a COMPLETE walk; Lark's `threadHistory` takes `stopAt` for a FRESH walk and its own live continuation still wins (one call). After a restart the next walk pages from the newest back to the stop (the cut pages re-read, the dedup absorbs them — bounded by FIRST_INGEST_MAX like an uncut walk). Gates: test-channels-engine ⑱ (a'') (restart = every reply for 4 calls, in-process = 2, the stop on disk before the append, cleared by the complete walk; the stop-less copy = 200 of 250) + test-channels-lark-shape (stopAt honoured fresh, the continuation wins, the stopAt-blind copy). **verify r3 — THE REACTION CEILING COUNTS REQUESTS (MEDIUM):** rule 20b's promise — a scroll storm spends ≤ `channels.reactionsPerMin` (20) a minute and the timer's message passes keep their budget — counted LIST CALLS, but a Lark list is paged (≤ REACTION_PAGES_MAX = 3 requests) and the budget is metered per request: one window batch of 20 rows each carrying > 100 reactions spent 60 requests = Lark's whole minute and the timer's pass right after was refused (`verify/r3-rx-pages.mjs`). ### src/server/channels-engine.js + channels-wiring.js + src/routes/channels.js (ORCH)

**lane channel-self-unread (2.369.228, userW inc-muxekkry-clfb + B-c91b) — THE OWNER'S OWN MESSAGE IS READ.** Every append site (`landById`, the ingest's index update, the thread walk) counts through `countFresh` = `FO.readAdvance` (a self record moves `readAt` to its instant and re-derives the row past it); `unreadSince` = `store.countSince(…, keep)` minus the owner's records (push flush, `markRead`); the push batch's `selfAt` also moves `readAt`; `onFresh`'s match loop skips `FO.selfRead` records for every watcher (keyword / regex / place / all). The digest's kept unread (B-f32b) follows the rows. src/channel-store.js `countSince(adapterId, convId, sinceAt, keep = null)`. Tests: test-channels-engine (㉓ (S) site 1 + ㉕ site 2, digest, markRead, 2 controls), test-channel-agent-watch ⑧ (+ control).

**THE VIEWS ARE PACED INSIDE A PASS (lane channel-drain-scale, 2026-10-06).** Every answered fetch with news broadcast at once (`digest` → `adapterView` → `schedulerView` → `clockCensus` per step). `VIEW_PACE_MS` (250, physical): a pass says its early keys at most once per window (`sayEarly`) + its end; a key answered inside the window waits WITH its answer (`answerAfterSaid`) for the window's broadcast — a timer ≤ 250 ms or the pass's end (`flushEarly` before every exit and the safety net) — so the broadcast still precedes the answer (r8) and `early` keeps its rule. Gate test-channels-census-pace: 10 300 rows + 300 refreshes, 201 broadcasts → 3, every changed key named, no answer before its key's broadcast; control: the per-fetch broadcast restored (201). The loop yield (batches between steps) is the 2.369.226 hotfix's.

**THE CENSUS IS AN INDEX (lane scheduler-census-index, B-7978, 2026-10-07).** channels-engine.js `clockCensus` (still paced, `censusEveryMs`) reads `clockIndexed(rec, t)`: per account `censusIx` = each row's judgement (src/channel-census.js) + the counters + `order` (finite instants, soonest first) + `dirty`. `markDue(key)` marks the census index beside the due index (index writes via `onTouch`, poll stamps, a watch start; null = stale). A census re-judges the dirty rows, then the head of `order` the clock passed (spliced once, re-put past `t`); an O(rows) build only when absent / stale / the due index's signature changed (tiers, lane) / `t` < the last census / dirty > rows/8 + 256. `schedulerScan` = THE DEFINITION, reached only by `schedulerExact`; `schedulerIndexed` / `censusIndexStats` ({builds, rejudged, rowsRead, lastBuildMs}) for the gates. The kept row facts' minute re-sum (`ROW_RESUM_MS`) is removed: 100 ms of a minute's pass at 90 298 rows. Measured by scripts/measure-channels-pass.mjs (`CENSUS_INDEX_PROOF` in channels-engine.js).

lane channel-feed-authority: `dueList` reads THE DUE INDEX (`dueIx` per account: sorted (at,key) lower bounds + owed-mark set; re-keyed by `store.index.onTouch`, the wrapped `store.stamps.set`, a watch start; rebuilt O(rows) on a lane / tier-setting change) and judges candidates with `dueRow` (the one rule; `all` still walks); `historyFeed` drives an authoritative feed inside `feedPage`; `admitListed` = discovery's row write shared with feed births; `FEED_ONLY_REWALK_MS` (24 h listing re-walk under feed-only); test seams `dueListOf` / `dueIndexStats`.


**THE FAMILY SPLIT (lane dc-channels-seams, 2026-10-05 — rv-channels-core C11).** The engine's one `create()` closure lost three families, moved VERBATIM into their own files (src/server/channels-access.js, channels-outbound.js, channels-auth.js — their entries below); the essays in this section still describe their functions, now living there. What stays here: ingest (log-before-anchor), poll / feed / recheck, the drain's driving (`pass`, `serialWake` — no scheduling decision across an await), the wake machinery (`onFresh` … `wakeNow`, the R4 `billedWake` ONE door), the adapters (`adapterFor`, the R5 token CAS `tokensFor`, the pace), views / push / threads / reactions / attachments / people, scheduling (`tick`, `start`, `stop` — which releases the stash listeners `offStash` / `offStashGate`, kept here), the raw API's engine side, and THE COMPOSITION ROOT: `const engineCtx = { … }` names every field a family may read (the engine's deps, shared state, its own doors, the shared module constants; `get stopped()` / `get timer()` for its two `let`s), then `const { … } = Object.assign(engineCtx, ChannelsAccess.create(engineCtx))`, the same for ChannelsOutbound and ChannelsAuth (that order: a family reads an EARLIER family's answer from the context at creation, a later one's through a one-line call-time forwarder — access reads outbound's `sendIdentityFor` / `proposalsFor` / `agentProposalView` that way). test-architecture §79 is the census (each family's requires = its row; every field it reads is the root's or an earlier family's; every late door a later family's answer). Suites read the four files as ONE text through scripts/channels-engine-src.mjs `engineSource(repo)` (each family inlined as a hoisted function after the engine's text, its own lines keeping their numbers), so a patched copy is one closed world.

**lane gmail-quota-share (2026-10-05) — THE BUDGET IS LEARNED.** `budgetDecl(rec).limit` is the LEARNED ceiling (`learnedOf` = src/channel-budget.js's 'boot' over `rec.budgetLearned`), `.setting` its cap; `paceDecl` scales the per-second setting by the same ratio; `failPass` steps 'refused' (burstStart = the ladder's first strike) inside the record write it already makes, the good pass steps 'quiet-minute'; `budgetView().learned` feeds the card sentence; `speakSlowed` / `retractSlowed` = one For-you item per (account, day). **Lane R5 (2026-09-26, the owner: "gmail一直被限速 你可能要控制下gmail默认的读取速度") — THE PACE + THE RATE LADDER.** ① `paceDecl(rec)` reads the adapter's `caps.pace` (`{unitsPerSec, settingKey, cost}`) through `setting()` (SETTING_BOUNDS: `channels.gmailUnitsPerSec` 5–100, `channels.larkRequestsPerSec` 1–50, default = the module's) and COUPLES it to the minute: unitsPerSec = min(setting, budget/60), burst = min(setting, budget/2). The bucket (`e.paceTok {tokens, at}`) lives on a PHYSICAL clock (`deps.paceClock`, default `performance.now()`), charged by `charge()` (so every metered unit and the 1-unit non-metered call drain it); `facts().pace` hands the drain the level NOW; the driver performs `wait` through `sleepFor(e, ms)` (a referenced timer, woken by `stop()` / `dropLive()` AND by `pokeDrain` — a request filed during the sleep is judged at the very next step, a refusal never waits out the ≤ 1 s sleep (lane R5 verify; the bucket is per ACCOUNT, two accounts of one vendor user sum); `deps.sleep` injectable); the adapter's `deps.pace(units)` = `paceWait` (loop until the bucket holds min(units, burst), no-op when no pace is declared; a stop / drop mid-sleep throws a typed `paceAborted` the pass settles as `stopped` / `account-changed`, never a failure). **lane R5 verify r2: `paceWait` judges ONE caller at a time per account in arrival order (`paceQueues`, a promise FIFO keyed by the account id) and RESERVES the units it lets through in the same synchronous step (`e.paceInflight`, released by the `charge()` that follows; `bucketSeen` = the raw bucket minus the reservation is what every judgement and the drain's `facts().pace` read, `bucketOf` the raw one the meter charges) — the check-then-charge across the adapter's `await pace()` let 20 concurrent attachment fetches leave in one instant (400 units in a second on the real Gmail adapter) and starved a page-back behind the pass for the whole ingest. Verify r3: `paceWait(adapterId, units, rec)` ABORTS (typed, `accountChanged`) when the entry it queued against is gone or replaced — a `dropLive` under a full queue (remove / option rebuild) let 17 × 20 units leave within 1 ms, unpaced; `bucketSeen` caps at burst BEFORE subtracting the reservation; a reservation older than PACE_RESERVE_TTL_MS (2 s, never metered = a contract violation) is dropped with a log line; gates ③g (iii)/(iv) + controls.** ② `failPass`: `rate-limited` ⇒ `e.rateStrikes++`, `nextAt` = the vendor's `detail.retryAfterSec` (1 s – 15 min) else RATE_BACKOFF_MS [5, 10, 20, 40, 60] s, the bucket EMPTIED, `consecutiveFailures` untouched, "For you" only at RATE_STRIKES_LOUD (10) — every other code keeps BACKOFF_MS [30 s … 15 min] and the 3-strike item; a good pass / re-authorize / reconnect clears both ladders; **ONE open item per account (verify r2): `speakFailure` retracts the standing `rec.failureItem` as `superseded` (`retractFailure(rec, why)`) before filing — the two ladders had filed two items and the first outlived the recovery.** ③ The view: `backoff {kind: rate|failure, until, strikes, retryAfterSec}`, `vendor` (the module's `vendorNameOf(record)` else `caps.vendorName`), `pace {unitsPerSec, perSec, burst, unit, settingKey, spentLastSec, fetchUnits}`, `budget.perSec`, `scheduler.firstIngest {done, total, etaSec}` (listed, not paused, not vendor-refused conversations with / without `walkedAt`; null once done). ④ A long pass broadcasts its progress at most every PROGRESS_EVERY_MS (5 s) — the rows read since (then not re-said at the end: `early`) + the adapters. Gates: test-channels-aggregate ③b (a transport failure's words), ③d (the rate ladder + its pre-R5 control), ③e (873 paced first reads + the pace-off control + the progress broadcasts, under a real-time watchdog so a driver that spins on `wait` is RED, not a hang), ③f (a refusal filed during a pace wait is answered at sight, real timers, + the no-wake control), ③d′ (two ladders, one open item, + the no-supersede control), ③g (6 concurrent attachment fetches paced ≥ 2 s and a page-back filed mid-ingest taking the next slot, real timers, + the R5 build's paceWait as the control: 120 units in one instant); ⑥d/⑥f pin the back-off door on the FAILURE ladder (transport).
**Lane R5 verify r4 (2026-09-27) — THE ONE EXIT, A CENSUS.** Every lifecycle end of an account's right to call the vendor takes `dropLive(id, why)` — `removeRecord` ('removed'), `setEnabled(false)` ('disabled' — r3 had recorded 18 queued fetches finishing, paced, after the owner disabled the account), `disconnect` ('disconnected', BEFORE the token is cleared — the queued calls used to leave with the Bearer captured before their wait; the entry is rebuilt at once so the card answers the adapter's own `unknown`), `setOptions` on a `rebuild` option, `applyRebind` ('client switched'), `inlineLegacyClient` ('client moved onto the account'), `connect`'s refused begin; `stop()` wakes the same sleepers under `stopped`. `dropLive` disarms the lane, deletes the ONE `live` entry (`live.delete(` has that one site; `live.set(` has one, `adapterFor`), settles the waiters `account-changed`, wakes every pace sleeper (`paceWait` re-checks `live.get(id) !== e0` after EVERY await and throws the typed abort), and parks the entry's minute window + per-second bucket as a GHOST in `paceCarry` — the meter dep charges the ghost when no entry is live (a call that passed the gate before the drop is still charged) and the rebuilt entry inherits it (`adapterFor`), so an exit never refills a bucket (a disable/enable was a fresh 80-unit burst); `removeRecord` drops the ghost. `outlived(rec, e)` (= `stopped || live.get(rec.id) !== e`) guards the write after every vendor call — `ingest` (the page is dropped, `why:'account-changed'`; a remove() mid-fetch used to resurrect the removed account's index row + log page), `discover` (mints no row), `loadOlder`, `attachment` (no cache file; `attachment()` also refuses a disabled account `disabled`). Gate: test-channels-aggregate ③g (v) the exit census over the engine's code (one `live.delete`, one `live.set`, every listed verb's block carries its `dropLive(`, every `dropLive(` call inside a listed verb, the four vendor-then-write paths carry `outlived`; four text controls — the r3 setEnabled, a self-deleting removeRecord, an ingest without the guard, an unlisted dropping verb — and a comment-hygiene control), (vi) disable / disconnect under a full queue (0 calls after, aborted by name, a fresh fetch `disabled`; the minute's spend kept; the r3 setEnabled as a driven control: 4 calls after), (vii) remove() under an in-flight pass fetch / attachment fetch writes nothing (the r3 ingest as a driven control: the row resurrected), (viii) disable + enable after an emptying burst waits (a forgetting exit as the control: 1 ms).

**Lane discovery-cursor-persist (B-6638, 2026-10-08) — THE LISTING CURSOR IS THE RECORD'S.** Discovery's walk state (`e.disc`) is born from the account record (`discFromRecord(rec)` → the PURE drain's `discoveryOf` + `listingVerdict`): `rec.discovery = {cursor, startedAt, at, complete, completeAt}` in adapters.json, beside the feed's `feed.carrying`. `discover()` writes it at every walk's end (complete, cut by the budget or DISCOVERY_MAX_PAGES, or thrown) through `keepDisc` — `store.index.flush()` FIRST, then `saveAdapters()` (a failed flush leaves the record's cursor where it was: the cursor never reaches disk ahead of the rows it listed; test-channels-engine's OWED BEFORE CURSOR crash leg went red without the flush). A boot therefore RESUMES a cut walk from its page (with its `startedAt`, so the unlisting rule stays exact) and never re-lists an account it listed whole (`completeAt` feeds `discoveryDue`'s periodic net). A kept cursor the vendor refuses (`Drain.cursorRefused`: the adapter's typed `detail.cursorRefused` — Gmail 400 "Invalid pageToken", Slack `invalid_cursor`, Lark a page_token refusal — or a `not-found` on a call that carried a cursor) is caught INSIDE the `vendor()` call (no failure, no back-off) ⇒ ONE walk from the first page, said in one journal line ("the vendor refused the kept listing cursor (…) — the listing is walked again from its first page"). `dropLive` (every lifecycle verb: client switch, re-connect, options, disable, remove) clears `rec.discovery` ⇒ the rebuilt entry re-lists from page 1 as before; the owner's re-list = a forced refresh (`Drain.turn`'s `force` wants discovery; with no cursor held it starts at page 1). No adapter lacks stable page tokens: fake / agents answer one page (`cursor: null`). Gates: test-channels-aggregate ㉓ (restart ⇒ 0 listing pages; CONTROL the in-memory base ⇒ 100; a walk cut at page 40 resumes with 60; a refused cursor ⇒ 1 + 100, said once), test-channel-drain (the verdict table), test-channel-adapter-contract (the listing cursor contract).

Gates: test-channels-engine (142), test-channels-aggregate (fast), test-channels-aggregate-ui (heavy). **LANE R2 VERIFY (2026-09-26), five invariants:** ① an INHERITED grain's wakes run one at a time — `wake()` / `flushPending()` go through `inScope(rec, convId, fn)` = `serialWake('scope:acct:<id>'|'scope:pat:<id>')` INSIDE the conversation's chain (the key `flushScope` holds;
