**LANE R2 VERIFY r5 (2026-09-26) — THE REFRESH REQUEST SET: a refresh is a REQUEST, the pass loop is the ONE JUDGE.** Three rounds each found one money defect at the SAME seam — `refresh()` deciding a vendor call against the account's single-flight `pass()` with N callers deciding concurrently (r2: an answer from a foreign pass; r3: the back-off door; r4: a pass per waiter) — and each fix patched the caller's side of it. Now the caller has no side: `refresh(adapterId, convId, {origin})` (the owner's press `refresh`, a window's `open`) and `agentRefresh` (reach first, then `origin:'agent'`) are thin wrappers over **`requestRefresh(rec, e, key, {origin, principal})`**, which appends `{key, origin, principal, at}` to **`e.requests`** (a Map key → waiters) and pokes the loop (`pokeDrain`: ONE pending `setImmediate` drain per account — a burst in one tick is one pass; a pass in flight drains in its `finally` via `e.drainAfter`; the immediate is never unref'd, so a process whose only pending work is an awaited refresh does not exit before the answer). **THE DRAIN** (inside `pass`, `origin:'request'` — such a pass fetches the requested keys and nothing else: no discovery, no due list — an agent's one-conversation refresh never pulls the account's due list forward): every requested key is judged ONCE, in this order — a TIMER/KICK pass in flight that has the key in its due queue carries the waiters (THE RIDER RULE: no gate, charged to the timer); THE BACK-OFF GATE (`backoff && !pressed` ⇒ `backoffRefusal`, where `pressed` = the owner's press (`origin:'refresh'` among the waiters) granted to ONE key per drain while `e.ownerPressEpoch !== e.backoffEpoch`); THE AGENT SHARE (`agentShareRefusal`, only when every waiter is the agent's — `by:'agent'`); THE VENDOR BUDGET (`affordable`, re-judged at the fetch: a cut answers `vendor-budget`, never `0 new`); THE PER-CONVERSATION FLOOR (`floorRefusal(key)`, the agent's, per key per pass); then the key goes to the HEAD of the queue with `by` (`owner` if any waiter is the owner's press or a window's open, else `agent`) — `e.chargeBy = d.by` per FETCH now, not per pass. ONE FETCH PER KEY PER PASS (`done`); a request filed after the drain but before its key's fetch rides it (`take` right before `ingest`); one filed DURING its key's fetch waits for the next drain (the floor for an agent, honest; a second fetch for the owner) — so an `ok` is always a fetch of ITS key that ENDED after the call began. Answers are RECORDED (`w.outcome`) and DELIVERED in the `finally` after `e.passing` is cleared (a caller that awaits its refresh then runs a pass finds the account free; a reader after an `ok` sees the pass's stamps); a waiter no branch answered hears the pass's typed failure (`{code, retryAfterSec, backoffUntil}` — r4's shape) or `failed`. **THE WINDOW RULE (owner decision, r5):** `e.backoffEpoch` increments only when a back-off BEGINS from outside one (`wasInBackoff` false at pass entry); a failure INSIDE a window (the honoured press itself, a forced pass) extends `nextAt` and keeps the press consumed — the owner's door climbs the ladder at most one step per window, the timer's own retries at `nextAt` climb the rest; a drain that fetched nothing inside a back-off returns `why:'backoff'` and touches neither `failures` nor `nextAt`. **BOUNDS, all typed:** `REFRESH_QUEUE_CAP` 200 waiters per account (`refresh-queue-full`, 429, `retryAfterSec:1`); `REFRESH_WAIT_MS` 30 s ⇒ `{ok, pending}` and the waiter leaves the set (nobody listening ⇒ no fetch for it); `dropLive(id, why)` (the five former `live.delete` sites: client switched / connect refused / removed / client moved / options changed) settles every waiter `account-changed` (409) and clears the drain; `stop()` settles `stopped` (503); the tick pokes a set nobody poked (a safety net, never the path). Requests are IN MEMORY — a restart drops them (their HTTP calls fail with the connection) and boot re-files none. `refreshQueueOf(adapterId)` → `{waiters, keys, draining, passing}` for suites and diagnostics. `pass()` lost its `only` option. `watch` still pre-checks `inBackoff` for its `fetched` HINT (whether a request was filed); the drain alone judges the fetch. **THE CLOSING VERIFY (r5 Part 2) found two starvations in the Part-1 drain and closed both:** ① a continuous request storm kept `e.passing` set through every tick and the tick skipped a busy account ⇒ the timer's due list never ran (measured: 0/35 due rows in 600 ms of storm) — now a tick that finds the account busy WHILE DUE sets `e.timerDue`, and the next pass of ANY origin does the timer's work (`timerWork = !backoff && (origin !== 'request' || e.timerDue)`); ② a request filed behind a long timer pass waited for the WHOLE pass (a 40-row pass: fetched at position 40; at 873 rows it would have left as `pending` with its fetch never made) — now the drain runs at EVERY FETCH BOUNDARY (`if (e.requests.size) drain(i)` at the top of each loop iteration; a spliced head item is fetched next) and a requested key already queued and unfetched is PROMOTED to that boundary (`promote(queued, at)`), so any request is fetched within one fetch of its filing; the ONE-FETCH rule now spares an item WITH waiters (`done.has(d.key) && !d.waiters.length`) — a request filed after its key's fetch in this pass is judged anew (the floor for an agent; a second fetch for the owner), never skipped unanswered. The answer itself still lands when the pass ends (by design; a long timer pass ⇒ `pending` at 30 s with the fetch already made and broadcast). `tick` is exported (the suites drive the scheduler's step by hand). Also from the closing verify: a waiter a running pass holds is tracked on `e.inflight` and settled by `stop()` / `dropLive` too (a hung adapter's waiter was invisible to `stop()`), and the 30 s bound's timer is REFERENCED (cleared the moment the waiter settles) — an unref'd one let a process with nothing else to do exit before the `pending` answer. Gate: test-channels-aggregate ⑥g (the storm vs the timer, the request behind a 40-row pass at position 1 + a due-but-late row promoted to position 2, the 200 cap, stop, remove) + the drain-once CONTROL (0/35, position 40). Gates: test-channels-aggregate ⑥f (the 70-cell concurrency table + the every-press control) with ⑥b/⑥d/⑥e's controls RE-POINTED at the drain's own anchor lines (`answer(d.waiters, …)` → everyone from the first fetch; `// THE BACK-OFF GATE` removed; one item per waiter + `// THE RIDER RULE` + `// ONE FETCH PER KEY PER PASS` + the late `take` removed); channel-words words `vendor-budget` / `refresh-floor` / `refresh-queue-full` / `account-changed` / `stopped`; the panel's Refresh-now toast says "still running" on `pending`.

**LANE R2 VERIFY r6 (2026-09-26, the independent closing verify) — two majors, three gate blind spots.** ① THE OWNER'S RESERVE: `requestRefresh` judged the cap for every origin alike, so ONE agent's storm (200 concurrent `vibespace-channels refresh` filed while a fetch held the pass) refused the OWNER's Refresh press and a window's open with `refresh-queue-full` (measured). Now the cap is per origin — an agent is refused once the set holds `REFRESH_QUEUE_CAP − REFRESH_OWNER_RESERVE` (180) waiters of ANY origin, the owner's press / a window's open only at the cap (200) — an agent can never fill the last 20 slots; the refusal carries `cap`, `refreshQueueOf` counts `agents`. ② A REFUSAL IS DELIVERED WHEN IT IS JUDGED: every answer used to wait for the pass's end, so behind a long timer pass a floor / share / budget / back-off refusal judged in the first second reached the agent as `{ok, pending}` at `agentRefresh`'s 15 s race and the CLI printed "refresh started — still running" for a request that was REFUSED and never fetched (measured: an 18 s pass, refused at 0.4 s, heard `pending` at 15.0 s; now heard `refresh-floor` at 0.4 s). `answer()` resolves an `ok:false` outcome at drain time; an `ok` is still recorded and delivered in the finally ON PURPOSE — the r5 starvation guard (⑥c, ⑥g(1)) rests on a lane that awaits its `ok` not re-filing INSIDE the pass it rides, so a request storm stays N short passes each picking up `e.timerDue`, never one pass that outlives every tick (delivering `ok` early re-created 0/35 due rows). ③ `pass()` asked for a TIMER or FORCED pass while another is in flight now runs AFTER it (`e.passing.then(after, after)`) instead of coalescing into it: a refusal lands while its request pass is still writing its stamps, so a caller that awaited one and asked for a pass was handed that ending request pass (⑥c: 40 → 20 hot polls); and the four forced passes (connect / re-authorize / finishAuth / setOptions) asked of a busy account were silently un-forced before. Held under attack (scripts in the r6 report): the back-off window epoch (a press during the opening pass IS the window's press, 2 calls, failures 2; two windows ⇒ two presses; the press's own 429 steps the exponent exactly once; an agent request queued before the back-off and drained after it is refused, never fetched; a press at a boundary before the failing row is a plain request and the window keeps its press), `e.timerDue` (the due rows a request pass carries are charged to the timer; an agent's request on a due row in that pass RIDES — no floor, the timer pays; in a pass without the turn it is its own: the floor), a 25 ms owner trickle for 60 s (the 45-row pass ended at 4.7 s, 45/45 due rows, 2392/2392 settled, 0 `pending`), the budget per FETCH (10/min ⇒ exactly 10 calls, the rest `vendor-budget` by name, riders charged to the timer), settlement under adapter throw / `store-blocked` / a hung adapter / stop / remove (every waiter typed, the set empty), boot (no request file; 591 ≤ 600 calls at the first pass over 873 due rows). Lows left: a request stream faster than the fetch rate defers the due rows for its duration (bounded for agents by share + floor; an owner-origin flood is a human); riders promoted to one boundary come out LIFO; `vibespace-channels` exits 1 (an error) on `account-changed` / `stopped` where 4 (a refusal, retry) is meant; the CLI gate drives only `refresh-floor` / `vendor-budget`; an `ok` behind a very long pass is still heard at the pass's end (`pending` at 15 / 30 s, late-but-true — the fuller design honours `timerDue` at every boundary and interleaves requests with due rows). Gates: test-channels-aggregate 244 → 258 — ⑥f's judge reads `answeredAt` (an `ok` must have a fetch of its key that ended between the call and its ANSWER; CONTROL: the early-answer drain, caught by the instant alone once the owed fetch has landed), ⑥g(3b) the reserve (+ the no-reserve control: the owner refused), ⑥g(6) the budget cut mid-pass — the cut sweep and the drain's own budget line, both unreached by ⑥f's `budget` state, which trips the TOP gate (+ controls: each line answering `ok, 0 new` — both survived all 70 cells before), ⑥g(7) the refusal heard at the first boundary of a 2.7 s pass (+ the record-for-the-end control: heard at 2.7 s).

**LANE R2 VERIFY r7 (2026-09-26) — the two r6 mediums shipped, one medium found, everything else held.** ① AN `ok` IS HEARD AT ITS FETCH: r6 held a true answer for the pass's end on purpose (an early `ok` let an awaiting lane re-file INSIDE the pass it rides — one pass outlived every tick and the due list never ran, 0/35), so behind a long timer pass the agent heard `pending` at 15 s and the owner at 30 s for a fetch that had landed (measured 2786 ms of a 2787 ms pass; now 124 ms). `answer()` resolves EVERY outcome at once; the starvation is closed structurally instead of by delay: `takeTimerTurn(at)` — a tick that found the pass in flight while due set `e.timerDue`, and the pass takes it at its NEXT fetch boundary (discovery if due, the due rows by the clock NOW appended by 'timer', a row this pass already fetched that is due again has its `done` mark lifted; the rider rule searches PENDING items only, `j ≥ at`) — and `interleave(at)`: a request never takes two fetches in a row while a due row waits (`lastBy`), so a saturating stream gives the due list half the fetches (a 2.5 s ten-lane storm: 35/35 due rows DURING it; the no-interleave copy 0/35 during, all 35 only after; a 25 ms trickle with a mid-way re-due: 64–65 of 70 due fetches, every request answered, p50 38 ms — the oversubscribed stream's own p95 ≈ 2.9 s is the honest cost; r6's bytes: 25/70, p50 1648 ms). The per-conversation stamps an `ok` promises (records, anchor, `lastPollAt`) are `ingest`'s, written before the answer; the account's stamps (`lastPass`, the back-off cleared) still land at the pass's end — a pass asked in between runs after it (r6). ② ONE PASS QUEUED PER ACCOUNT (medium, B3): r6's `e.passing.then(after, after)` ran one pass PER ASK, so three forced asks behind a held pass (three Re-authorize presses, three option saves) ran three full forced ingests (measured: 3 discoveries, 80 fetches); `e.after = {force, origin, p}` — a second ask coalesces (`force` sticky), every asker resolves with it (1 discovery, 40 fetches). ③ `vibespace-channels`: `REFRESH_REFUSED` = the codes the agent route answers with a retry-able status (429 / 409 `account-changed` / 503 `stopped`) — exit 4 with the sentence; test-channels-agent-cli DERIVES the set from `chanAnswer`'s status table (the two reply-only retry-ables `send-not-available` / `rate-floor` excepted by name and proven absent from the pass / request-set region), one fixture per code driven to exit 4, `pending` exit 0, a channel-words case per code. ④ riders promoted at one boundary keep their filing order (`at + k`). `idle(adapterId)` = a suite's settle (no pass in flight or queued, no drain, no waiter) — an `ok` no longer marks the pass's end. HELD (measured on r7): the reserve is per ACCOUNT (X's 180 agents leave Y's owner and agent free); `open` is owner-class, so 20 window opens on top of 180 agents spend the owner's own reserve and the press is refused `refresh-queue-full` (the rule: the reserve is the HUMAN's — press + open — and a human's own flood can fill it; low, it drains within one boundary); a jbt_ never reaches `/api/agent/channels/*` (`agentSession` takes vsst_ only); a refusal leaves `e.requests` the instant it resolves (the settled guard; the finally's resolve is a no-op); an agent + the owner on ONE key = ONE fetch charged to the owner, agent +0 (a key is judged by its highest origin — the rider rule, not a refusal); ⑥f's at-start mutant (the RIGHT fetch answered at its START) caught 3/3 cells by the instant alone; a loop fetching one over the budget caught by ⑥g(6); r6's held #11 (the ledger: the turn taken at a boundary ⇒ timer +45, an agent's due-row request rides at +0, floor-refused with no turn) and #13 (an adapter throw mid-drain: 1 ok + 4 typed `transport` with the retry, set empty). Lows left: the owner's own window flood (above); a request stream heavier than the vendor carries beside the due list backs its own tail up (bounded by `pending` at 30 s / the cap). Gates: test-channels-aggregate 258 → 271 (⑥g(8) + r6's ok-for-the-end control, ⑥g(9) storm + trickle + the no-interleave control, ⑥g(10) + the per-ask control, ⑥f's at-start control, ⑥g(6)'s one-over control, ⑥g(1) counted during AND after `idle`), test-channels-agent-cli 25 → 38.

**LANE R2 VERIFY r8 (2026-09-26) — the independent closing verify of r7: one major (fixed), the rest held or recorded.** THE FRONT RUN in `drain(at)`: r7 spliced every boundary's new head at `at` (LIFO across boundaries), promoted riders there, and its rider lookup skipped a key the pass had already fetched — with r7's never-ending pass under a stream, the earliest waiter of every key starved until the stream stopped (the owner's one press under a 4-lane stream heard `pending` at 30 s; 395 vendor calls for 398 requests on 5 keys) and the owner's rider sat behind 180 agent riders (position 181). Now: the requested items at the front (`waiters.length`) are the run; this boundary's head goes after it, its riders join it, a re-request rides ANY pending item of its key (`j >= at`), and the run is ordered humans (`refresh` / `open`) before agents, each class in filing order (gate ⑥g(11) + r7's drain as the control). Recorded: the Refresh toast precedes the window's repaint by the pass's remainder (`notify` at the pass's end); a request waits for a taken turn's discovery; a stopped engine's pass keeps fetching; an ingest in flight at `remove()` re-creates the index row; the CLI census is route-derived only. Full essay: kb-bugfix-invariants r8.

**LANE R2 VERIFY r9 (2026-09-26) — THE DRAIN IS PURE; THIS ENGINE ONLY DRIVES IT.** Every scheduling decision r5–r8 wrote into `pass()` — which key next, who is answered with what, when a refusal is judged, the timer's turn, the interleave, the front run, the rider lookups, the boundary splices, the one-fetch dedup, the cut sweep — moved into PURE `src/channel-drain.js` (the essay above: 17 numbered rules). `pass()` builds the snapshot (`e.dq` = the account's waiters in filing order + the pass; the FACTS from `win(e)`, `budgetDecl`, `lastPollOf`, the back-off epochs, `live.get(rec.id) !== e`), loops `Drain.next` → performs the ONE action it names → `Drain.apply` (the vendor call is the only await between two steps) and keeps ONLY: request admission through `Drain.admit` (`requestRefresh`), the vendor call (`fetchOne` → `ingest`, `discover`, the host scan), the store append (inside `ingest`), the notify, the ledger charge (`e.chargeBy` = the action's `chargeTo`), the answer delivery (`deliver` — exactly the ids an action names; `refusalFor` picks the sentence builder by the action's RULE; `settlementFor`), the failure bookkeeping (`failPass`) and the queued pass (`Drain.queueAsk`). `e.requests` / `e.inflight` are gone (`e.dq` + `e.waiters`: id → the settle-able promise; `w.resolve` withdraws from the drain). Measured: the pass region 231 → 214 lines, its 94-line imperative scheduling block deleted; the engine 4662 → 4650 lines; the decisions are the model's 427 lines (240 of code). Every external surface is unchanged (routes, CLI exit codes, channel-words, the panel, `refreshQueueOf` — which gains `held` — `tick`, `idle`, `budgetView` / `spentBy`, `adapterView`). BEHAVIOUR THAT CHANGED ON PURPOSE: ① the r8 medium — a requested key with news is broadcast AT its fetch, before the answer (`notify([key])`; the pass's end broadcast names only the rest), so the Refresh toast and the window repaint together (pinned ⑥g(8b): the broadcast 0 ms before the answer, ~1.8 s before the pass's end; control = the driver without it, the key named 1778 ms after the answer); ② the share is judged per FETCH (rule 11); ③ THE BOUND (rule 15) — a pass with no due row ends after 25 request fetches in a row and the next starts at once, so a stream no longer keeps one pass (and the forced ingest queued behind it) alive; ④ discovery never ahead of a waiting human, once per pass (r8 low); ⑤ a stopped engine's / removed account's pass ends at its next step (r8 low (c): 43 vendor calls after `stop()` → 0); ⑥ inside a back-off an item whose owner left is refused, the press not spent (found by the walk). HELD, measured on this machine against r8's own bytes: the 70-cell table, ⑥b–⑥g unchanged (the trickle p50 195 ms vs r8's 201 ms, the one-key stream max 62 ms both, the press under four lanes 187 vs 185 ms, the owner's rider at position 1). The integration gate test-channels-aggregate 276 → 278: every control re-pointed through `closedWorld` (a patched model copy required by absolute path from a patched engine copy — the real driver over the one patched rule), r7's combined drain control split into three per-rule copies (no ride → (a), LIFO → (b), owner last → (c)), four setup asserts folded into one, (b)'s press filed from the continuation of whichever lane receives the stream's 5th answer instead of a 200 ms timer (a timer landing in a due-row fetch let ANY newest-first order serve the press at once — the LIFO control was a coin flip; r8's baseline early-answer control was itself red 1 run in 1 on this machine for the same class of reason), + (8b).

**r4 — THE ACCOUNT CARRIES ITS OWN CLIENT; CARDS WORK LIKE MOUNT ROWS (2.369.165, integrations chunk 2; docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md r4 §2.3/§2.4/§2.6/§8.1, D3/D4/D5/D7).** ① **`clientFor(rec)`** = the resolver shape every adapter already reads, PER RECORD (`resolverFor(rec)` is what `adapterFor` hands the adapter): `custom` ⇒ the record's `credential {appId, appSecretEnc}` opened with THIS engine's `.channels-key` (`custom-missing` / `custom-undecryptable` by name, never a preset); `own` ⇒ the copied client, else the retired card's values via the store's `legacyOwnValues` while the copy is scheduled; `cluster:<k>` / null ⇒ the store unchanged (a withdrawn preset is `preset-gone` naming its key). ② **THE CHOICE** (`clientChoice`): `cluster:<k>` (also `clientPreset:'<k>'`, the storage dialog's spelling), `custom` + `credential {appId, appSecret}` (also `clientId` + `clientSecret`) — validated against the row's declared fields and SEALED at once (`sealCustom`: `400 invalid-client` names the field and the rule, never the value), `own` ⇒ `400 own-retired`, an unknown key ⇒ `400 unknown-credential`. ③ **THE TRANSIENT CONSENT** (`startOAuth` / `oauthStatus` / `oauthCallback`): the adapter's OWN begin/exchange runs against an in-memory record (`pending:<hex>`, its token sealed in memory, 30-min TTL); `connect(kind, {flowId, name, options})` CREATES the record at that moment with the flow's client and token (the flow is taken once; `404 no-flow`, `409 flow-not-done` / `flow-failed`, `400 flow-client-mismatch` / `flow-kind-mismatch`); the status `token` is the FLOW ID (the handle the shared consent block writes into its field — never a credential). The pre-r4 record-first `connect` (no flowId) still works. ④ **`reauthorize(id, choice?)` = the mount semantics**: the same client ⇒ its consent (a same-id custom client with a new secret replaces the secret first); a DIFFERENT client is a re-authorization under it (`rebind:true`) run as a pending flow filed under the account's id — the account keeps its old client AND token until the consent lands, then `applyRebind` replaces both in ONE write (a failed consent changes nothing and says `lastAuthError`); `credential-bound` is gone. ⑤ **`duplicate(id, {name})`** over the exported DECLARED `DUPLICATE_FIELDS` (kind; client — the custom secret RE-SEALED with a fresh nonce; filters = the declared options; the push exclusivity claim; the sender line) and `DUPLICATE_NEVER` (token, tracked, assignments, reach, log): an UNAUTHORIZED `<label> (copy)` that consents on its own; `blankRecord(kind)` is the suites' baseline. ⑥ **`referencesOf(id)`** = assignments of its conversations + reach grants with `scope.kind==='adapter'` naming it + its UNSETTLED outbox proposals (any non-terminal state, `unknown` included); agent groups are not counted (D5). **`remove(id)`** refuses `409 account-referenced {refs}` naming each kind; otherwise record + index rows go (logs stay); builtin refused. **`disconnect` drops the token for EVERY account** — the pre-r4 "a further account's disconnect removes it" special case is deleted. ⑦ `setLabel`, `setCustomSecret` (same id only; another id / a preset = `409 client-change-needs-reauth`), `adapterConfig(id)` (D3: the owner-only config with the custom secret in the clear — the storage `GET /api/mounts/:id/config` rule; never broadcast, never logged). ⑧ **THE LEGACY `own` COPY** (`inlineLegacyClient` single-flight / `inlineLegacyClients` for the migration): decrypt through `legacyOwnValues` (`.integrations-key`), RE-SEAL under `.channels-key` onto the record, write, THEN stamp `custom` (a crash between leaves `own` + the copy, which is served and finished); run when a record is read (`adapterFor` / `clientFor`) and by `2026-09-channel-custom-client-inline`; a failure is logged once per cause and the record keeps `own`. The legacy stamp's token evidence binds `own` while the legacy values are complete. ⑨ The digest: every adapter row carries `bindsPerAccount`, `presets`, `clientHint`, `clientFields`, `customClient {appId, secretSet, secretMasked, undecryptable}`; the digest adds `kinds` (every connectable type with its presets, hint, fields, console setup and options — the type-first dialog's input). No Test runner is registered for an account-bound row (D7). adapters.json is written 0600 (it holds sealed tokens and sealed client secrets). routes/channels.js: `POST /api/channels/oauth/start|callback`, `GET /api/channels/oauth/status` (declared before `GET /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId`, which would match), `connect {flowId, name, options, …choice}`, `reauthorize {…choice}`, `POST /adapters/:id/duplicate`, `DELETE /adapters/:id` (409 with `detail.refs`), `GET /adapters/:id/config`, `PUT /adapters/:id {label | credential}`; `fail()`'s detail whitelist gained `errors` / `refs` / `key` / `offered`. Gate: test-channels-accounts (123: ⓪–⑪, a patched-copy control per rule + the pre-r4 engine from git as the control for the retired behaviours), test-migrations (the own → custom leg).

The ingest engine (`create(deps)`): the per-adapter loop with its single
flight, the pass that appends to the durable log BEFORE it advances an anchor,
the ONE broadcast per pass, the digest the panel and every `channels-updated`
carry, and the store's serialized index owner — of which the engine is the only
writer. **The lane is ASKED, never read off `caps`**: the tick's cadence is
`laneState(...).pollCadence` and the scan source is `scanState(...)`, so a
demoted or dead push lane gets the fast cadence back immediately with nothing
else in the tree deciding it a second time. Filtering, assignment and the wake
decision arrived in P2; the outbox, policy and reach in P3 (below).
The routes take `host` everywhere and refuse another machine BY NAME. The
wiring is one `create(deps)` factory called once from server.js, whose channel
flush rides the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.

**THE ACCOUNT MODEL (2026-09-22, owner: "为啥不能和mount那种类似，管理的是账号，
每个账号添加的时候可以选oauth client？").** The panel manages ACCOUNTS the way
the storage mounts do — a Gmail mount stores only the preset KEY of the OAuth
client it was authorized under — and the engine had ONE record per kind whose
credential was "the integration row's current pick", so a refresh token minted
under client A was refreshed with client B the moment the pick changed (Google
answers `invalid_client`; the model itself broke §14.2's "never a silent
swap"). Invariants, one sentence each: N adapter records per kind, the FIRST
keeping `id === kind` (every existing record, conversation, reach entry and
filter valid untouched) and every further one `<kind>:<8 hex>` from
`mintAdapterId`; every record carries `credentialKey` (`cluster:<presetKey>` |
`own`), stamped at CONNECT from the wizard's choice — validated against
`offeredCredentials` and refused `400 unknown-credential` BY NAME otherwise,
the row's own pick (`defaultCredentialKey`) when omitted — and never re-picked
by the row afterwards; `adapterFor` hands the key down in `adapterDeps` and
the adapter also reads it LIVE off the record (so the migration's stamp lands
on an adapter built before it); `connect(kind, {credentialKey, newAccount})`
mints only with `newAccount` or on a kind with no record, else it is the P1a
per-kind path re-authorizing the FIRST account (its `credentialKey` handed
there); `reauthorize(adapterId, {credentialKey})` is BY ID, never by kind —
a key RE-BINDS a TOKEN-LESS record (never authenticated / disconnected:
nothing is minted under its key; the live adapter is dropped so `adapterFor`
rebuilds it under the new key, exactly as an options change does — measured:
the stamp alone left the consent URL on the old client) and is refused
`400 credential-bound` BY NAME on a record HOLDING a token bound elsewhere
(its stamp, else what the token itself names), never dropped (verifier r1);
a legacy record's missing key is stamped by `credentialKeyEvidence`; a FURTHER account's
`disconnect` REMOVES its record, live entry, wake windows and index rows —
only its own, through the two serialized doors — while the first account's
keeps the record (P1a unchanged); `adapterView` carries `credentialKey`,
`credentialLabel` (a preset's env label; `own` is worded by the client),
`credential` (the facts FOR THAT KEY), `credentials` (the offered list, the
"Add account" step's input), `credentialDefault` (the row's CURRENT pick = what
a further account is bound to unless the wizard says otherwise — never this
account's own key; c2), `auth.credentialKey` and `auth.tokenHeld` (does the
record HOLD a token — the client's Connect verb re-binds only a token-less
account); `available[]` carries `credentials` and `credentialDefault` too;
`stampCredentialKeys()` is the migration's verb, through
`credentialKeyEvidence(rec, mod)`: the client the record's OWN TOKEN names
wins when this instance still offers it (a Gmail token carries the
`clusterKey` it was exchanged under, null = `own`; `evidence:'token'`), else
the row's current pick (`evidence:'row-pick'` — what refreshed it until now;
a Lark token names nothing), every stamped row naming its evidence and the
token's key; the live records mutated synchronously, the write queued through
`saveAdapters`, a record whose token names nothing offered and whose
integration resolves to nothing left unstamped (verifier r1: stamping the pick
alone re-bound an org1-minted token to the channels client whenever the pick
had flipped before the upgrade — the case the model exists for). Gate:
scripts/test-channels-accounts.mjs (77) — incl. a patched-copy PRE-FIX
control (both the hand-down and the record stamp removed) that reproduces
the silent swap, ⑤ bound-vs-token-less; scripts/test-migrations.mjs (82) —
the token-evidence legs.

**A ROUTE MAY NOT MINT AN INDEX ROW (r2).** `POST /track` and `POST /read` on
ANY adapter/conversation id wrote a permanent, invisible row into `index.json`
— a file read on every render and deep-cloned by `digest()` on every broadcast
— while the track route's own `404 No such conversation` was UNREACHABLE dead
code, because `setTracked` set `found = true` unconditionally. `known()` now
resolves the adapter from the records and the conversation from the index
snapshot BEFORE anything is mutated, both mutators take the `{create:false}`
entry, and `POST /read` answers 404 too. A `tracked:true` orphan would resume
ingesting the day its adapter id was reused.

**`markRead` DOES NOT BROADCAST A NO-OP, AND ITS DEFAULT INSTANT IS THE NEWEST
RECORD'S (r2).** Both halves are load-bearing, and together they are what
broke a self-feeding loop between this engine and an open window. (1) "Read"
means "I have seen everything this conversation holds", and a vendor is free
to stamp a record ahead of our clock (the fake adapter spreads a day over the
whole current UTC day, so future-dated records are ALWAYS present; a real
vendor's clock skew does the same) — with `now()` those stay unread for ever,
`unread` never reaches 0 and nothing watching it can settle. Taking the newest
record is also strictly MORE honest in the other direction: a record arriving
between it and this instant stays unread instead of being silently marked
read. (2) Every broadcast recomputes the digest (deep-cloning the index),
re-renders every panel and re-reads every open window's tail, so notifying
when nothing moved turned ONE open window into ~490 requests a second, for
ever, with the user touching nothing — rewriting `readAt` ~500 times a second,
i.e. destroying the mark it was setting. The cache-invalidation law is one
DIRTY signal, one computation; an unchanged value is not a dirty signal.

**THE DIGEST CARRIES NO HUMAN SENTENCE (r2)** — see src/channel-caps.js: this
payload is broadcast to every client at once while the language is per DEVICE,
so a sentence composed here is English for everybody by construction.

**THE INGEST IS GATED ON THE RESOLVER (r3, high).** The r2 engine asked
`scanState()` for the CHIP and then called `adapter.history()` regardless,
while `scan.hostFacts` had NO producer anywhere in the product (`scanHost`
had zero callers; the seed wrote `hostFacts: null` and nothing replaced it), so
the resolver could only ever answer `host-facts-stale` — and the fake adapter
re-derived its own source. Measured on the shipped seam: 11 records ingested,
anchor advanced, unread badged, chip "not scanning" — the honesty contract
publishing the opposite of what happened. Three things changed, each with
its own control: (1) `pass()` PRODUCES the facts — `scan.hostFacts` trigger
③ of the three the design names (§4 / §5 invariant 7): unconditionally before
a scan pass that would advance the anchor, the store analogue of "re-resolve
at approval time". ① (the connect wizard) is P1's and ② (the first panel
render past the TTL) is subsumed, because a render has no side effects — the
r2 loop lesson — and every scan pass refreshes anyway. The round trip spends
one request and the facts land on the LIVE row through the serialized door.
(2) `ingest()` asks `laneOrScan()` BEFORE a byte is fetched and refuses a scan
lane with no source (`complete:false`, the anchor stays, `why` carried) — a
refused lane is NOT a failed pass, which is what tells it apart from the
registry's own refusal. (3) The resolved source is HANDED to `history()` as
`opts.source`, and the lane label written on the entry is the RESOLVED lane.
`laneOrScan` now asks `laneState` and follows its `via` (r2 read `caps.receive`
there AND in the ingest label). The pre-fix control wires three patched copies
— engine, registry, fake — to each other, and reproduces the r2 numbers.

**"READ" IS THE NEWEST RECORD'S FOR PAST-STAMPED RECORDS TOO (r3).** r2
spelled the default `Math.max(now(), newest.at)` — right for the fake adapter,
whose records are always future-dated (and whose suite ASSERTED so), and
`now()` for every adapter whose records are stamped in the PAST, i.e. every
real one. There a message stamped before the mark but fetched after it (the
routine shape: the poll interval is 30-300 s) was SILENTLY MARKED READ and
never badged, and `changed` was true on every call, so the no-op-broadcast
rule was structurally inert. The stamp is now the newest record's, or the
existing mark when there is no record (nothing to have seen). The leg drives a
real-vendor-shaped adapter with a growing world and a backdated arrival; the
control is the r2 spelling.

**TRACKING BROADCASTS BEFORE THE PASS IT KICKS (r3).** `setTracked(true)`'s
only notification was the pass it kicked, and a pass the request budget could
not afford returned before `notify()` — so the flag was on disk, the route had
answered `{ok:true}`, and NO client learned, including the one that clicked
(the panel repaints only on the broadcast). Measured: 26 of 30 tracks silent (the verifier measured 19 — the count follows the budget clock)
under the 20/min budget with a 30-conversation adapter (the design measures
~50 for a real account). `setTracked` now notifies on BOTH branches, after the
convCaps refresh and before the pass; the pass adds its own broadcast when it
ingests something. The digest also hands `enabled` to `freshnessClaim`, so a
row on a disabled adapter and an untracked row are published `off`.

Gates: scripts/test-channels-engine.mjs (fast — the r2 + r3 defects above over
the REAL store, each with a patched-copy PRE-FIX control, plus P1a's ⑤ BURST DAY:
newest-first paging to the anchor over the real loop, 340 + 320 records whole with
zero duplicates, the anchor advancing only after a complete walk and never on a
budget-cut one — the boundary, a burst wider than one pass can walk, is stated) +
scripts/test-channels-e2e.mjs (heavy — the P0 exit conditions end to end, incl.
the scan lane's chip/log agreement on the real server) +
scripts/test-channels-i18n.mjs (heavy — a3 of the comm-panel polish: the eight
surfaces rendered under zh AND ja through scripts/dbg-comm-surfaces.mjs, ZERO
Latin-only visible text outside a PRINTED allowlist, a planted-literal negative
control before chrome; a digest code that reaches the screen as English is
what it catches).

P1a (2026-09-16), the real adapters wired: `REAL_ADAPTERS` (lark, gmail) is
the ONE list the engine reads for what is connectable and what each row
declares; the adapter's OWN token is `auth.tokenEnc` on the record, encrypted
by the engine's secret-box on `data/.channels-key` (a SECOND store from the
integrations layer's, §13), decrypted only for the adapter that owns it and
never in `adapterView`; the engine registers each row's Test runner on the
integrations store (the consumer owns the runner, the store dispatches);
`connect(kind)` asks the credential facts BEFORE any record exists and refuses
with a typed `auth-expired {needsCredentials}` — the route answers `409
needs-credentials` — when the row resolves to none, so a refused connect mints
NO adapter row (measured on a fresh worktree boot: it used to leave a
permanent row behind and the PUT/disconnect 404s answered 200 about it); on
a fresh record the row is persisted only after `auth.begin()` returned, and a
begin that throws drops the live instance;
`finishAuth` is paste-back through the adapter's own `auth.finish`;
`onAuthDone` re-asks auth, kicks a pass on success and SAYS a failure on the
record (`lastAuthError`); `disconnect` clears the token and retracts any
failure item; a never-authenticated record is `not-connected` and passes
nothing, while a dead token fails with the vendor's typed refusal and SPEAKS
(fence 8: ONE "For you" item after `FAILURES_BEFORE_LOUD`, naming adapter /
code / vendor words / remedy, retracted by the SAME producer on the first
passing pass — only its own still-open item); discovery pages the adapter's
cursor up to `DISCOVERY_PAGES`; `setOptions` refuses undeclared keys and
values outside `choices` by name and rebuilds the live adapter for a
`rebuild:true` option. The digest carries `available` (connectable kinds not
yet connected, with the credential facts for the wizard's three copy paths)
and each adapter row's `connectable`/`integration`/`credential`/`flow`
(never the flow's `state` secret)/`lastAuthError`/`failureItem`/`options`/
`optionsSchema`. Routes: `POST /api/channels/adapters/:kind/connect`,
`POST …/:id/auth/finish` `{url}`, `POST …/:id/auth/cancel`,
`POST …/:id/disconnect`, `PUT …/:id` `{enabled?, options?}`. Gates:
test-channels-lark-shape + test-channels-gmail-shape (the engine verbs over
the real engine) + test-channels-engine.

**P1b (2026-09-16), the push lanes wired.** `syncPushLanes()` (every tick +
the mutations that change the answer) arms a lane when `pushWanted` — a push
adapter with a live half, enabled, its switch on (an opt-in lane needs an
explicit `true`), a `connected` auth — and stops it when not; every callback
is keyed on the arm token, so a superseded lane reaches nothing. `onPushEvent`
IS FENCE 11: the record lands in the durable log FIRST and the function
RETURNS (= the ack) before the index moves or a client is told; the index
update + broadcast are coalesced per batch (`PUSH_NOTIFY_DEBOUNCE_MS`, one
broadcast never one per message); vendor event ids are remembered
(`PUSH_EVENT_DEDUP_MAX`) so an at-least-once replay is acked and absorbed.
Content rides only while `laneState().carryContent` and the conversation is
TRACKED (invariant 6); otherwise the event is a cursor KICK — one kick-origin
pass per `KICK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` per adapter, respecting the backoff, a kick
arriving mid-pass runs after it. THE MEASUREMENT: `ingest()` samples only
while push carries content, only on an already-anchored conversation (a first
walk is a backlog), only records stamped after `push.contentSince`; a TIMER
pass finding a new record is a miss, a KICK pass finding one is push doing
its job; in kick mode NOTHING is sampled (no ratchet). `checkDemotion` writes
`demotedAt`/`demotedWhy`/`demoted{missed,total,rate}`, logs one line and
broadcasts; the connection stays up (demoted, not stopped). `setPush(id,
{enabled?, claimedExclusive?})` is the ONE way back: a re-declaration zeroes
the counters, clears the demotion and retries the lane ONCE with a fresh arm;
`pushView` publishes the public half (never the raw sample batches), `null`
on an adapter without a push lane. A heartbeat only refreshes `lastEventAt`
in memory; a state TRANSITION persists and broadcasts (`adapters.update`
writes bytes every call). Route: `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id {push}`
(`400 no-push-lane` / a claim outside the closed set refused by name). Gate:
test-channels-push (65).

**P2 — assign, filter, wake (design §7; fences 2 + 12).** Invariants, one
sentence each:

- THE FUNNEL: every lane calls `onFresh(rec, convId, fresh, {lane, origin})`
  with exactly the records that became durable (`appendRecords` now returns
  `fresh`), from `ingest()` after the index step and from `onPushEvent`'s
  content branch (never awaited there — the ack is that function's return);
  after that nothing knows the lane.
- The coalescing window (`coalesceSeconds()` = `channels.pushCoalesceSeconds`,
  default 60, fractional honoured, 0 = wake per message) opens ONLY while
  `laneState().carryContent` holds and `notify:'wake'` — a poll or scan pass
  is already a batch — gated on the RESOLVED lane, never `caps.receive`.
- Hits that must wait are PENDING ON THE INDEX (`en.pending`, bounded to
  `PENDING_CAP` with `pendingElided`), persisted BEFORE the timer exists, so a
  restart delivers them (`scheduleBootPending` → one digest per conversation
  after `BOOT_PENDING_DELAY_MS`); `stop()` only clears timers.
- A hold is a delay, never a drop: a later direct wake CARRIES the entry's
  pending hits along and only the NEW hits are re-held on a refusal.
- `wake()` resolves the target (`liveSessions()`; a group rotates over its
  live members with the cursor in `ix.rotations`, none ⇒ held with a named
  reason), asks `paceVerdict` (held, never dropped), renders the block, and
  calls `deliver.deliverToConversation(cid, text, {kind:'notification',
  spendReason:'channel-message', fromName, cardText})` — the ladder authorizes,
  charges the slot it authorized and releases its hold; the engine adds
  NOTHING beside it (fence 2; test-spend-paths lists the site as an allowed
  forward with its reason); a refusal is `deliver.stashFor(cid, …)` — the
  ladder's own durable stash, drained at the agent's next injection.
- The two derived ledgers (`stats.msgs`/`stats.hits`) are written through a
  non-fatal `ledger()` — a failed write costs one stale number and is SAID,
  never the wake that follows.
- `setAssignment` writes ONE `reachEntries` row `{principal, scope, level:
  'visible', origin:'assignment'}` and `null` removes ONLY rows with that
  origin (a user's grant on the same pair is byte-identical after); both are
  audited. `setFilter` keeps one filter per conversation in `ix.filters`
  (`f-<adapter>/<conv>`), refuses to clear one a filtered assignment still
  names (`filter-in-use`). `estimateFilter` reads `ESTIMATE_CAP` (5000)
  records off the log and passes `capHit` as the estimator's honesty input.
- The digest carries `assignment` (via `assignmentView`: `authority` clamped
  by `authorityCapsFor`, `authorityStored`/`authorityClamped`/`authorityWhy`),
  `filter`, `stats` (`statsView`), `authorityCaps` and `wakeLatency`
  (`wakeLatencyFor`: push = window + ack budget, poll = `pollInterval.hot`
  which the tick itself now uses for an adapter with an assigned row, scan =
  `scanLatency[source]`, reconcile = `RECONCILE_SECONDS`).
- Decision 9 as shipped: `policyRequiresReview` defaults to true (every v1
  adapter is external) until P3's policy store writes `entry.policy.mode`.

Routes (src/routes/channels.js): `PUT …/:adapterId/:convId/assignment`
`{assignment|null, estimateAtSet?}` (404 not-found · 400 bad-assignment /
no-such-filter · 409 authority-capped), `PUT …/filter` `{filter|null,
estimate?}` (400 bad-filter / filter-in-use), `POST …/estimate` `{filter}`.
Wiring: server.js hands `deliver`, `serverSetting` and `liveSessions` (cid +
name + task-group ids per live session) to channels-wiring. Gate:
test-channels-engine ⑥ (125) + test-channels-lane-parity (33) +
test-spend-paths (262).

**P3 — OUTBOX · POLICY · REACH (design §8, §9, §11).** Invariants, one sentence
each: `propose` refuses with the typed `send-not-available` and creates
NOTHING when no identity is offered (refreshing `convCaps` once when the
cached answer is `unknown`/`stale`); a proposal's authority is the user's
`send` or the assignment's EFFECTIVE (clamped) authority, else `draft`;
`decideOutbound` runs with the guards read from settings
(`channels.guardLinksReview` / `guardAttachmentsReview` / `offHoursTz` /
`offHoursStart` / `offHoursEnd`); `direct` sends at once, `review` lands in
`awaiting-approval`. `approve` RE-RESOLVES `convCaps` UNCONDITIONALLY before
the send and a "not offered" answer stops with `send-not-available` + the
adapter's reason, the proposal `failed`, the receipt carrying that reason.
`sendNow` writes the audit ATTEMPT line before the request and the OUTCOME
line after (a crash between them is the state `reconcile` exists for); a
typed refusal is `failed`, a throw is `unknown` and `unknown` is never retried
— the USER gets a For-you item instead. The per-conversation "For you" POINTER
has a count-free text (dedupe-by-text is the idempotence), the count + latest
body in `detail`, its id persisted as `pendingTodoId` on the conversation row,
retracted by this producer alone when the last proposal leaves
`awaiting-approval`, and an inbox throw (the open cap) DEGRADES to the rail
badge + the Outbox window. The RECEIPT rides the ladder with `noWake` (spend
reason `channel-receipt`) unless the assignment's `receiptWake` opted in, a
refusal stashed through the ladder's own stash. Every outbox audit line carries
`draftedBy` / `approvedBy` / `sentAs` / `identityMarking` and none of it reaches
the message body. Policy reads own > adapter `policyDefault` > review. Reach:
`setReach` writes/removes only the USER-origin row; `request` files ONE For-you
item and `decideRequest` approves into EXACTLY ONE visible grant; the agent
reads (`listFor` / `readFor` / `statusFor`) resolve reach FIRST and answer the
uniform not-found. The TTL sweep (24 h) runs from the tick once a minute. The
store gained `outbox.json` (single-owner door, bounded at `OUTBOX_KEEP` = 500
terminal proposals) and `auditTail()`.

P4 (§9.4/§9.5) — EXACTLY ONCE OR HONESTLY UNKNOWN: `sendNow` stamps
`attemptAt` + the WIRE text (`wire`) on the proposal BEFORE the request (what a
reconcile compares against), hands a two-phase adapter's handle to the store the
moment `onHandle` fires (`sendHandle`), and reads a transport failure AFTER the
request left (`detail.lost`) as `unknown` — never `failed`; the OUTCOME audit
line says `lost`. `reconcile(id)` is the ONLY way out of `unknown`, asked by a
PERSON (the card's Check outcome / the route), gated by `canReconcile` on the
adapter's declared idempotency (`none` ⇒ typed `reconcile-not-available`,
audited as `reconcile-refused`); the adapter is asked with the SAME key, the
attempt instant, the wire text and the handle; landed ⇒ `sent` by actor
`reconcile` with the receipt owed now and the unknown-outcome item retracted by
this producer; not-landed ⇒ `failed`; else still unknown with `reconcile.n`
counted — nothing is ever re-sent by the engine. `sweepSending()` runs from
`start()`: a `sending` corpse becomes `unknown` by actor `boot` (`lost-at-boot`).
THE SENDER HONESTY LINE is OFF by default (`channels.senderHonestyLine`; the
adapter record's `senderHonestyLine` true/false/null overrides it via
`setSenderHonesty`, audited) and appended at send time ONLY for an agent-drafted
proposal — `proposalView.honestyLine` says so BEFORE the approval and the
recorded fact after. A send's `observed` sender_type is recorded on the adapter
row as `identityObserved` (the digest carries it) and LOGGED with the flip it
licenses while the declaration is still `unknown`. Gates: test-channel-outbox
(107), test-channel-acl (38), test-channels-identity (55),
test-channels-agent-cli (19), test-channels-e2e (heavy).

**WAKES ON ONE CONVERSATION ARE SERIALIZED (2026-09-16, the P4 verifier):**
`wake()` and `flushPending()` queue on a per-key promise chain (`serialWake`)
and only `wakeNow` delivers, so the boot flush (5 s) and the first tick's
direct wake (5 s) cannot both carry the same held hits (two billed turns);
a wake clears from `pending` ONLY the record ids it carried (`heldIds`) — the
old `pending = []` also dropped a hit that went pending DURING the RPC through
a window's keepPending; a direct wake that carries a window's hits clears that
window's timer (the window's delivery is this wake). Gate: test-channels-engine
⑥ (i)/(j), 140.

**g3 — THE OWNER'S OWN MESSAGE (2.369.159, design §22.2 ①: "an IM, not a feed").** `propose(ctx, a, c, {…, direct:true})` from the USER (`POST /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId/send` — the composer's Send) skips the policy and its guards: the decision is `{mode:'direct', reasons:[], detail:{ownMessage:true}}` and the send is AS THE USER; it still rides the whole outbox machinery (the record, the audit propose → attempt → outcome, the lost answer's `unknown` that is never re-sent, the receipt path). Only `sendAs:'user'` qualifies — a conversation offering only the bot identity answers `send-not-available` WITH the send-as-user reason (`sendIdentityFor` returns `userWhy`), because a bot message is not the owner speaking; an AGENT's `direct` is ignored (agent drafts are what the policy exists for). The digest's conversation row carries `lastText` (the ingest tracks the newest APPENDED record's text + instant apart from `lastAt` — discovery may already have set `lastAt` from the vendor's listing to that very instant — and the push batch does the same). Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §2 (the link that would force review does not hold the owner's own words; the same text without `direct` is review — the control) + test-channels-e2e ⑩b.

**r3 — THE SIDE DOORS, THE FIRST SCREEN, A BLOCKED STORE (2.369.159, 2026-09-23 verifier, each leg RED on the pre-fix tree).** ① `propose(ctx, a, c, input, guards)` and `approve(id, {text, by, consent, mayWake})` pass a send that STARTS A TURN (`sendStartsTurn(rec)` = the adapter module's declaration) through `wakeGate(convId, n, guards)`: `n` = 1 when it goes out now (a direct decision / an approve) else 0; `consent(n)` first — `wake-count-mismatch` `{wakes}` with nothing created (an approve's proposal stays awaiting) — then `mayWake(convId)` — `rate-floor` with nothing created / the proposal still awaiting; a granted slot is refunded when the send ended anything but `sent`/`unknown` (`wakeRefundIfUnsent`). `routes/channels.js` `wakeGuards(body)` = `{consent: ownerConsent(body), mayWake: auth off ? groups.pacerFor('user') : null}` — THE SAME persisted ledger as the group routes (keyed `user|<conversation>`, so a target the group route just woke is floored on the side door too); no groups engine with auth off ⇒ a pacer that refuses by name. `answer3`: `wake-count-mismatch` 409, `rate-floor` 429. test-architecture §49 censuses every `router.post/put` in this file that reaches `engine().propose/approve` or `ge.post/create/invite`: it must hand consent AND the pacer (a planted door is the control). The agent route `/api/agent/channels/reply` hands the agent's own `wakeFloorFor(cid)` (429 `rate-floor` in `chanAnswer`). ② `groupReply` passes the refusal's `group` view on a `wake-count-mismatch` (the panel repaints before its next click). ③ `digest()` carries `quarantined` `[{file, to, why, at, blocked}]` (the first screen names a set-aside store; the For-you item alone left a real instance's vanished accounts unexplained), and the boot inbox item for a BLOCKED entry says it could NOT be set aside (its own i18n key) instead of "set aside as <its own name>". ④ A blocked family's refusal is `{code:'store-blocked', status:503}` from the store; `fail()` answers it as `{error, code}` (it was 500 with `code:null`). Gate: test-channel-groups §2c · §3j; test-channel-store §r3; test-architecture §49.

**r4 — A THROW AFTER THE GRANT GIVES THE SLOT BACK (2.369.159, 2026-09-23 verifier, the leg RED on the pre-fix tree).** `propose` and `approve` wrap everything after a granted `wakeGate` in try/catch: a throw (a blocked store's 503 `store-blocked` from the door, an EACCES / ENOSPC write after the door ran) calls `wakeRefundIfUnsent(gate, guards, convId, id, {threw:true})` and rethrows. The refund reads WHERE the act died: `sent`/`unknown` keep the slot; a proposal whose adapter send was CALLED (`sendLeft` — the id set right before `adapter.send`, cleared when `sendNow` returns, so an entry that survives is a sendNow that threw after the request may have left) keeps the slot; anything else returns the PAIR and the sender's minute (`mayWake.refund(convId, {attempted:false})` — nothing reached the authorizer, so it was not an attempt). Without a throw the r3 rule stands (a refusal returns the pair, keeps the attempt). Before: the grant outlived the throw, so the retry once the store was back was a 429 blaming "a wake less than 30 s ago" that never happened, and eight such errors floored an unrelated group wake for a minute. Gate: test-channel-groups §3j (① /send, door refused → 503, ledger byte-equal, retry SENT · ② /propose, EACCES after fn ran → same · ③ approve, transition refused → 503, ledger equal, still awaiting, re-approve SENT · ④ CONTROL: delivered then the outcome write refused ⇒ the floor stays, retry 429).

**R4 (2026-09-27) — ACCESS and NOTIFICATION, two operations, access first (design §24).** THE GRAINS: `convGrainOf(en)` / `accountGrainOf` / `patternsOf` read each grain's `{access, watchers}` through `F.grainOf` (a pre-split record merged — the engine STARTS before the migration runner); `liftGrainInPlace` lifts a record inside `update()` before any write reaches it (the ledger is never written to a copy); `effectiveFor(en)` = `F.effectiveGrants`. THE VERBS: `setGrain(adapterId, grain, {access?, watchers?, pattern?})` = ONE index update — validates access, mints each inline filter's id `f-<key>|<kind:id>` / `f-<kind>-<id>|<kind:id>` BEFORE the validator (the hotfix's order), validates watchers against the resulting access (`watcher-needs-access`), keeps a kept row's createdAt / estimate / ledger, drops the watcher of a principal whose access went, writes exactly the reach rows the access diff names (`origin:'access'`, per principal), deletes filters nothing references, clears the changed watchers' windows, `prunePending` drops hits nobody waits for, audits `acl` grant/revoke + `watch` set/unset; `setAccess` / `setWatchers` / `removePattern`; `setAssignment` / `setScopeAssignment` = the COMPATIBILITY write (the pre-split validator, then one access + one watcher row). THE WAKE PATH per WATCHER: `onFresh` matches each watcher with its OWN filter (named agents first, then groups), `en.stats.hits` counts the union once, each watcher its own; pending entries carry `for: <kind:id>` (`PENDING_CAP` per watcher, `pendingElidedBy[pk]`; an untagged pre-split entry belongs to the first watcher); windows are `<a>/<c>|<pk>` and `scope:acct:<id>|<pk>` / `scope:pat:<id>|<pk>` (`pendingWindows()` answers `{key, principal, kind}`); `inScope` queues a grain watcher's wake on its (scope, principal) chain (the r2 cap invariant PER watcher — the line the ⑨b / ⑨c controls patch is unchanged); `wakeNow(…, {pk, batch})` reads THAT watcher's ledger, writes it + the conversation history (`p: pk`), and a session the batch already reached gets only the hits it has not seen (none ⇒ no wake, counted delivered); `flushScope(rec, source, patternId, pk)` / `flushPending(…, {pk})` (no pk ⇒ every watcher). THE READS: `rowView` = `access` + `watchers` (each principal once, authority clamped) + the compatibility `assignment` summary; `conversationView.own` / `inherits` / `adapterView.accountGrain` (+ `assignment` alias) / `patterns` = `grainView` (the two lists + the first watcher flat); `adapterView.policy`; `listFor` = `access {authority, via}` + `watched {notify, mode, via}` (+ the pre-R4 `assigned` / `authority`); `accessFor(ctx)` (the status route); `propose` authority = the caller's own access rows; `receipt` wakes only the drafter's OWN watcher (its groups read from `liveSessions`); `referencesOf` names access rows (`kind:'access'`); `removeRecord` also clears the account's scope timers. COMPOSE (B-6acc): `compose(ctx, adapterId, {to, cc, subject, text, why, attachments})` — reach first (access to the WHOLE account: account-scope grants, else the uniform not-found), `caps.compose` (else `compose-not-available`), `P.validateCompose`, `composeCaps` (else `send-not-available` + why, nothing created), authority = the caller's account access rows, `policyFor(rec, null)` (the account's own policy `rec.policy` — `setAccountPolicy`, `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id {policy}` — else the adapter default), the proposal keyed `<a>/~compose/<id>` with `compose:{to, cc, subject}`, ONE account-level For-you pointer (`composePointerSync`, `rec.composeTodoId`), approve re-asks `composeCaps`, `sendNow` calls `adapter.compose` and adopts the thread id as `convId`, reconcile passes `compose`. `searchFor(ctx, q, {adapterId})` = the store's search over the VISIBLE conversations' logs only (`convIds`), newest first. `migrateGrants()` = `2026-09-channels-access-watchers` (plan computed synchronously; blocked store throws). ROUTES: `PUT …/access`, `PUT …/watchers` at the account (`/api/channels/adapters/:id/…`), rule (`…/patterns/:pid/…`) and conversation (`/api/channels/:a/:c/…`) grains; `POST …/patterns {pattern, access[, watchers]}` / `PUT …/patterns/:pid {pattern?, access?, watchers?}` (a `{assignment}` body = the compatibility write); `DELETE …/patterns/:pid` = `removePattern`; the estimate takes `principal`; refusals carry `code` + `why` + `rule` + `principal` + `index`. Gates: test-channels-engine ⑪ + ⑩ (rewritten to the two lists), test-channels-aggregate ⑨ / ⑨c / ⑨d, test-channel-acl, test-channels-accounts (refs `access`), test-migrations. **R4 verify r2 (2026-09-27):** THE LADDER IS AN AWAIT — `stillInEffect(rec, convId, pk, target)` is asked AFTER `deliverToConversation` returns (wakeNow, and its scope twin in flushScope): a refused block whose watcher lost its notification / access mid-flight (or whose group target left the group) is DROPPED by name (ledger `refused:'access-removed'`, the carried hits cleared — nobody waits for them), never stashed for a principal that no longer holds access. A RECEIPT WAKE IS A BILLED TURN: `receipt()` reads the opted-in watcher's `paceVerdict` — over its `dailyWakeCap` the receipt still reaches the drafter with `noWake` (its next turn) and the watcher's `lastRefusal` says `receipt: daily wake cap …`; a delivered receipt wake is written to the watcher's and the conversation's ledger (`receipt:<id>`), so five rejected proposals under a cap of 2 are five receipts and two billed turns, and the next fresh record is held. `orphanWatchers()` (exported) is the boot census of notification rows without an access row at their grain — `F.grainOf` leaves them INERT (the invariant holds at READ, not only at write); `start()` names them once. **R4 verify r3 (2026-09-27):** `receipt()` resolves the opted-in watcher ONCE for its chain keys and queues `receiptNow` on the conversation's chain then the watcher's scope chain (`serialWake` — the order every wake takes), re-reading the watcher and its ledger INSIDE that section: five concurrent rejects under a cap of 2 are two billed turns, not five (the check-then-write race r2 closed for wakes was open on the receipt path); a receipt with no opted-in watcher takes no chain. `stillInEffect` answers `{watched, targetGone}` (`IN_EFFECT` when the ladder said ok): NOT watched ⇒ dropped by name (`access-removed`); watched but the group member woken is no longer a live member ⇒ the hits are HELD (`refused:'member-gone'`, fresh ones re-filed pending, carried ones kept, never stashed for the dead session) and the advanced rotation cursor routes the next wake elsewhere — `refusalWords` is the one speller of the ledger's `why`/`refused` pair for wakes and scope digests.

**R4 verify r4 (2026-09-27) — THE ONE DOOR TO A BILLED CHANNEL TURN.** `billedWake({conv, scopeOf}, fn)`: takes the conversation's chain (`serialWake`, PRIVATE to the door — `wakeChains` is touched only by `serialWake`), then — resolved INSIDE that section, never before it — the watcher's scope chain (`scopeFor` re-reads the effective grain; a scope that MOVED while the wake waited is re-taken under the new key, ≤ `SCOPE_BOUNCE_MAX` 4) and runs `fn` there. The three SECTION BODIES — `wakeNow` (the wake), `flushScopeNow` (the account / rule digest), `receiptNow` (the drafter's receipt) — are called ONLY as the door's `fn` (`wake()`, `flushPending` per watcher inside the conversation door, `flushScope`, `receipt` whose opt-in is read inside the conversation section). Inside each body: the cap read (`paceVerdict`), `reserveWake` (the row `{id, reserved:true, ok:true, lane:'reserved'}` on the watcher's ledger BEFORE the ladder — it counts at once; no row ⇒ `ledger-unwritable`, the hits held, no ladder call), the ladder, `finalizeRow` by id (a failing finalize leaves the reservation COUNTED — fail closed), and a `stopped` check (a wake queued behind one in flight when `stop()` ran holds its fresh hits, `why:'stopped'`). `inScope` and the hand-taken chain in `wake` are gone. `channel-store.js` `markDirty` after `close()` flushes NOW (the hold a stopped wake writes used to be dropped by the debounce guard). THE CHAIN CENSUS (2026-09-27): `onFresh` → `wake()` → door(conv → scope); a coalesce / digest window's timer and the boot flush → `flushPending` → door(conv) → door(scope) per watcher; the scope-digest timer and its boot leftover → `flushScope` → door(scope); reject / approve outcome / `expireSweep` / `sendNow` → `receipt` → door(conv → scope); the group rotation cursor and the ledger are written only inside the bodies; the stash drain (agent-routes) and the migration re-tag open no turn; the owner's approved send (channels/agents.js) and agent messaging (groups-engine, agent-routes) are `peer-message` turns outside the channel cap by design (`wakeGate` / the groups pacer). Gates: test-channels-engine ⑪(j)(k) + ⑫ (the grep-derived census over the shipped bytes, seven controls; ⑪(h)'s copy doubles as the bypass control); test-channels-aggregate ⑨c (the pre-fix shape = the door's scope leg gone AND the row written after).

**R4 verify r5 (2026-09-27) — the door's remaining edges.** ① `reserveWake` stamps `{bootId, pid}` (a per-process `BOOT_ID` minted at `create`); `releaseStaleReservations()` runs in `start()` (tracked) and drops every `reserved:true` ledger row whose `bootId` is NOT this boot's — a crash between the reservation and the finalize used to hold the cap slot for 24 h with no live process; a row with no `bootId` (legacy) is a previous boot's and released, a row of THIS boot (an in-flight wake) is never touched. ② `F.digestCap(w)` = the read-time cap: a `notify:'digest'` watcher with `dailyWakeCap:0` reads as 1 (a digest is a paced wake — cap 0 would never deliver); the three `paceVerdict` sites (`wakeNow`, `flushScopeNow`, `receiptNow`) read through it; `validateWatcher` / `validateAssignment` REFUSE a new cap-0 digest (`digest-cap-zero`, in `ASSIGN_REFUSALS`, worded en/zh/ja via `assignmentRefusalText`); `capZeroDigests()` names stored legacy ones once at boot (the store is not rewritten). ③ `onFresh` matches each record and prepares each watcher inside its own try/catch (a matcher throw on one record is logged by name and skipped, never dropping the conversation's batch) and awaits the door calls with `Promise.allSettled` — the cross-conversation blast radius was already bounded by `track` (a throw never ends the pass). Gates: ⑪(l) (a poison record skipped, the good record still wakes; control loses it), ⑪(m) (a dead boot's reservations released, a same-boot one survives; control releases everything), ⑪(n) (cap-0 digest refused + read-as-1 + boot census; control drops the coercion).

**ALL AGENTS — THE WATCHER FAN-OUT IN THE ENGINE (lane everyone-principal, 2026-10-02).** `effectiveFor` stays the VIEW answer (one All row on every card / digest / agent view); every WAKE path reads `wakeEffOf(en)` = `F.fanOutWatchers(effectiveFor(en), fanTargets())` (`fanTargets` = the live roster's `{cid, name}`; `base` = the unexpanded answer): onFresh's per-watcher pass, `wakeNow`, `flushPending`, `flushScopeNow`'s per-conversation scan, `scopeFor`, `stillInEffect`, `prunePending`, `scheduleBootPending` (10 sites, pinned). So each running conversation under All is its OWN watcher key: its pending hits (`for: everyone:*><cid>`, ≤ PENDING_CAP each — a burst under a digest holds N × the cap of record copies at most), its coalesce / digest timers, its scope chain (`acct:<id>|everyone:*><cid>` — the cap read and the ledger write of one wake never straddle another's) and its LEDGER: `watcherRef` for a fan key finds the stored All row and returns `{stats: row.stats.fan[<cid>]}` (created, pruned with `F.pruneFan`), so reserve / finalize / refusal / hits all land in that conversation's ledger; `storedWatcherFor(holder, pk)` answers a fan key as that conversation's watcher while it runs (null once it stopped — its hits are dropped, never stashed for a conversation that is gone); `resolveTarget` names the fan item's ONE conversation (`via:'everyone'`; the stored row itself is never a target); `othersFor` reads `base` (the "also on this conversation" line says "all agents", never one line per conversation); `ledgerView` counts `F.ledgerRowsOf`; `releaseStaleReservations` sweeps every fan ledger too; the public `flushScope(adapterId, source, patternId)` (no pk) flushes an All watcher once PER running conversation (each its own digest). A named agent beside All is never billed twice for the same hits (the batch's `got` dedup — the agent's own watcher sorts first). The request door answers `via` (an All grant ⇒ "already allowed", no card). Gate: test-everyone-principal ③ (the real engine: 3 running × cap 2 ⇒ exactly 2 each, a later conversation fresh, controls: one shared ledger ⇒ 2 in all, no cap ⇒ every hit bills everybody).

**B-f32b (lane channel-index-copy, 2026-10-03) — A READ OF ONE CONVERSATION COSTS THAT CONVERSATION.** `known()` = `store.index.has` (never `snapshot()`), `convFor` = `peek`; whole scans read `live()` (or `rows()` + `touch()` inside an update). THE KEPT ROW FACTS (`rowFactsNow`): per account, what the clock does not move (listed, unread, unlisted, paused, overridden, reading, walked) from `index.onTouch` — a partial digest re-reads the touched rows only; a full digest / a whole-map touch / `ROW_RESUM_MS` (60 s) re-sums. THE PACED CENSUS (r2, the coordinator's ruling): `schedulerScan(rec, t)` = the census from every row (the definition; exported as `schedulerExact` for the gates); `schedulerView` = the kept facts + the CLOCK counts (hot / warm / cold / due) walked at most once per `censusEveryMs` (`CENSUS_EVERY_MS` 5 s) per account; a broadcast inside the window arms ONE trailing walk + `notify([], {full:false})` through `censusTimer` (deps — a suite injects both; never armed from a trailing broadcast); `censusStats()` = walks per account. Gates: test-channels-index-scale, test-channels-census-pace.

### src/server/channels-outbound.js (ORCH — a family of channels-engine.js)

**WHAT THE CARD SHOWS IS WHAT LANDS (lane lark-upload-preflight, 2.369.229).** `filesOfferFor(rec, cc)` = the `send-attachment` offer over the files row judged from the account's HELD scopes (the module's `capsOfScopes` — an account fact, never a stale cache), else the conversation's cached row. PROPOSE: `attachPrepare(rec, proposal, ctx, cc)` refuses a file the account cannot carry as `bad-proposal` / `attachments-not-sendable` with `requiredScopes` and the owner's Re-authorize step in the sentence (nothing created). CARD: `proposalView` adds `filesBlocked {why, requiredScopes}` to an awaiting proposal with stored files the account cannot carry; channel-policy `shownFields` covers it (a card drawn before the change approves nothing — changed-since-shown). APPROVE: `withoutFiles` (the card's "Send without the file", POST …/approve `withoutFiles:true`) — a plain Approve of a blocked card is refused `attachments-not-sendable`, nothing sent; a files-only proposal cannot go without them (`nothing-without-files`); `withoutFiles` stamps `filesLeftOut` and the send hands the adapter no file, the result's parts gain one `left-out` part per file (reason "partly sent — … NOT landed …"). PARTIAL SEND: `speakPartial(p)` (beside the agent's receipt, after a `sent` transition whose parts missed) files ONE For-you item, origin channels, `open-channel` keyed `outbox:<proposal id>` (never merged with the conversation's approval pointer), "Sent to <title> WITHOUT the file <names>: <why>" + the Re-authorize step, urgency high, i18n keys; a part the owner left out himself files nothing. test-architecture §65 names it as an owner surface.

**Lane dc-channels-seams (2026-10-05).** `create(engineCtx)` → the outbox, moved verbatim: the guards and the honesty line (`guardsFromSettings`, `honestyLineFor`, `noteIdentityObserved`, `identityFor`, `sendIdentityFor`), the proposal views (`proposalView`, `agentProposalView` + its withholding, `drafterSees`, `stashGate`, `outboxView`), `transition` (a guard asked inside the store's serialized write), the wake gate + refund, the reply target (`replyTargetFor`, `replyRecheck`), the outbox's attachments, `propose` / `proposeReaction` / `compose` / `composePointerSync`, the decision (`approve`, `reject`, `prepareEdit`, `withdrawProposal`, `replaceProposal`, `onProposal`), the receipts (`receipt`, `receiptNow`, `noteReceiptStash`, `reconcileReceiptFates`), THE SEND (`sendNow` — the attempt line BEFORE the request, the outcome after; `sendReactionNow`), `reconcile` / `reconcileReaction`, the sweeps (`sweepSending`, `sweepReplaces`, `expireSweep`, `filesSweep`) and `pointerSync`. A billed wake goes through the engine's ONE door (`billedWake`, from the context). The engine keeps the stash listeners (`offStash` → `noteReceiptStash`, `offStashGate` → `stashGate`) and the expiry sweep's clock.
