last connect failure and a filed "For you" item are SAID on the section; the
tracked picker is a checkbox per discovered conversation (tracked is opt-in,
each tick a `/track` POST that is refused loudly and reverted); the options
editor renders the adapter's DECLARED `optionsSchema` (a select for
`choices`, `''` restores the default) and PUTs `{options}`; Disconnect is
confirmed; Enable/Disable PUTs `{enabled}`. Invariants, one sentence each:
nothing here branches on an adapter's kind; every string that a vendor, a
peer or the server composed renders through textContent; the "next phase"
empty text is retired — an instance with no adapter shows the connect rows.

**THE ACCOUNT MODEL (2026-09-22, the owner's mounts analogy — c2, the wizard
and the panel; the server half is channels-engine's).** One sentence per
invariant: every Connect / "Add account…" entry lands in `startConnect(app,
spec)` and MINTS (`newAccount: true`) — the P1a per-kind re-point of the first
record is never issued by this client; the wizard's spec (`wizardSpec`) is read
off the digest alone — `credentials` (what the integration offers a NEW
account right now), `credentialDefault` (the row's own pick, pre-picked never
forced) — from an `available[]` entry or an existing account's row, the same
three fields; the CREDENTIAL step (`showCredentialStep`, stepper index 0) is
drawn ONLY when more than one credential is offered — exactly one ⇒ that key
rides the connect body and the step is skipped silently (no empty step, no
extra click), none ⇒ the body carries no key and the server stamps the row's
pick; the step is a radio per offered credential (a preset by its env LABEL —
data, rendered through textContent, never translated — `own` worded here as
"Own client"), Cancel there mints nothing, Continue posts `{credentialKey,
newAccount:true}` and `showFlowDialog(…, shell)` moves the SAME dialog on to
the consent step; an existing account re-authorizes ITSELF — the status-line
verb and the ⋯ menu's Re-authorize / Connect post `/adapters/:id/reauthorize`
by id, never the kind; a TOKEN-LESS account (`auth.tokenHeld` false: never
authenticated, or disconnected) runs the credential step FIRST when more than
one is offered — its OWN key pre-picked, never the row's default over it —
through `showCredentialStep(app, spec, {submit})` posting `{credentialKey}`
to ITS `/reauthorize` (a re-bind; exactly one offered rides the body
silently, as for a new account), while a HELD token posts `{}` — the server
refuses another key by name (`credential-bound`, worded in channel-words:
disconnect first, or add another account); "Add account…" (⋯ menu, `3_auth` order 15, gated on
`connectable`) opens the wizard for another account of that kind; a section is
NAMED BY ITS ACCOUNT (`accountName`: the token's user when the auth carries one,
else the kind's label, NUMBERED "Gmail account 2" in record order only when
the kind holds more than one — a lone account keeps its plain name; the head's
tooltip keeps the kind beside the account); the credential chip
(`.chan-cred-chip`, the preset's label / "Own client") is drawn only where it
disambiguates — the kind holds several accounts OR the integration offers
several credentials — and never for a legacy record with no key; every section
carries `data-adapter=<id>`. Gate: test-integrations-ui ⑩ (two offered ⇒ the
step with the chosen key in the body; "Add account…" ⇒ two sections with
distinct names + chips; Connect on a token-less account = the credential step
with its OWN key pre-picked, the chosen key posted to ITS /reauthorize and
re-bound server-side, the second section's to ITS id; one offered ⇒ skipped;
the withdrawn preset said by name on the account it minted).

The rail panel (adapters as sections, a freshness chip on every row, the
`channel-row` menu and the ⚙ row as CONTRIBUTIONS registered by the module
that owns them — gear-menu.js never learns the row's name; since 2.369.124 the
row files itself under the Communication ▸ head with `parent:'comm'`, order 10) and the conversation window (a registered window type; plain text through
textContent on every path; a composer ONLY where `offers()` allows one, and a
named reason where it does not). The panel repaints from the digest the engine
broadcasts rather than re-fetching; the window re-reads its own tail when its
id is named (§10.4).

**MARKING READ IS A USER ACTION, NOT A REPAINT SIDE EFFECT (r2).** The POST
lived at the end of `render()`, which the broadcast handler calls — so the
engine's notify re-rendered the window, the render POSTed /read, the POST
notified, and the cycle ran at ~490 requests a second for ever (measured in
headless chrome on the shipped fake adapter's own data: 5,482 broadcasts and
5,479 /read POSTs over ten IDLE seconds with ONE window open). It is now
issued when the window OPENS and when the user touches it, and only while the
last drawn summary says there is something unread.

**THE PAGE BOUNDARY IS A RECORD, NOT AN INSTANT (r2)** — the window sends
`before` AND `beforeId` (the store's `(at, vendorId)` total order).

**THE FRESHNESS SENTENCE IS COMPOSED HERE (r2)** — both files import the PURE
`src/channel-caps.js` directly and render `freshnessText` / `identityWarningText`
with their own `t`, because the digest is broadcast to every client while the
language is per DEVICE.

**THE MANAGER OWNS TITLES (r3).** `winInfo.setTitle?.(c.title || convId)` was
a PERMANENT no-op — the winInfo literal (src/lib/window.js) has no such member
and none is ever assigned, `setTitle(id, t)` is a WindowManager method — so
every channel window's title bar, taskbar entry and tab label read "Channel"
and two open conversations were indistinguishable. The same
silent-optional-call shape as the `off?.()` r2 removed; jobs-panel.js had the
identical call. Both now call `app.wm.setTitle(winInfo.id, …)`, the e2e leg
reads the title off the window, and test-window-types censuses the idiom
across src/lib. The panel's section header also says `disabled` for a
disabled adapter, beside its rows' "not polling" chips.

**THE ws HANDLER IS REMOVED BY NAME (r2).** `ws.onGlobal()` returned undefined,
so `off?.()` in both teardowns was a silent no-op: a CLOSED channel window kept
re-rendering, kept fetching and kept POSTing /read over the user's mark (3,689
POSTs in six seconds from three closed windows, and the mark itself
overwritten), holding its whole detached DOM subtree alive. `onGlobal` now
RETURNS its own unsubscribe — that is the load-bearing half, MEASURED:
reverting it alone reddens the contract pin while reverting the two teardowns
alone is ALL PASS — and the named-const teardown is a belt that does not depend
on a return value nobody asserts.


**g3 — THE PANEL IS AN IM (2.369.159; design §22, the owner's clarification of 2026-09-22 "the first screen is the group list, a simple IM").** One sentence per invariant:
the FIRST SCREEN is ONE list (`.chan-groups`, rows `.chan-grow` — distinct classes from the account rows `.chan-row`, so nothing that counts or measures the account rows ever sees a group row) of every agent group and every TRACKED conversation of a non-built-in source, sorted by last activity (`groupListRows`); a row is glyph · name · time / source chip (`Agents` / `Direct` / the account's label) · last line · unread, carrying `data-grow` (the key), `data-group` (a group) and `data-at` (the instant it is ordered by); archived groups fold apart under "Archived groups (n)" (per page session); an UNTRACKED external conversation is NOT in it (nothing fetched, no history — its Track verb stays in the account's section) and neither are the built-in agents SOURCES; the accounts (every non-built-in adapter's section + the Connect block) and the **Message watcher** (the built-in section, found by its `builtin` FACT — the pre-g3 `kind === 'agents' || id === 'agents'` spelling is gone) are SECONDARY `.chan-part`s below, each folded by the user, the fold PATCHed to user state as `channelsPanelFolds` (merge-only, only the known parts, only a literal true — `foldsFrom`; lane channels-fold: a part in `FOLDED_BY_DEFAULT` — `internal` — is folded until a literal false opens it), loaded once per page and followed from other clients through `user-state-updated` (every live panel repaints; a panel no longer in the document is pruned at the next dispatch); the panel draws from TWO broadcasts, each carrying its own recomputed half — `channels-updated` the digest, `channel-groups-updated` the owner's group list (with `unread`) — and neither repaint fetches (test-channels-groups-e2e ⑥ counts both routes; test-channels-e2e ⑬ still counts `/api/channels`); the bar's house button **New group** (plus glyph + label, the label hidden only under 160 px) opens `showGroupMembersDialog`; a group row's context menu is the group's own verbs (Open / Members & notifications… / Invite… / Rename… / Archive), a channel row keeps the `channel-row` contributions.
THE COMPOSER IS DECIDED BY `composerMode`, NEVER AN ADAPTER ID: an external conversation offering `sendAsUser` ⇒ **Send** (`data-channel-direct`, `POST …/send` — the owner's own words out at once, as the owner; the note says the outbox holds only agent drafts; the toast words `sent` / `failed` / `unknown` by state); only `sendAsBot` ⇒ **Propose** (`data-channel-propose`, `POST …/propose`) with "Sending as you is not offered here (<the send-as-user reason>)" before the policy sentence; nothing offered ⇒ the untracked footer or the named read-only reason, NO composer element (P0's exit condition unchanged); the inline outbox cards stay for agent drafts.
AN AGENT GROUP IS THE SAME `channel` WINDOW TYPE (`openSpec {action:'openChannel', adapterId: GROUP_ADAPTER_ID, convId: <groupId>}` — layout restore, sync, tabs, taskbar unchanged, `isGroupConv` routes it to `openGroupWindow`): the log from `/api/channel-groups/:id/messages` (paged upward by `before`), a system record (create / invite / leave / kick / rename / archive) worded HERE by kind in the device's language (`groupSysText`; the record's own `text` is the agent-facing English, the fallback), the invite's context under its record (`.chanmsg-ctx`), the owner's messages drawn as "You"; the bar = the name + a members chip (`data-group-members`) + ⋯ (the group's verbs) + a meta line (Agent group / Direct conversation · You (observer) · member names · Archived); THE COMPOSER SENDS DIRECTLY AS YOU (`data-group-composer`, `data-group-send` → `POST /api/channel-groups/:id/post`, never `/propose`): `@` opens an autocomplete over the member names (`mentionQuery`/`mentionCandidates`/`insertMention`; ↑/↓/Enter/Tab/Esc, Esc stops at the popup), a PREVIEW under the box names who THIS text would wake — "Will wake alpha, beta — 2 billed turn(s)" in amber, else "nobody is woken" (`wakePreview` = the model's own `mentionsIn` + the D2 table; test-channels-groups-ui proves it equals the engine's `wakeVerdict` over notify³ × five texts) — and the send answers with its record (drawn at once, deduplicated by `vendorId` against the broadcast's `messages`) and the wake echo in the toast (`wakeEchoText`: woke N = N billed turns, said at 0; refused wakes "not billed"; who reads it next turn); an archived group has no composer; the window marks the group READ on open and on touch while it has unread (`POST …/read`, a user act, never a repaint); the broadcast updates the bar from the list and appends the new records — no full re-render per event.
XSS: every group name, member name, invite context, last line and message body reaches the DOM through textContent (`el()`, `.textContent`, createModalShell's title, showContextMenu's plain `label`) — test-channels-groups-ui's census over the five client files has ZERO innerHTML writes, with a planted `title.innerHTML = r.title` as its control, and test-channels-groups-e2e renders a hostile `<img onerror>` name as text in the row, the bar and the window title.
THE NARROW-RAIL THRESHOLD IS 160 px (was 180, MEASURED): the taller IM panel scrolls at the default 260 px sidebar and the list's own 15 px scrollbar dropped the content box from 187 to 172 px — under 180, so the DEFAULT width drew the narrow layout whenever the list scrolled (latent on any long list before g3; test-channels-e2e ⑫(a) went red on exactly that). Gate: test-channels-groups-ui (fast) + test-channels-groups-e2e (heavy) + test-channels-e2e ⑩b/⑫/⑬.

**r3 (agent groups, 2026-09-23):** the conversation composer reads the adapter row's `sendStartsTurn` (from `GET /api/channels/:a/:c`'s `adapter`): the note says "it wakes this agent: 1 billed turn" (amber) and the Send carries `expectWakes: 1` (0 elsewhere). The GROUP composer posts through `fetchJson` itself (not `groupPost`) so a `409 wake-count-mismatch` that carries the server's `group` view REPAINTS the bar, the preview and the @-autocomplete before the toast — a member renamed since the window drew it no longer makes every click a 409 (the server also re-announces renamed members: groups-engine `noteRoster`). The panel draws one `chan-quarantine-note` warning line per `digest.quarantined` entry above the group list (adapters.json: "your accounts were reset, reconnect them"; blocked: "could NOT be set aside — changes are refused"), zh + ja.

**R4 (2026-09-27) — two operations, access first:** the account ⋯ = Grant access… (order 10) · Notify… (11) · Conversations matching a rule… (12, a new rule starts with its access); the conversation row menu = Grant access… · Notify… (the retired "交给一个 agent…" / "Assign & filter…" / "Assign to an agent…" and their words are gone from the code and both dictionaries); `grainLines(a)` draws "Access: A (may send), Group · 工作 (drafts) · Notify: A wake per batch on a filter" for the account (`a.accountGrain`) and "Rule: … → Access: … · Notify: …" per rule through `grainSummaryText`, a click = `showGrainMenu` (the two operations; a rule adds Remove the rule). The row's line 3 and the window chip read `assignmentSummary(conv)` = the same two facts from the row's `access` / `watchers` + "(account)" / "(rule)"; the window chip opens Notify… when the conversation has access of its own, else Grant access… (unassigned words: "Grant access…" / "No agent has access here — nobody sees it, nobody is woken."). SEAM (lane R3 on the first screen): this lane touched only the account ⋯ items, `grainLines`, the row menu's `3_assign` group, the accountCard comment and the chip's two strings — never the first-screen list arithmetic or the status tag.


**Lane channel-rich (2026-09-28).** `renderRecord(rec, {…, mail})`: a record with a formatted body (`role: 'body'`) gets the mail frame's SLOT under its text body (`createMailFrames` in src/lib/channel-mail-frame.js, created once per window beside `folds`, with the window's `mailModes` memory) — the ONLY srcdoc on the channel surface, never in this file (test-channels-images §⑤'s no-innerHTML pin and test-channel-record ⑧ hold); `renderAttachments` never draws a `role: 'body'` attachment as a file chip. **D3:** a bot author's name wears the bot mark — `icon('robot', 11, 'chanmsg-bot')` (the icon library's SVG, `role=img`, titled / labelled t('Bot')) between the name and the time.
**lane channel-threads (2026-09-28) — the window's three additions, all keyed and textContent.** `renderRecord(rec, {cont, base, folds, ctx})` draws a reply's QUOTE LINE (`quoteLine`: a click jumps — flash when drawn, page up ≤ 5 pages when loaded but not drawn, a toast when older than everything loaded; a parent never stored is said in words), a root's THREAD CHIP in its head and a reply's dim `in thread` tag (`channel-thread-pane.js`), and the REACTION STRIP (`reaction-picker.js`, `+` only where `react` is offered). A reply or a root breaks the author run (its line needs a head). The list and its composer are one column (`.chanwin-main`) inside `.chanwin-split`, where the thread pane sits beside (≥ 620 px) or over (< 620 px) it — never inline, never in the layout. A `channels-updated` broadcast carrying `patches` / `rereadReactions` / `threads` is applied IN PLACE (the strips by key, the chips re-spelled — and a `threads` entry whose `root` is a drawn row that headed no topic (a plain message or a quote just answered with `reply_in_thread`) makes that row a `topic-root` and grows its chip; no `/messages` fetch, no row rebuilt) and returns before the page patch; a message broadcast's `patchNow` re-read also reconciles every drawn row's strip by key (attack 16 — a window that missed a `patches` broadcast heals on the next one). THE TRICKLE: an IntersectionObserver over the rows (list + pane) asks `POST …/reactions/refresh` for the visible ids (debounced 800 ms, newest first, ≤ 20, skipping ids asked within the TTL) and holds itself quiet on the ceiling's refusal. `drawRxNote` = the one line that says reading reactions needs a permission (Re-authorize PUTs `options.reactions:'read'` first; ✕ hides it on this device per account).


**The internal block (lane channels-badges, 2026-10-03).** `build()` draws `fs.shown` through PURE `internalBlock` (folded = `FOLDS.internal`, never under a query); `internalHead(block)` is a KEPT `<button class="chan-ihead">` patched in place (chevron · the VibeSpace badge · "VibeSpace internal" · (N) · @-you · unread), its click `setFold('internal', …)` = user state `channelsPanelFolds.internal` (PANEL_PARTS) ⇒ the `user-state-updated` broadcast folds every client. FOLDED BY DEFAULT (lane channels-fold — the owner, 2026-10-03: `foldsFrom` reads an absent `internal` as folded, the user's unfold is `internal: false`, synced the same way; before the folds load the panel draws the default). test-channels-groups-e2e ①b (the default on a fresh user state, the unfold PATCHes `false`), ⑧ (it survives a reload), ⑪ (a second client's fresh load, both ways). Both account heads (`accountCard`, `section`) draw `accountBadge(badge, 'chan-sec-kind', name)`, the badge handed down from the build's ONE `accountBadges(adapters)` map (a per-build local — no long-lived Map for test-record-clear-census H4) (the kind tile `kindGlyph` is retired). test-channels-groups-e2e ⑪ census: every row's badge ≡ its card's icon (glyph + hue + title); the fold persisted and synced to a second client.

### src/lib/channel-groups-view.js (PURE)

**R3 (2026-09-26, design §23) — src/lib/channel-focus.js (PURE, imports nothing; re-exported here):**
- `statusTag(row, now)` returns the ONE tag of a first-screen row (`{kind:'conv', conv}` or a digest row itself; a `groupListRows` AGENT GROUP row — `kind:'group'` WITH its `group` — wears none; a digest row's own `kind` is the conversation's and never means that). The priority: awaiting (outbox.awaiting) › unknown (outbox.unknown) › assigned (the effective assignment: the CONVERSATION grain always; a pattern / account grain ONLY once it acted on the row — a wake DELIVERED within 24 h (`touch.wake.ok === true`, lane ≠ `none`) or a held one — D4, the integrator's ruling 2026-09-27: handing the owner's 824-thread mailbox to an agent must not put all 824 back on the first screen; otherwise the row falls through; the tag carries `grain`, `held` rides it) › read | new-since-read (the newest agent read inside FOCUS_WINDOW_MS 24 h, EXCLUSIVE edge; `lastAt > upTo` splits the one fact) › held (`heldOf`: pending, or a last wake with lane `none`, or a refusal newer than the last wake, inside the 7-day HELD_WINDOW_MS; a STASH is not held) › replied (`touch.selfAt` inside 24 h).
- `focusRows(rows, now)` = the non-archived agent groups + every tagged conversation, in the input's (activity) order.
- `filterRows(rows, q)` = a case-insensitive substring over title / source label / last line.
- `firstScreen(rows, {view, q, now})` → `{view, focus, all, shown, moreInAll}` (the counts are the WHOLE lists).
- **The R3 × R4 seam (2.369.191):** `heldPending(touch, now, watchers)` = the pending hits that are HELD — the engine's `touchView` sends `touch.pendingFor` `[{p, n, oldest}]` per principal; a principal whose R4 watcher row is `notify:'digest'` with its window (`oldest` + `digestMinutes`, edge EXCLUSIVE) still open is the digest waiting, not held; an orphan / legacy (`p: null`) hit is held; a touch without `pendingFor` falls back to the total. `heldOf(touch, now, watchers)` and `statusTag` pass the row's `watchers` (`c.watchers`). Gate test-channels-focus ⑦ (a table, the real engine, the pre-seam total and a statusTag without the watchers as controls).

Words: channel-words `statusTagParts(tag, {now, t})` → `{before, who, after, tone, icon, title}` (the name travels through `t()` as a marker, so zh "{agent} 读过" and en "→ {agent}" both split), `agoText` (just now / Nm ago / Nh ago), `viewSwitchText`, `attachmentReasonText`. All take an injected `t` so the width census words them in every language from one process.

THE IM-FIRST PANEL'S ARITHMETIC (g3): DOM-free and word-free — every function returns STRUCTURE and the panel / window say the words with the device's `t`; its only import is the PURE group model (`GROUP_ADAPTER_ID`, `NOTIFY_MODES`, `DEFAULT_NOTIFY`, `OWNER`, `mentionsIn` — spelled once there; test-architecture's EXCEPTIONS row names the edge). `groupListRows({groups, conversations, adapters})` → `{rows, archived}` (groups + TRACKED non-built-in conversations, newest activity first, order a property of the data); `composerMode({group}|{conv})` → group | archived | direct | propose (+ the send-as-user `why`) | untracked | readonly (+ `why`); `mentionQuery(text, caret)` (an `@` at the start or after whitespace/an opening bracket, read up to the CARET; `x@y` is an address) / `mentionCandidates(members, q)` (prefix first, then substring, never the owner) / `insertMention`; `memberRows(group)` (the owner FIRST as the observer, an unknown stored mode reads as the default); `pickerSections(sessions, tasks, {exclude})` (one section per Task Group by title, each session ONCE, no-group last, members DISABLED, nothing pre-selected — D1); `wakePreview(group, text)` (who a draft sent as You would wake — mute never, an @ yes, `always` yes); `wakeCount(answer)`; `foldsFrom(userState)` + `PANEL_PARTS` + `FOLDED_BY_DEFAULT` (`internal`: absent = folded, lane channels-fold). Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §1 (incl. the wake-preview PARITY with the engine's `wakeVerdict` and a mute-blind preview as its control).

### src/lib/channel-group-dialogs.js (CLIENT)

THE AGENT-GROUP DIALOGS (g3, design §22.5): `showGroupMembersDialog(app, {group?})` = New group (name + members + opening context + "Wake now", default ON) or Invite… (the same dialog minus the name, existing members drawn disabled "already a member"): the members come from `GET /api/channel-groups/roster` titled by the sidebar's Task Groups (`groupTitle`), ONE checkbox per session and none per group (D1), the echo under Wake now says the cost BEFORE the click ("will wake N agent(s) (N billed turn(s))" / "nobody is woken — they read it on their next turn"), Create is disabled until a name and two agents (Invite: one) are picked, the answer's wake echo is the toast and a created group's window opens at once (never waiting for the broadcast); `showGroupDetail(app, group)` = the member list (the owner first as "You (observer)" — "sees everything, never woken"; every member's notify mode as a select the OWNER may change for anyone, reverted with a toast on refusal; creator chip; "not running" for a member whose session is not live; Remove, confirmed, a pair's removal saying the direct conversation will be archived) + Invite… (not on a pair) / Rename… / Archive (danger), repainted IN PLACE from `channel-groups-updated` (skipped while a select is mid-choice); `renameGroup` / `archiveGroup` via showInputDialog / showConfirmDialog; `groupPost` toasts every refusal by its CODE (`groupErrorText`). Every agent-controlled string is textContent. Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §3 + test-channels-groups-e2e ①④.

## Index essays (moved VERBATIM from the CLAUDE.md index on 2026-09-15 — CLAUDE.md keeps the head of each entry; this section is the full text)

### src/plugin-manifest.js

src/plugin-manifest.js — PURE plugin manifest validator (Plugin Ph2, 2.369.24): id=<publisher>.<name>=folder, semver, engines.vibespace min, client tier, server flag, contributes windows/agentTools/routes, declared capabilities; 2.369.43-.44 hardening = cleanText() on every free-text field (it reaches generated code), fs paths COLLAPSED **and their `*` wildcard MODELLED as the string prefix node matches** before the forbidden-root test (`/*` / `<parent>/*` used to pass; B-7638: the two rules meet at `~/.*` — collapsing the dot emitted `<home>*` = the whole home dir + every sibling home, so a `.` segment before `*` is refused), agentTools ⇒ needsConsent

### src/server/plugin-loader.js

src/server/plugin-loader.js — PLUGIN LOADER (Ph2): data/plugins/<id>/ manifests → sandboxed iframe assets at /plugins/<id>/ (opaque-origin CSP), forked server.js processes (IPC v1: route/tool/shutdown, crash backoff, parked after 5/10min), /api/plugins/<id>/x/* proxy (nosniff + sandbox CSP, no document content-type from an untrusted plugin), generated agent-tool shims data/bin/vibespace-tool-<id>-<name> → /api/agent/plugin-tool/ (bearer-validated; manifest text enters them ONLY through jsLiteral), data/plugin-registry.json (consent is per PACKAGE: contentHash+source, a different package under a trusted id is disabled + re-prompted — gated on the REGISTRY record, never on a folder having been replaced: 2.369.44, consent outlives a hand-deleted plugin dir), broadcasts plugins-manifests-updated. Example: docs/examples/hello-plugin

### src/channel-record.js

src/channel-record.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE normalized message record every channel adapter produces (docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §4): {id, convId, adapterId, vendorId, at, author, text, mentions, attachments, replyTo, threadKey, raw}. THREE rules: **`vendorId` IS THE DEDUP KEY** (a replayed page must be a no-op — Lark's anchor semantics guarantee one at every boundary; a screen-scraping source DECLARES a minted key with `raw.synthetic`, because the invariant wants A key, not a vendor-issued one, while an UNDECLARED minted key turns every re-scan into a batch of duplicates); **`@_user_N` are PER-MESSAGE ORDINALS, not identities** (resolved against that message's own `mentions`, and an ordinal with nothing behind it is left VERBATIM — inventing a name is the mis-attribution the rule exists to stop); **an external body may not carry OUR OWN frame syntax** (`<system-reminder>`/`<vibespace-*>`/`<task-notification>`/`<persisted-output>`/`<local-command-stdout>`/`<command-name>`/`<command-args>` are neutered at NORMALIZATION, because the record is the one shape every consumer reads). **r2: the neutering runs over EVERY peer-controlled field, not just `text`** — `author.name`, `mentions[].name` and `attachments[].name` came out with LIVE frames, which made that claim false at SOURCE while §7.5's agent block renders `from <author>`; `peerText()` is the ONE door, attributes are matched too, and the fixed half of the pattern is held by a grep-derived FRAME CENSUS (every hyphenated tag the tree writes must be neutered or classified as prose) because a hand-written list is the tool this class defeats. **§25 (2026-09-27): an OPTIONAL `blocks` render tree (`OPTIONAL_FIELDS`) whose SCHEMA lives here — `BLOCK_KINDS`/`RUN_KINDS`/`BLOCK_LIMITS`/`safeHref`/`validateBlocks` (rule 3 over every string of the tree, an unsafe href demoted to text, refusals by name); makeRecord keeps only a valid tree.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **verify r2 (lane lark-threads ⑥):** `peerName` answers null for a name with NO visible character — the joiners it keeps for Persian / Indic / emoji words (U+200C / U+200D) never make a name alone (a joiner-only name was a blank head / alias / nickname instead of the id).

### src/channel-caps.js

**Lane dc-channels-blocks (2026-10-05):** `pushUnavailableText(code, {t, words})` renders the LIVE LANE's declared words (live/lark.js + live/gmail.js `UNAVAILABLE_WORDS` {code → i18nKey}, exported by the adapter as `unavailableWords`, validated by the registry, carried by the engine's `pushView` as `unavailableWords` while the lane is parked); an undeclared code falls back to the lane's own `why`. No lane code is spelled here.

src/channel-caps.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE place that answers "does this control exist" and "which lane is carrying this row RIGHT NOW" (design §4/§6.4/§12.5). Two axes MODELLED not flattened: how messages arrive (push|poll|scan + the per-PLATFORM `scanSources`/`scanLatency`/`historyBySource`) and what may be sent as whom (`sendAs`, narrowed per conversation by `convCaps`). **`laneState` = DEMOTED > LIVE > CLAIM** and `unknown` (the default) never carries content; liveness needs POSITIVE evidence and a demoted or dead push lane answers `via:'poll'` because that is where the records come from — the fact used to live in three stores with nothing saying which won (the `opencode-events` round-4 lesson: a lane that lies about being active is worse than no lane, because it turns the fallback OFF). **`scanState` = FACTS FRESH > PLATFORM > CLIENT PRESENT > READ GRANT > `'ui'`**, with ONE deliberate exception: a REFUSED read is the NAMED `tcc-denied` with `source:null` and never a silent fall back, because swapping a 15-second lane for a 5-minute one turns the latency on the row — this class's whole honesty contract — into a lie. `convCaps`/`scan.hostFacts` are CACHES (vendor round trips, not re-derivable) and pay for it with a 6h TTL + an honest degrade. `offers` needs BOTH halves and renders `unknown` as "not offered + a reason"; `freshnessClaim` takes its clock as an argument because it answers "how long ago". **r2: THE RESOLVERS RETURN STRUCTURE AND THE CLIENT SAYS THE WORDS** — `freshnessClaim` answers `{kind, state, seconds}` and `freshnessText(claim,{t})` renders it (the engine called the old composing form with no translator, so nine human-visible strings shipped English-only to a zh/ja UI, invisible to the build's i18n scan because they left the server as DATA; and the server structurally cannot take a translator — the digest is broadcast to every client while the language is per DEVICE). `state` exists because `kind` alone collapses "not scanning" with "not scanned yet"; `identityWarning` keeps only the adapter's OWN `verbatim` sentence on the wire. **`authState(record, now)`** is the same discipline for "is this adapter authenticated": the LAST PASS's `auth-expired` outranks a stamped expiry that has not arrived (a revoked credential carries a perfectly future one), a passed expiry is `expired`, and NO credential is `unknown` — never the stub whose two ternary branches were both `'connected'`. **r3: `freshnessClaim(caps, lane, entry, now, {enabled})` answers `state:'off'` + `why` (`untracked` / `adapter-disabled` / the scan resolver's own reason) for a row nothing will ever fetch** — untracked is the DEFAULT state of every discovered row and "within 5m" there was a promise about a fetch that would never happen; `tracked` is read STRICTLY, and `freshnessText` renders `off` as "not polling" / "not scanning" by lane. **P1b: `pushSamplesAdd`/`pushMissRate`/`pushDemotionVerdict` = the exclusivity MEASUREMENT over a ROLLING window (24 h or the last 200 records, whichever is larger; 2 % over ≥ 20; never true for a lane already demoted), `pushLaneText` = the adapter row's sentence WITH the numbers, `caps.pushOptIn` = the poll lane until `push.enabled === true`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **verify r2 (lane lark-threads ②):** `feedThreadsText` names the hits waiting for a by-id read (`missingWaiting`) — "{n} waiting to be read one by one" (zh/ja).

### src/text-window.js

src/text-window.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS — the server, the daemon via transcript-service, and the client bundle share it) THE ATTACH SLAB IS A TEXT WINDOW (chat pipeline perf lane A, 2.369.167; **bounded by GROWTH and asked for per attach since perf r1**). `TEXT_WINDOW` = the frozen table {minText 24, minRecords 50, maxRecords 400, maxGrowthBytes 128 KiB}; `isTextCard(m)` = a user message with non-empty text (never a tool_result carrier) or an assistant message with a non-empty `text` block — thinking, tools, system/info cards, image-only attachments and rewound messages do not count; `textWindow(list, opts) → {start, textCount, reason, growth}` walks back from the tail until minText text cards are inside, never fewer than minRecords (tail(50) is the FLOOR — nothing ever gets less than before; the floor's own records are never even measured), never more than maxRecords, and PAST the floor stops before a record that would take the bytes past the floor over `maxGrowthBytes` (`sizeOf` injectable; default = the record's JSON length, the unit a ws frame's `data.length` counts) — a pasted image (≈ 540 KB of base64) past the floor therefore ENDS the walk, it is never pulled in for the text around it; `reason` ∈ text | maxRecords | maxGrowth | all; `sliceTextWindow` = what every normalizer's `tailWindow(opts)` returns. **`attachWindowOpts(hint)` + `SLAB_HINTS` (perf r1): the attach frame's `slab` word → the opts — `'floor'` = `{minText:0}` = tail(minRecords) exactly; anything else (absent = an older client, `'text'`) = the text window. Both ws attach paths read this ONE mapping; the client decides the word (src/lib/view-visibility.js `attachSlab`).** DETERMINISTIC by construction (the 2.369.2 identical-skip depends on the same list giving the same start). **WHY THE GROWTH BUDGET (perf r1, the verifier's 19-window probe): the first cut bounded the WHOLE window at 2 MiB, and on the 6 MB §1c fixture the walk to 24 text pulled a 513 KB image in past the floor — 208 records / 1.55 MB per attach vs tail(50)'s 637 KB; shipped to every one of 19 windows that was 29.8 MB per cold open (master 12.3 MB), first paint median 277 → 756 ms, server CPU +78 %, and the 14 hidden windows of a restart paid it too.** Numbers (the claude normalizer over the whole generated file, printed by test-text-window every run; the fixture's byte cut depends on the scratch cwd, so counts move by a few per machine): 6 MB = 822 records, floor 50 rec / 622–637 KB / 5 text, text window 103 rec / 750–768 KB / 12 text (maxGrowth); 48 MB = 5,832–5,892 records, floor 72–118 KB, text window 73–112 records / 108–218 KB / 22–24 text (on one cut the next record past the budget is a 501 KB image). The first cut's "3,779 records / 222 records / 896 KB / 188 records / 832 KB frame" numbers came from ONE 48 MB single-window run and did not reproduce within 20 % on the harness fixture (×2.4 frame, ×2.5 first paint on 6 MB, 114 samples) — the claim is the BOUND, not a ratio. Gate: scripts/test-text-window.mjs (fast).

### src/quota-model.js

src/quota-model.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the bundle and the shipped statusline carry it) THE TYPED LIMIT SET (2026-09-09): an account key holds a LIST of limits — {limitId, name, scope plan|model|credits|overage, windows[{kind,minutes,usedPct,resetsAt,state running|empty|unknown,measuredAt}], flags, provenance} — because the vendors send several at once (B-9213: codex pushed `codex` + `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark` + `premium` in ONE conversation, all collapsed last-writer-wins into one file with the plan limit GONE) and because a window that has not started reports `resetsAt = now + duration` on every read (B-8b12: a sliding reset became a precise panel time, an EDF deadline and an auto-resume arm). `limitFor` = the ONE accessor, `remaining`/`deadline` ignore empty windows, `mergeLimitSets` merges per limitId. Also `windowRefutes`/`wallAttribution` = whose wall is this (inc-mttbrtc0-6049): a running window's reset cannot move before it ends, so a contradicting reset REFUTES a member but identifies nobody — the slot ledger identifies, the window corroborates, and only their agreement moves a byte. **r2: `refutationStrength(kind)` says how much that refutation is worth — WEEKLY (7d/scoped) `decisive` (0 self-contradictions in 9998 judged readings here), FIVE-HOUR `corroborating` only (73.72 % of its refutations are true positives, but 13/1706 of its own producer's readings contradict its own stamp — B-9213 inside the plan bucket), anything unmeasured `none`; refusing a wall is money too, so a 5h disagreement nothing corroborates leaves the pin and SAYS so.** **r3: a bucket that makes a CLAIM must keep counting — `windowState` tests the stated spend BEFORE the reset (a deadline says whether a window STARTED, never whether it is spent), a stored `state` may not survive a producer re-stating the numbers (producers drop it at the restate, `fromLegacy` keeps the clock-free `usedPct > 0` belt for files older builds wrote — but a `status`-only event leaves it, or a genuinely empty window flips to running), and `toLegacyView(set,{nowSec})`'s `fiveHour` is THE BINDING BURST CONSTRAINT — ranked by `windowRemaining` on the accessor's own clock (a passed reset means the window ROLLED OVER and is full; ranking on raw `usedPct` re-created the very defect, accessor 50 % vs pool 90 %) with the plan window SEEDED so it wins every tie — so the projection can never be more optimistic than `remaining()`.** **r6: `markScopedEnumeration`/`scopedEnumeration`/`authoritativeScopesOf` = DID THIS READ SEE THE WHOLE SET — the ONE rule the enumerating producers ask before they may RETIRE a limit, marked on the parse result as a NON-ENUMERABLE, SYMBOL-KEYED property so a spread / a JSON round trip / a preserve-merge all lose it (no authority = the safe direction) and no stored file can forge it.** **B-9f4b: the r5 half counts only a model cap the parse NAMED (`scopedNamedCount` — a display name, a `seven_day_<model>` key, a panel line; a codename bucket never), and `toLegacyView` never projects the limit promoted into the plan slot a second time as a `scopedWeekly` row.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **THE MODEL-CAP LANE (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21):** `MODEL_CAP_PLACEHOLDER` = {limitId 'model:cap', name 'Model cap'} — scope model, family null: it counts for the account-level min (the conservative direction), governs no named family, and is NEVER the plan; `scopedLimitId(name)` is the ONE id spelling (fromLegacy, the harness builder and the naming rule ask it; 'Model cap' round-trips to model:cap); `nameModelCapLane({limits, scoped, resetsAt, hint, jitterSec})` is the PURE ladder — the sidecar family with this reset → an existing model limit with this reset (±WINDOW_JITTER_SEC) → the hint family among several → else the placeholder; a window with NO reset is named only by a hint matching a cap the account has SHOWN; `foldPlaceholderCap`, run by every `mergeLimitSets`, is the ONE permitted collapse: the placeholder folds into the single NAMED model limit sharing its weekly reset (the newer window wins), stays put on a different or absent reset or an ambiguous pair, and two NAMED limits still never collapse (test-quota-model ⑲). The legacy projection is untouched: a plan-less set still projects its only window-bearing limit (⑭, codex's rule), so a claude file whose first reading is an un-windowed bucket event shows it as `sevenDay` until the first 5h/7d event lands — bounded, documented, never the case on 2.1.274 where every record states the plan windows.

### src/usage-cache-write.js

src/usage-cache-write.js — THE ONE WRITE PATH for data/usage-cache/*.json (design-account-hardening §4.2): validates the typed set, merges per limit, stamps source/fetchedAt per LIMIT, writes the legacy buckets as a DERIVED VIEW beside `limits`, owns the `.window-`/`.slot-` sidecars, and composes (never forks) the slot/window guards. A grep-derived standing sweep fails any other writer; the reader census fails any unclassified raw-bucket reader. **r2: a CLAUDE array with no `plan` limit takes its plan limit from the legacy view — the shipped statusline (the one allowlisted whole-object writer) now spreads the stored object instead of enumerating what to keep, and DROPS the single limit it can measure so this rung rebuilds it with that object's own source/clock; every other limit keeps the provenance of the producer that measured it.** **r5: the LIFT is the other half — a legacy object is ONE reading spread over a carry-forward, so `carryUnmeasuredLimits` (lift-only, WINDOW granularity, never applied to a typed set) keeps the previous reading's `source`/`fetchedAt`/`measuredAt` for any claim (`quotaModel.limitClaimKey` — the numbers, never the clock or the derived state) the write did not move, and `authoritativeScopes` lets ONLY a producer whose own parse enumerated a scope retire a limit it no longer names. A file's `source` and a limit's `source` are different questions and may disagree.** **r6: the right to retire is asked of the PARSE (`quotaModel.authoritativeScopesOf`), which each producer marks only when it dropped nothing — the three claude parsers disagreed on one vendor state, so six of the seven sites retired a spent cap they could never have seen; and the retirement line now NAMES the claim it drops (`model:opus (100% 7d, running)`), because removing a limit removes a constraint the pool reads.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **The lift rung restores a MODEL cap too (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** a claude object whose `limits` array lacks the limit a legacy `scopedWeekly` entry names is that entry's reading — the statusline drops the `model:<name>` limit it measured exactly as it drops the plan one (2.1.274 ships `rate_limits.model_scoped[]`) — restored with the object's own provenance; every write-path write projects the array INTO `scopedWeekly`, so an entry only outlives its limit through the producer that cannot construct one (test-quota-model ⑲ LIFT).

server.js — BOOTSTRAP + WIRING ONLY (~1910 lines since the 2.325.0 拆分; the arch suite RATCHETS it — ≤2100, lowered to ≤1907 by lane dc-seams-server (1905 on its base + 2.369.215's two wiring lines): the editor routes → src/routes/editor.js, recordUsageAttribution → src/server/usage-attribution.js, the setup-token sweep → the claude descriptor's expirySweep). **One HOT PATH still lives here and it is named: `refreshWebuiPids()`** — it runs IN-BAND on every kill (ws-handler, before the broadcast) and 3 s after every create, so it asks `cli-identity.readChildPids` and starts NO child process per session (the `pgrep -P` it replaces blocked the loop 9,180.6 ms for 61 sessions at 1,560 MB RSS for the identical 244 pids). server.js is in BOTH halves of the test-architecture §45 spawn census — half (b) finds it by looking up where `refreshWebuiPids` is DEFINED — and its four surviving spawns (auto-update `git pull`/`npm install`/`npm run build`, `resolveCmd`'s `/usr/bin/which`) each carry a BOOT-ONLY reason. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### scripts/ci.mjs

scripts/ci.mjs — THE RELEASE GATE, TWO TIERS (B-4c5a, 2026-09-07): the tier table `{name, tier:'fast'|'heavy', why}` + EXCLUDED-with-a-reason, both runners, the detached `--heavy-launch`, the push-blocking `--check-heavy`, `--status`, `--census`, and (round 2) the MACHINE lock that keeps one heavy tier per box + `machineGlobalFixtures` (PURE: a suite claiming a literal port it binds or a fixed `/tmp` path it creates — banned in the fast tier, asserted over every fast row). Exit codes: 0 green · 1 red · 2 refused (dirty tree / bad `--only`) · 3 did not run (never got the lock) · 4 ABORTED (superseded / lock taken / terminated) — 0 and 1 are the only VERDICTS and no no-verdict path may ever exit 0. `killedFromOutside` is an ALLOWLIST of SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP (round 4): a crash signal is a fact about the code under test. `fastGate` also takes `--isolate --sha=<x>` (round 5): the hook runs the FAST tier in a scratch worktree AT a pushed ref's tip when that tip is not the commit you have checked out, writes NO green marker for it, and NAMES its subject in the closing line. `runSuite` SKIPS (never fails) a suite the gated commit does not contain (round 6 — the table is this gate's, the sources are that commit's; both tiers count them, the heavy marker carries `absent`, and a run where every suite was absent claims nothing). Imported (never re-run) by test-architecture §43 so the census rides in `npm run build`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **2.369.104 THE SCRATCH-ORPHAN REAPER (owner 2026-09-16 "系统变得异常缓慢，进程树里有大量vibespace相关进程", the KVM went blank): every worktree server a gate suite boots spawns a DETACHED `vibespace-device` daemon (setsid, by design — production's must outlive a server restart) plus wrapper/child node processes, and a suite's teardown kills only the server it spawned. Measured: 504 device daemons (34.8 GB RSS, up to 76 h old) + 552 node processes under /tmp/vs-* + 2,137 orphaned `dtach -a` bridge clients, 86 GB used, load 15. `scratchOrphans({procRoot, now, staleMs, self})` is PURE over a proc root (test-ci-gate §9 drives a fake one): a process's ROOTS are its cwd, HOME, VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT, VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT, AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR / _PROFILE / _CONFIG and a `--user-data-dir=` argv (`scratchRootsOf`, `ROOT_ENV`; lane H verify r1 added the last four), and it is grouped by the FIRST that lies under a `/tmp/vs-<name>-<random>` scratch dir (`SCRATCH_ROOT_RE` — the shape scripts/scratch.mjs mints; production is rooted in a checkout); a GONE root lists every member nobody alive outside the group owns (walking parents through fellow members reaches systemd/init or a vanished pid — never a live process outside the group), WHATEVER ITS NAME; an EXISTING root lists its members only when EVERY member is unowned AND older than the 10-min fixture stale floor, and then only the KNOWN executables (`REAP_NAMES` + `vibespace-device*` + `chrome*` — the name allowlist survives for this rule alone); a ci.mjs runner is never a candidate (the isolated heavy tier lives in /tmp/vs-ci-heavy-* for its whole run) and this process + its ancestors are skipped. `reapScratchOrphans` SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs after 3 s; the heavy tier never calls `runSuite`, so master's wiring alone reaped nothing between heavy suites), at the start of every `heavyLaunch`, and by hand as `node scripts/ci.mjs --reap`. 不变量=a process a suite starts is the suite's to end, and when the suite cannot (a detached daemon) the gate owns the standing sweep — evidence-based (root + ownership + age), never a name heuristic, never production.** **LANE H VERIFY r1 (2026-09-25) — CANDIDACY IS EVIDENCE, NEVER A NAME.** The sweep had a name gate that ran BEFORE the evidence (`if (!named) continue;` ahead of the root lookup), and its roots were only cwd / HOME / the two device roots. the tiers'/launcher's catch sites print it, reapByHand catches on both paths (`--reap refused: …`, exit 2). test-scratch-reaper 132: §2 579 (a deleted cwd outside the shape, never stat'd — a spy on fs.statSync), 581 (an exists-denied root whose cwd link is a linked dir), the X1c line in (12b), §3b the vanished table × 4; controls (23) the stat unconfined, (24) the linked directory unasked.

**Lane mirror-green r2 (2026-10-03) — SHARDS.** `--heavy --shard <i>/<n>` runs ONE slice of the heavy tier — what each job of the Actions `heavy-shards` matrix runs (4 slices, `timeout-minutes: 45` each, `fail-fast: false`); one aggregate `heavy` job (`needs: heavy-shards`, `if: always()`, green only on `success`) is the tier's single status. PURE `shardPlan(suites, n, {serial, fixtures, sourceOf})`: the serial group (`scheduleLanes`' own judgement — SERIAL rows + machineGlobalFixtures) whole in shard 1, every other suite in shard 1 + FNV-1a(name) mod n (`shardHash`) — a function of the names and n alone (same table ⇒ same split whatever its order or the markers; adding a suite moves no other). `shardCensus(suites, shards, serial)` → problems (a suite in no shard / in two / sharded but not heavy / the serial group split). `parseShard('i/n')` (1 ≤ i ≤ n, else exit 2); `--shard` with `--only` / `--affected` = exit 2; `--dry-run` lists the slice (no lock, no build). A shard's marker is PARTIAL (`partial` = its names, `shard: 'i/n'`), never the tier's verdict. No `--shard` = the whole tier, unchanged. Runner balance (.198 + .200 logs, 7790 s summed): 45 / 65 / 60 / 48 suites = 1329 / 2044 / 2519 / 1899 s. Gate: test-ci-gate §8b (censuses at n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, order independence, insertion stability, the CLI's four dry-run listings = the tier, ci.yml's matrix = every slice + the aggregate; controls: a dropped / doubled suite, a split serial group, a 3-of-4 matrix).

**Lane fast-budget (2026-10-04) — FAST LANES.** The Actions `fast` job was cancelled at its 15 min on .202/.203/.205 and never wrote a verdict: 269 suites one after another, 792 s summed here, ×1.34 on the runner. Fix, two halves. (1) Every fast suite over THE TIER RULE's 10 s was profiled (a per-line elapsed stamp; the gaps name the leg): the accidental costs were fixed in the suite — re-scans of an unchanged tree per planted control (memoise by text / path), waits on the jobs engine's 5 s `_sweep` tick (ask the sweep), a re-arm judged by sleeping on real intervals (capture the watch's own setInterval and fire it), a fake daemon whose pid was the suite's own (an 8 s stop grace) — and the suites whose cost IS the real clocks, children or Workers they judge moved to heavy as `slow —` rows saying so (reset-credit-ui, browser-windows, browser-cli-pin, browser-kept, windows-device-fs, vnc-view, desktop-stream-keepalive, agentd-worker-pool, scratch-reaper, and exit-run as a heavy SERIAL row: it judges regex complexity by hrtime ratios). (2) `fastGate` runs over `fastLaneCount()` = min(4, cpus) lanes by `os.availableParallelism()` (a taskset / cpuset shrinks it; 4 on the 4-cpu runner — 3 lanes measured 192 s there against 165 s; `VIBESPACE_CI_FAST_LANES` overrides), longest first by each row's own measured `· N s` (`scheduleFastLanes` over `scheduleLanes`), fail-fast kept (a red starts nothing new and SIGTERMs the suites in flight; theirs print as "stopped", never as a verdict), the async reaper after every suite. `FAST_SERIAL` holds the CLOCK judges — a bound ≤ 1 s or a ratio of two clocks, from a census of hrtime / performance.now / `Date.now() - t0 <` over the fast suites — which run alone after the parallel lanes drain, since the pre-push hook runs on a busy box and a verdict may not depend on load; a ≥ 2 s bound that only tells answered from hung, and every work-meter judge, stays parallel; test-fixture-isolation is `last`. A new fast suite that judges the clock belongs in FAST_SERIAL with its reason. The run closes with the lanes' wall vs the suites summed, the 10 slowest and an informational WARNING per fast suite over 10 s (a clock gate flakes, so it never fails the run). Measured in the runner's shape (depth-1 clone, node 22, taskset 0-3): ≈ 845 s serial before (build + 269 suites), **165 s** after (build 12 s + 4 lanes 102 s + the serial lane 51 s; 438 s of suites); the real runner reads 1.30× that shape, ≈ 4.2 min with setup against the job's 15.

### scripts/scratch-run.mjs — the run record (B-1d08, 2026-09-29)

WHO OWNS A SCRATCH ROOT, in one module both sides share — node builtins only, because the gate's stub repositories copy ci.mjs with its siblings. `RUN_RECORD` = `.vs-run.json`; `procStat(pid, procRoot)` = `/proc/<pid>/stat` parsed (`comm`, `state`, `ppid`, `starttime` = field 22, `exitCode` = field 52, a zombie's waitpid status); `machineBootId(procRoot)`; `makeRunRecord({pid, run})`; `stampScratchRun(dir, opts)` (tmp + rename); `readRunRecord(dir)` (null unless a positive pid AND starttime — a record that cannot prove an identity is no record); `runOwnerState(rec, {procRoot, bootId})` → `{alive, why}` (another boot / gone / a zombie / reused ⇒ dead). Writers: scratch.mjs `scratchDir` + `scratchHome`, mutant-copy's dirs, ci.mjs `addScratchWorktree`. Reader: ci.mjs `judgeScratch`. A suite that PLANTS a detached process on purpose plants it under a root made by `scratchDir` (live owner) — never under a root it removed.

### scripts/vendor-response-census.mjs — THE VENDOR-RESPONSE CENSUS (lane lark-threads verify r3, 2026-10-01)

Not a test (never a `test-*.mjs`): ONE implementation both shape suites import. `blank(src)` blanks every comment and string/template body to spaces (same length — a comment is not a call); `functionSpans` finds every named function / method / arrow with its brace-matched body; `vendorTouching` is the fixpoint of "its body calls `api(` / `callJson(` / `fetchFn(` / `f(` or a function that does"; `responseCensus(src, {direct, raw, judgeFn, rateOkIds})` then judges (a) every raw send: inside the judge (`callJson`), `typedFailure(` within 12 lines (the resource bytes), or a lane's status judge (`.status = r.status` + `.permanent`), else RED; (b) every `catch` (block form and `.catch(` promise form — the chain walked back over `.then(…)` / an IIFE to its head): a try that never reaches a send is `no-vendor`; otherwise `rethrows-rate` (an `if (… 'rate-limited' …) throw`), `ends-throw` (the last statement throws the caught error or `map(e)`, every earlier `return` after a POSITIVE `e.code === '<not rate-limited>'` / `vc === N` test), `raw-fetch` (the try holds only the raw primitive and the catch throws), `rate-ok` (a marker on the catch line with a row in the module's `RATE_OK`), else RED with the line. `censusLine` prints the classes for the suite's log. The suites pin the class COUNTS per file (a silent reclassification is seen) and run three planted copies: a bare fetch, a swallowing try/catch, a judge that maps 429 to ok (judged by behaviour through `history()` / `listConversations()` on a mutant-copy load).

### scripts/mutant-copy.mjs (B-0220 generalized, batch r1)

scripts/mutant-copy.mjs — THE ONE place a negative control's PATCHED COPY of a product module is written (NOT a test-*.mjs, like scratch.mjs — no tier). `mutantCopies(name, repo)` → `{dir, files, write, load, pathFor}`: `dir` = `scratch('<name>-mut')` (per pid, removed on 'exit' by ONE module-level exit handler over every dir the process made — a listener per call put an eleven-control suite past Node's ten-listener warning, the 2.369.187 mirror log); `write(origRel, src, tag?, {esm?, name?, selfPath?})` → the copy's absolute path (`selfPath: true`, CJS only, B-3052 r3: a SELF-SPAWNING script — data/bin/vibespace-remote-keeper runs its daemon as `spawn(node, [__filename, 'daemon', …])` — gets only `require` rebound; its `__filename`/`__dirname` stay the copy's own, or the copy would hand its daemon role to the real file and the control would judge the original) — CJS (`.cjs`, so CommonJS whatever package.json says) gets `var require = require('node:module').createRequire(<real path>), __filename = <real path>, __dirname = <real dir>;` inserted on the original's FIRST-STATEMENT line (after a shebang and after a `'use strict'` directive — a statement before the directive would silently drop strict mode; never inside a leading comment), so `./x`/`../x` reach the very files AND require-cache entries a sibling reached and every line number is the original's; ESM (`.mjs`; chosen by the source's own syntax — top-level import/export, no `require(`/`module.exports` — or `esm:true`) gets every relative specifier (`from`, bare `import '…'`, `import('…')`) and `import.meta.url` rewritten to the real file's URL (`rebaseEsm`); `name` + `pathFor(name, ext)` let a CLOSED WORLD of copies require/import EACH OTHER by absolute path (quota-model ⑯/⑰, fable-cap-pool-storm's stdout chain, channels-engine's registry+fake+engine trio, xpra-client's proto/client/view trio); `load` = `write` + require (CJS only). `copiesCensus(files, dir, repo, {minCopies, match})` → two rows for the suite's own `ok`: git's view of `src/` INCLUDING ignored files narrowed to this pid (or `match`, for names with no pid) is empty, and every copy exists outside the checkout in `dir` — taken WHILE the copies exist (after exit it passes on the pre-fix placement too). `sweepLegacy(repo, dirs, re)` removes what a PRE-FIX run stranded, dead PIDs only. Used by 27 suites; test-architecture §51 is the census (no `scripts/*.mjs` write into `src/`, no wildcard `.js` ignore under `src/`, the helper's CJS/ESM contract driven; a write is judged by its TARGET — `writeFileSync`'s first argument, `copyFileSync`'s SECOND, top-level commas only: copying a product module OUT of `src/` into a scratch dir is exactly what a control should do — the 2.369.168 integration's test-browser-verbs controls were counted by their source path until then). A copy that is loaded INTO a worktree (restore-liveness' e2e boot) is installed from the raw patched text, never from the rebound copy (whose require points at THIS checkout).

### scripts/test-new-member-wake.mjs + test-auto-resume-loop.mjs

scripts/test-new-member-wake.mjs + test-auto-resume-loop.mjs — THE PAIR (B-0220): every patched copy test-new-member-wake loads goes through `loadCopy(origRel, src)` (since batch r1 a thin delegate to scripts/mutant-copy.mjs, the one helper every suite uses) — written to `scratch('wake-mut')` as `.cjs`, its `require` re-bound on line 1 to `createRequire(<the real module's path>)` (relative requires and the require cache exactly as a sibling's; line numbers unchanged), NEVER a sibling in `src/` (a 2026-09-22 integration: test-auto-resume-loop's §5 `noteRecovered` census walked `src/` while the other suite's mutant engine sat there — 3 red, green alone; the old names were gitignored, which hid them from git only). §10 = the tree census taken WHILE the copies exist (`git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- src`) + the helper's ledger outside the checkout. `VS_WAKE_HOLD=<path>` = HOLD MODE: the suite writes `<path>.ready` (the copy paths) after §10 and waits for `<path>.go` (or its parent's death, or 5 min). test-auto-resume-loop starts such a held child FIRST, runs its whole self inside the hold, then releases it and asserts it green (heavy, ~14 s) — the concurrency held open deterministically, not raced for.
