### scripts/work-meter.mjs — THE WORK METER (lane-mirror-198, 2026-09-29): a complexity gate counts work, never the clock

scripts/work-meter.mjs — NOT a test-*.mjs (like scratch.mjs / mutant-copy.mjs — no tier). The instrument behind every "linear" / "bounded before the work" / "O(1) per hit" claim of the fast tier since the Actions mirror of 2.369.198 read test-channel-reactions' wall-clock pin at ×2.50 on a shared 4-vCPU runner (the .197 rebuild had only moved the coin flip from the median to the minimums; a ratio at its own boundary is a coin flip whichever statistic it takes). `startWorkMeter()` (idempotent) opens an inspector session and `Profiler.startPreciseCoverage({callCount, detailed})`: every basic block of every function compiled FROM THEN ON carries an exact execution counter, and V8 runs no optimized code while it is on (a hot function counts as a cold one). It MUST run before the measured modules are required — a function compiled earlier carries only its call count, and a re-required file gets the same compile from V8's compilation cache (measured); a copy at ANOTHER path (mutant-copy's `write`) is compiled afresh with counters, so a suite that starts the meter late measures a scratch copy, or measures natives only where they carry the claim (test-channels-lark-shape's cut-then-walk: `slice` and `matchAll` on the 4 KiB head). `measure(fn, files)` → `{blocks, native, total}` of ONE call: the counters of the scripts whose url ends with one of `files` are taken (reset) before and read after; the natives are patched only around the call — `includes`/`indexOf` add the elements scanned (the found index + 1, else the length), `filter`/`map`/`some`/`find`/`reduce`… the callbacks run, `shift`/`splice`/`unshift`/`join`/`sort` the elements moved (+ the comparator's calls), `slice`/`concat`/`Array.from` the result, a Set/Map op 1, an iterator's `next` 1 (`for…of`, spread and `new Set(list)` go through it once patched), a string walker (`replace`/`split`/`match`/`toLowerCase`/`indexOf`…) its receiver's length, `slice`/`repeat` the cut, `RegExp.test`/`exec` the string's length, `JSON.stringify` the bytes — restored in `finally`; the wrappers lean on originals captured at load, the counter resets AFTER the patching and is read BEFORE the unpatching (its own pushes and pops would count). `work(fn, files)` = the steady-state count: measured twice, the second reading — measured, the very first measured execution of a function reads a constant more (V8 folds its lazy compile's first run into the first take that sees it: 2 000 extra blocks on compactSide over 2 000 deltas, exact for ever after, fresh inputs included), and a module-level memo filling on its first sight of an input is not the parser's growth either. `linear(mk, run, n, files)` → `{n, c, w1, w2, r, ok}`: the inputs mk(0) / mk(n) / mk(2n) built OUTSIDE the measured call (its construction is not the parser's work — the first cut counted `'x'.repeat(n)` and read every cap red), the constant part c = mk(0)'s work subtracted, `r = w2 / w1 ≤ LINEAR_BOUND` (2.2: a linear parser reads 2.00, a quadratic 4; an input whose per-element cost is still growing at n — a by-list filling toward its cap — is measured from a larger n, the reactions 40-key rows from 8 000). `bounded(mk, run, n, files)` → a cut precedes the walk: twice the oversize input costs ≤ 1.25× + 256. `deterministic(fn, files)` → the meter's own proof (the reactions suite asserts it before its census). BLIND SPOTS, by name: a quadratic INSIDE V8's regex engine (catastrophic backtracking) counts as the string's length — a control built on it (test-channel-blocks (j)/(p)/(q), test-mail-frame's budgets) stays on the clock with a stated slack; an async call cannot be measured alone (other work interleaves — test-channels-lark-shape's page-size refusal); the event loop's own gaps (test-codex-zst's tick gap) are a wall-clock property. Users: test-channel-reactions ⑥/⑦ (+ the deterministic proof), test-channel-thread T6 / ⑤b, test-dial-facts, test-usage-ledger-perf (its brute-force reference measured as the control), test-channels-lark-shape.

`measureAsync(fn, files)` (lane channel-index-copy, B-f32b): the same take/patch held across an awaited call — a server route awaits. Everything the process runs meanwhile is counted, so the caller keeps timers out of the window (an injected clock, the store's idle tick captured; test-channels-index-scale measures its warm-up open once and discards it, the meter's first take of a function reading a constant more). Under the meter, patching `RegExp.prototype.exec` puts a `/g` replace on V8's slow path (one exec per match, each counted as the whole string) — re-indent with `replaceAll(string, …)`.

THE OPTIMIZER PIN (lane mirror-green, 2026-10-03): `startWorkMeter` sets `--no-turbofan` + `--no-maglev` for the whole process — an optimized frame never bumps the invocation counter a function's own count is read from, so a hot callee's calls vanished from a take (the .199/.200 mirror red, Node 22). Everything after `startWorkMeter` runs un-optimized (slower, exact); `deterministic` also returns the `warm` take. ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants.md

HONEST SCAN CHARGES + `judgeInChild` (lane work-meter-judges, .209): a forward scan is charged the span it walks — `s.indexOf(q, from)` / `includes` from `from` to the hit, a global / sticky regex `exec` / `test` from its lastIndex to the match's end (a tag loop `while ((m = RE.exec(s)))` reads n, not n² — the old whole-receiver charge made every such loop read quadratic), `startsWith` / `endsWith` the needle, a `trim` the whitespace it drops (V8 slices the rest without a copy). The one blind spot left is BACKTRACKING inside one exec: V8 release builds expose no regexp step counter (`--trace-regexp-bytecodes` is debug-only, perf is paranoid here), so a backtracking claim stays a clock DEADLINE. `judgeInChild({ module, run, mk, n, kind })` runs one `linear` / `bounded` verdict in a fresh node that starts the meter before requiring `module` (the real file or a patched copy's path) — the optimizer pin stays out of a suite whose other legs judge a deadline. Converted at .209: test-channel-blocks ⑱ (the inline reader ×2.00 on <li>/<br>/<td>/<p>; the re-reading CONTROL ×3.98 — it read ×2.37 by hrtime at int208's load), test-channel-thread ⑦ (the quote path), test-browser-tabs (tabOwners / cleanRoots linear, chipTitle bounded), test-channel-search (snippetOf bounded at 1 / 2 MiB), test-machine-card-fold (a 1 MiB -EncodedCommand refused with the same work at 2 MiB), test-peer-parsers ④ (the per-quote newline scan CONTROL by work ×3.98 vs ×2.01; the two round-2 regex controls by a 1 000 ms deadline at 64 KB in a child — 2.2 s vs 3 ms). test-browser-tabs, test-channel-search and test-machine-card-fold left FAST_SERIAL.

THE CLOCK-JUDGE CENSUS (lane work-meter-judges, .209): scripts/ci.mjs `clockJudgeLines(src)` finds a clock read (process.hrtime / performance.now / a Date.now delta) within CLOCK_WINDOW (6) lines of both an `ok(` and a complexity word (linear / quadratic / ratio / O(n), comment lines ignored); `CLOCK_JUDGES` lists every suite it finds with WHY it stays on the clock (a deadline, or regex backtracking). test-architecture's census leg reds a found-but-unlisted suite (a new clock-ratio complexity judge: convert it to the meter or list it) and a listed-but-not-found one; its CONTROL splices test-channel-thread's pre-.209 hrtime ratio back in and must see it found. Listed at .209: test-channel-blocks, test-channel-facts, test-channel-reactions (an unasserted print), test-exit-run, test-mail-frame, test-peer-parsers (③'s 40 regex-heavy rows: 19 read ×3–4 by charge artifacts in this lane's trial — a follow-up), test-peer-text-census.

### scripts/scratch.mjs `endRootedProcesses` — a suite owns what its server started (2026-09-25)

scripts/scratch.mjs `endRootedProcesses(root, {signal='SIGKILL', procRoot, self})` → the pids it signalled: every process whose cwd, HOME or any argv token (its start, or after `=`) lies in `root` — never this process or its ancestors; refuses anything but a `/tmp/…` root; synchronous (runs inside an 'exit' handler); `signal: 0` only LISTS. Why: a worktree server's terminal/chat sessions run under dtach, DETACHED by design (the KillMode=process rule), with the real HOME and cwd `/tmp`, so a suite that kills its server ends none of them — test-browser-resources left 140 dtach + pty-wrapper + zsh behind over 20 runs. Its ⓒ teardown now ends every process rooted in its worktree before removing it (zsh dies with its pty) and ASSERTS none is left (`signal: 0`); its exit reap covers the whole scratch root. The gate reaper's `argvScratchRoots` is the net for a suite that never reached its teardown.

### scripts/scratch.mjs `vncEnv` — the singleton Desktop's per-run names (2026-09-25)

scripts/scratch.mjs `vncEnv()` → `{VIBESPACE_VNC_DISPLAY: ':<n>', VIBESPACE_VNC_PORT: '<p>'}` — `p` from `freePort()`, `n` = `freeDisplay(p)`: the first number at or after `1000 + p % 20000` (`VNC_DISPLAY_RANGE`, far above the lowest-first `-displayfd` band the keepers draw from, below the X TCP ceiling) whose `/tmp/.X<n>-lock` AND `/tmp/.X11-unix/X<n>` are both absent (a lock alone is what a SIGKILLed server leaves; a `-displayfd` Xvfb holds only the socket — measured; `exists` is a parameter). Every suite that spawns `server.js` does `const VNC_ENV = await vncEnv();` right after its imports and spreads `...VNC_ENV` after its base env (so an explicit key still wins). Census: test-architecture §57 — every `spawn|fork(process.execPath|'node', [… 'server.js' | path.join(…, 'server.js')])` in a `scripts/test-*.mjs` outside a string / template / regex / comment (a data-range scanner: templates nest through `${…}`, a regex literal is told from a division by the token before it) names an env that carries `vncEnv(` or both literal names — inline, through a named variable, a spread of one, a function-built env or the `env` shorthand, followed ≤ 4 hops; the pre-fix shapes (named env, inline, no env at all, the preload and path.join argv forms) are its negative controls. 60 suites in scope; test-architecture and test-fixture-isolation spell the shape only inside string literals (their controls) and are out of scope by the rule, asserted — no exemption list.

scripts/scratch.mjs `deadPort()` / `deadPorts(n)` / `deadUrl(scheme='http', rest='')` (lane fixture-ports, B-b6cd, 2026-10-06) — a DEAD loopback port: bind 127.0.0.1:0, read, close (deadPorts holds all N until each is chosen, like freePorts). Dead for the next seconds only — take it at suite start, use it at once, never write it down. Every fake / stub that answers with an endpoint nothing should serve (a fake agent-browser's `get cdp-url`, a stub exit proxy) names one of these; a fixed "nobody listens on 19888" literal was alive on the dev box (mirror-green-220). test-architecture §81 is the census: a literal loopback endpoint in a string / template / regex token of scripts/test-*.mjs + scripts/*-stub*.mjs (comments never count; `host:${NAME}` / `'host:' + NAME` followed to a number-bound NAME) is an EXEMPT row (file → ports + reason: pure-function text, or a CONTRACT port — the Lark callback, rclone's OAuth loopback) or red; a row covering no hit is red; the census prints its table. Not covered (say so in a review): a port hidden behind `|| '<digits>'` (test-browser-providers' fake had one — converted by hand) and bare `':NNNN'` strings (rids, X displays — §57's / §6's).

### scripts/scratch.mjs `withoutVendorKeys` + the real-CLI legs (B-5f0b)

scripts/scratch.mjs `withoutVendorKeys(env)` / `VENDOR_KEY_ENV` — THE REAL-CLI LEG RULES (B-5f0b, 2.369.164 batch 3; the 2.369.69 red: a real `codex app-server` leg asserted before the server's own idle drain died on its 401, only under load). Every leg that runs a REAL claude / codex / opencode obeys two rules. ① **Its spawn env has no ambient vendor key**: `withoutVendorKeys()` drops OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (a fake HOME / CODEX_HOME removes the LOGIN, never an env key — a leaked key would bill the drained turn, and the two Anthropic names outrank the oat test-chat-e2e seeds; `agentEnv()` passes them through on purpose, it is the user's choice in production). test-architecture §50 is the census: a `scripts/test-*.mjs` / `probe-*.mjs` that resolves a real CLI BY NAME (`command -v claude|codex|opencode`, `spawn('codex'…`, `OPENCODE_CMD || 'opencode'`) imports and calls it, or declares `// real-cli-env: <reason ≥10 chars>` (env built from nothing, or a binary that is only read / asked `--version`: test-init-frame, test-permission-rules, test-stdout-registry). ② **It judges only after the child's TERMINAL signal, bounded**: `exit` for one-shots, the reply to its own request, `turn/completed` / `error` / a 401 for a server-started turn (test-queue-steer ⑩), `result` for a claude turn — scripts/probe-claude-stdout.mjs reports `sawResult`/`resultSubtype` and test-stdout-registry's `wireVerdict` SKIPs a capture that never reached its result (a budget expiry or a mid-turn death), control = the fake CLI's `FAKE_CLI_NO_RESULT` cut; test-vendor-whitelist's strace re-measurement reports a timeout-killed trace as `timedOut` (SKIP with evidence), never as a zero-connect measurement; test-opencode-s9 polls the live lane's `connected` and the second process's `external` row instead of one fixed sleep. Stub-only suites (test-codex-p2-wrapper, test-opencode-plugin, test-acp-harness) have no real-binary leg. Local pitfall: `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks` breaks the nvm `codex` shim and those legs SKIP — run them with NODE_OPTIONS unset to see them execute. **`stopWrapper(child, {dir, graceMs})` (2.369.172 r1):** kill → await the exit (SIGKILL after the grace) → `rmSync` with retries — the ONE way a suite ends a wrapper it spawned; since 2.369.172 a wrapper answers SIGTERM with a record whose last act creates its log file, so kill-then-rm in one tick races it (the mirror's `ENOTEMPTY` on test-codex-p2-client). Census: test-architecture §55.

### scripts/test-ax-budget.mjs

scripts/test-ax-budget.mjs — THE ACCESSIBILITY-TREE MEASUREMENT LEG (heavy; docs/design-accessibility-tree.zh.md §3 row 0 in its §8 lean form + §4's counting rules; chunk a0 of the lean set, 2.369.150). It counts what CHROME ITSELF serialises: `Accessibility.enable` (the renderer AX mode a UIA client switches on) → `Accessibility.getFullAXTree({depth:-1})`, TOTAL (every serialised node, ignored ones included — the payload HandleAXEvents pays for, what chrome://accessibility reports) and NON-IGNORED (the platform tree) per scope, a scope = `DOM.querySelectorAll` → backendNodeId → the AX node carrying that backendDOMNodeId, summed over childIds (list `.chat-message-list`, the window by a `data-ax-probe` handle, `.chat-minimap`, `#sidebar`); NEVER `getElementsByTagName('*')` (DOM size, not exposure). One chat window on the §1c fixture (scripts/huge-transcript-fixture.mjs, 36 MB by default so it opens in tail mode) in the LIVE window's rendering mode (content-visibility:auto), 1400×1000. Legs: ① positive control — the list's subtree > 200 (MEASURED 449 total / 130 non-ignored on the 50 tail cards ≈ 9 AX nodes per rendered card, not the design's 60–130: the §1c tail is fold-dominated and a folded member is display:none, out of the tree by §0 — the pin is measured ×0.45, the design's unfolded estimate was red on the first run); ② OQ1 — aria-hidden on the list must drop ≥ 80 % of its non-ignored subtree, and the suite PRINTS the named verdict: the list-level form, aria-hidden PER CARD and content-visibility:hidden PER CARD on the same baseline, each graded against the list's serialised total, with a role / ignoredReason histogram of what remains under the window and the list's scrollHeight in each state (layout neutrality); ③ the growth baseline — four top-edge page-ups (test-chat-paging §4b's idiom: scrollTop 0 + a −120 wheel, wait for `_windowStart` to fall), settle, re-measure, the Δ PRINTED against the baseline and the design's 5,000 per-window ceiling, asserted only that the rendered-card count grew (MEASURED 1001 → 3214 total, list 449 → 2638, 50 → 336 cards at ch 658 / sh 2574 — ~4 viewports: the trim's keep zone filling, inside a ±2-viewport band whole, so that Δ is the trim's, not the band's). **a1 ④–⑥ (the band, where the DOM outgrows it): a teleport into the elided middle (`_jumpToFileTime` on the user turn nearest the file's midpoint) + two 2,000-line gap slabs — the band census (in-view cards exposed, cards ≥ 3 viewports away aria-hidden), the GROWTH INVARIANT (the second slab moves TOTAL and NON-IGNORED ≤ 10 %), the §4 per-window ceiling (≤ 5,000 TOTAL), the setting's two meanings (false = the list, true = the band re-derived on the flip after the per-card state was wiped — with the view taken OUT of `app.sessions` for the flip, as a sub-agent viewer always is, and the pass's `why` = setting), and the NEGATIVE CONTROL — `_syncAxExposure` neutered at source in the scratch worktree (string-exact marker), bundle rebuilt, the same window / teleport / slabs: > 30 % growth and every far card exposed. `openFixtureWindow` closes whatever the restored layout brought back so every scope counts ONE list.** Every scratch name from scripts/scratch.mjs, ONBOARDED_SOURCE before the navigate, the isolated home + fixtureLitter census like every fixture carrier. 不变量=an accessibility budget is Chrome's own node count per scope, its pins are measured then ×-pinned, and a state the band would write is measured before the band is written. **⑦ FOCUS (verifier finding on a1): with focus emulation on (a headless page without system focus dispatches no focusin on `.focus()`), a capture-phase recorder reads the landing card's aria-hidden before any product listener and in a setTimeout(0) from the same task, beside Chrome's own "Blocked aria-hidden … descendant retained focus" warnings (`Log.entryAdded`; Chrome warns ONCE per element and repairs the platform tree itself — the warning, not the focused node's `ignored`, is the browser-level discriminator): ⑦a the handler blocked in-page (the pre-fix code) ⇒ still 'true' + ≥ 1 warning, ⑦b `.focus()` on a below-band card ⇒ exposed in-task, kept after the settle, exactly one card fewer hidden, view unmoved, ⑦c Shift+Tab from the first tabbable after the list ⇒ the list's last tabbable, exposed in-task, 0 warnings; red on the pre-fix chat-view.js (⑦b ×2, ⑦c).** **a2: ①b the minimap strip ≤ 10 TOTAL / NON-IGNORED for ≥ 100 markers (MEASURED 0 / 0 — the strip's own node leaves the tree; the in-page control strips the attribute, the scope must come back ≥ its marker count, the restore must empty it again), ④e the same pin on the slab, ④d re-pinned at a2's measured ×1.25 (window 4,576 / 516 → 5,700 / 650 — under the design's 5,000 on the worst slab), and the RECORDED block at the count section keeps a0 / a1 / a2's numbers side by side (a re-measure after the next step appends a line, never rewrites one).**

### scripts/test-ax-paint.mjs

scripts/test-ax-paint.mjs — THE PAINT-ONLY CENSUS (fast; design-accessibility-tree §3 rows 2 + 3 in their §8 lean form, chunk a2): from the SOURCE, every paint-only element is marked before it is born and the marking never took a control's only name. ① icons.js `_s()` emits `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` on the `<svg>`, asserted FUNCTIONALLY over every exported FILE_ICONS / UI_ICONS value (the two raw strings that bypass the helper — `python`, `alert` — are covered because the values are what ships); ② the icon-only `<button>` census over every src/lib template (an `${UI_ICONS.…}` / backend-icon interpolation / inline `<svg>` / entity with no letters beside it ⇒ `title=` or `aria-label=` required; the same rule over DOM-built `x = document.createElement('button')` … `x.innerHTML = <rhs>;` whose right-hand side, its icon references / tags / entities taken out, has no letter or digit left — the template branch's own test, so `UI_ICONS.k`, `UI_ICONS.k + ' '` and `` `${UI_ICONS.k}` `` are icon-only and `UI_ICONS.inbox + segs` carries text), the classifier negative-controlled on a fixture string AND the whole census over a scratch copy of src/lib with a nameless `nb.innerHTML = UI_ICONS.copy + ' ';` planted in chat-input.js (must flag exactly that button; verifier LOW-1 — the exact-statement classifier `x.innerHTML = UI_ICONS.k;` passed that form green); ③ every `.chat-code-ln` gutter, `.chat-diff-prefix`, `.chat-run-arrow`, spinner creation site (a census over `chat-spinner` / `upload-active-spinner`, 10 sites), the 8 resize handles, the `.chat-minimap` strip and the tab strip's `.tab-split-glyph` (2.369.162 — the split mark became an element when the CSS `⫿` glyph was deleted, so ④'s named-family list dropped `⫿`) carry the attribute, and the TOC button is a SIBLING of the strip (appended to the container, never inside the hidden subtree); ④ the CSS glyph census over chat/style/viewers/theme-editor.css — a `content:` string that is a GLYPH (an escape or a non-ASCII character and no letters) carries the alt-text form `content: '…' / ""` as the LAST content declaration of its rule (the plain declaration stays first as the fallback for a parser without the slash syntax) and no TEXT string carries it (`'Collapse'`, the customize-mode sentence — a first cut's "non-ASCII ⇒ glyph" rule caught the em-dash sentence, which is why the classifier refuses letters); ⑤ ci.mjs carries the suite. 不变量=an aria-hidden icon is no longer a name, so the census that hides icons is the census that checks every icon-only button still has one; a generated glyph is alt-text "" and a generated sentence never is.

### The paint-only layer (a2, 2.369.150 — design-accessibility-tree §3 row 2 + row 3 lean)

icons.js — `_s()`, the ONE helper every UI/file icon goes through, emits `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` on the `<svg>` (the `python` / `alert` raw strings carry the same two attributes by hand): an icon is paint, never a name or a tab stop; every icon-only button names itself with `title=` / `aria-label=` (test-ax-paint ② census, 7 buttons today, 0 unnamed). Gate: test-ax-paint ①②. `UI_ICONS.money` (2.369.189) = a coin with a dollar sign, THE credits glyph (usage-source `creditsChipHtml`); `coin` stays the chat status bar's budget-limited mark. The Doc window's bar (design 020, 2.369.223): `bold`, `italic`, `code`, `listUl`, `listOl`, `task`, `table`, `link`, `raw` (a page with a turned corner and `#`) beside the existing `image` / `chevronDown` / `more` / `chat` / `grip`.
highlight.js — the `.chat-code-ln` gutter span (both template sites, the truncation row too) is `aria-hidden`: a line number is paint; the text of the line stays exposed once. Gate: test-ax-paint ③.
chat-renderers.js — the `.chat-diff-prefix` span (both diff renderers) and the three tool-card spinners are `aria-hidden`; the copy path reads the prefix by `textContent` and is unaffected. Gate: test-ax-paint ③; test-owner-batch-2369-32's `</span>${mediaHtml}<details` seam untouched.

**THE LIVE WORKFLOW CARD'S TWO FRAGMENTS + THE CLI's AGENT WORDS (inc-mudv05ja-n5rv, 2.369.160).** The Workflow branch of `renderToolResult` draws the lifecycle chip through `renderTaskChip(ti)` and the live tree through `renderWorkflowLive(ti)` — the SAME two methods ChatView's in-place patch (`_patchWorkflowCard`) renders from, so a patched card and a fresh render can never draw two trees; phases carry `data-phase`, chips `data-agent-key` (`a:<agentId>` else `i:<index>`), the dot is `aria-hidden`. PURE exported `workflowAgentState(raw)` is the ONE vocabulary mapping: the CLI's working words `start` / `progress` (and the fixture's `running`) draw as `running` — production has never said `running` (8 buffers: 161 progress / 26 start / 253 done / 56 error), so chat.css's `[data-state="running"]` pulse and the tally's "N running" were dead until this; the chip's `data-state` AND the tally counts read it. `drawsWorkflowCard(msg)` answers whether renderToolMsg draws the Workflow RESULT card (not collab, a `tool_result`, not an error, toolName Workflow — mirrors the branch order) — the patch's gate. Gate: test-task-lifecycle (the vocabulary table + the end-to-end legs), test-fold-ux F2 (chrome, fed the real words: the dot pulses).
chat-view.js / chat-input.js / app.js / setup-flows.js / file-explorer-uploads.js — the `.chat-run-arrow` spans and every spinner (`chat-spinner`, `upload-active-spinner`) carry `aria-hidden` at creation; the label beside a spinner stays the live text. Gate: test-ax-paint ③ (a census over creation sites, not a list).
chat-minimap.js — the `.chat-minimap` strip is `aria-hidden` before it is appended (one marker div per user turn of the WHOLE conversation, uncapped — the one subtree that grew with the conversation's length, not the rendered window; a0 measured 201 nodes for 199 markers, a2 measures 0 — the strip's own node leaves the tree); the TOC button (`title` "Your messages (outline)") stays the accessible path to the same turns and is a SIBLING appended to the container, never inside the strip. Gate: test-ax-paint ③ + test-ax-budget ①b/④e (with the in-page control).
public/chat.css / style.css / viewers.css — every generated GLYPH (`\25B8` / `\25BE` / `\25B4` disclosure arrows, `\00B7` chip dots, the `\200e` LRM marks on paths, `†`, the role-indicator `\1F464` / `\2699` beside their font-size-0 text labels, the gear/context-menu `▸` / `\25C2`) is written twice — `content: '…'; content: '…' / "";` — so a parser with the alt-text syntax exposes nothing and one without keeps the glyph (the cascade takes the last VALID declaration); a generated SENTENCE (`'Collapse'`, `'Extra row — drag elements here'`) is never given the empty alt. Gate: test-ax-paint ④ (31 rules since 2.369.162 deleted the split tab's `⫿` — the split mark is the aria-hidden `.tab-split-glyph` element, ③; classifier negative-controlled).
MEASURED (test-ax-budget, Chrome 153, the §1c fixture): the 50-card baseline 1001 → 733 TOTAL / 516 → 260 NON-IGNORED, the window 724 → 462; after four page-ups 3214 → 2769; the 1,310-card slab window 5,448 → 4,576 TOTAL / 916 → 516 NON-IGNORED (now under the design's 5,000); the neutered-band control 20,158 → 14,871 — the paint-only layer is worth ≈ 16–36 % of a window on top of the band, and the strip's 201 nodes per window are gone.

### scripts/huge-transcript-fixture.mjs

scripts/huge-transcript-fixture.mjs — THE §1c HUGE COMPACT-MODE TRANSCRIPT GENERATOR, ONE implementation (2.369.150): `writeHugeTranscript({file, sid, cwd, targetBytes})` writes the measured shape of the owner's 976 MB conversation (inc-mubvu3a4-x8sb — the essay rides in the file verbatim: attachment / tool_use / thinking / text / bookkeeping mixes per 1000 lines, the size histograms, the fold-run lengths, the two-region tail, a valid PNG every ~700 lines) from a DETERMINISTIC seed (the shape is the fixture, not the seed) with every record id MINTED by scratch.mjs `fixtureSid`; returns `{lines, turns, images, bytes, kbPerLine, ms}`. Factored out of scripts/test-chat-paging.mjs so scripts/test-ax-budget.mjs measures the accessibility tree on EXACTLY the shape the paging suite pages — a second copy would be a twin that drifts. NOT a test-*.mjs on purpose (the tier census would demand a tier); the import graph carries it into both suites' impact scope. test-chat-trim-guard's fixtureSid pin reads THIS file and proves test-chat-paging is wired to it (the import + the call with SID3). 不变量=one generator, one seed, one shape; a suite that needs the huge fixture imports it, never re-spells it. **2.369.167 r1 — THE STOPPING POINT IS PART OF THE SHAPE:** every `base()` record carries `cwd`, and a suite's cwd is a scratch.mjs path ending in its pid (5 digits on a fresh Actions runner, 7 here), so counting REAL bytes moved the stop, the dense-tail boundary and the whole tail with the pid's digit count (test-chat-paging's runner fixture: 3,795 records with an image-free tail(50); here 3,785 with a 571 KB image in it). `push` now counts every record as if its cwd were `CANON_CWD` (29 bytes — test-chat-paging's scratch cwd under a 7-digit pid, so this box's fixture is byte-identical to before): the same records on every machine; only the cwd string differs. 不变量 += a fixture's shape is independent of the paths it embeds.

### spend-authorizer.js

spend-authorizer.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE CEILING ON EVERY TURN NOBODY TYPED (design-account-hardening §4.4c / P9 / D3 / D6, 2026-09-08): the closed `SPEND_REASONS` set, `budgetLimits` (the four D6 numbers as settings; an explicit 0 is a CHOICE), rolling hour/day `spendCounts`, `authorizeUnattendedSpend` (fail closed on: an identity it cannot name · an undeclared reason · a credential that cannot serve · **paid overage in use** · each cap — while IGNORANCE never blocks, P6), `noteUnattendedSpend` (two-phase: authorize answers, note charges) with the 80% notice once per axis per window, and `overageState`/`overageText` = THE ONE READER of `cache.overage`/`cache.spend` (captured since 2.289.0, read by NOBODY until now — with overage ON utilization stays under 1 while every token is billed, so `accountRemaining()` ranked the account spending real money as the one with the most headroom). **r2: `CAP_MAX`/`stampCap` make the enforceable range equal the schema's offered range (a flat 800-stamp ledger silently never fired any cap above it), and `overageState` now DATES the claim that blocks — a record whose own `resetsAt` has passed, or whose `asOf` is older than `OVERAGE_STALE_MS` (7 d), answers 'unknown' while keeping `stated`/`evidence`; only `inUse:'yes'` is bounded, because it is the only answer that refuses anything.** **r5 adds the RESERVATION half** — `RESERVE_TTL_MS`/`pendingCounts`/`reservePending`/`releasePending`/`expirePending` and a `pending` input to `authorizeUnattendedSpend`, so an authorization that has not yet become a charge still binds the ceiling (five concurrent deliveries on one slot spent 5 turns against a cap of 2), plus `LOAD_RETENTION` = the retention a reader that cannot yet know the limits must use (the boot prune ran with the DEFAULTS and forgave 236 turns per restart). **r4 adds `spendControlState` = THE ONE READER of codex's `cache.spendControlReached` (the THIRD field the design's §1.4 row named and the one r3 marked CLOSED with zero readers): three-state, dated on the SAME `OVERAGE_STALE_MS` (imported, never re-declared — a second window for one physical fact is how twins are born), refusing under its own name in the `identity-cannot-serve` class rather than the money one, so `spend.allowOverageTurns` deliberately does NOT unlock it — that setting consents to spending money, not to being refused by the vendor. And every verdict CARRIES the identity it resolved (`identity` on both the ok and the refusal path) precisely so the charge can name the same slot.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **B-ad05 (2026-09-17, USAGE CREDITS VISIBLE BEFORE THEY ARE SPENT): `overageState().mode` = `inUse` | `allowed` (overage present, `inUse:false`, no `status:'rejected'`/`disabledReason`) | `disabled` | `unknown`, and `overageAllowed(cache)` is that one question — an org-level configuration, so NOT date-bounded like `inUse:'no'`; it changes NO spend verdict (the guard refuses only once overage is IN USE — pinned in test-spend-paths §7c with a credits-allowed world whose continue fires).** **FINAL VERIFIER (2026-09-17): `mode:'allowed'` needs POSITIVE evidence — a vendor `status` that is not `rejected`, or a DATED `inUse:true` whose period ended or went stale; `{inUse:false}` with no status (the vendor omits `overageStatus` on ~a third of events, and the pre-fix merge wiped stored ones — two members on this instance carry exactly that shape, one of them overage-DISABLED) is `unknown`, never a last-resort rank or a "billing pay-per-use" sentence.**

### login-state.js

login-state.js — THE credential-state reader (2026-09-07, SHARED, fs-only): `loginState(credsPath)` → live|expired|wiped|missing|unreadable + `since` = the instant the login stopped being able to produce a reading. `parseAuth`'s boolean collapses four states; two matter — WIPED is a file that stays with empty tokens (its mtime is the last-known-good MARKER the repair migration proves foreignness with), and a doubly-expired login still reports loggedIn:true, the satisfiable gap `poolMembers()` never closed. **2026-09-07 r2 adds the ACCOUNT-level twin `accountLoginState(credsPath, {oatMintedAt})`** — a wiped dir + a valid long-lived token (B-211a) is a supported, spawnable, reading-PRODUCING account, so the panels (/api/usage `logins`) and the repair migration ask THAT one, while the pool's slot validation deliberately keeps the FILE one (a token rides spawn ENV; re-pointing a symlink can never hand it to a running CLI). `OAT_TTL_MS` lives here and AccountManager reads it. INTEGRATION (2026-09-07, both branches landed): `login-expiry.js` (PURE) and this module are TWO QUESTIONS, not a twin — login-expiry reads the LOGIN SESSION's absolute deadline off a parsed credential object (ok/expiring/expired/logged-out/unknown), this one reads the FILE and answers whether it can produce a reading RIGHT NOW plus WHEN it stopped (live/expired/wiped/missing/unreadable + `since`). The pool gates on BOTH (a member is unusable if either says so); the panels/repair ask `accountLoginState`. Collapsing them into one exported `loginState` is an OPEN follow-up, not done here — the two suites pin different state vocabularies. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### record-lateness.js

record-lateness.js — PURE (imports nothing, CJS) A LATE RECORD IS NOT A LIVE FACT (lane-hot-switch, 2026-09-30). **The incident:** the server crashed at 12:03 (EMFILE); one conversation's stdout bridge came back dead in both directions for three hours; a local re-attach at 15:05:14 (the broken-stdin detector, tripped by the owner's first message since the crash) released the whole backlog in three seconds and every stdout consumer took every record as NOW — hours-old readings overwrote fresh ones (a SPENT member's 5 h read 95 % again), a 12:15 Fable rejection another member answered was charged through its window-less banner to the member the link held at 15:05, the pool demoted that member and moved ten conversations onto the spent one. **The rule:** claude 2.1.281 stamps every `assistant` record (success and API error) with `timestamp` AT EMISSION (measured: a text block streamed for 25 s arrives 2 ms after its stamp). `judge(clock, rec, now, {remote})` = `late` when the record's own stamp is older than `LATE_MS` (2 min; `REMOTE_LATE_MS` 30 min for a remote session — another machine's clock may be skewed); an unstamped record (`rate_limit_event`, `result`) inherits the verdict of the stamped record that arrived within `BURST_MS` (15 s) before it (`observe` keeps that clock); with no such neighbour it is `unknown` and the caller asks `nextStampIn(rest of the buffer)` — the next stamped top-level record AHEAD in the same chunk (a rejected turn emits its `rate_limit_event` ms BEFORE its stamped error record; bounded to 8 records / 256 KiB, records are PARSED so a `timestamp` nested in content never counts); nothing ahead ⇒ live (a harness that stamps nothing behaves exactly as before). **ORCH half (usage-pool-engine):** BOTH feeds show every record to `noteStreamRecord(session, msg)` FIRST (the claude parse right after `JSON.parse`, `claudeSideEffects` at its top); `gateLiveFact` fronts the three live-fact consumers — `recordRateLimitEvent` (→ `recordRateLimitEventNow`), `markLimitBanner(session, text, rec)` (→ `markLimitBannerNow`), `noteTurnEnd(session, rec)` (a late turn end clears the per-turn pins and settles NOTHING: no pool evaluation, no disarm, no loop-breaker credit) — plus `noteSessionProduced(session, rec)` and the live odometer (`recordIsLate` in both feeds: a backlog's spend is the ledger scan's to book, by time). A late fact is counted per backlog episode (`session._lateBurst`) and journalled twice: `[stream] <id>: records arriving 3h02m late — a stalled bridge's backlog; …` at the first, `backlog over — N late fact(s) not taken as live (…)` when the first LIVE stamped record arrives. The parse binds `session._peekStamp = () => nextStampIn(lineBuf)` per attach. Session fields `_recordClock` / `_lateBurst` / `_peekStamp` (session-schema). NOT gated: `noteTurnStopped` (the idle record re-decides placement from CURRENT data, not from the record). Gate: test-hot-switch-incident §A (the incident's backlog through the real parse + engine + pool over real symlinks; controls: the gate removed, the look-ahead removed, the burst inheritance removed, the late-turn-end branch removed, the device feed's clock call removed). **verify r6 (lane reset-path, 2026-10-01) — A SYSTEMATIC OFFSET IS A CLOCK, NOT A BACKLOG (reproduced: a wrapper 5 min behind had every reading, wall and ⟳ of its session refused for good).** `observe(clock, rec, now, {remote})` keeps `clock.run` = {firstArrivedAt, n, minDelayMs, maxDelayMs} over CONSECUTIVE late stamped records (a live one ends it); ≥ SKEW_MIN_RECORDS (3) over ≥ SKEW_SPAN_MS (60 s) of arrivals with max − min ≤ SKEW_JITTER_MS (10 s) declares `clock.skewMs` = the smallest delay and returns `skew: {skewMs, n, spanMs}` once (a backlog's delays shrink as it drains, a drip-fed burst's grow — neither declares); a delay under skewMs − jitter re-learns it (`skew: {skewMs, corrected: true}`). `judge` / `verdictOfClock` subtract `skewOf(clock)` from every delay (a 3-h backlog ON an offset stream is still late). ORCH: `noteStreamRecord` passes the transport's bound, journals the declaration (`stream-clock-skew`) and the correction once; `liveFactVerdict`'s look-ahead carries the stream's offset. The first 60 s of an offset stream are dropped (counted, said at the burst's end). Gate: test-hot-switch-incident §A7 (12 PURE rows + the declaration-removed control) · test-reset-credit-ui S56 (the real codex consumer) + its control. **verify r7 (lane reset-path, 2026-10-02) — THE RUN IS A BAND, ONE RECORD OUTSIDE IT IS A CANDIDATE; THE FIRST MINUTE IS HELD.** r6's run ended only on a live record and was judged by its whole spread, so one out-of-band late record before the declaration (an NTP step, a keeper's replayed burst on a skewed remote stream, a 15-s loop stall) poisoned it for good — the stream never declared (reproduced PURE + on the engine). `extendRun(run, raw, now)` → `{run, inBand}`: a late record in the band extends the run; one outside it is `run.cand` = {arrivedAt, delayMs} and the next late record decides (fits the run ⇒ the candidate was a one-off; fits the candidate ⇒ the level moved, the candidate is the run with n = 2; neither ⇒ replaced); only an in-band record may declare (the span is the run's own records'). The drift boundary (|drift| ≤ SKEW_JITTER_MS / SKEW_SPAN_MS over the run ⇒ declared — a constant-latency pipe by shape) is the documented limit. ORCH: `noteLateFact(session, what, v, replay)` holds a fact gated while no offset is declared (`session._heldLate`, newest HELD_LATE_MAX 32), `replayHeldLate` re-runs each through its gate at the declaration, `endLateBurst(session, how)` discards them on a live record and words a declaration's close ("the offset stream's first minute over — N not replayed; a turn end is never replayed"). **verify r8 (2026-10-02):** T1 — the machine IS one pure step (`observe(clock, rec, now)`: the clock is the whole state, a restart a null clock, one clock per session for both feeds), walked exhaustively in test-record-lateness §3b (9 states × every sequence of ≤ 5 of 10 events = 999 990 sequences, 0 violations, every branch reached). ⑤ THE EDGE OF THE BOUND: a live record within SKEW_JITTER_MS under the bound that fits the run's band extends the run instead of ending it (hysteresis — a level straddling the bound declares at 60 s; a live record farther under, or outside the band, still ends every run); the engine ends the burst only when the run actually ended. ORCH r8: every held entry carries its account key + arrival instant; `replayHeldLate` reads the account's newest reading ONCE before any replay and a fact older than it is NOT replayed (② — said by count and kind); a codex replay runs at its own instant (`recordCodexQuotaSignal(…, {asOf})`); the ring keeps WALLS (④ — `HELD_WALL_KINDS`: the oldest reading goes first, every drop counted and said at the close); ONE For-you item per burst at its first late wall (⑥ — `fileLateWallItem` origin pool, resolved `stream-alive` / `offset-declared` / `wall-replayed`); `REPLAYING_HELD` (a WeakSet) keeps a re-entrant replayed record from closing the burst. Gate: test-record-lateness (fast, 53: THE SHAPE TABLE — 288 cells vs a hand-written truth with the edge rule, the invariants, T2's attacks incl. r8 ① ⑤, THE STEP TABLE walk, eight patched-copy controls, the wiring) · test-hot-switch-incident §A8 + §A7 · test-reset-credit-ui S60 + control, §4c (② ④ ⑥ on the real engine + four controls). **verify r9 ⑨ (pinned, test-record-lateness §3 ⑨):** a backlog that drains fast then STALLS inside the band for ≥ 60 s (a stuck bridge delivering at real-time speed with a constant lag) is a constant-latency pipe by shape — declared (skew = the stall's level, within the jitter past the bound) and CORRECTED the moment the pipe catches up; a stall shorter than the span and a straight drain never declare. The design's stated boundary (§3 ①), not a hole.

### slot-transitions.js

slot-transitions.js — THE credential re-point ledger (2026-09-07, SHARED): a symlink has no history, so every LATE attribution question fell back to the spawn-time org. data/slot-transitions.jsonl `{sessionId, poolId, from, to, at, why}`, sessionId null = the pool DEFAULT moved; **accounts.js is the SINGLE writer** (ensureSessionPoolLink/setPoolTarget cover spawn, engine, manual route, self-heal, removal); `slotAt(sid, ts)` answers by TIME, null = UNKNOWN never agreement (**r3: `sid` may be an ARRAY of webui keys — one conversation is carried by many over resumes — and a default-only hit for a NAMED session carries `ownLinkUnknown`; the DEDUP key is the LINK not the sessionId, or every pool shares one `__default__` bucket**); bounded, head APPENDED to data/archive/. **r2: the DEVICE's sealed-orders reflex re-points links while this server is down — its reported events land through `accounts.noteDeviceRepoint()` (idempotent under a replayed log), because "single writer" is an invariant only while every writer routes through it.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### reading-repair.js

reading-repair.js — the readings-by-slot DATA REPAIR (2026-09-07, run by migration `2026-09-reattribute-readings-by-slot`): re-attributes or archives-with-a-reason the provably-foreign entries in usage-cache / usage-anchors / attribution.ndjson, rebuilds each foreign cache from the newest anchor predating the wipe, voids the pairs it broke, drops rates.json so the estimator re-learns, and clears .attrib-rebake-v1 so the ledger re-bakes from the cleaned walk. **r2: a conversation whose LAST entry is archived is NAMED in .attrib-emptied.json (the re-bake deliberately skips a sid with no attribution entries and would otherwise keep the refuted account forever), and a member with a valid long-lived token is never marked dead just because its local credential dir is wiped (accountLoginState — such an account spawns and produces readings under its own key).** **r3: the two stores are keyed in DIFFERENT NAMESPACES (ledger = webui `sess-*`, attribution = claude conversation UUID) so the r2 lookup could never match a session row and every plan-C conversation silently got the POOL DEFAULT's answer written into the live store — `_sessionKeyMap(dataDir)` joins them through session-meta filenames, and only a session-scoped row may re-attribute; anything else is ARCHIVED with a reason naming the missing evidence.** Idempotent. Measured on a COPY of this instance: 3 caches / 248 anchors / 44 attribution entries. **ALSO the readings-by-WINDOW repair (`repairByWindow`, migration `2026-09-refile-readings-by-window`): each identity establishes its own weekly phases (7d AND every model-scoped bucket) from its OWN on-demand rows (≥5, ≥90 % after merging the ±60 s wobble), only the CURRENT roster may RECEIVE, and every anchor is judged PER BUCKET (r4) — the `{5h,7d}` primary half decides where the record goes, it carries only the buckets that agree with where it lands, every other bucket is archived with its own reason (the line keeps the original whole record), a record with no agreeing bucket is archived, a cache whose 7d agrees but whose scoped bucket does not is stripped in place, the rebuild picks only wholly-agreeing records and preserve-merges the previous scoped bucket rather than deleting the model cap the pool reads, and each roster account's window sidecar is SEEDED (scoped phases included) so the live guard is armed on the upgrade boot. Deciding on the 7d ALONE moved 443 of this instance's 476 re-files carrying a Fable bucket the destination contradicts — the 2.305.0 scoped-bucket class, created by the repair. Measured on a COPY: 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 41 pairs voided, 7 sidecars seeded, 1 cache rebuilt, census 0 contradicting buckets anywhere, idempotent, 52 ms.** **r5: an identity can hold MORE THAN ONE cache file — the cache half is keyed on the FILES the product accepts (`usageIdentityGroups`' own predicate; `__models__`/`host-*`/a removed account's zombie/a pool all named and skipped) and each is resolved with the product's own `identityKeyFor` (so the migration now gets the roster RECORDS, not just ids), the `acct:` LAST RESORT being the only rung that may ask the streams (one match, else left alone and said; a pseudo key never — `__global__` and `__global_codex__` are both recorded with a null accountId). Keying on the stream's DOMINANT accountId left `usage-cache/__global__.json` — same org, same identity, 47 rows in that stream — unrepaired AND unseeded, so the live guard (keyed by CACHE FILE NAME) was inert on it and one `sweepUsageAnchors` (freshest cache of a group) re-poisoned the just-cleaned stream. Also `_primaryDrops`: a primary bucket the record STATES but the window cannot date is archived with its own line instead of vanishing, the move counts PARTIAL, and the refile reason is the verdict of the bucket that decided it, never the `'window'` placeholder. Measured on a COPY: 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 42 pairs voided, **8 cache keys in an identity, 8 sidecars seeded, 0 without one, 0 contradicting buckets anywhere, 7106 rows in and out**, idempotent, 64 ms.** **④ THE IDENTITY ANCHOR IS DERIVED FROM THE API (B-855a c2, 2026-09-17, `repairSidecarsByApiPhase` — STANDING: every boot after the one-shots via the engine's `repairIdentityAnchors('boot')`, the human-triggered `POST /api/usage/repair-identity`, and once as migration `2026-09-repair-sidecars-by-api-phase`).** The panel is the producer B-855a showed can answer for another account, so it cannot be the identity anchor; the API phase of each roster claude subscription is derived from three witnesses — anchors whose 7d MOVED on a `rate-limit-event` (a 5h-only event re-anchors the file's carried-forward 7d: 6 of 12 on the polluted member, so a plain `source` filter is blind), the slot-verified readings the guard archived to readings-window-mismatch.ndjson (`entry.slot.slotOk`), and c1's `.apiwin-` — ≥3 rows, ≥60 % of the histogram (±120 s merged), else 'no-evidence' and the account is left alone. The API phase WINS: a contradicting `.window-` sidecar is archived (store `window-sidecar`, reason naming both phases) and re-stamped `{source:'api', verifiedAt, verifiedBy:'rate-limit-events', scopedRule:'same-phase-as-7d', n, of}` (an agreeing on-demand one is CONFIRMED to api; an api one is kept byte-identical), `.apiwin-` is written when absent; a cache whose 7d contradicts is archived (readings-foreign-usage-cache.ndjson, action replaced/emptied) and rebuilt via `_cacheFromAnchor` from the newest anchor that agrees WHOLLY (every scoped bucket judged on the 7d phase — the r4 measured same-phase rule; the r4 preserve source is only a dated, in-phase bucket, never an undated one riding a foreign record) or EMPTIED with `emptiedReason`; a cache whose only fault is a scoped bucket is stripped in place; then the last 24 h of archived own readings newer than the file are written back through `captureRateLimitEvent` in time order (idempotent by `fetchedAt`). MEASURED on a copy of this instance 2026-09-17: 10 identities with evidence (each ≥95 % on one phase), 3 sidecars re-stamped (each carried a fourth member's phase — four members shared ONE phase), 7 confirmed, 3 caches replaced, 128 readings re-admitted, second run all kept / 0 re-admitted, 90 ms; the member the owner felt rebuilt onto its OWN window (2026-09-24T09:00Z) with its own Fable 55 %, never the foreign 98 %. Gate: test-readings-attribution §20 (the fixture shaped like these stores + the untouched, confirmed, thin-evidence and emptied controls, idempotency) + test-migrations 42.** **FINAL VERIFIER (2026-09-17): `ORG_FIELDS` (`overage`, `spend`) are org-level billing facts, not readings — carried through `_cacheFromAnchor` and every emptied remnant (a rebuild that dropped them flipped the spend authorizer's only overage refusal from REFUSE to ALLOW and re-opened B-ad05 on the very boot that shipped it); `apiPhaseFor` no longer counts `.apiwin-` as evidence (it is the witness being judged — one poisoned live entry voted for itself) and skips an archived row the live path marked `witness.ok:false`; the repair also runs HOURLY (server.js, quiet unless it changed something). Pinned: test-readings-attribution §20 (org facts on replace + empty, the witness leg) + test-spend-paths §7c (the fail-closed census).**

### fixture-guard.js

fixture-guard.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE DECLARATION OF WHAT A TEST FIXTURE LOOKS LIKE, so no production reader can count one (2026-09-09): the `vs-` scratch prefix under a tmp root + the `e2e00000-0000-4000-8000-` synthetic session-id family, `fixtureLitter()` (the standing sweep as a pure decision; its OPT-IN `graceMs` — one caller, the whole-directory sweep — gives an UNDECLARED dir the SAME in-flight floor every sweeper already refuses to delete below, because a concurrent checkout's leftover was turning the mandatory gate red over a dir nothing was allowed to remove), the ONE declared real-home exception (`vs-wire-probe-`, which measures the INSTALLED CLI with the machine's real credentials) and the `FIXTURE_STALE_MS` that probe now READS instead of declaring its own copy. Two suites wrote synthetic transcripts — hand-written `assistant` records with a `usage` block and no API request behind them — into the developer's REAL ~/.claude/projects (their spawned server inherited HOME and can only discover what lives under its own home), and the PRODUCTION instance's usage walk ingested them: **79,533 permanent ledger rows** claiming Fable tokens nobody spent, `acct:null` so counted into the machine login's anchor `costSince`, i.e. into the burn rate the estimator spends against, plus 222 dead cursors. The window is SECONDS (both suites clean up on exit) and the damage is FOREVER — caught in the act mid-fix: a dir appeared at 14:25Z from another worktree and the ledger grew 5,406 rows at 14:26Z. `src/usage-walker.js` + `src/session-store.js` ask it (discovery on BOTH branches — local readdir and the DEVICE snapshot); data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan carries an INLINE COPY (checkout-less host) driven over one table by test-usage-walk-parity. THE ISOLATION AND THE REFUSAL ARE TWO HALVES OF ONE FIX and only the refusal survives a suite killed by a signal. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

Archives each shard VERBATIM under data/archive/usage-origin-backfill-<day>/ (+ a `_migration.json` naming who copied it) before rewriting it atomically; idempotent on `origin` already being present; an unparseable or non-object line is kept verbatim. ### fixture-ledger-purge.js

fixture-ledger-purge.js — the one-shot PURGE of test-fixture rows from the permanent ledger (2026-09-09, migration `2026-09-purge-test-fixture-ledger`): archives every fixture row with a PER-CLASS reason (fabricated vs a real CI-probe turn in a throwaway cwd — counts and TOKENS are per class so the fabricated half cannot hide inside the real one), drops the dead cursors + synthetic attribution entries, VOIDS the `costSince` of every anchor whose interval contained a removed row (the anchor RECORD is never removed — the reading is real, only the cost measured beside it is not) and drops rates.json. ### codex-fork-ledger-purge.js

codex-fork-ledger-purge.js — the one-shot ARCHIVE of forked codex rollouts' replayed rows (2.369.203, migration `2026-10-archive-codex-fork-replays`). A forked rollout (session_meta.forked_from_id) opens by replaying its ancestors' token_count records, all stamped at the fork instant (it replays their turn_contexts too, so "before the first turn_context" catches only 105 of 1,714 — the TIMESTAMP is the rule); the walk keyed them `cx:<fork thread>:<total>`, so the per-thread rid never met the ancestor's row: 1,661 double-counted rows on the author's instance (1,557 gpt-5.6-sol + 104 null-model, 278.5M tokens, ≈ $177, 2026-08-24..25). From this release both walkers (src/usage-walker.js + data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan, FORK REPLAY; the fork instant persists in the cursor as `forkTs`) skip a token_count within 2 s of a fork's session_meta — over the local corpus 1,714 of 1,714 replays, 0 genuine requests (the 3 cross-thread twins it leaves are three NON-fork threads whose identical first request is real). `purgeCodexForkReplays({dataDir, codexSessionsDir, id})` archives a row only when it is a LOCAL `cx:<thread>:<total>` row of a thread whose rollout here is a fork, inside that window, AND the ledger holds an earlier row of another thread with the same total and identical i/cr/o (a replay whose ancestor was never ingested is the request's only record — kept; a same-total row with other tokens is a real request — kept; host rows — their rollouts are not readable here — kept). Every copy of the rid is archived to data/archive/codex-fork-replays-<day>.ndjson with a reason, then the shard is rewritten atomically; idempotent. Dry run over a read of the production ledger 2026-10-03: 1,661 rows, 278,542,320 tokens, 0 kept-for-a-reason, 2.2 s. The estimator needs nothing voided: its interval costs are memo-keyed by the ledger's event count.

### ledger-slot-backfill.js

ledger-slot-backfill.js — the one-shot RE-KEY of the permanent ledger rows the OTel-observed org attributed (B-f69c ②, 2.369.163, owner decision ut-1c6c15a2db ②; migration `2026-09-backfill-ledger-by-slot`). **What it repairs:** from 2.361.0 until the 2026-09-07 attribution law two OTel paths chose a row's ACCOUNT — `truthLookup(rid)` overrode the bake, and corrective attribution entries (`recordAttribution({sid, acct: observed, pool, ts: Math.max(rec.ts, lastTs + 1)})`) taught every later bake the spawn-time org; the readings-by-slot repair only reached entries a DEAD member could date, so the rows kept the account each hot-switched conversation STARTED on. **Candidates by evidence only:** a local claude row billed THROUGH A POOL (a session with no pool reads one credential dir for its whole life, so its observed org IS its slot by construction — the refuted mechanism needs a re-point to lie) whose rid the OTel stash (`usage-history/otel-truth.ndjson`) names with a KNOWN org whose account IS the row's account, or whose governing attribution entry is CORRECTIVE and names it; a corrective entry is recognised by its writer's own spelling (same sid + account as a stash observation, `ts` = the observation's ts or the previous entry + 1 ms — `recordUsageAttribution` stamps `Date.now()`). Codex, remote-host and every other disagreeing row is UNTOUCHED (not this migration's evidence). **Which slot:** ① the slot-transition ledger, session-scoped only, through reading-repair's session-meta join (a pool-default answer is not evidence about a conversation that may have had its own link); ② the conversation's own attribution walk with the corrective entries set aside (the rule every row baked since 2026-09-07 follows). **Refusals from the reading-window rules:** `decideLagShadow` — inside SHADOW_MS of a re-point the request may have carried the previous slot's token and a row states no window, so `no-evidence` ⇒ unprovable; `deathMarkers`/`isForeign` — a slot whose login was already dead cannot have answered. **The slot-ledger rung's previous slot is read by the row's `why`, never by `from`'s truthiness (quota r1, reproduced):** the ledger spells "no earlier slot" and "the machine login / a member whose record is gone" alike (`from: null` — `poolCurrentFor` answers null when the previous target's record vanished), and a spawn records `from` = the pool DEFAULT read before its link existed. `FIRST_LINK_WHYS` (`spawn`, `session-link`) ⇒ prevSlot undefined (a brand-new process has no in-flight request on any earlier token, so no shadow); every other why is a re-point ⇒ prevSlot = `from ?? null`, null = the machine login (`__global__` in the shadow rule) — exactly what the walk rung's predecessor entry says. Before, a row 3 s after a `from:null` per-session switch was re-keyed (the verifier measured 4.10 USD of rows under sub-b's re-learned rate vs 3.08 on the oracle ledger — that one row) and a row 3 s after a spawn off the default was archived as a lag shadow that cannot exist. **Outcomes:** confirmed (the slot record names the row's own account) ⇒ untouched, decided BEFORE any refusal — a row that already says its slot was not mis-attributed, and the shadow question belongs to every row of the ledger, not to this migration; proven ⇒ re-keyed in place (tokens kept, `atype`/`aname` from the roster, `slotRekeyedBy` + `slotRekeyedFrom`, the original archived VERBATIM with the rung that proved it); unprovable ⇒ ARCHIVED with a per-row reason class (`lag-shadow` / `no-slot-record` / `dead-slot` / `pool-target-unresolved`) and removed from the live ledger — never a guess; the corrective entries themselves are archived out of attribution.ndjson. All to `data/archive/ledger-by-slot-<date>.ndjson`, archive BEFORE each atomic rewrite (an archive failure throws ⇒ the run fails and retries). **The estimator:** every identity whose anchor stream names an account that lost or gained a row is re-learned through the estimator's own `ratesFor` over the repaired ledger (pair costs recompute from the live ledger, so no `costSince` is voided); the previous `rates.json` entries are archived first. **Report:** `{rows, candidates, rekeyed, archived, untouched, confirmed, byRung, archivedWhy, stash, corrective, shards, identities, relearned, ms}` — ONE `[migrate] ledger-by-slot:` line, the counts in the ledger's report row, one info notice when anything moved. Idempotent by itself (a second run finds nothing: re-keyed rows are skipped, archived ones and correctives are gone). **Scale:** the transition ledger is indexed once (`indexTransitions` / `ownLedgerRow` = `slotAt`'s session-scoped half by binary search) — measured on a synthetic 300 000-row ledger with 20 000 transitions and 20 000 attribution entries: 1.6 s, 1.1 GB peak RSS. **Honest limits:** a stash row trimmed by the 30-day/12 MB boot trim leaves its row unidentifiable (untouched); a corrective entry written for an observation with no timestamp (`ts` 0 ⇒ `Date.now()` at ingest) is not recognisable and stays in the walk. Gate: test-migrations (the synthetic ledger + transitions fixture: 3 re-keyed on both rungs, 3 archived with reasons, confirmed rows (one inside a re-point's shadow) and out-of-scope rows (codex, remote, no pool) untouched — the pooled scope and the confirm-first order each with a patched-copy control, the two corrective spellings, the relearn, the re-bake guard, a byte-identical second run; quota r1: a `from:null` per-session re-point 3 s before a row ⇒ archived `lag-shadow`, the same re-point 20 min before ⇒ re-keyed, a row 3 s after a SPAWN whose `from` names the pool default ⇒ re-keyed — both red on quota 3). **A PASS IS RESUMABLE (quota r2, the r2 verifier's crash probe — a real SIGKILL at three kill points on the production-shaped copy):** the runner retries a migration that never recorded itself, and the retry used to (A, killed after a shard's archive append, before its rename) archive every row of that shard AGAIN — 75,646 archive lines with 32,837 duplicates instead of 42,821 — and report/notify only the remainder (28,285 / 4,540 of 37,399 / 5,337, which is what `migrations.json` `reports` kept); (B, killed after every shard, before the attribution rename) re-archive the 84 corrective entries and report 0 / 0 with NO notice at all; and (B and C, killed inside the relearn) never re-learn the estimator — the retry found nothing left to touch, so the rates stayed learned from the OTel-attributed ledger (the verifier's third kill point looked clean on the ledger; its rates were not). Now `readPriorArchive(archiveDir, id)` reads every `ledger-by-slot-*.ndjson` line this migration id wrote: `_appendArchive` skips a line whose identity (`_archKey`: store + file + rid + mid + ts + sid for a row, sid + ts + acct for an attribution entry, the entry for the rates line) an EARLIER pass already wrote — never within the pass, because two identical rows the ledger genuinely holds (12 on the production copy) are two rows leaving it; archive lines carry `action: 'rekeyed' | 'archived'` (+ `slot`); a pass that finishes appends a `store: 'pass'` marker, and lines after the last marker are an OPEN (crashed) pass whose counts (per key max(earlier, this pass)) and touched accounts (its archived rows' accounts + the rows it already re-keyed, `slotRekeyedBy === id`) are this pass's too. `report.total` = the whole repair, `report.resumed`; the migration's notice and its ledger report row state `total` (+ `thisPass` when resumed). Measured on the production-shaped copy at all three kill points: live ledger byte-identical to the uninterrupted run, zero extra archive lines (only the marker), totals 37,399 / 5,337 / 84, relearned 5. **ONE KEY PER ANCHORS FILE (quota r2, low):** five anchor files hold two spellings of one identity (`org:<uuid>` and the file-name form `org_<uuid>`); both resolve to the same file, so the relearn minted five phantom `rates.json` entries under the `_` spelling and reported "relearned 10" for 5 identities. The relearn now groups the collected keys by `anchorSlug` and keeps the spelling the sanitiser CHANGES (the one readers look up), naming the others in `report.anchorKeySpellings` for a separate cleanup. Gates: test-migrations (+15: the three kill points in a child process retried through the runner, the uninterrupted reference, a no-memory patched copy as the negative control, a genuinely duplicated row, the two-spelling anchors file). **quota r3 (two lows, red first):** ① **a FINISHED pass the runner never recorded** (killed between the pass marker and the runner's migrations.json rename) used to retry into a pass that found every row already re-keyed and nothing open — 0 / 0, no notice, the 37,399-row repair recorded as nothing. `readPriorArchive` now also returns `lastComplete` (the newest marker; markers carry `relearned` since r3) and a pass with no work of its own and nothing open states that marker's totals (`resumed: true`, `recovered: true`) without writing a second marker. ② **a torn archive tail** (ENOSPC / a short write left a fragment with no newline) swallowed the first line of the retry's append — one archived original with no readable archive line. Every append (`_appendLines`, the marker too) now checks the file's last byte and closes a fragment with a newline first; `readPriorArchive` counts unparseable lines (`report.archiveUnparseable`, one warn line). Gates: test-migrations (D) the marker-before-ledger SIGKILL + a no-recovery copy, (E) the torn tail + an append-straight-after copy.

### weekly-lanes-unfold.js

weekly-lanes-unfold.js — the one-shot REPAIR of the plan weekly lane (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21, migration `2026-09-weekly-lanes-unfold` through src/migration-runner.js): since 2.361.2 the rate_limit_event parse wrote the overage-included weekly type — 2.1.274's own PER-MODEL bucket, about twice the plan week — into the plan 7d, so every capped account's plan week held the bucket's number until its next panel. **Candidates = claude caches whose PLAN limit's `source` is `rate-limit-event`** — the only producer that states ONE plan window; a panel, the statusline and get_usage state both windows and would already have corrected the week, so a plan week they wrote is NEVER touched (`kept`). **Evidence = the newest NON-rejected event carrying `unifiedWindows` in the live session buffers linked to that credential slot** (session-meta `accountId` → the per-session pool link `pool-links/<pool>/<sess>`, else the pool default link, else the subscription itself; a remote or codex session is never evidence; the last 512 KiB of each `.buf`), **judged by the account's own established window** (`.window-<key>` plan reset ±120 s, `weeklyNear`; no sidecar or a foreign reset ⇒ `left` with the reason). The rewrite archives the pre-repair object under `data/archive/weekly-lanes-unfold-<day>/` (+ `_migration.json` naming the keys) and writes the event's WEEKLY lanes through `captureRateLimitEvent` — the plan 7d, the model cap named by the sidecar's family, the fold rule — with the 5-hour lane deliberately left out (a tail line has no clock of its own and the 5h was never the bucket's victim). **THE CLOCK never regresses the file's `fetchedAt`** (max of the buffer's mtime, the replaced window's `measuredAt` + 1, the file's `fetchedAt` + 1): the anchors sweep dedups on `fetchedAt <= seen` and both newest-wins merges (`__global__` ↔ usage-cache.json, global ↔ named account) rank on it, so a regressed stamp would lose to the number it corrected. Content-idempotent (`already` when the plan week equals the event's window); the report carries a verb per key (rederived / already / left / kept) and the registry logs it and files ONE server notice only when something was rewritten. The poisoned anchors of the bad period are NOT rewritten here — a same-source pair with a ≥5-point jump and no corroborating cost is tainted by the estimator's own rule. Censuses: test-quota-model ⑩ names it (its cache writes go through the write path; its own `writeFileSync` is the archive copy) and ⑪ classifies it `migrated`; test-rate-limit-capture ⑩ requires it to describe the type without spelling it. Gates: test-migrations (the incident fixture verbatim on disk — pool default + per-session link, an older windowed event and a rejection in the same tail, a panel-sourced neighbour, an orphan candidate, a foreign-window candidate, a codex session that must not count; the archive, the notice, idempotency, the ledger belt, and the in-process `/api/usage` payload) + test-restore-smoke (the same fixture seeded into a worktree server's own data/, the FIRST `/api/usage` of that boot reads sevenDay 0.43 · fiveHour 0.09 · Fable 0.87 and the ledger records the run). **r2 (2026-09-21): a repair the module itself could not perform — the archive unwritable, the write path refusing — is a `refused` key (never `left`), a cache dir that exists but cannot be listed is `unreadable` (a MISSING dir is a fresh instance: nothing to repair, a success), and the migration THROWS on either so the runner logs it and retries next boot instead of recording a refusal as applied; the keys already re-derived are `already` on the retry (test-migrations r2).**

### usage-walker.js

usage-walker.js — THE ledger walk, ONE module (2.297.0 twin-killer): UsageHistory.scan() consumes it IN-PROCESS (cursors injected, onEvent enrichment orchestrator-side), the daemon runs it as the usage-scan op child, and data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan mirrors it for checkout-less ssh hosts (parity-pinned). **ORIGIN (2026-09-10): every event says WHICH KIND of transcript produced it — `origin` 'main'|'subagent'|'workflow' stamped on ALL of them (never "missing means main": the backfill must be able to answer 'unknown'), plus `wf`/`agent`; an agent event's `cwd` is the PARENT PROJECT's and its own directory rides along as `wcwd` ONLY when it differs, so a worktree agent stops being its own row in "By project" (272 of this instance's 3,155 agent transcripts). A codex rollout is 'main' by RULE (the store merges a sub-agent's rollout into the parent thread). `makeProjectCwdReader` is the EXPORTED ladder — a conversation's cwd is not constant (3 of 782 top-level transcripts state more than one, and one of them is this instance's biggest spender: a rename left its FIRST record on `…/claude-code-webui` while its latest records and its project dir say `…/vibespace`, so "the first cwd" filed $7,828 of one conversation's agent spend in a SECOND project row), so a candidate is VERIFIED by encoding it forward to the project directory name (§5's deterministic direction) → the tail window → the conversation's MOST RECENT cwd → a sibling transcript; bounded 128 KiB windows, memoized. The backfill migration REQUIRES that export rather than keeping a third copy.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **THE PER-TICK BYTE BUDGET (2.369.167, perf lane ⑥): `runUsageWalk({…, budgetBytes, onBudget})` — with an `onBudget` hook (a function returning a promise; UsageHistory passes `() => new Promise(setImmediate)`) the walk YIELDS every `budgetBytes` of consumed transcript bytes and answers a PROMISE of the same `{events, cursors, cursorFile, filesTouched}`; without a hook it is the synchronous function it always was (`budgetBytes` ignored) — the daemon's `usage-scan` child (agentd.js) and the shipped scanner keep that form, a child has no loop to block. ONE WALK: the body is a generator (`walkSteps`, `scanFileWith`, `scanBufferSteps` for decompressed zst rollouts) whose `yield`s are the budget points, driven straight through (sync) or across one `await onBudget()` per yield (`driveYielding`); a yield sits only AFTER a whole line was consumed and its bytes added to `cur.offset`, so a suspended walk's cursors are always valid (one yield per whole budget: `spent %= budget`, a line is never split); a rejected hook rejects the walk and `steps.return()` closes the file it was parked in. Cursor semantics untouched (byte offsets, the incomplete trailing line unconsumed, size < offset ⇒ reset — a file truncated between two yields ends the read at EOF and resets on the next run exactly as the sync walk does —, zst plain-offset cursors, `pendMid` in the cursor, the device two-phase commit). The exported `scanBufferWith` is the sync spelling of `scanBufferSteps`. Gate: test-usage-walk-parity's budget block (a 7.4 MiB four-kind fixture incl. a zst rollout: yielding ≡ sync ≡ shipped scanner on events, cursors and filesTouched; ⌊consumed / 1 MiB⌋ yields; a hooked re-walk never yields; the rejected-hook fd check; rotation mid-walk; the UsageHistory/route leg). Measured by scripts/measure-usage-walk-yield.mjs (200 MB §1c ledger in a scratch HOME): max loop gap 359.6 → 7.9 ms, wall 358 → 352 ms.**

### login-expiry.js

login-expiry.js — PURE (零依赖) 登录会话寿命判定 (2026-09-07): `claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt` 是登录会话的**绝对**截止时间, 刷新 access token 不会推迟它(实测: 30 分钟前刷新过的成员仍然只剩 17 小时); 过期后 CLI 刷新拿到 invalid_grant 并把 accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt **清空**却保留截止时间与 scopes = 磁盘上"已登出"的形状. loginState(creds, now) → ok/expiring(<24h)/expired/logged-out/**unknown**(缺字段一律 unknown, 永不 'ok' — 读不出来是无知不是健康, 每个消费者都必须把 unknown 当作"不要拦"); NEAR_MS=30min 是"切换目标必须活过这次切换"的线(**r2: 那是关于自愿移动的规则 — 当前成员已经死透时, 20 分钟的登录仍然胜过零, 逃生要能落到它上面**); loginBlockedPhrase/loginBlockedText = 每个被拦成员**各说各的事实**(已过期/已登出/还剩 <t>), 绝不用一句话覆盖一张混着三种事实的名单; **r3 增 loginWallPhrase = 当前成员自己那条死登录的从句形式 — 它是 `fromLogin` 这个具名输出, 绝不能塞进 `deadBuckets` 假装成一个花光了的配额桶(桶会随窗口自愈, 登录不会; 那条每小时重复一次的通知因此开出了配额药方"等窗口重置", 而唯一要用户动手的那个账号是它唯一说不出名字的)**; reviewWarnings = 每成员每档只说一次的纯状态转移(换了截止时间=重新登录⇒旧账本作废; 跳过的档只发最紧急那条, 绝不补发已成历史的提醒; **r2 增可选 watchingSince: 在本账本诞生之前就死掉、且已不新鲜(>STALE_GRACE_MS=24h)的登录是既有状况, 记为已发但不发声 — 它的面是 Manage Agents 里那枚常驻红芯片, 不是事件收件箱**); **2026-09-07 增 `reloggedIn(info, prevExp)` = 真的开了新会话吗(三条各自承重: 必须重新**活着**('ok'/'expiring') — 被清空的文件保留截止时间且那个时间可以在未来, 只看"数字变大"会把已登出读成已恢复; 必须**现在有**可读截止时间('unknown'=无主张, 无主张永不推翻按事实发出的警告); 截止时间必须**变了** — 一个会话的截止时间终生固定, 变了只能来自新会话, 而保持不变的凭据重写(token 刷新/跨机拷贝/导入)是同一个会话, 什么都没修好也就什么都不能撤回; 刻意**不是**"变大": 短 SSO 策略给回来的截止时间可以比我们警告的那个**更早**(还剩 20h 时警告, 新会话只有 12h), 用 `>` 判会把那条已经不成立的条目永远留着; 而撤回也不会丢掉仍然成立的警告——同一轮里阶梯就按新截止时间重新武装) 与 `SHORT_SESSION_MS`(36h)+`shortSession(spanMs)` = 会话时长短到值得提一句 org SSO 策略(本机实测的截止时间是 5/9/12/16 **天**), 没测到就永远为假. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/login-expiry-watch.js

server/login-expiry-watch.js — 被动巡检(boot+5min, 只读文件, §ban-safety 零 vendor 调用): 每个登录最多三条"For you"收件箱条目(24h/1h/已过期), 点名账号与到期时刻, 账本 data/login-expiry.json 原子落盘(含 `since`=本账本开始盯梢的时刻) ⇒ 重启不重发、重新登录即静默、升级当天不会为几周前就死掉的账号刷一屏 urgent(r2: 实测该实例首次巡检发了 3 条, 全是非路由成员); 收件箱拒收就回滚该档下次重试(标成已发=静默失败); **r3: 条目文案按 `state` 分支而不是按档 — warnStageFor 把 'expired' 与 'logged-out' 收进同一个终端档, 档回答"多紧急", 状态回答"发生了什么"; CLI 清空 token 时**保留**截止时间, 所以被清空的记录可以带一个**未来**的截止时间(任何不可恢复的刷新都会产生这个形状: 会话被吊销/轮换, 或在隔离目录里显式登出), 于是条目对着 20 天后的时间戳说"已过期", 而同一行上的芯片(它是按 state 分支的)说"已登出" — 一条记录两个面互相矛盾.** **2026-09-07 恢复: 已经发出去的条目是一个断言, 发它的人必须撤回它** — 掉账本只让**将来**不再发, 而 owner 重新登录了两个成员(新 token, 截止时间 29 天后)之后, 收件箱里那条 `Claude login for "Member F" is signed out…` 仍然 open, 旁边同一行的芯片却早就变绿了; 现在成员行带 `items:[{id,text}]`(本 watch 为**这个**截止时间发过的条目 id, **落盘** — 警告与重新登录之间重启一次也必须还能撤回, 否则只是把同一个 bug 推后一步), `reloggedIn` 成立即逐条走 store 自己的 `setStatus(id,'done','system')`(落盘+广播 ⇒ 所有客户端实时更新)并只记一行 `X: re-logged in — N warning(s) cleared`; 三条禁令各配负控: **用户已处理的绝不重开也不重标**(非 open 一律原样丢出列表)、**别人发的绝不碰**(只认自己账本里的 id, 写之前还要复核 sessionKey 与文案 — agent 在别的会话发的 vibespace-ask 对它不可见)、**保持同一截止时间的凭据重写不算重新登录**; `resolvedBy:'system'` 既不是 user 也不是 agent, 面板已解决区标 `automatically`(自己消失的条目必须自己说明是自己消失的). **登录成功即立刻巡检**: 5 分钟的轮询意味着盯着自己刚修好的那条看很久, 所以每条 finalize 路由(relogin-finalize / subscription finalize——放在自动合并那条**提前 return** 之上, 两个出口都巡检 / codex device-auth)在登录确实成功时巡检; server.js 留住句柄并以 `getLoginExpiryWatch` 惰性 getter 下发; **r2 三条**: ①门要读那个方法**真给的答案** — r1 门在 `r.loggedIn` 上, 而 `accounts.reloginResolve` 的四种回答里**没有一种**带顶层 `loggedIn`(`{outcome:'pending'}` / `{outcome:'same'|'split', account}` / `{outcome:'moved', movedTo}`, 抓到的登录在**嵌套**的 account 里, 'moved' 干脆没有 account), 于是这个功能恰恰死在收件箱条目与登录芯片把用户送去的那条路上, 而套件绿只因它的 fixture **编了**那个形状(现在 §5b 的 fixture 由真 `reloginResolve` 对着临时 store 的一次真调用**捕获**而来); 门=`!!r.account?.loggedIn || r.outcome === 'moved'`('moved' 把活登录搬进了**另一条**记录, 要撤回的是那条的账本行; 'pending' 保持沉默) ②**被轮询的路由不许带无界副作用**: manage-agents 每 3s 打一次 relogin-finalize 打满 5 分钟且 'same' 会重复(实测 100 次轮询=100 次巡检) ⇒ 只在**变化**时巡检(`sweepOnLoginTransition` 比对答案自己的**凭据指纹**: outcome+记录+身份+access token 到期, 全部取自路由已经拿在手里的那个答案, **不是**第二个凭据读者); 刻意**不是**"这个账号已经扫过了"的布尔闩——重新登录一个**仍然登录着**的账号从第 1 次轮询起就答 'same'(离用户真正完成浏览器流程还有几分钟), 布尔闩会恰好跳过唯一重要的那次 ③自动合并那条要在 `mergeSubscription` **之后**再巡检一次: `fin` 之上那次跑的时候新凭据还在**丢弃记录**的目录里, 而带着 open 警告的是幸存记录, 它读到的是陈旧截止时间, 什么都撤不回; 合并前那次保留(它是所有非合并出口上唯一的一次), 因为巡检是幂等的(已钉); **只有一个读者**: 巡检问 `accounts.loginStateOf`, 正是芯片(roster 行的 `loginState`)的来源 ⇒ 两个面不可能对同一个文件各说各话, 失败只记日志绝不抛回登录路由. **24h/1h 条目的组织策略提示**: 实测该成员上一次登录会话不足 36h 才加 `(its last login session lasted only ~24 h — this org's session policy may be short)`; 承重的是"实测"——朴素判据(截止时间减凭据文件 mtime)会把健康的 30 天登录报成 20 小时(每次 access token 刷新都重写该文件而截止时间不动), 所以 `measureLoginSpan` 只在**目击**到登录时才信 mtime(**观察日志** `seen`——每个订阅每轮都写, 与稀疏的警告账本刻意分开: 健康成员没有警告行, 而它恰恰就是下次登录需要被目击的那个——≤3 轮前确认过、截止时间此后变了、文件写在那次确认之后), 把登录那次写入钉在一轮宽的窗口里; 没目击就什么都不说, 记下的 span 比当前剩余时间还短就是陈旧值同样不说; 用词是 "may be"(一个成员的一次会话是关于策略的证据, 不是对策略的读数); 摸文件的只有 `src/harnesses/claude.js`, 它在纯判定旁附上 `writtenAt`. 此前 VibeSpace 只在**一轮已经死掉之后**才反应(池的 auth-failure 驱逐), 用户看见一次失败、然后它"又好了", 从没有人被告知要重新登录. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### auto-resume-signal.js

auto-resume-signal.js — PURE (imports nothing, 2026-09-08): does a NORMALIZED quota reading say the wall a conversation is WAITING on is gone? `windowOpened` needs THREE facts and each was a real way to spend a billed turn into a wall — the limit **LANE** matches (`snapshot.limitId`; a codex login reports `codex` and `codex_bengalfox` minute by minute and the spark lane read 0% through the whole 32h stall), the reading **STATES THE BUCKET** the wait is about and reports it not spent (a `rate_limit_event` names exactly ONE bucket, so a healthy 7d reading says nothing about a 5h wall), and no SIBLING bucket of that lane is spent (the c1206711 rule); an arm that does not know its own wall (the pool's +45s near-arm) is never opened this way. `why` is contract, not prose — 'we cannot tell' (other-lane/other-bucket/unknown-bucket/no-reading) may never be spelled like 'yes'. `bucketSpent` is deliberately NOT the pool's 3-5% candidate gate: that one picks between accounts, this one authorises an unattended turn. PURE because both producers ask it (claude rate_limit_event, codex rate_limits_updated) — and NOT the weekly-phase fingerprint (reading-lag.js), which is an ACCOUNT identity rule and would answer 'differ' about the very reading that proves recovery (codex's weekly window is not phase-stable: the incident's two windows are 152320s apart).

### resume-continuity.js

resume-continuity.js — PURE **resume ladder** (B-6b6d, owner ruling 2026-09-07): `resumeSpawnPick({explicit, conversation, instanceDefault, resume, hasSource})` → `{value, origin: chosen|conversation|instance|harness}` — 一个对话在 resume/fork/restart 时保留**它自己的** model/effort, 实例默认值只对**新建**会话生效, 显式 per-session 选择仍然压过两者. 两个调用者一条法则: 客户端 session-lifecycle(`hasSource:false` — 只有服务端读得到对话自己的记录 ⇒ 续跑时什么都不发)与服务端 ws-create(在 buildSessionArgs **之前**, 经 harness descriptor 的 `store.lastTurn<Knob>` 读回). `hasSource` 由那个 hook 的**存在**推导, 绝不另立 caps 布尔; 没有来源的旋钮在 resume 时发**空**而不是默认值(无条件兜底本身就是这个缺陷); 有来源但为空(还没跑过 turn)才回落实例默认并**记日志**. **r2(2026-09-07)**: ①**claude 两个旋钮都没有来源** — 全量语料 2650 份转录里 `message.model` 从不带 `[1m]` 变体(而 CLI 自己的 `model_refusal_fallback` 证明会话就跑在 `claude-fable-5[1m]` 上), 且分类器改道记录写在**它描述的那条 assistant 之后** 2-10 行(r1 的 20 行向后窗口 139 次只命中 1 次, 16.8% 的主线程 assistant 记录落在改道区间内) ⇒ 读回来的 id 结构上不可命令, **删掉来源**而不是再加一层守卫, claude resume 两个旋钮都不发, 由 CLI 自己的会话记录(变体精确)决定 ②**opencode 有来源就给它**(`serve.facts().sessionModel`, 与 discover 共用同一份 v1 列表缓存, 服务关着就是 `''`⇒实例默认并记日志) ③`''` 是**明确选择**(新建会话对话框第一项 "Auto (model default)")只有 `undefined` 才是沉默 — 只在**新建**这一侧成立(续跑的线路是 `model || undefined`, 两者同字节), 客户端在新建时原样发送让空串活过线路. **r3 增 `applyOriginHint(origin, hint)`**: 新建会话由**客户端**解析实例默认值(它要给自己的芯片用, 且它独占 legacy `session.defaultEffort` 与 `settings.isModified` 这两个服务端看不到的事实)并原样上线 ⇒ 服务端看到的只是一个裸字串, 只能读成显式选择, 于是新建会话的 origin **永远**是 `'chosen'`, `'instance'`/`'harness'` 结构上不可达, 而那些**根本不显示选择器**的创建路径(openShellTerminal/工具栏/setup-flows/manage-agents)在会话属性里被写成"你为本会话的选择"; 客户端现在把它算出来又丢掉的那个 origin 一并发出(`spawnOriginHint`), 本函数只允许把服务端自己的 `'chosen'` **降级**成 `'instance'`/`'harness'`, 绝不上调、绝不改动**值**、绝不重指服务端独有的事实(`'conversation'`/`'chosen'`/垃圾一律忽略, 旧客户端不发就保持 master 的答案). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md
