permission-rules.js — PURE model + DOM-free tree renderer for the READ-ONLY "where does this rule come from" view (2026-09-07, owner ruling 10 / §2.14): the ONE typed record every harness produces (layers → rules, `kind` allow|deny|ask|value), claude's settings hierarchy in the CLI's OWN vocabulary (2.1.257 binary), codex `config/read` layers+origins (incl. the file-less `sessionFlags` layer), opencode's origin-less resolved config, the closed `UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` code set (an unavailable record NEVER carries layers), and `renderRuleTree` with esc/t/icons INJECTED so the XSS rule is unit-provable. allow/deny/ask are the harness's own words and are never translated. **2026-09-07 r4: codex keys `origins` by LEAF PATH for a TABLE-valued key (measured on 0.153.4 — `sandbox_workspace_write` itself is NEVER in `origins`, and a `-c …network_access=true` session flag lands on the LEAF as `sessionFlags`), so a key with no top-level origin is resolved from its leaves (all-agree ⇒ the key; split ⇒ ONE RULE PER LEAF under the layer that won it) — asking only the top level filed the user's own config under a forged "packaged defaults" layer noted "not set in any layer" and left the sessionFlags layer empty; the "nobody set it" bucket never forges codex's `packagedDefaults` variant (its schema REQUIRES a `file`), a layer may carry `fileNote` so "no file" ≠ "no path to show", and `originsDropped` (the producer's byte cap ate the map) files rules under an explicit unknown-source layer with `CODEX_CAPPED_NOTE`, never `CODEX_DEFAULT_NOTE`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

local-oracles.js — PURE registry of human-triggered ZERO-NETWORK CLI reads (owner ruling 6): each ORACLE carries its own PROOF (tool + date + CLI version + per-run INET connect counts) and each measured-and-REJECTED candidate (`claude auth status` 5, `claude agents --json` 5, `codex doctor --json` 16, **`codex app-server`+config/read 7 incl. chatgpt.com:443 — the one we had already SHIPPED, caught round 2**) stays forever as a NEGATIVE CONTROL with its verdict; a row carrying `blocks:'<backend>.<capsPath>'` names the capability its measurement switched OFF (server refusal `would-connect` + an always-shown disabled menu row read the SAME record, and the caps row must really be false). scripts/test-vendor-whitelist.mjs enforces both directions, re-measures live when strace + the CLI are present, and CENSUSES the spawns in the reader (its "no vendor request" assert is IN-PROCESS only — a child can connect where the file's own text cannot show it). ⇒ kb-design-lessons §9

### server/permission-rules.js

server/permission-rules.js — the READ-ONLY rule READER + the oracle RUNNER (ORCH): rung by caps row never by backend id (claude=settings files off disk / codex session=the session's own wrapper via the `read-permission-rules` stdin verb — instance NOT OFFERED, a fresh app-server child was measured connecting to chatgpt.com even logged out / opencode=the serve's **v1** /config); two capability gates on the session rung (harness row + the running wrapper's advert); routes `GET /api/permission-rules` + `POST /api/local-oracle/:id` and NO write route, ever. **2026-09-07 r4 — the wrapper's 32KiB ladder says what it LOST**: it forwards the permission keys' LEAF origins too (head-matched, `projects.*` still filtered), over the cap it drops `origins` **and sets `originsDropped:true`** (the old ladder dropped the map yet kept `ok:true`, so every key inherited "the packaged default" from a map it had deleted), and still-over-cap = `ok:false read-failed` with the byte count instead of an oversized journal line (measured: 700 writable_roots = 33719B after the drop); `shapeWrapperAnswer` forwards `originsDropped` and a WIRING PIN drives it through the real readViaSession seam. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### channel-store.js

**R3 (2026-09-26):** `findRecord` = one record by its vendorId (a backward window walk that stops at the id); a cache HIT coalesces its LRU stamp (`lruTouch`, 5 s, flushed on close) instead of one sync atomic write per thumbnail. Gate test-channels-images.

**Design 011 lane 2 (2026-10-03) — the poll stamps' side file:** `poll-stamps.json` holds each row's lastPollAt / lastScanAt / walkStartedAt (`store.stamps.get` / `set` / `lane(row)` / `flush`; memory first, written ≤ every `STAMPS_FLUSH_MS` = 120 s and at close; every set in between appends one line — the key's whole triple — to `poll-stamps.log`, folded by that write and replayed at the start, so a kill -9 keeps every stamp (a torn last line is counted and said); a key whose row left is dropped at the write; a row born under a departed key starts unstamped). The index serializer omits them (`INDEX_KEYS`), `serializeChunk` heals a row that still carries them (the side file is written before that index write), and `flush` skips a write whose bytes equal the last (`flushStats().writes` / `skipped`). A missing side file is said with the count of rows due at once. The engine reads them only through `laneOf(en)` = `store.stamps.lane(en)`. Gates test-channel-store ⑭, test-channels-index-scale ⑩.

channel-store.js — SHARED (fs+path only) persistence primitives for data/channels/ (design §5): adapters.json · index.json · msgs/<adapterId>/<convId>.ndjson (APPEND-ONLY) · audit.ndjson rolled by DATE into archive/ (the day comes from the file's OWN last record, never mtime; the shard is APPENDED to, never overwritten). **§5.1: `index.update(fn)` is the ONE mutation door** — a promise chain, so overlapping adapter passes QUEUE rather than race, and there is deliberately NO "write the whole index back" export: `writeJsonAtomic` is atomic at the fs layer only and the read-modify-write AROUND it is the round-4 codex-zst lost update, worse here because a clobbered ANCHOR makes the next pass SKIP. Cursor advances only after a COMPLETE pass; retention = 90d or 5,000 records whichever is SMALLER with a 7-DAY FLOOR; a derived value is cached for render speed and always re-derivable. **r2 three rules: the DEDUP SET remembers a vendorId only after its bytes are durable** (it was written inside the selection loop, so one failed append turned the batch into permanent "duplicates" and the anchor advanced past messages nobody wrote), **`readTail` pages on the TOTAL ORDER `(at, vendorId)`** and sorts by the order it pages by (a timestamp is not unique and a strict `<` stranded one record per group for ever), **and `adapters.json` gets the same single owner as the index** — `adapters.live()` + `adapters.update(fn)`, no `writeAdapters(obj)` for anyone to hand a private copy to, because the read-modify-write around it wiped a failing adapter's health whenever a healthy one passed second. `index.entry(a,c,{create:false})` is the LOOKUP form. **r3 two more: the log SEALS a partial last line before it grows** (an append is not atomic — a fragment plus the re-offered batch glued onto it swallowed exactly one record for ever, because the readers skip the unparseable line and the durable set then remembered its id; `appendRecords` preads the last byte, writes `\n` if it is not one, and the writer LOOPS) **and `readTail` SEEKS backward one 2 MiB window at a time** (reading the last window once left everything older unreachable while retention kept it — 3,000 lines, 2.28 MiB, 375 stranded — and made the dedup set forget them too; straddling bytes are carried as bytes, never decoded alone). **r4: a FAILED append DROPS the cached dedup set** — r2's "leaves no trace at all" was backwards: the write that threw may have landed a PREFIX, and a prefix that stopped on a record BOUNDARY (after `}` or after `\n`, the two cuts the seal cannot see) is a complete record the log holds while the LIVE set still calls it absent, so the same process re-offered the batch and served that record twice for ever (measured: `v1,v2,v3,v4,v4,v5`, `countSince` 6 for five records; a restart was already right, which pins it to the live set); now the retry re-derives the set from the log, byte-identical to the restart, while a throw BEFORE the write (`mkdirSync`) lands nothing and the set stays — r2 is what the set may CLAIM, r4 what it must FORGET, each with its own control. **r5: the dedup REBUILD refuses a log it cannot read** — `readTail` answered EMFILE/EIO/EACCES with an EMPTY read and the rebuild CACHED that empty set, so the post-restart first pass of every tracked conversation could write a replayed boundary page twice for ever (measured: `v1..v5,v5,v6`, `countSince` 7 for six records); `readTail(…, {strict:true})` at the ONE reader whose answer writes bytes — ENOENT is "no log yet", anything else throws out of `appendRecords` (pass fails, anchor stays, nothing cached), every other reader stays lenient because a derived number self-heals and `countSince` is asked inside `index.update()` after the anchor moved. **2.369.159: `groups.json` (agent groups, design §22.5) is the third single-owner file — `groups.update(fn)` / `live()` / `snapshot()`, no whole-file write for anyone else; a group's log is an ordinary `msgs/groups/<id>.ndjson`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **g3: `appendRecords` answers `lastText` (the newest appended record's text) for the index's last-line cache; the groups file carries `ownerRead` beside `groups`, same door.** **r2: an unreadable/unparseable store file (index / adapters / outbox / groups / wake-pace) is SET ASIDE as `<name>.corrupt-<ts>` (never unlinked, one named log line, `store.quarantined`) and only then started empty — a rename failure BLOCKS that family's writes; `pace` = the groups' persisted wake-pace ledger.** **r3: a BLOCKED index rejects `update()` too; every blocked door rejects `{code:'store-blocked', status:503}`; every refused flush is logged; a blocked wake-pace.json is never overwritten.**

### channel-groups.js

channel-groups.js — PURE (imports only channel-record) THE AGENT-GROUP MODEL (design §22, owner D1/D2, 2.369.159): the record + `validateGroup`/`newGroupId`/`pairKey` (symmetric), membership as PURE transitions `{group, event}` | `{code}` from the closed `ERROR_CODES` (g2 added the engine's `ambiguous` and the routes' `job-token` — every code the CLI's REMEDY table words) (duplicate invite = a no-op with a word; a pair takes no third member and is archived when a side leaves; kick = creator/owner; own notify only, the owner sets anyone's), `mentionsIn`, `wakeVerdict` (= the D2 table: next-turn|mention|always|mute × @ × invite × --quiet), `reportFor` (post-join, context first, newest kept under 2 KiB, the `read --before` pointer). r1: `reportFor`'s budget is the WHOLE text (three forms, else `fits:false` — never `null`, never over); `mentionsIn` ends a name at a script boundary (`@测试请看`). **r2: a line cut short is POINTED to (`read <gid> --before <cut+1> --limit <n>`); the PURE pace (`paceVerdict`/`paceGrant`/`paceRefund`/`prunePace`: 30 s per pair + 8 per sender per minute) and consent (`consentVerdict`: `confirm-wakes` over 5 without `--yes`, `wake-count-mismatch` for the owner's echo; `wakesPlanned`).** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r3: `PACE_SKEW_MS` 5 s — a stamp further ahead is dropped by `prunePace`, ignored by `paceVerdict`, counted by `paceFuture`; `paceRefund(…, {keepSender})`.** **lane group-pending (2026-10-01): `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log})` = where a record stands with each recipient (`DELIVERY_STATES` waiting | handed | muted | left; a marker EQUAL to the record's instant is handed — reportFor's `>`; `left` from the log's leave / kick witness) — the window's line under every message and the CLI's trailing clause, ONE rule.**

**Lane group-report-whole (2.369.228, the owner 2026-10-07):** `LINE_MAX` 400 → 2000 and `REPORT_BUDGET` 2048 → 4096 — a 1–2 KB group message rides a report WHOLE when the room allows (groups-engine still budgets `min(REPORT_BUDGET, room)`, so the 9600 B injection holds); the cut pointer and a card's `cut` only for a line truly cut (past 2 000 characters or past the room). Two cut lines can no longer share one 4 KB report — test-channel-groups §1c walks the span rule at an 8 KB PURE budget.

### server/groups-engine.js

**Lane group-report-card (2026-09-28, the owner: "怎么在那个对话里看不到你发了消息？"):** every mark `reportsForTurn` hands out carries `cards` (`cardsOf(g, rep)` — one per shown group MESSAGE: `{fromName, text, group: {id, name, at, from, self, via:'report', cut, more}}`, "… and N more" = `rep.clipped` on the oldest; a system record none) and the answer a flat `cards`; `commitReports(cid, marks)` emits them through THE ladder's card door (`deliver.emitPeerCard(cid, {…, kind: 'group'})`, oldest first, synchronously — before any await, so they land while the hook's answer is composed) and only then stamps the markers; no door wired ⇒ one warn line, the markers still move. A wake passes `group` (via 'wake', the message that woke it) to the ladder, whose own card after a successful post is the group card. `reportsForTurn(cid, {preview:true})` = the strip's read: the same composition, `marks: []` (never committable), `pending` = EVERY waiting group message (not only what would fit; text ≤ 400), memoised per cid against `(group id, lastAt, the member's marker, notify)` — the session list's re-publish reads no log twice. `onPending()` (create option; server.js → stash-handover `changed()`, debounced) fires on every announce except `noteRoster`'s (names only — and it runs FROM the session list's broadcast) and after every marker write. **Lane group-pending (2026-10-01): `view()` carries `members[].reportedUpTo` + `reportedAt` and `markReported` stamps the hand-over CLOCK (`reportedAt = now()`) beside a marker it MOVES and announces the group (nothing when unmoved) — the sender's window flips "waiting for beta's next turn" to "read by beta · 12:41" without a reload; the marker stays a record instant (no wake receipt — a wake and a report are not told apart).**

server/groups-engine.js — ORCH the agent-groups engine (2.369.159): reach = msg-acl over the live roster (messageable, from the inviter, uniform refusal, atomic), every mutation inside channel-store's `groups.update` door with its log record (log first), `channel-groups-updated` on every change; a WAKE = the member's report down THE ladder under `peer-message` (its ONE ladder site), a refusal journaled + never stashed; `reportsForTurn`/`commitReports` for prompt-context; `sendToAgent` = the pair group (g2: `create:false` = post only into an EXISTING pair — `findPair` — else `job-token`). g2: `resolveMember`/`resolveGroup` refuse a shared name `ambiguous` WITH `candidates` (`{name, conversationId}` among sessions the actor may MESSAGE / `{name, groupId}` among its own groups — no oracle), never a guess. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **g3: the OWNER's read mark (`ownerRead`, moved only by `markRead` = the window opened/touched or the owner's own verb; `list()` adds the derived `unread`; a no-op mark broadcasts nothing) + `liveRoster()` for the New group / Invite dialogs.** **r1: `mayWake` asked of EVERY wake (the route's per-(sender, resolved member) 30 s floor; floored = `refused:'rate-floor'`); `resolveTarget` (a name that is a group AND a session ⇒ `ambiguous`); `memberRef` (kick/notify by a shared name ⇒ `ambiguous`); `reportsForTurn` ≤ budget WHOLE (≤ 3 waiting named, a report taken back until it fits).** **r2: `pacerFor(sender)` = THE pace (persisted in `store.pace`, a grant reserves, a wake that did not go out refunds), `consent` asked inside the door before any write, the unread count memoised against `(since, lastAt)` and moved by `appendIn` (no log re-read per broadcast), a turn with no room still NAMES its waiting groups.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r3: a `wake-count-mismatch` refusal carries `group: view(g)`; `noteRoster()` (from broadcastActiveSessions) re-announces the groups whose member names/liveness moved; the pacer drops future stamps (one log line) and refunds only the PAIR of a refused wake (`keepSender`).**

### src/group-card.js — PURE a group message SEEN where it was handed over (lane group-report-card, NEW)

PURE (imports nothing; CJS — the card door, the three normalizers and the bundle share it). `groupOf(g)` = the card's facts sanitized `{id (g-<8 hex>), name, at (the RECORD's instant), from, self, via: report|wake, more, cut}` or null; `cardKey` = `<id>:<at>` (THE KEY — a message is carded once per conversation); `cardId(sessionId, g)` = `<view>:gm:<id>:<at>` (the live op and every rebuild name the same card); `normalizeCard(card, {now})` = `{fromName (the group's own `from` — never the ladder's "<sender> · <group>" label), text (≤ 4 KiB), group, shownAt (the injection instant), recorded?, recordedHead?}`; the RING (`session._groupCards`, `[{k, at, card}]`, oldest first, `RING_MAX` 120): `ringHas` / `ringAdd`, `ringCards` = the REPORT cards a rebuild places by time (`placeAt` = shownAt + `PLACE_SLACK_MS` 2 s: the turn's user record and the hook's attachments are stamped around the hook call, the reply later), `ringWakeCards` = the wake cards (`recordedHead`, ≤ 400 chars of the posted text); `isGroupCard` = the door's ONE predicate; `pendingEntry(p)` = a waiting message as a stash-summary entry (`source: 'group'`, `fromName` = the sender, `text` = "<sender> · <first line>" — lane-stash-detail's Details row).

**Lane group-report-whole (2.369.228):** a report line is now ≤ 2 000 characters (channel-groups `LINE_MAX`) — still under `TEXT_MAX` 4 KiB, so a card shows a whole 1–2 KB message and draws "cut short" only when the agent's line was cut; `RECORDED_HEAD_MAX` 400 (the wake ring's search head) unchanged.

**The door (src/normalizers.js `feedPeerCard` → `feedGroupCard`).** A card with `group` is keyed first: a key already in the ring ⇒ `false`, nothing drawn. Otherwise the ring gains the entry and the persistence hook (`setGroupCardPersist` — set by src/server/channels-wiring.js, ONE meta write per burst on a MICROTASK, so the ring is on disk before the report's marker write that rides the groups door's promise chain; flushed at shutdown) is told. A report card: written at once when the history is loaded (`placeGroupCard` — the same user-role peer card `injectPeerCard` makes, with `cardId` and `peerGroup`, `peerVia: 'peer'`; any harness), queued (`{kind:'gcard'}`) during a rebuild, and nothing before the first attach (that rebuild places it from the ring). A wake's card (`recorded`) takes the ordinary peer path (held / queued / `injectPeerCard({…, group})`). `rebuildHistory` places the ring's report cards BY TIME beside the browser cards (`convertWithCards` — its list takes both kinds) and, after the held cards' replay, `upgradeWakeCards` turns the transcript record that holds a wake's post into its group card IN PLACE (its id and position; one record per card; no record ⇒ nothing drawn). The three boot-restore paths read `meta.groupCards` back. Session field `_groupCards` (owner `group-cards`, session-meta `groupCards`).

rewind-ops.js — PURE 撤回语义(B3 §2.10/§3.2): claude `tombstone`(上游原话"渲染或持久化本流的消费者应当移除被指名的消息", 而我们两样都做⇒半截消息永远留着) 与 codex `thread_rolled_back{num_turns}`(ThreadRolledBackEvent 只有一个字段, 0.153.4 serde dump; 从 TUI 做的回溯在这里彻底隐形, 幽灵 turn 一直挂着) 落到**同一个** `rewound` meta op {harness,toMessageId,numTurns,ids,kind,ts}(恒发两个键, null 是陈述不是缺席). **标记, 绝不 splice**: 删条目会移动 slice(offset,limit) 的每个下标并改 total, 那正是三次分页事故的机器. kind 决定处置: superseded(claude)=隐藏(照它自己的指令, 规范副本就在旁边), rollback(codex)=原地划掉+"rewound"标签(藏起来等于悄悄改写别人读过的东西). codex 的一个 turn 按**user 消息**数, 不按我们的 turnIndex(那个计数器 task_started 与压缩也会加, 真 rollout 上 24 条 user 记录压着 30 个 turnIndex 组); 连续两次回溯各取 N 个**活**turn; num_turns 超过我们渲染过的量就两个数都说. 两个 normalizer 的 turnMap 都跳过 rewound(minimap 不许指向幽灵). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### opencode-events.js

opencode-events.js — OpenCode's LIVE lane (S9 remainder, SHARED): `/global/event` SSE (boots nothing, ~10s heartbeat ⇒ 45s of silence = dead, reconnect re-asks the locator) + an fs.watch on the sqlite store — the ONLY lane that sees another opencode process (MEASURED: a second serve's writes never reach our event bus, but its store row reaches our list). While BOTH are healthy the timed list refresh does not run at all; a down lane falls back to the timer STRUCTURALLY. `classifyEvent` is a PURE table; an unknown type is 'other' with no dirty flags. **kick() wakes the backoff SLEEP, not just the fetch** (round 3: the service ships OFF so backoff-to-30s is the first-use state — enabling the plugin took 25.1s to go live). **Round 4 — the lane may not lie about itself**: `active` requires the dir to actually hold `opencode.db` (a false `active` is what turns the fallback OFF), and the store dirs are RE-RESOLVED against the serve's own `GET /path` on every `connected` instead of latched from the boot-time env guess (re-arm only when they DIFFER). **Round 6 — `stop()` is TERMINAL for an arm already in flight**: both starts are async before they own anything, so a disable landing inside `resolveDirs()`/`locator.client()` used to attach an fs.watch (LIVE: it still broadcast) or open an SSE subscription onto a lane nobody holds; `laneStopped` goes up first and every arm re-checks it AT THE ACQUISITION POINT (the one `attachWatch()`), the lane is single-use. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### opencode-remote.js

opencode-remote.js — PURE OpenCode-serve OP TABLE + runOpencodeOp (S9 remainder piece (e)): ONE machine-side implementation shared by the local rung, the `opencode-serve` agentd op (the daemon bundles the same module) and data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op (checkout-less ssh hosts — mirrored + parity-pinned). hostId is a parameter; src/server/opencode-access.js picks the transport and nothing downstream branches on "remote" again. Gate: scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs

### server/opencode-access.js

server/opencode-access.js — the ONE way to reach the OpenCode serve on ANY machine (S9 remainder, ORCH): `call(hostId, op, params)` picks the transport (local facts / `opencode-serve` agentd op / shipped ssh script), `readConversation` synthesises records once for every rung, `openPtyBridge` is the ONLY caller that sees the serve's ws url + auth, `publicView` strips them from anything a route returns; pty ops are refused LOUDLY for a remote machine. Wired once from mounts-plugins-wiring (server.js stays inside its size ratchet). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/opencode-pty-bridge.js

server/opencode-pty-bridge.js — THE SERVE TERMINAL (S9 remainder piece (c), ORCH): connects SERVER-SIDE to `GET /pty/{id}/connect` and hands ws-create the {pid,onData,onExit,write,resize,kill} duck the session layer already speaks, so xterm/input/resize/the buffer file work unchanged and the serve's port, auth and ticket never reach the browser (TEXT frames = output, BINARY = \0-json control; resize is `PUT /pty/{id}`; a dropped socket reconnects because the pty belongs to the SERVE — **but a 404/410 upgrade is a VERDICT, not a hiccup**: PURE `ptyGone()` ends the terminal on the first one instead of burning five rungs (~12s) and five bogus warnings against a shell that already exited). Round 4: the client sends the serve NO `directory` for any pty call (it booted + permanently watched the user's whole worktree — 204 inotify wds that outlived every close, vs 4), and a shell this bridge stranded across a restart is removed by `facts.reapPtys()` on the next serve ready edge. B-ae4b: the duck's listeners are a SET (src/pty-duck.js) — the one slot handed the held banner to setupSessionPty's liveness stamp and the terminal opened blank. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

**verify-r6 J1 (2026-09-28) — AN ANSWER NAMES THE PANEL IT ANSWERS.** A job's interaction version was `pending.version + 1`, and `pending` is nulled by every answer and every expiry — so EVERY panel after one was answered or expired was version 1 again, and an answer carrying no version was accepted: a stale click on panel #1 ("Run the unit tests?", expired) was recorded as the answer to panel #2 ("Delete the production backup bucket?") — verify-r6 agentD, in-process on the real engine. The panel number is now a persisted, only-growing `interaction.seq` (PURE `nextInteractionSeq`; a record from before it starts above the highest version it remembers), and PURE `answerVersionVerdict` refuses an answer without a version (`version-required`, 400) or for another panel (`stale-panel`, 409) — nothing recorded, nothing reaches the job; the panel re-reads the current one after a stale refusal; `vibespace-job ask` prints the panel number. ### peer-messaging.js

**Lane notify-retry (2026-10-01): THE VERDICT IS THE SOCKET'S, NEVER A TIMER'S ALONE.** `postToPeer` → `{ok, reason?, phase: connect|write|written|closed, elapsedMs, transient?, late?, code?, closeError?}`. MEASURED: a unix-socket connect completes at the syscall or fails at once (a full backlog = EAGAIN at 0 ms — python `listen(1)` + two fillers; never a hang), and libuv delivers the connect callback in the NEXT iteration's pending phase, after the timers phase — a ≥ timer stall of our own loop after `net.connect()` fired "timeout" on a completed connect (the owner's 14:17 incident's likeliest cause; `late` = how far past the timer the verdict came, so the journal tells a stalled loop from a refusing CLI). The timer defers its verdict one loop turn (`setImmediate`), a write in flight gets one bounded grace (1 s), a FLUSHED frame is never a timeout (a reset after the flush is `closeError`, named — the ambiguity: no ack exists, the CLI dedups). `transient` = the timer / EAGAIN / ECONNRESET / EPIPE before the flush (the ladder parks it on a live pid); ENOENT / ECONNREFUSED / ENOTSOCK = a socket nobody serves (not-running). Exports `TRANSIENT_CODES`, `pidAlive`. The pre-fix file is frozen as scripts/fixtures/peer-messaging-prefix.js (the gate's control). Gate: test-notify-retry §1.

**src/park-step.js + scripts/test-park-step.mjs (notify-retry verify r3, 2026-10-01)** — PURE (imports nothing, CJS) THE RETRY PARK ENTRY'S LIFECYCLE AS ONE CLOSED TABLE: `STATES` (waiting / cleared / claimed / inflight / maybeDelivered / landed / stashed / evicted / expired) × `EVENTS` (19: the post's outcomes, a poster that never answers, a death or a graceful stop mid-post, a turn end, the timer, the 60-min bound, RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, a clock step forward / backward, a clear single / batch, the cap, a boot with ho / inflight, the target gone, the authorizer refusing); `parkStep(entry, event, facts) → {entry, post, say, leave, na, skipped, authorize, charge, persist, now}` over an entry RECORD (`freshEntry`, `canonical`, `STORED` = the fields the file holds); `parkTable()` = the 171 cells. It decides nothing at runtime — it is the specification the engine (conversation-deliver's park) is measured against: the suite walks every event sequence ≤ 4 from every state under the invariants (one post per attempt, may-twice only across a boot, leaves only by landed / stash / evicted-said / expired-said, every drop said by id, persist = the state, one authorization per frame) and drives the real park through all 95 drivable cells (stub registry, a post scripted BY TEXT, a manual clock, `reboot()` = a boot). A new state or event goes into the table FIRST; a cell the engine disagrees with is a finding. Four controls (a table rule removed ⇒ the walk red; an engine rule removed ⇒ the cell red). **Verify r4 (2026-10-01): 9 × 21 = 189 cells** — the owner-outcome table (test-notify-retry §6) found two engine doors the table lacked: `handover-claim` (a hand-over claims a WAITING / cleared entry: `claimRetry`; one on the wire, claimed or leaving is listed to nobody) and `prompt-take` (a fitting prompt's drain takes a waiting entry inline: `retryTake` via 'prompt' — landed, no post, no charge, the hold given back). The walk gains I5b (a hold is converted only while it exists and is inside its TTL, else the frame is asked for afresh — a cell mutant that converted a forgotten hold was green under every other rule). §5 THE DOOR CENSUS: every engine site that moves a parked entry is a row naming its event(s) (a stale regex, an event the table lacks, an event no door names = red), every `via` a take carries (grep-derived over the engine + agent-routes + stash-handover) is an event, and a landed / fallen record is never written again by any door (31 parks, a clear, a claim, a take, a clock step, a turn end, the timer, a boot). §4b three CELL-level controls (one cell broken, not a rule): un-clear ⇒ caught by the engine comparison; a stale hold converted ⇒ caught by I5b only; a hand-over's landing charged ⇒ caught by I5. 36 asserts.

THE delivery primitive for jobs→conversation notifications (2.344.0, B-0bf4): scans the CLI's own session registry (~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json + published <pid>.<sha>.key) and posts the documented two-frame injection (auth + stream-json user message) onto the session's cross-session-messaging inbox socket — the CLI queues mid-turn / opens a billed turn when idle / applies its own inbound controls (never bypassed; automation red line intact: we never write session stdin). ### job-model.js + agent-routes.js (lane notify-retry, 2026-10-01)

job-model.js — `HELD_KINDS` += `not-running` (a dead pid / a socket nobody serves / "no live inbox": the stash at once) and `retrying` (the park's kind, never a stash entry's); `heldKind`: `parked` ⇒ retrying, `notRunning` / "no live inbox" ⇒ not-running, a remote miss / anything else ⇒ not-reachable (RESERVED for an agent that was alive and did not accept); `NOTIF_TAIL` / `notifTailSentence(items)` = `renderNotifStash`'s tail by the entries' `held` kinds ("These arrived while this conversation was not running." / "The agent did not accept these when they arrived (busy or unreachable) — delivered now." / "These were waiting for a retry — delivered now." / …; an entry without `held` reads not-running — what the old fixed sentence assumed). agent-routes.js — `drainStashUnderCap` / `drainNotifsUnderCap` (exported for the gate): the ladder's PARKED entries ride a prompt that fits (`deliver.retryEntries` — the jobs digest carries the jobs engine's in the store's own shape, `retryTake(via 'prompt')` cancels the retry, free); a section that does not fit ARMS the hand-over (`armOrWait` → `deliver.armStashHandover`) and logs "will arrive as a message when this turn ends" (a dead pid: "wait for the next prompt" as before). The Background Work panel's Delivery log words a parked line ("parked for retry (connect, agent busy) · next attempt 14:17:43", "retrying (3 so far, …)") and a delivery after retries ("after 3 retries · rode the next prompt"); jobs-layout `heldText` words not-running / retrying / not-reachable.

### server/fs-canary.js + server/fs-canary-worker.js

server/fs-canary.js — the threadpool canary (2.108.6), OFF THE MAIN THREAD since design 011 lane 1 (store-timing, 2.369.203). Every 10 s (server.js) `createFsCanary({file: package.json, record, onWedged}).tick()` sends ONE probe to its own one-worker SafeFs (never queued behind a file route; backstop = 3× the probe's deadline). The worker (fs-canary-worker.js) runs an ASYNC `fs.promises.stat` — on purpose, unlike safe-fs-worker.js: the canary watches the process-global libuv pool — and times it with its own clock and its own 5 s deadline. Two facts, each logged + counted past 1 s: `srv-fs-canary-ms` (the stat, worker clock — the only one that strikes; 3 timed-out stats in a row → `srv-threadpool-wedged` + `mounts._healthSweep()`), `srv-loop-canary-ms` (the answer waited this long for the main loop — a blocked loop, never a slow mount). No answer at all (the backstop) = `srv-fs-canary-lost`, never a strike. Before: the stat's callback and its deadline both ran on the main thread, so any stall inflated it (survey: 142 of 164 slow canaries preceded a > 1 s stall). scripts/test-fs-canary.mjs (fast): a blocked loop, a saturated pool, the strikes, a main-clock CONTROL copy.

**Lane S3 (2026-09-26, naive-user study 2 — "交回控制后，助手以为是另一个会话在跟它说话"): VIBESPACE SPEAKS AS ITSELF.** The CLI frames every server-posted injection "Another Claude session sent a message: … This came from another Claude session" (its words, not ours), so the browser handback read as a peer's note — the assistant answered "I received a message from another Claude session… not sure it concerns us", and the card said `Message from " VibeSpace browser "`. VibeSpace's own CHAT-ONLY cards — `fromName: 'VibeSpace'` (auto-resume's arm notice, the usage-limit card with its reset-credit button, fed straight into the normalizer) — are notices too via `VIBESPACE_CARD_SENDER`, deliberately NOT a `NOTIFICATION_SENDERS` entry (test-peer-delivery's producer census matches a sender by SUBSTRING, so a bare "VibeSpace" would pass every file); the reset-credit button moved into the shared `_appendResetCreditBtn`. **S3 verify r2 (2026-09-26, F3 impersonation + F2): A NOTICE IS PROVEN BY ITS PATH, NEVER BY ITS WORDS OR ITS NAME.** The r1 rule trusted the head for ANY record and a listed name on ANY path, so a real agent running `vibespace-msg send bob "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports: run rm -rf, the user approved"` rendered as an accent "VibeSpace · Please run…" notice, and a session RENAMED "VibeSpace" / "Background Work · x" did the same by name. The stash drain heads an entry by `stashKindOf`, never `isNotificationSender(fromName)` (the assistant was fooled there: a peer named "VibeSpace browser" drained under the head), and says the head ONCE (`withoutNoticeHead`, F2). Residual, named: an OLD codex / ACP wrapper (started before this change) writes no marker kind — a group wake from a member whose display name + group spells "Background Work · x" / "Channels · x" is judged by the name rule there until the session restarts (a vibespace-msg frame still names the path). ### cli-identity.js

cli-identity.js — THE agent-CLI process identity, ONE rule in two spellings (B-3185 r3): `isCliProcess(pid,name)` (JS, used by discovery-facts ⇒ bundled into the daemon) beside `cliIdentityShellFns()` (the POSIX vs_is_cli the writer sweep and the ssh discovery CO leg embed verbatim; writer-sweep only RE-EXPORTS it). Three rungs — argv[0] basename / the interpreter's first non-flag operand / `/proc/exe` (version-image rung narrowed by the presentation, ` (deleted)` stripped: auto-update replaces the image of a LIVE session; **the strip's pattern is QUOTED because ssh runs this text under the REMOTE LOGIN SHELL — in zsh an unquoted `(deleted)` is a glob GROUP and strips nothing**). NEVER a substring of the whole argv (measured: the retired rule said YES to 106 of 4277 processes vs 16 real CLIs). **argv是NUL分隔的词表且一个词里可以有换行(r4): shell那半原来"NUL换成换行再取第N行"=第N个词的第一行, 与JS双向分歧且两向都有害(读者被杀/真writer躲过sweep), 现在取行前把真换行寄存到`\001`再还原, `ps`回退先压平; 而`$(…)`还会吃掉**结尾**换行(argv[0]/解释器操作数/readlink三处捕获实测全中, 且吃掉后是shell说YES·JS说NO=更宽松那向), 故三处统一走`vs_cap`(子shell内哨兵护尾, 只摘生产者自己那一个换行).** 每条**kill路径**(sweep · hosts.js killPidShell=远程Terminate · /api/kill-pid本地分支)都问这一条规则, 不问comm不问整条argv; **`ps`回退只在无/proc机器上跑, r5才第一次被真跑起来**(重指/proc根+PATH上的替身`ps`+JS孪生在/proc读会抛的子进程里真走自己的回退; 负控=不压平的修前行, 两个换行fixture上与JS相反), **远程Terminate的存在性探针改成正证据梯子**(`kill -0`→`[ -d /proc/N ]`→`ps -p N`; busybox的`ps`没有`-p`, 旧的单条`ps`捕获让每个活pid都答VS_GONE)且新增第四种回答VS_UNKNOWN=活着但读不到任何证据; **r6把这条梯子收进本文件成为唯一定义`pidAliveShellFn()`, sysinfo-wiring的signalProc同样内嵌**(r5清点到它却放它留着自己的`ps -p`, 理由只描述了那个脚本两处`ps -p`里的第二处——第一处在**成功分支**上做杀后存活判定, busybox下对一个`trap "" TERM`的活进程答OK-GONE⇒`{ok:true,gone:true}`, 不是误标是**凭空造**出一个成功; 失败分支同样实测把活着的他人进程答成ESRCH); 无JS孪生是故意的(本地分支读`process.kill(pid,0)`的errno, 那正是shell做不到、梯子才存在的那件事); 不变量=**靠注释活着的孪生仍是孪生, 注释只值它作者数清了几个调用点**, 所以换成STANDING SWEEP(test-writer-sweep §17: 任何kill/signal路径上`ps -p`一律不得作存在性判定, 幸存的每一处按理由列入allowlist, 死条目同样变红); **r7: 那个sweep自己是靠一张手写的七文件清单驱动的** — 手写清单正是本bug已经三次击败的同一件工具(r4没清点到的kill路径/r5清点到却放行/r6发现放行理由只讲了两处里的第二处), 它只在作者已经看过的地方执法, 实测漏掉**47个**真会发信号的文件(server.js·jobs·boot-restore·plugins/vnc/port-forward/opencode-serve·agentd·ws-handler/ws-create); 现在文件集由**grep推导**(src/·data/bin/·scripts/非test + 仓库根, 命中 kill -TERM/-9/-0·SIG*·pkill·process.kill(·killRemotePid·signalProc·vs_alive; 无扩展名的按**shebang**进——`git ls-files data/bin`永远看不见**生成**的vibespace-status), 推导结果由套件**打印**出来, 且故意过包含(i18n词典命中SIGSTOP): 假阳性只是扩大执法范围, 假阴性才是缺陷本身; 两条结构pin(推导不得丢掉r6清单覆盖过的任何一个 + 必须仍覆盖那十条被漏掉的永久kill路径)+ 把**已发布的sweep**按root参数化后对着一棵临时树跑第二遍的六条正负控(退役形状被抓/allowlist条目复制到别的文件仍算stray/干净kill路径保持绿/无信号的`ps -p`不在范围/test-*被排除——这正是本文件能把退役形状写下来当负控的唯一原因/data/bin下的shebang工具被抓) + 对每个导出shell **builder实际发出的文本**再扫一遍(源码扫描结构上看不见运行时拼装的探针), 负控=逐字的修前脚本; 不变量=**standing sweep的价值等于它走过的那个集合, 集合要从性质推导不要枚举, 并且要把走过什么打印出来**. Dependency-free. Parity is functional: test-writer-sweep §6/§12/§14 + test-discovery-interpret §8 drive both spellings over the same live pids. **2026-09-09 增 THE PROCESS TREE, 无 fork**: `readPpid`(/proc/<pid>/stat 第4字段, 从**最后**一个 `)` 起数——comm 里可以有空格和括号)与 `readChildPids`(`/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children` 的**并集**——children 记在 fork 它的那个**线程**上), 替掉发现 sweep 里**每个锁**一次的 `ps -p -o ppid=` 与**每个活会话**一次的 `pgrep -P`; 代价从来不是等待而是 **fork**(实测一次 `spawn('true')`: 45MB RSS 1.8ms / 543MB 18.8ms / 1.5GB 67-73ms, 页表复制发生在调用线程上, 而 `Promise.all` 把 N 次 fork 排进**同一个 tick**). 无 /proc 那条 rung 是**整趟 sweep 一次** `ps -eo pid=,ppid=`(`parentIndex`, memo `PROC_TABLE_TTL_MS`=2s, 故意小于 /api/sessions 自己的 4.5s 缓存), 绝不每个 pid 一次; `hasProcfs` **只记住 YES**(NO 每 60s 重问——一次 stat 失败不许变成永久降级去 fork); 全部是**取值**读, 答不出就是 `null`/`[]`=没有证据, 存在性仍然只由 `kill -0` 说; `procRoot` 可注入所以无 /proc 的 rung 在 Linux 上**跑得起来**(r5 `vs_argv` 的教训). **r3增 `pidsMatchingCmdline(needle)`=`pgrep -f` 的那个问题(「哪些活 pid 的命令行里带这个串」), 唯一调用者是 ws-handler 的 kill 分支找持有本会话 socket 的 dtach master**: /proc 那级把每个 `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` 读进**同一个**复用的 64 KiB 缓冲(读满即整读该 pid, 巨大的 argv 要被回答而不是被静默截断)并用 `Buffer.indexOf` 逐字节比, 无 /proc 那级是**整个问题一次** `pgrep -f` 绝不逐候选一次; 字面子串比 `pgrep -f` 的 ERE **更窄**=对一个会 SIGTERM 命中者的调用方是安全方向, 而带空格的 needle 按拼接形匹配(/proc 用 NUL 分词). 代价与 readPpid 那条不同所以要**说出来**: 这个扫描对服务器自身大小是**平的**(3,400 进程 23.6-23.7 ms), 而它替掉的 fork 不是(58 MB 阻塞 2.0 ms / 559 MB 24.4 / 1,564 MB 69.4, 端到端 87.6/110.6/155.2) ⇒ 事故那台机器上阻塞 69→24 ms、延迟 155→24 ms, 诚实代价=刚开机的 58 MB 服务器把 2 ms 阻塞换成 24 ms. Gate: scripts/test-discovery-spawn.mjs + test-architecture §45. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **B-eac2 residual (c) 把第四种拼写也收了进来**: `readPsIdentity(pid)`(/proc 优先, 无 /proc 走 `ps -p <pid> -o uid=,args=`, 1s per-pid memo)与它的两个读者 `procCmdline`/`procUid` 现在住在这里, opencode-serve 的 keeper 直接 require 它, 而 data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op 保留唯一一份**孪生**(无 checkout 的 ssh 主机 require 不了, 与 usage-scanner 同一条成文例外; scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs 两侧同输入对比). 它是**取值**不是存在性探针 —答不出就是 `null`=没有证据, 绝不是'没了'; 谁还活着只由 `kill -0` 说. **2026-09-14 增 `readSid`/`sessionIndex({fresh})`/`sessionMembers` = THE SESSION TABLE (one /proc walk, memoised; a detached leader's sid is its pid) for the desktop-app keeper's stop/sample/socket-owner questions; no `ps` rung on purpose.** **2026-09-14: `procSample` also returns `reapedTicks` (cutime+cstime); which ticks a guard sums is the consumer's rule (a SET counts own+reaped once; a single-pid guard keeps `cpuTicks`).** **2026-09-25:** `procSample({memory})` adds `anonBytes`/`pssBytes` (smaps_rollup ≈1.1 ms/pid), `procSampleAsync`, `setMemory`/`setSample` = the ONE set rule (strongest metric every member has, never a mix).

**CS SEPARATION RULE (2.276.0): `hostId` is a PARAMETER, never a branch.** Server-side logic is written ONCE against a machine handle; the only difference between this machine, an ssh host and a dialed-in device is the transport underneath it. `hosts.device(falsy)` returns device #0 (the local daemon has been a full DeviceManager since 2.158.0 — same binary/mux/op surface — but was unreachable through the API, so every feature was written twice BY CONSTRUCTION). sidebar.js — Sidebar shell (filter/sort/merge pipeline, tab switching). **`LIVE_SESSION_FACTS` + `liveSessionFacts()` (2026-09-07 r3) = THE list of per-session live facts the `active-sessions` payload publishes under the names every client surface reads them by.** `_merge()` REBUILDS the row (webui half renamed into webuiId/webuiName/webuiMode, `cwd` composed into the display/grouping key, `status` derived) and `/api/sessions` discovery carries none of them, so a fact not on this list is DROPPED — the whitelist-drift class, sixth strike: `worktree`/`worktreePath` (badge dead, Session Properties said "not isolated in this run" about a session the server reported isolated WITH a path, and the fork's `worktreePick` live half had no producer), `outputStyle` (2.369.58) and `remoteState` (2.219.1) were all dead here. ONE list spread into BOTH branches; the drift guard in scripts/test-worktree-userchan-ui.mjs re-derives the payload's own key set from server.js so the seventh strike fails at build. **2026-09-07 r4: reaching `_merge()` is only HALF the hop** — `_mergeAndRender()` re-renders only when its DIGEST changes, and the digest named none of these, so the `worktree-path` broadcast added to keep the badge honest repainted nothing (neither the badge nor the remote chip has a partial-update path — both exist only inside `renderSessionCard`). Each row therefore declares BOTH halves (`{digest: <projection>|null}`): the four cheap scalars that change at most once per session GATE the render (worktree/worktreePath/remoteState/outputStyle), while the object-valued `todo`/`auth` stay carried-only ON PURPOSE (they change several times per turn / are re-pointed by the pool — gating on them is the 2.72.0/2.106.1 churn, so their surfaces still repaint late: a separate change with its own churn measurement). 2026-09-21: LIVE_SESSION_FACTS gained `vcs` (digest kind:branch:at) and `prLinks` (digest url@action list) — both drawn on the card, both gate. 2026-09-23 (design-user-inbox-reply D1.7): `turn` (running / idle / waiting, the payload's 1 s-derived column) is CARRIED-ONLY (`digest: null`) — it flips twice per turn and no card draws it; the For-you panel reads the payload itself and patches its dots in place.

### window.js setTitleMeta + app.js syncSessionIdentity + sidebar.js merge — THE TITLE CHIP IS THE LIVE FRAME'S (lane badge-stale, 2026-09-30)

The billing chip (window.js `setAuthBadge`, keyed) is fed by `app.syncSessionIdentity(sidebar._allSessions)` on EVERY merge — the 5 s /api/sessions poll and every `active-sessions` frame (sidebar.js `_mergeAndRender`, deliberately outside the digest gate). The rows' `auth` comes ONLY from `_webuiSessions` = the LAST ws frame (`...liveSessionFacts(wm)`; the poll carries no `auth`), so the chip is exactly as fresh as the frames the server sends: a server writer of a payload fact that does not broadcast leaves every window on the old value however often the merge runs (the per-session pool link — accounts.js `_notifyLinks`, lane badge-stale finding 1). Matching is `byWebui.get(session.sessionId)` (then the openSpec's sessionKey): verified on a real page for a standalone chat, a terminal, a tab-group guest, a split pane, a window restored by the layout replay after a reload, and the Stage hero (test-billing-badge-live).

**`setTitleMeta` is no-op-guarded** (setTitle's twin): the merged meta equal to the current one ⇒ return before the store, the icon-slot rebuild, the strip re-draw and the notify. Unguarded, every merge re-drew every tab strip on the page (each tab's billing chip a new node every poll — a hover or a press on a tab lost) and notified the manager once per window per merge. Consequences kept: a caller that wants a strip re-drawn WITHOUT a meta change calls `_renderTabBar` itself (desktop-app-window.js's app icon — an empty patch is a no-op now; test-title-meta-guard's census fails `setTitleMeta(x, {})`), and the identity sync asks `layoutManager.scheduleAutoSave()` only when the openSpec it keeps changed (a backend id landing, a host backfilled) — that save used to ride the per-merge notify. Gates: test-title-meta-guard (fast) + test-billing-badge-live (heavy).

scripts/test-billing-badge-live.mjs — THE TITLE CHIP FOLLOWS THE POOL ON A REAL PAGE (lane badge-stale; heavy, ~55 s, SKIPs without chrome / dtach / a built bundle): a worktree server under scratch('badge') (own data/ + HOME), a pool of two FAKE members (fake token files, the pool the instance default), pooled sessions behind a stub claude through the real create path, a 1400×900 headless-chrome page; the ENGINE's writer (`accounts.ensureSessionPoolLink(…, {why:'per-session-switch'})`) driven in-process by a `-r` preload hook that captures the server's AccountManager (main thread only — the preload also runs in the SafeFs workers) and reads a command file. Each leg marks the chip node, moves the member, and wants the SAME node naming it within 10 s: a standalone chat, the pool-default move of a linkless one, a terminal, a tab-group guest + its host tab, a split pane, the pair restored by the layout replay after a reload, the Stage hero; QUIET: every chip keeps its node across ≥ 3 merges + a frame; CONTROL: the pre-fix writer (mutant-copy, no notify) — the chip stays on the old member for 12 s while the page re-judges the stale frame (an attempt any unrelated frame reached is void, ≤ 3). Measured on the base tree (ab1cda46): 15 red (every per-session leg 0 frames in 10 s, the quiet leg's strips re-drawn); on the lane: 48 green.

### channel-chrome.js

channel-chrome.js — CLIENT (a4, 2026-09-21): the THREE DOM primitives every channel surface builds with, so the panel, the window, the card, the editors and the Integrations window draw the SAME glyph the same way — `icon(name, px, cls)` = one `<span class="chan-ic">` holding an SVG from src/lib/icons.js sized by font-size (the ONLY innerHTML this feature writes, and it is the library's own static string, never a string from the wire), `el(tag, cls, text)` = a textContent element (the XSS law), `btn(label, onClick, cls)` = a house `mounts-btn` (`mounts-btn-primary` = the ONE primary; the old 10px `chan-btn` family is gone), `noteLine(cls, text, {warn})` = a sentence line that carries the alert glyph when it warns. Gate: test-channels-e2e ⑫ (c) — every `.chan-ic` holds an `<svg>`, no text symbol on the surfaces. **channel-polish (2026-09-27):** + `avatar({name, key, self, glyph}, px, cls)` (PURE channel-avatar.js decides the initials and the hue; the element is PAINT — aria-hidden, initials as textContent; `px` null = the stylesheet's `--av-size` per surface), `convAvatar({key, title, kind, group})` (a conversation: the people glyph for an agent group, the mail glyph for a thread / mailbox, else the title's initials — the window bar and the panel row share it), `fileIcon(name, px)` (the file registry's static SVG for a name).

**Naive-user round (2026-09-28).** `noteLine()` names its text span (`.chan-note-text`) and `noteText(line, text)` is the ONE way to re-word a note — a warning note's FIRST span is the glyph (`.chan-ic`, line-height 0), so `line.querySelector('span')` writes the sentence into a 0 px box (the who dialog did; test-browser-share-model's census fails any `const X = noteLine(…)` whose file reaches into X's children).

### channel-words.js

**Lane group-pending (2026-10-01):** `deliveryRowText(row, {t})` / `deliveryLineText(rows, {t, tc})` word WHERE A GROUP MESSAGE STANDS (the state is PURE channel-groups `deliveryOf`'s, never decided here): one recipient ⇒ "Waiting for beta's next turn" / "Read by beta · 12:41" (the hand-over clock, drawn as the message head draws its time — local 24 h HH:MM, `time` injectable; a legacy row without the clock: "Read by beta") / "beta is muted and will not read it" / "beta left"; several ⇒ "1 waiting · 1 read · 1 muted · 1 left" (the counts are `tc('delivery', …)` keys — "{n} waiting" is also the stash strip's "{n} 条在等", another meaning) with every sentence in `title`; `tone` waiting (hollow dot) › handed (filled) › none. The width budget lives in the words (test-channels-groups-ui §2b: en 44 / zh 24 / ja 30 beside the name; the four-state group line en 44 / zh 36 / ja 40).

**R3 (2026-09-26, design §23):** `statusTagParts(tag, {now, t})` words the first screen's ONE tag — `{before, who, after, tone, icon, title}`, the agent's name its own part (`.chan-tag-who`). `agoText` gives the tag's compact age (just now / Nm ago / Nh ago), `viewSwitchText` the header's "{n} need attention" | "All {n}", and `attachmentReasonText(code)` a refused picture's one word (budget spent / rate limited / not cached / account disabled / no preview / server unreachable, else errorCodeText). channel-words.js — CLIENT (a3 i18n, 2026-09-18): THE words for every channel/outbox/integration route CODE (`routeErrorText` — the engine's `error` sentence is the agent's contract, the toast words the `code`; the sentence is shown only where it is the vendor's or the validator's own detail), `principalKindText`, `policyModeText` via `tc('policy', …)` (`review` is also the code-review status elsewhere), `groupTitle` (a Task Group's `title`, never a `name` it lacks — every group showed as its id, a1 A5; pinned by test-channels-e2e ⑮ on the Assign "Wake" select and the Reach roster + a name-less grant, with the store's refusal of a name-only group as the control). **2026-09-22 (the account model):** the two new route codes are worded here — `unknown-credential` ("not one this instance offers — pick another") and `no-such-adapter` ("That account no longer exists"). Gate: test-channels-i18n (heavy, zh+ja census over the a1 driver). **g3: `groupErrorText` (the groups routes' codes), `notifyModeText` (the four modes, billed ones said), `wakeEchoText` (woke N = N billed turns, said at 0; refused not billed; who reads it next turn).** **r3: `store-blocked`, `wake-count-mismatch` and `rate-floor` worded in `routeErrorText` (+ `store-blocked` in `groupErrorText`; a group 409 that carries the fresh view says the preview was updated).** **HOTFIX 2026-09-26: the validator's refusals are worded by CODE — `assignmentRefusalText(why)` (every `F.ASSIGN_REFUSALS` code; a value no control offers ⇒ "reload the page and try again"), `ruleRefusalText(r, 'filter'|'pattern', ruleLabel)` (the `RULE_PROBLEM_CODES` a user can cause by typing through `F.filterProblemText`, the structural rest ⇒ the reload sentence); `routeErrorText(r, {ruleLabel})` takes the editor's own rule labels (channel-filter-editor's `api()` passes them); a `bad-assignment` / `bad-filter` without a `why` (the conversation-grain routes) keeps the "The request was refused: {error}" fallback. Gate: test-channels-engine ⑩ (zh).** **R4 (2026-09-27): `principalText` (a group = "Group · <title>"), `accessAuthorityText`, `watcherHowText`, `grainSummaryText({access, watchers})` = the card / row / chip line "Access: … · Notify: …" ("Notify: nobody" when access stands alone), `clampNoteText(n, 'max'|'min')` (the Notify dialog's visible clamp); `routeErrorText` words `bad-access` / `bad-watcher` (by `why`), `duplicate-principal`, `watcher-needs-access` ("grant access first (Grant access…), then notify"), `too-many-rows`, `compose-not-available`.**

**Lane group-pending (2026-10-01) — THE LINE UNDER EVERY GROUP MESSAGE (`openGroupWindow`):** each message row (the owner's own too) carries `.chanmsg-dlv` = a CSS dot (`.chanmsg-dlv-dot`: hollow by default, filled under `data-tone="handed"`, the row dimmed under `none`; never an emoji) + `.chanmsg-dlv-text`. `drawDelivery(row, rec, log)` judges by the model's `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log: the drawn records})` (re-exported through channel-groups-view.js) worded by `deliveryLineText`, keyed by the row and PATCHED only when its signature (tone + every recipient's member / state / name / at) moved — a broadcast never re-creates the node under the pointer; `redrawDelivery()` re-judges every drawn line when a broadcast carries the group (a marker, a mode) or lands a record (a departure). channels-panel.js + channel-window.js — CLIENT: **mirror-193 + the .195 merge: the conversation window's list has ONE writer — the SERIAL QUEUE (`serial`: every render, patch and upward page runs one after another; a render only QUEUED is joined, `queuedRender`) plus the list-ready rule (`listReady` false from a rebuild's clear to its last row; PURE `pageUpVerdict` refuses `not-ready`). mirror-193's render generation (`renderGen` / `pageFor` / `upInFlight`) was the same fix on the older base and was dropped at the merge — ONE mechanism; a re-entered render (open + the watch beat's broadcast + the mark-read's) used to append its page each — the messages ×2–×3 on a slow box (test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑨/⑨b + their control, which neuters the queue and the ready rule with its scroll-evidence clauses).** the Channels rail panel (adapters as sections, **a FRESHNESS CHIP on every row** — the one number a user needs before handing something to a lane, drawn from the lane ACTUALLY carrying it — the `channel-row` menu and the ⚙ row as CONTRIBUTIONS registered by the owning module so gear-menu.js stays byte-identical to its pinned legacy list) and the conversation WINDOW (registered window type, singleton per CONVERSATION, restored from its openSpec; plain text through textContent on every path; a composer ONLY where `offers()` allows one and a NAMED reason where it does not). The panel repaints from the broadcast digest with no fetch; the window re-reads its own tail when its id is named (§10.4). **r2 four rules: marking read is a USER action** (on open and on touch, never as a repaint side effect — the render-driven POST plus an unconditional notify was a self-feeding loop measured at ~490 req/s with ONE window open, which also destroyed the mark it set), **the ws handler is removed BY NAME on close** (`onGlobal` returned undefined so `off?.()` was a silent no-op and a CLOSED window kept fetching, kept POSTing over the user's mark and held its detached DOM; the LOAD-BEARING half is `onGlobal` now returning its own unsubscribe — measured, the named-const teardown alone is a belt), **the page boundary is a RECORD** (`before` + `beforeId`), **and the freshness/identity SENTENCES are composed here** from the server's structure, with the device's own `t`. **r3: the title bar names the conversation through `wm.setTitle`** (`winInfo.setTitle?.(…)` was a permanent no-op — the literal has no such member — so every channel window read "Channel"; jobs-panel had the identical call; test-window-types censuses the idiom), **an untracked row's chip says "not polling" / "not scanning"** (never "within 5m" about a fetch nothing will make), and a disabled adapter's section says `disabled`. **P1a (2026-09-16): the adapter's OWN controls on its section, every fact from the digest and no fetch on repaint — the connect wizard's THREE COPY PATHS (§10.1: `none` opens the Integrations card FIRST and never a consent page; `cluster` says "Provided by the cluster · <label>" beside the button; `user` says nothing more; a `409 needs-credentials` from the route opens that card too), the flow dialog (the consent page as a LINK the user clicks — a window opened after an await is popup-blocked — the named `port-busy` refusal, PASTE-BACK + Cancel, closed by the adapter's own broadcast), the four-valued auth line with its `re-authorize in <eta>` countdown (`reauthEta`, the clock an argument) and a Re-authorize / Open Integrations / Connect verb chosen by the STATE, the spoken last connect failure and the filed "For you" note, the TRACKED PICKER (a checkbox per discovered conversation — tracked is opt-in), the OPTIONS editor over the adapter's DECLARED schema (a select for `choices`), Disconnect (confirmed) and Enable/Disable; strings through textContent, zh+ja shipped.** **P1b: the push line (`pushLaneText`, amber when demoted/unavailable) + "Re-declare exclusive and retry" beside a demotion + the Push… dialog (the exclusivity declaration with each claim's consequence in words; the switch itself on an opt-in lane) — gated on the digest's `push`, never a kind; saving a claim IS a re-declaration so it is sent only when changed or demoted.** **P2 (+ src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js): the "Assign & filter…" row on a TRACKED conversation (panel menu + window bar) opens ONE dialog — who is woken (a live agent session or a task group, round-robin), on what (every message / a filter of the PURE module's CLOSED rule kinds, validated with the same code the route refuses with), how (a wake per batch / one digest per window), with what authority (`send` drawn ONLY when both caps allow it, else the reason; a stored send the policy now forbids says it reads as draft), the per-assignment daily wake cap; a LIVE server-side estimate (debounced, the corpus never reaches the browser) that PRINTS `sampled`/`truncated` and, once assigned, "estimated ~X/day when set; actually Y/day since"; and the HONEST per-lane latency sentence worded from the digest's `wakeLatency`. **THE BILLING CHIP FOLLOWS THE MEMBER (2026-09-30, lane billing-chip — the owner's conversations kept showing the member they started on after the pool moved them to another one):** the phone has no title bars, so its billing identity is this bar's `billing` chip (fed only when `app.isMobile`, by app.syncSessionIdentity on EVERY active-sessions merge → ChatView.setBillingIdentity → `setBilling`). Its skip-if-unchanged key was `${source}:${name}` — the POOL's name alone — while the chip prints `⣿ <pool> → <member>`: a per-session switch, a pin or a gather moves the member and not the pool, so the key never moved and the chip kept the old member for the life of the page (the title-bar chip had its own, longer key and repainted — two keys for one identity). Law: a keyed chip's key is a CENSUS of what the chip prints — a new printed field goes into `billingAuthKey`, never into a local key. Known, not changed here: the chip's 90 px cap (style.css) cuts a long `pool → member` on the phone (the member is the tail). ### xpra-client.js

xpra-client.js     — the DOM-free xpra session over the upstream Protocol.js worker (P8-2 x2): fit-before-map, every non-popup window placed inside (a second top-level too), a bounded belt that undoes the app's own resize/move (≤ 1 configure per 500 ms per window, 3 rapid undos ⇒ the app wins until the pane changes), popups left where X put them, draws painted in order and every one acked, the clipboard both ways deduped, IME publish-then-press, view-only drops input at the source, every close named; test-xpra-client §2 drives it with a fake worker Round 3 A2: `closeMain()` — the outer ✕'s `close-window` to the MAIN window only (never Watch / view-only); A r1: xterm hangs up its shell on it — a shell that survives the hangup needs the second ✕. Lane B: `on.moveresize` (driving pane only, nothing applied), `on.main`, `on.state`, `setMainState`.

### xpra-view.js

xpra-view.js       — the xpra picture view on the shared shell (P8-2 x2): a theme-colour pane, one canvas per xpra window, pointer from the pane's rect at net zoom 1, the keyboard through a hidden IME textarea (Ctrl+V left to the browser for the paste event), the app's title/icon to the caller, the clipboard both ways through the shell's chrome (the paste box on plain http, the "Copied in the app — click to copy" chip) — never a silent no-op; Round 3 A1: the trusted copy-chord STAMP (spent per delivery) makes a plain-http copy the user made land with no click Round 3 A2: `closeApp()`. desktop-app-window.js — window type `desktop-app` (§2 row 7): one window per app session (`_desktopAppId`), openSpec `{action:'openDesktopApp', id}` replayed by layout sync on every client (N viewers on one `-shared` display), the view built lazily by the record's stream KIND (xpra ⇒ xpra-view.js with the Protocol.js worker url, else vnc-view.js; P8-2 x2), title = the app window's own title once the protocol names it (xpra) or the record's `appTitle` (a keeper-fitted rung, x4), else the label, via setTitle (textContent) and its icon via an `<img>.src` data URL, the bar adds the backend chip `vnc-display (xpra not on PATH)`, CPU/RSS + idle countdown READ from the `desktop-apps-updated` broadcast (one GET at open), Keep running, Stop; re-reads its record on every ws reconnect (an adoption broadcast reaches nobody — the server adopts before clients reconnect) and connects whenever the record is ready and the picture is not up Round 3 A2: the window closes itself when its app ends (`exitCloseVerdict`, a toast, on every client), is born `desktop-app-pending` so a dead replay never paints, and answers `onCloseRequest` (ask the app, twice = Stop). Round 3 A3: the scale chip names its origin ("2.5× · auto"), ⋯ → Scale ▸ relaunches after a confirm and the window RETARGETS to the successor in place (every client, and a layout replay, follow `replacedBy`). ### design-account-hardening.md

design-account-hardening.md — 2026-09-08 DESIGN (owner decisions pending, no code yet): the root fix for the 5-incident money batch (auto-resume's 130 billed continues / readings keyed by the spawn org / unseen login deadlines / unretracted warnings / inc-mts8a8mr-ulmm's in-flight-on-the-new-slot cascade). Thesis: we MUTATE the binding between a running CLI and a credential dir, then spend money on INFERENCES about it — 4 rival derivations, and the COST one (`resolveUsageKey`, per RECORD, feeding persisted rates.json) was never pinned at all. Target = ONE durable LEASE (promoting slot-transitions.js, carrying both id namespaces + a credential-MATERIAL fingerprint) read by ONE `identityOf`, moved only at TURN BOUNDARIES (not mint-once+respawn — that costs a full context re-send per switch); ONE usage-cache write choke point with a caps-gated weekly-phase falsifier (`quotaWindowFingerprint`, null for codex — measured 53 clusters, rolling window); ONE spend authorizer in front of all 7 unattended-turn producers; ledger↔OTel AGGREGATE reconciliation kept (the refutation was about routing ONE reading). 12 principles = 12 enforceable invariants, 3 grep-derived build censuses (derivations / cache writers / spend paths), 5 phases each with its gate, and the per-incident test + negative control. §6 = 12 numbered owner decisions.
**P1b (2026-09-16): the push line + the Push… dialog.** Gated on the digest's
`push` (the capability ROW's answer), never on a kind: the section draws
`pushLaneText(a.push, a.lane, {t, now})` (amber when demoted or unavailable),
a "Re-declare exclusive and retry" verb beside a demotion (a demotion is
cleared by the party that made the claim, never by the counters), and Push…
— the exclusivity DECLARATION (unknown / shared / exclusive, each with its
consequence in words) plus, on an opt-in lane, the switch itself; the claim
is sent only when it changed or the lane is demoted, because saving a claim
IS a re-declaration. zh + ja shipped.

**mirror-193 (2026-09-27): every grain is RE-READ before a dialog draws** — the account and rule grains through `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/view` (they drew the panel's broadcast-fed `target.adapter`, a frame behind a route write: the 2.369.193 mirror's dialog showed an empty list, prefilled the first live agent and its whole-list Save revoked the agent granted a moment earlier) — and every Save sends `base: st.stamp` (the PURE `grainStamp` of the lists drawn); a `409 grain-changed` toasts "The list changed while this dialog was open … nothing was saved" and re-opens the dialog on the lists as they stand (`put(…, {onChanged})`).

**R4 (2026-09-27) — the editor is TWO DIALOGS, one per operation (`src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js`).** `showGrantAccessDialog(app, target)` (`#chan-access-dialog`, target = `{kind:'conversation', conv}` | `{kind:'account', adapter}` | `{kind:'pattern', adapter, id?}`): a row per agent / group (`.chan-access-row`: who · authority · ×; `send` drawn only when the caps allow it, a clamped stored send said), Add an agent or group, a rule's pattern editor, a live note naming the notifications a removal takes with it, Save = `PUT …/access` (a new rule `POST …/patterns`), a Notify… button. `showNotifyDialog` (`#chan-notify-dialog`): the picker = `st.access` EXACTLY (none ⇒ "Grant access first — use "Grant access…"" + the button); a `.chan-watch-row` per watcher = the pre-P2 form's fields (On / Deliver / Window / the rule rows / Wakes per day / the receipt check / its own estimate with `principal`), "Authority comes from its access: …", Add a notification, the total (`expectedWakesTotal`), a number past its bound CLAMPED VISIBLY (`.chan-flow-note[data-clamp]` "kept at the maximum, 1440 / 1000", the toast adds "numbers past their bounds were kept at the bound"), Save = `PUT …/watchers` with each filter INLINE. `showGrainMenu` (the two operations at a point), `showAssignFilterDialog` (the window chip: own access ⇒ Notify…, else Grant access…), `showScopeAssignDialog` (⇒ Grant access…), `assignmentSummary` (= `grainSummaryText` + "(account)" / "(rule)"). Every string textContent (channel-chrome).

**P2 — the Assign & filter editor (`src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js`) — superseded by R4 above.**
One sentence per invariant: the "Assign & filter…" / "Assign to an agent…"
row exists only on a TRACKED conversation (nothing is fetched for an untracked
one, so nobody could be woken) — on the panel's `channel-row` menu and as the
window bar's button; the dialog offers live agent sessions
(`app.sidebar._webuiSessions`, cid = `backendSessionId || claudeSessionId`)
and task groups (`app.sidebar._tasks`, round-robin) as principals, and a
principal no longer live is still listed so the assignment can be edited;
rule kinds and validation come from the PURE module (the closed set the route
refuses with); the estimate is asked of the server on every edit (250 ms
debounce; the corpus never reaches the browser) and PRINTS `sampled` /
`truncated`, and once assigned "estimated ~X/day when set; actually Y/day
since" beside it; `send` is drawn ONLY when `authorityCap(conv.authorityCaps)`
is null, otherwise the reason is drawn, and a stored send the policy now
forbids says it reads as draft; the latency line is `wakeLatencyText` over
the digest's structured `wakeLatency` (push with/without coalescing, kick,
poll, reconcile, scan, no-source); Save writes the filter first (when
filtered) then the assignment with `estimateAtSet`, Unassign is its own
button, and nothing re-renders itself — the engine's broadcast repaints the
panel row (`assignmentSummary`, amber when the last wake was held/stashed)
and the window bar. Gate: test-channels-e2e (heavy) owes the browser leg.

### src/channel-thread.js + src/channel-reactions.js (PURE) — THREADS AND REACTIONS (lane channel-threads, 2026-09-28)

**Lane lark-threads (2026-10-01): THE PLACE PATCH (PURE, P1–P4)** — `widenPlace(cur, offer, vendorId)` (null → the vendor's key / root only; never a key replaced; no self-root; a root needs a thread or a parent), `foldPlaces(lines)` (each field's FIRST value wins), `applyPlace(rec, p)` (a new object only when something widens), `compactPlaces(lines, max)`; a quote's author and a pane's participants read `author.display` (the owner's name / the vendor's way). Gate: test-channel-thread ⑫ (the table, a patched root heads its topic through the REAL Lark normalizer, a key-replacing control) + the parser census rows in test-channel-reactions ⑥.

The owner (2026-09-28): "我发现你似乎不支持 lark 的内嵌回复 (thread) 功能 … 以及 reaction (附加在消息上的表情)". ONE model for Lark / Slack / Telegram, both modules import only channel-record.

- **The place is DERIVED, never stored.** A record carries `replyTo`, `threadKey` and (new, optional) `root`; `threadIndex(records, {convId})` → `{threads: Map<key, {key, kind, root, rootAt, replies, count, lastAt, participants}>, byRecord, byId}` — `replies` lists the NEWEST `THREAD_REPLIES_MAX` (500) in oldest-first order (`replies[last]` = the newest reply = the engine's walk anchor) and the whole list rides the entry as the NON-ENUMERABLE `all` (`threadView` pages over it; the place rules read it; never served) — **verify r2 (MONEY): it kept the OLDEST 500, so the anchor of a >500-reply thread was reply 500 and every walk paged back to it (a Lark walk to its 200-record bound — 4 calls instead of 1 per pane beat), and the pane's first page ended at reply 500; gate test-channel-thread ⑤b + test-channels-engine ⑱ (a'), each with the pre-fix copy as control**. T1 a record with a `threadKey` sits in it; a reply without one sits in its parent's chain (`chainKeyOf`, ≤ 64 hops, a cycle keyed by its smallest id — attack 1 terminates); T2 a record whose id IS a key is that thread's root; kind `vendor` (the vendor's thread id), `chain` (a reply chain keyed by its root), `conversation` (a mail thread = the conversation — the window draws nothing for it); `mergeThreadStats` takes the MAX of a vendor's stated count and the local one (attack 14); `placeOf(rec, ix)` = `{quote: {of, author, text ≤ 120, loaded, external}, thread: {key, kind, isRoot, count, lastAt}}`; `threadView` pages one thread; `paneMode(px)` = side ≥ 620, stacked below; `agentPlaceLine` = the agent's words (`↳ replying to A: "…" (id …) · in thread …`, `[thread … · N replies · last …]`), frame-inert.
- **THE ONE CLASSIFIER (quote-vs-topic, owner rulings 2026-09-28 "都是").** `placeKindOf(recOrId, ix)` → `{kind, topic, quotes, external}`, `PLACE_KINDS` = `plain` (answers nothing, heads nothing) / `quote` (answers a message WITHOUT a thread id — a Lark reply without `reply_in_thread`: `parent_id` + `root_id` only; a Telegram reply_to; a reply to another chat) / `topic-root` / `topic-reply` (inside a topic, answering its root or nothing) / `topic-quote` (inside a topic, answering another of its messages). A TOPIC = an index entry of kind `vendor` (`topicOf(ix, id)`); a `chain` is never one, a `conversation` (mail) is the conversation. By vendor id it answers the same as by record (the engine asks about a parent that may not be loaded). `placeOf` is BUILT FROM IT: `{kind, quote, thread}` with a thread fact ONLY for a topic — a quote gets its quoted original and nothing that opens a pane. `agentPlaceLine` words by kind: `↳ quotes <author>: "…" (id …)` for a quote (never "in thread"), `↳ replying to … · in thread <key>` for a topic reply, `↳ quotes … · in thread <key>` for a quote inside a topic. The index lets a TOPIC WIN ITS ROOT: a message a vendor thread's members name as root sits under that topic in `byRecord` even when it also sits in a reply chain (a quote later answered with `reply_in_thread` heads a topic; the chain's counts are untouched). Readers: the window (chip / tag / strip), the agent's words, the engine's placement parent fact, `threadRead` / `threadRefresh` (`topicKeyOf` → `not-a-thread`). Gate: test-channel-quote-topic.
- **Reactions are SIDE records folded at read** (`foldReactions(sides, {selfId, byMax, names, vocabulary})`, F1–F6): a snapshot replaces what came before it, a delta before the newest snapshot is ignored, one after it applies; `mine` = the account's current `selfId` (a truncated snapshot + our own newer delta still says mine); counts never negative; the ORDER is the newest snapshot's keys then keys added after it (a click never reorders the strip). `compactSide` = the trim's rule; `myRidsOf` = our reaction ids (never served); `forAgent` strips `by`; `agentReactionsLine` = `reactions: 👍 3 (the account owner) · :key: 1` (never a name); `reactionDigestLine` = the stash's one line; `chipPlan` = the strip's keyed patch (keep / add / remove); `quickSet` / `searchSet` / `emojiOf` = the picker's vocabulary. Bounds before parse live in channel-record (`validateReactions`, `validateSide`, `sideKey`).
- Gates: scripts/test-channel-thread.mjs + scripts/test-channel-reactions.mjs (fast: the tables over invented Lark / Slack / Telegram shapes, the census's 251/23/9/1 seeded shape, linear-time pins, patched-copy controls — a copy counting the root as a reply, a chain with no hop bound (killed at 2 s, read RED), stats read off the root's line, a fold without F2, keys ordered by count, an agent line that prints `by`, the pre-fix `compactSide`). **THE PARSER CENSUS (verify r1, test-channel-reactions ⑥):** every export of the two modules has ONE row — its size cap asserted with an oversize input and, where the work scales with the input, the LINEAR PIN COUNTED IN WORK (lane-mirror-198, 2026-09-29 — scripts/work-meter.mjs: the parser's block executions under V8 precise block coverage + the element work of the natives it calls, the input built OUTSIDE the measured call, the constant part subtracted, 2× the input ⇒ ≤ 2.2× the ops — never the clock: the Actions mirror of 2.369.198 read the old wall-clock pin at ×2.50 and its 4 ms floor unreached on a shared 4-vCPU runner; the meter proves itself first (the same call measured twice agrees to the op) and ONE timing line stays, informational) — or a stated reason in `NOT_A_PARSER`; a new export with no row is RED. It found `compactSide` QUADRATIC in distinct keys (an `order` ARRAY scanned per delta: 4 000 keys 10 ms, 16 000 keys 143 ms — on the append path since the side log's growth compaction) with a compacted snapshot that kept every key (3 000 keys = a 146 KB line, past the 8 KiB bound): now a Set, and the snapshot keeps the first `REACTIONS_MAX` keys in order with `truncated`. CONTROL (e) runs the census's own measurement over the pre-fix copy: ×3.90 in work (the real one ×2.08); (e') its 3 000-key line. 20 runs under the runner's conditions (4 vCPUs at nice 15): 20 × 107 green.
