### src/lib/channel-thread-pane.js + src/lib/reaction-picker.js (CLIENT)

- **channel-thread-pane.js**: `quoteLine` (quote-vs-topic: a `quote` / `topic-quote` place says "quoting a message not loaded / in another chat", `data-place-kind` = the classifier's kind), `threadChip` + `inThreadTag` drawn ONLY for a topic kind (`isTopicPlace(place)` — the server's `placeKindOf` word, never "has a thread fact"; a quote gets no chip, no tag, no pane) (+ `threadChipText`, re-spelled in place by a `threads` broadcast), the pane title `tc('channel', 'Thread')` (话题 / スレッド — collab-row's Codex "Thread" keeps its own word), and `createThreadPane(host, ctx)` — ONE pane per window (another thread replaces its content; each thread keeps its scroll, draft and reply target in a Map), never persisted. Open = the local fold (`GET …/thread/:msg`) then ONE walk where replies are listed separately (`POST …/refresh`, floored server-side; a refusal is said in the pane, never a spinner), re-walked every 60 s while open. Its composer sends `{inThread:true, replyTo}` (the root, or a reply picked through the row's hover bar — `pick(rec)`, lane reaction-hover; the old per-row ↩ button is gone) — direct or as a proposal by the conversation's own composer mode — and keeps the draft on a refusal (`topic-forbidden` redraws the foot as the read-only line). Its upward page goes through the window's PURE `pageUpVerdict` (a scroll event is displacement; the person's input is intent). Esc / Back / ✕ close it; focus returns to the chip WITHOUT scrolling the list (`preventScroll` — a Back keeps the reading position; the chrome leg measures the first row's offset). A successful send clears EVERY box of that thread (a broadcast that redrew the foot mid-send had made a new box from the draft — the sent text came back; found by the chrome leg's screenshot).
- **reaction-picker.js**: the strip (`renderReactionStrip` / `patchReactionStrip` — chips keyed by `data-key`, a count re-spelled, a new key appended; a message with NO reaction has NO strip and the last reaction gone takes the strip with it — lane reaction-hover moved adding into the message's hover bar, so no line is reserved; the glyph is CONTENT: text, OUR `…/emoji/<key>` picture as `img.src`, else `:key:`), `toggleReaction` (the route's folded answer flips the chip — never optimistic, never retried), `refaceStrips` (a chip drawn as `:key:` before the vocabulary loaded gets its glyph / picture in place when the window's `emoji-set` arrives — the server's first fold after a boot runs before its set is cached), the who-list popover on a right click / long press, and `openReactionPicker` (createPopover: the quick row, a search box, a keyed grid of the keys the set lists; arrows + Enter) — opened from the bar's Add reaction (anchored under its button) or the phone's long-press menu.
- Gate: scripts/test-channel-threads-ui.mjs (heavy: **⑥'s control is FONT-INDEPENDENT (lane-mirror-197, 2026-09-29):** its premise — "the one-line ja composer text is wider than its box at 360 px" — is a fact about the font, and the Actions runner has no CJK family (DejaVu's fallback boxes are narrower than the glyphs a ja user sees), so there the line FIT and the pre-fix nowrap rule had nothing to cut (`cutNow:false`, red on both attempts, reproduced here under a DejaVu-only fontconfig); the control now measures the one-line width under the injected pre-fix rule and, where the line fits its box, narrows the box BY CONSTRUCTION to 60 % of that width and judges the RULE there — pre-fix cut (`cutNow`), the product rule whole (`wholeAtBox`) because it wrapped (`wrapped`) — and its sentence says which world it judged; the runner also gets `fonts-noto-cjk` now (ci.yml, heavy job, with the reason). Rule: a control's premise is measured, never assumed from the glyphs of the box it was written on; the brief's legs a–h in chrome over the fake adapter + one disabled Lark room; (q) quote-vs-topic: the Lark room's quote draws its strip and no tag, what it quotes no chip, a strip click flashes the parent and opens no pane, the topic keeps tag / chip / pane titled 话题, no 线程 in the zh window); the custom-emoji picture route is in test-vendor-whitelist §7 beside the attachment census (on demand, cache first, budget charged, + a control).

### src/channel-facts.js (PURE) + src/lib/channel-facts-view.js (CLIENT) — A MESSAGE'S FACTS (lanes message-facts + message-facts-lark, B-f066, 2026-10-03)

The owner: "gmail thread 展示的时候缺乏细节（收件人，cc，reply-to）… 不同 provider 可能针对消息都有类似的独特机制，怎么制定统一方案处理". Design 007 (docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §30).

- **The schema lives beside the record** (src/channel-record.js): `facts: [{k, v, more?, cut?}]`, optional; SEVEN closed value types `FACT_TYPES` (parties · party · time · line · level · count · flag); `FACT_SCHEMA` = the closed kinds (each a type, a level's words, `nameless: true` = a `party` row that may say THAT without naming WHO — `v: {}`); `validateFacts` refuses by name (`unknown-kind`, `bad-value`, `duplicate-kind`, `too-many`), every string through `peerName`, ≤ 50 parties then `more`, ≤ 16 KB. A record without facts is byte-identical. A fact learned later = the side kind `fx` (validated, folded at read by `foldFacts`: per kind the later wins, a flag never un-happens; compacted by the store's trim).
- **The table** (`FACT_KINDS`, this module): one row per kind — type, `label` (an English dictionary key), `where` (`summary` / `chip` / `details`, `detail: true` = a chip that is also a details row), `mutable`, `agent` (`line` / `count` / `none`), chip words (`chipWords` per level, `chipWord` with `{v}`, `chipBare` for a nameless party). The suite holds FACT_KINDS ⇔ FACT_SCHEMA (same kinds, same order) and every word in zh/ja. Rows nobody emits are NOT declared (the dead-row rule; the paper test prints Slack / Telegram / Outlook's).
- **Who emits what** (`caps.facts`, validated at registration; the contract suite holds every emit to it): Gmail — to, cc, bcc (own SENT mail only), reply-to, sender, list, delivered-to, subject, importance, automated (`factsFromHeaders` at ingest; `factsOf` = one metadata read of a stored thread on a person's Details click). Lark — via (the app, `sender_type: app`), forwarded-from (a merged forward, nameless), edited (`updated` at `update_time`), recalled (`deleted`), all chips, emitted by `toRecord` (module-private `factsOfItem`); no `factsOf`. lark.js `recordView` renames the via party with the head when an app's name is learned later (through `validateFacts`).
- **Printers (by VALUE TYPE, never a kind):** `summaryOf` (the one-line button: "to me, Alice +3 · cc Carol"), `chipsOf` (a time chip hands its instant to the view, which words it in the title), `detailRows`, `mapFactStrings` (the engine's belt door `agentFacts`), `agentFactLines` (the agent's ONE line; a nameless party / a flag = the bare key; under `inertFrameLine`). A peer's name holding our separators (`, " < > · +N`) is RFC-5322-quoted (verify r1 F1).
- **The view** draws by type with textContent only: the summary toggle (open state in `folds`), the chips (chips-only facts go beside the time — `chanmsg-facts-inline`), the details `dl` ("+N" expands in place), a "Details" ask on a record stored before its facts (only where `factsOf` exists).
- Gates: scripts/test-channel-facts.mjs (fast: §1 table ⇔ schema ⇔ words + the V7 censuses — no kind or adapter id named in the view / table / engine section; §5 the paper test; §6 Gmail; §7 the contract; §8 the backfill route; §9 verify r1; §10 Lark — emitted ⊆ declared over every recorded Lark item with a red control, the name door with a red control, late fx), test-channels-gmail-shape, test-channels-lark-shape ⑤c, test-channel-record (the name-site census: a new `name: String(` in a channels file needs a SITES row), test-peer-text-census (doors agentFacts / agentFactLines, row m.factsText), heavy test-channel-window-render ⑬ (a mail thread) + ⑬b (a Lark room's chips).

- **THE SENDER'S ADDRESS (lane channel-window-tidy, 2.369.204 — the owner: "email thread里还是没有展示每条消息的metadata（cc，收件人，发件人具体地址啥的）"):** the head shows the author's NAME only (its title never carried the address), so the From address lived nowhere on the page. `detailRows(facts, t, {from})` puts the record's AUTHOR first — `{k: 'from', label: 'From', values: ["Name · address"]}` ("me · address" for the account's own; the address once when it is the name) — not a fact kind (every record has an author; nothing is stored). The view passes `fromOf(rec)` (the vendor's name, never the owner's alias) to `detailsList` (and through its "+N"); channel-window.js keeps `row._author` so a row filled by another row's Details ask names its sender too. Every party of the details is "Name · address" on the page; the summary's tooltip is no longer the only place an address lives. Gates: test-channel-facts (the judge + a patched-copy control with no From row), test-channel-window-render ⑬ / ⑥b.

### src/lib/msg-bar-model.js (PURE) + src/lib/channel-msg-bar.js (CLIENT) — THE MESSAGE ACTION BAR (lane reaction-hover, 2026-10-01)

The owner: "这个加表情的加号太丑了。做成 lark 官方那种鼠标指上去才会在消息的右侧出现，不改变上下布局关系。" + "把 reply in thread，quote 也都放在鼠标悬浮按钮里". Before: every message wore a strip line holding a boxed `+` (even with no reaction), the pane's replies an absolutely-placed ↩, the group window's rows a TEXT "⋯"; the main list had no human door to a quote or to a new thread at all.

- **PURE `msgBarActions({sys, cleared, group, inPane, place, conv, composer})`** = the row's actions in the ONE closed order `react · thread · quote · more`: `react` ⇔ `offers.react.offered`; `thread` ⇔ `offers.threadReply.offered` and the channel declares `thread` (unknown placements ⇒ the offer stands); `quote` ⇔ declared `quote` (known placements only — the view's `threads.placements`, PURE `placementsOf` on the server) + a composer that can send (`direct` | `propose`) + NOT inside a topic (`inTopic` = the ONE classifier's `topic-*` kind — the engine's PL5 would refuse it) + never in the pane; a system line / a cleared message none; a group row `more`. `barKey` = what a re-sync depends on (offers, placements, composer, the read-note title); `barKeyStep` = the toolbar's ← → Home End (wrapping), every other key not the bar's.
- **CLIENT `renderMsgBar(acts)`** = a `role=toolbar` div, one `.chanmsg-bar-btn[data-act]` per action (the library SVG through `icon()` — `emojiAdd` / `thread` / `quote` / `more`, never a text glyph; `title` + `aria-label`), ONE tab stop (the first button; arrows move it); a press stops at the button. `syncMsgBar(row, acts)` patches a drawn bar IN PLACE (same ids ⇒ words re-spelled; other ids ⇒ the buttons replaced in the kept bar; none ⇒ removed). `holdBarOpen(button, pop)` keeps `.open` while a popover it opened is up and gives the keyboard back to the button when that popover closes with the focus inside it (Esc). `msgActionMenu` = the same actions as a context menu.
- **CSS (the overlay):** `.chanmsg-bar` is `position:absolute; right:6px; top:var(--chanmsg-line-mid, 11px); translateY(-50%)` — its middle on the first line, z-index 2, `--bg-dialog` + border + `--radius` + a small shadow; hidden = `opacity:0; pointer-events:none` (inherited — the press reaches the message); shown on `.chanmsg:hover > .chanmsg-bar`, `.chanmsg-bar:has(:focus-visible)` (a mouse click leaves no stuck bar) and `.chanmsg-bar.open`. **Never drawn on a TOUCH device = `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)`** — `hover: none` alone matched headless Chrome (and a pen) on a fine pointer, where the bar is the only door (the first chrome run read every button at a 0×0 rect: the product's old ⋯ rule already said "and coarse").

### src/agent-env.js (PURE)

THE SPAWN-ENV SANITIZER, one rule for two processes (2026-09-14, the P0b
round-1 verifier's HIGH). `agentEnv(base, {keep})` drops every `VIBESPACE_*`
not in the keep set (secrets + server config), every `npm_*` (nested-npm
hazard) and `AGENT_ENV_DROP` (PORT/HOST/NODE_ENV/NODE_OPTIONS + the ambient
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` pair); `daemonEnv(base)` is the same rule with
`DAEMON_ENV_KEEP` = `AGENT_ENV_KEEP` ∪ the two names the daemon tier itself
reads (`VIBESPACE_NODE_MODULES`, `VIBESPACE_AGENTD_VERSION`) — DERIVED from
the daemon tier's own `process.env.VIBESPACE_*` reads and pinned that way by
test-agentd-session, never typed from memory. Imports nothing, reads no
process: `src/ws-handler.js` re-exports it as the `agentEnv` every spawn site
already requires from there (with its `process.env` default), and the daemon
bundles it. **Why two processes**: the daemon is a SECOND HOLDER of the
server env — `DeviceManager._spawnLocal` spawned it with `{...process.env}`
and `agentd.spawnEnv()` laid the server's sanitized session env OVER the
daemon's raw `process.env`, so every daemon child (a pipe-session claude, an
`open-session` pty, `run-cmd`) inherited whatever the daemon was born with;
measured by the verifier on a worktree server with `agentd.localPipeSessions:
true`: a real `claude` CLI whose /proc/<pid>/environ carried the full 40-char
cluster integration secret, handed down by a daemon spawned by a PREVIOUS
server life (the daemon survives restarts by design, so a WITHDRAWN cluster
default kept flowing into new sessions), plus the drive presets. §14.11.1's
"by construction cannot reach any agent child" was true of the dtach path
only. Now a daemon is born sanitized at all THREE birth sites (`_spawnLocal`,
the `--stdio` bridge's spawn, the upgrade re-exec — the one moment a RUNNING
daemon's environ can be cleaned; honest count: the re-exec that INSTALLS
this bundle is run by the OLDER daemon's code with the raw env, so a daemon
born under an older build is cleaned at the FOLLOWING re-exec or a restart)
and `spawnEnv()` sanitizes its BASE on every child spawn regardless — so a
daemon's CHILDREN are protected from the moment this bundle runs, whatever
the daemon itself still holds; HOME/USER/LANG/PATH from the daemon's own environment
survive, because remote daemons run under launchd/systemd with an env the
server never sees. Gates: test-agentd-session (a real daemon born from the
real `_spawnLocal` under the secret — daemon environ clean, a pty child AND a
pipe-session child see 0 secret lines with a canary proving the read; a
daemon spawned BY HAND holding the secret — the previous-life shape — whose
children still see nothing; the PRE-FIX bundle, `...process.env` as the base,
handing it straight down as the control that makes the leg red-capable; the
keep-set derivation; the three wiring pins) + test-integration-registry §6(h)
(the HOLDERS census: no `env: process.env` / `env: { ...process.env` literal
in src/agentd/{client,agentd}.js, with both retired spellings as controls) +
test-architecture (PURE set).

**Lane app-system-env (2.369.211):** `VIBESPACE_APP_SYSTEM` stays OUT of both keep sets — the chart's app-system switch is a fact about the server process; `src/app-system-serve.js` reads it from `process.env` beside the sanitized env it is handed (test-agent-env pins the strip).

### src/secret-box.js (SHARED)

THE ONE at-rest encryption primitive, N key files (design §14.7, decision 24).
`secretBox(keyFile)` is a factory: mounts keeps `data/.mounts-key`
byte-for-byte, the integrations store gets `data/.integrations-key`, the
channels token store (P1) gets `data/.channels-key`. A key file is a
per-STORE blast radius — moving one is an irreversible data-loss path, and a
corrupted or rotated key must never take a second store with it. The
ciphertext is BYTE-IDENTICAL to mounts' former inline `_enc`/`_dec`
(aes-256-gcm, `iv.tag.data` as three base64 segments): test-secret-box's
PARITY leg encrypts with a patched copy of the pre-fix bytes and decrypts with
the box, and the reverse, so nothing an older build stored needs re-encrypting.

**THE DEFECT IT MUST NOT INHERIT (read off `src/mounts.js:360-367`, not
assumed):** mounts' `_key()` wrapped `readFileSync` in a BARE catch and minted
a fresh key on ANY read failure — right for exactly one errno, ENOENT; for
EACCES, EMFILE, EIO, a truncated or emptied file it OVERWROTE the key and
every stored ciphertext became undecryptable for ever, silently. Hidden only
because the file is 0600, owned by the service and rarely read; fd
exhaustion, a read-only mount or a crash mid-write all reach it. The box
creates the key ONLY on ENOENT; every other errno is a TYPED `SecretBoxError`
(`key-unreadable` / `key-malformed` — a 64-hex check, because an emptied file
is NOT a fresh key / `bad-ciphertext`) that a caller renders as "the key file
could not be read", the OPPOSITE sentence from "nothing configured"; it writes
tmp + `link(2)` (EEXIST refuses to clobber, so two minters land on ONE key)
with a rename-into-absence fallback, 0600, and never overwrites an existing
key file. The standing negative control is the bare-catch copy itself: on an
injected EACCES it mints, and the old ciphertext stops decrypting.
**`describeJsonError(e)` (r2, 2026-09-14)** lives here because it is the same
discipline one layer up: V8's `SyntaxError.message` quotes the source around
the error position, so logging `e.message` for a mistyped secret-bearing JSON
env printed the tail of the secret (six characters of a 40-char cluster key,
where masking permits four); the helper answers the class + the position
when V8 states one and never a quoted fragment, and BOTH readers of such an
env (the integrations store's cluster block and `MountManager.drivePresets`'
OAuth client presets) log it. Gate: scripts/test-secret-box.mjs (40; ⑦ = the
retired `e.message` carrying the tail as the control).

### src/integration-registry.js (PURE)

**2.369.195: `oauthClientVendorOf(row)`** — whose OAuth clients a `bindsPerAccount` row signs in with, DERIVED (never a second declaration): `delegate.to === 'drive-presets'` ⇒ `'google'` (Gmail uses the storage mounts' Google clients — that is why it delegates), else `null` (Lark's own app). The channels engine asks it before borrowing a storage mount's client (design-integrations-per-account §2.7).

### src/server/cluster-presets.js (ORCH) + src/preset-layers.js (PURE) — company presets from ONE cluster Secret, mounted and watched (lane cluster-presets, 2.369.200, B-53fe)

**Why.** A company preset (Google OAuth clients, a Lark app, a browser key) was an env var read at boot and written per helm release: a rotation = a helm upgrade + a pod roll per user, a release without the block silently had none (a fleet user). Now the chart mounts ONE namespace-wide Secret (`vibespace-cluster-presets`) into every pod plus the release's own Secret as the per-key override, and the server watches the directory. Rule for any new cluster-provided config: a mounted file that can change, never an env var.

**src/server/cluster-presets.js — THE reader of the presets directory.** `resolveDir(env, {useDefault})`: `VIBESPACE_PRESETS_DIR` (set + empty = off) else `/etc/vibespace/presets` when it is a directory — the default counts ONLY for the server (`installForServer`); `sharedPresets()` made lazily in any other process reads only an explicit directory (a suite on a fleet pod never inherits the company's presets behind its env). Layout: `integrations.json` + `gdrive-clients.json` (cluster) and `override/…` (release). `create({dir, log, now, pollMs, debounceMs})`: a SYNC boot read (the kubelet's tmpfs, a few KiB, `stat` size ≤ `MAX_BYTES` 1 MiB before any read — a network directory here would put a sync read on the boot path, so the directory must be local) and one boot line (`[presets] <dir>: integrations N|absent, Google clients N|absent`); `start()` = `fs.watch(dir, {persistent:false})` (the kubelet's atomic `..data` rename; never a subPath — those never update) + a `pollMs` (30 s) STAT-SIGNATURE poll (`readlink ..data` + ino/size/mtime of the four files — a missed event, a plain directory's in-place `override/` edit), debounced 300 ms, `reload()` SINGLE-FLIGHT (a request during a run runs ONCE more after it). A reload reads only when the signature moved, and THE READ IS KEYED ON THE TREE IT READ (verify r1 ①, reproduced): a `..data` swap landing BETWEEN two slot reads made a snapshot with one file from the old tree and one from the new — published to every listener with a "changed" line, corrected by the next event (two notices for one edit) — so the signature is taken AGAIN after the reads; moved ⇒ the tree now seen is read instead (≤ `RE_READS` 3, then left to the next event / poll); nothing torn is ever published. A file in the directory (or override/) the reader does not know — a self-hosting typo, a key a newer chart projects first — is SAID once per set by name (`[presets] <dir>: ignored browser-keys.json — the files read are …`), never ignored in silence (the "future key" cell). Each file → `judge`: absent ⇒ that layer `null`; not-a-file / too-large / unreadable / unparseable (`describeJsonError` — the position, never a byte) / not-an-array ⇒ the slot KEEPS its previous list, the line said ONCE per transition (`… — keeping the previous presets` | `… — no presets from it until it is fixed`; `reads again` when it recovers), `status().errors[{layer, file, code, kept}]`. Only a DIFFERENT merged result replaces the snapshot — different VALUES or a different LAYER supplying a key (B-8145, 2.369.203: an override equal to the cluster's entry removed moves the key to the cluster with no value changing; the snapshot used to stay, so `/api/integrations` `presets.groups` kept saying "release" after the override was gone; `attributionOf(merged)` = the sorted `layerOf` pairs, compared beside the values). ONE journal line naming keys, only when a value moved (`[presets] changed (<dir>): Google clients: added org2; rotated org1 · integrations: removed lark/other · …now from / no longer in the presets directory`); listeners run with `{kinds, sources, prev, at}` — `kinds` = the kinds whose values moved (the integration store re-derives its cards only then), `sources` = the kinds whose attribution moved; `kinds` empty = only readability or a layer moved (the summary must still say it). `entries(kind)` = merged COPIES or `null` (the directory says nothing ⇒ the caller's env fallback); a present `[]` is an answer. `status()` = `{dir, items:[{kind, source, n}], updatedAt (newest file mtime, rounded), loadedAt, errors, present}` — value-free. `stop()` ends watch, poll and debounce. `setSharedPresets(inst)` for suites. Requires PURE preset-layers + secret-box's `describeJsonError`.

**src/preset-layers.js (PURE; imports only the PURE registry for a row's label; CJS so the server and the bundle share it; in test-architecture's PURE set).** `parseIntegrations` / `parseDriveClients` = the env readers' rules moved verbatim (throw on a non-array). `mergeLayers(kind, {cluster, release})` = the PER-KEY merge (identity: integrations row id + preset key, Google the key; a release entry replaces the cluster's in place, new ones append; within a layer the first of a key wins; both absent ⇒ `null`) → `{entries, layerOf}`. `diffEntries` / `diffEmpty` / `diffWords` (added / removed / rotated / relabeled BY NAME — values compared, never printed). `summarize` (groups by source cluster → release → env, zero counts dropped, errors `{layer, file, code, kept}`), `countItems`, `itemWords` ("3 Google clients", "1 Lark app", "<row label> key"), `presetsLine(summary, {t, ago, now})` → `{text, none, errors}` — the Integrations window's line ("Company presets: … — from the cluster, updated 2 min ago" / "… — from this release's own values" / "… — from the environment (a restart is needed to change them)" / "Company presets: none — ask your admin.").

**The chart (deploy/helm/vibespace-user, P2).** `presets.volume` (default true): a read-only projected volume at `presets.mountPath` from two `secret` sources, BOTH `optional: true` (no `defaultMode` — the kubelet's 0644 with the pod's `fsGroup: 1000`; the pod's only non-root principal is uid 1000 = the app = every agent session, which also holds NOPASSWD sudo and could read the server's env under the env form — the exposure is the same; verify r1 ②) — `presets.clusterSecret` and the release's OVERRIDE Secret `<release>-preset-override` (keys `gdriveClients` / `integrations` → the cluster files / `override/…`); no preset env with the volume (only `VIBESPACE_PRESETS_DIR`). `presets.override` (else the legacy `gdrive.clients` / `integrations`; the legacy single client → one `default` entry) fills the override Secret, rendered with `data:` (b64enc), NEVER `stringData:` (B-8145, 2.369.203): helm's 3-way merge nulls a dropped key IN THE FIELD the old manifest named it in, and `stringData` is write-only (folded into `data`, never stored) — so a key dropped from a stringData Secret stays in `data` for good (a test release kept its `gdriveClients` copy after `gdrive.clients: []`, and the per-key override shadowed the cluster's later rotation). The chart owns every key of that Secret (`data: {}` with no block). Suffix `-preset-override`, not `-presets`: a user named `cluster` would otherwise name the default cluster Secret. Under the volume form the release Secret carries no preset key; a release switched by the 2.369.200 chart keeps its stringData leftovers there, unread (deploy/README: list the key names, `kubectl patch … remove`), and its pod rolls once on the upgrade (the override source is a new Secret). The item list never depends on the values ⇒ the Deployment renders identical with or without an override ⇒ an override change is a Secret-only upgrade, no roll. `presets.volume=false` = the env form, byte-identical to 2.369.199. Kubelet: syncFrequency 1 m + Watch on the fleet (read-only `configz`, 2026-10-01) ⇒ "within ~2 min"; edit-to-swap unmeasured (no user pod mounted a Secret, no Secret edited by the lane).

**Gates.** test-cluster-presets (fast, 220 — §1 PURE + §2 the reader + §3 THE LAYER TABLE of verify r1: 36 file cells = {present, absent, unreadable (a 000 file; skipped as root, said), malformed, empty value, not an array} cluster × release over both keys ⇒ the effective preset per key, the typed error rows + ONE line each, the words, and never a value in any line / status / summary; the env cells and "the user's own key wins" AT THE CONSUMERS (`MountManager._driveClient` yields to a record's own client id — the connect path's `if (!cid)` is the wiring pin — and the REAL store's resolve with a saved key); a future key said by name; a swap mid-read never torn; the watch refused (EMFILE) ⇒ the poll carries; 40 swaps ⇒ one notice. Controls, one per rule: a whole-file override, the layers in the wrong order, a failure path dropping the previous presets, `e.message` in the line (V8 quotes the 10 bytes before a JSON error), no post-read re-check (a torn snapshot IS published), the stray line muted, `_driveClient` without the own-client rule, no poll behind a refused watch), test-integrations-store (fast, 29), test-mounts-oauth (fast, 17), test-helm-render (HEAVY — `helm` is a real external program — `reads` the chart, 19; controls: subPath, a required source, an env beside the volume; SKIPs loudly without helm; the byte comparison SKIPs on a shallow clone), test-integration-registry §6 (a″) the file-rung census (the directory env + default path + file name in CODE only in the reader, the chart template and named suites; comment lines stripped; planted offenders as controls).

**Next candidates for the same rung** (none moved here): the frp relay defaults (`VIBESPACE_FRPS_*` — a plugin keeper reads them as defaults; a live re-read would re-connect the relay: benefits, needs the keeper's restart path), the telemetry forward URL/token (a rotation today = a roll fleet-wide: benefits, trivially), Clerk (`ALLOWED_EMAILS` changes per user are rare and auth-critical — a live auth-config change needs its own design), cephfs / opslog / S3 (per-user mount credentials consumed once at boot by a kernel or rclone mount — a live change means a remount: little benefit), ceph-mint (a URL + token read per call: benefits, trivially).

`Integration` settings category, which holds `agents.*` and stays untouched;

2.369.124 it sits under the Communication ▸ head — `parent:'comm'`, order 30).
ONE CARD PER REGISTRY ROW in the Plugins card language, and the order inside
a card is load-bearing: source chip → the SETUP BLOCK ABOVE THE FIELDS
(callback URL as copyable monospace text + a Copy button that copies EXACTLY
that string, the callback note, the prerequisites checklist — above, because
a user who has filled two inputs and seen a green tick does not scroll back
up) → who serves the row (a radio pair, the cluster one greyed WITH the reason
when there is none; a DROPDOWN of the cluster's presets + "my own key" on a

a failure's words on the card) + Clear my keys (confirm dialog) → "used by".

src/channel-policy.js — PURE (imports only channel-record; bundled into the Outbox card) THE OUTBOX POLICY (design §9, P3): the proposal state machine (every transition names its actor; `unknown` leaves only through reconcile — a lost outcome is NEVER auto-retried), `decideOutbound` (guards stack ON the channel policy and only TIGHTEN it; unknown policy / unparseable guard ⇒ review; off-hours is OFF without a zone, never guessed), the §9.3 receipt with sentAs / identityMarking / identityMarkingText. **P4:** `sending→unknown` also by `boot`; `honestyLine`/`withHonestyLine` (OFF by default, agent drafts only); `canReconcile` (`none` cannot be asked) + `reconcileVerdict` (landed ⇒ sent / not-landed ⇒ failed / else stay). **R4 verify r2:** `validateCompose` refuses `bcc` / `replyTo` BY NAME (`why: 'bcc'|'replyTo'` — a field the verb does not carry is never silently dropped; the agent compose route forwards them so the refusal is reachable). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

**verify-r6 O1–O5 (2026-09-28) — WHAT THE OWNER APPROVES ON AN OUTBOX CARD IS WHAT IS SENT** (verify-r6 agentD; built by a fix agent in a snapshot, reviewed and applied as ONE commit — the five share hunks in this module, the engine and the card). **O1 (HIGH) the reply anchor:** a Lark reply is POSTed to `/messages/<replyTo>/reply` — the request names the MESSAGE, never the chat — so an agent proposing in A with a message id of chat B posted into B while the card showed A (on a direct-policy A with no card at all, past B's policy and reach). A reply may answer only a message the engine STORED for that same conversation (`replyAnchorVerdict` over `store.findRecord`): refused at propose (`bad-proposal`/`reply-anchor`), re-judged at approval and at send (`reply-anchor-gone`); lark.js refuses unless the stored anchor's `raw.chat_id` is this chat (`reply-anchor-elsewhere`); the card shows what it answers. **O2 (MED) recipients:** Gmail's reply recipients were decided at SEND time (the thread's newest message then); `caps.replyEnvelope` + `replyEnvelope(convId, {anchorId})` resolve To / Cc / Subject at propose for the anchor the engine picked, stored, shown and sent verbatim (one metadata read ≈ 40 Gmail units per reply). **O3 (MED) the envelope:** where / To / Cc / Subject / "In reply to" one wrapping line each — no `nowrap` / `ellipsis` / `overflow:hidden` on an envelope rule (a CSS census). **O4 (MED-LOW) the press:** a card that appeared or moved takes no trusted click for `ARM_MS` 700 (PURE `armVerdict` / `rearmVerdict`), and Approve carries `shown` = `shownDigest(view)`, compared before anything moves (`changed-since-shown`). **O5 (LOW-MED) hidden characters:** direction controls and zero-width characters refused by name in to / cc / subject / replyTo (joiners only in addresses and ids); a TEXT keeps them and the card draws each as a visible `U+XXXX` mark with one warning line. ### channels/lark.js

**THE UPLOAD SCOPES (lane lark-upload-preflight, 2.369.229 — MEASURED: a user-token upload without them answers 99991679 "required one of … [im:resource:upload, im:resource]").** `UPLOAD_SCOPES` = both; the consent asks for them beside the send pair (`consentScopes`), as the SECOND optional group (`OPTIONAL_SCOPE_GROUPS`: wide → upload → reactions → profiles → feed — an app that has not enabled them loses only them on the second press). `capsOfScopes` grows `files {send, why, requiredScopes}` (send pair AND either upload scope; else `attachments-not-sendable` + both scopes), so `convCaps` and the engine's credential re-judge carry it; `FILES_GRANT` (`filesGrant`, `any:true`) feeds the engine's `filesGrantView` → the account row's "One Re-authorize adds: sending files".

**THE CONSENT ASKS `im:resource` ONLY (lane lark-upload-scope-split, 2.369.241 — owner 2026-10-08).** Lark's own permission doc, quoted 2026-10-08: "im:resource:upload（上传文件V2，高级）— 该权限已不再维护，不可新增申请；你可申请开通权限 im:resource（获取与上传图片或文件资源）". V2 is DEPRECATED: no app can add it (the owner's console catalog has none), Lark refused every consent naming it (20027), and with the pair as ONE optional group the retry dropped the working V1 too. Now `UPLOAD_CONSENT_SCOPES` = `['im:resource']` is what `consentScopes` asks and the upload group (`OPTIONAL_SCOPE_GROUPS`: wide → im:resource → reactions → job → department → people → p2p → search); `UPLOAD_SCOPES` stays the API-level pair that judges a HELD token (`capsOfScopes`, `FILES_GRANT.scopes`, `any`) — a legacy token holding only V2 still uploads. `FILES_GRANT.asked` = what a consent can add: the files row's `requiredScopes` and `filesGrantView`'s `missing` / `refused` / `dropped` only ever name `im:resource`. Card: none held + refused ⇒ "Sending files is off: Lark refused im:resource — enable it in the app console and Re-authorize" (a warning); refused while a held V2 carries files ⇒ "Lark refused im:resource — sending files still works". A vendor 99991679 answer's own scope list (`requiredScopesOf`) is Lark's words and is kept. **lane channel-send-files (2.369.212): an agent's pictures and files.** `caps.sendAttachments` = Gmail's bounds; `sendWithFiles` = the text first, then per file `upload` (`callForm` multipart, the ONE `typedFailure` judge, paced + metered, `// gated-inline: upload`) + a `msg_type: image|file` message with the key (`attachmentPlan` PURE: an inline raster ≤ 10 MB ⇒ im/v1/images, else im/v1/files with `file_type` by the sniffed type / extension); the answer's `parts` say per piece what landed; the chain's catch = `RATE_OK` `send-parts` (it stops, never retries). slack.js twin: `sendFiles` (`files.getUploadURLExternal` → `uploadBytes` to files.slack.com, metered as `files.upload` → `files.completeUploadExternal`, text = the first file's `initial_comment`; no `files:write` ⇒ refused by name before any request). The engine stores `result.parts`, a partly-sent proposal's `reason` names what did not land (`P.partsWords`), `receiptFor` carries `parts`. Gate: scripts/test-channel-send-files.mjs.

**lane slack-file-send-key (2.369.242, B-2840): a Slack file send learns its message at ingest.** `files.completeUploadExternal` answers no share ts (send-files.json), so `sendFiles` keys the result and each part by the FILE id; a thread reply names the share MESSAGE's ts. No vendor call; a replay moves nothing.

channel-identity.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS) WHOSE ACCOUNT A CONSENT MAY LAND ON (lane R5 verify r5, 2026-09-27, credential class): `identityOf(token)` = the identity a token names (Gmail: the email, lowercased; Lark: open_id + union_id + user_id), `heldIdentity(rec)` = the record's stamp (a legacy record: its `auth.user` when it is an email), `identityMismatch(held, offered)` over the keys BOTH sides carry (one common key equal = the same person; open_id is per app, so a Lark rebind under another app matches on union_id / user_id; no common key = nothing to judge), `mismatchSentence`. The engine's ONE token door (`tokensFor(rec).write`) and `applyRebind` refuse a mismatch by name (`forbidden`, `detail.identityMismatch`; the card's last sign-in line names both) and stamp `rec.identity` from the first consent that names one — it survives a disconnect, only remove() forgets it; a duplicate never carries it. Before it a re-authorize as another Google / Lark user was stored `ok:true`, retargeting every assignment and grant on the record onto a stranger's mailbox. ### channels/gmail.js

channels/gmail.js — ORCH (design §6.3/§12.2/§14.2, P1a) THE GMAIL READ adapter — the DELEGATING row: the OAuth client comes from `resolveIntegration('gmail')` which resolves through the existing `VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS` presets (decision 5: `prefer:'channels'`; on a cluster-only two-preset env `org1`+`channels` with no `'default'` it answers `cluster/channels` and connects END TO END). EPHEMERAL loopback flow (gmail-sync's parameters verbatim, refresh_token required), a CONVERSATION IS A THREAD under the include query (`OPTIONS.query`, default `label:INBOX`, read LIVE off the record), ONE memoised `history.list?startHistoryId&historyTypes=messageAdded` per pass (nothing changed = one request; 404 = RESEED from the profile and walk every tracked thread once; a thread the vendor no longer serves is SKIPPED and said, never a frozen pass), the mailbox cursor IN MEMORY ON PURPOSE (it is mailbox-wide and only provably safe to advance once every named thread was walked — untracked ones never are), `threads.get?format=full` paged oldest-first past the anchor, the MIME tree to plain text (first text/plain, else stripped HTML, else the snippet), `identityMarking:'marked'` at `raw-headers`. `invalid_grant` on refresh is stamped ⇒ `needs-reauth`. `integrationTest` = `shape-only` (ZERO network; a Google client cannot be exchanged for anything alone). `EGRESS` declares its four hosts. **P1b: `receive:'push'` + `pushOptIn:true` — the Pub/Sub pull lane (src/channels/live/gmail.js) is OFF until `push.enabled === true`; `OPTIONS` gained `pushTopic`/`pushSubscription` (`relive:true` = restarts the LANE only); enabling adds the pubsub scope to the NEXT consent.** **P4 (send):** `sendAs ['user']` behind a scope that covers DRAFTS + SENDING — `gmail.compose` (R4 verify 2026-09-27: Google's method table lists mail.google.com | gmail.modify | gmail.compose for drafts.create / drafts.send / drafts.delete and adds gmail.send ONLY for messages.send, so the P4 consent's readonly + gmail.send minted tokens whose every reply would 403 at the draft); `sendVerbsOf(scopes)` is the ONE scope table (`reply` = compose|modify|mail; `compose` = those or the legacy gmail.send), `scopesFor()` asks readonly + compose (never gmail.send beside it — two consent rows for one thing), a held gmail.send-only token composes and is `send-scope-not-granted` for replies (the words say "reconnect (Re-authorize) to allow drafts and sending"); `idempotency two-phase` = drafts.create (the handle via `onHandle` BEFORE the send) → drafts.send, threading headers off the anchor's Message-ID; reconcile = draft still exists ⇒ never sent (discarded) / our SENT message in the thread ⇒ landed / else unknown. **R4 compose (B-6acc):** ONE `messages.send` of a fresh RFC-822 message carrying its own Message-ID (from the idempotency key) AND `X-VibeSpace-Proposal: <idemKey>` (`PROPOSAL_HEADER`, CR/LF-stripped); the handle = `{messageIdHeader, proposalHeader, to}`; a lost answer is reconciled by `rfc822msgid:` in the sent mail, then — should Gmail have rewritten the Message-ID (unmeasured without a real send) — by the proposal header among the ≤10 newest SENT messages to the first recipient since the attempt − 60 s (one metadata read each; a candidate without the header is never claimed ⇒ unknown); gate test-channels-gmail-shape ⑧ (the scope table) + ⑧b (header, both searches, nothing re-sent). **2026-09-22:** every `resolveIntegration('gmail', {credentialKey})` carries THE ACCOUNT's key (`deps.credentialKey`, else the live record's) so consent, refresh, status and Test name ONE OAuth client — two Gmail accounts under two presets refresh with their own client ids; `auth.state()` carries `credentialKey`/`whyCode`. **verify r5 (2026-09-27, credential class): the refresh's SUCCESS path writes ONLY while the store still holds the token it tried (`readToken()` re-read before `persistToken`) — a disconnect (cleared ⇒ the refreshed token is discarded, `auth-expired` "disconnected while its token was refreshed") or a re-authorize (a different token ⇒ superseded, `null`, the caller re-reads the store) that landed while the POST was in flight is never overwritten (measured before: 25/50 trials reverted a re-authorize; a disconnected account reconnected itself; a client-switch rebind ended with the old client's token ⇒ `invalid_grant`); a refused refresh of a since-replaced token is superseded the same way (its caller is served, not refused); a store write the disk refuses keeps the vendor's token in memory (`unsaved` {token, supersedes}: served by `readToken` while the store holds the token it supersedes, flushed single-flight by `persistToken` at the next request; a restart before it lands loses it); the gate refreshes a bearer that EXPIRED during the pace wait (`bearerExpired()` ⇒ one single-flight `accessToken()` after `meter`, before the send — 34 of 50 queued thumbnails at the 5 units/s floor went out expired, 401). Gate: gmail-shape ⑥c (h)–(j).** **verify r7: the profile's address goes through the ONE rule (`looksLikeEmail`: trimmed, case-folded, an address shape — whitespace / a bare word is nameless, refused by name); the consent write carries `consent: { cancelled }` (the loopback's `cancelled()`), the door's in-write refusal of a consent whose flow was ended meanwhile. Gate: gmail-shape ⑥c (l)–(m).**

### channels/live/lane.js + live/lark.js + live/gmail.js

channels/live/lane.js + live/lark.js + live/gmail.js — ORCH (design §6.4 / fence 11 / decisions 18+20, P1b) THE PUSH LANES: `lane.js` = the vendor-free CORE (liveness is POSITIVE evidence; THE ACK IS THE RETURN — a transport acks only after the engine's `onEvent()` resolved, which is after the record is durable; `stop()` is TERMINAL for an arm in flight — a connect landing after it is closed on the spot and `event()` answers `{ok:false, why:'stopped'}` WITHOUT calling the engine so the vendor redelivers; single-use; `err.permanent` ⇒ a named `unavailable` park); `live/lark.js` = the SDK long connection, required LAZILY (missing = `sdk-not-installed`, never a boot crash), the v2 event mapped to the REST item shape and the handler THROWING on a stopped lane (the app's view, not the user's — a chat the bot is not in is what the measurement demotes); `live/gmail.js` = `users.watch` (renewed daily) + a Pub/Sub PULL of THIS instance's subscription, a pulled note = a CURSOR KICK never mail, scope/options refused by name. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### channels/agents.js

channels/agents.js — ORCH (design §12.3, P3) THE BUILT-IN AGENTS ADAPTER behind the §4 contract: conversations = live agent sessions, reach = msg-acl through channel-acl's ONE crosswalk, send = THE delivery ladder (spendReason peer-message — an approved outbox message is the user's own), policyDefault direct, identityMarking marked/recipient-ui, idempotency none (a lost result is `unknown`, never retried). Seeded (not removable, no consent) whenever the wiring hands `liveSessions` in. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r3: the module declares `sendStartsTurn: true` — the engine's wake gate (consent echo + the owner's pace when auth is off) applies to its sends.**

### server/integration-store.js + server/integrations-wiring.js + routes/integrations.js

**2.369.165 (integrations chunk 2): an account-bound row is not a card — `list()` omits it, every card verb `404 binds-per-account`, `own` retired, `presetsFor` / `legacyOwnValues`; full text under the (ORCH) heading above.**
 **2.369.147 r3: `offeredCredentials(id)` ALWAYS lists `own` with `available` + `missing`; the engine's `assertOffered` refuses an unavailable key as 409 needs-credentials (never a silent preset).**
server/integration-store.js + server/integrations-wiring.js + routes/integrations.js — ORCH (design §14.3/§14.4, P0b): `data/integrations.json` (writeJsonAtomic) holds `values` (secrets through secret-box on `data/.integrations-key`) + `clusterKey` and NOTHING else — **`source` is DERIVED at read time, never stored**, and a cluster default's VALUES are read from the env at the moment of the question and never copied to disk (rotate the Secret ⇒ every consumer follows; inject-then-withdraw ⇒ `none` WITH the reason, never the old value). THE ONLY reader of `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATIONS` (JSON) and `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATION_<ID>_<FIELD>` (single-field; JSON wins, said once; unparseable = "no default", never a crash); the delegating gmail row resolves through the INJECTED `MountManager.drivePresets` with a saved `clusterKey` over `prefer` and a vanished saved key ⇒ `none` naming it. `resolveIntegration(id)` is the consumers' call and the only thing that leaves with plaintext (the channels engine hands it to every adapter and re-asks `auth.state()` on `onChange` — a withdrawn credential flips the ADAPTERS row to `needs-credentials`, not only the card); `publicView(id)` is THE one masked view every route + the `integrations-updated` broadcast carry. `clearUserValues` (DELETE, always) and `useClusterDefault` (PUT `{use:'cluster'}`, a NAMED refusal without a default) are TWO functions; `setClusterKey` stores the selector only; `test(id)` constructs NO vendor request — the CONSUMER registers the runner (the fake's fixture switch; lark/gmail/cloak = named `not-wired`), one in flight, 15 s, human-triggered only (censused). An unreadable key file is a TYPED `storeError`, never "nothing configured". The named twin: frp's relay token stays in its plugin card (§14.6). Routes: GET/GET one/PUT/POST test/DELETE behind the cookie auth; no route returns a secret's plaintext or calls `resolveIntegration` (pinned). Wiring = one `create(deps)` stanza in server.js (+4 lines). **r2 (2026-09-14): ONLY ENOENT MEANS "FRESH" — an unreadable existing store file is a TYPED `store-unreadable` (500) on every view/`list()`, logged once per transition, never cached, refused by every writer through `assertWritable()` (the former bare catch cached an empty state and the next unrelated write destroyed every stored credential); a not-a-store file is ARCHIVED as `integrations.json.corrupt-<ts>` first; the named twin `src/mounts.js _load()` is NOT fixed here. A non-delegating row's vanished saved `'default'` re-binds to the env's ONLY preset (`rebindSingle`, said in `why`); the mistyped-env log goes through `describeJsonError`.** **r3 (2026-09-15): a user secret the CURRENT key file cannot open NEVER falls through to the cluster — while any stored field is undecryptable the row answers `none` with the reason naming the fields (consumers included), `hasOwnValues` is a fact about the RECORD (Clear my keys shows; DELETE lands on the cluster because the user decided), the view carries a per-row `storeError {code:'values-undecryptable', message: <remedy>, fields}` (store-level codes outrank it), logged once per row per transition; and `envFieldName` lives HERE, the one resolver, censused out of every other file.** **THE ACCOUNT KEY (2026-09-22):** `resolveIntegration(id, {credentialKey})` — `cluster:<k>` INDEXES the preset list (`clusterPresetsFor`, factored out of `clusterDefaultFor`; a key the env stopped offering answers `none`/`preset-gone` naming it, NEVER another preset), `own` = the user's saved values alone (`own-missing` when absent), an unknown key `unknown-credential`, no key = today's precedence with `credentialKey` (the key a NEW account would be stamped with) on the answer; `offeredCredentials(id)` = the presets as `cluster:<k>` + `own` only while the values are complete and readable (key + label only); `test(id, {credentialKey})` probes one account's key. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/migrations.js

**`2026-09-browser-profiles-who-list` ("Who can use it" becomes a LIST, 2026-09-27; after `2026-09-browser-profiles-all-conversations`).** PURE `migrateWhoList` through the live keeper's `reshapeStore` when there is one, else the file (atomic, mode kept): a single session / task owner ⇒ a one-row list + every pin that authorized yesterday folded in (the fold is what keeps a pinned conversation in — a pin never authorizes after this release); a missing file is nothing, an unparsable one FAILS by name (ledger unstamped, retried). Report `{file, via, migrated:[{id, label, from, folded}], kept}`. Gate: test-migrations (+ the CONTROL: yesterday's admission let the pinned chat in, today's refuses it on the pre-migration file).

**Lane R2 verify (2026-09-26) — `2026-09-channels-aggregated-im`:** the runner is SYNCHRONOUS and the engine's door runs a microtask later, so the counts are the engine's synchronously computed PLAN (the rows the queued write changes), logged AND returned as the ledger's report row; a store that refuses writes (`blocked()`) throws ⇒ a FAILED run, retried next boot (it used to log zeros and record success). test-migrations pins both (197).

**2026-09-26:** `2026-09-channels-aggregated-im` — the engine's `migrateAggregated`: every `tracked` conversation gets `refresh = {every: 30, by: 'migration'}` (tracked ⇒ hot), a never-ingested one gets `readAt = now`, `tracked` is deleted, each account gets `linkedAt`; assignments kept. An engine-less boot throws (retry next boot) while the index still carries `tracked`. Gate: test-migrations (193).

**`2026-09-desktop-apps-host-key` (lane C1, 2026-09-25, design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.5 D8).** A desktop app may run on a PAIRED device now, so every record in data/desktop-apps.json names its machine: a record without a (non-empty string) `hostId` gains `'local'` — every record written before the lane ran on this machine (the keeper refused any other host). Through the live keeper's `reshapeStore(shape)` when `desktopKeeper` is wired (its in-memory store is what it saves next — a file edit beside it would be lost; `via:'keeper'`), else the file itself, atomic tmp+rename with its mode kept (`via:'file'`, no write when nothing needed a stamp); a missing / unreadable file is `via:'none'` and NOTHING is created (a keeper is never made to create a store here); a record that already names a machine is untouched. Returns `{file, via, records, stamped}`, one `[migrate] desktop-apps-host-key:` line. New records carry `hostId: 'local'` from `M.newRecord`. Gate: test-migrations (through the keeper AND through the file).

**`2026-09-channel-custom-client-inline` (2.369.165, integrations chunk 2).** Calls the engine's `inlineLegacyClients()` (the SAME copy the engine runs reader-side): every `own` account's saved client re-sealed under `.channels-key` onto its record, stamped `custom` after the write; a failure (e.g. `integration-key-missing`) FAILS the run by name and the record keeps `own`; no engine + an `own` record ⇒ fails by name; a fresh instance is a dry run. Gate: test-migrations (idempotent twice, the write order, reader-side, the missing key, the pre-r4 engine as the control).

**`2026-09-backfill-ledger-by-slot` (B-f69c ②, 2.369.163).** Runs src/ledger-slot-backfill.js over the instance's own stores (slot transitions, members and roster read off disk — no AccountManager exists yet), logs ONE `[migrate] ledger-by-slot:` line, returns `{rows, candidates, rekeyed, archived, untouched, confirmed, corrective, relearned}` for the ledger's report row and files one info notice when a row moved. server.js's post-migration `usageHistory.reloadEvents()` already covers a shard rewritten in place. Since quota r2 the returned counts are the WHOLE repair (`report.total` — a pass that resumes a crashed one counts both, `resumed: true` + `thisPass`), and the notice is filed on those totals, so a retry that finds only the remainder (or nothing) still says what was repaired. Since quota r3 that includes a retry after a FINISHED pass whose id the runner never recorded (killed between the marker and migrations.json): it states the marker's totals (`recovered: true`).

server/migrations.js — the instance's one-shot migration REGISTRY (2.328.0) through src/migration-runner.js (ledger-keyed, run at most once, failed = retry next boot, never block); `create({rootDir, serverNotice, homeDir, channels, userTodos, desktopKeeper, browserKeeper, accounts})` (**2026-09-28 `accounts` = the LIVE AccountManager or a getter — `2026-09-pool-manual-priority` reshapes THROUGH it (`accounts.migrateManualPools()`: a pool with `auto:false` gets `priority [its current target, …the others in list order]` + `auto:true`, so the owner's pick stays #1 and nothing moves at boot); with no store a manual pool FAILS the run by name (retried), nothing manual is a success; gate test-migrations**) (`desktopKeeper` / `browserKeeper` = the LIVE keepers or getters — a keeper loads its store at construction, so a reshape goes through its `reshapeStore`, the file only when none is wired) — `channels` (2026-09-22) is the CHANNELS ENGINE handle, because `data/channels/adapters.json` has ONE writer (the engine's serialized door) and a migration reshaping an adapter record must go through it, never a second store instance; `2026-09-channel-credential-key` stamps every legacy adapter record via `engine.stampCredentialKeys()` with the client its OWN TOKEN names when this instance still offers it (evidence `token` — a Gmail token records the preset key it was exchanged under), else its integration's CURRENT pick (evidence `row-pick`, what refreshed it until now), the [migrate] line naming the evidence per record (a record whose token names nothing offered and whose integration resolves to nothing stays unstamped; without an engine a legacy real record FAILS the run by name so a later boot retries it). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

**`2026-09-spend-notices-expire` (2.369.152) + `userTodos`.** `create({…, userTodos})` takes the LIVE UserTodoManager (or a getter) — server.js builds it long before the migrations run and holds the file in memory, so the row reshapes through `userTodos.reshapeItems()` (one save, one broadcast) and then calls the store's synchronous `flush()` on BOTH paths — the live store's save is a 500 ms debounce, and the atomic write must land BEFORE the runner records `applied[id]` (a crash in between would otherwise lose the reshaping with the ledger saying it ran; verifier LOW-1); with none (a suite, a boot without the inbox) it builds a PRIVATE manager on the same file with `expirySweepMs: 0`, flushes it through the store's own tmp+rename writer and stops it before returning; no file on disk = `store: 'absent'`, nothing created. The rule: `sessionName === 'Spending' && sessionKey === 'accounts'` — the name spend-guard's one `fileInbox` freezes on every item it files; on the owner's store it selects exactly the same 19 records as the text rule (/unattended turns|VibeSpace refused/ + by agent + accounts) and, unlike a text rule, survives a rewording. Every match becomes `kind: 'notice'` (resolved ones too — their status/resolvedAt/resolvedBy untouched — so a later ↺ reopens a notice, not an action); an OPEN match without `expiresAt` gets the end of the window it was ABOUT, through spend-guard's own `noticeExpiry(about, createdAt)` — `about` read from the detail spend-guard wrote (`Scope: hour` ⇒ +1 h, `Scope: day|instance` ⇒ +24 h, a `Refusal:` line ⇒ +6 h, none ⇒ +24 h, the longest window any spend notice talks about): an end already past ⇒ resolved `done`/`expired` with `resolvedAt` = THAT END (when it should have died — never the upgrade boot, so the retirements sort as old history instead of filling the popup's Recently-resolved slots; verifier LOW-2), kept, never deleted; an end still ahead ⇒ stamped as its `expiresAt`. Measured on a copy of the owner's store (876 items): 19 matched, 17 re-kinded, 13 retired (ends 1 h / 6 h / 24 h after filing), 2 fresh stamped (1 h, 6 h), 857 byte-identical, a second run a no-op. It RETURNS `{matched, rekinded, expired, stamped, store}` and the shared runner (src/migration-runner.js, since 2.369.152) records a plain-object return under `ledger.reports[id] = {at, …}` beside the `applied[id]` timestamp (which stays a number — every reader tests it for truth). Gate: test-migrations (live store — the FILE carries the change when run() returns / private store / absent / run-at-most-once / the scope-derived ends / controls = the registry without the row keeps 14 badge actions, and a patched copy with the flush behind `if (priv)` leaves the file unchanged with the ledger row written until the debounce fires).

### channel-outbox.js + channel-reach-editor.js

xterm.js maps the pointer by `clientX - rect.left` (ZOOMED px under `document.body.style.zoom`, the "UI scale (DPI)" setting) over a cell size it measured in LAYOUT px (`TextMetricsMeasureStrategy`, canvas `measureText`), so under a body zoom a drag at row 20 selected row 20×scale (measured on the real build: 1.25 → 25, 0.8 → 16; userW inc-mu92zsgw-6c9y). ### src/harness-settings.js — THE DECLARED HARNESS SETTINGS TABLES (PURE, docs/design-harness-settings.zh.md §2, 2.369.123)

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the SAME file is bundled into the browser, required by the server and carried by the daemon bundle). `HARNESS_SETTINGS = { claude, codex, opencode }`, each `{ prefix, category, files: { <id>: {rel, format} }, rows: [ROW] }`. A ROW is pure data — `key, type (boolean|number|string|text|enum), default, options, min/max/step, combobox, label, description, apply` — and its persisted path is `settingPath(prefix, key)` = `${prefix}.${key}`, **byte-identical to the old literal schema keys**, so data/settings.json needs no migration. `apply` is the CLOSED union: `{kind:'spawn', how, via?, live?, mode?}` (consumed by `adapter.buildSessionArgs` as `opts.settings.<key>`, or through the named top-level field when `via` is set — model/effort/permissionMode/extraArgs/outputStyle ride ws-create's resume ladder; `how` is DISPLAY TEXT, never the transport; `live` = the adapter verb the server writes to every running chat session of that harness on change; `mode` restricts to chat|terminal), `{kind:'server', how}` (read at a decision point through `harnessSetting()`), `{kind:'cli-config', file, path, off, onUninstall}` (written INTO the harness's own config file; a value equal to `off` is NOT written and never deleted). `checkTable(table, ctx)` is THE validator (type in the closed set, enum default among its options, no functions in a row, ≤50 rows, cli-config `file` ∈ `files` AND ∈ the descriptor's `configFiles` with the SAME `rel` object, read-only file refused by name, toml path `[section,key]|[key]` bare names + string/boolean/integer rows only, `off` required, `onUninstall` keep|strip, `rel` without `..`/separators, prefix = the descriptor's, a contributed table only its own id and never a built-in prefix); `coerce(row, raw)` = THE typed read (the row's default for unset/unreadable — the 36500 that lived twice; numbers clamped to min/max; booleans strict; **an `enum` row's domain IS its options (2026-09-21, verifier r7): a value outside them falls back to the row default — checkTable guarantees the default is listed — EXCEPT a `combobox` row, whose options are suggestions and whose typed value is the point. The old "closed vocabularies are validated where they become argv" was only true of argv: a cli-config row's value reached config.toml unchecked, codex 0.154.0 refuses to load an unknown `history.persistence` variant, and every receipt said ✓ applied while the prelude fanned `bogus` out to every remote host**; `refusedValue(row, raw)` names the dropped string so the ORCH half can warn at every sync); `checkRel` is exported (its TWIN lives in harness-config.js — the helper embeds that file's text alone; test-harness-settings §6b pins the two texts identical); `buildConfigPlan(specs)` = the plan `{v:1, files:[{harness, id, rel, format, createIfMissing, hooks?, set:[{key, path, value, onUninstall}]}]}`. `GENERIC_LEGACY_KEYS.autoResumeOnLimit = 'claude.autoResumeOnLimit'` — the one generic feature under a legacy `claude.` spelling, deliberately NOT a row (auto-resume is generic; the key stays because every per-session override is recorded against it), read by NAME so the server never spells a harness literal. **The codex `historyPersistence` row (the ONE managed config.toml row, owner D4)** carries its 0.154.0 evidence in the row comment: the binary's resolved-config template embeds `[history]` / `persistence = "save-all"` (5×), the `HistoryPersistence` struct name and the "(Session persistence is disabled; cannot …" branch; default 'save-all' (VibeSpace enforces rollouts persist), '' = leave config.toml alone. Gates: test-harness-settings §1/§2, test-harness-contract (identity + spawn conformance), test-architecture §46.

**2.369.155 — `claude.autoContinueAtUsageLimit` (boolean, default false, `apply:{kind:'spawn', how:'--settings autoContinueAtUsageLimit=false (while off)'}`).** Claude Code's own wait-and-continue at a usage limit, spawned OFF (owner ruling 2026-09-22). What it changes is PER MODE: chat sessions never run the CLI's continue (non-interactive launch — piped stdout), so there the row changes nothing and VibeSpace's auto-resume is the only producer; terminal sessions did run it and it was their ONLY automatic continue, so OFF leaves them stopped at a wall for the user (the row description says exactly this — pinned by test-fallback-policy §5b). The adapter consumes it (see the src/adapters/claude-code.js spawn-flags essay); test-harness-settings §3 pins the row, test-harness-contract proves it changes the spawn.

### src/server-root.js + scripts/test-server-root.mjs — THE ROOT VERDICT (lane hook-root-guard, B-c77a, 2026-10-02)

**Why it exists.** Twice a server booted from a lane WORKTREE wrote the owner's real CLI config: 2026-07-21 (a /tmp rail-smoke worktree pointed every hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` at its own path — MODULE_NOT_FOUND for two days after the worktree was removed) and 2026-10-01 (notify-retry verify r1, a worktree under `/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/` registered into `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.codex/hooks.json`). The old `hookRegistrationSafe()` knew only "my code is under `os.tmpdir()` or `/tmp/`": a worktree under `/var/tmp`, or beside the checkout, passed it. The law: **a server's root is judged before any owner-file write, and only a plain checkout is the owner's instance.**

**PURE (imports nothing; no env, no fs).** `rootVerdict({root, gitDir, gitCommonDir, tmpRoots, envOverride, force, home})` → `{ok:true, kind:'checkout'|'forced'} | {ok:false, kind:'worktree'|'tmp'|'override'|'unknown', why, checkout?, tmpRoot?}`; first match wins: (1) no absolute root ⇒ `unknown` (fail closed); (2) a linked WORKTREE — `gitDir` under `<gitCommonDir>/worktrees/` (git's own layout; the ORCH reads the `.git` FILE's `gitdir:` line and that dir's `commondir` file with fs, never a git child at boot) ⇒ `worktree`, naming the checkout (`<repo>/.git` → `<repo>`, a bare common dir names itself); a submodule (gitdir under `.git/modules/`) and a `--separate-git-dir` clone have no `commondir`, so gitDir = common dir and they stay checkouts; (3) under a tmp root (the caller passes `os.tmpdir()` + fixture-guard's `TMP_ROOTS` `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`; segment boundary — `/tmpx` is not under `/tmp`) ⇒ `tmp`; every `vs-` dir scripts/scratch.mjs mints lives under one, so the scratch prefix is covered by construction — a `vs-` name ELSEWHERE is a user's folder and is not judged; (4) `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` ⇒ `override` — one rule of four, never the only one (the 2026-10-01 server did not set it), and a worktree with it set still reports `worktree`. A refusal is lifted only by `VIBESPACE_FORCE_AGENT_HOOKS=1` AND a HOME under a tmp root (a suite registering into its OWN scratch home) ⇒ `forced`; FORCE with the real HOME is ignored and the why says so. Both env flags arrive as BOOLEANS (the caller compares to `'1'`). `refusalLine(v)` = THE journal sentence: `hooks not registered: this server runs from a git worktree of /home/…/vibespace — the owner's CLI config belongs to that checkout's instance` (tmp: `…runs from a temporary folder (<root> is under <tmp>) — a throwaway server never writes the owner's CLI config`; override: `…VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1 is set for this server`). `parseGitFile` / `checkoutOfCommonDir` / `isLinkedWorktree` / `isUnder` exported for the ORCH reader and the gate.

**Gate: scripts/test-server-root.mjs (fast, ~60 ms, 77).** ④ THE WRITER CENSUS (derived: every writer line in server.js + src/ outside src/lib and src/harness-config.js is one of 7 named rows — hooks register + strip, the cli-config sync, hosts install + uninstall, the ssh prelude, the dial device setup — each guarded on its line or in the 12 before; a planted unguarded writer is the negative control); ⑤ the wiring (fs facts, the one-line latch, the ws ctx, the 409, the status fields) and the words (every kind's "Not registered — …" line, zh + ja entries). ① the 32-row verdict table (every kind; worktree beside the checkout / under /var/tmp / under /tmp/vs-* / of a bare repo; submodule + separate-git-dir stay checkouts; segment boundaries; a `vs-` folder outside tmp; relative tmp roots ignored; override as one rule; FORCE with a scratch vs the real HOME; string flags are not booleans); ② parseGitFile, the three journal sentences word for word, purity (no require/import/process/fs in the code); ③ three mutant-copy controls through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs (the prefix without its segment boundary, the worktree rule dropped = the old guard, FORCE honoured whatever the HOME) — each must turn its NAMED rows red, plus the copies census.

**Verify r1 F1 (2026-10-02): A READ ERROR WAS "NO GIT" — EVERY WRITER WROTE.** The reader returned bare facts on ANY failure, so an unreadable `.git` (EACCES / EIO — an NFS hiccup on the owner's bindfs checkout stands in) and a worktree whose checkout was removed (a `.git` file whose gitdir is gone: no `commondir`, so gitDir = common dir) were both judged `checkout`, and all 7 writers wrote (reproduced on real git shapes under scratch: verify-r1 r1-repro/root-table.mjs, the before-fix log beside it). Now: ENOENT on `.git` is still "no git" (the docker image), every other stat / read failure on `.git`, on the gitdir it names or on `commondir` is the `error` fact ⇒ `rootVerdict` kind `unknown` (refused, fail CLOSED, FORCE under a scratch HOME still lifts it); a gone gitdir of the `<common>/worktrees/<name>` layout infers the common dir (`dangling: true`) and stays a `worktree` naming the checkout; a `.git` file without a `gitdir:` line is an error. The ORCH caches the facts only when read without error, so a transient error is judged again at the next writer and the hook-health probe (boot + 60 s, every 6 h) heals + notifies; at boot an `unknown` verdict also posts ONE server notice (`hook-root-unknown`) so the owner, not only the journal, hears it. The gate's ⑥ builds the shapes with real git under scratch (a clone, a worktree, a dangling worktree, a bare repo's worktree, a submodule, a symlink, no git, EACCES, a gitdir-less `.git` file) and checks the facts against `git rev-parse`; the writer census also sees raw `writeFileSync` toward a CLI config file name (three NOT_A_WRITE rows with their reasons: the codex seedDir's empty symlink target, two isolated config dirs) and a guard-less mutant copy of harness-config-sync.js goes red.

**Verify r2 (2026-10-02) — WHAT r1 ADDED, ATTACKED (r2-repro/t1-real.mjs on the shipped module over scratch shapes + server.js source facts):** ① (MED, fixed) an `unknown` at boot was left to the hook-health probe — 60 s after boot, then every 6 h — and the probe RETURNED SILENTLY while the root stayed unjudgeable (`if (!hookRegistrationSafe() …) return`), so a session started during an NFS stall got no hooks and its agent never learned the tools until the next 6-hour tick; when the verdict recovered the probe registered under the wrong words ("was broken (stale or missing path) and has been repaired"); and the unknown notice's memo was in memory (`_sentNotices`) ⇒ one toast PER BOOT while nothing was wrong. Now: PURE `REJUDGE_BACKOFF_MS` [30 s, 60 s, 2, 5, 10, 30 min] + `nextRejudgeDelay(attempt)` (then the cap for ever) — src/server/hook-root-watch.js `arm()` re-runs `sync()` on that ladder from the boot unknown AND from the probe's gate `probeMayRun()` (one timer, reset on recovery; server.js only wires it — its 2100-line ratchet); PURE `unknownNoticeDue(memo, cause)` + the memo PERSISTED in data/hook-root-notice.json (written only when a client saw the toast; removed at recovery) ⇒ once per CAUSE until the verdict changes; the ORCH remembers `_lastRootError` and, when `ensureAgentHooks` registers after it, `_registeredAfterError {at, error, since}` (set once) — `rootRecovery()`, `agentHooksStatus().registeredAfterError`, `cliConfigStatus().registeredAfterError` carry it; server.js says it ONCE (`hook-root-registered`, PURE `registeredAfterErrorLine`, i18n) and the probe says THAT instead of "repaired" for a never-registered root; the Settings chip, "Check machines…" and Manage Agents show `recoveredLine` ("Registered at HH:MM after an earlier read error (…) — sessions started since then have the tools"); both notices carry i18n keys (zh + ja). ② the probe: boot + 60 s, every 6 h; it WRITES only through `ensureAgentHooks` (gated) and `createHookHelper` (the server's own data/bin — not an owner file). ③ (LOW, fixed) facts read without error were cached for the process's life, so a `.git` converted in place (a checkout turned into a worktree while running) stayed `checkout` until a restart — `ROOT_FACTS_TTL_MS` 60 s (errors still never cached); the dangling worktree whose mount returns stays `worktree` (right). ④ FORCE census (grep-derived, gate ⑦): outside server-root.js the knob is spelled only at the ORCH's one env read. ⑤ src/agentd/agentd.js writes no CLI config file (grep-derived, with a planted control) — the hub's verdict is the only gate a host needs. ⑥ zh/ja for both notices + the chip line. Held: `_registeredAfterError` is per process (a restart after the recovery forgets the fact — the chip then shows the plain receipts).

### src/harness-config.js — THE SHARED CLI-CONFIG APPLIER (fs/path/os only; design §6, 2.369.123)

ONE implementation of "write these managed keys (and our hook entries) into a harness's own config file" for EVERY machine: required by the server for device #0 and **embedded as FILE TEXT into the shipped `data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs`** (createRequire mints its `require`; never `Function.toString` — a closure reference would become a free identifier, the 2.340.2/2.341.1 lost-binding class), so it must never use `__dirname`/`__filename`, never require ORCH, and every export must survive evaluation inside a function body. `cliConfigFile(spec, {createIfMissing})` = the descriptor-side file object over a table's `files.<id>` entry (the SAME `rel` array — one spelling — plus `file()` and the create policy); `writeJsonManaged(file, {createIfMissing}, mutate)` = the CAS writer moved verbatim out of agent-tool-generators (read → mutate → compare-and-swap re-read → tmp+rename; invalid JSON refused by name and never overwritten; a missing file created only when the plan says so and NEVER its directory — a missing `~/.codex` means codex is not installed; **it re-serialises the WHOLE file** — 2-space JSON + trailing newline, `\uXXXX` escapes decoded, exactly as Claude Code itself rewrites settings.json — so "only the touched line" is the TOML writer's promise, not this one's); **THE BYTES LAND ON THE REAL FILE (2026-09-21, verifier r7 — both writers share `readManaged` / `writeTarget` / `commitWrite`):** a symlinked config (the dotfiles pattern, `~/.codex/config.toml → dotfiles/codex.toml`) is written THROUGH — the tmp file goes beside the link's real target and the rename lands on the target, so the link survives and the dotfile keeps governing (before, a tmp+rename on the link path replaced it with a regular file at every boot, remote install, ssh-spawn prelude and dial spawn, receipts ✓); a dangling link is refused by name, never replaced; an existing-but-unreadable path (a directory, EACCES) is refused rather than "created" over; the file's own mode survives the rename (a 0600 config.toml carrying MCP tokens stays 0600 — chmod on the tmp beats the umask; a new file takes the umask's mode). `checkRel(rel)` — a TWIN of harness-settings.checkRel, text-identical (this file cannot require the PURE one) — re-checks every plan `rel` at `applyConfigPlan` / `readConfigPlan` (a `..`, separator or `~` segment ⇒ a `refused` receipt naming it and NOTHING joined under $HOME; `files[].file` null) and `decodePlan` drops such a plan whole (the helper then applies its hooks-only DEFAULT_PLAN). `findOurHookIn` / `registerHookEntries(root, events, hookCmd)` / `stripHookEntries(root, events)` = the hook-entry mutators the server's ensureAgentHooks/stripAgentHookEntries AND the remote helper share (the helper's private copy of the event table is gone — the plan's `hooks.events` carries it). **The TOML setter** `tomlSet(text, section, key, value)` → `{text, changed} | {refused}`: a conservative line tokenizer (blank | `[table]` | `[[aot]]` | `key = value` | opaque lines inside a multi-line string or multi-line array; anything else = refuse), edits ONE line — replaces the value in place keeping indentation/spacing/the trailing comment, or inserts `key = value` after the section's last key line, or replaces the dotted `section.key = …` spelling in place when the file already uses it, or appends `[section]` + the line at the end (top-level keys go after the last root key, before the first header) — string (basic-string escaped) / boolean / safe-integer values only, byte-identical output when the value is already there (idempotent), CRLF preserved; REFUSES BY NAME an inline table (`section = {…}` or the value itself), an array of tables, a multi-line string, an array/float/date value, a duplicate key, a `[section.key]` sub-table where the key should be, **a root scalar named like the section (`history = 5` — appending `[history]` after it is a duplicate key; codex 0.154.0 refuses the file), and a table defined BOTH by dotted root keys and a `[section]` header (already invalid TOML — never reported applied)**; dotted root keys alone (`history.max_bytes = 5`, no header) get the new line in THAT spelling (`history.persistence = …` after the last such line) because a `[history]` header after them is the same duplicate-key refusal (2026-09-21, both orders verified on 0.154.0). `tomlGet` reads one scalar for the receipts. `writeTomlManaged(file, {createIfMissing}, sets)` = the same CAS + tmp+rename law (any refusal throws by name and nothing is written). `applyConfigPlan(plan, {home, hookCmd, uninstall})` → `{receipts, files}` (managed keys always; hook entries only with a `hookCmd` = the remote helper; `uninstall` strips ONLY hook entries, never a managed key — the retention a user asked for is not "our entry"); `readConfigPlan(plan, {home})` = READ-ONLY receipts (applied | differs(current) | missing | unreadable(reason)); `ensureCliConfig({plan, home})` = the design's name for the local apply; receipt lines `CFG|harness|key|state|current|want|reason` (the three free fields encodeURIComponent(JSON) so a `|`/newline in a value cannot shear a line; `CFG|*|*|unknown|` = an older helper, `no-node` = no interpreter) with `formatReceiptLines`/`parseReceiptLines`; `encodePlan`/`decodePlan` = base64 JSON (shell-safe bare, refuses a foreign `v`).
