### src/workflow-disk.js — THE RUN DIR IS THE TRUTH WHEN THE STREAM IS GONE (2026-09-26)

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the route, the bundle and node tests share it; test-architecture PURE set). Owner, on a View Workflow window titled with its run's name: chip 运行中, "11 个 agent · 10 完成 · 运行中…", a note claiming phase names and labels appear when the run finishes, eleven "(agent)" rows under ONE phase titled with that same sentence — for a run whose newest file was two days old (the 11th agent never wrote a `result`, no terminal snapshot) and whose launching session's live tree had been lost to seven server restarts and a displaced 40-record `taskRecords` ring. The old skeleton (`liveWorkflowFromParts`) wrote `label: ''`, that phase title and `status: 'running'` UNCONDITIONALLY — and the labels were on disk.

**The format, MEASURED over 495 local run dirs (CLI 2.1.201 → 2.1.281, keys/counts only):** `journal.jsonl` record types = `launched` {type} (since 2.1.267), `started` {type, key, agentId} + {label, phase} since 2.1.267 (2.1.263 and older: none), `result` {type, key, agentId, result}, `failed` {type, key, agentId} (600 lines; never beside a result for the same agent; 232 retried under the same key, 368 the last attempt — the terminal snapshot calls those agents `error`). `agent-<id>.meta.json` = {agentType, spawnDepth} always (+ spawnedWithWorktree / worktreePath sometimes), + {description = the label, workflowPhase = the phase title, requestShape, requestNonInteractive} since 2.1.267, `model` on many agents since 2.1.226. Agent ids = 17 hex chars (4122/4122). journal `phase` == snapshot `phaseTitle` for 692/692 agents; journal first-seen phase order == snapshot phase index order in 136/137 labelled runs; 3 of 495 runs have no terminal snapshot.

**API.** `STALL_MS` = 10 min. `journalAttemptsFromText(text)` — MOVED VERBATIM from routes/sessions.js (done / superseded / started unchanged, proven against the pre-move body) + additive `failed` Set and `info` Map(agentId → {label, phase}). `parseRunDir({runId, journalLines (array or text), metas {agentId: meta}, agentFiles, scriptName, snapshotPresent, newestMtime, now, liveTree})` → the `/api/workflow` live view: agents in SPAWN order (journal started order → transcripts the journal has not named → meta-only ids), each `{index, label = started.label ?? meta.description ?? '', model = meta.model || '', state = done | superseded | error (a failed record, additive) | progress, agentId, phaseTitle = started.phase ?? meta.workflowPhase ?? '', onDisk}`; phases in first-seen order, one final `untitled` phase for agents with none ("Other" beside named phases, "Agents" when nothing is named — a pre-2.1.267 run); `workflowName` from `<name>-<runId>.js`; LIVENESS: `liveTree` (the route passes `treeAlive(ti, Date.now())` — a FRESH open tree, lane Q) ⇒ running (`liveness:'tree'`); unknown mtime or clock ⇒ running (`'unknown'` — no evidence either way, e.g. a host whose stat answered nothing); `now − newestMtime < STALL_MS` ⇒ running (`'recent'`); else `status:'stalled'`, `stall: {lastActivityAt, unfinished: [labels of agents still in progress]}` (a superseded or failed attempt is never "unfinished"). Only a STALLED view carries a time — a running view is byte-identical across polls (the window re-renders only on a changed run). `snapshotPresent` ⇒ `resumed: true` (the route only passes it on the resume rule). `agoWords(ms, t)` (floor minutes; the existing 'just now' / '{n} min ago' / '{n} h ago' / '{n} d ago' keys) and `stallWords(view, {t, now})` → `{label: t('Stalled'), detail: 'Last activity {ago}; {n} unfinished agent(s)' | 'Last activity {ago}' | …, unfinished}` or null — THE ONE wording of a stalled run: the window's chip / meta line AND the chat card's chip call it. **Lane Q verify (2026-09-26):** `treeAlive(ti, now)` = is the launching session's stream tree proof of life NOW — `ti.workflow` present, the task OPEN (no status / `running` / `finished` by `closedBy:'level'`, a guess — a task_updated / notification / completed close is the harness's verdict and never proof), and `now − ti.aliveAt < STALL_MS` (no `aliveAt` ⇒ false: no evidence). `liveNoteKind(view)` → `'stalled'` | `'tree'` | `'files'` | null — the window's note, THE STALL FIRST.

**Wiring.** routes/sessions.js: `liveView(parts, {runId, snapshotPresent, now})` = the ONE seam of every live return (local no-snapshot + resumed, remote no-snapshot + resumed): `parseRunDir` over the parts (tree liveness = `treeAlive(ti, Date.now())` — THIS server's clock, the one that stamped `aliveAt`; `now` judges only the FILES), then `mergeLiveWorkflow` when this server holds the tree (fresh or not — a stale tree still lends its labels and tokens to a stalled view). `readRunDirParts(runDir, runId)` reads OFF the event loop (fs.promises): the journal, every file's mtime (newest = the run's last sign of life), each `agent-<id>.meta.json` (cached by path + mtime, ≤ 4000 entries — written once at spawn) and the script name. The terminal-snapshot path is UNCHANGED (normalizeWorkflowSnapshot + the journal's superseded tagging). hosts.js `fetchWorkflowState`: the compound probe adds `NOW:$(date +%s)` (the HOST's clock judges the host's mtimes — no skew) and a trailing nonce-delimited META section, one `<file>\t<json>` line per `agent-*.meta.json` (4000 B each, newlines folded, 40 KB total — snapshot 700 K + journal 250 K + metas 40 K stays under the dial run-cmd's 1 MB slice); the parse yields `metas` + `now`; an absent META section leaves `metas: {}` (labels then come from the journal alone — never the old skeleton). The chat card: chat-status-bar's existing 8 s `/api/workflow` poll calls `onWorkflowVerdict(runId, {status:'stalled', stall} | null)` for every answer and drops a stalled run from the running ⛭ chip; ChatView `_setWorkflowVerdict` keeps `_wfVerdicts` (runId → verdict) and, only on a CHANGE, schedules `_patchWorkflowCard` for each rendered card whose View Workflow button names the run; `renderTaskChip(ti, verdict)` → `taskStatusChipHtml` draws `.chat-task-status-chip.warn` "Stalled" with the sentence as its title when `ti.status === 'running'` and the verdict is stalled (renderToolMsg asks `getWorkflowVerdict(runId)` at render, the patch passes `_workflowVerdict(runId)`). **Lane Q verify (2026-09-26, six findings, all fixed):** ① THE TREE HAS A CLOCK — the builder's known limit (a tree REPLAYED from persisted `taskRecords` after a restart re-proved a run that stalled days ago "running", liveness `tree`, for as long as it sat in the 40-task ring) is gone: message-manager stamps `taskInfo.aliveAt` on every task_started / task_progress (Date.now() on the live stream; the persisted `cur.at` on a replay — `taskReplayRecords` yields `{record, at}` and `rebuildHistory` calls `mm.replay(record, {at})`; NOTHING in a history conversion, whose surviving stdout ring may hold days-old task records with no arrival time) and the route counts the tree only through `treeAlive`. TRADE-OFF (named on purpose): a live run whose agents AND tree are both quiet for 10 min (one long tool call inside an agent writes nothing, and the CLI sends no task_progress heartbeat while an agent runs quietly) reads Stalled until its next record or file write — the files' own rule, self-healing within one poll. ② the level set names a CARD by any of its keys (message-manager; the wf_ run-id key the ack registered used to be "not named" and soft-close the card the short key kept open — below, and the 2.369.147 entry) + the belt: `treeAlive` counts a level close as open. ③ the status bar KEEPS a stalled run tracked (`wf.stalled`, re-asked every `WF_STALLED_POLL_MS` = 15 s, never drawn in the running ⛭ chip — `_runningWorkflows()`); a `running` answer clears the flag and the card's verdict (the card follows the window back within one period, measured 16 s); only a terminal answer or a 404 lets go. ④ the note by `liveNoteKind` (window paragraph above). ⑤ label/phase `title`s. ⑥ the remote twin: the probe's `NMT:` = the newest mtime of EVERY file of the run dir (meta.json too — the local `readRunDirParts` rule; JMT/AMT stay the resume rule's inputs, as locally), and an answer without its `NOW:` line judges with NO clock (`now: 0` ⇒ liveness `unknown`, running) instead of the hub's clock against the host's mtimes.

Gates: scripts/test-workflow-disk.mjs (fast, 68; 95 after lane Q verify) + test-fold-ux F5 (heavy; 97 after lane Q) + test-workflow-live-view (census; 23 — the per-KEY level-set control) + test-task-lifecycle (chip helper pin; the aliveAt stamp).

### docs/design-mobile-gaps.md — the mobile gaps batch (2.369.125): harness lessons that outlive it

The review (2026-09-20, HEAD 0875cc6a) measured 59 desktop features on a 390×844 phone; this batch closes its top 10 + the measured defects (the per-file essays above). Cross-cutting facts the suite paid for, keep them: ① **a fresh instance's first-run wizard covers the nav bar** (`#welcome.onboarding` is `position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:9600`) — a hit-test at the inbox button's centre answered `#welcome`; a chrome suite that taps chrome on a fresh data dir must model a returning user (`localStorage vs-onboarded=1` via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` BEFORE navigation), never `.click()` around it. ② `showContextMenu(x, y, items, className)` takes ONE class name — the row class is `className + '-item'` over the whole string; add modifiers with `classList.add` afterwards. ③ Long-presses in a suite are REAL touch sequences (`Input.dispatchTouchEvent` touchStart → hold 700 ms → touchEnd) through installLongPressContextMenu, never a synthesized `contextmenu` — that is the path a phone takes. ④ A read-only viewer has no ChatSearch: a control whose verb cannot fire is not rendered (the magnifier), and the suite proves the live case with a stub `claude` behind the REAL chat-wrapper (`CLAUDE_CMD`, the CODEX_CMD precedent) — the only way to a non-read-only chat window without a vendor CLI. ⑤ The ONE touch-target block in style.css lifts nav / sidebar header+search+tabs / status chips / dropdown rows / settings nav / terminal keys to ≥ 36 px; the ⚙ gear rows are another lane's (docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md) and are not in it — design #8 hands them over by name. ⑥ (r2) A CROSS-CLIENT feature is verified across two clients: the battery opens a SECOND CDP page (`PUT /json/new`, a 1280×800 desktop, `connectPage` factory) on the same server and asserts on BOTH ends — a phone's real tap marks it user-dirty (layout.js's capture pointerdown), a desktop's `userInput()` is a bare Shift key (the same gate), and "the save arrived" is `layoutManager._lastRemoteSeq` growing on the receiver, never a sleep. Two laws the r2 findings paid for: a client that cannot DISPLAY a state still CARRIES it (§6b guard 5), and a layout-sync REPLAY produces the window it names (never a panel). ⑦ A synthesized `KeyboardEvent` is not cancelable unless asked; a handler ordering built on `defaultPrevented` is invisible to such a test AND to any real handler that closes without preventing — order by phase (capture) and by the presence of the layer above. ⑧ TWO TABS IN ONE HEADLESS WINDOW: Chrome acks input (touch / key) only on the FOREGROUND tab — `PUT /json/new` fronts the new tab, and the first `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` on the now-hidden phone tab hung the battery for 10 minutes with both pages fully responsive to `Runtime.evaluate` (the Puppeteer `bringToFront` class). Every input helper calls `Page.bringToFront` on its own page first; evaluation needs no fronting. Gate: scripts/test-mobile-gaps.mjs (heavy; 72 checks).

Gate: test-helper-ask ⑦ + its control.

### docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md (+ English twin design-app-persistence.md) — apps that survive a pod recreation (2026-09-27; DESIGN, awaiting owner D1–D6)

The owner's question after desktop apps shipped: users and their agents must be able to install apps that are still there — with their data — after the fleet pod is recreated; SteamDeck-like or system-vs-chroot? Method: four independent proposals (persistent overlay upper / chroot "app system" / Nix on the PVC / manifest replay + local .deb cache) scored by three independent judges on one rubric (persistence, agent-installable, privilege, image-update safety, boot latency, disk, GUI fidelity under xpra, ops, effort), every factual claim checked against the kernel and the chart. Facts that bind the design: only the HOME PVC survives; the pod already performs kernel mounts from inside (`mount -t ceph`) where the chart grants CAP_SYS_ADMIN + AppArmor Unconfined (conditional on fuse/cephfs; all production pods have it today); the only convention so far is `~/.vibespace-init.sh` replayed synchronously before node starts; the install door that exists is the xpra install plan (plan → `sudo -n sh -c` → detached slot → streamed log) and the plugin boot replay. Recommendation = three layers, one manifest, one gate: Layer 0 (every pod, no image/chart change) a server-owned `~/.vibespace/apps/manifest.json` + a sha256-indexed `file:` .deb repository on the PVC + ONE package slot per machine (the xpra INSTALL_LAUNCHER generalised) + `vibespace-app` (agents only PROPOSE; a For-you item under a new origin `apps`; cookie-only execute routes; approval turns the package's .desktop into catalog rows the agent may open by id); Layer 1 (pods with the cap) the app system — a same-release minbase on the PVC entered per launch by a root helper (sudo direct-exec on the keeper's pid, private mount namespace, rbinds, chroot, drop to the user) so nothing is replayed at boot and an image upgrade never touches it (a release change = human-triggered Rebase into rootfs.next, Roll back keeps rootfs.prev); Layer 2 (cap-less pods) the same manifest replayed offline after listen. Overlay-as-truth rejected (the one design that can make a pod fail to boot; fleet-wide reinstall per image; stacking-depth EINVAL; xattr-sensitive backups) but its ops rules absorbed (image stamp, boot-path scripts never from the PVC, smoke test + safe mode before listen, resolv.conf rebind, fsGroup walk). Nix parked. §5 = seventeen probes with pass criteria to run on a test pod BEFORE code; §6 = the plan (P0 probes 1 d → Layer 0 10–13 d → Layer 1 12–13 d → ops 1–2 d) and the gates each phase must carry; §7 = D1–D6 with defaults. The raw review (four proposals + three judgments) is kept in the personal project group's shared context, never in this repo.

### docs/design-split-ux.zh.md (+ design-split-ux.md) — the side-by-side UX design (2026-09-23, lane-split)
The owner's three (four) problems reproduced in headless Chrome (`scripts/dbg-split-gesture.mjs`, a scratch server, two chat windows on stub sessions): a window dragged 409 px LEFT and released on the target's title bar entered a split with the window on the RIGHT (the half of the TARGET'S bar decided, never the drag direction); a drag to the workspace's left edge over a snapped window's title bar split while the snap indicator was showing (the split branch ran before the snap); the strip rendered the chain order [A,B] over a pair [B,A]; the only split mark was a 9 px `⫿` pseudo-glyph (a tofu box on this box's fonts) and the divider's colour equalled the window border; 80 % of a title bar was a split zone. DECIDED (owner's second directive: no drag-time complexity, the tab merge stays the one exception, a button after the merge): R1 no drag-time split at all — the title-bar zone is deleted, no body zone; entries = the ⫿ button on any ≥ 2-tab strip (active tab LEFT beside the most recently active other tab), the window menu's "Beside {name} (on the right)", command mode `v`/`V`; the programmatic `createWindow({intoChain})` unchanged; right after a user merge the button pulses once + a 5 s toast offers "Show side by side" (showToast gains `action`). R2 the verbs name the side, the pointer never. R3 the strip in split mode renders VISUAL order through PURE `visualTabOrder` with an aria-hidden divider glyph between the pane tabs and owner-colour underlines (variant A of three pixel-checked mockups under docs/mockups/split-ux/: A 29 / B 18 / C 19 on the 6-criterion rubric; B squeezed the names into the owner's "Vi…"). R4 the same button is the badge in split mode (click: Unsplit / Swap), the divider's resting colour is brighter than a border and its right-click carries the two items. R5 every announced split entry gets a 5 s "Undo" restoring both windows' pre-split rects. R6 the phone unchanged. Three build chunks (model + wm core / verbs + surfaces / the chrome gate `test-split-ux` + release) with red-first legs and the i18n table live in the doc's §6. **SHIPPED 2.369.162** (all three chunks; gates test-window-binding-model 96, test-contributions 203, test-split-ux 73 — red on 2.369.160).

### docs/design-reset-credits.zh.md — the reset-credit consumption design (2026-09-22)
Owner rulings: auto-consumption is NEVER the default; a UI button wherever an interface exists (codex: `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume` via the wrapper's `codex-reset-credit` verb; claude: none — the web 'Reset for free' is the CLI's hidden interactive `/limit-reset`, so the button is disabled WITH its reason); an advanced `auto` option whose timing follows the vendor's mechanics — OpenAI RESTARTS the window at consumption (the remaining quota is discarded, the natural reset slides to t+P ⇒ use only at the wall, and only when the wait saved ≥ MIN_WAIT), Anthropic REFILLS the current window in place (the deadline stays ⇒ use at the wall while enough of the window remains; a grant near its use-by date is use-it-or-lose-it). A credit keeps the conversation on the SAME account (warm cache), a pool switch cold-starts it — the ladder should fork on warmth (§8 ① awaits the owner). Modes `off` (default) / `ask` (one For-you decision at the wall) / `auto`; every verdict is a PURE `resetCreditVerdict` with a spoken reason; consumption always passes the spend authorizer. Phases: P1 codex (supersedes B-51fd), P2 claude passive detection, P3 claude consumption when the CLI exposes a non-interactive interface.

### src/backlog-select.js — PURE backlog priority + ownership-aware selection (2.369.154)
Imports nothing; CJS (the bundle can share it). `PRIORITIES = ['high','normal','low']` (closed; absent/unknown reads as normal), `priorityRank`, `priorityMarker` (`!` high · `↓` low · '' normal — the ONE spelling every text rendering prints), `sortBacklog(items)` = open first by priority then NEWEST `addedAt` (ties by id), then resolved by `resolvedAt` desc — never mutates; `selectReminders(open, sessionKey, {limit=5, isLive?})` → `{mine, mineTotal, unclaimedHigh:[{id,text,stale?}], unclaimedHighTotal, othersCount}`: a session is reminded of what it OWNS first, an open HIGH item no LIVE session owns is surfaced to everybody (`isLive(key)` absent ⇒ every claim counts; a high item whose claimants are all gone is `stale:true`), the rest is a count. `escapeItemText`/`unescapeItemText`/`markedText` (r2): the marker sits AFTER the id, so a text that itself begins `! `/`↓ ` gains ONE backslash when written (also the markdown escape) and the reader strips one — every text rendering prints `markedText(b)`. Every reader goes through it: `_backlogNoteLines` (injection), `renderTaskMd` (TASK.md), GET /api/agent/task + the task-backlog route's `findIdx` numbering (so the CLI's numbers are the route's). The owner's ruling it implements: no store cap — priority + ownership choose what each push shows. Gate: scripts/test-backlog-priority.mjs (oldest-first negative control). **THE CLEANUP NUDGE (2.369.154):** `ownedOpen(items, key)` = open items the key CLAIMED or PARKED (`addedBy` — unclaiming your own parked item does not make it someone else's clutter), each once; `nudgeThreshold(v)` = the setting value as a number — only a finite number or a numeric string counts (negative ⇒ 0, floored); absent / blank / NaN / a boolean / any other type ⇒ `NUDGE_DEFAULT` 20 (r3: a stored `true` coerced to 1 and nudged every session); `backlogNudge(items, key, {threshold, nowMs, staleDays=14})` → null under the threshold or at 0 (= off), else `{owned, stale, oldest:[≤3 {id, ageDays, text≤60}], threshold, staleDays}` (items without `addedAt` are neither stale nor oldest); `nudgeText(nudge, gid)` = THE ONE agent-facing paragraph (English, never translated) — count, stale count, the oldest ids with ages, then `backlog-done` / `backlog-drop` / merge-with-`backlog-edit <id> --detail`; ≤ `NUDGE_MAX_BYTES` 500 (oldest texts shrink 60 → 40 → 24 → 12 → ids only), whitespace collapsed to one line, UTF-8 counted without Buffer (`utf8Bytes`; the bundle shares the module). `nudgeTextAll(entries[{nudge, gid, group}])` (r2) = the several-groups form under the SAME one 500 B budget: one entry ⇒ exactly `nudgeText`; N ⇒ one paragraph "You hold <total> open backlog items across N Task Groups, each past the cleanup threshold: <group>: <owned> (<stale> older than 14 d; oldest: …); …" + the same cleanup sentence with `--group <group> ` — the oldest ids go first, then groups collapse into `+N more groups`. Gate: scripts/test-backlog-nudge.mjs (addedBy / 0-gate / byte-budget controls).

### src/stop-nudge.js — PURE the Stop nudge's verdict: a turn that bookkept itself stops free (B-a8f0, lane stop-nudge-free)
Imports nothing; CJS. `stopNudgeVerdict({now, turnStartedAt, bookkeptAt, statusAt, lastNudgeAt, nudgesUnanswered, staleMin, cooldownMin, maxUnanswered})` → `{block, why}`, `why` from the closed `STOP_NUDGE_WHYS`: **`bookkept-this-turn`** (`bookkeptAt ≥ turnStartedAt` ⇒ never block — the FIRST rule, before every other), then the old time rule in its old order — `cooldown` · `fresh-status` · `never-answered` (the D8 exit condition) · `stale`. `turnStartOf(s)` = the later of `_userInputAt` / `_machineInputAt` (the last person / machine input starts the turn that is stopping now), or null; a null start (a restored session, a terminal turn the ws did not stamp) never earns a free pass — the time rule decides, and its blocking verdict is named **`no-turn-start`** (= `stale` with the start unknown; `STOP_NUDGE_BLOCKING` = those two). The settings arrive clamped by the route (0 = that rule off). WHY: measured 2026-10-02, 250 of 329 unattended billed turns in 24 h were this nudge — the old rule read only the status store's age, so a long turn that ran `vibespace-status working` at its start was asked again at its end and `vibespace-task progress` / `vibespace-ask` counted for nothing. Gate: test-stop-nudge (PURE table + first-rule-cut control, the route over a real express app, the route census).

### src/task-groups.js — backlog `priority` (2.369.154)
Items carry `priority: 'high'|'normal'|'low'`; `update()` / `importBundle` / `importFromFile` normalize anything else to normal (items stored before the field read as normal, no migration). `renderTaskMd` lists open items in `sortBacklog` order with the marker after the id and `(unclaimed)` when nobody holds one; `renderRepoFile` writes `- [ ] [B-xxxx] ! text` (`↓` low, none = normal) and the import regex takes the optional marker. **r2: the writer adds frontmatter `backlog_priority: markers` and `markedText` (a normal text beginning `! `/`↓ ` is written `\! …`); the reader parses markers + strips one backslash ONLY in a file carrying that key — a file without it (every pre-priority file) is read VERBATIM, all normal, `! text` stays text.** `_backlogNoteLines` = `selectReminders`: ≤ 5 owned lines (marker on high/low), `- … +N more claimed by you`, ONE `- unclaimed HIGH: [B-x] text · …` line (each text ≤ 100 chars, `+N more`), then the count line; a session owning nothing gets the pointer line + the same unclaimed-HIGH line. **r2: the unclaimed-HIGH line spends a BYTE budget on item text (`HIGH_LINE_TEXT_BYTES` 600; past it ids only), and `renderMultiContext` passes ONE budget shared by every group (N CJK groups no longer add ~1.5 KB each); `isLiveClaim` (agent-routes' `liveClaimPredicate()` = every key a session in `activeSessions` answers to, status key + `webui:<id>`) makes a claim by a session no longer running count as unowned there — the entry reads `(claimant not running)`.** `snapshotForDiff` carries `p`, so a priority change reaches the owner as `- Backlog priority normal → high [B-x]` (a snapshot without `p` is never read as a change). Gate: test-backlog-priority.

### src/task-groups.js — the backlog cleanup nudge: every full context injection + every turn (2.369.154)
`_backlogNoteLines(t, {…, nudgeAt, nudge=true})` ends — after the count line (or the pointer + unclaimed-HIGH lines of a session owning no claimed item) — with ONE `nudgeTextAll([entry])` (= `nudgeText`) line when `backlogNudge(t.backlog, sessionKey, {threshold})` is non-null; the words are the route's (one PURE helper). The note rides every FULL context injection (SessionStart, the codex first prompt, a full re-delivery) — NOT the turns in between: those get the same paragraph from prompt-context through `backlogNudgeFor(groupIds, sessionKey, {multi, tools, nudgeAt})` (r2: until then a session that never ran a backlog verb met it once per session, while the comment claimed "once per turn"). `backlogNudgeFor` = ONE paragraph (`nudgeTextAll`, one 500 B budget) for every listed group this session is over the threshold in; '' when none / no session key / the task tool off. **Multi-group (r2, verifier: 2 groups × 25 CJK items = 10.8 KB SessionStart, past the 10240 wrap):** `renderMultiContext` passes `nudge:false` to each group's note and appends `backlogNudgeFor(ids)` ONCE after the groups layer, and the claimed-item lines share ONE text budget across groups (`MINE_LINE_TEXT_BYTES` 1500, like the unclaimed-HIGH line's 600; past it an item keeps id + marker + a 40-char clip and `†`) — 2 / 3 groups × 60 CJK items now render 7.8 / 9.0 KB untrimmed; the route's `capInline` is the belt beyond that. A single-group context is unchanged (each item its own 160-char clip). `threshold` = the explicit `nudgeAt` or `backlogNudgeAt()` = `nudgeThreshold(this._getSetting('tasks.backlogNudgeAt'))` (server.js builds the store with `getSetting: (k) => serverSetting(k)`, so it reads the same setting the route does). The multi-group layer gets `--group <id> ` in its commands through the same `gid`. Setting row: `tasks.backlogNudgeAt` (number, default 20, min 0 = off, max 1000, category Integration beside the Stop-nudge rows, liveApply). Gate: test-backlog-nudge §3 (a cut-copy control), §3b (every turn, pre-fix route control), §3c (2 / 3 groups × 60 CJK ≤ 9600 B untrimmed with ONE paragraph; per-group-paragraph, no-item-budget and no-cap controls).

### src/task-groups.js + src/lib/task-log.js — the Activity log ARCHIVE (2.369.204, the owner 2026-10-03: "进展记录不再删除")

**Before:** data/task-groups.json kept the newest 500 Activity entries per Task Group and DROPPED the rest (`slice(-500)` at addProgress, importFromFile, importBundle) — 个人项目's 500 were 4.5 days, 工作's 12.4, VibeSpace 车道's 316 in 0.6 days. Entries dropped before this release are gone; nothing to recover.
**Store (ONE writer):** the live list still holds `LIVE_PROGRESS` (500); `_keepLive(id, list)` MOVES the overflow — `_archiveProgress` appends it (oldest first) to `data/task-groups-archive/<taskId>/<YYYY-MM>.ndjson` (the entry's own `at`, UTC month; one JSON line per entry) BEFORE the list is trimmed and saved; a crash between the two leaves the entry twice (every reader dedups by id), a failed append keeps the overflow LIVE (logged with the errno only). A month file is append-only except for a clear and a config import (each rewrites ONE month file, tmp + rename). The store's writes stay synchronous, so the flush-on-SIGTERM rule holds unchanged.
**Read:** `readProgress(id, {before, limit ≤ 200})` = the live list, then the month files newest-first (months above `before`'s skipped by name); in a month a binary search over line starts (`monthCut`, 128 KB windows — one line always fits) finds the cut, then chunks are read BACKWARDS; ≤ 4 MB per page (`ARCHIVE_READ_BUDGET`); an instant shared with the page's last entry rides along (a `before` cursor never skips one); `more` = ask again with before = the last `at`. Route: `GET /api/tasks/:id/progress?before=&limit=` (server.js, cookie; an agent's `vsst_` only for a group `groupsForSession` gives it, a `jbt_` never — with sign-in on, the cookie middleware refuses a bare Bearer first, as for every /api/tasks route).
**Every door that changes the words:** `clearProgress` looks in the live list, then the archive (`_archiveFind`: a P- id → every month; an ms `at` → its month), asks the caller's verdict of the archived entry, rewrites each month file a target (or a live entry's crash duplicate) sits in ONCE — ARCHIVE FIRST, then the live entries, ONE `_save()` — and stamps `t.archiveClearedAt` so open Task log windows re-read their archive rows; the owner's "Clear content…" and `vibespace-task progress-redact` both reach it through src/server/record-clear.js. `remove(id)` deletes the group's archive directory FIRST. `exportBundle()` carries `archive: {taskId: {YYYY-MM: ndjson}}` inside the tasks section (Backup & migrate's four touch points already carry it); `importBundle` MERGES each month by id (a cleared copy wins, time order), tmp + rename.
**Task log window (task-log.js):** `allEntries()` = the archive rows read so far + the live list — shownEntries, the selection bar, entryOf (the row menu) and Copy as Markdown all read it, so Find, Select…, Clear selected act on archive rows too. The list is newest first, so OLDER = further DOWN: a sentinel row (`.task-log-older`, 2 px) closes the list while older entries may exist; when it comes within one screen of the body's bottom (a capture scroll listener + a check after every paint) the next page (100) is read and the sentinel becomes a skeleton row (`.task-log-skel`) meanwhile — no button (the owner's rule 2026-10-03). Entries a broadcast moved out of the live list stay where the reader saw them (refresh() keeps them as archive rows). A clear that reached the archive (`archiveClearedAt` moved) bumps `older.gen` and re-reads the held rows (patched in place by key); a page begun before it is dropped (census H7 row `generation`).
**Gates:** test-progress-archive (fast, the real store in a scratch dir: moved-not-dropped, write-before-trim, a failed append keeps live, month split, a crash duplicate read once, a full walk, a shared-ms boundary, bounded bytes in a 5.7 MB month, archive clear by id / at / verdict / duplicate, delete, export + merge-import; 5 patched-copy controls); test-record-clear-census (§A `'task-groups-archive'` owned by task-groups.js, §C route row `reads`, H7 order row); test-record-clear-walk (a planted archived line probed through the route and the file, cleared by the owner's clear-many); test-record-clear-client ⑦ (chrome, zh: the Task log scrolled down past the live 500 into the archive — 620 rows once each, a skeleton seen, no button — then a clear of an archived entry patched in place).

### src/reset-credit.js — THE RESET-CREDIT VERDICT (PURE, docs/design-reset-credits.zh.md §2/§4, 2.369.157)

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the engine and p2's confirm dialog share one spelling). `resetCreditVerdict({vendor, wallHit, remainingPct, resetsAtSec, nowSec, periodSec, weekQuota, burnRate, creditsLeft, useBySec, cooldownUntilSec, replenishes, inTurn, warm, poolAlternative, ladderPosition})` → `{use, reason, valueFraction, windowFraction, waitSavedSec}`; `reason` is from the CLOSED `REASONS` set and every refusal has words (`reasonText`). COMMON PRECONDITIONS, in order: a known vendor; `wallHit === true` (NEVER proactive); `creditsLeft` not ≤ 0 (null = unknown ≠ zero — the vendor answers "nothing to reset" harmlessly); a grant not past its use-by; not inside `cooldownUntilSec` (the engine's one-try-per-limit-event floor); THE LADDER FORK — warm = `warm || inTurn`; a COLD conversation at position `wall` is refused `cold-switch-first` unless `poolAlternative === false` (null = unknown ⇒ switch first) or `ladderPosition === 'after-switch'`. OPENAI (a credit RE-OPENS the period): use at the wall at once; `valueFraction = (R−t)/P + (1−q)`; the ONE refusal is `last-credit-low-value` — `creditsLeft === 1` and `windowFraction = (R−t)/P < CREDIT_FLOOR (0.1)`, strict. THE FLOOR COMPARES THE WINDOW TERM, NOT THE SUM: at a wall q ≈ 0, so (1−q) ≈ 1 for every wall and the sum can never fall under 0.1 — §4's own example ("只剩十分之一个窗口") is the window term; an unknown R or P never refuses. ANTHROPIC (a credit REFILLS IN PLACE, the deadline unchanged — the ReLU): `valueFraction = min(1, b·(R−t)/W)`; use ⇔ ≥ 1 (the knee `kneeSec = W/b`, inclusive) ∨ use-by within `USE_BY_IMMINENT_SEC` (24 h) ∨ `replenishes`; else `below-knee-keep`, or `burn-unknown` when b/W/R are missing. `windowPaceRate({usedFraction, resetsAtSec, periodSec, nowSec})` = the window's average pace (used ÷ time since R−P; unit window-fractions/s, so W = 1) — the estimator learns utilization per DOLLAR, not per second, so it is not the pace. `describeUse(vendor, verdict, {nowSec, resetsAtSec, periodSec, creditsLeft, fmtTime})` → `{text, lines:[{key, params}]}` = THE dialog / For-you / notice sentences (openai: a new <period> window until t+P, the natural reset, the wait saved, the credits left / the last one; anthropic: refills until R, the period unchanged); keys are `i18nKey`-marked with zh+ja rows; **r2: the knee is decided on the UNROUNDED ratio `b·(R−t)/W` — rounding to 3 decimals first fired `above-knee` up to 0.05 % below W/b; only the REPORTED `valueFraction` is rounded (table row: one second below the knee ⇒ `below-knee-keep`, with the rounded-knee patched copy as its control)**; `fmtTime` defaults to an ISO minute in UTC (the client passes its locale formatter). `offerOf(x)` = the ONE sanitizer of a card's `{available, mode}` offer (positive integer + a known mode, else null), used by both normalizers. Consumer: the engine's `resetCreditRung` (only codex reaches it today — `capsOf('claude').resetCredit` is false; the anthropic table is ready for P3). Gate: scripts/test-reset-credit-verdict.mjs (fast; both vendors' tables, the knee, the floor, the sentences, five patched-copy controls, the wiring pins) + test-codex-pool §R (the real engine).

**2.369.157 r5 — THE LEAVING CARRIER'S TWO STATES.** `REFUSAL_CODES` gains `restart_pending` (`refusalLine(code, {member})`: the only conversation holding this login is being restarted onto {member} — a credit sent through it could be lost); `dialogModel` draws NO line for `restartPending.inFlight` (the refusal says it, Confirm disabled) and, for `restartPending.pending` (the pool moved, no client asked yet), the first line after the account is `…keeps this login until a client restarts it onto {member}…` (Confirm allowed). The r4 sentence "is being restarted onto" is gone — it was said when no request had gone out.

**2.369.157 p2 — THE MANUAL USE's WORDS.** `offerOf` keeps an optional `accountKey` (a plain id, `/^[\w.:@-]{1,120}$/`; anything else dropped) so a card's button knows WHICH account. `dialogModel(preview, {nowSec, fmtTime})` → `{lines, refusal, canConfirm}` = the confirm dialog's sentences as `{key, params}`: `Account: {account}`, then (openai, NOT at a wall) `The {pct}% still left in the current window is discarded.`, then `describeUse`'s lines with the wait saved ONLY at a wall (`remainingPct ≤ 0` — nobody waits on an open window); `refusal` = `refusalLine(code, {until, why, member})` for the server-named `code` (`REFUSAL_CODES`: not_supported / no_live_session / no_credits / cooldown / spend_refused; an unknown vendor ⇒ not_supported), and `canConfirm` is false whenever a refusal exists. `rosterResetOffer(u, {capable})` = the roster chip: capable ⇒ the stored count (`u.resetCredits.availableCount`, > 0) with a usable button; not capable ⇒ only a passive grant sample (`u.resetGrant {resetsLeft, useBySec}`, design §7 P2 — no producer yet) with a disabled one. Gate: test-reset-credit-ui §1/§2.

`openResetCreditDialog(app, {accountKey, sessionId?, todoId?})` → `'used'|'declined'|'closed'|'failed'` — the ONLY way a person spends a stored reset credit; three entry points call it (the Manage Agents roster's "Use…", the chat wall / arm card's button, the ask-mode For-you item) and no client file sends the raw ws `codex-reset-credit` verb (the census in test-reset-credit-ui §4). ### lane reset-path (2026-10-01) — THE FLOOR ARMS ONLY ON A CONSUME THAT WENT OUT · THE HELPER PATH · THE CARD THE CREDIT OUTLIVED · THE ANSWERED ⟳

The owner's four reports on the codex reset credit, one lane (design-reset-credits §17; incidents in kb-bugfix-invariants).

**src/reset-credit.js — the attempt's rules (PURE).** `creditAnswerOf(payload)` → `{outcome, sent, answered, keyed}`: a vendor outcome went out (a KEYED `alreadyRedeemed` = this press's reset); keyless + an error naming `idempotencyKey` = `refused-stale` (a wrapper older than the key, refused locally by codex, never sent); "timed out after" = `unanswered` (sent) unless the payload says it was never sent (`not-sent`); an answered error after a retry (attempts ≥ 2) stays `unanswered` (money-safe); any other error = answered, nothing spent. `FLOOR_OUTCOMES = reset | unanswered | no-answer`. `attemptBlock(t, {now})` → `in_flight` (written, not yet sent, ≤ `RESET_CREDIT_ACK_MS` 90 s — the 2.369.199 wrapper's worst answer is 30 + 30 + 20 s, a spend hold lives 3 min) | `cooldown` (THE floor, `RESET_CREDIT_FLOOR_MS` 10 min, from the SEND) | null. `rungBlockUntil` adds the AUTO rung's one-try-per-limit-EVENT bound (an attempt on this `<identity>|<stated reset>` that ended, whatever it ended in, is not retried before that reset — the floor no longer covers a `nothingToReset`). `REFUSAL_CODES` + `in_flight`. `helperLine(preview)` = the dialog's helper sentence (`no-session` / `wrapper-predates`, never a refusal); `dialogModel(p, {harness})` leads with `Account: {harness} · {account}` ("Codex · CLI login"). R3: `offerOf` keeps `resetsAtSec` + a sanitized `resolved`; `offerResolution(offer, cardTs, ev)` (ev = `{kind:'used', at, untilSec}` | `{kind:'reading', at, usable}`; a fact older than the card answers nothing; a reading past the card's stated reset ⇒ `reset`, a usable one ⇒ `open`); `resetCreditCardView(rc)` → `{button, line}` — the renderer and the in-place patch read it. Gates: test-reset-credit-verdict §8 (the answer / block / rung tables + 4 patched-copy controls).

**verify r3 (2026-10-01) — THE CHAIN, THE CLOCK, THE CLOSED ENUM, THE SUPERSESSION, THE TABLE.** `attemptBlock` walks the whole chain (the newest unsettled attempt that has not lapsed blocks wherever it sits; a lapsed head never hides a live one; only an all-lapsed chain is free, and the newest lapsed one is said); `priorForPress(prev, opts)` = the prior a new attempt carries (the newest unsettled, its tail cut to live entries, ≤ `MAX_PRIOR_TAIL` 8); `armedByClock(t, {now, ackMs})` = the instant the floor runs from — the send, the write for a carrier that cannot report past the ack window, else 0 — and `isUnsettled(t, {now, floorMs, ackMs})` / `unsettledInChain` / `settleByReading(t, r, opts)` / `isLapsed(t, now, opts)` are judged by the clock (the engine passes `clockOpts()`; the timers only make the verdict durable). `VENDOR_OUTCOMES` = the measured consume enum (reset / nothingToReset / noCredit / alreadyRedeemed; test-codex-protocol-drift ③ pins it equal to every table): `creditAnswerOf` reads any other word — or an answer with none — as `unknown-outcome` (sent, answered, unknown effect: FLOOR + UNSETTLED). `supersede(prior, at, opts)` stamps every prior with the newer attempt's send (`supersededAt`; `settleByReading` refuses a reading at or after it) and drops a lapsed one (nothing can settle it now); the engine calls it at `noteResetCreditSent`, `onResetCreditUnknown` and the boot revive. THE TABLE: `ATTEMPT_PHASES`, `PERSISTED_FIELDS` + `persistedView(t)` (what the engine writes), `phaseOf(t, opts)`, `attemptStep(t, ev, opts) → {t, effects: {charge, release, minted, refused, settle, walk, notice, dropped}}` — one pure step over the persisted record; a session press is refused by the block, a helper press over an unsettled chain is admitted with that attempt as its prior and its send refused (`unsettled-prior`) until a reading settled it; `skipped` = the helper's read-first said no. **verify r10 (2026-10-02) — THE WORD A RESTART LOSES, AND WHICH HALF THE BOOT GUESSES.** Three facts on the attempt record since r10: (1) `sentGuessed` (persisted) — the boot marks it ONLY on a record with no send on file (`revive()`: `!(sentAt > 0)`), and `revivedReadFirstWaiting` requires it: a press SENT before the restart keeps its send as a fact and is never re-opened by a replayed `beforeReset` push (r9 keyed on `revivedAt` alone — reproduced: a go to nobody, `not-sent`, a second key over a consume that went out). `noteResetCreditSent(t, now, {proof})` ends the guess: a `reset_credit_sent` RECORD (`proof: 'record'` — live, or read back from the file at its own instant) carries the send instant and replaces the guessed one; an ANSWER that proves a send (`proof: 'answer'`, handleResetCreditResult) ends the guess but keeps the earliest-known instant (the parity walk under a short floor caught a re-stamp to the answer's arrival). (2) THE CHARGE IS ON DISK WITH THE SEND: `noteResetCreditSent` persists AFTER `charged = true` (it persisted before and never after, so the file said charged:false for every sent-and-unanswered press and the boot charged the same consume twice — reproduced). (3) `catchUpResetCreditFromBuffer(session, id)` — THE WORD A RESTART LOSES: r9 ② takes the wrapper's push / `skipped` only when it reaches the new engine LIVE, i.e. a restart shorter than the wrapper's 25-s wait; a longer one leaves them in the wrapper's own buffer file (dtach replays nothing, the repaint goes to clients and skips chat). The codex stdout consumer calls it at `attach()` before the first live byte; it does nothing (no file read) unless THIS session has an attempt open or revived unknown; then the file's tail (512 KiB, local only) is scanned for the key's `reset_credit_sent` / `reset_credit_result` / `rate_limits_updated` records, each fed through `recordCodexQuotaSignal(session, p, null, {asOf: its stamp})` — a reading is stamped when it was taken (a pre-consume read stamped at the attach would "settle" the consume that followed it); a `beforeReset` push that a send / result of its key follows is dropped (answered before the restart); a reading older than LATE_MS is dropped; keyed sent / result always taken; a re-attach re-reads it (every keyed record is idempotent on its record). `onResetCreditSentRecord(session, payload, now)` takes `now` = asOf for a file record. The 1-s debounce window before the attach is the honest remainder (the orphan path covers it: ⑤ pinned — the floor, then the helper's read-first settles it). **verify r8 T0 (2026-10-02) — THE READ BEFORE EVERY PRESS (the owner's YES on ut-cdaa01aff0, "好的没问题"): one more vendor read per human press, BOTH carriers, never the auto rung.** `readBeforePress()` is TRUE. ONE table judges the read on both carriers — PURE `preConsumeVerdict(t, {readOk, freshWindow, freshCount, now})` → `{go, why, window?, prior?}`, rows in order: `window-moved` (the read states a window other than the one the dialog showed ⇒ no consume — what you approve is what runs; an EARLIER restatement is a move too), `prior-*` (an unsettled, not-lapsed prior ⇒ no; a prior settled landed / expired / untold ⇒ no; only one settled NOT LANDED lets the consume through; a LAPSED prior blocks nothing whether or not this very reading just settled it), `read-failed` (the read itself failed ⇒ the consume STILL goes out on the count the dialog showed, SAID — a failed read never blocks a person's press; an unsettled prior still refuses first), `no-credits` (the read counts zero ⇒ no, said), else go. **verify r2 — THE WITNESS-LESS ATTEMPT, THE CLOCK, THE LAPSE, THE EXITED APP-SERVER (the money class).** `creditsAt` is `null` when no count was known at the press — never 0 (`Number(null)` fabricated a witness no reading could contradict: "count still 1 ≥ 0" freed every unanswered consume on an unknown-count account; a stored 0 is read as unknown at boot). `settleByReading` (PURE) gained: `untold` (the reading carries a count the attempt never had — the block ends, the person is told the count the account holds now, the next press spends on it); a window restated EARLIER than the reset it had is never a credit's new window (`R1 > R0` only); one that rolled to its next natural reset within `RESET_GRACE_SEC` (60) is the clock; an attempt with no window is `expired` once `windowStartSec` (the engine's `readingWindowStart`: the reading's longest window's start) is past its send; the "past the reset" expiry waits the minute of grace. `lapseAtOf` / `isLapsed` / `attemptBlock.lapsed`: an unsettled attempt LAPSES at its wall's stated reset + grace (else `RESET_CREDIT_LAPSE_MS` 7 d after the send) — free, carried on the preview as `lapsed {sinceSec, atSec}` and said by `lapsedLine` ("the count shown may be one high"), still unsettled on its record so a late reading settles it for the ledger; the helper's `readFirst` skips a lapsed prior. `creditAnswerOf` reads a carrier that says `sent:true, answered:false` as `unanswered` whatever its words (the helper's app-server exited after taking the consume — the engine's helper-done payload carries `answered`). ### scripts/test-codex-protocol-drift.mjs + scripts/codex-protocol-census.mjs + scripts/measure-codex-protocol.mjs + scripts/fixtures/codex-app-server/ — THE CODEX PROTOCOL DRIFT GATE (lane-codex-0159, 2026-09-30)

Born of the incident: every codex reset credit failed with "Invalid request: missing field `idempotencyKey`" — the wrapper sent `consume {}` (written 2026-08-24 against an older CLI) and nothing compared the wrapper's requests with what the installed CLI accepts. **Measured: the key is required on 0.153.4 too** (the 0.153.4 binary, taken offline from the local npm cache, answers `{}` with the same words and its schema dump equals the vendored codex-server-request-responses.json byte for byte) — the credit was broken before the 0.159.3 update, which only made it visible.
- **scripts/fixtures/codex-app-server/<version>-methods.json** — MEASURED, never hand-edited: `clientRequests` (every request the CLI serves: `required` + known `properties`, from its own JSON Schema), `wrapperMethods` (the wrapper's methods + the CLI's own answer to `{}`), `serverNotifications` / `serverRequests` / `clientNotifications`, `resetCreditOutcomes`, `unknownMethodError`, `how` (incl. the strace network record). Two tables: 0.153.4 and 0.159.3.
- **scripts/measure-codex-protocol.mjs** (maintainer tool, never in a gate, never run by the server): `codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental` (launch-free) + a live app-server inside an EMPTY network namespace (`unshare -rn`, else `sudo -n unshare -n` + setpriv back to the user; neither ⇒ the live half SKIPS by name) with an empty CODEX_HOME and vendor keys stripped, each wrapper method sent with `{}`; with strace every connect/sendto is recorded and an internet-family call that SUCCEEDED aborts before anything is written (measured: 10 DNS attempts for the vendor host, all ENETUNREACH). `--codex <bin>` measures another binary; `--scratch <dir>`.

### src/lib/reconnect-queue.js + scripts/test-reconnect-storm.mjs — RECONNECT HYGIENE (chat pipeline perf lane ⑤b, 2.369.167)

  src/lib/reconnect-queue.js — THE APP'S RECONNECT QUEUE (DOM-free, timers + microtask injected; imports only view-visibility's `reconnectSlot`). `createReconnectQueue({rankOf, setTimer, clearTimer, defer, slot})` → `{enqueue, take, cancel, reset, has, snapshot, size}`. App (src/lib/app.js) owns ONE instance, `app._reconnectQueue`, built in init beside the reconnect handler with `rankOf = app._reconnectRank(view)` = `[desktop rank, window rank]` (the active desktop 0 — its minimized windows and tab hosts are next to the user — then 1 + the desktop's index; windows by the manager's order; an unknown view last). A socket drop calls `reset()` (every pending slot superseded, the `_reattachGen` rule); the terminal re-attach loop in the same handler is untouched. **Order-independent by construction:** WsManager notifies every state listener in ONE synchronous pass, so a pass = whatever enqueued before the microtask; `flush` orders it by rank and arms slot k at `reconnectSlot({suspended:true, index:k})` — the App's handler may run before or after the views'. `take(view)` = un-hidden before its slot (the caller attaches now); `cancel(view)` = dispose. Traces `reconnect:queued {slot, delay}` on the view. **WHY (inc-mtndq0vb's third layer):** after a drop every ChatView re-attached in the same tick — 19 windows in one second in the incident, 14 of them hidden; the server answers attaches FIFO (single-flight rebuilds, 2.369.16), so the windows the user was looking at waited behind the ones nobody could see. Backward compatible: client-only, no wire change — an old server sees fewer simultaneous attaches and nothing else.

  scripts/test-reconnect-storm.mjs — THE STORM HARNESS (heavy, chrome; perf chunks C and D measure on it). Per variant: a scratch worktree server (scratch.mjs paths/ports, fake HOME, `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1`) + 19 LIVE chat sessions through the real create path (`resume` of 6 MB §1c transcripts from scripts/huge-transcript-fixture.mjs; the REAL data/bin/chat-wrapper.js driving a stub `claude` that prints its stream-json init for the resumed id and idles on stdin); a headless page lays out 14 HIDDEN windows FIRST in window order (5 on desktop B, 5 on C, 2 tab hosts behind their guests, 2 minimized) and 5 displayed, then `app.ws.ws.close()`. Server arrival = the synchronous `attach-ack`; receipt stamps are UNSHIFTED onto `globalHandlers`/`_stateListeners` so no view's handler runs first. The CONTROL is a second worktree whose chat-view has the stagger neutered by a runtime marker (asserted in the bundle — esbuild folds a bare `false &&` and drops comments). Besides the product's `srv-loop-gap-ms` it runs the server with `node -r <scratch preload>` = `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay` (5 ms) logging the max delay per 250 ms — a harness-only instrument, never a production knob. Asserts (a)–(f) of the lane spec + a CONTROL-shows-the-storm leg (≥ 15/s) + one attach per window + no page exception. Every run kills its sessions (`kill` over ws, then `pkill -f <worktree>` for dtach leftovers), chrome and servers, removes worktrees/homes. `VS_STORM_ONLY=fix` is a debugging aid, never the gate. ~4 min here. **perf chunk C (2.369.167): LIVE TURNS BETWEEN DROPS** — before each drop every transcript grows by a live turn as the CLI writes it while nobody is attached (`VS_STORM_APPEND_KB`, default 64 KB; `appendLiveTurn`), so every re-attach meets a CHANGED file; the preload also counts every `.jsonl` byte the server process reads, per thread (openSync/readSync/readFileSync wrapped — readFileSync's own internal reads not counted twice; flushed as `<ms> <thread> <bytes>` per 250 ms), printed beside the product's `srv-jsonl-parse-bytes` / `srv-jsonl-parse-ms` Σ; (g) = the fix's MAIN thread reads ≤ 2 × the appended bytes + ≤ 16 KiB per session (the probes + the 4-byte zstd magic read; measured exactly 2 × appended + 19 × 8196) over the storm (TWO readers see each new byte once: this cache and the task-event scan, `scanTaskEventsFull`, incremental by byte cursor since 2.180.1) (and so does `srv-jsonl-parse-bytes`). `VS_STORM_APPEND_KB=0` restores chunk B's exact storm. **(j) r1 — THE STALL IS CONSTRUCTED (2.369.167 r1, the mirror's red on 3207e03b: ws-lagged 0, queue 0):** the first cut throttled the page's network (the runner's chrome never throttles websocket reads — its page drained the 25.6 MB burst at 0 queue) and busy-waited only after 20 s; it was green here by this page's natural lag (the UNPACED burst is cut here with no stall at all, full CPU and `taskset -c 0`). Now the stub's `VS_BIG_BURST n=<n> pace=<s>` emits 400 KB tool results one per `BIG_PACE_S` = 0.15 s, stops at the harness's `<stub>.stop` file and reports `<round> <emitted>` in `<stub>.done`; ① CONTROL: 64 paced frames on a page that drains ⇒ 0 ws-lagged, 0 traced, the PAGE socket's queue ≤ the limit (a preload column: sockets that advertised `op-seq` on an attach — the harness's own ctl socket never does, and it now drops > 64 KB frames unparsed), equal to the server; ② FREEZE: `Debugger.enable` + `Debugger.pause` (a no-op evaluate nudges it; `Debugger.paused` confirms it) BEFORE a burst of ≤ 160 frames that the server's own journal line (`a client stopped draining`) stops at once — whatever the machine's socket buffers absorb, the queue reaches the limit — then `Debugger.resume`; asserts: paused before the burst and no re-attach while frozen, exactly ONE ws-lagged over both legs, the queue after any msg frame in (limit, limit + one frame], one traced lagged + equal to the server ≤ 10 s after the resume. `VS_STORM_BIG_PACE=none` (debugging aid) sends the unpaced burst.

### src/op-seq.js + src/server/session-broadcast.js — RESUME BY SEQ + THE EXPLICIT `lagged` (chat pipeline perf lane chunk D, 2.369.167 — the one wire change)

  src/op-seq.js — PURE (imports nothing, CJS). `createOpRing({cap = 2000, maxBytes = 4 MiB})` → `{push(msg) → {seq, frame}, since(seq) → {ops, seq} | {ops:null, lagged:true, oldest, seq}, reset(), seq, oldest, size, bytes}`: `push` stamps the NEXT seq on a shallow copy and serializes ONCE — the ring keeps that exact text, so a replay is byte-identical to what a connected client received; eviction by count AND bytes (a streamed edit restates the whole content each time), the newest frame always kept; `since` answers only for a number the ring handed out (a future, negative or non-integer seq is "not covered"); `reset` forgets frames, never renumbers. `laggedVerdict({bufferedAmount, limitBytes = 4 MiB})` — strictly above, a missing reading is never a verdict. `resumeVerdict({ring, normEpoch, sinceSeq, sinceEpoch})` → `{held, replay, opSeq}` or `{held:false, why: no-since|epoch|no-ring|outside-ring, opSeq}`. `attachedWithReplay(payload, frames)` splices the frames into the payload's JSON as raw text (no parse, no re-serialization). Gate: scripts/test-op-seq.mjs (fast).

  src/server/session-broadcast.js — ORCH, THE broadcast choke point (server.js's `broadcastToSession`). ① stamps `seq` from the session's ring on `msg` frames whose `sessionId` is the session's own id (a sub-agent virtual session's frames ride the parent's clients map unstamped — its viewer has no seq to resume from); ② per client: a stamped frame is skipped for an entry marked `lagged`; an entry with `caps` ∋ `op-seq` AND `resumeArmed` (an `attached` went out on it) whose socket `bufferedAmount` exceeds the limit is marked lagged, sent ONE `lagged {sessionId, normEpoch, seq}` (seq = the last frame it was handed), and reported (`ws-lagged` event with the queue size + a journal line). NEVER cut: a client without the capability (an old tab cannot answer — today's unbounded delivery) and a capable one not yet answered by `attached` (no view exists to answer; a mark set then would silence the view that the attached creates). Non-`msg` frames are never cut (small status frames; the view needs them to stay honest). `resumeFor` / `attachedFrameText` / `armResume` / `clientCaps` are the attach's four calls (ws-handler). Memory: ≤ 2000 frames and ≤ 4 MiB of text per session, nothing that was not already sent.

  INVARIANTS: (1) 2.369.2 strengthened — a same-epoch re-attach inside the ring rebuilds NOTHING (no loadHistory, not even the identical compare, no catch-up fetch); outside it / on a new epoch the ladder (identical-skip → `_reattachCatchUp` / `_fullViewReset` + 0–500 ms jitter) is unchanged. (2) Ordering: the verdict and the send are synchronous; the replay is the ring's frames verbatim; the normalizer is still written only through feedLive/feedPeerCard. (3) No silent drop, no unbounded queue for a capable client. (4) Both capability gates (client `caps`, server `opSeq`). (5) attach-ack + the re-attach ladder + the kill ack/resend untouched. (6) Bounded memory. (7) inc-msp3klen's class (a reply 14.5 min late on a wedged socket) is now VISIBLE as `ws-lagged`; the 2.322.0 watchdog stays the self-heal.

  Gates: test-op-seq (fast, pure table), test-attach-rebuild ⑤ (the REAL normalizer + the REAL broadcast + fake ws clients: seq on every frame, the cut, a byte-identical replay, outside-ring / epoch ⇒ full, the reset — red on the unfixed tree against a verbatim copy of the 2.369.160 broadcast), test-session-schema (`_opRing`), test-attach-ack (heavy, real server: an unknown epoch still gets ack then a plain attached; a covered seq gets ack then held), test-reconnect-storm (heavy: (h) slab frames fix 0 / control 19 + bytes on the wire, (i) records in flight across the drop ⇒ every window equals the server, (j) the lagged leg).

### src/agent-tool-rules.js — VIBESPACE'S OWN AGENT TOOLS NEVER ASK PER COMMAND (PURE, lane L, 2026-09-25)

**verify-r6 K1–K5 (2026-09-28) — THE PERMISSION CARD SHOWS WHAT ALLOW RUNS, AND ALLOW RUNS THE REQUEST** (verify-r6 agentA; built by a fix agent in a snapshot, reviewed and applied as ONE commit — the five share this module, helper-ask.js and the card). **K1 (HIGH) the helper card** showed `askTarget(ask)` — the command's FIRST line, ≤ 200 chars, no ellipsis — while Allow sent the whole input (`ls -la⏎curl … | sh` read "Bash ls -la"): `askSubject(ask)` is the whole request, drawn in a wrapping `<pre>` above Allow and carried whole in the For-you detail (cut past 6000 and said so); `askTarget` is only a summary that marks its cut. **K2 (HIGH) the plain words** dropped sub-commands (`vibespace-browser get text | sort -o ~/.bashrc` read "Agent browser · Read the page"): a filter / quiet command is left out only when EVERY argument is on its row (`FILTER_ARGS` / `QUIET_ARGS`, `inertArgs`); any unquoted redirection (glued too), run-time expansion, bare assignment or `${X:=}` / `$[` names the command or drops the plain words; the card ALWAYS shows the raw command under them. **K3 (MED) Always Allow** named only its rules: PURE `updatesText` spells every update (a mode change, directories, unknown types) as visible lines on the card. **K4 (LOW-MED) the server writes its own record, not the client's** (see kb-api `permission-response`). **K5 (MED) hidden characters:** every hidden character on every permission surface is drawn as `⟦U+XXXX⟧`; when any is present the card warns, shows the whole marked request, Allow needs a second press after 600 ms (`secondPressVerdict`), Always Allow is withheld (card and server). Gates: test-helper-ask ⑳, test-agent-tool-rules ⑭, controls per fix.

PURE (imports nothing; CJS — required by the claude adapter, bundled into the chat renderer, read by the tests). The naive-user study 2 (SharedContext/vibespace-naive-study-2-collab-20260925.md): in the product-default permission mode every browser step was a "Permission: Bash" card (7–15 per task), "Always Allow" never stopped the next one, and a person refused `vibespace-browser close --all` fearing it closed other people's browsers.

- **`AGENT_TOOL_RULES`** (frozen): `{tool, verbs: null | [verb], why, held?, ask?}`. Whole tools: vibespace-browser / -status / -task / -ask / -docs / -msg / -window / -channels. **r2: `vibespace-page` is VERB-LISTED** (`PAGE_VERBS`: list, kit) and HOLDS `publish` — which is also its `ask` verb (owner 2026-09-25: publishing puts a page under the user's name, `--public` a link anyone can open; it keeps asking). Every `ask` verb is a `held` verb, never a listed one (suite ①). The browser row's `why` states THE TRADE-OFF: anything the agent can read it can type or upload into a page without asking (an upload from the credential stores is refused by the CLI, src/browser-verbs.js). `vibespace-job` is VERB-LISTED (`JOB_VERBS`: list, show, poll, answers, logs, progress, ask, docs, stop, rm, notify, notify-cron, announce, subscribe, unsubscribe) and HOLDS `run` / `start` (they run any shell command via `sh -c`, outside the CLI's own Bash check) and `access` (a grant of control is the user's). **`HELD_TOOLS`** = every other `vibespace-*` AGENT_TOOLS entry with its reason (vibespace-exit runs commands on another machine; the statusline / keeper / hooks / login helper are not agent verbs). The suite censuses hosts.js AGENT_TOOLS into exactly one of the two, and every job verb into listed-or-held — a new tool or verb must be decided here.
- **`claudeAllowRules()`** → `Bash(<tool>:*)` / `Bash(<tool> <verb>:*)` for a verb-listed tool. **`claudeAskRules()`** (r2) → `Bash(vibespace-page publish:*)`, carried as `permissions.ask` in the same `--settings` JSON: 2.1.281 decides deny > ask > allow and checks ask rules before the permission mode, so a user's own broader allow never pre-approves a publish, and a CLI without ask support still asks because publish is not in the allow list at all. **r3 (integrator 2026-09-26) — the ask rule follows the SPAWN mode**: since the ask check outranks the mode, the rule may only ride a spawn whose mode asks anyway — **`ASK_RULE_MODES`** (frozen: default, manual, acceptEdits, plan); **`claudeAskRulesFor(mode)`** = `claudeAskRules()` there, `[]` anywhere else (bypassPermissions: publish runs as it always did; dontAsk: refused as it always was; auto / unknown: the mode decides); **`spawnPermissionMode(argv)`** = `--dangerously-skip-permissions` ⇒ 'bypassPermissions' (2.1.281 `Rvr`'s first candidate), else the LAST `--permission-mode <v>` / `=<v>`, else null (no flag — the CLI's own setting, unknown at spawn). The allow list never depends on the mode (verb-listed everywhere). SPELLING, measured on 2.1.281: `X:*` is the legacy PREFIX form the validator still accepts ("Bash(npm run:*) - prefix matching (legacy)") and the matcher reads as `cmd === prefix || cmd.startsWith(prefix + " ")` after collapsing blank runs; the newer `X *` wildcard compiles to `^X( .*)?$` — the same set. The legacy spelling is shipped because remote hosts may run an older CLI. A COMPOUND line is split by the CLI and every sub-command must be allowed on its own, so `vibespace-browser open x && rm -rf y` still asks for the `rm`.
- **`parseRule` / `ruleMatchesCommand`** = a mirror of the CLI's `ZZt`/`xOe` (prefix / wildcard / exact) for the tests; **`coveredByAgentToolRules`** answers for ONE simple command (a compound ⇒ false; a matching shipped ASK rule ⇒ false — ask beats allow).
- **`alwaysAllowFor(suggestions, command)` → `{updates, withheld}`** (r2; **`widenSuggestions(suggestions, command)`** = its `.updates`) — the CLI's "Always Allow" suggestion is the command's first two words (`fCn`: `s.slice(0,2).join(" ")`, `ten()` writes `Bash(<words> *)` to localSettings for EVERY command); for a whole tool of ours it becomes the whole-tool rule, a listed verb its verb rule. **A HELD tool or a held verb** (`vibespace-job run *` = every future shell command through that verb; `vibespace-exit run *`; a pattern over a verb-listed tool such as `vibespace-job *` / `:*` / `r*`) is NARROWED to the exact command line the card is for — the CLI's own `een` form, ruleContent = the command, no ` *` — or WITHHELD when it cannot be spelled (a compound: which sub-command is remembered is the CLI's split; a line holding `*`, which 2.1.281's `Ut` would read as a wildcard; a newline; another verb; a head that is not the bare tool); an exact rule for a held command is kept. **An ASK verb is always withheld** (no allow rule can win over the shipped ask rule). An update left with no rule is dropped; foreign rules untouched; deduped; never mutates. `withheld` = the sentence the card shows where the button would be (`WITHHELD_ASK` "Publishing a page asks every time — Always Allow is not offered." / `WITHHELD_HELD`). **`rulesText`** spells the rules for the tooltip.
- **`splitShell`** — a quote-aware split into simple commands (`;` `&&` `||` `|` newlines; `2>&1`-style words kept); substitution / backticks / heredoc / subshell / an unbalanced quote ⇒ null (the card shows the raw command). **`describeAgentCommand(cmd)`** → `{browser, tools, steps:[{tool, verb, key, params}], others, scope}` or null. **r2 — THE CARD WEARS OUR FACE ONLY FOR THE EXACT HEAD THE CLI'S RULE TRUSTS:** a word is read as one of our tools (or a filter / a quiet command) only when it IS the bare name — 2.1.281 never path-strips a head on the allow path, so `./data/bin/vibespace-browser open x` / `/tmp/evil/vibespace-browser open x` DO ask, and dressing that card as "Permission: Agent browser — Open x" is the one card a naive user clicks Allow on; the same for a `VAR=value` prefix outside `SAFE_ENV` (`VIBESPACE_BROWSER=`, `AGENT_BROWSER_*=` — `PATH=`, `NODE_OPTIONS=` choose what runs). Such a segment is named in `others` AS WRITTEN (`/tmp/evil/vibespace-browser`, `PATH=… vibespace-browser`; a long path keeps its tail), and a line of nothing else is null (the raw Bash card); the pending / error / done tool-card heads go through the same classifier. Pipes into filters (grep/head/tail/jq…), `sleep`/`echo` and the safe `VAR=value` prefixes are read past; anything else in the line is named in `others` (and then `browser` is false — a line that also runs `pgrep` is never dressed as the browser); a redirect into a file is not the tool's act. Every `key` is an English sentence behind the `i18nKey()` marker (zh+ja in the dictionaries; the client renders with t()); `SCOPE_CLOSE_ALL` = "Closes only this conversation's browser — browsers of other sessions are not touched." **`agentCommandText(input)`** = claude's `command` string or codex's argv (`bash -lc <script>` → the script). DISPLAY ONLY — never a permission decision.
- **r2 display words (F6):** `vibespace-job rm|stop` ⇒ "Stop or remove one of its background jobs", `notify-cron` ⇒ "Schedule a reminder that wakes this conversation", `access` (held — its card still appears) ⇒ "Let others see or control one of its background jobs"; `vibespace-page list` ⇒ "List the pages it published" (zh + ja; its retired `kit` verb's words left with it, lane design-docs).
- **`CODEX_NOTE`** — why codex gets nothing: its only per-command allow is an execpolicy `.rules` file under CODEX_HOME (no per-spawn flag in 0.154.0 — a write into the user's own config), and its default workspace-write sandbox with network on already runs these tools without asking.

Consumers: src/adapters/claude-code.js (the spawn's `--settings permissions.allow` + — in a mode that asks anyway, r3 — `permissions.ask`, row `claude.allowAgentTools`), src/lib/chat-renderers.js (plain words, the browser face, the widened / narrowed / withheld Always Allow). Gates: scripts/test-agent-tool-rules.mjs (fast, 134) + scripts/test-new-session-dialog.mjs (heavy, 58); the upload refusal: test-browser-verbs.

### src/browser-stream.js — MULTIVIEW (lane P, docs/design-browser-multiview.zh.md §2 A1 / §4 B-89d0)

**THE STRIP'S LIST.** `browserListFor(status, {activity, helpers})` = the ONE list the Agent browser window's strip and its `own/cap` chip read, derived from the keeper's status answer (GET /api/browser/session/:id) and nothing else: `attachments` (lease order) ∪ the session's OWN managed ephemeral browser (`ephemeral`, never a child's record, never another key's) ∪ `children` (by number). Rows `{ref, kind, profileId, alias, label, state, driver, isDefault, owners, helper}`: `ref` = what a strip tab / a pop-out asks the bridge for (a profile id, `EPHEMERAL_REF` = `~ephemeral` — never a valid alias or id —, a child handle); `state` = `running` (only the client's `activity` knows a command is in flight) / `idle` (live) / `released` (not live) / `ended` (failed); `driver` = `you` when the keeper's `inputs` say the user holds that pair (a child's input key is ITS handle), else `agent` / `helper`; `owners` = how many OTHER conversations hold the profile (a count, never a name). Every ok target carries `ref`; `hello` names `ref` + `handle`. **HELPER NAMING BY WITNESS:** `taskOpeningsOf` (a parent-line Task/Agent tool_use → `{id, description, agentType}`), `newChildWitnessesOf` (a sidechain Bash tool_use whose command runs `vibespace-browser … new-child`, `NEW_CHILD_RE`), `witnessClosesOf` (a sidechain user record's tool_results → `{id, text}`, text capped 4 KiB), `namesHandle(text, handle)` (a WHOLE token — `….1` is not named by `….10`), `bindHelpers(state, ev)` (PURE, returns a new state: events `task` / `witness` (a window OPENS) / `child` (a mint) / `witness-close` (the window CLOSES and is judged); **lane P verify (2026-09-26, finding 4): paired at the CLOSE, never by order** — a child is named only when EXACTLY ONE mint arrived inside that witness's window, NO other witness was open at any moment of it (`overlapped`), and the result's text names that handle; a mint arriving while no witness is open is `orphan` ("Helper N" for good, never claimed by a later witness — a `new-child` run inside a script, a witness the JSONL watcher delivers late, a background Bash); `mints` keeps ≤ 2 (two already means "not one"); bounded 64/64/128. The old rule paired the open halves by ORDER, so a script's mint inside another helper's window took that helper's Task description), `helperNames(state)` (handle → the Task's description, only for a witnessed child). `VIEWER_CONTROL_TYPES` gains `pass` (`viewerMessageVerdict` → `{kind:'pass', to}`, lane P verify finding 3). The twin of helper-ask.js / helper-asks.js for the asks a conversation's OWN turn is parked on. ORCH `src/server/main-asks.js`: `install({userTodos, sessionKeyFor, activeSessions, readAskedAt, persistAskedAt})` (server.js, on the helper's line) adds `sync` as a SECOND pending-asks observer (normalizers `addAsksObserver`, beside the helpers' one slot); `sync(session, now)` reads the session's waiting MAIN asks (`mm.pendingAsks()` minus helpers, else `pendingAsksOf(mm.messages)` — codex / ACP keep no pending level; their permission ops reach it through feedLive's `permissionOpsVersion`, counted in MessageWindow `_emit`), resolves every open `main-ask` item whose request no longer waits, and files ONE item at 60 s (origin `agent`, kind `action`, urgency `high`; user-todos `ACTION_IDENTITY['main-ask'] = 'requestId'` = one item per ask; an OPEN item for the request IS the filing — a restart's rebuilt card, even renamed, never files a second). No visible-window skip. The first-seen instant rides session meta `mainAskedAt` (written on change, order-insensitive) — a restart files at 60 s from the ASK's instant. `forget(session)` (session-stdout exit path + ws kill path) clears timers and resolves the items. Client: `main-ask` is a CARD action (inbox-reply: no typed reply), the For-you click lands on the card in its window (user-todos-actions jump → goToWindow, the desktop switch), the detail renders verbatim. Gate: test-parked-ask-inbox (fast).

### message-manager.js — lane S1 (a helper's permission ask)

`_processControlRequest`: in the PARENT normalizer (`_subView` false) a `helperAskOf(raw)` ask goes to `_noteHelperAsk` → the helper's Agent card (`_taskMsgFor(null, agentId)`) gets `helperAsks: [{…ask, resolved, at}]` (edit op `{helperAsks}`), or the ask is HELD per agent id (`_helperOrphans`) until a `taskMsgByTaskId.set` site adopts it (`_adoptHelperOrphans` at all three — a rebuild replays task records after the transcript). A helper's OWN view (`sub-…`) attaches the ask to its tool card as always; an ask whose tool card is not there yet is held by tool_use_id (`_askStash`) and applied when the tool_use is minted. `_processControlResponse` / `_processControlCancel` also settle a helper ask (`allowed`/`denied` / `cancelled`) and drop a held one; **a WITHDRAWAL wins over our own answer (verify r2)** — 2.1.281 removes a request's abort listener in its `finally` the moment it settles (read in the binary), so a `control_cancel_request` for a request we already answered proves the answer reached the CLI after the withdrawal and was dropped (measured: 4 of 10 race rounds read "✓ Allowed" on a stopped helper); `_settleHelperAsk(rid, event)` — **verify r3: the ONE writer of `resolved`, and it writes only what THE TABLE says** (`askTransition(askState(ask, card), event)` over `ASK_RECORD_EVENTS`: `record-allow`/`record-deny` from a control_response, `withdraw` from a control_cancel_request, `result-allow`/`result-deny` from `noteHelperResult(toolUseId, text, isError, emit)` — the helper's tool_result for the ASKED call, live from the stdout consumer's two sidechain sites through normalizers' `noteHelperResults`, at a rebuild from session-store's `helperResults`; `_resolutionFromResult` picks which); the override (withdraw beats our answer), "a record beats a derived end" and "nothing else overwrites a settled ask" are CELLS, not code here (test-helper-ask ⑨: the control is a patched TABLE bound into a copy of this file by absolute path). `setHelperAskedAt(map)` = the persisted first-seen instants a rebuilt ask is stamped with (verify r3). `_emit` re-derives the pending set after any edit carrying `permission` / `helperAsks` / `taskInfo` and emits ONE `meta` op `pending-asks` per change (`pendingAsks()`, `pendingAsksVersion`, over `_askIds` = the cards that ever asked). `helperAskById`, `helperCallOf`, `helperAskRecordsFor` serve the gate's routing and seeding. `_taskMsgFor` finds a card by its MINTED id (`<session>:t:<tool_use_id>`, role tool) when no index holds it — a background helper's launch ack is an ARRAY of text blocks in real records, so the ack synthesis never indexed an Agent card and a restart's task replay found nothing. Gate: test-helper-ask ②③⑥.

### src/normalizers.js — lane S1: the helper's view sees the control records

`feedLive` (and `drainQueue` after a rebuild) hands every `control_request` / `control_response` / `control_cancel_request` to the helper's own view too (`routeToHelperView`: the ask's helper through the parent card or `session._taskRecords`, an answer/withdrawal through `helperAskById`) — so an answer from EITHER window settles BOTH cards — and tells the ONE pending-asks observer (`setAsksObserver`, the ORCH inbox) when `pendingAsksVersion` moved. `seedHelperView(session, ptuid, sub)` hands a view created after its asks (the stdout consumer's two creation sites, the ws live attach) the parent's unanswered asks for that helper; `rebuildHistory` seeds every existing view and notifies after its drain. Gate: test-helper-ask ②③⑤⑥ (a patched copy without the route leaves the helper's card button-less). **Verify r3:** `noteHelperResults(session, msg)` (the stdout consumer's two sidechain sites) hands a helper's `user` tool_result record to `mm.noteHelperResult` — the table's result rows (a sidechain record never reaches the parent normalizer otherwise); held behind the rebuild gate (`_rebuildQueue` kind `helper-result`). `rebuildHistory(…, {helperResults})` applies session-store's `helperResults()` AFTER the transcript + the task replay (a record wins over a derived end; the write law makes the order faithful) and stamps `mm.setHelperAskedAt(session._helperAskedAt)` first.

**Verify r4:** `rebuildHistory` calls `mm.sealPendingAsks()` (MessageManager: `_asksSig` = the rebuilt list's signature) before `notifyAsks` — the attach payload carries `pendingAsks`, so the first live edit after a restart emits a `pending-asks` op only for a CHANGE (before: an unchanged, often empty, set was re-announced on the first lifecycle edit — the effect walk saw it). `pendingHelperApprovals(session)` = the helpers' waiting asks in `pendingPermissions`' shape (`{requestId, toolName, input, kind:null, resolved:null, helperCall}`, `helperCall` = the parent's Agent call) for the takeover's stale sweep (browser-handback; wired in mounts-plugins-wiring as `approvals.pendingHelpers`). Gate: test-helper-ask ⑬ (r4) + ⑰.

### ws-handler.js — lane S1

`permission-response` (verify r3): the whole case is ONE lookup — `helper-asks.answerFrame(data, {activeSessions, adapterRegistry, feedLive})` (which session answers, what it knows, what the table says a press does from that state) — and a refusal is sent as `{type:'error', scope:'action', code: permission-settled | permission-unrouted, settled: <state>, message}` to the window that pressed (its card flipped itself optimistically); ws-handler calls neither `settledState` nor `answerPermission` itself (test-helper-ask ⑤, test-attach-rebuild, test-browser-takeover pins).
