**Download (lane viewer-download, 2.369.212):** every window that shows ONE file can download it through **src/lib/file-download.js** — `hostParam(host)` (THE `&host=<id>` spelling; Files' `_hp()` is it), `fileDownloadUrl(path, host)` (`/api/download?path=…`, the route's Content-Disposition names the file), `startFileDownload({path, host, dirty})` (a `/api/file/info` stat on the file's machine first — a refusal is an error toast — then a temporary `<a download>` click; a dirty editor adds one "saved version" toast), `fileDownloadButton` / `wireFileDownload(winInfo, target)` (the SVG button; the target rides on `winInfo._fileDownload`, which the title-bar menu's `window.download` row reads). `FileViewer.open` re-seats the window's button after every render (`_seatDownload`: the Word toolbar right after "Open in LibreOffice" / before the page count, the image or archive toolbar, else `.viewer-download-float` beside the ⟳); HexViewer and CodeEditor wire it in their constructors. Files' row Download starts through the same helper. Census: scripts/test-viewer-download.mjs (every registry viewer kind → a wired window, unlisted = red); heavy: scripts/test-viewer-download-chrome.mjs.

`FileViewer.open` (a viewer window: `/api/file/info` for binary detection, the floating ⟳ reload with `_bustTs`) and `FileViewer.renderInto(container, …)` (shared by the window and the explorer's preview panel) dispatch by `getViewerType(ext)` from file-types.js; `RENDERED_VIEWERS` is the if-chain's list (test-window-binding-model pins them equal). **The docx branch (lane docx-viewer, 2026-09-27)** asks the PURE `viewerVerdict(ext)` FIRST: a legacy binary `.doc`/`.dot` (file-types routes `doc` to viewer 'docx') gets `showDocxRefusal(container, refusalText('binary-word', t))` — a named sentence, no fetch (the old path ended in JSZip's "Can't find end of central directory"); everything else goes to `renderDocxViewer(container, rawUrl, { signal: ctl.signal })` in src/lib/docx-viewer.js. file-viewer.js no longer imports docx-preview (docx-viewer.js is its ONE importer — a pin). **Superseded renders:** renderInto captures its own `AbortController` (`const ctl = container._viewerCtl = …`); its catch returns early when `ctl.signal.aborted` — a render that loses the race to a newer one (the explorer preview moved to the next file, the window closed) never writes its error over its successor's container. Gate: test-docx-viewer-model ⑫ (wiring pins).
**"Open in LibreOffice" (§7.9 of docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md, lane office-desktop follow-up, 2026-09-27):** the docx branch hands the viewer `office: FileViewer._officeOpener(app, filePath, host)` — `{file, open(anchor)}` or null (no button: no door on the page, or a path the verdict refuses). The app is the PURE **`openWithVerdict({file: filePath, machine: {hostId: h, fileHost: h}})`**'s `catalogId` (the file's own module — Writer for .docx), NEVER a hard-coded exec / catalog id / route; `file` = the verdict's folded REAL path on the file's machine (the window's `filePath`, never its host-labelled title); `h` = the FILE's host (null = this machine) — the app runs where the file is. A click: `app.officeOfferAt(anchor, {host: h, file})` FIRST (LibreOffice absent there ⇒ the explorer row's sentence + "Install LibreOffice on <machine>…" under the button, done), else **THE DOOR** `app.openWithDesktopApp({catalogId: v.catalogId, file: v.file, host: h})`, which says its own refusals; a throw is a toast. The explorer's preview panel (renderInto with the explorer's app + host) gets the same button. ### src/lib/docx-viewer.js — the Word viewer's DOM half

`renderDocxViewer(container, rawUrl, {signal})` builds `.docx-viewer` = `.media-toolbar.docx-toolbar` (role toolbar) + `.docx-scroll` (the surround, `var(--bg-workspace)`, padding 16/24 px, `scrollbar-gutter: stable` so fit width never oscillates with the scrollbar) ⊃ `.docx-status` ("Rendering…", painted before the parse via a double rAF bounded by 120 ms) + `.docx-sizer` (the scaled page stack's size; `margin: 0 auto` centres, overflow hidden) ⊃ `.docx-host` (absolute, `width: max-content`, `transform: scale(T)` from the top-left, `.docx-pending` = visibility hidden until shown) whose **open shadow root** holds the library's style box, body box and `PAPER_CSS` (after them — a specificity tie goes to us). Invariants, each measured (kb-features §DOCX has the numbers):
- **Everything the library writes lives in the shadow root.** Its CSS text is unescaped (style ids, font names, numbering text); in the light DOM a crafted style font name restyled `<body>` (test-docx-viewer ⑪ control), and the app's own rules distorted the document. Never move the render back to the light DOM.
- **Paper:** `.docx-wrapper` transparent, padding 0, `position: relative` (page `offsetTop`s are wrapper-relative); each `section.docx` `background: var(--paper)` (defined once in style.css `:root`, white in every theme) + `box-shadow: var(--shadow-window)`, 16 px apart. No literal colour here or in viewers.css's docx block (pins). The document's inline colours (`w:background`, runs) always win.
- **Before render, on the parsed document** (`parseAsync` → mutate → `renderDocument`): `applyHeaderInheritance` (PURE `inheritHeaderFooterRefs` over every section's props — Word's Link to Previous, per type), `applyStyleTabs` (PURE `styleTabsResolver` — a paragraph with no stops of its own gets its style's via basedOn: the library reads them one line too early), `applySymbolBullets` (PURE `symbolBullet` — Symbol/Wingdings private-use bullets → Unicode), `interceptAltChunks` (the library is handed '' and the real HTML is stashed), `registerEmbeddedFonts` (FontFace API on `document.fonts`, faces + blob URLs removed on abort — `ignoreFonts: true` because Chrome ignores `@font-face` in a shadow root).
- **The tab-stop pass runs at NET scale 1.** With `experimental: true` the library schedules `setTimeout(pass, 500)` at the end of render and measures with getBoundingClientRect (which includes the body's UI-scale zoom AND our transform) against a pixel→point ratio from `offsetWidth` (which includes neither). So the host carries `scale(1 / uiScale())` while hidden, and — when the render produced any `.docx-tab-stop` — a `sleep(500)` queued AFTER the library's timer (same delay, later ⇒ runs after) gates the reveal. A window with no width yet (background tab, hidden desktop) waits (`laidOut`) before rendering at all.
- **After render, before reveal:** `neutraliseLinks` (PURE `linkVerdict`: external ⇒ `target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer` + title; `#name` ⇒ `data-docx-anchor`, a shadow-root click listener scrolls to `shadow.getElementById(name)` without touching location.hash; anything else loses its href + `.docx-link-blocked` + a title naming the scheme), `rehostAltChunks` (each library iframe replaced by a fresh `sandbox=""` iframe whose srcdoc starts with a `default-src 'none'` CSP meta).
- **Zoom state** `{mode: 'fit'|'scale', scale}`: `applyScale(T, anchor)` keeps the content point under the anchor fixed (the pointer for Ctrl+wheel, the pane's top-centre for buttons), sets the transform and the sizer to `W×T` / `H×T` (`W`/`H` = the host's unscaled offset size), re-measures page tops. Fit width = `fitWidthScale(scroll.clientWidth, W)` (W = the widest page) re-run by a ResizeObserver on the scroller; a ResizeObserver on the host follows late images/fonts. The mode + scale persist in `localStorage['vibespace.docx-zoom']` (`parseZoomPref`/`serializeZoomPref`). At reveal a scroll wider than the pane is centred.
- **Toolbar** from the PURE `toolbarModel(state, t)`: nodes created once keyed by item id and PATCHED (text, title, aria-label, disabled, `.active`/aria-pressed) — never rebuilt; icon-only buttons carry `UI_ICONS.zoomOut`/`zoomIn` + title + aria-label; the count (`pageIndexAt` on a rAF-throttled scroll) is empty while rendering. `.docx-toolbar` leaves 44 px on the right for the viewer window's floating ⟳ reload.
- **Refusals:** the fetched bytes are sniffed (`sniffVerdict`) before JSZip sees them — 'ole' / 'empty' / 'other' ⇒ the root is removed and `showDocxRefusal` names it. A fetch/parse failure throws to renderInto's red `.empty-hint`; an abort at any await returns null silently.
- **Timing marks:** `performance.measure('docx-parse' | 'docx-render')` (latest only; marks cleared) — test-docx-viewer ⑧ reads them.
- **"Open in LibreOffice" (§7.9):** `renderDocxViewer(…, {signal, office})` — `office = {file, open(anchor)}` from file-viewer.js (which decides what a click does); this module only draws the model's `office` item (the `external` SVG + its words in `.docx-tool-label`, `aria-label` = the name, `title` = the sentence of what happens; no `aria-pressed` — an action, not a toggle) and calls `office.open(button)` once per click (a second click while the first is on its way does nothing). The item is `live`: enabled while the page still renders — and never disabled at all (a machine without LibreOffice is answered by the click, never by a greyed button). CSS: the bar is a size container; under 520 px the words hide and the icon stays (still named).

`ZOOM_MIN/MAX` 0.25/4, `ZOOM_STEPS` (the −/+ ladder), `FIT_PAD` 24, `ZOOM_PREF_KEY` 'vibespace.docx-zoom', `WHEEL_DIVISOR` 500. `clampScale`; `fitWidthScale(paneW, pageW, {pad})` (no size ⇒ 1, never 0/NaN); `zoomStep(scale, dir)` (a between-rungs scale goes to the NEXT rung in that direction); `wheelScale(scale, deltaY)` (×e^(−deltaY/500), one notch ≈ one rung, symmetric); `zoomLabel`; `pageIndexAt(scrollTop, pageTops, {viewportH, scrollH})` (probe line a third down; at the end of the scroll ⇒ the last page; −1 without pages); `viewerVerdict(ext)` (docx/docm/dotx/dotm render, doc/dot refuse 'binary-word'); `sniffVerdict(bytes)` ('zip' | 'ole' | 'empty' | 'other'); `refusalText(code, t)`; `linkVerdict(href)` (an ALLOWLIST — http/https/mailto external, `#name` anchor, every other scheme incl. a relative target blocked; ASCII whitespace/controls stripped before the scheme is read, as a browser does); `inheritHeaderFooterRefs(sections)` (per type, inputs untouched); `styleTabsResolver(styles)` (memoised, basedOn chain, cycle-safe); `SYMBOL_BULLETS` + `symbolBullet(levelText, font)` (the font decides: U+F0A7 is a club in Symbol, a square in Wingdings; unknown font ⇒ only U+F0B7); `parseZoomPref`/`serializeZoomPref` (junk ⇒ fit); `toolbarModel(state, t, {office})` (ids fit · actual · out · zoom · in · spacer · [office] · pages; every human string through the injected t; `office` = the file's basename ⇒ the "Open in LibreOffice" item: icon `external` + words, `aria`, `title` naming the file, `live`, never `disabled`, no `pressed`). ### src/stash-summary.js + src/server/stash-handover.js + src/lib/stash-strip.js — WHAT WAITS FOR AN AGENT (2026-09-27, NEW)

### src/server/browser-keeper.js — the switch's START-FAILURE ROLLBACK + the digest's backends (2026-09-27)

`switchBackend` commits `p.provider = to` before `start()`, so ANY refusal `start()` throws used to leave the profile stranded on a backend that cannot start. Now every throw puts the provider back, clears a seed the switch minted, commits, starts the OLD browser once when it ran before the switch (a browser that was not running is not started by a rollback — nobody asked for it) and rethrows the original refusal with `restored` (the profile is as it was) / `from` / `to` attached; `fail()` in routes/browser.js spreads exactly those three. `switcherView` hands the rows the profile's leases + `inputsView()` + a `binaryOf` (the cloak executable re-shaped, `configured` = the setting is non-empty; null for every other row and for a paired machine's profile) + the install facts, and answers `live`. `installVerdict` = `SW.installFacts` with `npm = whichOnPath('npm') !== null` (the POST's own probe) — GET, the view and Manage Agents share it. The digest carries `backends[id] = backendFact + choices`; `choicesFor(id)` answers the agent's blocked route.

### src/record-clear.js — "Clear content…" (2026-09-28, the owner's ask)

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the server, the client bundle and the suites share it). The owner: a peer agent wrote content from an unrelated mailbox into the 工作 Task Group's records, the product had no way to scrub it, and a hand edit of data/ is forbidden (the running server owns the stores; the group log is append-only). ONE definition of: the CLOSED set of record kinds (`activity` · `todo` · `status` · `job` · `group-message`); `clearedFields(kind, record)` = the text fields a clear replaces (`text` op: a non-empty string becomes `CLEARED_TEXT`; `drop`: a present non-empty value becomes null; `empty`: a list becomes [] — a job's panel answers; verify r3: a job's `interaction.pending` — the ASK it waits on — is dropped with the words, the engine flips the job back to `up`), record-aware for ONE case (a Background-Work For-you item's `sessionName` carries the job's name ⇒ dropped); `applyClear(record, {kind, by, at})` IN PLACE (a live job object keeps its runtime-only fields) → `{changed, paths}` — nothing held words ⇒ `changed:false`, no stamp (an already-cleared record keeps its FIRST stamp; a state-only status entry is never marked); `clearedRecord` = the same on a copy; `clearVerdict({kind, caller, record, key?})` — owner: any; agent: only its OWN session's record (activity `session` ∈ its keys incl. the pre-conversation `webui:<id>`; todo: its key + `origin:'agent'` + no producer `action`/`i18n` — a helper's ask under its key is the server's; status: its key + `setBy:'agent'`; job: its conversation + not user-created; group-message: its conversation + a message, never a system record); a FORK still borrowing its parent's id (`_forkRequested`) ⇒ `pending_fork`; a job token ⇒ `job_token`; every refusal a code in `REFUSALS` with its HTTP status and plain sentence. THE SENTENCE IS A STRUCTURE: stores write the English key `"[cleared at the user's request]"` and `clearedAt`/`clearedBy` ('owner' | the clearing agent's session key); `clearedAt` IS the flag (never `cleared`, which session-status history already uses for "the status was cleared"); `CLEARED_WORDS` = the owner's words (zh 已按用户要求清除 · ja ユーザーの要請により消去済み), which live in i18n-zh.js / i18n-ja.js only. `foldClears(records, index)` = a group log as every reader sees it (replacement records dropped, every record a replacement or the group's `cleared` index names cleared, order kept). `recordAt` / `recordWords` / `previewWords` = what the confirm dialog names. Gate: test-record-clear (fast).

### src/server/record-clear.js + src/routes/records-clear.js — THE entry point and the owner's routes

ORCH. `create({tasks, userTodos, sessionStatus, getJobs, getGroups, log})` → `clear(item, {caller})` / `clearMany(items, {caller})`: the caller is judged before any lookup (a job token never learns whether an id exists), items are grouped by STORE CONTAINER (one Task Group, one session key, one agent group, all todos, all jobs) so a batch is ONE write + ONE broadcast per container, each store's door is called with `allow = clearVerdict` asked of every record right before it changes, and ONE journal line per container call: `[clear] <kind> <container> — <n> cleared by <owner|key>: <ids>` (ids and counts only — repeating the words would re-publish them into journalctl / the opslog; a failure is `… — FAILED: <why>`). A job's clear CASCADES to its For-you items (their words name it). The routes (`POST /api/records/clear`, `/clear-many`, ≤ 200) refuse an agent `vsst_`/`jbt_` Bearer first (`agent_forbidden`, the user-todos-reply precedent); with sign-in OFF the owner cannot be told apart from a token-less local curl (said in the header, like channels.js). The agent's own verbs (`/api/agent/task/progress-redact`, `/api/agent/user-todo {clear}`) live in agent-routes.js (`agentClearCaller`: its keys, conversation, `pendingFork`) and go through the same entry point. server.js wires it in one line (`getRecordClear` into setupAgentRoutes, lazy getters for the jobs engine and the groups engine).

### "Clear content…" in the five stores (2026-09-28)

Each store has ONE door, called only by the entry point above; each rewrites every copy of the words it owns and broadcasts as it always does:
- **src/task-groups.js `clearProgress(groupId, refs)`** — Activity entries now carry a stable `P-<6 hex>` id (minted in addProgress, backfilled idempotently at load — the backlog-id precedent — kept by importBundle / importFromFile); a ref is an id or the entry's ms `at` (two entries of one ms ⇒ `ambiguous`). The note becomes the sentence, the detail goes (no "† has detail"). ONE `_save()` — which also regenerates every context folder's TASK.md (a folder on a disconnected storage catches up at the next syncAllContextMd, as before; ctx-sync never ships `.vibespace/`) — ONE `tasks-updated`. `updatedAt` moves, `contentUpdatedAt` does NOT: the injection renders from the store on every call, and the diff snapshot keys activity by `lastProgressAt`, which a clear keeps — a clear is not news to a member agent (`_groupSnap` never held activity words). The UI-added entries (`session: null`) are the owner's only.
- **src/user-todos.js `clearItems(ids)`** — title → the sentence; detail, `i18n` (a client prefers it over `text`), option chips, the reply go; a jobs item's label too. The resolved PREVIEW is derived per snapshot, so the one broadcast rewrites every client's copy; `restoreDetails` never restores into a cleared item (it is not `detailTruncated`) and the client's map forgets its whole text; `ensureDetail` re-checks after its GET. A cleared item never matches a re-file by text (`add`) nor `resolveByAgent` by text. A producer that retracts by `it.text === saved` (channels, login watch) no longer finds a cleared item — the owner resolves it by hand.
- **src/session-status.js `clearHistory(key, ats)`** — an entry is named by (key, at). The reason → the sentence, the detail (a vcs row's branch) goes; the CURRENT record, when its reason OR its detail still says the entry's words (verify r1: an entry set with `--detail` and no reason left the current record's detail — the "Now" row's expander — untouched under a reason-only match), and a queued status-override notice quoting them (injected into the agent's next turn) follow. History is not in the broadcast; `_notify()` makes Session Properties refetch.
- **src/jobs.js `clearJobs(ids)`** — a cron parent takes its runs (`<name> run`), in the registry AND the archive. Name → the sentence (the family of cleared jobs groups under it); note, context, progress, the notify action's text, every run's last line, every delivery reason, the panel answers go; the COMMAND stays (✕ removes it). ARCHIVE FIRST (the 2026-09-16 law): the archive copy is written through `_writeArchive` before anything else changes; a failed write changes nothing. Then the event ring (`announced: …`), the held stash — EVERY held notification of a cleared job loses all its words (verify r1: a `--notify` cron's held entry carries the action's OWN text as `text`, `_notifyOwner(job, {what: a.text || job.name})`, and only the `announced:` prefix was rewritten, so the reminder's words rode into the owner conversation's next turn through renderNotifStash) —, the spill files under data/job-notifications-read/ (each line keeps time + id), one `_save()`, one `jobs-updated {cleared}`. A cleared job's snapshot serves no log tail for a run the clear COVERED (a run started at or before `clearedAt`) and says so — `logWithheld: true` (verify r2: an empty tail printed "(no log)", as if the run said nothing; `vibespace-job logs` / `poll` now print "withheld — this job's content was cleared", the panel "The log is hidden — …"); a run that STARTED after the clear is new output and is served (a cron cleared once keeps its later logs). The run's log file is the process's own output (kept like a transcript until the 14-day GC). Snapshot keys `clearedAt`/`clearedBy` on live and archived alike (test-jobs-triage parity; `logWithheld` appears only with a tail). **Verify r3 (the reader-census round; each reproduced on the real engine before the fix, each pinned with its pre-fix copy as the control in test-record-clear-stores §4b):** ① the job's ASK went untouched — `interaction.pending` (the panel: a title + markdown blocks the owner answers from the For-you item / the panel dialog, served WHOLE by `GET /api/jobs/:id` `interaction`) was not in SHAPES.job; it is dropped now, a job parked `awaiting-user` on it goes back to `up` (it may ask again) and its ask's For-you item is resolved (`resolveByJob` no longer tells the ask apart by its words alone — a cleared item has none — so an answered / expired / withdrawn panel closes the cleared ask too); ② `_finalizeRun` re-stamped `run.lastLine` from the log when a run that STARTED before the clear ended after it (under a forced stop / OOM the process's own last words, re-published into every list and snapshot while the same run's tail was withheld) — a covered run keeps no last line; ③ the spill rewrite was LINE-based while a multi-line notification (an announce with newlines) spilled its continuation lines under the entry — the spill writes ONE line per notification now (⏎ marks the breaks), and a legacy entry's continuation lines go with it; ④ a SECOND clear of a job whose record was already cleared (it announced afterwards: the words live in the ring / the stash / a spill, never in the record) returned `already` before the derived-copy sweep — the sweep runs for `already` too; ⑤ a delivery IN FLIGHT when the owner cleared the job stashed afterwards with the words it captured — an event is stamped `at` when born (`_notifyOwner`) and one born before `clearedAt` is held as the sentence; ⑥ the delivery LADDER's own stash (data/msg-stash.json): a codex owner conversation's wrapper hands a notification it could not queue back to the ladder WHOLE under `Background Work · <name>` (stdout/codex-events.js `peer_message_result ok:false`), drained into that conversation's next turn — `clearJobs` now asks the ladder (`d.redactStash`, conversation-deliver's `redactStash(match)`) to replace every entry filed under a cleared job's name (the names are read before the record loses them). ⑦ a PUBLISHED service's port forward is labelled `service: <name>` (the Ports panel, data/port-forwards.json) — relabelled with the sentence through `pf.forward` (the door that labelled it) when a running service is cleared.
- **src/server/groups-engine.js `clearMessages({group, ids})`** — the log is APPEND-ONLY, so a clear WRITES: one REPLACEMENT record per cleared record (`gx-…`, `raw:{kind:'cleared', of, by}`, the clear's instant — the log stays in time order) appended inside the groups door, then the group's `cleared` INDEX in groups.json (log first, index second). `readFolded` = every reader (the owner's window, `vibespace-msg read`, unread counts, next-turn reports, wakes) folds through `foldClears` and asks for as many extra records as the group holds replacements (≤ 5000), so a page stays full; the index covers a page that does not reach the replacement. `lastAt` never moves (no unread, no re-sort); `lastText` becomes the sentence + `lastCleared` when the newest record was cleared (appendIn resets it). THE ORIGINAL LINE STAYS ON DISK in msgs/groups/<id>.ndjson: a group log is never rolled or trimmed (trim runs on adapter logs only), so there is no roll to compact on. One channels-audit row (`kind:'clear'`, ids, by — no words), one `channel-groups-updated` carrying `cleared: [{groupId, vendorId, record}]`. THE OTHER READER (verify r1): the channels engine's generic `messages()` (`GET /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId/messages`) read any store log by path — `groups/<gid>` included — and served the ORIGINAL line after a clear; it now answers null (404 "No such conversation") for anything the engine does not `known()`, the gate `loadOlder` / `readFor` / `attachment` already had (test-channels-engine ⑰, with the un-gated copy as the control). **Verify r3:** the ladder's stash again — a group WAKE a codex member's wrapper could not queue is handed back WHOLE (the report text, a line per record) and drained into that member's next turn; `clearMessages` now asks `deliver.redactStash` to rewrite every line of a held report naming this group (`(<gid>)` in its head) that repeats a cleared record's words (the first 40 code points of the whitespace-collapsed text — the report's own line form, possibly cut — are the witness); the engine itself never stashes a wake (a refused wake rides the next report), the wrapper's hand-back does. THE READER CENSUS (scripts/test-record-clear-census.mjs, fast) is the standing answer to "one more copy": every store-log read in the tree must be inside channel-store, this engine's `readFolded` / `clearMessages`, or a channels-engine function whose declared gate stands before the read — a raw reader added anywhere is RED (four patched-copy controls).

The surfaces — each with a VISIBLE door as well as the right-click / long-press menu (verify r2: four of five were right-click only): **task-log.js** Activity tab — rows KEYED by the entry id (`data-pid`), patched in place on every `tasks-updated` (the Find box, a ticked selection, an expanded detail survive another client's clear), a ⋯ per row, the search box is the "Find…" box on this tab (an entry it matches by its detail ALONE opens that detail — a paint-made open is not the user's, one the user closes stays closed until the Find text changes), `Select…` ⇄ `Done` (tc select) shows checkboxes and the bar "Select all shown (N)" · "N selected" · "Clear selected (N)" (only picks SHOWN under the current filter are acted on; picks keyed by id; a CLEARED row has no checkbox — a spacer keeps the column — no ⋯ and no menu while selecting; a batch that went through ENDS Select mode); day / time cells in the device's locale (verify r2: en-US on a zh page); ### LANE-PAIRING (B-7007, 2026-09-28) — pairing that says WHERE and WHY · exit access with a WHO

The owner's MacBook, 2026-09-27: the pairing dialog offered ONE address (the frp relay) the Mac's network could not reach; the owner hand-edited `dial.json` (a typo host over `wss://`); every re-open of the row's Re-pair minted a NEW token (`POST /api/device/dial-pair` rotated `dialTokenHash` on every call), so the daemon dialed with a stale one; the server journal said "dial REJECTED — token mismatch" while the row said only "offline"; the daemon logged nothing usable; and the frp-named root put the daemon's socket at 106 bytes over macOS's 104. Separately, exit access was ONE boolean per machine opening it to every conversation for both borrowing its network and running shell commands on it, with no audit. Spec: /tmp/vibespace-lanes/pairing/spec.md (the lane's design, §0–§16). Owner defaults built: a token is minted ONLY on "Generate a new command" (no plaintext at rest); a `jbt_` job token never uses an exit; the run bound is ONE number, 30 s (daemon, CLI help, card).

**verify-r6 — THE DECLARED BOUNDARIES of "what you approve is what runs" (so the next round does not re-find them).** ① **Two hubs behind one relay name (r5 A1's 409 across hubs) is OUT OF SCOPE:** A1's verdict is over ONE hub's `hosts.list()`; two hubs share no state. frps names are first-come — if hub A drops and hub B takes the subdomain, the device's dials land on B, which holds no matching hash (`token-mismatch`, the daemon retries with backoff): a denial while B holds the name, never a silent cut, and B cannot answer A's pairing. What B DOES get is the device's raw dial token (a bearer header sent to whatever answers the URL) — relay tenancy (infrastructure trust), not the pairing model; the right home is a future hub-identity pin (a cert fingerprint / key challenge in dial.json before the token is sent). ② **A local agent is the hub user:** the answer routes refuse any bearer, but an agent running on the hub can read `data/auth.json` (cookie tokens, plaintext) or restart the server with auth off — `data/` is the trust root; the asks guard against an agent following the rules and against OTHER machines, not against a local process with the owner's file access (hashing tokens at rest would not close it: it can write the file). ③ **Auth off:** `/ws` needs no cookie and the cookie-only answer routes admit any local caller — the human-witness nonce proposed in docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md is where the exit ask, the permission card and the confirmation card would join.


### src/dial-facts.js — PURE THE DIAL'S FACTS (lane-pairing ①③⑤, NEW)

Imports nothing; CJS — the daemon bundle AND the browser bundle carry it. ① `dialAddressCandidates({origin, relay, hostname, interfaces, port, deviceId})` → one row per distinct base `{kind, base, dialUrl, label, note, plain, rank}`: the browser's origin first, the relay second (omitted when equal), then Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10, or a `tailscale*`/`ts*`/`utun*` interface carrying one), LAN (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), public, this host's name, global-unicast IPv6 (bracketed); loopback, link-local and `internal` interfaces are never rows; a base is http unless it came from the origin / the relay with https. `dialBaseVerdict(input)` = THE ONLY way a custom address enters (`http(s)://`, `ws(s)://` → http(s), a bare `host[:port]`; refuses `scheme` / `path` / `query` / `port` / `host` / `empty`); the route re-runs it. ③ `dialFailureOf(err, {up, upMs})` → `{code, detail, status?}` over the CLOSED `DIAL_FAIL_CODES` (dns · tls incl. `wrong version number` · not-ws · refused-connect · timeout · unreachable · reset · refused-token-mismatch / -no-pairing / -no-device-id / -unknown · http-<status> · closed-before-hello · lost · other); `detail` ≤ 200 chars, no control characters, no token. `dialHeadersOf` / `parseDialHeaders` (the daemon's per-attempt hints — the server treats them as untrusted: closed codes, ≤ 80 bytes). `nextDialStatus` (the device's `state/dial-status.json` reducer: `lost` is the link's end, not a failed dial). `dialLogLine`. `refusalSentence(code, deviceId)` (the server's words the daemon logs and the installer prints; verify-r2: the `token-mismatch` sentence covers a removed pairing too — the gate answers it for an unknown name). **verify-r2 (the dial endpoint) `refusalBudget({max 30, globalMax 300, windowMs 10 min, keys 4096})` = the dial refusals' JOURNAL budget: `hit(ip, deviceKey, now)` → `{log, summary: 'key'|'global'|null}` — per key (`refusalAddressKey(ip)`: IPv4 / a `::ffff:`-mapped one as is, IPv6 by its /64, plus the paired name when a pairing answers to it, so two devices behind the relay's one address never mute each other; guessed names share the address's key), `max` lines then ONE summary; the window's ceiling counts LINES (a noisy key spends only its own share; ≤ `globalMax` + 1 lines per window whatever the rotation); O(1) per hit, the map ≤ `keys` (oldest window dropped first — the WIP's whole-map sweep past 4 096 keys was quadratic, 3.3 s for 40 000 rotating addresses, and logged every one). A LOG budget only — never a lock, never the row's record.** ⑤ `dialCheckLines` (the `--dial-check` exit code + remedy per class). THE ROW: `dialRowState(h)` → `{state, at, n, reason, host}` over `auth-fail · connected · refused · silent · never · unknown` (auth-fail is judged before connected; `refused` only when the refusal is newer than BOTH the last connect and the current mint — a refusal of the token a Generate retired is not news); `dialReasonOf` maps a stored code to the closed words. Gate: scripts/test-dial-facts.mjs (fast).

**verify-r4 F1 (2026-09-28) — THE DEVICE STATES THE ADDRESS IT DIALS; THE HOST HEADER IS THE LAST PROXY'S FACT.** naive-user N-sheet made the pairing sheet check "the address the device connected through" and read it off `lastAccept.host` — the `Host` header AS IT REACHED THIS SERVER. A proxy decides that header: VibeSpace's own frp relay (subdomain mode) writes `hostHeaderRewrite = "127.0.0.1"` (src/plugins.js), nginx's default is its upstream (`$proxy_host`, `127.0.0.1:3456`). Reproduced with a real daemon behind a Host-rewriting relay: the sheet checked **Custom… http://127.0.0.1** "这台设备正在通过它连接", Generate + "send it over its link" wrote `ws://127.0.0.1/api/device-dial` into the device's `dial.json`, and the device then dialed its own port 80 (`refused-connect`, streak 4) — the N-sheet HIGH reborn for every relay-paired device (a TLS proxy on :8443 would also have been read as http: the scheme was guessed from the port). FIX: the daemon states its own dial URL's BASE on every attempt — `x-vibespace-dial-base` (PURE `dialBaseOfUrl`: scheme ws→http / wss→https + host[:port]; no path, no query, never the token; ≤ `DIAL_BASE_MAX` 270 bytes), `parseDialHeaders` reads it through the ONE `dialBaseVerdict` (junk ⇒ `dialed: null`), the gate records it as `facts.dialed` APART from `facts.host` (the journal keeps the header), `noteDial` stores `lastAccept.dialed` / `lastRefusal.dialed` (re-judged). `dialDefaultChoice`'s `connected` reads ONLY `lastAccept.dialed`; a device too old to state it falls to `paired` (`mintedBase` — it states it after its first self-upgrade). The row's `{host}` ("…a network that reaches {host}?", "…cannot reach {host}") is the device's stated address or the CURRENT command's `mintedHost` (`never` names only the latter) — never the header. The sheet's tag follows the link: "the address this device connects through" only while it is dialed in, else "…last connected through" (a relay that moved, a laptop on another network). CENSUS (test-dial-facts): no `.host` of `lastAccept` / `lastRefusal` is read from `dialDefaultChoice` to the end of the module; CONTROL (n) = the header read again ⇒ the relay cell checks `https://127.0.0.1`. Chrome leg (test-pair-dialog-ui): a real daemon behind a Host-rewriting relay — the sheet checks the stated address, the in-place push keeps `dial.json` on the relay.

**verify-r4 F3 (2026-09-28) — A ROW ONLY FOR AN ADDRESS THE SERVER'S SOCKET ACCEPTS.** `dialAddressCandidates` listed what the MACHINE has (`os.networkInterfaces()`), never what the server LISTENS on. Reproduced with `HOST=127.0.0.1` (the README's "local-only"): the dialog listed the Tailscale, two LAN and the hostname addresses, checked the tailnet one "reachable from your tailnet" — and every one refused the connection (ECONNREFUSED ×4, world B). And the DEFAULT `HOST=0.0.0.0` is IPv4-only in node, so a global IPv6 row could never answer. FIX: the address route reads the socket's bound address (`server.address().address`, else `HOST`) and passes it as `bind`; PURE `bindAdmits(bind)` → `{v4, v6, any, loopbackOnly}`: none said ⇒ everything (a caller from before), `0.0.0.0` ⇒ IPv4 only, `::` ⇒ both, a loopback bind ⇒ NO interface or hostname row, one address ⇒ that row only (IPv4-mapped read as IPv4; no hostname row — the name may resolve elsewhere). The origin and the relay rows stay (how the browser — and a proxy — reach the server). The route answers `listen: {address, loopbackOnly}` and the picker says it above the list ("This VibeSpace listens only on this machine (…), so another device cannot reach it directly. Use the relay, or type the address of a proxy in front of it under Custom… (or restart VibeSpace with HOST=0.0.0.0)."). `dialDefaultChoice` with nothing reachable: the relay-publish row when offered (`relayPublishable`), else Custom… EMPTY — never a loopback row checked (naive-user N-loop's `only-loopback ⇒ that row` is superseded: the dialog pairs ANOTHER machine; the loopback row stays pickable). Gate: test-dial-facts (a bind table of 8 cells, `loopbackOnly`, the default cells, wiring pins; CONTROL (o) = the bind ignored ⇒ the tailnet row checked on a loopback-bound server).

**verify-r4 F6 (2026-09-28) — A NEW PAIRING UNDER AN EXISTING NAME IS A REPLACEMENT, SAID BEFORE THE BUTTON.** The dial-pair route treats an existing device id as a RE-PAIR: the token rotates, the device dialed in on the old command is disconnected at once (verify-r2 B8-r2), and the record — its mounts, its "Who can use it" lists — belongs to whatever runs the new command. "Pair a device" said nothing before Create when the typed name was taken (reproduced: a connected device's name ⇒ generation 2, the device cut; the words came only after). PURE `deviceIdOf(input)` is THE name rule (`\w` and `-`, ≤ 32 — the route mints under it, the address route reads it, the dialog sends it; the dialog used to judge the UNCUT name, so a 36-character name the route truncated onto an existing id was a silent replacement) and `pairNameVerdict(input, hosts)` → `{exists, online, name, deviceId}`; the dialog re-judges on every keystroke and, for a taken name, shows the replacement sentence (connected: "…that device is disconnected now and its command stops working"; offline: "…the command it holds stops working"; both point to the row's pairing icon) and the button reads "Replace its pairing". ### src/sock-path.js — SHARED WHERE A UNIX SOCKET MAY LIVE (lane-pairing ④, NEW)

node builtins only (`crypto`; `fs` by injection); the daemon bundles it. `SUN_PATH_MAX` per platform (darwin/BSD 104, linux/sunos 108, incl. the NUL; unknown = 104). `daemonSocketPath({root, platform, tmpdir, xdgRuntimeDir, uid, tmpBase})` = THE RUNG LADDER, the first that fits: natural `<root>/state/agentd.sock` → `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/vibespace/d-<sha1(root)[0..12]>.sock` → a PER-USER `TMPDIR` (macOS `/var/folders/…` only) → the LITERAL `/tmp/vs-dev-<uid>/d-<h>.sock`; none ⇒ `{path: null, code: 'socket_path_too_long', tried}` (`tooLongLine` names every rung's bytes). `socketDirVerdict(lstat, uid)` / `ensureSocketDir(dir, {fs, uid})`: a short directory is made 0700 and VERIFIED (not a symlink, a directory, ours, no group/other bits) — else `socket_dir_hijacked`, never a socket in somebody else's directory (browser-profiles r4's lesson). `witnessOrRule({root, …})` = THE READER (the `--stdio` bridge, src/agentd/client.js `_sock`): the daemon's witness `<root>/state/socket-path` when it names a live socket, else the rule with the caller's own environment (launchd/systemd and a shell need not agree on TMPDIR). `socketPathFits(p, platform)` — asked by the channel socket (src/ws-create.js: over ⇒ the channel is not offered, named), the tailscale plugin (src/plugins.js: refused at start, named) and server.js's one boot line about data/sockets. Gate: scripts/test-sock-path.mjs (fast — the ladder table, the verdict with a patched lstat, the witness + client.js reader, THE CENSUS of every socket path the tree builds, a bound-108 control); heavy: test-agentd-dial's 120-byte-root leg.

### src/exit-reach.js — PURE WHO MAY USE A MACHINE AS AN EXIT (lane-pairing ⑥, NEW)

Imports only window-reach's principal spelling (`sessionKeyOf`, `callerKeys`, `normPrincipal`, `principalKey`, `principalsNow`) — NOT an extension of window-reach (a per-window record with one level and a share mode; this is per-machine with two grants, an "everyone" mode, an ask switch and a run ledger — two closed censuses beat one open one). A host record's `exit = {use: {mode, who}, run: {mode, who, ask}, updatedAt, updatedBy, lastRun}`, modes `nobody | everyone | only`. `exitAccessOf(h)` = THE ONE READER: `exit` present ⇒ normalized (junk rows DROPPED, a bad mode or a non-object grant ⇒ the WHOLE access `unknown` ⇒ both grants refused); absent + `allowExit === true` ⇒ everyone / everyone (the pre-migration read); absent ⇒ nobody. `exitVerdict(access, grant, ctx)` (ctx = `{sessionKeys, groupIds, unreadable, forkPending}`) — a session row beats a group row; no hit + a group row + an unreadable store ⇒ `groups_unreadable` (never not_granted); a pending fork nothing reached ⇒ `fork_pending`. `agentView` (the caller's own two answers, never another principal). `exitStamp` / `exitBaseVerdict` (channel-filter's stamp shape: order is not a change; a stale base ⇒ `list_changed {added, removed}`). `patchVerdict` (shape → base → mode → rows → dedup → 64 → empty → ask). `askState` / `answerVerdict` (60 s; only `by: 'user'`). `runRecord` (120-char head). `resolveMachine` (over the list the caller hands in). `refusalText` — the agent's sentences: the grant it lacks + "the user can allow it under 'Who can use it' on the machine row (Remote tab)", never another conversation's name, a group title or a key (the words census). `cardText` / `cliLine`. `migrateExitAccess`. `EXIT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000` (= the daemon's run-cmd cap; test-architecture §66c pins the literal). **ALL AGENTS (lane everyone-principal, 2026-10-02): the picker's All row IS the `everyone` mode — never a second spelling.** A `who` row of kind `everyone` is refused `bad_principal` at the write ("All agents is the mode "everyone", not a row of the list") and dropped at the read (`normWho`). `everyone` KEEPS the rows it was given (`normGrant` reads `who` for everyone too, `patchVerdict` validates them like `only`'s — empty allowed, `storedExit` writes them when non-empty): `exitVerdict` is unchanged (everyone ⇒ ok, the kept rows decide nothing), and taking All away (the dialog sends `only` with those rows) restores exactly the conversations and Task Groups picked before; `nobody` keeps none. The stamp carries the kept rows (a stale dialog cannot overwrite them). Gate: test-everyone-principal ② (+ test-exit-reach 256 unchanged).

A host record gains `dial: {generation, tokenMintedAt, mintedHost, lastProbeAt, firstConnectAt, lastConnectAt, lastDisconnectAt, lastRefusal {code, at, from, attempt, last, daemon, host}, lastAccept {…}, lastAuthFail {at}}` written by `noteDial(deviceId, event, facts)` (minted | refused | accepted | disconnected | authFail | probed) — in memory at once; persisted NOW on minted / accepted / a refusal whose code changed / the first auth failure, else through `_saveThrottled(key)` (one write per machine per 60 s; a skipped write is flushed by an unref'd timer at the window's end and by `flushThrottled()` at SIGTERM — a crash loses ≤ 60 s of repeat-refusal timestamps, never a code); it returns `{changed}` (the PURE row state moved) so the caller broadcasts. `exit` is written by `setExitAccess(id, exit)` (keeps `lastRun`, strips `allowExit`) and `setLastRun(id, rec)` (throttled; a pre-migration record is lifted through `migrateExitAccess`). `reshapeStore(fn)` = the migration's door (the manager holds hosts.json whole). `setAllowExit` is gone. `list()` exposes `dial` + `exit` whole (cookie route; the refusal's `from` address is the owner's own device, shown in the row's tooltip, never to agents).

### src/pairing-token.js — THE ONE DOOR OF A PAIRING TOKEN (lane-pairing verify-r3, NEW, SHARED)

A pairing is two secrets: the DIAL token (`vsdt_` + 36 hex — the hub keeps only its sha256 on the device's record, `hosts.json` `dialTokenHash`; whoever holds the token dials in AS the device) and the HOST token (`vsht_` + 48 hex — the hub's `data/agentd/host-<id>.token`, 0600, presented in every mux hello; the device's `state/token`, compared against the hello). `mintToken(kind)` / `tokenHash(token)` / `tokenMatches(token, hash)` — the compare is `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over the two 32-byte digests (a missing / malformed side is `false`), never `!==` (which stops at the first differing character — r2's gate compared the digests with `!==`, the device's hello the same, and the dial session bridge compared the RAW host token with `!==` on a loopback port any local process can knock on). node `crypto` only; SHARED (the daemon bundles it). Every site names it: the gate + the minter (dial-pairing.js), the hub's host-token store (server.js `agentdHostToken`), device #0's key (client.js `_ensureLocalToken`), the device's hello (agentd.js), the dial session bridge. **A token written onto a device goes through the device's `place-secret` op** (0600 at open, tmp + rename): the in-place push of B8 used fsWrite-then-chmod (a window at the umask's mode, a failed chmod swallowed) — now `placeSecret`, the old pair only for a daemon without the op or a root outside its `$HOME` (the op's own fence; the device's state dir is 0700), and the journal names which (`… pushed in place (place-secret)`). Gates: test-dial-facts — THE DOOR CENSUS, grep-derived over every tracked server / src / device-tool / installer file that handles a pairing token (17 of 301): R1 no sha256 outside the door, R2 no `vsdt_` / `vsht_` value built elsewhere, R3 no `===` / `!==` against a pairing token or its digest, R4 no log line interpolating a token, R5 no device secret written but through `placeSecret` (the fsWrite fallback only right after it), R6 no token in a child's argv (a spawn / execFile line, the installer's node children); two exemptions by line, each with its reason and a staleness check (the standalone installer's own on-device key; client.js's "changed ⇒ rewrite" of device #0's digest); the door's three verbs; the wiring of every site; a planted site per rule is caught (six controls). test-dial-token-sinks pins the push's `place-secret` road at runtime.

The verdict is PURE `duplicateDialVerdict({current:{boot, alive}, incoming:{boot}})` over the daemon's per-process boot id (`x-vibespace-daemon-boot`, remembered per device at accept in `dialBootOf`): no current / the SAME known boot ⇒ replace unasked (a daemon re-dialing after its own drop); anything else — a different boot, or NO boot on either side (**verify-r2 B9-r2a**: r1 let a header-less newcomer replace unasked, so a stolen pairing on an old bundle evicted the live device at will, 9 accepts / 8 closes in 8 s) ⇒ `probe` — the probe goes THROUGH `deviceForDial` bounded by `DUP_PROBE_MS` (1.5 s) so a hello still in flight is JOINED (r1 read `connected:false` as dead and let a newcomer inside the hello's round trip evict a healthy device), then the current DeviceManager gets `DUP_PROBE_MS` to answer `dm.ping()` (mux PING→PONG, `Mux.ping(ms)`): answered ⇒ the newcomer is REFUSED by name (`refuseDial 'duplicate-device'`, the way out first in the sentence; its daemon logs `dial-out refused — duplicate-device: …` and backs off to 30 s), `hosts.noteDial('duplicate')` ⇒ `dial.lastDuplicate {at, from, boot, daemon}` (persisted at once when the row's 10-min note is not already on — verify-r2: r1's "at once for every new boot" wrote hosts.json per knock for a copy sending a fresh id each time) and PURE `dialRowState().dup` carries it for 10 min — `dialStateText` appends "Another device is also dialing in as this one (from …, …)" on the row, the Machines card and the pairing sheet; silent ⇒ replaced (a crashed machine's half-open socket, the pre-B9 rule). After the probe the current stream is re-read (the world may have moved while asking). Gates: test-dial-facts B9 (the cells incl. the header-less ones, the header round trip, the 401's classification, the row's dup, a never-refuse control + a control with r1's no-boot pass) + test-dial-link-kept's B9-r2a block (the real admitDial over an answering fake daemon: a header-less newcomer refused, the hello-in-flight window joined, a silent current replaced after the probe, a closed-world control — dial-pairing.js bound to a dial-facts.js with r1's rule — admitting it) + test-agentd-dial's B9 legs (two REAL daemons on one pairing: 1 accept / 0 closes / ≤ 4 broadcasts in 9 s, the copy's file + log, A's link kept, A killed ⇒ the copy admitted on its next attempt; the no-boot-header copy refused all the same; the same copy under the patched server = the flap back = the control).** `deviceForDial`'s catch notes `authFail` when the DEVICE refused our host key — src/agentd/client.js's connect loop now THROWS that refusal at once for a dialed (`stream`) device instead of retrying the same key for a minute and ending on a generic error (the auth failure had never reached any caller); ### scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.sh + .ps1, data/bin/vibespace-exit (lane-pairing ⑤⑥, CHANGED)

The installers check the dial address BEFORE they write anything: the scheme (ws:// or wss://, exit 2, before any fetch), then — once the bundle is on disk — `vibespace-device.js --dial-check` with the root in the env; a non-zero exit prints "✗ nothing was installed — the device cannot dial <host:port>: <the check's line>" and exits with the check's code before the host token, `dial.json` or the launchd / systemd unit (PowerShell: the scheduled task) exist. `--no-check` (`-NoCheck`) skips it. A failed bundle fetch says to pick another address (exit 12). vibespace-exit: `list` prints only the machines open to this conversation (`network: yes/no · commands: yes/ask/no`); a `not_granted` adds the way out (the user, "Who can use it"); `run` says `# waiting for the user's approval (up to 60 s)…` when the call outlives a second and the machine asks, prints the server's one-line record, exits 124 on a timeout; the help says 30 s. docs/agent/index-manual.md's `exit` row says the same.

### Migration 2026-09-exit-access-lists (src/server/migrations.js, lane-pairing ⑥)

`create()` gains `hosts` (the LIVE HostManager). Archives every record's `allowExit` to `data/archive/hosts-allow-exit-<ts>.json` FIRST, then lifts each record through PURE `migrateExitAccess` (on ⇒ everyone / everyone — behaviour unchanged; off / absent ⇒ nobody / nobody; an `exit` kept) and strips the boolean, through `hosts.reshapeStore` (the file directly only in a suite, atomic, its mode kept); an unreadable hosts.json fails the run by name (retried next boot, nothing touched); a second pass changes nothing. Gate: test-migrations.

### scripts/test-approval-census.mjs — THE APPROVAL CENSUS: what you approve is what runs (lane-pairing verify-r6, NEW)

Three verify rounds in a row found a HIGH in ONE class — the thing the owner APPROVES (a command above Allow, an address he sends to a device) differing from the thing that RUNS; r5 fixed the instances, this suite is the class gate. Every place the product performs an ACTION on the strength of a human's click on a surface that DISPLAYS what will happen is found by grep and claimed by a row proving, or declaring with a reason, (a) SAME RECORD — display and execution from one immutable record (id + version, a hash, or one captured value); (b) RE-CHECK at execution (still open · still this action's · unchanged); (c) NO OTHER WRITER between display and click (an agent filing, a peer message, a broadcast, another client); (d) FORMAT — direction / format controls that make display ≠ execution refused at the door or shown.

**§1 THE CAPTURE RULE (verify-r6 E1).** Every client dialog that gates an action — each `await showConfirmDialog(` / `await showInputDialog(` in the tracked src/lib files (87) — is read to the end of its enclosing async function: after the await the action may read no LIVE state (the explorer's `currentPath` / `_host` / `_hp()` / `_hb()`, the sidebar's `_hostsData`, the system panel's `getHostId()`), because another client or a broadcast moves that state while the dialog is open. Exemptions carry a reason and a stale one is red. The textual rule does not see a loop body or a closure defined above the await — those ops are pinned one by one (E1's `_here()` pins). CONTROL (e1): the pre-fix explorer Delete ⇒ red.

**§1b THE CONFIRM SHOWS WHAT IT CONFIRMS (verify-r6 D1).** `showConfirmDialog` takes ONE options object; a call passing `(title, message)` as strings destructured to nothing and rendered a blank "Confirm / OK" — twice: setup-flows' layout restore (fixed with a comment) and then plugins-ui's Stop frp / Tailscale, whose OK stopped the public URLs or the tailnet with nothing said. Every call site now passes an object literal (or a ternary of two) — the census reads each call's first argument — and the function reads a string first argument as the (title, message) pair, so a missed call still shows what OK does. CONTROL (d1): the pre-fix Stop confirm ⇒ red.

**§1c A PRESS COUNTS ONLY ON WHAT SAT STILL WHERE IT WAS READ (verify-r6 V1).** Two For-you surfaces put a different "Allow … to run a command?" under a pointer already on its way (verify-r6 agentA): the popup / mini inbox (a resolved exit row drops its command and buttons, the row below slides up — a double-click, or the first ask's 60 s expiry, landed the press on the NEXT ask's Allow; the inc-mtw02kbq-kj96 class on the one button that runs a command) and the For-you window (Allow advances to the next item, whose pane shows Allow in the same place — a double-click allowed it unread). PURE `src/lib/press-arm.js`: `pressVerdict` counts an Allow only once it stayed put `ARM_MS` (700) since it appeared or moved, `armAfterLayout` re-stamps after a layout pass; the popup re-stamps every Allow after each row pass (`armExitButtons`), the window stamps its pane when its item changes; an early press does nothing and says so (zh/ja). Deny is never gated. The channel outbox card carries its own arming (channel-policy `armVerdict`, same 700 ms). Gate: the census's §1c tables, the two wiring pins, CONTROL (v1). **Lane browser-propose verify r1:** `togglePopup` ran its row pass (which samples every Allow / Approve top) BEFORE `anchorFixedPopup` placed the popup, so the first press after EVERY open read as "moved under the pointer" and was refused with its toast (reproduced in chrome: sampled at 696 px, pressed at 709 px after 900 ms still) — the popup now samples again after the anchor (armed from the open). Gate: test-browser-propose-chrome ⑦ + a §1c wiring pin.

**§1d THE ONE HIDDEN-CHARACTER DOOR (verify-r6 Z2) — `src/hidden-chars.js` (PURE, CJS, NEW).** A character that REORDERS a line (the bidi controls) or is NOT DRAWN (every Unicode format character — zero-width space / joiners, soft hyphen, BOM, invisible operators, tags — the Hangul fillers, the line / paragraph separators, every control character but tab and line feed) makes what a person reads differ from what runs or is sent. r6 found four approval surfaces each spelling its OWN set — the exit door (exit-reach), the outbox (channel-policy), the permission card (helper-ask), the browser confirmation card (browser-takeover) — none the same, and three of them written as RAW characters in the source (invisible to a reviewer too; channel-avatar's name filter as well). `hiddenCharsOf(value, {allowCR, allowJoiners, max})` / `revealParts` / `revealHidden({open, close})` / `isHidden` / `codeOf` are the set; a door refuses (exit-reach strict; channel-policy strict for an address / an id, joiners kept in a subject), a display marks (the permission card ⟦U+XXXX⟧ keeping CR, the outbox text keeping CR + joiners, the confirmation card ⟨U+XXXX⟩ marking tab / line feed too). Variation selectors are never hidden (emoji). Gate: the census's §1d — no tracked product file carries such a character raw, every surface asks the module and spells no set of its own, the set's table; CONTROLS (z2a) a surface's own set, (z2b) a raw RLO.

**§3 THE APPROVAL ROWS (verify-r6 — the round's deliverable).** The DOORS are grep-derived: every client call whose URL carries an answer verb (`/asks/`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `reset-credit`, `handback`, `takeover`, `dial-pair`, `/install`, `open-with`, `/pin`, `/confirm`, `/:act`, `/:verdict`, `resolve-many` …), every server route with one, every `type: 'permission-response'` frame and every For-you producer's `action: {type}` — 71 hits today, each claimed by exactly ONE of 16 rows (exit-ask, permission-card, reset-credit, dial-pair, install, outbox, reach-request, browser-confirm, browser-handback, jobs-answer, desktop-takeover, plugins, own-installs, inbox-close, not-an-approval, agent-side). A row proves (a) SAME RECORD, (b) RE-CHECK, (c) NO OTHER WRITER, (d) FORMAT — each a PIN (a regex that must match its file, comments stripped) or a DECLARATION with its reason — and names its GATE (an assertion that must exist by its words in its suite). A hit no row claims — a NEW approval surface — is red until it has a row; a dead door, an empty (a)–(d), a missing pin or gate is red; the table prints (P pinned / D declared). **§3b THE TWO CLASS CELLS:** THE MERGE CELL (the real For-you store — the record the exit ask, the helper ask and the reset-credit item display from: an agent's filing of a producer item's own text is filed BESIDE it for every producer; an identity-keyed producer's next question is its own item) and THE RE-CHECK CELL (the real ExitProxyManager: Allow on an item changed after it was shown ⇒ ask_changed, nothing runs). CONTROLS (α) text-keyed merge re-enabled for ONE producer (the reset-credit item) and (β) the exit route without its re-check — each turns its cell red.

**§2 AGENT HTML NEVER RESTYLES AN APPROVAL (verify-r6 H1).** Agent, peer and file markdown (assistant text, peer messages, agent reports, a job panel's md block, a previewed markdown file, a For-you item) was sanitized with DOMPurify's DEFAULT config, which keeps `<style>`, `style=` and `class=` — one agent message could rewrite the command every exit ask shows above Allow (`.ut-exit-cmd{font-size:0}.ut-exit-cmd::before{content:"echo hello"}`), hide an outbox card's text, or cover the page with a fixed layer / a borrowed product class (verify-r6 agentD, reproduced in headless Chrome with the real purify + marked). All of it now goes through `src/lib/safe-html.js` `sanitizeHtml`: its own DOMPurify instance, no CSS, `class` only `language-*` on pre/code, no forms / controls / top layer, `id`/`name` namespaced, no `data-*`, HTML only (no inline SVG / MathML), links open beside the app, and a THROW (never a silent pass-through) without a DOM. The rule: HTML somebody else wrote may format its own text, never style, position or wire anything of ours. Gate: the census's §2 — every DOMPurify use / markdown parse in src/ goes through it (416 files), the config, the hooks, the fail-closed door, a class census over every class in public/*.css, controls (h1)–(h6).

**verify-r6 S1 — A PROCESS ROW'S KILL GOES WHERE THE ROW CAME FROM.** The System panel's Terminate / Force kill confirmed '"node" (pid 4242) will receive SIGKILL' and then sent `{host: getHostId(), pid}` — the panel's machine read AFTER the dialog; a panel rebuild while it was open (a machine removed ⇒ back to "This machine") or a machine switch racing the table's refresh sent the signal to the same pid on ANOTHER machine. `_buildProcManager` now keeps `dataHost` (the machine the drawn listing came from) and each row's action captures `{host, pid}` from it before the confirm; THE CAPTURE RULE's exemption for this site is gone and CONTROL (s1) (the pre-fix line) reddens it. Held (LOW): the pid itself carries no start-time witness — a pid reused on the same machine within the dialog's lifetime is signalled.

**verify-r6 I1 — THE INSTALL RUNS THE PLAN THE DIALOG SHOWED, OR NOTHING.** The install dialog (desktop-app-launcher `showInstallDialog`) shows GET install-plan's commands — run as root — and the POST sent only `{host, what}`; `installPackage` recomputed the plan from the machine's facts AT THE PRESS, so facts that moved in between (the package sources now offer an old xpra, the xpra on PATH, sudo) ran another plan — the xpra.org signing key + repo + a priority-1001 pin — the owner never read (verify-r6 agentB). desktop-access `planDigest(plan)` (sha256 of commands + source + packages) rides GET install-plan as `digest`; the dialog sends it as `planDigest`; `installPackage({expectDigest})` refuses a different plan `plan_changed` BEFORE anything runs, carrying the new plan + digest, and the dialog redraws the commands above the button (the next press names the new plan). A caller that names no digest (an older client, the API) keeps the pre-r6 behaviour; a re-attached running install runs no plan and is not judged. Gate: test-office-open §13 (the REAL access layer over a stub device whose facts move between the two reads, the route streaming the refusal, CONTROL (i1)) + the wiring pins.

**verify-r6 R1 — A RESET CREDIT IS SPENT ON THE WINDOW THE DIALOG SHOWED.** The reset-credit dialog shows the account's spent window (its reset instant, what the credit discards, the wait it saves) from GET …/reset-credit and POSTed only `{sessionId}`; `consumeResetCreditFor` re-derived the preview at the press, so a dialog left open past the reset spent the credit on the FRESH window — it had said "0% discarded" (verify-r6 agentB). The POST now carries `expect: {resetsAtSec}` (the window shown) and the engine refuses a window that reset or moved `preview_changed` (409) BEFORE the writer — nothing spent, nothing charged, no cooldown stamped; the dialog words it (PURE `refusalLine`). A caller naming no window keeps the pre-r6 behaviour. Gate: test-reset-credit-ui §3 (the real engine + route: a moved and a past window refused, the shown one spent once, CONTROL (r1)).

### src/browser-human.js + BROWSE YOURSELF (B-6ae8, 2026-09-28; docs/design-browse-yourself.md + its OWNER DECISIONS)

**The ask and the model.** The owner: "我能自己打开一个浏览器profile用它浏览吗" — and, deciding the design's questions, "我其实也相当于是一个agent而已": one profile = ONE Chrome shared by every conversation on it (each on its own tabs, owner ruling A), and the user is ONE MORE HOLDER with his OWN pinned tab. Opening it pauses, interrupts and tells NO agent; the 2026-09-27 takeover ruling applies only when he drives an AGENT's tab from a conversation's live view (that path is unchanged). His actions are recorded like an agent's (default on, a per-profile opt-out). Close = his tab / window only; Quit the whole browser = a stop for everyone, its confirm naming the conversations that lose their tabs. The keep while away: 12 h when HE launched the browser (`browser.humanKeepMs`), the 10-min takeover idle when he joined a browser an agent launched. Paired-machine profiles are not in v1 (no button).

**PURE src/browser-human.js** (imports nothing; CJS — keeper, routes, bridge, recorder and bundle share one spelling). The key `hu-<the profile id's 8 hex>` is DERIVED, never minted, and never matches a browser key (`bk-…`) — every admission, chat card, binding, told, pin and cap path that gates on a browser key rejects it by construction. `browseYourselfVerdict` — the order is the decision: not-found · `not_attachable` (a conversation's own temporary browser) · `remote_profile` · `not_ours` (a provider that only connects / a window target) · `backend_unavailable` · `browser_restarting` · `profile_locked` (another browser — maybe his own Chrome — holds the folder) · `browser_unstable` · focus (a window of his already drives: not an error) · `cap` (a LAUNCH at the machine ceiling; a join never counts) · rejoin · join · launch; "Who can use it" is NOT an input (the owner may browse every profile). `humanStep` (driving / away / ended `released|left|stopped|restart`), `humanAttachVerdict` (the window his press opened TAKES; another live window of his keeps it and this one watches; else take — "Continue here" is a claim), `humanEndChoices` (Close + Quit the whole browser, ONE confirm only when a conversation is on it), `keepFor`, `addressVerdict` (http / https / about:blank; a bare host gains https, loopback http; else `not_web` "Only web addresses"), `navArgv`, THE ACT AGGREGATOR `humanActStep` / `humanActFlush` / `humanActDueIn` (forwarded input → acts: a click at a point, press + release farther than 5 px = a drag of two points, a chord by name, typing as `«N chars»` — never the text — a scroll; a burst ends after 1.2 s / 0.7 s), `humanRefusalText` / `humanStateLine` (`t` injected).

**ORCH src/server/browser-keeper.js.** `humans` Map — mirrored to the registry (`reg.humans`, verify r1 H4: a restart restores him AWAY; the recorder ends his open session `restart` and it re-opens at his next take). `browse(profileId)` (single flight per profile): the verdict → the SAME `start()` an agent's first command uses (a launch-time refusal passes through with its own words) → `leaseCliOpts` (the keeper browser's RAW CDP url under his session `vs-hu-…` — never the directory, never mediated) → `--pin-tab tab new` (HIS tab; `ownTab` = its target id) → holder `away` + a one-time `fresh` token → `human-start` on the lease seam (the recorder arms before the answer, `settleArming`). **`holdersOn(profileId)` = the conversations' leases + his row**: the idle clock (`browserIdle`), the heal (`leasedNow`), `lastLeaseDroppedAt` and the switch's hold read it — `inputsView` reports 'user' and `switchVerdict` / `switcherRows` / `holdOf` take `humans`, so a backend switch while he browses is a PROPOSAL and the dialog's card offers "Close my browsing". THE HOLDER CENSUS (test-browser-human ③) classifies every `reg.leases` site of the file as conversation-only or holder — a new site is red until the table says which. His controls: `humanTake` / `humanPass` / `humanRelease` / `humanAttach` = the PURE browser-takeover verdicts over HIS input state (never in `inputs`; events carry `human: true` and the handback announcer returns on them — no card, notice, stale sweep, inbox or delivery). `navigateHuman` = the daemon's own `open` / `back` / `forward` / `reload` / `tab <ref>` under HIS session (U3, measured: an agent's pinned tab keeps its page). `endHuman(reason)` closes his own tab, the tab he is on and his session (never `--all`, never an agent's tab), starts the idle clock when he was the last holder and says `human-end`; `closeHuman` = Close, `quitHuman` = today's Stop + the count of conversations; `sweepHumans` (the tick): away past the keep ⇒ `left`, the browser no longer live ⇒ `stopped`. `stop()` ends him `stopped` AND marks `reg.tabClosed` for every conversation lease of the stopped browser (never a switch — it re-opens its own tabs — an ephemeral record or a mediated lease): the heavy leg caught the real 0.38.1 answering `tab_gone` to the conversation's next command after a Quit; the mark makes its next attach bind a new tab first (the owner's "they reopen with `tab new` on their next command"). `updateProfile` takes `recordMine`.

**ORCH src/server/browser-stream.js (the bridge).** A third query shape `?browse=<hu-key>&fresh=<token>`: relay `human:<key>` (no conversation, NO TAB ANCHOR — a login popup he opened keeps his input; the anchor rule stays on every agent relay), the liveness check skipped, `humanAttach` decides take / claim / watch (`mode` cause `elsewhere`), the `claim` viewer verb = Continue here, `pass` = `humanPass`; `human-end` ⇒ `{type:'status', state:'human-ended', reason, deleted}` to every window of his and the relay ends; a view never starts a browser (`not_browsing` / `browser_stopped`). His forwarded input feeds the act aggregator; each act is a synthetic command / result pair (`hu-act-N`, `holder:'user'`) delivered to the TAPS only — never a viewer. `tapHuman(key, fn)`; the bridge installs its cross-relay `viewerAlive` in the keeper.

**ORCH src/server/browser-trace.js (the recorder).** `human-start` ⇒ a session marker `{holder:'user', recorded}`; `human-end` ⇒ its end with the reason (`left` joined END_REASONS). `watchHuman` arms a tap on his relay at `human-start` / `human-driving` when the trace is on AND `recordsMine(profile)`; `unwatchHuman` at away / end / the opt-out; a `recordMine` flip arms or disarms at once. His entries: `holder:'user'`, sessionId null, text `you: …`. The housekeeping rows carry `human` (keeper.humanOf), `recordMine`, `canBrowse` (PURE browser-trace.js: local, a provider that starts a browser). His markers never become a chat card (browser-sessions `chatCardsFor` skips holder user; the wiring's onSession matches a marker by a conversation's OWN key — pinned).

**Routes — cookie only, no agent twin** (src/routes/browser.js): `POST /api/browser/profiles/:id/browse`, `POST /api/browser/browse/:key/navigate` / `close` / `quit` (+ STATUS rows `remote_profile` 400, `not_ours` 409, `not_browsing` 409, `browser_stopped` 409, `not_web` 400, `nav_failed` 502). src/routes/browser-trace.js: `/api/browser/actions` and `/api/browser/sessions` accept `browserKey=hu-…` (his Sessions list, his replay).

**CLIENT.** src/lib/browser-live-window.js — `app.browseYourself(profileId)` (ONE POST; a refusal worded by its code) → `openBrowserHuman` (sync id `win-bhuman-<profile>` — two clients converge on one window; openSpec `{action:'openBrowserLive', profileId, human:true}` replays in watch). His window: the badge ("You are browsing" / "You're browsing this in another window" / "You were browsing it — Continue" / "You are not browsing it now"), Continue browsing / Continue here, **Close** (never folds) + **Quit the whole browser** (folds at priority 3; the confirm from `humanEndChoices`, names as the sidebar shows them), THE ADDRESS ROW (Back · Forward · Reload · the address — the caret there on a blank page; keys typed there never reach the page; a mode record never robs it of focus), the end line, clickable Tabs rows (his popups), the touch Keyboard button, Browse again after an end; no bind / URL / web-view hand-off. src/lib/browser-trace-view.js — the row's FIRST act **Browse yourself** / **Open your browsing window** (only with `canBrowse`: never a greyed button), his state line, **Also record my own actions** (PATCH `recordMine`), the who cell's "You can always browse it yourself.", his Sessions rows ("You · {time} · {dur}", Replay only with acts). src/lib/browser-switcher(-model).js — the empty line's **Open it yourself** (a local profile whose browser is not running — the "a site blocks my agent" path) and the card he blocks: "Close my browsing". src/lib/browser-replay-window.js — the target accepts his key. Setting `browser.humanKeepMs` (Agent browser, 12 h; 0 = until Close or the browser stops).

**Measured (U1 / U3: the real agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome 154 through the real keeper, scratch HOME).** U3: `--pin-tab open` under `vs-hu-…` navigates HIS tab; the agent's pinned tab keeps its page after open / back / forward / reload / popups. U1: a `target=_blank` click and a `window.open` from his pinned tab appear in his session's `tabs` records at once (not followed by themselves); `tab <CDP targetId>` switches HIS stream to the popup — hence the clickable Tabs pane, no unpinned fallback. Close's `tab close` + `close` end his tab and connection; the browser stays `ready`; tabs his pages opened stay (a browser's rule). NOT measured: U2 (a real phone's soft keyboard — the Keyboard button focuses the sink inside the tap) and U4 (a `confirmActions` in the machine's config would ask HIM on his own navigation — accepted).

**Gates.** scripts/test-browser-human.mjs (fast, 6 s): ① the PURE tables + five patched-copy controls; ② the REAL keeper + routes over a fake 0.38.1 (launch / join / rejoin / focus, no pause of the conversation on it, the address row under his session only, Close, Quit + the conversation's new tab on its next command, the keep, a narrowing that leaves him, Delete…, the switch proposal, the ceiling, every refusal; CONTROL an idle-leases-only keeper copy) and ②b the REAL bridge + recorder over fake upstreams (take / watch / claim, no anchor on his relay with the agent relay's `tab_switched` as the control, his acts one entry each with a byte census finding no typed word, no card, the opt-out, `human-ended`, a view never starts a browser); ③ the censuses (no card for him + a by-profile control, the holder census, no agent route / CLI reaches `/browse` or a `hu-` key, the announcer pin); ④ the words in zh + ja. scripts/test-browser-human-ui.mjs (heavy, ~20 s): the real 0.38.1 + Chrome + a headless Chrome client — the panel row's real click, the address field, keys + a 6-character IME commit read back from the page, the conversation working throughout (no pause line in the journal), Close (his tab gone from Chrome's own target list, the same Chrome pid), join, his recorded session + replay, Quit (the confirm names the conversation as the sidebar shows it; its next command opens the browser again), the bar at 360 px on a touch device in en / zh / ja. ② **HIS HOLDER SURVIVES A RESTART (H4 kill class, MAJOR).** The holder lived in keeper memory only: reproduced over the real keeper + the fake 0.38.1 (verify/repro-f2) — 40 min into his browsing a restart (an Update) adopted the browser with NO holder, and its idle clock (`lastLeaseDroppedAt || startedAt` = the launch) STOPPED it at the first tick under his page (`idle`); his window's re-attach answered `browser_stopped` and Browse yourself launched a new browser + a second `tab new`.
