### src/file-disposition.js — THE one Content-Disposition that names a file (lane raw-filename, 2026-09-28)

PURE (imports nothing, CJS; test-architecture's PURE set). userW: "我从vibespace预览里下载文件，文件名都叫raw". `contentDisposition(name, type)` → `<inline|attachment>; filename="<ASCII fallback>"; filename*=UTF-8''<RFC 8187 value>` — ALWAYS both forms (Chrome, Firefox and Safari read `filename*` first; the fallback serves anything older). The fallback is printable ASCII only: `"` and `\` dropped (the quoted-string's delimiter and escape), every other character `_` (a CJK name falls back to `__ 2026.png`, the real name rides `filename*`). `filename*` is percent-encoded to attr-char — `'()*` too, which encodeURIComponent leaves alone. Control characters (CR, LF, TAB, …) are dropped from BOTH: no browser writes one into a saved name, and a raw CR/LF — or ANY character above U+00FF — in a header value makes Node's `setHeader` THROW `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` (inside an async route = a request never answered; see remote-fs.js below). A lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD (encodeURIComponent throws on one). An empty name (a root, a trailing-slash-only path, only control characters) ⇒ `null` = the caller sends no header, exactly as before. `type` is `inline` unless `attachment` is asked for by name. `fileNameOf(p)` = the last POSIX segment, trailing slashes ignored — local paths here and remote paths on an ssh host / paired device are all POSIX. Gate: scripts/test-raw-filename.mjs ① (the table + a 3 000-name seeded sweep over controls / Latin-1 / CJK / Hangul / lone surrogates / private use / emoji: every value printable ASCII, accepted by `http.validateHeaderValue`, and express's own `content-disposition` parser — the independent oracle — reads back the name minus controls).

### src/routes/files.js — GET /api/file/raw is NAMED (lane raw-filename)

Every preview element streams from `/api/file/raw?path=…[&host=]` — the viewer's `<img>`, `<video>`, `<audio>` and the PDF `<iframe>` (file-viewer.js), the chat's image thumbs + overlay (chat-renderers.js `imageRawUrl`), the Background Work panel's pictures (jobs-panel.js), the explorer's preview pane. The route answered with a bare `res.sendFile(filePath)`, so the browser's OWN save controls ("Save image as…", the PDF viewer's download button, a video's download control, a drag to the desktop) named the file after the URL's last path segment: `raw` (Chrome adds the type's extension: `raw.png`, `raw.pdf` — measured, test-raw-filename-chrome ④). The toolbar / explorer Download buttons go through `/api/download` and were never affected.

Now `res.sendFile(filePath, { dotfiles: 'allow', headers: { 'Content-Disposition': contentDisposition(fileNameOf(filePath), 'inline') } })`. INVARIANTS: ① `inline`, never `attachment` — an attachment turns the PDF `<iframe>` preview into a download the moment it opens (measured: test-raw-filename-chrome ④b). ② The name rides only a SUCCESSFUL transfer: sendFile's `headers` option is applied on send's `'headers'` event (exactly how `res.download` does it), so a 404 / 403 / the 503 fail-fast answer byte-for-byte as before; 200, 206 (Range — a `<video>` seeks this way) and HEAD are named. ③ `dotfiles: 'allow'` (r2 (3)): with `dotfiles` undefined send applies its LEGACY rule — a file whose BASENAME starts with `.` answered 404, so `.hidden.png` could not be previewed and `/api/download` of `.env` was a 404 too (`res.download(filePath, { dotfiles: 'allow' })` now). That rule protects a web ROOT; these routes serve the paths the user opened and `/api/file/content` reads dotfiles anyway. `/api/file/serve/*` keeps the legacy rule (declared, not asked). ④ send's mime lookup (`^.*[./\\]`) cannot cross a CR in a name, so such a file is `application/octet-stream` (pre-existing, unchanged). The remote branch (`?host=`) names inside `RemoteFs.downloadTo` (below). `/api/download`, `/api/download-zip` and `/api/file/serve/*` are untouched.

THE CENSUS (scripts/test-raw-filename.mjs ⑥): every byte-serving site — `sendFile(` / `.pipe(res` / `res.download(` / `.downloadTo(` / `.downloadZipTo(` — under src/routes/**, src/server/**, src/*.js and server.js is a row: NAMED (a `Content-Disposition` inside the handler's own source span, verified) or DECLARED with the reason a browser never saves it under a meaningless name (path-addressed URLs that end in the file's own name — `/api/file/serve/*`, recordings, plugin assets, the node tarball relay, /dav, xterm.css; agent-only routes; proxies; an HTML page; a trace frame named `before`/`after` by its URL). An unclassified site, a site claimed twice or a dead row is red; CONTROLS: the naming stripped ⇒ red on the raw row, a planted nameless route ⇒ an unclassified site. A NEW route that streams bytes a browser can show must name them (`contentDisposition`) or be declared with a reason.

### src/remote-fs.js — downloadTo ALWAYS names the file (lane raw-filename)

`downloadTo(id, filePath, res, {attachment})`: `attachment` (the `/api/download?host=` caller) = `contentDisposition(name, 'attachment')`, both forms (r2, below); otherwise `inline` + both forms from src/file-disposition.js, set JUST BEFORE THE FIRST BYTE, or at a successful EMPTY end (a zero-byte file is named) — both transports through a `beforeBody` hook: ssh = `_streamChild` (a `once('data')` registered AHEAD of the pipe — listeners run in order, so it names before the pipe's first write), dial = `_devStreamTo`. r2 (3) — `_streamChild(child, res, {beforeBody})` OWNS THE SSH STREAM: the response ENDS ON THE CHILD'S EXIT (`pipe(res, {end: false})`), so a command that fails before its first byte answers 404 with the caller's name and type withdrawn — before, pipe's default end had already sent an EMPTY 200 by the time `cat`'s exit code arrived (the `code !== 0 && !res.headersSent` 404 was dead code), so a missing remote file previewed as nothing and a remote Download saved an empty file under the name; a failed spawn (no ssh binary) answers 502 — an unhandled child `'error'` was server.js's `uncaughtException` ⇒ `process.exit(1)`, the whole hub; and a viewer that goes away (`res` 'close' before the child's) ENDS the child — an unpiped stdout blocked the remote `cat` forever, one leaked ssh per aborted `<video>` seek. `downloadZipTo` uses the same helper (a missing folder = 404, no zip type) and its dial branch is `notFoundOnFail` now; `_devStreamTo` withdraws the name and type before a 404 / 502. Gate: test-raw-filename ③ (the REAL RemoteFs over a fake ssh host whose `_spawn` exec's the same `cat` locally, and a fake dial device whose `runStream` does) + ③b (missing file / folder ⇒ 404 on raw, download, download-zip, both transports; zero-byte ⇒ 200 named; no ssh binary ⇒ 502 with no uncaught error; an abort after the first chunk of 32 MB ⇒ the child ended — CONTROLS the pre-r2 stream: the empty 200, the uncaught ENOENT, the child still blocked) + ⑤ (a copy without the inline naming ⇒ both legs red).

r2 (coordinator, 2026-09-28) — REMOTE DOWNLOAD OF A CJK NAME WAS NEVER ANSWERED: the ATTACHMENT headers (`downloadTo`'s and `downloadZipTo`'s `filename="<raw name>"`) put the raw name into the header, so a file or folder name with any character above U+00FF (every CJK name) made `setHeader` throw `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` synchronously inside the async route — server.js's log-only `unhandledRejection` swallowed it: on a remote machine Download / Download as Zip of `截图.png` / `报告/` hung (the control in test-raw-filename ⑤ reproduces it: no answer in 2 s, three unhandled ERR_INVALID_CHAR). FIX, two halves: both headers are `contentDisposition(…, 'attachment')` — printable ASCII by construction (`(base || 'archive') + '.zip'` for the zip); and files.js's `remoteStream(res, fn)` wraps EVERY remote streaming dispatch (raw, download, download-zip) so any synchronous throw from a remote stream helper is a 502 with no name, never a hang (the class had bitten before: the dial `_spawn`, B-0d70 review). test-raw-filename ⑦ = THE SPELLING CENSUS: every Content-Disposition value in the tree is `contentDisposition()`'s (directly or through the variable it assigned) or DECLARED ASCII by construction (channels.js's two forms, the local zip's filename*, published-pages' dispositionName, the config export's dated name).

r2 (2) — THE CODE EDITOR'S ⇩ DOWNLOAD DROPPED THE HOST: src/lib/code-editor.js opened `/api/download?path=…` without `&host=`, so for a remote file (`this._host`) it asked THIS machine for a path of the same name (a 404, or the WRONG file when one existed). It carries `this._host` now. test-raw-filename ⑧ = THE CLIENT HOST CENSUS: every `/api/file/raw?path=`, `/api/download?path=`, `/api/download-zip?path=` built in src/lib/** carries the machine (`hq`, `_hp()`, `host`) or is DECLARED local-only (jobs-panel's picture — a Background Work job runs on this machine); CONTROL the pre-r2 line ⇒ red; test-raw-filename-chrome ⑤ presses the REAL button in an editor opened locally and on host `box` (red on the reverted line). Not in scope and declared: the editor's HTML preview builds `<base href="/api/file/serve/<dir>/?host=…">`, but `/api/file/serve/*` has no remote dispatch and a base href drops its query — a REMOTE HTML file's relative assets are asked of this machine.

### CHANGELOG.md + CHANGELOG.zh.md + CHANGELOG.ja.md — the user's changelog (2026-09-30)
  The three files a user reads — in ⚙ → Update VibeSpace… (every entry between the running version and the latest, in the device's language) and on GitHub. The rules are docs/changelog-style.md: the title (`# Changelog` / `# 更新日志` / `# 更新履歴`) + ONE intro line pointing at the engineering log, then one entry per version, newest first, `## <version> — <YYYY-MM-DD>` (nothing else on the line), the sections Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed / Security / Maintenance in that order (新增 / 更改 / 修复 / 移除 / 安全 / 维护; 追加 / 変更 / 修正 / 削除 / セキュリティ / メンテナンス), one plain one-line bullet per change (en ≤ 160, zh / ja ≤ 90 code points), UI names spelled as the i18n dictionaries spell them; a version with nothing a user would notice = the one exact Maintenance line. NEVER in these files: lane / round / verify / census / control / patched copy, suite or file names, function names, shas, backlog / incident ids, §, kb references, counts of tests, how something was measured, quotes of anyone's messages (the English file bans CJK text outright). The English file is the canonical text and the list of versions; zh / ja have the SAME versions, dates, sections and bullet counts (parity) — only the words differ, written as a native changelog would be. Built on 2026-09-30 from 825 versions rewritten in 25 slices (writers + judges + translators; the old text is the engineering log), plus 2.369.198 written from its engineering block. **A release writes its entry in all three files AND its engineering section in the same commit;** a branch may write the next version's entry before the integrator bumps package.json (the gate accepts package.json's version or the next patch). Gate: scripts/test-changelog-style.mjs (fast). Gate inputs for the pre-push hook's `is_code_path` (the zh / ja files and the engineering log are listed there; test-ci-gate §4 derives the set).

### docs/changelog-engineering.md — the engineers' record of every release
  The old CHANGELOG.md, moved VERBATIM on 2026-09-30 under a short header (what this file is; that CHANGELOG.md is the user's). Below its own `# Changelog` title: every release up to 2.369.198 exactly as it was written (headings `## <version> — <summary>`). Above that title, newest first: every later release's section under the same `## <version> — <date>` heading as its user entry — free-form: the lanes, the verification rounds and their findings, the gate reds and their causes, measurements, the choices made and why. test-changelog-style requires a section here for every user version from 2.369.198 on; test-codex-effort-meta's claim checks and test-harness-honesty's version marker read a release's TOPIC here (the user file's headings name none; a REF from before the move falls back to its CHANGELOG.md). It is a gate input (pre-push `is_code_path`). The file is > 2 MB: a `git show <ref>:` read of it needs an explicit maxBuffer (test-codex-effort-meta's ENOBUFS control reads it).

### src/changelog-style.js (PURE, imports nothing)
  The executable form of docs/changelog-style.md, ONE table per language: `SECTIONS` (the six section words in their order), `MAINTENANCE_LINE`, `TITLE`, `MAX_BULLET` (en 160 / zh 90 / ja 90 code points), `BANNED` ([pattern, rule] — lane, round N, verify, census, patched copy, control, test-suite name, file path, commit sha, backlog id, incident id, § / 不变量, owner, user pseudonym, integrator, tier, suite, kb reference, wiring pin, mutant, the zh / ja jargon rows), `CJK` (the English file's quote detector: U+3000–U+9FFF, U+FF00–U+FFEF). `lint(text, lang)` → problems `{line, version, rule, message}` whose `rule` names what broke (`title`, `preamble`, `heading`, `order`, `date-order`, `section-unknown`, `section-order`, `bullet-before-section`, `length`, `nested`, `banned:<rule>`, `banned:cjk`, `maintenance`, `no-section`, `stray-line`); `parity(en, text, lang)` → `version-count` / `version-order` / `date` / `sections`; `versionsOf`, `headedVersions` (any `## <version>` heading — the engineering log's old headings carry a summary), `compareVersions`, `engineeringGaps(user, log, since = ENGINEERING_LOG_SINCE '2.369.198')`. ### src/server/ops-routes.js — `canonicalFile()` + `GET /api/changelog-diff?lang=` (2026-09-30)
  ONE reader of a file on the canonical repo's raw master (`canonicalFile(name, timeoutMs)` → `{ok, status, text}`, never throws) serves /api/version's package.json and the user changelogs. `VIBESPACE_CHANGELOG_FIXTURE_DIR` (TEST ONLY) reads the same names from a local directory — a missing file answers 404 — so no gate reaches the network. The changelog is cached PER LANGUAGE (`changelogCache[lang] = {text, fetchedAt}`) under the old rules (15 min; `fresh` = a 60-s floor; stamped even on failure; a network failure keeps the last text, a 404 = the canonical has no such file). `lang` ∈ en / zh / ja (else en); the ENGLISH file lists the versions and each entry comes from the language file when that file heads the version, else in English — every entry carries `lang` (so an older canonical without the translations, or a version not translated yet, degrades per entry, never to nothing). Response `{current, latest, lang, entries:[{version, head, body, lang}], atLatest}`; the parser still keys on `## <version>` (old-format files parse unchanged). Old clients (no `lang`) get English.

### The Update dialog (app.js `_showUpdateConfirmDialog` + `changelogEntryEl`) + scripts/test-update-dialog.mjs (heavy)
  The dialog asks `/api/changelog-diff?fresh=1&lang=<resolveLang()>` — the device's resolved UI language (what `vibespace.lang` resolves to) — and builds each entry with DOM + textContent (the text comes off the network): `v<version> — <date>` (just `v<version>` for an old-format head), an `h4.ucl-sec` per `### Section` line (the word comes from the file, already in the user's language — no t() key), a `ul.ucl-items` per run of `- ` lines, any other line a `p.ucl-para` (an old-format entry served to a new client; `**bold**` markers dropped) — never a `<pre>`; the entry box carries `lang` so CJK text gets its font. CSS: `.ucl-sec` / `.ucl-items` / `.ucl-para` (the retired `.ucl-body` was the pre-wrap wall). The heavy suite opens ⚙ → Update VibeSpace… the way a person does (mouse at 1280 px, touch at 390 px) on a worktree server whose canonical is a fixture built from the REAL files (top entries relabelled newer than the running version; the second-newest replaced by the old-format engineering block, absent from zh; no ja file): zh and en at both widths, ja at 1280 px — dated version lines, section headings in the right language, li counts = the file's bullets, the untranslated entry in English, the old-format entry as paragraphs, only div / h4 / ul / li / p inside the list, the dialog fits a phone; screenshots kept in the suite's shots dir.

The rules a conversation's own browser keeps its logins + tabs by: `keptUrl` (http(s) only, user:password stripped, ≤ 2048, never cut into another address), `keptTitle` (the name door), `keptTabsOf` (web pages, ≤ 20, ONE current tab, nothing else — no tab / target id), `mergeTabs` (the stop: CDP decides WHICH pages, the relay their ORDER and the current one), `stopWhyOf` / `restoreKindFor` (D2: turn-idle / idle / heal / restart / conversation-gone ⇒ `auto`; user / agent ⇒ none), `keptLimits` (the three settings, MB → bytes, floors 64 / 256), `keptEndVerdict` (D1 — a Terminate is not an end; `endsAtTerminate` is the one flag; an hour's grace for a key no binding names), `CACHE_SUBDIRS` vs `NEVER_TRIMMED`, `keptRetentionPlan` (per conversation: caches first, logins never; total: whole STOPPED entries least-recently-used first; a running one is only reported; a CARRIED one — a live session carries its key, only its browser stopped — is never removed whole, reported by key: verify F2), `normalizeKeptStore` (every entry judged on the way out; a child key never an entry; the directory never carried — derived from the key where used). ### src/server/browser-kept.js — ORCH THE KEPT BROWSERS' STORE (lane browser-resume, chunk A, NEW)
`create({dataDir, keeper (getter), liveKeys, bindings?, serverSetting, broadcast, log, now, execFileImpl, sweepEveryMs, endsAtTerminate})` → `noteStart / noteTabs / noteStop / noteDeliberate / latestOf / has / keys / get / brief / list / limits / forget / adopted / sweep / boot / shutdown / dirOf`. `data/browser-kept.json` via writeJsonAtomic 0600 (a corrupt file SET ASIDE `.corrupt-<ts>` with its bytes); a running browser's list persisted at most every 30 s (`saveSoon`), flushed at `shutdown` (called by the keeper's). `dirOf(bk)` = `data/browser-profiles/<bk>`, derived — never read from the store. A deliberate close heard ≤ 2 min before a stop names it, one heard just after re-words it (`amend` in `noteDeliberate`). `forget` refuses a live / starting browser (`kept_live`) and never removes a directory a registered profile names (`keeper.profileDirRegistered` — the entry goes, the directory stays); a removal (and a cache trim) RENAMES aside first (`<dir>.removing-<ms>-<hex>`, atomic) then removes — a start meanwhile lands on a fresh directory, never a half-deleted one; `removeEntry` re-asks liveness after its await; the sweep's two rules pass `unlessCarried` so a key a live session carries is re-asked AT THE ACT (`carriedNow`, fail closed) — the plan's rows carry `carried` read after the measure's await (verify F2). `sweep` (boot + hourly + the panel's Sweep; single flight): D1's ends (nothing ends when the live sessions or the bindings cannot be read), `du -sbl` over every directory + cache subdir (a child process, 120 s timeout), the PURE plan, each act re-asking liveness first, sizes written back, one journal line per rule, `browser-kept-updated` broadcast. Wired in mounts-plugins-wiring before the keeper (`kept: browserKept`), booted after the keeper's boot. Gate: test-browser-kept ④ (+ 100 real scratch dirs under a fake du).

**Verify r2 (Y1c).** Every read (`get` / `brief` / `list`) JUDGES the directory on disk (`judged`: `statSync` of `dirOf(bk)`; gone ⇒ `hasDir:false`, kind tabs-only, said once per key) — the file's `hasDir` is what the last stop saw, not a fact of the disk; the file is never rewritten for it (the next start makes a fresh directory and notes `hasDir` again). Gate: test-browser-kept ④ + ⑬ control.

### src/fd-budget.js + src/server/fd-gauge.js — THE SERVER'S FILE HANDLES, COUNTED AND NAMED (lane-dead-bridge, 2026-09-30, NEW)

**verify r1: a notice nobody was there to see does not spend the hour.** `serverNotice` answers how many clients received it and does not burn its key at 0 (a boot probe fires into an empty client set); the gauge and the write-error blame now take that count — undelivered ⇒ tried again at the next sample / the next failed write — while the `[fd]` journal line keeps its own once-an-hour clock (`lastJournalAt` / `journaled`). A sink that answers no count is taken as heard (the suites' stubs). Gate: test-fd-limit §E (no client ⇒ tried again next minute, journalled once; once heard, not again in the hour).

**The incident.** 12:03:17 `EMFILE: too many open files, open '…/data/session-status.json.tmp'` from session-status's 500 ms debounce timer (a bare writeFileSync) ⇒ uncaughtException ⇒ exit(1). The server was NOT out of handles (soft 524288 — node raises its own; ~75 held). The workspace is `fuse.bindfs` (root, started by fstab — its own `.mount` unit) at the default soft 1024, sitting at 947 (~700 of them another group's mmapped venv — lane-lark-p2p r3 note, 12:05; `sudo prlimit --pid 3482 --nofile=65536:524288` was applied then and reverts when bindfs restarts — the durable fix is a `[Mount] LimitNOFILE=` drop-in, the machine owner's). A FUSE daemon's EMFILE is relayed to the caller's open() verbatim.

**PURE src/fd-budget.js** (imports nothing): `readLimits` (/proc/self/limits → {soft, hard}), `fdKind` / `tallyKinds` (readlink targets → socket/pipe/pty/anon/file/device/other + the busiest folders), `gaugeVerdict` (≥ 80 % of the soft limit ⇒ high; a report at most once per hour; RE-JUDGED EVERY SAMPLE so it falls the moment the count drops — never latched), `fdBudget({sessions, clients, streams, workers, pipes, base})` (the boot estimate; per-item costs measured on production: 1 pty master per local dtach attach, 3 handles per event loop, ~20 child stdio pipes), `mountOf` (longest mount-point prefix in /proc/self/mountinfo; `\040` decoded), `emfileBlame` (`this-server` when our own count ≥ 90 % of our soft limit · `file-system` when the path is on a `fuse*` mount and we are far below · `system` for ENFILE · `unknown` otherwise, both numbers said), `gaugeWords` ({text, i18n}). The two notice sentences are `i18nKey` constants (GAUGE_KEY, FS_BLAME_KEY) with zh/ja.

**ORCH src/server/fd-gauge.js** (procfs only, never a mountpoint, never a spawn): `bootLine(work)` = `[fd] open-files limit: soft S / hard H (node raises its soft limit …); open now: N; estimate for K session(s): E (…)` — logged by server.js right after restoreSessions; `start()` = an async /proc/self/fd sample every 60 s (readdir counts all; readlink only the first SAMPLE_CAP 4096) → ONE server notice an hour (key `fd-gauge:<hour>`, `i18n`) naming the holders by kind; `blame(err, file)` (SYNC — the crash handler calls it for EMFILE/ENFILE) and `reportWriteError(err, file, {failures, retryMs})` (one journal line per failure streak, one notice an hour per (code, mount)). **A FULL TABLE IS NOT BLINDNESS:** at EMFILE even /proc/self/fd and /proc/self/limits cannot be opened, so a readdir refused with EMFILE/ENFILE IS the verdict (count = the last-known soft limit — procfs is never a FUSE daemon) and the limits are cached from the last good read.

**The stores (session-status.js + user-todos.js, twins):** the debounce timer calls `_flushFromTimer()` — a failed write keeps the state DIRTY, retries with backoff 1 s → 60 s (unref'd), and calls `onWriteError` (server.js → fdGauge.reportWriteError). The exit-path `flush()` still throws to its (guarding) callers. **src/channel-store.js's index** got the same rule (`flushFromTimer` for the debounce AND the 2 s interval; `dirty` cleared only once the write landed — it was cleared BEFORE the write, so a failed one was silently dropped): MEASURED in test-restore-liveness ⑤, a server held at a full table died in THIS timer once session-status was fixed. A minute at a full table then met: session-status (named), the channels index (owed + retried), port-forwards / usage cursors / integrations (already guarded) — none ended the server. Not a census of every timer write in the tree: a writer that fires less often than once a minute at a full table is not covered by that measurement. Gates: test-fd-limit (fast, 43: §A template, §B the node-raise premise measured, §C boot line + estimate, §D gauge walk + a LATCHED copy caught, §E the ORCH gauge over a fake /proc, §F blame + mountOf, §G the guarded flushes + the PRE-FIX copy dying of EISDIR in a child, §H wiring) + test-restore-liveness ⑤ (a prlimit'd server with its table filled survives the status write and names "This server ran out … holds 640 of 640"; the pre-fix copy dies of it).

### src/bridge-liveness.js + src/server/bridge-watch.js — THE DEAD-BRIDGE WATCH (lane-dead-bridge, 2026-09-30, NEW)

**Why the bridge stayed dead** (reproduced: scripts/test-dead-bridge.mjs §1 on raw dtach 0.9 + node-pty, §2–§4 on a worktree server). ① node-pty's forkpty master has NO FD_CLOEXEC (node-pty 1.1.0 sets only O_NONBLOCK) and libuv closes nothing on spawn ⇒ every process the server spawns AFTER an attach inherits that attach's pty master (production, measured via /proc/*/fdinfo tty-index: rclone mounts, a Background Work job's wrapper + sh + python3, agent-browser + chrome, and every LATER dtach client — a chain). ② The crash path (`uncaughtException` → flush → exit) killed no attach pty; the clean shutdown does (`s.pty.kill()` ⇒ SIGHUP). With the masters held elsewhere the kernel never hangs the ptys up ⇒ the old clients survive, reparented to systemd --user, blocked writing to a pty nobody reads (13 still alive in production at 16:40). ③ dtach 0.9's master: pty_activity() reads one chunk then select()s until ANY attached client is writable (or the listening socket is readable) and loops; the main loop runs control → clients → pty, so a NEW client accepted while the pty is readable is followed by pty_activity BEFORE its MSG_ATTACH packet is read ⇒ never attached, the master stuck again. ④ dtach -a writes its own `\e[H\e[J` to its stdout on connect ⇒ the 09-09 attach probe's "byte within 4.6 s" is the CLIENT's, not the master's: it reads a dead bridge as alive. ⑤ The wrapper's TTY stdout write is synchronous (node tty) ⇒ the wrapper blocks entirely (its .buf persist timer never runs — the buffer-file witness is BLIND to this shape); the CLI's pipe stdout is asynchronous ⇒ claude queued three hours in memory and kept calling the API (the OTel witness sees it). ⑥ Ending the orphan unsticks the master by itself (0 % CPU, no spin), but dtach DISCARDS every read while no client is attached ⇒ attach FIRST, then kill: the dropped read is the one the master held, older than everything still in the pty (measured: an unbroken run from before the freeze); kill-then-attach 400 ms later lost 81 records.

**PURE src/bridge-liveness.js:** `orphanAttachVerdict({argv, ppid, parentComm, ttyNr, socketsDir, selfPid})` — a `dtach -a|-c|-A <socketsDir>/cw-*` WITH a controlling terminal (stat tty_nr ≠ 0) whose parent is init or a subreaper named `systemd`. MEASURED: a session the server CREATED is attached by the `dtach -c` process itself (it forks the master and stays as the client) — same argv as its master, told apart ONLY by the tty (master: tty_nr 0, fd 1 /dev/null); a process with no tty is NEVER a candidate (ending a master ends the session). Kept: ours (ppid = this server), a person's own attach (parent alive), the daemon's, another tree's socket, a prefix-sibling dir, an escaping path, a non-`cw-` socket. `bridgeVerdict({now, silenceMs, lastByteAt, attachedAt, bufMtimeMs, lastApiAt, heals})` — since = max(last byte, the watch's start); silent ≥ N AND (buffer-file mtime OR an OTel api_request) > since + 20 s ⇒ `dead`; no witness ⇒ `quiet` (never healed); 3 heals an hour ⇒ `budget`. `silenceMsOf` (the setting, default 3 min, 0 = off), `tickMsOf` (a quarter of the silence, 2–30 s), `spanWords`, the catch-up reducer (`catchUpStart/Note/Settled/LostAt/Card` — records counted through record-lateness's `judge`; settled by a record stamped ≤ 10 s ago or 15 s of quiet; the card only when something came AND the gap ≥ 60 s).

**ORCH src/server/bridge-watch.js:** `endAttachPtys()` = THE teardown (shutdownNow AND the uncaughtException handler — the crash path had none); `sweepOrphans({socketPath, why})` (sync procfs scan of `dtach` comms, SIGKILL, one journal line `[bridge] <why>: ended N orphaned dtach attach client(s) …`); `bootSweep()` (server.js, 1.5 s after restoreSessions; async — a session with an orphan first waits ≤ 3 s for its OWN restored attach's first byte, i.e. the client connected, then the orphans are ended) + a catch-up armed on every freed session; `tick()` (async stat of `data/session-buffers/<id>.buf`, `otelIngest.lastApiRequestAt(claudeSessionId)`; a talking session costs no stat); `heal` = `reattachLocalPty(id, s, 'dead bridge: no output for 2m32s while the CLI made an API request …', {kind:'heal'})`; `afterReattach(id, s, {kind, silentSince})` — session-stdout's `reattachLocalPty` calls it after EVERY local re-attach (the watch, the broken-stdin detector, the attach probe): arms the catch-up and, once the new pty produced its first byte, sweeps that socket's orphans. A heal that brought nothing (no record, ≤ 6 bytes) doubles that session's silence (cap 1 h) — a CLI whose requests print nothing (background agents) is quiet, not dead. The catch-up's records are counted in the claude parse (`session._bridgeCatchUp?.note?.(msg)` right after `noteStreamRecord`); when it settles: `[bridge] <id>: heal caught up N record(s) / B byte(s) — L of them stamped > 2 min before they arrived …` and ONE peer card from VibeSpace (`kind:'notification'`): "The connection to this conversation's output was lost at HH:MM and restored at HH:MM — N records caught up (they are shown, not re-run)." (journalled as `[bridge] <id>: card — …`). The engine's gate (lane-hot-switch) keeps every late record from moving the pool or the readings. Session fields `_bridgeHeals` / `_bridgeCatchUp` / `_bridgeEmptyHeals` (owner `bridge`). Setting `session.deadBridgeMinutes` (Session, default 3, 0 = off, zh/ja). otel-ingest: `lastApiRequestAt(sid)` — the newest api_request per conversation, kept for EVERY parsed row (no rid / no org still proves the CLI worked), memory only, ≤ 2000 sids.

**Gates:** test-bridge-liveness (fast, 56: the orphan table incl. the production rows + a copy without the tty guard reading the MASTER as an orphan; the verdict table; the catch-up + card; the watch over a fake /proc: what it ends, quiet vs dead, the budget said once, the empty-heal backoff; the wiring), test-dead-bridge (heavy, ~7 min: §1 the mechanism + the order control, §2 SIGKILL with a job holding the master ⇒ the boot sweep, §3 the pre-fix copy stays DARK 25 s while the CLI writes 1 200 records, §4 a paused client the sweep may not touch ⇒ the watch heals at ~152 s on the OTel witness, the late gate's journal line, 8 000+ records caught up / 2 000+ late, the card in the chat, one heal), test-restore-liveness ⑤.

### src/design-model.js — PURE THE DESIGN CANVAS MODEL (lane design-core, 2026-10-02, NEW)
VibeSpace's own design canvas (owner 2026-10-02: build our own instead of depending on the Claude CLI's kit; docs/design-design-window.md §3 is the contract the hub and the window share). CJS, imports nothing — the hub requires it, the window bundles it. An artboard is one plain, complete HTML document in the conversation's folder (`designs/<slug>/<Name>.html`), `design.json` places them (optional), images sit beside them and are referenced by name. `validateManifest(json)` (a string or a parsed value) → `{ok, manifest}` | `{ok:false, refusals:[{code, where, why}]}`: CLOSED keys at every level (top / page / artboard row / note / launch — a key the loader would drop is refused BY NAME, never ignored), bounds (w/h 120–8000, coordinates ±100000, x and y both or neither, note w 40–4000, ≤ 40 artboards / 40 pages / 200 notes, note text ≤ 5000, title ≤ 120, the 8 named note colours, print fixed|flow, launch canvas{page?} | focused{file}), names on the grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9 _.-]{0,80}\.html$` unique ignoring case, every page reference checked; refusals bounded at 50; the codes are the closed `CODES` set. `layoutOf(manifest, names)` → `{frames, warnings}`: manifest rows as written; rows without x/y and the folder's unlisted artboards (Main.html first, then by name) auto-placed in rows below every placed frame of their page (80 px between frames, a new row 120 px down past 8000 px of width); `missing` (listed, not on disk) and `dup` (a case twin) flags; overlaps WARNED, never moved. `artboardVerdict(name, html, {assets, bytes})`: name grammar, ≤ 2 MiB (UTF-8 bytes), `<html>` + `<body>`, no `<base>`, every relative reference (`src=` on a tag, `url()` in a style attribute or a `<style>` block — never inside a script, a comment or a textarea) is an image beside the artboard that exists and is ≤ 2 MiB; a root path, a subfolder, a non-image are `bad_ref` with what to do. `inlineAssets(html, readAsset)` = THE ONE bundler (the window's read AND publish): `readAsset(name)` → base64 | null; only the value span is replaced (a style attribute keeps its delimiters), a missing image is left as written and named, a reader answer that is not base64 is never spliced. `elementPath(nodes)` / `pickQuote({file, path, tag, text})` = the comment's quote line `Main.html › header > nav > a.cta ("Get started")` — every field is the frame's (untrusted): the path keeps selector characters only, text ≤ 120. `commentText(quote, text)` COMPOSES `[Design comment] <quote>: <text>`; the hub belts the whole line at its one door (src/server/design-engine.js). `bundleCanvas({manifest, files, runtimeJs})` = the published page (our shell + `<script type="application/json" id="vibespace-design-doc">` holding `{v:1, title, manifest, files}` with every `<` escaped, then the runtime — public/design-viewer.js once the window lane builds it, else `PLACEHOLDER_RUNTIME`, our own column of script-only sandboxed frames); `readBundle` is the inverse and refuses by name. `sizeVerdict` (warn past 8 MB, refuse at 25 MB) / `readCapsVerdict` (40 artboards, 24 MB per read). EVERY WALKER IS LINEAR BY CONSTRUCTION: the tag scan reads one code unit at a time (`charCodeAt` — no whole-string native from an offset inside a loop), so its work is the text's length; the gate measures it.

### src/lib/design-canvas-model.js — PURE the canvas's rules (NEW)

Imports ONE module — the hub's PURE src/design-model.js (int201) — DOM-free; node-imported by test-design-canvas, bundled into the window AND the published page's runtime (the viewer bundle carries the model). **The view** `{x, y, z}` (a world point is drawn at `x + wx·z`): `clampZoom` (0 / NaN ⇒ 1, never a collapsed world), `zoomStep` (the ladder 5 %…400 %; a between-rungs zoom goes to its neighbour), `zoomAt(view, z, anchor)` (the world point under the anchor stays), `panBy`, `pinchView` (distance ratio around the midpoint + the midpoint's travel), `toScreen` / `toWorld`, `boundsOf`, `fitView(bounds, pane, {pad 40, maxZ 1})` (a lone small artboard at its own size, an empty world / a pane with no size ⇒ the identity, never NaN), `focusView(rect, pane)` = one artboard at fit-width (≤ 2×) with `frameH` = its own height or the pane's when taller (its document scrolls inside). **The world:** `framesOf(manifest, names)` IS the hub's rule, imported (int201 — L2's reader-side twin became the import): design-model.js `validateManifest` (a manifest the hub would refuse is laid out WITHOUT it, as the hub's read does — never half-applied) then `layoutOf` (manifest rows as written, the rest Main.html first then by name, 80 px apart, a new row 120 px below past 8000 px, `missing` / `dup` marked), the page read through `pageOf` — for a reader holding only the manifest (the published page's state block); the window's read carries the hub's own placement, which wins (`hubFrames` bounds it). `LAYOUT` / `ENTRY_FILE` / `NOTE_COLORS` / `isArtboardName` / `stemOf` are read off design-model.js (one home for the numbers). `pagesOf` (none ⇒ ONE unnamed page), `pageOf` (an unknown page ⇒ the first), `notesOn` (bounded: text 5000, w 40–4000, an unknown colour gray), `NOTE_COLOR_VARS` (the eight named colours as theme tokens, color-mix tints — never a literal), `launchOf`. **The read:** `normalizeRead(resp)` accepts the read's spellings (a `frames` list = the hub's placement; artboards as a list with per-entry `ok/code/why` or a `verdict`, or a `files` map) and is LOUD: null (fetchJson's "never answered") ⇒ `{error:{code:'unreachable'}}`, a refusal keeps its code + the manifest refusals by name — never an empty canvas; `normalizeDoc` = a published page's `{v:1, title, manifest, files}` block. **THE PICK FENCE** (an artboard is agent-written HTML in the owner's logged-in page; its own scripts can post too): `PICK_KINDS` = the CLOSED set `design-pick` | `design-key` (Escape only), `FRAME_KINDS` = `design-mode`; `pickFence(data, frame)` drops a non-object / an unknown kind / a tag that is not a tag name, bounds every string (`cleanLine`: bounded BEFORE any work, controls + bidi + zero-width folded, path 200 / text 120), clamps the rect to the artboard and takes the FILE from the frame record (a message cannot claim another artboard); `routeMessage(ev, frames)` believes a message only when `ev.source` IS one of the canvas's frames' windows — by identity, never an origin string (every frame is an opaque origin). `quoteLine(pick)` = the composer's read-only line = the hub's own `pickQuote` over the same facts, imported (int201), the text folded first (hidden characters, one line) — the line the agent receives is spelled by the same function. **The frame documents:** `headInsertAt` (after `<head>`, else `<html>`, else the doctype — never before it: quirks mode — else 0; `indexOf` in a 64 KiB head window, never a regex over the artboard: bound before parse), `frameSrcdoc(html, pickerSrc)` = the picker FIRST in the head (before the artboard's scripts; `</script` / `<!--` escaped), `printCss(row)` (fixed = ONE page the artboard's size; flow = paginated, 12 mm), `printSrcdoc` (the stylesheet at the head's END, after the artboard's own, + the print call on load).

### src/lib/design-canvas.js — THE DESIGN CANVAS, the DOM core (NEW)

`createDesignCanvas(host, {signal, counterZoom, pickerSrc, words, onPick, onKey, onActivate, onChange})` → `{el, world, setFrames, updateFrame, fit, zoomBy, zoomTo, setPage, focus, setPick, setView, view, page, pages, focused, pick, frames, frameScreenRect, zoom, dispose}`. Imports ONLY the model — no App, utils, i18n or ws (the published page bundles it; the window injects its words and its `COUNTER_ZOOM`). **The viewport** sits at NET zoom 1 (`counterZoom` from the caller; inc-mtdrm922's rule — the pointer is read in viewport px) and the world is ONE transformed layer (`translate(x,y) scale(z)`, `--dc-inv` = 1/z for the constant-size name strips). **One frame per artboard:** `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc>` — never allow-same-origin, no other allowance (the gate pins it); `referrerpolicy=no-referrer`; `updateFrame(file, html, refused)` swaps ONE srcdoc in place and only when it changed (the element, the view and every other frame untouched); a refused frame draws a NAMED card (`words.refused(code, why)` — "artboard refused: …"; a listed-but-absent file its own sentence), never a blank box. **Navigating vs using:** on the canvas a transparent SHIELD lies over every frame, so wheel (pan; ctrl / ⌘ = zoom at the pointer; shift = sideways), drag and two-finger pinch move the canvas wherever the pointer is; a dblclick on a shield (desktop) / a touch tap (phone) is `onActivate(file, how)`; the FOCUSED view (`focus(file)`: one artboard at fit-width, the others and the notes hidden, the shield lifted, the pre-focus view restored by `focus(null)`) and the PICK mode (`setPick(on, color)`: every shield lifted, `design-mode` said to every frame and again at each frame's load) make the artboard live. A drag captures its pointer at the door and ends on up / cancel / lost capture. **The pick channel:** ONE `message` listener per canvas, on the caller's signal, through `routeMessage` over exactly this canvas's frames (their `contentWindow`, read at message time); a `design-pick` reaches `onPick` only in pick mode; the canvas posts ONE thing to its frames (`design-mode`). `setFrames(read, {keepView})`: the first read (or `keepView` false) applies the manifest's `launch` (a page fitted, or one artboard focused); a reload / manifest change keeps pan, zoom, page and focus and reloads no frame whose document is unchanged. Notes are TEXT (`textContent`), the core writes no innerHTML. A ResizeObserver fits the first time the pane gets a size (a hidden desktop / tab) and keeps a focused artboard at fit-width; a user-moved canvas is never re-fitted by a resize. Keys on the focused viewport: `+` / `-` / `0` (fit).

### src/lib/design-pick.js — THE ELEMENT PICKER, injected into every artboard frame (NEW)

`designPicker()` is a SELF-CONTAINED plain-ES5 function whose SOURCE TEXT is injected (`pickerSource()` = `(<fn>)();`, placed FIRST in the artboard's head by the model's `frameSrcdoc`) — never a closure over the module, never an argument from the artboard. Inside the frame (an opaque origin): it hears ONE kind, `design-mode {pick, color}`, and only from `e.source === parent`; `pick` must be exactly `true`; `color` (the theme accent the canvas reads) only when it is a `#hex` / `rgb()` shape. While picking: a fixed, pointer-events-none outline follows `pointerover` / `pointermove`; capture-phase listeners registered before the artboard's scripts swallow the press (`mousedown` / `mouseup` / `pointerup` / `dblclick` / `auxclick` / `contextmenu` / `submit` — `pointerdown` is stopped but not prevented, so a touch still makes its click) and the `click` posts `{kind:'design-pick', path, tag, text, rect}` to the parent (`'*'`: the canvas fences by source). `path` = the hub's `elementPath` grammar (tag, `#id` when it is an identifier else ≤ 2 identifier classes, html/body dropped, the last six steps with `… > `, ≤ 200), `text` = aria-label / alt / title / innerText (≤ 120, whitespace collapsed), `rect` = the element's box in the frame's viewport. `Escape` (any time) posts `{kind:'design-key', key:'Escape'}`. It reads no storage, cookie or network and evals nothing. Gate: test-design-canvas ④b (the source run under a mini DOM: only the parent's mode, the swallow, the path / text bounds, Escape, its message passing the canvas's fence unchanged and reading as the contract's quote line; THE MINIFIED source — built in-process by esbuild exactly as the bundle builds it — passing the same table; the census: every kind it sends ∈ `PICK_KINDS`, ONE kind heard ∈ `FRAME_KINDS`, ONE postMessage site; CONTROL = a copy without the parent check, which a foreign window switches on).

### src/lib/design-changes.js — THE CHANGES STRIP (NEW, lane design-changes, 2.369.203)

Design 003 §2.2 (/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/claude-design-replica.md): N changes cost one agent turn. Three chip sources, each a PREVIEW (no file write — owner Q1): a double-click on a text while picking (design-pick.js edits it in place; Enter / a click away reports `design-edit {edit:'text', ref, path, tag, from, to}`; Esc puts this edit's words back); the Style row (text colour / background / font size / spacing → `canvas.tell(file, {kind:'design-style', ref, prop, value})`, the frame previews it `!important` and reports `design-edit {edit:'style', …, from: the computed value}`); Add (a comment chip). THE TRUST RULES: a frame's report reaches the strip only through the canvas core (`canvas.listen`): a TEXT edit only while picking (or ≤ EDIT_GRACE_MS after), from the frame that has or just had the keyboard (iframe `blur` stamps `leftAt`), through its own frameKeyGate; a STYLE report only when it matches the nudge the strip itself asked for (`pending`). One chip per (file, ref, what) — `mergeEdit` keeps the first `from`, drops the chip when edited back. Kept per design in localStorage `vs-design-changes:<host>\u0001<dir>` (≤ 30; record-clear census H1 class `owner`); the previews live in the frame and end with its document (refs are `<frame seed>-<n>`, so an old chip's undo never touches a new document). × = `design-undo`. Send all = `POST /api/design/changes {sessionId, host, dir, items: itemsOf(list)}` ⇒ toast in the hub's words (sent / queued / stashed); a refusal = the floating chip, the chips stay. A chip's title is the hub's own `changeLine`. The phone: the strip appears only with a chip, 44 px targets.

### THE DOC WINDOW — lane doc-window (2.369.215; docs/design-artifacts.zh.md §Doc window)
A markdown deliverable is read, edited and annotated in ONE rendered view, and the conversation that owns it learns the edit by itself. The Design window is the precedent (a window per file, a 2 s watch, comment → THE typing sender / the stash, Send all = ONE message).

### src/doc-model.js — PURE the Doc window's rules (NEW)
CJS, imports nothing (the hub requires it, the window bundles it). **THE FIDELITY RULE** (owner: never a silent rewrite): `rawReasons(source)` = what the rich editor cannot carry even block by block — since lane doc-editor-wheel (2.369.221) only `crlf` and `too_big` (> 1 MiB), each with its plain-words WHY in `RAW_WHY` (the chip says it; zh/ja in the dictionaries). **`patchBlocks(source, maps, plan)`** = THE SAVE: the source's top-level block line ranges + the plan in the new order (`{keep: k}` = untouched block k, its lines byte-identical · `{text}` = an edited / new block) → the file with every untouched block and every line between blocks (blank lines, link and footnote definitions) byte-identical; a deleted block takes one blank run with it; new text gets a blank line from a non-blank neighbour; CRLF / overlap / order refused by name. `fidelityVerdict` (the whole-document compare) is kept for callers. Comments: `commentItem` keeps an optional `line` (the SOURCE line) ⇒ `commentsText` writes `① L12 "quote" — note`. The edit note, the conflict table: unchanged.

### src/lib/doc-markdown.js — the markdown on Tiptap v3 (lane doc-editor-wheel; bundled ONLY into the lazy editor)
**Inline HTML marks (lane doc-raw-blocks, 2.369.246 — a table whose cells held `<code>` read as source):** `HTML_MARKS` (code / kbd / sub / sup / b / strong / i / em ⇒ htmlCode / htmlKbd / htmlSub / htmlSup / htmlBold / htmlItalic, `attrs.tag` = the spelling) + `HtmlBreak` (`<br>` spellings) — `htmlInlineToken(src, lex)` is marked's inline tokenizer (on HtmlBreak's `markdownTokenizer`): a PAIR with no attribute, the close where marked reads it (the rest lexed with the tokenizer off, `scanning`), content without edge spaces ⇒ a mark token; else raw HTML ⇒ `hasHtml` ⇒ a raw block. Each mark's `renderMarkdown` writes its own tag back. Gate: test-doc-wheel's mark table (+ the backticks control).
**A bare `<word>` makes its block raw (diagnosed lane doc-print-fidelity, 2.369.241):** a brief's `/p/<id>` is CommonMark inline raw HTML (an unknown tag) ⇒ `hasHtml` carries the whole block (a heading, a list, a paragraph) as a raw block — by design (the editor would drop the tag); the reading render (doc-window-model `readingHtml`) shows it as text.
The wheel = Tiptap v3 3.31.4 (@tiptap/core, pm, starter-kit, markdown, extension-table, extension-list, extension-image, extension-link — pinned exact; 46 packages, all MIT; ProseMirror underneath, `@tiptap/markdown` = marked + each extension's parse/render), DOM-free (`MarkdownManager` + `getSchema`, node-imported by the suites). `extensions` (StarterKit with a SafeLink whose renderHTML re-validates `safeHref`, Table with `compactTable` — one row per line, no padding, `|` escaped — TaskList/TaskItem, Image through `safeImageSrc`, **RawBlock**). **LOAD = BLOCKS** (`blocksOf` cuts the source with Tiptap's own marked lexer — the tokens' `raw` concatenated IS the source — `loadDoc` parses each block alone with the file's link definitions appended ⇒ every node knows its block; a block the core would DROP words from, raw HTML, front matter ⇒ a **raw block**: carried as written, read-only in the rich view, edited in Raw). **SAVE = `saveDoc`**: the editor's top-level nodes LCS-aligned to the loaded ones; untouched blocks `{keep}`; an edited block by a **line merge** (`mergeBlock`: each line the person did not change keeps its SOURCE text — the `*` bullet, the `1)`, the `_em_`, bare `[XX]`, a table row's padding — the changed span spliced in) verified by re-parsing, else the serializer's text, else refused (`lossy` + its line); empty paragraphs (the editor's trailing one) write nothing. `sourceLine(loaded, doc, pos)` = a selection's SOURCE line (block map + the block serialized up to the position) for the comments strip. Edited blocks inline their reference links (target kept, label gone) — accepted (owner 2026-10-05).

### src/lib/doc-window-ui.js — THE DOC WINDOW'S UI (NEW, inside the lazy bundle)
Its CSS is one `<style id="doc-window-css">` (theme variables only; `.doc-window [hidden]` beats every display rule). **Open:** `/api/file/content` + `/api/file/info` → `docFidelity` → the ProseMirror view (history, Mod-b/i/\`, list keys, Mod-s; images through a nodeView setting `.src` — a relative src served by `/api/file/raw` beside the file; a link click never navigates, Ctrl/⌘-click opens it noopener) or RAW + the chip naming why. **Raw** (aria-pressed) toggles the CodeEditor in place; refused by the chip while the other side holds unsaved edits; back to rich re-judges the fidelity. **Save** = `M.saveVerdict` (the one "Overwrite the agent's newer version?" ask) → `POST /api/file/write {path: THIS window's path}` → `POST /api/doc/edited {summary: M.editSummary(before, after)}`; the raw editor's save is wrapped the same way. **Live:** `/api/file/info` every 2 s on this machine (none on a remote host), on refocus and on the `file-changed` relay → `M.conflictVerdict`: repaint = ONE replaceWith transaction (unchanged nodes keep their DOM, the pane's scroll restored, kept out of history), bar = "Reload (your edits go) | Keep editing". **Comments:** a non-empty selection (250 ms after the last view update, the view focused) → a `.doc-cpop` house popover "Comment" → a note box (a popover; a createModalShell sheet on a phone) → the strip (keyed rows quote + note + ×; localStorage `vs-doc-comments:<host>\u0001<path>`, ≤ 20, record-clear H1 `owner`) → Send all = `POST /api/doc/comments` once. `GET /api/doc/owner` decides the strip's "Open this document from a chat to send comments to it". The strip is a right column on a wide window and a bottom sheet below 640 px or on a phone (a ResizeObserver; 44 px targets on a phone). Every window-level listener is on the window's signal.
**Raw blocks READ (lane doc-raw-blocks, 2.369.246):** the `rawBlock` node view `rawView(node, view, getPos)` (wired in `uiExtensions`) = `div.doc-rawblock[data-raw-block][contenteditable=false][data-rendered]` → a `.doc-raw-head` button (the chip: `{kind} · kept as written · edit source` / `· cannot be rendered ·`) + `.doc-raw-read` (`rawReading(source, {Marked, sanitize: sanitizeHtml})` parsed in an inert DOMParser document, `wrapTables`, local `img` → /api/file/raw) or `.doc-raw-src` (the source, when it reads as nothing). The chip opens `.doc-raw-editor` (textarea `.doc-raw-edit` + Finish) IN PLACE; Esc / Finish / blur ⇒ `setNodeMarkup(pos, {source})` (emptied ⇒ the node is deleted); Ctrl+S commits + saves. `stopEvent` keeps the chip + the box away from ProseMirror; `ignoreMutation` true. The old `data-head` decoration is gone. `wrapTables(d)` (module level) is shared with `exportBody`.
**Export / print (lane doc-print-fidelity, 2.369.241):** `exportBody()` = `readingHtml(sourceNow(), {Marked, sanitize: sanitizeHtml})` → an inert DOMParser document (tables wrapped + `data-cols` = colsBand, local images inlined) — never `S.ed.getHTML()`; printDoc prints once the frame's fonts + images decode (≤ 5 s). **Width + leaving (lane doc-window-width-export, 2.369.239):** `root.dataset.width` = fit | comfortable from `columnRule` (`applyWidth` on every layout pass; the phone hides the `width` tool); `.doc-window[data-width="fit"] .doc-page{max-width:none}`. The bar's right end = comments · `width` (glyph + word, priority 5) · `more` (bar-fold `moreAlways`): its menu = the folded tools + `leaveRows()` — Download .md (`downloadMd`: `dirtyNow()` ⇒ "Save and download?" ⇒ `save()` / Raw's save, then an `<a download>` to `downloadHref`), Export HTML (`exportBody` = `sanitizeHtml(S.ed.getHTML())` from `deps`, tables wrapped, local images → data URLs; `buildExport` adds the `.doc-page .ProseMirror` lines of CSS + the tokens they use), Print (`printDoc`: iframe.doc-print-frame, sandbox allow-same-origin allow-modals, `contentWindow.print()`, `data-printed`, dropped after 120 s / on close), Copy as Markdown (`sourceNow`) / HTML. **Design 020 — the frame (lane doc-editor-ui, 2.369.223; the spec /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/q-020/doc-editor-ui.md, docs/design-doc-editor-wheel.md § UI):** ONE bar `.doc-bar` (36 px; 44 on a phone) of glyph buttons built by `tool(key, glyph, title, priority, act)` / `sep(priority)` into `BAR` and folded by the house `createBarFold` (handed in `deps` with `icons` = UI_ICONS — the lazy entry carries neither; the fold is created AFTER the frame is in the root so its ruler sits inside `.doc-window` and the phone rules reach the clones): [block style ▾ = `showContextMenu` 正文 / 标题 1–3 / 引用 / 代码块] 0 | B I 1 · </> 2 | • 1. ☑ 3 | table link image 4 | raw 5, then the ⋯ (its menu = the folded tools' own acts) and the comments button (glyph + count, priority 0, `margin-left:auto`); pressed state = `aria-pressed` from `isActive` per transaction. Link / Image ask through `showInputDialog` and refuse what `safeHref` / `safeImageSrc` refuse. ONE status strip `.doc-status` of KEYED chips patched in place (`renderStatus`): fidelity `.doc-chip` (every `say()`), conflict `.doc-conflict` (Reload from disk · Keep editing inline; its title the old sentence), comments `.doc-cmts-chip` (toggles the comments strip / sheet), the save dot `.doc-save-btn` at the right (`data-state` dirty → 未保存 · 上次 HH:MM, saved → 已保存 HH:MM [— the chat sees your edit…]; a click saves); the strip is `hidden` while every chip is. The comments strip is CLOSED until the button / chip / a new comment opens it (`S.stripOpen`; a sheet below 640 px). The page: `max-width: calc(76ch + 64px)` border-box, 15 / 1.6, the rhythm `> * + *` .75em, h2–h6 1.4em above, .5em after a heading (declared LAST: equal specificity beats the element rules); h1 26 / h2 20 / h3 16 (phone 23 / 18, 16 px gutters). Task items: doc-markdown's `TaskItem.configure({ HTMLAttributes: { 'data-type': 'taskItem' } })` — Tiptap's node view drew `li > label + div` WITHOUT the data-type its renderHTML carries, so the row rule never matched (the checkbox on its own line, red on c34711faa); the house checkbox is `appearance:none` + a clip-path tick in `--accent-fg`. Node DECORATIONS (a plugin, recomputed on docChanged only): a code block's fence language → `pre[data-lang]` (the `::after` chip), a raw block → `data-head` (`{kind} · edit in Raw`, the `::before` head). Images = a `figure.doc-fig` node view with the alt as `figcaption` (a failed load → `.doc-img-broken`). Tables: 6×10 cells, header nowrap + `--bg-input`, the pipe row's alignment as text-align, tabular numbers; the GRIPS `.doc-grip-row` / `.doc-grip-col` (page-absolute, straddling the table's left / top edge) follow the hovered cell — else the selection's (touch) — and open the SAME `tableMenu` with the selection moved into that cell (the bar's old ⋯ table button is gone). Glyphs are parsed SVG nodes (`glyph()` via DOMParser) — the window still writes no HTML strings (test-doc-model §7). Gates: test-doc-window §9 (the audit sample at 1280 / 390 × dark / light × zh / en), test-toolbar-fold §6 (the groups, the fold order, the glyphs, no literal colour / radius).

**The comment popover (lane doc-comment-dismiss, 2.369.229 — userW inc-muxrol54-uv2d):** `commentOffer(open)` (exported; scripts/test-doc-comment-pop.mjs drives it over the real createPopover in a mini-DOM) owns the Add-comment popover: ONE at a time, keyed to the selection's (from, to). `sync(sel)` runs on EVERY selection-plugin update (`selNow(view)` = null when the selection is empty, the editor is unfocused or the mode is Raw) and drops the popover the moment the key changes. `sync(sel, true)`, 250 ms after the last update, opens one through `offerComment({ from, to, view })` for a NEW key only. `dismiss()` (the plugin's `handleDOMEvents.blur`, the pane's `scroll`, the window's abort, the button before `noteBox`) drops it but keeps the key; the house closer and Esc do the same, so a dismissed selection is not offered again until it changes. createPopover's anchor (the pane) is the closer's exclusion: the keeper empties `_closeExclude`, so a press anywhere but the popover is outside, the text included.

### src/lib/design-home.js + src/design-tokens.js — design systems + the Design window's home (lane design-systems-home, 2.369.203, NEW; design 003 §2 S5 + S6)
Lane D of the Design window v2 (B-6351, /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/claude-design-replica.md). Owner rulings shipped as recommended: Q1 no hand edits written to files, Q2 no PPTX.
- **A design system** is a design folder holding system.md (the guide) + tokens.css (custom properties) + component artboards. The registry row carries `kind: 'system'|'design'` (the CLI says which at `new --kind system` / `open`: a folder with system.md AND tokens.css as regular files); `pub()` rows carry `kind`.
- **Model** (src/design-model.js, additive): design.json's closed `system: {name}` key (KEYS.system ['name'], refusals by name); scanHtml's result gains `css: [[start, end]]` (style attributes + <style> blocks). **src/design-tokens.js** (PURE, requires only design-model.js; NOT bundled into the viewer — test-design-canvas budgets public/design-viewer.js < 60 KB and the token code took it to 60.3): `tokensOf(css)` (custom properties + every colour literal / length their values hold), `tokenLint(html, css, {file})` (hex / rgb() / hsl() colours and the size of font-size / font outside the tokens → `not_token`; a custom property set differently from tokens.css → `token_drift`; var() fallbacks, url() spans, scripts and selectors never read; ≤ 6 per artboard + "N more"), `tokensVerdict(text)` (≤ 256 KB, no NUL, no `</style` — it is pasted into a <style>). Every scan linear (work-meter legs).
- **Engine**: `systems()`, `defaultSystem()` (`design.defaultSystem` through `serverSetting` — server.js passes it), `systemTokens(name)` (name / folder / '' = the default; `no_system` / `ambiguous` / `no_default` by name) reads ONE registered system's tokens.css (local: one O_NOFOLLOW open; an ssh host: the one remote read, whose script now also emits tokens.css) — the HUB WRITES NO FILE: the CLI writes the copy into the folder it made (writeInside, before register). Every read of a folder holding tokens.css lints each artboard (`systemCheck` in compose → warnings; `no_tokens` when design.json names a system and the file is gone). `rename` (row title + `named: true` — the user's name then wins over the agent's register --title and design.json's title in the read) and `unlist` (the row leaves; no fs op; `designs-updated {removed: true}`). Agent views belt system names (`agentSystems`, `agentSystemTokens`); `agentView` carries `kind` + `system`.
- **Routes**: owner `GET /api/design/systems`, `POST /api/design/rename`, `POST /api/design/unlist`; agent `GET /api/agent/design/systems`, `GET /api/agent/design/system?name=`; register takes `kind`.
- **CLI**: `new --kind system` (system.md + tokens.css skeleton + a Components artboard built only from var(--…)), `new --system <name>|none` (asked BEFORE anything is made; no flag = the default when set, said; a default naming nothing = made without, said), `systems` (pre-approved: DESIGN_VERBS 10), `open` re-registers with the folder's kind, `show` / `list` say system / follows.
- **Client**: design-home.js — `openDesignHome(app)` (design-window.js: `if (!d) return openDesignHome(app, { syncId })` — same kind `design`, same action, openSpec dir ''), keyed rows updated in place (a rename's input keeps focus), find, ⋯ (Open · Rename · Show in Files · Copy published link · Remove from the list with a confirm), live on `designs-updated`; ⚙ Tools ▸ Designs… (order 38, ungated); `systemSelect()` for the chat chip (hidden while no system exists; the default preselected; "No design system" over a default sends `--system none`), "All designs…" under the popover. Conversation names via browser-who-dialog.js `nameHelpers`.
- **Gates**: test-design-model §9 + 7 controls, test-design-routes §10 + 8 controls (incl. the CLI end to end), test-window-types (the no-folder open pins + a negative control), test-contributions (the seventh owner row), test-architecture (§62 door row, PURE row), test-agent-tool-rules (10 design verbs), test-design-docs (hub codes), heavy test-design-window K① (zh 375 px: the home, find, Rename, Open, Remove, the chip's select + All designs…).

### src/design-viewer-entry.js → public/design-viewer.js — THE PUBLISHED DESIGN'S RUNTIME (NEW, the second esbuild entry)

`npm run build` writes `public/design-viewer.js` (`esbuild src/design-viewer-entry.js --bundle --format=iife --platform=browser --target=es2020 --minify`, ~26 KB; gitignored like `public/novnc.js` — the precedent); the hub (design-model.js `bundleCanvas`, lane L1) reads it at publish and inlines it into the page — `/p/<id>` is ONE self-contained file (offline, nothing fetched; the hub's placeholder runtime stands in when the file is absent). On load (`DOMContentLoaded` or at once) `mountDesignViewer(document)`: reads `<script type="application/json" id="vibespace-design-doc">` → PURE `normalizeDoc` ({v:1, title, manifest, files} — anything else ⇒ "This page carries no VibeSpace design." in words), mounts into `#vibespace-design-root` (the hub's shell; created when absent), draws a bar (‹ Back to canvas while focused · the title · Fit · − · zoom % (= 100 %) · + · pages when > 1 · "Made with VibeSpace") and the SAME canvas core as the window (src/lib/design-canvas.js — no picker, no comment, no ws: a published page is for looking at); double-click / tap = one artboard at fit-width and live, Esc = back; a hint chip until the first open. Not the app: no i18n runtime (the dictionaries are 1.5 MB, forty times this file) — `WORDS` en / zh / ja by the READER's browser language (`wordsFor`), the same keys in each; no VibeSpace stylesheet — `VIEWER_CSS` defines the canvas's theme tokens on `:root` (dark, and light under `prefers-color-scheme: light`; every colour literal is a token definition) and the page chrome; the canvas's own rules come from `CANVAS_CSS` (injected by the core). Chrome by textContent only. Gate: test-design-canvas ⑥c (the build line, the gitignore, the imports = core + model only, the state block + root ids, no innerHTML, no picker, WORDS parity + the language pick, the colour-literal census, the entry built in-process under 60 KB). Seen in headless Chrome over a page built by the hub's own `bundleCanvas` (2026-10-02): fit, double-click focus at fit-width, Esc back, the page switch.

**design-canvas.js, the dblclick (found driving the runtime in Chrome):** a drag captures its pointer at pointerdown, and pointer capture RETARGETS the compatibility click pair — a `dblclick` listener on the shield never fired. The canvas now reads `dblclick` on the VIEWPORT and finds the frame by the world point under it on the page shown (`toWorld` + the frames' rects, the last drawn on top).

### src/lib/design-ask.js — THE QUESTIONS SHEET + the visual check (lane design-ask, 2.369.203, NEW; design 003 §2 S1 + S3)
Lane A of the Design window v2 (B-6351, /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/claude-design-replica.md). The shared contract (§2: `user.json`, the `tweaks` / `system` manifest keys) is NOT touched here.
- **Model** (src/design-model.js, additive): `ASK_LIMITS` (8 questions, 8 options — key `optionCount`, never `options`: test-record-clear-census reads `.options` in a sentence as a record's text field — q 200, help 400, option 80, an "Other…" answer 500, 64 KB in); `validateQuestions(json)` (a list or `{questions}`; closed keys; refusals by name with the existing CODES; `kind` default one, `other` default true — false drops "Other…" and then options are required); `answersVerdict(questions, body)` (an option travels as its INDEX — its words always come from the pending question; a question left out = decide for me; `{skip:true}`); `answersText(verdict)` = `[Design answers] platform: iPhone · tweak: Accent, "font pairing"` / `[Design answers] skipped — decide everything yourself` (composes only; our heads inside a piece softened).
- **Engine** (src/server/design-engine.js): the pending questions live on the registry row (`ask: {id: qa…, at, sessionId, conversationId, questions}`, re-judged at every read); `ask` refuses another conversation's design (`not_yours` — the row's session OR conversation must be the caller's) and replaces older questions; every change pushes `design-ask {host, dir, ask}` through broadcastAll (no sessionId, never the asker's ids); `answer` checks `askId` (`stale` / `no_questions`), belts the line (`ANSWERS_LINE_MAX` 10 000 — 8 full questions fit) and sends it through `userLine(…, prefer)` — the comment's own sender (one sender after the design-joint merge) factored out of `comment` with its pinned lines unchanged (THE typing sender, origin design-comment; else the stash, source design-comment, preferring the asking conversation); delivered ⇒ cleared, a refused send keeps the questions. `preview` = one artboard of a REGISTERED folder as the read inlines it (`bad_file` / `not_found` / `not_previewable`; a symlink is never followed — the read's own rule); `previewLink` mints a 24-byte ticket bound to ONE (host, dir, file) for 15 min (≤ 64 live, oldest first) because the agent's browser carries no bearer; every load re-reads.

A re-read keeps the same artboard on screen; a page change, a pick, a focus or a fresh layout ends it. ### src/lib/design-tweaks.js + src/design-user-layer.js — THE TWEAKS PANEL + THE USER'S LAYER (lane design-tweaks, 2.369.203, NEW; design 003 §2 S4)
Lane C of the Design window v2 (B-6351, /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/claude-design-replica.md): free knobs. The agent declares them in design.json; the owner moves them in OUR panel; the frames restyle with no agent turn; the values persist in `user.json`, the contract's second file (design 003 §2 "Two contract additions"), whose ONE writer is the hub on the owner's act.
- **Model, split by the viewer's budget.** design-model.js is CJS and is bundled WHOLE into public/design-viewer.js (the published page's runtime; test-design-canvas trips at 60 KB, lanes A + B had taken it from 44.6 to 55.2). So it carries only what the viewer path needs: `tweaks` in KEYS.top + the list's SHAPE (a list, ≤ 12 — by name), the fence word `tweakSay` (ONE `--property` or ONE `data-` attribute, never `data-vibespace-…`; `tweakWordOk`: ≤ 80 chars, no `< > { } ; \ \` !`, no comment, no hidden character, quotes closed — a value cannot close the rule, the block or the root tag), and `WALK` (its own tag-walk primitives, exported so the user layer walks with the SAME linear walker). Each knob's rules live in **src/design-user-layer.js** (PURE CJS, requires design-model only) and reach the manifest through a hook: `validateManifest(json, {tweaks: tweaksOf})` — `UL.validateDesign` is the hub's ONE reader of design.json (compose + the Tweaks read). Without the hook (the viewer, bundleCanvas / readBundle) the manifest keeps NO knobs: the published page needs none, their values are baked. Viewer: 67.5 KB with everything in the model → 57.8 KB split.
- **The knobs**: `{id, label?, kind: color|range|select|toggle, var | attr, default}` + range `min, max, step?, unit?` (closed set px rem em % vw vh ch fr deg ms s) / select `options` (2–12 words of the grammar); closed keys PER KIND, one knob per target, refusals by name (`tweaks[i].<key>`). What the CSS gets (`tweakText`): a range = number (4 decimals) + unit on a property, bare on an attribute; a toggle = 1 / 0 on a property, "true" / "false" on an attribute; a colour lower-cased.
- **The user's layer**: `validateUserLayer` (`{v:1, tweaks:{id: value}}`, closed keys, ≤ 16 KB — an agent-written file is judged like any input); `userValues(manifest, user)` = every declared knob at the user's value when it fits (`tweakValueOk`), else its default; a value that no longer fits / a knob that is gone is DROPPED and said (a warning `where: user.json`), never applied.
- **Baking** (`applyUser(html, manifest, user)`, called by the engine's compose on every served artboard → the window's read, `preview`, publish): ONE `<style id="vibespace-tweaks">:root{--x:v !important;…}</style>` right after `<head …>` (else after `<html …>`) + ONE marked run right after `<html` — ` data-vibespace-tweaks="N" data-a="…" …` — first, because the HTML parser keeps the FIRST of a repeated attribute (the user's value beats the one the agent wrote on `<html>`). EVERY declared knob is baked (defaults too) so the panel and the page always agree. `userLayerOf` finds the layer ONLY at those two exact places by a linear tag walk (`rootTags`: comments, doctype and raw text skipped; a commented-out `<html` is not the root) and only when it is exactly what applyUser writes — so `applyUser` is idempotent (strip, then inject) even over an artboard that already carries layer-shaped text, and a block that is not ours is kept. Every word is re-judged at bake time: a manifest that skipped validation cannot close the block or the root tag.
- **Restyle in place**: `tweakSwap(before, after)` → `[]` (same), the `design-tweak` messages (the documents differ ONLY in the layer, same knobs), or null (reload). design-canvas.js gained `setSwap(fn)` (the panel hands `tweakSwap` in — the canvas never imports the user layer, so the viewer stays small) and a `rec.live` flag (set on the frame's load, cleared on a srcdoc assignment): when a re-read changes a LIVE frame's html only in the layer, the canvas `say`s the messages instead of reassigning srcdoc — no white flash, the frame keeps its scroll and state, on this device and every other one. A frame mid-load always reloads (a message to a document that is being replaced would be lost).
- **Engine** (design-engine.js): `user.json` is read with the folder (local: O_NOFOLLOW like the artboards — a link or a non-file entry is recorded `link` and SAID, `user_not_file`; remote: the one read command emits it and `@@ULINK` for a link); compose bakes; the result carries `tweaks`, `user.tweaks` (the user's that fit) and `userWarnings`. `isWatchable` includes user.json (the 2 s sweep sees a hand edit). `readMeta` = design.json + user.json only (two O_NOFOLLOW opens spelled `(O_NOFOLLOW || 0) | O_RDONLY` — its own control; ssh: ONE `remoteMetaScript`). `setTweaks({values: {id: value|null}, reset})`: one write chain per folder, merge (null = back to the default), refusals `unknown_tweak` / `bad_tweak` (with what fits) / `bad_tweaks` / `not_tweakable`; the file in the manifest's order; local = lstat (a link / non-file → `user_not_file` by name) + a fresh `.user.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp` (O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW) + rename (a rename replaces the NAME, never a link's target); ssh = ONE `remoteUserWriteScript` (refuse a link / non-file, mktemp beside it, base64 in the command, mv). Then ONE `file-changed` for user.json (the watch primed — no second broadcast). `requestTweaks` = "+ Tweaks": `[Design tweaks] Add Tweaks to this design: …` through THE belt down `userLine` (sent / queued / stashed like a comment). agentView adds `tweaks` (labels / options belted) + `user {tweaks, warnings}`.
- **Routes** (owner only — an agent bearer 403): `GET /api/design/tweaks`, `POST /api/design/tweaks`, `POST /api/design/tweaks/request`.
- **Frame**: design-canvas-model.js FRAME_KINDS + `design-tweak` (frameSay → tweakSay); design-pick.js hears it from its parent only and sets ONE root custom property (inline `!important` — beats the baked block) or ONE root data attribute, the grammar re-judged; nothing is reported back.
- **Panel** (`mountDesignTweaks({winInfo, canvas, stage, button, signal, phone, host, dir, sayChip})`, `winInfo._designTweaks` for the heavy suite): the bar's "Tweaks" button (`btn('tweaks', 'sliders', …, priority 1)` + its ⋯ row via `ROW_ACTS.tweaks`); a side panel on the stage's LEFT under `--design-top-dock` (the questions' pill owns the top-right, the chip the bottom), a bottom sheet ≤ 768 px with 44 px targets. Colour (input type=color), range (+ readout), select (≤ 4 short options = radio pills, else a select), toggle (a switch). A move tells every frame at once and writes 300 ms after the last move (on release at once); a knob whose write has not landed keeps its value through a re-read (`moving`). Reset = defaults told + `{reset:true}`. No knobs: "This design has no tweaks yet." + an optional words box + **+ Tweaks**. `file-changed` for design.json / user.json re-reads the panel.
- **CLI**: `show` lists every knob and "→ the user set …"; `check` one line; both print user.json warnings. The manual (§2 example + key row, §4 "Tweaks — knobs the user moves without a turn") and the craft rule (§4 "Give the user knobs") teach it; never write user.json.
- **Gates**: test-design-model §5d (31 rules by name, user.json, userValues, applyUser exact / idempotent / re-judging, tweakSwap, tweakSay, the request line) + 5 linear shapes + 9 controls; test-design-routes §10 (26 legs: the read, the write, ONE file-changed, the swap, publish baked, refusals, links and a directory never read / written through, ssh = 2 commands, + Tweaks sent / stashed) + 8 controls; test-design-canvas (frameSay + picker rows, 2 controls); heavy test-design-window T① (a drag restyles with zero agent messages, the re-read restyles in place, zh + phone).

### Migration 2026-10-design-kit-removed (src/server/migrations.js, lane design-docs-removal)
The Design window replaced the Claude CLI's /design kit, and `data/design-kit/<cliVersion>/` (the CLI's skill text, seeding helper and editor payload, extracted at runtime by the retired module) is read by nothing. `removeDesignKit(dir)`: `lstat` first — ENOENT ⇒ `{removed:false, why:'absent'}`; a symlink or a file at the root is UNLINKED, never followed; a directory is counted (versions = its subdirectories, files + bytes over ≤ 4 levels, by `lstat`, a failing count never keeps the files) then `rmSync(recursive)` (links inside go as links). The report `{removed, kind, versions, files, bytes}` rides the ledger. It DELETES rather than archives — the one exception to archive-then-strip, said in its note: the content is the CLI vendor's, and keeping a copy is the thing to stop. A refusal (a permission) FAILS the run: not recorded, the `migration-failed:` server notice, retried next boot. `data/published-pages/` is never read — the three canvases published through the kit stay on `/p/<id>`. Not covered: the kit copies a remote host mirrored into `~/.vibespace/design-kit/` (no device migration; inert files).
